Title: Presentation to the International Monetary and Financial Committee of the IMF
text: PRESENTATION TO INTERNATIONAL MONETARY AND FINANCIAL COMMITTEEWASHINGTON D.C. April 16, 2005H.E. Vittorio CorboPresident, Central Bank of Chile Thank you very much, Mr President. Because a written submission covering this topic has already been distributed, I will concentrate my comments on five points, which we believe are at the heart of the Fund's work. First, we fully share the central idea that sound economic and financial policies and institutions are fundamental to stability and sustained growth and are the best vehicle for poverty reduction. Chile's historical experience is illustrative in this regard. This goes far beyond policies and institutions that have a direct effect on stability, including also respect for property rights and the promotion of competition. Second, under this framework, the guiding principle for the Fund's medium-term strategy should be the strengthening of those financial and economic policies and institutions that have a direct effect on stability and growth. For those policies and institutions whose effect on stability and growth is indirect, the Fund should help identify them and countries should be encouraged to work on them, but this should not be a central part of its activities. Indeed, the Fund should maintain its focus on the objectives set out in the Articles of Agreement. However, it is of great importance that when the Fund engages in issues outside its core activities, it allows countries to develop the most appropriate ways to deal with and manage them. We believe that the Fund has an important role to play in identifying weaknesses and proposing measures to overcome them, but this together with an adequate division of labor with the World Bank and other multilateral institutions. Policies and institutions should also be designed to build and strengthen countries' capacity to cope with turbulence. This is particularly important in the current context, where, as we saw this morning, despite a benign central economic outlook, there are, unfortunately, some significant risks. A third aspect that I would like to comment, Mr. President, is the role of the Fund in Supervision and Monitoring activities. These, as well as technical assistance and research, must be aligned with the framework outlined above. With regard to emerging economies, supervision and monitoring should be directed more towards building and strengthening these countries' economic and financial institutions, strengthening their resilience to adverse shocks, and improving the Fund's capacity to develop stress test analyses. In this respect, the work carried out in the context of the FSAP and ROSC initiatives provides a solid basis for future progress in this area. Of course, in this line of work, as in many other areas, the Fund must take into account the differences between the various Member States. The Fund's role in oversight and monitoring is essential to assess the stability of the global system and anticipate the emergence of systemic problems. In this context, the supervision and monitoring activities of industrial countries are as important as those of developing countries. Today, when the main risks facing the world economy are global imbalances, this need appears with greater relevance. In order to ensure that these imbalances are adequately resolved, it is important for the Fund to promote economic policy dialogue among industrial countries in the various forums in which it participates. As a fourth point, I would like to mention that the creation and strengthening of the economic and financial capacity of countries to face turbulence depends not only on the development of appropriate policies and institutions, but also on countries having access to international liquidity in times of low availability. This is particularly important for countries that have made significant progress in overcoming weaknesses and strengthening their macro-financial policies and institutions, but are still vulnerable to systemic risks. At this point, we believe that the review of existing facilities d0 or the development of new ones d0 for the provision of liquidity to face adverse shocks should continue. In addition, the Fund should give higher priority to exploring new initiatives to improve liquidity by international private markets. In this context, we believe that the Fund could play a key catalytic role, working together with private actors, in the development of markets that provide relief in periods of liquidity tightness. Finally, we believe that it is essential to make progress in increasing the representation of emerging countries in the Fund. This would better reflect in their governance the increased importance that developing countries have gained in the world economy. The appropriate forum for the latter is the forthcoming review of the quotas of its member countries.
text_original: PRESENTACIN AL COMIT MONETARIO Y FINANCIERO INTERNACIONAL WASHINGTON D.C. 16 de abril de 2005 H.E. Vittorio Corbo Presidente, Banco Central de Chile Muchas gracias Seor Presidente. Debido a que ya se ha distribuido una presentacin escrita que cubre este tpico, concentrar mis comentarios en cinco puntos, los que creemos constituyen el corazn del trabajo del Fondo. Primero, compartimos plenamente la idea central relativa a que polticas e instituciones econmicas y financieras adecuadas son fundamentales para la estabilidad y el crecimiento sostenido y son el mejor vehculo para reducir la pobreza. La experiencia histrica de Chile es ilustrativa en este sentido. Esto va mucho ms all de polticas e instituciones que tienen un efecto directo en la estabilidad, incluyendo tambin el respeto a los derechos de propiedad y la promocin de la competencia. Segundo, bajo este marco, el principio gua para la estrategia de mediano plazo del Fondo debera ser el fortalecimiento de aquellas polticas e instituciones financieras y econmicas que tienen un efecto directo sobre la estabilidad y el crecimiento. En lo que respecta a aquellas polticas e instituciones cuyo efecto sobre la estabilidad y el crecimiento es indirecto, el Fondo debera ayudar a identificarlas y los pases, por su parte, ser incentivados a trabajar en ellas, pero esto no debera constituirse en parte central de sus actividades. En efecto, el Fondo debera mantener su foco en los objetivos que se recogen en el Convenio Constitutivo. No obstante, es de gran importancia que cuando el Fondo participe en temas ajenos a sus actividades centrales, permita que los pases desarrollen las formas ms adecuadas para enfrentarlos y manejarlos. Creemos que el Fondo tiene un importante rol en la identificacin de debilidades y en la proposicin de medidas para superarlas, pero esto junto con una adecuada divisin del trabajo con el Banco Mundial y otras instituciones multilaterales. Las polticas e instituciones deberan tambin ser diseadas con el propsito de crear y fortalecer la capacidad de los pases para enfrentar turbulencias. Ello es particularmente importante en el contexto actual, en el que, como vimos esta maana, no obstante imperar un panorama econmico central benigno, existen, desafortunadamente, algunos riesgos significativos. Un tercer aspecto que me gustara comentar, Seor Presidente, es el rol del Fondo en actividades de Supervisin y Monitoreo. Estas, as como la asistencia tcnica e investigacin, deben estar alineadas con el marco antes sealado. En lo referente a economas emergentes, la supervisin y monitoreo deben dirigirse en mayor medida a crear y fortalecer las instituciones econmicas y financieras de estos pases, reforzar su resistencia a choques adversos y mejorar la capacidad del Fondo para desarrollar anlisis de pruebas de tensin. En este aspecto, el trabajo desarrollado en el contexto de las iniciativas FSAP y ROSC constituye un base slida para futuros progresos en esta materia. Por supuesto que en esta lnea de trabajo, as como en muchas otras reas, el Fondo debe tomar en consideracin las diferencias entre los diversos pases miembros. El rol del Fondo en la supervisin y monitoreo es esencial para evaluar la estabilidad del sistema global y anticipar el surgimiento de problemas sistmicos. En este contexto, las actividades de supervisin y monitoreo de los pases industriales son tan importantes como las de los pases en desarrollo. Hoy da, cuando los principales riesgos que enfrenta la economa mundial son los desbalances globales, esta necesidad aparece con mayor relevancia. Para asegurar una adecuada resolucin de estos desequilibrios, es importante que el Fondo promueva el dilogo, en materia de poltica econmica, entre los pases industriales en los diversos foros en que participa. Como cuarto punto quisiera mencionar que la creacin y fortalecimiento de la capacidad econmica y financiera de los pases para enfrentar turbulencias, no depende solo del desarrollo de polticas e instituciones apropiadas, sino tambin de que los pases cuenten con acceso a liquidez internacional en tiempos de baja disponibilidad. Esto es particularmente importante para pases que han hecho significativos progresos en la superacin de sus debilidades y en el fortalecimiento de sus polticas e instituciones macro financieras, pero que an son vulnerables a riesgos sistmicos. En este punto pensamos que la revisin de las facilidades existentes o el desarrollo de nuevas para la provisin de liquidez que permita enfrentar choques adversos debe continuar. Adems, el Fondo debe otorgar mayor prioridad a la exploracin de nuevas iniciativas que permitan mejorar la liquidez por parte de mercados privados internacionales. En este contexto creemos que el Fondo podra jugar un rol cataltico clave, trabajando junto a agentes privados, en el desarrollo de mercados que provean alivio en perodos de estrechez de liquidez. Finalmente, creemos que es fundamental avanzar en cuanto a aumentar la representatividad de los pases emergentes en el Fondo. Esto permitira reflejar de mejor manera en su gobemabilidad la mayor importancia que han cobrado los pases en desarrollo en la economa mundial. El foro apropiado para esto ltimo es la prxima revisin de las cuotas de sus pases miembros.

Title: Launch Ceremony Contest "The Economy + Close"
text: Words of Don Vittorio CorboLaunch Ceremony Contest "The Economy Close" April 26, 2005 This year marks eighty years of existence of the Central Bank of Chile. Since its creation, the institution has been focused on carrying out the conduct of the country's monetary policy in a technical and responsible manner. The profound political and economic changes that took place in this period, both nationally and internationally, including, of course, advances in the theory and practice of monetary policy, made it necessary to have an institution independent of the government of the day, to give greater credibility and stability to policy decisions, which became effective on October 10, 1989. From that date the Central Bank of Chile becomes an autonomous body, of a technical nature and constitutional rank. Throughout its 15 years of autonomy, a monetary, exchange rate and financial policy framework has been built that has contributed to maintaining a solid economy integrated internationally, with low and stable inflation, and better prepared to face shocks. This allows us today to focus on other relevant aspects of our work and that are complementary to this framework, such as how to communicate with the public and educate the population on economic issues. This work of education has a dual purpose. On the one hand, it contributes to improving the understanding in society as a whole about the logic and importance of the work of a central bank, strengthening the institutionality of its autonomy. On the other hand, it contributes to improving the education of the population, an objective in itself, given the importance of education for the development of peoples. The most advanced central banks have already taken up this challenge through an educational agenda aimed at broad sectors of society. The BCCh, in order to contribute to the understanding of these issues by the non-specialized public, has undertaken the "Economy for the Majority" program, which seeks to disseminate basic economic concepts among different sectors of the population and, especially, explain our work. We want students, small and medium-sized entrepreneurs, technicians and professionals from areas other than economics, to be able to approach this discipline in a simple way, but without sacrificing the rigor that characterizes these issues. The publication of the book "Economy for All", written by Carlos Massad, former president of the BCCh, was the first milestone of the Program. For the year 2005, a great initiative is the school contest "The economy near" that we are officially launching today. This competition, aimed at third- and fourth-grade students from all educational establishments in the country, is sponsored by the Ministry of Education and operates mainly through a website specially created for these purposes. Students, organized in groups and led by a teacher, must write an essay on one of the following topics: Why controlling inflation is important. What are the benefits of having a sound financial system. How the variation in the interest rate determined by the Central Bank affects. These issues are fundamental for the Central Bank of Chile in fulfilling its objective of ensuring the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of payments. Therefore, we seek that students develop one of these topics from a personal point of view and analyze from a practical perspective the effects that the decisions of the authority have in their immediate environment, which is undoubtedly an important challenge for our young people. So that this activity reaches as many students as possible, we have sent almost two thousand letters with informative material to directors and teachers of around a thousand establishments throughout Chile, inviting them to participate. In addition, less than a week ago a seminar entitled "Foundations of the Success of the Chilean Economy" was held, which brought together almost 150 professors from various places, who were also encouraged to participate. Finally, to support the groups we have set up a call center, where teachers and students can consult a specialist in pedagogy regarding their doubts. So far the results have been higher than our expectations. Registration for the contest began on AprilI and about 200 groups from 80 educational establishments in different regions of the country have already registered. Complete courses have been organized to participate in the contest, making it part of the regular activities of the subject, which has resulted in more than 800 students actively participating. In fact, we are accompanied in this ceremony by representatives of the first three registered groups of Santiago (SEK International School, Cardenal Ra9cl Silva Henr92quez Multipurpose School and Valle Hermoso Educational Center), whom I greet very especially. In addition, for the BCCh it is tremendously satisfying to see the excellent reception we have had in such diverse places in our country as Alto Hospicio, Yobilo, La Uni97n, Traigu8en and Panguipulli, to name a few. As a result of the large number of participating teams, we have arranged for a jury composed of specialists in pedagogy and economists from the Central Bank, to select the 10 best essays. These will then be sent to a jury composed of high personalities of the country, who have also wanted to support us in this initiative: Sergio Bitar Chacra Oscar Godoy Arcaya Hugo Lavados Montes Enrique Marshall Rivera Alejandra Mizala Salces Maria Elena Ovalle Molina Jorge Rodriguez Grossi Aristides Torche Lazo and who speaks to them, make up this jury. The three finalist teams will be invited to present their essays at the Central Bank, where the first three places will be defined with prizes for the teacher, the students and the educational establishment to which they belong. Additionally, the name of the winning teachers will be reported to the Ministry of Education, the respective Seremi and the College of Teachers, which constitutes a good incentive for the participation of teachers. I would like to thank the collaboration of the people of the Ministry of Education, the Minister, his closest collaborators, the "Enlaces" network, and the Undersecretary of Education, who together have helped to disseminate the contest. I would also like to thank, on behalf of the Board of the Central Bank, all the staff of the bank who have collaborated enthusiastically in this task, and to make a very special recognition to the counselor Mar92a Elena Ovalle, who on behalf of the board has led this project and contributed enormously to its success. We hope to have the collaboration of all of you in the dissemination of the contest and the Program, since only a joint effort, involving all actors in society, will ensure that the "Economy for the Majority" program remains in time and is an important contribution to education and progress in the country. I thank everyone here for joining us on this occasion. Thanks a lot.

Title: Economic Outlook for Chile
text: ECONOMIC OUTLOOK FOR CHILE Presentation of Mr. Vittorio Corbo, President of the Central Bank of Chile, in Master Class held at the University of Los Lagos in Puerto Montt. 27 July 2005 The Chilean economy continues the expansion phase that began in the second half of 2004, with output growth exceeding potential output. As for trend inflation, as expected, it is gradually approaching the center of the target range, despite the more pronounced increase in the CPI due to the incidence of fuel increases and unusual increases in the prices of some perishable goods and certain regulated tariffs. This macroeconomic picture has been supported by clearly expansionary monetary conditions, a favourable external environment, and an adequate macroeconomic policy framework . External Scenario The favorable external environment includes high global growth, although lower than the surprising 2004, terms of trade (ratio of export prices to import prices) that improve even from last year's high values, and financial conditions that remain auspicious despite the progress of the US interest-rate normalization cycle. Indeed, for many observers and policymakers, the low level of long-term interest rates in that country has become a conundrum. After a slowdown in global growth at the beginning of the second quarter, it has regained strength. Growth continues to be driven by the US, China, India and the rest of emerging Asia. In contrast, Europe continues to show very weak growth, while Japan improves at the margin. As for Latin America, after a good year in 2004, there is now a moderate slowdown in its growth. U.S. growth has picked up steam after showing weakness towards the end of the first quarter, driven by favorable financial conditions, improvements in the labor market and good expectations from entrepreneurs and households. Growth in domestic demand is led by private consumption and the expansion of investment in housing. More recently, exports have also become more dynamic. The strength of demand in the US is surprising, despite the high prices that oil has reached . In the case of China, the boost to its growth stems from its successful integration into the global economy, which is resulting in strong growth in investment and exports. This growth is increasingly spreading towards domestic consumption. India, on the other hand, continues to reap the rewards of reforms implemented over the past decade. Europe, with its rigidities in important markets, continues to show great difficulties in adapting to an increasingly globalised world. In the short term, slow growth is mainly associated with domestic demand that remains very weak, while exports are beginning to show greater dynamism (especially in Germany). As for Japan, after having ended 2004 practically stagnant, it now shows greater dynamism, mainly in consumption and investment, while exports begin to show signs of greater strength. In sum, the future prospects show a picture in which the world economy would lose some momentum this year and next, after having grown in 2004 at its highest rate in thirty years. But even so, the world economy would grow in the biennium 2005-2006 well above what it grew on average in the nineties. In the case of raw materials, including oil, the high dynamism of the world economy, especially of important consumers such as the US, China and India, together with a low short-term supply response, have led to significant increases in prices. For Chile, this has resulted in high prices for both mining products, especially copper, as well as oil. The net effect of these effects is that the terms of trade have improved again this year. To the extent that global activity maintains robust growth, the outlook is that the price of copper will remain high, although it will probably be reduced over time by the incorporation of new projects and the consequent increases in production. As far as oil is concerned, the outlook is now that prices will remain high for a long time, with the additional risk of further increases from high prices . International financial conditions have remained favourable with low long-term rates, good market access and low debt spreads, despite increases in short-term interest rates. This picture is partly the result of the high liquidity prevailing in international financial markets, which in turn reflects expansionary monetary policies in the main industrial countries. This environment has been conducive to the refinancing of liabilities of emerging countries in more favorable financial conditions, a situation that countries have taken advantage of and that has resulted in a general improvement in the risk ratings of the emerging world by rating agencies. This favorable financial scenario has begun, very gradually, to reverse as the US continues with its policy of slow normalization of its monetary policy. In the euro zone and Japan, markets for now expect a return to less accommodative monetary policy not to begin until well into 2006. Associated with the advance of the normalization of monetary policy in industrial countries, it is likely that there will also be an increase in both longer-term interest rates and the spreads paid by countries and companies with lower risk ratings. Internal Conditions In the domestic scenario, favorable financial conditions stand out, as a result of the evolution of international interest rates and a domestic monetary policy that, although in the process of normalization, remains clearly expansionary. Thus, interest rates on nominal bonds d0 for the same term d0 are below the averages observed last year, although they have risen in recent weeks. Long-term interest rate movements have closely followed the evolution of rates of similar instruments in industrial countries, especially the US. Meanwhile, the rates of the indexed documents of the Central Bank to five and ten years (BCU-5 and BCU-10) are lower than the average of the last two years, although they have rallied after reaching historical lows. The behavior of indexed rates is the result of the trajectories of nominal rates and the normalization of the inflation compensation prize. With regard to financing individuals and businesses, the cost of consumer loans and short-term financing lines has risen in line with increases in the monetary policy rate, while the cost of credit and long-term financing remains relatively stable. However, credit continues to show strong expansion. With the auspicious external scenario and the favorable financial conditions it faces, the Chilean economy has continued its expansionary cycle, both at the household and business levels. Households benefit from a more active labour market and financing conditions, especially for mortgage loans, which are very favourable. In contrast, they suffer the effects of high oil prices, which reduce their real disposable income. Companies benefit from external and internal markets that remain dynamic, higher profits and positive financial conditions. In addition, companies that produce primary goods benefit from the high prices of their products. As in the case of households, companies suffer the consequences of high fuel prices, which increase their costs. On the demand side, the surprising dynamism that continues to show investment, especially in machinery and equipment, stands out. This expansion is based on the good conditions faced by companies, the increasing exhaustion of excess capacity that emerged in the years of low growth, and positive economic expectations. Private consumption expands in line with improvements in the labor market, good financial conditions, and stable consumer expectations. As for the volumes exported, these are expanded driven by the growth of the world economy, good international prices and the successful global insertion of Chile, which has been favored in recent years by trade agreements with important foreign markets, especially the US and Europe. With regard to aggregate activity, it expanded 5.8% annually during the first quarter and 6.4% in the April-May two-month period, thanks to the high dynamism of trade, industry and construction. Trade expansion has gone hand in hand with the rebound observed in imports of consumer goods, as well as private consumption and industrial sales. The greater industrial activity has been associated with the expansion of the branches linked to exports and consumption. The construction sector continues to expand at rates close to 10% per year, fully reflecting favorable macroeconomic and financial conditions. Sectors linked to natural resources have performed unevenly. On the one hand, electricity generation increases its contribution to product growth thanks to greater water generation and a lower than projected restriction of Argentine gas. On the other hand, mining shows weak growth, reflecting that companies do not have capacity gaps and new projects in execution will only mature towards 2006-2007. Fisheries have maintained negative growth rates mainly due to the scarcity of resources. The evolution of domestic activity and demand shows that the domestic risks to this year's performance, which we identified only a few months ago in our Monetary Policy Report, have gradually dissipated. At the beginning of May, we assessed that the short-term energy supply situation could have a negative impact on growth prospects. Also, although a significant rebound in consumption was expected, this was only a projection, which was not without risks, given that inventories were relatively high. The greater traction of domestic demand remained to be confirmed. Thanks to the continued unprecedented dynamism of investment, the materialization of the expansion of private consumption, the maintenance of a favourable external environment -despite high oil prices-, and the improved hydrological conditions, the scenario of short-term growth is promising. In this dynamic macroeconomic picture, employment grows by over 4% in 12 months and its annualized increase, so far this year, also exceeds 4%. As has been identified by others, the best relative quality employment is the one that expands the most. vigorously at present. At the sector level, employment linked to services and transport leads the expansion of seasonally adjusted employment. In contrast, industrial employment continues to recover slowly (although the good news is that it stopped its contraction). As for the unemployment rate, now that the labor participation rate is stabilizing and employment is gaining a strong dynamism, it is beginning to show a clearly downward cycle. Outlook for Inflation As for inflation, as expected, it begins to rebound towards the center of the target range, leaving behind several quarters of excessively low rates. Several factors are behind this trend: fuel hikes associated with higher international oil prices, abnormal increases in some perishable goods, and increases in certain feed-in tariffs. Together, these higher prices pushed up CPI inflation and, to a lesser extent, core CPI inflation, which excludes fuels and some fruits and vegetables. As a result, the dynamics of these two measures of inflation exceed the projections that were had only a few months ago, including those of the central bank itself. In contrast, changes in the IPCX1 index (IPCX without feed-in tariffs and other indexed prices) are roughly in line with forecasts and with the reduction of capacity gaps, now that several quarters are already completed with output growth above potential output. Going forward, the recent increases in the CPI will end up having some second-round effects both in the CPI, which currently reaches 2.4% per year, and in the IPX1, which is still below 2%, which will affect the dynamics of these two variables for some time. Some of these effects were already included in our previous projections. On the other hand, improvements in the labour market and the reduction of working hours are beginning to be reflected in wage increases. However, these increases have been offset by increases in hourly productivity, thanks to which unit labour costs remain contained. As always, there is a high degree of uncertainty about what the effective performance of the economy will look like. Right now the uncertainty is mainly associated with the development of the external environment. The main sources of uncertainty on this front relate to: (i) the ultimate effects of high oil prices, and even further increases, on top of the already high prices we observe, on global financial activity and markets; (ii) an abrupt adjustment in the large US current account deficit, due to an also abrupt reduction in its external financing, with effects on international parities and long-term interest rates; and (iii) the eventual effects of the now more permanent geopolitical and terrorism risks. On the domestic front, the main risks relate to how the various price shocks we have observed and the evolution of different cost factors will be transmitted towards the medium-term inflationary trend. A particularly important factor, which we have highlighted on previous occasions, refers to unit labour costs, both in terms of the trajectory shown by hourly productivity as the current expansionary cycle develops, and in terms of wage developments. Final considerations The central scenario described above contemplates an economy expanding at a rate that exceeds its potential growth (allowing the slack to be filled) and increases in CPI inflation that, it is expected, will have some second-round effects. These two effects are going to end up manifesting themselves in trend inflation measures for some period of time. This will require the Central Bank to continue to reduce the clearly expansionary monetary stimulus still present in the economy. This is the only way to make this positive cycle sustainable over time. As usual, and as stated by the Council in the communiqu8es of the monetary policy meetings, the Central Bank will remain vigilant to ensure that inflation remains around the centre of the target range over the usual monetary policy horizon . Low and predictable inflation is the greatest contribution the Central Bank can make both to the long-term growth of the economy and to maintaining its ability to use counter-cyclical policy when circumstances warrant.
text_original: PERSPECTIVAS ECONMICAS DE CHILE Presentacin de don Vittorio Corbo, Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, en Clase Magistral efectuada en la Universidad de los Lagos en Puerto Montt. 27 de julio de 2005 La economa chilena contina la fase de expansin iniciada en la segunda mitad del 2004, con un crecimiento del producto que supera al del producto potencial. En cuanto a la inflacin de tendencia, de acuerdo con lo previsto, sta se aproxima gradualmente hacia el centro del rango meta, a pesar del aumento ms pronunciado del IPC por la incidencia de las alzas de los combustibles y de los aumentos poco usuales de los precios de algunos bienes perecibles y ciertas tarifas reguladas. Este cuadro macroeconmico ha estado apoyado por condiciones monetarias claramente expansivas, un entorno externo favorable, y un adecuado marco de polticas macroeconmicas. Escenario Externo El entorno externo favorable incluye un crecimiento mundial alto, aunque inferior al sorprendente 2004, trminos de intercambio (razn de precios de exportaciones a precios de importaciones) que mejoran incluso con respecto a los altos valores alcanzados el ao pasado, y condiciones financieras que se mantienen auspiciosas a pesar del avance del ciclo de normalizacin de las tasas de inters de los EE.UU. De hecho, para muchos observadores y autoridades, el bajo nivel que han alcanzado las tasas de inters de largo plazo en ese pas se ha convertido en un acertijo. Despus de una desaceleracin del crecimiento mundial a comienzos del segundo trimestre, ste ha retomado fuerzas. El crecimiento sigue impulsado por EE.UU., China, India y el resto de Asia emergente. En contraste, Europa contina mostrando un crecimiento muy dbil, mientras que Japn mejora en el margen. En cuanto a Amrica Latina, despus de un buen ao 2004, se est observando ahora una moderada desaceleracin en su crecimiento. El crecimiento de EE.UU. ha retomado fuerza despus de haber mostrado debilidad hacia fines del primer trimestre, impulsado por las favorables condiciones financieras, mejoras en el mercado laboral y buenas expectativas de empresarios y hogares. El crecimiento de la demanda interna es liderado por el consumo privado y por la expansin de la inversin en viviendas. Ms recientemente se observa tambin un mayor dinamismo de las exportaciones. Sorprende la fortaleza de la demanda en EE.UU., pese a los altos precios que ha alcanzado el petrleo. En el caso de China, el impulso a su crecimiento se deriva de su exitosa integracin a la economa global, que est resultando en un fuerte crecimiento de la inversin y de sus exportaciones. Este crecimiento se propaga en forma creciente hacia el consumo interno. India, por otra parte, sigue cosechando los frutos de las reformas implementadas durante la ltima dcada. Europa, con sus rigideces en importantes mercados, sigue mostrando grandes dificultades para adaptarse a un mundo cada vez ms globalizado. En el corto plazo, el lento crecimiento est asociado principalmente a una demanda interna que sigue muy dbil, mientras las exportaciones comienzan a mostrar mayor dinamismo (especialmente en Alemania). En cuanto a Japn, despus de haber terminado el 2004 prcticamente estancado, evidencia ahora un mayor dinamismo, principalmente en el consumo y la inversin, mientras las exportaciones comienzan a dar seales de mayor fortaleza. En suma, las perspectivas futuras muestran un cuadro en que la economa mundial perdera cierto empuje este ao y el prximo, despus de haber crecido el 2004 a su mayor tasa en treinta aos. Pero incluso as, la economa mundial crecera en el bienio 2005-2006 bastante por encima de lo que creci en promedio en la dcada de los noventa. En el caso de las materias primas -incluido el petrleo-, el alto dinamismo de la economa mundial, especialmente de importantes consumidores como EE.UU., China e India, unido a una baja respuesta de corto plazo de la oferta, han determinado aumentos importantes en los precios. Para Chile, esto ha resultado en altos precios tanto para los productos mineros, especialmente el cobre, como tambin para el petrleo. El efecto neto de estos efectos es que los trminos de intercambio han vuelto a mejorar este ao. En la medida que la actividad mundial mantenga un crecimiento robusto, las perspectivas son que el precio del cobre seguir alto, aunque probablemente ir reducindose en el tiempo por la incorporacin de nuevos proyectos y los consiguientes aumentos en produccin. En lo que se refiere al petrleo, las perspectivas son ahora que los precios se van a mantener altos por un tiempo prolongado, con el riesgo adicional de nuevos incrementos a partir de los altos precios imperantes. En cuanto a las condiciones financieras internacionales, stas se han mantenido favorables con tasas de largo plazo bajas, buen acceso a los mercados y bajos spreads de deuda, pese a los aumentos que han registrado las tasas de inters de corto plazo. Este cuadro es el resultado, en parte, de la alta liquidez imperante en los mercados financieros internacionales, lo que a su vez es el reflejo de polticas monetarias expansivas en los principales pases industriales. Este ambiente ha sido propicio para la refinanciacin de pasivos de pases emergentes en condiciones financieras ms favorables, situacin que los pases han aprovechado y que ha resultado en una mejora generalizada en las clasificaciones de riesgo del mundo emergente por parte de las agencias clasificadoras . Este escenario financiero favorable ha comenzado, muy gradualmente, a revertirse a medida que EE.UU. contina con su poltica de normalizacin pausada de su poltica monetaria. En la zona euro y en Japn, los mercados por ahora esperan que el retorno a una poltica monetaria menos acomodaticia no se inicie sino hasta entrado el 2006. Asociado al avance de la normalizacin de la poltica monetaria de los pases industriales, es probable que se d tambin un aumento tanto en las tasas de inters a mayores plazos como en los spreads que pagan los pases y empresas de menor clasificacin de riesgo. Condiciones Internas En el escenario interno destacan las favorables condiciones financieras, resultado de la evolucin de las tasas de inters internacionales y de una poltica monetaria domstica que, aunque en proceso de normalizacin, sigue siendo claramente expansiva. As, las tasas de inters de los bonos nominales para igual plazo estn por debajo de los promedios observados el ao pasado, aunque han subido en las ltimas semanas. Los movimientos de las tasas de inters de largo plazo han seguido de cerca la evolucin de las tasas de instrumentos similares en los pases industriales, especialmente de EE.UU.. En tanto, las tasas de los documentos indexados del Banco Central a cinco y diez aos (BCU-5 y BCU-10) son menores al promedio de los ltimos dos aos, aunque han remontado despus de alcanzar mnimos histricos. El comportamiento de las tasas indizadas es el resultado de las trayectorias de las tasas nominales y la normalizacin del premio de compensacin inflacionaria. En lo que se refiere al financiamiento a personas y empresas, el costo de los crditos de consumo y lneas de financiamiento de corto plazo ha aumentado en lnea con los aumentos de la tasa de poltica monetaria, mientras que el costo de los crditos y financiamiento de largo plazo permanece relativamente estable. Con todo, el crdito contina mostrando una fuerte expansin. Con el auspicioso escenario externo y las favorables condiciones financieras que enfrenta, la economa chilena ha continuado su ciclo expansivo, tanto a nivel de los hogares como de las empresas. Los hogares se benefician de un mercado laboral ms activo y condiciones de financiamiento, especialmente para crditos hipotecarios, muy favorables. En contraste, sufren los efectos de los elevados precios del petrleo, que reducen su ingreso disponible real. Las empresas se benefician con mercados externos e internos que se mantienen dinmicos, mayores utilidades y positivas condiciones financieras. Adems, las empresas que producen bienes primarios se benefician de los altos precios de sus productos. Al igual que en el caso de los hogares, las empresas sufren las consecuencias de los elevados precios de los combustibles, que incrementan sus costos. Por el lado de la demanda, destaca el sorpresivo dinamismo que contina mostrando la inversin, especialmente en maquinaria y equipos. Esta expansin se fundamenta en las buenas condiciones que enfrentan las empresas, el agotamiento creciente de los excesos de capacidad que emergieron en los aos de bajo crecimiento, y las positivas expectativas econmicas. El consumo privado se expande en lnea con las mejoras en el mercado laboral, las buenas condiciones financieras, y expectativas de los consumidores que se mantienen estables. En cuanto a los volmenes exportados, stos se expanden empujados por el crecimiento de la economa mundial, los buenos precios internacionales y la exitosa insercin global de Chile, la que se ha visto favorecida en los ltimos aos por acuerdos comerciales con importantes mercados externos, especialmente EE.UU. y Europa. En lo que se refiere a la actividad agregada, sta se expandi 5,8% anual durante el primer trimestre y 6,4% en el bimestre abril-mayo, gracias al alto dinamismo del comercio, la industria y la construccin. La expansin del comercio ha ido de la mano del repunte observado en las importaciones de bienes de consumo, as como del consumo privado y las ventas industriales. La mayor actividad industrial ha estado asociada a la expansin de las ramas ligadas a la exportacin y al consumo. El sector construccin contina expandindose a tasas cercanas al 10% anual, reflejando en plenitud las favorables condiciones macroeconmicas y financieras. Los sectores ligados a recursos naturales han tenido un desempeo dispar. Por una parte, la generacin de electricidad incrementa su contribucin al crecimiento del producto gracias a una mayor generacin hdrica y una restriccin de gas argentino inferior a la proyectada. Por otra, la minera muestra un dbil crecimiento, reflejo de que las empresas no tienen holguras de capacidad y los nuevos proyectos en ejecucin slo madurarn hacia el 2006-2007. La pesca ha mantenido tasas de crecimiento negativas fundamentalmente por la escasez de recursos. La evolucin de la actividad y de la demanda interna muestra que los riesgos internos para el desempeo de este ao, que identificamos hace solo algunos meses en nuestro Informe de Poltica Monetaria, se han ido disipando. A comienzos de mayo evaluamos que la situacin de abastecimiento energtico de corto plazo poda influir negativamente en las posibilidades de crecimiento. Asimismo, aunque se esperaba un repunte importante del consumo, esto era solo una proyeccin, la que no estaba exenta de riesgos, dado que los inventarios eran relativamente altos. Quedaba por confirmarse la mayor traccin de la demanda interna. Gracias al mantenimiento de un inusitado dinamismo de la inversin, a la materializacin de la expansin del consumo privado, al mantenimiento de un entorno externo favorable -pese a los elevados precios del petrleo-, y a las mejores condiciones hidrolgicas, el escenario de crecimiento de corto plazo es promisorio. En este cuadro macroeconmico dinmico, el empleo crece por sobre el 4% en 12 meses y su incremento anualizado, en lo que va del ao, supera tambin el 4%. Como ha sido identificado por otros, el empleo de mejor calidad relativa es el que se expande ms vigorosamente en la actualidad. A nivel de sectores, el empleo ligado a servicios y transporte lidera la expansin del empleo desestacionalizado. En contraste, el empleo industrial contina con una recuperacin lenta (aunque la buena noticia es que detuvo su contraccin). En cuanto a la tasa de desempleo, ahora que se estabiliza la tasa de participacin laboral y que el empleo cobra un fuerte dinamismo, sta comienza a mostrar un ciclo claramente descendente. Perspectivas para la Inflacin En cuanto a la inflacin, tal como se esperaba, sta comienza a repuntar hacia el centro del rango meta, dejando atrs varios trimestres de tasas excesivamente bajas. Varios factores estn detrs de esta tendencia: las alzas de los combustibles asociadas a los mayores precios internacionales del petrleo, las alzas anormales de algunos bienes perecibles, y los aumentos de ciertas tarifas reguladas. En su conjunto estos mayores precios empujaron al alza la inflacin del IPC y, en menor medida, la inflacin subyacente IPCX que excluye los combustibles y algunas frutas y verduras. Como resultado, la dinmica de estas dos medidas de inflacin supera las proyecciones que se tenan hace solo algunos meses, incluidas las del propio banco central. En contraste, las variaciones del ndice IPCX1 (IPCX sin tarifas reguladas y otros precios indexados) estn aproximadamente en lnea con lo previsto y con la reduccin de las brechas de capacidad, ahora que ya se completan varios trimestres con un crecimiento del producto por encima del producto potencial. Hacia delante, los recientes aumentos del IPC terminarn por tener algunos efectos de segunda vuelta tanto en el IPCX, que actualmente llega a 2,4% anual, como en el IPX1, que an se encuentra por debajo de 2%, lo cual afectar la dinmica de estas dos variables por algn tiempo. Parte de estos efectos ya se incluan en nuestras proyecciones anteriores. De otra parte, las mejoras en el mercado laboral y la reduccin de la jornada laboral comienzan a reflejarse en aumentos salariales. Sin embargo, estos aumentos se han visto compensados por aumentos de productividad horaria, gracias a lo cual los costos unitarios del trabajo se mantienen contenidos. Como siempre, existe un alto grado de incertidumbre respecto de cmo ser el desempeo efectivo de la economa. En este momento la incertidumbre est principalmente asociada al desarrollo del entorno externo. Las principales fuentes de incertidumbre en este frente se relacionan a: (i) los efectos ltimos de los altos precios del petrleo, e incluso de nuevos aumentos, por encima de los ya altos precios que observamos, sobre la actividad y los mercados financieros mundiales; (ii) que se d un ajuste abrupto en el elevado dficit en cuenta corriente de EE.UU., debido a una reduccin tambin abrupta de su financiamiento externo, con efectos en las paridades internacionales y en las tasas de inters de largo plazo; y (iii) los efectos eventuales de los ahora ms permanentes riesgos geopolticos y de terrorismo. En el frente interno, los principales riesgos se relacionan con la manera como se transmitirn hacia la tendencia inflacionaria de mediano plazo los distintos shocks de precios que hemos observado y la evolucin de los distintos factores de costo. Un factor particularmente importante, que hemos destacado en ocasiones anteriores, se refiere a los costos laborales unitarios, tanto en lo que respecta a la trayectoria que muestre la productividad horaria a medida que se desarrolle el ciclo expansivo actual, como a la evolucin de los salarios. Consideraciones Finales El escenario central descrito anteriormente contempla una economa que se expande a una tasa que supera su crecimiento potencial (lo que permite que se vayan copando las holguras) y aumentos de la inflacin del IPC que, se espera, tendr algunos efectos de segunda vuelta. Estos dos efectos se van a terminar manifestando en las medidas de inflacin de tendencia por algn perodo de tiempo. Esto requerir que el Banco Central contine reduciendo el estmulo monetario claramente expansivo an presente en la economa. Esta es la nica manera de hacer sostenible en el tiempo este ciclo positivo. Como es habitual, y como lo ha manifestado el Consejo en los comunicados de las reuniones de poltica monetaria, el Banco Central se mantendr atento para asegurar que la inflacin se mantenga en torno al centro del rango meta en el horizonte habitual de la poltica monetaria. Una inflacin baja y predecible es la mayor contribucin que el Banco Central puede hacer tanto para el crecimiento de largo plazo de la economa, como para mantener su capacidad de utilizar una poltica contra-cclica cuando las circunstancias lo ameriten.

Title: The Eighty Years of the Central Bank of Chile
text: The Eighty Years of the Central Bank of Chile Speech made by Mr. Vittorio Corbo, President of the Central Bank of Chile, on the occasion of the inauguration of the Exhibition of the Collection of Coins and Banknotes of the BCCh. Museum of Fine Arts, 2 August 2005 On this occasion, as we begin the month in which the anniversary of the Central Bank of Chile is celebrated, I would like to refer briefly to the history of our beloved bank, in particular to the circumstances and events that gave rise to its foundation. The concern about the need to provide the economy with an adequate amount of means of payment and establish a more efficient credit system, dates back to the colonial era and was a constant in the first 100 years of independent life of the country. However, it was only in 1840, after some commercial houses issued vouchers and tokens, that the discussion about the need to create commercial banks, or a national or State one, that would solve the problems of shortage of working capital and inefficiency of the credit system, focused until then on the figure of the lender, gained greater strength. There was already some concern in the discussions on the establishment of banks that the creation of a state-owned bank, which was also issued, could result in a disorderly expansion of working capital, which would jeopardize the survival of the bimetallic monetary system and result in inflation. For this reason, the idea prevailed that the work of creating money should be assumed by the State, through an entity independent of the government. In the midst of this controversy, in 1849 the first commercial bank was created, the Banco de Chile de Arcos, which within certain limits was authorized to issue convertible notes in metallic currency, which, however, were not accepted in the offices and fiscal treasuries. But, from its inception this bank encountered strong opposition from the established commerce of Valpara92so and Coquimbo, both because of the low credibility of the bills it issued, and because it reduced the income that the trade was obtaining from the seigniorage on the issuance of vouchers and tokens. Banco de Chile de Aros was short-lived: the government ended up withdrawing its issuing power as a result of the resistance it had created and the Supreme Court restricted the use of its banknotes. In the 1850s a major expansion of private banking began, in response to the economic boom associated with the discovery of gold in California, accentuating this in 1860, with the enactment of a very liberal banking law gestated by the renowned French economist Courcelle Seneuil. Monsieur Seneuil, who was against the creation of a state bank, had come to Chile as an advisor to the Ministry of Finance and professor of Political Economy at the University of Chile. Under this new law, which was in effect until 1925, banks could issue convertible notes in metal of 20, 50 and 500. The issue was subject to a ceiling equal to 150% of the banks' effective capital. These notes were accepted by the state in the payment of taxes and debt. Banks were also authorized to open current accounts, which were payable in notes or in coin. The entry into the sector was quite automatic and the capacity for regulation and control by the State was practically nil. In this scenario, the war between Chile and Spain in 1865 sharpened the financing needs of the State, which authorized the issuance of inconvertible notes to those banks that granted loans. This not only led to the suspension of convertibility, but also to an expansion of banking and issuance. The convertibility of cash notes was restored in 1866, but had to be suspended twelve years later because of a severe balance of payments crisis. Subsequently, several attempts were made to return to convertibility, but the lack of banking regulation and supervision, and events such as the Pacific War and a widespread shortage of gold in the world, which gave rise to 20 years of global deflation between 1875 and 1895, made this return extremely difficult. In addition, to finance the War of the Pacific first and the civil war of 1891 later, the State issued, for the first time, tax notes. In 1895 it was finally possible to return to convertibility, this time in a gold standard regime, but having chosen a very strong parity for the peso, and the external crisis of 1898, led to abandon it. That year, banks were prohibited from issuing banknotes as long as inconvertibility persisted, a restriction that ended up becoming permanent. Thus, in 1898 a period of full apogee of paper money began in Chile, which would last until the creation of the Central Bank in 1925. The continuous monetary expansion that was generated under this new regime gave rise to a long period of high and variable inflation coupled with a continuous depreciation of the currency. The experience of the previous decades led, at the beginning of the twentieth century, to think that some order had to be put in the issuance to control the creation of money, end the depreciation of the currency and, ultimately, with inflation. A proposal that achieved great support was the one that emerged in 1913 to create a Convertibility Fund. The proposal ultimately failed because of the problems caused by the First World War, which led to another expansion of the issue to cover the needs of helping the nitrate industry and banks in difficulty. After many and unsuccessful initiatives, both of the Executive and the Legislative, in 1918 the Minister of Finance Don Luis Claro Solar presented in the Chamber of Deputies a project on the creation of a Central Bank, but Congress did not make any decision on the matter. This initiative was followed by a proposal, in 1919, of the then Minister of Finance Mr. Guillermo Subercaseaux, later President of the BCCh, which however met with the opposition of the Senate because of its state character. But from this proposal began a deeper discussion d0 which also occurred in the international arena d0 on the need to create a Central Bank that would regulate the issuance, guarantee exchange rate stability and prepare the country for an eventual return to convertibility. The issue gained great strength in the period 1921-1925, focusing the discussion mainly on the ownership of the bank (whether it should be state, mixed or private) and on the monetary system to be adopted. The matter reached its peak with the Currency Week organized by the Faculty of Commerce of the Catholic University of Santiago in August 1924, an event in which various proposals were presented on how to solve Chile's monetary problem and, in particular, on how to create a stable currency. The majority position was that the order in the fiscal accounts and the creation of a central body controlled mostly by the private sector, which handled the issuance of means of payment, were fundamental elements to achieve the stability of the currency. In the end, it fell to the mission headed by Princeton University Professor Edwin Kemmerer to lay the foundations of the law that on August 21, 1925 created the Central Bank of Chile. The monetary regime of the gold standard was established, although this time more care was taken in choosing the initial parity of the peso. The Central Bank was created as an independent entity with a board of ten members, of which only three were appointed by the President of the Republic. The shareholders of the Central Bank were the State, domestic banks, foreign banks and the public. The State's participation in the Bank's capital reached a little more than 20% of it at the time of its foundation. However, the creation of the Central Bank of Chile did not end the monetary and exchange problems, but, on the contrary, these worsened after the (definitive) abandonment of convertibility in 1931, following the Great Depression and the great difficulties faced by the country due to the collapse of commodity prices. The Central Bank's early years were far from easy, with the country trying to adjust to the external shock of the Great Depression, with a fixed exchange rate and an explosive fiscal deficit. After the abandonment of convertibility, the country had to deal with inflation resulting from the expansions of the emission due to pressures from both the State and the private. Continued inflationary overflows led to the preparation of numerous stabilization programsd1in 1955-56, 1959-61, 1967, and 1978-82d1but all ended up failing due to the country's inability to control fiscal deficits and the permanent incoherence between fiscal, monetary, and exchange rate policies. The most recent history is known to all and we have referred to it on multiple occasions: the conquest of price stability was only possible after the return to fiscal responsibility from the eighties and the granting of autonomy to the Central Bank in 1989, with a Constitutional Organic Law that gave it the mandate to ensure price stability and internal and external payments. The construction of a safe and sound banking system, based on appropriate regulation and supervision, has also helped to achieve stability. It should be noted, however, that the objectives set out in the new institutionality of the Central Bank of Chile are common to those that have been set for other central banks in the world. This, because several factors have led countries since the eighties to have begun to consider as the priority objective of monetary policy the achievement and maintenance of low and stable inflation. First, the growing theoretical and empirical evidence that the attempt to permanently reduce unemployment through expansionary monetary policies inevitably results in an acceleration of inflation without a permanent effect on the unemployment rate. Second, the growing acceptance that economic agents form their expectations by taking into account the expected course of economic policies, correcting the notion that agents could be systematically mistaken. In these circumstances, the benefits of achieving lower unemployment with higher inflation vanish. And third, the broad consensus among economists that macroeconomic stability is a precondition for sustained growth, and thus that monetary policy can best make to influencing long-term growth is to help achieve and sustain low and even inflation. In order for a central bank to meet the objective of price stability more efficiently, it is necessary to protect the monetary authority from pressures associated with political cycles, which tempt it to seek temporary reductions in unemployment with an expansionary monetary policy that would end up resulting in an acceleration of inflation. The temptation is great, given that the costs are paid in the future (either with less growth and more unemployment, or when political pressure forces the introduction of adjustment programs to reduce inflation). To resolve this real temptation to pursue expansionary policies with short-term benefits and high medium- and long-term costs, innovation has been made by creating autonomous central banks with a clear mandate to achieve low and stable inflation and with a board of directors independent of the government. This is the mandate conferred by the Constitutional Organic Law on the Central Bank of Chile. The autonomous Central Bank has successfully introduced an inflation-targeting monetary policy scheme based on the quality of its staff and international developments in the theory and practice of monetary policy. With this institutionality, the country has finally managed to reduce inflation to levels similar to that of industrial countries, without major costs in terms of activity and employment, also reducing in the process the volatility of both inflation and output. Today, the Central Bank of Chile is a great asset for all Chileans. This, through the full fulfillment of its mandate to achieve and maintain price stability and the payment system, contributes in a fundamental way to the macroeconomic stability of the country, which is a necessary condition for achieving high and sustained growth rates that allow, in turn, to improve the living standards of the population, especially of those most in need. Many of the people who are with us this afternoon have been protagonists of this successful task, and this is an appropriate opportunity to publicly thank them for their valuable contribution to the construction of an institutionality that today is a source of legitimate pride for the country. But this task has not been exhausted, and the new generations must continue working so that this institutionality continues to deliver the fruits of the monetary and financial stability that was so elusive throughout our independent life. This is the best way in which the Central Bank of Chile can contribute to the economic development of our country. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Los Ochenta Aos del Banco Central de Chile Discurso efectuado por don Vittorio Corbo, Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, con motivo de la inauguracin de la Exposicin de la Coleccin de Monedas y Billetes del BCCh. Museo de Bellas Artes, 2 de agosto de 2005 En esta oportunidad, en que damos inicio al mes en que se celebra el aniversario del Banco Central de Chile, quisiera referirme brevemente a la historia de nuestro querido banco, en particular a las circunstancias y eventos que dieron origen a su fundacin. La preocupacin sobre la necesidad de proveer a la economa de una cantidad adecuada de medios de pago y establecer un sistema de crdito ms eficiente, se remonta a la poca de la Colonia y fue una constante en los primeros 100 aos de vida independiente del pas. Sin embargo, fue solo en 1840, luego de que algunas casas comerciales emitieran vales y fichas, que cobr mayor fuerza la discusin sobre la necesidad de crear bancos comerciales, o uno nacional o del Estado, que permitiera resolver los problemas de escasez de circulante e ineficiencia del sistema de crdito, centrado hasta entonces en la figura del prestamista. En los debates relativos al establecimiento de bancos ya exista cierta preocupacin de que la creacin de un banco estatal, que tambin fuese de emisin, poda terminar en una expansin desordenada del circulante, la que pondra en peligro la supervivencia del sistema monetario bimetlico y resultara inflacionaria. Por esta razn primaba la idea de que la labor de creacin de dinero la deba asumir el Estado, a travs de un ente independiente del gobierno. En medio de esta polmica, el ao 1849 se crea el primer banco comercial, el Banco de Chile de Arcos, el que dentro de ciertos lmites estaba autorizado para emitir billetes convertibles en moneda metlica, los que, sin embargo, no se aceptaban en las oficinas y tesoreras fiscales. Pero, desde su inicio este banco encontr una fuerte oposicin del comercio establecido de Valparaso y Coquimbo, tanto por la baja credibilidad de los billetes que emita, como porque reduca los ingresos que el comercio estaba obteniendo por el seoriaje sobre la emisin de vales y fichas. El Banco de Chile de Aros tuvo una corta vida: el gobierno termin retirndole la facultad emisora como resultado de la resistencia que haba creado y la Corte Suprema restringi el uso de sus billetes. En la dcada de 1850 se inici una expansin importante de la banca privada, en respuesta al auge econmico asociado al descubrimiento de oro en California, acentundose esta en 1860, con la promulgacin de una ley de bancos muy liberal gestada por el reputado economista francs Courcelle Seneuil. Monsieur Seneuil, quien era contrario a la creacin de un banco estatal, haba venido a Chile como asesor del Ministerio de Hacienda y profesor de Economa Poltica de la Universidad de Chile. De acuerdo con esta nueva ley, que estuvo vigente hasta 1925, los bancos podan emitir billetes convertibles en moneda metlica de $20, $50 y $500. La emisin estaba sujeta a un lmite mximo igual al 150 por ciento del capital efectivo de los bancos. Estos billetes eran aceptados por el Estado en el pago de impuestos y deuda. Los bancos tambin estaban autorizados a abrir cuentas corrientes, las cuales eran pagaderas en billetes o en moneda metlica. El ingreso al sector era bastante automtico y la capacidad de regulacin y fiscalizacin por parte del Estado era prcticamente nula. En este escenario, la guerra entre Chile y Espaa de 1865 agudiz las necesidades de financiamiento del Estado, que autoriz la emisin de billetes inconvertibles a aquellos bancos que le otorgaran prstamos. Esto no solo llev a la suspensin de la convertibilidad, sino tambin a una expansin de la banca y de la emisin. La convertibilidad de los billetes en metlico se restableci en 1866, pero debi suspenderse doce aos ms tarde a causa de una severa crisis de balanza de pagos. Posteriormente se hicieron varios intentos por volver a la convertibilidad, pero la falta de regulacin y supervisin bancaria, y eventos como la Guerra del Pacfico y una escasez generalizada de oro en el mundo, que dio origen a 20 aos de deflacin mundial entre 1875 y 1895, hicieron este retorno extremadamente difcil. Adems, para financiar la Guerra del Pacfico primero y la guerra civil de 1891 despus, el Estado emiti, por primera vez, billetes fiscales. En 1895 se logr finalmente volver a la convertibilidad, esta vez en un rgimen de patrn oro, pero el haber elegido una paridad muy fuerte para el peso, y la crisis externa de 1898, llevaron a abandonarla. Ese ao se prohibi a los bancos emitir billetes mientras persistiera la inconvertibilidad, restriccin que termin resultando permanente. As, en 1898 se inicia en Chile un perodo de pleno apogeo del papel moneda, que durara hasta la creacin del Banco Central en 1925. La continua expansin monetaria que se gener bajo este nuevo rgimen dio origen a un largo perodo de inflacin alta y variable unida a una continua depreciacin de la moneda. La experiencia de las dcadas anteriores llev, en los inicios del siglo veinte, a pensar que haba que poner algn orden en la emisin para controlar la creacin de dinero, terminar con la depreciacin de la moneda y, en ltimo trmino, con la inflacin. Una propuesta que logr gran apoyo fue la que surgi en 1913 de crear una Caja de Convertibilidad. La propuesta fracas en ltimo trmino por los problemas que acarre la Primera Guerra Mundial, que llevaron a otra expansin de la emisin para cubrir las necesidades de auxiliar a la industria salitrera y a los bancos en dificultades. Despus de muchas e infructuosas iniciativas, tanto del Ejecutivo como del Legislativo, en 1918 el Ministro de Hacienda don Luis Claro Solar present en la Cmara de Diputados un proyecto sobre la creacin de un Banco Central, pero el Congreso no tom ninguna decisin sobre la materia. Esta iniciativa fue seguida de una propuesta, en 1919, del entonces Ministro de Hacienda don Guillermo Subercaseaux, ms tarde Presidente del BCCh, la que sin embargo encontr la oposicin del Senado por el carcter estatal del mismo. Pero a partir de esta propuesta se inici una discusin ms profunda  que tambin se daba en el mbito internacional sobre la necesidad de crear un Banco Central que regulara la emisin, garantizara la estabilidad cambiara y preparara al pas para un eventual retomo a la convertibilidad. El tema tom gran fuerza en el perodo 1921-1925, centrndose la discusin principalmente en la propiedad del banco (si este deba ser estatal, mixto o privado) y en el sistema monetario que se adoptara. El asunto lleg a su apogeo con la Semana de la Moneda organizada por la Facultad de Comercio de la Universidad Catlica de Santiago en agosto de 1924, evento en el cual se presentaron variadas propuestas sobre cmo resolver el problema monetario de Chile y, en particular, sobre cmo crear una moneda estable. La postura mayoritaria fue que el orden en las cuentas fiscales y la creacin de un organismo central controlado mayoritariamente por el sector privado, que manejara la emisin de medios de pago, eran elementos fundamentales para alcanzar la estabilidad de la moneda. Al final le correspondi a la misin encabezada por el Profesor de la Universidad de Princeton, Edwin Kemmerer, sentar las bases de la ley que el 21 de agosto de 1925 cre el Banco Central de Chile. Se estableci el rgimen monetario del patrn oro, aunque esta vez se tuvo ms cuidado en la eleccin de la paridad inicial del peso. El Banco Central se cre como un ente independiente con un directorio de diez miembros, de los que solo tres eran nombrados por el Presidente de la Repblica. Los accionistas del Banco Central fueron el Estado, los bancos nacionales, los bancos extranjeros y el pblico. La participacin del Estado en el capital del Banco alcanzaba a un poco ms del 20% de este al momento de su fundacin. Sin embargo, la creacin del Banco Central de Chile no termin con los problemas monetarios y cambiarios, sino que, por el contrario, estos se agudizaron luego del abandono (definitivo) de la convertibilidad en 1931, a raz de la Gran Depresin y por las grandes dificultades que enfrent el pas por el colapso de los precios de las materias primas. Los primeros aos del Banco Central no fueron nada fciles, con el pas tratando de ajustarse al shock externo de la Gran Depresin, con tipo de cambio fijo y un explosivo dficit fiscal. Despus del abandono de la convertibilidad, el pas tuvo que lidiar con la inflacin que resultaba de las expansiones de la emisin debidas a presiones tanto del Estado como de los privados. Los continuos desbordes inflacionarios llevaron a preparar numerosos programas de estabilizacin en 1955-56, 1959-61, 1967 y 1978- 82, pero todos terminaron fracasando debido a la incapacidad del pas de controlar los dficit fiscales y a la permanente incoherencia entre las polticas fiscal, monetaria y cambiara. La historia ms reciente es por todos conocida y nos hemos referido a ella en mltiples oportunidades: la conquista de la estabilidad de precios solo fue posible luego del retomo a la responsabilidad fiscal a partir de los aos ochenta y del otorgamiento de autonoma al Banco Central en 1989, con una Ley Orgnica Constitucional que le entreg el mandato de velar por la estabilidad de precios y de los pagos internos y externos. Ha ayudado tambin en el logro de la estabilidad la construccin, a partir de la segunda mitad de los aos ochenta, de un sistema bancario seguro y slido, amparado en regulacin y supervisin apropiadas. Cabe sin embargo destacar que los objetivos planteados en la nueva institucionalidad del Banco Central de Chile son comunes a los que se le han fijado a otros bancos centrales en el mundo. Esto, por cuanto varios factores han llevado a que desde la dcada de los ochenta los pases se hayan comenzado a plantear como el objetivo prioritario de la poltica monetaria el logro y mantenimiento de una inflacin baja y estable. Primero, la creciente evidencia terica y emprica de que el intento de reducir en forma permanente el desempleo mediante polticas monetarias expansivas ocasiona, inevitablemente, una aceleracin de la inflacin sin un efecto permanente en la tasa de desempleo. Segundo, la creciente aceptacin de que los agentes econmicos forman sus expectativas tomando en cuenta el curso esperado de las polticas econmicas, corrigiendo la nocin de que los agentes se podan equivocar sistemticamente. En estas circunstancias, los beneficios de lograr menor desempleo con mayor inflacin se esfuman. Y tercero, el amplio consenso logrado entre los economistas en cuanto a que la estabilidad macroeconmica es una precondicin para el crecimiento sostenido y, por ende, que la mejor contribucin que puede hacer la poltica monetaria para influir en el crecimiento de largo plazo es ayudar a lograr y mantener una inflacin baja y pareja. Para que un banco central pueda cumplir en forma ms eficiente con el objetivo de estabilidad de precios, se requiere proteger a la autoridad monetaria de presiones asociadas a ciclos polticos, que la tienten a buscar bajas temporales en el desempleo con una poltica monetaria expansiva que terminara redundando en una aceleracin de la inflacin. La tentacin es grande, dado que los costos se pagan a futuro (ya sea con menos crecimiento y ms desempleo, o cuando la presin poltica obliga a introducir programas de ajuste para reducir la inflacin). Para resolver esta tentacin real de aplicar polticas expansivas con beneficios de corto plazo y altos costos de mediano y largo plazo, se ha innovado creando bancos centrales autnomos con el mandato claro de lograr una inflacin baja y estable y con un consejo directivo independiente del gobierno. Este es el mandato que confiere la Ley Orgnica Constitucional al Banco Central de Chile. El Banco Central autnomo ha introducido con xito un esquema de poltica monetaria de metas de inflacin amparado en la calidad de su personal y en los avances a nivel internacional en la teora y la prctica de la poltica monetaria. Con esta institucionalidad el pas ha logrado por fin reducir la inflacin a niveles similares a la de los pases industriales, sin grandes costos en trminos de actividad y empleo, disminuyendo tambin en el proceso la volatilidad tanto de la inflacin como del producto. Hoy, el Banco Central de Chile es un gran activo de todos los chilenos. Este, a travs del cabal cumplimiento de su mandato de alcanzar y mantener la estabilidad de precios y del sistema de pagos, contribuye de manera fundamental a la estabilidad macroeconmica del pas, que es una condicin necesaria para alcanzar tasas de crecimiento altas y sostenidas que permitan, a su vez, mejorar los estndares de vida de la poblacin, especialmente de los ms necesitados. Muchas de las personas que nos acompaan esta tarde han sido protagonistas de esta exitosa tarea, y esta es una oportunidad apropiada para agradecerles pblicamente por su valioso aporte a la construccin de una institucionalidad que hoy es motivo de legtimo orgullo para el pas. Pero esta tarea no se ha agotado, y las nuevas generaciones debern seguir trabajando para que esta institucionalidad siga entregando los frutos de la estabilidad monetaria y financiera que fuera tan esquiva a lo largo de nuestra vida independiente. Esta es la mejor forma en que el Banco Central de Chile puede contribuir al desarrollo econmico de nuestro pas. Muchas gracias.

Title: The Central Bank and Monetary Policy in Chile: A Synthesis of Eighty Years of Existence
text: The Central Bank and Monetary Policy in Chile: A Synthesis of Eighty Years of Existence Speech made by Mr. Vittorio Corbo, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Gala Dinner offered on the occasion of the Eightieth Anniversary of the Central Bank of Chile 18 August 2005 On this occasion, in which we celebrate eighty years of life of the Central Bank of Chile, I would like to briefly recount what were its origins and what have been the achievements made during the past eight decades. If we go back to the dawn of the Republic, or even earlier, we find documentation showing that the shortage of working capital was already a constant concern. This meant that from very early on there was an evident need to produce money in Chile, which was initially resolved through an authorization from the Crown to install a mint in the country and, later, Chile being an independent Republic, through the issuance of banknotes by commercial banks since the 1850s. But it was in 1860, with the first Banking Law, when private banks began to proliferate, which were authorized to issue notes convertible into gold. Also from that decade the concern about the shortage of working capital was replaced by a concern for the control of the issuance of means of payment, in order to avoid the harmful effects of inflation and the breakdown of the bimetallic system. And there was always the doubt of whether or not the issuance should be centralized and delivered exclusively to a single entity, whether private, public or mixed. This discussion intensifies between 1921 and 1925, and culminates in a political agreement to create a central bank based on the proposal of the commission headed by Princeton University professor Edwin Kemmerer. Thus, on August 22, 1925, the Central Bank of Chile was created, to "amply satisfy the need to provide the country with an institution that stabilizes the currency ..." At the time of the creation of the bank, two other related laws were also approved: the monetary law and the general banking law. The first established a gold standard regime; the second created a Superintendency of Banks that would supervise commercial banks. In order for the Central Bank to better fulfill its mission, it was conceived as an independent entity, with a board of directors where only three of its ten members were appointed by the President of the Republic. The rest were appointed by the other shareholders, trade union and trade union entities. At its foundation, the capital of the State in the Bank reached a little more than 20%. The purpose of this ownership and corporate governance structure was to prevent the Central Bank from being captured by the government or commercial banks. The institutionality established from these laws served as a framework for the economic evolution of the country in the following decades. In its first years of operation, under the gold standard monetary regime, inflation was reduced and loans to the public sector did not exceed the legal limit, which was set according to the State's participation in the Bank's capital. This was possible thanks to the fact that the strong expansion exhibited by public spending in the late twenties was mostly financed abroad. The export boom, expansionary fiscal policy and an expansionary monetary policy, in the form of successive reductions in the Central Bank's rediscount rate, led to strong economic growth in 1928 and 1929. But this changed abruptly with the onset of the Great Depression, which hit Chile with unprecedented intensity. The sharp fall in exportsd1both volume and pricesd1deteriorated the fiscal position, reduced growth, and accelerated the loss of reserves. At the same time, the collapse of external financing forced a sharp contraction of the current account deficit, which became very costly given the gold standard regime. It should not be surprising that in these circumstances a deflationary period began that ended, in July 1931, with the abandonment of the gold standard in the midst of a severe political and economic crisis that led, for the first time in our history, to the suspension of external debt service. The end of the link with gold in the midst of the Great Depression, in any case, was not a phenomenon typical of Chile, since it affected most countries in the world, including the United Kingdom (September 1931) and the United States (1933). After the Great Depression, between 1933 and 1938 there was a period of relative macroeconomic stability, supported by a marked improvement in the fiscal situation, an orderly monetary policy and the recovery of the world economy, with an average annual inflation of only 5.4%. But the Central Bank continued to grant credit to public institutions and the nitrate industry, beginning a period in which the development of Chile and the operation of the Central Bank were dominated by the fiscal situation. Thus, between 1938 and 1952 there was a strong expansion of credit associated with financing from both the public and private sectors. The corporate governance of the Central Bank, controlled by a majority of private sector representatives until 1947, facilitated this expansionary process of issuance. For most of this period, the Central Bank's rediscount rate remained at 4.5% per year, while average annual inflation reached 17%. Given the inability to control the growth of the issue, the main tools used to contain inflation were the fixing of prices of goods, multiple exchange rates, exchange controls and the policy of controlled readjustment of wages. Predictably, these measures were ineffective in controlling inflation, introducing distortions to relative prices, with significant efficiency costs.
