En la medida en que existan efectos de segunda ronda, tanto en la inflacin efectiva como en las expectativas de mediano plazo, que pongan en riesgo el logro de una inflacin de 3% entre 12 y 24 meses, el Banco Central tendr que actuar con ms energa para cumplir con su objetivo inflacionario. Si el alza de los combustibles sigue sin un traspaso notorio a inflacin subyacente, el efecto sobre la inflacin ser temporal. La inflacin esperada para el horizonte de 12 a 24 meses debera entonces volver naturalmente a la meta, sin requerir de acciones adicionales por parte de la autoridad monetaria, ms all de la normalizacin que responde a las condiciones cclicas, y que continuar a un ritmo que depender del comportamiento de la economa y hasta que se alcance un impulso monetario neutro.

Title: The Exchange Rate and Exchange Policy in Chile
text: The Exchange Rate and Exchange Policy in Chile Presentation by the President of the Central Bank of Chile, Mr. Vittorio Corbo, at the Special Session of the Senate of the Republic, January 3, 2006 Through you, Mr. President, I thank the Senate of the Republic for the opportunity to address the issue of the exchange rate and exchange rate policy in Chile. As a starting point, I would like to highlight three aspects. First, in the face of improvements in the terms of trade and in international financial conditions such as the one we have experienced in the last two years, it is normal and expected that there will be an appreciation of the real exchange rate, regardless of the exchange rate system. Second, the macroeconomic policy framework we have perfected in Chile over the past fifteen years, including the floating of the exchange rate, is the most appropriate for a small economy integrated into the rest of the world that is frequently subject to these changes in its external environment. Third, we know that even in a floating regime, occasionally, the exchange rate can depart from its fundamental values and that these deviations, when significant, can have negative consequences for the performance of the economy. For this reason, the Central Bank keeps open the possibility of intervening in the foreign exchange market. I. Measurement and evolution of the exchange rate and its fundamentals The effect of the recent appreciation of the peso on the competitiveness of tradable sectors has been on the front page of public discussion. Unfortunately, the discussion has emphasized the evolution of the nominal value of the peso-dollar parity, which, as I will argue, is not the correct variable to follow when measuring changes in external competitiveness (Figure 1: Nominal and Multilateral Exchange Rate). First, it is not correct to focus only on the bilateral peso dollar exchange rate since the United States represents less than 25% of our foreign trade (Figures 2 and 3: Trade Composition 2004 and U.S. Share of Chile's Trade). It is therefore crucial to look at how multilateral exchange rate measures evolve when assessing changes in competitiveness, that is, the exchange rate with respect to all our trading partners. Coinciding with the depreciation of the dollar in international markets, it is observed that the appreciation of the peso against the currencies of our main trading partners is significantly lower than the appreciation against the dollar (Figures 4 and 5: Nominal Exchange Rate Selected Economies). Second, when assessing changes in competitiveness, it is crucial to consider changes in Chile's relative costs vis-88-vis our trading partners. These are influenced by various factors, such as productivity, technology, cost of capital, etc. The multilateral real exchange rate (RTT)d1which shows how our trading partners' prices evolve relative to our domestic pricesd1provides an approximation of the behavior of these relative costs. This is relevant because external prices, although expressed in dollars, vary considerably (Figure 6: External Prices). To illustrate the importance of focusing on a multilateral and real measure of the exchange rate, one can compare the trajectories of the TCR and the TCN over the past twenty years. This shows that, from a longer-term perspective, a nominal depreciation is little informative about the evolution of the TCR. The same happens with calculations such as how many dollars a UF buys, which forget international inflation (Figure 7: Real and Nominal Exchange Rate) Even considering these measurement issues, the TCR is now approximately 8% below the average for the period 1990-2005, having gradually appreciated from the second quarter of 2003. This is clearly a matter of concern for some tradable sectors. However, the TCR is 14% above the low it reached in October 1997. (Figure 8: Real Exchange Rate) I want to emphasize, however, that although the real exchange rate is 8% more appreciated than the 1990-2005 average level, the fundamental variables that determine the TCR today are much more favorable than those observed, on average, over the last fifteen years. Thus, the fall in the real exchange rate in the last two years is mainly due to the favourable evolution of the terms of trade and international financial conditions. The terms of trade, heavily influenced by favourable copper and molybdenum prices, have risen by about 40 per cent from the 2002 average, while the spread on external bonds has fallen by more than half. (Figure 9: Terms of Trade and Spread) Our assessment is that, in the thick, the movements of the TCR have been the result of favorable changes in the external environment. There is no instability or contagion in international financial markets. Nor are imbalances observed in the rest of the economy, as evidenced by compliance with the fiscal rule and prudent levels of the current account assessed at long-term prices. So far we do not have sufficient background to conclude that the foreign exchange market is going through a situation that merits intervention. Interestingly, Chile's TCR appreciation is comparable to the appreciation of the Australian and New Zealand currencies among a group of commodity-exporting countries. (Figure 10: Real Exchange Rate in Commodity Exporting Countries) However, in recent weeks the TCR has approached levels that would only be consistent with the assumption that the current favorable external conditions will remain for a very long time. By the way, this is a possible, but unlikely scenario. Our assessment is that the favourable external situation is transitory and, therefore, that the real exchange rate should not remain at current levels for long. II. The macroeconomic policy regime The exchange rate policy of the Central Bank must be analyzed in the context of the macroeconomic and financial policy regime that is in force in our country. As is well known, the current policy regime has four key components: (i) A responsible fiscal policy that follows a structural surplus rule; (ii) An inflation-targeting monetary policy accompanied by a floating exchange rate policy, in which the Central Bank reserves the right to intervene in the market in exceptional situations; (iii) Financial integration with the rest of the world and (iv) Efficient regulation and supervision of the financial system. This regime of macroeconomic and financial policies is the result of the effort, experience and reflection of many people over many years. These policies have managed to provide the country with stability and growth, despite the volatility of the region and our terms of trade. These achievements are widely recognized internationally. I think it is important to clarify that monetary policy is not indifferent to the evolution of the exchange rate for two reasons. First, the evolution of the exchange rate is part of the analysis that feeds monetary policy decisions. The trajectory of the exchange rate can influence output and inflation projections, key variables in the conduct of monetary policy. In fact, the monetary policy decision of December 2005 took into account the nominal appreciation of the peso and its effects on the projected evolution of inflation, which led to a pause in the process of monetary policy normalization. There is, therefore, through the effects of the interest rate on the exchange rate, a degree of natural stabilization of the exchange rate in the monetary policy implemented by the Bank. The second reason why the exchange rate is important to the Central Bank is that in addition to the objective of price stability, it has the objective of ensuring financial stability. For this it is important to monitor the exchange rate and the potential risks that may introduce pronounced exchange rate variations, such as those that can be generated when there is a sharp correction of an exchange rate that has deviated from the value that can be explained by its fundamental determinants. In this context, the Bank maintains the option of intervening in the foreign exchange marketd1that is, changing its net foreign currency position by interacting with the private sectord1in exceptional situations. They are determined on a case-by-case basis, but they have in common the well-founded conclusion that there is an overreaction in market value that is considered harmful to the economy, coupled with the presumption that the action of intervening could have a stabilizing effect. Such an assessment would lead to such an assessment of changes in the real exchange rate that would be difficult to explain on the basis of present and expected changes in domestic and external conditions of productivity, terms of trade, external financing, and domestic demand. We recognize that markets don't always work well. However, any intervention risks eroding the credibility of the floating exchange rate regime, which implies sacrificing part of the benefits of this regime. Moreover, if the Central Bank misdiagnoses overreaction and tries to stop exchange rate movements that are justified by changes in fundamentals, then it also risks that the intervention will be ineffective and imply a high patrimonial cost for the Bank. This makes it necessary to be very careful when assessing the appropriateness and timeliness of exchange rate interventions. The benefits of flotation There are several reasons why Chile has ended up adopting a floating exchange rate regime. This point has been reached both by our experience with fixed and mixed exchange rate regimes (such as the exchange rate band) as well as by a better understanding of the phenomena involved. It can be said that in the seventies we learned about the importance of fiscal discipline; in the eighties on the importance of financial discipline; and in the nineties on exchange rate flexibility. First, floating exchange rates give the economy flexibility to deal with real external shocks, such as a change in the terms of trade, allowing for a faster response of relative prices and thus a much smaller impact on output and employment. In fact, the fall in output in the face of adverse terms-of-trade shocks is several times higher under fixed or mixed exchange rates than at low flexible exchange rates. The high fraction of basic products in our export basket, combined with price and wage rigidities, make the role of the exchange rate as an adjustment variable in the Chilean economy particularly important . In other words, if the Bank were to prioritize the objective of exchange rate stability, it could reduce the volatility of the currency, but it would accentuate fluctuations in interest rates, credit, output and employment. This volatility would hurt the vast majority of Chileans. Moreover, exchange rate stabilizations in semi-rigid regimes, such as exchange rate bands, are also not a lasting success. In these systems, exchange rate stability is only gained in the short run, until these regimes must be abandoned due to a balance of payments crisis, which often leads to a recession with great sacrifices of output and employment. Second, floating exchange rates facilitate adjustment to international financial shocks, or at least avoid aggravating the effects of such shocks. For example, attempts to temporarily sustain the exchange rate when its movement towards appreciation is due to a persistent reduction in the cost of external borrowing, generate expectations of appreciation, which in turn further reduce the cost of external credit and can lead to an expansionary bubble. Dynamics of this type seem to have been present in Chile between 1995 and 1998, the last years of the exchange rate band. Third, evidence suggests that intermediate exchange rate regimes (those halfway between fixed and floating regimes, such as exchange rate bands) are the most vulnerable to a balance of payments crisis, such as that described due to the increasing globalization of capital markets. Fourth, a flexible exchange rate allows for an autonomous monetary policy aimed at achieving an inflation target and stabilizing output around potential output. This is not possible under a fixed or prefixed exchange rate scheme, such as the scheme that the country had in the early eighties or the one that Argentina had in the nineties. It has been precisely the possibility of using a countercyclical policy together with confidence in its ability to maintain inflation around its target that has allowed the Central Bank to use a countercyclical monetary policy since 2001. Finally, a flexible exchange rate regime creates greater incentives for the private sector to increase its coverage against exchange rate risk, leading to lower levels of external indebtedness, lower dollarization of domestic liabilities and a more efficient allocation of exchange rate risk within the economy. This is clearly seen in the evolution of the exchange rate mismatch of Chilean firms before and after September 1999 (Figure 11: Exchange Mismatch of Chilean companies). The demand for exchange hedging generated by the float has been accompanied by a strong development of the foreign exchange derivatives market, allowing this to translate into a reduction in mismatches. This evolution is reflected in the rapid growth of the stock of foreign exchange derivatives in relation to foreign trade. (Figure 12: Foreign Exchange Derivatives Transactions). BIS data show that, within the set of emerging economies, Chile's derivatives market is one of the deepest, surpassing (as a fraction of GDP) the markets of Mexico and Brazil. (Figure 13: Other Derivatives Markets) Additional data from the BIS show that the term structure of these derivatives is similar to that observed in developed markets. It should also be noted that the costs of derivative contracts are no higher than those observed in other emerging economies. The recent modifications that allow the banking operations of foreign exchange options are an additional step in the deepening of the hedging market that facilitates access to these of companies that They face difficult access to the lines of credit required in forwards. Exchange rate floating is not a trouble-free schemed1short-term volatility may in some cases be one of them (Figure 14: Exchange Rate Volatility). However, we are convinced that for the Chilean economy these costs are lower than those of trying to manage the exchange rate systematically, which causes much more pronounced cycles and is the germ of financial instability. Questions to the exchange rate float: Myths or Realities? It has been argued that the costs to the Chilean economy of the Asian crisis are evidence of the risks of excessive confidence in a floating exchange rate and that we would be on the verge of a dynamic similar to that of 1995-1998. I want to rebut this presumption. First, lack of exchange rate flexibility was one of the factors contributing to the 1999 recession. Second, it was precisely the events of 1995-98 that led to the transition to a flexible exchange rate regime in 1999. Third, the current policy framework, which reflects what we and many other countries have learned over the past twenty years, is a very different framework than the one that prevailed at that time. Beyond the fact that macroeconomic conditions are very different, our current policy framework puts us in a better position today to face external shocks than we were in 1997-98. One of the lessons we have learned over the past 20 years is that in an economy integrated into international capital markets, the exchange rate regime (whatever it may be) must be credible. Otherwise, speculation against the exchange rate is impossible to counteract in a prolonged way, ending in a currency crisis and even in banking crises with high economic and social costs. This explains why the increasing financial openness of the nineties generated an international trend towards moving away from intermediate exchange rate regimes, with a massive shift on a global scale in particular towards floating regimes. In 2004, 46 per cent of countries operated with floating exchange rate regimes and each year this fraction It keeps increasing. In commodity exporting countries this figure rises to 100% of countries! Therefore, we can conclude that floating regimes are not an isolated fad, but reflect the culmination of a hard and long learning process made in the light of failed exchange rate experiences that often ended in costly banking and balance of payments crises. (Figure 15: Exchange rate regimes). It has also been argued that Central Bank policy would need to attempt to sustain a high real exchange rate (RMR) in order to promote exports. This idea assigns a target to monetary and exchange rate policy that it is not able to achieve. It is true that monetary and exchange rate policies can influence the short-term trajectory of the TCR and other real variables such as output and employment. However, both policies are not able to persistently influence these variables. In addition, orienting monetary and exchange instruments towards a TCR target would risk the Central Bank's (already negative) capital. Moreover, there is a risk of neglecting the fundamental objectives of controlling inflation, ensuring financial stability, and avoiding systemic crises. With the achievement of these objectives, the policies of the Central Bank ensure the main contribution to the sustained development of the Chilean economy. Finally, it has been argued that most countries that claim to have a flexible exchange rate effectively intervene regularly in the foreign exchange market, and that therefore the Central Bank of Chile's commitment to floating is extreme and exceptionald1of an orthodoxy not seen, according to some. This is not correct. Within a sample of small and open countries (with policy frameworks similar to ours), monetary authorities intervene very sporadically, as Chile has done in the recent past. On the other hand, in economies with greater financial and/or macroeconomic vulnerability, the authorities tend to intervene more in the foreign exchange market for fear that exchange rate fluctuations could generate significant financial risks or unanchor inflationary expectations. Many times this type of Interventions initiate the processes of misalignment. (Figure 16: Date of Last Foreign Exchange Intervention). III. Conclusion The real appreciation of the last two years is basically associated with a very favourable external situation. The terms of trade are considerably above their historical average. The cost of external financing is at historically low levels. This type of economic environment generates an exchange rate appreciation independent of the exchange rate regime. In our case, the TCN does much of the adjustment work. If we had a fixed exchange rate, the adjustment would be the same, but through higher inflation. The floating exchange rate regime is part of a macroeconomic and financial policy framework that is the result of the effort, experience and reflection of many people over many years. These policies have managed to provide the country with stability and growth, despite the volatility of the region and our terms of trade. This is how we have just closed a tremendously successful year in macroeconomic terms, with moderate inflation rates, reduced unemployment and growth levels in line with the long-term potential of the economy. These achievements are widely recognized internationally. In the current policy framework, given the normalization of the external environment, the real exchange rate is likely to depreciate, returning to its historical averages. However, if the exchange rate evolves towards securities that, in the evaluation of the Central Bank Council, are significantly removed from their fundamental determinants, rest assured that we would use the tools at our disposal, particularly interventions in the foreign exchange market.
text_original: El Tipo de Cambio y la Poltica Cambiaria en Chile Presentacin del Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, Sr. Vittorio Corbo, en la Sesin Especial del Senado de la Repblica, 3 de enero de 2006 Por su intermedio, Sr. Presidente, agradezco al Senado de la Repblica la oportunidad para poder referirme al tema del tipo de cambio y la poltica cambiaria en Chile. Como punto de partida quiero destacar tres aspectos. Primero, que frente a mejoras en los trminos de intercambio y en las condiciones financieras internacionales como la que hemos experimentado en los ltimos dos aos, es normal y esperable que se produzca una apreciacin del tipo de cambio real, sin importar cul es el sistema cambiario. Segundo, el marco de polticas macroeconmicas que hemos perfeccionado en Chile en los ltimos quince aos, incluyendo la flotacin del tipo de cambio, es el ms apropiado para una economa pequea e integrada al resto del mundo que est frecuentemente sujeta a estos cambios en su entorno externo. Tercero, sabemos que an en un rgimen de flotacin, ocasionalmente, el tipo de cambio puede alejarse de sus valores fundamentales y que estas desviaciones, cuando son significativas, pueden tener consecuencias negativas para el desempeo de la economa. Por esta razn, el Banco Central mantiene abierta la posibilidad de intervenir en el mercado cambiario.  Medicin y evolucin del tipo de cambio y de sus fundamentos El efecto de la reciente apreciacin del peso sobre la competitividad de los sectores transables ha estado en la primera plana de la discusin pblica. Desafortunadamente la discusin ha enfatizado la evolucin del valor nominal de la paridad peso-dlar, que, como argumentar, no es la variable correcta a seguir a la hora de medir cambios en la competitividad externa (Figura 1: Tipo de Cambio Nominal y Multilateral). En primer lugar, no es correcto concentrarse solo en el tipo de cambio bilateral peso dlar ya que Estados Unidos representa menos de 25% de nuestro comercio exterior (Figuras 2 y 3: Composicin Comercio 2004 y Participacin de EE.UU. en el comercio de Chile). Por ello es crucial mirar cmo evolucionan medidas de tipo de cambio multilateral a la hora de evaluar cambios en la competitividad, esto es el tipo de cambio respecto del conjunto de nuestros socios comerciales. Coincidiendo con la depreciacin del dlar en los mercados internacionales, se observa que la apreciacin del peso con respecto a las monedas de nuestros principales socios comerciales es significativamente menor que la apreciacin respecto del dlar (Figuras 4 y 5: Tipo de Cambio Nominal Economas Seleccionadas). En segundo lugar, a la hora de evaluar cambios en competitividad, es crucial considerar cambios en los costos relativos de Chile respecto de nuestros socios comerciales. En estos influyen diversos factores, como la productividad, la tecnologa, el costo de capital etc. El tipo de cambio real multilateral (TCR) que muestra cmo evolucionan los precios de nuestros socios comerciales en relacin con nuestros precios internosprovee una aproximacin al comportamiento de estos costos relativos. Esto es relevante porque los precios externos, aunque estn expresados en dlares, varan considerablemente (Figura 6: Precios Externos) Para ilustrar la importancia de concentrarse en una medicin multilateral y real del tipo de cambio se puede comparar las trayectorias del TCR y el TCN durante los ltimos veinte aos. Ello demuestra que, desde una perspectiva de mayor plazo, una depreciacin nominal es poco informativa sobre la evolucin del TCR. Lo mismo sucede con clculos como cuntos dlares compra una UF, que olvidan la inflacin internacional (Figura 7: Tipo de Cambio Real y Nominal) An considerando estos temas de medicin, el TCR se ubica hoy aproximadamente 8% bajo el promedio del periodo 1990-2005, habindose apreciado en forma gradual a partir del segundo trimestre del 2003. Ello evidentemente es un tema de preocupacin para algunos sectores transables. Sin embargo, el TCR se ubica 14% sobre el mnimo que alcanz en octubre de 1997. (Figura 8: Tipo de Cambio Real) Quiero enfatizar, sin embargo, que aunque el tipo de cambio real est 8% ms apreciado que el nivel promedio 1990-2005, las variables fundamentales que determinan el TCR hoy son mucho ms favorables que las observadas, en promedio, durante los ltimos quince aos. Es as como la cada del tipo de cambio real en los ltimos dos aos obedece mayoritariamente a la favorable evolucin de los trminos de intercambio y de las condiciones financieras internacionales. Los trminos de intercambio, muy influidos por los favorables precios del cobre y el molibdeno, han aumentado en cerca de un 40% en relacin al promedio 2002, mientras que el spread de los bonos externos ha cado a menos de la mitad. (Figura 9: Trminos de Intercambio y Spread) Nuestra evaluacin es que, en lo grueso, los movimientos del TCR han sido el resultado de cambios favorables en el entorno externo. No se observa inestabilidad ni contagio en los mercados financieros internacionales. Tampoco se observan desequilibrios en el resto de la economa, como lo demuestran el cumplimiento de la regla fiscal y los niveles prudentes de la cuenta corriente evaluada a precios de largo plazo. Hasta ahora no tenemos antecedentes suficientes para concluir que el mercado cambiario pasa por una situacin que amerite una intervencin. Un hecho destacable, adems, es que la apreciacin del TCR de Chile es comparable a la apreciacin que han experimentado las monedas de Australia y Nueva Zelanda entre un conjunto de pases exportadores de productos bsicos. (Figura 10: Tipo de Cambio Real en Pases Exportadores de Productos Bsicos) Sin embargo, en las ltimas semanas el TCR se ha acercado a niveles que solo seran coherentes con la presuncin que las actuales condiciones externas favorables se mantendrn por un tiempo muy prolongado. Por cierto, este es un escenario posible, pero improbable. Nuestra evaluacin es que la favorable coyuntura externa es transitoria y, por ende, que el tipo de cambio real no debiera permanecer por mucho tiempo en los actuales niveles.  El rgimen de polticas macroeconmicas La poltica cambiaria del Banco Central debe analizarse en el contexto del rgimen de polticas macroeconmicas y financieras que estn vigentes en nuestro pas. Como es sabido, el actual rgimen de polticas tiene cuatro componentes fundamentales: (i) Una poltica fiscal responsable que sigue una regla de supervit estructural; (ii) Una poltica monetaria de metas de inflacin acompaada de una poltica de flotacin cambiaria, en la que el Banco Central se reserva el derecho a intervenir en el mercado ante situaciones excepcionales; (iii) La integracin financiera con el resto del mundo y (iv) Una eficiente regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero. Este rgimen de polticas macroeconmicas y financieras es el resultado del esfuerzo, la experiencia y reflexin de muchas personas durante muchos aos. Estas polticas han logrado proveer al pas de estabilidad y crecimiento, pese a la volatilidad propia de la regin y de nuestros trminos de intercambio. Estos logros son ampliamente reconocidos internacionalmente. Creo importante aclarar que la poltica monetaria no es indiferente respecto de la evolucin del tipo de cambio por dos razones. Primero, la evolucin del tipo de cambio es parte del anlisis que alimenta las decisiones de poltica monetaria. La trayectoria del tipo de cambio puede influir sobre las proyecciones de producto y de inflacin, variables claves en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. De hecho, la decisin de poltica monetaria del pasado mes de diciembre del 2005 tom en cuenta la apreciacin nominal del peso y sus efectos sobre la evolucin proyectada de la inflacin lo que llev a decidir una pausa en el proceso de normalizacin de la poltica monetaria. Existe, por lo tanto, a travs de los efectos de la tasa de inters en el tipo de cambio, un grado de estabilizacin natural del tipo de cambio en la poltica monetaria que implementa el Banco. La segunda razn por la cual el tipo de cambio es importante para el Banco Central es que adems del objetivo de la estabilidad de precios, tiene el objetivo de velar por la estabilidad financiera. Para ello es importante hacer un seguimiento del tipo de cambio y los potenciales riesgos que puedan introducir variaciones cambiarias pronunciadas, tales como las que se pueden generar cuando se produce la correccin brusca de un tipo de cambio que se ha desviado del valor que puede ser explicado por sus determinantes fundamentales. En este contexto el Banco mantiene la opcin de intervenir en el mercado cambiario esto es, cambiar su posicin neta de moneda extranjera interactuando con el sector privado en situaciones excepcionales. Ellas se determinan caso a caso, pero tienen en comn la conclusin fundada de que existe una sobrerreaccin en el valor de mercado que se considera daina para la economa, unida a la presuncin de que la accin de intervenir podra tener un efecto estabilizador. Daran pie, a una evaluacin como sta, los casos en que se observaran variaciones del tipo de cambio real que seran difciles de explicar sobre la base de cambios presentes y esperadas en las condiciones internas y externas de productividad, de los trminos de intercambio, del financiamiento externo y de la demanda interna. Reconocemos que los mercados no siempre funcionan bien. Sin embargo, toda intervencin arriesga erosionar la credibilidad del rgimen de flotacin cambiaria, lo que implica sacrificar parte de los beneficios de este rgimen. Ms an, si el Banco Central equivoca el diagnstico de sobrerreaccin e intenta detener movimientos del tipo cambio que s se justifican por cambios en los fundamentales, entonces se arriesga adems, a que la intervencin sea inefectiva e implique un alto costo patrimonial para el Banco. Esto hace necesario ser muy cuidadoso al momento de evaluar la conveniencia y la oportunidad de las intervenciones cambiarias. Los beneficios de la flotacin Existen varias razones por las cuales Chile ha terminado adoptado un rgimen de flotacin cambiaria. Se ha llegado a este punto tanto por nuestra experiencia con regmenes cambiarios fijos y mixtos (como la banda cambiaria) as como, por una mejor comprensin de los fenmenos involucrados. Se puede decir que en los aos setenta aprendimos sobre la importancia de la disciplina fiscal; en los aos ochenta sobre la importancia de la disciplina financiera; y en los aos noventa sobre la flexibilidad cambiaria. En primer lugar, la flotacin cambiaria confiere a la economa flexibilidad para enfrentar choques externos reales, tales como un cambio de los trminos de intercambio, permitiendo una respuesta ms rpida de los precios relativos y por ende un impacto mucho menor en el producto y el empleo. De hecho, la cada del producto ante choques adversos en los trminos de intercambio es varias veces mayor bajo tipo de cambio fijo o mixto que bajo tipo de cambio flexible. La elevada fraccin de productos bsicos en nuestra canasta exportadora, combinada con rigideces de precios y salarios, hacen particularmente importante el rol del tipo de cambio como variable de ajuste en la economa chilena. Dicho de otra manera: si el Banco privilegiara el objetivo de estabilidad cambiaria podra reducir la volatilidad de la divisa, pero acentuara las fluctuaciones de las tasas de inters, del crdito, del producto y el empleo. Esta volatilidad perjudicara a la gran mayora de los chilenos. Ms an, tampoco tienen xito perdurable las estabilizaciones cambiarias en regmenes semi-rgidos, como las bandas cambiarias. En estos sistemas, solo se gana estabilidad cambiaria en el corto plazo, hasta que estos regmenes se deben abandonar por una crisis de balanza de pagos, que frecuentemente lleva a una recesin con grandes sacrificios de producto y empleo. En segundo lugar, la flotacin cambiaria facilita el ajuste a choques financieros internacionales, o al menos evita agravar los efectos de tales choques. Por ejemplo, los intentos de sostener temporalmente el tipo de cambio cuando su movimiento hacia la apreciacin obedece a una reduccin persistente en el costo del endeudamiento externo, generan expectativas de apreciacin, que a su vez reducen an ms el costo del crdito externo y pueden llevar a una burbuja expansiva. Dinmicas de este tipo parecen haber estado presentes en Chile entre 1995 y 1998, los ltimos aos de vigencia de la banda cambiaria. Tercero, la evidencia apunta a que los regmenes cambiarios intermedios (aquellos que se encuentran a medio camino entre los regmenes fijos y flotantes, como las bandas cambiarias) son los ms vulnerables a una crisis de balanza de pagos, como la descrita debido a la creciente globalizacin de los mercados de capitales. Cuarto, un tipo de cambio flexible permite implementar una poltica monetaria autnoma encaminada hacia el logro de una meta de inflacin y a estabilizar el producto en torno al producto potencial. Ello no es posible bajo un esquema de tipo de cambio fijo o prefijado, como el esquema que tena el pas a comienzos de los ochenta o el que tuvo Argentina en la dcada de los noventa. Ha sido justamente la posibilidad de utilizar una poltica anticclica junto a la confianza en su capacidad de mantener la inflacin en torno a su meta lo que le ha permitido al Banco Central utilizar una poltica monetaria anticclica desde el ao 2001. Por ltimo, un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible genera mayores incentivos al sector privado a incrementar su cobertura frente al riesgo cambiario, llevando a menores niveles de endeudamiento externo, una menor dolarizacin de los pasivos domsticos y una asignacin ms eficiente del riesgo cambiario al interior de la economa. Esto se ve claramente en la evolucin del descalce cambiario de firmas chilenas antes y despus de septiembre de 1999 (Figura 11: Descalce Cambiario empresas chilenas). La demanda por cobertura cambiaria que genera la flotacin ha venido acompaada de un fuerte desarrollo del mercado de derivados cambiarios, permitiendo que ello se traduzca en una reduccin de los descalces. Esta evolucin se refleja en el rpido crecimiento del stock de derivados cambiarios en relacin con el comercio exterior. (Figura 12: Transacciones de Derivados Cambiarios). Datos del BIS muestran que, dentro del conjunto de economas emergentes, el mercado de derivados de Chile es uno de los ms profundos, superando (como fraccin del PIB) a los mercados de Mxico y Brasil. (Figura 13: Otros Mercados de Derivados) Datos adicionales del BIS muestran que la estructura de plazos de estos derivados es similar a la observada en los mercados desarrollados. Tambin cabe notar que los costos de los contratos de derivados no son mayores que los observados en otras economas emergentes. Las recientes modificaciones que permiten las operaciones bancarias de opciones cambiarias son un paso adicional en la profundizacin del mercado de cobertura que facilita el acceso a stas de empresas que enfrentan un difcil acceso a las lneas de crdito que se requieren en las operaciones de forwards. La flotacin cambiaria no es un esquema que est exento de problemas la volatilidad de corto plazo puede en algunos casos ser uno de ellos (Figura 14: Volatilidad Cambiaria). Sin embargo, estamos convencidos de que para la economa chilena estos costos son menores que los de tratar de manejar el tipo de cambio de manera sistemtica, lo que causa ciclos mucho ms pronunciados y es germen de inestabilidad financiera. Cuestionamientos a la flotacin cambiaria: Mitos o Realidades? Se ha argumentado que los costos para la economa chilena de la crisis asitica son evidencia de los riesgos de una excesiva confianza en un tipo de cambio flotante y de que estaramos ad portas de una dinmica similar a la de 1995-1998. Quiero refutar esta presuncin. En primer lugar, la falta de flexibilidad cambiaria fue uno de los elementos que contribuyeron a la recesin de 1999. Segundo, fueron precisamente los eventos del periodo 1995-98 los que motivaron la transicin a un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible en 1999. Tercero, el marco actual de poltica, que refleja lo aprendido por nosotros y muchos otros pases en los ltimos veinte aos, es un marco muy diferente al que prevaleca en esa poca. Ms all de que las condiciones macroeconmicas son muy distintas, nuestro marco de poltica actual nos coloca hoy en mejor pie para enfrentar choques externos que lo que estuvimos en 1997-98. Una de las lecciones que hemos aprendido en los ltimos 20 aos es que en una economa integrada a los mercados de capitales internacionales el rgimen cambiario (cualquiera que este sea) debe ser creble. De otra manera, la especulacin contra el tipo de cambio resulta imposible de contrarrestar en forma prolongada, terminando en una crisis cambiaria e incluso en crisis bancarias con altos costos econmicos y sociales. Esto explica por qu la creciente apertura financiera de los aos noventa gener una tendencia internacional hacia el alejamiento de regmenes cambiarios intermedios, con un cambio masivo a escala mundial en particular hacia regimenes de flotacin. En el ao 2004, un 46% de los pases operaba con regmenes cambiarios flotantes y cada ao dicha fraccin sigue aumentando. En los pases exportadores de bienes bsicos esta cifra sube al 100% de los pases! Por lo tanto, podemos concluir que los regmenes de flotacin no constituyen una moda aislada, sino que reflejan la culminacin de un duro y largo proceso de aprendizaje hecho a la luz de las experiencias cambiarias fallidas que muchas veces terminaron en costosas crisis bancarias y de balanza de pagos. (Figura 15: Regmenes Cambiarios). Tambin se ha argumentado que sera necesario que la poltica del Banco Central intente sostener un tipo de cambio real (TCR) elevado de manera de promover las exportaciones. Esta idea le asigna un objetivo a la poltica monetaria y cambiaria que no es capaz de alcanzar. Es cierto que las polticas monetaria y cambiaria pueden influir en la trayectoria de corto plazo del TCR y de otras variables reales como el producto y el empleo. Sin embargo, ambas polticas no son capaces de influir de manera persistente en estas variables. Adems, orientar el instrumental monetario y cambiario hacia un objetivo de TCR arriesgara el capital (ya negativo) del Banco Central. Ms an, se corre el riesgo de descuidar los objetivos fundamentales de controlar la inflacin, asegurar la estabilidad financiera y evitar crisis sistmicas. Con el alcance de estos objetivos, las polticas del Banco Central aseguran la principal contribucin al desarrollo sostenido de la economa chilena. Por ltimo, se ha argumentado que la mayora de los pases que dicen tener un tipo de cambio flexible en la prctica intervienen en forma regular en el mercado cambiario, y que por lo tanto el compromiso con la flotacin del Banco Central de Chile es extremo y excepcional de una ortodoxia no vista, segn algunos. Esto no es correcto. Dentro de una muestra de pases pequeos y abiertos (con marcos de polticas similares al nuestro) las autoridades monetarias intervienen en forma muy espordica, tal como lo ha hecho Chile en el pasado reciente. Por otra parte, en economas con mayor vulnerabilidad financiera y/o macroeconmica, las autoridades tienden a intervenir ms en el mercado cambiario por temor a que las fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio puedan generar riesgos financieros significativos o desanclen las expectativas inflacionarias. Muchas veces este tipo de intervenciones dan inicio a los procesos de desalineamiento. (Figura 16: Fecha de ltima Intervencin Cambiaria).  Conclusin La apreciacin real de los ltimos dos aos est asociada, en lo fundamental, a una situacin externa muy favorable. Los trminos de intercambio estn considerablemente por encima de su promedio histrico. El costo del financiamiento externo se ubica en niveles histricamente bajos. Este tipo de entorno econmico genera una apreciacin cambiaria independiente del rgimen cambiario. En nuestro caso el TCN hace buena parte del trabajo de ajuste. Si tuvisemos un tipo de cambio fijo, el ajuste se dara igual, pero a travs de una mayor inflacin. El rgimen cambiario de flotacin es parte de un marco de polticas macroeconmicas y financieras que es el resultado del esfuerzo, la experiencia y la reflexin de muchas personas durante muchos aos. Estas polticas han logrado proveer al pas de estabilidad y crecimiento, pese a la volatilidad propia de la regin y de nuestros trminos de intercambio. Es as como acabamos de cerrar un ao tremendamente exitoso en trminos macroeconmicos, con tasas de inflacin moderadas, reduccin del desempleo y niveles de crecimiento en lnea con el potencial de largo plazo de la economa. Estos logros son ampliamente reconocidos internacionalmente. En el actual marco de polticas, ante la normalizacin del entorno externo lo ms probable es que el tipo de cambio real se deprecie, retornando a sus promedios histricos. Sin embargo, de evolucionar el tipo de cambio hacia valores que, en evaluacin del Consejo del Banco Central, se alejaran significativamente de sus determinantes fundamentales, tengan la tranquilidad de que utilizaramos las herramientas que estn a nuestra disposicin, particularmente las intervenciones en el mercado cambiario.

Title: Monetary Policy Report
text: MONETARY POLICY REPORT May 2006 Summary of the presentation made by Vittorio Corbo L, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Finance Commission of the Honorable Senate of the Republic, in Valpara92so, on May 17, 2006. The Chilean economy continues in an expansionary and relatively orderly cycle, with extraordinary external conditions, in particular very high terms of trade thanks to record copper prices. Growth in domestic activity and demand is gradually moving towards trend values, while capacity slack is gradually filling. Despite the sharp increase in international oil prices, the current expansionary cycle has not compromised price stability, although it does involve a slight temporary increase in CPI inflation. In recent months, annual CPI inflation fluctuated around 4% and core CPIX1 inflation approached 3%, both in line with previous projections. Inflation expectations remain well anchored at 3%. This scenario has allowed the normalisation of monetary policy to continue at a leisurely pace, currently maintaining an expansionary bias that, in the most likely scenario, is expected to continue reducing to ensure the convergence of inflation to 3% within the usual projection horizon. The timing of these adjustments will depend on the implications of news on activity, exchange rates, wages and prices on the projected path of inflation. The external outlook is exceptionally favorable for the Chilean economy. Global growth remains buoyant, with a better balance between the different economic zones. Chile's terms of trade are improving thanks to commodity prices which, contrary to projections, have continued to rise. The price of copper is close to US 4 a pound, after substantial increases in recent weeks, whose magnitude and speed are not easy to reconcile with recent and expected changes in demand and supply fundamentals. The price of oil has also continued to rise, both due to the strength of global demand and supply problems and the higher risk premium in the face of possible geopolitical problems. Financial conditions for emerging economies remain favorable, despite significant increases in long-term interest rates in developed economies. At the same time, while the US appears to be close to completing its monetary policy normalisation cycle, market expectations are rising for short-term interest rate hikes in the Eurozone and Japan, reflecting higher growth in these regions and their eventual impact on inflation. Internally, the Board of the Central Bank has continued with the process of gradual reduction of monetary stimulus initiated in the second part of 2004, with increases in the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) on two occasions since the last IPoM, which stands at 5%. In any case, it is estimated that the MPR is still below its neutral level. The cost of financing to households and companies gradually reflects the adjustment of the TPM, with market interest rates in the order of 100 basis points above the average of the previous year. Credit growth remains strong, although there is no further acceleration. Monetary aggregates stabilize their annual rate of increase at relatively high levels, following the increase at the end of 2005. Taking as a reference the average of the two weeks prior to the statistical close of this IPoM, it is estimated that the peso would today be at levels marginally below several estimates for the real exchange rate consistent with its long-term fundamental determinants, in particular the terms of trade. As a methodological assumption for the projections of this IPoM, a moderate depreciation of the peso in real terms is considered over the projection horizon, in line with the baseline scenario of gradual normalization of external conditions. In the first quarter of the year, domestic demand was framed in a scenario of slowdown, consistent with what was expected in January. On the consumption side, the durable component continues to grow at high rates and is favoured by good household financing conditions and dynamic employment, despite higher fuel prices. Regular consumption maintains moderate growth. Annual growth in gross fixed capital formation slowed in the first quarter, in line with projections, and in line with the evolution of the cycle. The projections of this MPI assume that fiscal policy remains framed by the structural surplus rule, with an increase in copper price reference values for 2007 in line with the assessment that current high prices would not be durable. The expansionary nature of fiscal policy will depend, among other factors, on the reference price that is finally determined. The scenarios for inflation that are delivered through the fan charts include, among other elements, several alternatives for this reference price, which are key to projecting the different macroeconomic variables. It also emerges as relevant, given the amounts involved, the effect that higher revenues from copper sales may have on the valuation of the peso in the short term. The way they are managed, both with respect to their destination and their name, can have effects on the local economy. The policy announced by the fiscal authority regarding the management of these surpluses helps to reduce these effects. In any case, it should be noted that with a less austere fiscal policy, the appreciation of the peso would be greater and the interest rate higher. In addition, the volume of mining shipments reversed the annual declines of much of 2005. As for industrial shipments, their volume remained dynamic, while that of agricultural shipments reflected the damage caused by climatic phenomena in 2005 to fruit production. Imports are at similar levels to those at the end of last year. The current account closed 2005 with a surplus of over half a percentage point of GDP. A surplus of more than 1.5 per cent of GDP is projected for 2006. GDP grew 6.3% in 2005, similar to what was estimated in January. In the first quarter of 2006 it increased at a lower rate, around 5%, affected by specific events in specific sectors. Agricultural activity fell in annual terms both due to climatic factors and elements linked to the transition that seems to be occurring in certain traditional crops. Thus, measured by its instantaneous expansion speed, activity suffered a slowdown in the first quarter of the year, which would be reversed in the current quarter. For 2006 as a whole, an expansion somewhat above trend is still expected, reaching a growth of between 5 and 6%. This means that growth in the second half of the year is considerably higher than in the first half and that the slowdown in the first quarter was punctual. By 2007 it is estimated that GDP would once again grow above its trend. The few capacity gaps that are still estimated to remain would be closed during 2006, with small but positive gaps in the rest of the projection horizon. The global outlook for the labour market shows some changes compared to the beginning of the year, highlighting the sustained increase in salaried employment and the upswing in labour participation. In this context, the available measure of labour productivity registered a significant slowdown in the first months of the year, although it is not evident that it is a trend phenomenon. Nominal hourly wages have slowed their annual growth rate, as expected once the impact of the reduction in working hours in early 2005 was removed from the comparison base. Unit labor costs are growing at higher annual rates than at the end of 2005, although with expected rates of expansion. How much of the greater annual variation in labour costs responds to genuine cost pressures is not easy to determine, due to a number of factors that are difficult to isolate; Among them, the volatility inherent in productivity measures and changes in the measurement of wage and employment surveys. In any case, with a tightening labour market, it is particularly important to monitor developments in wage pressures that may threaten future inflation developments. The different measures of inflation expectations remain well anchored at around 3%. Two-, five- and ten-year inflationary compensation averages 3%, as do inflation expectations reported in the survey of one- and two-year economic expectations. This differs from previous episodes of rising oil prices in pesos, in which inflation expectations tended to increase, at least temporarily. In the short term, core inflation in the CPIX1, although fluctuating, is projected at levels similar to the current ones. During 2007 and early 2008, it would be marginally above 3%, given a brief growth higher than the trend in 2007 and the effect of the slight increase in the real exchange rate assumed by the baseline scenario. For CPI inflation, meanwhile, a gradual reduction towards values even below 3% is projected at the end of the third and beginning of the fourth quarter of 2006, in important part due to the high comparison base of the same period of 2005. In the last months of the year it would increase again temporarily to figures above 3% per year, and then remain around the center of the target range until the end of the projection horizon. The higher expected price for oil in the baseline scenario has its main impact on inflation in 2006. Although more slowly than in previous IPoM, a convergence to its price considered long-term is expected, leading to a projected CPI inflation lower than that of the CPI and IPCX1 in 2007 and early 2008. This scenario is consistent with the methodological assumption of a gradual reduction in monetary impulse in the coming quarters with a trajectory comparable to that implied in the interest rate structure of the last two weeks. IPoM projections are constructed from the events that are considered most likely and that configure the base scenario. As usual, there are various sources of uncertainty that could lead to different results from the assumptions. Externally, the risk that the price of copper will be different from the projected one stands out. It could be lower, considering that recent increases have occurred without significant additional changes in their fundamentals. But it is also possible that higher prices will occur, given a scenario of greater demand, especially from China and India, and unforeseen problems in supply. The risk of the price of oil remaining at current levels or even rising stands out. This risk has increased and could have negative effects on global growth, as well as greater inflationary pressures, which has recently been warned by the IMF. While it is estimated that the world is today less sensitive to oil price increases, the high levels of recent weeks, and the fact that the price is now also affected by supply factors, could have more significant effects than those seen so far. The risk of a deterioration in international financial conditions remains present and is perceived somewhat higher. This is due to the increase in inflation in developed economies, the greater dynamism of domestic demand and the increase in fuel prices, in a context in which capacity slack has been taking over faster than anticipated, especially in the US. On the other hand, EM sovereign bonds have remained at unusually low levels, which maintains the risk of significant increases in the face of a possible reassessment of investors' risk appetite. This, for example, in the face of an abrupt deterioration in international liquidity conditions or a lower willingness of investors to take positions in instruments from emerging economies, particularly Latin America. They also highlight the signs of concern that the market has given for the performance of some specific economies in the region. The risk of a further decline in real estate asset prices remains prevalent in developed countries, where they have reached particularly high levels. The resulting deterioration in household wealth could lead to a larger-than-expected slowdown in private spending in these economies, construction activity and, ultimately, the pace of expansion of global activity. At the global level, there are several risks that are less likely in the short term, but if they occur they would have a noticeable impact. The possibility of disorderly adjustment of global savings-investment imbalances continues, leading to a deterioration in international financial conditions and a decline in global activity. In addition, the imbalances themselves could accentuate global trade disputes, leading to greater global protectionism, with consequent damage to trade and economic growth. While the extent of avian influenza is still unknown, it could have negative effects on global growth. Geopolitical risks and terrorist attacks also remain. Internally, there are risks associated with passing on recent copper price rises to the economy. This is related to expectations that high prices will continue, leading to higher than expected domestic demand, in a scenario of lower exchange rates and higher inflationary pressures. In this context, one would expect the consequent reaction of monetary policy, in order to maintain price stability and the sustainability of the expansionary cycle. It is even possible that expectations about this type of scenario will have effects that manifest themselves in the short term through movements in key financial prices, or if private agents advance their spending plans. It should be noted that the reference price of copper established for the purposes of calculating the structural revenues of the Treasury is a central element in the transmission of changes in the price of copper to the rest of the economy through public spending and, therefore, in the probability of materialization of this risk. Beyond the above, the slowdown already observed in annual domestic demand growth during the first quarter may not continue as projected. This, both due to the current favourable credit conditions and the robust growth of employment. Considering the high terms of trade facing the Chilean economy and the doubts of how this phenomenon will be absorbed, in addition to the exceptional international financial conditions, it is estimated that there is greater uncertainty regarding the path that domestic demand, activity and the exchange rate will follow in Chile. Finally, the effects of the oil price and its uncertain future evolution remain a major risk at the domestic level. Given that capacity gaps are already estimated to be scarce and would disappear in the coming quarters, it is possible that higher fuel prices, whether they have occurred or are about to occur, will have a more noticeable effect on core inflation than seen so far. The Board considers that, taken together, these different contingencies make the balance of risks to growth skewed upwards and balanced for inflation. The Council will be especially attentive to how the economy absorbs the unusual terms-of-trade scenario it faces, in a context of limited capacity gaps and an inflationary trend and inflation expectations aligned with the center of the target range. Of particular interest will be the behaviour of domestic demand, activity, key prices such as wages and the exchange rate, and their implications for inflation projected over the usual 12- to 24-month policy horizon.
text_original: INFORME DE POLTICA MONETARIA Mayo 2006 Resumen de la exposicin efectuada por Vittorio Corbo L, presidente del Banco Central de Chile, en la Comisin de Hacienda del Honorable Senado de la Repblica, en Valparaso, el 17 de mayo de 2006. La economa chilena contina en un ciclo expansivo y relativamente ordenado, con extraordinarias condiciones externas, en particular trminos de intercambio muy elevados gracias a los precios rcord del cobre. El crecimiento de la actividad y de la demanda interna transita gradualmente hacia valores de tendencia, mientras las holguras de capacidad se copan progresivamente. Pese al fuerte aumento del precio internacional del petrleo, el actual ciclo expansivo no ha comprometido la estabilidad de precios, aunque si involucra un leve aumento transitorio de la inflacin IPC. En los ltimos meses, la inflacin anual del IPC fluctu en torno a 4% y la inflacin subyacente IPCX1 se aproxim a 3%, ambas en lnea con las proyecciones previas. Las expectativas de inflacin se mantienen bien ancladas en 3%. Este escenario ha permitido que la normalizacin de la poltica monetaria contine a un ritmo pausado, mantenindose en la actualidad un sesgo expansivo que, en el escenario ms probable, se espera seguir reduciendo para asegurar la convergencia de la inflacin a 3% dentro del horizonte habitual de proyeccin. La oportunidad de estos ajustes depender de las implicancias de las noticias de actividad, tipo de cambio, salarios y precios sobre la trayectoria proyectada de la inflacin. El panorama externo es excepcionalmente favorable para la economa chilena. El crecimiento mundial sigue dinmico, con un mayor equilibrio entre las distintas zonas econmicas. Los trminos de intercambio de Chile mejoran de la mano de precios de productos bsicos que, contrariando las proyecciones, han seguido aumentando. El precio del cobre se ubica cerca de US$4 la libra, tras alzas sustanciales en las ltimas semanas, cuya magnitud y velocidad no son fciles de conciliar con cambios recientes y esperados en los fundamentos de demanda y oferta. El precio del petrleo tambin ha continuado aumentando, tanto por la fortaleza de la demanda mundial y problemas de oferta como por la mayor prima por riesgo frente a eventuales problemas geopolticos. Las condiciones financieras para las economas emergentes se mantienen favorables, pese a las alzas significativas de las tasas de inters de largo plazo en las economas desarrolladas. A la vez, mientras EE.UU. parece estar cerca de completar su ciclo de normalizacin de la poltica monetaria, aumentan las expectativas de mercado respecto de alzas en las tasas de inters de corto plazo en la Zona Euro y Japn, reflejo del mayor crecimiento en estas regiones y su eventual impacto en la inflacin. Internamente, el Consejo del Banco Central ha continuado con el proceso de reduccin gradual del estmulo monetario iniciado en la segunda parte del 2004, con aumentos de la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria (TPM) en dos ocasiones desde el ltimo IPoM, con lo que se ubica en 5%. En todo caso, se estima que la TPM an se encuentra por debajo de su nivel neutral. El costo del financiamiento a hogares y empresas refleja paulatinamente el ajuste de la TPM, con tasas de inters de mercado del orden de 100 puntos base por sobre el promedio del ao anterior. El crecimiento del crdito sigue fuerte, aunque ya no se aprecia una aceleracin adicional. Los agregados monetarios estabilizan su tasa de incremento anual en niveles relativamente altos, luego del aumento de fines del 2005. Como supuesto metodolgico para las proyecciones de este IPoM, se considera una depreciacin moderada del peso en trminos reales en el horizonte de proyeccin, en lnea con el escenario base de normalizacin gradual de las condiciones externas. En el primer trimestre del ao, la demanda interna se enmarc en un escenario de desaceleracin, coherente con lo previsto en enero. Por el lado del consumo, el componente durable se mantiene creciendo a tasas elevadas y favorecido por las buenas condiciones de financiamiento de los hogares y el dinamismo del empleo, pese al encarecimiento de los combustibles. El consumo habitual mantiene un crecimiento moderado. El crecimiento anual de la formacin bruta de capital fijo se desaceler en el primer trimestre, en lnea con lo proyectado, y de acuerdo con la evolucin del ciclo. Las proyecciones de este IPoM suponen que la poltica fiscal sigue enmarcada en la regla de supervit estructural, con un aumento de los valores de referencia del precio del cobre para el 2007 en lnea con la evaluacin de que los elevados precios actuales no seran duraderos. La expansividad de la poltica fiscal depender, entre otros factores, del precio de referencia que finalmente se determine. Los escenarios para la inflacin que se entregan a travs de los grficos de abanico contemplan, entre otros elementos, varias alternativas para este precio de referencia, que resultan clave para proyectar las distintas variables macroeconmicas. Tambin surge como relevante, dados los montos involucrados, el efecto que los mayores ingresos provenientes de las ventas de cobre puedan tener en la valoracin del peso en el corto plazo. La forma en que sean manejados, tanto respecto de su destino como de su denominacin, puede tener efectos sobre la economa local. La poltica anunciada por la autoridad fiscal referida al manejo de estos excedentes ayuda a disminuir estos efectos. En todo caso, cabe sealar que con una poltica fiscal menos austera, la apreciacin del peso sera mayor y la tasa de inters ms elevada.. A ello se sum que el volumen de envos mineros revirti las cadas anuales de gran parte del 2005. En cuanto a los envos industriales, su volumen sigui dinmico, mientras el de los envos agrcolas reflej los perjuicios causados por fenmenos climticos del 2005 en la produccin frutcola. Las importaciones estn en niveles similares a los de fines del ao pasado. La cuenta corriente cerr el 2005 con un supervit por sobre medio punto porcentual del PIB. Para el 2006 se proyecta un supervit mayor a 1,5% del PIB. El PIB creci 6,3% en el 2005, similar a lo estimado en enero. En el primer trimestre del 2006 aument a una tasa menor, en torno a 5%, afectado por hechos puntuales en sectores especficos. La actividad agrcola cay en trminos anuales tanto por factores climticos, como por elementos vinculados a la transicin que parece estar ocurriendo en ciertos cultivos tradicionales. As, medida por su velocidad de expansin instantnea, la actividad sufri una desaceleracin en el primer cuarto del ao, que sera revertida en el trimestre en curso. Para el 2006 en su conjunto se sigue esperando una expansin algo superior a la tendencia, llegando a un crecimiento de entre 5 y 6%. Esto supone que el crecimiento del segundo semestre es considerablemente mayor al del primero y que la desaceleracin del primer trimestre fue puntual. Para el 2007 se estima que el PIB crecera una vez ms por sobre su tendencia. Las escasas holguras de capacidad que se estima an persisten terminaran de cerrarse durante el 2006, con brechas pequeas pero positivas en el resto del horizonte de proyeccin. El panorama global del mercado laboral muestra algunos cambios respecto de comienzos de ao, destacando el sostenido incremento de la ocupacin asalariada y el repunte de la participacin laboral. En este contexto, la medida disponible de productividad del trabajo registr una desaceleracin significativa en los primeros meses del ao, aunque no es evidente que sea un fenmeno de tendencia. Las remuneraciones nominales por hora han disminuido su tasa de crecimiento anual, tal como era de esperar una vez que saliera de la base de comparacin el impacto del recorte de la jornada laboral de comienzos del 2005. Los costos laborales unitarios crecen a tasas anuales superiores a la de fines del 2005, aunque con velocidades de expansin que, de acuerdo con lo esperado, disminuyen. Cunto de la mayor variacin anual de los costos laborales responde a presiones genuinas de costos no es fcil de determinar, por una serie de factores difciles de aislar; entre ellos, la volatilidad propia de las medidas de productividad y los cambios en la medicin de las encuestas de salarios y empleo. En todo caso, con un mercado laboral cada vez ms estrecho, es especialmente importante seguir de cerca la evolucin de las presiones salariales que puedan amenazar la evolucin futura de la inflacin. Las distintas medidas de expectativas de inflacin se mantienen bien ancladas en torno a 3%. La compensacin inflacionaria a dos, cinco y diez aos se ubica en promedio en 3%, lo mismo que las expectativas de inflacin informadas en la encuesta de expectativas econmicas a uno y dos aos. Esto difiere de episodios previos de aumento del precio del petrleo en pesos, en los que las expectativas de inflacin tendan a incrementarse, al menos en forma temporal. La inflacin mensual del IPC estuvo en gran parte determinada por los cambios en el precio de los combustibles. As, la inflacin anual del IPC, ms all de los vaivenes mes a mes, oscil en torno a 4% en el primer cuatrimestre del 2006.
