text_original: X CONFERENCIA ANUAL DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE CHILE: CUENTA CORRIENTE Y FINANCIAMIENTO EXTERNO Discurso de bienvenida pronunciado por el Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, don Vittorio Corbo Lioi. 9 de noviembre de 2006 Estimados banqueros centrales, acadmicos y economistas visitantes. Estimadas amigas y amigos: sean ustedes muy bienvenidos. Siempre es motivo de satisfaccin congregar a un grupo de personas con las que se tienen intereses e inquietudes en comn, y si se trata de compartir dos das con los ms calificados estudiosos de los temas respectivos, hay que agregar el entusiasmo por la inyeccin de vitalidad y renovacin que estar recibiendo esta rea de pensamiento. Me llena de orgullo que ya estemos celebrando la Dcima Conferencia Anual del Banco Central de Chile, que se ha constituido en un evento tradicional de discusin de ideas relevantes para las polticas de la banca central y para el desarrollo econmico de nuestros pases. El tema de esta conferencia es la Cuenta Corriente y el Financiamiento Externo un tema crucial para una economa como la chilena histricamente muy abierta al comercio mundial de bienes, y cada vez ms integrada a los mercados de capitales internacionales. A modo de ilustracin, djenme mostrarles dos grficos. El primero muestra la evolucin de la suma de exportaciones ms importaciones sobre PIB desde mediados de los 70. Como se puede apreciar, gracias a un proceso sistemtico de integracin, Chile se ha vuelto una economa muy abierta al comercio exterior, tanto en comparacin con otras economas latinoamericanas como con el promedio mundial. Este otro grfico muestra la suma de nuestros activos y pasivos internacionales brutos sobre PIB. Esta es una medida del grado de integracin financiera de una economa. Me gustara destacar tres hechos aqu. Primero: en el ao 2004 el grado de integracin financiera de Chile estaba muy por sobre el promedio de las economas emergentes, pero an por debajo del promedio de las economas desarrolladas. Segundo: este proceso de integracin se ha acelerado desde mediados de los 90. Y tercero: a pesar de que la razn de pasivos ms activos sobre PIB es similar en los noventa y en los ochenta en cuanto a magnitud, la composicin de este total difiere sustancialmente, con mucho mayor peso de los activos internacionales brutos a partir de mediados de los 90. La integracin financiera tiene el potencial de acelerar el crecimiento econmico, permitiendo que el ahorro de otros pases financie proyectos de inversin rentables en Chile que de otra manera no se realizaran. Recordemos que el dficit de cuenta corriente no es ms que la brecha entre inversin y ahorro nacional. La integracin financiera permite adems suavizar las fluctuaciones del ingreso nacional y sus efectos sobre el consumo de los hogares y la inversin, sea que estas fluctuaciones respondan a variaciones de los precios de los bienes que exportamos e importamos (como en los ltimos aos) o a eventos locales que influyen en nuestra productividad. Para una economa que se sustenta en un nmero acotado de productos de exportacin, cuyos precios adems son altamente voltiles, esta suavizacin intertemporal del consumo es crucial. Gracias a la integracin financiera es posible aumentar la diversificacin del riesgo de nuestras carteras de activos, un hecho que los tenedores chilenos de activos han buscado aprovechar en forma creciente en los ltimos aos. En la prctica, sin embargo, estos beneficios potenciales de la apertura de la cuenta de capitales no siempre se materializan. Las economas emergentes en promedio se han caracterizado por tener cuentas corrientes contracclicas y un consumo altamente voltil en relacin con el ingreso corriente: justamente lo contrario de lo que predice la teora intertemporal de la cuenta corriente. Ms an, las economas emergentes han sufrido episodios de inestabilidad y en algunos casos crisis, asociados a frenazos bruscos de los flujos de capitales. Aislarse de los mercados financieros internacionales no es una opcin; los beneficios potenciales son simplemente muy grandes como para desaprovecharlos y las innovaciones de la tecnologa de la informacin y la comunicacin reducen la efectividad de eventuales controles. Se hace imperativo, entonces, entender a cabalidad los factores que determinan los flujos de capitales internacionales, desde y hacia economas emergentes como la nuestra. Esto nos permitir disear esquemas de poltica que aseguren que estos flujos aumenten el consumo y disminuyan la volatilidad, y no al revs. Simplificando, hay dos visiones imperantes con respecto al funcionamiento de los mercados financieros internacionales. La primera (de nfasis en factores internos) es que una economa con cuentas fiscales ordenadas, una poltica monetaria orientada a la estabilidad de precios y una adecuada regulacin financiera puede integrarse a los mercados de capitales internacionales sin exponerse a sufrir choques financieros desde el exterior. Esta visin enfatiza que el origen de la volatilidad que se le asocia a los flujos de capitales est en cada pas, siendo el sistema financiero internacional un mero amplificador. En esta visin, el rol de las polticas internas se limita a no ser fuente de choques. La segunda visin es que la fuente de los choques est en el sistema financiero internacional (ya sea en forma directa o por contagio desde otras economas emergentes). Las economas difieren en su grado de vulnerabilidad a dichos choques  por una combinacin de polticas pblicas y condiciones estructurales de la economa. En esta visin, el rol de las polticas pblicas esta ntimamente relacionado con las decisiones que toma el sector privado y las restricciones que enfrenta. Toda la discusin reciente de descalces cambiarios y de plazo, as como las decisiones de reservas ptimas y el uso de pasivos internacionales contingentes es parte de esta visin. Como Banco Central hemos tomado una visin eclctica, a medio camino entre ambas posturas. Creemos que es esencial tener un conjunto de polticas que no sean fuente de inestabilidad, y que adems ayuden a amortiguar los efectos de la volatilidad de los mercados financieros internacionales. La prudencia fiscal, un rgimen de metas de inflacin con un tipo de cambio flotante orientado a mantener la estabilidad de precios y una adecuada regulacin y supervisin financiera, todos aportan a estos objetivos. Ms an, hemos trabajado para brindarle herramientas al sector privado que lo ayuden a enfrentar las consecuencias de la volatilidad de los mercados financieros internacionales. Se preguntarn por qu, como Banco Central, nos interesa el tema del dficit de cuenta corriente y el financiamiento externo, en especial dado el rgimen de metas de inflacin con tipo de cambio flotante con el cual operamos en la actualidad? La primera parte de la pregunta es fcil. Tenemos un mandato de velar por el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos. Por tanto, para cumplir con nuestro mandato necesitamos comprender tanto el funcionamiento de los mercados financieros internacionales como los efectos de choques provenientes de dichos mercados en nuestro sistema financiero. Para ilustrar la importancia de esto, basta recordar cmo remeci nuestra economa la cada de la liquidez internacional que sigui a la Crisis Rusa en 1998- 99. Estrechamente relacionadas con el punto anterior, estn las polticas de reservas ptimas. La volatilidad del financiamiento externo y en particular la probabilidad de un corte sbito del flujo de fondos son ingredientes clave a considerar en el nivel y composicin de las reservas internacionales. Los flujos de capitales juegan tambin un rol importante en la conduccin de poltica monetaria en pos de nuestra meta de inflacin, por el impacto que las condiciones financieras internacionales tienen sobre la demanda agregada y el nivel de precios. Por ejemplo, una cada en el costo del financiamiento externo (como el que hemos vivido en los ltimos aos) es a todas luces expansivo. Finalmente, como Banco Central, la ley orgnica nos atribuye un conjunto de herramientas que determina el grado de apertura de la cuenta financiera. Recordarn que en 1998 bajamos el encaje a cero y que el 2001 eliminamos buena parte de las restricciones remanentes a la entrada y salida de capitales. Pero no todas. Hace apenas algunas semanas el Banco Central autoriz la emisin de bonos en pesos por parte de extranjeros en el mercado local. Este es un buen momento para volver a reflexionar sobre estos temas. Por un lado, porque el boom de precios bsicos que estamos viviendo en la regin va a terminar tarde o temprano, y como pas de ingreso medio, necesitaremos de financiamiento externo para continuar creciendo. Y, por otro, por la situacin de desbalances globales que hoy vive la economa mundial. El dficit de cuenta corriente de Estados Unidos plantea una incertidumbre respecto de cmo se deshar, y cmo los distintos escenarios y marcos de poltica afectarn a economas pequeas y abiertas como la chilena. Son preguntas ineludibles que debemos entender. Estos son los temas que nos convocan para estos dos das. Es una agenda ambiciosa, y los temas tienen una importancia crucial. Un primer bloque de la agenda evaluar los factores que explican el comportamiento de los flujos de capitales hacia economas emergentes, en particular la medida en que estn causados por choques internos, choques de demanda externos, o imperfecciones en los mercados financieros internacionales. En este bloque tendremos el honor de contar con la presentacin magistral del reconocido economista y amigo Guillermo Calvo. Adems tendremos la oportunidad de escuchar y discutir investigacin econmica reciente de Jaime Guajardo, Gita Gopinath, Graciela Kaminsky y Kevin Cowan. Chris Kent, Juan Pablo Medina y David Moreno revisarn y analizarn las experiencias con la cuenta corriente de diferentes regiones en las ltimas dcadas. Australia y Nueva Zelanda son muy buenos referentes, ya que son grandes exportadores de materias primas y siguen un esquema de metas de inflacin con tipo de cambio flotante, al igual que Chile. Para hacer el contrapunto, se presenta tambin la experiencia de los pases del Este Asitico. El programa de hoy y maana incluye tambin el tema de los desbalances globales. Como todos sabemos y como se ilustra en el tercer grfico, desde fines de los noventa, la mayora de las regiones en desarrollo han acumulado supervit en cuenta corriente, mientras las economas desarrolladas como un todo  y en particular, los Estados Unidos  han exhibido grandes dficit en cuenta corriente. Esta situacin de desequilibrio ha suscitado mucha preocupacin e investigacin en el ltimo tiempo, por lo que nuestra conferencia dedicar una buena parte de su agenda a explorar si esta situacin es de carcter transitorio o ms permanente, as como las implicancias que distintas soluciones plantean para la economa chilena. Para ello hemos invitado a importantes contribuyentes a este debate como son Sebastin Edwards, Mike Dooley, Barry Eichengreen y Roberto Zahler. Otro tema que no podamos excluir de este foro es la posicin internacional bruta de activos y pasivos. En lnea con el reciente aumento de los stocks brutos de activos internacionales, la profesin ha comenzado a analizar el efecto valoracin de estos stocks y sus implicancias sobre los flujos de capitales. Como el grueso de esta literatura se ha enfocado a las economas desarrolladas y en particular a EE.UU., esta conferencia ha querido tomar el tema desde la perspectiva de los pases en desarrollo, enfatizando preguntas respecto de la interaccin entre los stocks brutos y los flujos de capitales para Chile. Estos son los temas de los estudios que presentarn Pierre Olivier Gourinchas y Rodrigo Valds. Por ltimo, tendremos oportunidad de pensar sobre la interrelacin entre poltica cambiaria, reservas ptimas y cuenta corriente. Esto lo haremos en el contexto de la presentacin magistral de John Williamson y el estudio de Joshua Aizenman. Estos dos das de anlisis de temas extremadamente relevantes con economistas de primer nivel no habra sido posible sin la dedicacin de Kevin Cowan, Sebastin Edwards y Rodrigo Valds a pensar en los temas y personas ms calificadas para abordarlos. Adems, la muy eficiente colaboracin de David Rappoport y Mnica Correa en la organizacin fue vital. Por ltimo, el que presentadores y comentaristas de tan reconocida trayectoria hayan accedido a participar, asegura que hoy y maana sern dos das de mucho provecho. A todos ustedes, estimados participantes, les deseo una fructfera discusin y mucho aprendizaje. Title: Evolution and Prospects of the Chilean Economy
text: Evolution and Prospects of the Chilean Economy Presentation made by Mr. Vittorio Corbo, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at a breakfast organized by AMCHAM. November 23, 2006 Good morning, I appreciate your interest in this review of the latest developments in the local economy and in the world, and for the way in which we try to interpret them in the Central Bank. I think we are at a good time to analyse how the scenarios have changed and to what extent the new antecedents can support or discard what we expected in September, when our last Monetary Policy Report came to light. The prospective analysis that I will make today is timely, since we have already traveled some ground since the IPOM and today we have fresh information and news in some fields that help to refine our vision. In September, the Bank estimated that, in the central scenario, growth would be in the range of 4% to 5% this year and between 5 !4 and 6 VP/ o next, which would postpone closing gaps until late in 2007. These growth projections also had a downward bias for this year and were balanced for 2007. In inflation, the CPI variation was expected to remain at the top of the target range for a few more quarters, mainly due to a high oil price, but falling to 3% by the end of the projection horizon. The IPCX1, meanwhile, would continue to slowly approach 3%, somewhat exceeding this value during 2007 and approaching it again at the end of the projection horizon. With the new background, we can assess whether the central projection scenario is being validated or not. This is an exercise that we do rigorously and systematically in the Central Bank. This is an essential part of our work, because monetary policy must not only try to anticipate in the best possible way what is going to happen d1 that is, to project d1 but also to react appropriately to the new developments. Ideally, this reaction should be well understood by economic agents, so that the financial prices determined by the market reflect the likely course of monetary policy. After all, that is the main mechanism by which monetary policy is transmitted. Externally, global activity as a whole has evolved broadly in line with what was anticipated in September's IPOM, although there are developments in some regions. In the United States, the slowdown in the economy has intensified, driven by a significant correction in the housing market, reflecting a sharp drop in the number of those started, a stabilization of their nominal prices, and a marked increase in the stock for sale. In parallel, the futures markets anticipate a drop of between 5 and 10% in the price of homes for the next 12 months. There is, however, two pieces of good news. One is that home sales have stabilized, and if we add the sharp drop in housing starts, it should help reduce the inventory of unsold homes. The other is that the fall in this sector has not been reflected in private consumption, thanks to the fall in fuel prices, good labour market conditions and high stock prices. On the other hand, core inflation continues to exceed the level considered comfortable by some members of the Federal Open Market Committee. Growth in the Eurozone is becoming more widespread and strengthening, especially in the industrial sector. The unemployment rate fell to 7.8% in the third quarter. Expectations surveys are good and are on the rise. In fact, the area is growing above its potential. This narrowing of gaps anticipates future inflationary pressures that the ECB has been trying to contain with policy rate increases. Even with today's oil prices, the risk is upside in inflation, which means the market anticipates further interest rate hikes. Japan, meanwhile, maintains its strong dynamism and also grows above its potential. Emerging Asia continues to grow at high rates and the effects of the measures introduced to prevent overheating are already being felt in China. At the same time, demand growth is beginning to shift from investment to consumption. Going forward, the growth of the world economy will be conditioned, in large part, by the evolution of the US economy and its effects on the rest of the world. Most likely, the effects of the sharp adjustment in the housing sector will continue to be felt in the US, which should be completed during the first half of 2007. Inflation, while helped by several quarters of below-potential growth, remains above the comfort zone defined by some members of the Federal Open Market Committee. In addition, with the dynamism of consumption, the strength of the labor market, the fall in productivity and the stabilization of fuel prices, its reduction to less than 2% is not assured. Among the main risks is the acceleration of labor costs. The Eurozone and Japan should experience a slight slowdown in 2007. In contrast, another good year is expected for emerging Asia. As for primary products, their bulky prices have been revised downwards, which is most clearly seen in oil and, to a lesser extent, the price of copper and other metals. This downward correction in metal prices, especially copper, comes as no surprise. On the other hand, the sharp decline in the price of oil was not part of our central scenario, so it clearly constitutes news. In fact, the IPOM expected a price close to US 70 per barrel by the end of the year, while in recent weeks it has even reached less than US 60. These abrupt and unexpected falls in fuel prices have led to a significant reduction in CPI inflation in Chile, to the bottom of the target range, below previous projections. This is also contributed by lower core inflation CPIX1 (which excludes fuels, perishables, and some regulated services). Other indicators of the inflationary trend also show a decline and cost pressures are contained. The data for the end of the third quarter delivered today ratify the little dynamism of the activity that the partial figures had already anticipated. After nine quarters growing above trend, GDP grew below trend in the second and third quarters of this year. All this in a context where the external scenario and financial conditions were favorable and monetary policy was in the process of gradual normalization to favor the orderly convergence of the inflationary trend to the center of the target range, and capacity gaps were projected to close during 2006. In the last IPOM, we identified a number of factors that may explain part of this somewhat unexpected slowdown in output. These include transitory problems in mining production (landslides and strikes) and larger-than-expected effects of higher oil prices until the end of August. However, beyond the specific elements described above, it is difficult to explain this slowdown, given the good macroeconomic conditions that support growth. On the demand side, consumption remains buoyant, investment seems to have completed its adjustment and the volumes of non-mining exports continue to grow at high rates. However, a contractionary factor for domestic activity has been the strong dynamism of imports, which has moderated only gradually and continues to exceed projections. Domestic financial conditions are still advantageous. The MPR is below all neutral rate measures: long-term interest rates have fallen since mid-year, and today they are even lower than those in force before the monetary normalization process began; Bank financing of companies and households, although slowing at the margin, continues to grow at high rates; and the local stock index, IPSA, has recorded record highs so far in 2006, helped by strong corporate results. Since late 2001, the peso has appreciated against the dollar, as have most currencies. The real exchange rate is around the average of the last 15 years. The labour market remains dynamic. Employment continues to grow strongly, especially in the salaried component. Industrial and construction employment has grown vigorously in recent months. The unemployment rate has fallen to levels not seen since before the Asian Crisis. The market has adapted to the elements of this new scenario, correcting downwards its inflation expectations for the coming months. According to the surveys, these remain anchored at around 3% per year for the next twelve months and the following twelve. Inflationary compensation has decreased to 3% by these horizons. At the same time, activity growth projections for 2006 have also been revised downwards. For 2007, the underlying elements behind the expectation of a reacceleration in activity contemplated in the IPOM remain in force: a more expansionary fiscal policy, a positive external scenario and good domestic financial conditions. There are also new factors that strengthen this scenario. First, the sharp decline in fuel prices from August to date has an expansionary effect due to its impact on production costs. Second, this same decline increases real disposable personal income and should be an additional stimulus to private consumption. Third, the significant rise in stock prices, which has even surpassed external stock markets, due to its wealth effects and its effects on the cost of capital should strengthen private consumption and investment. Fourth, because of the intention of more investment that is identified by new projects in the cadastre of the Capital Goods Corporation, especially in mining and energy. And fifth, due to the level maintained by real estate sales, which have dispelled the risk of a weakening of the construction component that we anticipated in the IPOM. As reality reminds us permanently, the central stage is rarely given in its entirety. The main risks to this scenario, whose materialization may end up affecting growth, are mainly associated with the U.S. First, the adjustment of the housing sector may end up affecting private consumption, deepening the slowdown, and affecting growth in the rest of the world. Second, inflation may prove more persistent and force further increases in the interest rate with negative effects on bond markets and spreads in emerging countries. A third risk is associated with the possibility that oil prices may resume their upward trend. Internally, uncertainty focuses on the persistence of low CPI, CPI1 and other inflationary trend measures, probably due to the delay in closing capacity slack and lower fuel prices than projected, and the time it takes to resolve specific factors. and others not identified, which have affected the activity. The materialization or dissipation of these risks will build the new central scenario to which the Central Bank will have to react to the extent that it affects the vision of the evolution of prices and activity in the policy horizon. Precisely the incorporation of these new antecedents in the vision forward, especially on the inflationary front, led the Council of the BCCh to review its strategy of gradual monetary normalization. Being faithful to the idea of making these changes transparent, and considering that a fundamental part of the transmission of monetary policy occurs through expectations, the communiqu8es that accompanied the RPM of the last four months have included these adjustments in the monetary policy strategy. In August it was announced that although "in the most likely scenario, slow adjustments in the interest rate are still necessary... They may be less frequent in recent quarters." In September, he went further, "additional interest rate increases will be necessary.... However, its materialization could be delayed for a long time." In the IPOM that was published a few days after the RPM, the neutral interest rate estimate was adjusted downwards. In October, the expected speed of monetary normalization was further softened, publishing that "for an extended time, further increases in the MPR may not be necessary." Last week, in the post-RPM statement of November, the bias was removed from the communiqu8e allowing that in the following RPM the TPM can be maintained, raised or lowered: "future changes in the TPM ... They will depend on the new information that accumulates and its implications on projected inflation." The market has read these changes very well in the press releases and analysts' expectations of future TPM have reflected the change in strategy with a flattening of the forward curve and TPM expectations. This adjustment is expansive. In the coming months, the Council will closely monitor domestic and external developments to decide how to adjust its monetary policy to maintain price stability. That is the greatest contribution the Central Bank can make to the country's growth.
text_original: Evolucin y Perspectivas de la Economa Chilena Presentacin efectuada por don Vittorio Corbo, Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, en desayuno organizado por AMCHAM. 23 de noviembre de 2006 Buenos das, agradezco el inters por este repaso a los ltimos acontecimientos ocurridos en la economa local y en el mundo, y por la forma en que tratamos de interpretarlos en el Banco Central. Creo que estamos en un buen momento para analizar cmo han cambiado los escenarios y en qu medida los nuevos antecedentes pueden ir apoyando o desechando lo que esperbamos en septiembre, cuando sali a la luz nuestro ltimo Informe de Poltica Monetaria. El anlisis prospectivo que hoy har es oportuno, pues ya hemos recorrido algn terreno desde el IPOM y hoy tenemos informacin fresca y novedades en algunos campos que ayudan a afinar nuestra visin. En septiembre, el Banco estimaba que, en el escenario central, el crecimiento se ubicara en el rango de 4 % a 5 %% este ao y entre 5 !4 y 6 VP/o el prximo, lo que postergara los cierres de brechas hasta avanzado el ao 2007. Estas proyecciones de crecimiento tenan adems un sesgo a la baja para este ao y estaban balanceadas para el 2007. En inflacin, se esperaba que la variacin del IPC se mantuviera en la parte superior del rango meta por algunos trimestres ms, debido principalmente a un alto precio del petrleo, pero descendiendo al 3% para fines del horizonte de proyeccin. El IPCX1, en tanto, seguira acercndose lentamente al 3%, superando en algo este valor durante el 2007 y volviendo a acercarse a l a fines del horizonte de proyeccin. Con los nuevos antecedentes, podemos evaluar si el escenario central de proyecciones se est validando o no. Este es un ejercicio que hacemos rigurosa y sistemticamente en el Banco Central. Ello es parte esencial de nuestro trabajo, ya que la poltica monetaria no slo debe tratar de anticipar de la mejor manera posible lo que va a suceder o sea proyectar sino tambin reaccionar de manera adecuada a las novedades que se produzcan. Idealmente esta reaccin debe ser bien comprendida por los agentes econmicos, de modo que los precios financieros que determina el mercado reflejen el curso probable de la poltica monetaria. A fin de cuentas, ese es el mecanismo principal por el cual se transmite la poltica monetaria. En el mbito externo, la actividad mundial en su conjunto ha evolucionado a grandes rasgos en lnea con lo anticipado en el IPOM de septiembre, aunque hay novedades en algunas regiones. En Estados Unidos se ha intensificado la desaceleracin de la economa, empujada por una importante correccin del mercado de la vivienda, que refleja una pronunciada cada en el nmero de aquellas iniciadas, una estabilizacin de sus precios nominales, y un marcado aumento del stock a la venta. En paralelo, los mercados de futuros anticipan una baja de entre 5 y 10% en el precio de las viviendas para los prximos 12 meses. Hay, sin embargo, dos buenas noticias. Una es que la venta de casas se ha estabilizado, y si agregamos la fuerte cada de viviendas iniciadas, debera contribuir a reducir el inventario de casas sin vender. La otra es que la cada en este sector no se ha reflejado en el consumo privado, gracias a la cada del precio de los combustibles, a las buenas condiciones del mercado laboral y a los altos precios que han alcanzado las acciones. Por otra parte, la inflacin subyacente contina superando el nivel considerado como confortable por algunos miembros del Comit de Mercado Abierto de la Reserva Federal. El crecimiento de la Zona Euro se hace ms generalizado y se fortalece, especialmente en el sector industrial. La tasa de desempleo desciende a 7,8% en el tercer trimestre. Las encuestas de expectativas son buenas y van al alza. De hecho, la zona crece por encima de su potencial. Este estrechamiento de brechas anticipa presiones inflacionarias futuras que el BCE ha estado tratando de contener con aumentos de la tasa de poltica. Incluso con los precios del petrleo de hoy, el riesgo es hacia arriba en la inflacin, lo que se traduce en que el mercado anticipa nuevas alzas de la tasa de inters. Japn, en tanto, mantiene su fuerte dinamismo y crece tambin por encima de su potencial. Asia emergente sigue creciendo a tasas elevadas y en China ya se notan los efectos de las medidas introducidas para evitar un sobrecalentamiento. A la vez, comienza a desplazarse el crecimiento de la demanda desde inversin hacia consumo. Hacia delante, el crecimiento de la economa mundial estar condicionado, en parte importante, por la evolucin de la economa de EE.UU. y sus efectos en el resto del mundo. Lo ms probable es que en EE.UU. se sigan sintiendo los efectos del brusco ajuste del sector vivienda, el que debiera completarse durante el primer semestre del 2007. La inflacin, aunque ha cado ayudada por varios trimestres de crecimiento por debajo del potencial, sigue por encima de la zona de confort definida por algunos miembros del Comit de Mercado Abierto de la Reserva Federal. Adems, con el dinamismo del consumo, la fortaleza del mercado laboral, la cada de la productividad y la estabilizacin del precio de los combustibles, su reduccin a menos de 2% no est asegurada. Entre los principales riesgos est la aceleracin de los costos laborales. La Zona Euro y Japn deberan experimentar una leve desaceleracin el 2007. En contraste, se espera otro buen ao para Asia emergente. En cuanto a los productos primarios, sus abultados precios se han corregido a la baja, lo que se aprecia con ms claridad en el petrleo y, en menor medida, el precio del cobre y dems metales. Esta correccin a la baja de los precios de los metales, especialmente el cobre, no constituye una sorpresa. En cambio la pronunciada disminucin del precio del petrleo no era parte de nuestro escenario central, por lo que claramente constituye una noticia. De hecho, en el IPOM se esperaba un precio cercano a US$70 por barril para fin de ao, mientras que en las ltimas semanas ha llegado incluso a menos de US$60. Estas cadas abruptas e inesperadas de los precios de los combustibles han inducido una importante reduccin de la inflacin del IPC en Chile, hasta la parte inferior del rango meta, por debajo de proyecciones previas. A lo anterior tambin contribuye una menor inflacin subyacente IPCX1 (que excluye combustibles, perecibles, y algunos servicios regulados). Otros indicadores de la tendencia inflacionaria tambin muestran una declinacin y las presiones de costos estn contenidas. Los datos de cierre del tercer trimestre entregados hoy ratifican el poco dinamismo de la actividad que las cifras parciales ya haban anticipado. Despus de nueve trimestres creciendo por sobre su tendencia, el PIB creci por debajo de esta el segundo y el tercer trimestre de este ao. Todo esto en un contexto donde el escenario externo y las condiciones financieras eran favorables y la poltica monetaria estaba en proceso de normalizacin gradual para favorecer la convergencia ordenada de la tendencia inflacionaria al centro del rango meta, y se proyectaba un cierre de brechas de capacidad durante el 2006. En el ltimo IPOM, identificamos una serie de factores que pueden explicar parte de esta desaceleracin, un tanto inesperada, del producto. Entre estos destacan los problemas transitorios en la produccin minera (derrumbes y huelgas) y efectos mayores que los esperados de los mayores precios del petrleo vigentes hasta fines de agosto. Sin embargo, ms all de los elementos puntuales antes descritos, es difcil explicar esta desaceleracin, dadas las buenas condiciones macroeconmicas que apoyan el crecimiento. Por el lado de la demanda, el consumo mantiene su dinamismo, la inversin parece haber concluido su ajuste y los volmenes de las exportaciones no mineras siguen creciendo a tasas elevadas. Sin embargo, un factor contractivo para la actividad interna ha sido el fuerte dinamismo de las importaciones, que se ha moderado solo gradualmente y sigue superando las proyecciones. Las condiciones financieras internas an son ventajosas. La TPM se encuentra por debajo de todas las medidas de tasa neutral: las tasas de inters de largo plazo han descendido desde mediados de ao, y hoy son incluso inferiores a las vigentes antes de que se iniciara el proceso de normalizacin monetaria; el financiamiento bancario de empresas y hogares aunque se ha desacelerado en el margen, sigue creciendo a tasas elevadas; y el ndice burstil local, IPSA, ha registrado mximos histricos en lo que va del 2006, favorecido por lo buenos resultados corporativos. Desde fines del 2001, el peso se ha apreciado frente al dlar, al igual que la mayora de las monedas. El tipo de cambio real se ubica en tomo al promedio de los ltimos 15 aos. El mercado laboral mantiene su dinamismo. El empleo sigue creciendo con vigor, especialmente el componente asalariado. El empleo industrial y de construccin crecen vigorosamente en los ltimos meses. La tasa de desocupacin ha cado a niveles no vistos desde antes de la Crisis Asitica. El mercado se ha adaptado a los elementos de este nuevo escenario, corrigiendo a la baja sus expectativas de inflacin para los prximos meses. Segn las encuestas, estas se mantienen ancladas en torno al 3% anual para los prximos doce meses y los siguientes doce. La compensacin inflacionaria ha disminuido al 3% a estos horizontes. En paralelo, las proyecciones de crecimiento de la actividad para el ao 2006 tambin se han revisado a la baja. Para el ao 2007, siguen vigentes los elementos que subyacen tras la expectativa de una reaceleracin de la actividad contemplados en el IPOM: una poltica fiscal ms expansiva, un escenario externo positivo y buenas condiciones financieras internas. Tambin hay nuevos factores que fortalecen este escenario. Primero, la pronunciada baja de los combustibles desde agosto a la fecha tiene un efecto expansivo por su incidencia en los costos de produccin. Segundo, esta misma baja incrementa el ingreso personal disponible real y debera ser un estmulo adicional para el consumo privado. Tercero, la importante alza de los precios accionarios, que incluso ha superado a las bolsas externas, por sus efectos riqueza y por sus efectos en el costo del capital debera fortalecer el consumo privado y la inversin. Cuarto, por la intencin de ms inversin que se identifica por nuevos proyectos en el catastro de la Corporacin de Bienes de Capital, especialmente en minera y energa. Y quinto, por el nivel que mantienen las ventas inmobiliarias, que han disipado el riesgo de un debilitamiento del componente de construccin que anticipbamos en el IPOM. Como la realidad nos recuerda en forma permanente, rara vez se da el escenario central en su integridad. Los principales riesgos a este escenario, cuya materializacin puede terminar afectando el crecimiento, estn principalmente asociados con EE.UU. Primero, el ajuste del sector vivienda puede terminar afectando al consumo privado, profundizando la desaceleracin, y afectando de paso al crecimiento del resto del mundo. Segundo, la inflacin puede resultar ms persistente y obligar a nuevos aumentos en la tasa de inters con efectos negativos en los mercados de bonos y en los spreads de pases emergentes. Un tercer riesgo se asocia a la posibilidad de que los precios del petrleo puedan retomar su tendencia al alza. En lo interno, la incertidumbre se centra en la persistencia de los bajos registros de la inflacin IPC, IPCX1 y otras medidas de tendencia inflacionaria, debido probablemente al retraso en el cierre de holguras de capacidad y a precios de combustibles ms bajos que los proyectados, y en el tiempo que demoren en resolverse los factores puntuales, y otros no identificados, que han afectado la actividad. La materializacin o disipacin de estos riesgos van a ir construyendo el nuevo escenario central ante el cual el Banco Central tendr que ir reaccionando en la medida en que afecte la visin de la evolucin de precios y actividad en el horizonte de poltica. Justamente la incorporacin de estos nuevos antecedentes en la visin hacia delante, especialmente en el frente inflacionario, llevaron al Consejo del BCCh a revisar su estrategia de normalizacin monetaria gradual. Siendo fiel a la idea de hacer transparentes dichos cambios, y considerando que parte fundamental de la transmisin de la poltica monetaria ocurre a travs de las expectativas, los comunicados que acompaaron las RPM de los ltimos cuatro meses han recogido estos ajustes en la estrategia de poltica monetaria. En agosto se anunci que aunque en el escenario ms probable siguen siendo necesarios ajustes pausados en la tasa de inters... ellos podran ser menos frecuentes en los ltimos trimestres. En septiembre, se fue ms all, sern necesarios incrementos adicionales de la tasa de inters.... Sin embargo, su materializacin podra dilatarse por un tiempo prolongado. En el IPOM que se public unos das despus de la RPM se ajust a la baja la estimacin de tasa neutral de inters. En octubre se suaviz aun ms la velocidad de la normalizacin monetaria esperada publicando que por un tiempo prolongado, podran no ser necesarios nuevos incrementos en la TPM. La semana pasada, en el comunicado posterior a la RPM de noviembre, se quit el sesgo al comunicado dando cabida a que en las siguientes RPM la TPM pueda mantenerse, subir o bajar: cambios futuros en la TPM ... dependern de la nueva informacin que se acumule y sus implicancias sobre la inflacin proyectada. El mercado ha ledo muy bien estos cambios en los comunicados y las expectativas de TPM futura de los analistas han reflejado el cambio en la estrategia con un aplanamiento de la curva forward y de expectativas de TPM. Este ajuste es expansivo. En los meses que vienen, el Consejo seguir de cerca las noticias que surjan en el mbito interno y externo para decidir cmo ir ajustando su poltica monetaria en pro de mantener la estabilidad de precios. Esa es la mayor contribucin que el Banco Central puede hacer al crecimiento del pas.

Title: Central Banking, Analysis and Economic Policies of the Central Bank of Chile
text: Launch of volume 11 of the Central Bank of Chile's Book Series on Central Banking, Economic Analysis and Policy Santiago, March 19, 2007, 12.30 hrs. English Patio Introductory and Welcome Remarks Vittorio Corbo President of the Central Bank of Chile It is my pleasure to say a few introductory and welcoming words to this launching ceremony of a new volume of the series of books on Central Banking, Analysis and Economic Policies, published by the Central Bank of Chile. This series of books makes available to the national and foreign public an important part of the economic research carried out or promoted by the Central Bank of Chile. Its objective is to contribute to the study of central banking and the analysis of the economy in general, with emphasis on issues and policies related to the economic management of emerging countries, such as Chile. With this, we seek to contribute to greater information on the fundamentals of the policies we implement, as well as to promote dialogue with and among academics, economic analysts and economic policy makers in Chile and in the world. By collecting the work of domestic and foreign researchers and academics, this series shows how economic research and policy decision-making generate a space for beneficial mutual feedback. On the one hand, academics can help to understand the underlying reasons for the successes, failures, advantages and weaknesses of different economic policies, contributing to better design and more efficient implementation of these. On the other hand, the concrete adoption of policy options by policy makers provides a great opportunity for researchers to better understand and model the complex real world of policies and their outcomes. The Central Bank of Chile believes that only through a sound economic analysis can it fulfill the mandate that society has given it, namely, the efficient conduct of monetary policy, which ensures price stability and the normal functioning of the internal and external payment system. This is particularly important because effective policy decision-making demands increasing force. the application of analytical tools, relevant models and empirical analysis in different areas. Thus, monetary policy benefits from rigorous and high-level analyses in areas of study such as transmission mechanisms and monetary policy rules, the functioning and efficient regulation of financial markets, international economics and finance, the macroeconomics of savings, investment and economic growth, to name just a few areas that are dealt with directly in the volumes included in the series of books that brings us together today. The publication of these books is the result of the work of countless people working in the Central Bank or outside it. My special recognition goes to the many experts whose presentations led to the chapters of the books, to the commentators of those and to the editors of the 11 volumes. If we add all those who have worked in the elaboration of the studies incorporated in the books and in the production of volumes 1 to 11, we can notice that about 150 people have participated. I would also like to thank the outstanding members of the Editorial Committee of the series for their valuable contribution: Ricardo Caballero, professor at MIT; Jorge Desormeaux, Director of the Central Bank; Anne Krueger, former First Deputy Managing Director, International Monetary Fund; Frederic Mishkin, professor at Columbia University and member of the Board of Governors of the US Federal Reserve; Felipe Morand8e, dean of the Faculty of Economics and Business of the University of Chile; Andr8es Solimano, advisor to ECLAC; and Rodrigo Vald8es, Manager of the Studies Division of the Central Bank. I also highlight the continuous work of the editors of the series, Norman Loayza, from the World Bank, and Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel, from the Central Bank, who lead the editing and production team of the volumes. On this occasion, we present volume 11 of the Series, entitled "Monetary Policy under Inflation Targeting" and edited by Frederic Mishkin and Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel. This book focuses on a topic that is at the heart of the Central Bank of Chile's monetary policy: the inflation targeting framework. As John Taylor, professor at Stanford University, and Alan Bollard, Governor of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand, point out on the flap of the book we are presenting today, Chile was the second country in the world, after New Zealand, to adopt an inflation targeting scheme in 1990. During its first phase, between 1991 and 1999, the target scheme was partially adopted, with annual announcements of declining targets, an average policy horizon of only 8 months and coexisting with an exchange rate band. Starting in 2000, a second phase began, with a full inflation targeting scheme based on a stationary target, so that inflation would be in the target range of 2 to 4 per cent per year, centred at 3 per cent, most of the time. The design of monetary policy took into account a horizon of 12 to 24 months and a context of floating exchange rate. In addition, the Central Bank has formalized the framework for conducting its monetary policy, with monthly and pre-announced monetary policy meetings, communicating to the public the rationale, processes and results of its monetary policy decisions in the Monetary Policy Reports and in the Press Releases and Minutes of its Monetary Policy Meetings. The fundamentals of our monetary policy framework were recently updated taking take into account the evolution of the practice in this decade and are presented in detail in the document "The Monetary Policy of the Central Bank of Chile in the Inflation Targeting Framework", published in January of this year. The results that Chile has achieved with the application of a full inflation targeting scheme are very positive. The inflation target has been reached most of the time. Between 2000 and 2006, average CPI inflation was 2.9%, just one tenth below our inflation target. This places Chile among the target countries that have registered the smallest deviations from their effective inflation rates from the target. At the same time, volatility in both GDP and inflation has fallen significantly since the beginning of this decade. Medium- and long-term inflation expectations have remained anchored around the target, reflecting its importance as a stable monetary policy transmission mechanism and an adequate indicator of its credibility. Together with fiscal policy based on a structural surplus, monetary policy contributes to the country's macroeconomic stabilization. And this is recognized by the international rankings of quality of macroeconomic policies in general, and monetary policies in particular, which place Chile in the first places of the countries of the world. However, this new volume will contribute to a better understanding of the theoretical bases and empirical results of monetary policies under inflation targeting in Chile and in the world. The book brings together 14 chapters contributed by prominent executives and economists from international financial institutions and central banks around the world, together with prestigious university academics. The thematic coverage is broad, ranging from theoretical work on the fundamentals of monetary policy under inflation targeting, the specific design of the targeting scheme and the requirements that countries meet when adopting targets, to the growing international empirical evidence on the results of monetary policy in countries with inflation targets and the specific experience of Chile. The common denominator of these works is that they are located at the frontier of international research on this subject, contributing both to a better scientific understanding and to perfecting the conduct of monetary policy, both in Chile and in other countries with inflation targets. But I do not want to dwell here on the conclusions and implications of this book, because this is the role of the presenter of the volume. And no one could play a better role in presenting and commenting on this book than who preceded me in the Presidency of this Bank, leading the transition from the partial scheme to the full inflation targeting framework and who played a central role in the first attempt to use inflation targeting in Chile in the period 1965-1967. I therefore extend a warm welcome to Carlos Massad, former President of the Central Bank of Chile. Before giving the floor to Carlos Massad, I want to congratulate the editors of the book for their magnificent work and thank the work of the team of professionals who have collaborated in the supervision and edition of this volume: Consuelo Edwards, Mauricio Larra92n, e7lvaro Garc92a, Jennifer Hoover, M97nica Widoycovich, Carlos Arriagada, Ewald Stark, Claudio Sep9clveda, Dionisio Vio and M97nica Correa. Welcome to Carlos Massad.

Patio Ingls Palabras Introductorias y de Bienvenida Vittorio Corbo Presidente Banco Central de Chile Es un placer para mi decir algunas palabras introductorias y de bienvenida a esta ceremonia de lanzamiento de un nuevo volumen de la serie de libros sobre Banca Central, Anlisis y Polticas Econmicas, publicada por el Banco Central de Chile. Esta serie de libros pone a disposicin del pblico nacional y extranjero una parte importante de la investigacin econmica realizada o promovida por el Banco Central de Chile. Tiene como objetivo aportar al estudio de la banca central y al anlisis de la economa en general, con nfasis en temas y polticas relacionadas con la conduccin econmica de pases emergentes, como Chile. Con ello buscamos contribuir a una mayor informacin sobre los fundamentos de las polticas que implementamos, as como promover el dilogo con y entre acadmicos, analistas econmicos y responsables de polticas econmicas en Chile y en el mundo. Al recoger el trabajo de investigadores y acadmicos nacionales y extranjeros, esta serie muestra cmo la investigacin econmica y la toma de decisiones de polticas generan un espacio de beneficiosa retroalimentacin mutua. Por una parte, los acadmicos pueden ayudar a entender las razones subyacentes de los xitos, fracasos, ventajas y debilidades de diferentes polticas econmicas, contribuyendo a un mejor diseo y a una implementacin ms eficiente de stas. Por otra parte, la adopcin concreta de las opciones de poltica por los responsables de las mismas ofrece una gran oportunidad a los investigadores para comprender y modelar mejor el complejo mundo real de las polticas y sus resultados. El Banco Central de Chile considera que slo a travs de un anlisis econmico slido puede cumplir con el mandato que la sociedad le ha entregado, a saber, la conduccin eficiente de la poltica monetaria, que asegure la estabilidad de precios y el normal funcionamiento del sistema de pagos interno y externo. Esto es particularmente importante porque la toma eficaz de decisiones de poltica exige cada vez con mayor fuerza la aplicacin de herramientas analticas, modelos relevantes y anlisis emprico en diferentes reas. As, la poltica monetaria se beneficia de anlisis rigurosos y de alto nivel en reas de estudio tales como los mecanismos de transmisin y las reglas de poltica monetaria, el funcionamiento y la regulacin eficiente de los mercados financieros, la economa y las finanzas internacionales, la macroeconoma del ahorro, de la inversin y del crecimiento econmico, por nombrar slo algunas reas que se tratan directamente en los volmenes incluidos en la serie de libros que hoy nos congrega. La publicacin de estos libros es el resultado del trabajo de un sinnmero de personas que trabajan en el Banco Central o fuera de l. Vaya mi especial reconocimiento a los mltiples expertos cuyas presentaciones derivaron en los captulos de los libros, a los comentaristas de aquellas y a los editores de los 11 volmenes. Si sumamos a todos quienes han trabajado en la elaboracin de los estudios incorporados en los libros y en la produccin de los volmenes 1 al 11, podemos notar que han participado cerca de 150 personas. Asimismo, quiero agradecer la valiosa contribucin de los destacados miembros del Comit Editorial de la serie: Ricardo Caballero, profesor del MIT; Jorge Desormeaux, Consejero del Banco Central; Anne Krueger, Ex Primera Subdirectora Gerenta del Fondo Monetario Internacional; Frederic Mishkin, profesor de Columbia University y miembro de la Junta de Gobernadores de la Reserva Federal de EE.UU.; Felipe Morand, decano de la Facultad de Economa y Negocios de la Universidad de Chile; Andrs Solimano, asesor de la CEPAL; y Rodrigo Valds, Gerente de la Divisin Estudios del Banco Central. Destaco tambin la continua labor de los editores de la serie, Norman Loayza, del Banco Mundial, y Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel, del Banco Central, quienes encabezan el equipo de edicin y produccin de los volmenes. En esta ocasin, presentamos el volumen 11 de la Serie, titulado Poltica Monetaria bajo Metas de Inflacin y editado por Frederic Mishkin y Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel. Este libro se centra en un tpico que constituye el corazn de la poltica monetaria del Banco Central de Chile: el marco de metas de inflacin. Como destacan John Taylor, profesor de Stanford University y Alan Bollard, Gobernador del Banco de la Reserva de Nueva Zelanda, en la solapa del libro que estamos presentando hoy, Chile fue el segundo pas del mundo, despus de Nueva Zelanda, en adoptar un esquema de metas de inflacin en 1990. Durante su primera fase, entre 1991 y 1999, el esquema de metas se adopt de manera parcial, con anuncios anuales de metas declinantes, un horizonte de poltica promedio de slo 8 meses y coexistiendo con una banda cambiaria. A partir del ao 2000 se inici una segunda fase, con un esquema pleno de metas de inflacin basado en una meta estacionaria, de manera que la inflacin se ubicara la mayor parte del tiempo en el rango meta de 2 a 4% anual, centrado en 3%. El diseo de poltica monetaria tomaba en cuenta un horizonte de 12 a 24 meses y un contexto de tipo de cambio flotante. Adems el Banco Central ha formalizado el marco de conduccin de su poltica monetaria, con reuniones mensuales y preanunciadas de poltica monetaria, comunicando al pblico los fundamentos, los procesos y los resultados de sus decisiones de poltica monetaria en los Informes de Poltica Monetaria y en los Comunicados de Prensa y las Minutas de sus Reuniones de Poltica Monetaria. Los fundamentos de nuestro marco de poltica monetaria se actualizaron recientemente tomando en cuenta la evolucin de la prctica en esta dcada y se presentan detalladamente en el documento La Poltica Monetaria del Banco Central de Chile en el Marco de Metas de Inflacin, publicado en enero de este ao. Los resultados que ha logrado Chile con la aplicacin de un esquema pleno de metas de inflacin son muy positivos. La meta de inflacin se ha alcanzado la mayor parte del tiempo. Entre 2000 y 2006, la inflacin IPC promedio ha sido de 2,9%, apenas una dcima por debajo de nuestra inflacin meta. Ello sita a Chile entre los pases con metas que han registrado los menores desvos de sus tasas de inflacin efectivas respecto de la meta. Al mismo tiempo, la volatilidad tanto del PIB como de la inflacin ha cado significativamente desde comienzos de esta dcada. Las expectativas de inflacin de mediano y largo plazo se han mantenido ancladas en torno a la meta, lo que refleja su importancia como mecanismo estable de transmisin de la poltica monetaria e indicador adecuado de credibilidad de la misma. Conjuntamente con la poltica fiscal basada en un supervit estructural, la poltica monetaria contribuye a la estabilizacin macroeconmica del pas. Y as lo reconocen los rankings internacionales de calidad de polticas macroeconmicas en general, y de polticas monetarias en particular, que colocan a Chile en los primeros lugares de los pases del mundo. Ahora bien, este nuevo volumen contribuir a entender mejor las bases tericas y los resultados empricos de las polticas monetarias bajo metas de inflacin en Chile y en el mundo. El libro rene 14 captulos aportados por destacados ejecutivos y economistas de instituciones financieras internacionales y bancos centrales del mundo, junto a prestigiosos acadmicos universitarios. La cobertura temtica es amplia, pues abarca desde trabajos tericos sobre los fundamentos de la poltica monetaria bajo metas de inflacin, el diseo especfico del esquema de metas y los requisitos que cumplen los pases al adoptar las metas, hasta la creciente evidencia emprica internacional sobre los resultados de la poltica monetaria en pases con metas de inflacin y la experiencia especfica de Chile. El denominador comn de estos trabajos es que se sitan en la frontera de la investigacin internacional sobre este tema, contribuyendo tanto a una mejor comprensin cientfica como a perfeccionar la conduccin de la poltica monetaria, tanto en Chile como en otros pases con metas de inflacin. Pero no quiero abundar aqu en las conclusiones e implicancias de este libro, porque es ste el rol del presentador del volumen. Y nadie podra jugar un mejor papel en presentar y comentar este libro que quin me precedi en la Presidencia de este Banco, encabezando la transicin del esquema parcial al marco pleno de metas de inflacin y quien jug un rol central en el primer intento de uso de metas de inflacin en Chile en el perodo 1965-1967. Por lo tanto, doy la ms cordial bienvenida a Carlos Massad, ex presidente del Banco Central de Chile. Antes de dar la palabra a Carlos Massad, quiero felicitar a los editores del libro por su magnfica labor y agradecer el trabajo del equipo de profesionales que han colaborado en la supervisin y edicin de este volumen: Consuelo Edwards, Mauricio Larran, lvaro Garca, Jennifer Hoover, Mnica Widoycovich, Carlos Arriagada, Ewald Stark, Claudio Seplveda, Dionisio Vio y Mnica Correa. Demos la bienvenida a Carlos Massad.

The Role of the Central Bank in Capital Market Development The constitutional mandate of the bank is to ensure the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. Thus granted, the mandate is a fundamental pillar for the financial stability of our economy. However, unlike the monetary policy objective, financial stability is not a proprietary objective of the central bank, being shared with other regulatory and supervisory bodies. However, the central bank's contribution to the development of the capital market has covered various areas of the financial system, which I summarize below: 3.1 Payment infrastructure In 2000, the Council of the Central Bank decided to adopt a modernization program aimed at bringing our country's payment systems into line with international standards in this area. Our main objective was to increase the efficiency and security of high-value payment systems operating in the country. One of the most important milestones of this program was the implementation of the RTGS System in April 2004. The RTGS is an electronic system of interbank payments with gross settlement and in real time, operated by the Central Bank and to which all banks established in Chile have access. Without prejudice to the operation of the RTGS system, and recognizing the usefulness of netting or clearing payment settlement schemes, the Central Bank authorized at the end of 2005 the operation of the "High Value Payments Clearing House in Moneda Nacional" (CCAV), a company that is operated by a bank transfer support company, Combanc S.A. Payments made through this Chamber are final and irrevocable and once their daily business cycle is completed, the result of the clearing process is finally settled through the RTGS System. The development of these systems has been sustained: i) the number of operations carried out between them has more than doubled since their inception; (ii) the increased use of the system is largely explained by the increase in transactions carried out on behalf of third parties. On behalf of Interbank clients To this, the Central Bank has added other initiatives to modernize payment systems that contribute to minimizing operational risks and improving the conditions of access to financing for commercial banks. Firstly, the modality of delivery against payment of securities traded in the money market and, secondly, the availability of a Permanent Liquidity Facility in national currency (FLI), implemented in January 2005, is highlighted. There are still a number of aspects to modernize in our payment system and the Central Bank is actively evaluating and participating in these initiatives. In the first case, the challenge of increasing the security of settlements and clearing of foreign currency transactions remains. In the second case, the Central Bank has participated in the development of a Securities Clearing and Settlement System that will result in the creation of a Central Counterparty Chamber. This project, promoted by the Treasury and which is in the initial stages of its legal processing, will allow to operate with greater legal certainty of transactions and improve the security conditions of stock market operations . 3.2 Bank debt structure The Central Bank, during the nineties, was the main issuer of long-term public debt, a situation that has changed somewhat in recent years with issues on behalf of the Treasury. In any case, the market for long-term instruments already presented an interesting degree of development since the mid-eighties, as a result of the issuance of mortgage credit bills used to finance the purchase of real estate assets. This development was made possible, to a large extent, by the demand for long-term investment instruments created by the sustained accumulation of savings funds from the pension fund industry, the Central Bank's efforts to control inflation, and the existence of a widely accepted indexation unit in the economy. Traditionally, our long-term papers, known as PRCs, were denominated in development units (UF) and structured to be paid in the form of equal semi-annual coupons, that is, including capital amortization. This structure made it extremely difficult to estimate the yield curve and create deep markets in different sections of the curve. As a result of the above, the Central Bank, in August 2002, decided to restructure the composition of its debt, giving rise to the issuance of bullet bonds, which only consider interest payment coupons during the life of the bond, while the capital is canceled at the maturity of the last coupon. Thus, bonds were issued in pesos, denominated BCP, at 2 and 5 years and bonds in UF, denominated BCU, at 5 and 10 years, respectively. Instruments were also issued in dollars, denominated and payable in pesos, BCD, and denominated and payable in that currency, BCX, for terms of 2 to 5 years. Subsequently, in 2004, the first BCP for a longer term, 10 years, was issued. The objectives of this initiative were: (i) To modify the composition of the Central Bank's long-term debt, in order to increase the share of debt in pesos and its average term; ii) Adopt international standards for the issuance of Central Bank debt; iii) Strengthen the placement of benchmark securities, with a minimum size per issue, through the use of reopenings, repurchases and exchange of instruments. In turn, the nominalization of monetary policy put an end to a monetary regime that lasted 16 years, assimilating monetary management to the practice adopted by the other central banks of the world that conduct monetary policy actively. As otorgado, el mandato es un pilar fundamental para la estabilidad financiera de nuestra economa. No obstante, a diferencia del objetivo de poltica monetaria, la estabilidad financiera no es un objetivo privativo del banco central, siendo compartido con otros organismos regulatorios y de supervisin. Title: Exposition
text: V Meeting Chile-China Bilateral Business Council Central Cultural of Carabineros, June 10, 2011 Sebasti87n Claro, member of the Board of the Central Bank of Chile1 I am grateful for the invitation of the Chile-China bilateral council to present on this occasion the prospects of the Chinese economy. I will try to share with you some reflections on the medium-term prospects for this economy, ignoring very short-term considerations. At the end of my presentation I will make a few brief reflections on the challenges that this has for Chile and other developing economies. It is always convenient to have a historical vision of the processes of reform and transformation when one intends to have a medium-term perspective. For this, Figure 1 is a good starting point. For many centuries China was a great world power, with a strong presence in international trade. China's shipping fleet in the sixteenth century was the most important in the world, and its trade relations reached every known corner of humanity. For various reasons that are not worth discussing here, China began to close itself off to trade and with it there was a divergence from the rest of the world that led to their share of the world economy in the second half of the twentieth century was significantly reduced. After the reforms promoted by Deng Xiaoping in the early 1980s, the economy resumed high growth rates and a process of spectacular convergence from which all We are witnesses. Sustained growth rates of around 9% have allowed China to achieve a per capita income of around 5,000 USD (just over 10,000 USD PPP). per capita), figures unthinkable a couple of decades ago. For example, in 1980 GDP per capita PPP in today's dollars was 1,300, which is about 15% of today's level. Naturally, this has not only had a strong impact on world trade but also on poverty reduction for important sectors of the world. population. After more than two decades of a very successful process it is worth asking what lies ahead. 2 The experience of other countries that have experienced periods of prolonged boom provides important background. We will take a closer look at the transitions in Japan and South Korea. Once the Second World War ended in the case of Japan and in the late 1950s in the case of Korea, both countries began a process of growth. with rates around 9% real per year. This process was accompanied by a strong accumulation of 1 I appreciate the collaboration of Felipe Jaque in the preparation of this presentation. 2 See Claro, S, 2003 , "25 years of Economic Reforms in China: 1978.2003", Public Studies (91), for a more detailed analysis of this reform process . capital, which led many analysts and academics to emphasize perspiration rather than inspiration as key in this process. 3 After a few years, and when these economies reached per capita output levels around 10,000 USD in today's dollars (approximately 19,000 USD PPP), there is a clear break in the trend of GDP per capita. This break also coincides with approximately 30 years since the beginning of the reforms. This can be seen in Figure 2. Naturally, this break in the trend of GDP per capita is correlated with a fall in growth rates from 9% to 5%-6%. As we see in graph 3, which shows the average growth rates in 5-year windows, this change in trend is explained by a fall quite a bit. rapid growth rates in these economies. What is China's situation today? China's per capita income today is about 5,000 USD (10,000 USD per capita PPP). If we take 1985 as the effective start of reforms, China has been in transition for 25 years. With an average growth rate of 9%, population growth of 1.5% and real appreciation of 1.5%, China would reach per capita income (PPP) levels . around 19,000 USD in the second half of this decade, roughly 2018. As Figure 4 shows, it is surprising to see the similarity of the growth processes of Japan, South Korea, and China in equivalent instances of their transitions. . Obviously, a mechanical generalization of the experiences of Japan and Korea is not desirable. The situation of each country is different, and there are dimensions that are difficult to generalize. However, the economic forces that explain the convergence of Japan and Korea at growth rates close to 5% are very powerful. As Figure 5 shows, years of high growth in these economies coincide with periods of high savings, high investment, and declining consumption as a percentage. of GDP. As capital accumulates, its profitability begins to fall, discouraging investment and encouraging consumption. This process where the fall in the share of consumption is stabilizing d0 and partly reversed d0 coincides with a process of deepening in the financial market and a change in relative prices that encourages consumption. The reality of China today is surprising, and shows important similarities and in turn differences with. As Figure 6 shows, the savings rate in China is over 50 per cent of GDP, the investment rate is just under 50 per cent of GDP, and the consumption accounts for more than a third of GDP. The magnitude of these figures reveals two characteristics of the Chinese economy that are worth dwelling on. a) What explains the high savings and low level of consumption?, and 3 Young, A., 1995, d2The Tyranny of Numbers: Confronting the Statistical Realities of the East Asian Growth Experience,d3 Quarterly Journal of Economics (110). b) What explains the high rates of domestic investment, financed mainly by domestic savings? Much has been written and talked about high savings rates in China. 4 Already high at the beginning of the twenty-first century, in the last decade the savings rate in China has risen from about 35% to over 50%. This high savings rate is explained by high savings by households (20 %), companies ( 20%) and government (10%). It is possible to analyze each of these components separately. In the case of households, the explanations point to the shallow depth of social security programs. In the case of companies, the lack of deepening of the capital market and the weakness of corporate governance stand out, which limits the use of profits. to domestic savings and then re-investment. To be sure, there are also macroeconomic arguments for high savings rates . A high growth in the demand for money in a context of fixed exchange rate and closed capital account generates incentives for a decrease in the levels of domestic spending and increases in the trade balance. In turn, the policy of sterilizing exchange rate interventions limits the adjustment of relative prices that would tend to reverse d0 at least in part d0 trade surpluses in China. High savings rates are a source d0 the main source d0 of financing for fixed-asset investment in China. From that point of view, this could be seen as positive. However, this reflects at the same time consumption levels that are low, and therefore with repercussions on well-being. Over time, there are forces that will naturally drive a drop in savings rates . China's demographic transition is one of them; Greater exchange rate flexibility would also be. However, if rates of return in China are as high d0 as current investment rates suggest d0 incentives to save could remain at time, maintaining a strong momentum to growth. In other words, an investment rate in China close to 50% of GDP could be suggesting the presence of a very large push to the growth, which could divert China from the path followed by Japan and Korea. This leads us to analyze in greater detail a second characteristic of the Chinese economy. Why is the investment rate so high? , Does it effectively reflect such high rates of return? A closer look at investment in China suggests that one must be careful to reach this conclusion. There are several elements that justify this assertion. There are determinants of the savings rate that seem not to be directly related to the profitability that can be obtained from these funds. In the context of an economy with a closed capital account . and therefore in an economy where saving has limited alternative uses . Investment is a direct consequence of the high savings rate . To the extent that 4 Ver Yang, Zhang y Zhou, 2011, d2Why are Saving Rates so High in China?d3, NBER Working Paper 16771 That the causes of high savings rates are not altered, the Chinese economy currently has a great bias to investment independent of the rates of return of these. When one analyzes the profitability of the investment, signs of inefficiency appear. 5 Table 1 shows that a very large percentage of fixed asset investment in China is financed by retained earnings. In 2008, this figure reached 65%. This figure reflects a weakness of the financial system, which does not allow surplus companies to finance investment projects of other companies. To the extent that the investment is associated with those who save and not those who have the best projects, their profitability will be low. High savings and high investment are also a consequence of a financial system that does not adequately mediate funds. This is exactly what Figure 7 shows, which presents a crude measure of return on investment, understood as the amount of investment required to generate a GDP dollar . For example, an indicator of 5 shows that it takes to invest 5 to generate 1 of GDP. Of course, the 5 dollars are a stock that lasts over time (discounting its depreciation), while the GDP is the annual flow generated by the stock of Capital invested. Compared to South Korea and Japan at similar times in their growth period , investment in China is today more inefficient than in these other countries. It is remarkable to note also the natural upward trend in this ratio, thus reflecting the decline in investment returns as Capital becomes less scarce. Even with the evident availability of large projects in China , these elements suggest that no small part of the investment in China is made in profitable projects. Bounded. This reflects a low depth in the financial system, a banking system that is centralized and whose decisions do not necessarily obey risk/return criteria, and a Closed capital account in an economy with high savings rates. Why does this matter? Because the sacrifice of greater savings is not necessarily being made to obtain a high return on the funds invested. The evidence presented suggests that the permanence of this situation could be generating a liability to the state apparatus that is not sustainable to maintain over time. That is why not only is a transition expected and necessary in China towards an economy with higher levels of consumption and lower investment rates. This requires a number of important reforms d0 especially in its financial system d0 in order to facilitate better allocation of savings. This is the main challenge facing the Chinese economy going forward. High investment rates coupled with low rates of return are still giving a strong boost to 5 Ver Claro, S, 2006, d2Why does China Protect More its Labor.Intensive Industries?d3, Economics of Transition (14), y Claro, S, 2006, d2Supporting Inefficient Firms with Capital Subsidies: China and Germany in the 1990sd3, Journal of Comparative Economics (34), para un an87lisis detallado de la rentabilidad de las empresas en China. activity in China. But that will have to change in the coming years. Failure to do so puts the future stability of the financial system and fiscal accounts at risk. China's economic transition has been very successful so far, and there is no reason to think that this new challenge will not be adequately faced. Some considerations for developing countries I would not like to conclude without referring very briefly to the impact of China's development on third countries. There are many dimensions of interest, but I would like to emphasize one, which I consider central. China's economic transformation d0 regardless of how fast it takes forward d0 is producing a very significant shift in global demand for natural resources. Beyond the short-term swings in commodities, the trend towards an increase in the relative price of oil, copper and food partly reflects This new reality is important. (See figures 8 and 9.) This new reality is likely to be maintained for a reasonable time. The main implication of this is that for many years developing countries suffered from the abundance of good projects and the lack of financing. Reality today seems to be showing an abundance of funding. Apparently, the big challenge is to find the good projects. Two considerations in this process. First, there is always the temptation to think that these changes can be permanent. Although there are conditions to think that there is some profound change in the structure of the world economy, it is advisable to treat it as transitory, and therefore be very transitory, and therefore be very cautious in the management of these resources. Using the commodity boom to finance current consumption would be a great waste. It is essential to save and invest well in order to enable a sustainable change in development possibilities. Second, for a country like Chile, China's growth is highly beneficial. This is true not only because of the high price of copper, but because the forces that are pressing the mineral markets are the same ones that are pressing the food markets . China's growth implies a large food deficit in the world, and Chile has the natural conditions to take advantage of it.
