Title: Challenges of Financial Regulation in Chile
text: CHALLENGES OF FINANCIAL REGULATION IN CHILE* Rodrigo Vergara President Central Bank of Chile March 2013 Presentation made by the President of the Central Bank of Chile at the 1st Santander Public Policy Seminar "Capital Markets: New Rules New Game" held on March 21, 2013. My thanks to Gabriel Aparici and Kevin Cowan for their valuable contribution to this presentation. Good morning. I would like to take the opportunity given to me at this seminar to discuss what I believe are three fundamental lessons that we as central bankers have learned from the global financial crisis of 2008. At the same time, in the context of these lessons, I would like to tell you what the Central Bank of Chile has been doing in recent times in terms of financial stability, as well as what I think should be some priorities for the coming years in terms of financial regulation in our country. I think this kind of reflection is important, especially because there is a risk that we in Chile will be complacent, given the resilience of the local financial system to the events that culminated in the 2008 international crisis, and to our subsequent rapid economic recovery. There are lessons that one must assimilate, in order to avoid that in our system the type of vulnerabilities that have occurred in other parts of the world are generated. On the other hand, our high degree of financial integration means that our regulation is relatively aligned with international standards. This, however, does not imply adopting without further reflection, but rather adapting these standards to local realities and to a regulatory framework that has generally worked well. Let me start then by listing the 3 lessons I want to discuss with you today: 1) Risk-taking in the financial system varies over time, and interacts with economic and financial cycles. 2) Comprehensive monitoring of the financial system, and in particular of the interconnections of various agents with banks, is crucial. 3) Financial regulation should explicitly address the risks generated by systemic financial actors. Lesson 1: Risk-taking in the financial system varies over time, and interacts with economic and financial cycles. A very clear example of this phenomenon is related to the interactions that originated in several peripheral European countries between the granting of credit and economic activity. On the one hand, the growth of employment, wages and real estate values boosted the demand and supply of credit to households and companies. On the other hand, this credit gave a strong boost to aggregate demand, and thus to employment, wages and asset prices. In the boom phase, many of the traditional risk indicators of the system were stable or improved, until the financial shock from the US triggered the correction of activity and prices, leading to the fiscal and financial crisis through which several of these countries are still going through. Given the above, a broad discussion has been generated on the need to implement financial regulation that recognizes the interactions between activity, financial prices and risk-taking, and in particular in the expansionary phases of the cycle. The objective of this "macroprudential" regulation would be to compensate for risk-taking in expansionary phases, increasing the resilience of the financial system to negative shocks. While macroprudential regulation is theoretically attractive, its application as a common policy tool poses a number of challenges: a. Adequately identify the phases of the cycle in which this type of measures are implemented, avoiding the risks of advancing or delaying their application. Although some of the proposed regulations have automatic triggers, such as the provision regulations that have been introduced in Peru, in most cases implementing this type of regulation requires adequate monitoring of risks and a judgment on the timing and necessity of its application. A good example of this is the evolution of credit in developing economies, where it is very complex to separate "excessive" credit growth from a healthy process of financial deepening. Strictly speaking, this type of dilemma is present in the implementation of any countercyclical policy. b. Properly calibrate the effects of these measures. Although some countries have adopted such policies (e.g. Spain, Hong Kong, Brazil and China), the available history of their implementation is recent (post-2005 in most cases) and the literature seeking to determine the magnitude of their effects is still incipient.2 c. Resolve the convergence between macro and microprudential objectives. Even if the above problems are solved and the conclusion that it is necessary to modify a certain microprudential tool in order to mitigate risks to financial stability as a whole, it may happen that for certain financial intermediaries this has undesired costs. This is particularly true for "broad" macroprudential tools such as the countercyclical capital requirement in Basel II. d. Resolve the interactions between monetary policy and macroprudential regulation. As we have said in various documents and presentations3, the interest rate is often too thick an instrument for macroprudential objectives. e. And, finally, define an appropriate institutional design for its implementation. The challenge arises because it is necessary to coordinate central banks, which have experience and some relative advantages in monitoring aggregate risks of the financial system, with the actions of sectoral financial supervisors. 2 See box "International evidence of macroprudential policies linked to the real estate sector", Financial Stability Report June 2012. 3 For a discussion of the role of the monetary policy rate in the objectives of financial stability see Vergara (2012) "Macroeconomic and Financial Stability: Challenges for Monetary Policy", inaugural speech of the XVI Annual Conference of the Central Bank of Chile. 4 See Marshall 2012, "Implementation of Macroprudential Policies in Chile", Policy Papers Economic Na144. Given the above, in the short term I think it is convenient to perfect the more traditional way of dealing with systemic financial risks, which consists of incorporating these risks into the supervision and design of micro-prudential regulation. In this way, excessive risk-taking by some intermediaries can be corrected, and thus reduce the likelihood or cost of a subsequent correction. In Chile, in the past, the banking supervisor has expressed concern about issues with systemic implications on several occasions. For example, in the 90s, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions (SBIF) issued a regulation that required provisions for consumer loans based on their payment behavior throughout the banking system4. In the early 2000s, the SBIF instructed banks to carefully consider their clients' exchange rate mismatches in their risk assessments - and thus their provisioning policies. It should be noted that even this traditional way of addressing macro-financial risks requires a high level of coordination between the systemic risk monitor and the micro-prudential supervisor. This is the scheme that has been consolidated in Chile, with monitoring of systemic risks by the Central Bank, and coordination mechanisms between the Bank, financial supervisors and the Ministry of Finance. This coordination is embodied in cross-consultation mechanisms, in the recently created Financial Stability Board and through bilateral cooperation. What have we been doing at the Central Bank in recent years in the field of monitoring systemic risks and mitigating them? Good risk monitoring should assess the resilience of the financial system to stressful situations d1 falls in asset prices, higher unemployment or lower levels of disposable income, or closure of external financing. In this context, we are working on improving the banking stress exercises, which we shared with the SBIF and then published in the Financial Stability Report (FSI). As I mentioned before, in favorable cycles the indicators of financial intermediaries, companies and households tend to look healthy. It is therefore crucial to stress these financial indicators in the face of plausible risk scenarios. The improvements in these exercises are towards introducing interconnection mechanisms within banks both through cross-exposures on the balance sheet and through participation in common financial markets. For example, it is not the same to liquidate public papers in the face of an idiosyncratic shock (where you go out to sell alone) than to liquidate an asset in a generalized sale flre sale"}. Along the same lines, we have been working on liquidity stress test models d1 starting with the methodology developed as a result of Chile's 2011 Financial System Assessment Program (FSAP).5 5 Financial Sector Assessment Program conducted by the IMF and the World Bank. 6 See box "Potential effects of the bill on the processing of information on financial and economic obligations", Financial Stability Report December 2011. A second line of improvements aims to incorporate more realistic interactions between the financial sector and macroeconomics, both in the models used in stress tests and in the models used in monetary policy. The use of macroeconomic models that assume overly simple financial systems is a shortcoming widely recognized by economists and central bankers. On the other hand, we are making an important effort to generate data for the analysis of systemic financial risks. Since 2011 we have published accounts by institutional sector on a quarterly basis - which allows us and the market to better track consumer and investment financing sources, and household and corporate leverage levels. These statistics have also served as a basis for Chile's participation in the monitoring exercises of "non-bank financial intermediaries" carried out by the Financial Stability Board (FSB) annually. On the other hand, since 2007 we have raised the Household Financial Survey, which seeks to capture a broad set of information on the financial situation of households from different socioeconomic strata - complementing the information available in the Social Protection Survey and CASEN. The hopefully prompt approval of the bill of the System of Economic Obligations (SOE) should contribute in this direction6. On the other hand, in the IEF we have reported price indices for housing based on the universe of effective transactions of houses and apartments, which considerably improve the information available on prices in this sector. Finally, an important effort has been made at the level of all regulators, supervisors and the Ministry of Finance to strengthen coordination in pursuit of the analysis of systemic risks. This coordination, which is embodied in the sessions and working groups of the CEF, allows complementing the aggregate vision of the Central Bank with the sectoral analysis of each of the three financial superintendencies. And, more importantly, to provide the framework to coordinate decision-making in those cases in which risks to the financial system are detected, enhancing the "traditional" form of macro-financial regulation that I mentioned earlier. The submission of a bill validating this scheme should serve to consolidate the progress made in recent years. Parallel to the above, we have sought to strengthen our participation in global forums for the analysis and discussion of systemic financial risks, in the FSB vulnerability working group and as regional co-chair of the FSB Americas group. Before moving on to the second lesson of the global financial crisis, I would like to dwell on the issue of financial prices and the role of the Central Bank in monitoring them. As I mentioned just now, adequate systemic risk monitoring must consider the interactions between financial prices, macroeconomics and the financial sector. It is in this context that it becomes important to monitor certain key prices of the financial system, such as those of real estate. A misalignment of these prices with respect to their fundamentals can generate resource allocation problems, but the complex scenario arises when this misalignment coincides with an increase in the indebtedness of households, companies and financial intermediaries. Lesson 2: It is crucial that policymakers conduct comprehensive monitoring of the financial system, and in particular of the interconnections of various actors with banks. In part, the late reaction of regulators and supervisors in some developed countries to the gestation of vulnerabilities is due to a partial understanding of the financial system, excessively focused on banking. This partial understanding, which led to ignoring an important part of the financial system and its interconnections with banking, was based on two erroneous premises. First, that outside the center of the financial system, markets almost always operated efficiently. And second, that deviations from this behavior could be corrected ex post with expansionary policies (the so-called Greenspan put). A clear example of this omission was the scant monitoring of the process of securitization of mortgage loans in the United States, which occurred partly outside the traditional banking sector. Adequate monitoring of systemic financial risks requires expanding the perimeter traditionally viewed by central banks and supervisors. It is also necessary to understand the connections of this financial "periphery" with banking and other more regulated entities such as life insurance companies. Finally, the risks faced by these agents in the periphery must be understood and monitored, especially leveraged agents with term mismatches. We learned long ago that banks d0 also leveraged agents that transform liquidity d0 are vulnerable to changes in the perceived value of their assets or herd behavior of their sources of financing. This is the key to understanding the lender role of last resort of central banks, liquidity regulations and state deposit insurance. This monitoring is not trivial, partly because information is not always available in a timely manner, partly because of the speed with which financial markets develop. I must be clear on this matter. I am not suggesting that we should treat all financial actors as banks, but rather to be particularly careful when other agents begin to play an important role in the provision of financial services, or when interconnections with the core of the financial system become relevant. If such risks are detected, it is necessary to strengthen or adapt the regulation of agents outside the center of the financial system, and/or reduce the exposure of banks and insurance companies to these agents. There is an extensive international agenda that seeks to strengthen the functioning of certain markets and intermediaries that could become a risk for the banking sector or other intermediaries at the center of the financial system. In this way, it has been working in several international forums, as well as in specific countries, to reduce the vulnerability of monetary mutual funds to liquidity shocks, strengthen repo and securities lending markets by establishing adequate collateral standards, promoting self-regulation to avoid potential risks associated with some varieties of Exchange-traded Funds (ETFs). strengthening securitization mechanisms to avoid excessive risk-taking, and strengthening off-exchange, or OTC, derivatives markets. Several of these markets and intermediaries are relevant in Chile today, others are developing right now, some more likely to be in years to come. At the Central Bank we have been working on several initiatives in this context. First, in 2010 we had a process of technical discussion with the Superintendence of Securities and Insurance regarding the risks of the old scheme of valuation of monetary mutual funds in Chile at amortized historical cost. We believe that the move towards a market valuation scheme taken by the SVS was an important step in reducing the funding risks of banks as well as companies and households that save via mutual funds7. Our assessment is that this has been well assimilated by the market. 7 See box "New valuation standard for type 1 mutual funds", Financial Stability Report, December 2010. On the other hand, our concern regarding Exchange-traded Funds (ETFs) refers to the importance of incorporating global best practices into their design in Chile, particularly with regard to synthetic ETFs and securities lending associated with ETFs. In the case of the synthetic ETF, the concern is about the counterparty risk arising from the return swaps that are included in the ETF; In the case of securities loans, the concern is to have reasonable standards in the collateral that support these operations. We have also been working together with the SBIF on the new standard on non-bank credit cards. Given the mandate of the Central Bank, the main objective of the standard is to achieve security in the means of payment, which implies that the merchant is paid in a certain and timely manner, and that the holder of the medium has security of its acceptance in the affiliated businesses. We believe that the new regulations that were put into consultation, to the extent that they strengthen the requirements of capital, liquidity, risk management and specify the scope of the supervision of the SBIF, meets this objective. As a complement to the SBIF's direct oversight, the regulation strengthens the information requirements that issuers must provide to the public. This increased information, together with the increased information requirements that the SVS has already requested from those issuers that issue public instruments, strengthens the risk management tools of banks, life insurance companies and AFPs that lend or hold securities of issuers, increasing their resilience to possible problems in this sector. In terms of means of payment, I take this opportunity to reiterate what we have raised in the IEF, in terms of supporting the idea of expanding, with due regulation, the participation of non-banking entities in the issuance of retail pre-paid instruments. In the context of strengthening regulation in the face of "shocks" that could come from outside the Chilean financial system, it is also worth mentioning the regulations recently published by the SBIF, after consulting the Central Bank, on the limits of concentration of deposits abroad. Given the greater risk of external banking as a result of the vulnerabilities still present in the global financial system, it was important to close an existing asymmetry between the treatment of the concentration of credits and deposits abroad. Of course, generating robust OTC (over the counter) derivatives markets is also a priority. I will come back to this later. Lesson 3: Regulation must explicitly address the risks generated by systemic financial actors. The global financial crisis has shown that the existence of "too big to fail" financial actors leads to increased ex-ante risk-taking and costly ex-post bailouts. The reluctance of authorities in Europe and the United States to let down any relevant financial institution after the chaos generated by the bankruptcy of Lehman Brothers is the direct consequence of concerns about the systemic consequences of such a fall. This has led to an active global discussion on how to address too big to fail both through prudential financial regulation, limiting the size or complexity of the entity or increasing its resilience, and in better resolution mechanisms in case of being faced with financial problems. At the global level, the prudential agenda has advanced in two directions: directly limiting the size and interconnections of intermediaries through structural regulation (as in the Volcker rule in the US or in the Vickers Commission proposals in the United Kingdom) or through stricter regulatory and supervisory requirements for those entities defined as systemic (such as systemic capital defined in Basel III). In Chile there are already regulations in this area (at least for banks). The Superintendency of Banks (after consulting the Central Bank) has the power to limit mergers or require more capital from banking entities that have a significant market share after the merger. However, this rule is insufficient because it limits the SBIF's actions to mergers in Chile, ignoring both organic growth and mergers abroad. An additional limitation is that it limits the definition of systemic to market share, ignoring aspects such as interconnections with the rest of the system. Possibly the Superintendent is going to go into more detail on this issue, but I would like to advance a couple of ideas on an eventual reform of the General Banking Law. In Chile, we have a very good law. This has been proven in practice. In fact, it has several components that had been discarded in the Basel II standardsd1but have returned to being international standards in Basel IIId1as a reason for total leverage, and a low dependence on external rating agencies. However, there are aspects that do need to be refined to approach the new global standards. The level and definition of capital should be close to that of Basel III. Market risk should be incorporated into capital requirements. And by the way, capital surcharges for systemic entities must be improved in the direction I just mentioned. On the other hand, and understanding that this is a matter of competence of the Executive, I cannot fail to raise the convenience of this type of modification being made in an expansionary cycle, in order to avoid the complex dynamics that several countries face today as they are strengthening capital standards for banks in the middle of a recession. I would also like to mention that we are working in coordination with the SBIF on an analysis of liquidity regulations, assessing the need for changes in line with the Liquidity Coverage Ratio proposed in Basel III, but taking into account the particularities of our financial markets and the fact that (unlike many developed economies) we already have a quantitative liquidity standard. A second priority in the area of systemic entities is the development of better infrastructure to clear OTC derivatives. As we described in a recent policy paper, the derivatives market in Chile is exclusively OTC. This structure strongly and unnecessarily increases the degree of interconnectedness between the agents of the financial system, increasing the systemic impact of problems on any bank or other participating intermediary. In this context, the optimal solution would be for part of these operations to go to a market for derivatives traded on the exchange and cleared via a Central Counterparty (CCP8). In a CCP scheme, risk is mitigated through an appropriate collateral/collateral provision mechanism. On the other hand, stock market transactions would make price formation in this market more transparent. In the absence of this optimal solution, we see very favorably the development of alternative platforms that achieve the same safeguards in clearing and information issues for the market and supervisors, even if the transactions remain OTC. See box "OTC Derivatives Infrastructure in Chile", Financial Stability Report June 2012. A third priority in the area of systemic institutions is for the Committee of Superintendents to continue advancing with its work of monitoring financial conglomerates. Substantial progress has been made in this area over the past year. It should be noted that this monitoring does not correspond to a process of consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates, but to an intermediate step that allows the Superintendencies to improve their supervision and the Central Bank to have a map of entities that could eventually be systemic. On the other hand, and as long as there is no consolidated supervision of financial conglomerates in Chile, it is important that cross-exposures of institutions of the same group are limited. In this, we consider it key to continue advancing in reducing exposures to related agents in insurance companies, as proposed in the Bill that is under discussion in Congress. I would like to close with a couple of general reflections on the situation of the Chilean financial sector. As we put it in our Financial Stability Report for the second half of 2012, our overview of the financial system is positive. Household debt has continued to grow in line with their disposable income. Corporate debt, meanwhile, has grown somewhat above GDP, driven by the dynamism of local bank credit and external financing via bonds, but in a context of high investment dynamism. Meanwhile, banks maintain capital levels above regulatory levels, a more diversified external financing base and a stable liquidity position. Notwithstanding the above, on the one hand the financial and fiscal situation in Europe is far from normalizing. On the other hand, the risk-free interest rate in the major countries remains at historically low levels. In a context of abundant external financing, it is particularly important to be careful that financial vulnerabilities are not incubated, due to greater leverage of households, companies and financial intermediaries, and greater exchange rate and liquidity mismatches. It is also important to continue monitoring the evolution of key financial prices and their interaction with indebtedness in banks and other local financial agents. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Desafos de la regulacin financiera en Chile* Rodrigo Vergara Presidente Banco Central de Chile Marzo 2013 Presentacin efectuada por el Presidente del Banco Central de Chile en el 1er Seminario de Polticas Pblicas Santander Mercado de Capitales: Nuevas Reglas Nuevo Juego realizado el da 21 de marzo de 2013. Mis agradecimientos a Gabriel Aparici y Kevin Cowan por su valioso aporte a esta presentacin. Muy buenos das. Quisiera tomar la oportunidad que se me da en este seminario para discutir lo que me parece son tres lecciones fundamentales que como banqueros centrales hemos aprendido de la crisis financiera global de 2008. A su vez, en el contexto de estas lecciones, contarles lo que ha estado haciendo en el ltimo tiempo el Banco Central de Chile en materia de estabilidad financiera, as como lo que creo debiesen ser algunas prioridades para los prximos aos en materia de regulacin financiera en nuestro pas. Creo que este tipo de reflexin es importante, en especial porque existe el riesgo de que en Chile seamos autocomplacientes, dada la resiliencia del sistema financiero local a los eventos que culminaron en la crisis internacional de 2008, y a nuestra rpida recuperacin econmica posterior. Hay lecciones que uno debe asimilar, a modo de evitar que en nuestro sistema se generen el tipo de vulnerabilidades que se han dado en otras partes del mundo. Por otro lado, nuestro alto grado de integracin financiera obliga a que nuestra regulacin est relativamente alineada con los estndares internacionales. Esto, sin embargo, no implica adoptar sin mayor reflexin, sino ms bien adaptar dichos estndares a las realidades locales y a un marco de regulacin que en lo general ha funcionado bien. Djenme comenzar entonces por listar las 3 lecciones que quiero discutir con ustedes hoy:  La toma de riesgos en el sistema financiero vara en el tiempo, e interacta con los ciclos econmicos y financieros.  Es crucial un monitoreo amplio del sistema financiero, y en particular de las interconexiones de diversos agentes con la banca.  La regulacin financiera debe abordar explcitamente los riesgos que generan los agentes financieros sistmicos. Leccin 1: La toma de riesgos en el sistema financiero vara en el tiempo, e interacta con los ciclos econmicos y financieros. Un ejemplo muy claro de este fenmeno dice relacin con las interacciones que se originaron en varios pases de Europa perifrica entre el otorgamiento de crdito y la actividad econmica. Por un lado el crecimiento del empleo, salarios y los valores de los inmuebles impulsaron la demanda y oferta de crdito a hogares y empresas. Por otro, este crdito daba un fuerte impulso a la demanda agregada, y por tanto al empleo, salarios y precios de activos. En la fase de boom muchos de los indicadores tradicionales de riesgo del sistema se mostraron estables o mejoraron, hasta que el shock financiero proveniente de EEUU gatillo la correccin de la actividad y los precios, llevando a la crisis fiscal y financiera por la cual an estn pasando varios de estos pases Dado lo anterior se ha generado una amplia discusin sobre la necesidad de implementar regulacin financiera que reconozca las interacciones entre la actividad, los precios financieros y la toma de riesgos, y en particular en las fases expansivas del ciclo. El objetivo de esta regulacin macroprudencial sera de compensar la toma de riesgos en las fases expansivas, aumentando la resiliencia del sistema financiero a shocks negativos. Si bien la regulacin macro-prudencial es tericamente atractiva, su aplicacin como una herramienta de poltica habitual reviste una serie de desafos:  Identificar adecuadamente las fases del ciclo en las cuales se implementan este tipo de medidas, evitando los riesgos de adelantar o retrasar su aplicacin. Si bien algunas de las regulaciones propuestas tienen gatillos automticos, tales como la normativa de provisiones que se ha introducido en Per en la mayora de los casos implementar este tipo de normativa requiere de un adecuado monitoreo de los riesgos y un juicio sobre el momento y necesidad de su aplicacin. Un buen ejemplo de esto es la evolucin del crdito en economas en vas de desarrollo, donde es muy complejo separar un crecimiento excesivo del crdito de un sano proceso de profundizacin financiera. En rigor este tipo de dilema est presente en la implementacin de cualquier poltica contracclica.  Calibrar adecuadamente los efectos de estas medidas. Si bien algunos pases han adoptado este tipo de polticas (por ejemplo Espaa, Honk Kong, Brasil y China), la historia disponible sobre su aplicacin es reciente (posterior a 2005 en la mayora de los casos) y la literatura que busca determinar la magnitud de sus efectos es an incipiente  Resolver la convergencia entre objetivos macro y micro prudenciales. An solucionando los problemas anteriores y llegndose a la conclusin de que es necesario modificar una determinada herramienta microprudencial con el objetivo de atenuar riesgos para la estabilidad financiera en su conjunto, puede ocurrir que para determinados intermediarios financieros ello tenga costos no deseados. Esto es particularmente cierto en el caso de herramientas macroprudenciales amplias como el requerimiento de capital anticclico contemplado en Basilea II.  Resolver las interacciones entre poltica monetaria y regulacin macroprudencial. Tal como hemos dicho en diversos documentos y presentaciones, la tasa de inters es muchas veces un instrumento demasiado grueso para objetivos macroprudenciales.  Y, finalmente, definir un diseo institucional apropiado para su implementacin. El desafo surge pues se requiere coordinar a los bancos centrales, que tienen experiencia y algunas ventajas relativas en monitorear riesgos agregados del sistema financiero, con el accionar de los supervisores financieros sectoriales. Dado lo anterior, en el corto plazo creo conveniente perfeccionar la forma ms tradicional de hacer frente a riesgos financieros sistmicos, que consiste en la incorporacin de dichos riesgos en la supervisin y el diseo de regulacin micro-prudencial. De esta manera, se puede corregir la toma excesiva de riesgo por parte de algunos intermediarios, y reducir as la probabilidad o el costo de una correccin posterior. En Chile, en el pasado, el supervisor bancario ha expresado preocupacin por temas con alcances sistmicos en varias oportunidades. Por ejemplo en los aos 90, la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras (SBIF) dict una normativa que exiga constituir provisiones para los crditos de consumo en base a su comportamiento de pago en todo el sistema bancario. A principios de los aos 2000, la SBIF imparti instrucciones a los bancos para que sus evaluaciones de riesgo - y por consiguiente sus polticas de provisiones - considerasen cuidadosamente el descalce cambiario de sus clientes. Cabe destacar que incluso esta forma tradicional de abordar los riesgos macro-financieros, requiere de un alto nivel de coordinacin entre quien monitorea los riesgos sistmicos y el supervisor micro-prudencial. Este es el esquema que se ha ido consolidando en Chile, con un monitoreo de riesgos sistmicos por parte del Banco Central, y mecanismos de coordinacin entre el Banco, los supervisores financieros y el Ministerio de Hacienda. Esta coordinacin se materializa en mecanismos de consulta cruzada, en el recientemente creado Consejo de Estabilidad Financiera y mediante cooperacin bilateral. Que hemos estado haciendo en el Banco Central en los ltimos aos en el mbito de monitoreo de riesgos sistmicos y su mitigacin? Un buen monitoreo de riesgos debe evaluar la resiliencia del sistema financiero a situaciones de stress  de cadas en el precio de activos, de mayor desempleo o menores niveles de ingreso disponible, o de cierre de financiamiento externo. En este contexto estamos trabajando en mejorar los ejercicios de tensin de la banca, que compartimos con la SBIF y luego publicamos en el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera (IEF). Como mencion antes, en ciclos favorables los indicadores de intermediarios financieros, empresas y hogares tienden a verse saludables. Por ello es crucial tensionar dichos indicadores financieros ante escenarios de riesgo plausibles. Las mejoras en dichos ejercicios van hacia introducir mecanismos de interconexin al interior de la banca tanto por exposiciones cruzadas en el balance como por participacin en mercados financieros comunes. Por ejemplo, no es lo mismo liquidar papeles pblicos ante un shock idiosincrtico (donde se sale a vender solo) a liquidar un activo en una venta generalizada ^flre sale"}. En esta misma lnea hemos estado trabajando en modelos de stress test de liquidez  partiendo con la metodologa elaborada a raz del Financial System Assesment Program (FSAP) de Chile de 2011. Una segunda lnea de mejoras apunta a incorporar interacciones ms realistas entre el sector financiero y la macroeconoma, tanto en los modelos usados en los stress test como en los modelos usados en la poltica monetaria. El uso de modelos macroeconmicos que asumen sistemas financieros demasiado simples es una deficiencia ampliamente reconocida por economistas y banqueros centrales. Por otra parte, estamos haciendo un esfuerzo importante por generar datos para el anlisis de riesgos financieros sistmicos. Desde 2011 publicamos las cuentas por sector institucional en forma trimestral - lo que nos permite a nosotros y al mercado mejorar el seguimiento de las fuentes de financiamiento del consumo y la inversin, y de los niveles de apalancamiento de hogares y empresas. Estas estadsticas han servido, adems como base para la participacin de Chile en los ejercicios de monitoreo de "intermediarios financieros no bancarios realizado por el Financial Stability Board (FSB), anualmente. Por otra parte, desde el 2007 hemos levantado la Encuesta Financiera de Hogares, que busca capturar un conjunto amplio de informacin sobre la situacin financiera de hogares de distintos estratos socioeconmicos - complementando la informacin disponible en la Encuesta de Proteccin Social y la CASEN. La ojal pronta aprobacin del proyecto de ley del Sistema de Obligaciones Econmicas (SOE) debiese aportar en esta direccin. Por otra parte, en el IEF hemos reportado ndices de precios para la vivienda basados en el universo de transacciones efectivas de casas y departamentos, que mejoran considerablemente la informacin disponible en materia de precios en este sector. Finalmente, se ha hecho un esfuerzo importante a nivel de todos los reguladores, supervisores y el Ministerio de Hacienda de fortalecer la coordinacin en pos del anlisis de riesgos sistmicos. Esta coordinacin, que se materializa en las sesiones y grupos de trabajo del CEF, permite complementar la visin agregada del Banco Central con el anlisis sectorial de cada una de las tres superintendencias financieras. Y, lo que es ms importante, proveer el marco para coordinar la toma de decisiones en aquellos casos en que se detecten riesgos al sistema financiero, potenciando la forma tradicional de la regulacin macro financiera que mencion anteriormente. El envo de un proyecto de ley que valida este esquema debiese servir para consolidar los avances en aos recientes. Paralelo a lo anterior, hemos buscado fortalecer nuestra participacin en foros globales de anlisis y discusin de riesgos financieros sistmicos, en el grupo de trabajo de vulnerabilidades del FSB y como co-chair regional del grupo de las Amricas del FSB. Antes de pasar a la segunda leccin de la crisis financiera global quisiera detenerme en el tema de los precios financieros y el rol que le cabe al Banco Central en su monitoreo. Como mencion recin, un adecuado monitoreo de riesgo sistmico debe considerar las interacciones entre precios financieros, la macroeconoma y el sector financiero. Es en este contexto que se hace importante monitorear ciertos precios claves del sistema financiero, como los de los bienes inmobiliarios. Un desalineamiento de dichos precios respecto a sus fundamentales puede generar problemas de asignacin de recursos, pero el escenario complejo surge cuando este desalineamiento coindice con un aumento en el endeudamiento de hogares, empresas y los intermediarios financieros. Leccin nmero 2: Es crucial que las autoridades realicen un monitoreo amplio del sistema financiero, y en particular de las interconexiones de diversos agentes con la banca. En parte, la tarda reaccin de reguladores y supervisores en algunos pases desarrollados a la gestacin de vulnerabilidades se debe a una comprensin parcial del sistema financiero, excesivamente focalizada en la banca. Esta comprensin parcial, que llev a ignorar una parte importante del sistema financiero y de sus interconexiones con la banca, se basaba en dos premisas erradas. En primer lugar, que fuera del centro del sistema financiero los mercados operaban casi siempre en forma eficiente. Y segundo, que las desviaciones de este comportamiento podran corregirse ex post con polticas expansivas (el llamado Greenspan put). Un ejemplo claro de esta omisin fue el escaso monitoreo que se realiz del proceso de securitizacin de crditos hipotecarios en Estados Unidos, que ocurra en parte fuera del sector bancario tradicional. Un adecuado monitoreo de riesgos financieros sistmicos requiere ampliar el permetro que tradicionalmente miran los bancos centrales y supervisores. Se requiere, asimismo, entender las conexiones de esta "periferia financiera con la banca y los otros entes ms regulados como las compaas de seguro de vida. Por ltimo, se debe entender y monitorear los riesgos que enfrentan estos agentes en la periferia, en especial los agentes apalancados con descalces de plazo. Hace tiempo aprendimos que los bancos -tambin agentes apalancados que transforman liquidez son vulnerables a cambios en el valor percibido de sus activos o a comportamientos de manada de sus fuentes de financiamiento. Esta es la clave que lleva a entender el rol de prestamista de ltima instancia de los bancos centrales, las normativas de liquidez y los seguros de depsito estatales. Este monitoreo no es trivial, en parte porque la informacin no siempre est disponible en forma oportuna, en parte por la velocidad con la cual se desarrollan los mercados financieros. Debo ser claro en esta materia. No estoy sugiriendo que debamos tratar a todos los agentes financieros como bancos, sino ms bien de tener particular cuidado cuando otros agentes comienzan a jugar un rol importante en la provisin de servicios financieros, o cuando las interconexiones con el centro del sistema financiero se vuelven relevantes. Si se detectan dichos riesgos se hace necesario fortalecer o adecuar la regulacin de los agentes que estn fuera del centro del sistema financiero, y/o reducir la exposicin de los bancos y compaas de seguros a estos agentes. Hay una extensa agenda internacional que busca robustecer el funcionamiento de ciertos mercados e intermediarios que pudiesen llegar a ser un riesgo para el sector bancario u otros intermediarios al centro del sistema financiero. De esta manera se ha estado trabajando en varios foros internacionales, as como en pases especficos, en reducir la vulnerabilidad de los fondos mutuos monetarios a shocks de liquidez, fortalecer los mercados de repo y prstamos de valores estableciendo estndares adecuados de colateral, promoviendo la autorregulacin para evitar potenciales riesgos asociados a algunas variedades de Fondos Transados en Bolsa (ETF), robusteciendo los mecanismos de securitizacin para evitar una excesiva toma de riesgos, y robusteciendo los mercados de derivados transados fuera de bolsa, o OTC. Varios de estos mercados e intermediarios son relevantes en Chile hoy, otros se estn desarrollando en este momento, algunos ms probablemente lo sern en aos venideros. En el Banco Central hemos estado trabajando en varias iniciativas en este contexto. En primer lugar, el ao 2010 tuvimos un proceso de discusin tcnica con la Superintendencia de Valores y Seguros respecto a los riesgos del antiguo esquema de valorizacin de los fondos mutuos monetarios en Chile a costo histrico amortizado. Creemos que el avance hacia un esquema de valorizacin de mercado tomado por la SVS fue un paso importante en reducir los riesgos de fondeo de la banca as como de las empresas y hogares que ahorran va fondos mutuos. Nuestra apreciacin es que ello ha sido bien asimilado por el mercado. Por otra parte, nuestra preocupacin en cuanto a los Fondos Transados en Bolsa (ETFs por sus siglas en ingls) se refiere a la importancia de incorporar las mejores prcticas globales al diseo de stos en Chile, en particular en lo que concierne a ETFs sintticos y prstamos de valores asociados a los ETFs. En el caso del ETF sinttico, la preocupacin es por el riesgo de contraparte que surge por los swaps de retornos que se incluyen en el ETF; en el caso de los prstamos de valores la preocupacin es por tener estndares razonables en los colaterales que respaldan estas operaciones. Asimismo, hemos estado trabajando en conjunto con la SBIF en la nueva norma sobre tarjetas de crdito no bancarias. Dado el mandato del Banco Central, el principal objetivo de la norma es lograr seguridad en los medios de pago, lo que implica que al comercio se le pague en forma cierta y oportuna, y que el tenedor del medio tenga seguridad de su aceptacin en los comercios afiliados. Creemos que la nueva normativa que fue puesta en consulta, en la medida que fortalece los requisitos de capital, liquidez, gestin de riesgos y precisa el alcance de la supervisin de la SBIF, cumple con este objetivo. Como complemento a la supervisin directa de la SBIF, la normativa fortalece los requisitos de informacin que los emisores deben entregar al pblico. Esta mayor informacin, en conjunto con los mayores requisitos de informacin que la SVS ya ha solicitado de aquellos emisores que emiten instrumentos pblicos, fortalece las herramientas de gestin de riesgo de bancos, compaas de seguro de vida y AFPs que prestan o son tenedores de ttulos de los emisores, aumentando su resiliencia a eventuales problemas en este sector. En materia de medios de pago aprovecho la ocasin para reiterar lo que hemos planteado en el IEF, en cuanto a apoyar la idea de ampliar, con la debida regulacin, la participacin de entidades no bancarias en la emisin de instrumentos de pre-pago minoristas. En el contexto de fortalecer la regulacin ante "shocks que pudiesen venir de fuera del sistema financiero chileno, cabe destacar tambin la normativa que public recientemente la SBIF, previa consulta del Banco Central, sobre los lmites de concentracin de depsitos en el exterior. Dado el mayor riesgo de la banca externa como consecuencia de las vulnerabilidades an presentes en el sistema financiero global resultaba importante cerrar una asimetra existente entre el tratamiento de la concentracin de crditos y depsitos en el exterior. Por cierto que generar mercados de derivados OTC (over the counter) robustos tambin es una prioridad. Volver sobre este tema ms adelante. Leccin 3: la regulacin debe abordar explcitamente los riesgos que generan los agentes financieros sistmicos. La crisis financiera global ha mostrado que la existencia de agentes financieros "demasiados grandes para quebrar (en ingls, too big to fail) lleva a una mayor toma de riesgo ex ante y a costosos rescates ex post. La reticencia de las autoridades en Europa y Estados Unidos de dejar caer cualquier institucin financiera relevante luego del caos que gener la quiebra de Lehman Brothers es la consecuencia directa de la preocupacin por las consecuencias sistmicas de dicha cada. Esto ha llevado a una activa discusin global sobre cmo abordar el too big to fail tanto a travs de la regulacin financiera prudencial, limitando el tamao o complejidad del ente o aumentado su resiliencia, como en mejores mecanismos de resolucin en caso de verse enfrentado a problemas financieros. A nivel global la agenda prudencial ha avanzado en dos direcciones: limitando directamente el tamao e interconexiones de los intermediarios mediante regulacin estructural (como en la regla de Volcker en EE.UU. o en las propuestas de la comisin Vickers en el Reino Unido) o mediante requisitos regulatorios y de supervisin ms estrictos para aquellos entes definidos como sistmicos (tales como el capital sistmico que se define en Basilea III). En Chile ya existe normativa en este mbito (al menos para bancos). La Superintendencia de Bancos (previa consulta al Banco Central) tiene la facultad de limitar fusiones o exigir ms capital a entes bancarios que post fusin tengan una participacin de mercado significativa. Sin embargo esta norma es insuficiente porque limita el accionar de la SBIF a fusiones en Chile, ignorando tanto el crecimiento orgnico o las fusiones en el exterior. Una limitacin adicional es que acota la definicin de sistmico a participacin de mercado, ignorando aspectos como las interconexiones con el resto del sistema. Posiblemente el Superintendente va a entrar en ms detalle en este tema, pero quisiera adelantar un par de ideas sobre una eventual reforma a la Ley General de Bancos. En Chile, tenemos una muy buena ley. Ello se ha probado en la prctica. De hecho tiene varios componentes que haban sido descartados en los estndares de Basilea II pero que han vuelto a ser estndares internacionales en Basilea III  como una razn de apalancamiento total, y una baja dependencia de agencias clasificadoras externas. Sin embargo, hay aspectos que s deben perfeccionarse para acercarse a los nuevos estndares globales. El nivel y definicin de capital debe acercarse al de Basilea III. Debe incorporarse el riesgo de mercado en los requisitos de capital. Y por cierto, deben perfeccionarse los recargos de capital para entes sistmico en la direccin que les acabo de mencionar. Por otra parte, y entendiendo que esto es materia de competencia del Ejecutivo, no puedo dejar de plantear la conveniencia de que este tipo de modificaciones se haga en un ciclo expansivo, a modo de evitar la compleja dinmica que enfrentan hoy varios pases al estar robusteciendo estndares de capital para la banca en el medio de una recesin. Aprovecho tambin de mencionar que estamos trabajando en forma coordinada con la SBIF en un anlisis de la normativa de liquidez, evaluando la necesidad de introducir cambios en lnea con la Razn de Cobertura de Liquidez propuesta en Basilea III, pero teniendo en cuenta las particularidades de nuestros mercados financieros y el hecho de que (a diferencia de muchas economas desarrolladas) ya tenemos una norma de liquidez cuantitativa. Una segunda prioridad en el mbito de entes sistmicos est en el desarrollo de una mejor infraestructura para compensar derivados OTC. Tal como describimos en un reciente documento de poltica, el mercado de derivados en Chile es exclusivamente OTC. Esta estructura aumenta fuerte e innecesariamente el grado de interconexin entre los agentes del sistema financiero, incrementando el impacto sistmico de problemas en cualquier banco u otro intermediario partcipe. En este contexto la solucin ptima sera que parte de estas operaciones pase a un mercado de derivados transados en bolsa y compensados va una Entidad de Contraparte Central (ECC). En un esquema de ECC, el riesgo se mitiga a travs de un adecuado mecanismo de provisin de colaterales/garantas. Por otra parte, las transacciones en bolsa haran ms transparente la formacin de precios en este mercado. En ausencia de esta solucin ptima vemos en forma muy favorable el desarrollo de plataformas alternativas que logren los mismos resguardos en temas de compensacin y de informacin para el mercado y los supervisores, incluso si las transacciones siguen siendo OTC. Una tercera prioridad en el mbito de las instituciones sistmicas es que el Comit de Superintendentes siga avanzando con su labor de monitoreo de los conglomerados financieros. En el ltimo ao se han logrado avances sustanciales en esta rea. Cabe destacar que este monitoreo no corresponde a un proceso de supervisin consolidada de conglomerados financieros, sino a un paso intermedio que le permite a las Superintendencias mejorar su supervisin y al Banco Central tener un mapa de entes que pudiesen eventualmente ser sistmicos. Por otra parte, y mientras en Chile no exista supervisin consolidada de conglomerados financieros, es importante que las exposiciones cruzadas de instituciones del mismo grupo estn limitadas. En esto, consideramos clave seguir avanzando en reducir las exposiciones a agentes relacionadas en las compaas de seguros, tal como est planteado en el Proyecto de Ley que se encuentra en discusin en el Congreso. Quisiera cerrar con un par de reflexiones generales sobre la situacin del sector financiero chileno. Tal como lo planteamos en nuestro Informe de Estabilidad Financiera del segundo semestre de 2012, nuestra visin general del sistema financiero es positiva. La deuda de los hogares ha seguido creciendo en lnea con su ingreso disponible. Por su parte, la deuda de las empresas ha crecido algo por sobre el PIB, impulsada por el dinamismo del crdito bancario local y el financiamiento externo va bonos, pero en un contexto de alto dinamismo de la inversin. En tanto, la banca mantiene niveles de capital por sobre los niveles regulatorios, una base de financiamiento externo ms diversificada y una posicin de liquidez estable. No obstante lo anterior, por una parte la situacin financiera y fiscal en Europa est lejos de normalizarse. Por otra parte, la tasa de inters libre de riesgo en los principales pases sigue en niveles histricamente bajos. En un contexto de abundante financiamiento externo es particularmente relevante estar atento a que no se incuben vulnerabilidades financieras, debido a un mayor apalancamiento de hogares, empresas e intermediarios financieros, y a mayores descalces cambiarios y de liquidez. Tambin es importante seguir monitoreando la evolucin de precios financieros claves y su interaccin con el endeudamiento en bancos y otros agentes financieros locales. Muchas gracias.

Title: Launch of the community outreach program "Central in your Life"
text: CENTRAL LAUNCH IN YOUR LIFE SPEECH PRESIDENT RODRIGO VERGARA "The consolidation of the trends outlined in the last IPoM could require adjustments in the Monetary Policy Rate in the coming months. The Council closely monitors developments in the external and domestic macroeconomic scenario and its impact on inflation, and reaffirms its commitment to conduct monetary policy flexibly, so that projected inflation is 3% over the policy horizon." What I have read to you d0 and that probably very few understood d0 is the final paragraph of the statement issued by the Central Bank at the end of the last Monetary Policy Meeting. It is, by the way, a technical language, aimed at a specialized market. And it must be so to achieve our objective that inflation in Chile remains low and stable. Not that it disappears, but that it is not a headache for the inhabitants of the country, as if it was until a few decades ago. The dilemma of central banks is how to maintain this technical language and, at the same time, reach all economic agents: housewives, workers, students and small, medium and large entrepreneurs . The decisions taken by the Central Bank d0 certainly communicated with messages that seem to be written in another language d0 have an important effect on everyday life. The lowering, rising or maintaining the interest rate will have an impact on the cost of money or, in other words, on the rates of credits, both to companies and individuals, whether mortgage or consumer. And it will also have an impact on the different types of savings incentives. All Chileans are actors within a market, within an economy that for many people is complex and difficult to understand, which affects their quality of life and ultimately, the development of a quiet and prosperous family life. The role of the institution I preside over is directly related to people's quality of life. One of our main objectives is the challenge of maintaining price stability. But it is also a challenge for people to understand and internalize what is behind concepts such as saving, spending, investing, offering, demand for products and services, interest rates, employment, growth. Concepts often difficult to assimilate, but that have relevance when making personal decisions, because they affect the finances of each one of us. One way to solve the dilemma of central banks is to develop areas that foster the understanding of this complex language, through economic and financial education programs . The Central Bank of Chile has always made an effort to bring people closer to its work, through various initiatives such as its school competition, its guided tours or its recently inaugurated Numismatic Museum, which contains the largest and most important collection of coins and banknotes that exists in Chile. But we've always wanted to do more. Today we wanted to get out of the thick walls of the building in which the Central Bank of Chile operates. We have chosen a symbolic place such as the Baquedano Station of the Santiago Metro, the nerve center of this city and Chile, to launch a new program of outreach to the community, which we will call Central en tu Vida. This program brings together under one umbrella and a single brand all the actions it carries out and those that it plans to carry out in the future to satisfy the need of people to know more about the functioning of the economy and the financial system, to understand it better and make informed decisions. This will now include the school contest The Economy Closer, aimed at third and fourth year students from all over the country and which this year is in its ninth version. Information and education that is also part of this community outreach program . To mark its effort to connect with people, the Bank today showed a bus with the image of the Central in your Life program. A bus that during the next few weeks will be transporting students and members of community organizations from their place of work or study to the Bank building, where they can receive information in simple language about economics and finance, in a visit that will include the Numismatic Museum. In my capacity as President of the Central Bank and on behalf of the Council that I chair and all the officials of this institution who are committed to this challenge, it is an honor for me to launch this program, which is part of the many initiatives of economic and financial education that are being developed by various public and private organizations . We highly value this effort that is being made, embodied first in a Financial Education Board and then in the creation of a Technical Secretariat dedicated to the same subject. This is the best way to adapt to the needs that arise in the population as the country has a more developed economic framework and financial system . For the Central Bank, this is a milestone in its institutional history. And we wanted to take this step convinced that the future of the Chilean economy will be strongly linked to the knowledge that people have of its complexities, so that they can make their purchase, savings, spending or investment decisions in a responsible and informed way. We are an institution, public and autonomous and, therefore, we are fully aware of the role and responsibility assigned to us by Chilean society. We understand that this role and responsibility lies first of all in fulfilling the mandate assigned to us by Constitutional Organic Law. But we also want all Chileans to understand why we do what we do and to understand our economic institutions in greater depth . Understanding the economy is a central axis in the life of every person, because much of their daily decisions are related in some way to the evolution of economic events. It's hard, of course. Therefore, we hope that this program of outreach to the community that we have called Central in your Life, is another contribution so that citizens not only understand our work, but incorporate this type of information into their daily lives and, in that way, reach their own development and be part of the development of the country. We are proud of this new community outreach program and trust that it will contribute to the financial education of our population. I want to end by thanking all the officials of the Central Bank of Chile who worked tirelessly to make this project a reality, especially the Institutional Affairs Management, led by Claudia Varela, and the Communications Management, led by Luis Alvarez. I do not forget other areas of the Bank that were also directly involved in this project, such as Informatics and Monetary Policy Strategy and Communication. I must also mention the rest of the Council and the General Manager, who always gave his support to this project and enriched it with suggestions in its different stages. Thanks a lot

Title: Some Thoughts on Retail Payment Methods
text: SOME THOUGHTS ON RETAIL PAYMENT METHODS* Rodrigo Vergara President Central Bank of ChileApril 3, 2013* Presentation made by the President of the Central Bank of Chile at the International Seminar "The Modernization of Payment Methods in Chile" organized by Universidad Andr8es Bello on April 3, 2013. My thanks to Gabriel Aparici, Kevin Cowan and Pablo Furche for their valuable contribution to this presentation. I want to start by thanking the Faculty of Economics and Business of the Andr8es Bello University for inviting me to present some introductory words in this international seminar on the Modernization of Retail Payment Methods in Chile. Retail payment systems are originally linked directly to one of the fundamental functions of central banking: the issuance of money. In their initial stage of development they have a relatively simple structure, where the means of payment used is the money issued by the Central Bank and there are few interconnections between their users. Thus, in its simplest version, making a payment with cash does not require more interaction than that of those directly involved in the transaction. If the same transaction is paid using a check, it is required that there is at least one bank where to deposit or cash it. However, over time retail payment systems have become increasingly complex, with increases in the number of participants and interconnections between them, as well as in the type of instruments used. In line with this development, the degree and type of involvement of central banks - given their mandates and powers - has been changing, becoming more active, which is no longer limited only to the provision of cash or the safeguarding of bank current accounts. There are two characteristics that make an active involvement of regulatory authorities in retail means of payment particularly relevant. In the first place, even when the probability that retail means of payment, or the systems associated with them, can cause or transmit disruptions that severely impact other institutions of the financial system is low, it is clear that the problems that affect them can have an impact on a large number of users or associated businesses. In this way, although they are not necessarily systemic in the conventional view of the term, they can have massive and very important impacts, even in dimensions other than the strictly financial one. Secondly d1 and as this seminar today demonstrates d1 this is a particularly dynamic area in terms of technology, so follow-up and involvement in these developments is required. The support we have provided to this seminar and to the workshops on means of payment of the UNAB are a part of this involvement and follow-up. For these reasons, and as noted by the Bank for International Settlements (BIS), it is in the interest of central banks that retail payments be secure and efficient. By security we understand the adequate protection of both the holder of the means of payment - against malicious uses, the loss of resources that immobilized in the medium or the non-acceptance of the instrument - and that of the associated merchants that accept said means of payment. In the particular case of commerce, it seeks to ensure that it obtains payment for goods or services sold in a certain and timely manner. We believe that these principles apply to all means of payment - regardless of the platform that triggers the transaction - and that they are therefore applicable to the means that are being discussed here today, regardless of whether or not the participants are financial agents (in the traditional sense of the word). In the case of the Central Bank of Chile in particular, it is also important to remember that ensuring the normal functioning of internal and external payments is one of the two mandates entrusted to it by its Constitutional Organic Law. In Chile in recent times, retail means of payment, or the systems associated with them, have been present in the public discussion for different reasons, not all of them of positive connotation. On the one hand, events have occurred that can have a negative impact on the perception of public opinion regarding the reliability of means of payment, such as massive cloning of cards and everything that happened a couple of years ago with a non-bank issuer of credit cards. More positive are the efforts made by the Government with the constitution of an intergovernmental working group dedicated to financial inclusion, which we hope can make an effective contribution to the development of institutions in this area, as well as to even greater access of the population to retail payment instruments. In our opinion, although various figures show that the possession and use of these instruments seem to be consistent with the level of development of the country, the analysis by economic stratum shows that there are relevant differences between them. In fact, we think that in Chile the most relevant margin of efficiency for retail payment methods is to provide valuable services at a reasonable price to lower-income segments of the population. In this sense, we believe that the recent announcement by the Executive to send a legal initiative that allows non-banking entities to issue prepaid cards subject to regulation and supervision according to the risks involved, as well as encouraging the payment of social benefits through electronic means, are initiatives that should collaborate for a greater development of retail payments. As mentioned by the IEF, initiatives of this type can be a relevant boost for financial inclusion and competition in payment methods. Finally, the role of the private sector in bringing to the domestic market more modern instruments or technologies that should strengthen the security of the system, such as cards that will now incorporate a chip instead of the magnetic stripe, should be highlighted. We hope that other initiatives or innovations can do something similar with the efficiency of the system. However, even though regulation may change and the supply of instruments increases, it is essential that these innovations are adequately adopted by all consumers in order to have a modern retail payment system. In this sense, one of the results of the Central Bank's Household Financial Survey, which should particularly draw the attention of the participants of this seminar, is that lack of knowledge and distrust in the system are the most mentioned reasons as obstacles to a more massive adoption of Internet banking services. Overcoming these obstacles requires decisive action on both financial education and consumer protection. While the importance of each of these issues alone far exceeds that of the use of means of payment, it is very important to keep them in mind in this discussion. On the other hand, I would like to reiterate what we pointed out in the last Financial Stability Report. For the Central Bank of Chile it is in the interest that the development and innovation in retail means of payment are not inhibited for regulatory reasons. However, when advancing in this area, we must not lose sight of the importance of safeguarding other public goods as important or more important, such as the trust and public faith of the people who use the means of payment available to them. Depending on how innovations relate to the normal functioning of the payment system, this may require prudential regulation and supervisory issues. To conclude this brief introduction, I would like to reiterate my gratitude to UNAB for the development of this initiative, which brings together participants from Chile and abroad, both from the public and private sectors. In a particularly dynamic area such as retail payments, which is somehow reflected in the heterogeneity of the public and the entities that will exhibit during the morning, instances like this are valuable because they allow to know first-hand the concerns and concerns of all those involved. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Algunas Reflexiones Sobre los Medios de Pagos Minoristas* Rodrigo Vergara Presidente Banco Central de Chile 3 de abril de 2013* Presentacin efectuada por el Presidente del Banco Central de Chile en el Seminario Internacional La Modernizacin de los medios de Pago en Chile organizado por la Universidad Andrs Bello el da 3 de abril de 2013. Mis agradecimientos a Gabriel Aparici, Kevin Cowan y Pablo Furche por su valioso aporte a esta presentacin. Quiero partir agradeciendo a la Facultad de Economa y Negocios de la Universidad Andrs Bello el haberme invitado para exponer unas palabras introductoria en este seminario internacional sobre la Modernizacin de los Medios de Pago Minoristas en Chile. Los sistemas de pago minoristas se vinculan en su origen directamente con una de las funciones fundamentales de la banca central: la emisin de dinero. En su etapa inicial de desarrollo poseen una estructura relativamente simple, donde el medio de pago que se utiliza es el dinero emitido por el Banco Central y existen pocas interconexiones entre sus usuarios. As, en su versin ms simple, la realizacin de un pago con dinero en efectivo no requiere ms interaccin que la de quienes participan directamente en la transaccin. Si la misma transaccin se paga utilizando un cheque, se requiere que al menos exista un banco donde depositarlo o cobrarlo por efectivo. Sin embargo, a travs del tiempo los sistemas de pago minoristas se han hecho cada vez ms complejos, con aumentos en el nmero de participantes y de interconexiones entre ellos, as como en el tipo de instrumentos utilizados. En lnea con este desarrollo, el grado y tipo de involucramiento de los bancos centrales - habida cuenta de sus mandatos y atribuciones  ha ido cambiando, pasando a tener un rol ms activo, el que ya no se limita slo a la provisin del efectivo o el resguardo de las cuentas corrientes bancarias Hay dos caractersticas que hacen particularmente relevante un involucramiento activo de las autoridades regulatorias en los medios de pago minoristas. En primer lugar, an cuando es baja la probabilidad de que los medios de pago minoristas, o los sistemas asociados a los mismos, puedan provocar o transmitir disrupciones que impacten de manera severa a otras instituciones del sistema financiero, es claro que los problemas que los afecten pueden tener un impacto en un amplio nmero de usuarios o comercios asociados. De esta manera, si bien no necesariamente son sistmicos en la visin convencional del trmino, s pueden tener impactos masivos y de gran importancia, incluso en dimensiones distintas de la estrictamente financiera. En segundo lugar y como bien lo demuestra este seminario hoy este es un mbito particularmente dinmico en trminos tecnolgicos, por lo que se requiere un seguimiento e involucramiento en dichos desarrollos. El apoyo que hemos brindado a este seminario y a los talleres sobre medios de pago de la UNAB son una parte de este involucramiento y seguimiento. Por las razones expuestas, y tal como seala el Banco Internacional de Pagos (BIS, por su sigla en ingls), es de inters para los bancos centrales que los pagos minoristas sean seguros y eficientes. Por seguridad entendemos el resguardo adecuado tanto del tenedor del medio de pago - frente a usos maliciosos, la prdida de los recursos que inmoviliz en el medio o la no aceptacin del instrumento - como el de los comercios asociados que aceptan dicho medio de pago. En el caso particular del comercio, se busca resguardar que obtenga el pago de los bienes o servicios vendidos en forma cierta y oportuna. Creemos que estos principios se aplican a todos los medios de pago - independiente de la plataforma que gatilla la transaccin - y que por tanto son aplicables a los medios que se estn discutiendo hoy aqu, con independencia de si los partcipes son o no agentes financieros (en el sentido tradicional de la palabra). En el caso del Banco Central de Chile en particular, es importante recordar adems que velar por el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos es uno de los dos mandatos que su Ley Orgnica Constitucional le encomienda. En Chile en el ltimo tiempo los medios de pago minoristas, o los sistemas asociados a ellos, han estado presentes en la discusin pblica por distintos motivos, no todos de connotacin positiva. Por una parte, han ocurrido eventos que pueden incidir negativamente en la percepcin de la opinin pblica respecto de la confiabilidad de los medios de pago, como es el caso de clonaciones masivas de tarjetas y de todo lo sucedido hace un par de aos con un emisor no bancario de tarjetas de crdito. Ms positivos son los esfuerzos realizados por el Gobierno con la constitucin de un grupo de trabajo intergubemamental dedicado a la inclusin financiera, el que esperamos pueda hacer una contribucin efectiva para el desarrollo de una institucionalidad en la materia, as como para un acceso an mayor de la poblacin a los instrumentos de pago minorista. A nuestro entender, an cuando diversas cifras muestran que la tenencia y uso de estos instrumentos parecieran ser coherentes con el nivel de desarrollo del pas, el anlisis por estrato econmico muestra que existen diferencias relevantes entre ellos. De hecho, pensamos que en Chile el margen de eficiencia ms relevante para los medios de pago minorista est en proveer servicios valiosos a un precio razonable a los segmentos de la poblacin de menores ingresos. En este sentido, estimamos que el reciente anuncio del Ejecutivo de enviar una iniciativa legal que permita que entidades no bancarias puedan emitir tarjetas de prepago sujetas a una regulacin y supervisin acorde a los riesgos involucrados, as como el incentivar el pago de beneficios sociales a travs de medios electrnicos, son iniciativas que deberan colaborar para un mayor desarrollo de los pagos minoristas. Tal como menciona el IEF, iniciativas de este tipo pueden ser un impulso relevante para la inclusin financiera y la competencia en los medios de pago. Por ltimo, se debe destacar el rol del sector privado en acercar al mercado domstico instrumentos o tecnologas ms modernas que debieran fortalecer la seguridad del sistema, como las tarjetas que ahora incorporarn un chip en vez de la banda magntica. Esperamos que otras iniciativas o innovaciones puedan hacer algo similar con la eficiencia del sistema. No obstante lo anterior, an cuando la regulacin puede cambiar y la oferta de instrumentos aumentar, para contar con sistema de pago minoristas moderno es fundamental que estas innovaciones sean adoptadas en forma adecuada por todos los consumidores. En este sentido, uno de los resultados de la Encuesta Financiera de Hogares del Banco Central, que debiera llamar particularmente la atencin de los participantes de este seminario, es que la falta de conocimientos y la desconfianza en el sistema son las razones ms mencionadas como obstculos para una adopcin ms masiva de los servicios de banca por internet. Superar esos obstculos requiere una accin decidida tanto en materia de educacin financiera como de proteccin al consumidor. Si bien la importancia de cada uno de esos temas por s solos excede largamente la del uso de medios de pago, es muy importante tenerlos presente en esta discusin. Por otra parte, quisiera reiterar lo que sealamos en el ltimo Informe de Estabilidad Financiera. Para el Banco Central de Chile es de inters que el desarrollo y la innovacin en los medios de pago minoristas no sean inhibidos por motivos regulatorios. Sin embargo, al avanzar en esta materia no se debe perder de vista la importancia de resguardar otros bienes pblicos tanto o ms importantes como son la confianza y la fe pblica de las personas que utilizan los medios de pago de los cuales disponen. Dependiendo de cmo las innovaciones se relacionen con el normal funcionamiento del sistema de pagos, lo anterior puede requerir dictar regulacin prudencial y resolver temas de supervisin. Para concluir esta breve introduccin, quiero reiterar el agradecimiento a la UNAB por el desarrollo de esta iniciativa que rene en un mismo foro a participantes de Chile y del exterior, tanto del sector pblico como del sector privado. En un rea especialmente dinmica como los pagos minoristas, lo que de alguna manera est reflejado en la heterogeneidad del pblico y de las entidades que expondrn durante la maana, instancias como esta son valorables pues permiten conocer de primera mano las preocupaciones e inquietudes de todos los involucrados. Muchas gracias.
