Title: A brief review of the history of the Central Bank of Chile
text: A BRIEF REVIEW OF THE HISTORY OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE* Rodrigo Vergara President Central Bank of ChileOctober 24, 2014 Opening speech of the Central Bank Conference, "The Role of Central Banks in the New Times". I thank Enrique Orellana for his valuable comments. Good morning, I warmly welcome you to this Conference in which we celebrate the 25 years of autonomy of the Central Bank of Chile. In recent years, central banks around the world have been taking a greater role in society. Although they always had a relevant role, in recent times this role has become increasingly visible to the general public. The greater recognition of the actions of central banks has gone hand in hand with inflation that has moderated and stabilized in a large part of economies, the significant role that these institutions played in mitigating the effects of the financial crisis of 2008 and 2009 and, of course, the attitude of central banks that have become increasingly transparent and have understood the importance of understanding and dissemination of their actions has in the formation of expectations and the good final result of their decisions. In the case of the Central Bank of Chile, which I have the honour of chairing, this growing transparency and communication has also been accompanied by the obligations imposed on us by the correct use of the autonomy that society has granted us. We have been given the ability to influence our decisions in a meaningful way in the daily lives of all Chileans, and we must be extremely responsible. Today, the Chilean economy has a macroeconomic policy scheme within which the Central Bank plays a key role. On the one hand, with a monetary policy based on medium-term inflation targets that has been successful. Added to this is a policy of exchange rate flexibility, which has allowed us to give the necessary space for the economy to make the adjustments it requires naturally and without limiting the actions of monetary policy. This is accompanied by a serious and responsible fiscal policy, based on a structural rule that has been a commitment of the various governments. Also of an adequate supervision and financial regulation and of an economy whose commercial and financial opening to the world is very significant. Beyond the deviations that inflation has had from the 3 per cent target that we have defined, inflation has averaged 3.1 per cent if we consider the period from the full introduction of this system in 2001 to the present day. These results are diametrically different from those observed in past decades. Let me do some history. The Central Bank of Chile was founded in August 1925, with the mission of "providing the country with an institution that stabilizes the currency and regulates interest rates and discounts, to avoid disturbances in the industrial and financial development of the Nation and promote its economic progress", as established in Decree Law number 486 that gave it life. At first, the objective of its creation was to solve an old concern of the Republic, which was to provide an adequate amount of circulating and that would allow the normal development of the national economy1. */ Corbo and Hern87ndez (2005). The first years of the Central Bank's life were relatively quiet, however the beginning of the Great Depression in 1929 gave way to a period of sharp contraction. economic in which the country and its population suffered significant consequences. The years immediately following provided some relief, but incubated the problems that would haunt the national economy for several decades. Mainly, a fiscal and monetary institutionality that was not able to separate, together with a financial system whose capacity to grant credit was very limited and forced the Central Bank to take a role in that area that went far beyond what we would consider reasonable today. All this led to an endemic inflationary problem being installed in Chile from the forties. The high social cost that inflation caused implied that its control was a significant issue in the different governments that were installed in the country from that time. In all of them, macroeconomic programs aimed at their control and stabilization were designed with different mechanisms. Price controls, wage controls or different schemes for determining the exchange rate emerged. All of them, for various reasons, failed. Perhaps the fundamental reason was the lack of a political agreement that would isolate monetary issuance from fiscal financing. Either because the Treasury did not have the capacity to generate its own resources that would allow it to avoid resorting to the issue, or because the Central Bank was a source of credit for sectors that the financial market did not serve. In the early seventies, the inflationary problem became much greater, perhaps because the economy became more closed or because macro and microeconomic imbalances worsened, along with a fiscal policy that became much more expansionary. Thus, by 1973 inflation reached its historical record level: 508 percent per year, with figures that remained in triple digits for quite some time, thanks to the oil shock of that time. In the second half of the seventies, inflation began a process of sustained reduction, hand in hand with the strong changes in the macroeconomic structure imposed by the Government. The economy was opened to foreign trade, price and wage controls were eliminated, and the financial market was liberalized, among several measures. More importantly, the fiscal situation improved significantly, even reaching surpluses in the second part of the seventies. Along with this, a nominal anchor was established in the economy, through, first, a controlled devaluation of the nominal exchange rate and, then, with its fixing in 1979. Although this scheme managed to reduce inflation significantly and the annual increase in the CPI fell to single digits between late 1981 and mid-1982, it also incubated serious imbalances. These culminated in a strong exchange rate arrears, over-indebtedness, high risks in the financial system d0 the product of weak supervision and regulation d0 and a very high current account deficit. The sudden increase in interest rates in the United States caused the outbreak of a major economic crisis in Latin America, known as the external debt crisis, with very significant costs in terms of output and employment. Chile was no exception and this not only resulted in an economic crisis of proportions, but also implied the bankruptcy of a significant part of the financial system and the default of external debt, which, by the way, fed back the economic crisis. In the following years, the Central Bank fulfilled functions mainly aimed at overcoming this crisis, especially with regard to the rescue of the financial system. Although the economy suffered a significant loss of output, inflation rose again and remained at rates between 10 and 35 percent for the remainder of the eighties. This, in an environment in which fiscal deficits were reduced and turned into surpluses, the economy resumed higher growth rates and normalized its situation of international payments. A significant part of this improvement in macroeconomic performance, at least in terms of growth and the resolution of the most immediate problems, occurred from the establishment of a macroeconomic scheme that aimed to avoid repeating the mistakes of the past. In the first place, providing the Treasury with an institutionality that would allow it to develop a serious and responsible fiscal policy without having to resort to financing via issuance. Second, with a growing commercial and, in the following decade, financial openness. Third, with the development of a new scheme of regulation and supervision of the financial system that would avoid the incubation of the distortions that led to the banking crisis of the eighties. However, inflation remained at levels above those considered desirable. Thus, at the end of the eighties, the establishment of an autonomous Central Bank began to be discussed, whose clear mission was the control of inflation. Although the 1980 Constitution had established this autonomous Central Bank, until 1989 no steps had been taken in that direction, partly because the urgencies of the time pointed towards other areas. As the first President of the autonomous Central Bank describes very well in a document published a few years ago2, the idea of giving autonomy to the Central Bank was not easy to realize. The transition from an authoritarian to a democratic regime, and the latter's natural fears about the enclaves of power that the outgoing government could leave, provoked arduous discussion and significant doubts about the viability of this decision. In fact, although the impact that an autonomous Central Bank could have on the control of inflation was assessed, doubts about the democratic nature of its origin were a factor that put at risk the future viability of this decision. 2/ Bianchi (2008). However, in October 1989 Law 18,840 was published, which would give life to the autonomous Central Bank from December of that same year. The challenges posed by this new institutionality were diverse and significant. First, to establish a Council of technical quality, but at the same time sufficiently representative of the different political positions, which at the moment diverged markedly from each other. Second, once established, develop effective coordination mechanisms between the Government and the Bank. Third, to reduce inflation that had remained high for several years and increased again in the early nineties. Undoubtedly, the commitment and human and professional capacity of the members of the first Council allowed the work within the Bank to flow in a very good way and to put aside the initial fears. Also the country vision of the economic team of the new Government, which allowed to establish bridges of understanding and coordination that developed in a very good way and has never represented a problem to develop the work of the Bank. The new Law of the Central Bank of Chile imposed two objectives: the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. The first was obvious, and involved in practice reducing inflation to levels comparable to developed economies. The second, whose textual interpretation was originally relatively narrow and only referred to the payment system, has been expanded to incorporate elements of financial stability. It should be remembered that in Chile banking supervision is outside the Central Bank, although the Institution has regulatory powers over the financial system in various areas. Thus, the Board of the new Central Bank decided, from 1990, to approach the reduction of inflation as a gradual and sustained process, setting inflation targets for December of each year. Thus, inflation fell from levels close to 30 per cent per annum in 1990 to around 3 per cent in 2000. This, hand in hand with a monetary policy whose orientation was, unambiguously, aimed at controlling inflation. The nineties represented for the Chilean economy a period of prosperity, with high growth, economic development, poverty reduction, and inflation that was declining. The final years of that decade, however, were high. The Asian crisis strongly impacted the national economy, and put the Central Bank under stress. The strong turbulence in the international financial markets and the questioning of emerging economies called into question monetary policy and exchange rate policy. Beginning in 1999, once inflation had reached levels considered close to those desirable over the medium term, the Bank made a new shift in its policies. A medium-term inflation targeting scheme was adopted with all its ingredients that would be effective from 2001 onwards and the free floating of the exchange rate was decreed. Of course, keeping the possibility of intervening in the exchange market if necessary, which has been used on rare and exceptional occasions. The establishment of the medium-term inflation targeting scheme considered a target of 3 percent over a two-year horizon, with a tolerance range of one percentage point above and below this figure. It also brought with it an increasing process of transparency and openness about the Bank's work. The Monthly Monetary Policy Meetings were established in 1999, the publication of the Monetary Policy Report (MPR) began in May 2000 and there was an increasing flow of information to the general public3. 3/ For a description and analysis of the progress of the Central Bank of Chile in terms of information and transparency, see Vergara (2014). Prior to that, the Central Bank, as indicated in its Law, presented once a year a report to the Minister of Finance and the Senate of the Republic, which was done in September. The current IPoM, in addition to being presented in September, is presented in March, June and December. The Law also provides for the publication of the Annual Report in April of each year. Today, in addition to the quarterly Monetary Policy Report and the Annual Report, the Bank presents another series of reports, highlighting the Financial Stability Report (FSI) which, since 2004, is published in June and December of each year. Over the years, the Bank's delivery of information to the general public has increased and diversified, building a website where a significant diversity of background information can now be found, with a gap that has been reduced to the minimum possible. The Bank has also developed a growing community outreach program at all levels. I highlight the development of the contest "The Economy Close", which is aimed at school students to better understand the Bank's work. Thus, we have reached our days. With inflation that, as I mentioned at the beginning, has averaged 3.1 percent over the last thirteen years and volatility that has decreased. It is also very significant that inflation is no longer a constant concern for the general public. Several years ago, when public opinion polls asked about people's top concerns, inflation always appeared among the top ones. That is not the case today. The control of inflation has also implied unprecedented processes for this Central Bank. In the past, our country had to change its monetary unit repeatedly as a result of the loss of value imposed by high inflation. Thus, we went from pesos to escudos in 1960 and from escudos to pesos in 1975. All changes in that the old monetary unit was equivalent to a minimum fraction of the new. In recent years, for the first time in our history, the Bank carried out a change of the family of banknotes without a change of the monetary unit or an economic crisis behind it. Thus, between 2009 and 2011 the Bank designed and put into circulation a complete renovation of banknotes, adopting modern technologies and designs. The development of the autonomous Central Bank has also implied a major change in the organizational structure and competencies of those who work at the Bank today. The current organizational chart, functions and dependencies have little to do with what was there in 1990. The number of civil servants has been significantly reduced and professionalized. We have adopted best market practices and have moved closer to the standards held by central banks in the world's major economies. The road has not been without problems, but the dedication and professionalism of the Bank's members has allowed us to move forward and improve every day. The 18 professionals who have made up the Council from 1990 to date have left an important legacy. To all of them, and to the officials who accompanied them, our greatest thanks and recognition for the Bank they have forged. Thanks a lot References Bianchi, A. 2008. The Autonomy of the Central Bank of Chile: Origin and Legitimation. Economic Policy Papers, 26. Corbo V. and L. Hern87ndez. 2005. Eighty Years of History of the Central Bank of Chile. Working Papers Central Bank of Chile, 345. Vergara R. 2014. Transparency Regime and its Relationship with the Constitutional Autonomy of the Central Bank of Chile. In Transparency in Chile, Achievements and Challenges Five Years of Validity of the Law. J. E. Cheyre and N. Cobo editors.
text_original: Un Breve Repaso a la Historia del Banco Central de Chile* Rodrigo Vergara Presidente Banco Central de Chile 24 de octubre de 2014 ^Discurso de apertura de la Conferencia del Banco Central, El Rol de los Bancos Centrales en los Nuevos Tiempos. Agradezco a Enrique Orellana por sus valiosos comentarios. Buenos das, les doy una cordial bienvenida a esta Conferencia en que celebramos los 25 aos de autonoma del Banco Central de Chile. En los ltimos aos los bancos centrales alrededor del mundo han ido tomando un mayor rol en la sociedad. Aunque siempre tuvieron un rol relevante, en el ltimo tiempo este papel se ha vuelto crecientemente ms visible para el pblico en general. El mayor reconocimiento del accionar de los bancos centrales ha ido de la mano de una inflacin que se ha moderado y estabilizado en gran parte de las economas, del significativo rol que estas instituciones cumplieron en mitigar los efectos de la crisis financiera de 2008 y 2009 y, por supuesto, de la propia actitud de los bancos centrales que se han vuelto cada vez ms transparentes y han entendido la importancia que la comprensin y difusin de sus acciones tiene en la formacin de expectativas y el buen resultado final de sus decisiones. En el caso del Banco Central de Chile, que tengo el honor de presidir, esta creciente transparencia y comunicacin ha estado acompaada tambin de las obligaciones que nos impone el correcto uso de la autonoma que la sociedad nos ha otorgado. Se nos ha dado la capacidad de influir con nuestras decisiones de forma significativa en la vida diaria de todos los chilenos, y debemos ser extremadamente responsables. Hoy, la economa chilena cuenta con un esquema de polticas macroeconmicas dentro del cual el Banco Central juega un rol clave. Por un lado, con una poltica monetaria basada en metas de inflacin de mediano plazo que ha sido exitosa. Se suma una poltica de flexibilidad cambiara, que nos ha permitido dar el espacio necesario para que la economa realice los ajustes que requiere de forma natural y sin que ello limite el accionar de la poltica monetaria. Esto se acompaa de una poltica fiscal seria y responsable, basada en una regla estructural que ha sido un compromiso de los distintos gobiernos. Tambin de una adecuada supervisin y regulacin financiera y de una economa cuya apertura comercial y financiera al mundo es muy significativa. Ms all de las desviaciones que la inflacin ha tenido respecto de la meta de 3 por ciento que nos hemos definido, la inflacin ha promediado 3,1 por ciento si consideramos el perodo que va desde la plena instauracin de este sistema en 2001 a nuestros das. Estos resultados son diametralmente distintos de los que se observaron en dcadas pasadas. Permtanme hacer algo de historia. El Banco Central de Chile fue fundando en agosto de 1925, con la misin de dotar al pas de una institucin que estabilice la moneda y regule las tasas de intereses y descuentos, para evitar perturbaciones en el desenvolvimiento industrial y financiero de la Nacin y fomentar su progreso econmico, como se estableci en el Decreto de Ley nmero 486 que le dio vida. En un principio, el objetivo de su creacin fue resolver una vieja preocupacin de la Repblica, que era proveer de una cantidad de circulante adecuada y que permitira el normal desenvolvimiento de la economa nacional/. Los primeros aos de vida del Banco Central fueron relativamente tranquilos, sin embargo el comienzo de la Gran Depresin en 1929 dio pas a un perodo de fuerte contraccin econmica en que el pas y su poblacin sufri consecuencias significativas. Los aos inmediatamente posteriores dieron algo de alivio, pero incubaron los problemas que perseguiran a la economa nacional por varias dcadas. Principalmente, una institucionalidad fiscal y monetaria que no era capaz de separarse, junto con un sistema financiero cuya capacidad de otorgar crdito era muy reducida y obligaba al Banco Central a tomar un papel en ese mbito que iba bastante ms all de lo que hoy consideraramos razonable. Todo esto llev a que a partir de la dcada de los cuarenta se instalara en Chile un problema inflacionario endmico. El alto costo social que la inflacin provocaba implic que su control fuera un tema significativo en los distintos gobiernos que se instalaron en el pas a partir de esa poca. En todos ellos, se disearon programas macroeconmicos que apuntaban a su control y estabilizacin con distintos mecanismos. Surgieron los controles de precios, de salarios o distintos esquemas de determinacin del tipo de cambio. Todos ellos, por diversas razones, fracasaron. Tal vez la razn fundamental fue la falta de un acuerdo poltico que aislara la emisin monetaria del financiamiento fiscal. Ya fuera porque el Fisco no tena la capacidad de generar recursos propios que le permitieran evitar acudir a la emisin, o porque el Banco Central era una fuente de crdito para sectores que el mercado financiero no atenda. A comienzos de los setenta, el problema inflacionario se hizo mucho mayor, tal vez porque la economa se hizo ms cerrada o porque los desequilibrios macro y microeconmicos se agudizaron, junto con una poltica fiscal que se hizo mucho ms expansiva. As, para 1973 la inflacin lleg a su nivel rcord histrico: 508 por ciento anual, con cifras que se mantuvieron en tres dgitos por bastante tiempo, merced al shock petrolero de esa poca. En la segunda mitad de los setenta, la inflacin comenz un proceso de sostenida reduccin, de la mano de los fuertes cambios en la estructura macroeconmica que impuso el Gobierno. Se abri la economa al comercio exterior, se eliminaron controles de precios y salarios, y se liberaliz el mercado financiero, entre varias medidas. Ms importante, se mejor de forma significativa la situacin fiscal, llegando incluso a supervits en la segunda parte de los setenta. Junto con esto, se instaur un ancla nominal en la economa, a travs, primero, de una devaluacin controlada del tipo de cambio nominal y, luego, con su fijacin en 1979. Si bien este esquema logr reducir la inflacin de forma significativa y el incremento anual del IPC se redujo a cifras de un dgito entre fines de 1981 y mediados de 1982, tambin incub graves desequilibrios. Estos, culminaron en un fuerte atraso cambiario, un sobre endeudamiento, elevados riesgos en el sistema financiero producto de una dbil supervisin y regulacin y un altsimo dficit de la cuenta corriente. El sbito aumento de las tasas de inters en Estados Unidos, provoc el estallido de una crisis econmica de grandes dimensiones en Amrica Latina, conocida como la crisis de la deuda externa, con costos muy relevantes en trminos de producto y empleo. Chile no fue la excepcin y ello no solo se tradujo en una crisis econmica de proporciones, sino tambin implic la quiebra de un parte significativa del sistema financiero y la cesacin de pagos de la deuda externa, lo que, por cierto, retroaliment la crisis econmica. En los aos posteriores, el Banco Central cumpli funciones principalmente orientadas a la superacin de esta crisis, especialmente respecto del rescate del sistema financiero. Aunque la economa sufri una significativa prdida de producto, la inflacin volvi a aumentar y se mantuvo en tasas entre 10 y 35 por ciento por todo lo que quedaba de la dcada de los ochenta. Esto, en un ambiente en que los dficits fiscales se redujeron y convirtieron en supervits, la economa retom tasas de crecimiento mayores y fue normalizando su situacin de pagos internacionales. Parte significativa de esta mejora en el desempeo macroeconmico, al menos en lo que a crecimiento y la resolucin de los problemas ms inmediatos se refiere, se dio a partir del establecimiento de un esquema macroeconmico que apuntaba a no volver a cometer los errores del pasado. En primer lugar, dotando al Fisco de una institucionalidad que le permitira desarrollar una poltica fiscal seria y responsable sin tener que acudir al financiamiento va la emisin. Segundo, con una creciente apertura comercial y, en la dcada siguiente, financiera. Tercero, con el desarrollo de un nuevo esquema de regulacin y supervisin del sistema financiero que evitara la incubacin de las distorsiones que llevaron a la crisis bancaria de los ochenta. Sin embargo, la inflacin segua en niveles por sobre los que se consideraban deseables. As, a fines de los ochenta, se comenz a discutir la instauracin de un Banco Central autnomo, que tuviera como misin clara el control de la inflacin. Si bien la Constitucin de 1980 haba establecido este Banco Central autnomo, hasta 1989 no se haba dado ningn paso en esa direccin, en parte porque las urgencias del momento apuntaban hacia otros mbitos. Como muy bien lo describe el primer Presidente del Banco Central autnomo en un documento publicado hace unos aos/, la idea de darle autonoma al Banco Central no fue fcil de concretar. El paso de un rgimen autoritario a uno democrtico, y los naturales temores de este ltimo sobre los enclaves de poder que podra dejar el Gobierno saliente, provocaron una ardua discusin y dudas significativas sobre la viabilidad de esta decisin. De hecho, aunque se valoraba el impacto que un Banco Central autnomo podra tener en el control de la inflacin, las dudas sobre lo democrtico de su origen eran un factor que pona en riesgo la viabilidad futura de esta decisin. Con todo, en octubre de 1989 se public la Ley 18.840 que dara vida al Banco Central autnomo a partir de diciembre de ese mismo ao. Los desafos que esta nueva institucionalidad planteaba eran diversos y significativos. Primero, establecer un Consejo de calidad tcnica, pero que a la vez fuera lo suficientemente representativo de las distintas posiciones polticas, que dado el momento divergan notablemente entre s. Segundo, una vez establecido, desarrollar mecanismos de coordinacin efectivos entre el Gobierno y el Banco. Tercero, lograr reducir una inflacin que se haba mantenido por varios aos en cifras altas y volva a aumentar a comienzos de los noventa. Sin duda que el compromiso y capacidad humana y profesional de los integrantes del primer Consejo, permiti que el trabajo al interior del Banco fluyera de muy buena forma y se dejaran de lado los temores iniciales. Tambin la visin de pas del equipo econmico del nuevo Gobierno, que permiti establecer puentes de entendimiento y una coordinacin que se desarroll de muy buena forma y nunca ha representado un problema para desarrollar el trabajo del Banco. La nueva Ley del Banco Central de Chile le impona dos objetivos: la estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y extemos. El primero era evidente, e implicaba en la prctica reducir la inflacin a niveles comparables con las economas desarrolladas. El segundo, cuya interpretacin textual fue en su origen relativamente estrecha y solo referida al sistema de pagos, se ha ido ampliando para incorporar elementos de estabilidad financiera. Se debe recordar que en Chile la supervisin bancaria est fuera del Banco Central, aunque la Institucin tiene facultades regulatorias sobre el sistema financiero en diversos mbitos. As entonces, el Consejo del nuevo Banco Central decidi, a partir de 1990, abordar la reduccin de la inflacin como un proceso gradual y sostenido, estableciendo objetivos de inflacin para diciembre de cada ao. De este modo, la inflacin baj desde niveles cercanos a 30 por ciento anual en 1990 a valores en torno a 3 por ciento en 2000. Esto, de la mano de una poltica monetaria cuya orientacin estaba, sin ambigedades, dirigida al control de la inflacin. La dcada de los noventa represent para la economa chilena un perodo de bonanza, con alto crecimiento, desarrollo econmico, reduccin de la pobreza, y una inflacin que iba en descenso. Los aos finales de esa dcada, sin embargo, fueron lgidos. La crisis asitica impact con fuerza a la economa nacional, y puso bajo tensin al Banco Central. Las fuertes turbulencias en los mercados financieros internacionales y el cuestionamiento sobre las economas emergentes, coloc en entredicho la poltica monetaria y la poltica cambiara. A partir de 1999, una vez que la inflacin ya haba llegado a niveles que se consideraban cercanos a los deseables en el mediano plazo, el Banco dio un nuevo giro a sus polticas. Se adopt un esquema de metas de inflacin de mediano plazo con todos sus ingredientes que se hara efectivo desde 2001 en adelante y se decret la libre flotacin del tipo de cambio. Por supuesto, guardando la posibilidad de intervenir en el mercado cambiario de ser necesario, lo que ha sido utilizado en contadas y excepcionales ocasiones. La instauracin del esquema de metas de inflacin de mediano plazo consider una meta de 3 por ciento en un horizonte de dos aos, con un rango de tolerancia de un punto porcentual por sobre y por debajo de esta cifra. Tambin llev consigo un creciente proceso de transparencia y apertura sobre el trabajo del Banco. Se establecieron las Reuniones Mensuales de Poltica Monetaria en 1999, se comenz a publicar el Informe de Poltica Monetaria (IPoM) en mayo de 2000 y se dio un creciente flujo de informacin al pblico en general/. Previo a eso el Banco Central, tal como lo indica su Ley, presentaba una vez al ao un Informe al Ministro de Hacienda y al Senado de la Repblica, lo que se realizaba en septiembre. El IPoM actual, adems de presentarse en septiembre, se presenta en marzo, junio y diciembre. La Ley establece asimismo la publicacin de la Memoria Anual en abril de cada ao. Hoy, adems del Informe de Poltica Monetaria con periodicidad trimestral y de la Memoria Anual, el Banco presenta otra serie de reportes, destacando el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera (IEF) que, a partir de 2004, se publica en junio y diciembre de cada ao. El paso de los aos ha aumentado y diversificado la entrega de informacin que el Banco realiza al pblico general, construyendo una pgina web en la que hoy puede hallarse una diversidad significativa de antecedentes, con un desfase que ha ido reducindose a lo mnimo posible. El Banco tambin ha desarrollado un creciente programa de acercamiento a la comunidad en todos sus niveles. Destaco el desarrollo del concurso La Economa + Cerca, que est dirigido para que alumnos de colegios comprendan de mejor manera el quehacer del Banco. As, hemos llegado a nuestros das. Con una inflacin que, como mencion en un comienzo, ha promediado 3,1 por ciento en los ltimos trece aos y una volatilidad que ha disminuido. Muy significativo es tambin que la inflacin ha dejado de ser una preocupacin constante para el pblico general. Hace varios aos, cuando las encuestas de opinin pblica consultaban sobre las principales preocupaciones de las personas, la inflacin siempre apareca dentro de las principales. Hoy no es as. El control de la inflacin tambin ha implicado procesos inditos para este Banco Central. En el pasado, nuestro pas debi cambiar su unidad monetaria en reiteradas ocasiones producto de la prdida de valor que impona la elevada inflacin. As, pasamos de pesos a escudos en 1960 y de escudos a pesos en 1975. Todos cambios en que la antigua unidad monetaria equivala a una fraccin mnima de la nueva. En los ltimos aos, por primera vez en nuestra historia, el Banco llev a cabo un cambio de la familia de billetes sin que detrs estuviera un cambio de la unidad monetaria o una crisis econmica. As, entre 2009 y 2011 el Banco dise y puso en circulacin una completa renovacin de los billetes, adoptando tecnologas y diseos modernos. El desarrollo del Banco Central autnomo tambin ha implicado un cambio importante en la estructura organizacional y las competencias de quienes trabajan hoy en el Banco. El organigrama, funciones y dependencias actuales poco tienen que ver con lo que haba en 1990. La planta de funcionarios se ha reducido y profesionalizado de modo significativo. Hemos adoptado las mejores prcticas de mercado y nos hemos acercado a los estndares que mantiene la banca central en las principales economas del mundo. El camino no ha estado exento de problemas, pero la dedicacin y profesionalismo de los integrantes del Banco ha permitido salir adelante y mejorar cada da. Los 18 profesionales que han integrado el Consejo desde 1990 a la fecha han dejado un legado importante. A todos ellos, y a los funcionarios que les acompaaron, nuestros mayores agradecimientos y reconocimiento por el Banco que han forjado. Muchas gracias Referencias Bianchi, A. 2008. Title: Award speech of the contest "Economy + close"
text: SPEECH PRESIDENT AWARD CEREMONY 2014 - ECONOMY NEAR Dear friends, It was in this same place when ten years ago, under the Presidency of Don Vittorio Corbo, and with the impulse of the Counselor, Mrs. Mar92a Elena Ovalle, this beloved school contest called "Economy close" was born. It has been ten years in which around 30 thousand students from all over Chile have participated in this contest, with about 3 thousand 500 works prepared by students belonging to 2 thousand 200 educational establishments throughout the country. This contest is one of the cornerstones of a community outreach program, called Central en tu Vida, which at the same time is part of the growing efforts being made in Chile to develop financial education policies. The purpose is to provide the population with simpler learning tools that are closer to people, so that they can learn in easy terms the main topics of the economy that are related to their daily lives. What we want is to be a contribution to improve their quality of life, as far as possible and with this grain of sand. It has been ten years of competition, ten years of massive participation and ten years of enthusiastic and voluntary contribution of authorities and experts who have become part of the process of selecting works in the various stages that end in the election of the finalists and winners. There is a first stage in which Bank economists volunteer to make a preliminary process of selection of the jobs that arrive. They are proofreaders who dedicate several hours of their lives to a work that magnifies them for becoming part of one of the public roles of this institution. The final phase has always had a Jury made up of outstanding professionals, including authorities of successive governments, deans of university schools of economics and experts in education, and the winning professor of the previous version, who make the final selection that allows to have winning works of high quality. We will always be deeply grateful to each of them, because both proofreaders and juries are a relevant part of the success of this contest. With a spirit of avant-garde and renewal, we decided as a Bank to take advantage of this important milestone of the contest that celebrates ten years of history and introduced several novelties. As many of you know, until last year, the competition consisted of groups of third and fourth year students having to submit a written work on some topics related to the role of the Central Bank. The three finalist groups presented their work during a morning before the jury in the Council Chamber, a jury that then met to determine the first, second and third place. But we wanted to broaden participation, taking charge of the deep partnership that already exists in the new generations between learning and technology. In this line, one of the main innovations was to ask students to send us short videos instead of written work, using any device to record them and any audiovisual technique, in which they addressed the importance of dealing with inflation. In addition, we decided to extend the call to ALL secondary education, from First to Fourth year in order to improve our reach in young schoolchildren. And to make a differentiation between them, we created two categories of participants: one of first and second year and another, of third and fourth year. We could not be happier with the response to this initiative. We managed to strengthen participation in relation to previous years, receiving registration 581 groups composed of 1,638 students and 381 teachers, all of them belonging to 275 schools located in 127 communes from Arica to Punta Arenas. At the time of the closing of the participation of the contest, which we launched at the beginning of May and that we closed in mid-August, 323 videos were received, made by 252 groups of the Third to Fourth middle year category, and by 71 groups of the First to Second Middle year category, all belonging to a universe of 168 educational establishments throughout Chile. There was a hard promotion work behind it. For several months we worked on the design and distribution of various graphic pieces that were sent to almost 3,000 educational establishments in Chile and that were in various stations of the Santiago Metro. We visited schools where we had the opportunity to talk to them about the theme of the Contest: What is inflation and why is it important to keep it low and stable? and encourage them to participate. The first of these visits, where the 2014 version of this Contest was inaugurated, was carried out by the President of the Bank and the others by economists who actively participate in this Community Outreach Program, reaching more than a thousand students in the Metropolitan Region. Dozens of teachers from educational establishments throughout the country have arrived at the Bank, who for a day receive training on the functioning of the Chilean economy and the role of the Central Bank. They are days that are also transmitted to regions via streaming and allow at the same time, to deliver greater knowledge of specific topics to teachers and encourage them to participate in this contest. These ten years have been of development and consolidation of a school contest to which we have great affection, because it allows us to be close to students and teachers, who are undoubtedly the best allies to promote significant changes in people's lives around financial education. But also, these ten years are the beginning of a new life cycle in the contest, where we will speak in the audiovisual language of the new generations of students of all secondary education, to project and increase the scope of this contest towards the future and with it, bring the economy closer and closer to people, in a simple and entertaining way. That is our desire. I would like to thank the finalists for this year, for whom I ask for a loud applause... (APPLAUSE FROM THE AUDIENCE) These 6 teachers and 17 students visit us from different locations in the country. Some came from Copiap97, others from Concepci97n, others from Chillan, others from La Serena and others from our capital. Their ages range from 15 to 18 years and have shown high-flying creativity. In a few more minutes, when we see their finalist videos, you will realize that they made enormous efforts to explain in 3 minutes and in a simple way the theme of this year's contest: What is inflation and why is it important to keep it low and stable? Thank you for participating in this contest, and I hope you will become protagonists in your communities and localities to spread this contest, but beyond, to spread the importance of financial education. I would like to conclude by thanking in a special way this year's Jury, composed of the Minister of Education, Nicol87s Eyzaguirre; the Minister of Finance, Alberto Arenas; Superintendent of Banks and Financial Institutions Eric Parrado; the Dean of the Faculty of Economics and Business of the University of Chile, Manuel Agos92n; the Executive Director of the Education2020 Foundation, Mirentxu Anaya; the winning teacher of the contest "Economy close" of the year 2013, Carolina Ponce; the Director of the Bank, Pablo Garc92a and who speaks to them. Without their help and enthusiasm to collaborate, we would not have been able to be here today. I would also like to give special thanks to the Bank's official economists who enthusiastically and voluntarily made the preliminary selection of this year's papers. Every year we feel that this ceremony shows in a special way our effort to reach out to the community. But it's part of a much larger work. The Central Bank's "Central en tu vida" program has a special website with abundant content on economic issues in easily accessible language, on various platforms such as mini plays and virtual classes, educational videos and Carlos Massad's book, Economy for All. But this program also includes guided tours of the Bank, which include the Numismatic Museum and talks by specialists from the Bank. Today we have a Youtube channel, where the audiovisual content of the institution is; a twitter account and, recently, a Smartphone application with a Statistical Database. We enter fully into the 21st century. We always try to be close to the frontier of international best practices and we are concerned to always go as far as possible in the development of tools and solutions that allow us to better comply with our main mandates. We are deeply committed to the challenge of promoting financial education, a challenge we share with several public institutions and non-governmental organizations. We are also deeply committed to the need for a National Financial Education Strategy and we want initiatives such as those of this school contest to be replicated throughout Chile. A financially educated country is a country that can go much further in the development of its financial system and that is a notorious contribution to global economic development and, consequently, to the well-being of its inhabitants. Thank you all for joining us in these ten years of the School Contest The Closest Economy; Thank you for helping us in the reception and review of these creative works; for helping us organize the logistics of the contest, and for keeping alive this spirit that keeps us young and close to Chileans, in touch with their realities, and close to their needs. I invite you to enjoy this ceremony, to watch the finalist videos and to be part of an always exciting award. Thanks a lot
text_original: DISCURSO PRESIDENTE CEREMONIA PREMIACIN 2014 - ECONOMA + CERCA Estimados amigos y amigas: Fue en este mismo lugar cuando hace diez aos atrs, bajo la Presidencia de don Vittorio Corbo, y con el impulso de la Consejera, seora Mara Elena Ovalle, naci este querido concurso escolar llamado Economa + cerca. Han sido diez aos en que alrededor 30 mil alumnos de todo Chile han participado en este certamen, con cerca de 3 mil 500 trabajos elaborados por estudiantes pertenecientes a 2 mil 200 establecimientos educacionales de todo el pas. Este concurso es una de las piedras angulares de un programa de acercamiento a la comunidad, llamado Central en tu Vida, que a la vez es parte de los esfuerzos crecientes que se estn realizando en Chile por desarrollar polticas de educacin financiera. Lo que queremos es ser un aporte en mejorar su calidad de vida, en la medida de lo posible y con este grano de arena. Hay una primera etapa en que economistas del Banco se ofrecen como voluntarios para hacer un proceso preliminar de seleccin de los trabajos que llegan. Son correctores que dedican varias horas de sus vidas a una labor que los engrandece por hacerse parte de uno de los roles pblicos de esta institucin. La fase final ha contado siempre con un Jurado que integran destacados profesionales, entre autoridades de sucesivos gobiernos, decanos de escuelas universitarias de economa y expertos en educacin, y el profesor ganador de la versin anterior, quienes hacen la seleccin final que permite contar con trabajos ganadores de alta calidad. Siempre estaremos profundamente agradecidos de cada uno de ellos, porque tanto correctores como jurados son parte relevante del xito de este concurso. Con un espritu de vanguardia y renovacin, decidimos como Banco aprovechar este importante hito del concurso que cumple diez aos de historia e introdujimos varias novedades. Como muchos de ustedes saben, hasta el ao pasado, el concurso consista en que grupos de alumnos de tercero y cuarto ao medio deban enviar un trabajo escrito sobre algunos temas relacionados con el rol del Banco Central. Los tres grupos finalistas exponan sus trabajos durante una maana ante el jurado en la Sala de Consejo, jurado que luego se reuna para determinar el primer, segundo y tercer lugar. Pero quisimos ampliar la participacin, hacindonos cargo de la profunda asociacin que ya existe en las nuevas generaciones entre aprendizaje y tecnologa. En esa lnea, una de las principales innovaciones fue pedir a los alumnos que en lugar de trabajos escritos nos enviaran videos breves, usando cualquier aparato para grabarlos y cualquier tcnica audiovisual, en que abordaran la importancia de hacer frente a la inflacin. No podemos estar ms contentos con la respuesta a esta iniciativa. Logramos fortalecer la participacin en relacin a los aos anteriores, recibiendo la inscripcin 581 grupos compuestos por 1.638 alumnos y 381 profesores, todos ellos pertenecientes a 275 colegios ubicados en 127 comunas desde Arica a Punta Arenas. Al momento del cierre de la participacin del concurso, que lanzamos a principios de mayo y que cerramos a mediados de agosto, se recibieron 323 videos, realizados por 252 grupos de la categora Tercero a Cuarto ao medio, y por 71 grupos de la categora Primero a Segundo ao medio, todos pertenecientes a un universo de 168 establecimientos educacionales de todo Chile. Hubo detrs de ello un duro trabajo de promocin. Durante varios meses se trabaj en el diseo y distribucin de diversas piezas grficas que fueron enviadas a casi 3.000 establecimientos educacionales de Chile y que estuvieron en diversas estaciones del Metro de Santiago. Se visit colegios donde tuvimos oportunidad de hablarles sobre el tema del Concurso: Qu es la inflacin y por qu es importante mantenerla baja y estable? e incentivarlos a participar. La primera de estas visitas, donde se dio por inaugurada la versin 2014 de este Concurso, fue realizada por el Presidente del Banco y las otras por economistas que participan activamente en este Programa de acercamiento a la comunidad, logrando llegar a ms de mil alumnos de la Regin Metropolitana. Hasta el Banco han llegado decenas de profesores de establecimientos educacionales de todo el pas, quienes durante un da reciben una capacitacin sobre el funcionamiento de la economa chilena y el rol que le compete al Banco Central. Son jornadas que adems se transmiten a regiones va streaming y permiten al mismo tiempo, entregar mayores conocimientos de temas especficos a los maestros e incentivarlos para participar en este concurso. Estos diez aos han sido de desarrollo y consolidacin de un certamen escolar al que le tenemos un gran cario, pues nos permite estar cerca de los estudiantes y de los profesores, quienes son sin duda,los mejores aliados para impulsar cambios significativos en la vida de las personas en torno a la educacin financieraLa OCDE as lo ha dicho de forma reiterada. Pero tambin, estos diez aos son el comienzo de un nuevo ciclo de vida en el concurso, en donde hablaremos en el idioma audiovisual de las nuevas generaciones de alumnos de toda la enseanza media, para proyectar e incrementar el alcance de este concurso hacia el futuro y con l, acercar la economa cada vez ms a las personas, de forma simple y entretenida. Ese es nuestro anhelo. Quisiera agradecer la presencia de los finalistas de este ao, para quienes pido un fuerte aplauso... (APLAUSOS DEL PBLICO) Estos 6 profesores y 17 alumnos nos visitan desde diversas localidades del pas. Algunos llegaron desde Copiap, otros desde Concepcin, otros desde Chillan, otros desde La Serena y otros desde nuestra capital. Sus edades van de los 15 a los 18 aos y han mostrado una creatividad de alto vuelo. En algunos minutos ms, cuando veamos sus videos finalistas, se darn cuenta que hicieron enormes esfuerzos por explicar en 3 minutos y de forma simple la temtica de este ao del concurso: Qu es la inflacin y por qu es importante mantenerla baja y estable? Gracias a ustedes por participar en este concurso, y espero que se conviertan en actores protagonistas en sus comunidades y localidades para difundir este concurso, pero ms all, para difundir la importancia de la educacin financiera. Quisiera terminar agradeciendo de forma especial al Jurado de este ao, compuesto por el Ministro de Educacin, Nicols Eyzaguirre; el Ministro de Hacienda, Alberto Arenas; el Superintendente de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras Eric Parrado; el Decano de la Facultad de Economa y Negocios de la Universidad de Chile, Manuel Agosn; la Directora Ejecutiva de la Fundacin Educacin2020, Mirentxu Anaya; la profesora ganadora del concurso Economa + cerca del ao 2013, Carolina Ponce; el Consejero del Banco, Pablo Garca y quien les habla. Sin su ayuda y sin su entusiasmo para colaborar no habramos podido estar aqu hoy presentes. Tambin quiero dar un agradecimiento especial a los economistas funcionarios del Banco que de manera entusiasta y voluntaria hicieron la seleccin preliminar de trabajos de este ao. Cada ao sentimos que esta ceremonia muestra de manera especial nuestro esfuerzo de acercamiento a la comunidad. Pero es parte de un trabajo mucho ms amplio. El programa Central en tu vida del Banco Central cuenta con un sitio web especial con abundante contenido de temas econmicos en lenguaje fcilmente accesible, en plataformas diversas como mini obras de teatro y clases virtuales, videos educativos y el libro de Carlos Massad, Economa para todos. Pero este programa tambin contempla visitas guiadas al Banco, que incluyen el Museo Numismtico y charlas de especialistas del Banco. Hoy contamos con un canal de Youtube, donde est el contenido audiovisual de la institucin; una cuenta de twitter y, recientemente, una aplicacin para Smartphone con una Base de Datos Estadsticos. Entramos de lleno en el siglo 21. Tratamos siempre de estar cerca de la frontera de las mejores prcticas internacionales y tenemos la inquietud de llegar siempre lo ms lejos posible en el desarrollo de herramientas y soluciones que nos permitan cumplir de mejor forma con nuestros principales mandatos. Estamos profundamente comprometidos con el desafo de impulsar la educacin financiera, desafo que compartimos con varias instituciones pblicas y organismos no gubernamentales. Estamos tambin profundamente comprometidos con la necesidad de contar con una Estrategia Nacional de Educacin Financiera y queremos que iniciativas como las de este concurso escolar puedan ser replicadas a lo largo de todo Chile. Un pas financieramente educado es un pas que puede ir mucho ms all en el desarrollo de su sistema financiero y eso es una contribucin notoria al desarrollo econmico global y, por consecuencia, al bienestar de sus habitantes. Gracias a todos por acompaarnos en estos diez aos del Concurso Escolar La Economa Ms Cerca; gracias por ayudarnos en la recepcin y revisin de estos trabajos creativos; por ayudarnos a organizar la logstica del concurso, y por mantener vivo este espritu que nos mantiene jvenes y cerca de los chilenos, en contacto con sus realidades, y cerca de sus necesidades. Los invito a disfrutar de esta ceremonia, a ver los videos finalistas y a ser parte de una siempre emocionante premiacin. Muchas gracias,

Title: Equity and Macrofinancial Stability
text: Equity and Macrofinancial Stability 1 Pablo Garc92a Silva, Director, Central Bank of Chile June 4, 2014 Introduction I want to thank the organizers for the invitation they gave me to open this Congress, to share some points of view regarding the relationship between equity and macrofinancial stability, both transcendent issues in the world and in Chile. I must admit that it is not usual for both issues to be discussed simultaneously in Chile. Discussions on macro-financial stability have focused mainly on events abroad. Examples of this are the Argentine crisis of 2001-2002, the global financial crisis of 2008, or the sovereign crisis in the euro zone during the years 2011 and 2012. The analysis and discussion of these issues has been circumscribed to macroeconomists and finance experts, who either analyze and study what happens outside, or design and operate. Hypothetical stress scenarios. In contrast to the above, it is evident that the debate on equity is quite alive and active in our country. The levels of inequality of income and opportunities in our society have never been favorable, but now a fairly transversal social consensus has emerged regarding the fact that It is necessary to take care of this problem. However, expert analysis of the causes and dynamics of income inequality in Chile has focused on the microeconomics of the labor market and education, and expert analysis of social policies. As I pointed out, it is unusual for Chile to see a convergence of this dialogue on issues of equity and macrofinancial stability. There may be good and bad reasons for this. On the one hand, we have to recognize that for several decades we have not experienced episodes of severe financial instability in Chile, such as the crisis of 1982-1983 , or of inflation of two or three digits, as during part of the seventies. It is therefore good news that we do not have to discuss the consequences of hecatombs as those on equity, broadly understood. Undoubtedly, having an institutional economic and financial policy that aims to preserve price stability and avoid 1 Presentation made at the XVI National Congress of Commercial Engineering Students of Chile, CONCAIC, organized by the University of Concepci97n, Los Angeles campus. I appreciate the support of Sindy Olea and Camilo P8erez and the comments received. crisis has contributed to this good news. Indeed, Chile escaped having excessively negative consequences in the financial crisis of 2008 and 2009, thanks precisely to the fact that a policy system has been built. which has been adequately preventive to avoid crises and agile enough to give room for maneuver when the external environment becomes difficult. But on the other hand, it is desirable that in the profession we exercise more actively the dialogue between macroeconomists and microeconomists on issues of common interest. The growing availability of much more disaggregated information, together with greater computational processing capacity, in fact allows to open a joint work space where the macroeconomic implications of the aggregation of individual behaviours, but also the disaggregated impact of systemic shocks. In addition, understanding that macrofinancial stability is a broad concept, encompassing dimensions of social welfare, also allows us to understand the rationality of macroeconomic policy management , more beyond its immediate objectives of, for example, growth and inflation. It therefore allows us to understand why the Central Bank of Chile has as its objectives the normal functioning of payments and price stability . Just because we haven't had inflationary or financial crises in several decades doesn't mean we can let our guard down , since complacency is the root of policy mistakes. economic that can generate quite catastrophic situations. This can also not only interrupt our plans as a society to move to a fairer economy, but also take us back to scenarios of more inequality and fragility for those most vulnerable segments of our economy. Some initial concepts In this presentation I will try to make this link between stability and equity, from the practical point of view, empirically showing the relationship between these variables in various episodes, both in Chile as in other parts of the world. But, first, it is necessary to review some basic concepts. By macrofinancial stability we mean an environment where there is an absence of crisis. That is, the concept of stability will be defined as the opposite of that of instability. This may be Manichean, but the debate on how to define macrofinancial stability has been quite long and difficult. We may have difficulty defining a situation of stability, but it is not difficult for us to recognize when the economy is going through periods of instability or crisis. The macro-financial dimension encompasses both aspects of macroeconomic stability, such as price stability, and the stability or normal functioning of financial intermediation. Therefore, a situation of hyperinflation or very high inflation, or a banking crisis that collapses a relevant segment of the system, are cases of macrofinancial instability. Generally , macroeconomics courses study and evaluate the effects on macroeconomic aggregates of these phenomena, and there is considerable consensus that these effects They can be very significant. However, and this is a point I want to emphasize today, episodes of instability also have conceptually relevant distributional effects. Take for example the case of a banking crisis, which results in the bankruptcy of a significant number of institutions. The immediate effect of a phenomenon like this is that it affects the value of the liabilities of the banking system, liabilities that have typically been vehicles for channeling the accumulated resources of savers. However, it is possible that those households with greater information and a higher level of wealth may have a greater capacity to diversify their investments, both within the domestic banking system and abroad. Therefore, the potential equity impact of a banking crisis may be relatively smaller on them than on segments of households that have less capacity for diversification, and therefore kept a greater fraction of their financial savings in the local banking system. Moreover, as is usual for banking crises to be accompanied by balance of payments and exchange rate crises, those households with savings abroad can even to benefit from this crisis. Crises in bank intermediation tend to hurt savers more than debtors, including the government, since the latter can also engage in defaulting behavior. Finally , this type of crisis entails significant real costs in unemployment and fall in consumption, which will most severely affect household welfare. who have less capacity to diversify their sources of employment or to resort to assets to compensate for the fall in their incomes. In short, a situation of financial instability, or rightly of banking crisis, generates large transfers of wealth between agents in the economy, with those most affected being those who are less likely to diversify their savings. financial, either by smaller size or availability of information. Such a crisis is therefore very likely to increase inequality and fragility among the most vulnerable households. Price instability, such as in situations of hyperinflation or high inflation, also has harmful effects in terms of equity. Indeed , periods of sharp price escalations eat away at the purchasing power of households whose livelihood is a fixed monetary income in pesos, and which Readjusts only sporadically. Even, accelerate the pace of Readjustability, without addressing the underlying reasons for the inflationary situation, only serves to accelerate the escalation of prices. Again, those households with greater capacity for diversification and access, for example, to financial instruments with adjustability, or savings abroad, have a greater capacity to face the negative effects of episodes of high inflation. Thus, not only is inflation an unlegislated tax, but it is inherently regressive. Evidence on equity and macrofinancial stability The cases of the United States, Argentina, Iceland and our own are useful to exemplify these effects with concrete magnitudes. 2 As can be seen in Graphs 1 to 4, periods of financial instability are associated with both relevant increases in measures of inequality (measured as the Gini coefficient or as the Fraction of income received by the highest percentiles of the distribution). In the US, the highest levels of inequality have been observed in periods of banking crisis, the Great Depression, and the financial crisis of 2008 .2009. In Argentina, hyperinflation and the external and exchange rate crisis of 2001 .2002 led to significant increases in the fraction of the population living below the poverty line, as well as increases in inequality measured by the Gini coefficient. In Iceland, the crisis that began in 2008 and lasted until 2010 also led to significant increases in inequality and poverty indicators . Finally, in Chile, the banking crisis and depression in 1982-1983 caused very significant increases in unemployment, but also in inequality indicators, which in fact They took longer to fall than unemployment. Taking a more general sample of countries, and cross-referencing the information on banking crises identified by Reinhart and Rogoff (2009) with that of inequality indicators compiled by Solt (2009), it can be seen that, even in the absence of controls for other determinants, the Gini coefficient increases after a banking crisis. This is supported by more careful studies of the relationship between inequality and financial crisis, as well as inequality and the business cycle. 3 Other considerations Various observers have suggested that the relationship between equity and stability does not go one way. In fact, the relationship between income distribution and the frequency of banking crises in the US. has been used to argue that a situation of 2 Atkinson and Morelli (2014) present a more general sweep of case studies. 3 Barlevy y Tsiddon (2006), Malinen (2013). Excessive inequality can in turn lead to financial instability, and that this is also linked to the way the financial industry is regulated . 4 One form of this argument goes something like this: Financial deregulation allows for an excessive expansion of the financial system, which is the segment where it is common for them to concentrate. higher wages in developed economies, and thus increases income inequality . But at the same time, deregulation increases risk-taking and leverage, and weakens household and financial institutions' balance sheets, increasing the likelihood of a banking crisis. In fact , in some episodes, such as Iceland, where a financial sector that expanded excessively also contracted very quickly with the crisis, it is possible to see a decrease in inequality because the segments better The financial system's salaries contract even faster than average. For now, empirical studies on this link have not reached conclusions. definitive generals. 5 Policy conclusions and lessons In this presentation, I have outlined some considerations on the linkages between equity and episodes of macroeconomic and financial instability. The evidence is relatively clear that the latter are events that severely affect not only the usual macroeconomic aggregates, but also the levels of inequality in society. Throughout history, it has been demonstrated that financial crises and episodes of high inflation generate important transfers of income and wealth, which usually end up harming the most important segments. vulnerable and with fewer resources in society. That is why maintaining financial and macroeconomic stability are not pilgrim objectives for economic authorities but essential tasks. Probably, with the exception of natural disasters, there are no events worse than financial crises and episodes of very high inflation, which can reverse progress in terms of of prosperity and inclusive growth in countries. Maintaining permanent vigilance, avoiding complacency and ensuring a robust and active prudential regulatory and supervisory framework are some ingredients to avoid episodes of instability. text_original: Equidad y Estabilidad Macrofinanciera 1 Pablo Garca Silva, Consejero, Banco Central de Chile 4 de Junio de 2014 Introduccin Quiero agradecer a los organizadores la invitacin que me hicieron a abrir este Congreso, para compartir algunos puntos de vista relativos a la relacin entre equidad y estabilidad macrofinanciera, temas ambos trascendentes en el mundo y en Chile. Debo reconocer que no es habitual que en Chile se discuta de ambos temas de forma simultnea. Las discusiones sobre estabilidad macrofinanciera se han centrado sobre todo en los eventos en el exterior. Ejemplos de ello son la crisis Argentina de 20012002, la crisis financiera global de 2008, o la crisis soberana en la zona euro durante los aos 2011 y 2012. El anlisis y discusin de estos asuntos ha estado circunscrito a los macroeconomistas y expertos en finanzas, que o analizan y estudian lo que pasa afuera, o disean y operan hipotticos escenarios de estrs. En contraste con lo anterior, es evidente que el debate sobre equidad est bastante vivo y activo en nuestro pas. Los niveles de desigualdad del ingreso y de oportunidades en nuestra sociedad no han sido nunca favorables, pero ahora ha emergido un consenso social bastante transversal respecto a que es necesario hacerse cargo de este problema. Sin embargo, el anlisis experto sobre las causas y dinmicas de la desigualdad del ingreso en Chile ha estado centrado en la microeconoma del mercado del trabajo y la educacin, y en el anlisis experto en polticas sociales. Como seal, no es habitual que en Chile veamos una convergencia de este dilogo en temas de equidad y estabilidad macrofinanciera. Puede haber buenas y malas razones para ello. Por un lado, tenemos que reconocer que desde hace varias dcadas no experimentamos en Chile episodios de inestabilidad financiera severa, como la crisis de 19821983, o de inflacin de dos o tres dgitos, como durante parte de la dcada del setenta. Es por lo tanto una buena noticia que no tengamos que discutir las consecuencias de hecatombes como aquellas en la equidad, entendida de manera amplia. Sin duda que disponer de una institucionalidad de poltica econmica y financiera que tiene como objetivos el preservar la estabilidad de precios y evitar 1 Presentacin realizada en el XVI Congreso Nacional de Estudiantes de Ingeniera Comercial de Chile, CONCAIC, organizado por la Universidad de Concepcin, campus Los ngeles. Agradezco el apoyo de Sindy Olea y Camilo Prez y los comentarios recibidos. crisis ha contribuido a esta buena noticia. De hecho, Chile escap de tener consecuencias excesivamente negativas en la crisis financiera de 2008 y 2009, gracias precisamente a que se ha construido un sistema de polticas que ha sido lo adecuadamente preventivo para evitar crisis y suficientemente gil como para dar espacio de maniobra cuando el entorno externo se torna difcil. Pero por otro lado, es deseable que en la profesin ejerzamos de forma ms activa el dilogo entre macroeconomistas y microeconomistas sobre temas de inters comn. La creciente disponibilidad de informacin mucho ms desagregada, junto con mayor capacidad de procesamiento computacional, permite de hecho abrir un espacio de trabajo conjunto donde se pueden estudiar las implicancias macroeconmicas de la agregacin de comportamientos individuales, pero tambin el impacto desagregado de shocks sistmicos. Adems, entender que la estabilidad macrofinanciera es un concepto amplio, que engloba dimensiones del bienestar social, tambin permite entender la racionalidad de la gestin de polticas macroeconmicas, ms all de sus objetivos inmediatos de, por ejemplo, crecimiento e inflacin. Permite por tanto entender por qu el Banco Central de Chile tiene como sus objetivos el normal funcionamiento de los pagos y la estabilidad de precios. Que no hayamos tenido crisis inflacionarias o financieras en varias dcadas no significa que podemos bajar la guardia, puesto que de la complacencia nace la raz de errores de poltica econmica que pueden generar situaciones bastante catastrficas. Ello adems puede no slo interrumpir nuestros planes como sociedad para avanzar a una economa ms justa, sino retrotraernos a escenarios de ms desigualdad y fragilidad para aquellos segmentos ms vulnerables de nuestra economa. Algunos conceptos iniciales En esta presentacin intentar hacer esta vinculacin entre estabilidad y equidad, desde el punto de vista prctico, mostrando empricamente la relacin entre estas variables en diversos episodios, tanto en Chile como en otras partes del mundo. Pero, primero, es necesario revisar algunos conceptos bsicos. Por estabilidad macrofinanciera entenderemos un entorno donde hay ausencia de crisis. Es decir, el concepto de estabilidad se definir como el opuesto al de inestabilidad. Esto puede ser algo maniqueo, pero el debate sobre cmo definir estabilidad macrofinanciera ha sido bastante largo y difcil. Podremos tener dificultades para definir una situacin de estabilidad, pero no nos cuesta reconocer cuando la economa est transitando por perodos de inestabilidad o crisis. La dimensin macrofinanciera engloba tanto aspectos de estabilidad macroeconmica, como por ejemplo la estabilidad de precios, como la estabilidad o normal funcionamiento de la intermediacin financiera. Por lo tanto, una situacin de hiperinflacin o muy elevada inflacin, o una crisis bancaria que colapsa un segmento relevante del sistema, son casos de inestabilidad macrofinanciera. Generalmente en los cursos de macroeconoma se estudian y evalan los efectos sobre los agregados macroeconmicos de estos fenmenos, y existe bastante consenso en que esos efectos pueden ser muy significativos. Sin embargo, y es un punto que quiero enfatizar hoy, los episodios de inestabilidad tienen tambin desde el punto de vista conceptual efectos distributivos relevantes. Tomemos por ejemplo el caso de una crisis bancaria, que resulta en la quiebra de un nmero importante de instituciones. El efecto inmediato de un fenmeno como este es que se afecta el valor de los pasivos del sistema bancario, pasivos que han sido tpicamente vehculos para canalizar los recursos acumulados de los ahorristas. Sin embargo, es posible que aquellos hogares con mayor informacin y mayor nivel de riqueza, puedan tener una mayor capacidad para diversificar sus inversiones, tanto dentro del sistema bancario domstico como en el exterior. Por lo tanto, el potencial impacto patrimonial de una crisis bancaria puede ser relativamente menor sobre ellos que sobre los segmentos de hogares que tienen menor capacidad de diversificacin, y que por tanto mantenan una mayor fraccin de su ahorro financiero en el sistema bancario local. Ms an, como es habitual que las crisis bancarias vengan acompaadas de crisis de balanza de pagos y cambiarias, aquellos hogares con ahorros en el exterior pueden incluso verse beneficiados en esta crisis. Las crisis de la intermediacin bancaria tienden a perjudicar ms a los ahorristas que a los deudores, incluyendo al gobierno, puesto que este ltimo puede tambin entrar en comportamiento de cesacin de pagos. Finalmente, este tipo de crisis conlleva significativos costos reales en desempleo y cada en consumo, lo que afectar ms severamente el bienestar de los hogares que disponen de menor capacidad de diversificar sus fuentes de empleo o recurrir a activos para compensar la cada de sus ingresos. En sntesis, una situacin de inestabilidad financiera, o derechamente de crisis bancaria, genera grandes transferencias de riqueza entre agentes en la economa, siendo aquellos ms perjudicados quienes tienen menores posibilidades de diversificar sus ahorros financieros, sea por menor tamao o disponibilidad de informacin. Una crisis de este tipo es muy probable, por tanto, que aumente la desigualdad y fragilidad de los hogares ms vulnerables. La inestabilidad de precios, como en situaciones de hiperinflacin o elevada inflacin, tiene tambin efectos nocivos en trminos de equidad. En efecto, perodos de escaladas fuertes en los precios carcomen el poder adquisitivo de los hogares cuyo sustento es un ingreso monetario fijo en pesos, y que se reajusta slo de forma espordica. Incluso, acelerar el ritmo de reajustabilidad, sin enfrentar las razones de fondo de la situacin inflacionaria, slo sirve para acelerar la escalada de los precios. Nuevamente, aquellos hogares con mayor capacidad de diversificacin y acceso, por ejemplo, a instrumentos financieros con reajustabilidad, o ahorros en el exterior, tienen una mayor capacidad de enfrentar los efectos negativos de los episodios de alta inflacin. As, no slo la inflacin es un impuesto no legislado, sino que es intrnsecamente regresivo. Evidencia sobre equidad y estabilidad macrofinanciera Los casos de EE.UU., Argentina, Islandia y el nuestro propio son tiles para ejemplificar con magnitudes concretas estos efectos.2 Como se puede ver en los grficos 1 a 4, los perodos de inestabilidad financiera tienen asociados tanto incrementos relevantes de las medidas de desigualdad (sea medida como el coeficiente de Gini o como la fraccin del ingreso percibida por los percentiles ms altos de la distribucin). En EE.UU., los niveles mayores de desigualdad se han observado en los perodos de crisis bancaria, la Gran Depresin y la crisis financiera de 20082009. En Argentina, la hiperinflacin y la crisis externa y cambiaria de 20012002 llevaron a incrementos significativos en la fraccin de la poblacin que viva por debajo de la lnea de pobreza, as como a incrementos en la desigualdad medida con el coeficiente Gini. En Islandia, la crisis que comenz en 2008 y se extendi hasta 2010 provoc tambin incrementos relevantes de la desigualdad y los indicadores de pobreza. Finalmente, en Chile, la crisis bancaria y depresin en 19821983 provoc incrementos muy significativos en el desempleo, pero tambin en los indicadores de desigualdad, los que de hecho demoraron ms en caer que la desocupacin. Tomando una muestra ms general de pases, y cruzando la informacin de crisis bancarias identificadas por Reinhart y Rogoff (2009) con la de indicadores de desigualdad compilada por Solt (2009), se aprecia que, an en ausencia de controles por otros determinantes, el coeficiente de Gini se incrementa con posterioridad a una crisis bancaria. Esto se ve refrendado por estudios ms cuidadosos de la relacin entre desigualdad y crisis financiera, as como desigualdad y el ciclo econmico. 3 Otras consideraciones Diversos observadores han sugerido que la relacin entre equidad y estabilidad no va en una sola direccin. De hecho, la relacin que se aprecia entre la distribucin del ingreso y la frecuencia de crisis bancarias en EE.UU. se ha usado para argumentar que una situacin de 2 Atkinson y Morelli (2014) presentan un barrido ms general de estudios de caso. 3 Barlevy y Tsiddon (2006), Malinen (2013). desigualdad excesiva puede a su vez provocar inestabilidad financiera, y que esto adems est vinculado a la forma como se regula la industria financiera. 4 Una forma de este argumento va ms o menos as: La desregulacin financiera permite una expansin excesiva del sistema financiero, que es el segmento donde es habitual se concentren las mayores remuneraciones en las economas desarrolladas, y por tanto aumenta la desigualdad del ingreso. Pero al mismo tiempo, la desregulacin aumenta la toma de riesgos y el apalancamiento, y fragiliza los balances de los hogares y de las entidades financieras, aumentando la probabilidad de crisis bancaria. De hecho, en algunos episodios, como el de Islandia, donde un sector financiero que se expandi de manera excesiva se contrajo tambin muy rpidamente con la crisis, es posible ver una disminucin en la desigualdad pues los segmentos mejor remunerados del sistema financiero se contraen incluso ms rpido que el promedio. Por ahora, los estudios empricos sobre este vnculo no han llegado a conclusiones generales definitivas.5 Conclusiones y lecciones de poltica En esta presentacin he esbozado algunas consideraciones sobre los vnculos entre equidad y episodios de inestabilidad macroeconmica y financiera. La evidencia es relativamente clara en cuanto a que estos ltimos son eventos que afectan de manera severa no slo los agregados macroeconmicos habituales, sino tambin los niveles de desigualdad en la sociedad. A lo largo de la historia ha quedado demostrado que las crisis financieras y los episodios de alta inflacin generan importantes transferencias de ingreso y riqueza, las que habitualmente terminan perjudicando a los segmentos ms vulnerables y de menores recursos de la sociedad. Es por ello que la mantencin de la estabilidad financiera y macroeconmica no son objetivos peregrinos para las autoridades econmicas sino que tareas esenciales. Probablemente, salvo las catstrofes naturales, no hay eventos peores que las crisis financieras y los episodios de muy elevada inflacin, que puedan retrotraer el progreso en trminos de prosperidad y crecimiento inclusivo en los pases. Mantener una vigilancia permanente, evitando la autocomplacencia y asegurando un marco de regulacin y supervisin prudencial robusto y activo, son algunos ingredientes para evitar episodios de inestabilidad.
