Title: Economic Outlook
text: ECONOMIC OUTLOOK Mario Marcel C.1/President, Central Bank of ChileMarzo 2017 Recent months have been characterized by more favourable prospects in the external scenario. In the developed world, short-term data indicate activity that is becoming more dynamic. Three elements are particularly novel in this regard: first, that the greatest dynamism is observed in all developed economies, with significant improvements in the outlook for Europe and Japan that add to the progress already shown by the United States; secondly, that manufacturing and investment have recovered significantly, after several years of lagging behind service activity and consumption; and, third, that inflation has begun to recover, albeit at different rates. This greater international dynamism began before the election in the United States and extends beyond this country. Therefore, their origins must be sought elsewhere. One plausible hypothesis is that the expansionary monetary policies of several of these countries ended up being effective and that expectations that greater monetary activism would help overcome the hangover of the financial crisis are proving more valid than the alternative hypothesis of secular stagnation of the world economy. Even so, expansionary monetary policies, particularly through non-traditional means, are leaving an important legacy in exchange rate matters. Whether or not it was their original motivation, they have generated a currency competition between large economies whose dynamics are not easy to stop. Similarly, massive bond purchases have influenced the prices of financial assets and injected large volumes of liquidity into the markets. This has also affected the exchange rates of emerging economies which, as a result of massive capital inflows, have imported deflation over the last year. How to reverse this process and its financial and exchange rate effects is more complex than a traditional monetary policy adjustment through the interest rate. Any adjustments in monetary and even fiscal policy in developed countries should begin to be incorporated into the analysis of the economic environment of emerging countries and Chile in particular. The Federal Reserve raised its interest rate for the second time in December and has signaled a somewhat faster withdrawal of monetary stimulus, without disrupting financial markets. These signals have been linked to the prospect of more active fiscal policy as the U.S. economy approaches full employment. How much additional economic boost fiscal policy can inject into the United States before pressuring productive capacity, exchange rates, or Federal Reserve decisions is V Presented on Tuesday, March 7 at the Council of the Americas dinner. something that deserves the utmost attention. For its part, the Eurozone is intensifying the discussion on the end of the European Central Bank's quantitative easing programs, a discussion that is also beginning to be outlined in Japan. In the emerging world, China's current situation contrasts sharply with what we observed a year ago, when uncertainty prevailed, subjecting emerging countries to a strong episode of financial stress. Today there is greater stability, with current and projected growth remaining close to 6.5%, while capital outflows that have repeatedly worried the Chinese authorities seem to be moderating. In this picture, the outlook for the emerging world looks better than expected some time ago. Global financial conditions remain favorable, the world will grow more than in previous years, and commodity prices have improved. Partly as an expression of this, currencies that depreciated significantly after the US elections have gradually recovered their relative value. However, the global economy remains exposed to significant risks. Although any projection scenario is always subject to uncertainty, it seems that it has expanded. We have seen how global financial markets have become very sensitive to any change or hint of change in the United States, Europe, China or another economy or market that at one time may be considered relevant. It would not be surprising that new definitions of the United States government, unexpected results in the electoral processes in Europe or episodes of financial instability in China that question the convictions that are forming the markets, can produce significant financial turbulence that affects emerging countries through financial and exchange channels. In other words, the current relative external calm, while encouraging, is still far from being fully reliable. The Chilean economy still does not seem to react significantly to the improved external outlook. The activity data for the last quarter of 2016 and the beginning of 2017 surprised to the downside. As in previous years, part of the slower expansion of the economy came from a mining sector that in the last year has been hit hard by productive disruptions, but there has also been a lower performance of sectors other than natural resources. On the latter, the evolution of construction should be highlighted. After several years in which the sector was boosted by the mining boom and all its externalities to other areas of the economy, 2014 saw a significant decline. In 2015, however, the construction of new homes had a significant boost due to the effects of the tax reform. Sales had a very relevant increase, reaching record levels. In mid-2016 this effect began to dissipate, the pace of sales fell and sectoral indicators began to show a less positive scenario. It adds an investment that fails to rebound, an economy that grows at low rates, stagnant salaried employment and stricter mortgage credit conditions for the foot required in the purchase of a home. On the expenditure side, the behavior of investment and exports is striking. Local and external financial conditions have remained expansionary for a long time. Internally, the level of commercial placement rates is close to its historical lows, as are long-term rates. Despite these favourable credit conditions, investment has failed to pick up after the end of the mining boom . The level of imports of capital goods stood at values between 800 and 900 million dollars. Investment in infrastructure shows low dynamism as does engineering services, while, as I said, the real estate area has deteriorated after the strong boost it received in 2015. On the export side, their volumes have shown annual falls in the last two years, mainly observable in industrial shipments. This result is striking despite the significant depreciation of the peso from 2013 to date. However, it should be borne in mind that the depreciation of the peso has not been a particular phenomenon of the Chilean economy but rather reflects a global appreciation of the dollar. In this sense, the mere depreciation of the Chilean peso against the dollar has not meant an automatic gain in competitiveness, especially considering that since the peso's strongest point in the first half of 2013, its nominal depreciation has been lower than that of other emerging economies. On the other hand, the destination markets for national exports have gone through a rather complex economic scenario. Thus, 2016 closed with an annual growth of 1.5% according to available data. For 2017, private projections with information from recent months bet on an expansion below 2%. Although this figure remains within the 1.5-2.5% growth range that we projected last December, in our March IPoM soon, we will publish new projections that account for how the recent and expected evolution of the macroeconomic scenario will affect projected growth. For now, after the Imacec of 1.7% annually in January of this year, the February figure will be affected by the drop in mining production derived from the strike in Escondida and the base comparison effect left by the leap year of 2016. This seems enough to anticipate a first quarter of 2017 that will be no better than the last quarter of 2016. In any case, it is important to note that some partial data on domestic spending and its determinants show a somewhat more benign picture. Consumption has continued to grow at rates of the order of 2% for several quarters. The confidence of companies and consumers has stopped deteriorating and even shows some improvement at the top, although they still remain in the pessimism zone. The unemployment rate remains low and wage indicators continue to show growth around their historical averages. However, some of these strengths depend on labour market behaviour. The sustained stagnation that salaried job creation has shown since mid-2016 is worrying, even with an annual drop in the most recent data. Lately, the deterioration in this variable has been accompanied by increases in the number of inactive people, in the self-employed and in the proportion of part-time jobs. Any further weaknesses in this area may have significant effects on private consumption, especially when consumer credit slows at the margin. On the inflation side, the data set of the last two months has offered surprises in both directions, so the scenario we expected in December does not show major variations. Thus, it is still the case that core inflation (the IPCSAE) of goods shows a sharp decline in its annual variation, in line with an exchange rate that has appreciated in the last year. At the same time, the services CPPI also declines, in line with an activity gap that has widened moderately and also with its own inertia. In the immediate term, we expect core inflation to continue to decline in the coming months, then return to 3% and fluctuate around that value until the end of the policy horizon. Private inflation expectations are consistent with this scenario, remaining anchored to 3% over two years. The convergence of inflation to the target will be helped by an external scenario that, in general terms, will be similar or somewhat better than a few months ago, and by an economy that will resume higher growth rates in the coming quarters. As we pointed out in the December IPoM, a more expansionary monetary policy is necessary to ensure the achievement of the inflation target of 3% in 24 months in the presence of a weakening of domestic demand and an exchange rate appreciation. Part of this greater expansionary activity was already achieved in January, when we reduced the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) by 25 basis points. The scenario in which these guidelines were formulated remains fully valid, regardless of shorter-term data. To this end, it is important to note that the lower growth, concentrated in the fourth quarter of 2016 and the first quarter of 2017, will further widen the activity gap, raising the importance of demand factors in the evolution of inflation. This is reflected in the projected path for core inflation. Thus, beyond the behavior of more volatile prices in the short term, such as fuels and food, a more expansionary monetary policy is now necessary to achieve the inflation target. Three elements should be highlighted on this. The first is that the objective of monetary policy remains, as always, price stability. What today justifies its expansionary bias is the risk of inflation remaining below the target, not that the economy grows little. The calibration of monetary policy is made, within the macro models that support it, to achieve the inflation target, not to achieve a level or rate of GDP growth. However, given the mechanisms with which the economy operates, it is highly likely that low inflation is associated with weak activity and that expansionary monetary policy can influence both. Second, to the extent that the objective of monetary policy is inflation in the medium term, its effectiveness must be measured in terms of its ability to influence inflation. To the extent that changes in the policy rate affect market interest rates, monetary policy has multiple transmission channels to inflation, some through domestic demand and activity, others through asset prices. Third, the determinants of inflation and the effectiveness of monetary policy transmission channels may vary over the cycle or in response to idiosyncratic factors, but in principle, a larger activity gap should raise the importance of domestic demand. It should be noted that the activity gap projected for 2017 is the highest in recent years and therefore it is possible that in the coming future the trajectory of core inflation will be more influenced by this variable than what happened a year or two ago. At the close, I think it is important to visualize where the opportunities are for greater dynamism in the second half of the year. In this regard, the most visible signals come from the external sector. The best tone in the developed world is certainly good news. To the extent that it is maintained and the growth of this part of the world improves, the rest of the emerging economies will benefit, either by greater demand, by better prices of our exports or by a better mix of economic policies. Secondly, the Chilean economy has sustained a period of low growth, showing a significant degree of maturity. Companies and consumers have been able to react to this period by ordering their financial burdens, improving their processes, reducing their costs. All this without macroeconomic indicators having suffered too much, discounting of course the low growth. The price of energy has fallen and security of supply has increased, which is very important for key sectors of the Chilean economy. Financial conditions remain very favourable. The nominal exchange rate has helped the export sector to have higher returns in pesos, which has undoubtedly allowed it to improve its financial position. The labor market does not show the stress levels of three or four years ago, when the cost of labor was rising driven by the extemalities generated by the mining boom in the north of the country. I think this is enough to keep us on a good footing for the economy to be able to return to a more dynamic path when general sentiments improve. But this arrangement is not something that lasts forever. Hopefully, in addition to the greater concern expressed by the political world about growth, there will be a sense of urgency and an effort to carry out initiatives that ensure this.
text_original: Coyuntura Econmica Mario Marcel C.1/ Presidente, Banco Central de Chile Marzo 2017 Los ltimos meses se han caracterizado por perspectivas ms favorables en el escenario externo. En el mundo desarrollado, los datos coyunturales indican una actividad que est adquiriendo mayor dinamismo. Tres elementos son particularmente novedosos a este respecto: primero, que el mayor dinamismo se observa en todas las economas desarrolladas, con mejoras significativas en las perspectivas para Europa y Japn que se suman al avance que ya mostraba Estados Unidos; segundo, que la industria manufacturera y la inversin han tenido una importante recuperacin, despus de varios aos de rezago respecto de la actividad de servicios y el consumo; y, tercero, que la inflacin ha comenzado a recuperarse, aunque con distintos ritmos. Este mayor dinamismo internacional se inici antes de la eleccin en Estados Unidos y se extiende ms all de este pas. Por lo tanto, sus orgenes hay que buscarlos en otra parte. Una hiptesis plausible es que las polticas monetarias expansivas de varios de estos pases terminaron siendo efectivas y que las expectativas de que un mayor activismo monetario ayudara a superar la resaca de la crisis financiera estn probando ser ms vlidas que la hiptesis alternativa de estancamiento secular de la economa mundial. Aun as, las polticas monetarias expansivas, particularmente a travs de medios no tradicionales, estn dejando un legado importante en materia cambiara. Haya sido o no su motivacin original, estas han generado una competencia cambiara entre las grandes economas cuya dinmica no es fcil de detener. Del mismo modo, la compra masiva de bonos ha influido sobre los precios de los activos financieros y ha inyectado grandes volmenes de liquidez a los mercados. Esto ha incidido tambin sobre los tipos de cambio de las economas emergentes que, como producto de entradas masivas de capitales, han importado deflacin durante el ltimo ao. La forma de revertir este proceso y sus efectos financieros y cambiarios es ms compleja que un ajuste de poltica monetaria tradicional a travs de la tasa de inters. Los eventuales ajustes en la poltica monetaria e incluso fiscal en los pases desarrollados deben empezar a incorporarse al anlisis del entorno econmico de los pases emergentes y de Chile en particular. La Reserva Federal aument su tasa de inters por segunda vez en diciembre y ha dado seales de un retiro algo ms rpido del estmulo monetario, sin que ello haya provocado disrupciones en los mercados financieros. Estas seales han sido vinculadas a la perspectiva de una poltica fiscal ms activa, en momentos en que la economa estadounidense se aproxima al pleno empleo. Cunto impulso econmico adicional pueda inyectar la poltica fiscal en Estados Unidos antes de presionar la capacidad productiva, los tipos de cambio o las decisiones de la Reserva Federal es V Presentado el martes 7 de marzo en la cena del Council of the Americas. algo que merece la mxima atencin. Por su parte, en la Eurozona se est intensificando la discusin sobre el trmino de los programas de alivio cuantitativo del Banco Central Europeo, discusin que comienza a esbozarse tambin en Japn. En el mundo emergente, la situacin actual de China contrasta claramente con lo que observbamos hace un ao, cuando se impona la incertidumbre, sometiendo a los pases emergentes a un fuerte episodio de estrs financiero. Hoy se aprecia mayor estabilidad, con un crecimiento actual y proyectado que se mantiene en las proximidades del 6,5%, mientras parecen moderarse las salidas de capitales que han preocupado recurrentemente a las autoridades chinas. En este cuadro, el panorama para el mundo emergente se aprecia mejor que lo esperado hace un tiempo. Las condiciones financieras globales siguen siendo favorables, el mundo crecer ms que en aos anteriores y los precios de las materias primas han mejorado. En parte como expresin de ello, las monedas que se depreciaron significativamente tras las elecciones en Estados Unidos han recuperado paulatinamente su valor relativo. Con todo, la economa mundial sigue estando expuesta a riesgos importantes. Aunque cualquier escenario de proyeccin siempre est sujeto a incertidumbre, pareciera que esta se ha ampliado. Hemos visto cmo los mercados financieros globales se han vuelto muy sensibles a cualquier cambio o atisbo de cambio en Estados Unidos, Europa, China u otra economa o mercado que en un momento pueda considerarse relevante. No sera de extraar que nuevas definiciones del gobierno de Estados Unidos, resultados inesperados en los procesos eleccionarios en Europa o episodios de inestabilidad financiera en China que cuestionen las convicciones que se van formando los mercados, puedan producir turbulencias financieras significativas que afecten a los pases emergentes a travs de canales financieros y cambiarios. En otras palabras, la relativa calma externa actual, aunque alentadora, est lejos an de ser plenamente confiable. La economa chilena todava no parece reaccionar significativamente al mejor panorama externo. Los datos de actividad del ltimo trimestre del 2016 y comienzos del 2017 sorprendieron a la baja. Como en aos anteriores, parte de la menor expansin de la economa provino de un sector minero que en el ltimo ao ha sido muy afectado por disrupciones productivas, pero tambin se ha producido un desempeo ms bajo de los sectores distintos de recursos naturales. Sobre esto ltimo, debe destacarse la evolucin de la construccin. Tras varios aos en que el sector se vio impulsado por el boom minero y todas sus externalidades hacia otros rubros de la economa, el 2014 se apreci una importante baja. En el 2015, sin embargo, la construccin de viviendas nuevas, tuvo un significativo impulso por los efectos de la reforma tributaria. Las ventas tuvieron un aumento muy relevante, llegando a niveles rcord. A mediados del 2016 ese efecto comenz a disiparse, el ritmo de ventas baj y los indicadores sectoriales empezaron a dar cuenta de un escenario menos positivo. Se suma una inversin que no logra repuntar, una economa que crece a tasas bajas, un empleo asalariado estancado y condiciones de otorgamiento de crdito hipotecario ms estrictas por el pie exigido en la compra de una vivienda. Del lado del gasto es llamativo el comportamiento de la inversin y las exportaciones. Las condiciones financieras locales y externas se han mantenido expansivas por largo tiempo. Internamente, el nivel de las tasas de colocacin comerciales est cercano a sus mnimos histricos, lo mismo que las tasas de largo plazo. Pese a estas favorables condiciones de crdito, la inversin no ha logrado repuntar tras el fin del boom minero. El nivel de las importaciones de bienes de capital se estacion en valores entre 800 a 900 millones de dlares. La inversin en infraestructura muestra un bajo dinamismo al igual que los servicios de ingeniera, mientras que, como ya coment, el rea inmobiliaria se ha deteriorado tras el fuerte impulso que recibi el 2015. Por el lado de las exportaciones, sus volmenes han mostrado cadas anuales en los ltimos dos aos, principalmente observables en los envos industriales. Llama la atencin este resultado pese a la importante depreciacin del peso desde el 2013 a la fecha. Sin embargo, se deben tener presente que la depreciacin del peso no ha sido un fenmeno particular de la economa chilena sino que ms bien refleja una apreciacin global del dlar. En ese sentido, la sola depreciacin del peso chileno respecto del dlar no ha significado una ganancia de competitividad de forma automtica, especialmente considerando que desde el punto de mayor fortaleza del peso en el primer semestre del 2013, su depreciacin nominal ha sido menor que la de otras economas emergentes. Por otro lado, los mercados de destino de las exportaciones nacionales han atravesado por un escenario econmico ms bien complejo. As, el 2016 cerr con un crecimiento anual de 1,5% segn los datos disponibles. Para el 2017, las proyecciones privadas con informacin de los ltimos meses apuestan a una expansin por debajo de 2%. Aunque esta cifra se mantiene dentro del rango de crecimiento de 1,5-2,5% que proyectamos en diciembre pasado, prximamente, en nuestro IPoM de marzo, publicaremos nuevas proyecciones que den cuenta de cmo la evolucin reciente y esperada del escenario macroeconmico afectar el crecimiento proyectado. Por lo pronto, luego del Imacec de 1,7% anual de enero de este ao, la cifra de febrero estar afectada por la baja en la produccin minera derivada de la huelga en Escondida y el efecto de base de comparacin que dej el ao bisiesto del 2016. Esto parece suficiente para anticipar un el primer trimestre del 2017 que no ser mejor que el ltimo del 2016. De todos modos, es importante notar que algunos datos parciales del gasto interno y sus determinantes muestran un panorama algo ms benigno. El consumo ha seguido creciendo a tasas del orden de 2% por varios trimestres. La confianza de empresas y consumidores ha dejado de deteriorarse e incluso muestra alguna mejora en la punta, aunque todava se mantienen en la zona de pesimismo. La tasa de desempleo se mantiene baja y los indicadores de salarios siguen mostrando crecimientos en torno a sus promedios histricos. No obstante, algunas de estas fortalezas dependen del comportamiento del mercado del trabajo. Es preocupante el sostenido estancamiento que la creacin de empleo asalariado muestra desde mediados del 2016, incluso con una cada anual en el dato ms reciente. Ultimamente, el deterioro en esta variable ha estado acompaado de aumentos en el nmero de inactivos, en las personas que trabajan por cuenta propia y en la proporcin de empleos a jornada parcial. Cualquier debilidad adicional en este mbito puede tener efectos relevantes sobre el consumo privado, especialmente cuando el crdito de consumo se desacelera en el margen. Por el lado de la inflacin, el conjunto de datos de los ltimos dos meses ha ofrecido sorpresas en ambas direcciones, con lo que el escenario que preveamos en diciembre no muestra mayores variaciones. As, sigue siendo el caso que la inflacin subyacente el IPCSAE de bienes muestra una fuerte baja de su variacin anual, en lnea con un tipo de cambio que se ha apreciado en el ltimo ao. Al mismo tiempo, el IPCSAE de servicios tambin desciende, acorde con una brecha de actividad que se ha ampliado moderadamente y tambin con su propia inercia. En lo inmediato, esperamos que la inflacin subyacente siga descendiendo en los prximos meses, para luego retornar a 3% y fluctuar en tomo a ese valor hasta el fin del horizonte de poltica. Las expectativas privadas de inflacin son coherentes con este escenario, mantenindose ancladas a 3% a dos aos plazo. La convergencia de la inflacin a la meta ser ayudada por un escenario externo que, en trminos generales, ser similar o algo mejor que hace unos meses, y por una economa que retomar mayores tasas de crecimiento en los prximos trimestres. Tal como lo sealamos en el IPoM de diciembre, una poltica monetaria ms expansiva es necesaria para asegurar el logro de la meta de inflacin de 3% en 24 meses en presencia de un debilitamiento de la demanda interna y una apreciacin cambiara. Parte de esa mayor expansividad ya la concretamos en enero, cuando redujimos la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria (TPM) en 25 puntos base. El escenario en que se formularon estas orientaciones sigue plenamente vigente, independientemente de los datos de ms corto plazo. A este efecto es importante notar que el menor crecimiento, concentrado en el cuarto trimestre del 2016 y primero del 2017 ampliar adicionalmente la brecha de actividad, elevando la importancia de los factores de demanda en la evolucin de la inflacin. Esto se refleja en la trayectoria proyectada para la inflacin subyacente. De este modo, ms all del comportamiento de precios ms voltiles en el corto plazo, como los combustibles y los alimentos, hoy es necesaria una poltica monetaria ms expansiva para lograr la meta de inflacin. Sobre esto cabe resaltar tres elementos. El primero es que el objetivo de la poltica monetaria sigue siendo, como siempre, la estabilidad de precios. Lo que hoy justifica su sesgo expansivo es el riesgo de una inflacin que se quede debajo de la meta, no que la economa crezca poco. La calibracin de la poltica monetaria est hecha, dentro de los modelos macro que la sustentan, para el logro de la meta de inflacin, no para lograr un nivel o tasa de crecimiento del PIB. Con todo, dado los mecanismos con los que funciona la economa, es altamente probable que una inflacin baja est asociada a una actividad dbil y que una poltica monetaria expansiva pueda influir sobre ambas. En segundo lugar, en la medida que el objetivo de la Poltica Monetaria es la inflacin en el mediano plazo, su efectividad debe medirse en trminos de su capacidad para influir sobre esta ltima. En la medida que cambios de la tasa de poltica incidan sobre las tasas de inters de mercado, la poltica monetaria tiene mltiples canales de transmisin hacia la inflacin, algunos a travs de la demanda interna y la actividad, otros a travs de los precios de los activos. En tercer lugar, los determinantes de la inflacin y la eficacia de los canales de transmisin de la poltica monetaria pueden variar a lo largo del ciclo o en respuesta a factores idiosincrticos, pero en principio, una mayor brecha de actividad debera elevar la importancia de la demanda interna. Cabe destacar que la brecha de actividad proyectada para el 2017 es la ms alta de los ltimos aos y por tanto es posible que en lo venidero la trayectoria de la inflacin subyacente est ms influenciada por esta variable que lo que ocurra hace uno o dos aos atrs. Al cierre, creo importante visualizar dnde estn las oportunidades para un mayor dinamismo en la segunda mitad del ao. A este respecto, las seales ms visibles provienen del sector externo. El mejor tono del mundo desarrollado es sin duda una buena noticia. En la medida que se mantenga y el crecimiento de esta parte del mundo mejore, el resto de las economas emergentes nos veremos beneficiadas, ya sea por una mayor demanda, por mejores precios de nuestras exportaciones o por un mejor mix de polticas econmicas. En segundo lugar, la economa chilena ha sostenido un perodo de bajo crecimiento dando muestra de un grado de madurez importante. Empresas y consumidores han sabido reaccionar a este perodo ordenando sus cargas financieras, mejorando sus procesos, reduciendo sus costos. Todo eso sin que los indicadores macroeconmicos hayan sufrido en demasa, descontado por supuesto el bajo crecimiento. El precio de la energa ha descendido y la seguridad del abastecimiento ha aumentado, lo que es muy importante para sectores claves de la economa chilena. Las condiciones financieras siguen siendo muy favorables. El tipo de cambio nominal ha ayudado al sector exportador a tener mayores retornos en pesos, lo que sin duda le ha permitido mejorar su posicin financiera. El mercado laboral no muestra los niveles de estrs de hace tres o cuatro aos, cuando el costo de la mano de obra suba impulsado por las extemalidades que generaba el boom minero en el norte del pas. Creo que esto es suficiente para mantenernos en un buen pie para que la economa sea capaz de retomar una senda de mayor dinamismo cuando los nimos generales mejoren. Pero esta disposicin no es algo que dure para siempre. Ojal que a la mayor preocupacin que manifiesta el mundo poltico por el crecimiento, se sume en los prximos meses un sentido de urgencia y un esfuerzo por concretar iniciativas que as lo aseguren.

Title: The Monetary Policy of the Central Bank of Chile in the Framework of Inflation Targeting and Inflation Policy...
text: Central Bank of Chile March 2020 Opening remarks launch policy documents "The Monetary Policy of the Central Bank of Chile in the Inflation Targeting Framework" and "Financial Policy of the Central Bank of Chile" Mario Marcel, President of the Central Bank of Chile March 12, 2020 Good afternoon, everyone. Welcome to the launch of the monetary and financial policy framework documents of the Central Bank of Chile. While thanking the former Presidents of the Bank, Jos8e de Gregorio and Rodrigo Vergara for the comments they will share with us, I would like to recognize the specialists and managers of the Monetary Policy and Financial Policy divisions for the work they did in preparing these documents over the past few months. I would also like to thank my colleagues in the Council for the comments and suggestions they made in the successive rounds of discussion and review. The documents we will discuss today were published in mid-February, but their preparation occupied much of 2019, involving a special challenge for the Bank. In the case of the monetary policy framework document, the aim was to update an excellent previous document, from 2007, incorporating experience in its implementation and changes in the monetary policy environment. In the case of the financial policy framework document, the aim was to generate the first document of its kind, after some failed attempts in the past, explaining the approach, methodology and communication mechanisms applied by the bank in the prospective analysis of financial risks and its link with the regulatory agenda to which it contributes. In addition, it places all this within the institutional architecture that resulted from the approval of the new General Banking Law. Beyond the specificities of both documents, they recognize and incorporate the interactions between monetary and financial policy and both seek to use language more accessible to the public. The best recognition we can make to this work is not to give formal thanks to its authors. More significant is to explain why the documents they have produced are important, especially at a time when so many urgent new economic challenges are facing the country, the economic authorities and the Central Bank in particular. More provocatively, we may ask why devote so much time and effort to these technical documents when the country seems faced with the combination of an internal social crisis, a global epidemic, an oil price war and a visible deterioration of the international economy. To answer this question, it is important to return to an issue that has increasingly concerned us: trust in institutions. Over the past ten years, citizens' trust in their institutions has deteriorated in a large number of countries, from different regions, at different levels of development and with governments of different political orientations. In addition to being transversal, this is a worrying phenomenon, because it affects the main capital that institutions have to carry out their work. Central Bank of Chile March 2020 The trust of citizens is essential for public institutions, because it allows aligning the behavior of people, companies and organizations with the objectives of public policy. When mistrust prevails, transaction costs, opportunistic behavior, and market and state failures of various kinds increase. The importance of credibility for institutions was recognized several decades ago by economic thought, when the rational expectations approach questioned the possibility of sustaining information asymmetries in the long term, and theories about dynamic inconsistency pointed to the inefficiency of discretion in the management of public policies. Nowhere has this evolution of economic thought been more influential than in the conduct of monetary policy. Indeed, the fact that economic agents were able to identify and anticipate the behavior patterns of the authorities weakened the ability of monetary policy to generate real profits with nominal surprises. But once theoretically and empirically questioned the value of discretion in the conduct of monetary policy, the question arose why not use the rules in favor of the latter's objectives, aligning its objectives with the expectations and behavior of economic agents. This is how the value of the rules for the conduct of monetary policy arises, from which transparency in the conduct and implementation of monetary policy and the independence or autonomy of the institutions in charge of its implementation acquire greater value. This triad of rules of monetary policy, transparency and institutional autonomy has not only been picked up by dozens of countries in the world, but has extended to the field of financial stability, when conceptually, operationally and institutionally designing the macroprudential instruments with which it has responded to the costly financial crisis of 2008-2009. While in the case of monetary policy the results of this architecture are in sight, with a significant and sustained reduction in inflation, in the second we are still a stage of design and construction. This implies an answer to the question of how to strengthen trust in institutions: make their actions more predictable, explaining how and on the basis of what background decisions are made; developing the capacity to respond in a timely manner to changes in the environment; raising transparency and accountability for its results. These three elements - predictable frameworks for action, high standards of transparency and a solid institutional basis - are set out in the monetary and financial policy framework documents we are discussing today. They express, therefore, an effort to strengthen credibility and confidence in the Central Bank of Chile, as the institution responsible for ensuring, as our organic law indicates, the stability of the currency and the continuity of internal and external payments. 1. Objectives of the two Policy Frameworks and how they fit into the BCCh's Institutional Strategy The Central Bank of Chile develops its monetary policy with a combination of rules, transparency and institutional autonomy, expressed in a conceptual framework of inflation targeting. This was initially declared in 1990 and fully adopted from September 1999, together with a flexible exchange rate regime. With regard to its financial policy, the Central Bank seeks to contribute, within its sphere of competence, to the stability of the system through the assessment of financial risks, as well as the direct and indirect generation of regulations. Both functions share wide spaces of complementarity. Central Bank of Chile March 2020 After twenty years of application, the inflation targeting framework has demonstrated its relevance for the Chilean economy, allowing the Central Bank to manage its monetary policy independently, with inflation averaging 3.2% between 2001 and 2019, and two-year inflation expectations that have remained anchored to the 3% target for much of the last two decades. It has also allowed the country to mitigate the effects of significant external shocks, such as those observed during the global financial crisis of 2008-2009, and to face significant internal shocks, such as the earthquake and tsunami of February 2010. Today, the value of this policy framework is reflected in price stability, the anchoring of inflation expectations, and the resilience of the economy even in the face of large-scale domestic and domestic shocks. For its part, the Chilean financial system has gained coverage, depth and stability as a result of a development of a regulatory framework that has been able to respond to the country's needs and identify and mitigate new sources of risk. With this, the financial system has contributed to raising the competitiveness and resilience of the economy, and avoided financial crises originating not only in the country itself, but in other latitudes. The document "The Monetary Policy of the Central Bank of Chile" corresponds to an update of the document published in January 2007. Like its previous version, it presents the institutional framework within which monetary policy operates, the Council's vision of the policy framework, including its objectives, the conduct and operation of monetary policy, and the role of transparency and communications. The Council considered it appropriate to provide an update of this document, in order to reflect the experience accumulated in the two decades of operation of the inflation targeting framework, the institutional developments that have been implemented in this and other areas of economic policy and the lessons learned from the experience of other countries. With this, it cooperates in facilitating the understanding by society and economic agents of the rationality of monetary policy decisions. The document "Financial Policy of the Central Bank of Chile" presents the conceptual framework and institutional context in which financial policy operates, as well as the analysis methodology required for its conduct and implementation. It also includes the role played by transparency and communication of the diagnosis of the state of the financial system and, when applicable, the policy decisions of the Council. This seeks to systematize the framework within which the BCCh makes its contribution to the objective of safeguarding the country's financial stability. While financial stability has always been one of the fundamental objectives of the BCCh, financial policy has been modernized and brought into line with international best practices over the past decade, a trend seen in several countries following the global financial crisis of the late 2000s. The Council considered the publication of this document appropriate, given that the institutional framework for the regulation and supervision of the financial system has undergone important changes in Chile, including the expansion of macroprudential policy instruments. The preparation of these documents is part of the Strategic Plan 2018-2022 adopted by the Bank and includes recommendations of the Independent Evaluation Panel that the Bank's Board invited to evaluate the institution's performance in fulfilling its two main institutional mandates. The Institutional strategy includes as its first focus "Strengthening the Bank's response capacity and intellectual leadership to meet the institutional objectives defined in its Constitutional Organic Law, incorporating the reality of an increasingly complex environment." In particular, it states that "The Bank must be able to strengthen the application of the inflation targeting framework in a changing macroeconomic context. Central Bank of Chile March 2020 both externally and internally. Similarly, we must be able to identify, monitor and mitigate risks to financial stability in a market characterized by high dynamism and globalization. Moreover, we must be able to understand the interactions, complementarities and tensions that occur between these two areas. To do this, we must consolidate and develop analytical capabilities in long-term aspects and challenges in macroeconomic and financial issues, which will allow us to consolidate intellectual leadership in the community of central banks, especially in emerging countries." For its part, the Independent Evaluation Panel, made up of five leading economists, was consulted to review the Bank's independence, the influence and impact of its policy actions, the adequacy of its policy framework, and the policy tools to achieve its price stability and financial objectives; the effectiveness of your organization, procedures, and policy tools for those objectives, and the quality of your communications. After 12 months of intense work in the field and interviews with observers and protagonists of the Bank's recent management, including the former presidents who are with us today and whom we thank for their willingness, the Panel indicated that this is " a high-quality and very professional Central Bank," whose "analysis and conduct of policy meet high standards, comparable to inflation-targeting central banks in advanced economies." At the same time, the Panel made 40 recommendations, 22 of them related to monetary policy, 13 to financial policy and five to general corporate issues or legal issues outside the scope of the Board. These recommendations include strengthening the monetary policy decision-making process, expanding the instruments to respond to larger shocks, leveling the functions linked to financial stability, and improving communications and transparency. These recommendations were incorporated into the preparation of the framework documents that we present today, so that, six months after receiving the Panel's Report, we have complied with about half of its recommendations. With these advances, based on a solid foundation, the BCCh should be placed within the group of central banks with the highest standards of transparency and effectiveness in the world. 2. Brief description of the monetary policy framework document and its differences from the 2007 document As I mentioned earlier, the Monetary Policy Framework document reflects the structure of the document published in 2007. This begins with a detailed description of the legal and institutional framework in which the Central Bank operates as an autonomous body, with a legal mandate that gives it "to ensure the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments", and the powers and instruments it has to achieve its objective. The document discusses how the objective of price stability translates in practice into the maintenance of low, stable and predictable inflation over time. Subsequently, the document discusses in detail the main components of the inflation targeting scheme and flexible exchange rate, which for two decades the Central Bank has used as the conceptual framework to conduct monetary policy. This scheme translates into an operating target of projected inflation over a horizon of up to 2 years to be 3%. This commitment guides the expectations of economic agents and transforms the inflation target into the nominal anchor of the economy. The paper discusses how the choice of a 3% target derives from an analysis of the advantages and disadvantages of other possible levels. Inflation of 3% is low enough to be a source of stability that reduces uncertainty Central Bank of Chile March 2020 and increase growth and welfare, and at the same time facilitates the adjustment of relative prices and is at a sufficient distance from the zero limit on the nominal rate. The document argues that the horizon of up to 2 years established for the inflation target, recognizes the lags with which monetary policy affects activity and prices, and reduces product volatility, limiting the effects of transitory fluctuations on inflation. It also argues about the importance of exchange rate flexibility, which allows the exchange rate to adjust in the presence of real shocks, reducing the risk of sustained deviations in relative prices. Under the floating scheme, the BCCh reserves the option of intervening in the exchange market in exceptional circumstances, with the aim of limiting overreactions in that market that may jeopardize the BCCh's price stability and payment objectives, but never having as its final objective a specific level of the exchange rate. This section ends with a discussion of the central role of transparency and communication in an inflation targeting scheme, in which future inflation expectations are key in determining contemporary inflation developments. The ability to convey the rationality of the inflation projection, and how the BCCh's response, is essential to the credibility of the BCCh's policy and commitment to price stability. The following sections of the paper discuss the operation of monetary policy, both in terms of the decision-making process and the instruments with which it is implemented. Regarding decision-making, the document summarizes the logistics of monetary policy meetings in which the value of the monetary policy rate is determined, and the central importance of projections of future inflation, generated by statistical and economic models that are complemented by elements of judgment of the staff and the Council. in the discussion on possible monetary policy options and in the final vote of the Council. In this process, information once again plays a key role in increasing the effectiveness of monetary policy. This is reflected in the documents associated with the conduct of monetary policy, such as the official Council communiqu8e, the minutes of the monetary policy meeting and the Monetary Policy Report. This entire section covers changes to the frequency, structure and communication of monetary policy decisions since the end of 2017. The document also explains how the Central Bank executes its monetary policy by influencing the daily interbank interest rate, that is, the rate at which banks grant loans to each other, from one day to the next (overnight). The BCCh conducts its monetary policy by controlling the supply of liquidity or monetary base, so that the resulting interest rate is located around the monetary policy rate. Thus, the monetary policy rate corresponds to the interbank rate target that the BCCh wants to achieve. The document also discusses in detail the instruments with which the Bank affects this interbank rate through liquidity management. In its last section, the document emphasizes the importance of transparency and the Central Bank's communication policy, and addresses in detail all the instruments and publications with which the Bank informs the public of its work. This new document does not represent a break with respect to what was proposed in the document proposed in 2007, nor does it change the fundamentals of the way of doing monetary policy. This new version updates the previous document to reflect the experience accumulated in more than a decade and the lessons that the Bank learned in that time, as well as the natural evolution that the monetary policy scheme has experienced based on what has been learned and the changes that the Chilean and world economy has experienced. In that sense, I want to emphasize three examples of updating practices that translate into elements that in this version have a different emphasis than they had in the document of the last decade. Central Bank of Chile March 2020 First, this paper emphasizes more strongly how, while maintaining a focus on stable inflation, monetary policy can also be an important countercyclical tool. This role is especially relevant in the case of small and open economies such as Chile's, since many of the shocks that affect it require changes in relative prices to rearrange productive factors and demand between sectors, a process that is facilitated when monetary policy responds adequately through the management of the interest rate. and allowing the exchange rate to move quickly to its equilibrium value. The countercyclical role of monetary policy is enhanced by the existence of a flexible exchange rate regime, which facilitates the adjustment of an economy against shocks by allowing movements in relative prices, and by the credibility of the Bank's inflation target. Secondly, the document makes explicit that the range of between 2 and 4% ceases to be a parameter of the inflation targeting framework, emphasizing the operational objective of monetary policy, this being the one that projected inflation is located at 3% per year over a horizon of up to 2 years. While it is true that the range was mentioned as one of the parameters that defined the inflation targeting regime in the past, in practice it has not played a role in the decision-making process to set the MPR in the last decade. In this sense, the fact that inflation was outside the range of 2% to 4% did not determine that the reaction of monetary policy has been mechanically more intense. The latter depends on the elements that affect projected inflation, such as the nature and persistence of shocks, the initial state of the economy, and the evolution of inflation expectations. This does not mean that the range of 2 to 4% will disappear, but in the new document it is limited to the area where it makes the most sense: the evaluation of the effectiveness of monetary policy. Thus, the objective of projected inflation at 3% per year for around two years implies that inflation should fluctuate most of the time between the aforementioned values, as it has indeed done. Third, this paper discusses in much greater detail the interaction between monetary policy and financial policy. Both policies are interdependent, and play a central role for the two objectives sought by the Central Bank. On the one hand, the monetary policy framework based on an inflation-targeting regime with a flexible exchange rate contributes to overall macroeconomic stability, thereby facilitating the achievement of the financial stability objective. On the other hand, the financial system has a central role in the transmission of monetary policy which requires that changes in the monetary policy rate be transferred to the rest of the market rates. An unstable financial system can hinder this transfer and thus put price stability at risk. 4. Brief description of the financial framework document The financial sector plays a fundamental role in the economy, as it allows the flow of resources to more efficient uses, thus contributing to the welfare and development of the country. While each participant in the system is driven by individual goals, there is a common and shared interest that is their stability. As a BCCh, we believe that financial stability exists when the financial system performs its functions normally, or without relevant disruptions, even in the face of adverse temporary situations. In this context, the second part of our mandate to "ensure the normal functioning of internal and external payments" is an implicit reference to safeguarding financial stability, since a significant disruption in the financial system can mean the loss of the normal functioning of payments. Preserving financial stability is a complex and wide-ranging task, so it cannot be addressed by a single institution. That is why in Chile, the Ministry of Finance, the CMF, the Superintendency of Pensions The Central Bank of Chile March 2020 and the BCCh contribute to the fulfillment of this objective from their respective roles, functions, and legal attributions. The distribution of powers among the above-mentioned institutions has allowed interest in the proper functioning of the financial system to be part of the nature of all of them. Indeed, our economic and financial institutions have fostered strong and efficient coordination and cooperation mechanisms between these entities, which are essential to avoid blind areas, over-regulation or regulatory arbitrage. In particular, the BCCh fulfills its legal responsibilities by enhancing collaboration with the entities in charge of financial supervision, without interfering in the fulfillment of their respective functions. In this context, for example, the BCCh affects certain matters of financial regulation, relevant from a macro-financial perspective, but does not participate in supervisory processes exercised exclusively by the CMF, the Superintendency of Pensions and other supervisory entities. Among the institutional coordination mechanisms available in Chile, it is especially relevant to highlight the Financial Stability Board (FSB) and the preparation of previous reports in the process of generating standards. In the first place, the CEF institutionalizes the permanent commitment to share and discuss risk assessments on the financial system, this instance enshrined in Law No. 20,789 of 2014, has as its purpose the effective coordination between authorities. From its role as permanent advisor to this body chaired by the Minister of Finance, the BCCh has actively collaborated in the monitoring of systemic risks. Our prospective vision allows us to identify macro-financial risks and detect vulnerabilities that may be developing in our system. In the CEF we have suggested regulatory and legal changes to deal with the accumulation of risks, contributing to the articulation of responses to episodes of financial stress. Secondly, the so-called "advance reports" basically consist of the obligation of the body empowered to issue a regulation to request the prior opinion of another body. This mechanism is part of a tradition of collaboration and articulation between the BCCh and supervisors, where one of the guiding criteria has been the best international practices adapted to the local reality. This is how the current prudential regulatory framework considers our opinion in sensitive matters for financial stability such as: the determination of hybrid capital instruments; the regulation applicable to risk-weighted assets; methodology and determination of capital charges for systemic banks; the adoption of operating rules for central counterparties, clearing houses and securities settlement; and on limits on investment abroad, exchange coverage and alternative assets, for insurance companies and pension funds. In all the cases mentioned, with the exception of the pension fund regulations, the regulator and supervisor is the CMF and therefore it is the institution requesting this report. Similarly, the law requires Prior Reports from the CMF and other regulators in the process of issuing standards entrusted to the BCCh. This institutional framework is part of the content addressed in the financial policy document. This is the first record in our history that reflects on our role in the caution of financial stability and delves into how we execute our Financial Policy within the perimeter of our legal powers. Within these faculties, I highlight the management of critical infrastructure such as the RTGS system, regulatory attributions, macroprudential tools, in addition to our role as advisor to the Executive Branch and the CEF in matters related to our functions. We also participate in regularization mechanisms Central Bank of Chile Early March 2020 through our role as lender of last resort to the banking sector and we have broad powers in international foreign exchange operations. The exercise of our powers is based on the framework of analysis developed by our Financial Policy Division, which broadly consists of the monitoring, investigation and evaluation of all the risks to which the different components of the financial system are exposed, especially the banking sector, payment systems, financial market infrastructures, non-bank credit intermediaries and institutional investors. The process of assessing the state of the financial system begins with the identification of those risks that may materialize in the face of shocks that have the potential to generate important changes in the sector. The impact of these shocks will depend on the intrinsic characteristics and situation of the financial system, i.e. its vulnerabilities and mitigators. On the one hand, vulnerabilities are those conditions of the financial system, or of agents that participate in it, that weaken its ability to face a shock or have the capacity to amplify its effects. For example, a high level of corporate indebtedness can be seen as vulnerable to an economic slowdown. On the other hand, mitigators are those elements that tend to contain the impacts of a shock. For example, a regulatory framework and market practices that keep banks with healthy capital ratios and an adequate level of provisions. Based on the above analysis, the state of the financial system is determined. At this point we distinguish four states: stable, vulnerable, unstable and crisis situation. The stage of stability or normality is one in which the identified vulnerabilities are limited and there is a constant development of mitigators that determine a limited risk scenario. While less stable states are characterized by the presence of vulnerabilities that have the potential to amplify the impact of a disruptive event. In an extreme case, the financial system could find itself in a crisis scenario, understood as the materialization of systemic risk. The materialization of this scenario could have the consequence of hindering the normal functioning of the components of the financial system. This framework of analysis allows us to prepare a diagnosis of the situation of the financial system. This diagnosis is the basis for the conduct of our financial policy and, consequently, for all decisions regarding the implementation of the different actions allowed by our legal framework. Under a normal scenario, preventive actions are taken, for example, continuous monitoring of a prospective nature, we manage our regulatory powers to help keep the financial system stable, we warn of potential vulnerabilities and risks, and we manage the macroprudential policy tools we have. In the event that there is a shift towards scenarios of greater vulnerability, financial policy will seek to increase the resilience of the system and mitigate possible impacts. In these circumstances, in addition to the policy actions used in normal scenarios, specific tools can be used, such as, for example, activating or deactivating the countercyclical capital requirement, providing liquidity facilities or applying restrictions for international exchange operations. In case of observing the materialization of systemic risk scenarios, the purpose of our financial policy will be to help the administration of the crisis with all the legal powers that we have. For example, we execute our role as lender of last resort. The analysis, conduction and implementation of our financial policy has a technical and independent seal which is communicated transparently and periodically to the entire community. In this context, our main channels of disclosure are the Financial Stability Report (FSR), explanatory minutes and Central Bank of Chile March 2020 research, publication and issuance of regulations, regulatory compendiums, and both internal and external presentations that the members of the Board and senior executives of the BCCh make to different stakeholders. Likewise, we comply with the legal provisions on Access to Public Information, Probity in Public Function, Lobbying and Management of Private Interests. Here I would like to delve into the IEF. This biannual communication document contributes to the understanding of the financial system and its potential risks. It provides the public with a technical and rigorous analysis of the state of the financial system and, in turn, disseminates the results of the research agenda developed by the BCCh related to these issues. This report presents the analysis of the monitoring carried out during the semester to the national and international financial market, credit users and the banking system, as well as the capacity of the financial system to adapt to adverse economic situations, posing vulnerabilities and risks, exposing mitigators and suggesting policies. In this way, the document "Financial Policy of the Central Bank of Chile" is in itself an exercise in transparency that seeks to show the entire community of ours what to do and contribute to the financial stability of our country. 5. Relevance of monetary and financial policy frameworks in stress scenarios Having understood the meaning of the monetary and financial policy framework documents and explained their main contents, it is worth asking about their usefulness at times such as the one we are experiencing. After all, we are making this presentation at a time when far-reaching internal and external tensions are coming together. In the course of this day, the main stock exchanges of the world have had falls of between 5% and 10%, which accumulate to falls of the previous days, as a result of the alarm over the expansion of COVID-19, the restrictions on activity imposed by control measures, the oil price war and a generalized overturn in risk appetite in financial markets. With this, we have seen sharp changes in the prices of currencies and financial assets that affect emerging economies, including Chile. What is the point of having policy frameworks for monetary and financial policy in this context? First, having applied these frameworks disciplined over the years creates greater space for appropriate policy responses. It is very different to face this situation with stable inflation, low exposure to exchange risk, a deep capital market and a solid financial system. Today there are many countries that face global turbulence with severe restrictions on some of these levels. Fortunately, Chile is not one of them. Second, these frameworks allow policy decisions to be made with greater certainty about their effectiveness. This occurs either because the operation of shock absorbers complements policy actions or because the transmission of them is more effective. In this regard, it highlights the role of floating exchange rates in cushioning external shocks and the relevance of a sound financial system for the effective transmission of monetary policy. Third, the medium-term perspective that characterizes Chile's monetary and financial policy frameworks helps minimize potential conflicts between objectives. In this regard, it highlights the value of a medium-term inflation target to avoid excessive volatility of policy decisions and to reconcile price stability with stability of economic activity. The value of this target is strengthened in the monetary policy framework document by limiting the meaning of the so-called "target range" from a normative dimension, to a reference for the subsequent evaluation of the effectiveness of monetary policy. This is reinforced Central Bank of Chile March 2020 by focusing near-term inflation monitoring on a measure of core inflation, which excludes more volatile and less persistent price fluctuations. In the field of financial policy, something similar happens with the prospective risk assessment, which makes it possible to warn economic agents and regulators of their presence. A good example of this has been the systematic reduction in exposure to exchange risk that the Chilean economy has been experiencing for several decades. This is how the regulatory restrictions to the mismatch change in financial institutions has been added to the development of hedging mechanisms. This is what makes it possible to avoid that even in a context of significant devaluation of the peso, as in 2014 and today, it generates large costs for economic agents and risks for financial stability. Finally, these monetary and financial policy frameworks do not seek to impose a straitjacket on the Bank's actions, which could limit the possibility of articulating exceptional measures in exceptional situations. Thus, in recent months the Bank has applied extraordinary measures to reduce volatility and ensure liquidity to reduce the impact of portfolio adjustments in the face of a significant increase in uncertainty. This has protected the process of price formation, payment flows and access to credit. To this end, the Bank has resorted to options provided for in the policy frameworks themselves or in its Organic Law. This does not mean, by the way, that the Chilean economy can emerge unscathed from shocks as important as those observed today. It would be irresponsible to give a sense of total immunity, especially when part of the shocks have an internal origin. However, we can assure that the Bank has instruments to respond to new challenges facing the country and that its Board has the will and willingness to use them according to their potential effectiveness, the nature of the problems they face, and the well-being of Chileans. That is why, by presenting these documents, we can tell the country that it can expect honesty, professionalism and decisiveness from us, both in normal moments and in times of tension. This is because the Central Bank of Chile does not work for narrow economic interests, nor for a political sector, nor for a certain model, but for the country as a whole. This is the true meaning of our autonomy. The documents we are presenting today are a good demonstration of the exercise of this exercise. Thanks a lot.

Ellos expresan, en consecuencia, un esfuerzo por fortalecer la credibilidad y confianza en el Banco Central de Chile, como la institucin responsable de asegurar, como lo seala nuestra ley orgnica, la estabilidad de la moneda y la continuidad de pagos internos y externos. 1. Objetivos de los dos Marcos de Poltica y cmo se enmarcan en la Estrategia Institucional del BCCh El Banco Central de Chile desarrolla su poltica monetaria con una combinacin de reglas, transparencia y autonoma institucional, expresado en un marco conceptual de metas de inflacin. Este fue declarado inicialmente en 1990 y adoptado en plenitud a partir de septiembre de 1999, junto con un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible. En cuanto a su poltica financiera, el Banco Central procura contribuir, desde su mbito de competencia, a la estabilidad del sistema mediante la evaluacin de riesgos financieros, as como la generacin, directa e indirecta de regulaciones. Ambas funciones comparten amplios espacios de complementariedad. Banco Central de Chile Marzo 2020 Tras veinte aos de aplicacin, el marco de metas de inflacin ha demostrado su relevancia para la economa chilena, permitiendo al Banco Central manejar su poltica monetaria de manera independiente, con una inflacin que promedi 3,2% entre 2001 y 2019, y expectativas de inflacin a dos aos plazo que se han mantenido ancladas a la meta de 3% durante gran parte de las ltimas dos dcadas. Hoy en da el valor de este marco de poltica se refleja en la estabilidad de precios, el anclaje de expectativas de inflacin y la resiliencia de la economa an frente a shocks internos e internos de gran magnitud.
