Then, I will carry out an analysis of economic events, in the context of the medium-term scenarios that the Central Bank develops and maintains. Finally, I will make an analysis of the prospects of our economy in the current conjuncture. O objectives and roles of the Central Bank The Constitutional Organic Law of the Central Bank establishes that its objective is "to ensure the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments." Controlling inflation is the means by which monetary policy contributes to the well-being of the population. Low and stable inflation promotes a better functioning economy and higher economic growth, while preventing the erosion of people's incomes, which is especially important for the poorest. The effects that monetary policy can have on economic activity and employment in the short and medium term arise from the different channels through which its changes are transmitted to affect inflation. Monetary policy cannot influence long-term growth beyond its contribution to price stability. However, this policy follows a countercyclical approach that also seeks to avoid extreme variations in domestic spending and output, which can cause unnecessary risks in the financial market, such as recession and unemployment. In other words, the Central Bank seeks to achieve its main objective in the most efficient way possible, from a growth and employment perspective. Thus, in periods of recession, the policy interest rate, compatible with a certain level of inflation, is lower than in periods of economic boom. To be sure, the Bank has been very successful in its inflation targeting. Recall that at the beginning of the nineties, annual inflation reached almost 30% and for this year a variation in the consumer price index (CPI) is expected to be around 2.5% (graph 1). Very important in this process was the autonomy granted to the Central Bank in 1989, which has made it possible to reduce inflation to levels comparable to those of developed economies, with a credibility that is essential for the achievement of its objective of price stability. Today, the Chilean economy is more mature in terms of the mix of macroeconomic policies, which combines an inflation targeting scheme, a floating exchange rate regime, integration into international financial markets and a fiscal policy subject to rules, starting in 2000. This has meant for the government to orient fiscal policy, following a pre-announced rule based on the achievement of a structural surplus of 1% of gross domestic product (GDP). All this creates a favorable environment of high credibility of the institutions where the anti-inflationary will of the Central Bank is not discussed and economic agents expect that inflation will be controlled and will remain at reduced levels within the established range of 2% to 4%, permanently. Now, if I were to ask what variable the discussion focuses on today, there would be agreement in affirming that it is economic growth. This is the main concern because, despite the stability achieved, we have not been able to resume high growth. In addition, the expectations of the actors have been successively affected by various events, internal and external, of a rather negative nature. If we review our recent history in terms of growth, we observe that between 1986 and 1997, our country grew on average at 7.6% (system of national accounts based on 1986) and ranked fourth among 148 countries considered by the IMF as emerging economies. However, the country has not been immune to the wave of international crises since the late nineties. Economic growth has suffered and Chile experienced its first recession in a long time in 1999. In recent years, the actual growth of the product has been lower than expected, both by the authorities of G obierno and by the different analysts of the market. Overall, growth and aggregate spending projections have had to be continuously modified. The magnitude of these revisions has varied according to the source, but all have been consistently downward (tables 1 and 2). So what explains the low growth in the period 1998-2001? The hypotheses raised by some studies1 on the subject, consider that this poor performance can be attributed to the external shocks of this period that meant a fall in terms of trade2 of approximately 10% in 1998 and more than 8% in 2001. Only for this year is expected a maintenance with respect to 2001. It was also a period in which there were lower inflows of external capital, among others. On the domestic front, other arguments put forward are related to a contractionary monetary policy, associated with situations of excess spending in the economy, ups and downs of fiscal policy and changes in labor institutions. Another cause can be attributed to the fact that there are many institutions still weak in relevant sectors such as health and education, the financial system and the public sector, among others. This argument is based on the fact that the poor economic performance of recent years compared to much of the nineties may reflect diminishing returns on the growth rate of economic reforms implemented in the past. This would force us to be increasingly creative in order to achieve greater impulses for growth, since the mere maintenance of the reforms of the past, although a necessary condition, is not enough, nor is a process of change without clear horizons and goals. As you can see, there may be several hypotheses that explain this situation, but the fundamental thing is to do what is necessary so that we grow again close to our potential product. This is defined as the highest level of output that can be achieved, given the stock of capital, technology and population volume, without accelerating the trajectory of inflation. The estimation of potential GDP, as an indicator of the economic capacity of a country, allows us to have an approximation of the expected evolution of the economy, orienting, therefore, the ways of implementing macroeconomic policies to bring as close as possible the effective behavior to the estimated potential. All this, while maintaining price stability, which is the main objective of a central bank. I think it is very important to mention as well, the role of financial markets in economic growth. The quality of a country's financial infrastructure directly affects its economic growth potential, as it fulfils fundamental functions in a market economy: (1) it provides the means of payment for transactions, (2) it facilitates the accumulation of people's savings, (3) it mobilizes financial resources towards the new ideas that drive growth, (4) monitors the efficiency of its administration and (5) delivers the instruments 1 El Crecimiento Econ97mico de Chile, Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel and Francisco Gallego, 2002, Banco Central de Chile. 2 Relationship between average import and export prices for traded goods and services. to mitigate the risk of families and businesses. The effectiveness of fulfilling all these functions has a direct impact on the growth of the economy, the breadth of its cycles and its ability to adjust to a constantly changing global environment. The Chilean economy has relatively deep financial markets relative to countries with comparable incomes and even higher than ours. For example, the volume of bank credit in our country reaches 70% of GDP, the highest in Latin America and, above the world average, comparable with countries such as Spain. However, modernization challenges remain. To conclude this introduction, I would like to highlight the importance of economic information and the relevance of its transparency and timeliness for the effectiveness of monetary policy. Since May 2000, the Central Bank of Chile has published, every four months, its Monetary Policy Report (IPoM), which is presented to the Senate Finance Committee. The main objectives of this publication are to inform and explain the Council's view on recent and expected inflation developments and their implications for the conduct of monetary policy. It also contributes to the formation of market expectations by providing information on the future trajectory of inflation and output. Likewise, the summary minutes of the minutes of the monthly monetary policy sessions with a lag of three months are published, which includes the identification of the vote. Certainly, these two elements have been fundamental from the perspective of transparency and efficiency in the conduct of monetary policy. Economic scenarios 2002-2003 Economic events usually have several causes. These generate policy responses whose effects take some time to fully manifest. Some of these events are motivated by external factors, while others are more determined by internal conditions. In turn, the reasons for the current situation are manifested aspects of the functioning of the economy in the short and medium term, since demand stimuli go hand in hand with changes in the allocation of resources. The causes, policy reactions and their consequences in the current situation can be summarized in the following facts that have characterized the performance of our economy during the first half of 2002: - At the international level, although the prospects for growth in the world economy and a gradual recovery of the terms of trade expected in the May IPoM have been maintained so far, factors have emerged that make up a scenario of greater risk in the global growth outlook. - Some trading partners in the region continue to deteriorate sharply in their performance. This has generated greater financial uncertainty, which may have more prolonged effects on investment flows to the region in general, and Chile in particular. - Internally, the scenario has been characterized by a product that has had a moderate rate of growth in the first months of the year, with a gradual recovery of levels. Domestic demand has also recovered from the levels at the end of last year, but at a slower pace than expected. This poor performance of domestic spending has been partially offset by higher-than-expected growth in the export sector, which has meant that the GDP trajectory is not substantially different from what was anticipated. The trend in domestic expenditure, however, suggests growth rates lower than those contained in the central scenario described in the latest Monetary Policy Report over the coming quarters. - The maintenance of inflation at limited levels that do not represent risk factors has allowed the Central Bank to steadily increase its monetary impulse over the last seven months, favouring a more dynamic path of activity. Going forward, inflation is expected to converge to the center of the target range over the usual policy horizon. In short, we believe that the future developments of the aforementioned factors, referring to the solidity of the recovery of the world economy, the resolution of economic, political and social conflicts in important countries in the region and the strength of the recovery of domestic demand, are key factors in the future evolution of our country. World economy Since the global slowdown that began in mid-2000, the world's major economies have followed a path of recovery in activity levels during the first half of 2002. The global situation continues the expected course of acceleration in growth, this time with news showing that Asia is entering a phase of greater dynamism, offsetting the performance of other areas. The most likely evolution of commodity prices continues in line with expectations in the May IPoM. The risks of this scenario, however, have become increasingly asymmetric: the danger of terrorism, the problems in the Middle East and the recent evolution of the stock markets, explained by the financial scandals in large US companies, point to alternative scenarios of lower activity and/or greater risk aversion on the part of investors. Japan's growth projections have been revised upwards, while the European zone remains stable, with prospects for recovery in the coming year. This backdrop supports a scenario in which the world economy recovers gradually over the course of 2002 and stronger in 2003. It should be noted that consensus global growth projections, weighted at purchasing power parity (PPP), are 2.8 percent for 2002 and 3.9 percent for 2003 (Table 3). In recent weeks, international financial markets have shown a more persistently depreciating dollar, an especially negative trajectory of stock markets, particularly in the United States, and falling long-term interest rates. The effects of these events on the Chilean economy will depend on the evolution of international financial markets in the coming months. Indeed, the impact of possible lower levels of activity in advanced countries must be compared with changes in the cost and flows of financing to emerging economies, as well as with the response of export prices to changes in parities and possible lower levels of global activity. However, it is still too early to determine the magnitude of these effects and their impact on our economy. The prospects for a more favorable trajectory of the international scenario with respect to previous years are expressed in the evolution of the prices of our exports. For this year, only a slight increase in the price of copper is expected, to be around US 0.73 per pound, with a further increase towards 2003 and 2004. So far, this development is offset by projections of higher oil prices (Chart 2). This means that the terms of trade will remain at average levels similar to those of last year this year, to rebound by around 4% annual average during 2003 (Chart 3). Regional situation The second key factor for the future of our economy is the regional situation. Unfortunately, we have had negative surprises, because the regional situation has deteriorated markedly. For the second consecutive year, Latin America's output will remain virtually stagnant in 2002. We began to be affected by the Argentine situation last year, and recently Brazil is the biggest focus of concern. For some weeks, the coupling of domestic financial variables with Brazil's risk has increased, which, although relatively intense, has allowed national financial and price stability to remain in compatible ranges. In general terms, regional risks appear as asymmetric, especially due to the evolution of the political situation in some countries such as Peru, Colombia, Venezuela, Bolivia, apart from those already known in Brazil and Argentina. Next, we will analyze the most relevant effects of the regional scenario, focused on the latter two countries because they are the most important with respect to Latin America. We will see the effects of transmission through financial markets, trade flows and equity changes of Chilean companies with investments in neighboring countries. I want to emphasize, in any case, that there is a considerable consensus among national and international analysts that the Latin American neighborhood is one of the ones with the greatest uncertainty and worse performances in the current world situation. Foreign trade is one of the variables in which the adverse effects of the regional crisis are expressed. All exports to Argentina fell by about 60%, and the flow of tourists fell by about half in the first quarter of 2002. An annual and combined projection of these two effects shows that they have a direct impact of around 0.3 percentage points on GDP growth in 2002, an effect that increases to approximately 0.5 if indirect effects are considered (Table 4). In the past, the export sector has shown considerable flexibility, so the effects on trade can be expected to be transitory, to the extent that other markets (internal or external) for these products or services can be found. Although for now imports from Argentina have not shown significant increases, it is not ruled out that the depreciation of the Argentine peso will encourage greater flows of goods from that country. In the case of Brazil, the trade effects are more limited. Industrial exports in 2001 were equivalent to 0.5% of GDP, while in the case of Argentina these exports were 0.7% of GDP. In addition, about 75% of Chilean exports to Brazil have the capacity to be destined for other markets. This is so, since the vast majority of exports to Brazil are mining (50%), and a high probability of redestination is also applied to a large part of the other exports (Table 5). In the case of exports to Argentina, only 50% could be redirected. Finally, the magnitude of the fall in Brazil's exports will probably be lower than that of Argentina, and may even take place in a period of better global environment. Given that the commercial effect of the Brazilian crisis is much smaller and limited, we can say that the main impact would be expressed through the financial markets, as we have recently observed. As with the worsening of Argentina's situation in the second half of 2001, the foreign exchange market has reacted to increased uncertainty in Brazil, producing a nominal depreciation of around 8 per cent of the Chilean peso since the end of April (Figure 4). At the same time, in international financial markets, the spread on Chilean external debt instruments has increased by around 80 basis points over the same period (Chart 5). In any case, this increase so far does not seem particularly worrying. The main reason is that, apart from remaining at historically satisfactory levels, so far their increase has not translated into a significant increase in external financing costs, because in the last two months there has been a significant decrease in the medium and long-term yield of US treasury papers. partially offsetting the increases in spreads. It is also reassuring that the increase in the Chilean spread is associated more with a generalized increase in risk aversion associated with emerging countries than with a specific effect of Brazil's situation on Chile's credit risk. This is reflected in the fact that Chilean spreads have not been punished more than those of other emerging countries, outside the American continent. Part of these financial effects are due to unexpected portfolio adjustments of companies and investors, which are usually of some transitory nature. However, there is also a part that could become more durable as financial flows to the region as a whole suffer, more than they already have. In the projection scenarios that the Central Bank has considered most likely, there has been a conservative view of capital flows to emerging economies. In any case, the materialization of the trade agreement with the European Union could give a positive boost to this type of investment in the medium term. A third effect of the region's economic difficulties is expressed in capital losses and the performance status of companies that have invested in neighboring economies. This effect is reflected in the stock prices and spreads of corporate debt, all of which translates into a lower income-generating capacity of these companies. In the case of Argentina alone, the decline in profits earned from investments in that country was estimated to directly affect national income in 2002 by about 0.2 per cent of GDP. In the case of investments in Brazil, these effects would have a substantially smaller magnitude. Where the Brazilian crisis could have differentiated and more adverse regional effects is in the behavior of capital flows and stock prices. Capital flows for equity acquisitions in Latin America have been steadily declining since May 2002. Similarly, according to the Institute for International Finance, gross flows to the region declined from the monthly average of U S 4 billion in the period January-April 2002 to almost zero in May 2002 (Figure 6). A similar behavior is showing net portfolio investment to and from Chile. I would like to emphasize that Brazil has an important advantage over Argentina, as its economy is better prepared to adapt to changes. First, the floating exchange rate regime implies a more gradual and efficient adjustment mechanism than under a convertibility regime. Second, the financial system and the productive sectors have better natural coverage through financial instruments that cover exchange rate risks. As an example of this, it should be noted that, after the average depreciation of 57% of this currency in 1999, the financial market maintained a solid position. It should be remembered that Brazil is a relatively more closed, large economy, which suggests that exchange rate movements have fewer domestic impacts, compared to countries such as Argentina or Uruguay. However, we must not underestimate the effect of financial changes in the dynamics of the debt that this economy could suffer. Internal situation The third determining factor of the future evolution of our economy is related to domestic factors. In 2001, we saw a sharp contraction in domestic demand, especially in the second half of the year. Part of this phenomenon was due to factors that proved transitory, such as the September attacks and the crisis in Argentina. Although the fall in the most sensitive components of domestic demand, such as inventories, durable consumption and investment in machinery, was partially reversed in the first months of this year, this recovery has moderated considerably in the most recent (Chart 7). Similarly, the more stable components of expenditure, in particular regular consumption, which grew relatively steadily during 2001, have slowed sharply in recent months (Chart 8). There are a number of factors that allow hypotheses to be made regarding the low dynamism of domestic spending in recent months. First, recent years have seen a marked decline in private expectations for medium-term growth, which directly affects permanent income growth. Second, consumer confidence remains low. Although the available measurements reflect a reversal of the pessimism observed in the third quarter of last year, they are still at depressed levels compared to the average of previous years. Third, the incipient dynamism seen in job creation since the middle of last year, especially in the private sector, excluding government employment programmes, has stalled during the second quarter of this year (Figure 9). In particular, employment in industry and commerce, which pushed employment growth towards the end of 2001, has fallen in absolute terms. All this background has been negatively surprising. Although estimates show that a positive growth rate of expenditure and GDP was maintained during the second quarter of this year, the dynamism is lower than estimated some time ago. Spending, in particular, is clearly underperforming in the May Report, which calls into question, beyond the international situation, the strength of the recovery process in activity. Inflationary dynamics have also revealed that there are larger-than-expected gaps in goods and factor markets. In June, the CPI showed a variation of -0.1%, accumulating an annual increase of only 2.0% (graph 10). In turn, core inflation -which excludes the prices of perishable goods and fuels- had the same monthly variation, although with a growth in twelve months of 2.7%. It is possible that during some specific months, during the rest of the year, inflation in 12 months will be below 2%. More in the medium term, private expectations are around 2.5% per year, for one-year horizons, and close to 3% for two-year horizons. These perspectives show the absence of significant inflationary pressures, which has led to successive reductions in the monetary policy rate this year, from a level of 6.5% in January to 3.25% today. In addition, the greatest degree of monetary policy expansion can be seen in the interest rates of the various instruments of the Central Bank, which have reached historically low levels. Conclusions and perspectives The reductions in the monetary policy rate decreed by the Central Bank have been based on a substantial and broad decrease in the medium-term inflation outlook, which has been accompanied by lower than expected effective inflation d0 total and core d0 lower. Meanwhile, fiscal policy, in line with the countercyclical capacity of the structural surplus rule, is contributing to the boost in aggregate demand with an impact of close to 5% for 2002 as a whole, while public investment will grow by around 11%. This combination of monetary and fiscal policies is consistent with the real depreciation of the peso in recent years, which has allowed a dynamism of exports that has more than offset the effect on the volume exported of the fall in global trade. The global economy continues to expand at a similar pace to that expected in previous months, although with heterogeneity across geographies. However, the growth prospects of trading partners have suffered from the negative performance of some Latin American countries. In addition, the risks associated with the deterioration of the main stock markets have become more prominent. For its part, the financial turbulence in the region has become more significant than in previous months. Domestically, the accumulated history indicates that during the second quarter, both spending and output would have expanded compared to the immediately preceding quarter, although at a slower pace than expected in the May Monetary Policy Report. The difference is most evident in the case of spending, for which a greater acceleration was expected at this time of the year. This trajectory, added to the evolution of the international scenario, suggests lower growth rates than those contained in the Report for the coming quarters. Some of the circumstances described have conflicting inflationary implications. However, low inflation, persistent capacity gaps, and the observed low pass-through of exchange rate depreciation to prices anticipate that inflation will converge toward the center of the target range over the usual policy horizon. This is consistent with the new monetary impulse favouring a more dynamic path of activity. The current mix of macroeconomic policies, i.e. an inflation-targeting regime, floating exchange rate and the structural surplus fiscal rule, make it possible to better cushion the effects of external fluctuations. In an environment as uncertain as the current one, it is essential to inject flexibility into the markets, so that adapting to new scenarios is as inexpensive as possible. Although the Chilean economy has shown a high degree of flexibility in the past, it is always possible to increase it. In this way, additional benefits can be obtained, from the point of view of accommodating the fluctuations to which a small and open economy such as Chile's is inevitably subject. From the point of view of the functioning of markets for goods and services, the degree of competition and regulation are of particular importance. In the markets of productive factors, flexibility in the labor market and in the capital market are relevant. At present, in each of these areas, there are significant challenges expressed in the possibility of adopting structural policies, which would better prepare the economy to compete in global markets and better cope with external shocks. Finally, I think it is convenient to emphasize that the monetary policy of the Central Bank has as its main objective to keep inflation at a low and stable level, defined as a range of 2% to 4% centered on 3%, in a permanent time horizon. This objective is symmetrical, so the Council considers deviations to be harmful both above 4% and below 2%. Going forward, CPI inflation is expected to gradually converge from its current levels towards the center of the target range over the next two years. This path is consistent with a gradual acceleration in activity and spending, which is supported by recent monetary policy measures. However, as always, there are a multitude of risks, which are currently particularly asymmetrical. The Central Bank, in its May Monetary Policy Report, in its central scenario, projected inflation and economic growth with the latest available background at the time. Two months have passed since those projections, and we have seen a regional environment deteriorate markedly in addition to the string of accounting scandals in the US, along with a shadow of doubt about the speed and robustness of the growth recovery process in the developed world. Likewise, at the domestic level, the prolongation of high levels of unemployment could continue to limit the growth of consumer spending. The precise implications of these developments on the medium-term outlook are difficult to assess in the current situation, as a result of the state of flow of the international scenario, but as a whole they point to more limited growth and, probably, to lower inflationary pressures. As usual, the next Monetary Policy Report, in September this year, will contain the Council's vision by that date, on the medium-term growth and inflation outlook. It is important to note that, precisely, these are the antecedents that guide the conduct of monetary policy in the current inflation targeting scheme.
text_original: Economa Chilena: Coyuntura y Perspectivas Exposicin de la seora Mara Elena Ovalle M., Consejera del Banco Central de Chile, en el ciclo de Conferencias Regionales organizado por el Diario, en Iquioue, el 17 de julio de 2002. En esta exposicin me referir, en primer lugar, a los objetivos del Banco Central, a su relacin con el crecimiento de la economa y a la importancia de la informacin econmica que proporciona para el desarrollo de las distintas actividades del pas. Luego, realizar un anlisis de los acontecimientos econmicos, en el contexto de los escenarios de mediano plazo que elabora y mantiene el Banco Central. Finalmente, har un anlisis de las perspectivas de nuestra economa en la coyuntura actual. O bjetivos y roles del Banco Central La Ley Orgnica Constitucional del Banco Central establece que su objetivo es velar por la estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos. El control dla inflacin es el medio por el cual la poltica monetaria contribuye al bienestar de la poblacin. Una inflacin baja y estable promueve un mejor funcionamiento de la economa y un mayor crecimiento econmico, al tiempo que evita la erosin de los ingresos de las personas, lo que es especialmente importante para los ms pobres. Los efectos que la poltica monetaria puede tener sobre la actividad econmica y el empleo a corto y mediano plazo, surgen de los distintos canales, mediante los cuales se transmiten sus cambios para llegara afectarla inflacin. La poltica monetaria no puede influir sobre el crecimiento de largo plazo ms all de su contribucin a la estabilidad de precios. Sin embargo, esta poltica sigue una orientacin anticclica que busca tambin evitar las variaciones extremas del gasto interno y el producto, que pueden provocar riesgos innecesarios en el mercado financiero, como son la recesin y el desempleo. En otras palabras, el Banco Central busca conseguir su objetivo principal de la manera ms eficiente posible, desde una perspectiva de crecimiento y empleo. De este modo, en perodos de recesin, la tasa de inters de poltica, compatible con cierto nivel de inflacin es menor que en perodos de auge de la economa. Sin duda, el Banco ha sido muy exitoso en su objetivo de inflacin. Recordemos que a comienzos de los noventa, la inflacin anual llegaba casi a 30% y para este ao se espera una variacin del ndice de precios al consumidor (IPC) en torno a 2,5% (grfico 1). Fue muy importante en este proceso la autonoma otorgada al Banco Central en 1989, lo que ha permitido reducir la inflacin hasta niveles comparables a los de economas desarrolladas, con una credibilidad que es esencial para la consecucin de su objetivo de estabilidad de precios. Hoy, la economa chilena es ms madura en cuanto a la mezcla de polticas macroeconmicas, la que conjuga un esquema de metas de inflacin, un rgimen de flotacin cambiara, integracin a los mercados financieros internacionales y una poltica fiscal sujeta a reglas, a partir del 2000. Esto ha significado para el gobierno orientar la poltica fiscal, siguiendo una regla preanunciada basada en el logro de un supervit estructural de 1% del producto interno bruto (PIB). Todo ello crea un entorno favorable de alta credibilidad de las instituciones donde no se discute la voluntad antiinflacionaria del Banco Central y los agentes econmicos esperan que la inflacin estar controlada y permanecer en niveles reducidos dentro del rango establecido de 2% a 4%, en forma permanente. Ahora bien, si yo preguntara cul es la variable en la que se centra hoy la discusin, habra coincidencia en afirmar que es el crecimiento econmico. Esta es la principal preocupacin porque, pese a la estabilidad alcanzada, no hemos podido retomar un crecimiento elevado. Adems, las expectativas de los agentes se han visto sucesivamente afectadas por distintos acontecimientos, internos y externos, de ndole ms bien negativos. Si revisamos nuestra historia reciente en materia de crecimiento, observamos que entre 1986 y 1997, nuestro pas creci en promedio al 7,6% (sistema de cuentas nacionales con base 1986) y ocup un cuarto lugar entre 148 pases considerados por el FMI como economas emergentes. Sin embargo, el pas no ha sido inmune a la ola de crisis internacionales desde fines de los aos noventa. El crecimiento econmico se ha resentido y Chile experiment en 1999 su primera recesin en mucho tiempo. En los ltimos aos, el crecimiento efectivo del producto ha sido menor al esperado, tanto por las autoridades de G obierno como por los distintos analistas del mercado. En general, las proyecciones de crecimiento y gasto agregado han debido modificarse continuamente. La magnitud de estas revisiones ha variado segn la fuente, pero todas han sido sistemticamente a la baja (cuadros 1 y 2). Qu explica entonces el bajo crecimiento en el perodo 1998- 2001 ? Las hiptesis que plantean algunos estudios1 sobre el tema, consideran que este magro desempeo puede atribuirse a los shocks externos de este perodo que significaron una cada de los trminos de intercambio2 de aproximadamente 10% en el ao 1998 y ms de 8% en 2001. Recin para este ao se espera una mantencin respecto del 2001. Asimismo, se trat de un perodo en el que hubo menores influjos de capital externo, entre otros. En el frente interno, otros argumentos que se esgrimen, tienen relacin con una poltica monetaria contractiva, asociada a situaciones de exceso de gasto de la economa, altibajos de la poltica fiscal y cambios en la institucionalidad laboral. Otra de las causas puede atribuirse a que hay muchas instituciones an dbiles en sectores relevantes como salud y educacin, sistema financiero y sector pblico, entre otros. Este argumento se fundamenta en que el pobre desempeo econmico de los aos recientes respecto de gran parte de los noventa, puede ser reflejo de retornos decrecientes sobre la tasa de crecimiento de las reformas econmicas aplicadas en el pasado. Esto obligara a ser cada vez ms creativos para lograr la consecucin de mayores impulsos para el crecimiento, pues la sola mantencin de las reformas del pasado, si bien es una condicin necesaria, no es suficiente, como tampoco lo es un proceso de cambios sin horizontes y metas claras. Como se puede observar, diversas pueden ser las hiptesis que expliquen esta situacin, pero lo fundamental es hacer lo necesario para que volvamos a crecer cerca de nuestro producto potencial. Este, se define como el mayor nivel de producto que se puede alcanzar, dado el stocke capital, la tecnologa y el volumen de poblacin, sin acelerar la trayectoria de la inflacin. La estimacin del PIB potencial, como indicador de la capacidad econmica de un pas, permite disponer de una aproximacin de la evolucin esperada de la economa, orientando, por lo tanto, las formas de implementacin de las polticas macroeconmicas para acercar lo ms posible el comportamiento efectivo al potencial estimado. Todo ello, manteniendo la estabilidad de precios, que es el principal objetivo de un banco central. Creo que es muy importante mencionar tambin, el rol de los mercados financieros en el crecimiento econmico. La calidad de la infraestructura financiera de un pas afecta directamente su potencial de crecimiento econmico, pues cumple funciones fundamentales en una economa de mercado: (1) provee los medios de pagos para las transacciones, (2) facilita la acumulacin de ahorro de las personas, (3) moviliza los recursos financieros hacia las nuevas deas que impulsan el crecimiento, (4) supervisa la eficiencia de su administracin y (5) entrega los instrumentos  El Crecimiento Econmico de Chile, Klaus Schmidt-Hebbel y Francisco Gallego, 2002, Banco Central de Chile.  Relacin entre los precios promedios de importacin y de exportacin para los bienes y servicios que son objeto del intercambio. para atenuar el riesgo de las familias y las empresas. La efectividad para cumplir todas estas funciones incide directamente en el crecimiento de la economa, en la amplitud de sus ciclos y en su capacidad para ajustarse a un entorno global en permanente cambio. La economa chilena tiene mercados financieros relativamente profundos respecto de pases de ingresos comparables e incluso superiores al nuestro. Por ejemplo, el volumen del crdito bancario en nuestro pas alcanza a 70% del PIB, el mayor de Amrica Latina y, sobre el promedio mundial, comparable con pases como Espaa. Sin embargo, hay desafos de modernizacin pendientes. Para finalizar esta introduccin, me gustara destacar la importancia de la informacin econmica y lo relevante de su transparencia y oportunidad para la eficacia de la poltica monetaria. Desde mayo del 2000, el Banco Central de Chile publica, cuatrimestralmente, su Informe de Poltica Monetaria (IPoM), el cual es presentado ante la comisin de Hacienda del Senado. Los principales objetivos de esta publicacin son informar y explicar la visin del Consejo sobre la evolucin reciente y esperada de la inflacin y sus consecuencias para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Tambin contribuye a la formacin de expectativas del mercado por cuanto provee informacin sobre la trayectoria futura de la inflacin y del producto. Asimismo, se publican las minutas resumen de las actas de las sesiones mensuales de poltica monetaria con un desfase de tres meses, donde se incluye la identificacin de la votacin. Ciertamente, estos dos elementos han sido fundamentales desde la perspectiva de la transparencia y eficiencia de la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria. Escenarios econmicos 2002-2003 Los acontecimientos econmicos tienen, habitualmente, varias causas. stas generan respuestas de polticas econmicas cuyos efectos tardan algn tiempo en manifestarse plenamente. Algunos de estos hechos estn motivados por factores externos, mientras que otros estn ms determinados por condiciones internas. A su vez, en las razones de la actual coyuntura se manifiestan aspectos del funcionamiento de la economa en el corto y en el mediano plazo, ya que los estmulos de la demanda van de la mano con cambios en la asignacin de recursos. Las causas, las reacciones de poltica y sus consecuencias en la situacin actual pueden resumirse en los siguientes hechos que han caracterizado el desempeo de nuestra economa durante el primer semestre de 2002: - En el plano internacional, si bien hasta ahora se han mantenido las perspectivas de crecimiento de la economa mundial y de paulatina recuperacin de los trminos de intercambio esperados en el IPoM de mayo, han surgido factores que configuran un escenario de mayor riesgo en el panorama del crecimiento global.  Algunos socios comerciales de la regin continan con fuertes deterioros en su desempeo. Esto ha generado una mayor incertidumbre financiera, la que puede tener efectos ms prolongados sobre los flujos de inversin a la regin en general, ya Chile, en particular.  A nivel interno, el escenario se ha caracterizado por un producto que ha tenido un ritmo moderado de crecimiento en los primeros meses del ao, con una paulatina recuperacin de niveles. La demanda interna ha tenido tambin una recuperacin respecto de los niveles de fines del ao pasado, pero a un ritmo menor del esperado. Este pobre desempeo del gasto interno ha sido parcialmente compensado por un crecimiento superior al esperado del sector exportador, lo que ha permitido que la trayectoria del PIB no sea sustancialmente distinta de lo anticipado. La evolucin del gasto interno, no obstante, hace prever para los prximos trimestres tasas de crecimiento menores que las contenidas en el escenario central descrito en el ltimo Informe de Poltica Monetaria.  La mantencin de la inflacin en niveles acotados que no representen factores de riesgo, ha permitido que el Banco Central aumente sostenidamente el impulso monetario durante los ltimos siete meses, favoreciendo una trayectoria ms dinmica de la actividad. En adelante, se espera que la inflacin converger hasta el centro del rango meta en el horizonte habitual de poltica. En definitiva, consideramos que los desarrollos futuros de los factores antes sealados, referidos a la solidez del repunte de la economa mundial, a la solucin de los conflictos econmicos, polticos y sociales de importantes pases dla regin y a la fuerza de la recuperacin de la demanda interna, son factores claves en la evolucin futura de nuestro pas. Economa mundial Desde la desaceleracin global que se inici a mediados del ao 2000, las principales economas del mundo han seguido una trayectoria de recuperacin en los niveles de actividad durante el primer semestre de 2002. La situacin global contina el curso previsto de aceleracin en el crecimiento, esta vez con noticias que muestran que Asia est entrando en una fase de mayor dinamismo, compensando el desempeo de otras reas. La evolucin ms probable de los precios de los commoditiescontina en lnea con lo esperado en el IPoM de mayo. Los riesgos de este escenario, sin embargo, se han tornado crecientemente ms asimtricos: el peligro de terrorismo, los problemas en el medio oriente y la evolucin reciente de las bolsas, explicada por los escndalos financieros en grandes empresas de EE.UU., apuntan a escenarios alternativos de menor actividad y/o mayor aversin al riesgo por parte de los inversionistas. Las proyecciones de crecimiento de Japn han sido corregidas al alza, mientras que la zona europea se mantiene estable, con perspectivas de recuperacin en el prximo ao. Estos antecedentes respaldan un escenario en que la economa mundial se recupera gradualmente en el transcurso del ao 2002 y con ms fuerza en 2003. Cabe sealar que las proyecciones de crecimiento mundial de consenso, ponderado a paridad del poder de compra (PPC), son de 2,8% para 2002 y 3,9% para 2003 (cuadro 3). En las ltimas semanas, los mercados financieros internacionales han mostrado un dlar que se ha depreciado en forma ms persistente, una trayectoria especialmente negativa de los mercados accionarios, particularmente en Estados Unidos, y tasas de inters de largo plazo a la baja. Los efectos de estos hechos en la economa chilena dependern de la evolucin que sigan los mercados financieros internacionales en los prximos meses. En efecto, el impacto de los eventuales menores niveles de actividad en pases avanzados debe ser cotejado con los cambios en el costo y en los flujos de financiamiento hacia las economas emergentes, as como con la respuesta de los precios de los productos de exportacin a los cambios en las paridades y los eventuales menores niveles de actividad mundial. No obstante, an es muy pronto para determinar la magnitud de estos efectos y su incidencia en nuestra economa. Las perspectivas de una trayectoria ms favorable del escenario internacional respecto de los aos previos, se expresa en la evolucin de los precios de nuestras exportaciones. Para este ao se espera slo un leve aumento en el precio del cobre, para ubicarse en torno a US$ 0,73 por libra, con un incremento adicional hacia 2003 y 2004. Hasta el momento, esta evolucin se ve compensada con proyecciones de un mayor precio del petrleo (grfico 2). Esto significa que los trminos del intercambio se mantendrn este ao en niveles promedios similares a los del ao pasado, para repuntar en torno a un 4% promedio anual durante el ao 2003 (grfico 3). Situacin regional El segundo factor clave para el futuro de nuestra economa es la situacin regional. Desgraciadamente, hemos tenido sorpresas negativas, pues, la situacin regional se ha deteriorado marcadamente. Por segundo ao consecutivo, el producto de Amrica Latina permanecer prcticamente estancado en el 2002. Comenz afectndonos la situacin argentina el ao pasado, y recientemente Brasil, es el mayor foco de preocupacin. Desde hace algunas semanas, se ha visto incrementado el acople de las variables financieras domsticas con el riesgo de Brasil, el que si bien ha sido de relativa intensidad, ha permitido mantener en rangos compatibles la estabilidad financiera nacional y de precios. En trminos generales, los riesgos regionales aparecen como asimtricos, especialmente por la evolucin que est teniendo la situacin poltica en algunos pases como Per, Colombia, Venezuela, Bolivia, aparte de los ya conocidos de Brasil y Argentina. A continuacin, analizaremos los efectos ms relevantes del escenario regional, centrado en estos ltimos dos pases por ser los de mayor peso respecto de Amrica Latina. Veremos los efectos de la transmisin por la va de los mercados financieros, los flujos de comercio y los cambios patrimoniales de las empresas chilenas con inversiones en los pases vecinos. Quiero destacar, en todo caso, que existe bastante consenso entre los analistas nacionales e internacionales, de que la vecindad latinoamericana es una de las que posee mayor incertidumbre y peores desempeos en la actual coyuntura mundial. El comercio exterior es una de las variables en que se expresan los efectos adversos dla crisis regional. I\l uestras exportaciones a Argentina cayeron en torno a 60%, y el flujo de turistas disminuy a cerca de la mitad en el primer trimestre del ao 2002. Una proyeccin anual y combinada de estos dos efectos muestra que ellos tienen una incidencia directa en torno a 0,3 puntos porcentuales en el crecimiento del PIB del 2002, efecto que aumenta aproximadamente a 0,5 si se consideran los efectos indirectos (cuadro 4). En el pasado, el sector exportador ha mostrado bastante flexibilidad, por lo que se puede esperar que los efectos en el comercio sean de carcter transitorio, en la medida que se logre encontrar otros mercados (internos o externos) para estos productos o servicios. Aunque por ahora las importaciones desde Argentina no han mostrado incrementos relevantes, no es descartable que la depreciacin del peso argentino incentive mayores flujos de bienes desde ese pas. En el caso de Brasil, los efectos comerciales son ms acotados. Las exportaciones industriales en el ao 2001 equivalen a un 0,5% del PIB, mientras que en el caso de Argentina estas exportaciones fueron 0,7% del PIB. Adems, alrededor del 75% de las exportaciones chilenas a Brasil tienen la capacidad de ser destinadas a otros mercados. Esto es as, pues la gran mayora de las exportaciones a Brasil son mineras (50%), aplicndose tambin una alta probabilidad de redestino a buena parte de las dems exportaciones (cuadro 5). En el caso de las exportaciones a Argentina, slo 50% se poda redestinar. Por ltimo, la magnitud de la cada de las exportaciones de Brasil, probablemente ser inferior a la de Argentina, pudiendo incluso, realizarse en un perodo de mejor entorno global. Dado que el efecto comercial de la crisis brasilea es bastante menor y acotado, podemos decir que el principal impacto se expresara a travs de los mercados financieros, tal como lo hemos observado recientemente. Del mismo modo como ocurri con el agravamiento de la situacin argentina en el segundo semestre de 2001, el mercado cambiarlo ha reaccionado ante el aumento de la incertidumbre en Brasil, produciendo una depreciacin nominal en torno al 8% del peso chileno desde fines de abril (grfico 4). Paralelamente, en los mercados financieros internacionales el spreadde los instrumentos de deuda externa chilena se ha incrementado en torno a 80 puntos base en el mismo perodo (grfico 5). En todo caso, este aumento hasta ahora no parece especialmente preocupante. La razn principal es que, aparte de que se mantienen en niveles histricamente satisfactorios, hasta ahora su incremento no se ha traducido en un aumento relevante en los costos de financiamiento externo, porque en los ltimos dos meses se ha observado una significativa disminucin en el rendimiento a mediano y largo plazo de los papeles del tesoro americano, compensando en parte los aumentos de spreads. Tambin, es tranquilizador el hecho de que el incremento del spread chileno se asocia ms bien a un incremento generalizado en la aversin al riesgo asociado a pases emergentes, que a un efecto especfico de la situacin de Brasil sobre el riesgo crediticio de Chile. Esto se refleja en que los spreadschilenos no se han visto ms castigados que los de otros pases emergentes, fuera del continente americano. Una parte de estos efectos financieros obedece a ajustes inesperados de portafolio de empresas e inversionistas, los que por lo general tienen algn carcter transitorio. Sin embargo, tambin hay una parte que podra llegar a ser ms duradera en la medida que se resientan los flujos financieros hacia la regin en su conjunto, ms de lo que ya lo han hecho. En los escenarios de proyeccin que ha considerado el Banco Central como ms probables, se ha tenido una visin conservadora sobre los flujos de capital hacia economas emergentes. En todo caso, la materializacin del acuerdo comercial con la Unin Europea podra dar un impulso positivo a este tipo de inversin en el mediano plazo. Un tercer efecto de las dificultades econmicas de la regin se expresa en las prdidas patrimoniales y en el estado de los resultados de las empresas que han invertido en las economas vecinas. Este efecto se refleja en las cotizaciones burstiles y en los spreads de la deuda de las empresas, todo lo cual se traduce en una menor capacidad de generacin de renta de estas empresas. Slo en el caso de Argentina, se estim que la disminucin en las utilidades devengadas de las inversiones en ese pas afecta directamente el ingreso nacional del ao 2002 en aproximadamente 0,2% del PIB. Para el caso de las inversiones en Brasil, estos efectos tendran una magnitud sustancialmente menor. Donde la crisis brasilea s podra tener efectos regionales diferenciados y ms adversos, es en el comportamiento de los flujos de capitales y en los precios accionarios. Los flujos de capital para la adquisicin de acciones en Amrica Latina se han estado reduciendo sistemticamente a contarde mayo de 2002. Similarmente, de acuerdo con el Institute for International Finance, los flujos brutos hacia la regin disminuyeron desde U S$ 4 mil millones, promedio mensual, en el perodo enero-abril de 2002, a casi cero en mayo de 2002 (grfico 6). Un comportamiento similar est mostrando la inversin de cartera neta desde y hacia Chile. Deseara destacar que Brasil tiene una ventaja importante en relacin con Argentina, pues, su economa est mejor preparada para adaptarse a los cambios. En primer lugar, el rgimen cambiario de flotacin implica un mecanismo de ajuste ms gradual y eficiente que bajo un rgimen de convertibilidad. Segundo, el sistema financiero y los sectores productivos disponen de una mejor cobertura natural a travs de instrumentos financieros que cubren los riesgos cambiarios. Como un ejemplo de ello, hay que sealar que, tras la depreciacin promedio de 57% de esta moneda en 1999, el mercado financiero mantuvo una posicin slida. Cabe recordar que Brasil es una economa relativamente ms cerrada, de gran tamao, lo cual sugiere que los movimientos cambiarios tienen menores impactos domsticos, en comparacin con pases como Argentina o Uruguay. No hay que despreciar, sin embargo, el efecto de cambios financieros en la dinmica de la deuda que podra sufrir esta economa. Situacin interna El tercer factor determinante de la evolucin futura de nuestra economa dice relacin con factores domsticos. Durante el ao 2001 observamos una fuerte contraccin de la demanda interna, sobre todo en el segundo semestre. Una parte de este fenmeno se debi a factores que resultaron transitorios, como los atentados de septiembre y la crisis en Argentina. Aunque la cada de los componentes ms sensibles de la demanda interna, como las existencias, el consumo de durables y la inversin en maquinaria se revirti parcialmente en los primeros meses de este ao, esta recuperacin se ha moderado bastante en lo ms reciente (grfico 7). De la misma forma, los componentes ms estables del gasto, en particular el consumo habitual, que crecieron de forma relativamente constante durante el 2001, en los ltimos meses se han desacelerado de forma marcada (grfico 8). Existe una serie de factores que permite esgrimir hiptesis respecto del bajo dinamismo del gasto interno en los ltimos meses. En primer lugar, en los aos recientes hemos presenciado una disminucin marcada de las expectativas privadas de crecimiento de mediano plazo, lo que afecta directamente el crecimiento del ingreso permanente. En segundo lugar, la confianza de los consumidores se mantiene en niveles bajos. Aunque las mediciones disponibles reflejan una reversin del pesimismo observado en el tercer trimestre del ao pasado, an se encuentran en niveles deprimidos si se comparan con el promedio de los aos anteriores. En tercer lugar, el incipiente dinamismo que se apreci en la creacin de empleo desde mediados del ao pasado, sobre todo privado, es decir excluyendo los programas de empleo gubernamentales, se ha detenido durante el segundo trimestre de este ao (grfico 9). En particular, el empleo en la industria y el comercio, que empujaron el crecimiento de la ocupacin hacia fines del 2001, ha cado en trminos absolutos. Todos estos antecedentes han sorprendido negativamente. Si bien las estimaciones muestran que se mantuvo una velocidad de crecimiento positiva del gasto y del PIB durante el segundo trimestre del presente ao, el dinamismo es menor al que se estimaba hace un tiempo. El gasto, en particular, est teniendo una evolucin claramente por debajo de lo previsto en el Informe de mayo, lo que pone en duda, ms all de la situacin internacional, la fortaleza del proceso de recuperacin de la actividad. La dinmica inflacionaria ha revelado tambin que existen holguras mayores a las esperadas en los mercados de bienes y de factores. En el mes de junio, el IPC present una variacin de -0,1%, acumulando un incremento anual de slo 2,0% (grfico 10). A su vez la inflacin subyacente -que excluye los precios de perec bles y combustibles-tuvo igual variacin mensual, aunque con un crecimiento en doce meses de 2,7%. Es posible que durante algunos meses puntuales, durante lo que resta del ao, la inflacin en 12 meses se ubique por debajo de 2%. Ms en el mediano plazo, las expectativas privadas se ubican en torno a 2,5% anual, para horizontes de un ao, y cercanas a 3% para horizontes de dos aos. Estas perspectivas muestran la ausencia de presiones inflacionarias significativas, lo que ha motivado las sucesivas reducciones de la tasa de poltica monetaria durante este ao, pasando desde un nivel de 6,5% en enero al 3,25% actual. Adems, el mayor grado de expansin de la poltica monetaria se aprecia en las tasas de inters de los distintos instrumentos del Banco Central, las que han llegado a niveles histricamente bajos. Conclusiones y perspectivas Las reducciones en la tasa de poltica monetaria decretadas por el Banco Central, se han sustentado en una disminucin sustantiva y amplia en las perspectivas de inflacin de mediano plazo, que ha sido acompaada por una inflacin efectiva total y subyacente menor a la prevista. En tanto, la poltica fiscal, de acuerdo con la capacidad contracclica de la regla de supervit estructural, est aportando al impulso de demanda agregada con un impacto cercano al 5% para el ao 2002 en su conjunto, mientras la inversin pblica crecer en torno al 11 %. Esta combinacin de polticas monetaria y fiscal es congruente con la depreciacin real del peso en los ltimos aos, lo que ha permitido un dinamismo de las exportaciones que ha ms que compensado el efecto sobre el volumen exportado de la cada del comercio global. La economa mundial contina expandindose a un ritmo similar al previsto en meses anteriores, aunque con heterogeneidad en las distintas zonas geogrficas. No obstante, las perspectivas de crecimiento de los socios comerciales se han resentido por la negativa evolucin de algunos pases latinoamericanos. Adicionalmente, los riesgos asociados al deterioro de los principales mercados burstiles han cobrado mayor preponderancia. Por su parte, las turbulencias financieras en la regin se han tornado ms significativas que en meses anteriores. En el mbito interno, los antecedentes acumulados indican que durante el segundo trimestre, tanto el gasto como el producto se habran expandido respecto del trimestre inmediatamente anterior, aunque a un ritmo menor que el previsto en el Informe de Poltica Monetaria de mayo. La diferencia es ms evidente en el caso del gasto, para el cual se esperaba una mayor aceleracin a esta altura del ao. Esta trayectoria, sumada a la evolucin del escenario internacional, hace prever tasas de crecimiento menores que las contenidas en dicho Informe para los prximos trimestres. Algunas de las circunstancias descritas tienen implicancias inflacionarias contrapuestas. Sin embargo, el bajo nivel de la inflacin, la persistencia que han mostrado las brechas de capacidad y el reducido traspaso observado de la depreciacin del tipo de cambio a los precios, anticipan que la inflacin converger hacia el centro del rango meta en el horizonte habitual de poltica. Ello es coherente con el nuevo impulso monetario que favorece una trayectoria ms dinmica de la actividad. La mezcla actual de polticas macroeconmicas, vale decir, un rgimen de metas de inflacin, la flotacin cambiara y la regla fiscal de supervit estructural, permiten amortiguar mejor los efectos de las fluctuaciones externas. En un entorno tan incierto como el actual, es esencial inyectar flexibilidad en los mercados, de tal forma que la adaptacin a nuevos escenarios sea lo menos costosa posible. Aunque la economa chilena ha mostrado un alto grado de flexibilidad en el pasado, siempre es posible aumentarla. De esta forma, se pueden obtener beneficios adicionales, desde el punto de vista de acomodar las fluctuaciones a las que inevitablemente se ve sujeta una economa pequea y abierta como la chilena. Desde el punto de vista del funcionamiento de los mercados de bienes y servicios, revisten particular importancia el grado de competencia y la regulacin. En los mercados de factores productivos son relevantes la flexibilidad en el mercado laboral y en el mercado de capitales. En la actualidad, en cada uno de estos mbitos hay importantes desafos que se expresan en la posibilidad de adoptar polticas estructurales, que prepararan mejor a la economa para competir en los mercados globales y hacer frente de mejor forma a los shocks externos. Finalmente, creo conveniente enfatizar que la poltica monetaria del Banco Central tiene como principal objetivo mantener la inflacin en un nivel bajo y estable, definido como un rango de 2% a 4% centrado en 3%, en un horizonte de tiempo permanente. Este objetivo es simtrico, por lo que el Consejo estima como perjudiciales desviaciones tanto por sobre el 4% como por debajo del 2%. Hacia adelante, se espera que la inflacin del IPC converja gradualmente, desde sus niveles actuales, hacia el centro del rango meta en los prximos dos aos. Esta trayectoria es congruente con una aceleracin gradual de la actividad y del gasto, lo que se ve favorecido por las recientes medidas de poltica monetaria. Sin embargo, y como siempre, existe una multitud de riesgos, que en la actualidad tienen un carcter particularmente asimtrico. El Banco Central, en su Informe de Poltica Monetaria de mayo, en su escenario central, proyect la inflacin y el crecimiento econmico con los ltimos antecedentes disponibles en ese momento. Han transcurrido dos meses desde esas proyecciones y hemos observado un entorno regional que se ha deteriorado marcadamente a lo que se suma la seguidilla de escndalos contables en EE.UU., junto con una sombra de duda respecto a la velocidad y robustez del proceso de recuperacin del crecimiento en el mundo desarrollado. Asimismo, en el mbito interno, la prolongacin de niveles elevados de desocupacin, podra continuar limitando el crecimiento del gasto en consumo. Las implicancias precisas de estos desarrollos sobre el panorama de mediano plazo son difciles de evaluar en la actual coyuntura, producto del estado de flujo del escenario internacional, pero en su conjunto apuntan a un crecimiento ms acotado y, probablemente, a menores presiones inflacionarias. Como es habitual, el prximo Informe de Poltica Monetaria, en septiembre de este ao, contendr la visin del Consejo a esa fecha, sobre las perspectivas de crecimiento e inflacin de mediano plazo. Es importante destacar que, justamente, esos son los antecedentes que guan la conduccin de la poltica monetaria en el esquema actual de metas de inflacin.

Title: Monetary Policy of the Central Bank: Year 2003
text: Monetary Policy of the Central Bank: Year 2003 Mar92a Elena O Valle de V. Banco Central de Chile, September 12, 2003, Antofagasta. I. Introduction First of all, I want to express the pleasure we have to be in Antofagasta today, in this 3rd meeting of the Central Bank with Regions. As you know, the Central Bank conducts the country's monetary and exchange rate policy to meet the objectives of currency stability and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. To fulfill these purposes, it is essential to have a deep knowledge of the country's economy and to have a very transparent communication of the way of doing politics. Therefore, the reason for these meetings is to strengthen ties with you and increase, on our part, the knowledge of the realities of each of the sectors and regions of the country, and at the same time, allow you to know directly the policy frameworks and procedures of the Issuing Institute. My presentation will focus mainly on the Monetary Policy Report (IPOM) that the Central Bank Council presented last Wednesday in the Senate Finance Committee, but first, I would like to make a brief introduction on the path chosen by the Central Bank to achieve inflation control and on its current policy scheme. a5 Inflation control and current policy scheme. To begin with, I would like to point out something that you will hear many times throughout this meeting, namely that the monetary policy of the Central Bank of Chile has as its main objective to keep inflation at a low and stable level, defined as a range of 2 to 4%, centered at 3%. Controlling inflation is the way in which monetary policy contributes to the well-being of the population, since it promotes a better functioning of the economy and greater economic growth, while avoiding the erosion of the incomes of people, especially the poorest. In addition, the monetary policy stance towards a low and stable inflation target helps to moderate fluctuations in employment and domestic output. The Central Bank seeks to achieve its inflation target in the most efficient way possible, from a growth and employment perspective. In other words, if there is more than one possible policy interest rate trajectory to maintain inflation around the target, we will choose the one that has the least potential sacrifice for growth in domestic demand and, in addition, in economic activity and employment. This is reflected, in part, in the decision to focus the inflation target over a 24-month term, so as to take into account that the effects of monetary policy on inflation are felt most strongly over the medium term and that transitory price shocks do not necessarily require changes in monetary policy. such as the likely effects on the CPI of the VAT increase in October. In contrast, if we had a goal to achieve in a shorter term, monetary policy would have to be much more active, with the risk of exacerbating the business cycle and eventually generating unnecessary costs for the economy. In historical terms, inflation rates comparable to the level of industrialized countries were achieved in Chile on the basis of two policy guidelines: the use of gradualist but persistent mechanisms to contain inflation, and consistency in the management of the different instruments of monetary policy. The gradualness and consistency are due both to the recognition that the high degree of indexation of the national economy limited the speed, at which it is possible to reduce inflation, and to the credibility costs that would be incurred if inflationary gains were reversed. The experience of the nineties was one of gradual and sustained progress, in which the control of inflation did not lead to major imbalances and that, due to its solidity, augured that its results would be lasting. In this period, the reduction in inflation in Chile was based on: - a great discipline and conviction to advance steadily in the fight against inflation; recognition of the constraints imposed by the existence of indexation mechanisms in the economy; the implementation of a well-defined nominal anchor that can be updated in the face of new developments in the macroeconomic environment; - an exchange rate policy based on the objective of maintaining a narrow current account deficit and avoiding the use of the nominal exchange rate as an anti-inflationary tool; and - a flexible macroeconomic policy scheme capable of reacting in a timely manner to changes in macroeconomic conditions. Slide 1: Inflation Targets 1990 - 2003 When analyzing Chile's experience with inflation targeting, two stages can be clearly distinguished. The first and most extensive corresponds to the transition from high inflation rates to the long-term levels that are the objective of the Central Bank, that is, the period from September 1990 to September 1999. At this stage, the Central Bank carried out a hard monetary policy, defining a short-term horizon for the inflation target (one year) and applying a target point since 1994. However, the reduction in inflation was planned to materialize very gradually, reflecting concerns about economic growth in the short and medium term. In this period, the Central Bank also pursued a secondary objective, defined as a level of current account deficit considered sustainable over time, within a context of nominal exchange rate floating within an indexed band. Inflation Targeting: 1990 - 2003 The second stage of the implementation of inflation targeting began in September 1999, when the exchange rate band was finally abandoned, implementing a free-floating regime for our currency. Achieving flexibility in the foreign exchange market required careful preparation, which had been carried out since 1997 and culminated with the floating of the peso in September 1999. What happened in that period showed that trying to maintain an exchange rate within a band does not help absorb external shocks, such as that of the Asian crisis, or internal ones such as excess spending in the economy, giving very few degrees of freedom to monetary policy. At the beginning of this second stage, it was also announced that the annual target points had been passed to a permanent target range: inflation had been brought to levels that do not damage the economy, after 10 years of effort and for the first time in seventy years. The credibility of the BCCh's policies and the maturity of the Chilean financial system made it possible to achieve significant progress in recent years with the elimination of regulations that led to the liberalization of the capital account of the balance of payments. This is consistent with avoiding movements in the real exchange rate beyond what is considered reasonable for a small economy open to international trade. Among the most important deregulations is the elimination of unremunerated reserve requirements for capital inflows and the requirements of at least one year for some types of capital, which were in place for much of the last decade. On the other hand, to advance in the de-indexation of the economy, the BCCh took another very important step in August 2001, abandoning the use of real rates in UF as an instrument of monetary policy for nominal rates in pesos. Nominalization is consistent with the convergence of local inflation to reduced levels and intemacionalmente comparable with that of the main economies and, in particular, with the floating exchange rate regime in operation since 1999. This policy made it possible to make the Monetary Policy Interest Rate (MPR) directly comparable with the rates in force in the rest of the countries of the world and to better regulate international capital movements. At the same time, it allows the introduction of increasing the nominalization of indexed short-term variables and prevents transitory inflationary impacts from lasting over time through their transfer to the rest of the economy through them. In summary, the current scheme of policies implemented by the Central Bank has the following components: Permanent inflation targets (target range) Free floating of the exchange rate Movements change them without restrictions Capital movements with minimum regulations - Nominalization of the monetary policy rate Thanks to this policy scheme implemented in Chile in recent years, together with a rules-based fiscal policy, the Chilean economy has achieved positive growth rates in an environment of stable and controlled inflation. This policy framework has proven to be robust to a series of shocks and turbulences that, in other episodes of history, led our economy to depressions and financial crises, risks now diminished 3 in the economy of Chile. In addition, it allows us to look more confidently at our relationship with the world, and to move forward with confidence in the negotiation of opening and integration schemes that contain elements of reciprocity and mutual benefit. This does not mean that we are immune to external events, we will suffer or benefit from their consequences. But it does mean that we will be able to absorb the possible negative effects of such events at lower private and social costs. A recent World Bank report highlights the resilience of the Chilean economy and concludes that our country is one of those that suffered the least from the economic difficulties of 2001 and 2002 in Latin America thanks to its effective integration into the world economy and its appropriate macroeconomic policies. II. Monetary Policy Report As I noted earlier, the second part of my presentation will refer to the Monetary Policy Report for September 2003. This Report is the main instrument available to the BC to transmit its policies and is a contribution in terms of transparency in the conduct of monetary policy. It is proven that this type of report, used by other central banks of developed countries, increases the effectiveness of such policy and also contributes to increasing the credibility and accountability of the Bank, as well as public support for the monetary policy decisions chosen. Our Report is published quarterly in January, May and September, and the first of them was published in May 2000, with the aim of informing and explaining to the general public what is the vision of the Board of the BC on the recent and expected evolution of inflation and its consequences. Another purpose of the report is to publicly expose the medium-term analysis framework used in the formulation of monetary policy and provide useful information to the market that contributes to the formation of expectations about the future trajectory of inflation and output. It should be noted that each of the Reports includes boxes that present more detailed studies and considerations on topics relevant to the assessment of inflation and monetary policy. As an example, this Report includes, among others, boxes on "Monetary Policy Decisions in the last 3 months"; "Chile-United States FTA"; "Indirect taxes and inflation"; "The importance of the Risk Balance". I would like to mention in particular the box "Evaluation of the Monetary Policy Report", which is based on a study carried out by economists from CEPR (Centre for Economic Policy Research), IICMB (International Center for Monetary and Banking Studies) and I It is a research center formed 19 years ago, which promotes economic research on issues of policy relevance, with an emphasis on Europe. It encourages the direct conduct of research in selected areas, specialized conferences and publications. As can be seen, these projections have remained relatively stable, with downward adjustments in the euro area and emerging Asia. While most industrialized countries had a weak second quarter, the world is expected to pick up a more dynamic pace of growth for the second half of the year, led by the United States and Asia. Contributing to this scenario are the expansionary monetary policies applied in most of the world throughout the year, the strong fiscal impulse in the United States, the disappearance of the uncertainty caused by the war between the United States and Iraq, the control of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS) and the better financial conditions in the world environment. In the last report, the US economic situation was one of the risk elements accompanying the baseline scenario, along with the impact of SARS on Asian economies and its possible effects on the rest of the world. Today, these risks have moderated. Some indicators of the US economy have begun to show positive signs of recovery, which strengthens the growth considered in the central scenario for this year. However, stronger indicators, particularly those related to non-residential investment and the US labour market, are still expected to underpin the recovery over the coming years. Likewise, the depreciation of the dollar on average during 2003 will allow the high current account deficit of the balance of payments of that economy to be adjusted in a less traumatic way. In emerging economies, on the other hand, the impact of SARS on activity in Asia was quite limited and at present everything seems to indicate that it has disappeared as an element of risk. Likewise, monetary conditions in Chile remain clearly expansionary, despite marginally lower credit growth and increases in some lending interest rates. A proper conduct of monetary policy makes it necessary to continue to carefully assess the effect on projected inflation that changes in indirect taxes will ultimately have, because in a medium-term perspective, one-time movements in the price level should not induce corrective monetary policy actions.
