However, there are a number of relevant risks that the BC considers in its analysis and that configure alternative scenarios for both inflation and growth, which constitute the balance of risks for both variables. The importance of risk analysis lies in the fact that, in practice, any projection exercise is subject to significant degrees of uncertainty. There is little certainty regarding the direction that the international economy will take, for example, in the future or the price of commodities (commodilies). The use of projections based on expert opinions allows for the most informed opinion available, but does not eliminate this uncertainty. The risk balance sheet is the instrument used by the Board to communicate in the reports its perception of the most relevant implications of the different sources of uncertainty. For now, there is not enough background to indicate that the central scenario of projection for the medium term has very different characteristics from those considered by the consensus. However, the possibility remains that the expected acceleration in activity will follow a different course than expected and there is uncertainty regarding the actual consequences of the changes shown in the cost measures. The realization of growth rates of activity and spending over time, which allow reducing the existing slacks, depends, among other factors, on a consolidation of the most promising external scenario, which has been affirmed in the most recent years, and a sustained recovery in the terms of trade. The most recent news in these areas, together with the entry into force of the various free trade agreements and the maintenance, despite changes in the margin, of favorable financial conditions for Chile, allow us to expect d0 with less uncertainty than in past reports d0 a better medium-term outlook, although concerns persist about possible alternative scenarios. In particular, there are still risks of negative deviations on the international stage. Domestically, a scenario of higher growth than the one outlined in this Report cannot be ruled out. In recent days there have been significant changes in the exchange rate, country risk and other prices of financial assets that reflect greater optimism about the course that the national economy will take. If these conditions are maintained sustainably, a scenario of higher growth in domestic demand, particularly investment, could be configured, accompanied by a somewhat larger than expected current account deficit and more capital flows. On the other hand, although it is estimated that the low rate of productivity growth in recent quarters is of a temporary nature, it is not ruled out that it persists over time and affects the diagnosis of medium-term growth and the effective magnitude of capacity gaps. Moreover, if a scenario of a smaller rebound in labour productivity is not accompanied by a slow pace of nominal wage expansion, this could result in higher-than-expected inflationary pressures. In this regard, it is worth mentioning the historical difficulty that wages have shown in adjusting to changes in labor market conditions, especially in circumstances such as the current ones, when high unemployment rates persist. With regard to the imported components of inflation, the experience of past years shows that the Chilean economy has been able to accommodate changes in relative prices without causing persistent effects on inflation. This is partly thanks to the credibility of the inflation target, but also due to a significant capacity to substitute external suppliers and a fall in import prices of various goods that continues, despite the nominal depreciation of the dollar against other currencies. However, there could be considerably different scenarios for external inflation, with effects on the trajectory of domestic prices. Finally, although scenarios for the price of crude oil other than those considered in the central scenario of this Report seem likely, their impact on the medium-term path of inflation in Chile would be limited. In weighting the above background, the Board of the ECB considers that the alternative scenarios reflect, as a whole, a balanced balance of risks for activity, as well as for inflation. III. Perspectives and Conclusions - The recovery of activity, had a fall during the2nd quarter , mainly affected by industry. For the coming quarters, a recovery in activity is expected, especially driven by the mining sector, with which, in the most likely scenario, economic growth this year will be between 3.0% and 3.5%. For 2004, activity is expected to grow by 4% - 5% - The main concerns stem especially from the US recovery since 2004, the trajectory of oil prices and labor productivity. - CPI inflation, including the likely impact of the VAT increase, will remain in the centre of the target range, as will core inflation. - Although an increase in annual CPI inflation is still anticipated, which will keep it for several quarters in the upper half of the target range (3.5% as of Dec 2004), towards the end of the projection horizon (Sept 2005) both will converge to values somewhat above 3%. - If the most likely scenario is true, with average inflation slightly below 3% but marginally above 3% at the end of the horizon, and in the absence of shocks, it is foreseeable that some of the marked momentum of the MP will be reduced in the future. - Alternative scenarios, such as those mentioned, have different implications for the eventual path of monetary policy. - The central bank will continue to use its policies flexibly, so as to confront persistent movements in projected inflation that move it away from the 3% target in one direction or another. To conclude, I cannot fail to stress that in recent years a reserve of macroeconomic stability and credibility has been gradually built, and thanks to this we have been able to differentiate ourselves from other emerging economies. The adoption of a policy framework such as the one mentioned in this presentation constitutes a true pillar of Chile's economic and financial stability. We are less vulnerable today than other emerging economies. Our strengths lie in an appropriate mix of monetary and fiscal policies; a policy of flexibility would change; macroeconomic stability; a very small current account deficit; a sound and well-supervised financial system; a reasonable, private and mostly medium- and long-term external debt; low public debt; and a highly distorted, competitive economy with a broad predominance of economic freedom. This has been recognized recently in the latest report by the IMF on Chile. It lavishes praise on the way in which economic policy has been conducted in our country, especially praising the significant strengthening that the set of macroeconomic policies has experienced, and in particular the space they have generated to allow a considerable boost to domestic demand. A favourable view was also expressed regarding progress in terms of transparency of both fiscal and monetary policy, and I believe that the report just presented is an important part of this progress.

Introduccin En primer lugar, quiero expresarles el agrado que tenemos de estar hoy en Antofagasta, en este 3er encuentro del Banco Central con Regiones. Como ustedes saben, el Banco Central conduce la poltica monetaria y cambiara del pas para cumplir con los objetivos de estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos. Para cumplir con estos fines, es esencial, un conocimiento profundo de la economa del pas y tener una comunicacin muy transparente de la forma de hacer poltica. Por ello, la razn de estos encuentros es estrechar vnculos con ustedes e incrementar, por parte nuestra, el conocimiento de las realidades de cada uno de los sectores y regiones del pas, y a la vez, permitirles conocer en forma directa los marcos de poltica y procedimientos del Instituto Emisor. Mi presentacin se va a centrar principalmente en el Informe de Poltica Monetaria (IPOM) que el consejo del Banco Central present el mircoles recin pasado en la Comisin de Hacienda del Senado, pero antes, me gustara hacer una breve introduccin sobre el camino escogido por el Banco Central para lograr el control de la inflacin y sobre su actual esquema de polticas.  Control de la inflacin y actual esquema de polticas. Para comenzar, quisiera sealar algo que van a or muchas veces a lo largo de este encuentro, esto es, que la poltica monetaria del Banco Central de Chile tiene como principal objetivo mantener la inflacin en un nivel bajo y estable, definido como un rango de 2 a 4%, centrado en 3%. El control de la inflacin es la manera en que la poltica monetaria contribuye al bienestar de la poblacin, ya que, ello promueve un mejor funcionamiento de la economa y un mayor crecimiento econmico, al tiempo que evita la erosin de los ingresos de las personas, principalmente de los ms pobres. Adems, la orientacin de la poltica monetaria hacia el logro de una meta de inflacin situada en un nivel bajo y estable, ayuda a que se moderen las fluctuaciones del empleo y la produccin nacional. El Banco Central busca conseguir su objetivo inflacionario de la manera ms eficiente posible, desde una perspectiva de crecimiento y empleo. En otras palabras, si para mantener la inflacin en tomo a la meta hay ms de una trayectoria posible de las tasas de inters de poltica, escogeremos aquella que tenga el menor sacrificio potencial de crecimiento de la demanda intema y, por aadidura, de la actividad econmica y el empleo. Esto se refleja, en parte, en la decisin de centrar el objetivo inflacionario a un plazo de 24 meses, de modo de tomar en cuenta que los efectos de la poltica monetaria sobre la inflacin se sienten con ms fuerza en un plazo mediano y que shocks transitorios sobre los precios no requieren necesariamente de cambios en la poltica monetaria, como por ejemplo, los probables efectos sobre el IPC que tenga el incremento del IVA en octubre. En contraste, si tuviramos una meta a conseguir en un plazo ms corto, la poltica monetaria tendra que ser mucho ms activa, con el riesgo de exacerbar el ciclo econmico y eventualmente generar costos innecesarios para la economa. En trminos histricos, la obtencin de tasas de inflacin comparables al nivel de pases industrializados se logr en Chile sobre la base de dos directrices de poltica: el uso de mecanismos gradualistas, pero persistentes de contencin de la inflacin, y la consistencia en el manejo de los distintos instrumentos de la poltica monetaria. La gradualidad y consistencia obedecen tanto al reconocimiento que el alto grado de indizacin de la economa nacional limitaba la velocidad, a la cual es posible disminuir la inflacin, como a los costos de credibilidad en que se incurrira si los logros inflacionarios se revirtiesen. La experiencia de los noventa, fue de un avance gradual y sostenido, en que el control de la inflacin no motiv desequilibrios mayores y que, por su solidez, permita augurar que sus resultados fueran duraderos. En este perodo, la reduccin de la inflacin en Chile se bas en:  una gran disciplina y conviccin para avanzar sostenidamente en la lucha anti-inflacionaria; el reconocimiento de las restricciones que impone la existencia de mecanismos de indizacin en la economa; la implementacin de un ancla nominal bien definida y actualizable ante nuevos desarrollos del entorno macroeconmico;  una poltica cambiara basada en el objetivo de mantener un dficit de cuenta corriente acotado y evitar el uso del tipo de cambio nominal como herramienta anti-inflacionaria; y  un esquema de poltica macroeconmica flexible y capaz de reaccionar oportunamente ante cambios de las condiciones macroeconmicas. Lmina 1: Metas de Inflacin 1990 - 2003 Metas de Inflacin: 1990 - 2003 Metas de Inflacin: 1990 - 2003 La segunda etapa de la implementacin de metas de inflacin comenz en septiembre de 1999, cuando la banda cambiara fue finalmente abandonada implantndose un rgimen de libre flotacin para nuestra moneda. Llegar a la flexibilidad en el mercado cambiario requiri de una cuidadosa preparacin, la que se vena realizando desde 1997 y culmin con la flotacin del peso en septiembre de 1999. Lo ocurrido en ese perodo demostr que pretender mantener un tipo de cambio dentro de una banda no ayuda a absorber impactos externos, como el de la crisis asitica, o internos como el exceso de gasto de la economa, dndole muy pocos grados de libertad a la poltica monetaria.En el comienzo de esta segunda etapa, se anunci, adems, el paso de las metas punto anuales a una meta rango de carcter permanente: se haba logrado llevar la inflacin a niveles que no daan la economa, despus de 10 aos de esfuerzo y por primera vez en setenta aos. La credibilidad en las polticas del BCCh y la madurez del sistema financiero chileno permitieron lograr, en los ltimos aos avances significativos con la eliminacin de regulaciones que llevaron a la liberalizacin de la cuenta de capitales de la balanza de pagos. Ello es consistente con evitar movimientos del tipo de cambio real ms all de lo que se considera razonable para una economa pequea y abierta al comercio internacional. Entre las desregulaciones ms importantes se encuentra la eliminacin del encaje no remunerado a las entradas de capital y los requerimientos de permanencia de al menos un ao para algunos tipos de capital, los cuales estuvieron vigentes durante gran parte de la dcada pasada. Por otro lado, para avanzar en la des-indizacin de la economa el BCCh dio otro paso muy importante en agosto de 2001, al abandonar el uso de tasas reales en UF como instrumento de poltica monetaria por tasas nominales en pesos. La nominalizacin, es consistente con la convergencia de la inflacin local a niveles reducidos e intemacionalmente comparables con el de las principales economas y, en particular, con el rgimen de flotacin cambiara en operacin desde 1999. Esta poltica permiti hacer directamente comparable la Tasa de Inters de Poltica Monetaria (TPM) con las tasas vigentes en el resto de los pases del mundo y regular mejor los movimientos internacionales de capitales. A la vez, permite introducir en forma creciente la nominalizacin a las variables de corto plazo indizadas y evitar que impactos inflacionarios transitorios perduren en el tiempo a travs de su traspaso al resto de la economa mediante stas. En sntesis, el esquema actual de polticas implementadas por el Banco Central tiene los siguientes componentes: Metas de inflacin permanentes (meta rango) Libre flotacin del tipo de cambio Movimientos cambiarlos sin restricciones Movimientos de capital con regulaciones mnimas - Nominalizacin de la tasa de poltica monetaria Gracias a este esquema de polticas implementado en Chile en los ltimos aos, junto con una poltica fiscal basada en reglas, la economa chilena ha logrado tasas positivas de crecimiento en un entorno de inflacin estable y controlada. Este marco de polticas ha demostrado ser robusto a una seguidilla de shocks y turbulencias que, en otros episodios de la historia, llevaron a nuestra economa a depresiones y crisis financieras, riesgos hoy disminuidos 3 en la economa de Chile. Adems, nos permite mirar con ms confianza nuestra relacin con el mundo, y avanzar con seguridad en la negociacin de esquemas de apertura e integracin que contengan elementos de reciprocidad y beneficio mutuo. Ello no significa que seamos inmunes a los acontecimientos externos, sufriremos o nos beneficiaremos de sus consecuencias. Pero s significa que podremos absorber con menores costos privados y sociales los eventuales efectos negativos de tales acontecimientos. Un informe reciente del Banco Mundial, destaca la capacidad de resistencia de la economa chilena y concluye que nuestro pas, es uno de los que menos sufrieron las dificultades econmicas de 2001 y 2002 en Amrica Latina gracias a su integracin efectiva en la economa mundial y a sus polticas macroeconmicas adecuadas. II. Informe de Poltica Monetaria Como seal anteriormente, la segunda parte de mi exposicin se referir al Informe de Poltica Monetaria correspondiente al mes de septiembre de 2003. Este Informe es el principal instrumento con que cuenta el BC para transmitir sus polticas y es un aporte en trminos de la transparencia en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Est comprobado que este tipo Informe usado por otros Bancos centrales de pases desarrollados, aumenta la eficacia de dicha poltica y contribuye tambin a aumentar la credibilidad y responsabilidad del Banco, as como el apoyo del pblico a las decisiones de poltica monetaria elegidas. Nuestro Informe se publica cuatrimestralmente en los meses de enero, mayo y septiembre, y el primero de ellos fue publicado en mayo de 2000, con el objetivo de informar y explicar al pblico general cual es la visin del Consejo del BC sobre la evolucin reciente y esperada de la inflacin y sus consecuencias. Otro de los propsitos del informe, es exponer pblicamente el marco de anlisis de mediano plazo utilizado en la formulacin de la poltica monetaria y proveer de informacin til al mercado que contribuya a la formacin de expectativas sobre la trayectoria futura de la inflacin y del producto. Cabe destacar que en cada uno de los Informes se incluyen recuadros que presentan estudios y consideraciones ms detalladas sobre temas relevantes para la evaluacin de la inflacin y de la poltica monetaria. Como ejemplo, en este Informe se incluyen, entre otros, recuadros sobre Decisiones de Poltica Monetaria en los ltimos 3 meses; TLC entre Chile y Estados Unidos; Impuestos indirectos e inflacin; La importancia del Balance de riesgos. Me gustara mencionar especialmente el recuadro Evaluacin del Informe de Poltica Monetaria, el cual basa en un estudio realizado por economistas del CEPR (Centre for Economic Policy Research), ICMB (International Center for Monetary and Banking Studies) y el Norges Bank (2003), en el que el informe elaborado por el Banco Central de Chile obtuvo el 5o lugar a escala mundial dentro de 20 pases, superando a naciones con larga tradicin y alta reputacin en la conduccin monetaria con metas de inflacin, tales como Australia y Canad. No obstante este satisfactorio resultado hay aspectos del informe que pueden ser susceptibles de mejoras, algunas de las cuales ya se abordan a contar de esta edicin: entregar mayor detalle del proceso de toma de decisiones entre los Informes, mayor informacin sobre la trayectoria de algunos precios y darle mayor importancia al balance de riesgos. El tipo de cambio nominal, por su parte, ha presentado vaivenes durante los ltimos meses, aunque con menor volatilidad que a comienzos de este ao, mantenindose en promedio en torno a $700 por dlar, mientras el tipo de cambio real (TCR) ha continuado con los altos niveles prevalecientes desde comienzos de ao. No obstante, en los das recientes hemos sido testigos de una importante apreciacin del peso, principalmente en los valores nominales. Paralelamente, durante los ltimos meses ha continuado la menor expansin del crecimiento anual del dinero ms lquido, fenmeno que tambin ha abarcado los agregados monetarios ms amplios en particular el M2A, que presenta las menores variaciones anuales desde mediados de los aos ochenta. Respecto de los movimientos futuros del tipo de cambio en el corto plazo, es indudable la dificultad que ello involucra en un esquema de flotacin como el que rige en Chile desde septiembre de 1999. En este Informe, como supuesto de trabajo, se postula una trayectoria que es coherente con los diferenciales interno y externo entre tasas de inters de mediano y largo plazo que se observan en la actualidad, y con el escenario de mejores condiciones externas con un mayor crecimiento de la actividad y el gasto. Ello implica una leve apreciacin real del peso en el horizonte de proyeccin, respecto de los niveles alcanzados durante las ltimas cuatro semanas. El peso ha sufrido algunos vaivenes en las ltimas semanas, reflejando los movimientos de los diferenciales de tasas externas e internas, de los trminos de intercambio y las noticias de la reactivacin mundial.En trminos globales, el sistema financiero mantuvo durante los ltimos meses sus caractersticas de estabilidad y solvencia, con elevados ndices de fortaleza patrimonial y rentabilidad y con riesgos, en general, estables y acotados. La importancia del anlisis de riesgos radica en que, en la prctica, todo ejercicio de proyeccin est sujeto a importantes grados de incertidumbre. Existe poca certeza con respecto a la direccin que tomar, por ejemplo, la economa internacional en el futuro o el precio de los productos bsicos (commodilies). El uso de proyecciones basadas en opiniones expertas permite contar con la opinin ms informada disponible, pero no elimina esta incertidumbre. El balance de riesgos es el instrumento que usa el Consejo para comunicar en los informes su percepcin sobre las implicancias ms relevantes de las distintas fuentes de incertidumbre. Sin embargo, persiste la posibilidad de que la esperada aceleracin de la actividad siga un curso diferente al previsto y existe incertidumbre respecto de las consecuencias efectivas de los cambios que muestran las medidas de costos. La concrecin de tasas de expansin de la actividad y el gasto crecientes en el tiempo, que permitan reducir las holguras existentes en la actualidad, depende, entre otros factores, de un afianzamiento del ms promisorio escenario externo, que se ha afirmado en lo ms reciente, y una recuperacin sostenida de los trminos de intercambio. Las noticias ms recientes en estos mbitos, junto con la entrada en vigencia de los diversos tratados de libre comercio y la mantencin, pese a cambios en el margen, de condiciones financieras favorables para Chile, permiten esperar con menor incertidumbre que en Informes pasados un mejor panorama de mediano plazo, aunque persiste la preocupacin sobre posibles escenarios alternativos. En particular, an subsisten riesgos de desviaciones negativas en el escenario internacional. En el mbito interno, no se puede descartar un escenario de mayor crecimiento que el delineado en este Informe. En los ltimos das han ocurrido cambios relevantes en el tipo de cambio, el riesgo pas y otros precios de activos financieros que reflejan un mayor optimismo sobre el curso que tomar la economa nacional. De mantenerse sostenidamente estas condiciones se podra configurar un escenario de mayor crecimiento de la demanda interna, en particular de la inversin, acompaado de un dficit de la cuenta corriente algo mayor al previsto y ms flujos de capitales. Por otra parte, aunque se estima que el bajo ritmo de crecimiento de la productividad en trimestres recientes es de carcter coyuntural, no se descarta que persista en el tiempo e incida en el diagnstico de crecimiento de mediano plazo y en la magnitud efectiva de las holguras de capacidad. Adems, si un escenario de menor repunte de la productividad del trabajo no va acompaado de un ritmo reducido de expansin de los salarios nominales, ello podra redundar en presiones inflacionarias superiores a las previstas. Al respecto, cabe mencionar la dificultad histrica que han mostrado los salarios para ajustarse a los cambios en las condiciones del mercado laboral, especialmente en circunstancias como las actuales, cuando persisten altas tasas de desempleo. Con relacin a los componentes importados de la inflacin, la experiencia de los aos pasados muestra que la economa chilena ha podido acomodar cambios en precios relativos sin causar efectos persistentes en la inflacin. Ello, en parte gracias a la credibilidad de la meta de inflacin, pero tambin por una importante capacidad de sustituir proveedores externos y por una cada de precios de importacin de diversos bienes que contina, a pesar de la depreciacin nominal del dlar respecto de otras monedas. Con todo, podran darse escenarios considerablemente diferentes para la inflacin externa, con efectos sobre la trayectoria de los precios internos. Finalmente, aunque escenarios para el precio del crudo distintos al considerado en el escenario central de este Informe parecen probables, su impacto en la trayectoria de mediano plazo de la inflacin en Chile sera acotado. En la ponderacin de los antecedentes sealados, el Consejo del BC estima que los escenarios alternativos reflejan en su conjunto, un balance de riesgos para la actividad equilibrado, al igual que para la inflacin. III. Perspectivas y Conclusiones  La recuperacin de la actividad, tuvo una cada durante el 2o trimestre, afectada principalmente por la industria. Para los prximos trimestres, se espera una recuperacin de la actividad, especialmente impulsada por el sector minera, con lo que, en el escenario ms probable, el crecimiento econmico este ao se situar entre 3.0% y 3.5%. Para 2004, se espera un crecimiento de la actividad entre 4% - 5%  Los principales preocupaciones provienen especialmente de la recuperacin de EEUU a partir del 2004, la trayectoria del precio del petrleo y la productividad del trabajo.  La inflacin IPC, incluyendo el probable impacto del incremento del IVA, se mantendr en el centro del rango meta, al igual que la inflacin subyacente.  Aunque se sigue anticipando un incremento de la inflacin anual IPCX que la mantendr por varios trimestres en la mitad superior del rango meta (3.5% a dic 2004), hacia fines del horizonte de proyeccin (sept 2005) ambas convergern a valores algo por sobre 3%.  De verificarse el escenario ms probable, con una inflacin promedio algo menor que 3% pero marginalmente por encima de 3% a fines del horizonte, y en ausencia de shocks, es previsible que en el futuro se reduzca parte del marcado impulso de la PM.  Escenarios alternativos, como los mencionados tienen implicancias distintas sobre la trayectoria eventual de la poltica monetaria.  El Banco Central continuar usando sus polticas con flexibilidad, de manera de confrontar movimientos persistentes en la inflacin proyectada que la alejen de la meta de 3% en una u otra direccin. Para finalizar, no puedo dejar de destacar que en los ltimos aos se ha construido paulatinamente una reserva de estabilidad macroeconmica y credibilidad, y gracias a ello hemos podido diferenciamos de otras economas emergentes. La adopcin de un esquema de polticas como el mencionado en esta presentacin, constituye un verdadero pilar de la estabilidad econmica y financiera de Chile. Somos hoy menos vulnerable que otros emergentes. Nuestras fortalezas radican en una combinacin apropiada de polticas monetaria y fiscal; una poltica de flexibilidad cambiara; estabilidad macroeconmica; un dficit en cuenta corriente muy reducido; un sistema financiero sano y bien supervisado; una deuda externa razonable, privada y mayoritariamente de mediano y largo plazo; una deuda pblica baja; y una economa sin grandes distorsiones, competitiva y de amplio predominio de libertad econmica. Lo anterior, ha sido reconocido recientemente, en el ltimo informe realizado por el FMI sobre Chile. En ste se emiten elogiosos comentarios a la forma en que se ha estado conduciendo la poltica econmica en nuestro pas, especialmente se alab el significativo fortalecimiento que ha experimentado el conjunto de polticas macroeconmicas , y en particular el espacio que stas han generado para permitir un impulso considerable a la demanda interna. Tambin se expres una opinin favorable respecto del avance en trminos de transparencia tanto de la poltica fiscal como monetaria, y creo que el informe recin presentado es parte importante de este avance.

Title: Evaluation and Prospects of the National and International Economy 2003-2004
text: Evaluation and Prospects of the National and International Economy 2003-2004 PRESENTATION BY MAReaA ELENA OVALLE M., DIRECTOR OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, HELD ON OCTOBER 22, 2003, IN THE BOARD ROOM OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE. Introduction First of all, I must thank the presence at this meeting of executives from different areas of national work. Representatives of the public sector, the business world, culture, the media, social aid organizations, the financial world and teaching are here. The idea of this call is part of the extension that the Central Bank has been carrying out through presentations to different audiences and in different cities of the country in order to publicize its objectives and procedures, thus increasing the transparency of its actions. We believe that providing you with this type of information is a valuable tool for the best performance of the different functions that you exercise, since the economic aspects are transversal to all the activities of a country. My presentation will focus mainly on the Monetary Policy Report (IPoM) that the Central Bank Council presented last September to the Senate Finance Committee. In this Inf97rmese makes an analysis of what happened in our economy and makes known what is the vision that is for the next twenty-four months. Before entering into the matter, I would like to make a brief introduction to the objectives of the Central Bank, highlighting the importance of institutionality, credibility and transparency of its policies in its actions. The Central Bank of Chile (BCCh) was created in 1 925, and is currently governed by the Constitutional Organic Law (LO C) approved in 1989. It is an institution of public law, with autonomous character, independent from the powers of the State, since it is only subject to the Political Constitution and its LO C that regulates its composition, organization, functions and attributions. The Central Bank is part of the new institutional framework established in the Constitution, and its inclusion in it was intended to give it the responsibility of maintaining macroeconomic stability, an essential matter in the development of the country and indispensable to preserve the confidence of internal and external investors. This avoided their dependence on the Government, which in the past resulted in fiscal indebtedness through inorganic issuance and the adoption of policies influenced by circumstances beyond their specific functions. The macroeconomic balance of a country stimulates the growth of production, investment, the promotion of employment and wages. Hence the importance of the Central Bank, whose fundamental objectives are: - Ensure the stability of the currency, which means the maintenance of the purchasing power of money, that is, the control of the inflationary process, due to the pernicious effects that it causes in the allocation of productive resources and in the distribution of income. - Ensure the normal functioning of internal and external payments, that is, that they are made smoothly. To this end, among other things, the Central Bank must safeguard the stability of the financial system and maintain an adequate volume of money both in the domestic economy and foreign currency for the purposes of payments abroad. In this introduction, I would like to emphasize that our great motivation for the realization of these meetings is based on the importance of transparency in the actions of an autonomous central bank. Through this transparency, we contribute to the public being able to understand and anticipate our decisions and, in this way, improve the effectiveness of monetary and financial policies and, at the same time, increase the credibility of the institution by making the Central Bank responsible for its actions before society as a whole. To further strengthen the credibility of the policy framework, we are convinced that the Central Bank should aim to foster a better understanding of monetary policy transmission mechanisms, increase public disclosure of statistical information and analytical methods used, and increase the transparency of projections and policy decisions. Not so many years ago, the vision of central bankers was very different from today. Monetary policy was believed to be more effective when it was formulated more "secretly" and it was disturbing to be too explicit about targets. It was thought that in case of an inadequate transmission of the same it would become more difficult to change course, thus preventing the necessary adjustments so that the market can evolve according to the desirable economic conditions at all times. To the extent that the functioning of markets and financial instruments were transformed and required lower levels of uncertainty to be more efficient, a change of appreciation arises on the need and importance of transparency, which began to be valued more and more. Today, financial markets work more efficiently because participants do not have to waste the enormous efforts of before in the continuous attempt to infer what the monetary policy decision is from unclear day-to-day signals. In addition, there has been the peculiarity that this greater transparency has not meant any restriction on the discretion available to us to adjust monetary policy in the appropriate direction whenever necessary. Consequently, today we move much more clearly in our policy decisions, including also information on the most relevant future risks. In that direction, we have been making efforts for some time to move towards greater transparency. These efforts are reflected in the preparation and publication of the quarterly monetary policy report (IPoM), the press releases that follow the monthly monetary policy meetings; the publication of the minutes of these meetings with a delay of 45 days; the information provided by the Central Bank on its website, in its many publications of a technical nature, and in the public interventions of its President, the members of the Council and the main executives of the Staf92. In short, experience has shown that transparency has contributed to improving the functioning of markets and, also, to enhancing our credibility with the public. Today, this type of openness is more than a useful instrument for the conduct of a country's economic policy, it is a duty of central banks to society. As noted above, from the beginning of its autonomy, BC Ch was granted full responsibility for the configuration and instrumentalization of monetary policy, as an independent body of the Government; It was given a clear mandate to achieve price stability and was given the powers to do so, which was a key factor in controlling inflation. This shows that good institutions, with serious and credible entities, are a key element, both in the setting of the main macroeconomic goals and in the reception by the market of the policies implemented by the authority. The creation of good institutions, not only monetary but also fiscal and financial, is a priority, and I believe that our country has understood this very well, since the prestige and solidity of our institutions and their policies has allowed us to achieve broad international recognition over the last few years. In particular, the autonomy of the Central Bank has been very important. Such a characteristic, coupled now with the transparency of our activities, is what makes us truly credible to the public, and what allows us to help them to judge for themselves whether our task is up to what they think it should be. Another point that I would like to highlight before going into the content of the IPoM, is the reason for our decision to focus the inflation target within 2 years. This is because the effects of monetary policy on inflation are felt most strongly over the medium term and transitory price shocks do not necessarily require changes in monetary policy, such as the likely CPI effects of the recent VAT increase. In contrast, if we had a goal to achieve in a shorter term, monetary policy would have to be much more active, with the risk of exacerbating the business cycle and, eventually, generating unnecessary costs for the economy. To face this medium-term scenario, we have an important asset, which are the solid fundamentals of our economy, and if the favorable conditions expected in the international scenario are also given and the current monetary conditions are maintained, we will have the recovery we expect. I do not want to miss the opportunity to point out to you that medium-term projection has dangers, especially when there are periods of low growth, as happened between 1998 and 2002. These dangers are impatience, pessimism and inflexibility, which can divert the economy from its long-term path. Impatience affects economic policies when faced with difficult episodes. It can manifest itself in policy actions that are not sustainable over time and that, sooner rather than later, must be corrected. However, the current mix of fiscal and monetary policy has us well removed from this risk. Fiscal policy is based on a rule aimed at establishing a structural surplus equivalent to 1% of gross domestic product (GDP), which has a moderation effect on the economic cycle and allows the public sector to make a greater contribution to national savings over the medium-term horizon, enabling higher investment growth and looser monetary conditions. Monetary policy, for its part, has managed to maintain price stability, as we will see in detail later. Today, we have historically low domestic interest rates and no danger of inflation. The second danger is waves of optimism and pessimism on the part of market players. These tend to have an influence on different economic episodes, especially when there is imperfect information and uncertainty, and can sometimes prolong recessionary or low growth periods. The perceptions of consumers and investors are reflected in their decisions, but at the same time they are the source of information for other agents by forming their own perceptions. Expectations feed on what happens in the very short term, generating situations of self-fulfilling prophecies, in which some agents follow the actions of others when forming their perceptions, rather than making their own evaluation of the fundamentals of the economy in a medium-term horizon. Therefore, for the Central Bank it is important to be as transparent as possible and deliver ever greater and more timely information to the market, thus contributing to the formation of expectations of agents, expanding the horizon that serves as the basis for their perceptions and reaffirming the common bases of the growth model. The third risk of the current scenario lies in market imperfections that hinder changes in relative prices or the decisions that flow from them. To accommodate the external cycles, which are at the origin of this phase of lower growth, the economy requires not only macroeconomic stability, but also flexibility in prices and markets, in order to facilitate the necessary sectoral adjustments, consistent with the new conditions of the economy. Monetary Policy Report (IPoM) 1. Inflation control and current policy framework To begin with, I would like to recall that the BCCh's main objective is to keep inflation at a low and stable level, defined as a range of 2 to 4%, centered at 3%. Controlling inflation is how monetary policy contributes to the well-being of the population, as it promotes a better functioning economy and greater economic growth, while avoiding the erosion of the incomes of people, especially the poorest. In addition, the monetary policy stance towards a low and stable inflation target helps to moderate fluctuations in employment and domestic output. The Central Bank seeks to achieve its inflation target in the most efficient way possible, from a growth and employment perspective. In other words, if there is more than one possible policy interest rate path to maintain inflation around the target, we will choose the one that has the least potential sacrifice for domestic demand growth and, in addition, economic activity and employment. The Chilean experience of the nineties in terms of inflation control was one of gradual and sustained progress, which did not lead to major imbalances and which, due to its solidity, augured that its results would be lasting. In this period, the reduction of inflation in Chile was based on great discipline and conviction to make sustained progress in the fight against inflation and on the recognition of the restrictions imposed by the existence of indexing mechanisms in the economy. The implementation of a well-defined nominal anchor and an exchange rate policy based on the objective of maintaining a narrow current account deficit and avoiding the use of the nominal exchange rate as an anti-inflationary tool also contributed. This resulted in a flexible macroeconomic policy scheme capable of timely response to changes in macroeconomic conditions (Chart 1). Within this Chilean experience, two stages can be clearly distinguished in relation to inflation targeting. The first and most extensive period runs from September 1990 to September 1999 and corresponds to the transition from high inflation rates to developed country levels. At this stage, the Central Bank carried out a hard monetary policy, defining a short-term horizon for the inflation target (one year) and applying a target point since 1994. However, the reduction in inflation was planned to materialize very gradually, reflecting concerns about economic growth in the short and medium term. In this period, the Central Bank also pursued a secondary objective, defined as a level of current account deficit considered sustainable over time, within a context of nominal exchange rate floating within an indexed band. The second stage of the implementation of inflation targeting began in September 1999, when the exchange rate band was finally abandoned, implementing a free-floating regime for our currency. Reaching flexibility in the exchange market required careful preparation, which had been carried out since 1997 and culminated with the floating of the peso in September 1999. What happened in that period showed that trying to maintain an exchange rate within a band does not help absorb external shocks, such as that of the Asian crisis, or internal ones such as excess spending in the economy, giving very few degrees of freedom to monetary policy. At the beginning of this second stage, it was also announced the transition from the annual point targets to a permanent range: inflation had been brought to levels that do not damage the economy and for the first time in seventy years. The control of inflation gave credibility to the policies of the BCCh and together with the maturity of the Chilean financial system allowed significant progress to be achieved in recent years with the elimination of regulations that led to the liberalization of the capital account of the balance of payments. This is consistent with avoiding movements in the real exchange rate beyond what is considered reasonable for a small economy open to international trade. Among the most important deregulations is the elimination of unremunerated reserve requirements for capital inflows and the requirements of at least one year for some types of capital, which were in place for much of the last decade. On the other hand, to advance in the deindexation of the economy, the BCCh took another very important step in August 2001, by abandoning the use of real rates in UF as an instrument of monetary policy for nominal rates in pesos. Chile was the only country in the world with real rates that involved a concept of readjustability as peculiar as the unit of tomentum. The nominalization of monetary policy made it possible to make the Monetary Policy Interest Rate (MPR) directly comparable with the rates in force in the rest of the countries of the world and to better regulate international capital movements, facilitating the process of financial integration into international markets. Nominalization is consistent with the convergence of local inflation to reduced levels and internationally comparable with that of the major economies and, in particular, with the floating exchange rate regime. In summary, the current scheme of policies implemented by the Central Bank has the following components: - Permanent inflation targets (range between 2 and 4%, centered on 3%). - Free floating of the exchange rate. - Movements change them without restrictions. - Capital movements with minimum regulations. - Nominalization of the monetary policy rate. Thanks to this policy scheme implemented in recent years, together with a rules-based fiscal policy, the Chilean economy has achieved positive growth rates in an environment of stable and controlled inflation. This policy framework has proven to be robust to a series of shocks and turbulence that, in other episodes of history, led our economy to depressions and financial crises, risks now diminished. In addition, it allows us to look more confidently at our relationship with the world and move forward with confidence in the negotiation of opening and integration schemes that contain elements of reciprocity and mutual benefit. This does not mean that we are immune to external events, we will suffer or benefit from their consequences. But it does mean that we will be able to absorb the possible negative effects of such events at lower private and social costs. A recent World Bank report highlights the resilience of the Chilean economy and concludes that our country suffers the least from the economic difficulties of 2001 and 2002 in Latin America, thanks to its effective integration into the world economy and its appropriate macroeconomic policies. 2. Assessment and prospects of the national and international economy 2003-2004 The figures contained in the IPoM have been updated in accordance with the latest available information discussed at the Monetary Policy Meeting held on Tuesday, October 14. This Report is the main instrument available to the Central Bank to transmit its policies and is a contribution in terms of transparency in the conduct of monetary policy. It is proven that this type of report used by other central banks of developed countries increases the effectiveness of such policy and also contributes to increasing the credibility and accountability of the Bank, as well as public support for the monetary policy decisions chosen. Our Report is published quarterly in January, May and September, and began in May 2000, with the aim of informing and explaining to the general public the vision of the Board of the Central Bank on recent and expected developments in inflation and its consequences. Another purpose of the Report is to publicly expose the medium-term analysis framework used in the formulation of monetary policy and provide useful information to the market that contributes to the formation of expectations about the future trajectory of inflation and output. It should be noted that each of the editions of this Inform includes boxes that present more detailed studies and considerations on topics relevant to the assessment of inflation and monetary policy. As an example, the September Report included, among others, boxes on "Monetary Policy Decisions in the last 3 months"; "Chile-United States FTA"; "Indirect taxes and inflation"; "The importance of the Risk Balance". I would particularly like to highlight the box referring to the Free Trade Agreement with the United States, which emphasizes the benefits that we will achieve with the signing of this agreement, which is expected to enter into force on January 1, 2004. As you know, the United States is Chile's main trading partner, considering jointly exports and imports by country during the last decade. Therefore, the Treaty is a great achievement for our economy and according to available estimates, it will have a positive impact on the country's product and foreign trade. The impact on output increases when considering, in addition to the traditional effects of trade liberalization, the effects of other factors, such as increased investment. It will also bring dynamic benefits over time that are not quantifiable, such as greater security when consolidating the policies of the Government, institutional improvements and higher standards of national policies, a dispute settlement mechanism and greater technological exchange that will mean productivity gains. Next, we will enter into the analysis of the specific chapters of the IPoM, first we will talk about the international scenario, we will see the trends of GDP and demand, then we will touch on some relevant aspects of domestic financial markets, and finally we will focus on prices and costs. I will also present to you the inflation and GDP projections, and the risk scenario we envision. To conclude the presentation, I will highlight the main conclusions of the Report. International scenario On the international scene, better activity prospects are beginning to consolidate, mainly based on the United States. and Japan. In both economies, their growth rates for the first quarter have been corrected upwards, and they show positive indicators for the second part of the year. In the case of the US, this reflects expansionary monetary and fiscal policies and higher productivity. In Japan, the external sector continues to lead growth and for the first time since 2000 the Tankan expectations survey showed positive values. On the other hand, growth in the euro area continues to be revised downwards, despite the fact that indicators of confidence and industrial activity indicate some improvement. For their part, Asian economies are the second engine of global growth, quickly overcoming the uncertainty caused by SARS. Thus, the most relevant changes in the external environment in the last four months have been: - The U.S. recovery for this year next. - Better prospects for emerging Asia. - Japan's surprise growth, and - Increased risk appetite. This scenario allows us to foresee a normal year 2004 for the world economy, after three years of low growth. Thus, global growth prospects have been revised upwards significantly over the past two months. For 2003, world growth is expected to be 2.5% weighted by Chile's main trading partners, and for the next two years this figure would be around 3.5% on average (Table 1). Regarding Monetary Policy Rates in the US and Europe, the Federal Reserve (FED) and the European Central Bank (ECB) cut their MPRs by 25 and 50bps last June and the markets do not expect further cuts, rather the beginning of a cycle of rate hikes is expected for 2004 (graph 2). On the other hand, risk aversion in emerging financial markets has continued to decline, reflected in falls in sovereign spreads and increases in risk appetite indicators. In the case of Chile, the reduction in the spread of its debt maturing in 2012 has been remarkable, which at the end of last year was almost 150 basis points, being today below 100 basis points (graph 3). In line with the expected recovery for global activity, the price of copper has evolved upwards with values close to USS 0.90 per pound in recent days. In this trajectory, a significant reduction in inventories has also contributed, largely explained by the greater demand from China and South Korea during this year. Projections for the coming years are 83 cents and 86 cents per pound for 2004 and 2005, respectively, although upward corrections in these values are expected if current metal price levels prevail (Chart 4). For the price of oil, the projections that were made in the past IPoM are around USS 28.5 per barrel this year and USS 26 next year, which will subtract about 1% from the terms of trade. The price of oil is expected to drop to USS 23 only in 2006. Annual growth of 0.8 per cent is projected for 2003 and an average increase of around 2.5 per cent per year is anticipated for 2004 and 2005. Activity, demand and employment In terms of domestic activity, the August indicator, recently published, showed a slowdown that for now we evaluate as explained mainly by specific and transitory factors associated with mining. This was due to technical problems that meant lower production in the companies, which should not be produced again in the future. On the other hand, the industry presented a more favorable performance, showing some signs of recovery with respect to the slowdown suffered in the second quarter of this year. On the other hand, the latest growth figures for domestic demand had a downward correction in the third quarter; However, towards the end of the year a significant recovery is expected, mainly due to higher imports. This would end 2003 with a growth in domestic demand of around 3 per cent, as expected some time ago (figure 5). Among the components of expenditure, investment weakened during the third quarter, as the machinery and equipment component and imports of capital goods were below what was observed in the first quarters of the year. At the same time, exports were very dynamic, in any case affected by a low base of comparison in 2002. Regarding consumption, during the second quarter it lost dynamism in relation to the previous quarters, however some positive indicators have appeared in the most recent, which opens the possibility of a faster recovery of this component, especially of habitual consumption. Likewise, consumer confidence, measured according to the survey of perception and expectations about the economy prepared by Adimark, shows a significant rebound in September, reaching a rate of 46%, the best since the beginning of 2000. The labour market during the June-August quarter confirmed the signs of lower dynamism observed since June, although total employment continued to grow, this time by 3.2% in twelve months. In seasonally adjusted terms, employment showed a fall as a result of the lower dynamics of employment linked to the private sector, which showed a decrease of 22,000 jobs in the moving quarter (graph 6). With regard to the composition of employment, recent emphasis has been placed on the growth of the secondary labour force sectors and also on the increase in women's participation in the labour force. Indeed, since the fourth quarter of 2002, women's participation in the labour market has shown a significant increase, returning to the historical highs prevailing in 2000, although the most recent information indicates a reversal. Different hypotheses can be raised in this regard. We have, on the one hand, that permanent changes could be taking place in the structure of the female labour market, so that the jobs that are being occupied would be linked to the more formal sector of the economy and, therefore, would be expected to be more permanent. On the other hand, however, the decline in the female labour force participation rate seen in the most recent information would suggest that the behaviour of the female labour force responded rather to a transitory cyclically-related shock (Figure 7). Domestic financial markets Since last month, the economy's medium- and long-term rates have seen increases that reflect greater optimism in the growth of the local economy, lower expectations of short-term inflation and the issuance of domestic debt by the Treasury. However, monetary conditions remain strongly expansionary, judging by the levels of interest rates prevailing in the economy and the conditions of the financial system (Chart 8). The banks' credit conditions have been more expansionary, and have been reflected in lower interest rates and a greater dynamism of placements, especially in the consumer loans segment, a segment in which important offers have focused on the most recent events. Also, housing loans continue to grow strongly. On the other hand, commercial placements have not increased significantly, mainly due to the lack of demand for this type of credit (Graph 9). One of the most outstanding developments in the financial markets in recent weeks has been the significant appreciation of the peso against the dollar (about 8% since the end of August). Among the phenomena that have contributed to this trajectory, the generalized weakness of the dollar in international markets (mainly against the euro and the yen) predominates on the external side, together with the improvement in the terms of trade of the Chilean economy, mainly due to the outstanding trajectory of the price of copper. All this is reflected in the fact that the real exchange rate has recently appreciated slightly. However, it should be noted that today it is around a value comparable to that of 1986, when the conditions facing the country were more complex. The level of the real exchange rate is clearly above the average of recent years (figure 10). Prices and costs Finally, the analysis of inflation in the short term shows that the inflation rate has had steep declines since last March, as previously stated at that time. However, last September's low inflation, which was mainly determined by the unusually lower price of non-perishable foodstuffs, was surprising but with effects probably only once. Core inflation, which excludes the price of goods and fuels, has also followed a lower trajectory than expected a few months ago. It is precisely because of these developments that the Council has decided to maintain the interest rate (Chart 11). Outlook for economic activity and inflation The available set of antecedents reaffirms a more favorable scenario for the activity, since the negative news of the mining sector is estimated as transitory and there are better international prospects for this and next year. Projections of better terms of trade have also been strengthened, with copper prices consistently above 80 cents, with external financial conditions more positive than some time ago. In the inflationary area, for now, it is estimated that the surprise of inflation in September does not change the underlying trends anticipated in the last IPoM. It should be noted that the lowest inflation recorded was concentrated in a particular group of goods (non-perished food) that allows this news to be associated with the competition that has been generated in the supermarket category. This set of precedents will take this year's economic growth to a range between 3 and 3.5%. For 2004, GDP growth is expected to be between 4 and 5 per cent. This better picture can be seen in the performance of local stock indices, which have performed very favorably in recent weeks. For its part, domestic spending will grow at a rate between 0.5 and 1% above GDP expansion during 2004-2005. This process will be consumption-driven, in response to improved national income and investment, in reaction to lower capacity gaps and a higher rate of return for firms. The 2003-2004 growth projections of the private sector have not changed substantially in recent months, and are within the Central Bank's projection range. In the most likely scenario estimated by the Council, the inflation trend should remain close to the target range. The impact of the recent VAT hike on the CPI will be transitory, because it only involves a one-time change in the price level. However, monetary policy must be careful so that this change for once does not spread towards inflation through second-round effects. Annual CPI inflation will average 2.7% over the next 24 months, with sharp swings. Core inflation (CPI), meanwhile, will temporarily reach values close to 3.5%. But the persistence of slack and a limited panorama of costs will make it descend towards the center of the target range. Indeed, inflation is likely to be temporarily below 2 percent in some specific months, especially in the first quarter of 2004. Risk scenarios As usual, the projections presented here correspond to the base scenario of the IPoM. However, there are a number of relevant risks that the Central Bank considers in its analysis and that configure alternative scenarios for both inflation and growth, which constitute the balance of risks for both variables. The importance of risk analysis lies in the fact that, in practice, any projection exercise is subject to significant degrees of uncertainty. There is little certainty regarding the direction that the international economy will take, for example, in the future or the price of commodities. The use of projections based on expert opinions allows for the most informed opinion available, but does not eliminate this uncertainty. The risk balance sheet is the instrument used by the Board to communicate in the reports its perception of the most relevant implications of the different sources of uncertainty. The realization of our projections depends on a greater consolidation of the external scenario, and a sustained recovery in the terms of trade. Therefore, the main sources of risk considered in the IPoM include: - Uncertainty in the oil market. - The high fiscal and current account deficits of the US - Europe's structural problems. - The fragility of financial systems in Japan and China. Internally, in recent weeks there have been favourable changes in the exchange rate, country risk and expectations, reflecting greater optimism. If these conditions are maintained sustainably, a scenario could be configured with a growth greater than that outlined here. One source of concern is the possible divergence in the future between nominal wage growth and labour productivity. The risk posed by external inflation is limited; That at least follows from recent experience, where the economy has accommodated changes in relative prices without lingering effects on inflation. Other external risksd1such as adverse movements in oil pricesd1have a limited impact on the medium-term path of inflation. However, the Board of the Central Bank estimates that the balance of risks is balanced, both for growth and inflation. Conclusions To conclude, I would like to present you with a summary table containing the main assumptions and projections considered by the Central Bank in September's IPoM. Projections for activity in 2003 and 2004 see the beginning of a phase of higher growth. This scenario is supported by higher global growth and better financial conditions. Towards the third quarter of 2005, in the most likely scenario, measures of total (CPI) and core (CPI) inflation will be 3.2-3.3%, with averages of 2.7% and 3.2% for the next 24 months, respectively (Table 2). The Council considers that the current monetary policy stance is consistent with the objective of keeping inflation within the target range. In any case, if capacity gaps close more quickly , monetary policy would tend to be less expansionary. As always, the Council will react flexibly to events that, in one direction or another, jeopardize the achievement of the inflation target. Finally, I cannot fail to emphasize that in recent years a reserve of macroeconomic stability and credibility has been gradually built that differentiates us from other emerging economies. The adoption of a policy framework such as the one mentioned in this presentation constitutes a true pillar of Chile's economic and financial stability. We are now less vulnerable than other emerging economies. Our strengths lie in: an appropriate mix of monetary and fiscal policies, a policy of exchange rate flexibility, macroeconomic stability, very small current account deficits, a sound and well-supervised financial system, a reasonable external debt d1 private and mostly medium- and long-term d1 a low public debt, and a highly distorted, competitive, and widely predominant economy of economic freedom. Additionally, during critical periods that have been experienced in recent times, the Central Bank has been flexible in the face of changes in the world economy. This combination of credibility and flexibility of the Issuing Institute is another of the great assets that the Chilean economy has.

Antes de entrar en materia, me gustara hacer una breve introduccin sobre los objetivos del Banco Central, destacando la importancia que tienen en su actuar la institucionalidad, la credibilidad y la transparencia de sus polticas. El Banco Central de Chile (BCCh) fue creado en 1 925, y actualmente est regido por la Ley Orgnica Constitucional (LO C) aprobada en 1989. Es una institucin de derecho pblico, con carcter autnomo, independiente frente a los poderes del Estado, ya que solo se encuentra sometido a la Constitucin Poltica y a su LO C que regula su composicin, organizacin, funciones y atribuciones. El Banco Central forma parte de la nueva institucionalidad establecida en la Constitucin, y su inclusin en ella, tuvo por objeto preciso entregarle la responsabilidad de mantenerla estabilidad macroeconmica, materia esencial en el desarrollo del pas e indispensable para preservar la confianza de los inversionistas internos y externos. Con ello, se evit su dependencia del Gobierno, que en el pasado se tradujo en endeudamiento fiscal a travs de emisin inorgnica y en adopcin de polticas influidas por circunstancias ajenas a sus funciones especficas. El equilibrio macroeconmico de un pas estimula el crecimiento de la produccin, de la inversin, el fomento del empleo y de los salarios. De all la importancia del Banco Central, cuyos objetivos fundamentales son:  Velar por la estabilidad de la moneda, lo que significa la mantencin del poder adquisitivo del dinero, esto es, el control del proceso inflacionario, por los efectos perniciosos que ste provoca en la asignacin de los recursos productivos y en la distribucin del ingreso.  Velar por el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos, es decir, que stos se efecten con fluidez. Para ello, entre otras cosas, el Banco Central debe cautelar la estabilidad del sistema financiero y mantener un volumen adecuado tanto de dinero en la economa interna como de divisas para los efectos de pagos al exterior. En esta introduccin, me gustara enfatizar que nuestra gran motivacin para la realizacin de estos encuentros, se basa en la importancia de la transparencia en el accionar de un banco central autnomo. A travs de esta transparencia, contribuimos a que el pblico sea capaz de entendery anticipar nuestras decisiones y, por esta va, mejorar la efectividad de las polticas monetaria y financiera y, al mismo tiempo, incrementar la credibilidad en la institucin haciendo al Banco Central responsable de su actuar frente a toda la sociedad. Para fortalecer an ms la credibilidad del marco de polticas, estamos convencidos de que el Banco Central debe tender a fomentar una mejor comprensin de los mecanismos de transmisin de la poltica monetaria, incrementar la divulgacin pblica de informacin estadstica y mtodos de anlisis utilizados, e incrementar la transparencia de las proyecciones y de las decisiones de poltica. No hace tantos aos, la visin de los banqueros centrales era muy distinta a la actual. Se crea que la poltica monetaria resultaba ms eficaz cuando se formulaba ms en secreto y resultaba inquietante ser demasiado explcitos en relacin con metas. Se pensaba que en caso de una inadecuada transmisin de las mismas se volvera ms difcil cambiar el rumbo, impidiendo de esa manera los necesarios ajustes para que el mercado pueda evolucionar segn las condiciones econmicas deseables en cada momento. En la medida en que el funcionamiento de los mercados y de los instrumentos financieros se fueron transformando y requiriendo de menores niveles de incertidumbre para ser ms eficientes, surge un cambio de apreciacin sobre la necesidad y la importancia de la transparencia, la que comenz a valorarse cada da ms. Hoy, los mercados financieros trabajan con mayor eficiencia porque los participantes no tienen que desperdiciar los enormes esfuerzos de antes en el intento continuo de inferir cul es la decisin de poltica monetaria a partir de seales poco claras del da a da. Adems, se ha dado la particularidad de que esta mayor transparencia no ha significado ninguna restriccin en la discrecionalidad de que disponemos para ajustar la poltica monetaria en la direccin que corresponda cada vez que sea necesario. Consecuentemente, hoy nos movemos con mucha mayor claridad en nuestras decisiones de poltica, incluyendo tambin la informacin sobre los riesgos futuros ms relevantes. En esa direccin, hace un tiempo que venimos haciendo esfuerzos por movernos hacia una mayor transparencia. Estos esfuerzos se reflejan en la preparacin y publicacin del informe cuatrimestral de poltica monetaria (IPoM)', los comunicados de prensa que siguen a las reuniones mensuales de poltica monetaria; la publicacin de las minutas de estas reuniones con un rezago de 45 das; la informacin que entrega el Banco Central en su pgina web, en sus mltiples publicaciones de carcter tcnico, y en las intervenciones pblicas de su Presidente, de los miembros del Consejo y de los principales ejecutivos del staf. En definitiva, la experiencia ha demostrado que la transparencia ha contribuido a mejorar el funcionamiento de los mercados y, tambin, a hacer mayor nuestra credibilidad por parte del pblico. Hoy, este tipo de apertura es ms que un instrumento til para la conduccin de la poltica econmica de un pas, es un deber de los bancos centrales con la sociedad. Como se seal anteriormente, desde el comienzo de su autonoma, al BC Ch se le concedi toda la responsabilidad en la configuracin e instrumentalizacin de la poltica monetaria, como cuerpo independiente del Gobierno; se le dio un claro mandato para que consiguiera la estabilidad de precios y se le concedieron las atribuciones para hacerlo, lo que fue un factor clave para el control de la inflacin. Ello demuestra que una buena institucionalidad, con entidades serias y crebles es un elemento clave, tanto en la fijacin de las principales metas macroeconmicas como en la recepcin por parte del mercado de las polticas implementadas por la autoridad. La creacin de buenas instituciones, no solo monetarias sino tambin fiscales y financieras es prioritaria, y creo que nuestro pas lo ha comprendido muy bien, ya que, el prestigio y solidez de nuestras instituciones y de sus polticas nos ha permitido lograr un amplio reconocimiento internacional a lo largo de los ltimos aos. En particular, la autonoma del Banco Central ha sido muy importante. Tal caracterstica, unida ahora a la transparencia de nuestras actividades, es lo que nos hace realmente crebles ante el pblico, y lo que nos permite ayudarles para que ellos mismos juzguen si nuestra tarea est a la altura de lo que ellos piensan que debe ser. Otro punto que me gustara destacar antes de entrar en el contenido del IPoM, es la razn de nuestra decisin de centrar el objetivo inflacionario en un plazo de 2 aos. Esto se debe a que los efectos de la poltica monetaria sobre la inflacin se sienten con ms fuerza en un plazo mediano y que shocks transitorios sobre los precios no requieren necesariamente de cambios en la poltica monetaria, como por ejemplo, los probables efectos sobre el IPC que tenga el reciente incremento del IVA. En contraste, si tuviramos una meta a conseguir en un plazo ms corto, la poltica monetaria tendra que ser mucho ms activa, con el riesgo de exacerbar el ciclo econmico y, eventualmente, generar costos innecesarios para la economa. Para enfrentar este escenario de mediano plazo, tenemos un activo importante, que son los slidos fundamentos de nuestra economa, y si adems se dan las favorables condiciones que se esperan en el escenario internacional y se mantienen las condiciones monetarias vigentes tendremos la recuperacin que esperamos. No quiero dejar pasar la ocasin de sealarles que el proyectar a mediano plazo tiene peligros, sobre todo cuando hay perodos de bajo crecimiento, como ocurri entre 1998 y 2002. Estos peligros son la impaciencia, el pesimismo y la inflexibilidad, que pueden desviar la economa de su senda de largo plazo. La impaciencia afecta las polticas econmicas cuando se enfrentan episodios difciles. Se puede manifestar en acciones de poltica que no son sostenibles en el tiempo y que, ms temprano que tarde, deben ser corregidas. Sin embargo, la actual combinacin de poltica fiscal y monetaria nos tiene adecuadamente alejados de este riesgo. La poltica fiscal est basada en una regla orientada a establecer un supervit estructural equivalente a 1% del producto interno bruto (PIB), la cual tiene un efecto de moderacin del ciclo econmico y permite que el sector pblico haga un mayor aporte al ahorro nacional en el horizonte de mediano plazo, posibilitando un mayor crecimiento de la inversin y condiciones monetarias ms holgadas. La poltica monetaria, por su parte, ha logrado mantener la estabilidad de precios, como veremos en detalle ms adelante. Hoy, tenemos tasas de inters internas histricamente bajas y sin peligro de inflacin. El segundo peligro son las olas de optimismo y pesimismo por parte de los agentes del mercado. stas suelen tener influencia en diferentes episodios econmicos, especialmente cuando existe informacin imperfecta e incertidumbre, pudiendo en ocasiones prolongar los perodos recesivos o de bajo crecimiento. Las percepciones de los consumidores e inversionistas se reflejan en sus decisiones, pero al mismo tiempo son la fuente de informacin de otros agentes al formar sus propias percepciones. Las expectativas se alimentan de lo que ocurre en el muy corto plazo, generando situaciones de profecas autocumplidas, en las cuales algunos agentes siguen las acciones de otros a la hora de formar sus percepciones, ms que hacer su propia evaluacin de los fundamentos de la economa en un horizonte de mediano plazo. Por ello, para el Banco Central estn importante ser lo ms transparente posible y entregar cada vez mayor y ms oportuna informacin al mercado, contribuyendo de esa manera a la formacin de expectativas de los agentes, ampliando el horizonte que sirve de base a sus percepciones y reafirmando las bases comunes del modelo de crecimiento. El tercer riesgo del actual escenario se encuentra en las imperfecciones del mercado que obstaculizan los cambios en los precios relativos o las decisiones que de ellos se desprenden. Para acomodar los ciclos externos, que estn en el origen de esta fase de menor crecimiento, la economa requiere no slo de estabilidad macroeconmica, sino tambin de flexibilidad en los precios y en los mercados, de modo de facilitar los necesarios ajustes sectoriales, concordantes con las nuevas condiciones de la economa. Informe de poltica monetaria (IPoM)  Control de la inflacin y actual esquema de polticas Para comenzar, quisiera recordar que la poltica monetaria del BCCh tiene como principal objetivo mantenerla inflacin en un nivel bajo y estable, definido como un rango de 2 a 4%, centrado en 3%. El control de la inflacin es la manera en que la poltica monetaria contribuye al bienestar de la poblacin, ya que ello promueve un mejor funcionamiento de la economa y un mayor crecimiento econmico, al tiempo que evita la erosin de los ingresos de las personas, principalmente de los ms pobres. Adems, la orientacin de la poltica monetaria hacia el logro de una meta de inflacin situada en un nivel bajo y estable, ayuda a que se moderen las fluctuaciones del empleo y la produccin nacional. El Banco Central busca conseguir su objetivo inflacionario de la manera ms eficiente posible, desde una perspectiva de crecimiento y empleo. En otras palabras, si para mantener la inflacin en torno a la meta hay ms de una trayectoria posible de las tasas de inters de poltica, escogeremos aquella que tenga el menor sacrificio potencial de crecimiento de la demanda interna y, por aadidura, de la actividad econmica y el empleo. La experiencia chilena de los noventa en materia de control de la inflacin fue de un avance gradual y sostenido, que no motiv desequilibrios mayores y que, por su solidez, permita augurar que sus resultados fueran duraderos. En este perodo, la reduccin de la inflacin en Chile se bas en una gran disciplina y conviccin para avanzar sostenidamente en la lucha antiinflacionaria y en el reconocimiento de las restricciones que impone la existencia de mecanismos de indizacin en la economa. Tambin contribuy la implementacin de un ancla nominal bien definida y una poltica cambiara basada en el objetivo de mantener un dficit de cuenta corriente acotado y evitar el uso del tipo de cambio nominal como herramienta antiinflacionaria. Con ello, se logr un esquema de poltica macroeconmica flexible y capaz de reaccionar oportunamente ante cambios de las condiciones macroeconmicas (grfico 1). Dentro de esta experiencia chilena se pueden distinguir claramente dos etapas en relacin con las metas de inflacin. La primera y ms extensa va desde septiembre de 1990 a septiembre de 1999 y corresponde a la transicin desde altas tasas de inflacin hacia los niveles de pases desarrollados. En esta etapa, el Banco Central efectu una poltica monetaria de corte duro, definiendo un horizonte de corto plazo para la meta de inflacin (un ao) y aplic una meta punto desde 1994. Sin embargo, la reduccin de la inflacin se planific para ser materializada de manera muy gradual, reflejando preocupacin por el crecimiento econmico en el corto y mediano plazo. En este perodo, el Banco Central tambin persigui un objetivo de carcter secundario, definido como un nivel de dficit de la cuenta corriente considerado sostenible en el tiempo, dentro de un contexto de tipo de cambio nominal flotando al interior de una banda indizada. La segunda etapa de la implementacin de metas de inflacin comenz en septiembre de 1999, cuando la banda cambiara fue finalmente abandonada implantndose un rgimen de libre flotacin para nuestra moneda. Llegar a la flexibilidad en el mercado cambiarlo requiri de una cuidadosa preparacin, la que se vena realizando desde 1997 y culmin con la flotacin del peso en septiembre de 1999. Lo ocurrido en ese perodo demostr que pretender mantener un tipo de cambio dentro de una banda no ayuda a absorber impactos externos, como el de la crisis asitica, o internos como el exceso de gasto de la economa, dndole muy pocos grados de libertad a la poltica monetaria. En el comienzo de esta segunda etapa, se anunci, adems, el paso de las metas punto anuales a una meta rango de carcter permanente: se haba logrado llevar la inflacin a niveles que no daan la economa y por primera vez en setenta aos. El control de la inflacin dio credibilidad en las polticas del BCCh y junto a la madurez del sistema financiero chileno permitieron lograr en los ltimos aos avances significativos con la eliminacin de regulaciones que llevaron a la liberalizacin de la cuenta de capitales de la balanza de pagos. Ello es consistente con evitar movimientos del tipo de cambio real ms all de lo que se considera razonable para una economa pequea y abierta al comercio internacional. Entre las desregulaciones ms importantes se encuentra la eliminacin del encaje no remunerado a las entradas de capital y los requerimientos de permanencia de al menos un ao para algunos tipos de capital, los cuales estuvieron vigentes durante gran parte de la dcada pasada. Por otro lado, para avanzar en la desindizacin de la economa, el BCCh dio otro paso muy importante en agosto del 2001, al abandonar el uso de tasas reales en UF como instrumento de poltica monetaria por tasas nominales en pesos. Chile era el nico pas del mundo con tasas reales que involucraban un concepto de reajustabilidad tan peculiar como lo es la unidad de tomento. La nominalizacin de la poltica monetaria permiti hacer directamente comparable la Tasa de Inters de Poltica Monetaria (TPM) con las tasas vigentes en el resto de los pases del mundo y regular mejor los movimientos internacionales de capitales, acilitando el proceso de integracin financiera a los mercados internacionales. La nominalizacin es consistente con la convergencia de la inflacin local a niveles reducidos e internacionalmente comparables con el de las principales economas y, en particular, con el rgimen de flotacin cambiara.
