En sntesis, el esquema actual de polticas implementadas por el Banco Central tiene los siguientes componentes:  Metas de inflacin permanentes (rango entre 2 y 4%, centrado en 3%).  Libre flotacin del tipo de cambio.  Movimientos cambiarlos sin restricciones.  Movimientos de capital con regulaciones mnimas.  Nominalizacin de la tasa de poltica monetaria. Gracias a este esquema de polticas implementado en los ltimos aos, junto con una poltica fiscal basada en reglas, la economa chilena ha logrado tasas positivas de crecimiento en un entorno de inflacin estable y controlada. Este marco de polticas ha demostrado ser robusto a una seguidilla de shocksy turbulencias que, en otros episodios de la historia, llevaron a nuestra economa a depresiones y crisis financieras, riesgos hoy disminuidos. Adems, nos permite mirar con ms confianza nuestra relacin con el mundo y avanzar con seguridad en la negociacin de esquemas de apertura e integracin que contengan elementos de reciprocidad y beneficio mutuo. Ello no significa que seamos inmunes a los acontecimientos externos, sufriremos o nos beneficiaremos de sus consecuencias. Pero s significa que podremos absorber con menores costos privados y sociales los eventuales efectos negativos de tales acontecimientos. Un informe reciente del Banco Mundial destaca la capacidad de resistencia de la economa chilena y concluye que nuestro pas es uno de los que menos sufri con las dificultades econmicas de 2001 y 2002 en Amrica Latina, gracias a su integracin efectiva en la economa mundial y a sus polticas macroeconmicas adecuadas.  Evaluacin y perspectivas de la economa nacional e internacional 2003-2004 Las cifras contenidas en el IPoM han sido actualizadas de acuerdo con la ltima informacin disponible discutida en la Reunin de Poltica Monetaria efectuada el martes 14 de octubre recin pasado. Este Informe es el principal instrumento con que cuenta el Banco C entral para transmitir sus polticas y es un aporte en trminos de la transparencia en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. Est comprobado que este tipo de informe usado por otros bancos centrales de pases desarrollados, aumenta la eficacia de dicha poltica y contribuye tambin a aumentar la credibilidad y responsabilidad del Banco, as como el apoyo del pblico a las decisiones de poltica monetaria elegidas. Nuestro Informe se publica cuatrimestralmente en los meses de enero, mayo y septiembre, y empez en mayo de 2000, con el objetivo de informar y explicar al pblico general cul es la visin del Consejo del Banco Central sobre la evolucin reciente y esperada de la inflacin y sus consecuencias. Otro de los propsitos del Informe, es exponer pblicamente el marco de anlisis de mediano plazo utilizado en la formulacin de la poltica monetaria y proveer de informacin til al mercado que contribuya a la formacin de expectativas sobre la trayectoria futura de la inflacin y del producto. Cabe destacar que en cada una de las ediciones de este Infrmese incluyen recuadros que presentan estudios y consideraciones ms detalladas sobre temas relevantes para la evaluacin de la inflacin y de la poltica monetaria. Como ejemplo, en el Informe de septiembre se incluyeron, entre otros, recuadros sobre Decisiones de Poltica Monetaria en los ltimos 3 meses; "TLC entre Chile y Estados Unidos; Impuestos indirectos e inflacin"; "La importancia del Balance de riesgos. Me gustara destacar especialmente el recuadro referido al Tratado de Libre Comercio con Estados Unidos que hace hincapi en los beneficios que lograremos con la firma de este acuerdo, el cual se espera entre en vigencia el 1 de enero de 2004. Como ustedes saben, Estados Unidos es el principal socio comercial de Chile, considerando conjuntamente exportaciones e importaciones por pas durante la ltima dcada. Por ello, el Tratado es un gran logro para nuestra economa y de acuerdo con las estimaciones disponibles, tendr un impacto positivo en el producto y el comercio exterior del pas. El impacto sobre el producto aumenta al considerar, adems de los efectos tradicionales dla apertura comercial, los efectos de otros factores, tales como mayor inversin. Tambin, traer beneficios dinmicos en el tiempo que no son cuantificables, como la mayor seguridad al consolidarse las polticas del G obierno, mejoras institucionales y mayores estndares de las polticas nacionales, un mecanismo de solucin de controversias y un mayor intercambio tecnolgico que significar aumentos de productividad. A continuacin, entraremos en el anlisis de los captulos especficos del IPoM, primero hablaremos del escenario internacional, veremos las tendencias del PIB y la demanda, luego tocaremos algunos aspectos relevantes de los mercados financieros domsticos, y finalmente nos centraremos en los precios y costos. Tambin les presentar las proyecciones de inflacin y PIB, y el escenario de riesgos que visualizamos. Para terminar la exposicin, destacar las principales conclusiones del Informe. Escenario internacional En el escenario internacional, comienzan a consolidarse mejores perspectivas de actividad, fundamentadas principalmente porEE.UU. y Japn. En ambas economas se han corregido al alza sus tasas de crecimiento del primer trimestre, y muestran indicadores positivos para la segunda parte del ao. En el caso de EE.UU., esto es reflejo de polticas monetarias y fiscales expansivas y mayor productividad. En Japn, el sector externo sigue liderando el crecimiento y por primera vez desde el ao 2000 la encuesta de expectativas Tankan mostr valores positivos. En cambio, en la zona euro el crecimiento sigue revisndose a la baja, no obstante que los indicadores de confianza y actividad industrial sealan alguna mejora. Por su parte, las economas asiticas se constituyen como el segundo motor de crecimiento mundial, superando rpidamente la incertidumbre provocada por el SARS. As, los cambios ms relevantes en el entorno externo en estos ltimos cuatro meses han sido:  La recuperacin de EE.UU. para estey el prximo ao.  Mejores perspectivas de Asia emergente.  El sorpresivo crecimiento de Japn, y  El aumento del apetito por riesgo. Este panorama permite prever un ao 2004 normal para la economa mundial, despus de tres aos de bajo crecimiento. As, las perspectivas de crecimiento mundial se han corregido al alza de manera importante en los ltimos dos meses. Para el 2003, se espera un crecimiento mundial de 2,5% ponderado por los principales socios comerciales de Chile, y para los prximos dos aos esta cifra se situara en torno a 3,5% en promedio (tabla 1). Respecto a las Tasas de Poltica Monetaria en EE.UU. y Europa, el Federal Reserve (FED) y el Banco Central Europeo (BCE) recortaron sus TPM en 25 y 50pb durante junio pasado y los mercados no esperan nuevos recortes, ms bien se espera el inicio de un ciclo de alzas de tasas para el ao 2004 (grfico 2). Por otra parte, se ha continuado reduciendo la aversin al riesgo de los mercados financieros emergentes, lo que se ha reflejado en cadas en los spreadssoberanos e incrementos de los indicadores de apetito por riesgo. En el caso de Chile, ha sido notable la reduccin del spreadde su deuda con vencimiento el 2012, la que a fines del ao pasado era de casi 150 puntos base, encontrndose hoy bajo los 100 puntos base (grfico 3). Acorde con la recuperacin prevista para la actividad mundial, el precio del cobre ha evolucionado al alza con valores cercanos a USS 0,90 por libra en los ltimos das. En esta trayectoria, ha contribuido adems una reduccin importante de los inventarios, explicada en gran medida por la mayor demanda de China y Corea del Sur durante este ao. Las proyecciones para los prximos aos se ubican en 83 centavos y 86 centavos de dlar por libra para el 2004 y el 2005, respectivamente, aunque es de esperar correcciones al alza en estos valores de prevalecer los niveles actuales del precio del metal (grfico 4). Para el precio del petrleo, las proyecciones que se hicieron en el pasado IPoMse ubican en torno a USS 28,5 por barril este ao y USS 26 el prximo, loque restar cerca de 1 % a los trminos de intercambio. Se espera que el precio del petrleo descienda a USS 23 recin el 2006. Para el 2003 se proyecta un crecimiento anual de 0,8% y para el 2004 y 2005 se anticipa un incremento promedio cercano a 2,5% anual. Actividad, demanda y empleo En trminos de actividad interna, el indicador de agosto, recientemente publicado, present una desaceleracin que por ahora evaluamos como explicada principalmente por factores puntuales y transitorios asociados a la minera. Ello se debi a problemas tcnicos que significaron una menor produccin en las compaas, los que no deberan volver a producirse en el futuro. Como contraparte, la industria present un comportamiento ms favorable, mostrando algunos signos de recuperacin respecto de la desaceleracin sufrida en el segundo trimestre de este ao. Por su parte, las ltimas cifras de crecimiento de la demanda interna tuvieron una correccin a la baja en el tercer trimestre; no obstante, hacia fines de ao se espera una recuperacin importante, principalmente por mayores importaciones. Con ello, se terminara el 2003 con un crecimiento de la demanda interna del orden de 3%, de acuerdo con lo previsto hace algn tiempo (grfico 5). Entre los componentes del gasto, la inversin se debilit durante el tercer trimestre, ya que el componente maquinaria y equipos y las importaciones de bienes de capital se ubicaron por debajo de lo observado en los primeros trimestres del ao. A su vez, las exportaciones registraron un alto dinamismo, en todo caso afectado por una baja base de comparacin en el 2002. Respecto al consumo, durante el segundo trimestre perdi dinamismo en relacin con los trimestres previos, no obstante han aparecido algunos indicadores positivos en lo ms reciente, lo que abre la posibilidad de una recuperacin ms rpida de este componente, especialmente de consumo habitual. Asimismo, la confianza del consumidor, medida segn la encuesta de percepcin y expectativas sobre la economa elaborada por Adimark, muestra un repunte significativo en el mes de septiembre, llegando a un ndice de 46%, el mejor desde comienzos de 2000. El mercado laboral durante el trimestre junio-agosto confirm las seales de menor dinamismo observadas desde junio, aunque el empleo total continu creciendo, esta vez en 3,2% en doce meses. En trminos desestacionalizados, el empleo mostr una cada producto de la menor dinmica del empleo ligado al sector privado, el que present una disminucin de 22.000 puestos de trabajo en el trimestre mvil (grfico 6). En cuanto a la composicin del empleo, en el ltimo tiempo ha destacado el crecimiento de los sectores de la fuerza de trabajo secundaria y tambin el incremento de la participacin de las mujeres en la fuerza de trabajo. En efecto, a partir del cuarto trimestre del 2002, la participacin de la mujer en el mercado laboral ha mostrado un significativo aumento, retornando a los mximos histricos prevalecientes en el 2000, aunque la informacin ms reciente indica una reversin. Distintas hiptesis pueden plantearse al respecto. Tenemos, por una parte, que podran estar ocurriendo cambios permanentes en la estructura del mercado laboral femenino, de forma tal que los puestos de trabajo que se estn ocupando estaran ligados al sector ms formal de la economa y, por lo mismo, se esperara que fueran ms permanentes. Sin embargo, por otra parte, la disminucin de la tasa de participacin de la fuerza de trabajo femenina que se ha visto en la informacin ms reciente dara cuenta de que el comportamiento de la fuerza laboral femenina respondi ms bien a un shock transitorio relacionado con el ciclo (grfico 7). Mercados financieros domsticos Desde el mes pasado, las tasas de mediano y largo plazo de la economa han experimentado aumentos que reflejan un mayor optimismo en el crecimiento de la economa local, menores expectativas de inflacin de corto plazo y la emisin de deuda interna por parte del Fisco. No obstante, las condiciones monetarias siguen siendo fuertemente expansivas, si juzgamos por los niveles de las tasas de inters vigentes en la economa y las condiciones del sistema financiero (grfico 8). Las condiciones crediticias de la banca han sido ms expansivas, y se han reflejado en menores tasas de inters y un mayor dinamismo de las colocaciones, especialmente en el segmento de crditos de consumo, segmento en el que se han centrado importantes ofertas en lo ms reciente. Tambin, los crditos para la vivienda siguen creciendo con fuerza. En cambio, las colocaciones comerciales no han tenido un incremento significativo, debido principalmente a la falta de demanda por este tipo de crditos (grfico 9). Uno de los hechos ms sobresalientes en los mercados financieros durante las ltimas semanas ha sido la importante apreciacin del peso respecto del dlar (cerca de 8% desde fines de agosto). Entre los fenmenos que han contribuido a esta trayectoria, predominan, por el lado externo, la debilidad generalizada del dlar en los mercados internacionales (principalmente respecto del euro y del yen), junto con la mejora de los trminos de intercambio de la economa chilena, principalmente por la destacada trayectoria del precio del cobre. Todo esto se ve reflejado en que el tipo de cambio real ha sufrido una leve apreciacin recientemente. Sin embargo, hay que destacar que hoy se ubica en torno a un valor comparable al del ao 1986, cuando las condiciones que enfrentaba el pas eran ms complejas. El nivel del tipo de cambio real es claramente superior al promedio de los ltimos aos (grfico 10). Precios y costos Por ltimo, el anlisis de la inflacin en el corto plazo muestra que la tasa de inflacin ha tenido descensos pronunciados desde marzo pasado, conforme se previo en aquel entonces. No obstante, la baja inflacin de septiembre pasado, que fue determinada principalmente por el inusual menor precio de los alimentos no perec bles, fue sorpresiva pero con efectos probablemente por una sola vez. Asimismo, la inflacin subyacente, que excluye el precio de perec bles y combustibles, ha seguido una trayectoria menor a la prevista hace algunos meses. Justamente por esta evolucin, el Consejo ha decidido mantener la tasa de inters (grfico 11). Perspectivas de actividad e inflacin El conjunto de antecedentes disponible reafirma un escenario ms propicio para la actividad, ya que las noticias negativas del sector minera se estiman como transitorias y existen mejores perspectivas internacionales para este y el prximo ao. Asimismo, se han do afianzando las proyecciones de mejores trminos de intercambio, con un precio del cobre sistemticamente por sobre los 80 centavos de dlar, con condiciones financieras externas ms positivas que hace algn tiempo. En el mbito inflacionario, por ahora, se estima que la sorpresa de la inflacin de septiembre no modifica las tendencias subyacentes anticipadas en el ltimo IPoM. Cabe destacar que la menor inflacin registrada se concentr en un grupo particular de bienes (alimentos no pereciles) que permite asociar esta noticia a la competencia que se ha generado en el rubro supermercados. Este conjunto de antecedentes llevar el crecimiento econmico de este ao a un rango entre 3 y 3,5%. Para el ao 2004, se espera un crecimiento del PIB entre 4 y 5%. Este mejor panorama se aprecia en el desempeo de los ndices accionarios locales que han tenido un comportamiento muy favorable en las ltimas semanas. Por su parte, el gasto interno crecer ana tasa entre 0,5 y 1% por sobre la expansin del PIB durante 2004-2005. Este proceso ser impulsado por el consumo, en respuesta a una mejora del ingreso nacional y la inversin, en reaccin a menores holguras de capacidad y una mayortasa de rentabilidad de las empresas. Las proyecciones de crecimiento 2003-2004 del sector privado no han cambiado de manera sustantiva en los ltimos meses, y se encuentran dentro del rango de proyeccin del Banco Central. En el escenario ms probable estimado por el Consejo, la tendencia de la inflacin debera mantenerse cerca del rango meta. El impacto de la reciente alza del IVA sobre el IPC ser transitorio, porque slo involucra un cambio por una sola vez en el nivel de precios. Sin embargo, la poltica monetaria debe cautelar para que este cambio por una vez no se propague hacia la inflacin a travs de efectos de segunda vuelta. La inflacin anual del IPC alcanzar un promedio de 2,7% en los prximos 24 meses, con vaivenes pronunciados. La inflacin subyacente (IPCX), en tanto, alcanzar transitoriamente valores cercanos a 3,5%. Pero la persistencia de holguras y un panorama acotado de costos la har descender hacia el centro del rango meta. De hecho, es probable que la inflacin se ubique transitoriamente debajo del 2% en algunos meses especficos, especialmente en el primer trimestre de 2004. Escenarios de riesgo Como es habitual, las proyecciones aqu presentadas corresponden al escenario base del IPoM. Sin embargo, existe una serie de riesgos relevantes que el Banco Central considera en su anlisis y que configuran escenarios alternativos tanto para la inflacin como para el crecimiento, los que constituyen el balance de riesgos para ambas variables. La importancia del anlisis de riesgos radica en que, en la prctica, todo ejercicio de proyeccin est sujeto a importantes grados de incertidumbre. Existe poca certeza con respecto a la direccin que tomar, por ejemplo, la economa internacional en el futuro o el precio de los productos bsicos. El uso de proyecciones basadas en opiniones expertas permite contar con la opinin ms informada disponible, pero no elimina esta incertidumbre. El balance de riesgos es el instrumento que usa el Consejo para comunicar en los informes su percepcin sobre las implicancias ms relevantes de las distintas fuentes de incertidumbre. La concrecin de nuestras proyecciones depende de un afianzamiento mayor del escenario externo, y una recuperacin sostenida de los trminos de intercambio. Por ende, las principales fuentes de riesgo consideradas en el IPoM, incluyen:  La incertidumbre en el mercado del petrleo.  Los altos dficit fiscales y de cuenta corriente de EE.UU.  Los problemas estructurales de Europa.  La fragilidad de los sistemas financieros en Japn y China. Internamente, en las ltimas semanas han ocurrido cambios favorables en el tipo de cambio, en el riesgo pasy en las expectativas, lo que refleja un mayor optimismo. De mantenerse sostenidamente estas condiciones, se podra configurar un escenario con un crecimiento mayor al delineado aqu. Una fuente de preocupacin es la posible divergencia que pueda darse en el futuro entre el crecimiento de los salarios nominales y la productividad del trabajo. El riesgo que representa la inflacin externa est acotado; eso al menos se deduce de la experiencia reciente, donde la economa ha acomodado cambios en precios relativos sin efectos persistentes en inflacin. Otros riesgos externoscomo movimientos adversos en el precio del petrleotendnan un impacto acotado sobre la trayectoria de mediano plazo de la inflacin. Con todo, el Consejo del Banco Central estima que el balance de riesgos est equilibrado, tanto para crecimiento como para inflacin. Conclusiones Para concluir, me gustara presentarles un cuadro resumen que contiene los principales supuestos y proyecciones considerados por el Banco Central en el IPoMde septiembre. Las proyecciones para la actividad en el 2003 y 2004 consideran el inicio de una fase de mayor crecimiento. Este panorama se apoya en un mayor crecimiento mundial y mejores condiciones financieras. Hacia el tercer trimestre de 2005, en el escenario ms probable, las medidas de inflacin total (IPC) y subyacente (IPCX) se ubicarn en 3,2-3,3%, con promedios de 2,7 y 3,2% para los prximos 24 meses, respectivamente (tabla 2). El Consejo estima que la actual orientacin de la poltica monetaria es compatible con el objetivo de mantener la inflacin dentro del rango meta. En todo caso, de verificarse un cierre ms rpido de las brechas de capacidad, la poltica monetaria tendera a una instancia menos expansiva. Como siempre, el Consejo reaccionar con flexibilidad frente a los eventos que, en una u otra direccin, pongan en peligro el logro de la meta de inflacin. Finalmente, no puedo dejar de destacar que en los ltimos aos se ha construido paulatinamente una reserva de estabilidad macroeconmica y credibilidad que nos diferencia de otras economas emergentes. La adopcin de un esquema de polticas como el mencionado en esta presentacin, constituye un verdadero pilar de la estabilidad econmica y financiera de Chile. Somos hoy menos vulnerables que otras economas emergentes. Nuestras fortalezas radican en: una combinacin apropiada de polticas monetaria y fiscal, una poltica de flexibilidad cambiara, estabilidad macroeconmica, dficit en cuenta corriente muy reducido, un sistema financiero sano y bien supervisado, una deuda externa razonable privada y mayoritariamente de mediano y largo plazo, una deuda pblica baja, y una economa sin grandes distorsiones, competitiva y de amplio predominio de libertad econmica. Adicionalmente, durante perodos crticos que se han vivido en el ltimo tiempo, el Banco Central ha sido flexible ante los cambios que ha sufrido la economa mundial. Esta combinacin de credibilidad y flexibilidad del Instituto Emisor es otro de los grandes activos que tiene la economa chilena.

Title: Farewell speech of the Director of the Central Bank of Chile, Mara Elena Ovalle
text: FAREWELL CEREMONY SPEECH Mar92a Elena Ovalle Central Bank of Chile, November 30, 2005 In a few days my 10-year term as Director of the Central Bank of Chile ends. My departure coincided with the celebration of the Bank's 80th anniversary, which has led to various historical accounts of our institution. Therefore, more than reviewing the detail of the last decade, I want to share with you 2 lessons that synthesize the main of my experience as a counselor. The first is that although the Central Bank is autonomous, its policies cannot be seen in isolation, but must be supported by a reasonable consensus among the different sectors and by a solid institutional framework. The second is rather a reflection on our contribution as people to the development of the country. Regarding the first, after 15 years of autonomy of the Central Bank, it has been possible to establish a framework of monetary, exchange and financial policy that has led to a solid and internationally integrated economy, with low and stable inflation. However, macroeconomic and financial policies are part of a broader approach to growth in an open economy. A good macroeconomic scheme can avoid disasters or bad outcomes, but it does not ensure high growth. Good governance requires a balanced agenda, which simultaneously reinforces these 3 pillars or bases: good policies, institutionality and consensus. The effectiveness of each of these factors depends on the state of the others. How has this experience been reflected in practice? Countries, like people, experience periods of success, pessimism, impatience, more or less difficult periods. But, what matters in the long run is how we face them, so that every time we make a balance, it is positive and leads to the certainty that we have advanced. If one makes a brief historical account, not exhaustive, of what happened in Chile, it is observed that after the return to democracy in 1990, there was an atmosphere full of high expectations, but also of great uncertainty. There was a tremendous need to seek unity and consolidate the process of opening up initiated by our economy in previous decades. Therefore, the macroeconomic policies of the Central Bank were defined in line with the policy of opening up to the world, achieving price stability and deepening the integration of national and international markets. The task was not easy, in a divided country that was emerging from a difficult period. But it was seen, or rather, felt the need to establish a dialogue between us, regardless of the different political positions. There was awareness that we were sailing in the same boat. Fiscal austerity was sought and a systematic effort was made to control inflation. Various actions were taken to stabilize the exchange rate at a level consistent with the balance of external accounts and many other measures to deepen international openness and increase social spending. This phase lasted until 1996, when the economy was growing by over 10% and great policy credibility had been achieved. Then it was time to shift priorities to microeconomic reforms to further sustain growth, mainly through schemes to increase private investment. This was again possible because there was a reasonable consensus framework in the policies and the institutions responsible for implementing them generated confidence among investors. But, as happens in our lives, in moments of glory, these successes as a country generated an excess of confidence, there was a weakening of consensus and an underestimation of the difficulties of the reform processes, even forgetting that the economy moves in cycles. The fact that the Mexican crisis in 1995 had no effect on Chile seemed to confirm that sense of immunity. Society became less tolerant, which affected the agenda of microeconomic and social reforms, but not the basic principles of the economic framework. In this scenario, the crisis of the Asian countries occurred and its contagion spread to most emerging economies, including ours. Thus, it became impossible to simultaneously maintain an exchange rate band, international capital mobility and an active monetary policy. Despite these facts, key institutions for macroeconomic governance applied prudent policies, which limited the effects derived from this new scenario. This was helped by the strong position and efficient supervision of banks, which were essential to limit financial contagion. The economic situation of the country, both internal and external during the years 1998-1999, was very difficult. There was great pessimism and at the same time great impatience to get out of the crisis. The problem was how to get out, without losing what was gained in so many areas and that it was necessary to maintain. The Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance played a decisive role in this stage, where a refinement of the macroeconomic scheme and a new approach to fiscal policy were applied. New actors were incorporated (business organizations, academic centers and all political sectors). This made it possible to break the vicious circle that stopped new reforms, generating the conditions of confidence to obtain a greater benefit from the improvement of the external environment that would come later. The first step was the decision of the Central Bank, in September 1999, to abandon the exchange rate band and opt for a flexible regime, which was a strategic move that allowed to better cope with changes in external conditions. In addition, the capital account of the Balance of Payments was fully opened and financial integration came to play a more prominent role in the strategy to gain resilience. This scheme was completed in 2000 with an improvement in the inflation targeting policy and greater transparency in the conduct of monetary policy (IPoM). The second step was the new approach to fiscal policy, of establishing the rule of maintaining a structural surplus equivalent to 1% of GDP. This rule, which began to be implemented in 2001, increased the credibility of fiscal policy and allowed for a countercyclical policy. This fact demonstrates that policy reforms can begin within institutions and then, depending on environmental conditions, garner the necessary political support for their implementation. There is no doubt that institutional capacity is one of the reserves that countries have to sustain progress. It is necessary to emphasize that without the independence of the Central Bank it would have been very difficult to renew the monetary policy framework. Another important development was the pro-growth agenda proposed by the private sector, which reached a formal agreement in early 2002. Consolidating this reform agenda took almost two years due to uncertainties and fears that came from abroad, but at the same time it favored the willingness of the various public and private actors to ensure that these new reforms were shared and that they reduced the problems that came from abroad. The factors that contributed to this were the country's institutional capacity and a new search for consensus. As you can see, to reach today's situation a lot of water has passed under the bridge. But, without a doubt, progress has been made. The economy is now in a position to face new challenges to increase its potential growth based on an orderly framework of macroeconomic policies. Renewed confidence has been generated in the ability of Chilean society to face these new challenges on its path to development. This is reflected in the high degree of consensus on the most relevant country-issues, such as the persistence of income inequalities, productivity gap with developed countries, the need to emphasize competition in the functioning of domestic markets and to consolidate integration with external markets. Gradually, the horizon in which public policies are debated is widening again. In short, the great lesson is that economic governance is based on good policies, a reasonable consensus among the different sectors and solid institutions. These elements reinforce each other and create a virtuous circle of good governance and growth. I think this is a great lesson. The second reflection is about our contribution as individuals to the development of the country. None of us is too old to have no strength or too young not to contribute. This is a particularly attractive time for Chile; We have opened ourselves to the world beyond the margins of our distant geography. Through this opening, infinite possibilities have entered to be able to grow and develop, but many changes have also been introduced, which sometimes distance us from our roots and confuse the soul. The change of culture we experience shakes even the value system that has given meaning to our lives. It is the task of our generation and of the generation to come, to discern, to open the new times, to seek new paths, knowing how to preserve what must endure. Today as never before we must be subjects of history: men and women capable of ordering their homes and humanizing changes. If in every era this has been an inalienable task, in this time in which purely rationalist modernity in the scientific, political and economic spheres has shown its gaps, greater demands arise to improve the homeland, to improve the human being. We live in a propitious moment to make a contribution to the being because we have become aware of emptiness. We must never forget our history, the characteristics of our country and our people, that is, what we really are and what we need. This leads us to be active participants in what happens in our institution, in our community, in our country. This leads each of us to go beyond the fulfillment of family or work obligations, as was present, for example, in the successful contest "La Econom92a Cerca", in whose preparation and development there was the voluntary participation of different divisions of the Bank. When we saw how schools across the country had been reached and the good that had been caused, the healthy pride was within us. I would like to make special mention of the impressive quality of our staff, I sincerely believe that they are undoubtedly part of the elite of our country. But I would like to make a reflection that I can allow myself not only because it is the time of my departure, but also because of the stage of maturity that I am living. I believe that it is essential that professionals are excellent in their respective disciplines, that they make the talents received perform without mediocrity. The country needs for its development, professionals of first quality, serious, creative, constant and studious. Seeking excellence is a way of loving if it is not done just to excel and satisfy the personal ego. It is essential that our work be comprehensive and inclusive. That professionals can be specialized, but never men or women of a single dimension. Our professionals must be profoundly human, sensitive, capable of being passionate about all manifestations of the spirit and grieving with everything that violates humanity. The integral man has that balance that allows him to be religious without being blessed, scientific without losing the other dimensions of humanity; artist without despising reason; athlete with awareness that the body cannot be the exclusive center of all care; socially restless without ever falling into demagogic simplism. Science, art, religion, sports must be amalgamated into a harmonious synthesis. A comprehensive formation also means educating affectivity. When the time comes for the final arching, the question will be whether we have known how to love. That is why our professional life must always be harmonized with family life and with the ability to build a faithful and deep friendship. Today I want to invite each of you to face new challenges with the greatest possible energy, legitimacy and conviction, in a responsible and constructive way. Without stopping. Delivering with enthusiasm and commitment the best of ourselves with the certainty that we will contribute to a better world. The time has come for the farewell. As you know, people pass and institutions remain. Now it's my turn, I leave with joy and satisfaction and, by my nature, full of challenges. I would like to thank my colleagues in the Council, those who preceded me and those who are with me today. Working with them was an honor and a constant challenge. Especially my thanks to Jorge Desormeaux, for his way of being and his permanent concern for others. Many times he transformed difficult moments into moments of hope. A deep and affectionate thanks to my direct assistants: my secretaries Cecilia and Isabel, my assistants Jenny, Claudia, Patricio, my driver Jos8e. His collaboration through these years is immeasurable, his enthusiasm and dedication in each of the projects we undertook was always a creative impulse and full of satisfactions. I never stopped feeling that with a team like the one I had, there were no limits. Actually, I cannot refer to all those I would like, but I want to thank each of you for everything I have received these years, which were not easy, but very enriching in the broad sense of my life. I would like to conclude by recalling the motivating words of Mother Teresa of Calcutta "... Behind each finish line, there is a starting line. Behind every achievement, there is another challenge Keep going even if everyone expects you to give up. Don't let the iron in you oxidize... When for years you can't run, jog. When you can't jog, walk. When you can't walk, use the cane, but never stop!" Thanks a lot.
text_original: DISCURSO CEREMONIA DESPEDIDA Mara Elena Ovalle Banco Central de Chile, 30 de Noviembre de 2005 En pocos das finaliza mi perodo de 10 aos como Consejera del Banco Central de Chile. Mi partida ha coincidido con la celebracin de los 80 aos de existencia del Banco, lo que ha motivado realizar distintos recuentos histricos acerca de nuestra Institucin. Por lo mismo, ms que repasar el detalle de la ltima dcada, quiero compartir con ustedes 2 lecciones que sintetizan lo principal de mi experiencia como consejera. La primera de ellas se refiere a que si bien el Banco Central es autnomo, sus polticas no pueden mirarse aisladamente, sino deben estar apoyadas en un consenso razonable entre los distintos sectores y en una slida institucionalidad. La segunda es ms bien una reflexin sobre nuestro aporte como personas al desarrollo del pas. Respecto a la primera, luego de 15 aos de autonoma del Banco Central se ha logrado establecer un marco de poltica monetaria, cambiara y financiera que ha llevado a una economa slida e integrada internacionalmente, con una inflacin baja y estable. Sin embargo, las polticas macroeconmicas y financieras son parte de un enfoque ms general de crecimiento en una economa abierta. Un buen esquema macroeconmico puede evitar desastres o malos resultados, pero no asegura un alto crecimiento. La buena gobernabilidad exige una agenda balanceada, que refuerce simultneamente estos 3 pilares o bases: buenas polticas, institucionalidad y consenso. La eficacia de cada uno de estos factores depende del estado de los dems.  Cmo se ha visto reflejada en la prctica esta experiencia? Los pases, al igual que las personas, experimentan perodos de xito, de pesimismo, de impaciencia, perodos ms o menos difciles. Pero, lo que a la larga importa es como los enfrentamos, para que cada vez que hagamos un balance, ste sea positivo y lleve a la certeza que hemos avanzado. Si uno hace un breve recuento histrico, no exhaustivo, de lo ocurrido en Chile, se observa que tras el retomo a la democracia en 1990, se viva un ambiente cargado de altas expectativas, pero tambin de mucha incertidumbre. Haba una tremenda necesidad de buscar la unidad y consolidar el proceso de apertura iniciado por nuestra economa en las dcadas anteriores. Por ello, las polticas macroeconmicas del Banco Central se definieron en lnea con la poltica de apertura al mundo, el logro de la estabilidad de precios y la profundizacin de la integracin de los mercados nacional e internacional. La tarea no era fcil, en un pas dividido que vena saliendo de un perodo difcil. Pero se vio, o ms bien, se sinti la necesidad de establecer un dilogo entre nosotros, no importando las distintas posiciones polticas. Hubo conciencia que navegbamos en un mismo barco. Se busc la austeridad fiscal y se hizo un esfuerzo sistemtico para controlar la inflacin. Se tomaron distintas acciones para estabilizar el tipo de cambio en un nivel coherente con el equilibrio de las cuentas externas y muchas otras medidas para profundizar la apertura internacional e incrementar el gasto social. Esta fase se extendi hasta 1996, cuando la economa creca sobre el 10% y se haba logrado gran credibilidad en las polticas. Luego, lleg el momento de desplazar las prioridades hacia reformas microeconmicas para seguir sosteniendo el crecimiento, principalmente a travs de esquemas para aumentar la inversin privada. Esto nuevamente fue posible porque haba un marco de consenso razonable en las polticas y las instituciones encargadas de aplicarlas generaron confianza entre los inversionistas. Pero, como ocurre en nuestras vidas, en momentos de gloria, estos xitos como pas nos generaron un exceso de confianza, hubo un debilitamiento de los consensos y una subestimacin de las dificultades de los procesos de reformas, incluso olvidando que la economa se mueve por ciclos. El hecho que la crisis mexicana en 1995 no tuviera efectos en Chile pareci confirmar esa sensacin de inmunidad. La sociedad se volvi menos tolerante, lo que afect la agenda de reformas microeconmicas y sociales, pero no los principios bsicos del marco econmico. En este escenario se produjo la crisis de los pases asiticos y su contagio se extendi a la mayora de las economas emergentes, entre ellas la nuestra. As, se hizo imposible mantener simultneamente una banda cambiara, la movilidad internacional de capitales y una poltica monetaria activa. A pesar de estos hechos, las instituciones claves para la gobemabilidad macroeconmica aplicaron polticas prudentes, que acotaron los efectos que se derivaban de este nuevo escenario. A ello contribuy la slida posicin y eficiente supervisin de la banca, que fueron esenciales para limitar el contagio financiero. La situacin econmica del pas, tanto interna como externa durante los aos 1998-1999 se present muy difcil. Se senta un gran pesimismo y al mismo tiempo gran impaciencia para salir de la crisis. El problema era cmo salir, sin perder lo ganado en tantas reas y que era necesario mantener. El Banco Central y el Ministerio de Hacienda tuvieron un papel decisivo en esta etapa, donde se aplic un perfeccionamiento del esquema macroeconmico y un nuevo enfoque en la poltica fiscal. Se incorporaron nuevos actores (organizaciones empresariales, centros acadmicos y todos los sectores polticos). Esto permiti romper el crculo vicioso que detena nuevas reformas, generando las condiciones de confianza para obtener un mayor beneficio del mejoramiento del ambiente externo que vendra ms tarde. El primer paso fue la decisin del Banco Central, en septiembre de 1999, de abandonar la banda cambiara y optar por un rgimen flexible, lo que era un movimiento estratgico que permita enfrentar mejor los cambios en las condiciones externas. Adems, la cuenta de capital de la Balanza de Pagos se abri completamente y la integracin financiera pas a jugar un rol ms destacado en la estrategia para ganar resiliencia. Este esquema fue completado el ao 2000 con una mejora en la poltica de metas de inflacin y mayor transparencia en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria (IPoM). El segundo paso fue el nuevo enfoque de la poltica fiscal, de establecer la regla de mantener un supervit estructural equivalente a un 1% del PIB. Esta regla, que se comenz a aplicar en el 2001 aument la credibilidad de la poltica fiscal y permiti una poltica anticclica. Este hecho demuestra que las reformas de poltica pueden comenzar dentro de las instituciones y luego, dependiendo de las condiciones del entorno, obtener el apoyo poltico necesario para su implementacin. No hay duda que la capacidad institucional es una de las reservas que tienen los pases para sostener el progreso. Es necesario destacar que sin la independencia del Banco Central habra sido muy difcil renovar el marco de poltica monetaria. Otro hecho importante fue la agenda pro crecimiento propuesta por el sector privado, que alcanz un acuerdo formal a comienzos del 2002. Consolidar esta agenda de reformas tom casi dos aos por incertidumbres y temores que venan del exterior, pero al mismo tiempo favoreci la disposicin de los diversos actores pblicos y privados de lograr que estas nuevas reformas fueran compartidas y que redujeran los problemas que venan del exterior. Los factores que contribuyeron a ello fueron la capacidad institucional del pas y una nueva bsqueda de consensos. Como ven, para llegar a la situacin de hoy ha pasado mucha agua bajo el puente. Pero, sin lugar a dudas, se ha avanzado. La economa est hoy en condiciones de plantearse nuevos desafos para incrementar su crecimiento potencial a partir de un marco ordenado de polticas macroeconmicas. Se ha generado una renovada confianza en la capacidad de la sociedad chilena para enfrentar estos nuevos desafos en su camino al desarrollo. Esto se refleja en el alto grado de consenso sobre los temas-pas ms relevantes, como son la persistencia de desigualdades del ingreso, brecha de la productividad con los pases desarrollados, necesidad de enfatizar la competencia en el funcionamiento de los mercados internos y de consolidar la integracin con los mercados externos. Gradualmente, se vuelve a ampliar el horizonte en que se debaten las polticas pblicas. En sntesis, la gran leccin es que la gobernabilidad econmica se apoya en buenas polticas, en un consenso razonable entre los distintos sectores y en una slida institucionalidad. Estos elementos se refuerzan entre si y crean un crculo virtuoso de buena gobernabilidad y crecimiento. Yo creo que esta es una gran leccin. La segunda reflexin es sobre nuestra contribucin como individuos al desarrollo del pas. Ninguno de nosotros es demasiado viejo para no tener fuerzas ni demasiado joven como para no aportar. Este es un momento particularmente atractivo para Chile; nos hemos abierto al mundo traspasando los mrgenes de nuestra lejana geografa. Por esa apertura han entrado infinitas posibilidades para poder crecer y desarrollamos, pero tambin se han introducido muchos cambios, que a veces nos alejan de nuestras races y confunden el alma. El cambio de cultura que experimentamos remece hasta el sistema de valores que ha dado sentido a nuestras vidas. Es tarea de nuestra generacin y de la que viene, discernir, abrir los nuevos tiempos, buscar nuevos caminos, sabiendo conservar aquello que debe perdurar. Hoy como nunca antes debemos ser sujetos de la historia: hombres y mujeres capaces de ordenar su casa y humanizar los cambios. Si en toda poca sta ha sido tarea irrenunciable, en este tiempo en que la modernidad puramente racionalista en lo cientfico, lo poltico y lo econmico ha mostrado sus vacos, surgen mayores exigencias de mejorar la patria, de mejorar al ser humano. Vivimos un momento propicio para hacer un aporte al ser porque hemos tomado conciencia del vaco. Nunca debemos olvidar nuestra historia, las caractersticas de nuestro pas y nuestra gente, es decir, lo que en verdad somos y lo que necesitamos. Ello nos conduce a ser partcipes activos de lo que ocurre en nuestra institucin, en nuestra comunidad, en nuestro pas. Esto lleva a que cada uno de nosotros d ms all del cumplimiento de las obligaciones familiares o laborales, como se hizo presente, por ejemplo, en el exitoso concurso La Economa + Cerca, en cuya preparacin y desarrollo se tuvo la participacin voluntaria de distintas divisiones del Banco. Cuando vimos cmo se haba llegado a los colegios de todo el pas y el bien que se haba provocado, el sano orgullo estaba dentro de nosotros. Quisiera hacer especial mencin a la impresionante calidad de nuestro personal, creo sinceramente que forman parte, sin duda, de la elite de nuestro pas. Pero me gustara hacer una reflexin que me puedo permitir no slo porque es la hora de mi partida, sino tambin por la etapa de madurez que estoy viviendo. Creo que es indispensable que los profesionales sean excelentes en sus respectivas disciplinas, que hagan rendir los talentos recibidos sin mediocridad. El pas necesita para su desarrollo, profesionales de primera calidad, serios, creativos, constantes y estudiosos. El buscar la excelencia es un modo de amar si no se hace slo por sobresalir y satisfacer el ego personal. Es fundamental que nuestra labor sea integral e integradora. Que los profesionales puedan ser especializados, pero jams hombres o mujeres de una sola dimensin. Nuestros profesionales deben ser profundamente humanos, sensibles, capaces de apasionarse por todas las manifestaciones del espritu y dolerse con todo lo que quebranta la humanidad. El hombre integral tiene ese equilibrio que le permite ser religioso sin ser beato, cientfico sin perder las otras dimensiones de la humanidad; artista sin despreciar la razn; deportista con conciencia que el cuerpo no puede ser centro exclusivo de todos los cuidados; inquieto socialmente sin caer jams en el simplismo demaggico. Ciencia, arte, religin, deportes deben amalgamarse en una sntesis armnica. Una formacin integral supone tambin educar la afectividad. Cuando llegue la hora del arqueo final la pregunta ser si hemos sabido amar. Por eso nuestra vida profesional debe armonizarse siempre con la vida de familia y con la capacidad de construir una amistad fiel y profunda. Hoy quiero invitar a cada uno de Uds. a enfrentar nuevos desafos con la mayor energa, legitimidad y conviccin que les sea posible, de un modo responsable y constructivo. Sin detenerse. Entregando con entusiasmo y compromiso lo mejor de nosotros mismos con la certeza que vamos a contribuir a un mundo mejor. Ha llegado el momento de la despedida. Como ustedes saben las personas pasan y las instituciones quedan. Ahora es mi turno, parto con alegra y satisfaccin y, por mi naturaleza, llena de desafos. Quiero agradecer a mis colegas del Consejo, los que me antecedieron y los que hoy me acompaan. El trabajar con ellos fue un honor y un desafo constante. Especialmente mis agradecimientos a Jorge Desormeaux, por su forma de ser y su preocupacin permanente por los dems. Muchas veces transform momentos difciles en momentos de esperanza. Un agradecimiento profundo y con mucho afecto a mis ayudantes directos: mis secretarias Cecilia e Isabel, a mis asistentes Jenny, Claudia, Patricio, mi chofer Jos. Su colaboracin a travs de estos aos es inmedible, su entusiasmo y entrega en cada uno de los proyectos que emprendimos fue siempre un impulso creador y pleno de satisfacciones. Nunca dej de sentir que con un equipo como el que tuve no existan lmites. En realidad, no puedo referirme a todos los que quisiera, pero quiero agradecer a cada uno de ustedes por todo lo recibido estos aos, que no fueron fciles, pero si muy enriquecedores en el sentido amplio de mi vida. Quisiera finalizar recordando las motivadoras palabras de la Madre Teresa de Calcuta ...Detrs de cada lnea de llegada, hay una de partida. Detrs de cada logro, hay otro desafo Sigue aunque todos esperen que abandones. No dejes que se oxide el hierro que hay en t... Cuando por los aos no puedas correr, trota. Cuando no puedas trotar, camina. Cuando no puedas caminar, usa el bastn Pero nunca te detengas!. Muchas gracias.

Title: Exchange Policy in Chile
text: Politics would change PRESENTATION BY MR. JOS83 DE GREGORIO R., DIRECTOR OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, AT THE ROUND TABLE "WHERE THE COUNTRY IS GOING" ORGANIZED BY THE NEWSPAPER ESTRATEGIA, ON OCTOBER 17 , 2001. During the last time, the Chilean economy has been subject to serious turbulence coming from the international economy. The most important events of these turbulences have been the instability in some emerging economies, especially in Argentina, and then the confirmation that the world economy, particularly that of the United States, would perform poorer than expected after the terrorist attack of September 11. Domestically, recovery has been slower than budgeted. In this context, the main adjustment variable has been the exchange rate (graph 1), which has been at the center of the economic discussion. The objective of my presentation will be to analyze the evolution of the exchange rate, the current exchange rate policy and its fundamentals. Regime change it The discussion about the best exchange rate policy for a country is very long-standing. After many hybrid experiences between floating systems and fixed exchange rates, the prevailing opinion among academics, analysts and economic authorities has evolved towards the idea that it is best to adopt one of the two extremes. Either fix, irrevocably, the exchange rate or allow free floating in the market. This conclusion is not a fad nor is it to deny what was thought or recommended in the past, but is based on the high degrees of integration and sophistication that international financial markets have reached. Trying to manage the exchange rate leads, sooner or later, to speculative attacks that in periods of high turbulence are very costly and increasingly frequent. In times when the world was much less integrated, there was more room to manage the exchange rate; Today it is increasingly difficult and risky. If we want to take advantage of all the opportunities offered by capital movements, coherent macroeconomic policies are needed, and in our case, the adoption of a floating regime was a major step. When a fixed exchange rate is adopted, it becomes the anchor for prices and inflation. By setting the exchange rate, the authorities lose control over monetary policy, as they must be willing to buy and sell any amount of national currency in exchange for foreign currency to maintain parity. If the public wants to get rid of the domestic currency, the money will fall, because it will be exchanged for dollars at the fixed parity and control of interest rates is lost. If the authority is not prepared to provide all the foreign currency demanded at the fixed parity, it will not be sustainable. This scheme has been suggested for economies with high monetary volatility and low inflationary credibility in which it is more convenient to renounce the use of monetary policy for stabilizing purposes. Clearly, that is not the situation in our country. At the other extreme, in a free exchange rate regime, the market decides its level. In this case, the authority can control monetary policy. The anchor for prices and expectations is the inflation target. However, pure float in its most precise sense does not exist, since changes in interest rates have effects changing them. By changing domestic interest rates, central banks change the arbitrage conditions and the composition of investors' portfolios, thereby affecting the exchange rate. Moreover, in virtually every known experience, central banks intervene directly in the foreign exchange market, through the direct purchase and sale of foreign exchange, for a set of reasons that I will explain later. If central banks do not wish to change the interest rate, in order to maintain the independence of monetary policy, monetary impacts must be "sterilized" through countervailing operations. This is what has been done in Chile. So that the intervention does not alter the monetary policy rate, every time the Central Bank intervenes by selling reserves, it must replenish the pesos it has withdrawn. In the course of its history, Chile has not escaped experimentation in terms of changing regimes. In general, schemes with high market intervention were adopted, either through fixations d1 of a fixed value or a pre-established exchange rate d1 bands of different widths, etc. At different junctures, and different periods, what the vast majority of our experiences with very limited flexibility regimes show is that these systems end up aggravating, rather than smoothing, macroeconomic adjustments. The cause is always the same, and that is that in an economy like Chile's, small, open to the outside world and rich in natural resources, the real exchange rate must fluctuate significantly. This is what is observed in Chile throughout its history (graph 2). Something similar happens in other open and resource-intensive economies such as Australia, Canada and New Zealand. Under these conditions, any straitjacket for the exchange rate is very expensive, particularly in difficult periods. When there are rigidities, the currency tends to overvalue and becomes an appetizing target against which to speculate. That is why, in September 1 999, the Central Bank adopted a floating regime, which has many benefits. First, it has allowed monetary policy to continue to be used to achieve the inflation target. In addition, it has allowed the exchange rate to be the main variable that absorbs external shocks. Instead of letting interest rates and GDP adjust sharply to changing external conditions, the exchange rate makes adjustment more efficient, i.e. less costly, by shifting resource allocation signals between tradable and non-tradable sectors. It was also announced that the Bank reserved the option of intervening in the foreign exchange market in emergency situations. Reasons for a change intervention Having adopted a floating regime, the obvious question is why there are special conditions under which intervention should be made. There is an extensive literature on problems of functioning in financial markets. For example, discussions about the exuberance of stock markets and how they can go through long periods of overvaluation are well known. There is also plenty of evidence about excessive volatility in exchange markets, which also serves as the main argument for those who think that the exchange rate should be fixed. However, this is not enough to justify intervention, since there are failures in many markets, the vast majority do not recommend intervention. However, given that the exchange rate is a key variable in resource allocation and has important macroeconomic implications for our external accounts, growth and inflation, the possibility of the authorities intervening in the market is justified. Therefore, excessive fluctuations in the exchange rate not only have an impact on a specific market, but also have significant macroeconomic repercussions. Consequently, the fundamental reason for exceptionally making interventions is that markets can overreact, bringing the exchange rate to values far removed from their medium-term equilibrium. If so, these changes may unnecessarily translate into increases in inflation and poor microeconomic signals. Excessive depreciation could have contractionary effects on economic activity. Therefore, it is necessary to be prepared to provide liquidity in foreign currency, exceptionally, in times of turbulence. In times of high uncertainty, liquidity in the markets is reduced. The days with the greatest variations in the price of the dollar have been those with few amounts traded. The shallow depth of exchange markets can also produce sharp movements. For example, excessive depreciation can induce agents to increase their demand for hedging instruments, creating a vicious circle. This is possible to generate speculative bubbles and other negative behaviors in the orderly functioning of financial markets, which can end up with prices far removed from what is justified according to the fundamentals. In a floating regime, the Central Bank cannot try to set a price for the dollar. It would be a mistake to try to do so. This is the greatest risk of interventions because instead of inducing greater stability they can encourage speculation. The underlying reason for not looking for prices is that neither agents nor authorities can determine exactly what the equilibrium is; Therefore, the market must be allowed to find an appropriate balance consistent with the fundamentals of the economy. Based on the above, that is, with the idea that we could be facing turbulence with high possibilities that it is a transitory overreaction, and with the conviction that instead of looking for a price it is necessary to provide liquidity, the Central Bank announced on August 16 that it would intervene in the exchange market, given the special circumstances that our economy was going through. The intervention would be for a limited maximum amount, 2,000 million dollars in additional placements of readjustable promissory notes in dollars (PRD) with terms of 2 to 4 years, and a maximum of direct intervention through the sale of reserves for an amount of up to 2,000 million dollars. The intervention would also be limited in time, giving a deadline until the end of December, a period in which it is estimated that the main financial uncertainties should be moderately resolved. The intervention was announced before the terrorist attack of September 11, an event that further aggravated the external turbulence, and that gave new reasons to justify this policy decision. Clearly, it is difficult to think of a larger set of extraordinary circumstances in the world economy that would justify exchange rate intervention. The decision was not easy since the Board of the Central Bank is a firm supporter of floating exchange, but recognizing that this is an exceptional situation, it was decided to intervene in the spirit of the floating system adopted in September 1999, that is, defining the timing and amounts of interventions. All this occurs, in addition, in a context of mismatch between the Central Bank and the private sector, where the former is overactivated in dollars, while the private sector is overactivated in pesos, so that this decision is also justified by a special circumstance, in which exchanging assets denominated in dollars for assets in pesos is appropriate from the financial point of view, both for the private sector and for the Central Bank. Effectiveness of interventions There is an extensive literature that attempts to assess whether interventions are effective or not, and as in most of these issues, the results are inconclusive. The mechanisms through which interventions can have effects are varied, from effects on the composition of investors' portfolios, to signals that they provide about the future course of monetary policy. One difficulty in determining the effectiveness of interventions is that it is not possible to know exactly what would have happened in the market had there been no intervention. This means that at the current juncture we cannot determine exactly what would have happened if the Central Bank had not intervened in the exchange market. Therefore, to specify the effectiveness of the interventions it is necessary to use some indirect method, not always free of methodological problems. The other great difficulty, and which I believe is the most important in determining the effects of interventions, is that sometimes interventions occur in periods when the movements to change them are based on fundamental reasons, and the strength of the market is greater than that of the interventions. In this case, even if there are signs of a market overreaction, this may be justified. If so, interventions in such circumstances are, and it is good that they are, ineffective. This also avoids the temptation to intervene continuously. However, from the point of view of macroeconomic policy it is necessary to verify directly in the market, which is the case. It is much more costly not to act in the presence of an unanchored market, than to intervene when the fundamentals do not justify it. This is particularly true when sufficient reserves are available. In this way, the exchange intervention provides information on how well-founded fluctuations are in periods of turbulence and that serves to assess whether additional action is necessary to avoid the unwanted inflationary consequences of excessive depreciation. Real exchange rate One of the elements that crosses the question of whether we are in the presence of an unsustainable increase in the exchange rate, which could generate inflation and instability harmful to the economy, is first of all whether the depreciations of the peso are justified in fundamental phenomena and, on the other hand, if these depreciations incubate serious inflationary risks. I shall examine each of them below. With regard to the real exchange rate, it has depreciated in real terms by about 30% compared to the first half of 1 999, that is, in just over two years the real appreciation that occurred in eight years, since mid-1991, was reversed. But this has also been possible, because there are grounds for this to happen. Perhaps the strongest effect, which we have been feeling since 1 998, is a severe fall in the terms of trade (Chart 3). This has occurred as a result of the deterioration in the international growth scenario. Recent consensus estimates have lowered by about one percentage point our trading partners' growth projections for 2002, which are estimated to reach just 2 percent, with the United States growing between 1 and 1.2 percent for 2001 and 2002. The falling terms of trade means that our exports are now much cheaper than our imports; In other words, the relative valuation of the world for our goods is lower. Consequently, our prices and wages relative to the rest of the world (expressed in dollars) must also be lower, and therefore the exchange rate must depreciate in real terms. In other words, to generate the same current account deficit we need to have more exports and fewer imports (both in volume), and for this we need a real depreciation, which provides the incentives for productive resources to be reallocated to the tradable goods sector. This explains why growth today is led by exports. This effect has been very significant. By way of comparison, if the average terms of trade for the period 1 990-1 995 prevailed today, there would be additional revenues (net of import cost) of 4.4 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP). Undoubtedly, an income effect of this magnitude explains an important part of the correction of the exchange rate. It is also worth mentioning the limited availability of capital flows to emerging economies . The world has retreated to the emerging economies, and the end to nciation has been reduced. During its peak years, net private flows to emerging economies, 1,995-1,996, averaged more than 200 billion. In contrast, in the biennium 2000-2001, these were zero in net terms. Chile has not been oblivious to this phenomenon. In its record year, 1 996, private net flow reached almost 7 billion dollars, while in 2000 it reached almost one thousand four hundred million dollars and, so far this year, it is practically nil. Finally, it should be noted that in a scenario of lower expenditure growth, demand pressures on the non-tradable goods sector are lower, which induces the depreciation of the real exchange rate. Consequently, there are many factors that explain the real depreciation that has occurred in recent times. How much this depreciation should be is something that the market must find, and the objective of the Central Bank is that this happens within a framework consistent with macroeconomic balances. Even, according to the estimates of many domestic and foreign analysts, it is likely that the real exchange rate is above its long-term value, but that is not unusual in Chile. In fact, there are a number of factors that can contribute to the real exchange rate deviating from its long-term value persistently. For example, periods of strong capital flows put pressure on excessive appreciation. On the other hand, today, overreaction can help accelerate the process of reallocation of resources to the tradable sector. However, it is prudent to prevent excessive overflows, which can subsequently also be undone with force, which can generate inflation and more costly adjustments. Inflation and exchange rate For a long time it was thought that variations in the exchange rate would be mechanically translated into price changes. Hence the justifications for fixing the exchange rate and fears of devaluations. However, experience, particularly in the nineties, shows us that exchange rate fluctuations have a much smaller inflationary impact than expected. The European experience of the early nineties, as well as the cases of Australia and New Zealand during the Asian crisis, among others, show that it is possible to tolerate strong exchange rate fluctuations without these denoting significant and persistent changes in inflation (Figure 4). To the extent that the exchange rate contributes to a correction of relative prices, it is normal that it is accompanied by low inflation. A macroeconomic policy based on a flexible exchange rate scheme, where the inflationary anchor is not the exchange rate, with an effective and credible commitment to price stability, a fiscal policy consistent with this objective, and a sound financial system, are fundamental elements for the transfer of exchange rate to prices to occur with minimal inflationary consequences. Likewise, the adoption of credible inflation targets, in Chile or in the aforementioned countries, means that the price adjustments that must occur, due to the weakening of the local currency, are not accompanied by persistent expectations of higher inflation. Low aggregate demand and falling oil prices are also factors containing inflation during this juncture, and an exit from it, with productivity growth, should keep inflationary pressures under control. The Central Bank has acknowledged that an increase in inflation towards the ceiling of the target range (Chart 5) is possible as a result of the adjustment of some prices, but the inflation outlook remains within the stability objective. Of course, there are scenarios in which there could be unexpected inflationary pressures, in which case there should be no doubt that the central bank will take additional steps to keep inflation within the target range. Current monetary conditions A final point, to which I would like to refer, is the discussion of recent monetary expansion. The argument circulates that the high rates of expansion of monetary aggregates, in particular MIA, during the last months, would be incubating inflationary pressures and would be responsible for the increase in the exchange rate. The argument is simply that an increase in the supply of money beyond demand, generates that there are many pesos chasing few goods and dollars. The policy recommendation is straightforward: restrict liquidity. This argument, however, ignores that the evolution of money has been quite special during the last time, and even altered by the effect of the year 2000. As can be seen in Figure 6, after a sharp fall, money has been growing at accelerated rates, but starting from a very low base. It is even clearly observed that the recent average growth is lower than the trend growth of the nineties. More recently, money has been growing on average monthly, seasonally adjusted, below 1%. However, the most rigorous way to verify whether money is growing excessively is to estimate whether demand is growing consistently with conditions of lower nominal interest rates and output expansion. To do this, a demand for money up to 1 997 can be estimated and then dynamically simulated to the present, using the effective rate and output data. This exercise does not allow any change in liquidity preferences after 1 997; Therefore, it is the most conservative to analyze if there is excessive liquidity growth. If the quantity of money were above demand, we might think that there is excess growth, given low inflationary prospects. Figure 7 shows that the quantity of money is indeed consistent with demand. Therefore, there is no evidence that there is a persistent excess of money, more than required, chasing few goods and few dollars. It is also necessary to add that in a scheme where the monetary policy instrument is the interest rate, which is adjusted to achieve the inflation target within the range of 2% to 4%, centered on 3%, the demand for money may present volatility. The important thing is that expectations and policy actions are focused within the inflation target range. Therefore, the information obtained directly from monetary aggregates is partial, although of course not irrelevant. By way of conclusion In Chile, an exchange rate floating regime has been adopted, which is undoubtedly the most appropriate, given its characteristics of a small economy, open to the outside world and with a large endowment of natural resources. The flexibility of this system avoids costly adjustments to changes in the external and internal conditions of the economy that require adjustments in the real exchange rate. A floating system, together with a sound financial system, avoids the frequent exchange rate crises, which are aggravated when transmitted to the banking system, and through which many emerging economies have passed, and from which Chile in the past has not been exempt. Intervening exceptionally in the exchange market is justified when it is estimated that there may be an overreaction of the exchange rate, which can have negative repercussions on inflation and on the general behavior of the economy. This occurs because of a number of factors that affect the orderly functioning of financial markets, especially in periods of international turbulence. Current external conditions, especially the sharp fall in the terms of trade, as well as the scarcity of capital flows and the slow growth of aggregate demand on the domestic front, account for a significant part of the depreciation in the real exchange rate. In two years we have had a depreciation of the real exchange rate that has compensated for an appreciation that occurred in eight years. In the near future, our growth will be led by the tradable goods sector, and price signals indicate this. However, it would be a mistake to have a real exchange rate target. On many occasions attempts were made, at high cost, to bend the hand to the force of the facts. From the point of view of the strength of our economy, what matters is the strength of our internal and external balances, rather than specific levels for certain prices. We also need greater degrees of depth in financial markets and companies more aware of the need to hedge against exchange rate fluctuations. The set of macroeconomic policies has made it possible to accommodate the effects of real depreciation. A balanced fiscal policy and a monetary policy committed to an inflation target have limited the inflationary costs of these events, as has not happened before in our economic history, but as it does in macroeconomically stable and modern economies. Our economy is one of them, and today it is in a very good position to absorb, if not avoid, external turbulence. However, these policies require the necessary pragmatism to avoid short-term overreactions that produce more costs than benefits, and in this context the exceptional intervention that the Central Bank has been making in the exchange market is inscribed.
