text_original: La Poltica Cambiara Exposicin del seor Jos De Gregorio R., Consejero del Banco Central de Chile, en la mesa redonda Hacia Dnde Va el Pas organizada por el diario Estrategia, el 17 de octubre de 2001. Durante el ltimo tiempo, la economa chilena ha estado sujeta a serias turbulencias provenientes de la economa internacional. Los eventos ms importantes de estas turbulencias han sido la inestabilidad en algunas economas emergentes, especialmente en Argentina, y luego la confirmacin de que la economa mundial, en particular la de Estados Unidos, tendra un desempeo ms pobre que el esperado despus del ataque terrorista del 11 de septiembre. En el mbito interno, la recuperacin ha sido ms lenta de lo presupuestado. En este contexto, la principal variable de ajuste ha sido el tipo de cambio (grfico 1), el cual ha estado en el centro de la discusin econmica. El objetivo de mi presentacin ser analizar la evolucin del tipo de cambio, la poltica cambiara vigente y sus fundamentos. Rgimen cambiarlo La discusin sobre la mejor poltica cambiara para un pas es de muy larga data. Despus de muchas experiencias hbridas entre sistemas de flotacin y tipos de cambio fijos, la opinin prevaleciente entre acadmicos, analistas y autoridades econmicas ha evolucionado hacia la idea de que lo ms conveniente es adoptar alguno de los dos extremos. O fijar, irrevocablemente, el tipo de cambio o permitir la flotacin libre en el mercado. Esta conclusin no es una moda ni es renegar de lo que se pens o recomend en el pasado, sino que se fundamenta en los altos grados de integracin y sofisticacin que han alcanzado los mercados financieros internacionales. Tratar de manejar el tipo de cambio conduce, tarde o temprano, a ataques especulativos que en perodos de alta turbulencia son muy costosos y cada vez ms frecuentes. En pocas en que el mundo era mucho menos integrado haba mayor espacio para manejar el tipo de cambio; hoy es cada vez ms difcil y riesgoso. Si se desea aprovechar todas las oportunidades que ofrecen los movimientos de capital, es necesario adoptar polticas macroeco- nmicas coherentes, y en nuestro caso, la adopcin de un rgimen de flotacin constituy un gran paso. Cuando se adopta un tipo de cambio fijo, este pasa a ser el ancla para los precios y la inflacin. Al fijar el tipo de cambio, las autoridades pierden el control sobre la poltica monetaria, por cuanto deben estar dispuestas a comprar y vender cualquier cantidad de moneda nacional a cambio de divisas para mantener la paridad. Si el pblico quiere desprenderse de la moneda domstica, el dinero caer, pues ser cambiado por dlares a la paridad fija y se pierde el control de las tasas de inters. Si la autoridad no est preparada para proveer toda la moneda extranjera que se demanda a la paridad fija, sta no ser sustentable. Este esquema se ha sugerido para economas con alta volatilidad monetaria y baja credibilidad inflacionaria en las cuales resulta ms conveniente renunciar al uso de la poltica monetaria con propsitos estabilizadores. Claramente, no es esa la situacin de nuestro pas. En el otro extremo, en un rgimen de tipo de cambio libre, el mercado es quien decide su nivel. En este caso, la autoridad puede controlar la poltica monetaria.El ancla para los precios y las expectativas es la meta de inflacin. No obstante, la flotacin pura en su sentido ms preciso no existe, ya que las modificaciones en las tasas de inters tienen efectos cambiarlos. Al modificar las tasas de inters domsticas, los bancos centrales cambian las condiciones de arbitraje y la composicin de la cartera de los inversionistas, con lo cual el tipo de cambio se ve afectado. Adems, en prcticamente todas las experiencias conocidas, los bancos centrales intervienen directamente en el mercado cambiarlo, a travs de la compra y venta directa de divisas, por un conjunto de razones que expondr ms adelante. Si los bancos centrales no desean cambiar la tasa de inters, para mantener la independencia de la poltica monetaria, se deben esterilizar los impactos monetarios a travs de operaciones compensatorias. Es lo que se ha estado haciendo en Chile. Para que la intervencin no altere la tasa de poltica monetaria, cada vez que el Banco Central interviene vendiendo reservas, debe reponer los pesos que ha retirado. En el transcurso de su historia, Chile no ha escapado a la experimentacin en materia de regmenes cambiarlos. En general, se adoptaron esquemas con alta intervencin en el mercado, ya sea a travs de fijaciones  de un valor fijo o una tasa de cambio preestablecida , bandas de distinto ancho, etc. En distintas coyunturas, y diversos perodos, lo que muestra la gran mayora de nuestras experiencias con regmenes de muy limitada flexibilidad, es que esos sistemas terminan por agravar, en vez de suavizar, los ajustes macroeconmicos. La causa es siempre la misma, y es que en una economa como la chilena, pequea, abierta al exterior y rica en recursos naturales, el tipo de cambio real debe fluctuar de manera importante. Eso es lo que se observa en Chile a travs de su historia (grfico 2). Algo similar ocurre en otras economas abiertas y con alta dotacin de recursos naturales como Australia, Canad y Nueva Zelanda. Bajo estas condiciones, cualquier camisa de fuerza para el tipo de cambio es muy costosa, en particular en perodos difciles. Cuando hay rigideces, la moneda tiende a sobrevaluarse y pasa a ser un objetivo apetitoso contra el cual especular. Por ello, en septiembre de 1 999, el Banco Central adopt un rgimen de flotacin, el que tiene muchos beneficios. En primer lugar, ha permitido que la poltica monetaria pueda seguir siendo utilizada para conseguir el objetivo inflacionario. Adems, ha permitido que el tipo de cambio sea la principal variable que absorba los shocks externos. En vez de dejar que las tasas de inters y el PIB se ajusten bruscamente a las cambiantes condiciones externas, el tipo de cambio hace el ajuste ms eficiente, es decir menos costoso, por la va de cambiar las seales de asignacin de recursos entre los sectores transables y no transables. Tambin se anunci que el Banco se reservaba la opcin de intervenir en el mercado cambiarlo en situaciones de excepcin. Razones para una intervencin cambiara Habiendo adoptado un rgimen de flotacin, la pregunta obvia es por qu existen condiciones especiales en las cuales se debe intervenir. Existe una amplia literatura sobre los problemas de funcionamiento en los mercados financieros. Por ejemplo, son conocidas las discusiones acerca de la exuberancia de las bolsas accionarias y cmo ellas pueden pasar por largos perodos de sobrevaloracin. Tambin existe bastante evidencia sobre los excesos de volatilidad en los mercados cambiarlos, lo que adems sirve como principal argumento para quienes piensan que hay que fijar el tipo de cambio. No obstante, esto no basta para justificar la intervencin, ya que habiendo fallas en muchos mercados, en la inmensa mayora no se recomienda intervenir. Sin embargo, dado que el tipo de cambio es una variable clave en la asignacin de recursos y tiene importantes repercusiones macroeconmicas sobre nuestras cuentas externas, crecimiento e inflacin, se justifica la posibilidad de que las autoridades intervengan el mercado. Por lo tanto, las fluctuaciones excesivas en el tipo de cambio no slo tienen impacto sobre un mercado especfico, sino que tambin tienen repercusiones macroeconmicas significativas. En consecuencia, la razn fundamental para realizar, excepcionalmente, intervenciones es que los mercados pueden sobrerreaccionar, llevando el tipo de cambio a valores muy alejados de su equilibrio de mediano plazo. De ser as, es posible que estos cambios se traduzcan innecesariamente en aumentos de la inflacin y malas seales microeconmicas. Depreciaciones excesivas podran tener efectos contractivos sobre la actividad econmica. Por ello, es necesario estar preparados para proveer liquidez en moneda extranjera, de manera excepcional, en momentos de turbulencia. En pocas de alta incertidumbre se reduce la liquidez en los mercados. Los das con las mayores variaciones en el precio del dlar han sido aquellos con pocos montos transados. La escasa profundidad de los mercados cambiarlos tambin puede producir movimientos bruscos. Por ejemplo, una depreciacin excesiva puede inducir a los agentes a incrementar su demanda por instrumentos de cobertura, pudiendo crearse un crculo vicioso. As es posible que se generen burbujas especulativas y otros comportamientos negativos en el funcionamiento ordenado de los mercados financieros, que pueden terminar con precios muy alejados de lo que se justifica de acuerdo con los fundamentos. En un rgimen de flotacin, el Banco Central no puede tratar de fijar un precio para el dlar. Sera un error intentar hacerlo. Este es el mayor riesgo de las intervenciones porque en vez de inducir mayor estabilidad pueden incentivar la especulacin. La razn de fondo para no buscar precios es que ni los agentes ni las autoridades pueden determinar con exactitud cul es el equilibrio; por ello, se debe permitir que el mercado encuentre un equilibrio adecuado y congruente con los fundamentos de la economa. Basados en lo anterior, es decir, con la dea de que podramos estar frente a turbulencias con altas posibilidades que sea una sobrerreaccin transitoria, y con la conviccin de que en vez de buscar un precio es necesario proveer liquidez, el Banco Central anunci el 16 de agosto que intervendra en el mercado cambiarlo, dadas las circunstancias especiales por las que atravesaba nuestra economa. La intervencin sera por un monto mximo limitado, 2.000 millones de dlares en colocaciones adicionales de pagars reajustables en dlares (PRD) a plazos de 2 a 4 aos, y un mximo de intervencin directa a travs de la venta de reservas por un monto de hasta 2.000 millones de dlares. La intervencin sera tambin acotada en el tiempo, dndose un plazo hasta fines de diciembre, perodo en el cual se estima que las principales incertidumbres financieras deberan estar medianamente resueltas. La intervencin se anunci antes del ataque terrorista del 11 de septiembre, evento que agrav an ms las turbulencias externas, y que dio nuevas razones para justificar esta decisin de poltica. Claramente, es difcil pensar un conjunto mayor de circunstancias extraordinarias en la economa mundial que justifiquen una intervencin cambiara. La decisin no fue fcil ya que el Consejo del Banco Central es firme partidario de la flotacin cambiara, pero reconociendo que esta es una situacin excepcional, se decidi intervenir en el espritu del sistema de flotacin adoptado en septiembre de 1999, esto es, definiendo la oportunidad y los montos de las intervenciones. Todo esto se da, adems, en un contexto de descalce entre el Banco Central y el sector privado, donde el primero se encuentra sobreactivado en dlares, mientras el sector privado est sobreactivado en pesos, de modo que esta decisin se justifica, tambin, por una circunstancia especial, en la cual intercambiar activos denominados en dlares por activos en pesos es apropiada desde el punto de vista financiero, tanto para el sector privado como para el Banco Central. Efectividad de las intervenciones Existe una extensa literatura que intenta evaluar si las intervenciones son efectivas o no, y como en la mayora de estos temas, los resultados son inconclusos. Los mecanismos a travs de los cuales las intervenciones pueden tener efectos son variados, desde efectos sobre la composicin de los portafolios de los inversionistas, hasta seales que estas entregan sobre el transcurrir futuro de la poltica monetaria. Una dificultad para determinar la efectividad de las intervenciones es que no se puede saber con exactitud qu hubiera pasado en el mercado de no haberse intervenido. Esto significa que en la actual coyuntura no podemos determinar exactamente qu hubiera ocurrido si el Banco Central no hubiera intervenido en el mercado cambiarlo. Por lo tanto, para precisar la efectividad de las intervenciones es necesario utilizar algn mtodo indirecto, no siempre exento de problemas metodolgicos. La otra gran dificultad, y que a mi juicio es la ms importante para determinar los efectos de las intervenciones, es que en algunas ocasiones estas ocurren en perodos en los cuales los movimientos cambiarlos estn basados en razones fundamentales, y la fuerza del mercado es mayor que la de las intervenciones. En este caso, a pesar de que haya seales de una sobrerreaccin de mercado, esta puede ser justificada. De ser as, las intervenciones en dichas circunstancias son, y es bueno que as lo sean, inefectivas. As se evita, adems, la tentacin de intervenir continuamente. Sin embargo, desde el punto de vista de poltica macroeconmica es necesario verificar directamente en el mercado, que este es el caso. Es mucho ms costoso no actuar en presencia de un mercado desanclado, que intervenir cuando los fundamentos no lo justifican. Esto es particularmente vlido cuando se dispone de suficientes reservas. De esta manera, la intervencin cambiara entrega informacin sobre cun fundadas son las fluctuaciones en perodos de turbulencia y que sirve para evaluar si es necesario emprender acciones adicionales para evitar las indeseadas consecuencias inflacionarias de una depreciacin excesiva. Tipo de cambio real Uno de los elementos que cruza la pregunta de si estamos en presencia de un aumento insostenible del tipo de cambio, que pueda generar inflacin e inestabilidad perjudiciales para la economa, es en primer lugar si se justifican las depreciaciones del peso en fenmenos fundamentales y, por otra parte, si estas depreciaciones incuban serios riesgos inflacionarios. Examinar, a continuacin, cada una de ellas. Respecto del tipo de cambio real, este se ha depreciado en trminos reales cerca de 30% respecto del primer semestre de 1 999, es decir, en poco ms de dos aos se revirti la apreciacin real que ocurri en ocho aos, desde mediados de 1991. Pero esto tambin ha sido posible, debido a que existen fundamentos para que as ocurra. Tal vez el efecto ms fuerte, y que venimos sintiendo ya desde 1 998 es una severa cada de los trminos de intercambio (grfico 3). Esto ha ocurrido como producto del deterioro en el escenario de crecimiento internacional. Recientes estimaciones de consenso han rebajado en aproximadamente un punto porcentual las proyecciones de crecimiento de nuestros socios comerciales para el 2002, que se estima llegar apenas a 2%, con Estados Unidos creciendo entre 1 y 1,2% para los aos 2001 y 2002. La cada de los trminos de intercambio significa que nuestras exportaciones son hoy mucho ms baratas que nuestras importaciones; en otras palabras, la valoracin relativa del mundo por nuestros bienes es menor. En consecuencia, nuestros precios y salarios respecto de los del resto del mundo (expresados en dlares) deben ser tambin menores, y, por lo tanto, el tipo de cambio se debe depreciar en trminos reales. En otras palabras, para generar el mismo dficit en cuenta corriente necesitamos tener ms exportaciones y menos importaciones (ambas en volumen), y para ello se necesita una depreciacin real, la que entrega los incentivos para que los recursos productivos se reasignen al sector de bienes transables. Esto explica que el crecimiento en la actualidad, est liderado por las exportaciones. Este efecto ha sido muy significativo. A modo de comparacin, si hoy prevalecieran los trminos de intercambio promedios del perodo 1 990-1 995 habra ingresos adicionales (netos de costo de importacin) de 4,4% del producto interno bruto (PIB). Sin duda, que un efecto ingreso de esa magnitud explica parte importante de la correccin del tipo de cambio. Asimismo, vale la pena mencionar la escasa disponibilidad de flujos de capitales a economas emergentes. El mundo se ha replegado respecto de las economas emergentes, y el fin a nciamiento se ha reducido. Durante sus aos de mayor auge, los flujos netos privados a economas emergentes, 1 995-1 996, superaron en promedio los 200 mil millones de dlares. En cambio, en el bienio 2000-2001, estos fueron cero en trminos netos. Chile no ha estado ajeno a este fenmeno. En su ao rcord, 1 996, el flujo neto privado lleg a casi 7 mil millones de dlares, mientras que el ao 2000 lleg a casi mil cuatrocientos millones de dlares y, en lo que va corrido de este ao, es prcticamente nulo. Por ltimo, hay que destacar que en un escenario de menor crecimiento del gasto, las presiones de demanda sobre el sector de bienes no transables son menores, lo que induce a la depreciacin del tipo de cambio real. En consecuencia, existen muchos factores que explican la depreciacin real ocurrida en el ltimo tiempo. Cunto debera ser esta depreciacin es algo que debe encontrar el mercado, y el objetivo del Banco Central es que esto ocurra dentro de un marco coherente con los equilibrios macroeconmicos. Incluso, de acuerdo con las estimaciones de muchos analistas nacionales y extranjeros, es probable que el tipo de cambio real est sobre su valor de largo plazo, pero eso no es algo inusual en Chile. De hecho, existe una serie de factores que pueden contribuir a que el tipo de cambio real se desve de su valor de largo plazo de manera persistente. Por ejemplo, perodos de fuertes flujos de capital presionan a una apreciacin excesiva. En cambio, hoy, la sobrerreaccin puede contribuir a acelerar el proceso de reasignacin de recursos al sector transable. Sin embargo, es prudente prevenir desbordes excesivos, que posteriormente se pueden deshacer tambin con fuerza, pudiendo generar inflacin y ajustes ms costosos. Inflacin y tipo de cambio Durante mucho tiempo se pens que las variaciones en el tipo de cambio se traduciran mecnicamente en cambios de precios. De ah las justificaciones para fijar el tipo de cambio y los temores a las devaluaciones. Sin embargo, la experiencia, particularmente en los aos noventa, nos muestra que las fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio tienen un impacto inflacionario mucho menor del esperado. La experiencia europea de principios de la dcada del noventa, as como los casos de Australia y Nueva Zelanda durante la crisis asitica, entre otras, muestran que es posible tolerar fuertes fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio sin que estas denoten cambios significativos y persistentes en la inflacin (grfico 4). En la medida que el tipo de cambio contribuya a una correccin de precios relativos, es normal que vaya acompaado de baja inflacin. Una poltica macroeconmica basada en un esquema cambiarlo flexible, donde el ancla inflacionaria no es el tipo de cambio, con un compromiso efectivo y creble con la estabilidad de precios, una poltica fiscal consistente con este objetivo, y un sistema financiero slido, son elementos fundamentales para que el traspaso de tipo de cambio a precios ocurra con mnimas consecuencias inflacionarias. Asimismo, la adopcin de metas de inflacin crebles, en Chile o en los pases antes mencionados, permiten que los ajustes de precios que deban ocurrir, debido al debilitamiento de la moneda local, no vayan acompaados de expectativas persistentes de mayor inflacin. La baja demanda agregada y la cada del precio del petrleo tambin son factores que contienen la inflacin durante esta coyuntura, y una salida de ella, con crecimientos de la productividad, deberan mantener las presiones inflacionarias bajo control. El Banco Central ha reconocido que es posible un aumento de la inflacin hacia el techo del rango meta (grfico 5) como producto del ajuste de algunos precios, pero las perspectivas inflacionarias siguen estando dentro del objetivo de estabilidad. Por supuesto, existen escenarios en los cuales podra haber presiones inflacionarias inesperadas, en cuyo caso no debiera haber duda de que el Banco Central tomar las medidas adicionales para mantener la inflacin dentro del rango meta. Las condiciones monetarias actuales Un ltimo punto, al que quisiera referirme, es la discusin sobre la expansin monetaria reciente. Circula el argumento de que las altas tasas de expansin de los agregados monetarios, en particular MIA, durante los ltimos meses, estara incubando presiones inflacionarias y sera la responsable del aumento del tipo de cambio. El argumento es simplemente que un aumento de la oferta de dinero ms all de la demanda, genera que haya muchos pesos persiguiendo pocos bienes y dlares. La recomendacin de poltica es directa: restringir la liquidez. Este argumento, sin embargo, ignora que la evolucin del dinero ha sido bastante especial durante el ltimo tiempo, e incluso alterada por el efecto del ao 2000. Como se observa en el grfico 6, despus de una brusca cada, el dinero ha estado creciendo a tasas aceleradas, pero partiendo de una base muy baja. Incluso se observa claramente que el crecimiento promedio reciente es menor que el crecimiento de tendencia de los aos noventa. Ms recientemente, el dinero ha estado creciendo en promedio mensual, desestacionalizado, por debajo del 1%. No obstante lo anterior, la forma ms rigurosa de verificar si el dinero crece excesivamente es estimar si la demanda est creciendo de manera coherente con las condiciones de menores tasas de inters nominal y la expansin del producto. Para ello se puede estimar una demanda por dinero hasta 1 997 y luego simular dinmicamente hasta la actualidad, utilizando los datos efectivos de tasas y producto. Este ejercicio no admite ningn cambio en las preferencias por liquidez despus de 1 997; por lo tanto, es el ms conservador para analizar si hay crecimiento excesivo de la liquidez. Si la cantidad de dinero estuviera por encima de la demanda, podramos pensar que hay un exceso de crecimiento, dadas perspectivas inflacionarias bajas. El grfico 7 muestra que efectivamente la cantidad de dinero es consistente con la demanda. Por lo tanto, no hay evidencia de que haya un persistente exceso de dinero, ms del requerido, persiguiendo pocos bienes y pocos dlares. Es necesario agregar, tambin, que en un esquema donde el instrumento de poltica monetaria es la tasa de inters, la que se ajusta para conseguir la meta de inflacin dentro del rango de 2% a 4%, centrada en 3%, la demanda por dinero puede presentar volatilidad. Lo importante es que las expectativas y las acciones de poltica estn centradas dentro del rango meta de la inflacin. Por lo tanto, la informacin obtenida directamente de los agregados monetarios es parcial, aunque por supuesto no irrelevante. A modo de conclusin En Chile se ha adoptado un rgimen de flotacin cambiara, que es sin duda el ms adecuado, dadas sus caractersticas de economa pequea, abierta al exterior y con una gran dotacin de recursos naturales. La flexibilidad de este sistema evita costosos ajustes ante modificaciones en las condiciones externas e internas de la economa que requieran ajustes del tipo de cambio real. Un sistema de flotacin, en conjunto con un sistema financiero slido, evita las frecuentes crisis cambiaras, que se agravan al transmitirse al sistema bancario, y por las cuales han atravesado muchas economas emergentes, y de las que Chile en el pasado no ha estado exento. Intervenir excepcionalmente en el mercado cambiarlo se justifica cuando se estima que puede haber una sobrerreaccin del tipo de cambio, la que puede tener repercusiones negativas sobre la inflacin y en el comportamiento general de la economa. Esto ocurre por un conjunto de factores que afectan el funcionamiento ordenado de los mercados financieros, en especial en perodos de turbulencia internacional. Las condiciones externas actuales, en especial la fuerte cada de los trminos de intercambio, as como la escasez de flujos de capitales y el lento crecimiento de la demanda agregada en el frente interno, dan cuenta de parte importante de la depreciacin que ha sufrido el tipo de cambio real. En dos aos hemos tenido una depreciacin del tipo de cambio real que ha compensado una apreciacin ocurrida en ocho aos. En el futuro cercano, nuestro crecimiento vendr liderado por el sector de bienes transables, y las seales de precios as lo indican. Sin embargo, sera un error tener un objetivo de tipo de cambio real. En muchas oportunidades se intent, con elevados costos, doblarle la mano a la fuerza de los hechos. Desde el punto de vista de la fortaleza de nuestra economa lo que importa es la solidez de nuestros equilibrios internos y externos, ms que niveles especficos para ciertos precios. Asimismo, necesitamos mayores grados de profundidad en los mercados financieros y empresas ms conscientes de la necesidad de cubrirse ante fluctuaciones cambiaras. El conjunto de polticas macroeconmicas ha permitido acomodar los efectos de la depreciacin real. Una poltica fiscal equilibrada y una poltica monetaria comprometida con una meta de inflacin, han limitado los costos inflacionarios de estos eventos, como no ha ocurrido antes en nuestra historia econmica, pero como s ocurre en economas macroeconmicamente estables y modernas. Nuestra economa es una de ellas, y hoy est en muy buena posicin para absorber, aunque no evitar, las turbulencias externas. Sin embargo, estas polticas requieren del pragmatismo necesario para evitar sobrerreacciones de corto plazo que producen ms costos que beneficios, y en ese contexto se inscribe la intervencin excepcional que el Banco Central ha estado realizando en el mercado cambiarlo. Title: Copper Bonanza: Macroeconomic Impact and Policy Challenges
text: BONANZA DEL COBRE: IMPACTO MACROECONeeMICO Y DSAAFeaOs DE POLYTIC Jos8e De Gregorio. Central Bank of Chile May 2006 The price of copper is reaching historic record levels (Figure 1). After having reached in the years 2000-02 the three-year period of lowest copper price since the Great Depression, today we are punctually in values above the historical annual averages. Whether or not we will manage to beat this record will depend on the persistence of the increase we are observing, but certainly, our projections are that in real terms we will have the highest average annual price of the last 30 years. 1 Anything can happen in the years to come, and despite That the price of copper can continue to rise a little more, it is reasonable to think that it should recede. The problem is that we do not know how far it can go or when it will be returned and it is in this scenario of uncertainty in which we must make our economic policies. This boom environment is very good news for the Chilean economy, and to think otherwise is at least paradoxical. Although we can face possible sectoral tensions, we must take advantage of this opportunity to consolidate an economic policy that gives stability to the country and thus contribute to improving the living conditions of all Chileans. In this note I would like to address two issues. The first is to understand why our economy is growing less than in the past, when copper price booms also occurred. The second is to discuss the possible policy implications of this copper boom. In my discussion I would like to highlight the following points: a5 The main reason why the Chilean economy is not growing at 8 or 9%, as in past cycles of price increases, is that monetary, exchange rate and fiscal policies provide an important stabilizing element of the economic cycle. 2 Beyond possible changes, and if there are they are not very . Significantly, in potential growth, this is a very good result, because it guarantees that, when the external situation is reversed, we will not suffer the recessions to which we were accustomed in the past. This was already proven in the early years of this decade. a5 The consolidation of this policy scheme that generates greater stability is also based on the credibility that macroeconomic management has achieved in the country. This increases policy effectiveness and reduces business cycle costs. a5 The floating exchange rate regime has been successful. It certainly has costs in terms of peso volatility, which has increased with respect to the past, but the free float has avoided encouraging the inflow of short-term capital that could increase exchange rate pressures and has facilitated the adjustment of the economy to changes in the external scenario. 3 a5 The evidence shows that the evolution of the real exchange rate has been consistent with the huge gain in terms of trade that has occurred in recent years and, given current conditions, it is difficult to think that the real exchange rate can appreciate additionally significantly. a5 Fiscal policy successfully based on the 1% structural surplus rule faces a twofold challenge. First, it has been designed to spend the permanent components of the revenue increase, which is advisable from the point of view of the strength of our fiscal accounts. However, the implementation formula can add a degree of fiscal impulse with difficulties of being absorbed without major disruption given the current productive capacity. Why doesn't the economy grow much more? There has long been concern as to why the Chilean economy apparently overreacts to the price of copper. In particular, sharp falls in the price of copper lead us to recessions and accelerated increases to unsustainable expansions. Traditional macroeconomic mechanisms seem to be unable to explain why consumption, and more generally, aggregate spending, can grow at rates higher than those that could be explained by the impact on national income of an increase in the price of copper. In other words, it seems that in the past increases in the price of copper would trigger a euphoria difficult to explain. Copper is an important source of fiscal resources, but its importance is not so great as to explain its effects on the aggregate economy. The copper sector accounted for 13 per cent of GDP in nominal terms in 2005. Approximately two-thirds of this percentage is accounted for by foreign companies and their impact on employment is smaller. While I do not intend to summarize all the evidence here, Figure 2 shows that with prices not even as high as today's, the economy grew faster. This is how in the years 1978-80 we grew at 8.1%, in the period 1988-89 we grew at 8.9%, and in 95, at 10.1%. No doubt there are many other reasons that help us explain the actual growth of each year, but these figures clearly illustrate that today We are growing less than other periods of copper bonanza. 4 And this is the concern I want to address. That same year the Chilean economy grew 11.2%, three times more than in the previous three years and in the three subsequent years. A first explanation for the high impact that the price of copper has historically had on the national economy is that when copper rises, because the world economy is vigorous, or the dollar depreciates in the world, all commodities rise in price. In fact, the evolution of the price of copper is highly correlated with the terms of trade, beyond the direct effect of the price of copper (Figure 3). Consequently, we can think that the high price of copper is a reflection of many other positive international conditions. However, this does not seem to be enough to explain the sensitivity that GDP had in the past to fluctuations in the price of copper. That is why additional transmission channels need to be further explored. 5 Below I will review the two main causes that have occurred in the economic discussion about the overreaction of the economy to changes in the price of copper: Figure 3: Terms of Trade - Copper Price 260 240 220 200 Prat 2002 100 180 160 140 120 100 80 60 1965 1968 1971 1974 1977 1980 1983 1986 1989 1992 1995 1998 2001 350 300 250 USc/libgo out 200 150 100 50 2004 1.1. The macroeconomic policy framework TTPrecio copper From the Asian crisis, it became clear that financial markets can severely punish emerging economies, often without much foundation. On the other hand, there are periods in which the appetite to invest in emerging economies increases to levels that are difficult for them to absorb. Emerging economies can catch turbulence in distant and often disconnected markets. 5 In fact, Franken et al. (2005) find that it is the terms of trade and not the price of copper that affect the product. If we review the evolution of the financial markets during the nineties, we can see a period of accelerated expansion in the first half that culminates in a dramatic collapse of financing after the Asian crisis. These are the well-known sudden stops (Calvo, 2005). In the case of the Chilean economy it has been argued that when the price of copper increases, the value of the collateral of the economy increases, this reduces liquidity restrictions in financial markets and spending overflows. In the opposite case, and which has been argued could have happened with the recession of 99 in Chile, is that when the price of copper falls, external financing for Chile is cut because the value of its collateral, copper, falls (Caballero, 2002). This generates fluctuations in the type of financial accelerator discussed for domestic capital markets extended to global markets (Bernanke et al., 1996). While this mechanism may have operated at some point, it is difficult to think that it was relevant in the Chilean economy during the nineties. First, Chile did not lose access to international financial markets during the second half of the nineties. Moreover, after the Asian crisis in Chile, capital inflows did not stop, as in all countries suffering from the sudden stop, but the reversal of the capital and current account occurs through a massive outflow of capital, in particular pension funds and other investors that They preferred to protect themselves against an imminent depreciation of the peso. 6 On aggregate terms, this was consistent with an economy facing a sharp contraction in spending that resulted in a reduction in the current account deficit from levels close to 5 percent in 1998 to 0 percent in 1999. It is necessary to clarify that the fact that it is argued that there has not been a significant effect from the point of view of the changes in the international financial conditions facing Chile does not mean that there is no domestic financial accelerator. The evolution of indebtedness, particularly of smaller companies, after the liquidity crisis of 98, and the subsequent recovery indicate that their equity position is an important determinant of their financing capacities. 7 Finally, the experience of the beginning of the current decade is a first proof that despite having a very low copper price (the lowest three-year period since the Great Depression in 2001-2003) and an international recession in between, the economy did not collapse, as it managed to grow at an average of 3.4%. 8 Consequently, while the behavior of international financial markets is indeed relevant to our economic performance, it is far from being the main determinant of the reaction of the Chilean economy to changes in the price of copper, and international conditions in general. To effectively understand what is happening, we must look within, in particular our economic policies. 6 For more details see Cowan and De Gregorio (2005), where this phenomenon is called a sudden start of outlflows rather than a sudden stop of inflows. 7 This has also been confirmed in investment studies where cash flow is an important determinant of investment. See for example Medina and Vald8es (1998). 8 Strictly speaking, it must be considered that something that also prevented a fall is that the economy was already emerging from a recession, and this bad international scenario helps explain the decline in growth after the incipient recovery of 2000. A traditional reason why Latin American economies fluctuate excessively at the pace of the world economy and have more pronounced cycles is the destabilizing effect of fiscal policy. It is well known that most countries in the region, with the exception of Chile, have procyclical fiscal policies. This is due to the combination of improved external financing conditions and fiscal fragility. When the world economy is buoyant, the risk appetite of international investors increases, which encourages capital flows to emerging economies. This allows governments to spend that they could not do before due to lack of funding. At the root of this problem is fiscal fragility, which prevents less restricted access to international markets. This is not the case in Chile. In the case of Chile, it is not possible to justify that the increases in the price of copper in the last 25 years have generated fiscal expansions responsible for excessive growth and cause our recessions. Figure 4 shows that the fiscal balance does indeed improve when the price of copper increases. It may be discussed on the margins about its behavior around our recessions, but it is certainly far from having been a destabilizing element. On the contrary, viewed in a medium-term perspective, Chile's fiscal policy of the last 25 years has been stabilizing. This is particularly important today, when the increase in the price of copper is very high and all the increase is being saved to comply with the policy of maintaining a structural surplus of 1%. Therefore, we can say that the fiscal rule is an element that has contributed to the stability of the cycle. So, if fiscal policy has not been the main cause of past copper cycles, then why are exaggerated increases in private spending induced? A first option is simply to think that the private sector behaves strangely, but as I will argue here it does not seem to me a reasonable answer. In my opinion, what is behind the overflows of private spending has its origin in monetary policies and, mainly, exchange rate policies. Although its influence is somewhat more subtle than that of fiscal policy, its role is no less important. An emblematic case is that of the crisis of 82. The fiscal accounts were very orderly, and the current account deficit in 1981 was a whopping 13% of GDP. The economy grew at 6% with copper at just 127 cents a pound in today's currency (Figure 5). The problem was in the exchange-financial sphere. 2 0 -2 -4 -6 % PIB -8 -10 -12 -14 -16 1978 1980 1982 1984 1986 1988 1990 1992 1994 1996 1998 2000 2002 2004 Figure 5: Current Account Deficit - Copper Price 260 240 220 200 180 USc/libra 160 140 120 100 80 60 2006f DCCPrecio copper It is useful then to review the stabilizing effects of our current monetary and exchange rate policy scheme, which is known as inflation targeting. First, a credible inflation targeting scheme ensures the appropriate reaction of monetary policy to significant deviations of output from its level of full employment. In particular, positive demand shocks, which may result from improved external conditions, should be accompanied by an increase in the policy rate that avoids a de-anchoring of inflation and allows the economy to stabilize without suffering unsustainable expansions that are very costly to reverse. If these shocks cause an exchange rate drop that affects the inflation outlook, the monetary policy reaction is tempered. Also, when the Demand is depressed and the output gap is negative, the deflationary pressures this induces cause interest rates to fall. That happened between 2002 and early 2004 when the interest rate in Chile reached its lowest historical levels, which explains in an important way the recovery of the economy, already consolidated since last year. Secondly, another fundamental piece of this scheme is the floating exchange rate. The exchange rate contributes to stability by allowing adjustments of the real exchange rate to domestic economic conditions. A flexible exchange rate like the one we have in Chile facilitates adjustment as long as it is combined with a coherent macroeconomic policy scheme. If fiscal and monetary policies were inadequate, it would be possible to have exchange rate fluctuations that further exacerbate macroeconomic fluctuations. When the external situation is buoyant, the appreciation of the exchange rate allows to remove pressure on aggregate demand, activity and inflation, reducing the need for sudden movements in the interest rate. The movements of the exchange rate are a mechanism of adjustment of the economy, which when prevented from working tends to generate currency crises and problems greater than those that are tried to solve. Likewise, this scheme allows deviations from its long-term trend to be limited. And as the floating policy has been defined, if at any time it deviates to ranges that threaten stability generating risky imbalances, the option of intervention is not ruled out. What would be happening, for example, if the Central Bank had decided, through intervention, to graduate the appreciation that the economy has experienced in this time? The expectation that the exchange rate will appreciate lowers the cost of borrowing abroad, which would provide incentives for capital inflows, more pressures on the exchange rate, and greater growth and demand. Inflationary pressures would induce an increase in the interest rate with greater exchange rate impacts. The economy would grow more, the real exchange rate would appreciate, the current account deficit would increase, the price of stocks and assets in general would also rise, there would be euphoria, and of course, reversing this would be more costly. In fact, evidence shows that during the period of massive capital inflows in the nineties the countries that experienced the greatest capital inflows were those that had an administered exchange rate regime (Cowan and De Gregorio, 2005), regardless of whether or not they had capital controls. In other words, the attempt to curb appreciations generates more exchange rate pressures due to incentives for capital inflows. In this regard, our past experience is sobering. In 1997, with a current account deficit of 4.4% of GDP and copper around 1 per pound, the exchange rate reached its nineties low (Figure 6). At that time we tried to avoid the appreciation of the peso. There were capital controls, the exchange rate was managed within a band, and in 1997 international reserves equivalent to 4% of GDP were accumulated, to try to curb the effects of capital inflows that reached 8% of GDP. The defense of the exchange rate stimulated the inflow of capital. At that time market expectations were a gradual appreciation, even that was contemplated in the center of the band that contemplated a real fall of 2%. In this way, it was very advantageous to borrow abroad. Some clarifications TCRPrecio copper The situation today is very different. During that time the exchange rate bet was unilateral. They all bet on appreciation. Today the scenario is more balanced, and even expectations tend to be stabilizing. Currently, the Central Bank's expectations survey contemplates a depreciation of 3% at one year and 7% at two years. At peak depreciation in early 2003, a 3% drop was expected at 12 and 24 months. What is expected is that there will be the same prediction upwards as downwards, and in our case there is some reversal of sudden movements. The problem is that when the exchange rate appreciates and an appreciation is still expected, the situation becomes much more complex to manage, the same happens in the opposite direction. Therefore, today we have a macroeconomic policy regime consisting of a countercyclical fiscal rule and an inflation targeting scheme with a flexible exchange rate that explain the bulk of the greater economic stability we are observing today. 9 In this way we can conclude that the Chilean economy is today more stable, which has the apparent cost of limiting expansion, but the enormous benefit of cushioning slowdowns. My discussion has been focused on the stability of GDP around its long-term trend. Therefore, I am not referring here to the long-term potential growth of 9 The fact that macroeconomic policies have made our economy more stable has recently been confirmed in studies by Larra92n and Parro (2006) and Garc92a and Restrepo (2006). Both works emphasize the role of the current fiscal rule versus no rule, and there is no evidence comparing the current rule with the one that prevailed in the nineties. the economy. That is, how much we can grow, given our economic characteristics, our policies, institutions and the quality of our resources. Beyond a possible slowdown resulting from convergence to higher GDP levels, I think we can still think that this growth is close to 5% per year, a figure quite high by international standards. Moreover, it is presumable that the effects of convergence have been offset by other important advances that have occurred in the last decade, such as the increase in our degrees of openness and integration into the global economy and the consolidation of macroeconomic stability. 10 Certainly, with improvements in fundamental aspects such as education, the functioning of markets and innovation, we could grow more in the long term, although obviously these are processes that take time to bear fruit and whose analysis is beyond the scope of the issue at hand today. I have been explicit in indicating that with macroeconomic policies we have been able to stabilize the cycle, however there is still no answer as to why perhaps this growth is not closer, for example, to 7%. I don't think there is a simple answer because the nature of the cycle has changed and what we know about our potential growth is also subject to uncertainty. Secondly, there are those who will say that today we are suffering from Dutch disease. There is no evidence to support this. In fact, predictions in the Dutch disease literature suggest that growth would occur in the natural resources sector, at the cost of a decline in industry and other tradable goods sectors. That has not happened in Chile, except for a slowdown in agriculture due to specific climatic factors and transition from traditional crops. Likewise, mining does not show the dynamism that would be expected from a phenomenon of this type, and the economy continues to grow at rates higher than the growth of the trend product, which has allowed the product gap to close. The economy and exports continue to grow, particularly those in the industrial sector. There is certainly a decline in the profitability of the tradable goods sector as a result of the appreciation of the peso, which does not mean that this is a disease. This is part of the process of adjusting to an increase in the terms of trade. One might also think that the private sector has a psychologically bipolar behavior: excessively euphoric on the rise, excessively depressive on the downside. The recent evolution of the Chilean economy shows that this is not the case. I do not believe that we can allude to perverse and destabilizing behaviour in the private sector if we do not consider the distortions induced by economic policy. In my opinion, it is economic policy that induces excessively spending or austere behaviour. In all the experiences of overspending that appears to be private, it has been macro policy that has stimulated it. On the other hand, the evidence shows that in Chile during the nineties the component of spending that increased the most was investment and part of the stimulus also occurred due to the greater inflow of capital, a flow that is not observed today. 10 In any event, the most important effect in empirical work is lower growth as a result of convergence, since other, more qualitative aspects of the determinants of growth are difficult to include in the projections. For this reason, for example, De Gregorio (2005) presents estimates of long-term growth that have fallen a few tenths over time, although the differences are not statistically significant and are mainly due to convergence and worse external conditions in the second half of the last decade. (Spilimbergo, 1999). 11 In this regard, it should be noted that perhaps another stabilizing effect of the cycle has to do with a characteristic of the copper sector: unlike the nineties, today there is no volume of investment projects in the portfolio such as those that existed in the past decade. Finally, it should be noted that falling growth volatility has occurred in many parts of the world and is not just a feature of the Chilean economy. Figures 7 and 8 show for a group of countries, as well as for some groupings, the maximum difference, positive in Figure 7 and negative in Figure 8, of annual growth with respect to the average for the nineties and for the current decade. 12 The figures show that volatility has indeed fallen in many countries, although this has not happened in Latin America as a whole nor in the world or the advanced economies, only a fall in the volatility of the Euro area is seen. 13 What most of these countries share is that they have adopted inflation targets and have high degrees of exchange rate flexibility. These inflation targeting schemes have been mostly adopted during the nineties. That is, a global look at other countries suggests that the monetary policy framework makes a difference in terms of output volatility. 14 2. Do's, don'ts, and what to expect? The rising price of copper has made us richer. Probably not permanently, but we have had a gain that we must handle properly. The longer this gain lasts, the more beneficial the bonanza will be and the more challenges we will have in managing it. That gain must be spent, but the most important challenge of fiscal policy is how to scale such spending, given the uncertainty about its magnitude and the constraints that the economy has to absorb it adequately. Consequently, we cannot spend all the additional revenue in the short term, nor can we charge it to a tax cut. In fact, everything I say below is, in a first approximation, valid both for an increase in spending and for a reduction in taxes. 15 One reason is prudence, and it is to save for the time when prices fall. Reasonable management of public finances suggests saving these windfall revenues. That's exactly what the surplus rule does. 11 The private current account deficit is currently very high, with the government surplus being several points of GDP. However, the moderate increase in aggregate demand would indicate that this deficit is the result of slow growth in domestic private income rather than an unsustainable increase in spending. 12 For 2006, the projection of the IMF's World Economic Outlook is considered. 13 In the case of Latin America, volatility measured by comparing minimum and maximum deviations from the average only increases in Argentina, Uruguay and Venezuela. 14 Mishkin and Schmidt-Hebbel (2005) show evidence supporting the idea that inflation-targeting countries perform better macroeconomically. In particular, they argue that: "Output volatility has not worsened, and if anything improved, after the adoption of inflation targeting". 15 Depending on what is spent on, or the nature of a tax cut, there may be some different effect of more spending or less taxation, but a priori there is no compelling reason to think that they are very different, particularly since increases in spending usually refer to transfers. But the tax-spending mix also has implications for long-term growth. But there are also reasons why one cannot spend all this money, even if it is hard, and hence the need for gradualness. 12 Let's think as if Chile had won the lottery, but the prize is given in annuities and at some point it will end without notice. Obviously you have to save for when the prize is discontinued. This is the same thing a family would do if they won such an award. But the family can also make big expenses that it could never do before, and even support them, because it has more wealth. I could buy a house, a car, even a second home if the prize is very large. Many of these purchases can be considered household investment because they are goods that will provide services for many years, even when the prize is over. All these costs have no aggregate impact. However, this is not the case when a country wins this lottery, because the expenses it makes do have repercussions on the entire economy. Therefore, the need for caution goes beyond prudence for the duration of this award, it also goes for the impact and capacity of the economy to absorb this expense. What happens is that economies have a certain maximum production capacity in the short term, and there are even limits in longer terms. If we spent all this extra income there wouldn't be many more goods to buy, unless we imported them all. The prices of goods would rise, generating inflation. This pressure on prices, particularly for non-tradable goods whose prices are not subject to international conditions, would lead to an appreciation of the real exchange rate. In other words, national goods would become more expensive than international goods. Interest rates would rise due to falling savings and inflationary pressures. In this way, higher spending would not translate into higher output, but into higher current-account deficits, higher interest rates, and a fall in the real exchange rate. In the extreme case that production is completely rigid, which is not the case but serves to clarify the point, an increase in government spending must be offset by a fall in other components of spending and they are investment and net exports via a rise in interest rates and a fall in the real exchange rate. That is, prices must change to make room for increased public spending. More generally, there will indeed be demand pressures that will increase production in the short run, but this is not lasting to the extent that what changes is not productive capacity and relative prices move further away from their long-run equilibrium. It can be argued that it is a small price to pay for having more spending. But that is not so. When the economy is growing, there are underlying inflationary pressures from increased activity, a cycle of rising interest rates, and pressures on exchange rate appreciation, so it is not desirable to add momentum to the economy. That is precisely what a countercyclical macroeconomic policy consists of, tempering fluctuations in output and relative prices. Of course this depends on grades and it will be the tax authorities who will ultimately decide the graduation of this process, but it is important to point out the challenges they have and the ways to address it. The structural surplus rule is a major contribution to stabilizing the cycle and constitutes a major advance in fiscal management. During the nineties, a first step was taken by limiting spending growth with GDP growth. However, that did have a undesirable procyclical component that had to be corrected with the recession of '99. The current rule ensures that if output is below full employment you can run a deficit, and the opposite occurs in times of limited capacity. This helps stabilize the business cycle. However, there remains a procyclical element that for the first time will become clearly evident this year and requires careful examination. This refers to the long-term price of copper. When the price of copper rises, so does the long-term price used in the rule. This in turn allows for further fiscal expansion. This occurs exactly at a time when the economy does not need additional fiscal impulses because GDP is above its trend. This is precisely because of the positive correlation between GDP, copper prices and global activity. The opposite case occurred when the rule was inaugurated in a cycle of very low copper prices. On that occasion the price was close to 80 cents a pound. Had we predicted the boom we are experiencing today, which is obviously hypothetical and impossible to achieve, fiscal policy would have been more expansionary. Similarly, if tomorrow the price unexpectedly collapses, we may have made a very optimistic budget. To illustrate this point you can perform the following exercise. Suppose that the price of copper is equal to the assumption in the last Monetary Policy Report, that is, this year it would be on average 2.6 dollars per pound and next year 2.25 dollars per pound. Now suppose that the price of reference copper is estimated, for the next 10 years, using an autoregressive process of first order estimated with historical data. That is, it is assumed that copper price increases persist over time to gradually adjust to its long-term trend assumed at 1 per pound. Finally, an annual autocorrelation coefficient of 0.75 is used, it is also estimated that 10 cents per pound represents higher revenues by 0.5% of GDP and a trend growth of 5% is assumed. 16 These calculations are illustrative and use rough estimates but serve to illustrate the fiscal policy dilemma. Based on these parameters, it could be estimated what is the expansion of public spending consistent with the rule. A review concludes that spending would have an annual growth rate of 15% in 2007 and 2% in 2008. Clearly, these magnitudes would exacerbate the business cycle. One might think that the expert committee should consider the macro implications of its estimate and act cautiously. But this is not the idea of the expert committee. In my opinion, institutions function when they do the task for which they were created. The challenge is then fiscal policy and they require some important decisions. I think we can think of three alternatives: 1. Do nothing and let this expansion of spending happen and then slow down. Fiscal policy is a datum for monetary policy and presumably this expansion, to the extent that it adds inflationary pressures, will mean higher interest rates, more appreciated real exchange rates and more growth in 2007. The situation would be reversed in 2008, with 16 Interest should also be added from the accumulating surplus, but there should not be a very significant change. For example, a surplus of 5% of GDP in an invested year to 5% per year gives 0.25% of GDP in interest which is about one percentage point of government spending. lower growth, exchange rate depreciation and probably somewhat lower rates. 2. Adjust the long-term price to give greater gradualness to the adjustment. This does not necessarily mean changing the rule, but it does mean modifying its implementation . One option is to say that you will think about the reference price looking ahead at 30 years, or alternatively use the price of the next 10 years weighted with the reference price of the previous year. The latter is equal to gradually adjusting to the reference price . 3. Use some of the potential "overspending", that which may have unwanted effects on the cycle, in areas of little macro impact. That is, they are fully consistent with the fiscal rule in their size of saving for when the bonanza has passed, and at the same time, be consistent with the economy's ability to absorb the largest spending without significant shocks. Here I would like to highlight and deepen a proposal presented in the presidential message of May 21 that has to do with unemployment insurance. If we want to reconcile macroeconomic stability with a commitment to spend the permanent component of the bonanza and at the same time make an important effort in the social sphere where we have enormous challenges, it is possible to increase the solidarity fund as well as grant a transfer of expenditure to individual unemployment insurance accounts. This is transforming public savings into private savings17, which eventually should not have an aggregate impact. It also has another great macroeconomic contribution and that is to provide an automatic stabilizer to the cycle. If there is something that fiscal policy in Chile has not had, it is automatic fiscal stabilizers on the expenditure side. In developed countries it is generous unemployment benefit systems that generate automatic expansions into recessions. However, this has serious incentive problems and in Chile it was innovated with a creative unemployment insurance system based on individual capitalization and a solidarity fund . This can have a major stabilizing impact. Therefore, in my opinion, increasing the solidarity fund of unemployment insurance as well as delivering a transfer to individual accounts is macroeconomically positive, is consistent with the fiscal rule and is of an important social content because it delivers resources to those who need it most in times of economic difficulty. To the extent that there are resources in the unemployment insurance accounts and they are not occupied, they will be complementary to the pensions of the beneficiaries with the subsidy. Here I have outlined a general idea that certainly requires more detailed analysis and care. How to ensure and design its progressivity in social terms? How to design it in a way that does not negatively affect job and job search decisions? How to graduate it so that it does not become current expenditure and is effectively savings for situations of unemployment? 18 These are some of the 17 This is obvious in the case of transferring resources to individual accounts, and in the case of the increase in the solidarity fund it is rather a matter of accounting conventions, although conceptually it is private sector savings where the beneficiary is not defined ex-ante. 18 Cowan, Huneeus and Micco (2006) develop a similar idea regarding individual accounts. This proposal consists of supplementing with public funds, with the same amount, the social security contributions and unemployment insurance of the lowest incomes. questions that should be answered to evaluate this proposal more carefully, but it can help address the challenges that fiscal policy will face. Another important aspect when analyzing the copper bonanza is to consider its exchange rate implications. As I have already discussed, the appreciation of the real exchange rate is part of the adjustment to the external shock, and with a floating system as well as an austere fiscal policy these effects are lessened. However, my impression is that at times there has been a tendency to overestimate the impact it has on the economy. The copper-producing sector is important, but an important part is external participation and the national part saves most of the extraordinary income. Empirical evidence, both for Chile and for OECD19 countries, indicates that an increase in the terms of trade of 10% results in an appreciation of about 3%. From 2003, when the real exchange rate reached the highest of this decade (Figure 9), to 2006, assuming that it remains constant for the rest of the year, the real exchange rate would have appreciated by 14%. On the other hand, although the real price of copper would have increased by 177%, the terms of trade will have increased by only 49%. Using historical elasticity we could explain the fall in the real exchange rate in the last three years by the effect of the terms-of-trade gain. To this we must add the fact that most of the increase in income from improved external conditions is saved and there are also no financial pressures, for example due to the abundance of capital inflows, to pressure the exchange rate. There are many other factors that determine the exchange rate, particularly in its short-term movements, but these calculations suggest that it is difficult for the real exchange rate to appreciate significantly at the current juncture. In monetary-exchange matters, we must persist with what has been done so far. As I have tried to argue, the monetary policy scheme is the most appropriate at the current juncture. Had we had this scheme in the late nineties, we would have weathered the emerging market crisis much better. Monetary policy is not measured by the activism of the authorities or by the number of measures taken, but by their results. What we have seen in recent years is the best contribution that macroeconomic policies can make to long-term growth. Of course, this is a necessary condition, not enough to grow further. Intervention is only justified when there is a significant misalignment that threatens the stability of the economy. It can never be ruled out, but experience shows that thinking that an appreciation can be graduated can generate unwanted effects that you want to avoid. The credibility of floating and possible interventions must be strengthened. We could intervene, be reassured and congratulated by pragmatists, but seriously damage the credibility and future functioning of our policy scheme. To intervene we need to be relatively convinced that there is an exchange rate overreaction, that it is harmful to the economy as a whole, and that intervention has a high probability of success. 19 C8espedes and De Gregorio (1999) and Broda (2001). On the other hand, we must be careful in arguing that we must fix problems in specific sectors through exchange rate intervention. Under the assumption that it is effective, on which there is an unresolved debate in particular when no obvious misalignments are observed, exchange intervention is requested for the damage suffered by some sectors. Affecting the exchange rate to go to the aid of specific sectors is a very inefficient policy, because the benefit that afflicted producers receive is also received by all others who do not need it. In other words, it is a very poorly targeted policy. Finally, I would like to refer to another proposal that is also circulating in the environment and that is the need to take advantage of this situation to take macro insurance for when the price of copper falls and thus avoid the excessive volatility generated by international financial markets. To discuss this idea, it is necessary to distinguish between the insurance that companies can take from the one that the country can take. Companies can look for mechanisms in derivatives markets to take advantage of the high price cycle. Even from public policy, insurance can be sought for specific problems, such as the price of fuel. However, these are business or policy-specific problems, but they are not macro relevant. In this regard, as I argued earlier, there is no evidence that in the recent past we have suffered particularly severe shocks from international financial markets, so buying macro insurance is something of the second order, which also involves high risks when dealing with exotic instruments. In any case, we must take advantage of continuing to improve the financial integration of Our economy and the functioning of the Chilean capital market to provide better management of corporate risks and facilitate investment financing. However, from the point of view of buying insurance, the best insurance for our economy is a good macroeconomic policy, and I believe that Chile has moved in the right direction, reaching a first-rate macroeconomic policy. The permanent challenge is knowing how to manage it. 3.By way of closure I would like to conclude by noting that I am convinced that the current macroeconomic policy scheme is the most efficient to manage this bonanza. As I pointed out earlier, success is not measured by the number of actions or the visibility of the measures taken. Nor have we adopted a fashionable regime nor is it the result of a lesson learned in books, or orthodoxy as others will say. I understand that many are irritated that the authorities say that more of the same must be done, but when we are convinced that this is the best thing for the country we must say so, as well as we must also be able to apply the necessary corrections. Chile has been characterized by its pragmatism in economic policy and where we are today is the result of learning from our mistakes and also from the mistakes and successes of others. Esto ayuda a la estabilizacin del ciclo econmico. Sin embargo, an queda un elemento procclico que por primera vez se har ntidamente evidente este ao y que requiere de un examen cuidadoso. Este se refiere al precio del cobre de largo plazo. Cuando el precio del cobre sube, tambin lo hace en alguna medida el precio de largo plazo que se usa en la regla. Esto a su vez permite una mayor expansin fiscal. Esta ocurre exactamente en momentos en que la economa no necesita de impulsos fiscales adicionales pues el PIB est por sobre su tendencia. Esto ocurre precisamente por la correlacin positiva entre PIB, precio del cobre y actividad mundial. El caso opuesto ocurri cuando se inaugur la regla en un ciclo de precios del cobre muy bajos. En esa ocasin el precio era cercano a los 80 centavos de dlar la libra. De haber predicho el boom que experimentamos hoy, algo obviamente hipottico e imposible de concretar, la poltica fiscal hubiera sido ms expansiva. Similarmente si maana el precio inesperadamente colapsa, podremos haber hecho un presupuesto muy optimista. Para ilustrar este punto se puede realizar el siguiente ejercicio. Supongamos que el precio del cobre es igual al supuesto en el ltimo Informe de Poltica Monetaria, es decir este ao sera en promedio 2,6 dlares por libra y el prximo ao 2,25 dlares por libra. Supongamos ahora que se estima el precio del cobre de referencia, para los 10 prximos aos, usando un proceso autorregresivo de primer orden estimado con datos histricos. Esto es, se asume que los aumentos del precio del cobre persisten en el tiempo para ajustarse gradualmente a su tendencia de largo plazo que se asume en 1 dlar la libra. Finalmente, se usa un coeficiente de autocorrelacin anual de 0,75, se estima adems que 10 centavos de dlar la libra representan mayores ingresos por 0,5% del PIB y se asume un crecimiento de tendencia del gasto de 5%.16 Estos clculos son ilustrativos y usan estimaciones gruesas pero sirven para ilustrar el dilema de la poltica fiscal. Basado en estos parmetros se podra estimar cul es la expansin del gasto pblico consistente con la regla. Al realizar este ejercicio se concluye que el gasto tendra una tasa de crecimiento anual de 15% el 2007 y de 2% el 2008. Claramente estas magnitudes exacerbaran el ciclo econmico. Alguien podra pensar que el comit de expertos debera considerar las repercusiones macro de su estimacin y actuar con cautela. Pero esta no es la idea del comit de expertos. A mi juicio las instituciones funcionan cuando hacen la tarea para la que fueron creadas. El desafo es entonces de la poltica fiscal y que requieren de algunas decisiones importantes. Creo que podemos pensar en tres alternativas:  No hacer nada y dejar que ocurra dicha expansin del gasto y frenar posteriormente. La poltica fiscal es un dato para la poltica monetaria y presumiblemente esta expansin, en la medida que agregue presiones inflacionarias, significar tasas de inters ms altas, tipo de cambio real ms apreciado y ms crecimiento el 2007. La situacin se revertira el 2008, con 16 Habra tambin que agregar los intereses del supervit que se va acumulando, pero no debera haber un cambio muy significativo. Por ejemplo, un supervit de 5% del PIB en un ao invertido a un 5% anual da 0,25% del PIB en intereses lo que es aproximadamente un punto porcentual del gasto de gobierno. menor crecimiento, depreciacin del tipo de cambio y tasas probablemente algo menores.  Ajustar el precio de largo plazo para darle mayor gradualidad al ajuste. Esto no necesariamente significa cambiar la regla, pero s implica modificar su forma de implementacin. Una opcin es decir que se pensar en el precio de referencia mirando a 30 aos haca adelante, o alternativamente usar el precio de los prximos 10 aos ponderado con el precio de referencia del ao anterior. Esto ltimo es igual a ajustarse gradualmente al precio de referencia.  Usar parte del potencial gasto excesivo, aquel que pueda tener efectos indeseados sobre el ciclo, en reas de poco impacto macro. Es decir que sean plenamente consistentes con la regla fiscal en su dimensin de ahorrar para cuando la bonanza haya pasado, y al mismo tiempo, ser consistentes con la capacidad de la economa de absorber el mayor gasto sin sobresaltos significativos. Aqu quisiera destacar y profundizar en una propuesta presentada en el mensaje presidencial del 21 de mayo que tiene que ver con el seguro de desempleo. Si se quiere conciliar estabilidad macroeconmica con compromiso de gastar el componente permanente de la bonanza y al mismo tiempo hacer un importante esfuerzo en el mbito social donde tenemos enormes desafos, es posible incrementar el fondo solidario as como otorgar una transferencia de gasto a las cuentas individuales de seguro de desempleo. Esto es transformar ahorro pblico en ahorro privado17, lo que eventualmente no debiera tener impacto agregado. Tiene adems otra gran contribucin macroeconmica y es la de proveer un estabilizador automtico al ciclo. Si hay algo que la poltica fiscal en Chile no ha tenido son estabilizadores automticos fiscales por el lado del gasto. En pases desarrollados estos son los generosos sistemas de subsidio de desempleo los que generan expansiones automticas en recesiones. Sin embargo, esto tiene serios problemas de incentivos y en Chile se innov con un creativo sistema de seguro de desempleo basado en la capitalizacin individual y un fondo solidario. Esto puede tener un impacto estabilizador importante. Por lo tanto, a mi juicio, el incrementar el fondo solidario del seguro de desempleo as como entregar una transferencia a las cuentas individuales es macroeconmicamente positivo, es consistente con la regla fiscal y es de un importante contenido social pues entrega recursos a quienes ms lo necesitan en tiempos de dificultad econmica. En la medida que haya recursos en las cuentas de seguro de desempleo y no se ocupan, sern complementarios a las pensiones de los beneficiarios con el subsidio. Aqu he esbozado una idea general que ciertamente requiere de anlisis ms detallado y cuidados. Cmo asegurar y disear su progresividad en trminos sociales? Cmo disearlo de manera que no afecte negativamente las decisiones de trabajo y bsqueda de empleo? Cmo graduarlo de manera que no se transforme en gasto corriente y sea efectivamente ahorro para situaciones de desempleo?18 Esas son algunas de las 17 Esto es obvio en el caso de transferir recursos a las cuentas individuales, y en el caso del incremento del fondo solidario es ms bien un tema de convenciones contables, aunque conceptualmente es ahorro del sector privado donde el beneficiario no est definido ex-ante. 18 Cowan, Huneeus y Micco (2006) desarrollan una idea similar respecto de las cuentas individuales. Otro aspecto importante a la hora de analizar la bonanza cuprfera es considerar sus implicancias cambiarias. Como ya discut, la apreciacin del tipo de cambio real es parte del ajuste al shock externo, y con un sistema de flotacin as como una poltica fiscal austera estos efectos son aminorados. Sin embargo mi impresin es que en algunos momentos se ha tendido a sobredimensionar el impacto que tiene sobre la economa. El sector productor de cobre es importante, pero una parte importante es participacin externa y la parte nacional ahorra la mayora de los ingresos extraordinarios. La evidencia emprica, tanto para Chile como para pases de la OECD19, indica que un aumento de los trminos de intercambios de 10% resulta en una apreciacin de alrededor de 3%. Desde el 2003, cuando el tipo de cambio real alcanz el mximo de esta dcada (figura 9), hasta el 2006, asumiendo que permanece constante por el resto del ao, el tipo de cambio real se habra apreciado un 14%. Por su parte aunque el precio real del cobre habra aumentado un 177%, los trminos de intercambio lo habrn hecho slo un 49%. Usando la elasticidad histrica podramos explicar la cada ocurrida en el tipo de cambio real en los ltimos tres aos por el efecto de la ganancia de trminos de intercambio. A esto debemos agregar el hecho de que la mayora del aumento de ingresos proveniente del mejoramiento de las condiciones externas se ahorra y asimismo no existen presiones financieras, por ejemplo debido a la abundancia de ingreso de capitales, que presionen el tipo de cambio. Existen muchos otros factores que determinan el tipo de cambio, en particular en sus movimientos de corto plazo, pero estos clculos sugieren que es difcil que en la coyuntura actual el tipo de cambio real se aprecie significativamente. En materia monetaria-cambiaria hay que persistir con lo hecho hasta ahora. Como he tratado de argumentar, el esquema de poltica monetaria es el ms adecuado en la actual coyuntura. De haber tenido este esquema a fines de los noventa habramos pasado mucho mejor la crisis de los mercados emergentes. La poltica monetaria no se mide por el activismo de las autoridades ni por el nmero de medidas que se toman sino que por sus resultados. Lo que hemos visto en aos recientes es la mejor contribucin que las polticas macroeconmicas pueden hacer al crecimiento de largo plazo. Por supuesto, esto es una condicin necesaria, no suficiente para crecer ms. La intervencin slo se justifica cuando se observa un desalineamiento significativo que ponga en peligro la estabilidad de la economa. Nunca se puede descartar, pero la experiencia muestra que pensar que se puede graduar una apreciacin puede generar efectos indeseados a los que se quiere evitar. Hay que fortalecer la credibilidad de la flotacin y las eventuales intervenciones. Se podra intervenir, quedar tranquilos y ser felicitados por pragmticos, pero daar seriamente la credibilidad y el funcionamiento futuro de nuestro esquema de poltica. Para intervenir necesitamos estar relativamente convencidos de que hay una sobrerreaccin cambiaria, que sta es daina para la economa como un todo, y que la intervencin tiene una probabilidad elevada de xito. 19 Cspedes y De Gregorio (1999) y Broda (2001).
