Por otra parte, hay que ser cuidadosos al argumentar que debemos arreglar problemas en sectores especficos por la va de la intervencin cambiaria. Bajo el supuesto de que es efectiva, sobre lo cual hay un debate no resuelto en particular cuando no se observan desalineamientos evidentes, se pide intervencin cambiaria por el dao que sufren algunos sectores. Afectar el tipo de cambio para ir en ayuda de sectores especficos es una poltica muy ineficiente, porque el beneficio que reciben los productores afligidos tambin lo reciben todos los otros que no lo necesitan. Es decir, es una poltica muy mal focalizada. Por ltimo, quisiera referirme a otra propuesta que tambin circula en el ambiente y es la necesidad de aprovechar esta coyuntura para tomar un seguro macro para cuando caiga el precio del cobre y as evitar la excesiva volatilidad que nos generan los mercados financieros internacionales. Para discutir esta idea hay que distinguir entre el seguro que pueden tomar las empresas del que puede tomar el pas. Las empresas pueden buscar mecanismos en los mercados de derivados para aprovechar el ciclo de precios altos. Incluso desde la poltica pblica se pueden buscar seguros para problemas especficos, como el precio de los combustibles. Sin embargo, estos son problemas de las empresas o de polticas especficas, pero no son relevantes desde el punto de vista macro. Al respecto, como argument anteriormente, no hay evidencia de que en el pasado reciente hayamos sufrido shocks particularmente severos de los mercados financieros internacionales, de manera que comprar un seguro macro es algo de segundo orden, que adems envuelve elevados riesgos al tratarse de instrumentos exticos. En todo caso s hay que aprovechar de seguir mejorando la integracin financiera de nuestra economa y el funcionamiento del mercado de capitales chileno para proveer un mejor manejo de los riesgos de las empresas y facilitar el financiamiento de la inversin. No obstante, desde el punto de vista de comprar seguros, el mejor seguro para nuestra economa es una buena poltica macroeconmica, y creo que Chile ha caminado en la direccin correcta llegando a tener una poltica macroeconmica de primer nivel. El desafo permanente es saber administrarla. 3. A modo de cierre Quisiera concluir sealando que soy un convencido de que el actual esquema de polticas macroeconmicas es el ms eficiente para manejar esta bonanza. Como seal anteriormente el xito no se mide por el nmero de acciones ni la visibilidad de las medidas que se tomen. Tampoco hemos adoptado un rgimen de moda ni es el resultado de una leccin aprendida en los libros, u ortodoxia como dirn otros. Title: Inflation Video Release
text: Inflation Video Release Central Bank of Chile Santiago, November 7, 2007 Throughout these almost 20 years of autonomy, the Central Bank of Chile has made an enormous effort to contain inflation, an evil that endemically affected our economy. Inflation was everywhere, affecting the quality of life of all Chileans, especially the poorest. Salaries that could be good, were diluted day by day, rapidly losing their value and the bills were also devalued with astonishing speed. You could talk a lot about inflation, and we have done so in many of our publications, and the balance will be almost absolutely loaded with negative effects. The adoption of a price stability scheme d0 supported by a highly responsible fiscal policy, a sound financial system and an economy integrated into the world d0 has sought precisely to eliminate from the daily lives of Chileans the constant concern caused by price rises and general instability. In this context the Central Bank was able to achieve a result that until a few years ago was unimaginable. First, have annual inflation in the single digits and then bring it to a figure around 3% most of the time. Something unprecedented in our modern economic history. With this achievement, the Bank contributed to achieving macroeconomic stability that has been a pillar of a process of sustained growth and development. It is precisely this stability to which we have become accustomed, which makes us all surprised these days when as a result of unusual shocks in food and energy prices we see levels of monthly inflation that, while still in the single digits, were already totally out of our minds and our habits. It is good to be concerned and take decisive action so that short-term effects beyond the control of the authorities remain precisely in the field of the conjunctural and temporary and do not end up affecting the inflationary trend in a lasting way. Giving in to this effort would only result in higher costs of returning to stability in the future. Moreover, inflation should be a permanent and not exclusive concern of these periods in which it escapes the tolerance range of the target established by the Central Bank. For this, it is necessary to always be aware of its negative effects, as well as the importance of keeping it under control. This conjunctural period of high inflation, which seems to be easing according to the latest figures, coincides with a project of the Central Bank framed in its firm intention to also contribute to the economic and financial formation of all Chileans. In our search for tools that make it easier to understand economic issues transcendent to the lives of our compatriots, we watched an interesting video that the European Central Bank distributed mainly among students and that explained in an easy and playful way the importance of price stability, its contribution to macroeconomic stability and finally to the welfare of society. We thought then of adapting it to our reality, given the similarity of the objectives of the Central Bank of Chile with those of the European Central Bank. The Central Bank of Chile requested authorization from ECB President Jean Claude Trichet to adapt this video to Chile and his positive response came without delay. The video was adapted both in its audio and in some images to the Chilean reality and the objectives of the Central Bank of Chile and we believe that it can become a valuable piece to educate Chileans about price stability. In about seven minutes, it explains why inflation is harmful and why it is important to keep it under control. It is a cartoon story easy to watch and understand and, above all, entertaining and didactic. The release of this video is a great pride for us. We are taking another step in our task of bringing the economy closer to the people, taking them out of the technical field, because it affects everyone's daily lives. A good knowledge and understanding of economic phenomena such as inflation and the need for price stability, helps to make appropriate decisions, to reduce risk and uncertainty, and, in a special way, to account for the whole society of our task and why we believe that it is important for the good development of our country. We will make an effort to distribute this video in schools, universities and make it accessible to the greatest number of Chileans, through our website. In a first phase, it will be distributed to 2,500 schools in the country and our goal is that all educational establishments in Chile receive it in a short period of time. It is a task that we hope will also have the strong support of authorities, organizations and the media, so that it reaches more and more Chileans. The Central Bank of Chile has set out to bring the economy to an ever broader degree of understanding, convinced that in doing so we contribute to consolidating stability and improving the effectiveness of our policies, which ultimately results in a contribution to the progress of Chile and the well-being of all those who inhabit it. Thanks a lot

Se podra hablar mucho de la inflacin, y as lo hemos hecho en muchas de nuestras publicaciones, y la balanza estar casi absolutamente cargada a los efectos negativos. Es precisamente esta estabilidad a la que nos hemos acostumbrado, la que nos hace sorprendemos a todos en estos das en que como resultado de shocks inusuales en precios de alimentos y de la energa vemos niveles de inflaciones mensuales que, si bien continan siendo de un dgito, ya estaban totalmente fuera de nuestras mentes y nuestras costumbres. Este perodo coyuntural de inflacin alta, que parece estar cediendo de acuerdo a las ltimas cifras, coincide con un proyecto del Banco Central enmarcado en su firme propsito de contribuir tambin a la formacin econmica y financiera de todos los chilenos. En nuestra bsqueda de herramientas que hagan ms fcil la comprensin de temas econmicos trascendentes para la vida de nuestros compatriotas, vimos un interesante video que el Banco Central Europeo distribuy principalmente entre estudiantes y que explicaba de manera fcil y ldica la importancia de la estabilidad de precios, su contribucin a la estabilidad macroeconmica y finalmente al bienestar de la sociedad. Pensamos entonces en adaptarlo a nuestra realidad, dada la similitud que tienen los objetivos del Banco Central de Chile con los del Banco Central Europeo. El Banco Central de Chile pidi autorizacin al Presidente del BCE, Jean Claude Trichet para adaptar este video a Chile y su respuesta positiva lleg sin demora. El video fue adaptado tanto en su audio como en algunas imgenes a la realidad chilena y a los objetivos del Banco Central de Chile y creemos que se puede convertir en una pieza valiosa para educar a los chilenos acerca de la estabilidad de precios. En alrededor de siete minutos, se explica por qu la inflacin es daina y por qu es importante mantenerla controlada. Es una historia en dibujos animados fcil de ver y entender y, por sobre todo, entretenida y didctica. El lanzamiento de este video, constituye para nosotros un gran orgullo. Estamos dando un paso ms en nuestra tarea de acercar la economa a la gente, sacndola del mbito tcnico, pues ella afecta la vida cotidiana de todos. Un buen conocimiento y comprensin de fenmenos econmicos como la inflacin y la necesidad de contar con estabilidad de precios, ayuda a tomar decisiones adecuadas, a aminorar el riesgo y la incertidumbre, y, de manera especial, a dar cuenta a toda la sociedad de nuestra tarea y por qu creemos que ella es importante para el buen desarrollo de nuestro pas. Haremos un esfuerzo en distribuir este video en colegios, universidades y hacerlo accesible a la mayor cantidad de chilenos, a travs de nuestra pgina web. En una primera fase, se distribuir a 2.500 colegios del pas y nuestra meta es que lo reciban en breve lapso todos los establecimientos educacionales de Chile. Es una tarea que esperamos cuente tambin con el decidido apoyo de autoridades, organizaciones y medios de difusin, de manera que llegue cada vez ms a una mayor cantidad de chilenos. El Banco Central de Chile se ha propuesto llevar la economa a un grado de comprensin cada vez ms amplio, convencidos que con ello contribuimos a consolidar la estabilidad y a mejorar la efectividad de nuestras polticas, lo que finalmente redunda en una contribucin al progreso de Chile y al bienestar de todos quienes lo habitan. Muchas gracias

Title: The Exchange Rate and Exchange Policy in Chile
text: The Exchange Rate and Exchange Policy in Chile* Jos8e De Gregorio President Central Bank of Chile March 18, 2008 Mr. President, through you, I would like to thank the Honourable Chamber of Deputies for inviting me to speak on the exchange rate situation and exchange rate policy. We are aware that we live in very complex times for our economy, not only because of the exchange rate, but also in inflation and growth, due to the extraordinary volatility and uncertainty that we are witnessing in developed economies. We understand the difficulties that some important economic sectors of our country are facing in the face of the appreciation that the exchange rate has experienced in recent months. All these factors are present in the analyses we carry out every day, analyses that constitute the basis on which we make our decisions. We are very attentive, always, to the evolution of the relevant variables to meet the objectives set by law. In January 2006, the President of the Central Bank went to the Senate to speak on the issue of exchangerate 1. On that occasion, the situation was very different. Inflation was contained, and the last monthly record had been annualized inflation of 3.7%. After three months in which it slightly exceeded 4%, for the next 16 months it remained within the tolerance range. The monetary policy rate was 4.5%, while the Federal Funds Rate in the United States was 4.25%. The price of copper was 2.1 a pound. Finally, the real exchange rate index was 86.6 (base 1986100). Today, however, we are facing a real exchange rate index which, with the data of the last week, would have fallen to 82.4, that is, 5% lower than in January 2006. The last inflation record in 12 months reached 8.1%, with a monetary policy rate of 6.25%. In the United States the rate is 2.25%, and there are expectations that it will continue to fall. The situation is certainly more complex than in 2006. The United States, the world's largest economy, is experiencing great difficulties. Its financial system has become extremely fragile and the likelihood of a prolonged recession has increased significantly. This is also the case in a context in which inflationary pressures at the global level have increased. That is why it seems to us of first importance to come to present on the exchange rate situation within the framework of our economic policy and the international situation, in the context of our policy of transparency and to give a regular account of the situation of the economy. A small economy like ours is incapable of developing in isolation from the rest of the world. The export sector plays a crucial role in this international insertion. It has been doing so successfully in recent decades. In this context, the exchange rate is a key price for the Chilean economy, and its most recent evolution is a cause for concern for all. Within this world where there are always uncertainties and there is room for different interpretations, I will try to present our vision of what is behind the severe appreciation of the peso in recent months, an appreciation not only significant, but also surprising. Before continuing, it is important to note that exchange rate and monetary policies have significant effects on financial markets. That is why central banks, in normal situations, act gradually and predictably. We have learned, for example, that it is preferable to move the interest rate gradually to reduce the volatility of the financial cost of companies and individuals. On the other hand, when a central bank evaluates the use of exceptional tools in extraordinary circumstances, it does not anticipate policy actions that may be under evaluation. Undoubtedly, once extraordinary decisions have been taken, within our framework of transparency, the Central Bank will give a public account of the reason for these measures. Moreover, we will evaluate its effectiveness on an ongoing basis, as we have done in previous situations . In this presentation, I will first review our monetary and exchange rate policy framework. Next, I will refer to the global trends of the dollar and argue that it is necessary to put recent events in a global perspective, to later analyze the current exchange rate situation and policy options. Exchange rate policy in the inflation targeting scheme After experimenting with various macroeconomic management schemes in the last forty years, we have adopted a flexible inflation targeting scheme to guide monetary policy and an exchange rate floating policy in which the Central Bank reserves the right to intervene in exceptional situations. In this scheme, our inflation target is to be around 3% most of the time, with a tolerance range of plus/minus 1 percentage point. As inflation is controllable with lag and it is also necessary to take into account how measures aimed at stabilizing inflation affect growth2, our operational objective is to ensure that the two-year inflation projection is at around 3%. Thus, it is clear that our scheme does not ignore the global economic context, paying attention to variables such as the level of activity, the exchange rate or politics. 2 Jos8e De Gregorio (2006), "Inflation Target Scheme in Emerging Economies", Economic Policy Document, No. 18, Central Bank of Chile. fiscal. But what orders decision-making are the prospects for future inflation, with the understanding that with this the economy will be located around its levels of full employment, with stable inflation and with exchange rates and interest rates that will be around the values determined by their long-term fundamentals. The developed world has been more stable in terms of inflation and the business cycle since the mid-eighties, a trend known as the "Great Moderation". Something similar has happened with emerging economies since the second half of the nineties. There are multiple explanations for this moderation, but the successful conduct of monetary policy in a credible manner consistent with price stability has undoubtedly played a major role and is now a guarantee of resilience to international turbulence. There are many reasons why a floating exchange rate scheme is best suited for our economy. The floating exchange rate gives the economy flexibility to adjust to sudden changes in external conditions, mitigating the effects on employment and output. In particular, floating exchange rates facilitate adjustment to fluctuations in international financial conditions, and certainly avoids aggravating the effects of these conditions. Finally, a credible flexible exchange rate regime creates greater incentives for the private sector to reduce its exposure to foreign exchange risk. It is enough to remember that the crises in our country have traditionally been associated with exchange rate rigidities in the last fifty years. A floating regime is likely to bring greater exchange rate volatility and uncertainty, at least over short horizons. However, these costs are not enough to offset the aforementioned benefits of floating. Moreover, a foreign exchange insurance market has been developed that, although it does not allow to ensure profitability, allows to reduce the costs of volatility. At present, the amount of foreign exchange insurance contracts is 638 billion dollars, compared to 140 billion dollars in 2000. The spot market has deepened. Daily transactions went from 1 billion in 1999 to 2.9 billion in 2007. Meanwhile, the average daily derivative transaction in the market, which was only 502 million in 1999, reached 2.285 billion in 2007. Obviously, higher amounts traded are not directly related to the exchange situation, revealing rather the deepening and development of our financial markets. In any case, as we have pointed out on multiple occasions, floating exchange rates are the norm but it is not a dogma: it admits exchange rate intervention in exceptional cases, as we did in 2001 and 2002. The measures are determined on a case-by-case basis, but they have in common the well-founded perception that there is significant exchange rate misalignment, which is considered harmful, coupled with the well-founded presumption that intervention could have a stabilizing effect. Let me now explain how the exchange rate is incorporated into our inflation targeting scheme, directly and without euphemisms. When the Central Bank raises the interest rate to ensure that inflation converges to its target, it operates through Two mechanisms. Higher interest rates reduce demand for local goods, particularly investment and consumption of durable goods, putting pressure on a lower level of activity, which moderates price increases. In an open economy, the exchange rate is the second adjustment mechanism. When the Central Bank raises the rate unexpectedly, the exchange rate appreciates. This has a direct effect on the inflation of tradable goods and also contributes, together with the increase in rates, to reduce the demand for domestic goods, and thus to control inflation. Hypothetically speaking, what would happen in this context if the exchange rate effect of a rate hike could be eliminated? In this case, rate movements should be more abrupt and the adjustment would occur only through less economic activity, making it much more expensive to control inflation. On the other hand, if the exchange rate appreciates due to changes in external conditions, such as a fall in international interest rates or an increase in our terms of trade, the direct and indirect effects of this appreciation allow a less contractionary monetary policy to be exercised. In practice in recent months, this is exactly how we have taken into account exchange rate movements. In the monetary policy meetings of February and March, we considered that, if the real appreciation of the peso persists, it will reduce inflationary pressures, which we have communicated to the public and the markets in our statements and minutes. The Bank estimates that the real appreciation of the peso has effects on inflation in our policy horizon, and therefore the evolution of the exchange rate has taken pressure off rates. In other words, if the exchange rate had not appreciated as it has, interest rates today would most likely be much higher. The current reality of the dollar in international markets The problem of the dollar must be understood in a global context. To a large extent, what is happening in Chile is happening in the world as a whole. On the one hand, the weakness of the dollar is linked to the huge global imbalances observed in the world for several years. The United States has had an annual current account deficit of US638 trillion (5.4% of GDP) since 2002, which should sooner or later lead to a weakening of the dollar and a slowdown in its economy. We have repeatedly warned about this in our monetary policy and financial stability reports. On the other hand, the serious consequences of the mortgage crisis in the US have been added, which has probably acted as a trigger for this adjustment, but at the same time has revealed unsuspected weaknesses in the financial system of that country. We are witnessing, then, a combination between an adjustment that was seen coming and a conjunctural ingredient that has intensely accentuated the weakness of the dollar in international markets. The fall of the dollar is a worldwide phenomenon. Therefore, the appreciation of the peso against the dollar is greater than against other currencies. A few years ago (at its peak), the dollar traded at 0.83 per euro, and the peso/euro parity was 477. Today the dollar is trading at 1.6 per euro, and the peso/euro parity rises to 680. I understand that this argument It is not convincing for those who export in dollars and whose prices have not risen in this period. But, from the point of view of the global balance of our economy, it is necessary to consider the value of our currency with all our trading partners. While the peso has strengthened 10.9% against the dollar since January 2006, its multilateral appreciation is 2.1%. The local situation The Chilean peso is one of the currencies that have strengthened the most against the dollar this year. Therefore, it is incumbent upon us to analyze the set of factors that contribute to explaining the local strengthening of the dollar in multilateral and real terms. A first factor mentioned when analyzing the fall in the exchange rate is the higher interest rate differentials with the US. This has not happened only in Chile, but in most countries, since it is the Federal Reserve that has aggressively lowered its monetary policy rate, while the rest of the world has had minor changes. It is important to note that, in a floating scheme, an appreciation can be generated without the need for capital to enter. In fact, the antecedents of the financial account in our balance of payments do not show a massive inflow of capital that pressures the exchange rate, but, on the contrary, thanks to the fiscal rule, in the net our economy is exporting capital abroad. It is true that there may be arbitrage capital flows, but these are not of a magnitude that is clearly perceived in the external accounts, particularly in comparison with the substantial capital outflows and what was observed, in terms of portfolio flows, prior to the Asian crisis. The situation of our external accounts today differs markedly from the period prior to the Asian crisis, where a significant real appreciation was also observed. While in 1997 we saw capital inflows (excluding reserves) of US6,742 million (8.1% of GDP at the time), in a context of Intense accumulation of reserves of US3.3 billion, in 2007 there was an outflow of capital of US10.12 billion (6.1% of GDP). If we look at portfolio capital inflows3, in 1997 they entered US 2,600 million, while in 2007 US 400 million left. It is not evident that the most recent swings in these positions cause significant movements in the exchange rate beyond changes in the interest rate differential. A circumstance where we could observe speculative pressures would be in the event that we had tried to graduate the appreciation of the exchange rate. We have witnessed in Chile and many other emerging economies how these attempts invite speculation and capital inflows. In a floating exchange rate scheme, precisely the fall in the exchange rate reduces the incentives for international interest rate arbitrage. Another important factor in the evolution of the peso/dollar parity is the high price of copper. The Chilean economy has had a significant gain in terms of trade, which puts downward pressure on the exchange rate because the economy is able to sustain higher levels of spending in the long term without facing external difficulties. Notwithstanding the above, the fall in the exchange rate could be greater than that which could explain the evolution of its fundamentals, so we cannot rule out at this juncture that the peso is overappreciated. However, due to the unusual degree of uncertainty and volatility at the global level, it is difficult to make this assessment with certainty. For example, the weakening of the US dollar in real terms could be persistent. We cannot yet know to what extent nominal exchange rate appreciation is nothing more than a compensating effect of the higher dollar inflation that is being felt in the world, and which is likely to increase. We have seen how the depreciation of the dollar has made it possible to mitigate the effects on the price of fuel and food prices in pesos. Had this appreciation not occurred, we would be facing higher prices. Something more unusual is that throughout our history the peso has depreciated in periods of international financial turbulence, an aspect that has not occurred today. One possible explanation is that d0 relatively speaking d0 we have become a low-risk market for international investments. Chile has a solid fiscal position, a robust financial system and no direct exposure to the subprime mortgage market, and is part of the group of emerging commodity-producing economies that for now seem to have decoupled from external difficulties. Moreover, we have substantially improved our external debt situation. Just a few years ago we were indebted for about 50% of our GDP. Today we are practically net creditors. That increases the attractiveness of our economy at times like the present. If in this inflationary situation with global slowdown we were depreciating, it would be a reflection of serious problems. The challenges of monetary policy Today we face an unprecedented challenge, which directly affects all Chilean families, which is inflation. We cannot give in our effort to bring inflation to its target, because not doing so would make it more costly to control in the future, which would have even more intense effects on economic activity, the exchange rate and access to financing by companies and families. We have been and will continue to be very attentive to the evolution of the exchange rate, which is a relevant factor for our monetary policy decisions. We cannot rule out intervention in the foreign exchange market to the extent that we see a misalignment that threatens the stability of the economy, and to the extent that we have the presumption that the intervention will be effective. This cannot be a hasty decision. We know of many experiences of unsustainable interventions that fueled speculation and defeated themselves. In Latin America we have seen a group of countries that have been intervening for some time and have not escaped the appreciation of their currencies, even with high interest rate levels. Acting at inappropriate times or in contradiction with the rest of the policy objectives can cause effects contrary to those desired. This is why it is necessary to be very careful when evaluating the convenience and appropriateness of a foreign exchange intervention. The Central Bank may apply capital controls, as is the case with respect to international exchange operations from abroad whose remittance is made after such a measure. Even this can be applied under certain conditions according to our FTA with the United States. The reserve requirement is not applicable to international foreign exchange operations carried out by Pension Funds. The very principle of non-retroactivity contained in the law, prevents the application reserve requirements for capital returns originated in operations already carried out abroad by persons domiciled or resident in Chile. As a whole, this leads to significant funds of Chileans invested abroad, exceeding US130 billion, to which in no case would reserve requirements be applied, significantly reducing the potential effectiveness of a measure like this. In addition, the evidence regarding reserve requirements reveals that it segments access to external credit. While large companies, which obtain long-term financing, could continue to benefit from reduced interest rates internationally, small companies that finance themselves for short terms would see their financing cost rise significantly. We have observed in the most recent that a number of economies have imposed some degrees of controls on capital flows, which has not prevented their currencies from appreciating and from having high interest rates. Our own experience of the nineties shows how, despite imposing capital controls, the exchange rate appreciated significantly. The only economies that have been successful are those that have widespread controls or are excluded from international financial markets. Finally, we must remember that the context in which lace was applied in the nineties was very different from today. There was a massive net inflow of capital, an overheated economy and interest rates much higher than today. We know that we will be under a lot of pressure. There will be those who ask us to intervene, or adjust our monetary policy in one direction or another. Many of these pressures will originate from the expression of legitimate concerns on the part of those sectors that have seen their prices fall in pesos. But it is in this aspect where the legitimacy of the autonomy that the Constitution gives to the Central Bank of Chile takes on particular importance and value. In a context where our legal mandate is to ensure price and financial stability, which must take into account the general orientation of the Government's economic policy, we will act accordingly. We must evaluate and take the decisions that are, in our opinion, the most consistent with these objectives. I want to point out in this Honorable Chamber of Deputies that we act with the conviction that we are making the best decisions to give stability to our economy and expand its spaces for growth. If our decisions have costs in the short term, it is because we act with the certainty that in return they will bring enormous benefits in the long term. It is not a stubbornness or a blind attitude. Nor does it mean that in the Bank we do not have discussions and analyses from different perspectives and with different, and very legitimate, judgments. Nor does it mean that we act on the basis of dogmas or rigid doctrines. We are not ignorant of the problems. On the contrary, we are continuously and carefully monitoring the situation, and incorporating it into our monetary policy decisions. That we do not act directly in the foreign exchange market or in the capital account does not mean that we are not attentive. Failure to act is a policy decision that is justified at the current juncture and that may change as local and global economic conditions evolve. Given the current instability and uncertainty to At the global level, we must avoid falling into the temptation of acting hastily and inopportunely. We must explain to the country how we are fulfilling our mandate. Therefore, I believe that this has been a great opportunity to come and raise our vision on the exchange rate issue with a high vision. Something that certainly occupies and will continue to occupy an important place in our agenda. I would therefore like to reiterate my thanks to the Chamber of Deputies for allowing me to present our proposals here. As I said, the seriousness in the management of monetary policy and its formulation on solid technical bases by an autonomous body such as the Central Bank is a relevant factor to ensure stability and growth prospects for our economy. That also applies, of course, to the decisions we take on the exchange rate. We understand the concern of some sectors, but we have an obligation to look at all the variables. We act on that basis and I assure you that we put all our effort into it, to comply with what the law commands us . Thanks a lot.

Antes de continuar, es importante destacar que las polticas cambiarias y monetarias tienen efectos relevantes sobre los mercados financieros. Es por ello que los bancos centrales, en situaciones normales, actuamos de manera gradual y previsible. Hemos aprendido, por ejemplo, que es preferible mover la tasa de inters gradualmente para reducir la volatilidad del costo financiero de empresas y personas. Ms an, evaluaremos su efectividad en forma permanente, tal como lo hemos hecho en situaciones previas. En esta presentacin resear, en primer lugar, nuestro marco de polticas monetaria y cambiaria. A continuacin me referir a las tendencias globales del dlar y plantear que es necesario poner los eventos recientes en una perspectiva global, para posteriormente analizar la actual coyuntura cambiaria y las opciones de poltica. La poltica cambiaria en el esquema de metas de inflacin Luego de experimentar con variados esquemas de manejo macroeconmico en los ltimos cuarenta aos, hemos adoptado un esquema de metas de inflacin flexible para guiar la poltica monetaria y una poltica de flotacin del tipo de cambio en la que el Banco Central se reserva el derecho a intervenir ante situaciones excepcionales. As, es evidente que nuestro esquema no ignora el contexto econmico global, prestando atencin a variables como el nivel de actividad, el tipo de cambio o la poltica 2 Jos De Gregorio (2006), Esquema de Metas de Inflacin em Economias Emergentes, Documento de Poltica Econmica, N18, Banco Central de Chile. fiscal. Pero lo que ordena la toma de decisiones son las perspectivas de inflacin a futuro, en el entendido de que con ello la economa se ubicar en torno a sus niveles de pleno empleo, con una inflacin estable y con tipos de cambio y tasas de inters que estarn en torno a los valores determinados por sus fundamentos de largo plazo. Hay mltiples explicaciones para esta moderacin, pero la exitosa conduccin de la poltica monetaria de manera creble y coherente con la estabilidad de precios sin duda ha desempeado un papel preponderante y es hoy da garanta de resiliencia frente a las turbulencias internacionales. Existen muchas razones por las cuales un esquema de flotacin cambiaria es el ms adecuado para nuestra economa. La flotacin cambiaria le da a la economa flexibilidad para que se ajuste a cambios bruscos en las condiciones externas, atenuando los efectos en el empleo y el producto. En particular, la flotacin cambiaria facilita el ajuste a fluctuaciones de las condiciones financieras internacionales, y sin duda evita agravar los efectos de estas. Por ltimo, un rgimen de tipo de cambio flexible creble genera mayores incentivos al sector privado para reducir su exposicin al riesgo cambiario. Basta recordar que las crisis en nuestro pas han estado tradicionalmente asociadas a rigideces cambiarias en los ltimos cincuenta aos. Es posible que un rgimen de flotacin traiga consigo una mayor volatilidad e incertidumbre cambiaria, al menos a horizontes cortos. Sin embargo, estos costos no alcanzan a contrarrestar los beneficios ya mencionados de la flotacin. Ms aun, se ha desarrollado un mercado de seguros de cambio que, si bien no permite asegurar rentabilidad, permiten reducir los costos de la volatilidad. En la actualidad el monto de contratos de seguros cambiarios es 638 mil millones de dlares, mientras que en 2000 era de 140 mil millones de dlares. El mercado spot se ha profundizado. Las transacciones diarias pasaron de mil millones de dlares en 1999 a 2.900 millones de dlares en 2007. Mientras, el monto de transacciones diarias promedio de derivados en el mercado, que era de slo 502 millones de dlares en 1999, en 2007 alcanz los 2.285 millones de dlares. Evidentemente, mayores montos transados no tienen relacin directa con la situacin cambiaria, revelando ms bien la profundizacin y desarrollo de nuestros mercados financieros. En todo caso, como hemos sealado en mltiples oportunidades, la flotacin cambiaria es la norma pero no es un dogma: admite intervencin cambiaria en casos excepcionales, tal como lo hicimos en 2001 y 2002. Las medidas se determinan caso a caso, pero tienen en comn la percepcin fundada de que existe un desalineamiento cambiario significativo, que se considera daino, unida a la presuncin tambin fundada de que la accin de intervenir podra tener un efecto estabilizador. Permtanme ahora explicar cmo se incorpora el tipo de cambio en nuestro esquema de metas de inflacin, de manera directa y sin eufemismos. Cuando el Banco Central sube la tasa de inters para asegurar que la inflacin converja a su meta, esta opera a travs de dos mecanismos. El alza de tasas de inters reduce la demanda por bienes locales, en particular la inversin y el consumo de bienes durables, presionando a un menor nivel de actividad, el cual modera los aumentos de precios. En una economa abierta, el tipo de cambio es el segundo mecanismo de ajuste. Cuando el Banco Central sube la tasa en forma inesperada, el tipo de cambio se aprecia. Esto tiene un efecto directo sobre la inflacin de los bienes transables y adems contribuye, junto al alza de tasas, a reducir la demanda por bienes nacionales, y con ello a controlar la inflacin. Hablando en forma hipottica, Qu ocurrira en este contexto si se pudiera eliminar el efecto cambiario de un alza de tasa? En tal caso los movimientos de tasas deberan ser ms bruscos y el ajuste ocurrira nicamente por la va de menor actividad econmica, haciendo mucho ms costoso el control de la inflacin. Por otra parte, si el tipo de cambio se aprecia debido a cambios en las condiciones externas, como por ejemplo una cada en las tasas de inters internacionales o un aumento de nuestros trminos de intercambio, los efectos directos e indirectos de esta apreciacin permiten ejercer una poltica monetaria menos contractiva. En la prctica de los ltimos meses, es exactamente as como hemos tomado en cuenta los movimientos cambiarios. En las reuniones de poltica monetaria de febrero y marzo hemos considerado que, de persistir la apreciacin real del peso, esta reducir las presiones inflacionarias, lo que hemos comunicado al pblico y a los mercados en nuestros comunicados y minutas. El Banco estima que la apreciacin real del peso tiene efectos sobre la inflacin en nuestro horizonte de poltica, y por ello la evolucin del tipo de cambio ha quitado presin sobre las tasas. Dicho de otro modo, si el tipo de cambio no se hubiera apreciado como lo ha hecho, lo ms probable es que las tasas de inters hoy da seran mucho ms altas. La realidad actual del dlar en los mercados internacionales El problema del dlar hay que entenderlo en un contexto global. En buena medida, lo que est ocurriendo en Chile est ocurriendo en el mundo como un todo. Por un lado, la debilidad del dlar se vincula con los enormes desbalances globales observados en el mundo por varios aos. Estados Unidos ha tenido en promedio anual un dficit en su cuenta corriente de US$638 billones (5,4% del PIB) desde el ao 2002, lo que tena que producir, tarde o temprano, un debilitamiento del dlar y una desaceleracin de su economa. Esto lo hemos advertido en reiteradas ocasiones en nuestros informes de poltica monetaria y de estabilidad financiera. Por otro lado, se han agregado las graves consecuencias de la crisis hipotecaria en EE.UU., que probablemente ha actuado como gatillo de este ajuste, pero a la vez ha revelado debilidades insospechadas en el sistema financiero de ese pas. Estamos en presencia, entonces, de una combinacin entre un ajuste que se vea venir y un ingrediente coyuntural que ha acentuado intensamente la debilidad del dlar en los mercados internacionales. La cada del dlar es un fenmeno mundial. Por ello, la apreciacin del peso respecto del dlar es mayor que respecto de otras monedas. Hace unos aos (en su peak), el dlar lleg a cotizarse a 0,83 por euro, y la paridad peso/euro era de 477. Hoy da el dlar se cotiza a 1,6 por euro, y la paridad peso/euro se eleva a 680. Entiendo que este argumento no es convincente para quienes exportan en dlares y cuyos precios no han subido en este perodo. Pero, desde el punto de vista del equilibrio global de nuestra economa, es necesario considerar el valor de nuestra moneda con todos nuestros socios comerciales. Mientras el peso se ha fortalecido un 10,9% respecto del dlar desde enero del 2006, su apreciacin multilateral es de 2,1%. La coyuntura local El peso chileno es una de las monedas que ms se han fortalecido respecto del dlar durante este ao. Por lo tanto, nos corresponde analizar el conjunto de factores que contribuyen a explicar el fortalecimiento local del dlar en trminos multilaterales y reales. Un primer factor que se menciona al analizar la cada del tipo de cambio son los mayores diferenciales de tasas de inters con EE.UU. Esto no ha ocurrido slo en Chile, sino que en la mayora de los pases, pues es la Reserva Federal la que ha bajado en forma agresiva su tasa de poltica monetaria, mientras el resto del mundo ha tenido cambios de menor envergadura. Es importante sealar que, en un esquema de flotacin, se puede generar una apreciacin sin necesidad de que ingresen capitales. De hecho, los antecedentes de la cuenta financiera en nuestra balanza de pagos no muestran una entrada masiva de capitales que presione el tipo de cambio, sino, por el contrario, gracias a la regla fiscal, en el neto nuestra economa est exportando capitales al exterior. Es cierto que puede haber flujos de capitales de arbitraje, pero estos no son de una magnitud que se perciba claramente en las cuentas externas, particularmente en comparacin con los sustanciales flujos de salida de capitales y con lo que se observ, en trminos de flujos de portafolio, previo a la crisis asitica. La situacin de nuestras cuentas externas difiere hoy marcadamente del perodo previo a la crisis asitica, donde tambin se observ una apreciacin real relevante. Mientras en 1997 vimos entradas de capitales (excluyendo reservas) por US$6.742 millones (8,1% del PIB de la poca), en un contexto de acumulacin intensa de reservas por US$3.300 millones, en el ao 2007 se produjo una salida de capitales por US$10.120 millones (6,1% del PIB). Si observamos las entradas de capitales de portafolio3, en 1997 entraron US$2.600 millones, mientras que en 2007 salieron US$400 millones. Tasas de Poltica Monetaria Esperadas en Chile y EE.UU. En la actualidad, efectivamente es posible tomar posiciones en pesos chilenos sin necesidad de entradas de capitales, sino que a travs de instrumentos derivados. No es evidente que los vaivenes ms recientes de estas posiciones sean causa de movimientos importantes en el tipo de cambio ms all de los cambios en el diferencial de tasas de inters. Una circunstancia donde podramos observar presiones especulativas sera en el caso de que hubisemos intentado graduar la apreciacin del tipo de cambio. Hemos sido testigos en Chile y en muchas otras economas emergentes cmo estos intentos invitan a la especulacin y a la entrada de capitales. En un esquema de flotacin cambiaria, precisamente la cada del tipo de cambio reduce los incentivos al arbitraje internacional de tasas de inters. Otro factor importante en la evolucin de la paridad peso/dlar es el elevado precio del cobre. La economa chilena ha tenido una importante ganancia de trminos de intercambio, lo que presiona a la baja del tipo de cambio pues la economa es capaz de sostener en el largo plazo mayores niveles de gasto sin enfrentar dificultades externas. Dada la regla fiscal, las ganancias que se estiman transitorias se estn ahorrando ntegramente en el exterior, lo que ha evitado una apreciacin aun mayor. 3 Las que incluyen la colocacin de bonos en el exterior, los flujos asociados a fondos de inversin de capital extranjero y los asociados a ADR. No obstante lo anterior, la cada del tipo de cambio podra ser mayor que la que pudieran explicar la evolucin de sus fundamentales, por lo que no podemos descartar en esta coyuntura que el peso est sobreapreciado. Sin embargo, debido al inusual grado de incertidumbre y volatilidad a nivel global, es difcil hacer esta evaluacin con certeza. Por ejemplo, el debilitamiento del dlar norteamericano en trminos reales podra ser persistente. No podemos saber an hasta qu punto la apreciacin cambiaria nominal no es ms que un efecto compensador de la mayor inflacin en dlares que se est dejando sentir en el mundo, y que probablemente recrudezca. Hemos visto cmo la depreciacin del dlar ha permitido mitigar los efectos sobre la cotizacin de los precios de combustibles y alimentos en pesos. De no haber ocurrido esta apreciacin estaramos enfrentando precios ms altos. Algo ms inusual es que a lo largo de nuestra historia el peso se ha depreciado en perodos de turbulencia financiera internacional, aspecto que hoy no se ha dado. Una posible explicacin es que en trminos relativos nos hemos vuelto un mercado de poco riesgo para las inversiones internacionales. Chile tiene una situacin fiscal slida, un sistema financiero robusto y sin exposicin directa al mercado hipotecario subprime, y es parte del conjunto de economas emergentes productoras de bienes bsicos que por ahora parecen haberse desacoplado de las dificultades externas. Ms an, hemos mejorado sustancialmente nuestra situacin deudora con el exterior. Hace apenas unos aos ramos deudores por cerca del 50% de nuestro PIB. Hoy somos prcticamente acreedores netos. Eso aumenta el atractivo de nuestra economa en momentos como el actual. Si en esta coyuntura inflacionaria con desaceleracin mundial nos estuviramos depreciando sera un reflejo de problemas serios.
