Los desafos de la poltica monetaria Hoy da enfrentamos un desafo indito, que afecta directamente a todas las familias chilenas, que es la inflacin. No podemos ceder en nuestro esfuerzo de hacer converger la inflacin a su meta, pues no hacerlo hara ms costoso su control en el futuro, lo que tendra efectos aun ms intensos en la actividad econmica, el tipo de cambio y el acceso al financiamiento por parte de empresas y familias. Hemos estado y seguiremos estando muy atentos a la evolucin del tipo de cambio, el cual es un factor relevante para nuestras decisiones de poltica monetaria. No podemos descartar una intervencin en el mercado cambiario en la medida en que veamos un desalineamiento que amenace la estabilidad de la economa, y en la medida que tengamos la presuncin de que la intervencin ser efectiva. Esta no puede ser una decisin apresurada. Conocemos muchas experiencias de intervenciones insostenibles que alimentaron la especulacin y se derrotaron a s mismas. En Amrica Latina hemos visto un conjunto de pases que ya llevan un tiempo interviniendo y no se han escapado de la apreciacin de sus monedas, incluso con niveles de tasas de inters elevadas. Actuar en momentos inadecuados o en contradiccin con el resto de los objetivos de poltica puede provocar efectos contrarios a los deseados. Por esto es necesario ser muy cuidadosos al momento de evaluar la conveniencia y la oportunidad de una intervencin cambiaria. El Banco Central puede aplicar controles de capital, como es el caso del encaje respecto de las operaciones de cambios internacionales provenientes del exterior cuya remesa se efecte con posterioridad a dicha medida. Incluso este se puede aplicar bajo ciertas condiciones de acuerdo a nuestro TLC con los Estados Unidos. El encaje no es aplicable a las operaciones de cambios internacionales que efecten los Fondos de Pensiones. El mismo principio de irretroactividad contenido en la ley, impide la aplicacin de encaje a los retornos de capitales originados en operaciones ya realizadas en el exterior por personas domiciliadas o residentes en Chile. En su conjunto, esto lleva a que existan fondos significativos de chilenos invertidos en el exterior, superiores a los US$130 mil millones, a los que en ningn caso se les aplicara encaje, reduciendo de manera importante la potencial efectividad de una medida como sta. Adicionalmente, la evidencia respecto del encaje revela que ste segmenta el acceso al crdito externo. Mientras las empresas grandes, que logran financiamiento a plazos largos, podran seguir beneficindose de tasas de inters reducidas a nivel internacional, las empresas pequeas que se financian a plazos cortos veran su costo de financiamiento subir de manera relevante. Hemos observado en lo ms reciente que un nmero de economas han impuesto ciertos grados de controles a los flujos de capitales, lo que no ha evitado que sus monedas se aprecien, y que tengan tasas de inters elevadas. Nuestra propia experiencia de los aos noventa muestra como, a pesar de imponer controles de capitales, el tipo de cambio se apreci de manera significativa. Las nicas economas que han tenido xito, son la que cuentan con controles generalizados o estn excluidas de los mercados financieros internacionales. Por ultimo, debemos recordar que el contexto en el que se aplico el encaje en los noventa fue muy distinto al actual. Haba una entrada neta masiva de capitales, una economia sobrecalentada y tasas de interes muy superiores a las actuales. Sabemos que estaremos sometidos a muchas presiones. Habr quienes nos pidan intervenir, o ajustar en una u otra direccin nuestra poltica monetaria. Muchas de esas presiones se originarn expresando legtimas preocupaciones por parte de aquellos sectores que han visto caer sus precios en pesos. Pero es en este aspecto donde la legitimidad de la autonoma que le da la Constitucin al Banco Central de Chile cobra particular importancia y valor. En un contexto donde nuestro mandato legal es velar por la estabilidad de precios y financiera, que debe tener presente la orientacin general de la poltica econmica del Gobierno, actuaremos de acuerdo a ello. Debemos evaluar y tomar las decisiones que sean, a nuestro juicio, las ms coherentes con estos objetivos. Quiero sealar en esta Honorable Cmara de Diputados que actuamos con la conviccin de que estamos tomando las mejores decisiones para darle estabilidad a nuestra economa y ampliar sus espacios de crecimiento. Si nuestras decisiones tienen costos en el corto plazo, es porque actuamos con la certeza de que a cambio traern enormes beneficios en el largo plazo. No es una obcecacin ni una actitud ciega. No significa tampoco que en el Banco no tengamos discusiones y anlisis desde distintas pticas y con diversos, y muy legtimos, juicios. Tampoco significa que actuemos sobre la base de dogmas o doctrinas rgidas. No ignoramos los problemas. Por el contrario, estamos monitoreando de forma continua y cuidadosa la situacin, y la incorporamos en nuestras decisiones de poltica monetaria. Que no actuemos directamente en el mercado cambiario o en la cuenta de capitales no significa que no estemos atentos. No actuar es una decisin de poltica que se justifica en la coyuntura actual y que puede cambiar segn vayan evolucionando las condiciones econmicas locales y globales. Dada la actual inestabilidad e incertidumbre a nivel global, tenemos que evitar caer en la tentacin de actuar de forma apresurada e inoportuna. Debemos explicarle al pas cmo estamos cumpliendo nuestro mandato. Por ello, estimo que esta ha sido una gran oportunidad para venir a plantear con altura de miras nuestra visin sobre el tema cambiario. Algo que ciertamente ocupa y seguir ocupando un lugar importante en nuestra agenda. Reitero entonces mi agradecimiento a la Cmara de Diputados por permitirme exponer aqu nuestros planteamientos. Como dije, la seriedad en el manejo de la poltica monetaria y su formulacin sobre slidas bases tcnicas por un organismo autnomo como el Banco Central es un factor relevante para asegurar estabilidad y perspectivas de crecimiento para nuestra economa. Ello se aplica tambin, desde luego, a las decisiones que adoptemos en materia de tipo de cambio. Entendemos la preocupacin de algunos sectores, pero tenemos la obligacin de mirar el conjunto de las variables. Actuamos sobre esa base y les aseguro que ponemos todo nuestro esfuerzo en ello, para cumplir con lo que nos manda la ley. Muchas gracias.

Title: Recent Policy Developments and Decisions in the Chilean Economy
text: Recent Policy Developments and Decisions in the Chilean Economy Jos8e de Gregorio*President Central Bank of ChileApril 2008 I appreciate the invitation of the Chilean-American Chamber of Commerce to speak about the situation and prospects of the Chilean economy. The past week has been full of news, and to inform not only here, but also in Chile, of the logic of the decisions we have adopted and how they are framed in our monetary policy scheme, I have decided to write this presentation in our language and I will try to do my best when translating the presentation into English. The Chilean economy is going through a complex situation. The Central Bank of Chile organizes its monetary policy with an inflationary objective that aims to ensure that inflation measured in twelve months is most of the time at 3% with a tolerance margin of /- 1 percentage point. In 2007 inflation rose significantly, closing the year and beginning this with records close to 8%. Private expectations for domestic growth have tended to adjust downwards, while we continue to face an extraordinarily uncertain external scenario. The increase in inflation was mainly due to higher international food and fuel prices, aggravated by weather problems that increased the price of perishable food. We take into account that a good part of these phenomena is beyond the control of monetary policy. More precisely, we recognize that while changes in relative prices must materialize, our responsibility is that they do not lead to more persistent inflationary consequences. That is why the Central Bank has defined a two-year horizon for inflation to return to the target. This is done firstly because monetary policy is lagging, secondly because transitory inflationary shocks are allowed to unravel without the need to tighten monetary policy, and thirdly because the costs in terms of activity of keeping inflation stable are recognized. It is for this last aspect that it is misleading to say that because we have inflation targets, the only variable that we analyze when making decisions is current inflation, since in our scheme all the antecedents enter into the evaluation of future inflationary dynamics. In this way, a credible inflationary commitment scheme allows not only price stability but also stabilizes the economic cycle, reducing the social costs of adjustments. That is why yielding to inflation, compromising the credibility that has taken many years to build, may have some short-term benefits but a considerable future cost in terms of activity and stability. Presentado a la Chilean-American Chamber of Commerce. Washington D.C., 14 de abril, 2008. Macroeconomic. It would then be irresponsible to compromise stability in order to weather short-term pressures. But at the same time we must use our instruments with the flexibility that is required when dealing with highly complex scenarios. And that's what we're doing. We are aware that several of these arguments have been mentioned before. However, we believe that we must strive to clearly convey our points, reiterating our mission and objectives, so that they are not misinterpreted or misunderstood. From July of last year, until January of this year, the monetary policy rate has increased from 5% to 6.25% to avoid that the persistent increases in food and fuel prices do not generate unwanted dynamics that could cause a de-anchoring of expectations and a persistence of inflations outside the target beyond the policy horizon. To make these decisions you look at a set of indicators, all of which affect inflation. This is how the fact that the outlook for activity has weakened in recent months and the exchange rate has appreciated. All this should lead to lower future inflationary tensions, taking pressure off monetary policy. In other words, if activity has not weakened and the exchange rate has not appreciated, the interest rate today should be higher. Recent inflation news, although still high, suggests that inflationary spread is not unusual or excessive, and is consistent with the convergence of inflation to 3 percent over the policy horizon. This has made it possible to remove the bias on the interest rate, which until last month was positive. That is, with the information available at the beginning of last March, it was estimated that in the most likely scenario the next movement would be upward. The market had already anticipated that the intensity of the bias in March had reduced from the previous meeting. With the latest information available, our assessment is that it is equally likely that in the future the rate will increase or decrease. In this context, it is relevant to note that the recent decisions of the Bank Board do not rule out future increases in the policy rate, but it is equally likely that reductions may occur. The elements that could influence upward decisions in the monetary policy rate are linked to preventive actions against new shocks of higher international food prices, which continue to show very significant volatility. On the other hand, the enormous uncertainty regarding the evolution of external conditions has a fairly strong bias towards scenarios of weaker future growth, which if materialized would detract from the underlying trend of inflation. Special mention should be made of the evolution of the exchange rate, which also suggests relatively significant disinflationary pressures. The peso, like the vast majority of the world's currencies, has appreciated against the US dollar. The sustainability of the significant US current account deficit, coupled with the Fed's aggressive interest rate cuts in recent months, have weakened the dollar and strengthened the currencies of the rest of the world. Likewise, another important factor in Chile has been the increase in the price of copper to levels that constitute historical records. However, the evidence shows that in Chile this appreciation has been mitigated in part by the operation of fiscal policy, which saves abroad the transitory component of these greater increases associated with the high price of copper. Likewise, a flexible exchange rate policy that does not encourage speculative positions, within the framework of an inflation-targeting scheme, also mitigates sustained deviations from the exchange rate. Still, the peso's appreciation has been severe and unexpected. In fact, according to various estimates, its level is today below what is estimated to be its long-term levels, that is, once its fundamental determinants such as, for example, the price of copper, return to more coherent values their long-term equilibrium. Although it is possible to find reasons that explain its evolution, such as the widening of the interest rate differential, the Central Bank Council has not ruled out the possibility that the value of the peso has suffered an overreaction. Nor can it be ruled out that in the current international scenario there will be a sharp correction in commodity prices, with complex consequences on inflation and the normal development of the Chilean economy. Given the current external uncertainties and the low price of the currency, the Council considered it prudent to initiate a programme to increase our international liquidity to cushion potential adverse external scenarios or situations of credit disruption in international markets. This program contemplates an increase of the order of 50% of the current stock of net international reserves within eight months. The form of intervention in the foreign exchange market follows the commitment made by the Central Bank when the float began in 1999 and is the most coherent way of intervening in the context of the inflation targeting scheme with a flexible exchange rate. This is not very different from the modality adopted when we decumulated reserves in 2001 and 2002. That is, it is an exceptional measure that is carried out by announcing a deadline, a total amount for the intervention, and how it is programmed in time. In this way there is an explicit commitment not to pretend to fix a value, or range, for the exchange rate, thus reducing the space for speculation. We have seen in many experiences that when interventions pursue specific values, or the authority systematically tries to surprise the market, as well as to have incompatible objectives, massive capital inflows are encouraged to speculate, putting more pressure on the strengthening of the currency. These capital inflows in turn are combated with capital controls, entering a vicious circle of controls, intervention and speculation. In our scheme, the exchange rate continues to be determined by the market, with a new, and massive, source of demand by the Central Bank. We are aware that this is an exceptional decision, determined by the unusual degrees of external uncertainty. We are also aware of the importance of exchange rate policy being conducted in a manner consistent with monetary policy. On the one hand, it is our norm to compensate for any monetary effect of the accumulation of reserves so as not to affect the implementation of monetary policy. On the other hand, we know of the speculative consequences that occur when monetary policy and reserve management collide with each other. Accumulating reserves at a time when a significant increase in interest rates is expected to be inconsistent and ineffective. Venture capitalists can make huge profits when policymakers commit to goals that are inconsistent with each other. We have witnessed many experiences in emerging economies trying to control the exchange rate in conjunction with increasingly restrictive monetary policies. In Chile we have not rushed to make exceptional decisions, nor have we incorporated an exchange rate target into our policy, which is manifested in the use of a simple rule of accumulation. We have also waited for some reassurance on inflation. The risks have not disappeared, and unfortunately the situation of the previous weeks limited our possibilities to continue waiting for the resolution of these uncertainties. However, recent developments in the macroeconomic environment have identified elements that could put downward pressure on inflation. That has allowed us to remove the bias and maintain the policy rate at our last meeting. Chile has never been better prepared to face an international crisis, but we cannot be complacent. The decision taken last week to accumulate in the next 8 months a total of 8 billion dollars in reserves to strengthen the international liquidity position of the Chilean economy is an investment in stability. It is desirable, as well as unlikely, that very serious events do not happen, but we want to minimize their potential impact should they occur. Inflation is still high, but our conclusion from yesterday's meeting was that maintaining the rate and removing bias was the right decision for convergence of inflation to its target over the policy horizon. This provides a framework of coherence between the PM and the accumulation of reserves, in addition to being an appropriate time to intervene in the foreign exchange market since the exchange rate is below what we estimate should be located in the long term. Given our unwavering commitment to price stability, what we are pointing out with this measure is that our inflation targeting scheme and the current monetary policy instance can accommodate a depreciation of the peso, something that a couple of months ago we could not have assured. In any case, the value of the dollar will continue to be set by the market and monetary policy will continue to be used flexibly to ensure compliance with our inflation target.
text_original: Desarrollos y Decisiones de Poltica Recientes en la Economa Chilena Jos De Gregorio* Presidente Banco Central de Chile Abril 2008 Agradezco la invitacin de la Chilean-American Chamber of Commerce para hablar sobre la coyuntura y perspectivas de la economa chilena. La semana pasada ha estado llena de novedades, y para informar no solo aqu, sino que tambin en Chile, de la lgica de las decisiones que hemos adoptado y como se enmarcan en nuestro esquema de poltica monetaria, es que he decidido escribir esta presentacin en nuestro idioma y tratar de hacer mi mejor esfuerzo al traducir la presentacin al ingls. La economa chilena atraviesa por una coyuntura compleja. El Banco Central de Chile organiza su poltica monetaria con un objetivo inflacionario que tiene como meta que la inflacin medida en doce meses se ubique la mayor parte del tiempo en 3% con un margen de tolerancia de +/- 1 punto porcentual. El ao 2007 la inflacin se elev de manera importante, cerrando el ao y comenzando este con registros cercanos al 8%. Las expectativas privadas de crecimiento domstico se han tendido a ajustar a la baja, mientras que continuamos enfrentando un escenario externo extraordinariamente incierto. El aumento de la inflacin se debi fundamentalmente al aumento de los precios internacionales de alimentos y combustibles, agravado por problemas climticos que aumentaron el precio de los alimentos perecibles. Tomamos en cuenta que buena parte de estos fenmenos est fuera del control de la poltica monetaria. Ms precisamente, reconocemos que aunque los cambios en precios relativos deben materializarse, nuestra responsabilidad es que ello no acarree consecuencias inflacionarias ms persistentes. Por eso el Banco Central ha definido un horizonte de dos aos para que la inflacin vuelva a la meta. Esto se hace en primer lugar porque la poltica monetaria acta con rezagos, en segundo lugar porque se permite que los shocks inflacionarios transitorios se deshagan sin necesidad de endurecer la poltica monetaria, y en tercer lugar porque se reconocen los costos en trminos de actividad de mantener la inflacin estable. Es por este ltimo aspecto que es equvoco decir que por tener metas de inflacin la nica variable que analizamos al tomar decisiones es la inflacin actual, puesto que en nuestro esquema todos los antecedentes entran en la evaluacin de las dinmicas inflacionarias a futuro. De esta forma, un esquema de compromiso inflacionario creble permite no slo tener estabilidad de precios sino que tambin estabiliza el ciclo econmico, reduciendo los costos sociales de los ajustes. Es por ello que ceder en la inflacin, comprometiendo la credibilidad que ha costado muchos aos construir, puede tener algunos beneficios de corto plazo pero un considerable costo futuro en trminos de actividad y estabilidad Presentado a la Chilean-American Chamber of Commerce. Washington D.C., 14 de abril, 2008. macroeconmica. Sera entonces una irresponsabilidad comprometer la estabilidad para capear presiones de corto plazo. Pero al mismo tiempo debemos usar nuestros instrumentos con la flexibilidad que se requiere a la hora de abordar escenarios altamente complejos. Y es eso lo que estamos haciendo. Estamos conscientes que varios de estos argumentos los hemos mencionado antes. Sin embargo, consideramos que debemos esforzamos por transmitir claramente nuestros puntos, reiterando nuestra misin y objetivos, de forma de que no sean malinterpretados o malentendidos. Desde julio del ao pasado, hasta enero de este ao, la tasa de poltica monetaria ha aumentado desde 5% a 6,25% para evitar que los persistentes aumentos de precios de alimentos y combustibles no generen dinmicas indeseadas que puedan provocar un desanclaje de expectativas y una persistencia de inflaciones fuera de la meta ms all del horizonte de poltica. Para tomar estas decisiones se mira un conjunto de indicadores, todos los cuales afectan la inflacin. Es as como se ha incorporado el hecho que las perspectivas de actividad se han debilitado en los ltimos meses y el tipo de cambio se ha apreciado. Todo ello debera generar menores tensiones inflacionarias futuras, quitando presin a la poltica monetaria. Dicho de otra forma, de no haberse debilitado la actividad ni apreciado el tipo de cambio, la tasa de inters hoy da debera ser ms elevada. Las noticias recientes en materia de inflacin, aunque con registros an elevados, sugieren que la propagacin inflacionaria no est siendo inusual o excesiva, y son coherentes con la convergencia de la inflacin a 3% dentro del horizonte de polticas. Esto ha permitido quitar el sesgo sobre la tasa de inters, el que hasta el mes pasado era positivo. Es decir, con la informacin disponible a principios de marzo pasado, se estimaba que en el escenario ms probable el siguiente movimiento sera al alza. El mercado ya haba anticipado que la intensidad del sesgo en marzo se haba reducido respecto de la reunin previa. Con la ltima informacin disponible, nuestra evaluacin es que es igualmente probable que en el futuro la tasa aumente o disminuya. En este contexto es relevante destacar que las recientes decisiones del Consejo del Banco no descartan aumentos futuros de la tasa de poltica, pero es igualmente probable que puedan ocurrir reducciones. Los elementos que podran incidir en decisiones al alza de la tasa de poltica monetaria se vinculan con acciones preventivas frente a nuevos embates de mayores precios internacionales de los alimentos, los que siguen mostrando una muy significativa volatilidad. Por otra parte, la enorme incertidumbre respecto de la evolucin de las condiciones externas tiene un sesgo bastante fuerte hacia escenarios de crecimiento futuro ms debilitado, los que de materializarse le quitaran fuerza a la tendencia subyacente de la inflacin. Mencin especial debe hacerse de la evolucin del tipo de cambio, la cual sugiere tambin presiones desinflacionarias relativamente importantes. El peso, al igual que la gran mayora de las monedas del mundo, se ha apreciado respecto del dlar norteamericano. La sostenibilidad del significativo dficit en cuenta corriente de los EE.UU., unido a la agresiva reduccin de la tasa de inters aplicada por la Fed en meses recientes, han debilitado el dlar y fortalecido las monedas del resto del mundo. Asimismo, otro factor importante en Chile ha sido el aumento del precio del cobre a niveles que constituyen rcords histricos. Con todo, la evidencia muestra que en Chile esta apreciacin ha sido mitigada en parte por la operacin de la poltica fiscal, que ahorra en el exterior el componente transitorio de estos mayores incrementos asociados al elevado precio del cobre. Asimismo, una poltica de tipo de cambio flexible que no alienta la toma de posiciones especulativas, en el marco de un esquema de metas de inflacin, mitiga tambin las desviaciones sostenidas del tipo de cambio. An as, la apreciacin del peso ha sido severa e inesperada. De hecho, de acuerdo a diversas estimaciones, su nivel est hoy da por debajo de lo que se estima son sus niveles de largo plazo, es decir, una vez que sus determinantes fundamentales como, por ejemplo, el precio del cobre, vuelvan a valores ms coherentes su equilibrio de largo plazo. Aunque es posible encontrar razones que expliquen su evolucin, como la ampliacin del diferencial de tasas de inters, el Consejo del Banco Central no ha descartado la posibilidad que el valor del peso haya sufrido una sobrerreaccin. Tampoco se puede descartar que en el actual escenario internacional se produzca una correccin brusca de los precios de commodities, con complejas consecuencias sobre la inflacin y el normal desenvolvimiento de la economa chilena. Dadas las actuales incertidumbres externas y el bajo precio de la divisa, el Consejo ha estimado prudente iniciar un programa de aumento de nuestra liquidez internacional que permita amortiguar potenciales escenarios externos adversos o situaciones de disrupcin del crdito en los mercados internacionales. Este programa contempla un aumento del orden de 50% del stock actual de reservas internacionales netas en un plazo de ocho meses. La forma de intervencin en el mercado cambiario sigue el compromiso adoptado por el Banco Central cuando se inici la flotacin en 1999 y es la forma ms coherente de intervenir en el contexto del esquema de metas de inflacin con tipo de cambio flexible. Esta no es muy distinta de la modalidad adoptada cuando desacumulamos reservas en los aos 2001 y 2002. Es decir, es una medida excepcional que se realiza anunciado un plazo, un monto total para la intervencin, y como se programa esta en el tiempo. De esta forma hay un compromiso explcito de no pretender fijar un valor, o rango, para el tipo de cambio, reduciendo as el espacio para la especulacin. Hemos visto en muchas experiencias que cuando las intervenciones persiguen valores especficos, o la autoridad intenta sorprender sistemticamente al mercado, as como tener objetivos incompatibles entre s, se incentivan masivas entradas de capitales a especular, presionando ms al fortalecimiento de la moneda. Estas entradas de capitales a su vez son combatidas con controles de capital, entrando en un crculo vicioso de controles, intervencin y especulacin. En nuestro esquema el tipo de cambio lo sigue determinando el mercado, con una nueva, y masiva, fuente de demanda por parte del Banco Central. Estamos concientes que esta es una decisin excepcional, determinada por los inusuales grados de incertidumbre externa. Tambin somos concientes de la importancia de que la poltica cambiara se conduzca de forma congruente con la poltica monetaria. Por un lado, es nuestra norma compensar todo efecto monetario de la acumulacin de reservas de forma de no afectar la implementacin de la poltica monetaria. Por otro lado, sabemos de las consecuencias especulativas que ocurren cuando la poltica monetaria y el manejo de reservas chocan entre s. Acumular reservas en un momento en el cual se prev un importante aumento de las tasas de inters es incoherente e inefectivo. Los inversionistas de riesgo pueden obtener enormes ganancias cuando las autoridades se comprometen con objetivos que son inconsistentes entre s. Hemos sido testigos en muchas experiencias en economas emergentes que intentan controlar el tipo de cambio en conjunto con polticas monetarias crecientemente restrictivas. En Chile no nos hemos apresurado en tomar decisiones excepcionales, ni tampoco hemos incorporado un objetivo cambiario en nuestra poltica, lo que se manifiesta en el uso de una regla simple de acumulacin. Tambin hemos esperado a tener cierta tranquilidad en materia inflacionaria. Los riesgos no han desaparecido, y desafortunadamente la coyuntura de las semanas anteriores nos limitaba las posibilidades de seguir esperando para la resolucin de estas incertidumbres. No obstante, en la reciente evolucin del entorno macroeconmico han aparecido elementos que podran presionar a la baja de la inflacin. Eso nos ha permitido quitar el sesgo y mantener la tasa de poltica monetaria en nuestra ltima reunin. Chile nunca ha estado mejor preparado para enfrentar una crisis internacional, pero no podemos ser complacientes. La decisin tomada la semana pasada, de acumular en los prximos 8 meses un total de 8 mil millones de dlares en reservas para fortalecer la posicin de liquidez internacional de la economa chilena es una inversin en estabilidad. Es deseable, adems de poco probable, que no sucedan eventos muy graves, pero queremos minimizar su potencial impacto en caso de que ellos ocurran. La inflacin es an alta, pero nuestra conclusin de la reunin de ayer fue que la mantencin de la tasa y la eliminacin el sesgo era la decisin adecuada para la convergencia de la inflacin a su meta en el horizonte de polticas. Esto provee un marco de coherencia entre la PM y la acumulacin de reservas, adems que es un momento adecuado para intervenir en el mercado cambiario pues el tipo de cambio est por debajo de lo que estimamos debera ubicarse en el largo plazo. Dado nuestro irrenunciable compromiso con la estabilidad de precios, lo que estamos sealando con esta medida es que nuestro esquema de metas de inflacin y la actual instancia de poltica monetaria puede acomodar una depreciacin del peso, algo que hace un par de meses atrs no podramos haber asegurado. En todo caso, el valor del dlar lo seguir fijando el mercado y la poltica monetaria seguir siendo usada con flexibilidad para asegurar el cumplimiento de nuestra meta de inflacin.

Title: Monetary Policy Report
text: PRESENTATION OF THE I OLITICAL REPORT M ONETARIA BEFORE LA COMISSION OF H ACIENDA D THE HONORABLE SENADO OF THE REPUBLICA Jos8e De Gregorio President Central Bank of Chile May 12, 2008 Mr. Chairman of the Finance Committee, Senator Eduardo Frei Ruiz-Tagle, Senators, I appreciate the invitation made to the Board of the Central Bank of Chile to present this Monetary Policy Report (IPoM), which contains our vision of the recent macroeconomic and financial events of the Chilean economy, as well as its prospects. The context of the presentation of this Report is particularly complex. Several of the risks we made present at our January IPoM have become reality. We are witnessing one of the most acute financial crises the world has gone through since the Great Depression. Developed economies have suffered from growth, particularly in the US, while commodity prices have reached very high levels. In fact, the world economy faces an inflationary shock of a magnitude only comparable to that which occurred in the seventies. Certainly, our country benefits from a high price of copper, but its effects are adequately attenuated by the macroeconomic policy framework, in particular, the rule of the structural surplus that saves transitory income abroad, and exchange rate flexibility in an inflation-targeting scheme. However, the degrees of integration of our economy, as well as the functioning of national markets, have meant that international price shocks are transmitted without much lag to the Chilean economy. This allows, on the one hand, to give the right signals for the allocation of resources and, on the other, it poses a very important challenge to monetary policy, which is to allow the necessary adjustments in relative prices not to result in persistent increases in inflation above its target. If this happens, it would be much more costly to maintain price stability. In this sense, we have a flexible inflation targeting framework that allows us to adequately accommodate these changes in relative prices, safeguarding the control of inflation, which makes possible a stable development of the Chilean economy. Our economy has not been immune to the external scenario. But our macroeconomic management framework has adequately weathered international turbulence, so the negative impact of this international environment has been significantly smaller compared to our past experiences and those of the developing world in general. All of the above has significantly changed the macroeconomic outlook that we presented in our January Monetary Policy Report, which constitutes a framework of analysis quite different from the one that prevailed in that month. Although with a significant depreciation in the last month, the peso is at levels lower than those observed in January; The global growth scenario deteriorated, and economic activity accentuated the weakness it showed in the second half of 2007. International prices of Raw materials and food show new increases, highlighting what has happened with the price of oil, which has reached levels hitherto unsuspected for some time. Annual CPI inflation, meanwhile, remains at elevated levels, well above target, which remains a matter of particular concern, given our commitment to use monetary policy to ensure its convergence to the target within the policy horizon. respect. Although annual CPI inflation continued to rise in the first quarter, this increase was somewhat more moderate than expected in January, and without the unusual figures observed in the second half of 2007 (Chart 1). In addition, with the available background, we estimate that, in the most likely scenario, this decline will continue in the coming quarters, to converge to its target level on the policy horizon. This projection is based, among other factors, on an inflationary spread that remains consistent with its normal patterns, on medium- and long-term inflation expectations in line with the target and on the projected trajectory of capacity gaps . On the capacity gap side, in the first quarter activity accentuated the weakness it showed in the second half of 2007. In any case, higher energy prices are consistent with the conditions we face as a country in terms of energy supply. For this reason, they provide incentives for sectoral investments that are foreseen in the sector and that are already appreciated in the data of the cadastre of engineering works . Undoubtedly, the risks around the external scenario are very broad, and most of these exhibit a negative bias in terms of their impact on domestic growth. A non-negligible probability has begun to be given to extremely negative scenarios, whose consequences on the national economy could be more damaging. In the US, for example, the dispersion and shift in private analysts' growth projections for 2008 and 2009 (Figure 9) is striking. Added to this is the apparent decoupling observed by commodity prices, particularly metals such as copper, in a scenario of weak growth, which is at least surprising. Consequently, it cannot be ruled out that in the face of a less favorable global inflationary outlook, the policy reactions of the main central banks will motivate an abrupt correction of riskier asset valuations, and even commodity prices, with abrupt changes in conditions. financial for emerging economies. Therefore, and given the risks that any of these extreme scenarios materialize, the Council began in April an intervention program in the foreign exchange market to strengthen the international liquidity position of the Chilean economy, announcing an increase in international reserves of US8 billion, within eight months. Thus, in addition to the macroeconomic policy framework d0 based on exchange rate flexibility, inflation targeting, fiscal rule, and prudential financial supervision d0 that puts the Chilean economy in a favorable position to adequately weather turbulence, this program of accumulation of Reserves will make it possible to better cope with the eventuality of an additional, severe and abrupt deterioration of the external environment. This increase in reserves also modifies the central bank's foreign currency position, which is consistent with the assessment that the real exchange rate was below the level that would prevail once global real and financial conditions normalize at the time of intervention . Although the probability of an extreme scenario can be discussed, there is no doubt that, if it occurs, it would be very costly for the national economy, so our goal is to minimize its potential impact if it occurs. In intervening, we considered that its likely exchange rate effect was consistent with the monetary policy instance of that year. timing and with inflationary convergence. As we reported, the inflation scenario we observed in March was able to accommodate an exchange rate depreciation without affecting the convergence of inflation to its target. This does not mean, of course, compromising monetary policy flexibility. Going forward we will move in one direction or another if the projected inflation trajectory threatens to deviate from the target. Indeed, the form of intervention, which does not target a specific value of the exchange rate, is precisely intended to keep unchanged the ability of monetary policy to control inflation. In any case, if more adverse scenarios do not occur, the international liquidity position of the Chilean economy will have strengthened. The entire macroeconomic picture that I have described to you has allowed the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to remain at 6.25% since January and to remove the bias to its future trajectory in April, in a context in which the nominal exchange rate increased after the announcement of the reserve purchase program. Different measures of market expectations for the MPR show a flatter trajectory than in January, indicating that the MPR could be in a range of plus or minus 25 basis points from its current level by the end of the year. In any case, I reiterate the Council's commitment to conduct monetary policy so that projected inflation is 3 % over the policy horizon. Therefore, as we have communicated in our last two monetary policy meetings, future changes in the MPR will depend on the new information that accumulates. Of particular importance for this will be the implications for inflation of the development of the complex international scenario, the degree of spread of the inflationary shocks of past months to other prices and the emergence of new inflationary pressures. The baseline projection scenario of this Report considers, as a methodological assumption, that in the coming quarters the MPR will follow a trajectory similar to that deduced from the different measures of expectations of the private sector in force in the two weeks prior to the statistical closure of this IPoM. Before concluding, I would like to mention a few points regarding the conduct of monetary policy and the inflation targeting framework. The Central Bank orients its policies towards achieving a medium-term inflation objective rather than attempting a shorter-term one. Firstly, because changes in its monetary policy have effects on the level of activity and on prices laggingbehind 2/. Secondly, because of the disadvantage of printing high volatility to interest rates, activity, employment and other variables, which would occur if there was a shorter-term horizon. Finally, because there are temporary movements in some prices that should not be subject to neutralization by monetary policy. The latter is precisely what is happening today. Inflation in Chile has risen significantly as a result of a global phenomenon of changes in relative prices, over which we have no control. That is why the Central Bank has not used its policy instruments to combat the direct effect of these changes, since they are beyond our control, but to ensure that inflationary pressures are not incubated that could affect the credibility and inflationary anchor of the economy, thus preventing inflation from returning to its target within the Policy horizon . We do not consider it appropriate or constructive that, in the face of a complex inflationary situation, we circumstantially alter our policy framework, either by shortening the horizon to ensure a faster convergence of the macroeconomic variable more 2/ Empirical evidence indicates that two to five quarters are required for Chile to respond to a change in monetary policy to achieve its most intense effect on demand and output, and four to eight quarters for this change to have its maximum effect on inflation. deviating from its normal level, or lengthening the horizon at the risk of severely affecting the anti-inflationary credibility that the country has worked so hard to build. A two-year horizon gives the necessary flexibility to adequately face, and without overreactions, the short-term impact of global inflation on Chile. The credibility of monetary policy is strengthened when temptations to change it for short-term benefits that are debatable, and at best, very small, are resisted. The public's credibility in the monetary authority's commitment to its objective is central to the effectiveness of monetary policy and is at the heart of achieving a stable business cycle with low fluctuations in unemployment and inflation. This is why it is necessary to monitor the inflation expectations implicit in the determination of prices and wages. To this end, various measures of inflationary expectations are analyzed, such as those deduced from the prices of financial assets and those reported in the various surveys, as well as the evolution of wages and prices compared with the usual propagation mechanisms . Under certain circumstances, private expectations over different horizons may differ systematically from the inflation target, which undoubtedly makes it very difficult to meet the target, significantly increasing the costs of stability. At the current juncture, we do not expect this to be happening, and that is why we have pointed out in the communiqu8es of our monetary policy meetings that long-term inflation expectations are anchored at 3%, even though some specific measures of inflationary compensation are well above 3% (Chart 15). Title: The Central Bank and Financial Stability
text: EL BANCO CENTRAL Y LA ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA Jos8e de Gregorio. President Central Bank of Chile June 2008 Good morning. I would like to begin by thanking the organizers of this event, where we will present the Financial Stability Report for the first half of this year. The preparation and dissemination of this report is of particular importance, as in it we inform the President of the Republic and the Senate, as well as the financial sector and the wider public, of one of the two objectives that the Law confers on the Central Bank, which are price stability and financial stability. The analysis we make in this Report is of particular interest in view of the current fragility of the international context, especially in the main financial centres of the world, and where risks persist that international economic activity will continue to deteriorate. In this presentation I will refer first to the objective of financial stability, then to some lessons that the recent international financial crisis has left us, to finish commenting on the main contents of the Report. Financial stability The Central Bank of Chile is mandated to ensure the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. The first translates into maintaining low, stable and sustainable inflation over time. As we are witnessing today, this is a particularly difficult task in the current international context of significant supply shocks, but one to which the Central Bank will continue to pursue with determination. The second mandate, which is the one that summons us today, corresponds to financial stability. This concept of stability has to do with the preservation of the primary functions of financial markets and institutions: (i) the intermediation of credit and savings in general, (ii) the provision of liquidity, (iii) the provision of means and services of payment, and (iv) the transfer of risks. Financial stability also includes adequate access for the Chilean economy to international financial markets, which requires an adequate exchange rate policy scheme and financial integration with the rest of the world. In Chile we have adopted a floating exchange rate scheme and increasing financial openness abroad . Financial stability is not an exclusive mission of the Central Bank, but shared, and often coordinated, with the superintendencies of the sector. . Presentation of the Financial Stability Report for the first half of 2008, at a meeting organized by the Association of Banks, the Santiago Stock Exchange, the Association of Insurers of Chile and the Electronic Exchange. Santiago, June 17, 2008. financial and the Ministry of Finance. Private financial market actors also play an important role through self-regulation and market discipline. Each of those involved addresses stability from different areas. In our case, we do it from the point of view of aggregate stability. We have often been faced with focused tensions. Our role is to monitor that these specific issues do not impact the rest of the system. An efficient and stable financial system is an essential component in the functioning of a modern and competitive economy. The relationship between a country's financial development and its economic growth is close. Deep and efficient financial markets help strengthen economic growth and reduce its volatility (Figures 1 and 2). However, financial crises can have a significant impact on the overall health and stability of economies. Periods of financial instability are extremely costly in terms of output and economic well-being. Without going any further, it is enough to remember the Chilean financial crisis of the early 80s, that of Argentina in 2001 and the financial crises suffered by the "Asian tigers" at the end of the last decade. For example, sudden stops in capital inflows, such as those experienced by several countries in 1999, have been estimated to generate cumulative growth losses of the order of 7 per cent of GDP (Figure 3). The subprime crisis, which financial markets in the US and some European countries are going through, is the latest example of the costs that financial instability can entail, and a stark reminder that greater Levels of economic development and sophistication of markets and financial intermediaries do not guarantee the normal functioning of the financial system. To measure these costs, remember that, as a result of this crisis, the US economy is expected to slow down from annual growth rates of 3% in the middle of last year, when the crisis broke out, to rates around 1% this year. The two mandates of the Central Bank are closely interrelated . Low and predictable inflation is a necessary condition for an efficient and stable financial system. Higher inflation implies uncertainty about the level of future prices, distorting savings and borrowing decisions, leading to short-term or exchange-rate indexed financial contracts or inhibiting the development of the financial system. Here it is enough to recall the difficulties faced by countries with inflationary histories in increasing their debt maturities and reducing the degree of indexation to rates or the exchange rate in their public and private debt markets (Figure 4). The exchange rate regime, on the other hand, is instrumental to both objectives. The floating exchange rate scheme allows for the monetary independence required by an inflationary targeting regime. Thus, the Report emphasizes the high degree of independence that nominal short and medium-term rates have had from the Chilean economy, in a period of high volatility and substantial changes in interest rates in developed economies. On the other hand, the regime Exchange rate plays an important role in financial stability. A flexible exchange rate induces economic agents to reduce their exposure to foreign exchange risk, encouraging the development of hedging markets (Figures 5 and 6). In rigid exchange rate regimes, by contrast, the monetary authority implicitly fulfils the role of "insurer" by inducing severe moral hazard problems, and leading to costly crises when the authority is forced to abandon the commitment to exchange rate stability. Just as low inflation is a necessary condition for financial development, a stable and efficient financial system is paramount for the conduct of monetary policy. The effectiveness of monetary policy depends crucially on the functioning of financial intermediaries and markets, since it is these that allow an efficient transfer of monetary policy to real variables. In turn, a stable financial system gives the Central Bank the space to adopt contractionary monetary policies when inflationary conditions require it. The recent rate hike decided by the Bank's Board last Tuesday is a clear example of this flexibility. On the contrary, the collision of the objectives of price stability and financial stability is precisely the dilemma that the US Federal Reserve has faced in recent months. On the one hand, the international rise in basic prices is generating growing inflationary pressures. On the other hand, as detailed in this Report, many of the signs of weakness in the US financial system that led to the drastic cuts in the Federal Reserve's policy rate at the beginning have persisted. of this year. We have in Chile a financial system that, for our level of economic development, is sophisticated and deep (figure 7). Undoubtedly, the Central Bank plays a role in continuing to deepen and sophisticate this system, as well as enhancing its integration into the international financial system. The effort that the Bank has been developing in the nominalization and in the creation of a yield curve in pesos and UF in conjunction with the Ministry of Finance, is a Example of the above. However, our fundamental contribution is to prevent potentially costly situations of instability, and to mitigate the consequences derived from the materialization of unpredictable episodes of instability. The tools with which the Central Bank fulfils its preventive role are detailed in the first column of the table (Table 1). These include the regulation and supervision of the payment system, the management of liquidity in pesos via monetary operations, the management of international reserves and the provision of a basic payment infrastructure . The second column details the tools with which the Central Bank can mitigate the consequences of episodes of instability, among which are its role as lender of last resort, the guarantee mechanism for demand deposits, operations with reserves and the regulation of the foreign exchange market. We also believe, like other central banks around the world, that we can further contribute to financial stability by providing systemic analysis that financial intermediaries can consider in their own risk assessment. The report we are presenting this morning is a central part of this complementary analysis to the analysis carried out by the agencies. supervisors in respect of financial institutions or groups of institutions with similar characteristics. The availability of adequate information, in a timely manner, is crucial for monitoring the financial system. With this objective in mind, last year the Central Bank, together with the University of Chile , conducted the first financial survey of households in Chile. This survey, the first results of which are reported in this Report (see Box III.1), collects detailed information on the financial situation of Chilean households. It includes levels of indebtedness, financial assets and insurance uses, thus allowing accurate monitoring of the financial situation of households. This information will be made public in disaggregated form in the coming months, with which we hope to make an important contribution to academics, regulators and financial analysts. Before entering fully into the subprime crisis, I would like to refer to the role played by international reserves in protecting the country's economy, and in particular the financial system, from substantial contractions in international liquidity. On the one hand, a strong liquidity position reduces the likelihood of external credit constraints . On the other hand, when they do occur, reserves make it possible to supplement the private availability of liquidity with public liquidity. As the Report highlights, so far companies and financial institutions have not seen their access to external financing closed. However, the persistence of the instability of international financial markets led the Central Bank to initiate a process of accumulation of reserves of 8,000 million dollars, which significantly increases the ratio of reserves to GDP. No doubt this process has costs, but we consider that the benefits it provides as liquidity insurance more than compensate them. Some lessons from the subprime crisis I would like to share with you some thoughts on the lessons we have learned from the financial crisis that developed economies are still going through. Few of these are new, generally reinforcing lessons we should have learned by now, after several financial crises. Liquidity risks are a lesson that reappears strongly in this crisis. Reliance on short-term funding sources to finance illiquid assets exposes leveraged financial intermediaries to loss of confidence and runs. The "historic" form of these runs is what was seen in the UK, with Northern Rock, where depositors queued outside the bank to withdraw their funds. But a run, this time by investors, was what ended up sinking Bear Stearns, and threatened the insolvency of other US banks until the Fed intervened decisively in its rescue and in the expansion of liquidity provision for Investment Banks (Figures 8 and 9). As a Central Bank, we are attentive to the lessons that are being decided in this regard and the relevance they have for the updating of our regulatory framework. The subprime crisis has also opened a debate regarding the risks of financial innovation and, therefore, the need to regulate such innovation. Let me tell you, first of all, that I am convinced that financial innovation is good. Moreover, I believe that many times costs are attributed to innovation that rather correspond to bad decisions by companies or other financial intermediaries. Other times the problems are of inconsistent economic policies. However, I believe that progress must be made in innovation processes, but with the appropriate safeguards. First, gradualness and adequate delivery of information is important. Second, incentives and potential conflicts of interest posed by new instruments and processes need to be carefully reviewed . Another lesson d0 which is not new either d0 has to do with the role, at this point essential, that financial risk control and management systems fulfill. A true system of control and management of financial risk starts with the definition of policies at the highest level, the board, by the involvement of senior management in follow-up and monitoring, and, ultimately, by the development of an organizational culture that is able to adequately combine profitability and leadership objectives with prudence and sensitivity to risk. In this same area, an issue that is at the center of the discussion of financial reforms in developed countries is the global incentive structure of financial intermediaries. Several analysts have argued that executive pay and bonus incentives played a role in the irrational expansion of real estate credit in the U.S. to customers with minimal probability of payment. I believe that this is an issue that all actors in the financial system must follow closely. The role played by risk rating agencies in the subprime crisis also appears as an important corollary of the current crisis. We can begin by recalling the accumulation of criticism that rating agencies received for their performance in the Asian crisis, where in some cases they maintained high ratings for countries that were already falling into deep financial crises. This is a complex issue, due to the sophistication of some financial instruments, but especially because of the incentives with which the rating agencies operate. This is also an issue of growing importance. We have seen a gradual move towards institutionalizing the role of rating agencies, including their classifications into portfolio constraints, bank provisions, etc. In some ways this is a process of "outsourcing" financial regulation, which relies crucially on the skills and, especially, incentives of rating agencies. The fact that classification work is carried out by private agencies is a good thing. The classification process is complex and subject to many difficulties. However, imagine that in this crisis, or in the Asian one, the classifications had been made by official agencies. The problem of moral hazard and the demands for bailout that would have fallen on the authorities would have been incontrovertible. That is why it is important to keep in mind that the classifications only impose restrictions on eligible financial instruments in investment portfolios, but, ultimately, the risk is assumed by investors. Finally, the events that have occurred in recent months in the main international financial centers highlight the relevance of systemic analysis. of the financial aspects of an economy. This in order to detect and prevent sources of potential instability or developments of greater risk to the stability of the economy, and to act decisively when circumstances warrant it. It is impossible to attribute the severity of the subprime crisis to a single set of financial actors. It involved credit originator agents who aggressively promoted forms of loan with a higher risk of non-payment; intermediaries that packaged these credits into the various varieties of securitized assets; risk classifiers that evaluated these products; investment vehicles that invested relying on market financing; and demanders of these assets both in the U.S. and in other economies. All this in a context of low interest rates, low risk premiums and sustained increases in house prices. The Financial Stability Report Today we present the ninth version of the Financial Stability Report that the Central Bank of Chile began publishing in 2004. The purpose of this Report is to present the Bank's Board's view of recent macro-financial events that could affect the financial stability of the Chilean economy, and to assess the resilience of the system to the most likely risk scenarios. In addition to the above, the Report reviews the policies and measures that contribute to the functioning of the payment system. This report identifies three closely related external threats to the stability of Chile's financial system. The first is a global credit crunch, the second a generalized weakening of international economic activity, and the third, excessive increases in interest rates in developed economies as a result of higher inflation. However, the current economic policy scheme, the prudential regulation framework, the banking equity situation, and the solvency levels of the Chilean economy should facilitate an eventual adjustment to these restrictive conditions. Undoubtedly , a significant external deterioration would have a significant negative impact on the Chilean economy. However, the analysis contained in the report we are presenting today suggests that the Chilean financial system would be prepared to face this deterioration without becoming a source of risk or volatility that threatens financial stability. The Council hopes that the publication of this Report will contribute to the analysis and public discussion of these matters, of the greatest relevance for the development of the economy and the well-being of all Chileans. Thanks a lot. text_original: EL BANCO CENTRAL Y LA ESTABILIDAD FINANCIERA Jos De Gregorio Presidente Banco Central de Chile Junio 2008 Buenos das. Quisiera comenzar agradeciendo a los organizadores de este evento, donde presentaremos el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera del primer semestre de este ao. La preparacin y difusin de este informe es de particular importancia, pues en l informamos a la Presidenta de la Repblica y al Senado, as como al sector financiero y al pblico ms amplio respecto de uno de los dos objetivos que la Ley confiere al Banco Central, cuales son la estabilidad de precios y la estabilidad financiera. El anlisis que hacemos en este Informe reviste especial inters frente a la fragilidad actual del contexto internacional, en especial de los principales centros financieros del mundo, y donde persisten riesgos de que la actividad econmica internacional siga deteriorndose. En esta presentacin me referir primero al objetivo de estabilidad financiera, luego a algunas lecciones que nos ha dejado la reciente crisis financiera internacional, para terminar comentando los principales contenidos del Informe. La estabilidad financiera El Banco Central de Chile tiene como mandatos velar por la estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos. El primero se traduce en mantener una inflacin baja, estable y sostenible en el tiempo. Como somos testigos hoy, esta es una tarea especialmente difcil en el actual contexto internacional de importantes shocks de oferta, pero a la cual el Banco Central se seguir abocando con determinacin. El segundo mandato, que es el que hoy nos convoca, corresponde a la estabilidad financiera. Este concepto de estabilidad tiene que ver con la preservacin de las funciones primordiales de los mercados e instituciones financieras: (i) la intermediacin del crdito y del ahorro en general, (ii) la provisin de liquidez, (iii) la provisin de medios y servicios de pago, y (iv) la transferencia de riesgos. La estabilidad financiera engloba, adems, el adecuado acceso de la economa chilena a los mercados financieros internacionales, lo que requiere un adecuado esquema de poltica cambiaria y de integracin financiera con el resto del mundo. En Chile hemos adoptado un esquema de flotacin cambiaria y de creciente apertura financiera al exterior. La estabilidad financiera no es una misin exclusiva del Banco Central, sino compartida, y muchas veces coordinada con las superintendencias del sector  Presentacin del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera del primer semestre del 2008, en reunin organizada por la Asociacin de Bancos, la Bolsa de Comercio de Santiago, la Asociacin de Aseguradores de Chile y la Bolsa Electrnica. Santiago, 17 de junio de 2008. financiero y el Ministerio de Hacienda. Los actores privados del mercado financiero tambin juegan un papel importante a travs de la autorregulacin y la disciplina de mercado. Cada uno de los involucrados aborda la estabilidad desde diversos mbitos. En nuestro caso, lo hacemos desde el punto de vista de la estabilidad agregada. Hemos estado muchas veces enfrentados a tensiones focalizadas. Nuestro rol es monitorear que estos problemas especficos no repercutan en el resto del sistema. Un sistema financiero eficiente y estable es un componente esencial en del funcionamiento de una economa moderna y competitiva. La relacin entre el desarrollo financiero de un pas y su crecimiento econmico es estrecha. Mercados financieros profundos y eficientes contribuyen a fortalecer el crecimiento econmico y a reducir su volatilidad (figuras 1 y 2). No obstante, las crisis financieras pueden tener repercusiones importantes sobre la salud y estabilidad global de las economas. Los perodos de inestabilidad financiera son extremadamente costosos en trminos de producto y bienestar econmico. Sin ir ms lejos, basta recordar la crisis financiera chilena de principios de los 80, la de Argentina en el 2001 y las crisis financieras que sufrieron los tigres asiticos a fines de la dcada pasada. Se ha estimado, por ejemplo, que las interrupciones repentinas (sudden stops) de la entrada de capitales, como la que experimentaron varios pases en 1999 generaron prdidas acumuladas de crecimiento del orden de 7% del PIB (figura 3). La crisis subprime, por la cual atraviesan los mercados financieros de EE.UU. y algunos pases europeos, es el ejemplo ms reciente de los costos que puede significar la inestabilidad financiera, y un claro recordatorio de que mayores niveles de desarrollo econmico y sofisticacin de los mercados e intermediarios financieros no garantizan el normal funcionamiento del sistema financiero. Para dimensionar estos costos, recordemos que, como consecuencia de esta crisis, se espera que la economa norteamericana se desacelere desde tasas de crecimiento anuales de 3% a mediados del ao pasado, cuando se desata la crisis, a tasas en torno a 1% este ao. Los dos mandatos del Banco Central estn estrechamente relacionados entre s. Una inflacin baja y predecible es condicin necesaria para un sistema financiero eficiente y estable. La mayor inflacin implica incertidumbre sobre el nivel de precios futuros, distorsionando las decisiones de ahorro y de endeudamiento, llevando a contratos financieros de corto plazo o indexados al tipo de cambio o inhibiendo el desarrollo del sistema financiero. Aqu basta recordar las dificultades que han enfrentado pases con historiales inflacionarios para aumentar los plazos de su deuda y reducir el grado de indexacin a tasas o al tipo de cambio en sus mercados de deuda pblicos y privados (figura 4). El rgimen cambiario, por su parte, es instrumental a ambos objetivos. El esquema de flotacin cambiaria permite contar con la independencia monetaria que requiere un rgimen de metas inflacionarias. Es as como en el Informe se enfatiza el alto grado de independencia que han tenido las tasas nominales de corto y mediano plazo de la economa chilena, en un periodo de alta volatilidad y cambios sustanciales en las tasas de inters de las economas desarrolladas. Por otro lado, el rgimen cambiario juega un importante rol en la estabilidad financiera. Un tipo de cambio flexible induce a los agentes econmicos a reducir su exposicin al riesgo cambiario, incentivando el desarrollo de los mercados de cobertura (figuras 5 y 6). En regmenes cambiarios rgidos, en cambio, la autoridad monetaria cumple implcitamente el papel de asegurador induciendo severos problemas de riesgo moral, y llevando a costosas crisis cuando la autoridad se ve obligada a abandonar el compromiso de estabilidad cambiaria. As como una baja inflacin es condicin necesaria para el desarrollo financiero, un sistema financiero estable y eficiente es primordial para la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. La efectividad de poltica monetaria depende crucialmente del funcionamiento de los intermediarios y mercados financieros, pues son estos lo que permiten un traspaso eficiente de la poltica monetaria a variables reales. A su vez, un sistema financiero estable da el espacio al Banco Central para poder adoptar polticas monetarias contractivas cuando las condiciones inflacionarias as lo requieran. La reciente alza de tasas que decidi el Consejo del Banco el martes pasado es un claro ejemplo de esta flexibilidad. Por el contrario, la colisin de los objetivos de estabilidad de precios y estabilidad financiera, es justamente el dilema que ha enfrentado en meses pasados la Reserva Federal de EE.UU. Por un lado, el alza internacional de precios bsicos est generando crecientes presiones inflacionarias. Por otro, como detallamos en este Informe, han persistido muchas de las seales de debilidad en el sistema financiero norteamericano que motivaron las drsticas bajas en la tasa de poltica de la Reserva Federal a comienzos de este ao. Tenemos en Chile un sistema financiero que, para nuestro nivel de desarrollo econmico, es sofisticado y profundo (figura 7). Sin lugar a dudas el Banco Central juega un rol en continuar profundizando y sofisticando este sistema, as como potenciando su integracin al sistema financiero internacional. El esfuerzo que viene desarrollando el Banco en la nominalizacin y en la creacin de una curva de rendimiento en pesos y UF en conjunto con el Ministerio de Hacienda, es un ejemplo de lo anterior. Sin embargo, nuestro aporte fundamental es prevenir situaciones de inestabilidad potencialmente costosas, y mitigar las consecuencias derivadas de la materializacin de episodios de inestabilidad imprevisibles. Las herramientas con las cuales el Banco Central cumple su papel preventivo se detallan en la primera columna del cuadro (tabla 1). Estas incluyen la regulacin y supervisin del sistema de pagos, el manejo de la liquidez en pesos va operaciones monetarias, el manejo de las reservas internacionales y la provisin de una infraestructura bsica de pagos. La segunda columna detalla las herramientas con las cuales el Banco Central puede mitigar las consecuencias de episodios de inestabilidad, entre las que se encuentran su rol como prestamista de ltima instancia, el mecanismo de garanta de los depsitos vista, operaciones con reservas y la regulacin del mercado cambiario. Creemos adems, al igual que otros bancos centrales del mundo, que podemos contribuir en forma adicional a la estabilidad financiera aportando un anlisis sistmico que los intermediarios financieros puedan considerar en su propia evaluacin de riesgos. El Informe que presentamos esta maana es parte central de este anlisis complementario al anlisis que llevan a cabo los organismos supervisores respecto de entidades financieras o grupos de instituciones de caractersticas similares. La disponibilidad de la informacin adecuada, en forma oportuna, es crucial para el monitoreo del sistema financiero. Con este objetivo en mente, el ao pasado el Banco Central, en conjunto con la Universidad de Chile, levant la primera encuesta financiera de hogares de Chile. Esta encuesta, cuyos primeros resultados se reportan en este Informe (ver Recuadro III.1), recolecta informacin detallada de la situacin financiera de los hogares chilenos. En ella se incluyen niveles de endeudamiento, activos financieros y usos de seguros, permitiendo as un monitoreo preciso de la situacin financiera de los hogares. Esta informacin se har pblica en forma desagregada en los prximos meses, con lo que esperamos hacer un aporte importante tanto a acadmicos, como a reguladores y analistas financieros. Antes de entrar de lleno a discutir la crisis subprime, quisiera referirme al papel que juegan las reservas internacionales en proteger a la economa del pas, y en particular el sistema financiero, de contracciones sustanciales en la liquidez internacional. Por un lado, una posicin slida de liquidez reduce la probabilidad de que ocurran restricciones al crdito externo. Por otro, cuando s ocurren, las reservas permiten complementar con liquidez pblica la disponibilidad privada de liquidez. Como destaca el Informe, hasta ahora las empresas e instituciones financieras no han visto cerrarse su acceso a financiamiento externo. No obstante, la persistencia de la inestabilidad de los mercados financieros internacionales llev al Banco Central a iniciar un proceso de acumulacin de reservas por 8.000 millones de dlares, lo que aumenta significativamente la razn de reservas a PIB. Sin duda este proceso tiene costos, pero consideramos que los beneficios que provee como seguro de liquidez ms que los compensan. Algunas lecciones de la crisis subprime Quisiera compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones respecto de las lecciones que hemos ido obteniendo de la crisis financiera por la que an atraviesan las economas desarrolladas. Pocas de estas son nuevas, en general refuerzan lecciones que deberamos haber aprendido ya, tras varias crisis financieras. Los riesgos de liquidez son una leccin que reaparece con fuerza en esta crisis. La dependencia de fuentes de financiamiento de corto plazo para financiar activos ilquidos expone a los intermediarios financieros apalancados a prdidas de confianza y corridas. La forma histrica de estas corridas es la que se vio en el Reino Unido, con Northern Rock, donde los depositantes hacan colas afuera del banco para retirar sus fondos. Pero una corrida, esta vez de inversionistas, fue lo que termin por hundir a Bear Stearns, y amenaz con la insolvencia a otros bancos de EE.UU. hasta que la Fed intervino decididamente en su rescate y en la ampliacin de provisin de liquidez para Bancos de Inversin (figuras 8 y 9). Como Banco Central estamos atentos a las lecciones que se vayan decantando en este sentido y la relevancia que estas tengan para la actualizacin de nuestro marco regulatorio. La crisis subprime tambin ha abierto un debate respecto de los riesgos de la innovacin financiera y, por lo tanto, la necesidad de normar dicha innovacin. Djenme plantearles, en primer lugar, que soy un convencido de que la innovacin financiera es buena. Ms an, creo que muchas veces se le atribuyen costos a la innovacin que ms bien corresponden a malas decisiones de empresas u otros intermediarios financieros. Otras veces los problemas son de polticas econmicas inconsistentes. Con todo, creo que debe avanzarse en los procesos de innovacin, pero con los debidos resguardos. En primer lugar, es importante la gradualidad y la adecuada entrega de informacin. En segundo lugar, es necesario revisar con detencin los incentivos y posibles conflictos de inters que planteen los nuevos instrumentos y procesos. Otra leccin que tampoco es nueva tiene que ver con el rol, a estas alturas imprescindible, que cumplen los sistemas de control y gestin de los riesgos financieros. Un verdadero sistema de control y gestin de riesgo financiero parte por la definicin de polticas al ms alto nivel, el directorio, por el involucramiento de la alta administracin en el seguimiento y monitoreo, y, a fin de cuentas, por el desarrollo de una cultura organizacional que sea capaz de combinar adecuadamente los objetivos de rentabilidad y liderazgo con la prudencia y la sensibilidad al riesgo. En este mismo mbito, un tema que est en el centro de la discusin de reformas financieras en pases desarrollados es la estructura global de incentivos de los intermediarios financieros. Varios analistas han argumentado que los incentivos salariales y de bonos de los ejecutivos tuvieron que ver con la expansin irracional del crdito inmobiliario en los EE.UU. a clientes con mnima probabilidad de pago. Creo que este es un tema que todos los actores del sistema financiero debemos seguir con atencin. El rol que jugaron las clasificadoras de riesgo en la crisis subprime aparece tambin como importante corolario de la crisis actual. Podemos comenzar recordando el cmulo de crticas que recibieron las clasificadoras por su desempeo en la crisis asitica, donde en algunos casos mantuvieron altas clasificaciones para pases que ya estaban cayendo en profundas crisis financieras. Este es un tema complejo, por la sofisticacin de algunos instrumentos financieros, pero en especial por los incentivos con los que operan las clasificadoras. Este es, adems, un tema de creciente importancia. Hemos visto un avance gradual hacia la institucionalizacin del rol de las clasificadoras, incluyendo sus clasificaciones en restricciones de portafolio, provisiones bancarias, etc. De alguna manera este es un proceso de externalizacin de la regulacin financiera, que descansa crucialmente en las habilidades y, en especial, en los incentivos de las clasificadoras. El que labores de clasificacin sean realizadas por agencias privadas es algo positivo. El proceso de clasificacin es complejo y est sujeto a muchas dificultades. No obstante, imaginemos que en esta crisis, o en la asitica, las clasificaciones las hubiesen realizado agencias oficiales. El problema de riesgo moral y las demandas de salvataje que hubieran recado sobre las autoridades habran sido incontrarrestables. Es por ello que es importante tener presente que las clasificaciones solo imponen restricciones a los instrumentos financieros elegibles en las carteras de inversin, pero, en definitiva, el riesgo lo asumen los inversionistas. Finalmente, los eventos ocurridos en los ltimos meses en los principales centros financieros internacionales ponen de manifiesto la relevancia del anlisis sistmico de los aspectos financieros de una economa. Ello con el fin de detectar y prevenir focos de potencial inestabilidad o desarrollos de mayor riesgo para la estabilidad de la economa, y de actuar con decisin cuando las circunstancias lo ameriten. Es imposible atribuir la severidad de la crisis subprime a un solo conjunto de agentes financieros. En ella interactuaron agentes originadores de crdito que impulsaron agresivamente formas de prstamo de mayor riesgo de no pago; intermediarios que empaquetaron dichos crditos en las diversas variedades de activos securitizados; clasificadores de riesgo que evaluaron estos productos; vehculos de inversin que invirtieron descansando en el financiamiento de mercado, y demandantes de estos activos tanto en EE.UU. como en otras economas. Todo esto en un contexto de tasas de inters bajas, primas de riesgo bajas y aumentos sostenidos en los precios de la vivienda. El Informe de Estabilidad Financiera Hoy da presentamos la novena versin del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera que el Banco Central de Chile comenzara a publicar en 2004. El propsito de este Informe es dar a conocer la visin del Consejo del Banco respecto de los sucesos macro-financieros recientes que podran incidir en la estabilidad financiera de la economa chilena, y evaluar la resiliencia del sistema a los escenarios de riesgo ms probables. Junto a lo anterior, en el Informe se pasa revista a las polticas y medidas que contribuyen al funcionamiento del sistema de pagos. Este informe identifica tres amenazas externas estrechamente relacionadas a la estabilidad del sistema financiero chileno. La primera es un credit crunch global, la segunda un debilitamiento generalizado de la actividad econmica internacional, y la tercera, alzas desmedidas en las tasas de inters de las economas desarrolladas producto de una mayor inflacin. Con todo, el actual esquema de polticas econmicas, el marco de regulacin prudencial, la situacin patrimonial de la banca, y los niveles de solvencia de la economa chilena, deberan facilitar un eventual ajuste a dichas condiciones restrictivas. Sin duda que un deterioro externo relevante tendra un impacto negativo relevante en la economa chilena. Sin embargo, el anlisis contenido en el Informe que presentamos hoy sugiere que el sistema financiero chileno estara preparado para enfrentar este deterioro sin convertirse en una fuente de riesgo o volatilidad que amenacen la estabilidad financiera. El Consejo espera que la publicacin de este Informe contribuya al anlisis y la discusin pblica de estas materias, de la mayor relevancia para el desarrollo de la economa y el bienestar de todos los chilenos. Muchas gracias.
