Title: Award ceremony speech contest "The economy + close"
text: AWARD CEREMONY SPEECH CONTEST "THE ECONOMY CLOSE" October 28, 2009 Madam Minister of Education Members of the Jury Dear directors, teachers and students of the finalist groups Ladies and gentlemen: We are finishing today the fifth version of the contest "Za econom92a cerca', whose objective is that third and fourth grade students from all over the country, can internalize, investigate and analyze, from their daily reality, economic issues as relevant as the link between the work of the Central Bank, price stability and the welfare of the population, as well as the importance of the autonomy of this Bank and the soundness of the financial system. Once again we can say that we feel enormously satisfied. First, because of the positive response to our call and, second, because we are increasingly successful in promoting the importance of education in economic and financial issues, as a means to improve people's decision-making, improve the quality of life of the population and make the functioning of financial markets and monetary policy more efficient. We have always been convinced that access to economic knowledge at this stage of the educational process improves the preparation of these young people to face the reality of decisions in their adult lives. And we have always been convinced that this same knowledge can be propagated by them in their school and family environment. Along these lines, the "Economy for the Majority" Program, which the Bank has been developing for six years and which has been accompanied by seminars for students and guided tours, added workshops for high school social science teachers this year. 533 students participated in the Seminars this year, while in the workshops, we had the assistance of 85 teachers, belonging to 69 schools in different parts of the country. In both activities, talks were given on the main economic concepts involved in the treatment of the four topics proposed in the contest: inflation, banks and financial system, monetary policy rate and autonomy of the Central Bank. The good evaluation we have had from the teachers, encourages us to continue next year with this activity and do it even more intensely. In this fifth version of the contest, 996 groups of students belonging to municipal, subsidized and paid schools from all over the country were registered. These groups sent 522 papers prepared by 1,989 students from 238 educational establishments. These works were evaluated by a group of 35 Bank professionals, who made a pre-selection with rigorous technical criteria, based on a strict evaluation guideline that considered technical mastery and originality in the practical application of the topics. In the first stage, 67 works were classified in the pre-selected category. In the next stage, a second group of 6 economists from the Central Bank, defined the 10 finalists. I would like to express to all the Bank's professionals who participated in this correction and evaluation phase, our special appreciation for their enthusiastic support and for the valuable work they have done. The jury present here today, and which I had the honor of chairing, evaluated the 10 finalist works, following this same rigorous guideline, a task not without difficulties, since we find works of remarkable quality and originality. From this evaluation emerged the three finalist groups that presented and defended their essays before the jury in solemn presentations made this morning in the Council Chamber, in a process that could be followed throughout the country, thanks to a live broadcast made through the contest website. You could appreciate it. These presentations gave an account of a good theoretical and conceptual management of the finalist teams, allowing us to visualize the development of economic processes in a simple and sometimes playful way, without losing the precision required in the analysis of the interdependencies of economic agents. Madam Minister, ladies and gentlemen academics, esteemed counselors, executives and officials of this Institution, the awards that we deliver today represent the culmination of a long process carried out throughout the year, which seeks to contribute to the great project of having a population more educated in matters of economics and finance. Distinguished finalist students and teachers. You are already on this path and I ask you to continue on it. Their enthusiasm, dedication and effort in the elaboration and presentation of their work, is a concrete demonstration that our effort to spread the understanding of the world of the economy in which daily life takes place, has fruits that will continue to spread, contributing to the effectiveness of our policies and the well-being of all Chileans. I thank all those who made this initiative possible, especially the members of the jury, the guide teachers and students participating in the 522 works submitted; in particular, those who are with us today, as well as the officials of the Central Bank. Each one contributed with his effort, his creativity and his time so that through this contest the economy is closer and closer to the people. THANKS A LOT
text_original: DISCURSO CEREMONIA DE PREMIACIN CONCURSO "LA ECONOMA + CERCA 28 de octubre de 2009 Seora Ministra de Educacin Seores miembros del Jurado Estimados directores, profesores y alumnos de los grupos finalistas Seoras y seores: Estamos finalizando hoy la quinta versin del concurso Za economa + cerca ', cuyo objetivo es que alumnos de tercero y cuarto medio de todo el pas, puedan interiorizarse, investigar y analizar, a partir de su realidad cotidiana, temas econmicos tan relevantes como el vnculo entre el quehacer del Banco Central, la estabilidad de precios y el bienestar de la poblacin, as como la importancia de la autonoma de este Banco y de la solidez del sistema financiero. Una vez ms podemos decir que nos sentimos enormemente satisfechos. Primero, por la respuesta positiva a nuestra convocatoria y, segundo, porque estamos logrando cada vez con mayor xito promover la importancia que tiene la educacin en temas econmicos y financieros, como un medio para mejorar la toma de decisiones de las personas, mejorar la calidad de vida de la poblacin y hacer ms eficiente el funcionamiento de los mercados financieros y de la poltica monetaria. En esta lnea, el Programa Economa para la Mayora, que el Banco desarrolla desde hace seis aos y que ha sido acompaado de seminarios a estudiantes y visitas guiadas, agreg en este ao talleres a profesores de ciencias sociales de enseanza media. En ambas actividades se dictaron charlas sobre los principales conceptos econmicos involucrados en el tratamiento de los cuatro temas propuestos en el concurso: inflacin, bancos y sistema financiero, tasa de poltica monetaria y autonoma del Banco Central. La buena evaluacin que hemos tenido de parte de los profesores, nos alienta a continuar el prximo ao con esta actividad y hacerlo de manera an ms intensa. En esta quinta versin del concurso se inscribieron 996 grupos de estudiantes pertenecientes a colegios municipales, subvencionados y pagados de todo el pas. Estos grupos enviaron 522 trabajos elaborados por 1.989 alumnos de 238 establecimientos educacionales. Estos trabajos fueron evaluados por un grupo de 35 profesionales del Banco, quienes realizaron una preseleccin con riguroso criterio tcnico, sobre la base de una estricta pauta de evaluacin que consider el dominio tcnico y la originalidad en la aplicacin prctica de los temas. En la primera etapa clasificaron 67 trabajos en categora de preseleccionados. En la etapa siguiente, un segundo grupo de 6 economistas del Banco Central, defini a los 10 finalistas. Quiero expresar a todos los profesionales del Banco que participaron en esta fase de correccin y evaluacin, nuestro especial reconocimiento por su apoyo entusiasta y por la valiosa labor realizada. El jurado hoy aqu presente, y que tuve el honor de presidir, evalu los 10 trabajos finalistas, siguiendo esta misma pauta rigurosa, tarea no carente de dificultades, ya que nos encontramos con trabajos de notable calidad y originalidad. De esta evaluacin surgieron los tres grupos finalistas que expusieron y defendieron sus ensayos ante el jurado en solemnes presentaciones realizadas esta maana en la Sala de Consejo, en un proceso que pudo ser seguido en todo el pas, gracias a una transmisin en vivo realizada a travs del sitio web del concurso. Ustedes pudieron apreciarlo. Estas presentaciones dieron cuenta de un buen manejo terico y conceptual de los equipos finalistas, permitindonos visualizar el desarrollo de los procesos econmicos en forma simple y en ocasiones, ldica, sin perder por ello la precisin requerida en el anlisis de las interdependencias de los agentes econmicos. Seora ministra, seoras y seores acadmicos, estimados consejeros, ejecutivos y funcionarios de esta Institucin, los premios que hoy entregamos representan la culminacin de un largo proceso realizado a lo largo del ao, que busca contribuir al gran proyecto de tener una poblacin ms educada en temas de economa y finanzas. Distinguidos alumnos finalistas y profesores. Ustedes ya estn en este camino y les pido que continen en l. Su entusiasmo, dedicacin y esfuerzo en la elaboracin y presentacin de sus trabajos, es una demostracin concreta de que nuestro esfuerzo por difundir la comprensin del mundo de la economa en el que se desarrolla la vida diaria, tiene frutos que continuarn extendindose, contribuyendo a la efectividad de nuestras polticas y al bienestar de todos los chilenos. Agradezco a todos quienes hicieron posible esta iniciativa, en especial, a los integrantes del jurado, a los profesores gua y alumnos participantes de los 522 trabajos enviados; en particular, los que hoy nos acompaan, as como a los funcionarios del Banco Central. Cada uno aport con su esfuerzo, su creatividad y su tiempo para que a travs de este concurso la economa se encuentre cada vez ms cerca de la gente. MUCHAS GRACIAS

Title: Farewell Speech by Jorge Desormeaux
text: FAREWELL SPEECH BY JORGE DESORMEAUX Jos8e De Gregorio President of the Central Bank of Chile December 4, 2009 It is always difficult to write a farewell, in particular that of a great friend and professional such as Jorge Desormeaux. Today, Jorge ends his 10-year term as a director of the Central Bank of Chile and for the last two years has been its Vice President. His contribution to the Bank throughout this period has been very important, and his traces are present in our most relevant innovations, as well as in our multiple monetary policy decisions. He was always a very important voice when making decisions and in the most complex moments, his wisdom was always welcome. I have the pleasure of meeting Jorge Desormeaux many years ago, and being one of many who owe him a debt of gratitude. I met him around in 1984. When I was trying to publish my master's thesis, Jorge recommended some studies done by his classmates at MIT. At that time we were interested in knowing some parameters to calibrate fairly simple exercises of projection and macro consistency. In my case, my purpose was to estimate exchange rate elasticities of exports and imports, something that Jorge was also interested in. We can say with some consolation that, although 25 years have passed, such parameters are still necessary in today's models, much more sophisticated than those of then. This is a demonstration that either we are not that old, or that the economy has not progressed much, or that what we were doing was quite useful. I continued later to see Jorge, who in addition to his work as a teacher, was an outstanding analyst of the conjuncture. As I was in CIEPLAN among those who had to analyze the situation, talking with Jorge was always very useful. We continued to see each other, and I told him of my intention to go to MIT, to which he again gave me very valuable advice. He even invited me to eat at his house to talk about life in Cambridge, but as some of you will already foresee, we ended up talking about computers, and he already had one of the first laptops, which weighed about 5 kilos, and even more, we started playing some prehistoric video games today. Those who know the characters will know that we were widely defeated by Jorge's wife, an excellent pianist, so no one competed with him in psychomotor skills. After my departure out of Chile for a long time I lost track of him, but I had the pleasure of reuniting with him in the last 8 and a half years as colleagues in the Board of the Bank. We still talk about economy, models and technology, although we have suspended video games. Jorge's farewell shows a new step in the consolidation of the Bank's autonomy. Jorge Desormeaux is the fourth director in these 20 years to serve a ten-year term in office. Before that they were Alfonso Serrano, Jorge Marshall and Mar92a Elena Ovalle. He was a Director under three terms of Presidents of the Republic and under three presidents of the Central Bank. This highlights the foundation of autonomy, which is to transcend political conjunctures by always putting in its decisions the conviction that the country's development depends to a large extent on a stable economy and institutional framework, within which the objective of price stability by an independent central bank plays a key role. In these periods he had to live highly complex, difficult and crucial situations for the Institution, some of them with high public impact, in which it was necessary to show mettle to face them successfully, and Jorge was one of those who allowed the short-term costs not to leave deep scars, but to be a real opportunity to improve. It also had to be a leading player in an internal structural change that has allowed the Bank to advance by leaps and bounds in the design and implementation of an entire architecture consistent with the way of doing monetary policy, with increasingly abundant and timely information to the market, in accordance with the standards that are imposed as the best practices in the world. This change has consisted of a profound process of modernization in its internal management, aimed at making the fulfilment of its mandate even more efficient. In recent years, a whole process of strategic planning has been developed, which clearly defined the mission, vision and values of the organization and which is the basis for defining the strategic objectives, which are a road map for all Bank units to direct their efforts and resources. It is precisely these structural changes and the decisions that were taken on the basis of this architecture, which have allowed us to strengthen the credibility of this Institution, an indispensable attribute for the effective development of its work and which were put to the test in the two complex episodes that we experienced in 2008 and 2009. when we went from facing high inflation caused largely by an external price shock to the worst global financial crisis since the Great Depression. Jorge was also part of the gestation and development of one of the most relevant projects being developed by the Bank, which is the launch of a new family of banknotes, of which the 5,000 peso note is already in circulation. During these events, the Council has taken timely but difficult decisions, always prioritizing, within the framework of its own evaluations, the technical criteria that should always characterize this Institution and of which Jorge has been a faithful representative. Dear Counselors and Officers, We want to thank Jorge for everything he gave to the Central Bank of Chile throughout these ten years. He has been a fundamental piece in the functioning of an institution that has given so much to our country and that demands a permanent vocation of public service. Personally, I always appreciate and will appreciate your advice, your mettle in difficult times and your ability to seek agreements. You get the gratitude of each of us who are part of the Central Bank of Chile and your name was already inscribed in an important part of its history. Thank you very much Jorge and much success.
text_original: Discurso de Despedida de Jorge Desormeaux Jos De Gregorio Presidente Banco Central de Chile 4 de diciembre 2009 Siempre es difcil escribir una despedida, en particular la de un gran amigo y profesional como es Jorge Desormeaux. Hoy, Jorge termina su perodo de 10 aos como consejero del Banco Central de Chile y durante los ltimos dos aos ha sido su Vicepresidente. Su contribucin al Banco a lo largo de todo este perodo ha sido muy importante, y sus huellas estn presentes en nuestras innovaciones ms relevantes, as como en nuestras mltiples decisiones de poltica monetaria. Fue siempre una voz muy importante a la hora de tomar decisiones y en los momentos ms complejos, su sabidura fue siempre bienvenida. Tengo el gusto de conocer a Jorge Desormeaux hace muchos aos, y ser uno de tantos que tiene una deuda de gratitud con l. Lo conoc por ah por el ao 1984. Cuando estaba tratando de publicar mi tesis de magster, Jorge me recomend algunos estudios realizados por compaeros de cursos de l en MIT. En esa poca nos interesaba conocer algunos parmetros para calibrar ejercicios bastante simples de proyeccin y consistencia macro. En mi caso, mi propsito era estimar elasticidades de tipo de cambio de las exportaciones e importaciones, algo que a Jorge tambin le interesaba. An hablamos de economa, modelos y tecnologa, aunque hemos suspendido los videojuegos. La despedida de Jorge muestra un nuevo paso en la consolidacin de la autonoma del Banco. Jorge Desormeaux es el cuarto consejero que en estos 20 aos cumple un perodo de diez aos en el cargo. Antes fueron Alfonso Serrano, Jorge Marshall y Mara Elena Ovalle. Tambin le toc ser actor de primera lnea en un cambio estructural interno que ha permitido al Banco avanzar a pasos agigantados en el diseo e implementacin de toda una arquitectura coherente con la forma de hacer poltica monetaria, con informacin cada vez ms abundante y oportuna al mercado, acorde con los estndares que se imponen como las mejores prcticas en el mundo. En estos ltimos aos se ha desarrollado todo un proceso de planificacin estratgica, que defini claramente la misin, visin y valores de la organizacin y que es la base para definir los objetivos estratgicos, que son una carta de ruta para que todas las unidades del Banco orienten sus esfuerzos y recursos. Jorge tambin fue parte de la gestacin y desarrollo de uno de los proyectos ms relevantes que est desarrollando el Banco, que es el lanzamiento de una nueva familia de billetes, de la cual ya est en circulacin el billete de 5.000 pesos. Title: Inauguration of the Exhibition "Prat: Facets of a Hero"
text: SPEECH FOR THE OPENING OF THE EXHIBITION " PRAT: FACETS OF A HERO" Jos8e de GregorioPresident Central Bank of ChileMARCH 31, 2010 Lord Commander in Chief of the Navy, Admiral Edmundo Gonz87lez Gentlemen officers of the Chilean Navy Members of the Council Mr. Curator of the National Historical Museum and of this exhibition, Juan Manuel Mart92nez Distinguished members of the cultural world Managers, department heads and officials of the Bank Ladies and gentlemen Today we have put into circulation the new 10 thousand peso bill, the second of a new family of bills that will replace the one that has existed for approximately 30 years. And along with this milestone for the means of payment that are used throughout Chile, we want to pay tribute to who has illustrated and will continue to illustrate this new banknote and who has been a great protagonist of an important part of the history of Chile, our national hero Arturo Prat Chac97n. This tribute consists of bringing to the Central Bank an exhibition that shows a synthesis of Prat's life, which was a preamble to that major example delivered on May 21, 1879 in the Naval Battle of Iquique. "PRAT: FACETS OF A HERO", is the name of this exhibition that we inaugurate today and that we hope will be a new window for Chileans to know other human facets of this national hero who lives in the collective memory of our country. Arturo Prat Chac97n has been the protagonist of Chilean banknotes since 1933, when his portrait illustrated a 100 peso bill of that time. It was also part of the shield banknote, issued from 1962, the 50 peso note that was issued in 1975 and the 10 thousand pesos note issued in 1989 and that we begin to renew today. On this new banknote the image of Arturo Prat is based on the portrait made by Manuel Antonio Caro, a painting that you can see in this exhibition. The exhibition that we are inaugurating is an invitation made by the Bank to approach Prat's life, knowing other areas of his life and that show that he was an exceptional and exemplary person, of which all Chileans are proud. An exhibition that is also part of the extension work initiated some time ago by the Central Bank of Chile, with the purpose of promoting the process of learning and approaching the population about the role, objectives and heritage of the Institution. In this case, a task to link our means of payment with the culture of this country and its richness both in the diverse landscapes it has, and in those who have built its history. It is a task that the Bank has been carrying out since 2002 and that has been reflected in various exhibitions that make known, for example, its valuable Collection of Paintings and also of coins and banknotes. A work that also adds to numerous actions that this institution carries out to bring the work of the Bank closer to the population and among which are guided tours, talks to teachers, a massive contest for students and exhibitions. Until the end of last year, the exhibition "Gabriela: a universal look" was on display in this same area of the hall, with a selection of various texts and writings that testified to Mistral's deep thinking on various subjects and that was motivated by the circulation of the new 5,000 peso bill that bears the image of our outstanding poet. In the east wing of this same hall is the exhibition "Money in Chile, memory of a nation", which brings together a representative selection of the wide collection of banknotes and coins that are telling in coinage and images a transcendent part of the history of our country. Our challenge is to continue bringing the Bank closer to the community through various educational and cultural activities, in order to expand the understanding of the economic phenomena necessary to understand the performance and role of the Central Bank of Chile, and to publicize our valuable cultural heritage, as we are doing today. That is why we have been enthusiastic in uniting the entire framework of the circulation of the 10,000 peso note, the second of the New Family of Banknotes that Chile will have between now and 2011, a sample of who is the protagonist of this. I want to thank all the institutions and people who have been involved in the realization of this exhibition and, in particular, I want to express my gratitude to the Chilean Navy, represented today with the presence of the Commander in Chief, Admiral Edmundo Gonz87lez. Both the Chief Command of Valpara92so, and the Naval and Maritime Museum, have contributed to us with valuable paintings and pieces that can be appreciated in this exhibition. I also appreciate, as on previous occasions, the always attentive disposition of the National Historical Museum that has also made us valuable contributions in original pieces and objects of Arturo Prat and that are part of this exhibition. It is therefore a pride for the Central Bank of Chile to be able to house such valuable pieces that were part of the life of a great hero, a great man, a great Chilean, Arturo Prat. Ladies and gentlemen. I declare inaugurated the exhibition Arturo Prat, Facets of a Hero, which we hope will be visited by many Chileans and that it will be a contribution to a greater knowledge of who left his name inscribed with capital letters in our history. Thanks a lot.

Title: Inauguration of the Andres Bello Exhibition: Humanist of the Republic
text: OPENING SPEECH EXHIBITION ANDRES BELLO: HUMANIST OF THE REPUBLIC Jos8e De Gregorio President of the Central Bank of Chile August 5, 2010 With the launch of each new member of the renewed Banknote Family, the Central Bank of Chile pays tribute to the historical figure who shines each of the denominations that enter circulation. Last week, the new 20,000 peso bill entered circulation, which on its obverse bears the figure of a man who put at the service of Chile all his talent to be a transcendental part in the construction of the foundations in which our Homeland has developed. I am referring to Don Andr8es Bello, an intellectual of the highest level who moved from his native Venezuela to Chile, to make us an essential part of a legacy that covers all of Latin America. A tribute that materializes in this exhibition that we inaugurate today, so that Chileans of all ages can admire the current work of this great Humanist of the Republic. The Central Bank has recognized the figure of Bello since 1998, when he put his image on the 20,000 peso bill, which at that time was in circulation. The illustration of Bello's face on this banknote, which we now call antique, was based on a portrait of the painter Giovanni Mochi, made in 1881, for the centenary of Bello's birth. While on the new banknote, Bello's image is based on the painting made by the French artist Raymond Monvoisin, who portrayed first in the form of a drawing and then in an oil painting in 1844 a 61-year-old Bello when he assumed as Rector of the University of Chile. This portrait that became the best known of all, shows us a Bello with slumped shoulders, which suggests a look of sadness, but with an expression that accounts for a peaceful and serene state, typical of the maturity of life. This portrait whose original is part of this exhibition, can be appreciated by all of you, thanks to the loan kindly made by the Rector of the University of Chile, Mr. V92ctor P8erez. The exhibition Andr8es Bello, Humanist of the Republic, which we inaugurate today, is a new invitation made by the Bank to approach the life of this great intellectual, knowing new facets of his existence and that account for a sensitive man, who together with his outstanding and brilliant contribution, by the way the best known by all, He lived an existence with episodes of deep sadness for any human being, such as the experience of suffering the death of his first wife and 9 (of his 15 children) in life. The contribution and meaning of Bello's work undoubtedly transcends to this day, his legacy in the establishment of the bases of the republican system of our nation in the mid-nineteenth century, translates into fundamental works that I can not fail to mention as the "Civil Code of the Republic of Chile", much of which remains in force to this day; the creation of the University of Chile, undoubtedly a transcendental milestone in the history of our country. His contributions to the study and unity of our Spanish language are also fundamental to this day. As you can see in this exhibition, we must highlight the figure of Andr8es Bello as a public man, senator, educator, jurist, poet, translator; He tirelessly studied until his last days of American nature, medieval literature and even scientific subjects, such as astronomy. For all these reasons, the Bank wanted to make an exhibition that allows to make known to the public, a synthesis of a character not sufficiently known in all its various facets. Also within the framework of continuing with the extension work initiated some time ago by the Central Bank of Chile, with the purpose of promoting the process of learning and approaching the population on the role, objectives and heritage of the Institution. In this case, a task to link our means of payment with the culture of this country and its richness both in the diverse landscapes it has, and in those who have built its history. It is a work that the Bank has carried out in the last 8 years, on a permanent basis, which has been reflected in various exhibitions that make known, for example, its valuable Collection of Painting and also of coins and banknotes. A work that also adds to numerous actions that this institution carries out to bring the work of the Bank closer to the population and among which are guided tours for students, workshops for teachers, a school contest aimed at the whole country and various exhibitions. Until the end of last year, the exhibition "Gabriela: a universal look" was on display in this same area of the hall, with a selection of various texts and writings that testified to the thought of our Nobel Prize on various subjects, and which was motivated by the circulation of the first 5 thousand peso bill of this new family. Later, in March of this year and within the framework of the circulation of the new 10 thousand peso bill, we inaugurated the successful exhibition "Prat: Facets of a Hero", visited by more than 3 thousand people and which had a program of guided tours aimed at students from sixth grade to second year and that was also toured by the almost 2 thousand people who visited the Bank last Sunday of May on Heritage Day. Our challenge is to continue bringing the Bank closer to the community through various educational and cultural activities, in order to expand the understanding of the economic phenomena necessary to understand the performance and role of the Central Bank of Chile, and to publicize our valuable cultural heritage, as we are doing today. That is why we have been enthusiastic in uniting the entire framework of the circulation of the 20,000 peso banknote, the third of the New Family of Banknotes that Chile will have between now and 2011, a sample of who is the protagonist of this banknote and whose presence in this massive means of payment we should all feel proud. I want to thank all the institutions and people who have been involved in the realization of this exhibition and, in particular, express a gratitude to the University of Chile, represented by its Rector, Mr. V92ctor P8erez; the Andr8es Bello Central Archive of the same University; Special thanks to the National Institute, represented today by its Rector, Mr. Jorge Toro and a group of alumni, who generously contributed with the loan of unpublished material related to Bello, which we are proud to exhibit for the first time in a public way. I also appreciate, as in previous exhibitions, the always attentive disposition of the National Historical Museum, represented by its Director, Mrs. Ximena Cruzat, who has also made valuable contributions to us in original pieces and objects related to Bello that are part of this exhibition. My thanks to the Andr8es Bello University, represented by its Rector Ronaldo Kelly, who from September 7 will provide us with a complete documentary that covers the trajectory of Bello through 3 chapters of his life in Venezuela, London and Chile, and whose responsible is Eduardo Tironi. I thank Correos de Chile, for the interesting contribution of philatelic species included in this exhibition. I also want to thank the author of the texts of this exhibition, the outstanding historian Iv87n Jaksic, who provided us with part of his collection of books and publications of Bello, which you can appreciate in this exhibition. Finally, I would like, on behalf of the Council, to thank our Institutional Affairs Management for its great contribution in coordinating and staging this exhibition. For the Central Bank of Chile it is a pride to be able to house such valuable material related to the work and life of Andr8es Bello and we hope that it will become an invitation to know him in greater depth, through his innumerable writings. Ladies and gentlemen. We inaugurate the exhibition Andr8es Humanista de la Rep9cblica, which we hope will be visited by the number of public possible and will be open until next October. Title: 2010 Anniversary Ceremony Speech
text: SPEECH ANNIVERSARY CEREMONY 2010Jos8e De GregorioPresidentCentral Bank of Chile Dear officials of the Central Bank of Chile and esteemed fellow members of the Board of the Bank. Almost 85 years ago, on August 22, 1925, Decree Law number 486 that created the Central Bank of Chile was published in the Official Gazette of those years. The legal document bore the signatures of President Arturo Alessand96 Palma, and his Minister of Finance, Valent92n Magallanes. The creation of the Bank laid one of the pillars of an economic institutionality with which the vertiginous advances of the Twentieth Century would be faced. A pillar that had an important reinforcement when in 1989 the Constitutional Organic Law came into force that turned the Central Bank into an autonomous institution and that governs us today. Under this framework, we are set the objective of ensuring price stability and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. It is in this context where we must develop our work day by day and respond to a mandate given to us by the country, which although for many seems limited or difficult to understand, plays a central role in the search for economic progress. And this has been demonstrated in the current process of vigorous economic recovery, where monetary stimulus has played a fundamental role, and its timely withdrawal is key to the sustainability of growth. Having autonomy is not free. Having autonomy implies, in our case, being an institution with high standards of excellence and capable of giving a timely and broad account of all its actions, always looking at how to contribute in the best possible way to the well-being of all Chileans. Today, 85 years after its creation, we can say that the Central Bank of Chile is a solid, credible, high-level technical institution that is part of an institutional base that allows the country to move towards better living conditions for its inhabitants. Our mission is to nurture, maintain and enhance that credibility. There is the challenge of the work carried out daily by each of the officials who make up our organization. I want to say here that we have more than met this challenge. At last year's anniversary celebration ceremony, we were already navigating the difficult economic scenario that had kept us on our toes for many months. A crisis with few precedents in modern economic history. I told them at that time, that the country had to stay the course in a world that sailed in very turbulent waters, and that it was already We could perceive the first signs of recovery, so we could feel satisfied that we had faced those complex moments and be prepared to continue facing them. That's where we were when the country was rocked by a devastating natural disaster in the early hours of February 27. The earthquake, with its aftermath of death and destruction in a large area of the country, also imposed on us the requirement to keep the payment system running, so that this would not add to the main focus of concern that Chile had, which was the people. The Bank showed that it was prepared to withstand this unfortunate catastrophe. Testing our contingency plans for these events, officials responded with sacrifice and commitment to keep this institution working as normally as possible, on the basis of a sound financial and payments system. The earthquake also put us in front of the task of revising our analyses and projections, incorporating as quickly as possible all the variables that were affected by so much destruction. A little more than a month later, we were able to present the country with a comprehensive macroeconomic report that shed more light on its short, medium and long-term consequences. Having acted promptly, with technical efficiency and with realism, helped us enormously to face the new challenge imposed on us: to initiate a process of normalization of monetary policy, after 10 months of maintaining it at the lowest level recorded in Chile's economic history. Along with this, the Bank is faced with a succession of modernization efforts needed to accomplish our work even more effectively and that will continue to enable us to achieve standards held by central banks in developed countries. The ERP Solution project is in full development, a system that integrates the Bank's management, eliminating repetitive background capture and database duplication, so that they can tune in with other areas of the Institution. The realization of this project requires 20 employees to move to another downtown building, where the Bank has arranged facilities for this group to carry out an intense training process, which will allow the implementation of the new system. In September, another project of high relevance to the Bank will be operational in its first phase. This is the Alternative Operation Site (SOA), which will be located in the Country Club and will make it possible to maintain the Bank's critical activities in full operation, should the institutional building be left without the possibility of remaining in operation. This is crucial to smoothly fulfill the constitutional duty to ensure the functioning of the payment system. During 2010 we have continued with the change of the New Family of Banknotes, with the circulation of the new 10,000 and 20,000 peso notes, associated with press campaigns, advertising and dissemination actions such as exhibitions on Arturo Prat and Andr8es Bello, in the main hall of the Bank. We can feel very satisfied with the reception that these new banknotes have had and that it has its best expression in the fact that they quickly became accepted and reliable means of payment for Chileans. These are just some examples of how we are moving forward day by day. The Bank is a dynamic institution, which does not rest, which is always taking on new tasks and I am proud to say that they are faced with rigor, with professional and technical quality and with a high degree of commitment. It is you who every day assume your work responsibly and you who can share that pride, because it is the work of each one. As every year, today we deliver medals of recognition to those who have turned 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40 years old. Yes, as you have heard, there are three officials who are celebrating 40 years in this institution and who will receive their medals today. This is also a special occasion for a Bank official. In a few moments we will know who has been awarded the Spirit of the Central Bank Award, or in other words, who will be awarded for faithfully embodying the values of commitment, respect, excellence, probity and transparency, which are what the Bank wishes to promote. This award, which from this occasion will be delivered every two years, has been defined by the Council, after a selection process that has considered all Division Managements and that has been proposed among several names by a Committee specially designated for this purpose. Dear Council officials and colleagues, We celebrate this anniversary with the satisfaction of our duty accomplished. In recent years we have faced multiple events that have tested our ability to act with decision and technical rigor in order to achieve the objectives imposed by the Law. We can say that in the face of all these events, the Central Bank has maintained its good reputation and credibility. But this imposes on us the mission of continuing to maintain it in the face of new events that we must face within a world that changes extremely quickly. We have in any case the peace of mind of having a highly committed team and aware of its relevance within the public system to contribute to the well-being of all Chileans. A happy anniversary for all Thanks a lot

Title: Award Speech of the contest The Economy + Near
text: AWARD CEREMONY SPEECH CONTEST "THE ECONOMY CLOSE" November 2, 2010 Minister of Education Undersecretary of the Ministry of Finance Lord Mayor of the commune of Ca96ete Members of the Jury Dear directors, teachers and students of the finalist groups Ladies and gentlemen: For six years, we have been organizers of an activity that gives us great satisfaction and fills us with pride, the contest La Econom92a Cerca, because it allows us to verify the enthusiasm that the economy can produce in adolescents throughout the country, capable of putting their creativity at the service of the practical application of topics that seem complex. This contest brings us directly closer to a segment of the community that is understanding the complexities of society and is able to interpret them. Third and fourth grade students from all over the country internalize, investigate and understand, from their daily reality, economic issues as relevant as the link between the work of the Central Bank, price stability and the welfare of the population, as well as the importance of the autonomy of this Bank and the soundness of the financial system. What fills us with satisfaction is the favorable response to this call. And even more so in this particular year, marked by one of the worst disasters in its history, which obviously altered the school agenda and despite this, gave us a result higher than we expected. This only strengthens our commitment to education in economic and financial matters, as a means to improve people's decision-making, improve the quality of life of the population and make the functioning of financial markets and monetary policy more efficient. We hope that this will be a commitment of the whole country, because as the earlier understanding and knowledge of the functioning of our economy is known, the decisions of its agents in adult life can be more informed and contribute better to the development of the country. In its sixth version, which we close at this ceremony, the contest has demanded a special effort on the part of the Bank. With educational material, prepared from a didactic perspective, seminars have been held for students and training workshops for teachers, to which was added the realization of 5 talks given by Bank economists to students of Third and Fourth year middle, in schools of the Metropolitan Region. 560 students participated in these workshops. Also this year, outreach work was carried out in other regions. Councillor Enrique Marshall led the official launch of the contest before 200 students in the city of Nueva Imperial. 2 Seminars for schoolchildren were also held, within the framework of the Regional Meetings that the Bank organizes to disseminate its Monetary Policy Report, in April in Punta Arenas and in June in Antofagasta. These talks aim to explain the main economic concepts involved in the treatment of the four topics proposed in the contest: inflation, banks and financial system, monetary policy rate and autonomy of the Central Bank. The teacher training program continued, with a total of 6 workshops during the months of January, April and July, with the assistance of 90 teachers from 82 schools in various parts of the country. The good evaluation that the participating teachers have expressed to us, encourages us to continue and intensify this activity. In relation to these workshops I would like to highlight that both teachers of the finalist teams that presented their work today, Mrs. Victoria Burgos and Mrs. Alba Porto, participated in these workshops, which is a more than concrete proof of the effectiveness of this initiative. As for the results of the call for this sixth version of the contest, it should be mentioned that 968 groups of students belonging to municipal, subsidized and paid schools throughout the country were registered. These groups sent 420 papers prepared by 1,564 students from 191 educational establishments. The works were evaluated by a group of 28 Bank professionals, who made a pre- selection with rigorous technical criteria, based on a strict evaluation guideline that considered technical mastery and originality in the practical application of the topics. In the first stage, they classified 59 works in the pre-selected category, of which some of their teachers and students classified in this category are present here, whom we also congratulate for their outstanding results. In the next stage, a second group of 8 economists from the Central Bank, defined among the 59 shortlisted works the 10 finalists. I would like to express special appreciation to all the Bank's professionals who participated in both phases of correction and evaluation, who worked with dedication, enthusiasm and always maintaining strict rigor in the work carried out. The jury present here today, and which I had the honor of chairing, evaluated the 10 finalist works, following this same rigorous guideline, a task not without difficulties, since we find works of remarkable quality and originality. From this evaluation emerged the three finalist groups that presented and defended their essays before the jury in solemn presentations made this morning in the Council Chamber, in a process that could be followed in various parts of the country, thanks to a live broadcast made through the contest website. You could appreciate it. These presentations gave an account of a good theoretical and conceptual management of the finalist teams, allowing us to visualize the development of economic processes in a simple and original way, without losing the precision required in the analysis of the interdependencies of economic agents. Soon, we will know who will occupy the order of precedence of the first three places. As in any contest, there will be a first, second and third place. But you know, teachers and young finalists, that the most relevant thing is to have reached this stage and be part of a select group that had the same possibilities to occupy one of those places. You are already on this path and I ask you to continue on it. His enthusiasm, dedication and application of knowledge in the elaboration and presentation of his work, is a concrete demonstration that our effort to spread the understanding of the world of the economy in which daily life takes place, has fruits that will continue to spread, contributing to the effectiveness of our policies and the well-being of all Chileans. We have in you, young finalists, the symbol of a promising future for Chile. You will be the professionals of the future and who knows if anyone will be part of this institution in a few years. Mr. Minister, Mr. Undersecretary, Mr. Mayor of Ca96ete, invited authorities, members of the jury, esteemed counselors, executives and officials of this Institution. The awards that we will present today represent the culmination of a long process carried out throughout the year, which seeks to contribute to the great project of having a more educated population in economics and finance. I thank all those who made this initiative possible once again, especially the distinguished members of the jury, the guide teachers and students participating in the 420 works submitted; in particular, those who are with us today, as well as the officials of the Central Bank. Each one contributed with his effort, his creativity and his time so that through this contest the economy is closer and closer to the people. THANKS A LOT
