Title: Presentation of the book Financial Stability, Monetary Policy and Central Banking
text: Introduction to the presentation of the book Financial Stability, Monetary Policy and Central Banking Jose de Gregorio President Central Bank of Chile January 24, 2011 It is a pleasure for me to address a few words on the occasion of the launch of the book Financial Stability, Monetary Policy and Central Banking edited by Rodrigo Alfaro, on which corresponds to volume number 15 of the series of books "Central Banking, Analysis and Economic Policies". This series, which started in 2001, has reviewed a multitude of topics with depth and technical seriousness, becoming an important contribution to the Knowledge of economic and financial issues relevant to meetingthe objectives of the Central Bank. This book includes papers presented at the 2008 annual conference. For that dates the financial crisisd1which began in early 2007 with the announcement of Freddie Macd1 Regarding its mortgage portfolioand the subsequent bankruptcy of financial institutions in August 2007d1 had begun to put several economic policy debates in the economic policy debate Issues about financial regulation and the incentives it generated for institutions Financial. The excessiverisk-taking of these firms showed the fragility of a system. Complex and highly interconnected financial. It was precisely the latter elements that generated an environment conducive to the spread of a problem in The market of hipotecas subprime to multiple international financial markets. One of the biggest challenges at the onset of the global financial crisis was the need to improve the financial regulatory framework. A central point in this discussion Itcorresponds to the definition of financial stability, a subject that is explicitly addressed both in the work of Borio and Drehmann and in Schinasi, articles compiled in the This volume. In this area, one of the greatest difficulties for the authorities Economic is establishing an operational definition of financial stability, which is more Simple to implement in the case of monetary policy. In Chile, where we use a Flexible inflation targeting scheme, price stability is defined in terms of An inflation target of 3 percent over a two-year policy horizon and with a Margin of tolerance of b11 percentage point. To achieve this goal, the Central Bank has as its instrument the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR). In the case of financial stability, the authority could base its operations on the basis of of fragility indicators such as capital over total assets, dependence on external financing, maturity mismatch in financial instruments, etc. Without However, these are obtained in a lagging manner and contain partial information from the ifsystem risk situation. Another very important element when it comes to design of financial regulation is the definition of responsibilities and powers for the Maintenance of financial stability. In the case of Chile,the Organic Law on Constitution of the Central Bank of Chile indicates in the third article: "The purpose of the Bank shall be to ensure 1 for the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal payments, and external", which explicitly points out the function of ensuring financial stability. The last crisis and in particular the case of AIG added the well-known term too-big to fail the too interconnected to fail, which shows that the systemic importance of financial institutions are not only related to the size of the financial institutions but also with its importance in payment flows. This volume presents articles which highlightthe importance of interconnections in different contexts. By example in the work of Diebold and Yilmaz the authors quantify the effects of spillage of return and volatility in the stock markets of the region and the U.S. The results indicate that there is a spillover effect of volatility in episodes of financial turbulence. By On the other hand, Segoviano and Goodhart propose a measure of banking financial stability based on market perception of the strength of each institution (CDS) and on the degree of historically observed codependency. This measure does not only include a specific country but also foreign banks which infect their peers in episodes of financial turbulence. The recent financial crisis also posed a major challenge in what corresponds to macroeconomic modeling. This volume includes the work of Gray, Garc92a, Luna and Restrepo who incorporate into a standard model of analysis of monetary policy, a measure of risk in the banking system. Their results suggest that d1under this simplified frameworkd1 the monetary authority can move the border of efficiency of output volatility and inflation. This occurs when the TPM is adjusted by changes in themeasure of risk of the banking system. On the other hand, Cohen-Cole and Mart92nez-Garc92a extends the already classic works of Bernanke and Gertler and Bernanke, Gertler and Gilchrist on the cost of the firm's external financing by adding financial intermediaries and collateral restrictions that amplify shocks on Economy through credit channel. On the other hand, the presence of intermediaries Financial institutions that are restricted by capital regulations generate the channel of the sheetto of balance. In a different avenue of research, Goodhart, Tsomocos and Vardoulakis present a General equilibrium model with heterogeneous agents and whose equilibria allow NO Payment of some financial commitments. The authors havesimilar results in direction to those observed during the beginnings of the subprime crisis. One of the largest Challenges involving this line of research is the heterogeneity of the agents for which characterization at the microeconomic levelis highly necessary. In this line the bank has taken the initiative to raise the Household Financial Survey (EFH). This The project is unique in the region and the information obtained from this survey not only allows understand the heterogeneity of Chilean households, but has improved the analysis of risk of these by consolidating income, debts and assets. The book we present today contains the work of Fuenzalida and Ruiz-Tagle who used the EFH to analysethe Debt at risk held by households. Their results show the most households Vulnerable to unemployment they maintain a small proportion of total debt. In perspective, the 2008 annual conference was organized in what ended up being thefirst of a global financial crisis, although it took place in November 2008, when the crisis 2 It was at its most critical. In fact, in my introductory presentation of that I said: "We are now facing an international financial crisis that many agree in considering it the worst since the Great Depression, and whose origin has state in developed countries, in particularthe United States. Your initial symptoms They are known: accelerated financial innovation, credit expansion and price bubble of assets. However, its development and repercussions are unprecedented." The focus of that conference was on thedebate that exists to date regarding the The role of macroprudential policies and financial regulation in reducing risk of occurrence of financial crises, but also at that time I noted: "It's It is still too early to draw definitive lessons from the current crisis, which continues developing, so we are still in the damage containment phase." Well, some time has passed since then and we can draw lessons. The new Dimensions that have emerged laterthan the epicentre of the crisis have intensified the need to advance understanding of the role of financial markets and financial institutions in the transmission and design of monetary policy. This will be precisely the objective of the annual conference ofthe Central Bank of Chile this year 2011. Although today the financial turbulence has diminished, there are latent risks that must Remain alert to act promptly as we have done in the past. In this The present libro constitutes a contribution to the current discussion of how to face the challenge of maintaining financial stability and the importance of macro policies Prudential. Finally, I want to thank Mauricio Calani, Yan Carriere, and especially the editor Rodrigo Alfaro, for having prepared this book. Thanks a lot. 3
text_original: Introduccin a la presentacin del libro Estabilidad Financiera, Poltica Monetaria y Banca Central Jos De Gregorio Presidente Banco Central de Chile 24 de Enero de 2011 Es para mi un agrado dirigirles unas breves palabras con motivo del lanzamiento del libro Estabilidad Financiera, Poltica Monetaria y Banca Central editado por Rodrigo Alfaro, el cual corresponde al volumen nmero 15 de la serie de libros Banca Central, Anlisis y Polticas Econmicas. Esta serie, que parti el ao 2001, ha revisado una multitud de temas con profundidad y seriedad tcnica, convirtindose en una importante contribucin al conocimiento de temas econmicos y financieros relevantes para cumplir con los objetivos del Banco Central. El presente libro incluye los trabajos presentados en la conferencia anual de 2008. Para esa fecha la crisis financiera iniciada a principios del 2007 con el anuncio de Freddie Mac respecto de su cartera hipotecaria y la posterior quiebra de instituciones financieras en agosto del 2007 haba comenzado a poner en el debate de poltica econmica varios temas sobre la regulacin financiera y de los incentivos que ella generaba a las instituciones financieras. La excesiva toma de riesgos de estas firmas mostr la fragilidad de un sistema financiero complejo y altamente interconectado. Fueron precisamente estos ltimos elementos los que generaron un ambiente propicio para la propagacin de un problema en el mercado de hipotecas subprime a mltiples mercados financieros internacionales. Uno de los mayores desafos que se plantearon al inicio de la crisis financiera global fue la necesidad de mejorar el marco de regulacin financiera. Un punto central en esta discusin corresponde a la definicin de estabilidad financiera, tema que es explcitamente abordado tanto en el trabajo de Borio y Drehmann como en Schinasi, artculos compilados en el presente volumen. En este mbito, una de las mayores dificultades para las autoridades econmicas es establecer una definicin operativa de estabilidad financiera, la cual es ms sencilla de implementar para el caso de la poltica monetaria. En Chile, donde usamos un esquema de metas de inflacin flexible, la estabilidad de precios se define en trminos de una meta de inflacin de 3 por ciento en un horizonte de poltica de dos aos y con un margen de tolerancia de 1 punto porcentual. Para el logro de esta meta el Banco Central tiene como instrumento la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria (TPM). En el caso de estabilidad financiera la autoridad podra basar sus operaciones sobre la base de indicadores de fragilidad como capital sobre activos totales, dependencia de financiamiento externo, descalce de madureces en instrumentos financieros, etc. Sin embargo estos son obtenidos de forma rezagada y contienen informacin parcial de la situacin de riesgo del sistema. Otro elemento muy importante en lo que se refiere al diseo de la regulacin financiera es la definicin de responsabilidades y potestades para la mantencin de la estabilidad financiera. En el caso de Chile la Ley Orgnica Constitucional del Banco Central de Chile indica en el artculo tercero: El Banco tendr por objeto velar 1 por la estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos, lo que seala explcitamente la funcin de velar por la estabilidad financiera. La pasada crisis y en particular el caso de AIG adicionaron al conocido trmino too-big to fail el de too interconnected to fail, lo que pone de manifiesto que la importancia sistmica de las instituciones financieras no solo guardan relacin con el tamao de stas sino que con su importancia en los flujos de pagos. En el presente volumen se presentan artculos que dan cuenta de la importancia de las interconexiones en diferentes contextos. Por ejemplo en el trabajo de Diebold y Yilmaz los autores cuantifican los efectos de derrame de retorno y volatilidad en los mercados burstiles de la regin y EE.UU. Los resultados indican que existe efecto derrame de volatilidad en episodios de turbulencia financiera. Por otra parte, Segoviano y Goodhart proponen una medida de estabilidad financiera bancaria basado en percepcin de mercado de la fortaleza de cada institucin (CDS) y en el grado de codependencia histricamente observada. Dicha medida no solo incluye los bancos de un pas especfico sino que tambin bancos extranjeros los cuales contagian a sus pares en episodios de turbulencia financiera. Asimismo, la reciente crisis financiera impuso tambin un importante desafo en lo que corresponde a la modelacin macroeconmica. En el presente volumen se incluye el trabajo de Gray, Garca, Luna y Restrepo quienes incorporan a un modelo estndar de anlisis de poltica monetaria, una medida de riesgo del sistema bancario. Sus resultados sugieren que bajo este marco simplificado la autoridad monetaria puede mover la frontera de eficiencia de volatilidad del producto y la inflacin. Esto ocurre cuando la TPM se ajusta por cambios en la medida de riesgo del sistema bancario. Por otra parte, Cohen-Cole y Martnez-Garca extienden los ya clsicos trabajos de Bernanke y Gertler y de Bernanke, Gertler y Gilchrist sobre el costo del financiamiento externo de la firma agregando intermediarios financieros y restricciones de colaterales que amplifican los shocks sobre la economa a travs de canal del crdito. Por otro lado, la presencia de intermediarios financieros que estn restringidos por regulaciones de capital genera el canal de la hoja de balance. En una avenida de investigacin distinta, Goodhart, Tsomocos y Vardoulakis presentan un modelo de equilibrio general con agentes heterogneos y cuyos equilibrios permiten el no pago de algunos compromisos financieros. Los autores presentan resultados similares en direccin a los observados durante los inicios de la crisis subprime. Uno de los mayores desafos que involucran esta lnea de investigacin es la heterogeneidad de los agentes para lo cual la caracterizacin a nivel microeconmico es altamente necesaria. En esta lnea el banco ha tomado la iniciativa de levantar la Encuesta Financiera de Hogares (EFH). Este proyecto es nico en la regin y la informacin obtenida de esta encuesta no solo permite entender la heterogeneidad de los hogares chilenos, sino que ha mejorado el anlisis de riesgo de estos al consolidar ingresos, deudas y activos. El libro que hoy presentamos contiene el trabajo de Fuenzalida y Ruiz-Tagle quienes utilizaron la EFH para analizar la deuda en riesgo mantenida por los hogares. Sus resultados muestran los hogares ms vulnerables al desempleo mantienen una proporcin pequea de la deuda total. En perspectiva, la conferencia anual de 2008 se organiz en lo que termin siendo el inicio de una crisis financiera global, aunque se realiz en noviembre del 2008, cuando la crisis 2 estaba en su parte ms crtica. De hecho, en mi presentacin introductoria de esa conferencia plante: Ahora estamos frente a una crisis financiera internacional que muchos coinciden en considerar como la peor desde la Gran Depresin, y cuyo origen ha estado en los pases desarrollados, en particular los Estados Unidos. Sus sntomas iniciales son conocidos: acelerada innovacin financiera, expansin del crdito y burbuja en precios de activos. No obstante, su desarrollo y sus repercusiones son inditos. El centro de esa conferencia estuvo en dar luces al debate existente a la fecha respecto del papel de las polticas macro prudenciales y la regulacin financiera en la reduccin del riesgo de ocurrencia de crisis financieras, pero tambin en ese momento seal: Es temprano an para extraer lecciones definitivas de la actual crisis, que contina desarrollndose, por lo que todava estamos en la fase de contencin de daos. Pues bien, ya ha pasado tiempo desde entonces y podemos extraer lecciones. Las nuevas dimensiones que han emergido con posterioridad al epicentro de la crisis han intensificado la necesidad de avanzar en la comprensin del papel de los mercados financieros e instituciones financieras en la transmisin y el diseo de la poltica monetaria. Este ser precisamente el objetivo de la conferencia anual del Banco Central de Chile este ao 2011. Pese a que hoy la turbulencia financiera ha disminuido existen riesgos latentes que deben mantenernos alerta para actuar con prontitud como lo hemos hecho en el pasado. En este sentido el presente libro constituye una contribucin a la discusin actual de cmo enfrentar el desafo de mantener la estabilidad financiera y de la importancia de las polticas macro- prudenciales. Finalmente, quiero agradecer a Mauricio Calani, Yan Carriere, y de manera especial al editor Rodrigo Alfaro, por haber preparado este libro. Muchas gracias. 3

Title: Some Reflections on Challenges in the Financial System
text: SOME REFLECTIONS ON CHALLENGES IN THE FINANCIAL SYSTEM Jose de Gregorio* * Presentation made at the meeting of the Association of Banks and Financial Institutions, Friday, April 8, Zapallar. President Central Bank of ChileApril 2011 Introduction When I was invited to present at this meeting, I thought it was a good opportunity to discuss some relevant issues related to financial development and financial regulation. We have gone through a global crisis of proportions, with a financial system and an economy that were able to face the problems in a timely manner and emerge from the recession with vigor. Despite our relative resilience, there are multiple lessons from the crisis that we need to look at, and if necessary incorporate into our regulatory and supervisory framework. The ultimate objective of this regulation is to allow the financial system to continue growing and evolving in line with the needs of the country, without becoming a source of vulnerabilities and economic crises. In general, I like to emphasize that the origins of the financial crisis in the US lie in a very noble purpose: to allow many people who did not have access to buy a home to have it. How the story continued is well known and also regrettable. In the end, those who tried to favor ended up being harmed, not only because of the payment problems they faced, but because of a recession that brought unemployment and poverty. People who were not subject to credit were not only loaned to buy a house but, based on increases in home prices, were also allowed to change their car, fix the house, and even have a second home. When home prices fell, something that was not contemplated in the risk assessments, the system collapsed. Noble causes can lead to serious problems for financial stability. This tension between deepening and financial stability is not a phenomenon discovered in the recent financial crisis. In Latin America, and in Chile in particular, we lived it crudely in the early 80s. In fact, a few years ago, investigating the relationship between financial development and economic growth, which usually occur simultaneously, we found that in Latin America in the '80s the economies with higher levels of banking penetration had grown less (De Gregorio and Guidotti, 1995). This is not surprising. In economies with high degrees of banking, the financial collapse associated with the debt crisis was greater and its consequences worse. Recently, the enormous costs of activity, employment and welfare associated with financial crises have been highlighted again (Reinhart and Rogoff, 2009). What does appear to be a great lesson from the financial crisis is the complex interrelationship between interdependence and financial stability. On the one hand, interdependence is central to the functioning of a financial system. On the other hand, it is a powerful mechanism of contagion between countries, agents and asset classes, through which there is a risk that a "one-off" problem will become a systemic one, with very costly consequences for the affected economies. This systemic risk, implicit in an increasing interdependence between financial institutions, opens up very relevant challenges and debates in terms of the most appropriate design of the regulatory and supervisory architecture. In this sense, international experience suggests that a regulatory architecture that can be effective for certain levels of development could lose effectiveness in a short time in the face of increasingly rapid financial innovation processes. It is therefore a risk of lagging behind between regulatory architecture and innovation in the private sector, which represents a challenge typical of financial development. Undoubtedly, the traumatic experience lived in Chile served as the basis for building a solid financial system and strong regulation. It is to be hoped that the world will emerge from this crisis with stronger financial systems and that a renewed regulatory scheme will not be an impediment to healthy innovation. Regulation and Financial Stability High exposure to real estate from over-leveraged banks was at the heart of the recent financial crisis. And we saw this not only in the US, but in Ireland, Great Britain, in the Spanish savings banks and in many of the global financial institutions. Once the housing bubble collapsed, so did many banks, leading to the series of exceptional public policy measures of the last three years that you all know. As on several previous occasions, the vulnerability of the financial system arose from the interaction between leverage (especially short-term) and significant exposure to a pool of overvalued assets. In fact, in the face of a severe adjustment in the prices of structured assets d0 which in some cases led to the disappearance of the ability of certain markets to allocate prices d0 together with the high exposure of financial companies in this type of assets directly or through special investment vehicles, made the collapse of this bubble have unexpected consequences. especially in terms of its magnitude and ability to spread. However, financial history shows that these types of processes do not necessarily lead to a financial crisis. The collapse of the tech bubble in the early 2000s did not cause a crisis of the proportions of the subprime crisis. There is a long list of problems that interacted with each other in the gestation of this vulnerability. A structure of poor incentives in the securitization process led to a significant deterioration in credit policies. Financial products proliferated that nobody understood and that did not adequately diversify risk. Risk rating agencies were unable to assess the risk of complex instruments. In addition, in many cases the existing regulation privileged the purchase of this type of structured financial instruments, neglecting the incentives for a direct and granular evaluation of the credit subjects typical of the business model of the old traditional banking (which to a large extent continues to predominate in Chile). Moreover, in key financial centres, there was excessive reliance on market discipline and self-regulation, and in some cases clear conflicts of interest. This led to a significant degree of apathy on the part of supervisors, who clearly had tools to be more effective, even if some deficiencies remained in the legal frameworks. More recently, several developed economies have attempted to address these shortcomings through far-reaching regulatory and institutional reforms. The financial crisis originating in the United States was transmitted with unprecedented speed through the main economies of the world, due to the growing interconnectedness of the global financial system and a significant lack of information regarding the true financial situation of many agents in this global network. It is worth remembering in this regard the role played by stress tests in the US, and to a lesser extent in Europe, in helping certain markets return to normal. The increasing dependence of many banks in Europe and the U.S. on wholesale markets for financing, and on derivatives markets for risk management, were also central factors in this amplification. Perhaps one of the main lessons of the crisis is the need to monitor not only individual agents through micro-prudential supervision, but the financial system as a whole, in order to detect the incubation of systemic risks and address them in a timely manner. On the other hand, significant efforts have been made to understand the interrelationships between the different components of a financial system, which increase in complexity as it grows and develops. In Chile we have a long way to go in this direction. For several years, the Central Bank has been preparing the Financial Stability Report (FSB), with the purpose of assessing the strength of the financial system, reporting potential risks in a timely manner and accounting for policy measures adopted to mitigate them. In this line of systemic monitoring, since the end of last year it has been coordinating, together with the Ministry of Finance, and with the participation of the sectoral superintendencies of the financial system, the evaluation of the strength of the financial system by the IMF/WB through an FSAP (Financial Sector Assessment Program). In this context of systemic monitoring, in the IEF last December we reported a certain degree of optimism in stock prices regarding their fundamental determinants. As we said in that Report, the systemic risks of a price correction were minimal, as experience showed. It is certainly not the role of the Central Bank to analyze asset prices on an ongoing basis, so this type of opinion is only made exceptionally and when deemed appropriate. However, in the Monetary Policy Report presented on Monday it is reported that both in Chile and in many other emerging economies there have been adjustments in their stock markets. The IPSA showed a decrease of 16%, in dollars and pesos during the first quarter, a fall that is within the average of other economies if the declines registered since the second half of 2010 are considered. Considering a sample of 20 countries, these declines are in a range of 10 to 30% measured in dollars and 7 to 23% in local currency. This has pushed the price/earnings ratios in Chile to levels similar to those in other emerging economies. By its nature, the analysis and mitigation of systemic risks requires close coordination between the superintendencies of the financial system, the Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance. It is in this context that work has been done for years in the Capital Markets Committee, and the Committee of Superintendents. We believe, however, that there is room to formalize a coordination instance for the monitoring of systemic risks, and in which regulatory initiatives with systemic effects are analyzed. In this respect, the creation of a Council such as that proposed by the Desormeaux Commission is a positive initiative. However, we must be very careful in its formation, corporate governance and attributions. The devil is in the details! It is crucial to think of a lightweight structure whose purpose is the evaluation and coordination of regulations, and thus avoid overlapping powers, which weaken the powers and dilute the responsibilities of regulators and other authorities. In fact, as the Desormeaux Commission recognizes and as has been highlighted by the IMF and the OECD, we should move in the direction of granting greater autonomy to the superintendencies, for which it is essential to increase their degrees of accountability. In our country we are making progress in strengthening financial consumer protection mechanisms. This is an important advance, both for the well-being of the users of these services and for the stability of the financial system. In the end, an informed consumer is the best judge of his or her borrowing capacity. However, specialization in this area is important, as financial products are complex and customer protection decisions can have implications for financial stability. In this context, the idea of moving forward in separating customer protection from solvency supervision and regulation is positive, but as long as customer protection is adequately coordinated with the bodies that ensure financial stability. Twin peak models, with one branch occupied with prudential regulation and another on market behavior, and both integrated into a financial stability committee are an example of this type of coordination. Another advantage of a greater separation between solvency supervision and client protection is the exclusive dedication of the solvency supervisor due to the robustness of the institutions under its supervision, especially if it gives it the autonomy and resources to do so. Some regulatory challenges The financial system in Chile has shown great resilience to international shocks and we can affirm that we have a solid, well-capitalized and well-regulated banking system. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we cannot be oblivious to the international regulatory discussion and the need to adopt (albeit pragmatically and critically) some of the modifications that have emerged from the post-crisis international regulatory debate. In many of these modifications we have a good distance advanced in Chile. At the meeting last September, the BIS (Bank for International Settlements) agreed on new capital requirements and established a timetable for their gradual implementation, to be completed in early 2019. The main objectives of these requirements are to raise the quality, consistency and transparency of the capital base, strengthen risk coverage, restrict leverage levels and promote a counter-cyclical capital framework. Although this is an issue that requires a legal change, and therefore is an initiative of the Ministry of Finance, it is difficult to think that in the medium term Chile will not converge at least to these new international standards. For the rest, and as we reported in the December IEF, the level of capital and type of capital with which Chilean banks already operate would exceed the requirements for basic and total capital contemplated by the BIS for 2019. The BIS has also proposed the adoption of quantitative liquidity standards. In this case we are again a couple of steps ahead of the average of developed countries, given the existence of quantitative liquidity regulations as a Central Bank standard. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we believe it is important to review, and eventually improve, these regulations in light of the proposals of the BCBS (Basel Committee on Banking Supervision), the lessons on liquidity risk that events have yielded in the last 3 years and the growing interaction of Chilean banks with international funding markets. Securitization in Chile has advanced, fortunately not with the excesses that were committed in the United States. This is an important development to diversify risk and expand the capacity to grant credit. But this cannot be a tool to increase leverage by taking credits off the balance sheet. It is key that credit originators maintain a relevant portion of the riskiest positions, so as to maintain incentives to collect credits and that the business is not simply transformed into the granting of credits without further scrutiny. In Chile, the regulatory framework and market practices allow for healthy development, but careful monitoring of developments in this area is necessary. In this context, we see very favorably the approval in the MKIII of the legal changes that allow the creation of covered bonds. The figure of the hedged bond allows a "securitization" in the balance sheet, which achieves an adequate alignment of incentives when granting credits. This figure d1which has been very robust in the recent international contextd1 should tend to replace the figure of the mortgage bill that in the past helped so much to develop the mortgage debt market in Chile. Final Comment Let me conclude with a question. In Chile we have seen a process of continuous financial deepening since the beginning of 2000. Part of this process has resulted in the granting of credit to more people and companies, thus increasing their well-being and productivity (Marshall, 2011). However, there is a puzzle and that is why consumer credit rates are so high in Chile. On more than one occasion, exposing about the soundness of the Chilean financial system, I have been asked why, if everything looks like working well, consumer credit rates are so high, and you know what I tell you? That I do not have convincing explanations, because it is difficult to explain average rates of consumer loans of the order of 30 percent and more. We raised this issue some time ago in a Financial Stability Report, and it caused some controversy. Controversy is good when it leads to a technical discussion that allows us to advance our understanding of the financial system and the policies required to improve its functioning. The evidence on the behavior of the banking system, something we have studied in the Central Bank, shows that the transmission of the policy rate to market rates has not been very different from that observed in developed countries. Our evidence also shows that in lending to firms, margins are lower than in most emerging economies, and are at levels similar to those in developed countries, indicating that there is competition in this area. However, if there is competition at the level of credits to finance business activities, at the level of loans to finance housing and in the transfer of rates, it is difficult to think that this does not happen at the level of consumer credits. In particular, given that precisely in this segment there is a greater participation of non-bank agents. On the other hand, it is also difficult to explain spreads in Chile by credit risk. In an international context, the non-performing loan portfolio in Chile is low and the increases in the cycle have been moderate. I recognize that there are several additional hypotheses to explain this phenomenon, conservative banking, fixed administration costs and credit information that are high in relation to the average credit amount, among others. The point is to advance in understanding why these costs are higher in Chile than in other economies. In this way, in the next trip I can talk not only about the robustness of Chilean banking, but also explain in a convincing way, why this phenomenon occurs that generates so many questions. Thanks a lot. References De Gregorio, J. y P. Guidotti (1995), d2Financial Development and Economic Growthd3, WorldDevelopment, Vol. 23, Na1 3, pp. 433-448. Marshall, E. (2011), "Financial Inclusion: Advances and Challenges for Chile", presentation held at the inauguration of the academic year of the Business School of the University of Vi96a del Mar, April 1. Reinhart, C. y K. Rogoff (2009), d2This Time is Different; Eight Centuries of Financial Follyd3, Princeton University Press, Princeton, NJ.
text_original: Algunas Reflexiones sobre Desafos en el Sistema Financiero Jos De Gregorio Presidente Banco Central de Chile Abril de 2011 Introduccin Cuando me invitaron a presentar en esta reunin, me pareci una buena oportunidad para discutir algunos temas relevantes relacionados con el desarrollo financiero y la regulacin financiera. Hemos atravesado una crisis global de proporciones, con un sistema financiero y una economa que fueron capaces de enfrentar los problemas oportunamente y salir de la recesin con vigor. No obstante nuestra relativa resiliencia, hay mltiples lecciones de la crisis que debemos analizar, y de ser necesario incorporar a nuestro marco de regulacin y supervisin. El objetivo ltimo de esta regulacin es permitir que el sistema financiero siga creciendo y evolucionando en lnea con las necesidades del pas, sin convertirse en una fuente de vulnerabilidades y crisis econmicas. Por lo general, me gusta destacar que los orgenes de la crisis financiera en EE.UU. estn en un propsito muy noble: permitir que mucha gente que no tena acceso a comprar una vivienda pudiera tenerlo. Cmo prosigui la historia es algo bien conocido y tambin lamentable. Al final a quienes se trat de favorecer se les termin perjudicando, no solo por los problemas de pago que enfrentaron, sino por una recesin que trajo desempleo y pobreza. A personas que no eran sujetos de crdito no solo se les prest para comprar una casa sino que, basado en los aumentos de los precios de las viviendas, se les permiti que adems cambiaran su auto, arreglaran la casa, e incluso pudieran tener una segunda vivienda. Cuando los precios de las viviendas cayeron, algo que no estaba contemplado en las evaluaciones de riesgo, el sistema colapso. Nobles causas pueden conducir a serios problemas para la estabilidad financiera. Esta tensin entre profundizacin y estabilidad financiera no es un fenmeno descubierto en la crisis financiera reciente. En Amrica Latina, y en Chile en particular, lo vivimos crudamente a principios de los aos 80. De hecho, hace algunos aos, investigando la relacin entre desarrollo financiero y crecimiento econmico, que por lo general ocurren simultneamente, encontramos que en Amrica Latina en los 80 las economas con mayores niveles de bancarizacin haban crecido menos (De Gregorio y Guidotti, 1995). Esto no es sorprendente. En economas con elevados grados de bancarizacin el colapso financiero asociado a la crisis de la deuda fue mayor y sus consecuencias peores. Recientemente se ha vuelto a destacar los enormes costos de actividad, empleo y bienestar que estn asociados a las crisis financieras (Reinhart y Rogoff, 2009). Lo que s aparece como una gran leccin de la crisis financiera es la compleja interrelacin entre interdependencia y estabilidad financiera. Por un lado, la interdependencia es central para el funcionamiento de un sistema financiero. Por otro lado, es un mecanismo potente de contagio entre pases, agentes y clases de activos, mediante el cual se corre el riesgo de que un problema puntual se convierta en uno sistmico, con consecuencias muy costosas para las economas afectadas. Este riesgo sistmico implcito en una cada vez mayor interdependencia entre instituciones financieras, abre desafos y debates muy relevantes en trminos del diseo ms apropiado de la arquitectura de regulacin y supervisin. En este sentido, la experiencia internacional sugiere que una arquitectura regulatoria que pueda resultar efectiva para determinados niveles de desarrollo podra perder efectividad en poco tiempo frente a procesos de innovacin financiera cada vez ms rpidos. Se trata entonces de un riesgo de rezago entre arquitectura regulatoria e innovacin del sector privado, que representa un desafo propio del desarrollo financiero. Sin lugar a dudas que la traumtica experiencia vivida en Chile sirvi de base para ir construyendo un sistema financiero slido y una regulacin fuerte. Es de esperar que el mundo salga de esta crisis con sistemas financieros ms slidos y que un renovado esquema regulatorio no sea un impedimento para la sana innovacin. Regulacin y Estabilidad Financiera La alta exposicin al sector inmobiliario de bancos excesivamente apalancados estuvo en el centro de la crisis financiera reciente. Y esto no solo lo vimos en EE.UU., sino que en Irlanda, Gran Bretaa, en las cajas espaolas y en muchas de las instituciones financieras globales. Una vez que la burbuja inmobiliaria colapso, tambin lo hicieron muchos bancos, llevando a la serie de medidas de poltica pblica excepcionales de los ltimos tres aos que todos ustedes conocen. Como en varias ocasiones anteriores, la vulnerabilidad del sistema financiero surgi por la interaccin entre el apalancamiento (en especial el de corto plazo) y una exposicin significativa a un conjunto de activos sobrevalorados. De hecho, ante un ajuste severo en los precios de los activos estructurados que en algunos casos lleg a la desaparicin de la capacidad de determinados mercados de asignar precios junto con la elevada exposicin de las empresas financieras en este tipo de activos directamente o a travs de vehculos especiales de inversin, hicieron de el colapso de esta burbuja tuviera consecuencias inesperadas, especialmente en trminos de su magnitud y capacidad de propagacin. Sin embargo, la historia financiera demuestra que este tipo de procesos no necesariamente conducen a una crisis financiera. El colapso de la burbuja tecnolgica de principios de los 2000 no caus una crisis de las proporciones de la crisis subprime. Hay una larga lista de problemas que interactuaron entre si en la gestacin de esta vulnerabilidad. Una estructura de incentivos deficientes en el proceso de securitizacin llev a un deterioro significativo en las polticas de crdito. Proliferaron los productos financieros que nadie entenda y que no diversificaron adecuadamente el riesgo. Las agencias clasificadoras de riesgo fueron incapaces de evaluar el riesgo de instrumentos complejos. Adems, en muchos casos la regulacin existente privilegi la compra de este tipo instrumentos financieros estructurados, descuidando los incentivos para una evaluacin directa y granular de los sujetos de crdito propia del modelo de negocios de la antigua banca tradicional (que en gran medida sigue predominando en Chile). Por otra parte, en centros financieros claves, tuvo lugar una excesiva confianza en la disciplina de mercado y la autorregulacin, y en algunos casos claros conflictos de inters. Esto llev a un importante grado de desidia de los supervisores, los cuales claramente contaban con herramientas para ser ms efectivos, an cuando en los marcos legales subsistieran algunas deficiencias. En lo ms reciente, varias economas desarrolladas han intentado corregir estas deficiencias a travs de reformas regulatorias e institucionales de gran envergadura. La crisis financiera originada en EE.UU. se transmiti con una velocidad sin precedentes por las principales economas del mundo, debido a la creciente interconexin del sistema financiero global y a una falta importante de informacin respecto de la verdadera situacin financiera de muchos agentes en esta red global. Cabe recordar en este sentido el rol que jugaron los stress tests en EE.UU., y menor medida en Europa, en ayudar a que ciertos mercados volviesen a la normalidad. La creciente dependencia de muchos bancos en Europa y EE.UU. de mercados mayoristas para su financiamiento, y en mercados de derivados para su manejo de riesgos, tambin fueron factores centrales en dicha amplificacin. Quizs una de las principales lecciones de la crisis es la necesidad de monitorear no solo a los agentes individuales a travs de una supervisin micro-prudencial, sino que al sistema financiero como un todo, en post de detectar la incubacin de riesgos sistmicos y, abordarlos oportunamente. Por otra parte, se han hecho importantes esfuerzos en entender las interrelaciones entre los distintos componentes de un sistema financiero, que aumentan en complejidad conforme crece y se desarrolla. En Chile tenemos bastante camino avanzado en esta direccin. Por varios aos el Banco Central ha estado elaborando el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera (IEF), con el propsito de evaluar la fortaleza del sistema financiero, reportar en forma oportuna potenciales riesgos y dar cuenta de medidas de poltica adoptadas para mitigarlos. En esta lnea de monitoreo sistmico, desde fines del ao pasado se ha estado coordinando, junto con el Ministerio de Hacienda, y con la participacin de las superintendencias sectoriales del sistema financiero, la evaluacin de la fortaleza del sistema financiero por parte del IMF/WB mediante un FSAP (Financial Sector Assessment Program). En este contexto de monitoreo sistmico, en el IEF de diciembre ltimo dimos cuenta de un cierto grado de optimismo en los precios de las acciones respecto de sus determinantes fundamentales. Como dijimos en ese Informe, los riesgos sistmicos de una correccin en dichos precios eran mnimos, como la experiencia lo demostr. Ciertamente no es el rol del Banco Central analizar los precios de los activos de manera continua, por lo que este tipo de opinin solo se realiza en forma excepcional y cuando se estima oportuno. Con todo, en el Informe de Poltica Monetaria presentado este lunes se reporta que tanto en Chile como en muchas otras economas emergentes se han producido ajustes en sus bolsas. El IPSA mostr un descenso de 16%, en dlares y pesos durante el primer trimestre, cada que se encuentra dentro del promedio de otras economas si se consideran los descensos registrados a partir del segundo semestre del 2010. Considerando una muestra de 20 pases, estas cadas estn en un rango de 10 a 30% medidas en dlares y 7 a 23% en moneda local. Esto ha llevado a las razones precio/utilidad en Chile a niveles similares a los de otras economas emergentes. Por su naturaleza, el anlisis y mitigacin de los riesgos sistmicos requiere de una estrecha coordinacin entre las superintendencias del sistema financiero, el Banco Central y el Ministerio de Hacienda. Es en este contexto que se viene trabajando hace aos en el Comit de Mercado de Capitales, y el Comit de Superintendentes. Creemos, sin embargo, que existe espacio para formalizar una instancia de coordinacin para el monitoreo de riesgos sistmicos, y en la cual se analicen iniciativas regulatorias con efectos sistmicos. En este sentido, la creacin de un Consejo como el que plantea la Comisin Desormeaux es una iniciativa positiva. Sin embargo hay que ser muy cuidadosos en su conformacin, gobierno corporativo y atribuciones. El diablo est en los detalles! Es crucial pensar en una estructura liviana cuyo propsito sea la evaluacin y coordinacin de normativa, y as evitar la superposicin de atribuciones, que debiliten las facultades y diluyan las responsabilidades de los reguladores y otras autoridades. De hecho, tal y como reconoce la Comisin Desormeaux y como ha sido destacado por el FMI y la OECD, debiramos movernos en la direccin de otorgarle mayor autonoma a las superintendencias, para lo cual es fundamental aumentar sus grados de accountability. En nuestro pas estamos avanzando en el fortalecimiento de mecanismos de proteccin del consumidor financiero. Este es un avance importante, tanto para el bienestar de los usuarios de dichos servicios como para la estabilidad del sistema financiero. Al final, un consumidor informado es el mejor juez de su capacidad de endeudamiento. Sin embargo, es importante la especializacin en este mbito, pues los productos financieros son complejos y las decisiones de proteccin al cliente pueden tener implicancias sobre la estabilidad financiera. En este contexto, la idea de avanzar en separar la proteccin del cliente de la supervisin y regulacin de solvencia es positiva, pero siempre y cuando la proteccin al cliente est adecuadamente coordinada con las instancias que velan por la estabilidad financiera. Los modelos de twin peaks, con una rama ocupada de la regulacin prudencial y otra de las conductas de mercado, y ambas integradas en un comit de estabilidad financiera son un ejemplo de este tipo de coordinacin. Otra ventaja de una mayor separacin entre la supervisin de solvencia y la proteccin al cliente es la dedicacin exclusiva del supervisor de solvencia por la robustez de las instituciones bajo su fiscalizacin, en especial si le otorga la autonoma y recursos para hacerlo. Algunos Desafos Regulatorios El sistema financiero en Chile ha mostrado gran resilencia a los shocks internacionales y podemos afirmar que tenemos un sistema bancario slido, bien capitalizado y bien regulado. No obstante lo anterior, no podemos estar ajenos a la discusin regulatoria internacional y la necesidad de adoptar (si bien en forma pragmtica y crtica) algunas de las modificaciones que han ido emergiendo del debate regulatorio internacional post crisis. En muchas de estas modificaciones tenemos un buen trecho avanzado en Chile. En la reunin de septiembre ltimo, el BIS (Banco Internacional de Pagos) acord nuevos requerimientos de capital y estableci un calendario para su implementacin en forma gradual, para completarse a principios del 2019. Los principales objetivos de estos requerimientos son elevar la calidad, consistencia y transparencia de la base de capital, fortalecer la cobertura de riesgos, restringir los niveles de apalancamiento y promover un marco de capital contra-cclico. Si bien este es un tema que requiere un cambio legal, y por tanto es de iniciativa del Ministerio de Hacienda, es difcil pensar que en el mediano plazo Chile no converja al menos a estos nuevos estndares internacionales. Por lo dems, y tal como reportamos en el IEF de diciembre, el nivel de capital y tipo de capital con el cual ya opera la banca chilena excederan los requisitos para capital bsico y total contemplados por el BIS para el 2019. El BIS tambin ha propuesto la adopcin de estndares cuantitativos de liquidez. En este caso nuevamente estamos un par de pasos adelante del promedio de los pases desarrollados, dada la existencia de regulaciones cuantitativas de liquidez como norma del Banco Central. No obstante lo anterior, creemos importante revisar, y eventualmente perfeccionar, dicha normativa a la luz de las propuestas del BCBS (Basel Committee on Banking Supervisin), de las lecciones sobre riesgo de liquidez que han arrojado los eventos en los ltimos 3 aos y de la creciente interaccin de bancos chilenos con mercados de fondeo internacionales. La securitizacin en Chile ha avanzado, afortunadamente no con los excesos que se cometieron en Estados Unidos. Este es un desarrollo importante para diversificar el riesgo y ampliar la capacidad de otorgar crditos. Pero esto no puede ser una herramienta para aumentar el apalancamiento sacando crditos del balance. Es clave que los originadores del crdito mantengan una porcin relevante de las posiciones ms riesgosas, de manera de mantener los incentivos a cobrar los crditos y que el negocio no se transforme simplemente en el otorgamiento de crditos sin mayor escrutinio. En Chile el marco regulatorio y las prcticas de mercado permiten un desarrollo saludable, pero es necesario hacer un monitoreo cuidadoso de los desarrollos en este mbito. En este contexto, vemos muy favorablemente la aprobacin en el MKIII de los cambios legales que permiten la creacin de bonos cubiertos. La figura del bono cubierto permite una securitizacin en el balance, con lo que se logra una adecuada alineacin de incentivos a la hora de otorgar crditos. Esta figura que se ha mostrado muy robusta en el contexto internacional reciente debiese tender a reemplazar la figura de la letra hipotecaria que en el pasado tanto ayud a desarrollar el mercado de deuda hipotecaria en Chile. Comentario Final Permtanme concluir con una pregunta. En Chile hemos visto un proceso de profundizacin financiera continuo desde comienzos del 2000. Parte de este proceso se ha traducido en el otorgamiento de crditos a ms personas y empresas, aumentando de esta manera su bienestar y productividad (Marshall, 2011). No obstante existe un puzzle y es por qu las tasas de crditos de consumo son tan elevadas en Chile. En ms de alguna vez, exponiendo sobre la solidez del sistema financiero chileno me han preguntado por qu si todo se ve funcionando bien, las tasas de crditos de consumo son tan altas, y saben qu les digo? Que no tengo explicaciones convincentes, porque es difcil explicar tasas promedio de crditos de consumo del orden de 30 por ciento y ms. Este tema lo levantamos hace algn tiempo en un Informe de Estabilidad Financiera, y caus cierta controversia. Es buena la controversia cuando lleva a una discusin tcnica que permite avanzar en nuestra comprensin del sistema financiero y de las polticas requeridas para mejorar su funcionamiento. La evidencia sobre el comportamiento del sistema bancario, algo que hemos estudiado en el Banco Central, muestra que la transmisin de la tasa de poltica monetaria a las tasas de mercado no ha sido muy distinta de la observada en los pases desarrollados. Nuestra evidencia tambin muestra que en el crdito a las empresas los mrgenes son menores que en la mayora de las economas emergentes, y se ubican en niveles similares a los de los pases desarrollados, denotando que existe competencia en este mbito. Con todo, si existe competencia a nivel de crditos para financiar actividades empresariales, a nivel de prstamos para financiar viviendas y en traspaso de tasas, es difcil pensar que esto no ocurra a nivel de crditos de consumo. En especial, dado que justamente en este segmento existe una mayor participacin de agentes no bancarios. Por otra parte, tambin es difcil explicar los spreads en Chile por riesgo de crdito. En un contexto internacional, la cartera vencida en Chile es baja y las alzas en el ciclo han sido moderadas. Reconozco que existen varias hiptesis adicionales para explicar este fenmeno, una banca conservadora, costos fijos de administracin e informacin de los crditos que son altos en relacin con el monto del crdito promedio, entre otros. El punto es avanzar en entender por qu estos costos son porcentualmente ms altos en Chile que en otras economas. De esta manera, en el prximo viaje puedo hablar no solo de la robustez de la banca chilena, sino que explicar en forma convincente, el por qu ocurre este fenmeno que tantas preguntas genera. Muchas gracias. Referencias De Gregorio, J. y P. Guidotti (1995), Financial Development and Economic Growth, WorldDevelopment, Vol. 23, N 3, pp. 433-448. Marshall, E. (2011), Inclusin Financiera: Avances y Desafos para Chile, exposicin efectuada en la inauguracin del ao acadmico del la Escuela de Negocios de la Universidad de Via del Mar, 1 de abril. Reinhart, C. y K. Rogoff (2009), This Time is Different; Eight Centuries of Financial Folly, Princeton University Press, Princeton, NJ.

Title: Declaration
text: Statement by the Honorable Jos8e De Gregorio Governor of the Central Bank of Chile Speaking on behalf of the Southern Cone Countries of Latin America International Monetary and Financial Committee Meeting Washington, DC, April 16, 2011 The world economy is growing unevenly and is subject to many tensions. Most advanced economies (AE) are still recovering from the crisis and have weak fiscal positions. In contrast, emerging market economies (EM) have been growing strongly and some of them face the need to prevent overheating. At a global level, the buoyancy of EMs has contributed to higher commodity prices. This poses significant challenges to the membership and also to the IMF. How to keep bilateral and multilateral surveillance relevant under current circumstances, and how to ensure a well-functioning International Monetary System (IMS) going forward are key issues we currently face. I. Global Rebalancing: Policy Challenges High commodity prices and risks of overheating in some parts of the world suggest that the recovery phase has ended in several economies. Although growth remains markedly uneven, and thus appropriate policies differ according to country circumstances, there is a case for further moderation of the fiscal stance. In those AEs with high public debt burdens, short- term negative effects of fiscal consolidation on aggregate demand might be inevitable, but the trade-off between short-term gain and long-term pain will become increasingly unpalatable. In other economies where high growth and inflation are testing macroeconomic stabilization, a shift towards a more neutral fiscal stance should lessen the burden on monetary policy, and mitigate the risk of policy inconsistencies. However, given the rigidities in fiscal policy implementation, monetary policy adjustments geared towards price stability and sustainable growth should not be delayed. More debated tools are intervention in the foreign exchange market and the use of capital account policies. Regarding the former, its monetary effects should be sterilized, so as to shield the conduct of monetary policy, and should not limit real exchange rate adjustments in accordance with fundamentals. Economies with risks of internal overheating and structural surpluses in external accounts should allow their real exchange rate to appreciate as part of the adjustment. Regarding capital account policies, they can play both a macroeconomic role, if they succeed in reducing current account deficits and buoyant domestic demand, and a macro-prudential role, if they help avoid the build-up of financial vulnerabilities. However, their actual effectiveness in these areas is still a matter of debate. Apart from limitations to their effectiveness, capital controls bring about clear distortions, such as redirecting capital inflows from regulated segments of the financial system to unregulated ones, fostering the shadow banking system, and increasing market segmentation in terms of access to finance across households and firms. II. Implications for Surveillance Current global developments have a bearing for the Fundd5s approach to multilateral surveillance. Too often we see the divisive discussion on current accounts and real exchange rates take center stage in our debate. We should acknowledge that these are the results of saving and investment dynamics across economies, the true underlying forces driving global rebalancing. We encourage the Fund to include these trends in multilateral surveillance, for instance, by institutionalizing the monitoring of the indicators that it already provides in the context of the Mutual Assessment Process (MAP). Regarding capital account policies, we remain skeptical that eventual surveillance principles can have useful traction now. First, domestic financial systems are widely heterogeneous across countries. Cross-country portfolio shifts can occur through channels, such as cross- border derivative contracts, where our knowledge is still limited. Second, the dividing line between capital account policies and macro-prudential tools is blurred, and it is not obvious that precise guidelines can be usefully applied to this whole range of instruments. Third, history shows that financial integration has proceeded apace, in spite of short-term turmoil, without specific guidance or a structured multilateral process. The benefits of financial integration are strong enough that members will continue to embrace it, at a pace that has been, and will continue to be, dependent on country circumstances. We encourage the Fund to focus its efforts on understanding the actual implications, spillover effects, and distortions brought about by capital account and macroprudential measures. This would go a long way to prevent the collective action problem that arises from policies that spill across borders through financial interlinkages. If all countries apply policies which, at the margin, keep net capital flows constant, global adjustment will be impaired. At a later stage, when sufficient knowledge has been accumulated, the Fund can refine the rules of the game for policies that have cross-border financial implications. Thus, we welcome the preparation of spillover reports on an experimental basis under the Article IV Consultations for the five major economies. III. The International Monetary System (IMS) The financial crisis in core advanced economies led to a significant monetary expansion and a weakening of fiscal positions, putting pressure on the IMS in two related ways. The first is that while the supply of reserve currencies is mostly driven by country-specific circumstances, limited convertibility and flexibility prevail in several large dynamic economies. The second is related to the uncertainties on whether the IMS can provide for an adequate safety net to confront future international financial instability. The Fund is well placed to promote adequate collaboration between the main economic zones to face these challenges successfully. Insofar as furthering the role and changing the composition of the Special Drawing Rights (SDR), or the formalization of liquidity provision arrangements, do not replace realistic global policy coordination and dialogue, these initiatives should be welcomed. IV. . IMF Financing and Governance After the approval of the quota and governance reform package late last year, we support the timeline for implementation by the 2012 Annual Meetings. We welcome the activation of the New Arrangements to Borrow (NAB). We look forward to working with the new IMFC Chair towards increasing the effectiveness of the IMFC. Key elements in this path are to enhance the engagement of capitals in the IMFC process and strengthening the spirit of compromise. Macroeconomic and financial issues might become less pressing in the global political agenda over time, but the IMFC cannot lose sight of their importance. Practical steps that could be adopted are the exploration of synergies between multilateral processes such as the MAP and IMF spillover reports; increasing the number of joint G-20/IMFC activities, including restricted sessions; and scheduling the Deputies activities close to the date of IMFC meeting. Finally, we would like to reiterate our support for the selection of Management under a transparent, open and merit-based process.

Title: Consumer Credit Interest Rates
text: THANDLES OF INTER83S OF CREVENUE OF CONSUMO Jos8e De Gregorio. President Central Bank of Chile May 2011 . Presentation made to the Chamber of Deputies on Tuesday, May 3, 2011. The discussion about the level of consumer interest rates has gained particular importance in recent weeks. In June of last year, in the framework of a more general discussion on household indebtedness in Chile, we raised this issue in the Financial Stability Report prepared by Bank1. Most recently, on April 8 I exhibited this topic in the Banking Symposium, organized by the Association of Banks and Financial Institutions. I was invited to present my vision on the challenges of banking. I addressed issues related to development and financial regulation2. But also, I referred to the high The level of interest rates on consumer loans, which in my opinion requires a rigorous explanation. To understand the sensitivity of public opinion to this type of background, two simple data can be reviewed. First, as of December 2010, there were 2.8 million people with consumer loans in installments. Second, according to the Financial Survey of Households in 2007, raised by the Central Bank, 48% of households in Chile have some type of consumer debt3. The importance of the topic also indicates the need to advance in a discussion that allows deepening the analysis of this dimension of the functioning of the financial system . As of April, the average annual interest rate on consumer transactions, measured by the current interest rate for amounts below 200UF, was 32.9%4. The question is what are the factors that determine that the level of interest rates charged in Chile for consumer loans is so higher than that charged in other operations. The The main concern is that, relative to what has been observed in other economies, the spreadd1the difference between what it costs banks in the market to borrow and the rate at which they lendd1is relatively high in the consumer credit segment. This is what we reported in our Financial Stability Report of June last year5. No The same is true in the commercial credit segment, where spreads are even smaller than those of several developed economies (Chart 1). A much-cited explanation for this fact is often the insufficiency of competition among bank providers of these loans. However, recent studies do not find 1 Central Bank of Chile (2010). 2 De Gregorio (2011). 3 Fuenzalida and Ruiz-Tagle (2009). 4 Corresponds to the current interest rate calculated by the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions, which serves as the basis for calculating the conventional maximum rate. The average interest rate for all consumer loans, calculated by the Central Bank, it was 26% in March. This compares with average rates for commercial operations of the order of 8% in the same month. The statistics of average monthly and weekly rates are in - indicadores/index_db.htm. 5 Page 67, Graph 5. Significant evidence of lack of competition in this sector, where a diversity of non-bank suppliers also participate6. It is also difficult to reconcile problems in competition in this segment with the low spreads that, as I mentioned before, are seen in the segments of commercial and mortgage loans. However, it cannot be ruled out the existence of frictions in the financial market that limit an adequate process of setting interest rates. Although institutions may compete intensely for clients, in some segments of the population the market may not be functioning properly. This could respond, among many factors, to problems of information, customer mobility or regulation. Nor can it be ignored that the increase in the level of banking penetration observed in Chile during the last decade could have translated into some increase in average interest rates. Especially, if one considers that those customers who are currently out of banking, pay, on average, higher interest rates than bank rates (figure 2). In fact, the banking process consists precisely of access to the banking system for customers with less credit history and who belong to categories with higher payment risk. In the analysis of possible competition problems in the granting of consumer loans, it is also necessary to consider the volatility that the economic cycle imposes on the results of this segment. While the consumer credit business is comparatively more profitable in the upstream phases of the business cycle, in downturns there tend to be sharp reductions in incomes and increases in costs. During the years 2008 and 2009, the results of the banking specialized in the niche of consumer loans were reduced to zero and even reached negative figures for some quarters. On the contrary, banks with more diversified portfolios weathered the crisis with fewer effects on their results (Table 1). Banks with greater exposure to more cyclically-sensitive segments also show a slower recovery in their activity (Figure 3). Hence, it cannot be ruled out that higher intermediation margins are a response to this greater volatility. It should not be forgotten, in addition, that this is a regulated sector and subject to fairly strict standards when it comes to the management of credit portfolios. This may have some effect on the spreads charged by banks, because they must be prepared to build provisions and punish outcomes when cyclical conditions so require. For the Central Bank, the level of interest rates is of special importance, partly because it is a relevant element of the monetary policy transmission mechanism. The 6 Oda and Silva (2010 ), Gonz87lez and G97mez-Lobo (2010). Bank influences the demand conditions of the economy mainly affecting the short-term financing conditions of banks and, through these, the structure of interest rates to longer maturities. It is crucial, then, to measure how monetary policy decisions are transmitted to the conditions of credit supply in the economy. Available estimates indicate that the degree of pass-through of changes in the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) is relatively high. That is, when monetary policy becomes more expansionary or restrictive, market rates move in the same direction. They also compare favourably with estimates of the degree of handover. Available to other economies7. However, it is important to note that given the magnitude From the difference in the level of the MPR and the rate charged on consumer credit, it is clear that the level of the latter is determined by factors going beyond the MPR. In addition to its objective of inflation control, the Bank is also constitutionally mandated to ensure the normal functioning of internal and external payments. We understand that this financial stability mandate extends beyond avoiding and mitigating the risks of financial crises, and includes a concern for the proper functioning of the financial system. Part of this proper functioning is access to various financial products by households and companies. Similar to what happened in several economies, in Chile household indebtedness has grown significantly. In the period 2000-2010, it averaged a real increase of 12%8, which reflects a marked process of banking and the development of non-bank credit providers, such as commercial houses. Consistent with this, there is no evidence of significant restrictions on access to credit at the household level9. As a result of this process, the level of debt of Chilean households is somewhat higher than that of other emerging economies (Chart 4). This is not necessarily a sign of financial risk, since it depends on the debtors' ability to pay. In any case, it is estimated that this greater access to financial services by households has not affected the credit risk of the system. The indicators of non-performing loans and bank provisions have remained stable. The increases in the period 2008-2009 were relatively limited, and of a magnitude similar to those observed during the Asian crisis. The stability of credit risk indicators is also consistent with the 7 Becerra et al ( 2010), Jaramillo et al (2009), Berstein and Fuentes (2004) and De Gregorio (2009). 8 In a sample of 30 countries, between 2000 and 2005, the average annual real growth of credit to households was 21% (IMF, 2006). At the regional level, the strongest growth occurred in Emerging Europe, which grew 48% annually in the same period. In Latin America and developed countries, average growth fluctuated around 9% per year (14% in Chile, in the same period). 9 Vella and Ruiz-Tagle (2010). microeconomic household information reported by the 2007 Household Financial Survey. In sum, the financial development of household-oriented services has been favourable. Despite high levels of rates, access to credit has expanded. For this reason, it is necessary to have an accurate diagnosis of the determinants of the level of interest rates, so that this does not unnecessarily affect this favorable dynamic of financial development. This analysis must be very precise in explaining what are the determinants of consumer credit rates and to what extent they respond to them. These determinants include, among others, the risk of changes in the cost of funding due to the process of transformation of banks' terms, the level of risk aversion of banks, fixed and variable administration costs, and the quality of the Collateral10. The credit risk associated with heterogeneity in the behaviour of Customer payment and difficulty in identifying the credit history of some credit claimants is also an important factor. Only to the extent that it is identified what possible distortions in the system lead to levels of rates above those that would result from these determinants can measures be designed that are effective in correcting these distortions. In the meantime, it is possible to move forward with measures that can contribute to a better functioning of this market and that, at the same time, could hardly harm the financial deepening or stability of the banking system. Examples of these measures are changes that lead to more information about consumer debt, with adequate privacy safeguards, allowing financial institutions to reward good payers and, in the process, facilitating mobility between institutions. Another group of measures could be geared towards changes to reduce costs or administrative obstacles for customers to switch banks, changes that are conducive to improving the financial education of the public, and changes aimed at increasing and simplifying the information to which consumers have access by facilitating the comparison of bidders. The law and regulations on universal credits (Article 7 of Law No. 20,448) is a step in the latter direction. It establishes the obligation to offer standardized mortgage, consumer and credit card loans and, therefore, comparable, to all institutions that offer such products. The consumer's greater understanding of the financial product offered is facilitated by the obligation to inform, in a clear and visible way, the structure of interest and credit commissions, the associated expenses and the insurance they must have while the respective obligations remain in force. In particular, it highlights the obligation to deliver to the consumer 10 Ho and Saunders (1981), Angbazo (1997), Allen (1998) and Maudos and de Guevara (2004). the Annual Equivalent Cost of credit, a measure that summarizes in an annual rate the total costs borne by the consumer for the granting and normal service of the debt. It is also important to note that there are proposals that could eventually mean relevant risks to financial deepening. Therefore, I believe that it is not convenient to advance in its adoption without first having an adequate diagnosis of the causes behind high interest rates. This category includes initiatives that seek to introduce greater price controls, for example, by incorporating arbitrary reductions in conventional maximum rates. This type of action could lead to lower-income customers no longer being served by banks and tend to be held captive by unregulated financial institutions or those that operate outside the law. This would expose them not only to even higher interest rates, but also to other types of abuse. It should be recalled that the current legislation does not establish fixed maximums, but defines moving maximums based on the average of market interest rates, conferring on the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions (SBIF) powers to determine calculation methodologies . From the Central Bank's perspective, the protection of financial customers falls within its broader concern about financial stability, which requires continued effort by competent regulators and supervisors. However, it cannot be forgotten that the solvency of banking is also a relevant social good to preserve. In this sense, it is legitimate to discuss the receipts to the debtor client, but without neglecting the receipts to the depositing client. Thanks a lot. References Allen, L.
