Title: Speech Award Ceremony Contest "The Economy + Close"
text: AWARD CEREMONY SPEECH CONTEST "THE ECONOMY CLOSE" Jose de Gregorio President Central Bank of Chile November 9, 2011 The Closer Economy Contest is one of the most rewarding activities in the Central Bank's efforts to bring its complex issues to the community. We have done it uninterruptedly during the last seven years and we have never ceased to surprise by the enthusiasm and commitment with which third and fourth year students from schools and lyceums throughout Chile participate, with a tremendous creative effort to approach economic issues. Even more so in a difficult year, in which they have faced a complicated scenario for the development of their studies. A scenario that made us think that the degree of participation in this contest would be notoriously lower, which finally did not happen. We feel, then, pride. For all the students who, despite everything, took on this challenge and have sought the best way to understand economics and explain it in an attractive way. And we feel pride because in these works we see every year the seeds of the generations that will be called to direct the destinies of the country. We cannot hide our hope that among those who participate in this contest are especially those who will have some important responsibility in the economic destinies of Chile. The contest "The Economy Closer", whose seventh version we close at this ceremony, seeks that third- and fourth-grade students from all over the country form working groups that, under the leadership of a teacher, respond and explain creatively a topic predefined by the Bank, according to its importance within the institutional mission. Students should use everyday language to explain mainly the work of this institution, price stability, the financial system and the importance of autonomy. This year we received about 300 works from municipal, subsidized and private schools in all regions of the country, which were subjected to rigorous evaluations until reaching this final award ceremony of the winners. The contest is always a long process, which takes several months of hard work in which various teams participate. There is a preliminary phase of communication and motivation, with informative talks in schools and special seminars for teachers from all over the country. There is delivery of educational material and guided tours with talks by Bank specialists. After the papers are received, economists from the various areas of this Institution voluntarily participate as evaluators and select the finalist works that are submitted to a final review by a select jury. The selection criteria are especially rigorous and are made on an evaluation guideline that considers technical mastery and originality in the practical application of the topics. It is, therefore, a work in which many people are involved, moved by a commendable commitment to education in economic and financial issues. We are fully aware that this type of education allows citizens to have more tools that help them improve their economic decisions in everyday life, contributing to a better quality of life and a more efficient functioning of our economy. I want to highlight and congratulate the work of the Bank's professionals who were part of all phases of this competition. And I want to highlight in particular the work of the Jury, present here, which I had the honor of chairing. This jury had the mission of evaluating the ten finalist works, according to the same rigorous guideline applied in previous stages, extremely difficult work due to the level of the essays, which had a very remarkable quality and originality. Of these ten finalists, three were chosen, who throughout this morning presented their work to us in the Council Chamber. Presentations that could be followed live, thanks to a special internet broadcast and that could be permanently commented on the Twitter account, which the Central Bank created especially for this contest, in its first foray into the field of social networks. Any Chilean can also feel proud to see the quality of these presentations, the excellent conceptual management of the exhibitors and the ability to present them in a didactic, entertaining and, especially, original way. Soon we will know who occupied the first, second and third place. But before the celebrations, I want to say to all the participating students and teachers who are present here: you have been able to overcome all the stages of the contest. Feel with all the joy of having reached this stage and take that joy to your colleagues, as an example of what can be achieved when you put enthusiasm, creativity and commitment to take on a challenge. We hope that you will be protagonists in our economy, that you persevere in learning, because you will be much better prepared to face the new horizons that life is opening up for you. We will continue to persevere in bringing the economy to an increasing number of Chileans, so that their decisions are also increasingly better informed and that this contributes to the country continuing on the path of development. Authorities present, fellow directors, members of the Jury, Bank officials, participants and guests. I thank everyone for having been part of this new version of the Contest The Economy Closer to the Central Bank of Chile, whose eighth version we will begin to prepare from now. We can have the satisfaction of having contributed another grain of sand to the diffusion of our economy in a part of the new generations that will soon enter the world of decisions. Thanks a lot.

Title: Current Economic Scenario and Outlook
text: ESCENARIO ECONeeMICO ACTUAL Y PERSPECTIVAS Jos8e De Gregorio. President Central Bank of Chile November 2011 . Presented at meeting with the Confederation of Production and Commerce, November 22. I would like to begin by thanking you for the invitation to share with you our vision on the economic situation and its prospects. The world is going through a high degree of uncertainty, something we thought had passed 2010. On the one hand, developed economies and, in particular, the Eurozone are going through a complex financial, economic and political situation. The causes and consequences of the Great Recession of 2008 and 2009 have not yet been overcome. The financial fragility of households, firms, banks and governments remains and has even deepened in some countries. On the other hand, the emerging world managed to successfully weather the Great Recession, but today it is again sailing in troubled waters. These economies continue to grow, their unemployment levels remain limited, as does inflation. But the prognosis is uncertain. The most likely scenario is one in which the world economy will continue on this bifurcated path between developed and emerging (Table 1). Certainly, we will have noises that will be continuous product of the development of the news in Europe and in the United States, but in which the emerging world will be able to navigate without being dragged into a new crisis of proportions. The problem, however, is that alternative scenarios are extreme, and although of a low probability, their realization would have very significant effects on the global economy. Let me start with what is happening in the world. The situation in developed economies is the continuation of the crisis of 2008 and 2009. The high levels of fiscal indebtedness prior to the crisis, plus the fiscal cost associated with the recession and the stimulus plans implemented, the fragile situation on the part of private banks and the high levels of indebtedness of families and companies are still in force. The countries of the Eurozone have had to face problems of different kinds. Some originated in the fragility of private sector balance sheets, as in Ireland. Others, in the weakness of the public balance sheet, such as Greece. And others, with a little of both (figure 1). All this, aggravated by the weakness of activity, the fall in employment and its implications on the ability of debtors to pay, the quality of bank assets and the flow of taxes. There is no doubt that the European situation is very serious. The problem has been escalating from a small economy like Greece, to systemically much more important economies like Italy or Spain. In recent days, the increase in risk premiums is also occurring, although still limited, in other countries. The cost of financing in Europe has risen significantly in recent months and shows no signs of abating, which also feeds back into the problem by further complicating questions about the solvency and fiscal sustainability of some economies (Chart 2). We have seen a succession of agreements and measures that have been intended to be the definitive solution to the problems of the Eurozone, but for one reason or another have not been. The policies implemented and announced have been behind the curve. The July agreement was insufficient, now the October agreement also seems incomplete, at least in its implementation. How much longer it will take to solve the problems and how much Europe can resist without a definitive solution are the big questions. Today, the most likely situation It seems to point to a slow decanting, with agreements that will be taken to the extent of the problem faced. The European problem has two dimensions. On the one hand, it is a major crisis of confidence. Such events can cause economies that have a stable situation to be destabilized simply by a deterioration in confidence, for example, by the inability of the authorities to make appropriate decisions. This gives rise to what economists call multiple equilibria. The solution in this case is to take large-scale measures, for example guarantees for all European public debt, to restore confidence. If the economy moves toward a "good" equilibrium, the cost of both the solution and the effects of the crisis are lower. On the contrary, the cost is increasing. The fundamental problems affecting this region, which also require a clear path of solution in order to regain confidence, cannot be ignored. Some economies have very high levels of public and private debt, financial systems exposed to high-risk assets. Likewise, the asymmetries of competitiveness and growth among the economies of the region are also important. The same applies to the institutional and political constraints to face a crisis like the recent one. Nor can a messy solution be ruled out. This could start with the default of some country, the fall of some banks, and the potential exit of some economy from the euro. But just imagining what this mega crisis would be, largely anticipated, makes it difficult to think that in the face of this danger extreme measures are not adopted to avoid it. As a result, these extreme risks are unlikely to materialize today, but a gradual and prolonged deterioration in Europe is highly likely. It seems that the tunnel is long. In the United States, unlike in Europe, the market consensus is that the economy will continue to grow at low rates for an extended period. The problem, without a doubt, is the lack of tools to stimulate growth. Monetary policy reached the limit of its conventional instruments a long time ago. Unconventional tools have continued to expand, but their effectiveness is limited. Fiscal policy has no room for manoeuvre. We already witnessed in the middle of the year the difficult discussion on the extension of the debt limit. Before the end of the year, arrangements should be made for the evolution of the special fiscal stimulus measures still in place, as well as for the size and composition of the medium-term fiscal adjustment. The results remain to be seen. In the emerging world, economies, in general, grow at rates in line with their trend, inflation is under control, but they face numerous challenges. The first is whether they will be able to keep growing to their potential in a scenario where the developed world grows very slowly. So far, the traction that China imposes on the world economy has made it possible to avoid the lower demand from the developed world. But that traction is not infinite and there are also doubts about the strength of growth and the Chinese financial system. Other emerging economies of significant size, such as Brazil, are already showing clearer indications of a slowdown in their activity. For now, developments in commodity prices seem to indicate that a marked slowdown in growth in the emerging world is not in sight anytime soon. Another major challenge comes from managing a scenario in which developed economies remain depressed for a long time, with emerging economies continuing to grow at a reasonable pace. In this scenario, the emerging world is likely to face a significant inflow of capital, with all the implications it has for the management of macroeconomic policies. However, this scenario is not imminent and will occur only to the extent that Europe's financial tensions dissipate, thus reducing risk aversion and seeking refuge by international investors. Beyond all the speculations we can make about what will happen in the world, without a doubt what ultimately interests us is what will happen to our economy. So far, the effects of the situation in Europe do not seem to be too decisive in the behavior of the national economy, but without a doubt its intensification will begin to be felt throughout the world and also in Chile. The data for the third quarter showed an economy growing at rates slightly below 5% per year, with a slowing quarter-over-quarter expansion, which is part of the normal and healthy convergence towards growth rates in line with the trend. In the first half of the year, we saw much higher annual expansion rates, but in which the impact of comparing with the months in which activity was affected by the earthquake and tsunami of 2010 had a lot to do with it. The data for the third quarter also highlights the sustained strength of domestic spending. Private consumption, especially durable goods, and investment had high annual growth rates and increasing dynamism (Chart 3). In the inflationary sphere, short-term fluctuations have been influenced by the behavior of fuels and some foods, including the effect of the depreciation of the peso. Market expectations anticipate that we will close the year with inflation somewhat above what we expected in September, but within the tolerance range of the inflation target. Beyond these short-term fluctuations, inflation expectations have remained around the target over the relevant monetary policy horizon. In another area, the money and financial markets have functioned normally, although with greater volatility in the exchange rate and the stock market, which has been common in all economies of the world. A relevant question is what is the role of monetary policy at this juncture. To answer it, it is interesting to go back a little in time. At the beginning of the year, the inflationary outlook was more complex due to the increase in international food and oil prices, in addition to a closure of capacity slacks more than fast than expected. Inflation expectations rose rapidly and monetary policy reacted strongly to this scenario, bringing the MPR to normal ranges by mid-year. Then, the containment of inflationary pressures and the worsening of the external situation led to a pause in the adjustments of the MPR. Finally, in August the end of the rate hike cycle was announced, and then, in October, we indicated that, if the problems of advanced economies continue and this had consequences in the domestic scenario, the monetary policy rate could be adjusted downwards. The option of maintaining the MPR has the advantage of allowing time for the external situation to decline, as well as to be able to evaluate the intensity of its effects on the Chilean economy as well as the persistence of recent inflationary news. In addition, the starting point is relevant, due to the boost that the Chilean economy previously brought, the closing of the capacity gap and narrower conditions in the labor market. So far, it is difficult to distinguish the effects of the lower external impulse on the Chilean economy, because they occur in line with a gradual convergence of growth that we already anticipated. As I mentioned, recent activity and demand data indicate that the economy has evolved around what was projected in September, despite the worsening external. At the same time, medium-term inflation expectations remain around the target. There are always risks of making mistakes when making a decision. But experience has taught us the importance of maintaining the credibility of monetary policy. A monetary policy tightening that is not well-founded and not credible risks being counterproductive in its impact on the economy and inflation expectations. The experience of 2008 and 2009 is important in this area. At that time, we could have lowered the rate a couple of months earlier, but the very high inflation and still uncertain economic outlook would have diminished the credibility of that monetary policy. In that context, a rate cut would have ended up being slower and less effective. On the contrary, once we were certain of the seriousness of the situation, the MPR was reduced with unprecedented strength: 500 basis points in just two meetings and 775 basis points within six months. Moreover, as we have reiterated in recent months, changes in the monetary impulse are not only measured by movements in the MPR, the shorter-term rate, but by changes in the entire rate structure. In this sense, the removal of the contractionary bias that monetary policy had until August and the changes in the international scenario have reduced long-term interest rates in Chile, which reduces financial costs. In any case, its most recent developments are influenced by external events and changes in the perception of monetary policy (Graph 4). The evaluation that the market makes about the Chilean economy and, especially, what our future actions will be has also been gradually adjusted, something that has been more marked in the expectations that are extracted from financial prices. In the weeks immediately following the situation in Europe worsened, market prices and analysts' opinions began to incorporate significant and immediate cuts in the MPR. Today, the magnitude of these changes has been reduced and their timing has been postponed (Figure 5). The macroeconomic scenario we face is complex. The situation in advanced economies is complicated and in Europe it is very serious. What we consider most likely today is that we will continue to navigate in troubled waters for an extended time, but with a Chilean economy well prepared to face them. In this context, as I pointed out, it is within the options that a greater monetary impulse is needed than the current one. In any case, it is something that must be followed carefully. There are also alternative scenarios whose realization would entail significant costs, and in which the monetary policy reaction should be much more significant. Today, however, such situations are less likely to materialize. The important thing, however, is that whatever scenario we face, the Chilean economy, and monetary policy in particular, have the tools, flexibility and willingness to reduce the costs of a more negative external environment. Quisiera comenzar agradeciendo la invitacin para compartir con ustedes nuestra visin sobre la coyuntura econmica y sus perspectivas. El mundo atraviesa por un elevado grado de incertidumbre, algo que pensbamos superado el 2010. Por un lado, las economas desarrolladas y, en particular, la Eurozona atraviesan por una compleja situacin financiera, econmica y poltica. Las causas y consecuencias de la Gran Recesin del 2008 y 2009 an no han sido superadas. La fragilidad financiera de hogares, empresas, bancos y gobiernos se mantiene e incluso se ha profundizado en algunos pases. Por otro lado, el mundo emergente logr sortear con xito la Gran Recesin, pero hoy navega nuevamente en aguas turbulentas. Estas economas siguen creciendo, sus niveles de desempleo se mantienen acotados, lo mismo que la inflacin. Pero el pronstico es incierto. El escenario ms probable es uno en que la economa mundial seguir en esta senda bifurcada entre desarrollados y emergentes (tabla 1). Ciertamente, tendremos ruidos que sern continuos producto del desarrollo de las noticias en Europa y en Estados Unidos, pero en el que el mundo emergente podr navegar sin verse arrastrado a una nueva crisis de proporciones. El problema, sin embargo, es que los escenarios alternativos son extremos, y aunque de una baja probabilidad, su concrecin tendra efectos muy significativos en la economa global. Djenme partir por lo que sucede en el mundo. La situacin que viven las economas desarrolladas es la continuacin de la crisis del 2008 y 2009. Los altos niveles de endeudamiento fiscal previos a la crisis, ms el costo fiscal asociado a la recesin y los planes de estmulo aplicados, la frgil situacin de parte de la banca privada y los altos niveles de endeudamiento de familias y empresas an estn vigentes. Los pases de la Eurozona han debido enfrentarse a problemas de distinta ndole. Algunos originados en la fragilidad de las hojas de balance del sector privado, como en Irlanda. Otros, en la debilidad de la hoja de balance pblica, como Grecia. Y otros, con un poco de ambos (grfico 1). Todo esto, agravado por la debilidad de la actividad, la cada en el empleo y sus implicancias sobre la capacidad de pago de los deudores, la calidad de los activos bancarios y el flujo de tributos. Sin duda que la situacin europea es muy grave. El problema ha ido escalando desde una economa pequea como Grecia, hasta economas sistmicamente mucho ms importantes como Italia o Espaa. En los ltimos das, el aumento de las primas por riesgo tambin est dndose, aunque an de manera acotada, en otros pases. El costo de financiamiento en Europa ha aumentado significativamente en los ltimos meses y no da seales de reducirse, lo que tambin retroalimenta el problema al complicar an ms los cuestionamientos sobre la solvencia y sostenibilidad fiscal de algunas economas (grfico 2). Hemos visto una sucesin de acuerdos y medidas que han pretendido ser la solucin definitiva para los problemas de la Eurozona, pero que por una razn u otra no lo han sido. Las polticas implementadas y anunciadas han ido detrs de la curva. El acuerdo de julio fue insuficiente, ahora el de octubre tambin pareciera incompleto, al menos en su implementacin. Cunto ms tardarn en resolverse los problemas y cunto resiste Europa sin una solucin definitiva son las grandes preguntas. Hoy, la situacin ms probable parece apuntar a un decantamiento lento, con acuerdos que irn tomndose a la medida del problema que se enfrente. El problema europeo tiene dos dimensiones. Por un lado, es una gran crisis de confianza. Este tipo de eventos puede hacer que economas que tienen una situacin estable se desestabilicen simplemente por un deterioro de la confianza, por ejemplo, por la incapacidad de las autoridades de tomar decisiones apropiadas. Esto da origen a los que los economistas llamamos equilibrios mltiples. La solucin en este caso es tomar medidas de gran magnitud, por ejemplo garantas a toda la deuda pblica europea, que permitan recuperar la confianza. Si la economa se mueve hacia un equilibrio bueno, el costo tanto de la solucin como los efectos de la crisis es menor. El caso contrario, el costo es cada vez mayor. No se pueden ignorar los problemas fundamentales que afectan a esta regin, y que tambin requieren de un camino de solucin claro para recuperar la confianza. Algunas economas tienen niveles de deuda pblica y privada muy elevados, sistemas financieros expuestos a activos de alto riesgo. Asimismo, tambin son importantes las asimetras de competitividad y crecimiento entre las economas de la regin. Lo mismo, las limitaciones institucionales y polticas para enfrentar una crisis como la reciente. Tampoco se puede descartar una solucin desordenada. Esta podra partir por el default de algn pas, la cada de algunos bancos, y la potencial salida de alguna economa del euro. Pero solo imaginar en lo que sera esta mega crisis, en gran parte anticipada, hace difcil pensar que ante dicho peligro no se adopten medidas extremas para evitarlo. Por ello, hoy es poco probable que esos riesgos extremos se concreten, pero un deterioro gradual y prolongado de Europa es altamente probable. Parece que el tnel es largo. En Estados Unidos, a diferencia de Europa, el consenso de mercado apunta a que la economa se mantendr creciendo a tasas bajas por un periodo prolongado. El problema, sin duda, es la falta de herramientas que permitan estimular el crecimiento. La poltica monetaria lleg al lmite de sus instrumentos convencionales hace ya largo tiempo. Las herramientas no convencionales se han seguido expandiendo, pero su efectividad es limitada. La poltica fiscal no tiene espacio de maniobra. Ya fuimos testigos a mediados de ao de la difcil discusin sobre la ampliacin del lmite de deuda. Antes de fin de ao, deben establecerse acuerdos para la evolucin de las medidas especiales de estmulo fiscal que an estn vigentes, as como para la magnitud y composicin del ajuste fiscal de mediano plazo. Los resultados estn por verse. En el mundo emergente, las economas, en general, crecen a tasas acordes con su tendencia, la inflacin est bajo control, pero enfrentan numerosos desafos. El primero, es si sern capaces mantenerse creciendo a su potencial en un escenario en que el mundo desarrollado crezca muy lentamente. Hasta ahora, la traccin que China le impone a la economa mundial ha permitido sortear la menor demanda desde el mundo desarrollado. Pero esa traccin no es infinita y tambin existen dudas sobre la fortaleza del crecimiento y del sistema financiero chino. Otras economas emergentes de tamao relevante, como Brasil, ya muestran indicaciones ms claras de una desaceleracin de su actividad. Por ahora, la evolucin de los precios de las materias primas parece indicar que no se avizora en lo inmediato una desaceleracin marcada del crecimiento del mundo emergente. Otro desafo importante proviene del manejo de un escenario en que las economas desarrolladas se mantengan deprimidas por largo tiempo, con economas emergentes que sigan creciendo a un ritmo razonable. En ese escenario, es probable que el mundo emergente enfrente una entrada importante de flujos de capital, con todas las implicancias que tiene para el manejo de las polticas macroeconmicas. No obstante, este escenario no es inminente y ocurrir solo en la medida que las tensiones financieras de Europa se disipen, reduciendo as la aversin al riesgo y la bsqueda de refugio por parte de los inversionistas internacionales. Ms all de todas las especulaciones que podemos hacer sobre qu suceder en el mundo, sin duda que lo que al final nos interesa es qu suceder con nuestra economa. Hasta ahora, los efectos de la situacin en Europa no parecen ser demasiado determinantes en el comportamiento de la economa nacional, pero sin lugar a dudas su intensificacin se empezar a sentir en todo el mundo y tambin en Chile. Los datos del tercer trimestre mostraron una economa creciendo a tasas algo por debajo de 5% anual, con una velocidad de expansin trimestre a trimestre que va en descenso, lo que forma parte de la normal y sana convergencia hacia tasas de crecimiento acordes con la tendencia. En el primer semestre, vimos tasas de expansin anual muy superiores, pero en las que el impacto de compararse con los meses en que la actividad estuvo afectada por el terremoto y maremoto del 2010 tuvo mucho que ver. Resalta tambin de los datos del tercer trimestre la sostenida fortaleza del gasto interno. El consumo privado, especialmente el de bienes durables, y la inversin tuvieron tasas de expansin anual altas y con un dinamismo en aumento (grfico 3). En el mbito inflacionario, las fluctuaciones de corto plazo han estado influidas por el comportamiento de los combustibles y de algunos alimentos, incluyendo el efecto de la depreciacin del peso. Las expectativas de mercado anticipan que cerraremos el ao con una inflacin algo por sobre la que esperbamos en septiembre, pero dentro del rango de tolerancia de la meta de inflacin. Ms all de estas fluctuaciones de corto plazo, las expectativas de inflacin se han mantenido en torno a la meta en el horizonte relevante de poltica monetaria. En otro mbito, los mercados monetarios y financieros han funcionado con normalidad, aunque con mayor volatilidad en el tipo de cambio y la bolsa, lo que ha sido comn en todas las economas del mundo. Una pregunta relevante es cul es el rol de la poltica monetaria en esta coyuntura. Para responderla, es interesante volver un poco atrs en el tiempo. A comienzos de ao, el panorama inflacionario era ms complejo por el aumento en los precios internacionales de los alimentos y el petrleo, a lo que se sumaba un cierre de las holguras de capacidad ms rpido que lo previsto. Las expectativas de inflacin aumentaron rpidamente y la poltica monetaria reaccion con firmeza ante dicho escenario, llevando la TPM a rangos normales hacia mediados de ao. Luego, la contencin de las presiones inflacionarias y el agravamiento de la situacin externa llevaron a realizar una pausa en los ajustes de la TPM. Finalmente, en agosto se anunci el fin del ciclo de alza de la tasa y luego, en octubre, indicamos que, de continuar los problemas de las economas avanzadas y ello tuviera consecuencias en el escenario interno, la tasa de poltica monetaria podra ajustarse a la baja. La opcin de mantener la TPM tiene como ventaja dar tiempo para que la situacin externa decante, lo mismo que para poder evaluar la intensidad de sus efectos en la economa chilena as como la persistencia de las recientes noticias inflacionarias. Adems el punto de partida es relevante, por el impulso que traa previamente la economa chilena, el cierre de la brecha de capacidad y condiciones ms estrechas en el mercado laboral. Hasta ahora, es difcil distinguir los efectos del menor impulso externo sobre la economa chilena, porque ocurren en consonancia con una gradual convergencia del crecimiento que ya preveamos. Como lo mencion, los datos recientes de actividad y demanda indican que la economa ha evolucionado en torno a lo proyectado en septiembre, a pesar del empeoramiento externo. A su vez, las expectativas de inflacin de mediano plazo se mantienen en torno a la meta. Siempre existen riesgos de equivocarse al tomar una decisin. Pero la experiencia nos ha enseado la importancia de mantener la credibilidad de la poltica monetaria. Un ajuste de la poltica monetaria que no est bien fundamentado y no es creble corre el riesgo de ser contraproducente en su impacto sobre la economa y las expectativas inflacionarias. La experiencia del 2008 y 2009 es importante en este mbito. En esa poca, podramos haber bajado la tasa un par de meses antes, pero la muy alta inflacin y perspectivas econmicas an inciertas habran restado credibilidad a esa poltica monetaria. En ese contexto, una baja de tasas hubiera terminado siendo ms lenta y menos efectiva. Por el contrario, una vez que tuvimos la certeza de la gravedad de la situacin, la TPM se redujo con una fuerza indita: 500 puntos base en solo dos reuniones y 775 puntos base en un plazo de seis meses. Por lo dems, como lo hemos reiterado en los ltimos meses, los cambios en el impulso monetario no solo se miden por los movimientos de la TPM, la tasa de ms corto plazo, sino por los cambios en toda la estructura de tasas. En este sentido, el retiro del sesgo contractivo que tena la poltica monetaria hasta agosto y los cambios del escenario internacional han reducido las tasas de inters de largo plazo en Chile, lo que disminuye los costos financieros. En todo caso, su evolucin ms reciente est influenciada por los eventos externos y los cambios en la percepcin de la poltica monetaria (grfico 4). La evaluacin que el mercado realiza acerca de la economa chilena y, especialmente, de cul ser nuestro accionar futuro tambin ha ido ajustndose paulatinamente, algo que ha sido ms marcado en las expectativas que se extraen de los precios financieros. En las semanas inmediatamente posteriores a que la situacin en Europa recrudeciera, los precios de mercado y las opiniones de los analistas comenzaron a incorporar importantes e inmediatos recortes de la TPM. Hoy, la magnitud de estos cambios se ha reducido y su oportunidad se ha postergado (grfico 5). El escenario macroeconmico que enfrentamos es complejo. La situacin de las economas avanzadas es complicada y en Europa es muy grave. Lo que hoy consideramos ms probable es que seguiremos navegando en aguas turbulentas durante un tiempo prolongado, pero con una economa chilena bien preparada para enfrentarlas. En este contexto, como lo seal, est dentro de las opciones el que se necesite de un impulso monetario mayor al actual. En todo caso, es algo que se debe seguir con atencin. Tambin existen escenarios alternativos cuya concrecin acarreara costos significativos, y en los cuales la reaccin de poltica monetaria deber ser mucho ms significativa. Sin embargo, hoy esas situaciones tienen una menor probabilidad de concretarse. Lo importante, sin embargo, es que sea cual sea el escenario al que nos enfrentemos, la economa chilena, y la poltica monetaria en particular, tienen las herramientas, la flexibilidad y la disposicin necesaria para reducir los costos de un entorno externo ms negativo.
