Title: Trends and prospects of the Chilean economy
text: Trends and Perspectives of the Chilean Economy Presentation by Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, on the occasion of the Inauguration of the Academic Year of the Latin American Professional Institute of Foreign Trade, IPLACEX, Santiago, April 27, 1998 I would like to thank Mr. Hugo Fuentes, Rector of the Institute, for his invitation to participate in the inauguration of your academic year. I would like to take this opportunity to address two issues. First, recent trends in the Chilean economy, including the effects that stem from the Asian crisis. Second, the challenges and prospects we have for the coming years. This exercise allows us to reaffirm the direction of the Chilean economy and ratify our confidence in the policies that have been applied in recent years. I. Macroeconomic trends If we look at the Chilean economy with a medium-term view and incorporate a comparative analysis with other developing economies and advanced countries, there are three trends that stand out in Chile's economic performance: high growth, reduced inflation and external balance. 1. High growth During the period of just over a decade, average GDP growth has been close to 7% per year. With this rate, Chile far exceeds the records achieved by the main developed economies, of 2.4%, and by developing countries, of 4.9%, in the same period. Our country is among the fastest growing in the world in recent years. Chile's per capita income reached US 5,300 in 1997. However, according to calculations made by the World Bank, after adjusting for differences in purchasing power between countries, this figure is around US 10,000, one of the highest figures in Latin America. In 1997, GDP growth was 7.1 per cent and domestic expenditure growth was 9.5 per cent. For this year, the Central Bank has a growth projection of both variables around 5.5%, which means that the economy maintains, in the rest of the year, the current trend of slowdown in the rate of growth of economic activity and spending. It should be noted that in the fourth quarter of 1997 GDP grew by 9.6 per cent, while expenditure expanded to 13.7 per cent. This acceleration is combined with the worst-case external scenario, resulting in a need to slow economic activity during 1998. In any case, in a comparative analysis, the Chilean economy will continue to be, during this year, one of the fastest growing in the world. Gross fixed capital formation has experienced an increasing trend over the past decade, with an investment rate of 33% of GDP in 1997. During this year the country will maintain an investment rate similar to that of last year. This high level of investment has become the engine of growth and is the best sign of the confidence placed by national and foreign companies in the favorable prospects offered by the Chilean economy. Similarly, the national savings rate followed a growing trend in the second half of the 80s and has remained around 22% of GDP during the current decade. The rapid growth of economic activity is also reflected in the labour market. Over the past 10 years, the average rate of job creation has almost doubled the growth rate of the economically active population. As a result, the unemployment rate has fallen, the participation rate has risen, and real wages have increased at a pace similar to the average productivity increase, at around 3.5 per cent per year. In 1997, employment at the national level reached an average increase of 2.2 per cent over the same period last year, and so far this year this figure has reached 1.6 per cent. 2. Low inflation One of the greatest achievements of macroeconomic policy during the 90s has been the reduction of inflation to single-digit figures. The annual inflation rate reached 6.1 per cent in 1997 and is expected to decline further this year to reach the target of 4.5 per cent for 1998. In this way, the present will be the eighth consecutive year with decreasing annual inflation rates and the fifth consecutive that exhibits an annual inflation of one digit. These figures are unprecedented in Chilean economic history, particularly if one considers that inflation between 1930 and 1997, excluding the hyperinflation of the 70s, was 23% as an annual average. It is common for voices to arise in times of economic difficulties calling for weakening the anti-inflationary effort, in the belief that this will solve problems of the economy. Inflation does not solve economic problems, rather it tends to aggravate them. Perhaps it can postpone political problems in the short term, but we must bear in mind that when that happens the same ones who accept a little more inflation then propose to compensate for the lost purchasing power. And there we enter the classic price-wage spiral that led our economy to a great political and social failure. In the Chilean economy there are many economic and social benefits of moving towards lower levels of inflation. For this reason, the Central Bank attaches great importance to this objective and has set annual targets that allow a gradual and sustained reduction in inflation. The monetary policy that seeks to influence the market interest rate is managed so that the overall expenditure of the economy evolves in line with the productive capacity of the country. The application of this policy has made it possible, so far, to meet the inflation target. Another important factor in maintaining macroeconomic stability and a high level of domestic savings is the evolution of public sector finances. Fiscal savings have been above 4.5 percent of GDP over the past five years, and the fiscal surplus averages close to 2.0 percent of GDP over the same period. This is a result of fiscal discipline that few countries are able to emulate. The sustained decline in inflation has been even more relevant if one considers that it has been achieved within a period of sustained growth, low unemployment and solid external accounts. The common notion that reducing inflation comes at the expense of growth and employment has not been true in Chile's recent experience. 3. External balance The external balance is expressed in the moderate deficits in the current account that the country has maintained during the last decade, which on average have represented 3% of GDP according to the new measurement of the Central Bank. However, in recent years this figure has risen to about 5% of GDP. It is important to note that these deficits, including the figure close to 6% of GDP that is anticipated for this year, are fully sustainable and do not represent any external risk for the country. In the analysis of the external sector, it is important to consider a set of variables that determine the sustainability of balance of payments flows. Apart from GDP growth itself, in the case of Chile there is growth in exports, an adequate composition of the capital account, solid external solvency indicators and a capacity to respond to the current external crisis. Export growth in the last decade was 10% per year in real terms, a figure that is above average GDP growth. Exports are an important piece in the Chilean economic expansion of recent years and their growth rate will remain high in the coming years. The composition of the capital account shows two relevant characteristics. On the one hand, during the last ten years the total amount of foreign investment flows has increased considerably. On the other hand, external debt flows have been concentrated in medium and long-term revenues. External solvency indices indicate that international reserves and external debt remain very solid. The external debt-to-GDP ratio went from a level above 100% in the mid-eighties, to a value of 30% today. At the same time, external debt net of international reserves stands at less than 10% of GDP. Among the main consequences of the crisis in Asia on the Chilean economy is its negative effect on foreign trade and national income. The slowdown in the growth rate of activity in the rest of the world, especially in Asia, is generating lower demand for our main export products, implying lower prices, and therefore, lower returns. The degree of diversification by markets that our markets have reached, together with the flexibility of external sources, allow us to reduce the negative effect. Currently, 25% of exports are directed to Europe, whose economy is accelerating; 20% to North America showing high levels of growth; and 20% to Latin America, which still shows interesting growth, but has seen its growth decrease due to the crisis in Asia. The 35% that goes to Asia will undergo adjustments over time, following the reverse process that led our exporters to take advantage of diverting their shipments to the region in the years when it was the most dynamic in the world. The main effect of the external crisis has been a fall in the prices of our exports, which has been partially offset by a fall in the price of oil and lower external inflation. On current trends, the terms of trade in 1998 will deteriorate by around 5 per cent compared with 1997. The decline in the terms of trade is offset by a lower level of national income and, therefore, a lower capacity to spend with own resources and a greater need for financing. For this reason, it is reasonable that part of the adjustment to lower national income be made through a temporary widening of the current account deficit, that is, through financing, since to the extent that the fall in income is transitory, it is not justified to cut the level of spending. It is always prudent to ensure that the use of financing remains within reasonable limits and that its most intense use is strictly transitory, and therefore consistent with the economy's medium- and long-term borrowing capacity. Based on the whole of the antecedents of the external sector, it can be affirmed that Chile's country risk has decreased frankly throughout the nineties, which is reflected in the international classifications and the margins incorporated into the loans received by Chilean companies from abroad. On the other hand, the strength observed in the macroeconomic figures has resulted in a sustained real appreciation of the peso, which reaches an average rate of around 4% per year so far in the 90s. This situation has been propitiated by the significant productivity gains of the economy during these years, as well as by the overdepreciation of the peso in the years 1989-90. The exchange rate levels in the last two quarters reverse this trend and allow to increase the competitiveness of the export sectors without risking the anti-inflationary strategy. II. Challenges to growth In a medium-term perspective, it is important to note that comparative studies on economic growth draw two conclusions that I think we need to remember. First, countries' growth processes are unstable. Having achieved a high rate of growth in one decade rarely leads to dynamic growth in the following decade. Second, the capacity to grow depends fundamentally on internal factors of each country, among which is the quality of institutions, availability of productive factors and macroeconomic stability. Chile is a country that has the basic elements to maintain the path of growth it has shown for more than a decade. However, there are multiple tasks that are necessary to perfect the foundations of this growth. There are challenges that, properly faced, would allow the country's high growth to be sustained. This must be the ordering element in the economic discussion in Chile. Looking ahead, priorities for maintaining growth momentum can be grouped into three categories: a5 Improve the institutions that serve as a framework for the multiple economic decisions made by individuals, companies and governments. a5 mobilizing new resources to support physical and human capital formation; and a5 maintaining those policies that have made it possible to sustain economic stability, such as fiscal surpluses, falling inflation and balance in external accounts; 1. Institution-building As the growth process progresses, the task of improving institutions becomes more relevant. If the country has efficient and flexible institutions, they will tend to produce and maintain policies that promote economic stability and generate resources for physical and human capital formation. Thus, the central challenge to maintain the momentum of the growth of the Chilean economy lies in the improvement of its institutions. In order to make progress in strengthening institutions in our country, we must clearly point out that society's problem is to improve the incentive systems that guide decisions, both in the private and public sectors. The current debate is not whether or not the state should participate in society's self-governing processes. The central issue is to define what safeguards we must take to be confident that the action of the State will be effectively oriented towards the common good. A situation that tends to weaken institutions occurs when their action or the results of it are not directly observable by the agents of society. In this case, the way to improve the incentive system faced by the State is to increase information and transparency about its actions. A modern institutional system is one that acts in accordance with the principles of democracy, the improvement of markets, the promotion of growth, and the principles that endure in our civic traditions. 2. Formation of physical and human capital With regard to the second priority, it is known that one of the main challenges of the coming years is to improve the quality and level of education in the workforce. The government has resolved to address this task through an educational reform aimed at improving educational infrastructure and increasing both the quantity and quality of hours students spend in school. Another challenge of growth is to increase public infrastructure so that it is able to meet the growing requirements of the development process. On the other hand, despite the positive evolution that has taken place in the national savings rate during the last time, it is necessary that the effort deployed be increased over the years, in such a way as to satisfy the investment requirements associated with the process of economic growth, without risking the balance of the external accounts. 3. Macroeconomic stability In relation to the challenge of macroeconomic stability, it is necessary to recognize the effect of the new international scenario on the Chilean economy. According to our analysis, the effects of the Asian crisis on economic activity in Chile are limited. The current account deficit will widen to a perfectly manageable figure of around 6% of GDP; the economy will continue to travel its growth path, but at a more moderate pace with an expansion of around 5.5%, one of the highest in Latin America and internationally. Inflation will continue to decline towards the target of around 4.5% set for this year. Our financial system remains solid and progress continues to be made in making it more efficient and competitive, expanding its development possibilities. Thus, Chile's response to the Asian crisis has been embedded within the global context of its economic policy, whose fundamental objectives are to contribute to the achievement of currency and price stability; maintaining a strong and sustainable external position; the preservation of the internal payments system, which requires a solvent financial system; and the existence of budgetary fiscal discipline, all essential conditions for continued growth. The Central Bank remains vigilant to take policy actions to keep the economy on its course of sustained development and stability. The external crisis should not divert the Chilean economy from its path to price stability, which is reflected in an inflation rate similar to that of developed countries, a moderate current account deficit and discipline in the fiscal budget. These are the elements that allow to form a stable economic environment that facilitates economic initiatives. It is important to frame in this medium-term perspective the discussion that exists today on the exchange rate. Since mid-October, there has been a process of depreciation of the peso that reflects at least three relevant factors. First, the appreciation of the dollar in international markets. This is a factor that causes pressures on the nominal peso-dollar exchange rate, but does not represent a real depreciation of the peso, to the extent that it is offset by lower international inflation in dollars. Second, the greater uncertainty that exists in international financial markets with respect to emerging economies, including Chile, which has changed the perception of exchange risk. Third, the prospects for a more deficit current account balance are offset by an adjustment of relative prices in the real exchange rate that must accompany the reduction in the growth rate of domestic spending. On this last point there is often a degree of confusion in public discussion and I would like to dwell particularly here. Some have argued that there is a strategy of moderating the current account deficit through increases in the real exchange rate that is a substitute for the path of reducing spending growth from more restrictive monetary and fiscal policies. However, this option does not exist in practice. Under current economic conditions, it is not possible to generate a lasting adjustment in the real exchange rate without at the same time reducing the expenditure-output gap. When the economy is operating in the environment of full capacity, the adjustment between reduced spending and rising real exchange rates must be coordinated or inflationary pressures will result in diluting the initial adjustment. Indeed, if there is a depreciation of the nominal exchange rate, while the economy continues to spend at an exaggerated pace, then greater inflationary pressures are generated. In the medium term, it is inevitable that there will be an inflationary resurgence that, in a context of high degrees of wage indexation, cancels out the initial adjustment of relative prices. In this context, the authorities would be forced to act with an even tighter monetary and fiscal policy mix than initially required in order to placate these inflationary pressures. Similarly, it is not convenient for the country to accept a little more inflation in order to achieve a higher level of real exchange rate. In a period of adjustment of relative prices and greater volatility in financial markets, the inflation target and the coherence of policies with it play a key role in anchoring the expectations of economic agents. Ambiguity in this area is extremely dangerous, because it erodes the credibility of policies and the expectations that economic agents form about them. Without policy credibility, the evolution of inflation and other nominal variables that feed on inflationary expectations, such as the exchange rate and wages, and which in turn influence inflation, would be unanchored. Likewise, due to its visibility, the inflation target plays a key role in agreeing on policies that ensure a path consistent with basic macroeconomic balances. This position of the Central Bank, which emphasizes the role of the inflation target as a nominal anchor of our economy, is not an obstacle to relevant relative price adjustments. In particular, the nominal exchange rate has depreciated by around 10% from October to date, in stark contrast to its previous high stability. It is important to note that the Central Bank does not intend to unjustifiably curb increases in the real exchange rate. What is sought is that the trend of the real exchange rate is solid and not absorbed by higher inflation. This policy has better results in the medium term since it seeks to create conditions for an adjustment of the real exchange rate by the most effective way, which is to contain domestic inflation. Needless to say, success in achieving these objectives depends not only on the policies pursued by the Central Bank, but also on the support provided by fiscal policy, especially in periods of fluctuating external conditions. In conclusion, I would like to emphasize that Chile is currently in a privileged position to face the economic and financial turbulence of the external scenario and to project the pace of economic growth of recent years in the medium term. In this way we will be able to fulfill the aspiration of becoming a developed nation. But to continue obtaining results such as those of recent years, we must persevere in the same principles: macroeconomic balances, investment in physical and human capital, and institutional strengthening.
text_original: Tendencias y Perspectivas de la Economa Chilena Exposicin de Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, con motivo de la Inauguracin del Ao Acadmico del Instituto Profesional Latinoamericano de Comercio Exterior, IPLACEX, Santiago, 27 de abril de 1998 Quisiera agradecer la invitacin de don Hugo Fuentes, Rector del Instituto, a participar en la inauguracin de vuestro ao acadmico. Deseo aprovechar esta oportunidad para referirme a dos temas. Primero, las tendencias recientes de la economa chilena, incluyendo los efectos que provienen de la crisis asitica. Segundo, los desafos y las perspectivas que tenemos para los prximos aos. Este ejercicio nos permite reafirmar el rumbo de la economa chilena y ratificar nuestra confianza en las polticas que se han aplicado en los ltimos aos.  Tendencias macroeconmicas Si observamos la economa chilena con un mirada de mediano plazo e incorporamos un anlisis comparativo con otras economas en desarrollo y pases avanzados, hay tres tendencias que sobresalen en el desempeo econmico de Chile: alto crecimiento, reduccin de la inflacin y equilibrio externo.  Alto crecimiento Durante el perodo de algo ms de una dcada el crecimiento promedio del PIB ha sido cercano al 7% anual. Con esta tasa Chile supera ampliamente los registros logrados por las principales economas desarrolladas, de 2,4%, y por los pases en desarrollo, de 4,9%, en similar perodo. Nuestro pas se ubica entre los de mayor crecimiento en el mundo durante los ltimos aos. El ingreso per cpita de Chile alcanz a US$ 5.300 en 1997. No obstante, de acuerdo con los clculos efectuados por el Banco Mundial, luego de ajustes por diferencias en el poder de compra entre pases, esta cifra est en torno a US$ 10.000, una de las cifras ms altas de Latinoamrica. En 1997 el crecimiento del PIB fue de 7,1% y del gasto interno fue de 9,5%. Para el presente ao el Banco Central tiene una proyeccin de crecimiento de ambas variables en torno a 5,5%, lo que supone que la economa mantiene, en el resto del ao, la actual tendencia a la desaceleracin en el ritmo de crecimiento de la actividad econmica y el gasto. Hay que sealar que el cuarto trimestre de 1997 el PIB creci un 9,6%, mientras el gasto se expandi a un 13,7%. Esta aceleracin se combina con el escenario externo ms desfavorable, lo que genera como resultado una necesidad de desacelerar la actividad econmica durante 1998. En todo caso, en un anlisis comparativo, la economa chilena seguir siendo, durante este ao, una de las de mayor crecimiento en el mundo. La formacin bruta de capital fijo ha experimentado una tendencia creciente durante la ltima dcada, con una tasa de inversin de un 33% del PIB en 1997. Durante este ao el pas mantendr una tasa de inversin similar a la del ao pasado. Este elevado nivel de inversin se ha transformado en el motor del crecimiento y es la mejor seal de la confianza depositada por empresas nacionales y extranjeras en las favorables perspectivas que ofrece la economa chilena. Del mismo modo, la tasa de ahorro nacional sigui una tendencia creciente en la segunda mitad de los 80 y se ha mantenido en torno a un 22% del PIB durante la presente dcada. El rpido crecimiento de la actividad econmica tambin se refleja en el mercado laboral. En los ltimos 10 aos la tasa promedio de creacin de nuevos puestos de trabajo casi ha duplicado la tasa de crecimiento de la poblacin econmicamente activa. Como resultado, se ha reducido la tasa de desempleo, ha aumentado la tasa de participacin y se han incrementado los salarios reales a un ritmo similar al aumento promedio de la productividad, en torno de 3,5% anual. En 1997 la ocupacin a nivel nacional alcanz un incremento promedio de 2,2% respecto de igual perodo del ao anterior y en lo que va corrido de este ao esta cifra alcanza a un 1,6%.  Baja de la inflacin Uno de los mayores logros de la poltica macroeconmica durante los 90 ha sido la disminucin de la inflacin a cifras de un dgito. La tasa de inflacin anual alcanz un 6,1% en 1997 y se espera que contine disminuyendo durante este ao hasta alcanzar la meta de un 4,5% para 1998. De esta manera, el presente ser el octavo ao consecutivo con tasas de inflacin anual decrecientes y el quinto consecutivo que exhibe una inflacin anual de un dgito. Estas cifras no tienen precedente en la historia econmica chilena, en particular si se considera que la inflacin entre los aos 1930 y 1997, excluyendo la hiperinflacin de los aos 70, fue de 23% como promedio anual. Es frecuente que en los momentos de dificultades econmicas surjan voces llamando a debilitar el esfuerzo antiinflacionario, en la creencia de que ello resolver problemas de la economa. La inflacin no resuelve los problemas econmicos, ms bien tiende a agravarlos. Tal vez pueda postergar en el corto plazo problemas polticos, pero hay que tener en cuenta que cuando eso ocurre los mismos que aceptan algo ms de inflacin proponen luego compensar por el poder de compra perdido. Y ah entramos en la clsica espiral precios-salarios que condujo a nuestra economa a un gran fracaso poltico y social. En la economa chilena existen muchos beneficios econmicos y sociales de moverse hacia niveles menores de inflacin. Por este motivo el Banco Central le concede gran importancia a este objetivo y ha fijado metas anuales que permitan una reduccin gradual y sostenida de la inflacin. La poltica monetaria que busca influir sobre la tasa de inters de mercado es administrada de modo que el gasto global de la economa evolucione en lnea con la capacidad productiva del pas. La aplicacin de esta poltica ha permitido, hasta ahora, cumplir con la meta inflacionaria. Otro factor importante para mantener la estabilidad macroeconmica y un alto nivel de ahorro nacional se encuentra en la evolucin de las finanzas del sector pblico. El ahorro fiscal ha sido superior al 4,5% del PIB durante los ltimos cinco aos, y el supervit fiscal se ubica, en promedio, cercano al 2,0% del PIB durante el mismo perodo. Este es un resultado de disciplina fiscal que pocos pases son capaces de emular. La sostenida baja en la inflacin ha sido an ms relevante si se considera que se ha logrado dentro de un perodo de crecimiento sostenido, de un bajo nivel de desempleo y con slidas cuentas externas. La nocin comn de que la reduccin inflacionaria se consigue a costas del crecimiento y del empleo no se ha producido en la reciente experiencia chilena.  Equilibrio externo El equilibrio externo se expresa en los dficits moderados en la cuenta corriente que el pas ha mantenido durante la ltima dcada, los que en promedio han representado el 3% del PIB segn la nueva medicin del Banco Central. No obstante, en los ltimos aos esta cifra ha aumentado a cerca del 5% del PIB. Es importante sealar que estos dficit, incluyendo la cifra cercana a 6% del PIB que se anticipa para el presente ao, son plenamente sostenibles y no representan riesgo externo alguno para el pas. En el anlisis del sector externo es importante considerar un conjunto de variables que determinan la sostenibilidad de los flujos de la balanza de pagos. Aparte del propio crecimiento del PIB, en el caso de Chile se observa un crecimiento de las exportaciones, una adecuada composicin de la cuenta de capitales, slidos indicadores de solvencia externa y una capacidad de respuesta a la actual crisis externa. El crecimiento de las exportaciones en la ltima dcada fue de un 10% anual en trminos reales, cifra que se ubica por sobre el crecimiento promedio del PIB. Las exportaciones son una pieza importante en la expansin econmica chilena de los ltimos aos y su ritmo de crecimiento se mantendr elevado en los prximos aos. La composicin de la cuenta de capitales muestra dos caractersticas relevantes. Por una parte, durante los ltimos diez aos el monto total de flujos de inversin extranjera han aumentado considerablemente. Por otra, los flujos de deuda externa se han concentrado en ingresos de mediano y largo plazo. Los ndices de solvencia externa indican que las reservas internacionales y la deuda externa mantienen niveles de mucha solidez. La relacin deuda externa a PIB pas de un nivel superior a 100% a mediados de los ochenta, a un valor de 30% en la actualidad. Al mismo tiempo, la deuda externa neta de reservas internacionales se sita en menos del 10% del PIB. Entre las principales consecuencias de la crisis en Asia sobre la economa chilena se encuentra su efecto negativo sobre el comercio exterior y el ingreso nacional. La disminucin del ritmo de crecimiento de la actividad en el resto del mundo, en especial en Asia, est generando una menor demanda por nuestros principales productos de exportacin, implicando esto menores precios, y por ende, menores retornos. El grado de diversificacin por mercados que han alcanzado nuestras junto con la flexibilidad de los fujos externos, permiten aminorar el efecto negativo. En la actualidad 25% de las exportaciones se orienta a Europa, cuya economa se est acelerando; 20% a Norteamrica que muestra altos niveles de crecimiento; y un 20% a Amrica Latina, que an muestra crecimientos interesantes, pero ha visto disminuido su crecimiento por la crisis en Asia. El 35% que va al Asia va a sufrir readecuaciones en el tiempo, siguiendo el proceso inverso al que llev a nuestros exportadores a aprovechar las ventajas de desviar sus envos hacia la regin en los aos en que era la ms dinmica del mundo. El principal efecto de la crisis externa ha sido una cada en los precios de nuestras exportaciones, que ha sido parcialmente compensado con una baja en el precio del petrleo y una inflacin externa ms baja. De acuerdo a las tendencias actuales, los trminos de intercambio en 1998 se vern deteriorados en torno a un 5% respecto de 1997. La baja de los trminos de intercambio tiene como contrapartida un menor nivel de ingreso nacional y, por ende, una menor capacidad de gasto con recursos propios y mayor necesidad de financiamiento. Por esta razn, es razonable que una parte del ajuste al menor ingreso nacional se realice por la va de una ampliacin transitoria del dficit en cuenta corriente, esto es por la va del financiamiento, pues en la medida que la cada del ingreso sea transitoria no se justifica recortar el nivel de gasto. Siempre es prudente procurar que el uso de financiamiento se mantenga dentro de lmites razonables y que su uso ms intenso sea estrictamente transitorio, y por lo tanto consistente con la capacidad de endeudamiento de mediano y largo plazo de la economa. En base al conjunto de los antecedentes del sector externo se puede afirmar que el riesgo pas de Chile ha do en franca disminucin a lo largo de los noventa, lo que se refleja en las clasificaciones internacionales y los mrgenes incorporados a los prstamos que reciben las empresas chilenas desde el exterior. Por otra parte, la fortaleza observada en las cifras macroeconmicas se ha traducido en una sostenida apreciacin real del peso, la cual alcanza una tasa promedio del orden de 4% anual en lo que va corrido de los 90. Esta situacin se ha visto propiciada por las importantes ganancias de productividad de la economa durante estos aos, as como tambin por la sobre depreciacin del peso en los aos 1989-90. Los niveles del tipo de cambio en los ltimos dos trimestres revierten esta tendencia y permiten aumentar la competitividad de los sectores exportadores sin arriesgar la estrategia antiinflacionaria. II. Desafos para el crecimiento En una perspectiva de mediano plazo es importante sealar que de los estudios comparados sobre crecimiento econmico se extraen dos conclusiones que me parece preciso recordar. En primer lugar, los procesos de crecimiento de los pases son inestables. El hecho de haber logrado un alto ritmo de crecimiento en una dcada rara vez conduce a un crecimiento dinmico en la dcada siguiente. Segundo, la capacidad de crecer depende fundamentalmente de factores internos de cada pas, entre los cuales est la calidad de las instituciones, disponibilidad de factores productivos y estabilidad macroeconmica. Chile es un pas que cuenta con los elementos bsicos para mantener la senda de crecimiento que ha mostrado por ms de una dcada. No obstante, hay mltiples tareas que son necesarias para perfeccionar las bases de este crecimiento. Existen desafos que enfrentados adecuadamente permitiran mantener el elevado crecimiento que ha experimentado el pas. ste debe ser el elemento ordenador en la discusin econmica en Chile. Mirando hacia adelante, las prioridades para mantener el impulso del crecimiento se pueden agrupar en tres categoras:  perfeccionar las instituciones que sirven de marco a las mltiples decisiones econmicas que toman las personas, empresas y gobiernos.  movilizar nuevos recursos para apoyar la formacin de capital fsico y humano; y  mantener aquellas polticas que han permitido sostener la estabilidad econmica, como son el supervit fiscal, la inflacin descendente y el equilibrio en las cuentas externas;  Perfeccionamiento de las instituciones En la medida que avanza el proceso de crecimiento, la tarea de perfeccionar las instituciones adquiere mayor relevancia. Si el pas cuenta con instituciones eficientes y flexibles, stas tendern a producir y mantener las polticas que promuevan la estabilidad econmica y a generar los recursos para la formacin de capital fsico y humano. De este modo, el desafo central para mantener el impulso del crecimiento de la economa chilena se encuentra en el perfeccionamiento de sus instituciones. Para avanzar en el fortalecimiento de las instituciones en nuestro pas debemos sealar claramente que el problema de la sociedad es perfeccionar los sistemas de incentivos que orientan las decisiones, tanto en el sector privado como en el sector pblico. El debate actual no es si el Estado debe o no participar en los procesos de autogobierno de la sociedad. El tema central consiste en definir cules son los resguardos que debemos tomar para estar confiados en que la accin del Estado estar efectivamente orientada hacia el bien comn. Una situacin que tiende a debilitar a las instituciones se produce cuando su accin o los resultados de ella no son directamente observables por los agentes de la sociedad. En este caso, el camino para mejorar el sistema de incentivos que enfrenta el Estado es aumentar la informacin y transparencia sobre su accin. Un sistema institucional moderno es aquel que acta en concordancia con los principios de la democracia, el perfeccionamiento de los mercados, el impulso del crecimiento y los principios perdurables en nuestras tradiciones cvicas.  Formacin de capital fsico y humano Respecto a la segunda prioridad, es sabido que uno de los principales desafos de los aos venideros consiste en mejorar la calidad y el nivel de la educacin de la fuerza laboral. El gobierno ha resuelto encarar esta tarea mediante una reforma educacional que tiene por objeto mejorar la infraestructura educacional y aumentar tanto la cantidad como la calidad de las horas que los estudiantes pasan en la escuela. Otro de los desafos del crecimiento consiste en aumentar la infraestructura pblica de modo que sta sea capaz de enfrentar los crecientes requerimientos del proceso de desarrollo. Por otra parte, no obstante la positiva evolucin que se ha tenido en la tasa de ahorro nacional durante el ltimo tiempo, se requiere que el esfuerzo desplegado se vaya incrementando con los aos, de tal forma de satisfacer los requerimientos de inversin asociados al proceso de crecimiento econmico, sin arriesgar el equilibrio de las cuentas externas.  Estabilidad macroeconmica En relacin al desafo de la estabilidad macroeconmica se requiere reconocer el efecto del nuevo escenario internacional sobre la economa chilena. De acuerdo a nuestro anlisis, los efectos de la crisis asitica sobre la actividad econmica en Chile son acotados. El dficit en cuenta corriente se ampliar a una cifra perfectamente manejable, en torno a 6% del PIB; la economa continuar transitando por su senda de crecimiento, pero a un ritmo ms moderado con una expansin de alrededor de 5,5%, de las mayores en Amrica Latina y a nivel internacional. La inflacin continuar disminuyendo hacia la meta de alrededor de 4,5% planteada para este ao. Nuestro sistema financiero se mantiene slido y se contina avanzando en hacerlo ms eficiente y competitivo ampliando sus posibilidades de desarrollo. As, la respuesta de Chile a la crisis asitica ha estado inserta dentro del contexto global de su poltica econmica, cuyos objetivos fundamentales son contribuir al logro de la estabilidad de la moneda y de los precios; la mantencin de una posicin externa slida y sostenible; la preservacin del sistema de pagos internos, lo que requiere de un sistema financiero solvente; y la existencia de disciplina fiscal presupuestaria, todo ello condiciones indispensables para continuar creciendo. El Banco Central permanece atento para tomar las acciones de poltica para hacer que la economa se mantenga en su curso de desarrollo sostenido y estabilidad. La crisis externa no debe desviar a la economa chilena de su camino a la estabilidad de precios, que se refleja en una tasa de inflacin similar a la de los pases desarrollados, un dficit moderado en cuenta corriente y disciplina en el presupuesto fiscal. Estos son los elementos que permiten formar un entorno econmico estable que facilita las iniciativas econmicas. Es importante enmarcar en esta perspectiva de mediano plazo la discusin que hoy da existe sobre el tipo de cambio. Desde mediados de octubre se ha observado un proceso de depreciacin del peso que refleja de al menos tres factores relevantes. Primero, la apreciacin del dlar en los mercados internacionales. Este es un factor que causa presiones sobre el tipo de cambio nominal peso-dlar, pero no representa una depreciacin real del peso, en la medida que se ve compensada por una menor inflacin internacional en dlares. Segundo, la mayor incertidumbre que existe en los mercados financieros internacionales respecto a las economas emergentes, incluyendo a la chilena, lo que ha modificado la percepcin respecto del riesgo cambiarlo. Tercero, las perspectivas de un saldo de la cuenta corriente ms deficitario tienen como contraparte un ajuste de precios relativos en el tipo de cambio real que debe acompaar a la reduccin en la tasa de crecimiento en el gasto interno. Sobre este ltimo punto suele existir cierto grado de confusin en la discusin pblica y quisiera detenerme particularmente aqu. Algunos han planteado que existe una estrategia de moderacin del dficit de cuenta corriente por la va de aumentos en el tipo de cambio real que es sustitua de la va de reduccin en el crecimiento del gasto a partir de polticas monetaria y fiscal ms restrictivas. Sin embargo, esta opcin no existe en la prctica. En las actuales condiciones de la economa no es posible generar un ajuste duradero en el tipo de cambio real, sin que al mismo tiempo se produzca una reduccin en la brecha de gasto-producto. Cuando la economa se encuentra operando en el entorno de la plena capacidad, el ajuste entre la reduccin del gasto y el aumento del tipo de cambio real debe ser coordinado o, de lo contrario, se producirn presiones inflacionarias que diluyen el ajuste inicial. En efecto, si se produce una depreciacin del tipo de cambio nominal, al tiempo que la economa continua gastando a un ritmo exagerado, entonces se generan mayores presiones inflacionarias. En un plazo mediano es inevitable que se produzca un rebrote inflacionario que, en un contexto de altos grados de indizacin salarial, anula el ajuste inicial de precios relativos. En ese contexto, las autoridades se veran forzadas a actuar con una combinacin de polticas monetaria y fiscal an ms restrictiva que la requerida inicialmente con el fin de aplacar estas presiones inflacionarias. Del mismo modo, no es conveniente para el pas aceptar algo ms de inflacin con el fin de lograr un mayor nivel de tipo de cambio real. En una etapa de ajuste de precios relativos y mayor volatilidad en los mercados financieros, la meta de inflacin y la coherencia de las polticas con sta, desempean un rol clave para anclar las expectativas de los agentes econmicos. La ambigedad en esta materia es extremadamente peligrosa, porque erosiona la credibilidad de las polticas y las expectativas que sobre stas se forman los agentes econmicos. Sin credibilidad en las polticas, la evolucin de la inflacin y otras variables nominales que se alimentan de las expectativas inflacionarias, como el tipo de cambio y los salarios, y que a su vez influyen sobre la inflacin, quedaran desancladas. Asimismo, por su visibilidad, la meta de inflacin juega un rol clave para concertar polticas que aseguren una trayectoria coherente con los equilibrios macroeconmicos bsicos. Esta postura del Banco Central, que enfatiza el rol de la meta de inflacin como ancla nominal de nuestra economa, no es obstculo para que ocurran ajustes en precios relativos relevantes. En particular, el tipo de cambio nominal se ha depreciado en alrededor de un 10% desde octubre hasta la fecha, en abierto contraste con su gran estabilidad previa. Es importante sealar que el Banco Central no pretende frenar infundadamente aumentos en el tipo de cambio real. Lo que se busca es que la tendencia del tipo de cambio real sea slida y no absorbida por mayor inflacin. Esta poltica tiene mejores resultados en el mediano plazo ya que busca crear condiciones para un ajuste del tipo de cambio real por la via ms efectiva, que es la de contener la inflacin interna. Dems est decir que el xito en la consecucin de estos objetivos depende no slo de las polticas llevadas a cabo por el Banco Central, sino que tambin del apoyo que brinda la poltica fiscal, especialmente en perodos de fluctuacin en las condiciones externas. Al finalizar, quisiera insistir que en la actualidad Chile se encuentra en una posicin privilegiada para enfrentar las turbulencias econmicas y financieras del escenario externo y proyectar el ritmo de crecimiento econmico de los aos recientes en el mediano plazo. De esta forma podremos cumplir la aspiracin de convertirnos en una nacin desarrollada. Pero para seguir obteniendo resultados como los de los ltimos aos debemos perseverar en los mismos principios: equilibrios macroeconmicos, inversin en capital fsico y humano y fortalecimiento institucional.

Title: Analysis of the economic situation
text: Analysis of the economic situation Presentation by Jorge Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the ICU Panel, Santiago, September 2, 1998 External framework Following the financial turbulence that began in mid-1997 in Asia, international financial markets have maintained a high level of sensitivity, which goes beyond the outlook for the world economy. The expected balance sheet for global economic activity suggests that during 1998 there will be a reduction in the rate of expansion of world output by about 2 percentage points compared to the growth observed in 1997 and with similar growth in 1999. The crisis in the countries of Southeast Asia has led to a lower dynamism in the demand for the main commodities. In particular, the copper market has presented a depressed scenario during the last months, with a copper price around 75 cents per pound. The external outlook is not favorable to wait for the price recovery in the short term. In view of the above considerations, it is prudent to assume that, at least for the remainder of this year and next, the external situation will not change significantly from current levels. Effects on the Chilean economy The main effect of the deterioration in the external scenario on the national economy is a reduction in the terms of trade, by around 10%. This effect reduces national income and tends to raise the current account deficit. Secondly, there has been a fall in import prices for Chile, a situation that reduces import inflation pressures. However, this situation cannot be projected in the future, considering that the dollar is less likely to maintain the pace of international appreciation. Third, there are effects on foreign trade volumes. Although available figures show that the volume of exports remains dynamic, external markets will become more competitive as a result of the external crisis. Fourth, the capital account has seen greater diversification of domestic investor portfolios, a reduction in capital inflows through portfolio investment, and an increase in the cost of long-term external financing. Policy objectives In this external context, the policies of the fiscal and monetary authority have been aimed at strengthening the conditions of stability in the Chilean economy that will allow us to resume a medium-term growth path. To this end, the policies implemented are aimed at directing an orderly process of adjustment of domestic expenditure, in order to moderate the current account deficit and maintain a controlled inflationary path. The economic policy mix has been geared towards achieving a prudent mix between increased external financing and correction of the level of domestic spending. In particular, these policies are aimed at: a5 Channel the current account deficit for this year within prudent limits while achieving a significant reduction in the deficit for next year. a5 Maintain the inflation rate on a path of gradual and persistent reduction. This objective is even more important at a time of relative price adjustment and increased volatility in financial markets. This commitment by the authorities is reflected in the inflation target for 1999 of 4.3 percent and the projection for output growth of 3.8 percent. These goals reflect that the country remains on a path of austerity and discipline, which strengthens the stability of the Chilean economy in a context of external turbulence. Policies The inflation target and output projection for 1999 are fully consistent with current policies. These goals reflect the necessary restraint in the current scenario of the international economy and reaffirm the measures announced on June 25 by the economic authorities. In other words, current fiscal and monetary policies are adequately targeted to achieve the proposed inflation target within an environment of moderate growth and with significant improvements in the current account balance. In turn, fiscal and monetary policy instruments have the flexibility to accommodate changes in external circumstances. In the monetary area, an increase in the cost of credit has been driven in order to deliver the relevant price signals for a restriction of private spending by companies and consumers. In periods of turbulence, monetary policy has been aimed at maintaining tighter liquidity control in order not to exacerbate these volatilities and speculative cycles against the peso. In the exchange rate area, the actions of the Central Bank have sought to cushion the sudden movements of the nominal exchange rate. The Central Bank has chosen to make this exchange rate policy explicit through the current exchange rate band. The current exchange rate policy is fully consistent with the 1999 targets and is intended to give a clearer signal to the market of the range of nominal exchange rate values that are appropriate to the evolution of the fundamental variables of the Chilean economy. In the fiscal area, an important effort has been made to promote an adjustment of government and public enterprise expenditures in line with the reduction in government revenues. In addition, the government announced its willingness to ensure that public absorption shows an increase similar to GDP growth during this year, a fact that will allow maintaining a situation of surplus in the fiscal accounts. In addition, just as important as the cuts made in 1998 is the Finance Minister's announcement of a cautious fiscal policy for 1999, which sets for spending growth of 3.3%. In summary, a balanced set of actions involving monetary, exchange rate and fiscal policies has been adopted. This coordinated set of policies is consistent with macroeconomic objectives for the short and medium term. Results The policy mix in place has begun to show its impact on domestic spending. In the second quarter of the year, there was a significant moderation in the growth rate of domestic demand, especially in the growth of consumption and variation in inventories, which showed an annual rate of change of 4.7%. It also highlights the dynamism that still shows the formation of fixed capital. The preliminary background for the third quarter indicates that domestic demand will deepen this process of moderation and that domestic spending growth will be lower than output growth. With regard to the external sector, it should be noted that in the first half of 1998 the volume of exports of goods and services reached 8.3 per cent and that in the second quarter this figure was 11.6 per cent. In the case of "rest" exports, volume growth in the second quarter was close to 20%. Exports have also been steered towards markets less affected by the Asian crisis. In other words, despite external difficulties, exports remain buoyant. Imports, meanwhile, continue to show a downward growth rate. Within these, consumer imports show a clear slowdown. The progress observed in the moderation of imports should be deepened in the second part of the year. Inflation has remained stable in recent months. At present, the annual inflation rate is 5.2%. Further progress in inflation is expected to be observed in the second part of the year, in line with the 1998 and 1999 targets. The Central Bank will remain attentive to the evolution of inflation since the risks on this front cannot be ignored. The ongoing tightening and the authorities' commitment to the inflation trend have moderated the pass-through of cost-to-price pressures. It is important to note that there are no structural causes in the Chilean economy that prevent continuing to promote a reduction in the inflationary trend. Conclusions The adjustment programme is proceeding well and results are already being observed in terms of domestic spending, external accounts and inflation. To the extent that progress is being made in this direction, we have managed to further strengthen the medium-term stability of the Chilean economy and limit the effects of the external crisis. In addition, it is important to note that even with the new projections, the growth rates of the Chilean economy this year and next compare favorably with those of most countries in the world. Current policies have the capacity to achieve the objectives of strengthening the stability of the economy and gradually broadening the horizon of economic decisions. Austerity will last a longer time, but it is a sacrifice that compares very favorably with the costs that a loss of confidence in macroeconomic management could bring. These policies include the central bank's explicit commitment to a narrow range for the exchange rate, more flexible management of monetary policy, and the moderation stance in fiscal policy. It is important to reiterate that the fundamentals of the Chilean economy are solid and the latent risks are limited. The fixed capital investment rate in early 1998 was over 32 per cent of GDP. For more than a decade, exports have shown sustained real growth above GDP. The rate of employment growth is still above the rate of population growth. The position of financial solvency is also on excellent footing. The external solvency position, measured as the ratio of net external liabilities to GDP or to exports, has been steadily improving over the past decade. The external liquidity position is also extremely strong. In the face of external financial turbulence, the Central Bank will maintain a policy approach aimed at strengthening the stability of the economy, which means prudence in the formulation of economic objectives and a clear determination to apply the necessary policy instruments with all the necessary force.

Resultados La combinacin de polticas en aplicacin ha comenzado a mostrar su impacto sobre el gasto interno. Title: Economic Outlook and macroeconomic outlook
text: Economic Outlook and macroeconomic outlook Presentation by Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Meeting of the National Council of the Chilean Chamber of Construction, Antofagasta, November 20, 1998. I. External crisis and internal scenario The international scenario facing the Chilean economy is marked by the crisis that began in Asia, just over a year ago. Its effects have spread to the rest of the world's economies and high volatility persists in financial markets. All this produces the risks that are present in the current international situation, among which are a further deterioration of the economy in Japan; new rounds of financial distrust of Asian economies, waves of contagion to other emerging economies; a faster-than-expected slowdown in the U.S. economy, a slowdown in European economies as a result of the turnaround in Asia's trade balance, and the possibility of a more drastic correction in stock prices in U.S. and European stock markets. In recent weeks, advanced countries and multilateral organizations have taken important steps to mitigate these risks. However, uncertainties will continue to characterize developments in the world economy in 1999. Within this scenario, the most up-to-date projections indicate that world output will grow by around 2.0% this year and somewhat lower in 1999. This means that the rate of expansion of world output has halved compared to 1996 and 1997. This new external scenario found the Chilean economy in a phase of strong acceleration of domestic demand, which was not accompanied by a similar increase in national savings, but by a widening in the current account deficit. The main cause of this expansion is the combination of optimism among companies and consumers regarding the performance of the national economy and the availability of domestic and external financing. Thus, financial markets provided the necessary funds to validate spending decisions and further decouple the investment decisions of firms and households from their ability to save. The expansion of domestic demand became more evident during the fourth quarter of 1997 and was mainly channelled towards external markets, boosting real import growth of over 20%. However, some of the demand pressure also drifted towards domestic markets, generating very dynamic output growth and a narrowing labour market. Indeed, the rate of job creation began to increase in the second half of 1997, and this higher level of employment continued throughout the first part of this year, bringing the unemployment rate below its historical trend. II. Monetary policy in 1998 In this context of severe turbulence and alterations in external markets, and the rapid expansion of domestic demand, the application of an adjustment policy aimed at reducing, over a limited period of time, the current account deficit became inevitable, while maintaining the basic balances of the economy, which are the condition for medium-term growth. Economic policy consistent with these objectives is based on the restrictive stance of monetary and fiscal policies. In the monetary area, the Central Bank has promoted an increase in the cost of credit in order to deliver the relevant price signals for a restriction of private spending by companies and consumers. In the last year, monetary aggregates and global credit have shown a general slowdown in their pace of growth, signaling the trend that spending has followed throughout the year. Additionally, the interest rate has been used, along with other instruments, to defend the peso against sudden changes in financial expectations. For this reason, to the extent that the financial markets and domestic exchange rates have tended to calm down and greater stability is observed in the international financial markets, the Central Bank has reduced the interest rate twice: in mid-October and early November. In the exchange rate area, the actions of the Central Bank are aimed at recognizing and respecting the most permanent trends of the exchange rate, but seeking to cushion their sudden movements. This is how in twelve months there has been a nominal depreciation of the peso against the dollar of 11% and a real depreciation of around 4%. To make this policy more efficient, in June and September, the Central Bank made some adjustments to the exchange rate band, in order to allow a gradual and orderly depreciation of the peso, which is consistent with monetary policy and the international scenario of greater financial uncertainty. In this sense, exchange rate policy has kept exchange rate fluctuations within moderate margins, while at the same time, it has been consistent with a greater degree of flexibility, consistent with the economy's more fundamental trends and other macroeconomic policies. Fiscal policy has also made an important effort to support adjustment policy through a reduction in government expenditures, in line with the new external scenario and macroeconomic policy objectives. III. Economic developments in 1998 and prospects for 1999 The most recent precedents indicate that the main variables of the external sector, economic activity and inflation are moving in the desired direction, which supports the macroeconomic program that has been applied during this year and generates stable conditions that are favorable for the evolution of the economy in the medium term. 1. Trade balance and current account In the trade balance, the consequences of the external crisis are manifested in changes in the prices and quantities of trade in goods and services. In turn, the expansion of domestic activity influences the evolution of imports. The slowdown in the global economy has reduced the dynamism of demand for major commodities. Indeed, the dollar prices of primary goods have fallen by more than 18% in the last twelve months. In particular, the price of copper fluctuated around 75 cents per pound during 1998, although in the second half of this year it remained around 73 cents. In the current external scenario, it is prudent to assume that the price of copper in 1999 will not change significantly from the levels observed this year. On the other hand, the external crisis has also led to reductions in dollar prices of other raw materials and processed products in the economies most affected by the crisis. During the period from January to September 1998, the average price of imports, measured in dollars, fell by about 4.0 per cent compared with the same period last year. This situation should tend to reverse due to the depreciation of the dollar against the yen and the mark since the end of last August. External inflation of around 2 per cent is expected for 1999. Dollar prices of imports, excluding fuels, and non-copper exports are expected to evolve consistently with this projection. In sum, the reduction in the terms of trade of the Chilean economy will reach about 10% this year, which subtracts the equivalent of two percentage points from national income, and has a negative impact on the deficit of the trade balance estimated at US 1,400 million. For 1999, the terms of trade are projected to remain broadly unchanged from the level reached in 1998. Export volumes of goods and services have increased by 7.5 per cent during the period January-September 1998 over the same period last year. The volume of copper exports showed a growth of 13.3% and exports other than copper grew by 4.8% in this period. These figures show that the effect of the external crisis on real exports is smaller than that observed in other periods of slowdown in international activity, such as those in 1991 and 1993. The reason for this is the substantial geographical reorientation of exports. In fact, it can be seen that in the period from January to September, compared with the same months of 1997, the volume exported to Asia decreased by 7.1%, while that corresponding to the rest of the world grew by 17.2%, a phenomenon that is observed in different magnitudes for all categories of goods. The outlook for export volumes for next year should take into account the new conditions of the world economy, although a recovery in copper shipments abroad is expected due to the entry into operation of new projects in the mining sector. The expected trajectory for the rest of exports, on the other hand, is more moderate and uncertain, since it is highly dependent on world markets. As a result of these projections and considering the effects of the slowdown in domestic economic activity and the rise in the real exchange rate, it is estimated that the deficit in the trade balance will be around US 3,100 million in 1998 and close to US 1,900 million in 1999, almost 40% less than this year. Apart from the result of the trade balance, the current account deficit also involves the balance of services. For 1998 and 1999, a moderation in net expenditures from financial services is expected, which is consistent with the economic cycle and the lower accrual of foreign profits due to the decline in the price of copper. The non-financial services account, meanwhile, is expected to end 1999 with a balance similar to that of the current year. In this way, the current account deficit of 1998 will reach around US 5,150 million, but on a path of reduction towards next year, in which a figure close to US 4,000 million could be reached. This figure is a reflection of the great effort that the country is making by significantly adjusting its domestic demand and real exchange rate in the presence of a highly complex external scenario. In this way we approach the declared purpose for the medium term of placing this deficit at a level between 4% and 5% of GDP. It is worth stressing the inescapable need to take the risk of a large current account deficit very seriously. Our own experience of the early eighties is very illustrative in this regard, when after a deficit of 14% of GDP in 1981 a crisis of proportions occurred. 2. Capital account and balance of payments Three relevant developments can be observed in the evolution of the capital account in 1998: the increase in demand for international assets by domestic agents, the moderation in investment flows and external financing to Chile, and the increase in the cost of external financing. A very significant movement in the capital account during 1998 comes from the increase in demand for international assets by the private sector. These portfolio adequacy movements have been influenced by the greater degree of uncertainty in the international economy and the depreciation of the peso, reacting through greater demand for assets that reduce the changed risk and take advantage of greater international diversification of the asset portfolio. This phenomenon has put significant pressure on financial markets and changed them in the country. During this year there has been a significant outflow of investments from the AFPs abroad, with these investments expected to reach 5% of pension fund assets by the end of 1998. This rearrangement is explained by a policy of portfolio diversification of these entities. Capital outflows from this heading are expected to be lower than this year in 1999 because the most significant part of the asset recomposition has already been carried out. A similar phenomenon of portfolio adjustments has also occurred among non-institutional investors, including banks, companies and individuals, which is recorded as an outflow of capital and will reach a significant figure in 1998. To the extent that the greater degree of confidence observed in the financial markets is consolidated and to exchange them, it is very likely that the outflows associated with portfolio changes and hedges due to exchange rate fluctuations will tend to decrease compared to the 1998 figure. The most recent precedents point in this direction. The more uncertain external scenario has meant a lower availability of capital for all emerging economies. In the Chilean economy, there has been a reduction in capital inflows compared to the strong inflows of previous years, which should be interpreted as a normalization of these flows since the country has continued to attract medium and long-term financial resources. For 1999, the strength of medium- and long-term capital is expected to remain as important a source of financing as it has been until now, becoming a fundamental pillar within the capital account. In particular, foreign direct investment could reach about 4.2 billion in 1999. In other components of the capital account, such as portfolio investment, there is greater uncertainty. However, they do not reach a very significant figure in the financing of the balance of payments. Third, the greater preference of international investors for currencies, markets and instruments considered safer has led to a general increase in the cost of external financing in emerging economies. However, it should be noted that in the case of Chile these increases have been smaller than those registered in other economies in the region and the reduction in the reserve requirement rate has made it possible to compensate, at least partially, for this effect. For their part, interest rates in industrial countries, especially long-term ones, have tended to decline. The above background indicates that the external resource requirements, the US 4 billion current account deficit and the expected amortizations are financeable without resorting to international reserves, even in circumstances more complex than the current ones in terms of external financing. But even in a more restrictive scenario, an additional factor of reassurance regarding the future evolution of the external accounts is the solid position of international reserves of the Chilean economy. Indeed, the accumulated level of international reserves to date stands at a figure close to US15.5 billion, an amount that allows liquidity and external vulnerability indicators to be very favorable for the Chilean economy, compared to other economies also affected by the global crisis. 3. Economic activity The history accumulated to date indicates that the economy is moving on a trajectory of progressive moderation in its growth rate, a situation that has been accentuated in recent months. Output has shown a decline in its growth rate, going from an expansion of 6.8% in the first half of this year to 2.7% in the third quarter. This adjustment in the pace of expansion is especially visible in the evolution of the sectors that are most affected by the cyclical position of the economy, such as industry, construction and trade. However, we must also highlight some supply factors that affect the slowdown in output, such as the reduction in the growth of mining, lower fish catches and the consequences of drought for the agriculture and electricity sectors. For its part, domestic demand is evolving with an even greater slowdown than output. In the first half of the year the increase in domestic demand was 11.1% and in the third quarter of this year its growth reached only 0.5%. The significant reduction in dynamism observed in the third quarter was influenced by the reduction in gross fixed capital formation, which is determined by a manifestly high basis of comparison. This evolution means that the expenditure-output gap turned negative for the first time this year, standing at -2.2 percentage points. Current policies expect domestic demand to remain very moderate in 1999. Likewise, the evolution of the pace of job creation reflects the slowdown in economic activity. In the last quarter, ending in September, national employment registered an increase of 0.9%, a figure that compares with increases in employment of more than 2% observed in 1997 and in the first half of this year. In the coming months, the evolution of the unemployment rate will depend on the coherence between wage developments and general economic conditions. The value added of the construction sector has shown a medium-term trend slightly higher than the growth of aggregate output, although with more marked oscillations through the economic cycle. This fact led to a slight fall in the value added of the sector in 1991 and 1994, which were two years in which the slowdown in economic activity was manifested. Also during 1998 there has been a fall in the rate of growth of construction, which is likely to mean reduced growth in 1998 and very close to zero in 1999. It is important to note that the least dynamic activity within the sector will be construction, especially housing, whose evolution depends more closely on interest rates and financial market conditions. All these elements will lead to output growth that in 1998 and 1999 will be significantly lower than the trend growth of the last decade. Last September, in the context of the report to the Senate, the Central Bank projected a growth rate of 5 per cent for 1998 and around 3.8 per cent for 1999. The most recent records indicate that the accumulated growth until the third quarter reaches 5.4% and that for the year as a whole it will be between 4.5% and 5%. With regard to 1999, it must be reiterated that its effective value will depend on the evolution of the external scenario and the stability of the domestic financial market. 4. Inflation The inflation rate continues on a gradual downward path, consistent with the 1998 and 1999 targets of /-4.5 percent and /-4.3 percent, respectively. However, despite recent progress in reducing inflation, a risky environment persists, manifested in core inflation rates still above 5% per annum and wage growth that remains close to 8% per year. These developments make it necessary to maintain a very cautious attitude in observing the price trend. However, as has happened in the adjustment experiences of previous years, the slowdown in the pace of output growth should help consolidate a lower rate of inflation in the coming quarters. It is important to stress that moderation in nominal wage growth is also a necessary factor in sustaining employment levels, especially in the current adjustment period. IV. Conclusions The Chilean economy is facing complex times. The Asian crisis has put and will continue to test the country's ability to meet the challenges associated with these times of turbulence and international uncertainty. While the economy has its solid foundations, now is the time to reaffirm conviction in prudent and demanding macroeconomic policies. It is impossible for the country to maintain high growth as long as the external turbulence does not subside and a process of restoring stability in world markets is consolidated. Failure to recognize that a relatively harsher period must be faced would have an irremediably negative effect on the country's economic management, a situation that in itself would significantly deepen the effects of the Asian crisis. Easy solutions do not exist. All come with costs. The Central Bank's vision is clear at the current juncture: to reaffirm the commitment to the process of gradual but consistent reduction of inflation, as well as to reiterate the intention for the current account deficit to be reduced until it reaches reasonable levels, between 4% and 5% of GDP in the medium term. The background to the evolution of economic activity and domestic demand during the third quarter shows that the economy has taken the expected adjustment path, and it should come as no surprise if economic growth rates in twelve months show a further slowdown in the last quarter of the year. The reduction in the pace of economic growth is the inevitable consequence of the difficult external situation that the Chilean economy has had to face this year. At this point, there is practically no economy in the world that has not had to revise downwards its projections and pretensions of economic growth. More important, in fact, is to point out that it is precisely these adjustments that have driven a greater degree of confidence among economic agents and financial markets, predicting a moderate, gradual, but lasting recovery in the pace of economic growth over the next year. Monetary policy instruments will continue to be applied in a manner consistent with these purposes. The success of this undertaking will mean that the national economy will grow below its potential in 1998 and 1999, but will generate the stability necessary to maintain high growth in the medium term. But that outcome depends crucially on policy support. The equation is simple: the greater the support for macroeconomic policies, however demanding, the less sacrifice is made in slowing economic growth, employment and wages. The hasty easing of adjustment policies will only affect the stability achieved over a decade and reduce medium-term growth capacity.
text_original: Coyuntura y perspectivas macroeconmicas Exposicin de Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vicepresidente del Banco Central del Chile, en la Reunin del Consejo Nacional de la Cmara Chilena de la Construccin, Antofagasta, 20 de noviembre de 1998.  Crisis externa y escenario interno El escenario internacional que enfrenta la economa chilena est marcado por la crisis que se inici en Asia, hace algo ms de un ao. Sus efectos se han extendido al resto de las economas del mundo y persiste una elevada volatilidad en los mercados financieros. Todo ello produce los riesgos que estn presentes en la actual coyuntura internacional, entre los que se cuentan un deterioro adicional de la economa en Japn; nuevas rondas de desconfianza financiera sobre las economas asiticas, olas de contagio hacia otras economas emergentes; una desaceleracin ms rpida de lo esperado de la economa norteamericana, un freno de las economas europeas como consecuencia del vuelco en la balanza comercial de Asia, y la posibilidad de una correccin ms drstica en los precios de las acciones en los mercados burstiles de Estados Unidos y Europa. En las ltimas semanas los pases avanzados y los organismos multilaterales han dado pasos importantes para aminorar estos riesgos. No obstante, las incertidumbres continuaran caracterizando la evolucin de la economa mundial en 1999. Dentro de este escenario, las proyecciones ms actualizadas sealan que el producto mundial crecer alrededor de 2,0% el presente ao y una cifra algo menor en 1999. Esto significa que el ritmo de expansin del producto mundial se ha reducido a la mitad con respecto al observado en 1996 y 1997. Este nuevo escenario externo encontr a la economa chilena en una fase de fuerte aceleracin de la demanda interna, el cual no fue acompaado por un aumento similar del ahorro nacional, sino por una ampliacin en el dficit de la cuenta corriente. La principal causa de esta expansin est en la conjuncin de optimismo en empresas y consumidores respecto del desempeo de la economa nacional y de disponibilidad de financiamiento interno y externo. As, los mercados financieros proveyeron los fondos necesarios para validar las decisiones de gasto y desvincular en mayor grado las decisiones de inversin de las empresas y familias de su capacidad de ahorro. La expansin de la demanda interna se hizo ms evidente durante el cuarto trimestre de 1997 y se canaliz, en lo fundamental, hacia los mercados externos, impulsando el crecimiento de las importaciones reales sobre 20%. Sin embargo, parte de la presin de demanda tambin deriv hacia los mercados internos, generando un crecimiento muy dinmico del producto y un estrechamiento del mercado laboral. En efecto, el ritmo de creacin de empleos comenz a incrementarse en la segunda mitad de 1997, y este mayor nivel de empleo se mantuvo a lo largo de la primera parte del presente ao, llevando la tasa de desempleo por debajo de su tendencia histrica.  Poltica monetaria en 1998 En este panorama de fuertes turbulencias y alteraciones en los mercados externos, y de rpida expansin de la demanda interna se hizo inevitable la aplicacin de una poltica de ajuste orientada a reducir, en un perodo acotado de tiempo, el dficit de la cuenta corriente, manteniendo al mismo tiempo los equilibrios bsicos de la economa, que constituyen la condicin para favorecer el crecimiento de mediano plazo. La poltica econmica coherente con estos objetivos est basada en la orientacin restrictiva de las polticas monetaria y fiscal. En el rea monetaria el Banco Central ha impulsado un incremento en el costo del crdito con el fin de entregar las seales de precios relevantes para una restriccin del gasto privado de empresas y consumidores. En el ltimo ao, los agregados monetarios y el crdito global han mostrado una desaceleracin generalizada en su ritmo de crecimiento, sealando la tendencia que ha seguido el gasto a travs del ao. Adicionalmente, la tasa de inters ha sido utilizada, junto a otros instrumentos, para defender el peso ante los cambios bruscos en las expectativas financieras. Por esta razn, en la medida que los mercados financieros y cambiarlos domsticos se han tendido a calmar y se observa mayor estabilidad en los mercados financieros internacionales, el Banco Central ha reducido en dos ocasiones la tasa de inters: a mediados de octubre y comienzos de noviembre. En el rea cambiara, las acciones del Banco Central estn orientadas a reconocer y respetar las tendencias ms permanentes del tipo de cambio, pero buscando amortiguar sus movimientos bruscos. Es as como en doce meses se ha verificado una depreciacin nominal del peso con relacin al dlar de un 11% y una depreciacin real en torno a un 4%. Para hacer ms eficiente esta poltica el Banco Central realiz en junio y septiembre algunos ajustes a la banda cambiara, de modo de permitir una depreciacin gradual y ordenada del peso, la cual es coherente con la poltica monetaria y el escenario internacional de mayor incertidumbre financiera. Es en este sentido, la poltica cambiara ha mantenido las fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio dentro de mrgenes moderados, y al mismo tiempo, ha sido compatible con un mayor grado de flexibilidad, coherente con los las tendencias ms fundamentales de la economa y las restantes polticas macroeconmicas. La poltica fiscal tambin ha realizado un esfuerzo importante para apoyar la poltica de ajuste a travs de una reduccin de los gastos del gobierno, acorde con el nuevo escenario externo y los objetivos de las polticas macroeconmicas.  Desarrollos econmicos en 1998 y perspectivas para 1999 Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que las principales variables del sector externo, actividad econmica e inflacin se mueven en la direccin deseada, lo cual respalda el programa macroeconmico que se ha aplicado durante el presente ao y genera condiciones de estabilidad que son favorables para la evolucin de la economa en el mediano plazo. 1. Balanza comercial y cuenta corriente En la balanza comercial las consecuencias de la crisis externa se manifiestan en alteraciones en los precios y en las cantidades del comercio de bienes y servicios.
