A su vez, la expansin de la actividad interna influye en la evolucin de las importaciones. La desaceleracin de la economa mundial ha restado dinamismo a la demanda de los principales productos bsicos. En efecto, los precios en dlares de los bienes primarios muestran descensos superiores al 18% en los ltimos doce meses. En particular, el precio del cobre ha fluctuado cerca de los 75 centavos de dlar la libra durante 1998, aunque en el segundo semestre de este ao se ha mantenido en torno a los 73 centavos. En el actual panorama externo es prudente suponer que en 1999 el precio del cobre no variar significativamente respecto de los niveles observados este ao. Por otra parte, la crisis externa tambin ha originado reducciones en los precios en dlares de otras materias primas y productos elaborados en las economas ms afectadas por la crisis. Durante el perodo de enero a septiembre de 1998 el precio promedio de las importaciones, medido en dlares, ha cado cerca de 4,0% con relacin a igual perodo del ao anterior. Esta situacin debiera tender a revertirse en virtud de la depreciacin del dlar frente al yen y al marco desde fines de agosto pasado. Para 1999 se espera una inflacin externa del orden de 2%. Los precios en dlares de las importaciones, excepto los combustibles, y de las exportaciones no cobre se espera que muestren una evolucin coherente con esta proyeccin. En suma, la reduccin de los trminos de intercambio de la economa chilena alcanzar cerca del 10% en el presente ao, lo que resta del ingreso nacional el equivalente a dos puntos porcentuales, y tiene un impacto negativo sobre el dficit de la balanza comercial estimado en US$ 1.400 millones. Para 1999 se proyecta que los trminos de intercambio se mantendrn prcticamente invariables respecto del nivel alcanzado en 1998. Los volmenes de las exportaciones de bienes y servicios han aumentado en un 7,5% durante el perodo enero a septiembre de 1998 con respecto a igual perodo del ao anterior. El volumen de las exportaciones de cobre present un crecimiento de 13,3% y las exportaciones distintas de cobre crecieron en 4,8% en este perodo. Estas cifras muestran que el efecto de la crisis externa en las exportaciones reales es menor que el observado en otros perodos de desaceleracin de la actividad internacional, como los ocurridos en 1991 y en 1993. La razn de ello es la substancial reorientacin geogrfica de las exportaciones. En efecto, se observa que en el perodo de enero a septiembre, respecto de los mismos meses de 1997, el volumen exportado a Asia disminuy en 7,1%, en tanto que el correspondiente al resto del mundo creci en 17,2%, fenmeno que se observa en distinta magnitud para todas las categoras de bienes. Las perspectivas de los volmenes exportados para el prximo ao deben considerar las nuevas condiciones de la economa mundial, aunque se espera una recuperacin de los envos de cobre al exterior debido a la entrada en operacin de nuevos proyectos del sector minero. La trayectoria esperada para el resto de las exportaciones, en cambio, es ms moderada e incierta, pues es altamente dependiente de los mercados mundiales. Como resultado de estas proyecciones y considerando los efectos de la desaceleracin de la actividad econmica interna y del alza del tipo de cambio real, se estima que el dficit en la balanza comercial ser de alrededor de US$ 3.100 millones en 1998 y cercano a los US$ 1.900 millones en 1999, casi un 40% menos que en el presente ao. Aparte del resultado de la balanza comercial, en el dficit de la cuenta corriente tambin interviene la balanza de servicios. Para 1998 y 1999 se espera una moderacin en los egresos netos por concepto de servicios financieros, lo cual es coherente con el ciclo econmico y el menor devengo de utilidades extranjeras por la disminucin del precio del cobre. Por su parte, la cuenta de servicios no financieros se espera que finalice el ao 1999 con un saldo similar al del ao en curso. De esta manera, el dficit de cuenta corriente de 1998 alcanzar alrededor de los US$ 5.150 millones, pero sobre una trayectoria de reduccin hacia el prximo ao, en que se podra alcanzar una cifra cercana a los US$ 4.000 millones. Esta cifra es el reflejo del gran esfuerzo que est haciendo el pas ajustando significativamente su demanda interna y tipo de cambio real en presencia de un escenario externo altamente complejo. De esta manera nos aproximamos al propsito declarado para el mediano plazo de situar este dficit en un nivel entre 4% y 5% del PIB. Vale la pena insistir en la ineludible necesidad de tomar muy en serio el riesgo de un dficit de cuenta corriente elevado. Nuestra propia experiencia de principios de los aos ochenta es muy ilustrativa al respecto, cuando despus de un dficit de 14% del PIB en 1981 sobrevino una crisis de proporciones.  Cuenta de capitales y balanza de pagos En la evolucin de la cuenta de capitales durante 1998 se observan tres hechos relevantes: el aumento en la demanda de activos internacionales por parte de agentes domsticos, la moderacin en los flujos de inversin y financiamiento externo hacia Chile y el incremento en el costo del financiamiento externo. Un movimiento muy significativo en la cuenta de capitales durante 1998 proviene del aumento de la demanda por activos internacionales por parte del sector privado. Estos movimientos de adecuacin de cartera han estado influidos por el mayor grado de incertidumbre de la economa internacional y la depreciacin del peso, reaccionando a travs de una mayor demanda por activos que permitan reducir el riesgo cambiado y aprovechar las ventajas de una mayor diversificacin internacional de la cartera de activos. Este fenmeno, ha presionado en forma importante los mercados financieros y cambiarlos en el pas. Durante este ao se he producido una salida importante de inversiones de las AFP hacia el exterior, esperndose que a fines de 1998 estas inversiones alcancen al 5% de los activos de los fondos de pensiones. Esta reacomodacin se explica por una poltica de diversificacin de portafolio de estas entidades. Se espera que para 1999 la salida de capitales por este concepto sea inferior a la de este ao debido a que la parte ms significativa de la recomposicin de activos ya fue realizada. Un fenmeno similar de ajustes de cartera tambin se ha dado en los inversionistas no institucionales, incluyendo a bancos, empresas y personas naturales, lo cual se registra como una salida de capitales y alcanzar en 1998 una cifra significativa. En la medida que se consolide el mayor grado de confianza que se ha observado en los mercados financieros y cambiarlos es muy probable que las salidas asociadas a los cambios de cartera y coberturas por fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio, tienda a reducirse respecto del registro de 1998. Los antecedentes ms recientes apuntan en esta direccin. El escenario externo ms incierto ha significado una menor disponibilidad de capitales para todas las economas emergentes. En la economa chilena se ha observado una reduccin de las entradas de capital respecto de los fuertes influjos de aos anteriores, lo cual debe ser interpretado como una normalizacin de dichos flujos ya que el pas ha continuado atrayendo recursos financieros de mediano y largo plazo. Para 1999 se espera que la fortaleza de los capitales de mediano y largo plazo sigan siendo una fuente de financiamiento tan importante como lo ha sido hasta ahora, convirtindose en un pilar fundamental dentro de la cuenta de capitales. En particular, la inversin extranjera directa podra alcanzar unos US$ 4.200 millones en 1999. En otros componentes de la cuenta de capitales, como la inversin de cartera, existe mayor incertidumbre. Sin embargo, ellos no alcanzan una cifra muy significativa en el financiamiento de la balanza de pagos. En tercer lugar, la mayor preferencia de los inversionistas internacionales por las monedas, mercados e instrumentos considerados ms seguros, ha llevado a un incremento generalizado en el costo del financiamiento externo de las economas emergentes. Sin embargo, hay que destacar que en el caso de Chile estos aumentos han sido menores que los registrados en otras economas de la regin y la reduccin de la tasa de encaje ha permitido compensar, al menos parcialmente, este efecto. Por su parte, las tasas de inters de los pases industriales, especialmente las de largo plazo, han tendido a disminuir. Los antecedentes anteriores indican que las necesidades de recursos externos, el dficit de US$ 4.000 millones de la cuenta corriente y las amortizaciones previstas, son financiables sin recurrir a las reservas internacionales, an en circunstancias ms complejas que las actuales en materia de financiamiento externo. Pero an en un escenario ms restrictivo, un factor adicional de tranquilidad respecto de la evolucin futura de las cuentas externas es la slida posicin de reservas internacionales de la economa chilena. En efecto, el nivel acumulado de reservas internacionales a la fecha se sita en una cifra cercana a los US$15.500 millones, monto que permite que los indicadores de liquidez y vulnerabilidad externa sean muy favorables para la economa chilena, respecto de otras economas tambin tocadas por la crisis global.  Actividad econmica Los antecedentes acumulados hasta la fecha indican que la economa se mueve sobre una trayectoria de progresiva moderacin en su tasa de crecimiento, situacin que se ha acentuado en los ltimos meses. El producto ha mostrado una declinacin en su tasa de crecimiento, pasando de una expansin de 6,8% en el primer semestre de este ao a un 2,7% en el tercer trimestre. Este ajuste en el ritmo de expansin es especialmente visible en la evolucin de los sectores que son ms afectados por la posicin cclica de la economa, como la industria, construccin y comercio. Sin embargo, tambin hay que destacar algunos factores de oferta que inciden en la desaceleracin del producto, como la reduccin en el crecimiento de la minera, las menores capturas pesqueras y las consecuencias de la sequa para los sectores agricultura y electricidad. Por su parte, la demanda interna est evolucionando con una desaceleracin an mayor que el producto. En el primer semestre el aumento de la demanda interna fue de un 11,1% y en el tercer trimestre de este ao su crecimiento alcanz slo a 0,5%. En la significativa reduccin del dinamismo observado en el tercer trimestre influy la reduccin experimentada por la formacin bruta de capital fijo, la cual est determinada por una base de comparacin manifiestamente elevada. Esta evolucin significa que la brecha gasto-producto se torn negativa por primera vez en el ao, situndose en -2,2 puntos porcentuales. Las polticas actualmente vigentes consideran que la demanda interna mantenga un crecimiento muy moderado en 1999. Asimismo, la evolucin del ritmo de creacin de empleos refleja la desaceleracin de la actividad econmica. En el ltimo trimestre, finalizado en septiembre, la ocupacin nacional anot un incremento de 0,9%, cifra que se compara con aumentos de la ocupacin superiores al 2% observados en 1997 y en el primer semestre de este ao. En los prximos meses la evolucin de la tasa de desempleo depender de la coherencia entre la evolucin de los salarios y las condiciones generales de la economa. El valor agregado del sector construccin ha mostrado una tendencia de mediano plazo levemente superior al crecimiento del producto agregado, aunque con oscilaciones ms marcadas a travs del ciclo econmico. Este hecho llev a una leve cada en el valor agregado del sector en 1991 y 1994, que fueron dos aos en los que se manifest la desaceleracin de la actividad econmica. Tambin durante 1998 se ha observado una cada en el ritmo de crecimiento de la construccin, que probablemente significar un crecimiento reducido en 1998 y muy cercano a cero en 1999. Es importante destacar que la actividad de menor dinamismo dentro del sector ser la edificacin, especialmente habitacional, cuya evolucin depende ms cercanamente de las tasas de inters y de las condiciones del mercado financiero. Todos estos elementos llevarn a un crecimiento del producto que en 1998 y 1999 ser significativamente menor que el crecimiento de tendencia de la ltima dcada. En septiembre ltimo, en el marco del Informe al Senado, el Banco Central proyect una tasa de crecimiento de 5% para 1998 y en torno a 3,8% para 1999. Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que el crecimiento acumulado hasta el tercer trimestre alcanza a un 5,4% y que para el ao en su conjunto se situar entre 4,5% y 5%. Respecto de 1999 se debe reiterar que su valor efectivo depender de la evolucin del escenario externo y de la estabilidad del mercado financiero interno.  Inflacin La tasa de inflacin continua sobre una trayectoria de reduccin gradual, coherente con las metas de 1998 y 1999, de +/-4,5% y +/-4,3%, respectivamente. Sin embargo, a pesar de los progresos recientes en la reduccin de la inflacin, persiste un ambiente de riesgo que se manifiesta en ndices de inflacin subyacente an superiores al 5% anual y en crecimientos salariales que se mantienen cercanos a 8% anual. Esta evolucin obliga a mantener una actitud muy cautelosa en la observacin de la tendencia de los precios. No obstante, del mismo modo como ha sucedido en las experiencias de ajuste de aos anteriores, la desaceleracin en el ritmo de crecimiento del producto debe colaborar en la consolidacin de un menor ritmo inflacionario en los prximos trimestres. Es importante insistir en que la moderacin del crecimiento de los salarios nominales es, adems, un factor necesario para sustentar los niveles de empleo, especialmente en el actual perodo de ajuste.  Conclusiones La economa chilena enfrenta tiempos complejos. La crisis asitica ha puesto y seguir poniendo a prueba la capacidad del pas para enfrentar los retos asociados a estos tiempos de turbulencia e incertidumbre internacional. Aunque la economa tiene sus fundamentos slidos, sta es la hora de reafirmar la conviccin en polticas macroeconmicas prudentes y exigentes. Es imposible para el pas mantener un crecimiento elevado en tanto las turbulencias externas no amainen y se consolide un proceso de recuperacin de la estabilidad en los mercados mundiales. No reconocer que se debe afrontar un perodo relativamente ms duro provocara un efecto irremediablemente negativo en la administracin econmica del pas, situacin que por s misma profundizara significativamente los efectos de la crisis asitica. Las soluciones fciles no existen. Todas acarrean costos. La visin del Banco Central es clara en la actual coyuntura: reafirmar el compromiso con el proceso de reduccin gradual pero consistente de la inflacin, as como reiterar el propsito para que el dficit en cuenta corriente se reduzca hasta que alcance niveles razonables, entre 4% y 5% del PIB en el mediano plazo. Los antecedentes respecto de la evolucin de la actividad econmica y demanda interna durante el tercer trimestre muestran que la economa ha tomado la trayectoria de ajuste esperada, y no debera constituir una sorpresa si las tasas de crecimiento econmico en doce meses presentan una desaceleracin adicional en el ltimo trimestre del ao. La reduccin del ritmo de crecimiento econmico es la consecuencia inevitable de la difcil situacin externa que ha debido enfrentar la economa chilena durante el presente ao. A estas alturas, prcticamente no hay economa en el mundo que no haya debido revisar a la baja sus proyecciones y pretensiones de crecimiento econmico. Ms importante es, en realidad, sealar que son precisamente estos ajustes los que han impulsado un mayor grado de confianza entre los agentes econmicos y los mercados financieros, auspiciando una recuperacin moderada, gradual, pero duradera del ritmo de crecimiento econmico a travs del prximo ao. Los instrumentos de poltica monetaria se seguirn aplicando de manera coherente con estos propsitos. El xito de esta empresa se traducir en que la economa nacional crecer por debajo de su potencial en 1998 y 1999, pero generar la estabilidad necesaria para mantener un crecimiento elevado en el mediano plazo. Pero ese resultado depende en forma crucial del apoyo a las polticas. La ecuacin es simple: a mayor respaldo a las polticas macroeconmicas, por exigentes que sean, menor el sacrificio en cuanto a la desaceleracin del crecimiento econmico, del empleo y los salarios. El relajo apresurado de las polticas de ajuste slo afectar la estabilidad conseguida a lo largo de una dcada y reducirn la capacidad de crecimiento de mediano plazo.

Title: Monetary policy in 1998
text: Monetary policy in 1998 Presentation by Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, at ASIMETAL 98, Santiago, October 7, 1998. I. International scenario The international scenario facing the Chilean economy is marked by the progressive deterioration since the crisis began in Asia, just over a year ago. Its effects have spread to the rest of the world's economies and high volatility in financial markets persists. All this produces the risks that are present in the current international situation, among which are a further deterioration of the economy in Japan; new rounds of financial distrust of Asian economies, waves of contagion to other emerging economies; a faster-than-expected slowdown in the U.S. economy, a slowdown in European economies as a result of the turnaround in Asia's trade balance, and the possibility of a more drastic correction in stock prices in U.S. and European stock markets. Within this scenario of greater uncertainty, the most updated projections indicate that the world economy will grow around 2.0% this year. With regard to 1999, the Central Bank considers that this rate of growth will continue, although the new IMF projections anticipate growth of 2.5% for next year. II. Effects of the external scenario on the Chilean economy This external scenario has various effects on the Chilean economy, which are transmitted mainly through changes in the flows of the current account and capital account of the balance of payments. In the current account, the consequences of the external crisis are manifested in changes in the prices and quantities of trade in goods and services (including factor service). In the capital account, a distinction can be made between changes in investment capital flows and external financing to Chile and changes in the demand for international assets from domestic agents. (a) Effect on the terms of trade The slowdown in the global economy has reduced the dynamism of demand for major commodities. Indeed, the dollar prices of primary goods have fallen by more than 20% in the last twelve months. In particular, the price of copper fluctuated around 75 cents per pound during 1998. In the current external scenario, it is prudent to assume that for the remainder of this year and part of next, the situation will not change significantly. The medium-term outlook, meanwhile, is more optimistic, with values closer to one dollar a pound. On the other hand, the external crisis has also led to reductions in the dollar prices of other raw materials and processed products in the economies most affected by the crisis. Chile is favored by this fact, both for its effect on the current account and for the moderation in domestic inflationary pressures. During the period from January to July of this year, the average price of imports, measured in dollars, has fallen about 5.0% compared to the same period of the previous year. However, this situation cannot be projected for the future, considering that it is less likely that there will be additional decreases in the price of raw materials and, in addition, that the dollar will continue the pace of international appreciation that it has shown in the course of the last year. In sum, the reduction in the terms of trade of the Chilean economy will reach about 10% for this year, which subtracts from national income the equivalent of two percentage points, and has a negative impact on the deficit of the trade balance estimated at US 1,400 million. Part of this larger deficit is counterbalanced by the reduction in profits of foreign copper companies. (b) Effects on trade volumes Chilean export volumes increased by 7.3 per cent during the period January to July 1998 over the same period last year. The volume of copper exports grew by 14.5% and exports other than copper grew by 2.2% in the reporting period. These figures show that the effect of the external crisis on real exports is smaller than that observed in other periods of slowdown in international activity, such as those in 1991 and 1993. The reason for this is the substantial geographical reorientation of Chilean exports. In fact, it can be seen that in the period from January to July of this year, compared with the same months of 1997, the volume exported to Asia decreased by 7.9 per cent, while that corresponding to the rest of the world grew by 15.4 per cent, a phenomenon that is observed to varying degrees for all categories of goods. (c) External financing flows The third effect of the global crisis is the reduction in capital and financing flows into the country. During the first half of 1998, there was a significant decrease in portfolio investment from abroad. In any case, the sum of medium and long-term capital reached US 4,700 million in the first half of the year, substantially higher than the current account deficit in the same period and very similar to the flows received in previous years in relation to GDP. In turn, the greater preference of international investors for currencies, markets and instruments considered safer, has led to a general increase in the cost of external financing of emerging economies. However, it should be noted that these increases have been lower than those registered in other economies in the region and, in absolute terms, the cost of external financing for Chile remains well below the average for Latin America. For their part, interest rates in industrial countries, especially long-term ones, have tended to decline. III. The internal scenario of the Chilean economy The domestic scenario of the Chilean economy this year is characterized by three facts: the strong growth of domestic demand in the second half of 1997, changes in the demand for international assets of domestic agents and the solidity of the fundamentals of the economy. (a) Dynamism of domestic demand The strong dynamism of domestic demand has been a characteristic of the evolution of the economy in the present decade. In this period there has been a marked and sustained increase in the investment rate that has not been accompanied by a similar increase in national savings. Another way of looking at the same is the widening of the current account deficit over the past few years, even discounting the effect of adverse terms-of-trade fluctuations. The reason for this expansion is the good performance of the national economy, which generated an environment of greater optimism in companies and consumers, in a context of greater availability of domestic and external financing. In turn, the deepening of the domestic capital market and greater access to international financial markets provided the necessary funds to validate these spending decisions and further decouple the investment decisions of companies and households from their ability to save. These factors generated pressure for funds in the domestic market, driving up interest rates and, at the same time, a greater use of external savings (current account deficit). On the other hand, the strong willingness of international investors to increase their participation in the Chilean economy, even paying the cost of reserve requirements, more than provided the necessary resources to finance this deficit. Indeed, in 1997 the economy received net external resources of about 10 percent of GDP, almost double the financing requirements of the current account deficit. This expansion in domestic demand became more evident during the fourth quarter of 1997 and was mainly channelled into external markets, driving real import growth by over 20%. However, some of the demand pressure also shifted to domestic markets, generating very dynamic GDP growth and a narrowing labour market. Indeed, the pace of job creation began to increase in the second half of 1997, and this higher level of employment continued throughout the first part of this year, bringing the unemployment rate below its historical trend, while nominal wages continued to grow at rates close to 8% per year. (b) Accumulation of assets abroad Second, a very significant movement in the capital account during 1998 stems from increased demand for international assets by the private banking and non-banking sector. This movement has meant an increase in outflows for investments from Chile abroad d0 direct investments, portfolio investments and accumulation of other short-term assets d0 which in this period total just over US 4,400 million. These portfolio adequacy movements have been influenced by the greater degree of uncertainty in the international economy and the depreciation in the value of the peso over the last few months, reacting through a greater demand for assets that allow exchange risk hedging, as well as an increase in interest in taking advantage of greater international diversification of the asset portfolio. (c) Solid fundamentals of the Chilean economy The third characteristic of the Chilean economy is the recognized solidity of its fundamentals. The first indicator of the solidity of the fundamentals of the Chilean economy is the sustained reduction in the inflation rate. Secondly, the growth of the Chilean economy for more than a decade is based on a strong process of investment and productivity increases, which provides a good basis for medium-term growth. Third, Chile has good indicators of solvency and external liquidity, which is accompanied by adequate integration into external financial markets. The weight of external debt, the level of international reserves and the short-term financing needs of the Chilean economy compare favorably with those of other Latin American economies and those of Asian countries. Fourth, the Chilean financial system has tended towards progressive consolidation and deepening. At the same time, the financial system has good regulation and supervision. Solvency indicators, such as the level of capitalization and the proportion of the portfolio that is overdue, confirm this fact. The current external crisis has confirmed once again that it is not enough to maintain macroeconomic balances, but also requires the financial sector to be efficient and strong. Fifth, during the nineties, fiscal policy has made it possible to balance and strengthen public finances, reaching an average global surplus of 1.8% of GDP and substantially reducing public debt. In addition, the government has maintained high savings rates, which on average have been 4.5% of GDP and have made public savings one of the most stable components of national savings. IV. Monetary policy in 1998 This context of strengths, but also of strong turbulence and alterations in external markets, the rapid expansion of domestic demand and changes in the demand for international assets made inevitable the application of an adjustment policy aimed at containing the growth of domestic demand, to bring it towards levels in line with the new external scenario. while maintaining the basic balances of the economy, which are the condition for medium-term growth. In other words, the macroeconomic programme that has been in place since January 1998 aims to reduce the current account deficit over a limited period of time, without jeopardizing the economy's medium-term balances. Economic policy consistent with these objectives is based on the restrictive stance of monetary and fiscal policies. In the monetary area, the Central Bank has pushed for an increase in the cost of credit in order to deliver relevant price signals for a restriction of private spending by firms and consumers. In the last year, monetary aggregates and global credit have shown a general slowdown in their pace of growth, pointing to the trends that spending should take in the coming months. In the exchange rate area, the actions of the Central Bank are aimed at recognizing and respecting the most permanent trends of the exchange rate, but seeking to cushion their sudden movements. This is how in twelve months there has been a nominal depreciation of the peso in relation to the dollar of 14% and a real depreciation of around 6%. To make this policy more efficient, the Central Bank has made this exchange rate policy explicit, defining a narrower band for the exchange rate. In the fiscal area, an important effort has been made to promote an adjustment of government expenditures in line with the new external scenario and the objectives of macroeconomic policies. Important is the announcement regarding the growth of public expenditure for 1999, which helps to dispel doubts about the direction of fiscal policy in a year with presidential elections. It is important to recognize that one of the consequences of external turbulence is the natural uncertainty that occurs among private actors about the policies of authority. The macroeconomic programme that had been defined towards the end of 1997 needed to be adapted to the new realities. This fact generates a series of interactions between the market and the authority, where on the one hand legitimate doubts are opened regarding the prevailing policies and on the other, the new signals delivered by the authority must gain credibility. This has been one of the most relevant elements in the application of monetary policy this year and is manifested in two facts. First, the Central Bank's firm decision to maintain the inflation target at all times as a basis for ordering the rest of macroeconomic policies and as a signal for private sector decisions. Second, the greater effort to coordinate fiscal and monetary policy. In the absence of these two fundamental options, uncertainties would have increased rather than decreased. A frequent criticism of monetary policy this year suggests that an adjustment with a greater nominal devaluation would have led to an increase in the real exchange rate, which in turn would have generated a further reduction in imports and an increase in exports, helping to moderate the current account deficit more quickly. This view seems attractive, however the experience of many countries shows that behind its apparent benefits there are very significant risks. First, in the short term there are other determinants of the nominal exchange rate and interest rates, such as changes in the composition of portfolios, financial flows and investor expectations. The policies of the Central Bank must therefore maintain financial market confidence in all circumstances. Second, increases in the nominal exchange rate can lead to an increase in inflation, especially when the economy is operating with high domestic demand. Thirdly, policy objectives include achieving results over limited periods, so it is very important to consider the lags behind in macroeconomic policy instruments. All these factors can lead to an overflow of the exchange rate in the short term, which would produce other negative consequences for the growth of the economy, such as the feeding of greater financial uncertainty, volatility in key prices for the allocation of resources, the persistence of subsequent inflation and the need to develop new stabilization policies that would compromise growth for a longer period. The approach taken by monetary policy in 1998 is more balanced. Within an exchange rate band scheme, a nominal and real devaluation of the peso has been allowed, but policies have been applied that do not jeopardize economic stability and medium-term growth capacity. It is important to emphasize that analyst reports and academic studies on the Chilean economy tend to agree that the current exchange rate band is aligned with the medium-term equilibrium values of the real exchange rate in Chile and are consistent with other key prices of the economy, such as wages. V. Results and prospects The most recent background indicates that after three quarters of adjustment policies, the main economic variables are moving in the desired direction, which in turn supports the macroeconomic program that has been implemented this year. In particular, the inflation rate continues on a gradual downward path, and policies are well targeted to achieve the /-4.3 percent target for 1999 and to continue progress towards price stability in the years to come. Second, the current account deficit in 1998 will reach around 5.15 billion, but on a path of reduction next year, to be between 4 billion and 4.5 billion. In this way we approach the declared purpose for the medium term of placing this deficit at a level between 4% and 5% of GDP. Thirdly, the trend of adjustment in domestic demand is manifesting itself in this semester, as shown by the most recent figures for imports, sales of trade and industry, consumer credits. Finally, the expected trend in external demand is favourable despite the external crisis. On the one hand, the verification of very important growth rates for some products such as copper exports (due to the entry into operation of new projects and expansion of existing ones) and, possibly, the partial recovery of fishmeal production. On the other hand, the accentuation, in the second half of 1998 and, especially in 1999, of the adjustment trend in imports, with growth projected below GDP. All these elements will lead to GDP growth that will be significantly lower than the trend growth of the last decade. Last September, within the framework of the Report to the Senate, the Central Bank projected a growth rate of around 3.8%, although it must be reiterated that its effective value will depend on the evolution of the external scenario and the stability of the domestic financial market. Even with the moderate expansion expected for this and next year, the average economic growth of this decade will be the highest this century. VI. Conclusions The Chilean economy is facing complex times. The Asian crisis has put and will continue to test the country's ability to meet the challenges associated with these times of turbulence and international uncertainty. While the economy has its solid foundations, now is the time to reaffirm conviction in prudent and demanding macroeconomic policies. It is impossible for the country to maintain growth close to potential as long as the external turbulence does not subside and a process of recovery of stability in world markets is consolidated. Failure to recognize that a relatively harsher period must be faced would have an irremediably negative effect on the country's economic management, a situation that in itself would significantly deepen the effects of the Asian crisis. The globalization of markets and Chile's strong link with the rest of the world, which have allowed the country a decade of sustained growth, also contain a disciplining element on the management of macroeconomic policies that cannot be ignored and that requires a permanently cautious attitude and great zeal in defense of stability precisely in times of trial. Easy solutions do not exist. All come with costs. The Central Bank's vision is clear at the current juncture: to reaffirm its commitment to the process of gradual but consistent reduction of inflation, to a figure close to 3% per year, as well as to reiterate the intention for the current account deficit to be reduced from 1999 until it reaches reasonable levels between 4% and 5% of GDP in the medium term. Monetary policy instruments will continue to be applied in a manner consistent with these purposes. The success of this company will mean that the national economy will continue to grow at high rates in the coming years, although temporarily below its potential. But that success depends crucially on policy support. The equation is simple: the greater the support for macroeconomic policies, however demanding, the less sacrifice is made in slowing economic growth, employment and wages. The premature relaxation of adjustment policies or overreactions in the exchange rate will only affect the stability achieved over a decade and reduce the medium-term growth capacity.
text_original: La Poltica Monetaria en 1998 Exposicin de Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vicepresidente del Banco Central del Chile, en ASIMETAL 98, Santiago, 7 de octubre de 1998.  Escenario internacional El escenario internacional que enfrenta la economa chilena est marcado por el progresivo deterioro desde que se inici la crisis en Asia, hace algo ms de un ao. Sus efectos se han extendido al resto de las economas del mundo y persiste una elevada volatilidad de los mercados financieros. Todo ello produce los riesgos que estn presentes en la actual coyuntura internacional, entre los que se cuentan un deterioro adicional de la economa en Japn; nuevas rondas de desconfianza financiera sobre las economas asiticas, olas de contagio hacia otras economas emergentes; una desaceleracin ms rpida de lo esperado de la economa norteamericana, un freno de las economas europeas como consecuencia del vuelco en la balanza comercial de Asia, y la posibilidad de una correccin ms drstica en los precios de las acciones en los mercados burstiles de Estados Unidos y Europa. Dentro de este escenario de mayor incertidumbre, las proyecciones ms actualizadas sealan que la economa mundial crecer alrededor de 2,0% el presente ao. Respecto de 1999, el Banco Central considera que este ritmo de crecimiento de va mantener, aunque las nuevas proyecciones del FMI anticipan un crecimiento de 2,5% para el prximo ao.  Efectos del escenario externo sobre la economa chilena Este escenario externo tiene diversos efectos sobre la economa chilena, los que se transmiten, principalmente, a travs de cambios en los flujos de la cuenta corriente y cuenta de capital de la balanza de pagos. En la cuenta corriente las consecuencias de la crisis externa se manifiestan en alteraciones en los precios y en las cantidades del comercio de bienes y servicios (incluyendo el servicio de factores). En la cuenta de capitales se puede distinguir entre los cambios en los flujos de capitales de inversin y financiamiento externo hacia Chile y las variaciones en la demanda de activos internacionales de agentes domsticos.  Efecto sobre los trminos de intercambio La desaceleracin de la economa mundial ha restado dinamismo a la demanda de los principales productos bsicos. En efecto, los precios en dlares de los bienes primarios muestran descensos superiores al 20% en los ltimos doce meses. En particular, el precio del cobre ha fluctuado cerca de los 75 centavos de dlar la libra durante 1998. En el actual panorama externo es prudente suponer que en lo que resta del presente ao y parte del prximo, la situacin no variar significativamente. Las perspectivas de mediano plazo, en tanto, son ms optimistas, con valores ms cercanos a un dlar la libra. Por otra parte, la crisis externa tambin ha originado reducciones en los precios en dlares de otras materias primas y de los productos elaborados en las economas ms afectadas por la crisis. Chile se favorece por este hecho, tanto por su efecto sobre la cuenta corriente como por la moderacin en las presiones inflacionarias internas. Durante el perodo de enero a julio de este ao, el precio promedio de las importaciones, medido en dlares, ha cado cerca de 5,0% con relacin a igual perodo del ao anterior. Sin embargo, esta situacin no puede proyectarse a futuro, considerando que es menos probable que se produzcan disminuciones adicionales en el precio de las materias primas y que, adems, el dlar contine el ritmo de apreciacin internacional que ha mostrado en el curso del ltimo ao. En suma, la reduccin de los trminos de intercambio de la economa chilena alcanzar cerca del 10% para el presente ao, lo que resta del ingreso nacional el equivalente a dos puntos porcentuales, y tiene un impacto negativo sobre el dficit de la balanza comercial estimado en US$ 1.400 millones. Parte de este mayor dficit est contrapesado por la reduccin de las utilidades de las empresas extranjeras de cobre.  Efectos sobre los volmenes de comercio Los volmenes de las exportaciones chilenas han aumentado en un 7,3% durante el perodo enero a julio de 1998 con respecto a igual perodo del ao anterior. El volumen de las exportaciones de cobre present un crecimiento de 14,5% y las exportaciones distintas de cobre crecieron en 2,2% en el perodo sealado. Estas cifras muestran que el efecto de la crisis externa sobre las exportaciones reales es menor que el observado en otros perodos de desaceleracin de la actividad internacional, como los ocurridos en 1991 y en 1993. La razn de ello es la substancial reorientacin geogrfica de las exportaciones chilenas. En efecto, se observa que en el perodo de enero a julio de este ao, respecto de los mismos meses de 1997, el volumen exportado a Asia disminuy en 7,9%, en tanto que el correspondiente al resto del mundo creci en 15,4%, fenmeno que se observa en distinta magnitud para todas las categoras de bienes.  Flujos de financiamiento externo El tercer efecto de la crisis global es la reduccin en los flujos de capital y de financiamiento hacia el pas. Durante el primer semestre de 1998 se nota una importante disminucin en la inversin de cartera desde el exterior. En todo caso, la suma de capitales mediano y largo plazo alcanz a US$ 4.700 millones en el primer semestre, sustancialmente mayor que el dficit en cuenta corriente en el mismo perodo y muy similar a los flujos recibidos en aos anteriores con relacin al PIB. A su vez, la mayor preferencia de los inversionistas internacionales por las monedas, mercados e instrumentos considerados ms seguros, ha llevado a un incremento generalizado en el costo del financiamiento externo de las economas emergentes. Sin embargo, hay que destacar que estos aumentos han sido menores que los registrados en otras economas de la regin y, en trminos absolutos, el costo del financiamiento externo para Chile sigue siendo muy inferior al promedio de Amrica Latina. Por su parte, las tasas de inters de los pases industriales, especialmente las de largo plazo, han tendido a disminuir.  El escenario interno de la economa chilena El escenario interno de la economa chilena durante el presente ao est caracterizado por tres hechos: el fuerte crecimiento de la demanda interna en el segundo semestre de 1997, los cambios en la demanda por activos internacionales de los agentes internos y la solidez de los fundamentos de la economa.  Dinamismo de la demanda interna El fuerte dinamismo de la demanda interna ha sido una caracterstica de la evolucin de la economa en la presente dcada. En este perodo se ha observado un marcado y sostenido incremento en la tasa de inversin que no ha sido acompaado por un aumento similar del ahorro nacional. Otra forma de ver lo mismo es la ampliacin que ha mostrado el dficit de la cuenta corriente a lo largo de los ltimos aos, incluso descontando el efecto de las fluctuaciones adversas de los trminos de intercambio La razn de esta expansin est en el buen desempeo de la economa nacional, que gener un ambiente de mayor optimismo en las empresas y consumidores, en un contexto de mayor disponibilidad de financiamiento interno y externo. A su vez, la profundizacin del mercado de capitales domstico y el mayor acceso a los mercados financieros internacionales, proveyeron los fondos necesarios para validar estas decisiones de gasto y desvincular en mayor grado las decisiones de inversin de las empresas y familias de su capacidad de ahorro. Estos factores generaron una presin por fondos en el mercado domstico, impulsando al alza las tasas de inters y, a la vez, un mayor uso del ahorro externo (dficit de la cuenta corriente). Por su parte, la fuerte disposicin de los inversionistas internacionales por incrementar su participacin en la economa chilena, aun pagando el costo del encaje, aport con creces los recursos necesarios para financiar este dficit. En efecto, la economa recibi en 1997 recursos externos netos de aproximadamente 10% del PIB, casi el doble de los requerimientos de financiamiento del dficit de la cuenta corriente. Esta expansin de la demanda interna se hizo ms evidente durante el cuarto trimestre de 1997 y se canaliz, en lo fundamental, hacia los mercados externos, impulsando el crecimiento de las importaciones reales sobre 20%. Sin embargo, parte de la presin de demanda tambin deriv hacia los mercados internos, generando un crecimiento muy dinmico del PIB y un estrechamiento del mercado laboral. En efecto, el ritmo de creacin de empleos comenz a incrementarse en la segunda mitad de 1997, y este mayor nivel de empleo se mantuvo a lo largo de la primera parte del presente ao, llevando la tasa de desempleo por debajo de su tendencia histrica, al mismo tiempo que los salarios nominales permanecieron creciendo a tasas cercanas a 8% anual.  Acumulacin de activos en el exterior En segundo lugar, un movimiento muy significativo en la cuenta de capitales durante 1998 proviene del aumento de la demanda por activos internacionales por parte del sector privado bancario y no bancario. Este movimiento ha significado un aumento de las salidas por inversiones desde Chile hacia el exterior -inversiones directas, de cartera y acumulacin de otros activos de corto plazo- que en este perodo suman algo ms de US$ 4.400 millones. Estos movimientos de adecuacin de cartera han estado influidos por el mayor grado de incertidumbre de la economa internacional y la depreciacin ocurrida en el valor del peso a travs de los ltimos meses, reaccionando a travs de una mayor demanda por activos que permitan realizar coberturas de riesgo cambiado, as como tambin un aumento en el inters por aprovechar las ventajas de una mayor diversificacin internacional de la cartera de activos.  Solidez de los fundamentos de la economa chilena La tercera caracterstica de la economa chilena es la reconocida solidez de sus fundamentos. El primer indicador de la solidez de los fundamentos de la economa chilena es la sostenida reduccin de la tasa de inflacin. En segundo lugar, el crecimiento de la economa chilena por ms de una dcada est basado en un fuerte proceso de inversin y aumentos de productividad, lo que aporta un buen sustento para el crecimiento de mediano plazo. Tercero, Chile tiene buenos indicadores de solvencia y liquidez externa, lo que est acompaado de una adecuada integracin a los mercados financieros externos. El peso de la deuda externa, el nivel de las reservas internacionales y las necesidades de financiamiento de corto plazo de la economa chilena se comparan favorablemente con las de otras economas latinoamericanas y las de pases asiticos. Cuarto, el sistema financiero chileno ha tendido hacia una progresiva consolidacin y profundizacin. Al mismo tiempo, el sistema financiero tiene una buena regulacin y supervisin. Los indicadores de solvencia, como son el nivel de capitalizacin y la proporcin de la cartera que est vencida, confirman este hecho. La actual crisis externa ha confirmado una vez ms que no es suficiente mantener los equilibrios macroeconmicos, sino que tambin se requiere que el sector financiero sea eficiente y fuerte. Quinto, durante la dcada de los noventa la poltica fiscal ha permitido equilibrar y fortalecer las finanzas pblicas, alcanzando un supervit global promedio de 1,8% del PIB y disminuyendo substancialmente la deuda pblica. Adems, el gobierno ha mantenido altas tasas de ahorro, que en promedio han sido de 4,5% del PIB y que han convertido al ahorro pblico en uno de los componentes ms estables del ahorro nacional.  La poltica monetaria en 1998 Este contexto de fortalezas, pero tambin de fuertes turbulencias y alteraciones en los mercados externos, de rpida expansin de la demanda interna y de cambios en la demanda de activos internacionales hizo inevitable la aplicacin de una poltica de ajuste orientada a contener el crecimiento de la demanda interna, para llevarla hacia niveles acordes con el nuevo escenario externo, manteniendo al mismo tiempo los equilibrios bsicos de la economa, que constituyen la condicin para favorecer el crecimiento de mediano plazo. Es decir, el programa macroeconmico que se aplica desde enero de 1998 tiene como propsito reducir en un perodo acotado de tiempo el dficit de la cuenta corriente, sin arriesgar los equilibrios de mediano plazo de la economa. La poltica econmica coherente con estos objetivos esta basada en la orientacin restrictiva de las polticas monetaria y fiscal. En el rea monetaria, el Banco Central ha impulsado un incremento en el costo del crdito con el fin de entregar las seales de precios relevantes para una restriccin del gasto privado de empresas y consumidores. En el ltimo ao, los agregados monetarios y el crdito global han mostrado una desaceleracin generalizada en su ritmo de crecimiento, sealando las tendencias que debe tomar el gasto en los prximos meses. En el rea cambiara, las acciones del Banco Central estn orientadas a reconocer y respetar las tendencias ms permanentes del tipo de cambio, pero buscando amortiguar sus movimientos bruscos. Es as como en doce meses se ha verificado una depreciacin nominal del peso en relacin con el dlar de 14% y una depreciacin real en torno a 6%. Para hacer ms eficiente esta poltica el Banco Central ha explicitado esta poltica cambiara, definiendo una banda ms angosta para el tipo de cambio. En el rea fiscal, se ha realizado un esfuerzo de importancia para impulsar un ajuste de los gastos del gobierno acorde con el nuevo escenario externo y los objetivos de las polticas macroeconmicas. Es importante el anuncio respecto del crecimiento del gasto pblico para 1999, que contribuye a despejar dudas sobre la orientacin de la poltica fiscal en un ao con elecciones presidenciales. Es importante reconocer que uno de las consecuencias de las turbulencias externas es la natural incertidumbre que se produce entre los agentes privados sobre las polticas de la autoridad. El programa macroeconmico que se haba definido hacia fines de 1997 requera ser adaptado a las nuevas realidades. Este hecho genera una serie de interacciones entre el mercado y la autoridad, donde por una parte se abren dudas legtimas respecto de las polticas imperantes y por la otra, deben ganar credibilidad las nuevas seales que entrega la autoridad. Este ha sido uno de los elementos ms relevantes en la aplicacin de la poltica monetaria durante el presente ao y se manifiesta en dos hechos. Primero, la firme decisin del Banco Central de mantener en todo momento la meta de inflacin como base para el ordenamiento del resto de las polticas macroeconmicas y como seal para las decisiones del sector privado. Segundo, el mayor esfuerzo de coordinacin entre la poltica fiscal y monetaria. En ausencia de estas dos opciones fundamentales las incertidumbres habran aumentado y no disminuido. Una crtica frecuente que ha recibido la poltica monetaria durante el presente ao plantea que un ajuste con una mayor devaluacin nominal habra llevado a un aumento en el tipo de cambio real, lo que a su vez habra generado una reduccin adicional de las importaciones y un aumento de las exportaciones, contribuyendo a moderar ms rpidamente el dficit de la cuenta corriente. Este punto de vista parece atractivo, sin embargo la experiencia de numerosos pases muestra que detrs de sus aparentes beneficios hay riesgos muy significativos. Primero, en el corto plazo existen otros determinantes del tipo de cambio nominal y de las tasas de inters, como son los cambios en la composicin de las carteras, los flujos financieros y las expectativas de los inversionistas. Por consiguiente, las polticas del Banco Central deben mantener la confianza de los mercados financieros en toda circunstancia. Segundo, los aumentos en el tipo de cambio nominal pueden generar un aumento en la inflacin, especialmente cuando la economa est funcionando con una demanda interna elevada. Tercero, en los objetivos de las polticas est lograr resultados en perodos acotados, por lo que es muy importante considerar los rezagos con que actan los instrumentos de la poltica macroeconmica. Todos estos factores pueden llevar a una sobrerreacin del tipo de cambio en el corto plazo, lo que producira otras consecuencias negativas para el crecimiento de la economa, como es la alimentacin de mayor incertidumbre financiera, la volatilidad en precios claves para la asignacin de recursos, la persistencia de la inflacin posterior y la necesidad de elaborar nuevas polticas de estabilizacin que comprometeran el crecimiento por un perodo ms prolongado. El enfoque que ha aplicado la poltica monetaria en 1998 es ms balanceado. Dentro de un esquema de banda cambiara se ha permitido una devaluacin nominal y real del peso, pero se han aplicado polticas que no ponen en riesgo la estabilidad econmica y la capacidad de crecimiento de mediano plazo. Es importante subrayar que los informes de analistas y los estudios acadmicos sobre la economa chilena, tienden a coincidir que la actual banda cambiara est alineada con los valores de equilibrio de mediano plazo del tipo de cambio real en Chile y son coherentes con otros precios claves de la economa, como son salarios.  Resultados y perspectivas Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que luego de tres trimestres de aplicacin de las polticas de ajuste, las principales variables econmicas se mueven en la direccin deseada, lo que a su vez respalda el programa macroeconmico que se ha aplicado durante el presente ao. En particular, la tasa de inflacin continua sobre una trayectoria de reduccin gradual, y las polticas estn bien orientadas para conseguir la meta de +/-4,3% para 1999 y continuar en los aos venideros los avances hacia la estabilidad de precios. Segundo, el dficit de cuenta corriente de 1998 alcanzar alrededor de los US$ 5.150 millones, pero sobre una trayectoria de reduccin hacia el prximo ao, para situarse entre los US$ 4.000 millones y US$ 4.500 millones. De esta manera nos aproximamos al propsito declarado para el mediano plazo de situar este dficit en un nivel entre 4% y 5% del PIB. En tercer lugar, la tendencia de ajuste en la demanda interna se est manifestando en este semestre, como lo muestran las cifras ms recientes de importaciones, ventas del comercio y de la industria, crditos de consumo. Finalmente, la evolucin esperada de la demanda externa es favorable a pesar de la crisis externa. Por una parte, la constatacin de tasas de crecimiento muy importantes para algunos productos como las exportaciones de cobre (por la entrada en operacin de nuevos proyectos y ampliacin de otros existentes) y, posiblemente, la recuperacin parcial de la produccin de harina de pescado. Por otra, la acentuacin, en el segundo semestre de 1998 y, especialmente en 1999, de la tendencia de ajuste que llevan las importaciones, proyectndose un crecimiento por debajo del PIB. Todos estos elementos llevarn a un crecimiento del PIB que ser significativamente menor que el crecimiento de tendencia de la ltima dcada. En septiembre ltimo, en el marco del Informe al Senado, el Banco Central proyect una tasa de crecimiento en torno a 3,8%, aunque se debe reiterar que su valor efectivo depender de la evolucin del escenario externo y de la estabilidad del mercado financiero interno. An con la moderada expansin esperada para este y el prximo ao, el crecimiento econmico promedio de la presente dcada ser el mayor de este siglo.  Conclusiones La economa chilena enfrenta tiempos complejos. La crisis asitica ha puesto y seguir poniendo a prueba la capacidad del pas para enfrentar los retos asociados a estos tiempos de turbulencia e incertidumbre internacional. Aunque la economa tiene sus fundamentos slidos, sta es la hora de reafirmar la conviccin en polticas macroeconmicas prudentes y exigentes. Es imposible para el pas mantener un crecimiento cercano al potencial en tanto las turbulencias externas no amainen y se consolide un proceso de recuperacin de la estabilidad en los mercados mundiales. No reconocer que se debe afrontar un perodo relativamente ms duro provocara un efecto irremediablemente negativo en la administracin econmica del pas, situacin que por s misma profundizara significativamente los efectos de la crisis asitica. La globalizacin de los mercados y la fuerte vinculacin de Chile con el resto del mundo, que han permitido al pas una dcada de sostenido crecimiento, contienen tambin un elemento disciplinador sobre el manejo de las polticas macroeconmicas que no es posible soslayar y que obliga a una actitud permanentemente cautelosa y de gran celo en defensa de la estabilidad justamente en los momentos de prueba. Las soluciones fciles no existen. Todas acarrean costos. La visin del Banco Central es clara en la actual coyuntura: reafirmar el compromiso con el proceso de reduccin gradual pero consistente de la inflacin, hasta llevarla a una cifra cercana a 3% anual, as como reiterar el propsito para que el dficit en cuenta corriente se reduzca a partir de 1999 hasta que alcance niveles razonables entre 4% y 5% del PIB en el mediano plazo. Los instrumentos de poltica monetaria se seguirn aplicando de manera coherente con estos propsitos. El xito de esta empresa se traducir en que la economa nacional seguir creciendo a tasas altas en los prximos aos, aunque transitoriamente por debajo de su potencial. Pero ese xito depende en forma crucial del apoyo a las polticas. La ecuacin es simple: a mayor respaldo a las polticas macroeconmicas, por exigentes que sean, menor el sacrificio en cuanto a la desaceleracin del crecimiento econmico, del empleo y los salarios. El relajo prematuro de las polticas de ajuste o reacciones exageradas en el tipo de cambio, slo afectarn la estabilidad conseguida a lo largo de una dcada y reducirn la capacidad de crecimiento de mediano plazo.

Title: The Chilean economy: recent developments and prospects
text: The Chilean economy: recent developments and prospects Presentation by Jorge Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Seminario Visi97n Empresarial 2000, Universidad del Desarrollo, Santiago, September 30, 1999. I am grateful for the invitation of the Universidad del Desarrollo to participate in this Seminar. A few weeks ago, the Central Bank Council presented to the Senate a comprehensive report on the progress of the economy, the policies implemented and the outlook for the coming year. On the basis of this report, I would like to take this opportunity to refer to three subjects. In the first part, I will make some reflections on recent developments in the economy. In the second part, I will address the macroeconomic outlook and projections for the short and medium term. Finally, in the third part, I will refer to recent innovations in Central Bank policies. 1. Recent developments in the economy The evolution of the Chilean economy in the last two years is marked by two facts. The first is the external crisis, which began in Asia in the second half of 1997 and reached its greatest impact on global economic activity between the second half of 1998 and the first half of this year. The second fact is the depth and prolongation of the effects of this crisis in our country. The change in the external scenario at the end of 1997 was expressed in the contraction of the markets for our exports, the deterioration in the terms of trade, the increase in the cost of external financing and the reduction in capital flows. The magnitude of the fall in the terms of trade in 1998 reached the equivalent of 3% of GDP, a figure that in Latin America is only comparable to the scope of the crisis in Ecuador and Venezuela. The deterioration of external conditions explains most of the fall in economic activity in Chile, although most analyses of this period agree that the depth and prolongation of the recession are not entirely explained by the international crisis. Determining what additional factors acted to intensify external shocks is important, especially if this allows us to draw lessons in order to improve the operating conditions of the economy. On this occasion, I would like to explore the consequences of the increase in private sector debt, the underestimation of changed risk, and the limited diversification of non-bank private sector portfolios prior to the external crisis. One of the factors that has been at the basis of the good performance of the Chilean economy since the middle of the last decade is the growing openness to foreign markets. This fact means that the allocation of resources in Chile is quite specialized, which has allowed a rapid growth of exports to all markets of the world and greater integration into international financial markets. However, as we have seen since late 1997, the benefits of openness are accompanied by risks that originate in external markets and that are essential to manage properly. Chile's strategy to deal with the risks of globalization emphasizes maintaining healthy economic fundamentals. This means prudent macroeconomic policies, a stable financial system and a strong external solvency position. The lessons learned so far from the crisis in Asian countries confirm that this strategy is the most appropriate. However, these same lessons also allow us to reexamine the strengths and weaknesses of the functioning of the Chilean economy towards the end of 1997. The first effect of the crisis was manifested in the threat of a significant increase in the current account deficit, which was more worrying because the economy was in an expansionary cycle of its domestic demand. However, this expansion in domestic demand is important not only because of its effect on the current account deficit and the danger of an inflationary resurgence, but also because the deteriorating external scenario could have an adverse impact on the financial position of the private sector. The distinction between changes in expenditure and output flows, on the one hand, and changes in debt and equity levels, on the other, seems to be particularly important in explaining the depth and extent of the recent adjustment in private domestic demand. In particular, changes in the debt position and portfolio management decisions have accentuated the contraction in private demand. This is due to higher indebtedness, low diversification and underestimation of true exchange risk in private sector portfolios before the crisis. With regard to the increase in indebtedness, in the last 5 years there are two periods in which domestic demand expands above the trend of output. The first, between the beginning of 1995 and the beginning of 1996, had as counterpart an improvement in the terms of trade, so that it did not translate into a larger deficit in the current account. Spending and income grew at the same rate in this period. The second phase of expansion of expenditure above output occurs between the second half of 1997 and the beginning of 1998. This period coincides with a fall in the terms of trade, so domestic demand and output grow more than income. Much of this expansion was financed by strong capital inflows, which reached more than 10% of GDP in 1997. Considering that in these years the public sector presents a small surplus, the difference between domestic demand and income translates into an increase in the level of private debt. This debt increased from 22% of GDP at the beginning of 1995 to 31% of GDP in the first quarter of 1998. At the domestic level, this greater indebtedness is expressed in the expansion of loans to both companies and households. Between 1995 and the end of 1997, household debt (consumption and housing) to the financial system grew from 14 per cent to 19 per cent of GDP. In the case of companies, the increase in debt to the financial system is somewhat lower, from 37.5% to 40.4% of GDP in the same period. On the other hand, the ratio of debt equity in public limited companies rose from 0.32 times in 1995 to 0.45 times at the end of 1997. Along with this increase in debt levels, there is little diversification of the portfolios of the non-bank private sector, while the structure of assets and liabilities of companies had a clear mismatch to change it. These facts increased the risks implicit in the financial situation of the non-bank private sector. A reflection of the magnitude of this situation emerges from the changes that have occurred in portfolios since the crisis began. The trend has been a strong move towards increasing net foreign currency assets. For example, the AFPs' foreign assets rose from US225 million to US4,176 million between mid-1997 and mid-1999. Foreign currency deposits in the banking system rose from about 1.6 billion to 2.9 billion in the same period. Cumulative investments by the non-financial private sector abroad (through Chapter XII) increased from US4,302 million to US12,132 million in the last two years. In turn, total forward foreign exchange operations, which allow better management of exchange risk, rose from a net sold position of the financial sector equivalent to US1,219 million to US4,498 million in the same period. These figures show the mismatch and increased risk in private sector portfolios before the onset of the crisis. Increases in private debt do not represent a difficulty for the future stability of the economy as long as they remain within moderate ranges and are accompanied by proportional growth in output. With this, the relationship between debt and income remains limited. For example, if output grows at around 7% per year, international inflation is 2%, net payment to foreign direct investment is equivalent to 1% of GDP and the level of real debt sought to be maintained is 35% of GDP, then the current account deficit that keeps the debt-to-output ratio stable can be between 4% and 4.5% of GDP. As noted, towards the end of 1997 there was an increase in private spending in the economy, leading to a current account deficit well above this figure. Additionally, in this period the greatest risk is present due to the mismatch and the little diversification of the portfolios of the private sector. The question arises as to what are the reasons for the sharp swing in private sector spending and the increase in risk to its financial position. Undoubtedly, abundant capital flows and favorable expectations play a fundamental role in both events. A closer look at this period, however, must recognize that the interest rate differential and the extrapolation of the exchange rate appreciation trend reduced the expected cost of external financing and, most likely, led to an increase in desired levels of debt. In these circumstances there was a concentration of the private portfolio in pesos and UF, with a mismatch against positions in foreign currency, which was scarcely covered. Monetary policy lost part of its ability to affect the evolution of domestic spending and the current account deficit, because a segment of the market was created that had access to cheap external financing. By mid-1997 the domestic real interest rate was around 6.5%, the interest rate in dollars around 6.3% and the appreciation of the exchange rate with respect to the UF was more than 4% per year, which meant an interest differential that the current reserve did not cover. In the debate on exchange rate regimes that has followed the Asian crisis, emphasis is placed on both signals for the level of the real exchange rate and for the value of exchange rate risk. When the exchange rate system seeks to establish medium-term guidelines for the real exchange rate, consistent with a sustainable current account deficit, a conflict can arise between the stability of this signal and the tolerance of a currency risk that reflects market forces. The situation of the Chilean economy in 1997 can be seen as an example of this conflict. The result was an environment in which the true exchange risk was underestimated, leading to further increases in debt levels, without adopting a position aimed at hedging that risk. For the same reason, during this period there is little diversification, international and by currency, of the investors' portfolio, which also tends to generate a higher level of risk. The natural way out of this situation was a gradual correction in spending levels, a moderation of the uncovered exchange rate mismatch and a diversification in investments. With this, it would be possible to restore the evolution of the patrimonial position of the private sector to a sustainable trajectory and with a more limited risk. However, this process of gradual adjustment was made impossible by the external crisis. As the crisis spread and deepened, the option of a gradual return to sustainable levels of spending and moderation of portfolio risk became increasingly complex. In this environment, there is not only a sharp downward correction in spending flows due to lower income, but also a change in debt levels that the private sector wishes to maintain and a massive change in the composition of portfolios. The interaction between these three elements amplified the impact of the external crisis on the business cycle and financial prices, such as the exchange rate and the interest rate, and is of particular importance in explaining the sharp fall in domestic demand in 1999. A characteristic of financial markets is the existence of frictions that stem from information problems and incentives. For these reasons, credit tends to flow on more abundant and advantageous terms when agents have a stronger financial position and there are favorable prospects. The weakening of the private sector's financial position stems from falling national income due to lower terms of trade, rising costs of external financing affecting all emerging economies, expectations of devaluation, the danger of further tightening of external credit, policy credibility problems, and high domestic interest rates. This restricts the flows of financing available to this sector and also affects the demand for new financing. At the same time, there are linked effects between the financial situation of companies and households. The reduction in sales and employment reduces the expected income of households, which also adjust their financial position and level of spending. In addition, the fall in aggregate demand tends to reduce the value of the assets of companies and households, which tends to further deteriorate their financial position and access to new credit. The amplification of the effects of the external crisis through financial mechanisms also explains why the recovery of economic activity is slower. For this reason, the recovery of the equity position of the private sector is essential for the normalization of spending. This is a gradual process, influenced by perspectives on external conditions, the stance of macroeconomic policies, and the normalization of credit flows to firms and households. It is important to note that despite the greater effect of the external crisis on domestic demand and activity, the financial system has remained sound, as have liquidity and external solvency indicators. For this reason, Chile has kept its risk rating intact, a situation that contrasts sharply with other emerging economies. Regarding the lessons of this period, one of the most complex dilemmas of macroeconomic policy in small and open economies is how to prevent the consequences of expansions of private spending that are financed by external borrowing. These episodes usually raise deficits in the current account of the balance of payments and alter the real exchange rate. The more traditional view is that private sector imbalances tend to correct automatically. However, experience has shown that this approach has serious limitations. Similarly, fiscal policy flexibility to offset these fluctuations in private spending is limited. Hence, the need has arisen to move in two directions: first, the improvement of macroeconomic policy instruments to give more stability to aggregate demand in the face of changes in external conditions, and second, to improve the functioning of the different markets so that the adjustment to shocks is more efficient and less traumatic. In the first line, the improvement of policy instruments aims to achieve a lower degree of procyclicality of aggregate demand. This could be achieved, for example, by setting multi-year targets for both inflation and public expenditure growth. The effectiveness of these instruments, however, is not independent of the prevailing institutional framework. Thus, it is necessary to move towards greater transparency of monetary and fiscal policies, in order to ensure the credibility of these policies. Only if the institutional framework ensures the achievement of multi-year targets can this greater flexibility of policy instruments not erode their effectiveness. But there are also other institutional aspects that can contribute to achieving greater stability in aggregate demand. For example, better prudential regulation and supervision of the financial sector, aimed at promoting self-regulation of the sector, can reduce the risk of bubbles and credit booms. The most interesting developments, however, lie in the second line. That is, to achieve a better functioning of the markets so that the economy can adjust to the different shocks in a less traumatic way. This includes mechanisms to allow for greater diversification of public and private sector revenue sources. In addition, promoting the use of hedging instruments would reduce the impact of shocks on the wealth of individuals and companies, thus limiting the pro-cyclicality of credit. In the same vein, improving the functioning of markets entails reducing the rigidities of the economy. Perhaps the most important aspect in this case is to reduce the degree of indexation of our economy, which will be achieved in an increasing way now that we have reached sustainably low and credible levels of inflation. In addition, an important step in this direction has recently been achieved by allowing greater exchange rate flexibility, which will mean that in the future the private sector will correctly assess this risk and thus avoid the excesses of the past. It should be noted that this progress would not have been possible without the inflationary achievements to which I have just referred. Similarly, it is important to improve the quality of information for private investment decisions. For example, at present it is quite difficult to know the position of fit to change it in open corporations. The risks exist and to the extent that they are properly evaluated they can be better managed, reducing the vulnerabilities they represent. To the extent that we can draw conclusions from recent experience, we will be able to provide the Chilean economy not only with better conditions for reactivation, but also for medium-term growth. We at the Central Bank are actively working in this direction, as shown by the important policy innovations that have been adopted in recent months. 2. Outlook 1999 and 2000 In the current circumstances of the Chilean economy, the main task of economic policy is to create the conditions to resume the path of growth. No doubt this will be the result of the action of the multiple factors that influence private decisions. However, on this occasion, I would like to analyze four conditions to strengthen the recovery and ensure that it is linked to sustained growth in output. These conditions are: improvement of the external scenario, orientation of macroeconomic policies, functioning of the financial system and normalization of domestic demand. The gradual improvement of the external scenario is a first element that will support the recovery. Although the international situation is still complex, its prospects anticipate better international conditions relevant to Chile. In particular, a greater dynamism of external demand and an improvement in the terms of trade are expected. The IMF's latest estimates anticipate a gradual recovery in world output, reaching growth of 3.0 percent this year and 3.5 percent in 2000. In the case of Latin America, this recovery will mean going from practically zero growth in 1999 to 3.9% next year. The price of copper, meanwhile, rose from 65 cents per pound in the first half to 76 cents in the third quarter. The price of pulp has also tended to recover in recent months. A slower increase is observed in the country risk margins in financial loans, which have remained stable during this year. The volume of exports has maintained a substantial expansion throughout the period of the crisis. For example, in the second half of 1998 and in the first half of this year, the quantity index of exports of goods shows annual growth of the order of 8.2 per cent, somewhat higher than the growth of total exports of goods and services. These developments and the movements in the real exchange rate allow us to anticipate that the Chilean economy is in a position to take advantage of the opportunities presented by the recovery of foreign markets. This improvement in the external scenario, however, is not without threats. Among the main risk factors are the magnitude of possible additional increases in interest rates in the US and their negative impact on the growth of the US and world economy, and the reappearance of financial turbulence in Latin American markets as a result of the difficult situation that most of the economies of the region are going through. Second, the macroeconomic policy stance over the past year has clearly been expansionary. Monetary policy has sought to create appropriate financial conditions to boost a recovery in private domestic demand. The more dynamic behavior of monetary aggregates is consistent with the reduction in interest rates. For its part, the exchange rate has shown greater fluctuations, which respond to market trends. The average real exchange rate in the last quarter is about 7 per cent higher than the 1998 average. That is, monetary policy has an expansionary orientation, which is what corresponds in the current conditions and as long as there are no threats to inflation. Fiscal policy, for its part, has been a countercyclical driver of aggregate demand during 1999. The 12-month fiscal surplus narrowed significantly in the second half of 1998 and turned into deficits during the first half of this year. Towards the end of 1999 the fiscal accounts will show a deficit result, although a trend towards reversing this situation could begin in the second part of the year. This development is mainly linked to the position of the business cycle and the role that fiscal policy should play in the face of output fluctuations. This deficit should be reversed when the recovery in economic activity and the terms of trade allow tax revenues to normalize. Ensuring a trend in fiscal accounts towards more balanced levels is an essential element for the future development of Central Bank policies. Indeed, a possible continuation of the fiscal deficit would lead in the medium term to increased permanent pressures on domestic demand and the current account deficit of the balance of payments, which would ultimately raise the level of interest rates and introduce uncertainty in financial markets. This can further delay private spending decisions. In this sense, the design of the budget for the coming years is very important, in order to reconcile the indispensable credibility of a prudent fiscal policy, throughout the cycle, with the influence that short-term variables have on the deficit. A third element influencing the recovery is the functioning of the financial system.
