Recent developments in the performance of the banking system have shown solvency conditions, despite the difficulties in the economy. The accumulated profitability of the financial system before taxes reached 12.7% until August of this year, which is somewhat lower than historical figures, although higher than international standards. The non-performing loan portfolio as a percentage of total loans remained at around 1.7% between April and August, which does not represent a risk factor for financial stability. The wealth of the financial system, measured by the Basel indicator, has increased in the recent period. These figures provide confidence in the possibilities of recovery and medium-term growth, due to the role played by the financial system in the intermediation and allocation of resources in the economy. On the other hand, the growth of loans normally moves with some lag with respect to the economic cycle. For this reason, the fact that placements show practically zero real growth reflects the depth of the cycle, rather than a foretaste of the evolution of private demand. In summary, what we can infer from the figures of the financial sector is that this sector is solid and that it has the capacity to sustain the recovery. The laggard component to the recovery in global demand is domestic private demand. Given that external conditions and the stance of macroeconomic policies have a direct influence on the evolution of this demand, it is possible to expect a gradual recovery in the remainder of 1999 and more marked in the coming year. Both variables act with a lag in demand, which in this cycle has been longer than expected. Some indicators, such as the evolution of the most liquid monetary aggregates, the production and sales of industry, imports and sales of new homes point to a recovery in demand and economic growth. Other indicators, on the other hand, lag behind in the signs of recovery. This is the case for sales of commerce, sales of new cars and building permits. However, considering the determinants of private demand, both consumption and investment, it is possible to anticipate that the level of activity would begin to move on an expansion trajectory that would allow the economy to reach a growth rate of around 5% over the next year, an estimate that is consistent with the range of forecasts of various private analysts. This trajectory would be led by the recovery in domestic demand, estimated at around 7.5%. The effect of the recovery on the external accounts will lead to an increase in the current account deficit, which will reach around 1.5% of GDP by the end of the year, to levels of around 3.3% of GDP. This is mainly due to a strong recovery in the value of imports to restore diminished inventories and respond to expected growth in domestic demand. With regard to inflation, 1999 has seen a faster decline than anticipated, as a result of the impact of the business cycle on price formation and lower external inflation. Wages have continued to slow gradually, albeit at a slower pace than other prices, resulting in real increases despite falling employment and national income. There are conflicting elements in the future evolution of the inflation rate. On the one hand, the low inflation achieved this year will keep the usual inertial impulse in a wide range of prices of goods and services limited. Likewise, a gradual recovery rate of economic activity and the slack that exists in terms of employment and installed capacity should contribute to moderate demand pressures not pushing inflation. On the other hand, higher external inflation, together with the recovery of marketing margins in some sectors, especially imported goods, will be factors of upward pressure on prices. All in all, measures of core inflation and market and analyst prospects are focused on around 3.5% for 2000, although with still a wide dispersion. The latter should not be surprising given the greater uncertainty that can be associated with a turning point in a cycle as acute as the current one. 3. Central Bank Policies After the international crisis and considering its repercussions on the Chilean economy, the policies of the Central Bank have had some modifications that seek to improve the functioning of the economy, especially in its ability to adapt to changes in the external scenario. Three are the most important innovations introduced in this period. First, the capital account has been further opened up by reducing the reserve requirement rate to zero on the entry of certain categories of capital. This has made it possible to reduce the effect of the increase in the cost of external financing for Chilean companies and to facilitate the financial decisions of economic agents in a period of greater turbulence in foreign markets. Secondly, progress has been made in the process of easing the changed market by suspending the formal commitment to intervene in this market to sustain the limits of the exchange rate band. This change means that the risk of changing it becomes more transparent, which is a necessary condition for better financial management in the private sector. From now on, the market will be the agent in charge of determining the value of the currency and the Central Bank will only intervene in exceptional cases, a situation in which the reasons that were in view to make the decision to intervene will be explained. Likewise, to give credibility to this policy, disaggregated information on the holdings of international reserves and their changes will be provided. All of the above will allow a freer floating of the exchange rate and, as a consequence, degrees of greater monetary autonomy that, in turn, will facilitate in the future the management of potential external turbulence and the correct perception of risks by the private sector. Thirdly, a new inflation-targeting system has been announced, which responds to the diagnosis that the inflationary containment programme is moving to a different stage. For this reason, the Central Bank defined the inflation target of b1 3.5% for the year 2000 and simultaneously a range of 2% to 4% per year, centered on 3%, as the medium-term inflation target to be in force indefinitely since 2001. In the future, this range may be altered, but always respecting the central purpose of maintaining a low inflation environment. By prioritizing a gradual but persistent reduction in inflation, the new targeting system favors the maintenance of a low and more stable inflation environment, around parameters such as those currently observed. The most relevant aspect of this new scheme is that the inflation target has a horizon greater than one year, which provides an explicit and permanent signal of commitment to price stability. Among the advantages of working with a broader horizon is the possibility of accommodating events that affect inflation in the short term but do not alter its medium- and long-term trend. The extension of the horizon is also appropriate to adequately reflect the lags that characterize the impact of monetary policy on price developments and to moderate possible effects on activity. Finally, the specification of the inflation target must reconcile the permanent purpose of price stability with the operation of an environment of greater exchange rate flexibility, which can generate temporary pressures on inflation, both upwards and downwards. This is an appropriate environment to advance in reducing the degree of indexation of the Chilean economy, which will be achieved to the extent that we maintain sustainably low and credible inflation levels. In summary, the Central Bank estimates that there are no major obstacles for the economy to achieve a gradual recovery in its growth rate in the coming quarters, in a context of low inflation and a moderate current account deficit. The external conditions of the economy are showing a more favorable scenario, the monetary policy stance is clearly expansionary and the financial system is in a solid situation. These developments should lead to a gradual normalization of private domestic demand, which is the laggard component for the recovery of global demand. Central Bank policies will retain the flexibility necessary to adapt to economic developments and support economic recovery objectives within a framework of price stability.
text_original: La economa chilena: evolucin reciente y perspectivas Exposicin de Jorge Marshall, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, en el Seminario Visin Empresarial 2000, de la Universidad del Desarrollo, Santiago, 30 de septiembre de 1999. Agradezco la invitacin de la Universidad del Desarrollo a participar en este Seminario. Hace algunas semanas el Consejo del Banco Central present al Senado un completo informe sobre la marcha de la economa, las polticas aplicadas y las perspectivas para el prximo ao. Sobre la base de este informe, quisiera aprovechar esta oportunidad para referirme a tres materias. En la primera parte, har algunas reflexiones sobre la evolucin reciente de la economa. En la segunda parte, abordar las perspectivas y proyecciones macroeconmicas para el corto y mediano plazo. Finalmente, en la tercera parte, har referencia a las innovaciones recientes en las polticas del Banco Central.  Evolucin reciente de la economa La evolucin de la economa chilena en los ltimos dos aos est marcada por dos hechos. El primero es la crisis externa, que se inicia en Asia en el segundo semestre de 1997 y que alcanza su mayor impacto en la actividad econmica global entre el segundo semestre de 1998 y el primer semestre de este ao. El segundo hecho es la profundidad y prolongacin de los efectos de esta crisis en nuestro pas. El cambio en el escenario externo de fines de 1997 se expres en la contraccin de los mercados para nuestras exportaciones, el deterioro en los trminos de intercambio, el aumento en el costo del financiamiento externo y la reduccin en los flujos de capitales. La magnitud de la cada de los trminos de intercambio en 1998 alcanz al equivalente de un 3% del PIB, cifra que en Amrica Latina slo es comparable al alcance que tuvo la crisis en Ecuador y Venezuela. El deterioro de las condiciones externas explica la mayor parte de la cada en la actividad econmica en Chile, aunque la mayora de los anlisis sobre este perodo coincide en que la profundidad y prolongacin de la recesin no se explican enteramente por la crisis internacional. Determinar qu factores adicionales actuaron para intensificar los impactos externos es importante, especialmente si esto nos permite sacar lecciones en orden a perfeccionar las condiciones de funcionamiento de la economa. En esta oportunidad quisiera explorar las consecuencias que se derivan del aumento en la deuda del sector privado, la subestimacin del riesgo cambiado y la escasa diversificacin de las carteras del sector privado no bancario antes de la crisis externa. Uno de los factores que ha estado en la base del buen desempeo de la economa chilena desde mediados de la dcada pasada es la creciente apertura a los mercados externos. Este hecho significa que la asignacin de recursos en Chile es bastante especializada, lo cual ha permitido un crecimiento rpido de las exportaciones hacia todos los mercados del mundo y una mayor integracin a los mercados financieros internacionales. Sin embargo, como hemos comprobado desde fines de 1997, los beneficios de la apertura estn acompaados de riesgos que se originan en los mercados externos y que es fundamental administrar adecuadamente. La estrategia seguida por Chile para enfrentar los riesgos de la globalizacin enfatiza mantener los fundamentos econmicos sanos. El aspecto ms relevante de este nuevo esquema es que la meta de inflacin tiene un horizonte mayor a un ao, lo que entrega una seal explcita y permanente de compromiso con la estabilidad de precios. Entre las ventajas de trabajar con un horizonte ms amplio est la posibilidad de acomodar eventos que afectan la inflacin en el corto plazo pero que no alteran su tendencia de mediano y largo plazo. La extensin del horizonte tambin es apropiada para reflejar adecuadamente los rezagos que caracterizan el impacto de la poltica monetaria sobre la evolucin de los precios y moderar eventuales efectos sobre la actividad. Finalmente, la especificacin de la meta inflacionaria debe conciliar el propsito permanente de estabilidad de precios con la operacin de un ambiente de mayor flexibilidad cambiara, que puede generar presiones transitorias sobre la inflacin, tanto al alza como a la baja. Este es un ambiente apropiado para avanzar en disminuir el grado de indexacin de la economa chilena, lo que se lograr en la medida que mantengamos niveles de inflacin sostenidamente bajos y crebles En sntesis, el Banco Central estima que no existen obstculos importantes para que la economa alcance en los trimestres venideros una recuperacin gradual de su ritmo de crecimiento, en un contexto de baja inflacin y un dficit de cuenta corriente moderado. Las condiciones externas de la economa estn mostrando un escenario ms favorable, la orientacin de la poltica monetaria es claramente expansiva y el sistema financiero presenta una situacin slida. Estos hechos deben producir una gradual normalizacin de la demanda interna privada, que es el componente ms rezagado para la recuperacin de la demanda global. Las polticas del Banco Central conservarn la flexibilidad necesaria para adaptarse a los desarrollos econmicos y apoyar los objetivos de recuperacin econmica en un marco de estabilidad de precios.

Title: International capital mobility and financial market development
text: International mobility of capital and Development of financial markets Presentation by Jorge Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Meeting Economic "Regulationof the Capitales", Santiago, 24 May 2000. I appreciate the invitation to participate in this Meeting on the Regulation of the Capital. The theme proposed by the organizers of this meeting is important and timely. On the one hand, it allows us to analyze the challenges to advance in the development of the financial markets in Chile and, on the other hand, we can incorporate into this debate the Lessons from the recentglobal financial crisis and the recommendations emerging from the Review of the international financial architecture. The approach that the analysis of capital market regulation should have is given by the relationship between financial developmentand economic growth. The evidence empirical shows that countries with more efficient capital markets and Deep are in a position to achieve higher growth rates. Markets financial facilitates investment financing, improve resource allocation, support more efficient risk management and enable more stable currents of consumption and investment. Considering this favorable evidence, we must examine the challenges to continue in the itstrengthens and develops Chile's financial markets. The exhibitions gathered in this meeting, as well as the analysis of the multiple development experiences They indicate that an efficient and stable capital market is the resultof multiple factors, among which the quality of the institutional infrastructure of the country, macroeconomic stability, development of financial institutions and regulatory and supervisory practices. The absence of any of these factors can generate the conditions that trigger financial crises, such as those that have affected numerous countries in the last 20 years. In this exposition I will analyze, from thepoint of view and perspective of the Central Bank, the influence of the international capital mobility in the development of financial markets and in the requirements of prudential regulation. For this purpose I will explore, in the first part, the conditionsfor achieving efficiency and stability in financial markets. Later I will review the indicators of the development of the financial markets in Chile during the last decade. Thirdly, I will examine the Central Bank's policies for the International financial integration. Finally, I will summarize the main conclusions. Efficiency and stability of financial markets Financial stability requires, on the one hand, a high degree of confidence on the part of the Member States. participants in which markets canmaintain their operations over time without interruptions and, on the other hand, reasonable confidence that financial prices - 1 - reflect economic fundamentals and do not vary substantiallyin the short term when the fundamentals remain unchanged. In turn, the condition of efficiency requires that financial markets make a good allocation of resources, in terms of cost and Risk management. To achieve theseobjectives, financial markets need to be deep. In a small economy and intermediate development, such as Chile's, integration Financial with the rest of the world and international capital mobility are steps essentialto strengthen and improve the functioning of financial markets National. The benefits of international capital mobility in market development There are several financial institutions. First, it supports the efficiency and strength of the financial system, allowing lower financial costs, faster incorporation ofinnovations and better resource allocation. Second, it provides liquidity to the markets and reduces liquidity constraints in unfavourable periods. Third, it facilitates diversification of risks and protects the domestic economy fromexternal shocks. All this allows Stabilise income, consumption and investment flows, reducing the intensity of cycles and the traditional dependence of domestic economic activity on the prices of our exports. Fourth,international competition introduces discipline into the macroeconomic policies and encourages better financial policies. However, experience has shown time and again that to achieve these benefits Financial liberalization alone is not enough. The reason for this is that both the financial system domestic and international, operate under conditions of asymmetric information, in that one of the parties has more information about the potential profitability and risk of operations that lto another. This situation leads to problems of moral hazard, selection adverse and herd effect on financial markets. Information problems are They become more serious in economies that are just beginning their integration process. In addition, the existence of explicit and implicit insurance, either in the countries receiving the flows or in creditor countries contribute to the existence of excess capital flows or a misallocation of them. The same effect can also occur at the timeof rescue programmes carried out by multilateral organizations. These behaviors cause the financial system to take risks beyond what a financial system would recommend. situation of efficiency, which constitutes the rationality of regulation. These difficulties occur in markets that are characterized by volatile. In indicators summarizing the experience of the past decade is observed, for example, that the markets Advanced country stock market prices showed price volatilityof between 15% and 25%. The exchange parities of the main currencies have a volatility around 10%. In international bond markets price volatility is between 5% and 10% (Figure 1). To the extent that volatility reflects changes in variables It is not a basis for regulation. However, the problems of asymmetric information can widen the volatility of financial markets, Just as volatility also amplifies information problems. asymmetrical and high leverage. - 2 - In another field, the experience of the past decade shows that capital flows to emerging countries are also highly volatile and easily reversed (Chart 2). At the beginning of the 90s these flowsreached about US150 billion per year. They then grew rapidly to over US200 billion in the 1995 triennium. 1997. More recently these flows have been restricted to levels around US100 trillions and it is expected that in the coming years they will remain around these levels more Moderate. That is, apart from the benefits indicated, international capital mobility generates risks that may affect efficiency and stability objectives. First, there is a risk formacroeconomic stability when capital flows . inflows or output. reach high levels relative to the economy's ability to absorb or adjust to these movements. In this situation, asset prices They can misalignthemselves with their fundamentals and increase macroeconomic instability. Second, capital mobility makes risk management more complex financial, especially for the use of foreign currencies in operations International. Thirdly, capital mobility increases the risks of contagion of external financial crises. Consequently, the same fundamentals of financial regulation at the domestic level are present at the international level, which leads to the need to address the financial integration with the outside world with a vision that weighs both the benefits and the risks of international capital mobility. In the search for thisand balance has of great importance is the degree of development of domestic financial markets, including depth, liquidity and efficiency, because risks to stability macroeconomic are higher the less developed the less developed thefinancial markets are Domestic. Therefore, advancing in the deepening of the capital market in Chile is One of the main challenges we face today. In turn, by size of our economy This deepening must be supported byincreasing integration. international finance. However, apart from the development of the financial market, the efficiency and stability of the Financial systems are achieved with some degree of prudential regulation and with a Adequate supervision. In thissense, the second challenge we must face is to design regulatory and supervisory schemes that serve as a basis for a sound development of the financial system, capable of preventing crises. Development of financial markets in Chile Amore developed financial market is better able to integrate efficiently with the outside. In this sense, depth, efficiency and integration are mutually reinforcing processes within an appropriate regulatory framework. For this reason, It is relevant to analyze the recent development of the capital market and especially its degree of international financial integration. - 3 - With regard to the depth of the financial market, Chile presentsa development in line with the which corresponds to their level of per capita income (Figure 3). However, for mobility of capitals, contributing to the efficiency and stability of the financial markets, must be accompanied by a stable macroeconomic environment and adequate prudential regulation. In this regard, the policies of the Central Bank have followed by the criteria of gradualness and prudence. The first is based on the necessary sequence between the development of the domestic financial market and its capacity to Addressing and managing the new risks of international financial integration. The Prudential approach is due to the recognition of the risks of international mobility of capital, especially those derived from strong capital flows, such as observed in Chile until 1997. Although the application of these criteria has meant incurring microeconomic costs, they have allowed progress in integration financial with a more favourable composition of international liabilities .with more weighting of long-term debt and equity. and in better solvency conditions international. In the most recent period, the Central Bank has continued to take important steps towards the international financial integration. The Bank's policies Central in this matter can be grouped into four categories: operation of the foreign exchange market; capital outflow regulations; the - 5 - regulations on capital inflows and rules that improve information in the markets. (c) Capital inflow regulations The regulation of capital inflows was one of the most complex issues in manage for much of the past decade, due to the high number theyachieved capital flows to Chile, with the consequent risk to stability Macroeconomic. The world's appetite for investing in the country made us fear strong. Relative price misalignments in the short term, with effects on external solvency and trade-based economic growth. Under these conditions, the prudential regulations sought selectivity in capital flows, privileging investment and long-term debt. As I mentioned earlier, this Policy allowed progress in financial integration with a more favorable composition of international liabilities and in better conditions of international solvency. More recently, restrictions on capital inflows have been lifted under the The foreign exchange market has reached a greater development, with more depth and varianceof Instruments. Also contributing to this result is greater diversification in the domestic investor portfolios and moderation of capital flows to the country. Thus, in 1998 the reserve rate was reduced to zero and recently eliminated the minimum permanence restriction. - 7 - Other restrictions on capital inflows, such as amounts and classifications of risk to bond issues and ADRs have been systematically reduced. In fact There are currently no minimum amount requirements. An important step in financial integration policies is the recent modification of the The rule permitting the issuance of internationalrecurrent bonds in pesos or units of promotion. In this way, a new instrument is created that allows to improve the profile of risk of external debt. (d) Information Policies Another element necessary for capital mobility to support good functioning of financial markets is the quality of information for decision making. The Information is one of the most efficient instruments to deal with the imperfections of financial markets. For this reason, the actions of the Bancor Central are aimed at improve transparency in economic policy decisions and in the delivery of increasingly complete and specific information, reducing transaction costs and facilitating the efficient allocation of resources. An important example in this area is the recent publication of the Policy Report. Monetary, which presents theCentral Bank's view of recent developments in the economy and prospects over a two-year horizon. This Report gives more transparency to the fundamentals of monetary policy decisions. In the same Sense points to the information on thedates of monetary policy meetings and the publication of minutes of Council minutes, including individual votes of the directors. Chile has also signed the IMF's special data publication program. (SDDS), which establishes standardized criteria on periodicity and format of the information. Work is currently underway on the publication of the investment position international (IIP), which will present information on the stocks of assets andexpenditures of the economy as a whole and four subsectors: general government, monetary authorities, banking and other sectors. text_original: Movilidad internacional de capitales y desarrollo de los mercados financieros Exposicin de Jorge Marshall, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, en el Encuentro Econmico Regulacin del Mercado de Capitales, Santiago, 24 de mayo de 2000. Agradezco la invitacin a participar en este Encuentro sobre la Regulacin del Mercado de Capitales. El tema propuesto por los organizadores de esta reunin, es importante y oportuno. Por una parte, nos permite analizar los desafos para avanzar en el desarrollo de los mercados financieros en Chile y, por la otra, podemos incorporar a este debate las lecciones de la reciente crisis financiera global y las recomendaciones que emergen de la revisin a la arquitectura financiera internacional. El enfoque que debe tener el anlisis de la regulacin del mercado de capitales est dado por la relacin entre el desarrollo financiero y el crecimiento econmico. La evidencia emprica muestra que los pases que poseen mercados de capitales ms eficientes y profundos estn en condiciones de lograr tasas de crecimiento ms altas. Los mercados financieros facilitan el financiamiento de la inversin, mejoran la asignacin de recursos, admiten una administracin ms eficiente de los riesgos y permiten corrientes ms estables de consumo e inversin. Considerando esta favorable evidencia debemos examinar los desafos para continuar en la senda que fortalece y desarrolla los mercados financieros de Chile. Las exposiciones reunidas en este encuentro, as como los anlisis de las mltiples experiencias de desarrollo financiero, indican que un mercado de capitales eficiente y estable es el resultado de mltiples factores, entre los cuales destaca la calidad de la infraestructura institucional del pas, la estabilidad macroeconmica, el desarrollo de las instituciones financieras y las prcticas de regulacin y supervisin. La ausencia de cualquiera de estos factores puede generar las condiciones que gatillan crisis financieras, como las que han afectado a numerosos pases en los ltimos 20 aos. En esta exposicin analizar, desde el mbito y perspectiva del Banco Central, la influencia de la movilidad internacional de capitales en el desarrollo de los mercados financieros y en los requisitos de la regulacin prudencial. Para este efecto explorar, en la primera parte, las condiciones para lograr eficiencia y estabilidad en los mercados financieros. Luego revisar los indicadores del desarrollo de los mercados financieros en Chile durante la ltima dcada. En tercer lugar, examinar las polticas del Banco Central para la integracin financiera internacional. Finalmente, resumir las principales conclusiones. Eficiencia y estabilidad de los mercados financieros La estabilidad financiera requiere, por una parte, de un alto grado de confianza de los participantes en que los mercados pueden mantener sus operaciones en el tiempo sin interrupciones y, por la otra, de una razonable confianza en que los precios financieros - 1 - reflejan los fundamentos econmicos y que no varan sustancialmente en el corto plazo cuando los fundamentos no se modifican. A su vez, la condicin de eficiencia exige que los mercados financieros realicen una buena asignacin de los recursos, en trminos de costo y administracin de los riesgos. Para alcanzar estos objetivos es necesario que los mercados financieros sean profundos. En una economa pequea y de desarrollo intermedio, como la chilena, la integracin financiera con el resto del mundo y la movilidad internacional de capitales son pasos indispensables para fortalecer y mejorar el funcionamiento de los mercados financieros nacionales. Los beneficios de la movilidad internacional de capitales en el desarrollo de los mercados financieros son varios. Primero, apoya la eficiencia y la fortaleza del sistema financiero, permitiendo menores costos financieros, una incorporacin ms rpida de las innovaciones y una mejor asignacin de recursos. Segundo, aporta liquidez a los mercados y reduce las restricciones de liquidez en los perodos desfavorables. Tercero, facilita la diversificacin de riesgos y protege a la economa domstica de los shocks externos. Todo esto permite estabilizar los flujos de ingreso, consumo e inversin, reduciendo la intensidad de los ciclos y la tradicional dependencia que tiene la actividad econmica interna de los precios de nuestras exportaciones. Cuarto, la competencia internacional introduce disciplina en las polticas macroeconmicas e incentiva a aplicar mejores polticas financieras. Sin embargo, la experiencia ha mostrado una y otra vez que para conseguir estos beneficios no basta la sola liberalizacin financiera. La razn de ello es que tanto el sistema financiero domstico como el internacional, operan bajo condiciones de informacin asimtrica, en que una de las partes tiene ms informacin sobre la rentabilidad potencial y el riesgo de las operaciones que la otra. Esta situacin conduce a problemas de riesgo moral, seleccin adversa y efecto manada en los mercados financieros. Los problemas de informacin se hacen ms serios en economas que recin inician su proceso de integracin. Adems, la existencia de seguros explcitos e implcitos, ya sea en los pases que reciben los flujos o en los pases acreedores, contribuyen a que pueda existir un exceso en los flujos de capitales o una mala asignacin de los mismos. El mismo efecto tambin se puede producir a partir de los programas de rescate realizados por los organismos multilaterales. Estas conductas causan que el sistema financiero asuma riesgos ms all que los que recomendara una situacin de eficiencia, lo que constituye la racionalidad de la regulacin. Estas dificultades ocurren en mercados que se caracterizan por ser voltiles. En indicadores que resumen la experiencia de la dcada pasada se observa, por ejemplo, que los mercados burstiles de los pases avanzados mostraron una volatilidad en los precios de entre 15% y 25%. Las paridades cambiarias de las principales monedas tienen una volatilidad en torno a un 10%. En los mercados internacionales de bonos la volatilidad de los precios es entre 5% y 10% (Grfico 1). En la medida en que la volatilidad refleja los cambios de las variables fundamentales no constituye un fundamento para la regulacin. Sin embargo, los problemas de la informacin asimtrica pueden ampliar la volatilidad de los mercados financieros, del mismo modo como la volatilidad tambin amplifica los problemas de informacin asimtrica y de alto leverage. - 2 - En otro campo, la experiencia de la dcada pasada muestra que los flujos de capitales hacia los pases emergentes tambin son altamente voltiles y se revierten con facilidad (Grfico 2). A comienzos de los aos 90 estos flujos alcanzaron a unos US$150 billones anuales. Luego crecieron rpidamente hasta superar los US$200 billones en el trienio de 1995 a 1997. Ms recientemente estos flujos se han restringido a niveles en torno a los US$100 billones y se espera que en los prximos aos se mantengan alrededor de estos niveles ms moderados. Es decir, aparte de los beneficios sealados, la movilidad internacional de capitales genera riesgos que pueden afectar los objetivos de eficiencia y estabilidad. Primero, hay un riesgo para la estabilidad macroeconmica cuando los flujos de capitales de entrada o de salida alcanzan niveles elevados en relacin con la capacidad de la economa para absorber o ajustarse a estos movimientos. En esta situacin los precios de los activos pueden desalinearse de sus fundamentos y aumentar la inestabilidad macroeconmica. Segundo, la movilidad de capitales hace ms compleja la administracin de los riesgos financieros, especialmente por el uso de monedas extranjeras en las operaciones internacionales. Tercero, la movilidad de capitales acenta los riesgos de contagio de las crisis financieras externas. En consecuencia, los mismos fundamentos de la regulacin financiera a escala domstica estn presentes al nivel internacional, lo cual conduce a la necesidad de enfrentar la integracin financiera con el exterior con una visin que pondere tanto los beneficios como los riesgos de la movilidad internacional de capitales. En la bsqueda de este balance tiene gran importancia el grado de desarrollo de los mercados financieros domsticos, incluyendo profundidad, liquidez y eficiencia, debido a que los riesgos para la estabilidad macroeconmica son mayores mientras menos desarrollados esten los mercados financieros domsticos. Por tanto, avanzar en la profundizacin del mercado de capitales en Chile es uno de los principales desafos que enfrentamos en la actualidad. A su vez, por el tamao de nuestra economa esta profundizacin debe apoyarse en una creciente integracin financiera internacional. Sin embargo, aparte del desarrollo del mercado financiero, la eficiencia y estabilidad del sistema financiero se alcanzan con algn grado de regulacin prudencial y con una adecuada supervisin. En este sentido, el segundo desafo que debemos enfrentar es disear esquemas de regulacin y supervisin que sirvan de base para un desarrollo slido del sistema financiero, capaces de prevenir las crisis. Desarrollo de los mercados financieros en Chile Un mercado financiero ms desarrollado est en mejores condiciones para integrarse eficientemente con el exterior. En este sentido, profundidad, eficiencia e integracin son procesos que se refuerzan mutuamente en un marco regulatorio adecuado. Por esta razn, es relevante analizar el desarrollo reciente del mercado de capitales y especialmente su grado de integracin financiera internacional. - 3 - En materia de profundidad del mercado financiero, Chile presenta un desarrollo acorde al que corresponde a su nivel de ingreso por habitante (Grfico 3). Para un conjunto de pases seleccionados se aprecia una relacin positiva entre profundidad financiera y desarrollo. En efecto, los pases con mayor profundidad financiera son Estados Unidos y Japn. Chile muestra una mayor profundidad financiera que el resto de los pases de Amrica Latina y niveles similares a pases como Australia y Nueva Zelandia. La misma posicin relativa se observa en la relacin entre el endeudamiento del sector privado con instituciones financieras y el PIB (Grfico 4). Chile ocupa un lugar intermedio, por encima de otros pases de la regin. Es interesante apreciar el aumento de este indicador, desde un 47% en 1990 a un 68% en 1997. Respecto de la profundidad del mercado burstil, medido por el coeficiente de capitalizacin con relacin al PIB, Chile muestra niveles ms altos que varios pases desarrollados y muy superior al resto de Amrica Latina (Grfico 5). Sin embargo, en este caso los avances ms importantes se alcanzaron hasta mediados de los aos 90. En materia de integracin financiera se observa un progreso significativo durante la dcada pasada. Este avance se refleja tanto en el volumen como la composicin del financiamiento externo del sector privado, que ha presentado un crecimiento importante al pasar de una cifra cercana al 20% del PIB en 1990 a un nivel en torno a 60% del PIB el ao 1999 (Grfico 6). En la composicin de este aumento destacan la favorable evolucin de las colocaciones de bonos y ADR por parte empresas locales, principalmente durante la segunda mitad de la dcada. Del mismo modo como ha sido relevante la captacin de capitales externos por parte del sector privado, es importante destacar el significativo aumento en los activos internacionales de los inversionistas domsticos (Grfico 7). Las inversiones directas y de carteras del sector privado en el exterior representaban slo un 0,5% del PIB en 1990, mientras que en 1999 alcanzaron un 25% del PIB. Si se considera que la integracin es un proceso de dos vas que incluye pasivos y activos internacionales Chile presenta un alto grado de integracin financiera. La posicin de inversiones internacionales muestra que el pas no est significativamente distante de las economas ms desarrolladas (Grfico 8). Sin embargo, si comparamos el grado de integracin slo considerando la inversin de cartera, la situacin es distinta (Grfico 9). Aqu, si bien Chile ha avanzado en la ltima dcada, an se encuentra lejos de las economas ms desarrolladas. La liquidez de los mercados financieros es el aspecto menos desarrollado del mercado de capitales chileno. En el caso del mercado cambiario tanto spot como de derivados la liquidez en relacin con el PIB ha aumentado notablemente, aunque sigue siendo menor que en los pases desarrollados de acuerdo a las transacciones realizadas en 1998 (Grficos 10 y 11). Con todo, en la comparacin con los pases de la regin Chile presenta condiciones de liquidez algo menores que las de Mxico y mayores que las de Argentina y Brasil. En el caso de la liquidez del mercado accionario, en relacin con la capitalizacin de mercado, Chile exhibe los niveles ms bajos entre el conjunto de pases considerados - 4 - (Grfico 12). En este indicador se debe considerar, entre otros factores, la influencia de las caractersticas estructurales del mercado chileno. Por ltimo, en materia de sofisticacin del mercado financiero, se han logrado avances muy importantes en los ltimos aos, entre los cuales estn los derivados cambiarios y las transacciones de derivados con el exterior. A pesar de estos avances, Chile muestra an mercado financieros incompletos cuando se compara la variedad de productos con las economas ms desarrolladas, lo que nos indica el sentido y direccin del avance futuro. A partir del anlisis de los puntos anteriores se pueden concluir que Chile exhibe avances significativos en trminos de integracin con los mercados internacionales durante la ltima dcada, tanto en la atraccin de capitales externos como en la salida de inversionistas domsticos a otros mercados. Hay que destacar que ste ha sido un proceso gradual, que ha respetado la necesaria secuencia entre el desarrollo financiero domstico y la integracin financiera con el exterior. Por otra parte, si bien la profundidad de los mercados financieros domsticos se encuentra en un nivel conforme al grado de desarrollo econmico de Chile, existen aspectos que deberan ganar importancia, como son el desarrollo de nuevos productos financieros y la liquidez del mercado burstil y de renta fija. En este ltimo caso, sin embargo, se debe reconocer que existen tendencias ms globales hacia la integracin y centralizacin de las operaciones accionarias en un nmero menor de mercados que en el pasado. Polticas para la integracin financiera Como hemos sealado, la integracin financiera internacional es el paso natural para fortalecer y profundizar el mercado financiero chileno. Sin embargo, para que la movilidad de capitales sea un factor positivo, que contribuya a la eficiencia y estabilidad de los mercados financieros, debe estar acompaada de un ambiente macroeconmico estable y de una regulacin prudencial adecuada. En este sentido, las polticas del Banco Central han seguido los criterios de gradualidad y de prudencia. El primero se fundamenta en la necesaria secuencia entre el desarrollo del mercado financiero interno y su capacidad para enfrentar y administrar los nuevos riesgos de la integracin financiera internacional. El criterio de prudencia se debe al reconocimiento de los riesgos de la movilidad internacional de capitales, especialmente los que se derivan de los fuertes flujos de capitales, como los observados en Chile hasta 1997. A pesar que la aplicacin de estos criterios ha significado incurrir en costos microeconmicos, ellos han permitido avanzar en la integracin financiera con una composicin ms favorable de los pasivos internacionales con ms ponderacin de deuda de largo plazo y de capital y en mejores condiciones de solvencia internacional. En el perodo ms reciente el Banco Central ha continuado dando pasos importantes para la integracin financiera internacional. Podemos ahora afirmar que se han completado todas las medidas ms relevantes que permiten hacer de la movilidad internacional de capitales un medio para fortalecer el desarrollo del mercado financiero. Las polticas del Banco Central en esta materia se pueden agrupar en cuatro categoras: las orientadas al funcionamiento del mercado cambiario; las regulaciones a la salida de capitales; las - 5 - regulaciones a la entrada de capitales y las normas que perfeccionan la informacin en los mercados. El criterio aplicado en estas polticas ha sido eliminar las restricciones a los flujos de entrada y de salida en la medida que los mercados alcanzan una mayor flexibilidad, profundidad y eficiencia. (a) Desarrollo del mercado cambiario La movilidad internacional de capitales debe apoyarse en un ambiente macroeconmico estable. Particular importancia tiene para este efecto la coherencia entre la poltica monetaria y cambiaria. En el caso de Chile, el logro de una inflacin baja y el perfeccionamiento del esquema de poltica monetaria, que considera metas de inflacin de mediano plazo y la publicacin peridica de un Informe de Poltica Monetaria, constituyen pasos muy relevantes para captar los beneficios de una mayor movilidad de capitales. A su vez, el actual rgimen de flotacin cambiaria, en que el Banco Central se ha comprometido a intervenir slo en casos excepcionales y a explicar las razones cuando stas intervenciones se realicen, junto a las polticas para dotar de profundidad al mercado cambiario y ampliar el uso de instrumentos de cobertura de riesgos, son el complemento adecuado del rgimen monetario vigente en Chile. En una perspectiva ms amplia, las acciones del Banco Central se orientaron por varios aos a aumentar la integracin de los mercados cambiarios, hasta que en 1997 se liber el acceso al mercado cambiario formal. Con esta medida se logr la completa integracin del mercado cambiario y desapareci el margen entre el tipo de cambio del mercado formal e informal. Esta misma orientacin se ha mantenido en una serie de acciones de simplificacin de las operaciones cambiarias. Por ejemplo, en 1999 se redujeron las exigencias para ingresar capitales al pas, se eximi a los deudores de la obligacin de obtener autorizacin previa para ingresar crditos cuando se cumplen ciertos requisitos bsicos y se elimin la obligacin de liquidar en el mercado formal estos crditos. Tambin se autoriz a los inversionistas y aportantes de capital a disponer en el pas de las divisas ingresadas y postergar la liquidacin hasta el momento de la remesa. En materia de instrumentos para la profundizacin de los mercados tambin se han realizado avances significativos. En conjunto con la Superintendencia de Bancos se han autorizado en los ltimos dos aos las operaciones bancarias en futuros, forward y swap sobre moneda nacional y extranjera, tasas de inters y unidades de reajustabilidad autorizadas, entre s o con terceras partes establecidas en el pas o en el exterior. Tambin se elimin el requisito de autorizacin previa para operaciones de derivados de tasas de inters con el exterior. Es importante destacar que la profundizacin de mercado ha buscado compatibilizar el desarrollo de nuevos instrumentos con las necesidades de administrar adecuadamente los riesgos que ellos generan. En efecto, siempre que se ha autorizado el uso de nuevos instrumentos, primero se han adoptado las normas que limitan los riesgos que pueden asumir los bancos, como es el caso de la exposicin al riesgo cambiario y de tasa de inters. Las normas que requieren que los bancos se preocupen de los descalce de monedas de sus - 6 - deudores apuntan en este mismo sentido y permitirn seguir avanzando en la generacin de nuevos mercados e instrumentos financieros. (b) Regulaciones a la salida de capitales La regulacin de las salidas de capitales ha seguido la misma trayectoria que las polticas de desarrollo del mercado cambiario. De hecho, a medida que se fue liberalizando este mercado, se adoptaron diversas medidas para facilitar las inversiones de los residentes en el exterior. En efecto, en 1992 se elimin la autorizacin previa para inversiones en el exterior cuando stas se realizaban con divisas del mercado cambiario informal. Luego, con la unificacin de los mercados se ampli la gama de inversiones a realizar con divisas del mercado cambiario formal. Ya no hay limitaciones a la salida de capitales, lo cual ha permitido un crecimiento significativo de los activos internacionales de Chile durante la ltima dcada. Asimismo, coherente con esta poltica de facilitar las salidas de capitales se han ampliado los lmites a la composicin de la cartera de los inversionistas institucionales y bancos. En 1992 se autoriz por primera vez a las AFP a invertir en el extranjero un 1,5% del valor del fondo. Luego este porcentaje se fue aumentando hasta llegar a un 16% en la actualidad. Es importante recordar que en 1998, cuando el Congreso aprob la ampliacin de los lmites de las inversiones de las AFP en el exterior a un 20%, con un sub-lmite de 10% en renta variable, el total de estas inversiones alcanzaban, en promedio, a un 1% del valor del fondo. Por esta razn, los efectos que traera esta ampliacin eran an una incgnita. En la actualidad, a la luz de los positivos resultados alcanzados, se dan las condiciones para seguir avanzando con prudencia en esta materia. (c) Regulaciones a la entrada de capitales La regulacin de las entradas de capitales fue uno de los temas ms complejos de administrar durante gran parte de la dcada pasada, debido al elevado nivel que alcanzaron los flujos de capitales hacia Chile, con el consiguiente riesgo para la estabilidad macroeconmica. El apetito del mundo por invertir en el pas nos hizo temer fuertes desalineaciones de precios relativos en el corto plazo, con efectos sobre la solvencia externa y el crecimiento econmico basado en el comercio exterior. En estas condiciones, las regulaciones prudenciales buscaron una selectividad en los flujos de capitales, privilegiando la inversin y la deuda de largo plazo. Como mencion anteriormente, esta poltica permiti avanzar en la integracin financiera con una composicin ms favorable de los pasivos internacionales y en mejores condiciones de solvencia internacional. Ms recientemente las restricciones a la entrada de capitales se han eliminado conforme el mercado cambiario ha alcanzado un mayor desarrollo, con ms profundidad y variedad de instrumentos. Tambin han contribuido a este resultado la mayor diversificacin en las carteras de los inversionistas nacionales y la moderacin de los flujos de capitales hacia el pas. De esta manera, en 1998 se redujo a cero la tasa del encaje y recientemente se elimin la restriccin de permanencia mnima. - 7 - Otras restricciones a la entrada de capitales, como son los montos y las clasificaciones de riesgo para las emisiones de bonos y ADR han sido sistemticamente reducidas. De hecho, actualmente no existen requisitos de montos mnimos. Un paso importante en las polticas de integracin financiera es la reciente modificacin de la norma que admite la emisin de bonos internacionales reajustables en pesos o unidades de fomento. De esta manera se crea un nuevo instrumento que permite mejorar el perfil de riesgo de la deuda externa. (d) Polticas sobre informacin Otro elemento necesario para que la movilidad de capitales apoye el buen funcionamiento de los mercados financieros es la calidad de la informacin para la toma de decisiones. La informacin es uno de los instrumentos ms eficientes para enfrentar las imperfecciones de los mercados financieros. Por esta razn, las acciones del Banco Central estn orientadas a mejorar la transparencia en las decisiones de poltica econmica y en la entrega de informacin cada vez ms completa y especfica, disminuyendo los costos de transaccin y facilitando la eficiente asignacin de recursos. Un ejemplo importante en esta materia es la reciente publicacin del Informe de Poltica Monetaria, que presenta la visin del Banco Central de la evolucin reciente de la economa y de las perspectivas en un horizonte de dos aos. Este Informe da mayor transparencia a los fundamentos de las decisiones de poltica monetaria. En el mismo sentido apunta la informacin sobre las fechas de las reuniones de poltica monetaria y la publicacin de las minutas de las actas del Consejo, incluyendo las votaciones individuales de los consejeros. Por otra parte, Chile ha suscrito el programa especial de publicacin de datos del FMI (SDDS), que establece criterios estandarizados sobre periodicidad y formato de la informacin. Actualmente se est trabajando en la publicacin de la posicin de inversiones internacionales (IIP), que presentar informacin de los stocks de activos y pasivos de la economa como un todo y de cuatro subsectores: gobierno general, autoridades monetarias, sector bancario y los dems sectores. Desde el punto de vista del sector financiero, las acciones orientadas a mejorar la informacin de los mercados tienen una contraparte en el momento de aportar la informacin al Banco Central. La paulatina liberalizacin de las normas sobre movilidad de capitales ha llevado a sustituir los canales tradicionales de recopilacin de informacin por nuevas exigencias ms directas que cumplan este propsito. Es importante reconocer que para que los mercados operen con mejor informacin es indispensable el aporte del sector privado en proveerla. Conclusiones La primera conclusin de este anlisis es que Chile ha logrado un importante grado de integracin financiera en la ltima dcada. En la actualidad contamos con mercados ms desarrollados y profundos. Continuar en esta senda, mejorando los aspectos en que tenemos - 8 - un menor avance, es tambin el principal desafo que enfrentamos para fortalecer nuestro sistema financiero. Del mismo modo como se ha hecho hasta ahora, sta es una tarea que plantea mltiples responsabilidades, tanto al sector privado como a los organismos encargados de definir las polticas y aplicar la supervisin del sistema. En segundo lugar, la integracin financiera internacional apoya la profundidad y flexibilidad de los mercados. Estas condiciones, junto a un ambiente macroeconmico estable, permiten enfrentar mejor los shocks de la economa internacional. Cuando estos impactos ocurren, la mejor forma de absorberlos es distribuyendo sus efectos en muchos mercados y precios, lo que permite mantener corrientes ms estables de ingreso, consumo e inversin. Las acciones del Banco Central han estado encaminadas a avanzar gradualmente en esta direccin y en la actualidad podemos afirmar que se ha completado una etapa importante de este proceso. En tercer lugar, debemos reconocer que los riesgos asociados a la movilidad internacional de capitales seguirn presentes. En la medida que contemos con mercados ms profundos estaremos en mejores condiciones para administrar y absorber estos riesgos. En la actual etapa de la integracin internacional la flexibilidad del mercado cambiario y las polticas de informacin deben cumplir un rol ms relevante para enfrentar estos riesgos. Por ltimo quisiera insistir que Chile se encuentra en una posicin privilegiada para seguir avanzando en la tarea de fortalecer la eficiencia y estabilidad del sistema financiero. Para lograr xito en este desafo debemos reconocer que la integracin financiera internacional debe actuar como un complemento de la infraestructura institucional del pas, la estabilidad macroeconmica, la calidad de la administracin de las instituciones financieras y las prcticas de regulacin prudencial y supervisin. Con este enfoque coherente estaremos creando bases firmes y resistentes para aportar con nuestro trabajo al crecimiento y desarrollo del pas. Title: Economic recovery: assessment and prospects
text: Economic recovery: assessment and prospects Presentation by Jorge Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile at ENAPE 2000, Santiago, 27 July 2000 I want to thank the First Small Business Meeting for the opportunity to share with you some personal reflections on the progress of the economy. The theme of this panel reflects the willingness of the organizers to analyze in greater detail the progress of the recovery and the challenges to consolidate a sustained pace of growth. In the first part of this presentation I will review the situation based on the Monetary Policy Report of last May. This analysis shows that the recent evolution of the economy does not fundamentally alter the macroeconomic outlook presented by the Central Bank just over two months ago: economic activity growing at a rate of around 6% per year for the next two years and an inflation rate in line with the Central Bank's target. However, private sector growth expectations, for this and next year, have moved slightly lower over the past two months. This fact has generated some concern about the ongoing reactivation. For this reason, in the second part of the presentation I will make an assessment of this process. This analysis highlights the observation that the recovery of the Chilean economy and the growth expected until 2001 are clearly above the average of the emerging economies of Asia and Latin America after the Asian crisis. Despite this, it is also noted that the recent recovery shows a somewhat slower pace than previous periods of recovery. This fact can be explained by the change in the internal and external scenario of the economy and by the sectoral adjustments that are manifested as the recovery progresses. The recovery of the economy Since mid-1999, the Chilean economy has been on a trajectory of growth and low inflation. The core measure of inflation remains below 3% per year, while the annual change in the total CPI stands at 3.7%. The difference between these two measures of inflation is mainly explained by the increase in prices linked to oil, energy and transport during the current year. Despite this, there is no evidence of an acceleration in the rest of the prices at the consumer level, so the trend of inflation remains controlled. Externally, the outlook for the world economy for 2000 and 2001 is favourable, with an overall growth rate averaging slightly above 4 per cent per annum. Within this framework, the most relevant fact is the affirmation of the scenario of gradual slowdown of the US economy. In addition, the dynamism of economic activity in Europe has increased and there is a healthy speed of recovery in the emerging economies of Asia and Latin America, although the latter region moderated its pace of recovery during the first half of this year. The price of copper continues to fluctuate around 80 cents per pound, and an average price between 80 and 85 cents per pound is projected for this and next year. With regard to other export prices, the favourable trend in the price of pulp stands out, with an increase of 40 per cent over the 1999 average in the first half of the year. The price of oil, on the other hand, presents an adverse picture since in the last three months it has oscillated around US 28 per barrel. Although futures market prices anticipate a downward trajectory during the remainder of this year and, especially, in the next, the expected prices of oil and its derivatives have been corrected upwards since the May Monetary Policy Report. Despite this fact, it is expected that the relevant terms of trade for the Chilean economy will improve by about 5% over the next two years. International financing conditions have remained tight throughout the recovery period and no significant changes are expected for the remainder of the year. Despite this, in recent weeks the scenario of a gradual adjustment in the United States has been affirmed. This has mitigated international financial volatility and allowed a slight downward adjustment in longer-term external rates, as well as a decrease in Chile's sovereign prize. Domestically, the latest trend shows that monetary conditions have become more expansionary. Indeed, the monetary policy interest rate has remained at 5.5% since last March. However, between May and July, the PRBC90 rate fell by about 25 basis points, while the PRC8 rate fell by more than 35 basis points. These facts are consistent with the decline in the expectation of increases in the policy interest rate, while in the case of longer-term rates the decrease in external rates and sovereign risk also influences. The most liquid monetary aggregates (circulating and MIA) tend to stabilize after a slowdown in the first half of the year. This behavior has been similar to that presented by most indicators of industrial sales and production in this period, after discounting the effects associated with seasonal factors. On the other hand, the broader monetary aggregates (M2 and M7) maintained the signal of recovery. Total effective placements show a similar assessment. From the analysis of the components of credit to the private sector to June, it can be seen that credit to companies presents somewhat more dynamic conditions than in previous months. Credit to individuals, meanwhile, shows a stagnation in consumer loans and a recovery in housing loans, which is linked to the gradual recovery in domestic demand. Relative to the exchange rate, between May and July the peso depreciated by about 4 percent against the U.S. dollar and 5 percent against a broader basket of developed-country currencies. This trajectory is in the direction anticipated in the latest Central Bank Report, although to date it presents a greater intensity. International financial market volatilities and recent developments in domestic conditions have contributed to this exchange rate movement. With regard to economic activity, the initial diagnosis of gradual recovery persists: cumulative growth to May reached 6.1% annually, with a slightly higher increase in aggregate spending. This increase was supported by a recovery in the components of consumption and the accumulation of demand inventories. Gross capital formation fell by around 4% in the first quarter, although recent months have seen a change in the trend in imports of capital goods. Exports showed high growth during the first half of the year, with an annual expansion of 17.1% in value terms. The evolution recorded by sales abroad of the industrial sectors stands out, with an increase of 17.5% in the first half of the year and mining, with a growth of 24.6% in the same period. On the other hand, different oil imports continue on a path of increase, with annual growth rates of 16.3% in the first half of the year. In this area, the growth of imports of capital goods stands out, which reached 5.2% in the second quarter of the year. Trend that reverses the fall of 5.9% observed in the first quarter. Recent developments in the labour market also reflect the slow recovery in aggregate demand, although the most recent national data for the March-May rolling quarter show that employment growth excluding special programmes is 1.5% per year. This figure is higher than in previous moving quarters. Fiscal policy, meanwhile, is expected to remain more austere this year, after having shown an expansionary stance between 1996 and 1999. This development is consistent with the Budget Law approved for the year 2000 and with the intention indicated by the government authorities to gradually recover a fiscal surplus of 1% of GDP. The fiscal information for the first quarter of this year is consistent with the baseline scenario of the May Report. In summary, it can be concluded that so far the recovery in domestic demand has been based on private consumption and inventory replenishment. The prospects for a recovery in investment are still weak, at least for the remainder of this year, taking into account the surplus of installed capacity and the expected contraction in public investment. On the external demand side, there is a high level of dynamism. The balance of these factors allows us to maintain the projection of economic growth around 6% for the next two years. With regard to inflation, international fuel prices have oscillated around levels higher than those reflected by domestic prices. In addition, the recent evolution of the exchange rate may have a greater pass-through effect towards the prices of tradable goods, which to date has not been observed in the set of these prices. In any case, these events would mainly affect the short-term evolution of inflation, and not its trend represented by core inflation. Private sector inflation expectations, as derived from surveys conducted by the Central Bank, have moved marginally upwards from April, with inflation expected for December 2000 standing at 4.3% in July. Despite this higher inflation expectation for the current year, it should be noted that in 2001 it remained stable at 3.5%. Recovery in perspective To assess recent developments in the Chilean economy from a broader perspective, it is first possible to compare the pace of recovery of economic activity after the 1997-98 financial crisis in a number of emerging economies. For this purpose, figure 1 presents the levels of actual GDP for the period 1996-1999 and the most up-to-date estimate of the expected level for the years 2000 and 2001. (Consensus Forecast) Figure 1. Evolution of GDP (1996100) This comparison shows that, compared with 1996, Chile has maintained higher output levels throughout the period than the average of the emerging economies of Asia and Latin America. Asian countries had a fall in GDP in 1998 and have since experienced a clear recovery. According to these estimates, the GDP of these countries in 2001 will be 18 per cent higher than the level reached in 1996. The situation in Latin America is somewhat less favourable. GDP fell in 1999, a year later than in Asia, and in 2001 an average GDP level of 14% is expected to be 14% higher than in 1996. On the other hand, the actual and expected evolution of Chile's GDP is above the average of these two groups of countries. Like the rest of Latin America, Chile experienced a fall in GDP in 1999, but considering the whole period, it will reach a GDP level of 24% above the 1996 level in 2001. The first conclusion of this analysis is that the Chilean economy is in a clear process of recovering its growth rate. In addition, the recent and expected evolution of GDP in the Chilean economy is clearly above the average of emerging Asia and Latin America in the same period. A second approach to examining the recovery in a broader perspective is to compare the current recovery cycle of the Chilean economy with the growth observed in the 12 months following the lowest points of the cycles since 1990. Naturally, recovery periods show higher growth rates than the average for the decade. In this comparison, which uses only effective information, it is obtained that the rate of growth in the first year of recovery was between 8.1% and 11.4% in the cycles prior to the Asian crisis. On the other hand, one year after the fall in 1999, the rate of recovery reached 6.8%. Figure 2. While the magnitude of the difference is small when put in the context of normal fluctuations in the pace of growth of the Chilean economy, it is possible to consider the slower pace of growth of the Chilean economy. recovery as the result of the internal and external scenario facing the economy. To illustrate this fact, Table 1 shows the evolution of some variables that characterize this scenario, such as net capital flows, changes in household indebtedness, copper prices, interest rates, changes in the real exchange rate and world GDP growth. After the Asian crisis, there has been a change in the external financing conditions of all emerging economies and, in particular, of the Chilean economy. The recovery periods up to 1997 were characterised by significant and increasing capital inflows. For example, in the 1990-91 recovery, net external flows reached 3.8 percent of GDP, rising in the following years to 8.0 percent of GDP in the 1997-98 recovery. In the recovery of In 1999-2000, by contrast, net capital flows amounted to 0.1 per cent of GDP. Part of this phenomenon can be explained by the decline in capital flows to emerging economies, which should be considered a more durable factor, a consequence of the dynamism of productivity and investment in the United States and the fall in its savings, which has pushed the balance of international rates upwards. However, another part is due to the correction in the pace of expansion of domestic spending, which before the crisis presented figures that were clearly unsustainable. This last observation is reinforced by verifying the significant increase in real household debt with the financial system in the three recovery scenarios prior to the Asian crisis. The speed of expansion of this debt in these episodes constituted a strong stimulus factor to domestic demand. In the most recent period, in contrast, there has been a stagnation in household debt between the twelve months before and after the start of the recovery. This reflects a more cautious spending behaviour in this sector. Another relevant factor occurs with the price of copper, which reflects the evolution of the terms of trade. In the recovery periods of 1990-91 and 1994-95, the price of copper remained above its historical average. In the most recent period, in contrast and despite the recovery compared to 1999, the price of copper has been one of the lowest in the last decade. The medium-term outlook for the terms of trade is more favourable. Table 1.
