Por su parte, la poltica monetaria ha adoptado una posicin ms expansiva, lo cual tambin permite anticipar un aumento en la demanda agregada. Para el Banco Central, la poltica monetaria debe responder con flexibilidad a las desviaciones de la trayectoria proyectada de la inflacin en relacin con la meta establecida.

Title: Economic Scenarios
text: Capital flows to emerging economies Economic Scenarios PRESENTATION BY JORGE MARSHALL R., VICE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, MADE AT THE 2002 REGIONAL CONFERENCE SERIES, ORGANIZED BY EL DIARIO, IN COPIAPee, on May 1 7, 2002. In the aftermath of the Asian crisis, capital flows to emerging economies have remained around 40 percent below the level reached in 1996-97. While financial conditions in emerging economies have improved, and their sovereign spreads have shown a downward trend, including Chile's sovereign bonds, this has not translated into an increase in financial flows to these economies. Recent figures show that there has been a shortage of foreign direct investment flows, especially to Latin America. For this reason, the scenarios that we have considered most likely contain a conservative view of capital flows to emerging economies, although in the case of Chile, the materialization of the agreement with the European Union may give a new positive impetus to this type of investment. The May 2002 Monetary Policy Report, recently published by the Central Bank of Chile, highlights three key aspects of the current situation: a5 Output reached its slowest growth rate in the first months of the year, and now shows signs of gradual expansion. a5 Domestic demand has recovered since the beginning of the year, following the fall in 2001. a5 The inflation outlook has declined substantially and broadly. The evolution d0 recent and future d0 of these three fundamental variables is caused by a series of factors, some of them have been developing for several years and others have appeared more recently. The developments of these factors configure scenarios around which it is possible to think about the future. Precisely, one of the aspects that captures the most attention in the preparation of the Monetary Policy Report is the identification of the variables that drive the changes we observe in the economy. Establishing and analyzing these variables allows us to build different scenarios that illustrate the possible future developments of the economy. Among them is the central scenario, which serves as the basis for monetary policy decisions. On this occasion, we will analyze four factors that configure, in our opinion, future economic scenarios: international capital flows, the cycle of the world economy, the economic difficulties of the region and domestic expectations of medium-term growth. The cycle of the world economy The world economy experienced a sharp slowdown in 2001. World output growth slowed from 4.7 per cent in 2000 to 2.3 per cent in 2001. The effects of this cycle continue to be seen in the first months of this year, particularly in sharp declines in aggregate industrial production and trade flows. In addition, financial uncertainty increased in developed economies, especially in stock markets, last year, and the terrorist attacks of September 11 occurred. These conditions had an internal impact on increased uncertainty and a reduction in expenditure, which continued until the end of 2001. The latest figures show a more promising international outlook for the period 2002-2003, as the outlook for growth in global activity has improved, especially in the United States. There is also greater optimism in the growth prospects for the European zone, and even for Japan the projections indicate growth for next year. This background allows us to consider scenarios in which the world economy recovers gradually in the course of 2002 and more strongly in 2003. These developments on the international scene are expressed in the evolution of the prices of our exports. For this year only a slight increase in the price of copper is expected, to stand at USS 0.73 per pound, with a further increase towards 2003 and 2004. So far, this evolution is more than offset by higher projections for the price of oil during this year. This means that the terms of trade will remain this year at average levels similar to those of last year, to rebound 4% annual average during the 2003. The region's economic difficulties A third relevant factor for the future scenarios of the Chilean economy comes from the difficulties observed in the region. Latin America's output remained stagnant in 2001 and the outlook for 2002 is even worse. Of particular relevance are the effects of the critical situation that the trans-Andean economy is going through, but the outlook for most countries in the region is bleak. It is important to note that the effects of the regional situation have changed in relative importance, from a situation of fear of more significant financial contagion, until November 2001, to the dissipation of this risk, but also to the manifestation of adverse effects in the commercial sphere. Our exports to Argentina fell by around 60% and the flow of tourists decreased by about half in the first quarter of this year. An annual and combined projection of these two effects has a direct impact of around 0.3 percentage points on gross domestic product (GDP) growth, an effect that increases to about 0.5 if indirect effects are taken into account. The problems of the Argentine economy have also had a negative effect on the income-generating capacity of Chilean companies with operations in Argentina, which has been reflected in decreases in their equity value. It is estimated that the decline in profits earned from investments in that country directly affects national income in 2002 by about 0.2 per cent of GDP, to which must be added the effects of lower activity. The relevant scenarios consider a picture of stagnation of regional output in 2002 and a recovery in 2003, in line with greater regional stability and a scenario of global growth. Moderation of domestic demand A relevant aspect of the economy in 2001 was the decline in domestic demand, while output continued to grow. In this situation there is a transitory part, which should be reversed in the coming quarters, and another, which responds to the medium-term growth prospects. Undoubtedly, developments in the external scenario affected the most variable components of demand, such as inventories, durable consumption and investment in machinery. At present, the history of spending suggests that a rebound in these components of demand will consolidate. There are, on the other hand, components of domestic demand that respond to medium-term growth prospects and persistent unemployment. Regular consumption, which is one of the most stable components of spending, has shown a very moderate trend of growth. In recent years, we have witnessed a gradual decline in the medium-term outlook, measured in the growth anticipated by economic analysts for two years from now. This has an influence on the trend in consumption, private investment and employment. Considering this trend, the greater optimism shown by the ADIMARK Economic Perception Index in the first quarter of this year, which reverses the strong pessimism observed towards the third quarter of 2001, is especially important. This fact seems to indicate that consumer sentiments would be moving towards the perception of a future scenario more conducive to consumption decisions, although it is considered that the impulse of domestic demand will move only slightly above output growth. Estimating the lower uncertainty of the international scenario, it is possible to anticipate a gradual recovery of the most volatile components of spending. Moreover, given their fluctuating nature, it cannot be ruled out that the recovery process of these components of expenditure will follow a more accelerated trajectory. In any event, in order to sustain a more dynamic evolution of spending over a prolonged period, it is required that the other components of domestic demand, which share the share of expenditure, increase the rate of growth they have shown during the last quarters. Macroeconomic policies and prospects During this year, the Central Bank has reduced the monetary policy rate from 6.5% to 4%. This action has been based on a substantial and broad decline in the medium-term inflation outlook, which has been accompanied by lower than expected actual inflation d1 total and core d1 below. The greater degree of expansionary monetary policy has been appreciated in the interest rates of the different instruments of the Central Bank, which have reached historically low levels. The growth of placements remains somewhat more dynamic than at the beginning of the year, in particular consumer placements during March, which responded to the system's offers. On the other hand, the growth of money is in line with the rate of growth of activity, prices and the current level of interest rates. Fiscal policy, in line with the countercyclical potential of the structural surplus rule, will continue to contribute to the boost in aggregate demand through the growth of public spending with a macro impact of close to 5%. Meanwhile, public investment will grow 11%. Exports have also been significantly buoyant, especially non-traditional. These have been helped by the combination of macroeconomic policies and the cumulative depreciation of the real exchange rate in recent years, which has more than offset the effect of the fall in global trade on the volume exported. Capacity slacks will continue to limit underlying inflationary pressures, which are also mitigated by the stability of the peso and still high unemployment rates. The absence of inflationary pressures can be seen in the difference between the recent and foreseeable trajectory of core inflation for some time, when CPI inflation was expected to accelerate to figures of the order of 3.5% in the middle of this year. On the contrary, what is observed today are prospects of maintenance around 2.5% per year in the course of the coming quarters. In summary, together with the gradual dominance of favourable factors on the international scene, it is expected that there will be a boost from domestic sources, which will make it possible to consolidate the most recent economic trends, recovery in domestic demand and a gradual expansion in the pace of growth of output, which should reach growth of 3.0 per cent in 2002 and 5.8 per cent in 2003. This impulse comes from monetary stimulus, the countercyclical nature of fiscal policy, as well as the gradual recovery or normalization of some components of spending that contracted sharply during the second half of 2001. Under these conditions, the gradual acceleration in activity is expected to be accompanied by inflation in the centre of the target range. The Central Bank will continue to monitor the evolution of the different economic indicators, so as to adopt policy actions with the flexibility required to face the different risk scenarios and face deviations in inflation from the established target.
text_original: Los flujos de capitales a las economas emergentes Escenarios Econmicos Exposicin de Jorge Marshall R., Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, efectuada en el ciclo de Conferencias Regionales 2002, organizadas por El Diario, en Copiap, EL 1 7 DE MAYO DE 2002. Luego de la crisis asitica, los flujos de capitales a las economas emergentes se han mantenido en torno a 40% por debajo del nivel alcanzado en 1996-97. Si bien las condiciones financieras de las economas emergentes han mejorado, y sus spreads soberanos han mostrado una tendencia declinante, incluyendo los bonos soberanos de Chile, ello no se ha traducido en un aumento de los flujos financieros hacia estas economas. Las cifras recientes muestran que se ha acentuado la escasez de flujos de inversin extranjera directa, especialmente hacia Amrica Latina. Por esta razn, los escenarios que hemos considerado como ms probables contienen una visin conservadora sobre los flujos de capitales hacia economas emergentes, aunque en el caso de Chile, la materializacin del acuerdo con la Unin Europea puede dar un nuevo impulso positivo a este tipo de inversin. En el Informe de Poltica Monetaria de mayo del 2002, recientemente publicado por el Banco Central de Chile, se destacan tres aspectos claves de la actual coyuntura:  El producto alcanz su menor ritmo de crecimiento en los primeros meses del ao, y ahora presenta seales de una gradual expansin.  La demanda interna muestra una recuperacin desde comienzos del ao, luego de la cada del ao 2001.  Las perspectivas de la inflacin han experimentado una disminucin sustantiva y amplia. La evolucin reciente y futurade estas tres variables fundamentales es originada por una serie de factores, algunos de ellos vienen desarrollndose desde hace varios aos y otros han aparecido ms recientemente. Los desarrollos de estos factores configuran escenarios en torno a los cuales es posible pensar el futuro. Precisamente, uno de los aspectos que capta mayor atencin en la elaboracin del Informe de Poltica Monetaria es la identificacin de las variables que impulsan los cambios que observamos en la economa. Establecer y analizar estas variables permite construir diferentes escenarios que lustran los posibles desarrollos futuros de la economa. Entre ellos est el escenario central, que sirve de base a las decisiones de la poltica monetaria. En esta oportunidad, analizaremos cuatro factores que configuran, a nuestro juicio, los escenarios econmicos futuros: los flujos internacionales de capitales, el ciclo de la economa mundial, las dificultades econmicas de la regin y las expectativas internas de crecimiento de mediano plazo. El ciclo de la economa mundial La economa mundial experiment una fuerte desaceleracin en el 2001. El crecimiento del producto mundial se redujo de 4,7% en el 2000 a 2,3% en el 2001. Los efectos de este ciclo siguen observndose en los primeros meses de este ao, en particular en las fuertes cadas de la produccin industrial agregada y los flujos de comercio. Adicionalmente, el ao pasado se increment la incertidumbre financiera en economas desarrolladas, especialmente en los mercados burstiles, y se produjeron los ataques terroristas del 11 de septiembre. Estas condiciones repercutieron internamente en el aumento de la incertidumbre y en una reduccin del gasto, que se mantuvo hasta fines del 2001. Las cifras ms recientes muestran un panorama internacional ms promisorio para el perodo 2002-2003, en la medida que se ha consolidado una mejora en las perspectivas de crecimiento de la actividad mundial, especialmente en EE.UU. Tambin se aprecia un mayor optimismo en las perspectivas de crecimiento para la zona europea, e incluso para Japn las proyecciones indican crecimiento para el prximo ao. Estos antecedentes permiten considerar escenarios en que la economa mundial se recupera gradualmente en el transcurso del 2002 y con ms fuerza en el 2003. Estos desarrollos del escenario internacional se expresan en la evolucin de los precios de nuestras exportaciones. Para este ao se espera slo un aumento leve en el precio del cobre, para ubicarse en USS 0,73 por libra, con un incremento adicional hacia el 2003 y el 2004. Hasta el momento, esta evolucin se ve ms que compensada con mayores proyecciones para el precio del petrleo durante este ao. Esto significa que los trminos del intercambio se mantendrn este ao en niveles promedio similares a los del ao pasado, para repuntar 4% promedio anual durante el 2003. Las dificultades econmicas de la regin Un tercer factor relevante para los escenarios futuros de la economa chilena proviene de las dificultades que se observan en la regin. El producto de Amrica Latina permaneci estancado el ao 2001 y las perspectivas para el 2002 son an peores. Particular relevancia tienen los efectos de la crtica situacin por la que atraviesa la economa transandina, pero el panorama de la mayora de los pases de la regin es sombro. Es importante destacar que los efectos de la situacin regional han cambiado su importancia relativa, pasando de una situacin de temor a un contagio financiero ms significativo, hasta noviembre de 2001, a la disipacin de ese riesgo, pero tambin a la manifestacin de los efectos adversos en el mbito comercial. Nuestras exportaciones a Argentina cayeron en torno a 60% y el flujo de turistas disminuy a cerca de la mitad en el primer trimestre de este ao. Una proyeccin anual y combinada de estos dos efectos tiene una incidencia directa en torno a 0,3 puntos porcentuales en el crecimiento del producto interno bruto (PIB), efecto que aumenta a aproximadamente 0,5 si se consideran los efectos indirectos. Los problemas de la economa argentina tambin han tenido un efecto negativo sobre la capacidad de generacin de renta de empresas chilenas con operaciones en Argentina, lo que se ha reflejado en disminuciones en su valor patrimonial. Se estima que la disminucin en las utilidades devengadas de las inversiones en ese pas afecta directamente al ingreso nacional del 2002 en aproximadamente 0,2% del PIB, a lo que deben agregarse los efectos por menor actividad. Los escenarios relevantes consideran un cuadro de estancamiento del producto regional en el ao 2002 y una recuperacin en el 2003, acorde con una mayor estabilidad regional y un escenario de crecimiento global. Moderacin de la demanda interna Un aspecto relevante de la economa en el 2001 fue la disminucin de la demanda interna, mientras el producto se mantena creciendo. En esta situacin hay una parte transitoria, que debe revertirse en los prximos trimestres, y otra, que responde a las perspectivas de crecimiento de mediano plazo. Sin duda, los desarrollos del escenario externo afectaron a los componentes ms variables de la demanda, como son las existencias, el consumo de durablesy la inversin en maquinaria. En la actualidad, los antecedentes del gasto permiten esperar que se consolide un repunte en estos componentes de la demanda. Hay, por otra parte, componentes de la demanda interna que responden a las perspectivas de crecimiento de mediano plazo y a la persistencia del desempleo. El consumo habitual, que es uno de los componentes ms estables del gasto, ha mostrado una tendencia muy moderada de crecimiento. En los ltimos aos, hemos presenciado una paulatina disminucin en las perspectivas de mediano plazo, medidas en el crecimiento anticipado por los analistas econmicos para dentro de dos aos. Este hecho influye en la evolucin del consumo, en la inversin privada y en el empleo. Considerando esta tendencia, tiene especial importancia el mayor optimismo que muestra el ndice de Percepcin Econmica de ADIMARK en el primer trimestre de este ao, que revierte el fuerte pesimismo observado hacia del tercer trimestre del 2001. Este hecho parece indicar que los sentimientos de los consumidores se estaran moviendo hacia la percepcin de un escenario futuro ms conducente a decisiones de consumo, aunque se considera que el impulso de la demanda interna se mover slo levemente por encima del crecimiento del producto. Estimando la menor incertidumbre del escenario internacional, es posible anticipar una gradual recuperacin de los componentes ms voltiles del gasto. An ms, dada su naturaleza fluctuante, no se puede descartar que el proceso de recuperacin de estos componentes del gasto siga una trayectoria ms acelerada. En cualquier evento, para sostener una evolucin ms dinmica del gasto durante un perodo prolongado, se requiere que los dems componentes de la demanda interna, mayoritarios en la participacin en el gasto, aumenten el ritmo de crecimiento que han mostrado durante los ltimos trimestres. Polticas macroeconmicas y perspectivas Durante este ao, el Banco Central ha reducido de 6,5% a 4% la tasa de poltica monetaria. Esta accin ha estado basada en una disminucin sustantiva y amplia en las perspectivas de inflacin de mediano plazo, que ha sido acompaada por una inflacin efectiva total y subyacente menor a la prevista. El mayor grado de expansividad de la poltica monetaria se ha apreciado en las tasas de inters de los distintos instrumentos del Banco Central, las que han llegado a niveles histricamente bajos. El crecimiento de las colocaciones se mantiene algo ms dinmico que a principios de ao, en particular las colocaciones de consumo durante marzo, que respondieron a las ofertas del sistema. Por su lado, el crecimiento del dinero se encuentra acorde con el ritmo de crecimiento de la actividad, los precios y el nivel actual de las tasas de inters. La poltica fiscal, de acuerdo con el potencial contracclico de laregla de supervit estructural, continuar aportando al impulso de demanda agregada a travs del crecimiento del gasto pblico con impacto macro cercano a 5%. En tanto, la inversin pblica crecer 11%. Asimismo, las exportaciones han sustentado un importante dinamismo, en especial las no tradicionales. stas se han visto favorecidas por la combinacin de polticas macroeconmicas y la depreciacin acumulada del tipo de cambio real en los ltimos aos, lo que ha permitido ms que compensar el efecto de la cada del comercio global en el volumen exportado. Las holguras de capacidad seguirn acotando las presiones inflacionarias subyacentes, las que tambin se ven mitigadas por la estabilidad del peso y tasas de desocupacin todava elevadas. La ausencia de presiones Inflacionarias se aprecia en la diferencia entre la trayectoria reciente y previsible de la inflacin subyacente desde hace un tiempo, cuando se esperaba que la inflacin IPCX se acelerara hasta cifras del orden de 3,5% a mediados de este ao. Por el contrario, lo que hoy se observa son perspectivas de mantencin en torno a 2,5% anual en el curso de los prximos trimestres. En sntesis, junto al gradual predominio de los factores favorables del escenario internacional, se espera que exista un impulso de origen interno, que permitir consolidar las tendencias econmicas ms recientes, de recuperacin en la demanda interna y de una gradual expansin en el ritmo de crecimiento del producto, el que debe alcanzar un crecimiento de 3,0% durante el 2002 y de 5,8% en el 2003. Este impulso proviene del estmulo monetario, de la caracterstica contracclica de la poltica fiscal, as como de la recuperacin progresiva o normalizacin de algunos componentes del gasto que tuvieron fuertes contracciones durante la segunda mitad del 2001. En estas condiciones, se prev que la gradual aceleracin de la actividad sea acompaada por una inflacin en el centro del rango meta. El Banco Central continuar atento a la evolucin de los distintos indicadores econmicos, de modo de adoptar las acciones de poltica con la flexibilidad requerida para hacer frente a los distintos escenarios de riesgo y afrontar desviaciones de la inflacin respecto de la meta establecida.

Title: Economic scenarios: 2002-2003
text: of the world economy, the economic difficulties of the region and the strength of the recovery of domestic demand. Improved prospects for the world economy Economic scenarios: 2002-2003 PRESENTATION BY JORGE MARSHALL R., VICE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, HELD AT THE BUSINESS SEMINAR "ECONOMIC GROWTH, MONETARY POLICY AND NEW ECONOMIC SCENARIOS" ORGANIZED BY THE CATHOLIC UNIVERSITY OF THE MOST HOLY CONCEPTION, ON JUNE 26, 2002. Introduction In this presentation we will analyze recent economic events, in the context of the medium-term scenarios that the Central Bank develops and maintains. In the economic information for the first half of this year, the following facts stand out: - Output had its slowest growth rate in the first months of the year, while preliminary figures for the second quarter show a gradual expansion. - Domestic demand has recovered since the beginning of the year, but at a slower pace than anticipated. - The situation in Latin America has become more uncertain, which may have more persistent negative effects on investment flows to the region and Chile. - The best prospects for growth in the world economy and a gradual recovery in the terms of trade are maintained. - The inflation outlook remains aligned with the medium-term target. The trajectory of these developments will define the evolution of the economy in the coming quarters. In this sense, the key factors of the current situation are: the solidity of the upturn The major advanced economies showed a clear pick-up in activity levels in the first quarter of 2002, ending the cycle of sharp slowdown in output and global trade experienced in 2001. At present, the improved growth prospects for global activity for the period 2002-2003 have been consolidated. While growth prospects for this year in the United States have moderated slightly, in Japan and Asia-Pacific countries there have been upward corrections in growth projections, while the European zone remains stable, with prospects for recovery next year. This background supports the scenario in which the world economy recovers gradually in the course of 2002 and more strongly in 2003. In recent weeks, international financial markets have shown a more persistent depreciation of the dollar, a more negative trajectory of stock markets, especially in the United States, and falling long-term interest rates. Although these facts install a signal of caution in the global economy, their effect on the Chilean economy will depend on the trajectory that each of them follows in the coming months, since the negative effect of possible lower levels of activity in advanced countries must be compared with changes in the cost and in the flows of end towards emerging economies. as well as with the response of export prices to changes in parities. It is still too early to determine the magnitude of these effects. The consolidation of a more positive trajectory of the international scenario is expressed in the evolution of the prices of our exports. For this year only a slight increase in the price of copper is expected, to be around USS 0.73 per pound, with an additional increase towards 2003 and 2004. So far, this evolution is offset by higher projections for the price of oil. This means that the terms of trade will remain at average levels similar to those of 2001 this year, to rebound by around 4% annual average during 2003. Difficulties in Latin America Another relevant factor for the future of the Chilean economy comes from the difficulties observed in Latin America. For the second consecutive year, Latin America's output will remain virtually stagnant in 2002. Of particular relevance in this fact is the critical situation of Argentina, to which is now added the change in market expectations regarding Brazil. The most relevant effects of the regional scenario are transmitted through financial markets, trade flows and equity changes of Chilean companies with investments in neighboring countries. In the case of Brazil, the potential direct effects are smaller than in the crisis in Argentina, although the indirect effects, which operate through international financial markets, may reach a greater magnitude. The main impact of regional turbulence is expressed in financial markets. As happened with the worsening of the situation in Argentina between mid and late 2001, the exchange market has reacted to the increase in uncertainty in Brazil, causing a depreciation of around 8% in the nominal exchange rate, since the end of April, although with a minor effect on the real exchange rate due to the depreciation of the currencies of several of our trading partners. In addition, in international financial markets the spread of Chilean external debt instruments has increased in the same period. Part of these financial effects are due to unexpected portfolio adjustments of companies and investors, so it is rather transitory. However, there is also a part that could become more durable as financial flows to the region as a whole suffer. Although the scenarios that the Central Bank has considered most likely contain a conservative view of international capital flows and, in the case of Chile, the materialization of the agreement with the European Union may give some positive impetus to this type of investment, it is possible that the indirect effects of a worsening of Brazil's situation will have more lasting repercussions on emerging economies. Foreign trade is another source of the direct adverse effects of the regional crisis. In the case of Argentina, our exports fell by around 60% and the flow of tourists decreased by about half in the first quarter of this year. An annual and combined projection of these two effects has a direct impact of around 0.3 percentage points on gross domestic product (GDP) growth, an effect that increases to about 0.5 if indirect effects are considered. In the case of Brazil, the potential trade effects are more limited than in the case of Argentina. Industrial exports to Brazil in 2001 were equivalent to 0.5% of GDP, while in the case of Argentina, they reached 0.7% of GDP. In addition, in the case of Brazil, around three-quarters of Chilean exports have the capacity to be destined for other markets. This calculation is obtained by applying the criterion that shipments to Brazil represent less than 20% of exports of each item or that the same products are placed in at least fifteen other countries. Moreover, the magnitude of Brazil's import drop is likely to be smaller than Argentina's, and will occur in a period of global trade rebound. Exports by destination as a percentage of GDP (2001 and first quarter of 2002) A third effect of economic hardship in the region is expressed in capital losses and income statements of companies that have invested in neighboring economies. This effect is reflected in stock prices and spreadof debt of the companies that have made the investments, in addition to the lower income-generating capacity of these companies. Only in the case of Argentina was it estimated that the decline in profits earned from investments in that country directly affects national income in 2002 by approximately 0.2% of GDP. In the case of investments in Brazil, these effects are of a smaller magnitude. To the extent that more reliable information on these effects is available, the Central Bank incorporates them, both in its monetary policy decisions and in the continuous monitoring that makes its medium-term scenario more likely. Slow recovery in domestic demand A relevant aspect of the economy in 2001 was the decline in domestic demand, while output continued to grow. In this phenomenon there is a transitory part, which has already begun to reverse, and another more persistent part that responds to medium-term growth prospects. Undoubtedly, the developments of the external scenario affected the most variable components of demand, such as inventories, consumption of durables and investment in machinery. At present, the history of spending allows us to expect that the rebound shown by these components of demand will consolidate. There are, on the other hand, components of domestic demand that respond to medium-term growth prospects and persistent unemployment. Regular consumption, which is one of the most stable components of spending, has shown a very moderate trend of growth. Associated with this fact, in recent years we have witnessed a decrease in medium-term prospects, measured in the growth anticipated by economic analysts for two years from now, although in recent months this figure shows a slight increase. A similar trend is obtained from the ADIMARK Economic Perception Index, which since the end of 2001 reverses the strong pessimism observed towards the third quarter of that year, although it still shows low levels when compared with the average of past years and the latest increases in this indicator are rather modest. This trajectory seems to indicate that consumer sentiments would be moving very gradually towards a scenario more conducive to consumption decisions. Given regional uncertainty, some of the recovery in spending may be slower. In fact, the trend in second-quarter spending seems more leisurely than anticipated. However, given the nature of the most volatile components of demand, it cannot be ruled out that in the coming quarters its recovery process will follow a faster trajectory than that shown so far. Macroeconomic policies and prospects During this year, the Central Bank has reduced the monetary policy rate from 6.5% to 4%. This action has been based on a substantial and broad decline in the medium-term inflation outlook, which has been accompanied by lower than expected actual inflation d1 total and core d1 below. The greater degree of expansionary monetary policy can be seen in the interest rates of the various instruments of the Central Bank, which have reached historically low levels. However, the rates of the central bank's long-term resettable documents have reversed this trajectory since May, probably influenced by regional turbulence. Fiscal policy, meanwhile, in accordance with the countercyclical capacity of the structural surplus rule, is contributing to the boost of aggregate demand through the growth of public spending with a macroeconomic impact close to 5% for the year as a whole, while public investment will grow by around 11%. This combination of monetary and fiscal policies has made possible the depreciation of the real exchange rate in recent years, which has allowed a dynamism of exports that has more than offset the effect of the fall in global trade on the volume exported. Capacity slacks will continue to constrain underlying inflationary pressures. The expected evolution of inflation over the medium term remains within the expected ranges, although the short-term trajectory of total inflation will present significant ups and downs, resulting both from recent movements in the international price of fuels, fluctuations in the exchange market and base effects of comparison. Core inflation will remain fluctuating in the range of 2.5% to 3.0% over the next few months and around 3% towards the end of 2003. In summary, factors more favourable to economic recovery, such as improved prospects for the world economy and more favourable conditions for domestic momentum, should prevail over the more uncertain regional environment. Preliminary information for the second quarter of this year is consistent with this trend, although monthly figures should be considered with great caution. Under these conditions, the recovery trends in domestic demand and a gradual expansion in the pace of output growth, supported by monetary stimulus, the countercyclical nature of fiscal policy, as well as the normalization of some components of expenditure that contracted sharply during the second half of 2001, are expected to consolidate. Importantly, Chile's macroeconomic policy framework can better cushion the effects of external fluctuations. For macroeconomic policies to have the capacity to moderate external turbulence while stimulating domestic demand, it is essential that they be sustainable and consistent with the economy's medium-term scenario. This is expressed in the need to preserve the inflation-targeting regime, the floating exchange rate and the fiscal rule of structural surplus. Outside this framework, demand policies may have the opposite effect to that expected. In this scheme, the Central Bank will continue to monitor the evolution of the different economic indicators, in order to adopt policy actions with the flexibility required to face the different risk scenarios. At the same time, it is also essential to point out that the natural complement of this macroeconomic scheme is the flexibility of the markets for goods and productive factors. This feature is what facilitates changes in relative prices and gives better signals to take advantage of the most profitable opportunities. In this way, the macroeconomic policy regime is better strengthened and better results are obtained in the recovery of the growth of the Chilean economy.

Si bien en Estados Unidos se han moderado levemente las perspectivas de crecimiento para este ao, en Japn y en los pases de Asia-Pacfico se han producido correcciones al alza en las proyecciones de crecimiento, en tanto la zona europea se mantiene estable, con perspectivas de recuperacin en el prximo ao. En las semanas recientes, los mercados financieros internacionales han mostrado una depreciacin ms persistente del dlar, una trayectoria ms negativa de los mercados accionarios, especialmente en Estados Unidos, y tasas de inters de largo plazo a la baja. Si bien estos hechos instalan una seal de cautela en la economa global, su efecto en la economa chilena depender de la trayectoria que siga cada uno de ellos en los prximos meses, ya que el efecto negativo de eventuales menores niveles de actividad en pases avanzados debe ser cotejado con los cambios en el costo y en los flujos de fin andamiento hacia las economas emergentes, as como con la respuesta de los precios de los productos de exportacin a los cambios en las paridades. An es muy pronto para determinar la magnitud de estos efectos. Para este ao se espera slo un aumento leve en el precio del cobre, para ubicarse en torno a USS 0,73 por libra, con un incremento adicional hacia el 2003 y el 2004. Hasta el momento, esta evolucin se ve compensada con mayores proyecciones para el precio del petrleo. Esto significa que los trminos del intercambio se mantendrn este ao en niveles promedio similares a los del ao 2001, para repuntar en torno a un 4% promedio anual durante el 2003. Dificultades en Amrica Latina O tro factor relevante para el futuro de la economa chilena proviene de las dificultades que se observan en Amrica Latina. Por segundo ao consecutivo el producto de Amrica Latina permanecer prcticamente estancado en el 2002. Particular relevancia en este hecho tiene la crtica situacin de Argentina, a la que ahora se agrega el cambio en las expectativas de mercado respecto de Brasil. Los efectos ms relevantes del escenario regional se transmiten a travs de los mercados financieros, los flujos de comercio y los cambios patrimoniales de las empresas chilenas con inversiones en los pases vecinos. En el caso de Brasil, los potenciales efectos directos son de menor magnitud que en la crisis de Argentina, aunque los efectos indirectos, que operan a travs de los mercados financieros internacionales, pueden alcanzar una mayor magnitud. El principal impacto de las turbulencias regionales se expresa en los mercados financieros. Del mismo modo como ocurri con el agravamiento de la situacin de Argentina entre mediados y fines del 2001, el mercado cambiarlo ha reaccionado ante el aumento de la incertidumbre en Brasil, provocando una depreciacin en torno a 8% en el tipo de cambio nominal, desde fines de abril, aunque con un efecto menor en el tipo de cambio real por la depreciacin de las monedas de varios de nuestros socios comerciales. Adems, en los mercados financieros internacionales el spreadde los instrumentos de deuda externa chilena se ha incrementado en el mismo perodo. Una parte de estos efectos financieros obedece a ajustes inesperados de portafolio de empresas e inversionistas, por lo que tiene un carcter ms bien transitorio. Sin embargo, tambin hay una parte que podra llegar a ser ms duradera en la medida que se resientan los flujos financieros hacia la regin en su conjunto. Si bien los escenarios que ha considerado el Banco Central como ms probables contienen una visin conservadora sobre los flujos internacionales de capitales y, en el caso de Chile, la materializacin del acuerdo con la Unin Europea puede dar algn impulso positivo a este tipo de inversin, es posible que los efectos indirectos de un agravamiento de la situacin de Brasil tengan repercusiones ms duraderas en las economas emergentes. El comercio exterior es otra fuente en que se expresan los efectos directos adversos de la crisis regional. En el caso de Argentina, nuestras exportaciones cayeron en torno a 60% y el flujo de turistas disminuy a cerca de la mitad en el primer trimestre de este ao. En el caso de Brasil, los efectos comerciales potenciales son ms acotados que en el caso de Argentina. Las exportaciones industriales a Brasil en el 2001 equivalen a 0,5% del PIB, mientras que en el caso de Argentina, estas alcanzaron 0,7% del PIB. Adems, en el caso de Brasil alrededor de tres cuartas partes de las exportaciones chilenas tienen la capacidad de ser destinadas a otros mercados. Este clculo se obtiene de aplicar el criterio de que los envos a Brasil representen menos de 20% de las exportaciones de cada rubro o que los mismos productos sean colocados al menos en otros quince pases. Adems, la magnitud de la cada de las importaciones de Brasil ser probablemente inferior a la de Argentina, y ocurrir en un perodo de repunte del comercio global. En la medida en que se dispone de antecedentes ms confiables sobre estos efectos, el Banco Central los incorpora, tanto en sus decisiones de poltica monetaria, como en el continuo seguimiento que hace de su escenario de mediano plazo ms probable. Recuperacin lenta de la demanda interna Un aspecto relevante de la economa en el 2001 fue la disminucin de la demanda interna, mientras el producto se mantena creciendo. En este fenmeno hay una parte transitoria, que ya ha comenzado a revertirse, y otra parte ms persistente que responde a las perspectivas de crecimiento de mediano plazo. Sin duda, los desarrollos del escenario externo afectaron a los componentes ms variables dla demanda, como son las existencias, el consumo de durables y la inversin en maquinaria. En la actualidad, los antecedentes del gasto permiten esperar que se consolide el repunte que muestran estos componentes de la demanda. Hay, por otra parte, componentes de la demanda interna que responden a las perspectivas de crecimiento de mediano plazo y a la persistencia del desempleo. El consumo habitual, que es uno de los componentes ms estables del gasto, ha mostrado una tendencia muy moderada de crecimiento. Asociado a este hecho, en los ltimos aos hemos presenciado una disminucin en las perspectivas de mediano plazo, medidas en el crecimiento anticipado por los analistas econmicos para dentro de dos aos, aunque en los ltimos meses esta cifra muestra un leve incremento. Una tendencia similar se obtiene del ndice de Percepcin Econmica de ADIMARK, que desde fines del 2001 revierte el fuerte pesimismo observado hacia del tercer trimestre de ese ao, aunque an muestra niveles bajos cuando se compara con el promedio de los aos pasados y los ltimos incrementos de este indicador son ms bien modestos. Esta trayectoria parece indicar que los sentimientos de los consumidores se estaran moviendo muy gradualmente hacia un escenario ms conducente a decisiones de consumo. Considerando la incertidumbre regional es posible que una parte de la recuperacin del gasto sea ms lenta. De hecho, la tendencia del gasto en el segundo trimestre parece ms pausada que lo anticipado. Sin embargo, dada la naturaleza de los componentes ms voltiles de la demanda, no se puede descartar que en los prximos trimestres su proceso de recuperacin siga una trayectoria ms acelerada que la mostrada hasta el momento. Polticas macroeconmicas y perspectivas Durante este ao, el Banco Central ha reducido la tasa de poltica monetaria de 6,5% a 4%. Esta accin ha estado basada en una disminucin sustantiva y amplia en la perspectiva de inflacin de mediano plazo, que ha sido acompaada por una inflacin efectiva total y subyacente menor a la prevista. El mayor grado de expansividad de la poltica monetaria se aprecia en las tasas de inters de los distintos instrumentos del Banco Central, las que han llegado a niveles histricamente bajos. Sin embargo, las tasas de los documentos reajustables de largo plazo del Banco Central presentan una reversin de esta trayectoria desde mayo, probablemente influida por las turbulencias regionales. La poltica fiscal, en tanto, de acuerdo con la capacidad contracclica de la regla de supervit estructural, est aportando al impulso de demanda agregada a travs del crecimiento del gasto pblico con impacto macroeconmico cercano a 5% para el ao en su conjunto, mientras la inversin pblica crecer en torno a 11 %. Esta combinacin de polticas monetaria y fiscal ha posibilitado la depreciacin del tipo de cambio real en los ltimos aos, lo que ha permitido un dinamismo de las exportaciones que ha ms que compensado el efecto de la cada del comercio global en el volumen exportado. Por su parte, las holguras de capacidad seguirn acotando las presiones inflacionarias subyacentes. La evolucin esperada de la inflacin en el mediano plazo se mantiene dentro de los rangos previstos, aunque la trayectoria de corto plazo de la inflacin total presentar importantes altibajos, los que se derivan tanto de los movimientos recientes en el precio internacional de los combustibles, las fluctuaciones en el mercado cambiarlo y los efectos de base de comparacin. La inflacin subyacente se mantendr fluctuando en el rango 2,5% a 3,0% durante los prximos meses y en torno a 3% hacia fines del 2003. En sntesis, los factores ms favorables a la recuperacin de la economa, como son las mejores perspectivas de la economa mundial y las condiciones ms favorables para un impulso de origen interno, deben predominar sobre el ambiente regional ms incierto. La informacin preliminar del segundo trimestre de este ao es coherente con esta tendencia, aunque las cifras mensuales deben ser consideradas con mucha cautela. En estas condiciones, se espera que se consoliden las tendencias de recuperacin en la demanda interna y de una gradual expansin en el ritmo de crecimiento del producto, apoyado en el estmulo monetario, en la caracterstica contracclica de la poltica fiscal, as como la normalizacin de algunos componentes del gasto que tuvieron fuertes contracciones durante la segunda mitad del 2001. Es importante destacar que el marco de polticas macroeconmicas que se aplica en Chile permite amortiguar mejor los efectos de las fluctuaciones externas. Para que las polticas macroeconmicas tengan la capacidad de moderar las turbulencias externas y al mismo tiempo estimular la demanda interna, es indispensable que sean sostenibles y coherentes con el escenario de mediano plazo de la economa. Esto se expresa en la necesidad de preservar el rgimen de metas de inflacin, la flotacin cambiara y la regla fiscal de supervit estructural. Fuera de este marco, las polticas de demanda pueden tener un efecto contrario al esperado. En este esquema, el Banco Central continuar atento a la evolucin de los distintos indicadores econmicos, de modo de adoptar las acciones de poltica con la flexibilidad requerida para hacer frente a los distintos escenarios de riesgo. A su vez, es tambin fundamental sealar que el complemento natural de este esquema macroeconmico es la flexibilidad de los mercados de bienes y de factores productivos. Esta caracterstica es la que facilita los cambios en los precios relativos y otorga mejores seales para aprovechar las oportunidades ms rentables. De esta forma, se potencia mejor el rgimen de polticas macroeconmicas y se obtienen mejores resultados en la recuperacin del crecimiento de la economa chilena.

Title: Investment trends
text: Investment trends Jorge Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, Presentation at the Capital Goods Corporation Meeting, Santiago, May 29, 2003 I want to thank the Capital Goods Corporation, CBC, for the invitation to participate in this meeting on investment in our country. In this presentation I will analyze, first, the main determinants of investment; secondly, I will refer to the prospects for investment in Chile and, finally, I will present some conclusions. Determinants of investment One of the most important sources of the expansion of the Chilean economy since the mid-80s was the increase in the investment rate. The trend in gross fixed capital formation, measured in 1996 pesos, showed sustained growth up to 1998, except for a brief period during 1991. The investment rate rose from 17 per cent in 1986 to 27 per cent in 1998. During 1999, there was a fall in fixed capital investment, remaining at around 22% of output since then. The average levels of investment of the last fifteen years are high when compared with the historical standards of the Chilean economy, as well as in relation to other economies of similar level of development. In order to analyse the determinants of investment, it is useful to separate the two main components of gross fixed capital formation. In first place is the building and engineering construction component, which represents 60% of total fixed capital investment. In turn, its main components are housing construction, with 21%; non-residential construction, with 12% and engineering works, with 26%. Second are the purchases of machinery and equipment. This second component represents 40% of total fixed capital investment and is composed of imports of capital goods, which represents 37.7% and sales of machinery of domestic origin, with 2.6% of total fixed capital investment. Investment in construction is linked to the rate of growth of output, with about 4 to 5 quarters lagging. The accompanying graph shows output growth and the rate of investment in construction for the period 1986-2003. It can be seen that, taking into account the lag indicated, the series present a fairly similar dynamic. Additionally, investment in construction is influenced by the evolution of the interest rate, especially in long-term instruments. The components of housing investment and commercial buildings are the most sensitive to the interest rate. For this reason, this component of investment is currently being stimulated by low interest rates. Bank placements for housing maintain a high dynamism, only surpassed in recent quarters by the expansion of consumer loans. GDP Growth and Share of the FBKC/GDP Gross Training in Construction Capital (rate of change over 12 months and percentage) As for investment in machinery and equipment, which represents about 40% of total investment, its relationship with output growth is more indirect. In this case, there is a closer relationship between the evolution of investment and the profitability of productive activities, although also in this case there is a lag of around 4 quarters between the changes observed in profitability and its effect on the purchase of machinery. By the way, the profitability of companies is positively linked to the growth rate of output. The graph below shows the trajectory of investment in machinery and equipment and the profitability of firms, net of cost of capital (measured as the average operating profitability of firms publishing ECUs, minus the cost of capital rate in machinery). Until mid-1998, investment in machinery as a ratio of GDP showed a sustained upward trajectory. Subsequently, there is a fall in 1999 and relative stability since 2000. Net profitability of companies remained at 8 percentage points until the beginning of 1997. Profitability then fell to about 2 percentage points by the end of 1999. Since then, this indicator has shown, with ups and downs, a tendency to recover, both due to increases in the operating profitability of companies and lower interest rates. Investment Outlook With regard to the recent evolution and prospects for investment in Chile, the appropriate framework for the analysis is the latest Monetary Policy Report of the Central Bank, which anticipates a gradual improvement in the external scenario, approaching the trend growth rates of the global economy towards the end of next year. In addition, it is estimated that between 2003 and 2004 there will be a recovery in the terms of trade that will support a growth in national income higher than in recent years. In turn, progress towards greater degrees of financial stability in neighbouring countries will also reduce local uncertainties, supporting eventual increases in capital flows and a recovery in trade with the region. This set of antecedents, in addition to the expansionary monetary conditions of today, will take economic growth this year to figures of between 3 and 4%. On the other hand, the potential output of the economy is growing between 3.5 and 4% per year during this year and next. For this reason, activity growth of more than 4% is expected for 2004, which will lead to a reduction in capacity gaps by about 1% of GDP. For its part, the investment rate in recent years has remained stable at around 22% of output (measured at 1996 prices). This figure reflects that in the current phase of the cycle of the Chilean economy the impulses of demand must originate more in consumption and exports, and then reach investment in fixed capital. For this reason, what is expected in the short term is an evolution of investment close to output growth. Capacity slack in a number of sectors is currently hampering a strong pick-up in gross fixed capital formation at the aggregate level. In fact, imports and domestic sales of capital goods, which are associated with investment in machinery and equipment, show a moderate growth trend. Although imports of capital goods show greater dynamism at the margin, part of this recovery, however, seems to be associated with major projects in the pulp sector. The real estate market, on the other hand, has shown great vigor in the last four quarters, although it presents a lower dynamism in the margin. Real estate sales remain high, with about a thousand units per month (seasonally adjusted). According to the most recent information, stocks have grown more moderately, implying a reduction in the months needed to exhaust them. The current level of the latter indicator compares favourably with the average levels observed in the period 2000-2002. High levels of home sales are driven by low interest rates and more favourable economic prospects for households. Under these conditions, the dynamism of the real estate sector has begun to translate into a notable increase in building permits, both housing and establishments, so that greater activity and employment can be expected in the sector in the coming quarters. With regard to the engineering works component, which represents about a quarter of total fixed investment, the cadastre of private investment projects of March this year, which considers a review of both the projects under way during 2002 and those planned for 2003 and 2004, registered a decrease of approximately 6.0% for the period 2002-2004. with respect to what was reported in December 2002. This fall is mainly concentrated in the Real Estate and Public Works (Concessions) sectors. On the other hand, the Forestry and Ports sectors show a rebound in their investment, due to the entry of new projects to the cadastre. According to the 2003 budget, public sector investment will grow 6.8% in real terms over last year. Among the main destinations of this investment are road works of the Ministry of Public Works, the Urban Transport Plan in the Metropolitan Region, the expansion of the Metro network and the realization of urban development projects. As for the profitability of the businesses, the figures collected from the FECU show an increase that is maintained for several consecutive quarters. At the same time, the prevailing lower interest rates are seen in the decline in the ratio of financial expenses to total expenditures. By sector, those linked to export activities showed a significant recovery in their profitability, which is linked to the trajectory of the real exchange rate and the prices of export goods. In turn, non-export sectors show a sustained recovery in profitability from the lows they experienced in early 2000. Looking ahead, gross fixed capital formation growth is expected to be in line with the economy as a whole, supported by smaller slacks into next year and the recovery in profitability indicators. Going forward, the partial recovery in corporate profitability suggests greater dynamism in capital accumulation, especially in the export and import substitution sectors, where the recovery in profitability indicators is more noticeable. All this, together with a trajectory of public investment that does not deviate substantially from what was expected, will allow the fixed investment rate to increase slightly, especially during the coming year. The increases in profitability that we have seen in the last period are also manifested in company stock prices, reflecting better prospects for profitability in the future. This background also supports the projection of an increase in investment in machinery, although there is a significant lag between changes in profitability and the result in terms of greater investment. Conclusions In summary, the trends in the economy suggest that the recovery in economic activity will continue, mainly due to the gradual improvement in the external scenario and the stimulus of monetary policy. Going forward, economic growth this year is expected to reach figures of between 3 and 4%, a range equivalent to that forecast last January, while growth in activity is expected to be greater than 4% for 2004. This scenario reflects that there are currently favorable macroeconomic conditions for a rebound in fixed capital investment, although it should be noted that its effective recovery usually occurs with a lag with respect to economic activity. A favourable aspect for the investment outlook is the improvement in the profitability indicators of companies and in stock prices. These signals generate, also with lag, positive responses in investment in machinery and equipment. Finally, a relevant aspect in this analysis is the need to recognize that in recent years the growth of total factor productivity has been close to zero, mainly due to the cyclical position of the Chilean economy. From now on, however, a rebound in productivity indicators is expected, which is a condition for increases in the level of productive resources to become a higher rate of growth.
text_original: Tendencias de la inversin Jorge Marshall, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, Exposicin en el Encuentro de la Corporacin de Bienes de Capital, Santiago 29 de mayo de 2003 Quiero agradecer a la Corporacin de Bienes de Capital, CBC, la invitacin a participar en este encuentro sobre la inversin en nuestro pas. En esta exposicin analizar, en primer lugar, los principales determinantes de la inversin; en segundo lugar me referir a las perspectivas de la inversin en Chile y, finalmente, presentar algunas conclusiones. Determinantes de la inversin Una de las fuentes ms importantes de la expansin de la economa chilena desde mediados de los aos 80 fue el aumento en la tasa de inversin. En efecto, la evolucin de la formacin bruta de capital fijo, medida en pesos de 1996, muestra un crecimiento sostenido hasta 1998, exceptuando un breve perodo durante 1991. La tasa de inversin pas de un 17% en 1986 a un 27% en 1998. Durante 1999 se observ una cada de la inversin en capital fijo, mantenindose desde entonces en tomo a un 22% del producto. Los niveles promedio de la inversin de los ltimos quince aos son elevados cuando se comparan con los estndares histricos de la economa chilena, as como en relacin con otras economas de similar nivel de desarrollo. Para analizar los determinantes de la inversin conviene separar los dos componentes principales de la formacin bruta de capital fijo. En primer lugar est el componente de construccin edificios y obras de ingeniera, que representa un 60% de la inversin en capital fijo total. A su vez, sus componentes principales son la edificacin habitacional, con un 21%; la edificacin no habitacional, con un 12% y las obras de ingeniera, con un 26%. En segundo lugar estn las compras de maquinarias y equipos. Este segundo componente representa un 40% de la inversin en capital fijo total y est compuesto por la importacin de bienes de capital, que representa un 37,7% y las ventas de maquinarias origen nacional, con un 2,6% del total de la inversin en capital fijo. La inversin en construccin est vinculada a la tasa de crecimiento del producto, con unos 4 a 5 trimestres de rezago. En el grfico adjunto se muestra el crecimiento del producto y la tasa de inversin en construccin para el perodo 1986.2003. Se aprecia que, tomando en cuenta el rezago sealado, las series presentan una dinmica bastante similar. Adicionalmente, la inversin en construccin est influida por la evolucin de la tasa de inters, especialmente de instrumentos de largo plazo. Los componentes de inversin habitacional y de edificaciones comerciales son los ms sensibles a la tasa de inters. Por esta razn, en la actualidad este componente de la inversin est siendo estimulado por las bajas tasas de inters. Las colocaciones bancarias para viviendas mantienen un alto dinamismo, solo superado en los trimestres recientes por la expansin de las colocaciones de consumo. Crecimiento del PIB y Participacin de la fbkc/pib Formacin Bruta en Capital de Construccin (tasa de variacin en 12 meses y porcentaje) En cuanto a la inversin en maquinaria y equipo, que representa cerca de un 40% de la inversin total, su relacin con el crecimiento del producto es ms indirecta. En este caso, se observa una relacin ms estrecha entre la evolucin de la inversin y la rentabilidad de las actividades productivas, aunque tambin en este caso hay un rezago en torno a 4 trimestres entre los cambios observados en la rentabilidad y su efecto en la compra de maquinaria. Por cierto, la rentabilidad de las empresas est vinculada positivamente con la tasa de crecimiento del producto. En el grfico siguiente se presenta la trayectoria de la inversin en maquinaria y equipos y la rentabilidad de las empresas, neta de costo del capital (medida como la rentabilidad operacional promedio de las empresas que publican las FECU, menos la tasa de costo de capital en maquinaria). Hasta mediados de 1998 la inversin en maquinaria como razn del PIB muestra una trayectoria sostenidamente ascendente. Posteriormente se produce una cada en 1999 y una relativa estabilidad desde el 2000. Por su parte, la rentabilidad neta de las empresas se mantuvo en tomo a los 8 puntos porcentuales hasta comienzos de 1997. Luego, la rentabilidad se redujo hasta alrededor de 2 puntos porcentuales hacia fines de 1999. Desde entonces este indicador ha mostrado, con vaivenes, una tendencia a recuperarse, tanto por los aumentos en la rentabilidad operacional de las empresas como por las menores tasas de inters. Perspectivas de la inversin Con relacin a la evolucin reciente y las perspectivas de la inversin en Chile, el marco apropiado para realizar el anlisis es el ltimo Informe de Poltica Monetaria del Banco Central, en el cual se anticipa un mejoramiento gradual en el escenario externo, acercndose a las tasas de crecimiento de tendencia de la economa global hacia fines del prximo ao. Junto a ello, se considera que durante entre el 2003 y el 2004 se producir una recuperacin de los trminos de intercambio que apoyar un crecimiento del ingreso nacional superior al de aos recientes. A su vez, los avances hacia mayores grados de estabilidad financiera en pases vecinos permitirn tambin disminuir las incertidumbres locales, apoyando eventuales aumentos de los flujos de capital y una recuperacin del comercio con la regin. Este conjunto de antecedentes, adems de las condiciones monetarias expansivas de la actualidad, llevar el crecimiento econmico este ao hasta cifras de entre 3 y 4%. Por otra parte, el producto potencial de la economa est creciendo entre 3,5 y 4% por ao durante este ao y el prximo. Por esta razn se espera un crecimiento de la actividad mayor que 4% para el 2004, lo cual llevar a una reduccin de las brechas de capacidad en cerca de 1% del PIB. Por su parte, la tasa de inversin en los ltimos aos se ha mantenido estable en torno al 22% del producto (medida a precios de 1996). Esta cifra refleja que en la actual fase del ciclo de la economa chilena los impulsos de demanda se deben originar ms en el consumo y en las exportaciones, para luego llegar a la inversin en capital fijo. Por esta razn, lo que se espera en el corto plazo es una evolucin de la inversin cercana al crecimiento del producto. Las holguras de capacidad existentes en diversos sectores dificultan por el momento un repunte vigoroso de la formacin bruta de capital fijo a nivel agregado. De hecho, las importaciones y ventas internas de bienes de capital, que se asocian a inversin en maquinaria y equipos, muestran una tendencia de crecimiento moderado. Si bien las importaciones de bienes de capital muestran un mayor dinamismo en el margen, parte de esta recuperacin, no obstante, pareciera estar asociada a proyectos de envergadura en el sector de la celulosa. El mercado inmobiliario, por su lado, ha mostrado gran vigor en los ltimos cuatro trimestres, aunque presenta en el margen un menor dinamismo. Las ventas inmobiliarias continan altas, con cerca de mil unidades mensuales (desestacionalizadas). Segn la informacin ms reciente, los stocks han crecido de forma ms moderada, implicando una reduccin en los meses necesarios para agotarlos. El nivel actual de este ltimo indicador se compara favorablemente con los niveles promedio que se observaron en el perodo 2000-2002. Los elevados niveles de ventas de viviendas responden a las bajas tasas de inters y a las perspectivas econmicas ms favorables de los hogares. En estas condiciones, el dinamismo del sector inmobiliario ha comenzado a traducirse en un notable aumento de los permisos de edificacin, tanto habitacionales como de establecimientos, por lo que puede esperarse mayor actividad y empleo en el sector en los prximos trimestres. Respecto del componente de obras de ingeniera, que representa cerca de un cuarto del total de la inversin fija, el catastro de proyectos de inversin privada de marzo de este ao, que considera una revisin tanto de los proyectos en marcha durante el 2002 como de los planeados para el 2003 y 2004, registr una disminucin de aproximadamente 6,0% para el perodo 2002-2004, respecto de lo informado en diciembre del 2002. Esta cada se concentra principalmente en los sectores Inmobiliario y Obras Pblicas (Concesiones). Por otra parte, los sectores Forestal y Puertos muestran un repunte en su inversin, debido a la entrada de nuevos proyectos al catastro. De acuerdo con el presupuesto del ao 2003, la inversin del sector pblico crecer 6,8% real sobre el ao pasado. Dentro de los principales destinos de esta inversin se encuentran obras de vialidad del Ministerio de Obras Pblicas, el Plan de Transporte Urbano en la Regin Metropolitana, la ampliacin de la red del Metro y la realizacin de proyectos de desarrollo urbano. En cuanto a la rentabilidad de los negocios, las cifras recogidas de las FECU muestran un incremento que se mantiene por varios trimestres consecutivos. Al mismo tiempo, las menores tasas de inters prevalecientes se verifican en el descenso de la relacin entre gastos financieros y gastos totales. Por sectores, aquellos ligados a actividades exportadoras mostraron una importante recuperacin de su rentabilidad, lo que se vincula con la trayectoria del tipo de cambio real y los precios de los bienes de exportacin. A su vez, los sectores no exportadores muestran una sostenida recuperacin de su rentabilidad desde los mnimos que experimentaron a comienzos del 2000. Hacia el futuro, se espera que el crecimiento de la formacin bruta de capital fija est en lnea con la economa como un todo, apoyndose en las menores holguras hacia el prximo ao y la recuperacin de los indicadores de rentabilidad. Hacia adelante, la parcial recuperacin de la rentabilidad corporativa hace esperar un dinamismo mayor en la acumulacin de capital, especialmente de los sectores exportador y de sustitucin de importaciones, en que la recuperacin de los indicadores de rentabilidad es ms notoria. Todo esto, junto con una trayectoria de la inversin pblica que no se desve sustantivamente de lo previsto, permitir incrementar levemente la tasa de inversin fija, sobre todo durante el ao prximo. Los aumentos en la rentabilidad que hemos observado en el ltimo perodo tambin se manifiestan en las cotizaciones burstiles de las empresas, lo que refleja mejores perspectivas de rentabilidad en el futuro. Estos antecedentes tambin sustentan la proyeccin de un aumento en la inversin en maquinaria, aunque existe un importante rezago entre los cambios en la rentabilidad y el resultado en trminos de mayor inversin. Conclusiones En sntesis, las tendencias de la economa permiten anticipar que se mantiene la recuperacin de la actividad econmica, principalmente por la mejora gradual en el escenario externo y el estmulo de la poltica monetaria. Hacia adelante se espera que el crecimiento econmico este ao llegue hasta cifras de entre 3 y 4%, rango equivalente al previsto en enero pasado, mientras se espera un crecimiento de la actividad mayor que 4% para el 2004. Este panorama refleja que en la actualidad estn dadas las condiciones macroeconmicas favorables para un repunte de la inversin en capital fijo, aunque se debe sealar que su recuperacin efectiva ocurre normalmente con un rezago respecto de la actividad econmica. Un aspecto favorable para las perspectivas de la inversin es la mejora en los indicadores de rentabilidad de las empresas y en las cotizaciones burstiles. Estas seales generan, tambin con rezago, respuestas positivas en la inversin en maquinarias y equipos. Por ltimo, un aspecto relevante en este anlisis es la necesidad de reconocer que en los ltimos aos el crecimiento de la productividad total de factores ha sido cercano a cero, debido principalmente a la posicin cclica de la economa chilena. En adelante, en cambio, se espera un repunte en los indicadores de productividad, lo que es una condicin para que los aumentos en el nivel de los recursos productivos se conviertan en un mayor ritmo de crecimiento.

Title: Economic Outlook
text: Economic Outlook PRESENTATION BY JORGE MARSHALL R., VICE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, AT THE ROUND TABLE "PROJECTIONS AND EXPECTATIONS: WHAT AWAITS US IN THE NEXT THREE YEARS", HELD IN SANTIAGO, ON OCTOBER 16, 2003. Introduction The objective of this presentation is to formulate some reflections on the prospects of the Chilean economy in the short and medium term. In the first part of this exhibition I will review the highlights of the external environment. Then I will analyze the internal panorama of the economy. Finally, I will mention the main conclusions of the analysis. Recovery of global economic activity In the current international panorama, three elements stand out that are improving growth prospects in Chile. First, economic activity and world trade have begun a recovery and present better prospects. Second, the terms of trade are also improving. Third, international financial conditions remain favourable. Data from recent months shows a recovery underway in the US and Japan. In the case of the US, there is a recovery that is being boosted by monetary and fiscal policies. In addition, the profitability of companies has recovered, supported by significant increases in productivity. The recovery is also evident in Japan, with growth expected in 2003 above the average recorded since 1990. The external sector continues to lead growth in Japan. In Europe, this year's figures have been revised downwards; however, the latest indicators of confidence and industrial activity are pointing to some improvement. Emerging economies also have better growth prospects, especially in emerging Asia, with growth expected to be above 6 percent in 2003 and 2004. In the case of Latin America, expectations for this year remain low, although a firmer recovery is anticipated in 2004. This trend in global activity is manifested in the growth in the volume of world trade, which has grown on average 6% per year over the past three decades. However, in the last three years the rate of expansion of trade has been around 2% per year. International Monetary Fund (IMF) projections for 2004 and beyond show a return to growth close to 6% in real terms. As a result of this improved picture of global activity, the price of copper has shown an upward trend, reaching an average of 79.5 cents per pound in the third quarter. To the extent that the recovery observed in global activity consolidates, the price of this product should continue on a gradual upward path. For its part, the fluctuations observed in the price of oil are consistent with the projections of US28.5 per barrel for this year, US26 for 2004 and US23 for 2005. For all the above, the terms of trade are expected to have a weak recovery in 2003, but that in 2004 and 2005 they would grow at an average of close to 2.5% per year. Emerging financial markets continue to perform positively, reflected in falling spreads, stock market increases and currency appreciation. Chile's 2012 bond is currently below 100 basis points, about 50 basis points lower than the average for the first four months of this year. Although this trajectory is related to an improvement in the situation of emerging economies in general, it is also due to the credibility of domestic policies, the trade agreement with the US and the favorable evolution of the risk appetite of international investors. Projected further recovery of the domestic economy towards the end of 2003 With this international panorama, domestic activity should gain strength towards the end of 2003. Although domestic activity has remained upward since mid-2002, in the second quarter of this year the recovery weakened. The causes of this fact were transient and now show evidence of dissipating. In the third quarter, partial spending figures show that the dynamism continues, despite which growth in August was punctually lower. Household consumption figures and expectations are consistent with this gradual increase in the rate of growth. Indeed, the Adimark IPEC survey reached the highest level since the beginning of 2000 in September. In addition, the recent growth in supermarket sales validates the greater optimism that confidence surveys throw. In relation to investment, empirical evidence shows that increases in capital formation, both in construction and machinery, occur with several quarters lagging behind output growth. For this reason, the moderate dynamism of investment during this year should not be surprising and, therefore, a panorama of greater investment is anticipated towards next year, which will also be influenced by the improvement in the profitability indicators of companies and in stock prices. These trends support the scenario in which GDP grows in a range of 3.0 to 3.5% this year and between 4 and 5% in 2004. Expansionary financial conditions without risks to inflation Domestic financial markets are showing the effects of greater international stability and improved domestic growth prospects. One of the highlights in recent weeks has been the appreciation of the peso against the dollar. There are several elements that need to be considered in explaining this trend. First, there is a generalized depreciation of the dollar in international financial markets. Second, the scenario of an improvement in the terms of trade of the Chilean economy is gaining more strength. Third, local interest rates have tended to rise while external interest rates have declined, in addition to the decline in the sovereign spread . In any case, measures of the multilateral real exchange rate have tended to appreciate to a lesser extent. Currently, the TCR is at levels similar to the average observed since the beginning of 2001. Additionally, it is important to reiterate that the foreign exchange market works well and the float brings flexibility to the economy. Interest rates have tended to normalize to the extent that the scenario of better prospects for the domestic economy is affirmed. Credit conditions, meanwhile , remain buoyant, especially in the segment for consumer loans. Monetary aggregates, meanwhile, continue their normalization after the increases shown in the first months of this year. Monetary conditions in Chile remain expansionary, despite marginally lower credit growth and increases in some lending interest rates. Interest rates on Central Bank documents have remained stable. It is important to reiterate that the Central Bank uses its policies flexibly, so as to confront the most lasting deviations, in any direction, between projected inflation and the established target. So far, the path of inflation is well placed around the monetary policy target, although core inflation has followed a path below that anticipated a few months ago. The most recent precedents indicate that price pressures are lower than expected and the CPI is even expected to be occasionally below 2% in some months. However, these movements are considered essentially transitory. With the information available, the inflation projection remains around 3% in the next 12 to 24 months. These medium-term trends are influenced by several factors, among which a process of gradual decompression of margins and higher unit labor costs is anticipated. The inflation expectations obtained from the survey of private sector expectations remain at 3.0% for one and two years, similar to the results of the previous months. On the other hand, the expected inflation obtained from the difference between nominal and real rates has fallen somewhat, probably linked to the most recent evolution of the nominal exchange rate. Other relevant factors in the medium term In an assessment of the medium-term prospects of the economy, it is necessary to draw attention to some facts that will affect the chances of recovering higher growth in the economy, although the magnitude of their effects is still uncertain. There is a growing efficiency and credibility in macroeconomic policies to which is added a good functioning of the exchange rate float. This fact allows to achieve greater stability in internal activity. The formal sector of the economy has experienced high productivity growth. While this year's output is about 15% higher than in 1997, formal sector employment has remained constant. From the point of view of companies, this is a competitive advantage that can have a positive impact on resilience. In contrast to the above, margins on sales are below historical averages. This means that much of the cost reductions d0 generated by productivity gains d0 have been converted into lower margins, which can increase the normal lag of investment with respect to activity levels. Estimates of the direct effect of FTAs with Europe and the United States on GDPd1which are based on the increased efficiency generated by resource reallocationd1are in a one-time range of 0.1 to 1.2 percent. However, when dynamic and investment effects are added, magnitudes close to 10% are reached. In the latter case, we may witness a greater effect of FTAs on growth. Infrastructure investments being made in roads, ports and airports will lead to significant cost reductions. Similarly, the reform of the system for appointing senior government managers can have a significant influence on medium-term growth. Conclusions Projections for activity in 2003 and 2004 consider a phase of higher growth, due to the improved prospects of the international economy. Domestic financial conditions support this scenario in which GDP grows in a range of 3.0 to 3.5% this year and between 4 and 5% in 2004. Moreover, there are good conditions for the current recovery to turn into sustained growth. On the other hand, with the information available, inflation remains around 3% in the next 12 to 24 months.
