Tercero, las condiciones financieras internacionales mantienen una posicin favorable. La informacin de los meses recientes muestra una recuperacin en marcha en EE.UU. y Japn. En el caso de EE.UU., se observa una recuperacin que est recibiendo el impulso de las polticas monetaria y fiscal. Adems, la rentabilidad de las empresas se ha recuperado, apoyada por importantes incrementos de productividad. La recuperacin tambin se manifiesta en Japn, con un crecimiento esperado en el 2003 por encima del promedio que se registra desde 1990. El sector externo sigue liderando el crecimiento en Japn. En Europa, las cifras para este ao han sido corregidas a la baja; no obstante, los indicadores ms recientes de confianza y de actividad industrial estn sealando alguna mejora. En las economas emergentes tambin se presentan mejores perspectivas de crecimiento, especialmente en Asia emergente, con un crecimiento esperado por sobre el 6% en el 2003 y 2004. En el caso de Amrica Latina, las expectativas para este ao siguen bajas, aunque se anticipa una recuperacin ms firme en el 2004. Esta tendencia de la actividad global se manifiesta en el crecimiento del volumen del comercio mundial, que ha crecido en promedio 6% anual en las ltimas tres dcadas. Sin embargo, en los ltimos tres aos el ritmo de expansin del comercio ha estado en torno a 2% anual. Las proyecciones del Fondo Monetario Internacional (FMI) para el 2004 y los aos siguientes muestran un retorno a un crecimiento cercano a 6% real. Como consecuencia de este mejor panorama de la actividad mundial, el precio del cobre ha mostrado una tendencia ascendente, alcanzando un promedio de 79,5 centavos de dlar por libra en el tercer trimestre. En la medida en que la recuperacin que se observa en la actividad mundial se consolide, el precio de este producto debera continuar en una trayectoria de alza gradual. Por su parte, las oscilaciones observadas en el precio del petrleo son coherentes con las proyecciones de US$28,5 por barril para el presente ao, US$26 para el 2004 y US$23 para el 2005. Por todo lo anterior, se espera que los trminos de intercambio tengan una recuperacin dbil en el 2003, pero que en el 2004 y 2005 creceran a un promedio cercano a 2,5% anual. Los mercados financieros emergentes siguen mostrando una evolucin positiva, lo que se ha reflejado en cadas en los spreads, alzas en las bolsas y apreciacin de las monedas. El bono chileno 2012 se ubica en la actualidad por debajo de los 100 puntos base, unos 50 puntos menos que el promedio de los primeros cuatro meses de este ao. Si bien esta trayectoria se relaciona con una mejora en la situacin de las economas emergentes en general, tambin se debe a la credibilidad de las polticas internas, al acuerdo comercial con EE.UU. y a la favorable evolucin del apetito por riesgo de los inversionistas internacionales. Proyeccin de una mayor reactivacin de la economa interna hacia fines del 2003 Con este panorama internacional, la actividad interna debe tomar fuerza hacia fines del 2003. Si bien la actividad interna se ha mantenido al alza desde mediados del 2002, en el segundo trimestre de este ao la recuperacin se debilit. Las causas de este hecho fueron transitorias y ahora muestran evidencia de disiparse. En el tercer trimestre, las cifras parciales de gasto muestran que el dinamismo contina, a pesar de lo cual el crecimiento de agosto fue puntualmente menor. Las cifras de consumo y expectativas de los hogares son coherentes con esta evolucin de paulatino incremento en el ritmo de crecimiento. En efecto, la encuesta IPEC de Adimark alcanz en septiembre el mayor nivel desde comienzos del ao 2000. Adems, el reciente crecimiento de las ventas de supermercados valida el mayor optimismo que arrojan las encuestas de confianza. En relacin con la inversin, la evidencia emprica muestra que los aumentos en la formacin de capital, tanto en construccin como en maquinarias, se producen con varios trimestres de rezago respecto al crecimiento del producto. Por esta razn, no debe sorprender el moderado dinamismo de la inversin durante este ao y, por lo mismo, se anticipa un panorama de mayor inversin hacia el prximo ao, lo que tambin estar influido por la mejora en los indicadores de rentabilidad de las empresas y en las cotizaciones burstiles. Estas tendencias apoyan el escenario en que el PIB crece en un rango de 3,0 a 3,5% este ao y entre 4 y 5% en el 2004. Condiciones financieras expansivas sin riesgos para la inflacin Los mercados financieros internos estn mostrando los efectos de la mayor estabilidad internacional y de las mejores perspectivas de crecimiento interno. Uno de los hechos destacados en las ltimas semanas ha sido la apreciacin del peso respecto del dlar. Hay varios elementos que deben considerarse al explicar esta tendencia. Primero, hay una depreciacin generalizada del dlar en los mercados financieros internacionales. Segundo, adquiere ms fuerza el escenario de una mejora de los trminos de intercambio de la economa chilena. Tercero, las tasas de inters locales han tendido a aumentar mientras las externas han disminuido, a lo que se agrega el descenso del spread soberano. En todo caso, las mediciones del tipo de cambio real multilateral han tendido a apreciarse en menor magnitud. En la actualidad, el TCR est en niveles similares al promedio observado desde inicios del 2001. Adicionalmente, es importante reiterar que el mercado cambiario funciona bien y la flotacin aporta flexibilidad a la economa. Las tasas de inters han tendido a normalizarse en la medida en que se afirma el escenario de mejores perspectivas de la economa interna. Por su parte, las condiciones del crdito mantienen su dinamismo, especialmente en el segmento destinado a crditos de consumo. Los agregados monetarios, por su parte, continan su normalizacin luego de los aumentos mostrados en los primeros meses de este ao. Las condiciones monetarias en Chile siguen siendo expansivas, a pesar del marginalmente menor crecimiento del crdito y las alzas de algunas tasas de inters de colocacin. Las tasas de inters de los documentos del Banco Central han seguido estables. Es importante reiterar que el Banco Central utiliza sus polticas con flexibilidad, de manera de confrontar las desviaciones ms duraderas, en cualquier direccin, entre la inflacin proyectada y la meta establecida. Hasta el momento, la trayectoria de la inflacin est bien situada en torno a la meta de la poltica monetaria, aunque la inflacin subyacente ha seguido una trayectoria por debajo de la anticipada hace unos meses. Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que las presiones de precios son menores que las previstas e incluso se espera que el IPC se ubique puntualmente bajo 2% en algunos meses. Sin embargo, estos movimientos se consideran esencialmente transitorios. Con la informacin disponible se mantiene la proyeccin de inflacin en torno a 3% en los prximos 12 a 24 meses. Estas tendencias de mediano plazo estn influidas por varios factores, entre los cuales se anticipa un proceso de descompresin gradual de mrgenes y costos laborales unitarios mayores. Las expectativas de inflacin que se obtienen de la encuesta de expectativas del sector privado se mantienen en 3,0% para uno y dos aos plazo, similar a los resultados de los meses anteriores. Por su parte, la inflacin esperada que se obtiene de la diferencia entre tasas nominales y reales m uestra algn descenso, probablemente vinculado con la evolucin ms reciente del tipo de cambio nominal. Otros factores relevantes en el mediano plazo En una evaluacin de las perspectivas de mediano plazo de la economa, es necesario llamar la atencin de algunos hechos que van a incidir en las posibilidades de recuperar un crecimiento mayor de la economa, aunque la magnitud de sus efectos es an incierta. Se observa una creciente eficiencia y credibilidad en las polticas macroeconmicas a lo que se agrega un buen funcionamiento de la flotacin cambiara. Este hecho permite alcanzar una mayor estabilidad en la actividad interna. El sector formal de la economa ha experimentado un alto crecimiento de la productividad. Mientras el producto de este ao es alrededor de 15% mayor que el de 1997, el empleo del sector formal se ha mantenido constante. Desde el punto de vista de las empresas, esta es una ventaja competitiva que puede incidir positivamente en la capacidad de recuperacin. Contrastando con lo anterior, los mrgenes sobre ventas estn por debajo de los promedios histricos. Esto significa que gran parte de las reducciones de costos generadas por los aumentos de productividad se han convertido en menores mrgenes, lo que puede aumentar el rezago normal de la inversin respecto de los niveles de actividad. Las estimaciones del efecto directo de los TLC con Europa y Estados Unidos en el PIB que se basan en la mayor eficiencia generada por la reasignacin de recursos se encuentran en un rango de 0,1 a 1,2% por una sola vez. Sin embargo, cuando se agregan los efectos dinmicos y de inversin, se alcanzan magnitudes cercanas a 10%. En este ltimo caso, podemos presenciar un efecto mayor de los TLC en el crecimiento. Las inversiones en infraestructura que se estn realizando en carreteras, puertos y aeropuertos generarn reducciones importantes de costos. Del mismo modo, la reforma en el sistema de designacin de los altos directivos del Estado puede tener una influencia relevante en el crecimiento de mediano plazo. Conclusiones Las proyecciones para la actividad en el 2003 y 2004 consideran una fase de mayor crecimiento, debido a las mejores perspectivas de la economa internacional. Las condiciones financieras internas apoyan este escenario en que el PIB crece en un rango de 3,0 a 3,5% este ao y entre 4 y 5% en el 2004. Ms all, existen buenas condiciones para que la actual recuperacin se convierta en un crecimiento sostenido. Por otra parte, con la informacin disponible, la inflacin se mantiene en torno a 3% en los prximos 12 a 24 meses.

Title: Economic outlook and monetary policy
text: Economic Outlook and Monetary Policy PRESENTATION BY JORGE MARSHALL R., VICE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, AT THE 2003 REGIONAL CONFERENCES ORGANIZED BY THE DIARIO FINANCIERO, HELD IN TEMUCO, ON OCTOBER 30, 2003. Introduction The objective of this presentation is to formulate some personal reflections on the prospects of the Chilean economy in the short and medium term. The highlights of the current situation are as follows: - In the third quarter of this year, there was a turn in the international economy that confirms the global recovery. - Domestic activity began a recovery in the second half of 2002, which should gain strength by the end of this year. - Financial conditions remain expansionary and no risk to inflation is seen. These elements allow us to anticipate favorable economic conditions for the coming quarters, which may lead to the current recovery to sustained growth. Global economy The international scene experienced a turn in the third quarter of this year. World economic activity and trade are recovering and prospects for 2004 are improving. This allows our export prices to rise and external financial conditions to maintain a favourable position. Data from recent months show a recovery in the US and Japan. In the case of the US, the recovery is being boosted by monetary and fiscal policies. In addition, the profitability of companies has recovered, supported by significant increases in productivity. The recovery is also evident in Japan, with growth expected in 2003 above the average recorded since 1990. In Europe, in turn, confidence and industrial activity indicators are recovering. Emerging economies also have better growth prospects, especially in Asia, with growth expected to be above 6 percent in 2003 and 2004. In the case of Latin America, expectations for this year remain low, although a firmer recovery is anticipated in 2004. As a result of this improved outlook for global activity, the price of copper is higher than anticipated, reaching an average of 87 cents per pound in October. Oil price swings are consistent with projections of USS 26 per barrel for 2004 and USS 23 for 2005. For all the above, the terms of trade have begun to improve in the second half of this year. For 2004 and 2005, average growth of close to 2.5 per cent per year is anticipated. Emerging financial markets have stabilized after a period of falling spreads. Chile's 2012 bond was around 82 basis points in October, about 60 basis points lower than the average for the first half of this year. While this trajectory is related to an improvement in the situation of emerging economies in general, it is also due to the credibility of policies and favourable domestic expectations. Internal activity In this international scenario, domestic activity should gain strength towards the end of 2003 and especially in 2004. Household consumption figures and expectations are consistent with this gradual increase in the rate of growth. Indeed, the Adimark IPEC survey reached the highest level since the beginning of 2000 in September. In addition, the evolution of different consumption indicators validates the greater optimism shown by confidence surveys. Maintaining this trend depends, to a large extent, on the evolution of employment. In relation to investment, empirical evidence shows that increases in capital formation occur with several quarters lagging behind output growth. For this reason, the moderate dynamism of investment during this year should not be surprising . Formal sector firms have achieved productivity gains in recent years. For example, while output in 2003 is about 15 percent higher than in 1997, formal sector employment has remained constant. This is a competitive advantage when it comes to taking advantage of the momentum of the current external scenario and low interest rates. For this reason, greater private investment is anticipated towards next year, which is also influenced by the improvement in the profitability indicators of companies and in stock prices. Real exports are showing growth in line with the projection of 5.7% for this year and 6.4% in 2004. In addition, estimates of the direct effect of free trade agreements (FTAs) with Europe and the United States on gross domestic product (GDP)d1which is based on the increased efficiency generated by the reallocation of resourcesd1are in a one-time range of 0.1 to 1.2 percent. However, when dynamic and investment effects are added, magnitudes close to 10% are reached. In the latter case, we may see a larger effect of FTAs on growth, which also supports the shift from recovery to sustained growth. Monetary policy Financial markets are showing the effects of the improved international outlook, improved domestic growth prospects and the absence of inflationary pressures. The result is manifested in the appreciation in the real exchange rate and in the most recent decline in longer-term interest rates. There are two factors that must be considered in explaining the exchange rate appreciation. On the one hand, the general fall of the dollar in international financial markets. This effect leads to the peso/dollar ratio appreciating more than the peso's parity with other currencies. On the other hand, there is the strengthening of the peso that is expressed in the multilateral exchange rate. This appreciation is due to better growth expectations in the coming years, a favourable evolution of the terms of trade and the reduction in the risk premium that investors demand from Chilean securities. When market conditions produce these fluctuations, it is important to reiterate that monetary policy does not have the capacity to affect the real exchange rate of the economy, which is the relevant variable in the allocation of resources. Moreover, experience shows that when it attempts to do so, it causes distortions that do more harm than good in economic growth. This leads to reaffirm that the floating regime is a contribution to the stability and flexibility of the economy. For their part, interest rates have reacted to a scenario of lower inflationary pressures. This is a fact that is happening in Chile, as well as in the main developed economies, although each economy shows particularities that depend on internal evolution. While the weakening of inflationary pressures on a global scale is linked to the cyclical position of the economy, it is also being helped by structural factors, including the institutionality of monetary policy, the competition that comes with globalization, market deregulation and productivity gains observed in recent years. These factors influence the magnitude of inflation's response to changes in other areas of the economy, such as changes in the nominal exchange rate or external prices. However, these facts do not change the monetary nature of inflationary processes. Moreover, despite lower inflationary pressures, their consequences may be more damaging than before, because the economy is more integrated with the rest of the world and markets now react faster to changes in an economy's risk. As in other countries, this is reflected in a decline in inflation expectations and a reduction in longer-term rates. This movement is consistent with the market's perception that in the current economic cycle there has been greater room to maintain an expansionary stance in monetary policy for a longer period, even though, at the same time, the scenario of better growth prospects for aggregate demand is affirmed. Under these conditions, it is important to reiterate that the Central Bank uses its policies flexibly, so as to confront the most lasting deviations, in any direction, between projected inflation and the established target. So far, the path of inflation is well placed around the monetary policy target, although total and core inflation have followed a path below that anticipated a few months ago. The most recent record indicates that price pressures are lower than expected and the CPI is even expected to be below 2% in some months. However, more detailed information on price and cost developments suggests that this lower inflation in 12 months is transitory. The medium-term inflation projection continues to converge towards 3%, which is the nominal anchor of the economy. This trend, although less intense than anticipated, is influenced by several factors, among which there is a process of gradual decompression of margins and higher unit labor costs. Although with some fluctuations, private sector inflation expectations are consistent with this scenario. Conclusions Recent evidence of a better external scenario is consistent with GDP growth of between 3 and 3.5% for this year and 4 to 5% for 2004. Domestic financial conditions support this scenario. On the other hand, with the information available, medium-term inflation converges towards 3%. The conditions for moving from a phase of recovery to sustained growth are favourable.

Por esta razn, no debe sorprender el moderado dinamismo de la inversin durante este ao. Las empresas del sector formal han logrado aumentos de productividad en los ltimos aos. Por ejemplo, mientras el producto del 2003 es alrededor de 15% mayor que el de 1997, el empleo del sector formal se ha mantenido constante. Esta es una ventaja competitiva a la hora de aprovechar el impulso del actual escenario externo y las bajas tasas de inters. Por esta razn, se anticipa una mayor inversin privada hacia el prximo ao, lo que tambin est influido por la mejora en los indicadores de rentabilidad de las empresas y en las cotizaciones burstiles. Las exportaciones reales estn mostrando un crecimiento acorde con la proyeccin de 5,7% para el presente ao y de 6,4% en el 2004. Adems, las estimaciones del efecto directo de los tratados de libre comercio (TLC) con Europa y Estados Unidos en el producto interno bruto (PIB) que se basa en la mayor eficiencia generada por la reasignacin de recursosse encuentran en un rango de 0,1 a 1,2% por una sola vez. Sin embargo, cuando se agregan los efectos dinmicos y de inversin, se alcanzan magnitudes cercanas a 10%. En este ltimo caso, podemos presenciar un efecto mayor de los TLC en el crecimiento, lo que tambin apoya el paso de una recuperacin a un crecimiento sostenido. Poltica monetaria Los mercados financieros estn mostrando los efectos del mejor panorama internacional, de las mejores perspectivas de crecimiento interno y de la ausencia de presiones inflacionarias. El resultado se manifiesta en la apreciacin en el tipo de cambio real y en la ms reciente disminucin en las tasas de inters de mayor plazo. Hay dos factores que deben considerarse al explicar la apreciacin cambiara. Por una parte, la cada generalizada del dlar en los mercados financieros internacionales. Este efecto lleva a que la relacin peso/dlarse aprecie ms que la paridad del peso conotras monedas. Por otra parte, est el fortalecimiento del peso que se expresa en el tipo de cambio multilateral. Esta apreciacin obedece a mejores expectativas de crecimiento en los prximos aos, a una evolucin favorable de los trminos de intercambio y a la disminucin del premio por riesgo que los inversionistas exigen a los ttulos chilenos. Cuando las condiciones del mercado producen estas fluctuaciones, es importante reiterar que la poltica monetaria no tiene la capacidad de afectar el tipo de cambio real de la economa, que es la variable relevante en la asignacin de recursos. An ms, la experiencia muestra que cuando intenta hacerlo provoca distorsiones que generan ms daos que beneficios en el crecimiento econmico. Esto lleva a reafirmar que el rgimen de flotacin es un aporte a la estabilidad y flexibilidad de la economa. Por su parte, las tasas de inters han reaccionado a un escenario de menores presiones inflacionarias. Este es un hecho que est ocurriendo en Chile, as como en las principales economas desarrolladas, aunque cada economa muestra particularidades que dependen de la evolucin interna. Si bien el debilitamiento de las presiones inflacionarias a escala global est vinculado a la posicin cclica de la economa, tambin est siendo ayudado por factores estructurales, entre los que aparece la institucionalidad de la poltica monetaria, la competencia que viene con la globalizacin, la desregulacin de mercados y los aumentos de productividad observados en los ltimos aos. Estos factores influyen en la magnitud de la respuesta de la inflacin a los cambios que ocurren en otros mbitos de la economa, como son las variaciones en el tipo de cambio nominal o en los precios externos. Sin embargo, estos hechos no cambian la naturaleza monetaria de los procesos inflacionarios. Adems, a pesar de las menores presiones inflacionarias, sus consecuencias pueden ser ms dainas que antes, porque la economa est ms integrada al resto del mundo y los mercados, en la actualidad, reaccionan ms rpido ante cambios en el riesgo de una economa. Al igual que en otros pases, este hecho se refleja en una disminucin en las expectativas de inflacin y en una reduccin en las tasas de mayor plazo. Este movimiento es coherente con la percepcin del mercado de que en el actual ciclo econmico ha existido un mayor espacio para mantener por un mayor lapso una posicin expansiva en la poltica monetaria, aun cuando, al mismo tiempo, se afirma el escenario de mejores perspectivas de crecimiento de la demanda agregada. En estas condiciones es importante reiterar que el Banco Central utiliza sus polticas con flexibilidad, de manera de confrontar las desviaciones ms duraderas, en cualquier direccin, entre la inflacin proyectada y la meta establecida. Hasta el momento, la trayectoria de la inflacin est bien situada en torno a la meta de la poltica monetaria, aunque la inflacin total y la subyacente han seguido una trayectoria por debajo de la anticipada hace unos meses. Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que las presiones de precios son menores que las previstas e incluso se espera que el IPC se ubique bajo el 2% en algunos meses. Sin embargo, la informacin ms detallada de la evolucin de los precios y de los costos permite considerar que esta menor inflacin en 12 meses es transitoria. La proyeccin de inflacin de mediano plazo se mantiene convergiendo hacia 3%, que es el ancla nominal de la economa. Esta tendencia, si bien con menos intensidad que lo anticipado, est influida por varios factores, entre los cuales hay un proceso de descompresin gradual de mrgenes y costos laborales unitarios mayores. Si bien con algunas fluctuaciones, las expectativas de inflacin del sector privado son coherentes con este panorama. Conclusiones La evidencia reciente de un mejor escenario externo es coherente con un crecimiento del PIB entre 3 y 3,5% para este ao y de 4 a 5% para el 2004. Las condiciones financieras internas apoyan este escenario. Por otra parte, con la informacin disponible, la inflacin de mediano plazo converge hacia un 3%. Las condiciones para pasar de una fase de recuperacin a un crecimiento sostenido son favorables.

Title: Monetary Policy and Recovery
text: Monetary policy and recovery Presentation by Jorge Marshall Rivera, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile. VI Business Meeting of CORMA and Universidad del Desarrollo, Concepci97n, November 13, 2003. I want to thank Corma and the Universidad del Desarrollo for their invitation to participate in the VI Business Meeting and take this opportunity to share with you some personal reflections on the current conditions of the economy, its perspectives and the policies applied by the Central Bank. The central idea that I am interested in highlighting in this presentation is that behind the reactivation we are experiencing is the recovery of the international economy and also the credibility of macro policies in Chile, which allows us to take advantage of the opportunities offered by foreign markets. I mean a5 Since the third quarter of this year, there has been a positive turn in world activity and trade. This new scenario was quickly transmitted to Chile, starting with financial markets and household expectations. In this context, domestic activity maintains favourable prospects for 2004. a5 The best contribution that macro policy can make to this recovery is to continue applying the policy rules that have gained credibility in the markets and that allow us to take advantage of the best international scenario. These rules are expressed in the order of public finances, a monetary policy aimed at maintaining low inflation coupled with the floating exchange rate and the solvency of the financial system. These two elements, external scenario and credibility in domestic policies, are supporting the current recovery and allow us to anticipate favorable economic conditions for the coming quarters, which may lead the current recovery to sustained growth. From global economics to domestic activity The international scene experienced a turn in the third quarter of this year. World economic activity and trade are recovering and the positive outlook for 2004 is affirmed. This allows our export prices to rise and external financial conditions to maintain a favourable position. As a result of this better outlook for global activity, the price of copper is higher than anticipated, reaching an average of around 90 cents per pound in the last 30 days. Meanwhile, the fluctuations in oil prices are consistent with projections of US26 per barrel for 2004 and US23 for 2005. The terms of trade have begun to improve in the second half of this year and the outlook forward is for now higher than anticipated a few months ago. Emerging financial markets have stabilized after a period of falling spreads. Chile's 2012 bond is down from 80 basis points in November, about 70 basis points lower than the average for the first half of this year. While this trajectory is related to an improvement in the situation of emerging economies in general, it is also due to the credibility of policies and favourable domestic expectations. In this international scenario, domestic activity should continue on the path anticipated in the September Monetary Policy Report, with growth between 4% and 5% in 2004. The observed increases in consumption and household expectations are consistent with this gradual increase in the rate of growth. Adimark's IPEC survey reached its highest level in five years in October. In addition, the evolution of different consumption indicators validates the positive balance shown by confidence surveys. In relation to investment, empirical evidence shows that increases in capital formation occur with several quarters lagging behind output growth. For this reason, the moderate dynamism of investment during this year should not be surprising. Companies in the formal sector have achieved productivity gains in recent years, which is a competitive advantage when it comes to taking advantage of the momentum of the current external scenario and low interest rates. For this reason, greater private investment is anticipated towards next year, which is also influenced by the improvement in the profitability indicators of companies. Real exports are showing growth in line with the projection of 6.4% in 2004. In addition, estimates of the direct effect of FTAs with Europe and the United States on GDP, which is based on the greater efficiency generated by the reallocation of resources, is in a range of 0.1% to 1.2% for a single time. However, when dynamic and investment effects are added, magnitudes close to 10% are reached. In the latter case, we can see a greater effect of FTAs on growth, which also supports the shift from recovery to sustained growth. The contribution of monetary policy Apart from the boost coming from external conditions, the positive impact of the macro policy regime implemented in recent years should also be highlighted. The structural surplus rule has allowed for lower interest rates and a competitive real exchange rate. The application of flexible policy rules has generated confidence and credibility in institutions, which is a precondition for investment increases. It is correct to state that the effect on growth of macro policies is limited, so it must be complemented by micro policies and structural reforms. Moreover, in the case of Chile, macro policies have been providing virtually everything possible. However, this should not make us lose sight of the fact that without an environment of stability in the macroeconomy it would be very difficult to take advantage of the recovery of the global economy. In Chile, macro stability is based on three pillars: a5 Structural surplus rule that maintains order in public finances a5 monetary rule that keeps inflation low and allows exchange rate floating rate, and a5 rules that allow the solvency of the financial system. All these policies incorporate flexibility criteria, which allow them to obtain their greatest effect in supporting recovery, without neglecting the requirements of medium-term stability. Current monetary policy seeks to keep inflation in a symmetric range of 2 to 4%, centered at 3%, which must be permanently implemented over a medium-term horizon, defined over two years. This time perspective is due to the fact that short-term supply shocks are not avoidable with monetary policy, so some of the variability in short-run inflation does not originate from demand impulses. The central bank worries when the medium-term scenario of inflation exceeds or falls below the range. That is, the Central Bank does not seek inflation lower than that defined by its range, because of the risk of falling into deflation that can be very costly in terms of economic activity. For this purpose, a horizon is defined in which monetary policy is effective, so it can have more control over inflation. The main merit of this regime is that it responds to an established rule, which makes policies predictable, and at the same time incorporates a certain discretion, which allows to help in the economic cycle, as has been the case in recent years. In the case of monetary policy, low interest rates have supported the recovery to the extent that this has not meant distancing itself from the inflation target in the medium term. This monetary policy is complemented by a floating exchange rate regime, in which the only commitment of the Central Bank is to inflation. In practice, this scheme requires confidence in the market to autonomously determine the exchange rate. Experience in various economies that are financially integrated abroad shows that when the authorities try to influence the exchange rate, they end up causing distortions that do more harm than good to economic growth. On the other hand, exchange rate flexibility gives the economy the capacity to cope with external shocks, facilitating an adjustment that could otherwise be postponed and, therefore, more complex. That is, from the application of these policy rules, financial markets highly integrated with the rest of the world determine medium-term interest rates, asset prices and the exchange rate. Short-term variations in financial prices reflect changes in demand for Chilean assets. In relation to the recent appreciation of the peso, there are two factors that must be considered. First, there is a general fall of the dollar in international financial markets. While in the course of 2003 the appreciation of the Chilean peso reached 13%, the appreciation of several other currencies has been even greater. For example, in Canada and New Zealand it has been around 16% and in Australia and South Africa it reaches a figure close to 20%. This fact leads to the peso/dollar ratio appreciating more than the parity of the peso with other currencies. Secondly, there is the strengthening of the peso expressed in the multilateral exchange rate, which includes all our trading partners. This appreciation is due to better growth expectations in the coming years, a favorable evolution of the terms of trade, the reduction in the risk premium that investors demand from Chilean securities and also greater stability in Latin America. In this scenario, it is important to insist on the different reaction of monetary policy to supply and demand shocks, apart from the fact that the effects of monetary policy measures on inflation take several quarters to materialize. Shifts in demand have lasting effects on inflation, so they must be met with changes in monetary policy. On the contrary, supply shocks are transitory phenomena, which are usually accompanied by greater short-term volatility in inflation. Under these conditions, the Central Bank's action is aimed at preventing these latest impacts from being incorporated into inflation expectations, reaffirming its nominal anchor. The reduction in margins and the decline in the exchange rate in the second half of this year is producing a lower-than-anticipated trajectory of inflation. Current market inflation expectations, measured through differences between nominal and real interest rates, have also been reduced. This movement is consistent with the perception of the financial markets that in the current economic cycle there has been greater room to maintain an expansionary position in monetary policy for longer, even though at the same time the scenario of better prospects for growth in aggregate demand is confirmed. Under these conditions, it is important to reiterate that the Central Bank uses its policies flexibly, so as to confront the most lasting deviations, in any direction, between projected inflation and the established target. Conclusions In summary, when analyzing the current recovery in domestic activity, it is important to point out the role of the international economy and also the credibility of macro policies, which make it possible to take advantage of the opportunities offered by external markets. The best contribution macro policy can make to this recovery is to maintain stable policy rules. The same rules that are allowing us to take advantage of the best international scenario. These rules are expressed in the order of public finances, the maintenance of low inflation, the floating exchange rate and the solvency of the financial system.

VI Encuentro Empresarial de CORMA y Universidad del Desarrollo, Concepcin, 13 de noviembre de 2003. Quiero agradecer la invitacin de Corma y la Universidad del Desarrollo a participar en el VI Encuentro Empresarial y aprovechar esta oportunidad para compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones personales sobre las condiciones actuales de la economa, sus perspectivas y las polticas que aplica el Banco Central. Es decir,  Desde el tercer trimestre de este ao se observa un giro positivo en la actividad y el comercio mundial. Este nuevo panorama se transmiti rpidamente a Chile, partiendo por los mercados financieros y las expectativas de los hogares. En este contexto la actividad interna mantiene perspectivas favorables para el 2004.  El mejor aporte que puede hacer la poltica macro a esta recuperacin es continuar aplicando las reglas de poltica que han ganado credibilidad en los mercados y que permiten aprovechar el mejor escenario internacional. Estas reglas se expresan en el orden de las finanzas pblicas, una poltica monetaria orientada a mantener una inflacin baja unida a la flotacin cambiara y la solvencia del sistema financiero. Estos dos elementos, escenario externo y credibilidad en las polticas internas, estn apoyando la actual recuperacin y permiten anticipar condiciones econmicas favorables para los prximos trimestres, que pueden llevar la actual recuperacin a un crecimiento sostenido. De la econmica global a la actividad interna El panorama internacional experiment un giro en el tercer trimestre de este ao. La actividad econmica y el comercio mundial estn en recuperacin y las perspectivas positivas del 2004 se afirman. Esto permite que los precios de nuestras exportaciones suban y las condiciones financieras externas mantengan una posicin favorable. Como consecuencia de este mejor panorama de la actividad mundial el precio del cobre est por encima de lo anticipado, alcanzando en los ltimos 30 das un promedio en torno a los 90 centavos de dlar por libra. Por su parte, las oscilaciones en el precio del petrleo son coherentes con las proyecciones de US$26 por barril para el 2004 y US$23 para el 2005. Los trminos de intercambio han comenzado a mejorar en el segundo semestre de este ao y las perspectivas hacia delante estn por ahora por encima de lo anticipado hace algunos meses. Los mercados financieros emergentes se han estabilizado luego de un perodo de cadas en los spreads. El bono chileno 2012 ha bajado de los 80 puntos base en noviembre, unos 70 puntos base menos que el promedio del primer semestre de este ao. Si bien esta trayectoria se relaciona con una mejora en la situacin de las economas emergentes en general, tambin se debe a la credibilidad de las polticas y a las favorables expectativas internas. En este panorama internacional la actividad interna debe continuar en la trayectoria anticipada en el Informe de Poltica Monetaria de Septiembre, con un crecimiento entre 4% y 5% en el 2004. Los aumentos observados en el consumo y en las expectativas de los hogares son coherentes con esta evolucin de paulatino incremento en el ritmo de crecimiento. La encuesta IPEC de Adimark alcanz en octubre su mayor nivel en cinco aos. Adems, la evolucin de diferentes indicadores del consumo valida el balance positivo que muestran las encuestas de confianza. En relacin con la inversin, la evidencia emprica muestra que los aumentos en la formacin de capital, se producen con varios trimestres de rezago respecto al crecimiento del producto. Por esta razn no debe sorprender el moderado dinamismo de la inversin durante este ao. Las empresas del sector formal han logrado aumentos de productividad en los ltimos aos, lo que es una ventaja competitiva a la hora de aprovechar el impulso del actual escenario externo y las bajas tasas de inters. Por esta razn se anticipa una mayor inversin privada hacia el prximo ao, lo que tambin est influido por la mejora en los indicadores de rentabilidad de las empresas. Las exportaciones reales estn mostrando un crecimiento en lnea con la proyeccin de 6,4% en el 2004. Adems, las estimaciones del efecto directo de los TLC con Europa y Estados Unidos en el PIB, que se basa en la mayor eficiencia generada por la reasignacin de recursos, se encuentra en un rango de 0,1% a 1,2% por una sola vez. Sin embargo, cuando se agregan los efectos dinmicos y de inversin, se alcanzan magnitudes cercanas al 10%. En este ltimo caso podemos presenciar un efecto mayor de los TLC en el crecimiento, lo que tambin apoya el paso de una recuperacin a un crecimiento sostenido. El aporte de la poltica monetaria Aparte del impulso que viene de las condiciones externas, tambin se debe destacar el efecto positivo del rgimen de poltica macro aplicado en los ltimos aos. La regla de supervit estructural ha permitido tasas de inters ms bajas y un tipo de cambio real competitivo. La aplicacin de reglas flexibles de poltica ha generado confianza y credibilidad en las instituciones, que es una condicin previa a los aumentos de inversin. Es correcto afirmar que el efecto en el crecimiento de las polticas macro es limitado, por lo que debe ser complementado con polticas micro y reformas estructurales. Adems, en el caso de Chile las polticas macro han estado aportando prcticamente todo lo que es posible. Sin embargo, ello no debe hacernos perder de vista que sin un ambiente de estabilidad en la macroeconoma sera muy difcil aprovechar la recuperacin de la economa global. En Chile la estabilidad macro se apoya en tres pilares:  regla de supervit estructural que mantiene el orden en las finanzas pblicas  regla monetaria que mantiene la inflacin baja y permite la flotacin cambiara, y  reglas que permiten la solvencia del sistema financiero. Todas estas polticas incorporan criterios de flexibilidad, que permiten obtener su mayor efecto de apoyo a la reactivacin, sin descuidar las exigencias de la estabilidad de mediano plazo. La poltica monetaria actual procura mantener la inflacin en un rango simtrico de 2 a 4%, centrado en 3%, el cual debe ser cumplido de manera permanente en un horizonte de mediano plazo, definido en tomo a dos aos. Esta perspectiva de tiempo se debe a que los shocks de oferta de corto plazo no son evitables con la poltica monetaria, por lo que una parte de la variabilidad de la inflacin de corto plazo no se origina en los impulsos de demanda. El Banco Central se preocupa cuando el escenario de mediano plazo de la inflacin excede o se ubica por debajo del rango. Es decir, el Banco Central no busca una inflacin ms baja que la definida por su rango, por el riesgo de caer en una deflacin que puede resultar muy costosa en trminos de actividad econmica. Para este efecto se define un horizonte en el que la poltica monetaria es efectiva, por lo que puede tener ms control sobre la inflacin. El principal mrito de este rgimen es que responde a una regla establecida, lo que hace que las polticas sean predecibles, y al mismo tiempo incorpora cierta discrecionalidad, que permite ayudar en el ciclo econmico, como ha sido el caso en los aos recientes. En el caso de la poltica monetaria, las bajas tasas de inters han apoyado la recuperacin en la medida que ello no ha significado distanciarse de la meta de inflacin en el mediano plazo. Esta poltica monetaria es complementada con un rgimen de flotacin cambiara, en que el nico compromiso del Banco Central es con la inflacin. En la prctica este esquema exige confianza en el mercado para determinar de manera autnoma el tipo de cambio. La experiencia en diversas economas integradas financieramente con el exterior muestra que cuando la autoridad intenta influir en el tipo de cambio termina provocando distorsiones que generan ms daos que beneficios en el crecimiento econmico. En cambio, la flexibilidad cambiara confiere a la economa la capacidad para enfrentar los shocks externos, facilitando un ajuste que en caso contrario podra ser pospuesto y, por ende, ms complejo. Es decir, a partir de la aplicacin de estas reglas de poltica, los mercados financieros altamente integrados al resto del mundo, determinan las tasas de inters de mediano plazo, los precios de los activos y el tipo de cambio. Las variaciones de corto plazo en los precios financieros reflejan los cambios en la demanda por activos chilenos. Con relacin a la reciente apreciacin del peso, hay dos factores que se deben considerar. Primero, existe una cada generalizada del dlar en los mercados financieros internacionales. Mientras en el transcurso del 2003 la apreciacin del peso chileno alcanza a un 13%, la apreciacin de varias otras monedas ha sido an mayor. Por ejemplo, en Canad y Nueva Zelandia ha sido en tomo a un 16% y en Australia y Sudfrica alcanza a una cifra cercana al 20%. Este hecho lleva a que la relacin peso/dlar se aprecie ms que la paridad del peso con otras monedas. En segundo lugar, est el fortalecimiento del peso que se expresa en el tipo de cambio multilateral, que incluye todos nuestros socios comerciales. Esta apreciacin obedece a mejores expectativas de crecimiento en los prximos aos, a una evolucin favorable de los trminos de intercambio, -a la disminucin del premio por riesgo que los inversionistas exigen a los ttulos chilenos y tambin a la mayor estabilidad en Amrica Latina. En este escenario es importante insistir en la diferente reaccin de la poltica monetaria ante los shocks de oferta y de demanda, aparte de que los efectos de las medidas de poltica monetaria en la inflacin toman varios trimestres en materializarse. Los desplazamientos en la demanda tienen efectos duraderos en la inflacin, por lo que deben ser enfrentados con cambios en la poltica monetaria. Por el contrario, los shocks de oferta son fenmenos transitorios, que normalmente estn acompaados de una mayor volatilidad en el corto plazo en la inflacin. En estas condiciones la accin del Banco Central se orienta a evitar que estos ltimos impactos se incorporen a las expectativas de inflacin, reafirmando su ancla nominal. La reduccin de los mrgenes y la baja en el tipo de cambio en el segundo semestre de este ao est produciendo una trayectoria de la inflacin por debajo de lo anticipado. Las actuales expectativas de inflacin del mercado, medidas a travs de las diferencias entre tasas de inters nominales y reales, tambin se han reducido. Este movimiento es coherente con la percepcin de los mercados financieros de que en el actual ciclo econmico ha existido un mayor espacio para mantener una posicin expansiva en la poltica monetaria por ms tiempo, an cuando a la vez se confirma el escenario de mejores perspectivas de crecimiento de la demanda agregada. En estas condiciones es importante reiterar que el Banco Central utiliza sus polticas con flexibilidad, de manera de confrontar las desviaciones ms duraderas, en cualquier direccin, entre la inflacin proyectada y la meta establecida. Conclusiones En sntesis, cuando se analiza la actual recuperacin de la actividad interna es importante sealar el papel de la economa internacional y tambin la credibilidad de las polticas macro, que permite aprovechar las oportunidades que ofrecen los mercados externos. El mejor aporte que puede hacer la poltica macro a esta recuperacin es mantener reglas de poltica estable. Las mismas reglas que nos estn permitiendo aprovechar el mejor escenario internacional. Estas reglas se expresan en el orden de las finanzas pblicas, la mantencin de una inflacin baja, la flotacin cambiara y la solvencia del sistema financiero.

Title: Notes: National asset liability management americas
text: NATIONAL ASSET LIABILITY MANAGEMENT AMERICAS VIRTUAL CONFERENCE, 14th September- 18th September, 2020 Panel discussion: How has this year changed central banks strategic and tactical asset allocation? Joaqu92n Vial, Deputy Governor Central Bank of Chile My main focus will be on the changes in Central Bank Balance in the last year, with some comments on some of the challenges ahead. This has been a very eventful year for Chile, and the Central Bank in particular. Since September last year we had to deal with three major shocks with large impact in our balance sheet: October - November 2019: Large social unrest accompanied by widespread violence and looting, with a breakdown in public order and security. After a month and a half of turmoil, a political agreement to start a process leading to a new Constitution restore order. This process will take 2 years, and the first step is a Referendum to approve or reject this process and to choose the type of political body that will produce the proposal. This will take place at the end of October. This was a domestic shock, causing a lot of uncertainty, leading to massive portfolio shifts, mostly from domestic assets to foreign assets. It caused large short-term liquidity problems in the FX market as well as in the short-term domestic market. The Central Bank intervened in the FX market announcing a large program to sell USD in the spot market, as well as in the NDF market. In parallel we launched a program to buy back the remainder of our own long- term domestic debt, as well as a more traditional REPO Program. These measures calmed the markets, with just a fraction of the resources committed being used. March 2020: COVIDfinancial turmoil in global markets impacted Chile, followed by domestic lockdowns causing a massive (but partial) shut down of economic activity, particularly in Services. This was a global shock causing a shift in asset allocation favoring short-term liquidity, both in peso and USD. The main concern at the Bank with respect to the pandemic, c1n addition to the smoothing of the portfolio shift, was to prevent a sudden stop in domestic credit by banks, so in coordination with actions by the government, we provided liquidity to banks to promote actual increases in commercial credit. The idea was to help bridge the financial gap caused by the temporary interruption of economic activities. - Provisi97n of Domestic Liquidity: Program of purchases of Bank Debt, in addition to our own. - Extensi97n of FX liquidity through NDF (very limited in fact) - New Credit facility to banks: 4 year loans at a fixed interest rate (0.5%, the MPR), conditional to previous increases in commercial loans (USD 20 b. in the first stage, a second stage is now being implemented) August 2020: Withdrawal of 10% of Pensi97n Funds savings (capped). Large domestic liquidity shock (6% of GDP to be withdrawn in two installments, by more than 6 million affiliates in a week time each). Domestic liquidity squeeze for AFPs and money market institutions, with an impact on asset prices and the FX market. Severe operational stress both for AFPs and the Banking System. - New program to buy Bank Bonds (at a discount) - Purchase of Bank deposits - Quasi repo open to all financial market institutions, using Bank Bonds (temporary purchase of bonds) aimed to provide short -term liquidity. Only a fraction was used, partially because AFPs anticipated part of the adjustment. After the CB announcement markets calmed and the transfer of funds went smoothly. Overall impacts on the Central Bank Balance: - Large increase in size - Domestic Assets (and short- term debt) play now a major part in our Balance - Got us closer to a positive Net Assets Position - In March we moved to a new benchmark for International Reserves, shortening duration The recession and fiscal transfers program to deal with its consequences also brought major changes in the Fiscal Position. Large d8eficits expected now in 2020 (10% of GDP) and 2021, followed by Fiscal consolidation afterwards, with gross Public Debt expected to stabilize ci97se to 50% of GDP in 2024. Part of the funding has come from withdrawals in Sovereign Funds. One last word about International Reserves: they have not changed that much: from USD 38.9 b. a year ago to USD 37.7 b. at the end of August. In the meantime we have gained access to special liquidity facilities: FCL (IMF): USD 23.9 B. (two years) Repo FIMA (Fed): Up to USD 60 b. (USD 17.5 b. now) PBOC Swap line: USD 7.1 b. (equivalent). Some challenges ahead: 1. Revisi97n of the size and composition of International Reserves will take place in the next couple of years. 2. The winding down of the FCIC and different asset purchases, as the economy recovers. 3. Operational challenges to be able to manage a very different set of assets in our Balance. 4. Criteria and indicators to use the new ability to purchase Treasury Bonds in the secondary market, to deal with financial stability problems. Title: Present and Future of Sustainable Finance in Chile
text: Present and Future of Sustainable Finance in Chile Joaqu92n Vial - Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile November 18, 2020 I am grateful for the invitation of the Franco-Chilean Chamber of Commerce, as well as the sponsors and sponsors of this important seminar, to address a few words at the closing. This morning I would like to share with you a brief reflection on the importance of climate change for the financial sector and the role of regulators and, in particular, the Central Bank of Chile in this matter. Before starting, I tell you how it is customary that this intervention does not necessarily represent the position of the Board of the Central Bank of Chile. First, there is already a consensus that climate change will have a profound impact on human activity and the economic system that sustains it. The economic effects will be sufficiently relevant to justify important public policies aimed at reducing their impact. Some of its effects are already beginning to be felt. The Paris Agreement encourages different jurisdictions to establish long-term emission commitments (NDCs, Nationally determined committees) to prevent the earth's temperature from exceeding an increase of 2or, from pre-industrial levels (ideally only rise 1.5a1C) by 2050. Even if that goal is achieved, there will be substantial changes in the climate, the environment, and therefore in the economy. Additionally, NDCs involve large actions and investments, both public and private, which in turn will have effects on the economy. The financial sector is no stranger to these effects on the economy. This is already being recognized and incorporated into their decisions, both by the private sector and by regulators. In this regard, I would like to highlight the leadership of the Banque de France, which has strongly promoted the establishment of the Central Banks and Supervisors NetWork for Greening the Financial System (NGFS). Climate change generates direct effects on activities that put at risk the value of certain assets, impacting both the assets of their owners and their creditors. Recent examples of climate-related phenomena are the economic effects of wildfires on real estate developments and electrical distribution in California. In Chile, climate change represents direct risks to agricultural activities, especially in the center and north of the country, forestry activities in the center of the country, port activities along the Pacific coast and, of course, for hydroelectric generation in the central zone and real estate developments in areas where water scarcity is already suffered. Mining, for its part, is already making substantial investments to adapt to a scenario of water scarcity. But those are not the only risks: there are also so-called "transition risks" that refer to the impact on the value of assets of climate change mitigation measures. An example of this could be the value of thermoelectric plants in a scenario of regulatory measures to meet the goals of the Paris Agreements. In Chile, we have that an important part of our exports are energy-intensive, both in production (mining, pulp, for example) and in transport (fruits, salmon). A tax on carbon emissions at source could have a very significant impact on their competitiveness. In Chile we are acting to incorporate these variables in the design of public policies, and this morning we have witnessed initiatives relevant adopted by the private world. The creation of the Green Finance Board by the Ministry of Finance, which gave rise to the Public-Private Green Agreement, among other products, generates an important space for discussion, coordination and knowledge. The CMF, for its part, has worked on regulatory improvement with a focus on sustainability, for example with the publication in consultation of the Modification of the Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Report (General Standard, NCG, No. 386i) and has recently 1 The proposal incorporates new information requirements, in order to provide stakeholders, particularly investors, with a complete, understandable and comprehensive and published its Strategy to Confront Climate Change in Financial Markets ( - article-29873.html). The Central Bank of Chile is working on the assessment of climate risks for financial stability. Particularly, in the generation of knowledge for the monitoring of these risks. Finally, I would also like to point out that in Chile the Central Bank has a mandate for the production and dissemination of macroeconomic and financial statistics, including the preparation of National Accounts. An important project is currently being developed, in collaboration with the Ministry of the Environment, to generate a system of economic information that allows connecting the National Accounts with the physical statistics of emissions at the level of the different productive entities. We believe that this will be a fundamental contribution to evaluate the economic impacts of the mitigation measures adopted in Chile and abroad, as well as to evaluate costs and Benefits of actions to adapt to the direct and indirect effects of climate change. Environmental conditions are changing fast and times to act are shortening dramatically. Financial activity, which unites future and present in the economic field, will have to adapt even faster than the rest of economic activities to these new realities. Title: Reflections on Preparation and Disclosure of Financial Information in Presentation of Financial Book Presentation...
text: Reflections on Preparation and Disclosure of Financial Information in Presentation of Specialty Book1 2 Enrique Marshall Director Central Bank of Chile May 2008 Submitting a financial ledger is a serious challenge for someone who is not a financial accounting professional. Accounting is full of details and technicalities that cannot be avoided. They are at the heart of this book and commenting on them is no easy task. The publication of such a text is certainly very timely. The issue of the preparation and disclosure of financial statements has acquired great relevance at the global level. As far as our country is concerned, it is in full transition to international accounting standards. On the other hand, Congress is currently debating a bill on corporate governance that, in several of its 1 Presentation made in the framework of the launch of the book "Analysis of Financial Statements: Text and Cases" by Professor Fernando Bravo at the Faculty of Economics and Business of the University of Chile on May 7, 2008. 2 I am grateful for the support given in the preparation of this document to Mr. Carlos Valdivieso of the Guillermo Subercaseaux Institute of Banking Studies and Mr. C8esar Caro of the Central Bank of Chile. However, the content of this document is the sole responsibility of the author and does not bind the Central Bank of Chile. articles, touch on these matters. The implications of all this for the accounting profession and for companies are very significant. The author of this book, Mr. Fernando Bravo Herrera, is a distinguished professional with extensive experience in the fields of business management, consulting and university chairs, which gives him an undeniable authority for the treatment of these issues. The text, which contains a good thematic index, is organized into 10 chapters, in which Professor Bravo presents all the elements that he considers relevant for the analysis of the information contained in the financial statements of the companies. All this is complemented by a good selection of cases applied to our reality. In this perspective, the book is a valuable contribution in an area where the bibliography in Spanish is not abundant. The method of presentation is clear and didactic, even in complex terrain, which is a merit of the author. Therefore, the book can be used to support teaching at different levels, and even among students from other disciplines. It may also be used by a wide range of people interested in financial analysis of companies and decision-making, such as directors and senior executives. of companies, investors, financial creditors, commercial suppliers, and supervisors. It seems to me that the first chapters provide the appropriate general framework within which these matters should be located. It presents and analyzes issues related to the environment in which financial information is produced, its usefulness to different stakeholders, accounting principles and the quality of financial statements. In the following chapters, which constitute the substantive part of the book, the author addresses a selection of relevant topics, such as monetary correction, current replacement costs, cash flow statements, analysis of financial statements, use of financial ratios, and corporate reorganization and bankruptcy. Considering my approach to these issues, which is very directly related to my experience as a banking supervisor, I have preferred not to comment in detail on these chapters and rather take the opportunity to share with you some reflections arising from the revision of this text, but fed mainly by this professional experience. In Chile, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions (SBIF) is the entity that, in addition to exercising the supervision of banks, sets the applicable accounting standards. First, the accounting profession is strained and subject to significant challenges. Corporate scandals in developed countries in recent years have eroded market confidence in financial information disclosed by companies. New questions have arisen in connection with the current international financial crisis, especially in relation to the valuation of structured products. The restoration of trust will necessarily take some time. In the meantime, it is appropriate to continue with actions aimed at strengthening the accounting profession and disseminating international standards and recommendations in many areas, including that of directors and senior executives of companies and institutions. In that perspective, this book constitutes a valuable contribution. Second, the issue of financial statements must be raised in a broader context, such as management and corporate governance. This is well recorded in this book. Accounting is no longer an "accountant's task". It is today an integral responsibility of companies and institutions and, therefore, of their executives or managers at a higher level. Financial information is the main means of Communication with the environment in which companies operate and, in particular, with the markets in which they are valued. The current view is that the reliability and validity of financial statements depends not only on the academic preparation or experience of the professionals directly involved in the accounting functions, but on a much broader set of factors, including: the functioning of the board of directors and the audit committee, internal control systems, the role of external auditors, conflict of interest resolution mechanisms, insider trading rules, the treatment of transactions with management or ownership parties, and the role of regulators and supervisors. The information that flows from companies with good corporate governance and good management systems is considered as lower risk and therefore these companies generally receive a better price in their debt or equity issues. Third, accounting and financial disclosure has gained increasing public interest. Lack of information and lack of transparency can adversely affect the functioning of markets and compromise the efficient allocation of resources. For companies listed on the stock exchange or issuing government bonds, the provision of financial information is a Sine qua non requirement for investors to make their decisions correctly. For banks the requirements are even greater because they receive deposits from the public and, additionally, have access to financing from the Central Bank. The lack of information or its opacity can compromise the stability and proper functioning of the banking system. The financial crisis of the eighties provided important lessons in this regard. Therefore, issuers of publicly offered securities and banks are subject to regulation and supervision in these matters. But the public interest doesn't end there. In my opinion, there is an undoubted social benefit if the standards and practices of transparency and disclosure of accounting and financial information also reach a wide universe of companies. The reason is that in an environment of sound accounting practices and transparency in the disclosure of financial statements, risks are reduced and the channeling of credit is facilitated. All this favors economic efficiency. When the information is unreliable, banks raise the risk premiums and therefore the interest rates applied to customers, or require the constitution of guarantees. Many good projects are probably left without access to financing. This is a familiar story in Chile and other emerging economies. The General Banking Law (LGB), collecting our own experience, took charge of at least part of this problem after the crisis of the eighties. Article 160 of that law criminalized and punished the provision of false or maliciously incomplete information on statements of position or assets, causing damage to the creditor financial institution. Years later, the SBIF, in an initiative developed jointly with ABIF, took another important step by actively promoting the adoption of a single and simplified model for the presentation of the financial statements of small and medium-sized enterprises, which is known as the FECU-SME 3 file. Recently, the SII has undertaken an initiative along the same lines. All this reflects a public interest in the promotion of accounting and financial standards in a wide universe of companies, even well beyond the group of issuers of publicly offered securities. Fourth, accounting standards and practices have become globalized. The space for national discretion has been significantly reduced. In our country, the issuers of accounting standards are the College of Accountants, which dictates standards 3 On the ECU-SME file see and . general, the Superintendency of Securities and Insurance (SVS) which has powers in the field of open companies and the SBIF which has custody over banks. Gradually, the country has been moving towards international standards. This is consistent with the process of trade and financial liberalization that has taken place in the country. The truth is that it is quite difficult to conceive of a process of economic and financial integration without the adoption of global standards. At present, all three accountant standard-setters are promoting convergence processes. The most advanced are the banks, which already have guidelines and a timeline for the transition set by SBIF. The full implementation of the new standards is committed for next year. Moreover, these institutions are already applying reasonable valuation principles for their financial investments and instruments. Derivatives. 4 The systematic processing of accounting information under IFRS5 could be facilitated by the adoption of a complementary standard such as XBRL6. This is a powerful tool for managing financial information in digital format. Knowledge of this standard in our environment is quite scarce. In October 4 The regulation, in force since 2005, is contained in Chapter 7-12 of the SBIF Updated Collection of Standards (available at ). 5 Acronym for International Financial Reporting Standards". 6 Acronym for eXtensible Business Reporting Language. Last year, the second international congress on the subject was held in Santiago and was sponsored by the financial supervisors of our country. It is therefore a development that must be analyzed with great interest. 7 Fifth, financial accounting faces the serious challenge of change and innovation, especially in the financial realm. Business and finance have undergone very significant changes over the course of the last few decades. Innovation in financial products and services has been enormous. The recent financial crisis has highlighted how much progress had been made in developing new instruments. We now note, with some degree of concern, that progress was faster than the assimilation capacity of markets. Few understood the nature and, above all, the risks of some highly complex structured products. The crisis has also highlighted the risk involved in the use of legal vehicles by banks or other financial institutions. All this seems to be under public scrutiny today and there are sure to be corrections going forward. However, the innovation process will continue with us because it brings benefits and, ultimately, is intrinsic to development. The point I wish to make is that the profession 7 See inauguration speech given by the Superintendent of Banks and Financial Institutions on the occasion of the II XBRL International Congress, held in Santiago, October 8, 2007 (available in ). Accountants cannot and should not lag behind these developments. It must be present, contribute its points of view and thus contribute to their taking place within a framework of prudence and balance. Sixth, transparency and disclosure of financial information are necessary complements to a good banking and financial supervision scheme. The accounting profession and supervisors have had disagreements over the years. In our country, one of them was experienced on the occasion of the banking crisis of the eighties. The balance sheets published by the banks shortly before the crisis reflected a picture that was far from reality, as was evident when the institutions were intervened. Subsequently, some tension arose over the rules issued by the SBIF to represent rescue operations, including portfolio sales to the Central Bank and subordinated obligation. These norms involved significant deviations from commonly accepted standards. Indeed, reading banks' balance sheets became extremely complex under that regulatory framework. Only experts could understand what the banks' status statements showed. In the early nineties, under the exchange rate band regime, a new debate arose, this time on the accounting representation of foreign currency positions, which fortunately was well resolved. But the issue that has generated the greatest tension between accountants and supervisors over time, both in Chile and in other countries, is that of portfolio provisions. On more than one occasion, the standards issued by supervisors have collided with widely accepted accounting criteria. This has arisen, in certain circumstances, from the difficulty of reconciling two equally important public objectives, such as, on the one hand, the stability of the banking system and the protection of depositors and, on the other, the interest of investors who require information that accurately reflects the situation and performance of companies. Fortunately, this is a story that has been overcome over time. Supervisors now recognize the importance of transparency and proper disclosure of financial information by banks and financial institutions in general. For now, they are users of this information and therefore require that it meets quality standards to efficiently fulfill their work. But there is an additional argument. The effectiveness of the The supervisory function increases significantly when it is accompanied by adequate market discipline, which necessarily requires transparency and correct disclosure of financial information by financial institutions. For all these reasons, the modern vision points to a complementarity and mutual reinforcement between those who work in the field of supervision and financial accounting. This view is endorsed by the Basel Committee on Effective Banking Supervision, which in one of its global principles or recommendations has stated that "supervisors should be satisfied that each bank maintains adequate records in accordance with internationally accepted accounting policies and practices and that it regularly publishes information that reasonably reflects its financial position and profitability." 8 At the domestic level, it should be noted that the SBIF has carried out a significant modernization of the rules on portfolio provisions in recent years, with which they have already achieved an adequate conformity with widely accepted accounting standards. The SBIF's decision to implement IFRS is also 8 BIS, "Core Principles for Effective Banking Supervision", October 2006 (available in ) A clear sign of commitment to harmonize the prospects of both professions. 9 Before concluding, I would like to set out two challenges that could be taken up in future editions of this book or in complementary publications. The first concerns models for predicting failures and bankruptcies. This is a topic of growing interest that could be deepened. The second challenge concerns IFRS. As is known, these should be applied in Chile from next year and of course this will have a significant effect on the way in which the financial statements of companies are prepared and presented. I believe it is necessary to address this issue in depth. Migration poses very important challenges for organizations, especially in the field of human resources. Along the same lines, it would also be of great interest to evaluate the possible adoption of the XBRL standard, which is gaining increasing acceptance worldwide for the management of financial information in digital format. 9 See Gustavo Arriagada, "Regulation and Supervision under IFRS" (available in ). Current portfolio provisioning regulations are available in Chapter 7-10 of the SBIF Updated Collection of Standards (available at ). I conclude by congratulating Professor Fernando Bravo for this excellent book, which constitutes a very valuable contribution to a better analysis of the financial statements of companies.

Considerando mi aproximacin a estos temas, que se relaciona muy directamente con mi experiencia como supervisor bancario, he preferido no entrar a comentar en detalle estos captulos y aprovechar ms bien la oportunidad para compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones surgidas de la revisin de este texto, pero alimentadas principalmente por dicha experiencia profesional. En Chile, la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras (SBIF) es la entidad que, junto con ejercer la supervisin de los bancos, fija las normas contables aplicables. Primero, la profesin contable se encuentra tensionada y sometida a importantes desafos. Los escndalos corporativos ocurridos en los pases desarrollados en los ltimos aos deterioraron la confianza de los mercados en la informacin financiera divulgada por las empresas. Nuevas preguntas han surgido con motivo de la actual crisis financiera internacional, especialmente en relacin con la valoracin de los productos estructurados. El restablecimiento de la confianza tomar necesariamente algn tiempo. Entretanto, lo que corresponde es proseguir con las acciones orientadas a fortalecer la profesin contable y a difundir los estndares y recomendaciones internacionales en mltiples mbitos, incluyendo al de los directores y ejecutivos superiores de las empresas e instituciones. En esa perspectiva, este libro constituye una valiosa contribucin. Segundo, el tema de los estados financieros debe ser planteado en un contexto ms amplio, como es el de la gestin y los gobiernos corporativos. Ello est bien recogido en este libro. La contabilidad dej de ser una tarea de contadores. Es hoy una responsabilidad integral de las empresas e instituciones y, por consiguiente, de sus ejecutivos o administradores de nivel superior. La informacin financiera es el principal medio de comunicacin con el entorno en el que las empresas se desenvuelven y, en particular, con los mercados en los cuales stas son valorizadas. La visin actual es que la confiabilidad y validez de los estados financieros depende no slo de la preparacin acadmica o la experiencia de los profesionales directamente involucrados en las funciones contables, sino que de un conjunto mucho ms amplio de factores, entre los que se pueden mencionar: el funcionamiento del directorio y el comit de auditora, los sistemas de control interno, el rol de los auditores externos, los mecanismos de solucin para los conflictos de inters, las normas sobre informacin privilegiada, el tratamiento de las operaciones con partes vinculadas a la gestin o la propiedad, y el rol de los reguladores y supervisores. La informacin que fluye de las empresas con buenos gobiernos corporativos y buenos sistemas de gestin es considerada como de menor riesgo y por ello dichas empresas reciben por lo general una mejor cotizacin en sus emisiones de deuda o capital. Tercero, la divulgacin contable y financiera ha adquirido un creciente inters pblico. La falta de informacin y la falta de transparencia pueden afectar negativamente el funcionamiento de los mercados y comprometer la eficiente asignacin de los recursos. Para las empresas que cotizan en bolsa o emiten ttulos de deuda pblica, la provisin de informacin financiera es un requisito sine qua non para que los inversionistas puedan tomar sus decisiones en forma correcta. Para los bancos los requisitos son an mayores porque reciben depsitos del pblico y, adicionalmente, tienen acceso al financiamiento del Banco Central. La falta de informacin o la opacidad de la misma pueden comprometer la estabilidad y el buen funcionamiento del sistema bancario. La crisis financiera de los aos ochenta aport importantes lecciones en ese sentido. Por ello, los emisores de ttulos de oferta pblica y los bancos estn sometidos a regulacin y supervisin en estas materias. Pero el inters pblico no termina ah. En mi opinin, existe un indudable beneficio social si los estndares y prcticas de transparencia y divulgacin de la informacin contable y financiera alcanzan tambin a un universo amplio de empresas. La razn es que en un ambiente de sanas prcticas contables y transparencia en la divulgacin de los estados financieros, los riesgos disminuyen y se facilita la canalizacin del crdito. Todo ello favorece la eficiencia econmica. Cuando la informacin es poco confiable, los bancos suben las primas de riesgo y por tanto las tasas de inters aplicadas a los clientes, o bien exigen la constitucin de garantas. Probablemente, muchos buenos proyectos quedan sin acceso al financiamiento. Esta es una historia conocida en Chile y en otras economas emergentes. La Ley General de Bancos (LGB), recogiendo nuestra propia experiencia, se hizo cargo por lo menos de una parte de este problema despus de la crisis de los ochenta. En efecto, el artculo 160 de dicho cuerpo legal procedi a tipificar y sancionar como delito el suministro de datos falsos o maliciosamente incompletos acerca de estados de situacin o patrimonio, ocasionando perjuicios a la institucin financiera acreedora.
