Aos ms tarde, la SBIF, en una iniciativa desarrollada en conjunto con la ABIF, dio otro paso importante al promover activamente la adopcin de un modelo nico y simplificado para la presentacin de los estados financieros de las pequeas y medianas empresas, que se conoce como la ficha FECU-PYME3. Recientemente, el SII ha emprendido una iniciativa en la misma lnea. Todo ello da cuenta de un inters pblico en la promocin de estndares contables y financieros en un universo amplio de empresas, incluso bastante ms all del grupo de los emisores de ttulos de oferta pblica. Cuarto, las normas y prcticas contables se han globalizado. El espacio para la discrecin nacional se ha reducido significativamente. En nuestro pas, los emisores de normas contables son el Colegio de Contadores, que dicta normas 3 Sobre la ficha FECU-PYME ver www.sbif.cl y www.abif.cl. generales, la Superintendencia de Valores y Seguros (SVS) que tiene atribuciones en el mbito de las sociedades abiertas y la SBIF que tiene tuicin sobre los bancos. Gradualmente, el pas ha ido avanzando hacia normas internacionales. Ello es concordante con el proceso de apertura comercial y financiera que ha tenido lugar en el pas. La verdad es que resulta bastante difcil concebir un proceso de integracin econmica y financiera sin la adopcin de estndares globales. En estos momentos, los tres emisores de normas contables estn promoviendo procesos de convergencia. Los ms avanzados son los bancos, que ya cuentan con directrices y un cronograma para la transicin dispuesto por SBIF. La aplicacin integral de las nuevas normas est comprometida para el prximo ao. Por lo dems, estas instituciones ya se encuentran aplicando principios de valoracin razonable para sus inversiones financieras e instrumentos derivados.4 El procesamiento sistemtico de la informacin contable bajo IFRS5 se podra facilitar con la adopcin de un estndar complementario como es el conocido con la sigla en ingls XBRL6. Este constituye una poderosa herramienta para el manejo de la informacin financiera en formato digital. El conocimiento de este estndar en nuestro medio es bastante escaso. En octubre 4 La normativa, vigente desde 2005, est contenida en el Captulo 7-12 de la Recopilacin Actualizada de Normas de la SBIF (disponible en www.sbif.cl). 5 Sigla en ingls para Internacional Financial Reporting Standards. 6 Sigla en ingls para eXtensible Business Reporting Language. pasado se realiz el segundo congreso internacional sobre la materia en Santiago y cont con el patrocinio de los supervisores financieros de nuestro pas. Se trata por tanto de un desarrollo que debe ser analizado con mucho inters.7 Quinto, la contabilidad financiera enfrenta el serio desafo del cambio y la innovacin, especialmente en el mbito financiero. Los negocios y las finanzas han experimentado cambios muy significativos en el curso de las ltimas dcadas. La innovacin en materia de productos y servicios financieros ha sido enorme. La reciente crisis financiera ha puesto de relieve cunto se haba avanzado en el desarrollo de nuevos instrumentos. Advertimos ahora, con algn grado de preocupacin, que los avances fueron ms rpido que la capacidad de asimilacin de los mercados. Pocos entendan la naturaleza y, sobre todo, los riesgos de algunos productos estructurados altamente complejos. La crisis tambin ha puesto de manifiesto el riesgo que conlleva la utilizacin de vehculos legales por parte de bancos u otras instituciones financieras. Todo ello parece hoy bajo escrutinio pblico y con seguridad se producirn correcciones hacia delante. Sin embargo, el proceso de innovacin seguir con nosotros porque conlleva beneficios y, en ltimo trmino, es consustancial al desarrollo. El punto que deseo destacar es que la profesin 7 Ver discurso de inauguracin pronunciado por el Superintendente de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras con motivo del II Congreso Internacional XBRL, celebrado en Santiago, 8 de Octubre de 2007 (disponible en www.sbif.cl). contable no puede ni debe permanecer a la zaga de estos desarrollos. Debe estar presente, aportar sus puntos de vista y contribuir as a que stos tengan lugar en un marco de prudencia y equilibrio. Sexto, la transparencia y la divulgacin de informacin financiera son complementos necesarios de un buen esquema de supervisin bancaria y financiera. La profesin contable y los supervisores han tenido desencuentros a lo largo de los aos. En nuestro pas, uno de ellos se vivi con motivo de la crisis bancaria de los aos ochenta. Los balances publicados por los bancos poco antes de crisis reflejaban un cuadro que distaba mucho de la realidad, cmo qued en evidencia cuando las instituciones fueron intervenidas. Posteriormente, cierta tensin surgi con motivo de las normas dictadas por la SBIF para representar las operaciones de rescate, incluidas las ventas de cartera al Banco Central y la obligacin subordinada. Estas normas implicaban desviaciones significativas respecto de estndares comnmente aceptados. A decir verdad, la lectura de los balances de los bancos se torn extremadamente compleja bajo ese marco normativo. Slo los expertos podan entender lo que mostraban los estados de situacin de los bancos. A principios de los noventa, bajo el rgimen de banda cambiaria, surgi un nuevo debate, sta vez sobre la representacin contable de las posiciones en moneda extranjera, que afortunadamente fue bien resuelto. Pero el tema que mayor tensin ha generado entre contadores y supervisores a lo largo del tiempo, tanto en Chile como en otros pases, es el referido a las provisiones de cartera. En ms de una ocasin, las normas impartidas por los supervisores han entrado en colisin con criterios contables ampliamente aceptados. Ello ha surgido, en determinadas circunstancias, por la dificultad de conciliar dos objetivos pblicos igualmente importantes, como son, por un lado, la estabilidad del sistema bancario y la proteccin de los depositantes y, por otro, el inters de los inversionistas que exigen contar con informacin que refleje fielmente la situacin y los resultados de las empresas. Afortunadamente, sta es una historia que se ha ido superando con el transcurso del tiempo. Los supervisores reconocen en la actualidad la importancia de la transparencia y la correcta divulgacin de informacin financiera por parte de los bancos y las instituciones financieras en general. Por de pronto, ellos son usuarios de dicha informacin y por tanto requieren que sta cumpla con estndares de calidad para cumplir eficientemente con su trabajo. Pero existe un argumento adicional. La eficacia de la funcin supervisora se acrecienta significativamente cuando se ve acompaada de una adecuada disciplina de mercado, que requiere necesariamente de transparencia y correcta divulgacin de informacin financiera por parte de las instituciones financieras. Por todo ello, la visin moderna apunta a una complementacin y reforzamiento mutuo entre quienes se desenvuelven en el mbito de la supervisin y en el de la contabilidad financiera. Esta visin est refrendada por el Comit de Basilea sobre Supervisin Bancaria Efectiva que en uno de sus principios o recomendaciones globales ha sealado que los supervisores deben tener constancia de que cada banco mantiene registros adecuados conforme a las polticas y prcticas contables ampliamente aceptadas internacionalmente y que publica con regularidad informacin que refleja razonablemente su situacin financiera y su rentabilidad.8 En el plano interno, cabe destacar que la SBIF ha realizado una significativa modernizacin de las normas sobre provisiones de cartera en los ltimos aos, con lo cual stas ya han alcanzado una adecuada concordancia con estndares contables ampliamente aceptados. La decisin de la SBIF de aplicar las IFRS es tambin 8 BIS, Principios Bsicos para una Supervisin Bancaria Eficaz, Octubre 2006 (disponible en www.bis.org) una clara seal de compromiso por armonizar las perspectivas de ambas profesiones.9 Antes de finalizar, quisiera dejar planteados dos desafos que podran ser asumidos en prximas ediciones de este libro o en publicaciones complementarias. El primero se refiere a los modelos de prediccin de fracasos y quiebras. Este es un tema de creciente inters que podra ser profundizado. El segundo desafo se refiere a las IFRS. Como se sabe, stas debern entrar en aplicacin en Chile a partir del prximo ao y por supuesto ello tendr un significativo efecto en la forma de preparacin y presentacin de los estados financieros de las empresas. Estimo necesario abordar este tema con profundidad. La migracin plantea retos muy importantes para las organizaciones, especialmente en el mbito de los recursos humanos. En esa misma lnea sera tambin de mucho inters evaluar la posible adopcin del estndar XBRL, que gana creciente aceptacin a nivel mundial para el manejo de informacin financiera en formato digital. 9 Ver Gustavo Arriagada, Regulacin y Supervisin bajo IFRS (disponible en www.sbif.cl). La normativa vigente de provisiones de cartera se encuentra disponible en el Captulo 7-10 de la Recopilacin Actualizada de Normas de la SBIF (disponible en www.sbif.cl). Concluyo felicitando al profesor Fernando Bravo por este excelente libro que constituye una muy valiosa contribucin para un mejor anlisis de los estados financieros de las empresas.

Title: Central Bank Policies in the Current Situation
text: CENTRAL BANK POLICIES IN THE CURRENT SITUATION Enrique Marshall R. I Counselor I Speech delivered during the celebration of the 71st Anniversary of the Confederation of Retail Trade and Tourism of Chile, Santiago, July 15, 2009. Central Bank of ChileJuly 15, 2009 I appreciate the invitation to share with you the Central Bank's vision on recent developments and prospects for the national economy and to comment on the policies we have adopted. After a severe contraction in the last quarter of 2008 and the first of this year, the world economy has tended to stabilize and global growth prospects have stopped deteriorating and even show improvements in the margin. In all this, the performance of emerging economies and, in particular, Asian economies, has been key. Notwithstanding the above, the enthusiasm generated in previous months, with demonstrations in the stock and commodity markets, has moderated significantly. The most recent developments in these markets reflect both the state of weakness and deterioration in which the world economy still finds itself and the greater degree of uncertainty regarding the speed at which it would recover. As we have pointed out on several occasions, an open economy such as ours could not remain immune to the effects of the deterioration in the global macroeconomic and financial scenario. Domestically, the effects of the global crisis have been felt particularly strongly in demand and activity, which experienced a significant drop in the fourth quarter of 2008 and a somewhat smaller adjustment in the first and second quarters of 2009. This sharp drop in activity has led us to observe quite negative annual variation figures for Imacec in recent months, even though activity, evaluated month by month, remains stable or with slight falls. As a result of these developments in domestic activity, slacks have widened, inflationary pressures have been reduced, and the risks of annual inflation remaining very low for a long time have increased. In this context, fiscal and monetary policies have reacted decisively, giving impetus to the economy. The measures have been unprecedented both in terms of their magnitude or scope and because of the speed with which they have proceeded. The most recent actions, I mean the ones we announced last week, have also added a stamp of originality. As far as the Central Bank is concerned, the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) has been cut by 7.75 percentage points over the past seven months, bringing it to 0.5% annually, the lowest level on record. Due to the aggressiveness of the downgrade and the level reached by the policy interest rate, Chile has been placed at the head of emerging economies in terms of monetary impulse. In addition, we have announced complementary measures to strengthen the effects of monetary policy on interest rates and financial asset prices. Below I will refer in more detail to the diagnosis that led us to make those decisions. On the external front, the activity and demand indicators for June have had mixed signs and some have been below market expectations, which has marked a difference from the news of April and May that surprised positively and fueled a certain degree of optimism. In most economies, business confidence has taken hold, although it remains in rather pessimistic territory. As far as consumers are concerned, confidence indicators are improving in most cases, but this is a less widespread trend. Meanwhile, the labour market continues to show weakness in much of the world. In line with a scenario of contraction in activity and low inflation, central banks that still have slack have continued to cut interest rates and several of them have also implemented unconventional actions. In general, the measures adopted by central banks have been coordinated and complemented by fiscal stimulus programs, constituting a differentiating element from what happened during the Great Depression. Tensions in international financial markets continue to dissipate. However, structural problems in financial systems in the developed world persist and, most likely, a return to normalcy will still take some time. The financial conditions faced by emerging economies, which improved steadily until June, partially reversed in the last month. Stock markets, after a strong recovery in previous months, have seen downward corrections in most recently. Sovereign and corporate risk awards tended to rise between June and July. Notwithstanding the above, investment flows continue to show a return of investors to emerging economies. Commodity prices, after showing significant increases through June this year, have adjusted downwards in recent weeks, in response to news of activity coming from developed economies. Movements in the prices of gasoline and corn that have fallen more than 20% since the first half of June stand out. Meanwhile, copper and oil prices have fallen from the levels they reached in mid-June, trading this week at US 2.3 a pound and around US 60 a barrel, respectively. On the domestic front, financial markets have been functioning quite normally, which differentiates us when compared to developed countries. However, the perception of greater risk has not been cleared and this has an impact both on the conditions under which loans are granted and on the demand exercised by households and companies. To the extent that uncertainty dissipates and customer confidence is restored, we should observe greater normality and dynamism in the behavior of credit aggregates. The TPM cut has been passed on to a significant extent to market rates. This is evident for both consumer and commercial credit, which have declined significantly from their levels at the end of 2008. However, the rates faced by customers remain relatively high, considering the cyclical position in which the economy finds itself. The measures taken by the central bank last week should revive the downward adjustment in market rates. The movements observed these days, mainly in the risk-free or funding rates of banks, allow us to harbor reasonable optimism in this regard. Long-term rates rose from March, matching the trajectory seen in developed economies and more dynamic activity in the local bond market. In the most recent, these rates have been corrected downwards, responding to the actions announced by the Central Bank. Despite the weakness shown by activity in the second quarter, the prospects for a recovery in the second half remain strong and well supported. Fiscal policy and monetary policy are doing their job. Business and household expectations have tended to improve. It is therefore expected, as part of the most likely scenario, that activity will begin to show an increase in levels, after adjusting for seasonality, during the course of this semester, although negative annual variations will continue to be observed for some months due to the sharp fall already registered. Partial consumption and investment indicators for May and June reinforce the prospects for a recovery in demand. Several of them show a positive trend break. Thus, for example, retail sales of usual and durable goods, sales of new cars, cement shipments, building permits and imports, after adjusting for seasonality, exhibit stable or increasing levels. The trajectory of inflation is below expectations. The monthly variation of last June was only the second with a positive sign in the year. With all this, the annual variation exceeded the lower limit of the tolerance range of the target of 3%. Annual inflation is expected to continue falling and even reach negative values in the latter part of the year. Cost pressures have also eased, especially due to the appreciation of the peso in recent weeks and a labor market that feels the effects of the economic cycle. The market, through the different measures of inflation expectations, also anticipates a scenario of low inflation in the coming months. In these circumstances, the Central Bank decided last week to reduce the monetary policy rate again, taking it to a record low of just 0.5%. We believe that this is the lowest level that can be reached without interfering with the normal functioning of money markets. But the Central Bank did not limit itself to that. At the same time, it reported that the TPM will remain at that level for an extended period of time. Having reached this minimum level does not mean that the Central Bank has run out of tools to continue giving impetus to the economy. We have instruments and, I can assure you, that we will use them if necessary. Without going very far, together with the recent reduction of the MPR, the adoption of complementary measures, involving the use of new instruments, to reinforce the effects of monetary policy was reported. Among these actions is the establishment of a liquidity facility for banks, which will operate with terms of 90 and 180 days and with a rate level similar to the TPM. This reinforces the message that the latter will remain at its current level for a long time and creates favourable conditions for market rates to continue to fall. The global macro-financial crisis has had a severe impact on every economy on the planet, with virtually no exceptions. In that sense, the differences between countries, referring to the strength and health of their respective economies, have not manifested themselves with all the force that could have been expected. However, these differences will be very relevant during the exit from this crisis. Chile, due to its solid fundamentals and the effects of its expansionary policies, should move towards an earlier recovery and on a more solid basis than other countries. According to our projections, which coincide with the results of surveys conducted among analysts, this recovery would be evident in the course of the second half of this year. The Central Bank will continue to use its policy instruments flexibly to bring projected inflation to 3% over the policy horizon. This is the best contribution it can make to overcome the current adverse macroeconomic picture and promote the growth of the economy in the medium and long term. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Polticas del Banco Central en la Coyuntura Actual Enrique Marshall R. Consejero Banco Central de Chile 15 de julio de 2009 Agradezco la invitacin para compartir con ustedes la visin del Banco Central sobre la evolucin reciente y las perspectivas de la economa nacional y comentar las polticas que hemos adoptado. Luego de una severa contraccin en el ltimo trimestre del 2008 y el primero de este ao, la economa mundial ha tendido a estabilizarse y las perspectivas de crecimiento global han dejado de deteriorarse e incluso muestran mejoras en el margen. En todo ello, el desempeo de las economas emergentes y, en particular de las economas asiticas, ha resultado clave. Sin perjuicio de lo anterior, el entusiasmo que se gener en meses anteriores, con manifestaciones en los mercados burstiles y de materias primas, se ha moderado en forma importante. La evolucin ms reciente de dichos mercados da cuenta tanto del estado de debilidad y deterioro en que an se encuentra la economa mundial como del mayor grado de incertidumbre respecto de la velocidad a la cual sta se recuperara. Como lo hemos sealado en varias oportunidades, una economa abierta como la nuestra no poda permanecer inmune a los efectos del deterioro en el escenario macroeconmico y financiero mundial. En el plano interno, los efectos de la crisis global se han sentido con especial fuerza en la demanda y la actividad, las que experimentaron una significativa cada en el cuarto trimestre del 2008 y un ajuste algo menor en el primer y segundo trimestres del 2009. Esta fuerte cada de la actividad nos ha llevado a observar cifras de variacin anual del Imacec bastante negativas en los ltimos meses, aun cuando la actividad, evaluada mes a mes, se mantenga estable o con cadas leves. Como resultado de esta evolucin de la actividad interna, se han ampliado las holguras, se han reducido las presiones inflacionarias y han aumentado los riesgos de que la inflacin anual permanezca muy baja por un tiempo prolongado. En este contexto, las polticas fiscal y monetaria han reaccionado con decisin, imprimindole impulso a la economa. Las medidas han sido inditas tanto por su magnitud o envergadura como por la rapidez con que se ha procedido. Las acciones ms recientes, me refiero a las que anunciamos la semana pasada, han agregado tambin un sello de originalidad. En lo que se refiere al Banco Central, la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria (TPM) se ha recortado en 7,75 puntos porcentuales en el curso de los ltimos siete meses, llevndola a 0,5% anual, el nivel ms bajo desde que se tienen registros. Por la agresividad de la rebaja y el nivel alcanzado por la tasa de inters de poltica, Chile se ha ubicado a la cabeza de las economas emergentes en lo que ha impulso monetario se refiere. Adems, hemos anunciado medidas complementarias de manera de reforzar los efectos de la poltica monetaria sobre las tasas de inters y los precios de los activos financieros. A continuacin me referir con mayor detalle al diagnstico que nos llev a tomar esas decisiones. En el frente externo, los indicadores de actividad y demanda para junio han tenido signos mixtos y algunos han estado por debajo de lo esperado por el mercado, lo que ha marcado una diferencia respecto de las noticias de abril y mayo que sorprendieron positivamente y alimentaron cierto grado de optimismo. En la mayora de las economas, la confianza empresarial se ha afianzado, si bien sta permanece an en territorio ms bien pesimista. En lo que se refiere a los consumidores, los indicadores de confianza, en la mayora de los casos, presentan mejora, pero sta es una tendencia menos generalizada. Por su parte, el mercado laboral contina mostrando debilidad en gran parte del mundo. Acorde con un panorama de contraccin de la actividad y baja inflacin, los bancos centrales que an disponen de holguras han seguido recortando las tasas de inters y varios de ellos, adems, han implementado acciones no convencionales. En general, las medidas adoptadas por los bancos centrales se han coordinado y complementado con los programas de estmulo fiscal, constituyndose en un elemento diferenciador respecto de lo sucedido durante la Gran Depresin. Las tensiones en los mercados financieros internacionales continan disipndose. Sin embargo, los problemas estructurales de los sistemas financieros en el mundo desarrollado persisten y, lo ms probable, es que el retomo a la normalidad tome todava algn tiempo. Las condiciones financieras enfrentadas por las economas emergentes, que mejoraron sostenidamente hasta junio, volvieron atrs parcialmente en el ltimo mes. Los mercados accionarios, despus de una fuerte recuperacin en meses anteriores, han experimentado correcciones a la baja en lo ms reciente. Por su parte, los premios por riesgo soberano y corporativo tendieron a subir entre junio y julio. No obstante lo anterior, los flujos de inversin continan evidenciando un retomo de los inversionistas a las economas emergentes. Los precios de las materias primas, despus de exhibir importantes incrementos hasta junio de este ao, se han ajustado a la baja en las ltimas semanas, en respuesta a las noticias de actividad provenientes de las economas desarrolladas. Se destacan los movimientos en los precios de la gasolina y el maz que han cado ms de 20% desde la primera quincena de junio. En tanto, los precios del cobre y el petrleo se han reducido desde los niveles que alcanzaron a mediados de junio, cotizndose esta semana en US$2,3 la libra y en tomo a US$60 el barril, respectivamente. En el frente interno, los mercados financieros han estado funcionando con bastante normalidad, lo que nos diferencia al compararnos con los pases desarrollados. Con todo, la percepcin de mayor riesgo no se ha despejado y ello tiene incidencia tanto sobre las condiciones a las que los crditos son otorgados como sobre la demanda ejercida por parte de los hogares y las empresas. En la medida que la incertidumbre se disipe y la confianza de los clientes se reestablezca deberamos observar mayor normalidad y dinamismo en el comportamiento de los agregados crediticios. El recorte de la TPM se ha traspasado en parte importante a las tasas de mercado. Esto es evidente tanto para los crditos de consumo como para los crditos comerciales, que han descendido en forma apreciable desde los niveles que alcanzaron a fines del 2008. Sin embargo, las tasas enfrentadas por los clientes siguen siendo relativamente altas, considerando la posicin cclica en que se encuentra la economa. Las medidas adoptadas por el Banco Central la semana pasada deberan reimpulsar el ajuste hacia abajo en las tasas de mercado. Los movimientos observados en estos das, principalmente en las tasas libres de riesgo o de fondeo de los bancos, permiten abrigar un razonable optimismo en tal sentido. Las tasas de largo plazo subieron a partir de marzo, lo que coincidi con la trayectoria observada en las economas desarrolladas y una actividad ms dinmica en el mercado local de bonos. En lo ms reciente, estas tasas se han corregido a la baja, respondiendo a las acciones anunciadas por el Banco Central. No obstante la debilidad mostrada por la actividad en el segundo trimestre, las perspectivas de una recuperacin en el segundo semestre se mantienen vigentes y estn bien sustentadas. La poltica fiscal y la poltica monetaria estn haciendo su trabajo. Las expectativas de empresas y hogares han tendido a mejorar. Se prev entonces, como parte del escenario ms probable, que la actividad comenzar a mostrar un incremento de niveles, previo ajuste por estacionalidad, en el curso del presente semestre, si bien se seguirn observando variaciones anuales negativas por algunos meses debido a la fuerte cada ya registrada. Indicadores parciales de consumo e inversin de mayo y junio refuerzan las perspectivas de recuperacin de la demanda. Varios de ellos muestran un positivo quiebre de tendencia. As, por ejemplo, las ventas minoristas de bienes habituales y durables, las ventas de automviles nuevos, los despachos de cemento, los permisos de edificacin y las importaciones, previo ajuste por estacionalidad, exhiben niveles estables o en aumento. La trayectoria de la inflacin se ubica por debajo de lo anticipado. La variacin mensual de junio pasado fue recin la segunda con signo positivo en el ao. Con todo ello, la variacin anual traspas el lmite inferior del rango de tolerancia de la meta del 3%. Se espera que la inflacin anual siga cayendo e incluso que alcance valores negativos en la ltima parte del ao. Las presiones de costos tambin se han reducido, especialmente por la apreciacin del peso en las ltimas semanas y un mercado laboral que siente los efectos del ciclo econmico. El mercado, a travs de las distintas medidas de expectativas de inflacin, tambin anticipa un escenario de inflacin baja en los prximos meses. En estas circunstancias, el Banco Central decidi la semana pasada reducir nuevamente la tasa de poltica monetaria, llevndola a un mnimo histrico de solo 0,5%. Consideramos que este es el nivel ms bajo al que se puede llegar sin interferir con el normal funcionamiento de los mercados monetarios. Pero el Banco Central no se limit a ello. Comunic, al mismo tiempo, que la TPM permanecer en dicho nivel por un tiempo prolongado. El haber alcanzado este nivel mnimo no significa que el Banco Central se haya quedado sin herramientas para seguir imprimindole impulso a la economa. Tenemos instrumentos y, puedo asegurarles, que los vamos a utilizar si fuese necesario. Sin ir muy lejos, junto con la reciente reduccin de la TPM, se inform la adopcin de medidas complementarias, que conllevan el uso de nuevos instrumentos, para reforzar los efectos de la poltica monetaria. Entre estas acciones est el establecimiento de una facilidad de liquidez para los bancos, que operar con plazos de 90 y 180 das y con un nivel de tasa similar a la TPM. Con ello se refuerza el mensaje de que esta ltima permanecer en su actual nivel por un tiempo prolongado y se generan condiciones favorables para que las tasas de mercado sigan reducindose. La crisis macro-financiera global ha tenido un severo impacto en todas las economas del planeta, prcticamente sin excepciones. En ese sentido, las diferencias entre pases, referidas a la fortaleza y la salud de sus respectivas economas, no se han manifestado con toda la fuerza que se podra haber esperado. Sin embargo, esas diferencias sern muy relevantes durante la salida de esta crisis. Chile, por sus slidos fundamentos y por los efectos de sus polticas expansivas, debiera avanzar hacia una recuperacin ms temprana y sobre bases ms slidas que otros pases. Segn nuestras proyecciones, que coinciden con los resultados de las encuestas realizadas entre analistas, esa recuperacin se hara evidente en el curso del segundo semestre de este ao. El Banco Central continuar usando sus instrumentos de poltica con flexibilidad para que la inflacin proyectada se ubique en 3% en el horizonte de poltica. Esta es la mejor contribucin que puede hacer para superar el actual cuadro macroeconmico adverso y promover el crecimiento de la economa en el mediano y largo plazo. Muchas gracias.

Title: Comments on the development of credit unions
text: Comments on the development of credit unions Enrique Marshall Member of the BoardCentral Bank of ChileOctober 2010 1. Introduction I appreciate the invitation of the Chilean Federation of Credit Unions to address you at this ceremony convened to celebrate the International Day of Credit Unions. Although I agree in a personal capacity and my comments will be expressed in those terms, I think it is important to remember that the Central Bank has an institutional relationship with this sector, which is little known but which is clearly stated in its Law. Organic. It states that the Issuing Institute will establish the regulations to which banking companies, financial societies and savings and credit cooperatives will be subject in the collection of funds from the public and in other matters indicated. Credit unions have come a long way in our country. It is worth mentioning that Fecrecoop was founded 56 years ago, when a large part of the population did not have access to banking and financial services. In all this time, the sector has advanced a lot, but it has not been exempt from avatars. This anniversary finds the credit union system in a very good position. First, because its quantitative and qualitative presence has acquired relevance and significance in the country. Secondly, because its activities have been able to benefit from an environment of financial stability, which is very conducive to its development. And third, because our economy, beyond the blows caused first by the global crisis and then by the earthquake and tsunami of last February, remains on very solid foundations and now accounts for a vigorous recovery. Let me elaborate briefly on these three points. 2. Role of Credit Unions The credit union sector plays an important role in the provision of financial services in our country. Its operations cover more than one million people and its Loans reach a sum of the order of 2,500 million Dollars. It is clear that these figures may seem small, compared to those of the banking system, but it should be borne in mind that their activities are focused on loans aimed at the segment of people or households. In consumer credit, for example, credit unions share order of 6%. Within the sector, entities of very different sizes coexist. There are large and small, but this should be seen more as a strength than a weakness, because it reflects the ability to respond under different conditions and circumstances. Beyond this quantitative dimension, there are several rather qualitative aspects about the presence of credit unions that should be highlighted. One that I think is important is its incursion into productive microcredit, which has enormous economic and social implications, but which registers a rather limited specialized offer. In our country, some banks have programs aimed at microenterprises, but most have preferred to channel their offer through the banking of people without greater specialization. Therefore, the participation of the Savings and credit cooperatives in this line of activity must be recognized, valued and encouraged. It should also be mentioned its significant presence throughout the country and, particularly, in regions. The proportion of branches located outside the Metropolitan Region is considerably higher, for example, than that of commercial banks. The offices of banks located outside the capital represent 54% of the total, while among savings cooperatives and credit and I refer in this case to those supervised by the SBIF, this percentage rises to 76%. Another aspect that should be highlighted is the balance in its benefits. Credit unions, unlike other financial service providers, are not limited to extending credit. They promote savings products at the same time. Needless to say, this balance favours development Healthy financial. The customers of a credit union are its main asset. Hence his permanent effort to take care of the quality of services provided and to avoid non-transparent business practices. Banking in the country has advanced considerably in recent years. New segments of the population have accessed financial services. However, as in almost all countries, banking has not occupied all spaces, among other reasons, due to restrictions or limitations arising from its business models, their commercial policies or the distribution channels used. These spaces have been occupied by non-bank providers, including credit unions . Without this, the coverage of financial services would be much lower than observed. This is a phenomenon that is observed in many countries, even in those where banking has gone far. In countries, such as the United States and Germany, for example, where banking systems show great development, financial activities motivated by cooperativism have at the same time a Very relevant presence. Along the same lines, it should be noted that savings and credit cooperatives, at least in our country, provide services preferably to middle and lower social sectors, which normally face greater restrictions on access to the banking system. 3. Financial environment I said at the beginning that the sector has benefited from a stable financial environment. To be fair, this has benefited not only credit unions but the financial system in its broadest sense and, ultimately, the country as a whole. Financial stability is a major public policy objective. If this had been blurred in some countries, by the Enthusiasm generated by long years of stability Macroeconomic and excessive reliance on market discipline, the recent financial crisis has been responsible for reaffirm it forcefully. The objectives of public action in favour of stability may be difficult to specify, but there is considerable agreement that the effort should be aimed primarily at strengthening the reaction capacity of the financial system as a whole and at minimising the effects of possible crisis situations on economic activity and employment. Financial stability depends on not one but multiple Factors. Therefore, to preserve it, there must be a comprehensive framework of financial institutions, policies and practices, including coordination and communication mechanisms between authorities. In Chile, concern for stability has been very present over the past two or three decades. The country has made significant efforts to preserve and strengthen its economic and financial institutions. This allowed the actual financial effects of the recent international crisis to be limited. Fiscal policy has maintained a clear seal of responsibility and, in recent years, has also taken the form of a policy rule based on the concept of structural balance, thereby making policy transparent, predictable and sustainable. For its part, monetary policy has been conducted autonomously and technical criteria, under a regime that explicitly states a goal of Inflation of 3% per year with a two-way policy horizon years. All this has made a positive contribution to the financial stability. Regulation and supervision have also been pillars Fundamental. The regulation was completely redesigned After the crisis of the eighties, acquiring a clear prudential orientation that is maintained to this day. Consistent with this, supervision has been modernised, leaving behind a rather formal approach and replacing it with one that pays increasing attention to governance and the management of audited institutions, with the purpose of inducing changes or rectifications when weaknesses or vulnerabilities are identified. Although it is a factor of another order, the development of the market of Capital, driven by the private pension system, has also made a positive contribution to stability, by making medium- and long-term sources of financing, previously non-existent, available to the market. This became clear at the end of the 2008, when financial markets tightened and Chilean companies were able to substitute external financing for Emissions in the domestic market under convenient terms and conditions. This general framework of institutions, policies and practices proved solid and robust to face the global crisis. Unlike what happened in previous crises, such as that of the eighties and the Asian crisis, the financial effects were limited and tensions were overcome promptly and without major shocks. In the period of greatest intensity, the Central Bank, responding to its mandate to preserve stability, took decisive action, including the preventive accumulation of international reserves in 2008 and then the provision of financing in pesos and dollars from September/October of that same year. These actions They made it possible to dissipate internal financial tensions and ensure the normal functioning of the financial system. The credit union sector has not been on the sidelines of this institution-building process. Over the past decade, several initiatives have been undertaken to improve its regulatory and supervisory framework. In 2003, after a long process in Congress, the new General Law on Cooperatives was enacted. As a result, the SBIF extended its audit action from two to five entities. For its part, the Central Bank, in exercise of its powers, introduced the corresponding regulatory adjustments. All this was done in concordance with what happened in other areas of financial activity. 4. Current macroeconomic scenario and outlook Although the financial effects of the crisis were limited, its impact on activity and employment was ultimately significant. This occurred almost everywhere in the world, regardless of the position of greater or lesser solidity in which each economy found itself. Chile was no exception. The crisis was transmitted through the fall in export prices and the general deterioration of expectations and confidence of economic agents, which were triggered at the end of 2008. As a result, the domestic economy contracted for several quarters. The most affected demand component Investment resulted, while the items or sectors of activity that received the greatest impact were construction and industry. From the second half of 2009, domestic activity began to recover vigorously and, in these circumstances, was hit by the earthquake last February. This had significant effects, but the economy, relatively quickly, regained the dynamism it brought. The latest monthly figures show an annualized expansion of activity of the order of 7 or 8%. Congruent with As a result, employment has shown appreciable growth, while unemployment has tended to fall. This significant recovery, with growth rates above the world average, has been supported by macroeconomic policies and, in particular, by the expansionary monetary policy implemented by the Central Bank. It has also responded to the efforts to repair the damage caused by the earthquake, which is expressed in the dynamic behavior of the investment. But beyond that, this recovery has been made possible by the strong fundamentals of our economy. It does not present the Current problems in economies developed: deterioration in fiscal accounts, high indebtedness public and private, and fragility of financial systems. The prospects ahead are promising. According to the According to the Central Bank's projections, growth would be between 5 and 5.5% this year and would be in the range of 5.5 to 6.5% next year. The latest known figures, consistent with these projections, reaffirm this robust growth of the economy. Inflation, after observing low records for several quarters, has returned to the tolerance range and everything indicates that it will remain at 3% in the coming months. However, in the most recent, its evolution has been somewhat below what previously expected. In this context, the Central Bank has gradually proceeded to normalize monetary policy, to ensure that inflation is around 3% over the projection horizon. At its meeting yesterday, the Issuing Institute raised the MPR by 25 basis points, leaving it at 2.75%. The normalization process will continue, but Its pace will depend on the evolution of conditions internal and external macroeconomic sectors. However, significant risks remain that must be monitored, especially for their implications for policy monetary. On the external front, the latest news has shaped a picture marked by weaker growth in developed economies and greater dynamism in developed economies. emerging economies. In this context, expectations have emerged that the central banks of developed countries will implement new unconventional measures to provide stimulus to their respective countries. Economies. This has led to the long-term interest rates of the main economies consolidating at very low levels and has simultaneously generated tensions in the exchange markets globally, causing a generalized depreciation of the dollar. Internally, there is a risk that activity will continue to speed up than expected. Another factor of concern is the appreciative trend in weight. If it persists, this would have implications for both activity and inflation, which must be evaluated with extreme attention. In any case, the Central Bank has reiterated that it will continue to use its policies flexibly so that projected inflation is 3% on the policy horizon. This is their best contribution to supporting the sustained growth of the economy. 5. Final comments As I said at the beginning, the credit union sector has acquired relevance and significance. In these Moments also finds a financial and economic environment conducive to its development and consolidation. This could be used to occupy new spaces and achieve higher levels of participation, comparable to those observed in other countries in the region. The recent financial crisis leaves lessons that must be learned by all. Emerging economies, although they were not at the origin of the problems, must take this opportunity to review their own realities and advance in the improvement of their financial systems. Chile has institutional arrangements for financial stability that have generally worked well in the course of the last decades. Proof of this is the strength that It can showcase the entire financial system today. But there are pending tasks and challenges. It is necessary to have an instance of coordination and communication of the highest level, whose focus is financial stability. It must also be strengthened institutionally to the entities in charge of supervision, in a context in which financial activities have become increasingly complex. Finally, it would be desirable for the Central Bank to have a more active participation in the definition of prudential regulation. While many problems detected in this crisis, such as the high level of leverage or the excessive dependence on Financing from wholesale markets, are a Both alien to credit unions, they must nevertheless make a careful reading of what has happened and identify subjects or aspects where there are opportunities to improvement or improvement. In this perspective, perhaps the most important challenge is to assume the changes that have been observed in financial activity and that will continue in the future, without departing from the principles of the cooperativism or the traditional way of relating to its partners and deploying its activities. To this I would add the permanent need to strengthen the governance and internal management of institutions, providing Special attention to information systems and risk management. Finally a task for the authorities. They must continue to make progress in improving regulation and Industry supervision. Thank you very much for your attention.
text_original: Comentarios sobre el desarrollo de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito Enrique Marshall Miembro del Consejo Banco Central de Chile Octubre 2010  Introduccin Agradezco la invitacin de la Federacin Chilena de Cooperativas de Ahorro y Crdito para dirigirme a ustedes en esta ceremonia convocada para celebrar el da internacional de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito. Si bien concurro a ttulo personal y mis comentarios sern expresados en esos trminos, me parece importante recordar que el Banco Central tiene una relacin institucional con este sector, que es poco conocida pero que est claramente consignada en su Ley Orgnica. En sta se seala que el Instituto Emisor fijar las regulaciones a que se sujetarn las empresas bancarias, sociedades financieras y cooperativas de ahorro y crdito en la captacin de fondos del pblico y en otras materias que indica. Las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito han recorrido un largo camino en nuestro pas. Valga mencionar que Fecrecoop se fund hace 56 aos, cuando gran parte de la poblacin no tena acceso a los servicios bancarios y financieros. En todo este tiempo, el sector ha avanzado mucho, pero no ha estado exento de avatares. Este aniversario encuentra al sistema de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito en una muy buena posicin. Primero, porque su presencia tanto cuantitativa como cualitativa ha adquirido relevancia y significacin en el pas. Segundo, porque sus actividades se han podido beneficiar de un ambiente de estabilidad financiera, muy propicio para su desarrollo. Y tercero, porque nuestra economa, ms all de los golpes ocasionados primero por la crisis global y luego por el terremoto y maremoto de febrero pasado, permanece sobre bases muy slidas y en estos momentos da cuenta de una vigorosa recuperacin. Permtanme elaborar brevemente sobre estos tres puntos.  Rol de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito El sector de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito cumple un rol importante en la prestacin de servicios financieros en nuestro pas. Sus operaciones cubren a ms de un milln de personas y sus prstamos alcanzan una suma del orden de 2.500 millones de dlares. Es claro que estos guarismos pueden parecer pequeos, comparados con los del sistema bancario, pero habra que tener en cuenta que sus actividades estn focalizadas en crditos orientados al segmento de personas u hogares. En los crditos de consumo, por ejemplo, las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito alcanzan una participacin del orden de 6%. Al interior del sector coexisten entidades de muy distintos tamaos. Las hay grandes y pequeas, pero ello debe ser visto ms como una fortaleza que como una debilidad, porque refleja la capacidad para brindar respuesta bajo distintas condiciones y circunstancias. Ms all de esta dimensin cuantitativa, existen varios aspectos ms bien cualitativos sobre la presencia de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito que deben ser destacados. Uno que me parece importante es su incursin en el microcrdito productivo, que tiene enormes implicancias econmicas y sociales, pero que registra una oferta especializada ms bien limitada. En nuestro pas, algunos bancos tienen programas orientados a las microempresas, pero la mayora ha preferido canalizar su oferta a travs de la banca de personas sin mayor especializacin. Por tanto, la participacin de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito en esta lnea de actividad debe ser reconocida, valorada y estimulada. Tambin habra que mencionar su significativa presencia a lo largo de todo el pas y, particularmente, en regiones. La proporcin de oficinas o sucursales ubicadas fuera de la Regin Metropolitana es bastante ms alta, por ejemplo, que la de los bancos comerciales. Las oficinas de los bancos ubicadas fuera de la capital representan el 54% del total, mientras que entre las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito y me refiero en este caso a las supervisadas por la SBIF, este porcentaje se eleva al 76%. Otro aspecto que debe ser destacado es el equilibrio en sus prestaciones. Las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito, a diferencia de otros proveedores de servicios financieros, no se limitan a otorgar crditos. Promueven al mismo tiempo los productos de ahorro. Dems est sealar que ese equilibrio favorece un desarrollo financiero sano. Los clientes de una cooperativa de ahorro y crdito son su principal activo. De all entonces su permanente esfuerzo por cuidar la calidad de los servicios prestados y por evitar prcticas comerciales poco transparentes. La bancarizacin en el pas ha avanzado en forma considerable en los ltimos aos. Nuevos segmentos de la poblacin han accedido a los servicios financieros. Sin embargo, como ocurre en casi todos los pases, la banca no ha ocupado todos los espacios, entre otras razones, por restricciones o limitaciones que se derivan de sus modelos de negocio, sus polticas comerciales o los canales de distribucin utilizados. Estos espacios han sido ocupados por proveedores no bancarios, entre los que se incluyen las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito. Sin ello, la cobertura de los servicios financieros sera mucho menor que la observada. Este es un fenmeno que se observa en numerosos pases, incluso en aquellos donde la bancarizacin ha llegado lejos. En pases, como Estados Unidos y Alemania, por ejemplo, donde los sistemas bancarios muestran un gran desarrollo, las actividades financieras motivadas por el cooperativismo tienen al mismo tiempo una presencia muy relevante. En esta misma lnea, habra que sealar que las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito, por lo menos en nuestro pas, prestan servicios preferentemente a sectores sociales medios y bajos, que enfrentan normalmente mayores restricciones de acceso al sistema bancario.  Entorno financiero Deca al comenzar que el sector se ha beneficiado de un entorno financiero estable. Para ser justos, ello ha favorecido no slo a las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito sino que al sistema financiero en su acepcin ms amplia y, en ltimo trmino al conjunto del pas. La estabilidad financiera es un objetivo de poltica pblica de primer orden. Si ello se haba desdibujado en algunos pases, por el entusiasmo generado por largos aos de estabilidad macroeconmica y una excesiva confianza en la disciplina de los mercados, la reciente crisis financiera se ha encargado de reafirmarlo con fuerza. Los objetivos de una accin pblica en pro de la estabilidad pueden resultar difciles de precisar, pero existe bastante coincidencia en que el esfuerzo debe estar orientado principalmente a fortalecer la capacidad de reaccin del sistema financiero en su conjunto y a minimizar los efectos de eventuales cuadros de crisis sobre la actividad econmica y el empleo. La estabilidad financiera depende no de uno sino de mltiples factores. Por ello para preservarla se debe contar con un marco comprensivo de instituciones, polticas y prcticas financieras, incluidos mecanismos de coordinacin y comunicacin entre las autoridades. En Chile, la preocupacin por la estabilidad ha estado muy presente en el curso de las ltimas dos o tres dcadas. El pas ha desplegado esfuerzos apreciables por preservar y fortalecer su institucionalidad econmica y financiera. Ello permiti que los efectos propiamente financieros de la reciente crisis internacional resultaran acotados. La poltica fiscal ha mantenido un claro sello de responsabilidad y, en los ltimos aos, ha adoptado adems la forma de una regla de poltica basada en el concepto de balance estructural, con lo cual la poltica se ha tornado transparente, predecible y sustentable. Por su parte, la poltica monetaria se ha conducido con autonoma y criterios tcnicos, bajo un rgimen que explcita una meta de inflacin del 3% anual con un horizonte de poltica en tomo a dos aos. Todo ello ha efectuado una positiva contribucin a la estabilidad financiera. La regulacin y la supervisin tambin han sido pilares fundamentales. La regulacin fue completamente rediseada despus de la crisis de los aos ochenta, adquiriendo una clara orientacin prudencial que se mantiene hasta nuestros das. Coherente con ello, la supervisin se ha modernizado, lo que implica dejar atrs un enfoque ms bien formal y reemplazarlo por uno que presta creciente atencin a la gobernanza y a la gestin de las instituciones fiscalizadas, con el propsito de inducir cambios o rectificaciones cuando se identifican debilidades o vulnerabilidades. Si bien es un factor de otro orden, el desarrollo del mercado de capitales, impulsado por el sistema privado de pensiones, ha hecho tambin un positivo aporte a la estabilidad, al poner a disposicin del mercado fuentes de financiamiento de mediano y largo plazo, anteriormente inexistente. Esto qued de manifiesto a fines del 2008, cuando los mercados financieros se tensionaron y las empresas chilenas pudieron sustituir financiamiento externo por emisiones en el mercado domstico bajo trminos y condiciones convenientes. Este marco general de instituciones, polticas y prcticas se mostr slido y robusto para enfrentar la crisis global. A diferencia de lo ocurrido en crisis anteriores, como la de los ochenta y la asitica, los efectos propiamente financieros resultaron acotados y las tensiones se superaron con prontitud y sin mayores sobresaltos. En el perodo de mayor intensidad, el Banco Central, respondiendo a su mandato de preservar la estabilidad, adopt acciones decididas, entre ellas, la acumulacin preventiva de reservas internacionales en 2008 y luego la provisin de financiamiento en pesos y dlares a partir en septiembre/octubre de ese mismo ao. Estas acciones permitieron disipar las tensiones financieras internas y asegurar el normal funcionamiento del sistema financiero. El sector de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito no ha estado al margen de este proceso de fortalecimiento institucional. En el curso de la ltima dcada, varias iniciativas han sido llevadas a cabo en orden a perfeccionar su marco de regulacin y supervisin. En 2003, despus de una larga tramitacin en el Congreso, se promulg la nueva Ley General de Cooperativas. Como resultado de ello, la SBIF extendi su accin fiscalizadora de dos a cinco entidades. Por su parte el Banco Central, en uso de sus facultades, introdujo los ajustes normativos que correspondan. Todo ello se hizo en concordancia con lo que ocurra en otros mbitos de la actividad financiera.  Escenario macroeconmico actual y perspectivas Si bien los efectos financieros de la crisis fueron acotados, sus repercusiones sobre la actividad y el empleo resultaron finalmente significativos. Ello ocurri en prcticamente todo el mundo, independientemente de la posicin de mayor o menor solidez en la que se encontraba cada economa. Chile no fue la excepcin. La crisis se transmiti a travs de la cada en los precios de las exportaciones y por el deterioro generalizado de las expectativas y la confianza de los agentes econmicos, los que se gatillaron a fines de 2008. Como resultado de todo ello, la economa interna se contrajo durante varios trimestres. El componente de la demanda ms afectado result la inversin, mientras que los rubros o sectores de actividad que recibieron el mayor impacto fueron la construccin y la industria. A partir del segundo semestre de 2009, la actividad interna comenz a recuperarse con vigor y, en esas circunstancias, se vio azotada por el terremoto de febrero pasado. Este tuvo efectos significativos, pero la economa, con relativa rapidez, recobr el dinamismo que traa. Las ltimas cifras mensuales dan cuenta de una expansin anualizada de la actividad del orden de 7 u 8%. Congruente con ello, el empleo ha mostrado un crecimiento apreciable, mientras el desempleo ha tendido a disminuir. Esta significativa recuperacin, con tasas de crecimiento que superan al promedio mundial, ha estado apoyada por las polticas macroeconmicas y, en particular, por la poltica monetaria expansiva implementada por el Banco Central. Tambin ha respondido a los esfuerzos de reparacin de los daos producidos por el terremoto, lo que se expresa en el comportamiento dinmico de la inversin. Pero, ms all de ello, esta recuperacin ha sido posible gracias a los slidos fundamentos de nuestra economa. Esta no presenta los problemas que se observan actualmente en las economas desarrolladas: deterioro en las cuentas fiscales, alto endeudamiento pblico y privado, y fragilidad de los sistemas financieros. Las perspectivas hacia delante son promisorias. Segn las proyecciones del Banco Central, el crecimiento se ubicara entre 5 y 5,5% este ao y estara en el rango del 5,5 al 6,5% el prximo. Las ltimas cifras conocidas, coherentes con estas proyecciones, reafirman este crecimiento robusto de la economa. La inflacin, despus de observar registros bajos durante varios trimestres, ha vuelto al rango de tolerancia y todo indica que permanecer en tomo a 3% en los prximos meses. Sin embargo, en lo ms reciente, su evolucin ha estado algo por debajo de lo esperado con anterioridad. En este contexto, el Banco Central ha procedido, con gradualidad, a normalizar la poltica monetaria, para asegurar que la inflacin est en tomo a 3% en el horizonte de proyeccin. En su reunin del da de ayer, el Instituto Emisor subi la TPM en 25 puntos base, dejndola en 2,75%. El proceso de normalizacin continuar, pero su ritmo depender de la evolucin de las condiciones macroeconmicas internas y externas. Sin embargo, persisten riesgos significativos que deben ser monitoreados, sobre todo por sus implicancias para la poltica monetaria. En el mbito externo, las noticias ms recientes han ido configurando un panorama marcado por un crecimiento ms dbil en las economas desarrolladas y un mayor dinamismo en las economas emergentes. En este contexto, han surgido expectativas de que los bancos centrales de los pases desarrollados implementarn nuevas medidas no convencionales para brindar estmulo a sus respectivas economas. Esto ha llevado a que las tasas de inters de largo plazo de las principales economas se consoliden en niveles muy bajos y simultneamente ha generado tensiones en los mercados cambiarlos a nivel global, provocando una depreciacin generalizada del dlar. En el mbito interno, existe el riesgo de que la actividad mantenga una velocidad mayor que la prevista. Otro factor que despierta preocupacin es la tendencia apreciativa del peso. De persistir, ello tendra implicancias tanto para la actividad como para la inflacin, que deben ser evaluadas con extrema atencin. En todo caso, el Banco Central ha reiterado que seguir usando sus polticas con flexibilidad para que la inflacin proyectada se ubique en 3% en el horizonte de poltica. Esta es su mejor contribucin para apoyar el crecimiento sostenido de la economa.  Comentarios finales Como deca en un comienzo, el sector de las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito ha adquirido relevancia y significacin. En estos momentos encuentra, adems, un entorno financiero y econmico propicio para su desarrollo y consolidacin. Esto podra ser aprovechado para ocupar nuevos espacios y alcanzar niveles de participacin ms altos, comparables con los observados en otros pases de la regin. La reciente crisis financiera deja lecciones que deben ser aprendidas por todos. Las economas emergentes, si bien no estuvieron en el origen de los problemas, deben aprovechar esta oportunidad para revisar sus propias realidades y avanzar en el perfeccionamiento de sus sistemas financieros. Chile cuenta con arreglos institucionales en materia de estabilidad financiera que en trminos generales han funcionado bien en el curso de las ltimas dcadas. Prueba de ello es la fortaleza que puede exhibir hoy el conjunto del sistema financiero. Pero existen tareas pendientes y desafos. Se requiere contar con una instancia de coordinacin y comunicacin del ms alto nivel, cuyo foco sea la estabilidad financiera. Tambin se debe fortalecer institucionalmente a las entidades encargadas de la supervisin, en un contexto en el cual las actividades financieras han adquirido creciente complejidad. Por ltimo, sera conveniente que el Banco Central contara con una participacin ms activa en la definicin de la regulacin prudencial Si bien muchos problemas detectados en esta crisis, como el elevado nivel de apalancamiento o la excesiva dependencia del financiamiento proveniente de los mercados mayoristas, son un tanto ajenos a las cooperativas de ahorro y crdito, de todos modos stas deben hacer una lectura cuidadosa de lo acontecido e identificar materias o aspectos donde existen oportunidades de mejora o perfeccionamiento. En esa perspectiva, quiz el desafio ms importante es asumir los cambios que se han observado en la actividad financiera y que continuarn en el futuro, sin apartarse de los principios del cooperativismo ni de la forma tradicional de relacionarse con sus socios y desplegar sus actividades. A ello agregara la permanente necesidad de fortalecer la gobemanza y la gestin interna de las instituciones, prestando especial atencin a los sistemas de informacin y al manejo de los riesgos. Finalmente una tarea para las autoridades. Estas deben seguir avanzando en el perfeccionamiento de la regulacin y supervisin del sector. Muchas gracias por su atencin.

Title: Financial Inclusion: Progress and Challenges for Chile
text: Financial Inclusion: Progress and Challenges for Chile1 Enrique Marshall Member of the Board of the Central Bank of Chile April 2011 1 Presentation made at the inauguration of the academic year of the Business School of the Universidad Vi96a del Mar, on April 1, 2011. Introduction Three or four decades ago, the banking system served a small fraction of the population. It certainly catered to larger firms and higher-income segments of individuals or households. But many businesses and individuals lacked access to the system. Banking and financial activity had a certain stamp of exclusivity. This picture has changed in the course of recent decades. The financial industry has made efforts to reach new segments of the population. This has been facilitated by the very development of the economy and the consequent increase in people's incomes. The truth, in any case, is that progress in terms of access to services has been enormous, especially if you evaluate them in perspective. However, in this area, the country has not yet completed its task and there are significant gaps to close. I would like to take this opportunity to share with you some reflections on financial inclusion and, particularly, on its scope and implications for our country. Contents, scope and implications of financial inclusion The concept of financial inclusion has gained traction in recent years. Many countries are promoting programmes along these lines. The G20 has recently incorporated this theme into its deliberations. Some speak of banking, others of micro-credit or more broadly of micro-finance, others of retail banking or consumer banking. They are similar concepts that to some extent overlap, but inclusion seems to me the most comprehensive and the most useful for the design of public policies. Exclusion or inclusion, as you prefer to posit, admits degrees or nuances. There are, on the one hand, those who have access without major limitations, under reasonable terms and conditions. There are, on the other, those who completely lack formal financial services. But in between are those who have partial, incomplete or not entirely satisfactory access. Financial inclusion is primarily about providing access to the voiceless, but it also refers to improving or improving access for those who are still halfway there. Financial inclusion is a concept of almost universal application. In all countries, even the most advanced, there are gaps to close. Undoubtedly, the challenges vary from one country to another, depending among other elements on the level of development achieved. It is not the same to talk about financial inclusion in the United States than to do it in Chile, South Africa or Bangladesh. In advanced economies, the segments without access to services are generally reduced to the extremely poor or to narrow groups such as immigrants who lack documentation or credit history. In emerging economies, on the other hand, the tasks are more far-reaching and profound because there is still a significant fraction of the population partially or totally excluded from benefits. More than one could argue about the desirability of considering financial inclusion goals in very low-income countries or for extremely poor population groups. The argument would be that, in these circumstances, efforts should be aimed at meeting the basic needs of food, shelter and health and therefore, that financial services are not a priority for public policies. An excellent book entitled "The portfolios of the Poor" published in 2009 showed that this is a wrong view. 2 The authors of this publication report, after a very thorough field study, that the financial practices of the poor, despite the narrowness of their resources, are much more intense, sophisticated and varied than is normally assumed. Their financial activities arise as a result of the conditions they face. The range of instruments used is wide and decisions taken are based on risk, foresight and safety considerations, as is the case in advanced financial markets. The challenge for public policies, according to this work, is to create the conditions for the poor to also have formal providers. Financial inclusion should not be associated with social assistance goals or policies. It certainly has social implications, but its economic benefits are also evident. Financial services expand households' savings and consumption possibilities. They allow a better productive insertion of people. They lead to better use of entrepreneurial talents and productive investment opportunities among those who manage to emerge from exclusion. For banks, financial inclusion represents a business opportunity, because it means expanding their customer base and their activity volumes. Economic development will automatically bring progress on inclusion, but it is well worth taking the initiative and getting ahead of the curve. Investing in the customers of tomorrow can be very profitable if the evaluation is made with a medium or long-term horizon. 2 Portfolios of the Poors, How the Worldabs Poor Live on 2 a Day. Collins, D.; Morduch, J.; Rutherford, S.; Ruthven, O. Princeton University Press, 2009. To this should be added the positive effect on financial stability. Inclusion leads to a broadening of the depository and savings base in the financial system, which strengthens the stability of institutions and the system as a whole. One of the lessons of the financial crisis of recent years is that banks must rely more on small depositors than on large or very large depositors. The former are usually relatively stable, while the latter tend to move very easily from one institution to another or from one country to another, which gives the system a certain vulnerability. Financial inclusion must rest on solid foundations so that it generates the expected positive effects. For now, this means having a well-established culture of responsibility. On the side of suppliers, this must translate into good business practices, a lot of transparency and, above all, in an adequate containment of excesses. The worst of them all is people's over-indebtedness. Credit is a very good instrument, but poorly applied it can generate a lot of damage. When these excesses multiply, conditions are created for the emergence of a financial crisis. Responsibility must also be present among customers. In this perspective, a fundamental element is financial education, which is not reduced as some may believe to the simple delivery of information about the products and services offered and their rates. All this is very necessary, but financial education must go further. It is a task that must begin in schools and continue in universities. It is therefore a joint task for the educational and financial authorities. Its ultimate goal should be to promote behaviors of financial responsibility in the population. Another key point is that efforts should be aimed at providing not only micro-credit or consumer credit, but a balanced set of products and services that meet the needs in terms of savings, payments, financing and insurance. During Microcredit was once thought to be a magical tool for alleviating poverty and promoting development, but this vision has been left behind. Recent events in Bangladesh and India have generated a very intense public debate on microfinance and have raised the need for a new approach to the subject. 3 In the past, the first step in the financial life of Chileans was to open a savings account. Some of that is missed. In most countries, technology has been and will continue to be an important ally of financial inclusion. Tremendous progress in computing and communications has revolutionized performance and reduced costs. All this has facilitated the massification of services, especially in emerging economies. On the other hand, new risk assessment technologies, such as credit scoring and other similar methodologies, have made credit policies more flexible. The traditional criteria based on collateral, guarantees and equity have opened the way to criteria based on the expected behavior of customers, which facilitates the incorporation into the services of new segments of the population. Innovation has led at the same time to the emergence of non-bank institutions providing financial services. This has been key to facilitating the process of inclusion, especially in mid-stage developing economies. For commercial or regulatory reasons, banks temporarily leave spaces unfilled. This opens up the possibility of alternative providers such as credit unions and commercial houses. Recognising the positive contribution of these entities, financial inclusion should be geared towards making banks a viable option for a growing fraction of the population. 3 The criticisms that have arisen refer, on the one hand, to the excesses in trade policies (aggressiveness in the granting of credit, over-indebtedness of people, abuses in collection, and application of high interest rates); and on the other, to the low effectiveness of programs to overcome poverty and promote the development of people and their communities. Banking and financial activities are subject to regulation and supervision for considerations related mainly to financial stability and consumer protection. In addition, institutions are normally subject to relatively high management standards and business practices. All this can have implications for financial inclusion and give rise to conflicts between different objectives. "Know-your-customer" rules and policies, for example, may limit the possibility of covering immigrants since they typically lack a background for proper identification. The policy of setting a limit on interest charges also poses a complex dilemma. On the one hand, it provides protection to consumers, but on the other it can restrict access. This and other regulations should be carefully evaluated by the authorities in order to reduce their potential adverse effects. Achievements and progress in Chile Chile can exhibit very remarkable achievements and advances in financial inclusion in recent decades, without prejudice to recognizing pending tasks and challenges. In the banking field, several of its products and services have reached a high degree of penetration in the population. First of all, savings accounts that have had very broad coverage for a long time stand out. Currently, the number of accounts exceeds 13 million. Next, the instrument that has gained a lot of ground in recent years is the debit card, associated in most cases with a view account without checks. The current account, which is the most traditional service of banks, has not achieved the same degree of penetration and shows a rather gradual evolution over time. This is mainly explained by its administrative costs and, in particular, by those involved in the Check Processing. The bank account operated exclusively with debit card, which works like an electronic checkbook, is a similar instrument but with much lower costs. This has allowed its massification in a relatively short period of time. As for credit operations, they have expanded significantly. The total number of customers with loans in force in the banking system is around 3.6 million, a figure that alone suggests a significant degree of massification of benefits. Of this universe, just over 700 thousand are commercial customers; and 2.8 million are natural persons with consumer or housing credits. These are undoubtedly significant figures, but they show a degree of penetration somewhat lower than that observed in savings and payment instruments. This suggests that the banking system has faced certain limitations or restrictions in advancing in the field of credit. The massification of benefits has gone hand in hand with a significant expansion and modernization of financial infrastructure. The network of bank branches has grown and ATMs have multiplied. Along with this, the distribution of the latter throughout the country and within urban centers has improved significantly. Additionally, electronic banking has penetrated strongly. Thus, banking transactions materialized through checks have been significantly replaced by operations perfected through modern technology-intensive means. This has made it possible to move transactions out of bank branches, reduce costs and improve security standards. Financial inclusion, raised as banking, is an issue that has increasingly aroused the interest of banks. The trade association that brings them together has explicitly defined a banking program. This has made it possible to expand the number of establishments affiliated to bank credit card systems and to diversify their geographical coverage. At the same time, efforts have been made to improve the conditions offered to these countries. establishments, including a gradual reduction in the commissions charged. Along the same lines is the joint initiative of authorities, banks and commerce that reduced the retention period of checks from other places. 4 In addition, several institutions have deployed their own initiatives. Among them, we should highlight the micro-credit programs maintained by several banks and the program that seeks to reach remote places in the national territory by transforming a commercial establishment into a virtual bank box. 5 The space left by the banking industry, particularly in the realm of credit, has been filled by non-bank providers. Those that have gone further in this regard are the credit card systems of commercial houses. These provide a payment and credit instrument that, in most cases, allows transactions not only in merchants related to the issuer, but also in other affiliated establishments. It is therefore a product quite similar to that provided by banks. The figures shown by these non-bank issuers are quite significant. According to SBIF records, as of last December, the audited systems registered just over 16 million valid cards and about 6 million cards with operations. These are figures that exceed those exhibited by the banking industry. Savings and credit unions and compensation funds are added as service providers to commercial houses. The former register operations with more than one million people and the latter report around 2 million social credits. Further back should be other unregulated microcredit providers, many of which operate under the umbrella of foundations or non-governmental organizations, with a focus on combating poverty. The relative importance of all non-bank providers has become quite significant. At present, they explain 4 The SBIF issued a circular on the subject in May 2001. 5 State Bank program known as "Caja Vecina". Just under 50% of the amount in pesos of consumer loans granted. But perhaps its relevance is more clearly seen when considering the percentage of the population that is covered by these providers. According to the Central Bank's 2007 household financial survey, 64 per cent of households registered consumer credit from various sources, but only 24 per cent had operations with banks. The difference was covered by non-banking institutions, particularly commercial houses. When disaggregating the figures by income stratum, it is observed that the presence of non-bank suppliers and, particularly, of commercial houses is quite similar in all of them, while banking services tend to be concentrated in the highest strata. Regulators and supervisors, attentive to these developments, have introduced flexibilizations aimed at facilitating access to services. Along these lines, mention should be made of the elimination of the tax on transactions and checks (2008), the reduction of the stamp tax (2010), the gradual expansion of the number of tranches for the application of the maximum interest rate (several dates), the reform of the General Law on Cooperatives (2003), and numerous actions aimed at improving consumer protection. In an area related to financial education, we should highlight the educational program implemented by the SBIF through the portal, the "closer economy" program of the Central Bank, and a very recent initiative of the superintendencies of the financial sector whose objective is to serve citizens, promote financial culture and provide tools for decision-making.
