Title: Meeting of Central Bank Treasurers
text: Central Bank Treasurers Meeting1 Inaugural AddressDelivered by Enrique Marshall Vice-president Central Bank of ChileOctober 6, 2014 1 Inaugural speech delivered by Enrique Marshall, Vice President of the Central Bank of Chile, on the occasion of the Twelfth Meeting of Central Bank Treasurers, organized by CEMLA and the Central Bank of Chile, and held in Santiago, Chile between the days 6 and 8 October 2014. Good morning to everyone present. I would like to extend a warm welcome to our foreign guests. I hope you have an excellent stay in our country. On behalf of the President of the Central Bank of Chile and his Council, I am very pleased to inaugurate the Twelfth Meeting of Central Bank Treasurers, attended by representatives from Latin America and the Caribbean and special guests from Europe, North America and Asia. This is an activity organized jointly by CEMLA and the Central Bank of Chile. A recognition then goes to our co-organizer in the person of its Manager of Programs and Technical Meetings of Central Bank, Fernando S87nchez Cuadros, whose support and collaboration for the preparation of this meeting has been extremely valuable. A recognition also for the staff of the Central Bank of Chile, headed by our General Manager and the Treasury Manager, who worked hard to make all this possible. During the next three days, you, treasurers of the Central Bank of Latin America, will be gathered to analyze the matters that focus your attention today and the challenges you envision for the future. I would like to take this opportunity to share with you some reflections on this issuance and cash or treasury function that places central banks in such a direct and tangible relationship with citizens in general. It is difficult to visualize the functioning of an economy without the presence of notes and coins. Cash facilitates millions of transactions that are carried out every day and, in addition, it is usually a national symbol and therefore a letter of introduction for those who visit us in our respective countries. Our task as central bankers is to guarantee the liquidity of the financial system and preserve the normal functioning of the means of payment, including cash. This is a task that attracts the highest public interest and whose full fulfilment requires maintaining very high the trust that has been placed in us. Providing working capital to economic systems is essential to ensure widespread access to transactions, to facilitate many financial operations and, in general, to support economic activities. The exclusive power to issue held by our central banks is one of the powers or attributions set forth in our organic statutes and that we must exercise with extreme diligence. This legal mandate results in such important tasks as the efficient management of the cash cycle, and the timely response to contingencies of varied origins, including natural disasters, which can cause unwanted interruptions in the supply of working capital. In this context, the function of identifying and withdrawing counterfeits is also considered, which is key to maintaining public confidence and, ultimately, to preserving the integrity and stability of the payment system. In this perspective, it is essential that our analysis units permanently have a good diagnosis from which recommendations are made in order to prevent or mitigate the problem of counterfeiting. This implies, in any case, close cooperation with other public institutions involved in the formulation of preventive policies, in the approval of legal or regulatory provisions related to these matters, or in the investigation of those who commit crimes. All these issues will be at the centre of your deliberations in the course of these days. I would add to the list of subjects of high interest and topicality the technological advances in printing and minting with all their practical implications for our work, the experiences that have taken place in the region in terms of launching new banknotes and the lessons that arise from these processes, and the issues related to the care and conservation of cash that are always among your concerns. In Chile, in recent years, we made a complete change in the family of banknotes in circulation. We acquired an experience that we are happy to share with our colleagues from other countries. In the field of currencies, however, we have a project in the making, so it would be extremely useful for us to learn about other recent experiences. This type of exchange is very valuable in the context of these meetings. Banknotes and coins are symbolic expressions of each of our countries. They incorporate in their designs essential contents of who we are and our cultural background. Heroes, politicians, poets, saints, landscapes and anniversaries, are included in them to remind us of the stamp and identity of our peoples. Everyone knows that our banknotes respond to a very careful work of professionals and technicians who seek to reconcile various criteria, such as design, safety, functionality, durability and production costs. The task of the treasurers is to achieve a proper balance between all of them, which is not always easy. An undeniable fact of these times is the emergence of new means of payment, alternative to cash. Among them are plastic money and electronic media, which as we know have gained ground. However, evidence from our region and other developed economies shows that demand for banknotes and coins has continued to grow, even in some cases at fairly high rates. This reaffirms the basic function of central banks providing working capital. On the other hand, our institutions must remain attentive to factors or variables that may induce sudden or unexpected changes in the demand for cash, such as economic cycles or adjustments in the prices of certain services of mass use. Our research units should consider as part of their activities the formulation of scenarios that account for these potential changes. To this is added the need to consider variations in the prices of raw materials, such as those known in recent years, the introduction of new format or substrate options for banknotes, and possible changes in the preferences of citizens. All this highlights the wide spectrum of subjects that we must process within the framework of our tasks. In an operational area, an increasingly important task is the development and implementation of new facilities for the manufacture, storage, processing and distribution of cash. This is particularly relevant for those central banks that continue to operate in somewhat old buildings, designed to process much smaller volumes of working capital than today. We must bear in mind that decisions regarding installations take time and involve a long process of preparation prior to and then execution, so acting in advance is essential. Also in an operational area, central banks need to pay due attention to companies, other than banks, that have begun to play relevant roles in the cash cycle, such as securities carriers. It is desirable to establish precisely in which activities they may be involved, and to define or refine the regulatory frameworks governing them. Along the same lines, the issue of recycling of banknote waste appears. It is of great interest to know the experiences of central banks that are at the forefront of these issues. With these reflections I have sought to highlight the importance of the activities carried out by central banks in the field of the provision of working capital. This results in the need to ensure a permanent strengthening of our internal capacities and the human teams that deploy them. Meetings of this kind, which promote the exchange of knowledge and experience among those who perform tasks in this field, are extremely useful. I wish for the success of these days. I hope that they will be very fruitful for all and that their objectives will be fully achieved. I confess that we have deployed our best efforts so that everything goes well and so that our foreign visitors have a very good stay in our country. Thanks a lot.
text_original: Reunin de Tesoreros de Banca Central1 Discurso Inaugural Pronunciado por Enrique Marshall Vicepresidente Banco Central de Chile 6 de octubre, 2014 1 Discurso inaugural pronunciado por Enrique Marshall, Vicepresidente del Banco Central de Chile, con motivo de la Duodcima Reunin de Tesoreros de Banca Central, organizada por el CEMLA y el Banco Central de Chile, y celebrada en Santiago de Chile entre los das 6 y 8 de octubre de 2014. Muy buenos das a todos los presentes. Quisiera dar la ms cordial bienvenida a nuestros invitados extranjeros. Espero que tengan una excelente estada en nuestro pas. En nombre del Presidente del Banco Central de Chile y de su Consejo, me resulta muy grato inaugurar la Duodcima Reunin de Tesoreros de Banca Central, con la asistencia de representantes de Latinoamrica y el Caribe y de invitados especiales provenientes de Europa, Norteamrica y Asia. Esta es una actividad organizada conjuntamente por el CEMLA y el Banco Central de Chile. Vaya un reconocimiento entonces a nuestro coorganizador en la persona de su Gerente de Programas y Reuniones Tcnicas de Banca Central, Fernando Snchez Cuadros, cuyo apoyo y colaboracin para la preparacin de esta reunin ha sido extremadamente valioso. Un reconocimiento tambin para el staff del Banco Central de Chile, encabezado por nuestro Gerente General y la Gerente de Tesorera, que trabajaron con ahnco para que todo esto fuese posible. Durante los prximos tres das, ustedes, tesoreros de la banca central de Latinoamericana, estarn reunidos para analizar las materias que concentran hoy su atencin y los desafos que visualizan para el futuro. Me gustara aprovechar esta oportunidad para compartir con ustedes algunas reflexiones sobre esta funcin de emisin y caja o de tesorera que ubica a los bancos centrales en una relacin tan directa y tangible con la ciudadana en general. Resulta difcil visualizar el funcionamiento de una economa sin la presencia de billetes y monedas. El efectivo facilita millones de transacciones que se realizan da a da y, adems, es normalmente un smbolo nacional y por tanto una carta de presentacin para quienes nos visitan en nuestros respectivos pases. Nuestra tarea como banqueros centrales es garantizar la liquidez del sistema financiero y preservar el normal funcionamiento de los medios de pago, incluidos entre ellos el dinero efectivo. Se trata de una tarea que concita el ms alto inters pblico y cuyo cabal cumplimiento exige mantener muy en alto la confianza que se ha depositado en nosotros. Proveer de circulante a los sistemas econmicos es fundamental para garantizar un acceso generalizado a las transacciones, para facilitar muchas operaciones financieras y, en general, para brindar apoyo a las actividades econmicas. La potestad exclusiva de emitir que ostentan nuestros bancos centrales es una de las facultades o atribuciones consignadas en nuestros estatutos orgnicos y que debemos ejercer con extrema diligencia. De ese mandato legal se derivan tareas tan importantes como la gestin eficiente del ciclo del efectivo, y la respuesta oportuna frente a contingencias de variados orgenes, incluidos los desastres naturales, los que pueden provocar interrupciones indeseadas en el suministro de circulante. En ese marco, se plantea tambin la funcin de identificar y retirar los billetes falsos, que es clave para mantener la confianza del pblico y, en ltimo trmino, para preservar la integridad y estabilidad del sistema de pagos. En esa perspectiva, es fundamental que nuestras unidades de anlisis cuenten permanentemente con un buen diagnstico a partir del cual se formulen recomendaciones en orden a prevenir o mitigar el problema de las falsificaciones. Ello supone, en todo caso, una estrecha cooperacin con otras instituciones pblicas que participan en la formulacin de polticas preventivas, en la aprobacin de disposiciones legales o reglamentarias relacionadas con estos asuntos, o en la pesquisa de quienes comenten ilcitos. Todos estos temas estarn en el centro de vuestras deliberaciones en el transcurso de estos das. Agregara a la lista de materias de alto inters y actualidad los avances tecnolgicos en la impresin y acuacin con todas sus implicancias prcticas para nuestro trabajo, las experiencias que han tenido lugar en la regin en materia de lanzamiento de nuevos billetes y las lecciones que surgen de dichos procesos, y los temas referidos al cuidado y conservacin del efectivo que siempre estn entre vuestras preocupaciones. En Chile, en aos recin pasados, efectuamos un cambio completo en la familia de los billetes en circulacin. Adquirimos una experiencia que estamos gustosos de compartir con nuestros colegas de otros pases. En materia de monedas, en cambio, tenemos un proyecto en ciernes, de manera que sera para nosotros extremadamente til conocer otras experiencias recientes. Este tipo de intercambio resulta muy valioso en el marco de estas reuniones. Los billetes y monedas son expresiones simblicas de cada uno de nuestros pases. Incorporan en sus diseos contenidos esenciales de lo que somos y de nuestro bagaje cultural. Hroes, polticos, poetas, santos, paisajes y efemrides, se incluyen en ellos para recordarnos el sello y la identidad de nuestros pueblos. Por todos es sabido que nuestros billetes responden a un trabajo muy cuidadoso de profesionales y tcnicos que buscan conciliar diversos criterios, como son el diseo, la seguridad, la funcionalidad, la durabilidad y los costos de produccin. La tarea de los tesoreros es alcanzar un adecuado equilibrio entre todos ellos, lo que no siempre resulta fcil. Un hecho innegable de estos tiempos es el surgimiento de nuevos medios de pago, alternativos al efectivo. Entre ellos estn el dinero plstico y los medios electrnicos, que como sabemos han ganado terreno. Sin embargo, la evidencia de nuestra regin y de otras economas desarrolladas muestra que la demanda por billetes y monedas ha seguido creciendo, incluso en algunos casos a tasas bastante altas. Ello reafirma la funcin bsica de provisin de circulante que cumplen los bancos centrales. Por otro lado, nuestras instituciones deben permanecer atentas a factores o variables que pueden inducir cambios bruscos o inesperados en la demanda por efectivo, como por ejemplo, los ciclos econmicos o los ajustes en los precios de determinados servicios de uso masivo. Nuestras unidades de investigacin deben considerar como parte de sus actividades la formulacin de escenarios que den cuenta de estos potenciales cambios. A ello se suma la necesidad de considerar las variaciones en los precios de las materias primas, como las conocidas en los ltimos aos, la introduccin de nuevas opciones de formato o sustrato para los billetes, y los eventuales cambios en las preferencias de la ciudadana. Todo ello pone de relieve el amplio espectro de materias que debemos procesar en el marco de nuestras tareas. En un mbito operativo, una tarea que aparece como crecientemente importante es el desarrollo e implementacin de nuevas instalaciones para la fabricacin, almacenamiento, procesamiento y distribucin de efectivo. Ello adquiere particular relevancia para aquellos bancos centrales que siguen funcionando en edificios un tanto antiguos, diseados para procesar volmenes de circulante mucho menores que los actuales. Debemos tener presente que las decisiones en materia de instalaciones toman tiempo y suponen un largo proceso de preparacin previa y luego de ejecucin, de manera que actuar con anticipacin es esencial. Tambin en un mbito operativo, es necesario que los bancos centrales presten la debida atencin a las empresas, distintas a los bancos, que han comenzado a desempear roles relevantes en el ciclo del efectivo, como por ejemplo, las transportadoras de valores. Es conveniente establecer con precisin en qu actividades pueden intervenir, y definir o perfeccionar los marcos reglamentarios que las rigen. En esa misma lnea aparece el tema del reciclado de los residuos de billetes. Resulta de alto inters conocer las experiencias de los bancos centrales que se encuentran a la vanguardia en estos temas. Con estas reflexiones he buscado poner de relieve la importancia de las actividades que desempean los bancos centrales en el mbito de la provisin de circulante. De ello se deriva la necesidad de procurar un permanente fortalecimiento de nuestras capacidades internas y de los equipos humanos que las despliegan. Reuniones de este tipo, que promueven el intercambio de conocimientos y experiencias entre quienes cumplen tareas en este mbito, son extremadamente tiles. Hago votos por el xito de estas jomadas. Espero que resulten muy fructferas para todos y que se logren plenamente sus objetivos. Title: The Asian crisis and its consequences on the Chilean economy
text: The Asian Crisis and its consequences on the Chilean Economy Presentation by Mr. Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank, at the Seminar "Asia where?" organized by the Electronic Exchange of Chile. Santiago, April 7, 1998. I. -Introduction: 1. - I thank La Bolsa Electr97nica for its invitation to participate in the seminar: "Asia where?". Beyond being an ingenious play on words, the title raises a very pertinent question, especially after the onset of the Asian crisis that has generated an atmosphere of uncertainty. Economic conditions are always difficult to project, but the crisis widens the uncertainty by raising questions about how deep they will be or when the trend will change and the recovery will begin. If we are too optimistic and ahead of the curve of recovery, the cost may be the need for a new and more severe adjustment. It is better to err on the side of caution than recklessness. 2. - In the first part of this presentation I will refer to the gestation of the crisis and the common macroeconomic imbalances presented by the countries most seriously affected by it. This makes it possible to assess the extent to which the problems and risks that caused the crisis have been resolved, and more importantly, it allows us to understand the monetary authority's concern about achieving certain macroeconomic balances. Then, I will analyze the state of development in which the crisis in Asia is and what are the risk factors still latent. In the second part I will refer to the effect that the crisis has on the international economic scenario, its impact on the Chilean economy and the way in which the monetary authority is responding to these challenges. II. - Background to the crisis 3. - The Asian crisis broke out in July last year, when Thailand decided not to continue defending the Bath and let it float. The crisis then quickly spread to Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines, eventually affecting Korea, Taiwan and Hong Kong to varying degrees. In October 1997, Asian instability produced global turbulence, especially in emerging countries, which manifested themselves in exchange rate depreciations, falls in stock prices and significant increases in interest rates. 4. - The first question that arises is whether there are common elements present, to a greater or lesser degree, in the countries most seriously affected by the crisis. We visualize at least three. First, their current account deficits had widened, reaching in some cases (Thailand) levels of 8 percent of GDP, and, crucially, were increasingly financed by short-term borrowing. Second, financial systems were fragile, inefficient in intermediation of credit, and not subject to transparency requirements. Finally, there were political factors that contributed to increasing the uncertainty associated with this type of crisis. These factors are easily recognizable in countries such as Thailand and Indonesia and to a lesser extent in Malaysia, the Philippines and Korea. These are the same elements that, ex-post, the academic literature recognized were present in Mexico before the so-called tequilazo. The crisis factors are illustrative to underscore the authorities' concern to maintain macroeconomic balances and the solvency of the financial system. III. - Current situation 5. - Progress has been made in making adjustments to IMF programs, which have been implemented with varying degrees of intensity. These have meant implementing policies aimed at reducing excess spending and cleaning up financial systems, which have allowed in some cases to recover the confidence of international investors, and thus overcome the crisis. Thus, today we can see that the stock and exchange markets are stabilizing in most of the countries involved. 6. - However, the process is not yet concluded, and there are pockets of concern. It is necessary to hope that adjustment programmes will become widespread and that the policies implemented will show positive effects in terms of trends. Moreover, the process is still contingent on maintaining the political will to continue with the reforms and measures implemented until macroeconomic balances are restored and thus gradually investor confidence throughout 1998. If the corrective measures are not implemented, it is likely that nervousness will again be felt in the financial, exchange and stock markets, with the consequent extension and deepening of the real effects of the crisis. 7. - In the current international scenario, one of the biggest focuses of concern is in the Japanese economy, which is undoubtedly one of the pillars for the rest of the economies in the region. Economic indicators currently show that this country is in recession, and although policymakers have taken pains to quickly define some reforms, they do not seem to have borne fruit and many assess them as insufficient. Last December, important changes were announced in the financial field, aimed at recovering confidence and solving the solvency problems of banks in order to ensure their viability in the medium and long term. A significant fiscal program has been announced, based on increases in public spending in order to recover aggregate demand. Unfortunately, demand recovery policies will take some time to show their effects, and are constrained by the structural conditions of the Japanese economy. On the one hand, the weak medium-term fiscal position does not encourage the use of more aggressive tax-cutting policies. On the other hand, the adequacy of the financial system is effectively creating conditions for a credit crunch. It is widely believed in specialized media that the Japanese economy requires fundamental structural adjustments, which eliminate restrictions on the free movement of goods and the reallocation of resources. The success of the Japanese economy would generate extraordinarily favorable effects for the economies of the area and also for the global economy. 8. - A second focus of concern is the situation in Indonesia. While some of the political uncertainty has been overcome with the extension of the current government's term for a new period, delays in reaching a broad agreement with the IMF, and news that emerges from time to time regarding radical changes in exchange rate policy, are widening uncertainty, which in turn is reflected in their financial markets. 9. - In the rest of the countries, confidence has been recovering, particularly in Korea and Thailand, where the authorities have rapidly implemented a series of reforms that have partly restored lost confidence, especially in the weakest financial sector. This has been reflected in greater stability of their currencies and asset prices, which has allowed a gradual reduction in interest rates that had risen significantly at the beginning of the crisis. 10. - It should be noted that in the case of Malaysia, the IMF decided to advance part of the disbursements in response to the good progress of reforms. It is also important to note that today the contagion effect is no longer as significant as at the beginning of the crisis. At this point, international investors are more clearly differentiating one country from another. 11. - In Singapore, however, the confidence of international capital has already regained and financial markets have stabilized rapidly. With this, it has become clear that the instabilities experienced towards the end of last year have their explanation mainly in the "contagion effect", due to the close commercial relationship with the countries in crisis. In fact, Singapore has solid macroeconomic balances, positive indicators of external solvency and a healthy financial system, all which, after the initial panic, has allowed it to differentiate itself from its trading partners in crisis. 12. - Hong Kong, which even in the worst moments made public its decision to maintain its fixed exchange rate system, has also managed to restore stability to its markets to a large extent. This is mainly due to the fact that Hong Kong has none of the internal weaknesses of the countries in crisis, has a highly developed financial system, has a solid external position and a macroeconomic situation in balance. Indeed, Hong Kong has strong reserves, and China has offered it the backing of its own; local banks are among the most capitalized and most liquid in the world, have a current account deficit of just over 1% of GDP and have fiscal surpluses of the order of 2% of GDP. 13. - China, for its part, deserves special attention because of its size, accounting for 12% of global GDP and 37% of the region's. China has been relatively immune to the financial contagion of this crisis, and has been able to withstand the nervousness that has plagued its neighbors. This is explained by the fact that China has a relatively closed capital account and the capital inflown is mainly foreign investment; and also because, although competitiveness has been somewhat undermined by the devaluations of the region's currencies, it has not meant a great change since China had experienced in 1995 a significant improvement in its competitiveness due to the depreciation of the Yuan, its currency. All of the above, plus the large volume of international reserves it has, have allowed it not to use exchange rate policy as an adjustment variable and thus reassure the markets. It would be very serious if China were dragged into the war of devaluations; This would significantly expand the extent and depth of the crisis. But we are confident in the strength of China's economy and the responsibility of its authorities. IV. - Consequences for the World Economy 14. - The consequences of the Asian crisis on the world economy have been global, affecting economic growth, absolute and relative prices, i.e. inflation, real terms of trade and exchange rates, and financial variables, interest rates and capital flows. 15. - Global growth in 1998 will tend to be lower than previously expected. IMF projections at the end of last year indicated that the international economy would grow by about 3.5 percent during 1998, representing a fall of 0.6 percentage points from 1997 and 0.8 percentage points from the level of activity expected before the crisis worsened. It is likely that in the coming weeks a further decrease in this figure will be announced, but less than those already registered. At this point it is important to mention that, although the crisis will cause a slowdown in the level of activity, the world economy is currently with growth rates much higher than those observed in the early nineties. The G-7 economies, with the exception of Japan, are either beginning an expansionary cycle of domestic demand (Germany, France, Italy) or at an advanced stage of an expansion cycle that has shown growth rates much higher than historical and high productivity rates (United States, Canada, England). As expected, the greatest negative impacts in terms of growth will occur in the Asian economies that have been directly involved in the crisis and, secondly, in the economies of emerging countries, including some in Latin America. 16. - On the other hand, inflation has been declining significantly worldwide for about three years, and the pre-crisis outlook was for this trend to continue. In the current scenario, the fall in international inflation in dollar terms is likely to be accentuated, due to devaluations in Asia, the likely fall in global economic activity and the lower commodity prices that have been observed recently. This is not an inflationary crisis and can be a deflationary crisis. 17. - In turn, lower global growth prospects will tend to lead to lower demand for copper and other export commodities. This situation has already been reflected in a decline in the price of the metal, which is currently below 80 cents per pound, around 20 cents below its pre-crisis level. Estimates from various sources indicate an average price of around 80 cents for this year. The price of other basic products, such as pulp, has also felt the effect of the crisis, showing a significant fall between October and March; However, the price of pulp in recent weeks has begun a recovery. With regard to oil, a series of factors have led to its price going from an average of US 19 per barrel in 1997, to a cumulative average of around US 15 per barrel so far in 1998. While the price today is still lower than this average, we should expect a slight recovery in the coming months: consensus projections indicate a price of almost 17 per barrel by the end of 1998. 18. - Interest rates on "hard currencies" will also tend to be lower than initially expected, resulting from both lower growth and lower expected inflation. The market has indicated this initially, generating a fall in 10-year dollar rates from 6.5% to a rate around 5.6%. Viewed from a broader perspective, nominal interest rates are now at historic lows, mainly thanks to low levels of inflation. However, real rates are high today, mainly due to the high profitability of investment projects in the United States. In the case of emerging economies, however, interest rates should tend to be higher, especially in Asia, given the greater exchange rate risk they present. 19. Finally, capital flows to emerging Asia are likely to fall this year, forcing a reduction in the Asian region's aggregate current account deficits during 1998. It must be seen that this implies the need for deficits to widen in the rest of the world, and in particular in developed countries. For the rest of the emerging countries, and in particular in Latin America, it seems that the region would be somewhat less attractive for investors because its risk-return ratio has not improved for the moment and, therefore, a somewhat lower capital inflow is expected than in previous years. V. - Consequences for the Chilean Economy 20. - Among the main consequences of the crisis in Asia on the Chilean economy is its negative effect on foreign trade and national income. The slowdown in the growth rate of activity in the rest of the world, especially in Asia, is generating lower demand for our main export products, implying lower prices for our products, and therefore, lower returns. 21. - The degree of diversification by market that our exports have achieved (currently more than 3,500 products are exported to 180 countries) together with the flexibility of adjustment will reduce the negative effect: 25% of exports go to Europe whose economy is accelerating; 20% to North America showing high levels of growth; and 20% to Latin America, which has seen its growth decreased due to the crisis in Asia but still shows interesting growth. The 35% that goes to Asia will undergo adjustments over time, following the reverse process that led our exporters to take advantage of diverting their shipments to the region that until 1997 was the most dynamic in the world. 22. - Almost half of Chilean exports to Asia are destined for Japan, a country that has already been showing low growth for some years, and only 7% to the most affected countries that would be Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Korea. The latter will be the main subjects of reassignment. In any case, considering an international scenario of more depressed growth, we will face markets that grow less and therefore there will also be a greater difficulty in placing our non-traditional products, which have Latin America as their main destination (40%). 23. - Although it is estimated that the fall in the prices of our exports will be partially offset by a fall in oil prices and lower external inflation, the terms of trade will deteriorate by around 5 per cent compared to 1997. The deterioration in the terms of trade is offset by a lower level of national income and, therefore, a lower capacity to spend with own resources and a greater need for financing. 24. - It is reasonable that part of the adjustment to lower national income be made through a temporary widening of the current account deficit, that is, through financing, since to the extent that the fall in income is transitory, it is not justified to cut the level of spending. It is always prudent to ensure that the use of financing remains within reasonable limits and that its most intense use is strictly transitory, and therefore consistent with the economy's medium- and long-term borrowing capacity. 25. - The other part of the adjustment required for lower income should correspond to lower domestic expenditure. Thus, monetary policy has taken measures to bring about these results, reducing expenditure growth in a framework of price stability, and the economy shows the first signs of moving into this process. Inflation, although we expect some setbacks in the coming months, continues to decline, consistent with the targets set, and economic activity is expanding at a slower pace than at the end of 1997. 26. - Monetary policy has sought to regulate the expansion of aggregate domestic spending. Thus, the increase in short-term interest rates by the Central Bank is not only in response to a level of spending in the third and fourth quarters of last year inconsistent with the maintenance of internal balances, but also seeks to incorporate the most depressed international scenario; The short-term indicators for the first quarter would indicate that this spending adjustment has not yet occurred, although there are indicators that anticipate that it will be clearly shown in the coming quarters. The increase in short-term interest rates is compounded by the Government's decision to reduce investment expenditures by companies and others in the public sector. Meanwhile, the exchange rate policy implemented in this period sought to cushion the sudden movements of the nominal exchange rate without preventing its more permanent tendencies from manifesting, preventing the real exchange rate from deviating towards a trajectory inconsistent with external equilibrium. T7.- The policies in progress have contributed to the strengths exhibited by the Chilean economy, which allow facing the crisis and limiting its effects with greater security. These include: (i) the fact that as part of the general solvency exhibited by the country, after more than a decade of sustained growth and macroeconomic stability, the financial system also shows a solid position, with a structure of currencies in place; (ii) a low and declining level of inflation; and (iii) a non-significant level of short-term external debt (4.8 percent of total external debt at the end of 1997, and about 1.5 percent of GDP). 28. - The aforementioned economic strengths allow that, even with the adjustment measures recently implemented, a level of growth that is among the highest in Latin America, of the order of 5.5%, continues to be projected and that the inflation target continues to be met. VII.- Conclusions 29. - I would like to conclude this presentation by trying to answer the question of this seminar: Where are we going? At present, the international economy has entered a phase of stabilization, although some signs of nervousness and financial turbulence are still possible. The financial consequences of the crisis seem to be relatively limited, but its effects on real activity and in terms of global economic growth are beginning to be felt. That is, we begin to experience the symptoms in the real economy. In Asia, with some notable exceptions, the situation in the exchange and financial markets has tended towards greater stability, the necessary reforms have been implemented in most cases in a timely manner, particularly in the financial system -- a key element in this --, crisis and a process of adjustment in the levels and composition of spending is already underway that will lead to a notable turnaround in the region's trade balance. This would mean that the probability of new outbreaks that indicate an aggravation of the problem is not high. 30. - However, we must be careful. The results are yet to be seen in their entirety and it is still necessary to make more progress in the process of reforms that will allow the solid recovery of macroeconomic balances and thus, gradually, the confidence of international investors. It should not be forgotten that the markets are very sensitive and that at any sign of retreat they can overreact, with the consequent negative effects in terms of the extension and depth of the crisis. 31. - Our analysis indicates that the effects of the crisis in Chile are limited. The external current account deficit will widen, but to a perfectly manageable value of around 6% of GDP; the economy will continue to travel on its path of growth, but at a more moderate pace with an expansion of around 5.5%, the largest in Latin America and internationally. Inflation will continue to decline reaching the target of around 4.5% set for this year. Our financial system remains solid and progress continues to be made in making it more efficient and competitive, expanding its development possibilities. Thus, Chile's response to the Asian crisis has been embedded within the global context of its economic policy, whose fundamental objectives are to contribute to the achievement of currency and price stability; maintaining a strong and sustainable external position; the preservation of the internal payments system, which requires a solvent financial system; and the existence of budgetary fiscal discipline, all essential conditions for continued growth. The Central Bank remains vigilant to take, if necessary, further policy actions to deal with the crisis so that the economy remains on its course of sustained development and stability. Any additional contribution in moderating the economy's spending is welcome. 32. - A final thought. The train of development of our economy continues to run, although its speed this year will be somewhat slower. It is important to worry that all Chileans move forward in this process and that no one is left behind by the train. President Frei has shown particular concern about this, and has placed the emphasis of his policies on the social field. The President of the Republic, with a clear statesman's vision, has also expressed his firm decision to move forward in these matters without jeopardizing the macroeconomic balances achieved with so much effort. 33. - In difficult times, voices arise calling to weaken the anti-inflationary effort in the belief that this will solve problems of the economy. Inflation does not solve economic problems: it can only aggravate them. Perhaps it can solve political problems in the short term, redistributing income against workers. But we must bear in mind that when that happens, the same ones who propose a little more inflation then propose to compensate for the lost purchasing power. And there we enter the classic price-wage spiral that led our economy to a great political and social failure. 34. - The Central Bank reiterates its commitment to the inflation target and its decision to use its policies to achieve it.

Santiago, 7 de abril de 1998.  - Introduccin:  - Agradezco a La Bolsa Electrnica por su invitacin a participar en el seminario: "Asia dnde?". Ms all de ser un ingenioso juego de palabras, el ttulo plantea una pregunta muy pertinente, especialmente despus de iniciada la crisis asitica que ha generado un ambiente de incertidumbre. Esto permite evaluar hasta que punto los problemas y riesgos que originaron la crisis se han estado resolviendo, y ms importante an, permite comprender la preocupacin de la autoridad monetaria por la consecucin de ciertos equilibrios macroeconmicos. En la segunda parte me referir al efecto que la crisis tiene en el escenario econmico internacional, la repercusin de ste en la economa chilena y la forma en que la autoridad monetaria est respondiendo a estos desafos.  - Antecedentes de la crisis  - La crisis asitica se desat en julio del ao pasado, cuando Tailandia decide no seguir defendiendo el Bath y lo deja flotar. Luego, la crisis se expandi rpidamente a Indonesia, Malasia y Filipinas, para finalmente afectar en distinto grado a Corea, Taiwan y Hong Kong. En octubre de 1997, la inestabilidad asitica produjo turbulencias a nivel global, en especial en los pases emergentes, que se manifestaron en depreciaciones cambiaras, cadas en el precio de las acciones y significativos aumentos en las tasas de inters.  - La primera pregunta que surge es si existen elementos comunes presentes, en mayor o menor grado, en los pases ms seriamente afectados por la crisis. Visualizamos al menos tres. Primero, sus dficits en cuenta corriente se haban ampliado, alcanzando en algunos casos (Tailandia) niveles del 8% del PIB, y, lo que es crucial, eran crecientemente financiados con endeudamiento de corto plazo. Segundo, los sistemas financieros eran frgiles, ineficientes en la intermediacin del crdito y no sujetos a requisitos de transparencia. Por ltimo, existieron factores de orden poltico que contribuyeron a incrementar la incertidumbre asociada a este tipo de crisis. Estos factores son fcilmente reconocibles en pases como Tailandia e Indonesia y en menor grado en Malasia, Filipinas y Corea. Estos son los mismos elementos que, ex-post, la literatura acadmica reconoci que estaban presentes en Mxico antes del llamado tequilazo. Los factores de crisis son ilustrativos para subrayar la preocupacin que deben tener las autoridades por conservar los equilibrios macroeconmicos y la solvencia del sistema financiero.  - Situacin actual  - Se ha avanzado en realizar ajustes en el marco de programas del FMI, que se han aplicado con distinto grado de intensidad. Estos han significado implementar polticas dirigidas a disminuir el exceso de gasto y a sanear los sistemas financieros, las que han permitido en algunos casos ir recuperando la confianza de los inversionistas internacionales, y de esta forma ir sorteando la crisis. As, hoy da podemos ver que los mercados burstiles y cambiarios se estn estabilizando en la mayor parte de los pases involucrados.  - Sin embargo, todava el proceso no est concluido, y hay focos de preocupacin. Es necesario esperar que los programas de ajuste se generalicen y que las polticas implementadas muestren efectos positivos en trminos de tendencia. Adems, todava el proceso est supeditado a que se mantenga la voluntad poltica de seguir con las reformas y las medidas aplicadas hasta recuperar los equilibrios macroeconmicos y as, gradualmente, la confianza de los inversionistas a lo largo de 1998. De no seguir implementndose las medidas correctivas, es probable que nuevamente se vuelva a sentir el nerviosismo en los mercados financiero, cambiario y burstil, con la consecuente extensin y profundizacin de los efectos reales de la crisis.  - En el actual escenario internacional, uno de los mayores focos de preocupacin se encuentra en la economa japonesa, que sin duda es uno de los pilares para el resto de las economas de la regin. Los indicadores econmicos actualmente muestran que este pas se encuentra en recesin, y aunque las autoridades econmicas se han esmerado en definir con rapidez algunas reformas, estas no parecen haber rendido frutos y muchos las evalan como insuficientes. En diciembre pasado se anunciaron cambios importantes en el mbito financiero, tendientes a recuperar la confianza y resolver los problemas de solvencia de los bancos de tal modo de asegurar su viabilidad en el mediano y largo plazo. Se ha anunciado un significativo programa fiscal, basado en aumentos del gasto pblico con el fin de recuperar la demanda agregada. Lamentablemente las poltica de recuperacin de la demanda van a tomar algn tiempo en mostrar sus efectos, y se ven limitadas por las condiciones estructurales de la economa Japonesa. Por una parte, la dbil posicin fiscal de mediano plazo no estimula el uso de polticas ms agresivas de recorte de impuestos. Por otra, la adecuacin del sistema financiero est creando en los hechos condiciones para una contraccin del crdito. Es opinin generalizada en medios especializados que la economa japonesa requiere de ajustes estructurales de fondo, que eliminen restricciones al libre movimiento de bienes y a la reasignacin de recursos. El xito de la economa japonesa generara efectos extraordinariamente favorables para las economas del rea y tambin para la economa global.  - Un segundo foco de preocupacin es la situacin en Indonesia. Si bien algo de la incertidumbre poltica ha sido superada con la prolongacin del mandato del actual gobierno por un nuevo perodo, las demoras en llegar a un acuerdo amplio con el FMI, y las noticias que surgen de tiempo en tiempo respecto de modificaciones radicales en poltica cambiara, van ampliando la incertidumbre, la que a su vez se refleja en sus mercados financieros.  - En el resto de los pases, la confianza se ha ido recuperando, en particular en Corea y Tailandia, donde las autoridades han implementado en forma rpida una serie de reformas que han permitido restaurar en parte la confianza perdida, especialmente en el sector financiero que es el que presentaba mayor debilidad. Ello se ha ido reflejando en una mayor estabilidad de sus monedas y del precio de los activos, lo que ha permitido una reduccin gradual de las tasas de inters que haban registrado importantes aumentos al comienzos de la crisis.  - Cabe destacar que en el caso de Malasia el FMI decidi adelantar parte de los desembolsos en respuesta al buen avance de las reformas. Tambin, es importante destacar que hoy da el efecto contagio ya no es tan significativo como al inicio de la crisis. A estas alturas, los inversionistas internacionales estn diferenciando ms claramente un pas de otro.  - A su vez, en Singapur ya se ha recuperado la confianza de los capitales internacionales y los mercados financieros se estabilizaron rpidamente. Con ello ha quedado claro que las inestabilidades vividas hacia fines del ao pasado tienen su explicacin fundamentalmente en el "efecto contagio", debido a la estrecha relacin comercial con los pases en crisis. De hecho, Singapur presenta slidos equilibrios macroeconmicos, positivos indicadores de solvencia externa y un sistema financiero sano, todo lo que, luego del pnico inicial, ha permitido diferenciarlo de sus socios comerciales en crisis.  - Hong-Kong, que an en los peores momentos hizo pblica su decisin de mantener su sistema de tipo cambio fijo, tambin ha logrado restablecer en gran medida la estabilidad de sus mercados. Ello debido fundamentalmente a que Hong-Kong no presenta ninguna de las debilidades internas de los pases en crisis, posee un sistema financiero muy desarrollado, cuenta con una slida posicin externa y con una situacin macroeconmica en equilibrio. Efectivamente, Hong-Kong posee fuertes reservas, y China le ha ofrecido el respaldo de las suyas; los bancos locales se encuentran dentro de los ms capitalizados y con mayor liquidez del mundo, tiene un dficit en cuenta corriente de poco ms de un 1% del PIB y presenta supervit fiscales del orden de 2% del PIB.  - China, por su parte, merece especial atencin por su tamao, ya que representa un 12% del PIB mundial y un 37% del de la regin. China ha sido relativamente inmune al contagio financiero de esta crisis, y ha podido resistir el nerviosismo que ha afectado a sus vecinos. Ello se explica porque China posee una cuenta de capitales relativamente cerrada y los capitales ingresados son fundamentalmente inversin extranjera; y tambin porque, si bien la competitividad se ha socavado algo por las devaluaciones de las monedas de la regin, no ha significado un gran cambio pues China haba experimentado en 1995 una mejora significativa en su competitividad por la depreciacin del Yuan, su moneda. Todo lo anterior, ms el gran volumen de reservas internacionales que posee, le han permitido no utilizar la poltica cambiara como variable de ajuste y de este modo tranquilizar a los mercados. Sera muy grave que China se viera arrastrada a la guerra de devaluaciones; ello ampliara significativamente la extensin y profundidad de la crisis. Pero confiamos en la solidez de la economa China y la responsabilidad de sus autoridades.  - Consecuencias sobre la Economa Mundial  - Las consecuencias de la crisis de Asia sobre la economa mundial han sido globales, afectando el crecimiento econmico, los precios absolutos y relativos, esto es la inflacin, los trminos de intercambio y los tipo de cambio reales, y las variables financieras, las tasas de inters y los flujos de capital.  - El crecimiento mundial durante 1998 tender a ser menor al esperado anteriormente. Las proyecciones del FMI a fines del ao pasado indicaban que la economa internacional crecera alrededor de 3,5% durante 1998, representando una cada de 0,6 puntos porcentuales respecto de 1997 y de 0,8 puntos porcentuales respecto del nivel de actividad esperado antes del agravamiento de la crisis. Es probable que en las prximas semanas se de a conocer una nueva disminucin de esta cifra, pero menor que las ya registradas. En este punto es importante mencionar que, aunque la crisis provocar una desaceleracin del nivel de actividad, la economa mundial se encuentra actualmente con tasas de crecimiento muy superiores a las observadas a principios de los noventa. Las economas del G-7, a excepcin de Japn, estn ya sea comenzando un ciclo expansivo de su demanda interna (Alemania, Francia, Italia) o en una fase avanzada de un ciclo de expansin que ha mostrado tasas de crecimiento muy superiores a las histricas y altas tasas de productividad (Estados Unidos, Canad, Inglaterra). Como es de esperarse, los mayores impactos negativos en trminos de crecimiento se producirn en las economas de Asia que se han visto directamente involucradas en la crisis y, en segundo lugar, en las economas de pases emergentes, incluyendo algunos de Amrica Latina.  - Por otra parte, la inflacin ha estado declinando en forma importante en el mundo entero desde hace unos tres aos, y las perspectivas previas a la crisis eran que esta tendencia se mantuviese. En el escenario actual es probable que se acente la cada de la inflacin internacional en dlares, debido a las devaluaciones en Asia, la probable cada en la actividad econmica global y los menores precios de las materias primas que se han estado observando recientemente. Esta no es una crisis inflacionaria y puede ser una crisis deflacionaria.  - A su vez las menores perspectivas de crecimiento mundial tendern a provocar una menor demanda por cobre y otras materias primas de exportacin. Esta situacin ya se ha reflejado en una disminucin del precio del metal, que se ubica actualmente bajo los 80 centavos de dlar la libra, alrededor de 20 centavos por debajo de su nivel de pre-crisis. Las estimaciones de diversas fuentes indican un precio promedio de alrededor de 80 centavos para este ao. El precio de otros productos bsicos, como la celulosa, tambin ha sentido el efecto de la crisis, mostrando una significativa cada entre octubre y marzo; sin embargo, el precio de la celulosa en las ltimas semanas ha comenzado una recuperacin. Respecto del petrleo, una serie de factores han llevado a que su precio pasara de un promedio de US$ 19 el barril en 1997, a un promedio acumulado en torno a los US$ 15 el barril en lo que va corrido de 1998. Sin bien es cierto el precio hoy da es aun ms bajo que este promedio, deberamos esperar un leve recuperacin en los prximos meses: las proyecciones de consenso indican un precio de casi US$ 17 por barril para fines de 1998.  - Las tasas de inters de las "monedas duras" tambin tendern a ser menores a las esperadas inicialmente, producto tanto de un menor crecimiento como de una menor inflacin esperada. El mercado as lo ha indicado inicialmente, al generar una cada de las tasas en dlares a 10 aos desde 6,5% a una tasa en torno a 5,6%. Miradas desde una perspectiva ms amplia, las tasas de inters nominales se encuentran hoy da en mnimos histricos, fundamentalmente gracias a los bajos niveles de inflacin existentes. Sin embargo las tasa reales soy hoy da altas, debido principalmente a la alta rentabilidad de los proyectos de inversin en Estados Unidos. En el caso de las economas emergentes sin embargo, las tasas de inters debieran tender a ser mayores, especialmente en Asia, dado el mayor riesgo cambiario que estas presentan.  - Finalmente, cabe esperar que los flujos de capital hacia los pases emergentes de Asia probablemente sufran una cada durante este ao, lo que forzar a una reduccin en los dficit en la cuenta corriente agregada de la regin asitica durante 1998. Debe considerarse que esto implica la necesidad que los dficit se amplen en el resto del mundo, y en particular en los pases desarrollados. Para el resto de los pases emergentes, y en particular de Latinoamrica, parece que la regin sera algo menos atractiva para los inversionistas debido a que su relacin riesgo - retorno no ha mejorado por el momento y, por tanto, se espera un influjo de capitales algo menor que en aos anteriores.  - Consecuencias sobre la Economa Chilena  - Entre las principales consecuencias de la crisis en Asia sobre la economa chilena se encuentra su efecto negativo sobre el comercio exterior y el ingreso nacional. La disminucin del ritmo de crecimiento de la actividad en el resto del mundo, en especial en Asia, est generando una menor demanda por nuestros principales productos de exportacin, implicando esto menores precios para nuestros productos, y por ende, menores retornos.  - El grado de diversificacin por mercados que han alcanzado nuestras exportaciones (en la actualidad se exporta a 180 pases ms de 3.500 productos) junto con la flexibilidad de ajuste van aminorar el efecto negativo: 25% de las exportaciones va a Europa cuya economa se est acelerando; 20% a Norteamrica que muestra altos niveles de crecimiento; y un 20% a Amrica Latina, que ha visto disminuido su crecimiento por la crisis en Asia pero que an muestra crecimientos interesantes. El 35% que va al Asia va a sufrir readecuaciones en el tiempo, siguiendo el proceso inverso al que llev a nuestros exportadores a aprovechar las ventajas de desviar sus envos hacia la regin que hasta 1997 era la ms dinmica del orbe.  - Casi la mitad de las exportaciones chilenas que van al Asia tiene como destino Japn, pas que ya viene mostrando un crecimiento bajo desde hace algunos aos, y slo un 7% a los pases ms afectados que seran Tailandia, Indonesia, Filipinas y Corea. Estas ltimas sern los principales sujetos de reasignacin. En cualquier caso, considerando un escenario internacional de crecimiento ms deprimido, nos enfrentaremos a mercados que crecen menos y por tanto habr adems una mayor dificultad en colocar nuestros productos no tradicionales, los que tienen a Amrica Latina como destino principal (40%).  - Si bien se estima que la cada en los precios de nuestras exportaciones ser parcialmente compensada con una baja en el precio del petrleo y una inflacin externa ms baja, los trminos de intercambio se vern deteriorados en torno a un 5 por ciento respecto de 1997. El deterioro de los trminos de intercambio tiene como contrapartida un menor nivel de ingreso nacional y, por ende, una menor capacidad de gasto con recursos propios y mayor necesidad de financiamiento.  - Es razonable que una parte del ajuste al menor ingreso nacional se realice por la va de una ampliacin transitoria del dficit en cuenta corriente, esto es por la va del financiamiento, pues en la medida que la cada del ingreso sea transitoria no se justifica recortar el nivel de gasto. Siempre es prudente procurar que el uso de financiamiento se mantenga dentro de lmites razonables y que su uso ms intenso sea estrictamente transitorio, y por lo tanto consistente con la capacidad de endeudamiento de mediano y largo plazo de la economa.  - La otra parte del ajuste requerido por el menor ingreso debe corresponder a un menor gasto interno. As la poltica monetaria ha adoptado medidas para provocar esos resultados, reduciendo el crecimiento del gasto en un marco de estabilidad de los precios, y la economa presenta los primeros signos de encausarse en ese proceso. La inflacin, aunque esperamos algunos retrocesos en meses prximos, mantiene su declinacin, consistente con las metas fijadas, y la actividad econmica se expande a menor ritmo que a fines de 1997.  - La Poltica Monetaria ha buscado regular la expansin del gasto agregado interno. As, el aumento de las tasas de inters de corto plazo por parte del Banco Central no slo es en respuesta a un nivel de gasto en el tercer y cuarto trimestre del ao pasado inconsistente con la mantencin de los equilibrios internos sino que, adems, busca que la senda de gasto incorpore el escenario internacional ms deprimido; los indicadores de coyuntura del primer trimestre indicaran que este ajuste de gasto an no se ha producido, aunque hay indicadores que anticipan que se mostrar con claridad en los prximos trimestres. Al incremento de las tasas de inters de corto plazo se suma en el mismo sentido la decisin del Gobierno de reducir los gastos de inversin de las empresas y otros del sector pblico. En tanto la poltica cambiara implementada en este perodo busc amortiguar los movimientos bruscos del tipo de cambio nominal sin impedir que se manifiesten sus tendencias ms permanentes, evitando que el tipo de cambio real se desve hacia una trayectoria inconsistente con el equilibrio externo. T7.- Las polticas en curso han contribuido a las fortalezas que exhibe la economa chilena, las que permiten enfrentar la crisis y limitar sus efectos con mayor seguridad. Destacan entre stas: (i) el hecho que como parte de la solvencia general que exhibe el pas, despus de ms de una dcada de crecimiento sostenido y estabilidad macroeconmica, el sistema financiero muestra tambin una posicin slida, con una estructura de monedas calzada; (ii) un nivel de inflacin bajo y decreciente; y (iii) un nivel de deuda externa de corto plazo no significativo (4,8% de la deuda externa total a fines de 1997, y alrededor de 1,5% del PIB).  - Las fortalezas econmicas antes sealadas permiten que, an con las medidas de ajuste recientemente implementadas, se contine proyectando un nivel de crecimiento que se ubica dentro de los ms altos de Amrica Latina, del orden de 5,5%, y se logre seguir cumpliendo con la meta de inflacin. VII.- Conclusiones  - Quisiera concluir esta presentacin tratando de responder la pregunta de este seminario: Hacia donde vamos? En la actualidad la economa internacional ha entrado en una fase de estabilizacin, aunque todava son posibles algunas muestras de nerviosismo y de turbulencia financiera. Las consecuencias financieras de la crisis parecen estar ya relativamente acotadas, pero sus efectos sobre la actividad real y en trminos de crecimiento econmico mundial se empiezan a sentir. Esto es, empezamos a vivir los sntomas en la economa real. En Asia, con algunas notables excepciones, la situacin en los mercados cambiarios y financieros ha tendido hacia una mayor estabilidad, se han implementado en la generalidad de los casos en forma oportuna, las reformas necesarias, en particular en el sistema financiero -- pieza clave en esta crisis --, y ya est en marcha un proceso de ajuste en los niveles y composicin del gasto que llevar a un vuelco notable en la balanza comercial de la regin. Esto querra decir que la probabilidad de que se presenten nuevos focos que sealen un agravamiento del problema no es alta.  - No obstante, hay que ser cuidadosos. Los resultados an estn por verse en su totalidad y todava es necesario avanzar ms en el proceso de reformas que permitan recuperar en forma slida los equilibrios macroeconmicos y as, gradualmente, la confianza de los inversionistas internacionales. No hay que olvidar que los mercados son muy sensibles y que ante cualquier seal de retroceso pueden sobre-reaccionar, con los consecuentes efectos negativos en cunto a la extensin y profundidad de la crisis.  - Nuestro anlisis indica que los efectos de la crisis en Chile son acotados. El dficit externo en cuenta corriente se ampliar, pero a un valor perfectamente manejable en torno a 6% del PIB; la economa continuar transitando por su senda de crecimiento, pero a un ritmo ms moderado con una expansin de alrededor de 5.5%, de las mayores en Amrica Latina y a nivel internacional. La inflacin continuar disminuyendo alcanzando la meta de alrededor de 4.5% planteada para este ao. Nuestro sistema financiero se mantiene slido y se contina avanzando en hacerlo ms eficiente y competitivo ampliando sus posibilidades de desarrollo. As, la respuesta de Chile a la crisis asitica ha estado inserta dentro del contexto global de su poltica econmica, cuyos objetivos fundamentales son contribuir al logro de la estabilidad de la moneda y de los precios; la mantencin de una posicin externa slida y sostenible; la preservacin del sistema de pagos internos, lo que requiere de un sistema financiero solvente; y la existencia de disciplina fiscal presupuestaria, todo ello condiciones indispensables para continuar creciendo. El Banco Central permanece atento para tomar, si es necesario, nuevas acciones de poltica para hacer frente a la crisis de manera que la economa se mantenga en su curso de desarrollo sostenido y estabilidad. Cualquier contribucin adicional en materia de moderacin del gasto de la economa es bienvenida.  - Una reflexin final. El tren del desarrollo de nuestra economa contina en marcha, aunque su velocidad este ao ser algo ms lenta. Es importante preocuparse de que todos los chilenos avancemos en este proceso y que a nadie lo deje atrs el tren. El Presidente Fre ha mostrado especial preocupacin por esto, y ha puesto el nfasis de sus polticas en el campo social. Tambin ha manifestado el Presidente de la Repblica, con clara visin de estadista, su firme decisin de avanzar en estas materias sin poner en riesgo los equilibrios macroeconmicos alcanzados con tanto esfuerzo.  - En los momentos difciles, surgen voces llamando a debilitar el esfuerzo antiinflacionario en la creencia de que ello resolver problemas de la economa. La inflacin no resuelve problemas econmicos: slo puede agravarlos. Tal vez pueda resolver en el corto plazo problemas polticos, redistribuyendo ingresos en contra de los trabajadores. Pero hay que tener en cuenta que cuando eso ocurre los mismos que proponen un poquito ms de inflacin proponen luego compensar por el poder de compra perdido. Y ah entramos en la clsica espiral precios-salarios que condujo a nuestra economa a un gran fracaso poltico y social.  - El Banco Central reitera su compromiso con la meta de inflacin y su decisin de utilizar sus polticas para alcanzarla.

Title: The effects of international adjustment on Chilean exports
text: The effects of international adjustment on Chilean exports. Presentation by Mr. Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank, at Breakfast Conference organized by the Association of Exporters of Manufactures A.G. - ASEXMA, May 14, 1998. 1. - I thank the Association of Exporters for its kind invitation to participate in this meeting, which gives me the opportunity to share with you our vision on the effects of the Asian crisis, particularly those on the Chilean economy and the export sector. Thus I will begin this presentation with a quick reference to the gestation of the crisis, its state of development and the risk factors still latent. Secondly, I will analyse the effects of the Asian crisis on our external accounts, referring to the evolution of our exports by destination, stressing that national export activity has shown not only its dynamism, but also its ability to adapt to new circumstances. Finally, I will discuss the role played by the exchange rate and exchange rate policy at the current juncture. 2. - The international economy has seen global GDP growth slow down as a result of the crisis affecting countries in Southeast Asia, which has generated global infections. There are certain common elements in the countries most seriously affected by the crisis. First, in many cases current-account deficits had widened excessively for prolonged periods, and, crucially, these were increasingly financed by short-term external borrowing. Second, financial systems were inefficient in intermediation of funds and not subject to transparency and supervision requirements, showing excessive levels of risk. Finally, there were political factors, with institutional weaknesses that increased uncertainty regarding the ways to solve the problems that eventually triggered the crisis. 3. - At this stage of events, many of the countries directly affected by the crisis have made progress in their adjustment programs under agreements with the IMF. This has meant implementing policies aimed at reducing excess spending and cleaning up their financial systems, allowing in some cases to regain the confidence of international investors. Thus, today in Asia there is some greater stability of the stock markets and change them, although some specific episodes revive concern. The spiral of falling asset prices has stopped, but it is still necessary to wait for adjustment programs to become widespread and applied steadily until the policies implemented show positive effects in terms of trend. This adjustment process is conditional on maintaining the political will to continue with the reforms and measures implemented until macroeconomic balances are restored and thus gradually investor confidence throughout 1998. The reactions of the affected communities raise concerns that the application of corrective measures will be suspended, which would renew nervousness in the financial markets and change them, risking extending and deepening the real effects of the crisis. 4. The biggest focus of concern is Japan, which is sliding into recession, and although its authorities have taken pains to define reforms quickly, these have not yet borne fruit and many assess them as insufficient. The Japanese economy is a major creditor to the rest of the world and, unlike the rest of the Asian countries, has no foreign debt. This, while giving you time to find ways to overcome your problems, does not prevent the need to adjust your policies. In the rest of Asia, albeit with some ups and downs, confidence has been recovering, particularly in Korea and Thailand, where deep reforms were rapidly implemented. In Indonesia, there is still a sense of uncertainty, given the social instability in the face of expectations of a strong recession for 1998 and they are also facing price increases, as a result of the elimination of subsidies within the framework of the reforms required by the IMF. 5. - China has been relatively immune to the financial contagion of this crisis, but it has also been affected by speculation, being recently forced into an interest rate hike. China has a relatively closed capital account, receives capital mainly through foreign investment, and has a significant volume of international reserves. However, it must face expectations of devaluation based on speculation that local authorities will not accept the loss of competitiveness generated by the crisis. It would be very serious if China were dragged into a war of devaluations, given its relative importance in the region; However, there is confidence in the soundness of the economy and the responsibility of its authorities. Exports 6. - As noted, world growth in 1998 will be 3%, somewhat lower than the 4% recorded in 1996 and 1997, but a very reasonable rate in historical terms and higher than those observed in the early nineties. A similar or somewhat higher rate can be expected in 1999. As expected, the greatest impacts in terms of growth will occur in the four Asian economies that have been directly involved in the crisis and, secondly, in the economies of emerging countries, including those in Latin America. The slowdown in global economic activity has been reflected in reductions in commodity prices in general, particularly affecting those that, such as copper, gold and some forest products, are especially in demand in the region most affected by the crisis. The main impact of the Asian crisis on the external accounts of the Chilean economy has been in this way; It has led to a deterioration in the terms of trade and lower demand for our export products. A side effect is the reduction in net capital inflows, which in 1997 exerted significant expansionary pressures on domestic demand. 7. - The lower demand for our main export products implies lower prices for our products, and also in some cases falls in exported volumes. We expect a 10% drop in the prices of our exports this year, but it is estimated that export volumes will grow by 5%, with the highest volume growth corresponding to non-traditional exports (6.2%) and copper (5.3%). It is important to bear in mind that national export activity has shown on many occasions not only its dynamism but also its ability to adapt to new circumstances. Not only is the growth that is consistently higher than GDP remarkable, but also the flexibility to adapt to redirect our products towards markets that offer better conditions. This will allow us to reduce the negative impact on our export sector. 8. - In fact, if we look at the evolution by destination of our exports, it can be seen that throughout the decade the old continent has been losing relative share, ceding its first place as a destination for our exports to Asia and to a lesser extent to Latin America. Indeed, at the beginning of the decade, almost 40% of the total exported was destined for Europe, while Asia and Latin America represented 26% and 13% of total exports, respectively. The significant growth rates of Asia throughout this decade gave rise to a process of re-adjustment that led our exporters to take advantage of diverting their shipments to that region, which in 1997 came to represent 35% of total exports, while Europe currently takes only a quarter of our exports. It is undoubtedly expected that 35% of the total exported to Asia will undergo re-adjustments, following the reverse process that led our exporters to take advantage of redirecting their shipments to the region that until 1997 was the most dynamic in the world. I should note that the first quarter already saw a significant increase in our shipments of non-traditional products to Europe (32%), the United States (16%), and some regions in Latin America. This process must be maintained and strengthened. 9. - Thus, the real effects of the Asian crisis and its global impact are already beginning to be reflected in our statistics. Indeed, preliminary estimates for the first quarter of this year begin to show the impact of lower prices of our main export products, as well as lower external demand that affect us due to lower global growth and Asia in particular. During the first quarter of this year, export shipments registered a decrease of close to 10% compared to the same period last year, where Asia registered a decrease of 24%, which is reflecting that although the blows of this crisis cannot be avoided, the process of re-adaptation of our exports will at least mitigate them. This deterioration has been mainly contributed by the falls in the prices of our main export products, as volumes registered growth. Copper exports experienced a decrease of 22%, mainly due to price effect, with a significant increase in volume, while the main non-copper exports have in turn registered falls in prices and volumes exported, particularly in forest sector products (bleached pulp, wood chips and logs). For non-traditional exports, the most affected are the destinations to Asia of some seafood products (salmon and trout), which have been mainly impacted by lower demand from Asian countries. For all these products the falls are mainly concentrated in Japan and Korea. 10. - It is estimated that the fall in the prices of our exports will be partially offset by a fall in oil prices and lower external inflation, with the result that the terms of trade will deteriorate by around 5 per cent compared to 1997, which should be partly recovered during 1999. An additional element to keep in mind is that the high share of foreign investment in copper production and other major exports implies that in part the fall in the terms of trade will be offset by declines in profits earned by foreign investment, limiting the impact of the fall in export prices on national income and on the current account of the balance of payments. 11. - The deterioration in the terms of trade, net of the fall in profits earned by investments by non-residents, is offset by a lower level of national income and, therefore, a lower capacity to spend with own resources and a greater need for financing. It is reasonable that part of the adjustment to lower national income be made through a temporary widening of the current account deficit, that is, through financing, to the extent that the fall in income is considered transitory. As it is difficult to specify the length of the unfavorable period, it is prudent to ensure that the use of financing remains limited, leaving a margin for the economy's medium- and long-term borrowing capacity. The situation would change 12. - Another area of concern during this period was the evolution of the nominal exchange rate. At the end of October, a process of depreciation of the peso began, which, to a large extent, took economic agents by surprise. In fact, until the third quarter of 1997, the main topic of discussion regarding the exchange rate was the trend of appreciation of the peso and the strong capital inflows that the country had been receiving. The depreciation of the peso between October 1997 and March 1998 reflected at least three relevant factors. First, the appreciation of the dollar in international markets, a factor that causes upward pressure on the nominal peso-dollar exchange rate, but which in general terms does not represent a real depreciation of the peso to the extent that it is offset by lower international inflation in dollars. Secondly, the turbulence that affected the financial markets at a global level generated a change in the perception regarding the risk of changing it in the Chilean economy. This situation led agents to hedge their positions in foreign currency through forward dollar purchase operations, which indirectly pushed up the exchange rate due to the need for the financial system to eliminate the exchange risk associated with these contracts with purchases of currencies in the spot market. Third, the referred increase in the exchange rate is also the validation of a relative price adjustment, that is, in the real exchange rate, which results from efforts to reduce the growth rate in domestic spending to deal with the increase in the deficit. 13. On this last point there is often a degree of confusion in public discussion and I would like to dwell particularly on it. Some have argued that a deficit moderation strategy would be to increase the real exchange rate through increases in the nominal exchange rate, rather than reducing spending growth from tighter monetary and fiscal policies. However, this option only exists in the imagination of those who propose it: It is not possible to generate a lasting adjustment in the real exchange rate, without at the same time producing a reduction in domestic spending. This reduction may come directly from adjustment policies, or it may also come from an inflationary resurgence that reduces real wages. 14. - In the current conditions of the Chilean economy, with still dynamic spending and very low unemployment, a nominal devaluation is not an adequate way to generate sustainable increases in the real exchange rate. Under these conditions, a devaluation has mainly inflationary effects, and some impact on the real exchange rate only temporarily. If, as a result of the devaluation, the prices of tradable goods rise first and then the wages and prices of non-tradable goods, the devaluation will be inflationary and within a few months real wages and relative prices will be at their original value. To generate a real devaluation, it is necessary to create the conditions for real wages, measured in terms of tradable goods, to fall; that is, so that the effects of the devaluation are limited to the prices of tradable goods leaving nominal wages unchanged and non-tradable prices. Necessary conditions for such a thing to happen are that aggregate demand is weak, that the unemployment rate is rather high and, consequently, the indexation of wages weakens. None of these conditions are present in the Chilean economy today. It is not possible to raise the real exchange rate by force without at the same time reducing real wages, and in the conditions of the Chilean economy a reduction in real wages seems hardly achievable or justifiable. 15. - In a period of adjustment of relative prices and greater volatility in financial markets, the inflation target and the coherence of policies with it play a key role in anchoring the expectations of economic agents. Ambiguity in this area is extremely dangerous, because it erodes the credibility of policies. Without policy credibility, the evolution of inflation and other nominal variables, such as the exchange rate and wages, which in turn influence inflation, would be left adrift. Likewise, due to its visibility, the inflation target plays a key role in agreeing on policies that ensure a path consistent with basic macroeconomic balances. For all this, it is inconsistent to propose that one could be more flexible, accepting a little more inflation, in order to achieve a higher level of real exchange rate. 16. - This position of the Central Bank, which emphasizes the role of the inflation target as a nominal anchor of our economy, is not an obstacle to the occurrence of those adjustments in relevant relative prices determined by the market. In particular, in stark contrast to its previous high stability, the nominal exchange rate has depreciated by around 10% from October to date, taking full advantage of the margin opened by external conditions. It is important to note that the Central Bank does not intend to unjustifiably curb increases in the exchange rate, but seeks that these increases are based on solid fundamentals and that they are not quickly absorbed by higher inflation. In other words, we seek to make room for the modification of the real exchange rate by the most effective way to contain domestic inflation. Needless to say, success in achieving these goals and the costs to achieve them depend not only on the policies pursued by the Central Bank, but also on the support provided by fiscal policy, especially in periods of fluctuating external conditions. 17. - Consequently, the Central Bank has acted on the monetary front and changed it.
