Thus, the future outlook points to an increase in external inflation to levels slightly above 2%. Third, there are effects on foreign trade volumes. So far this year there has been a severe contraction in the destination markets of some of the exports. Excluding copper exports, the value of exports to Asia has declined by about 15 per cent annually in the first five months of 1998. And, at the same time, there is increased supply pressure from imports from Asia, as a result of the depreciation of currencies and the contraction of the region's markets. Fourth, there is also a reduction in capital inflows through portfolio investments and an increase in the cost of long-term external financing. However, it should be noted that the increases observed have been lower than in other economies in the region and, in absolute terms, Chile's cost of external financing continues to be much lower than that of any other country in the region. Likewise, the favorable investment risk classification achieved by Chile is maintained. 3. The Chilean Economy in the Short and Medium Term 3.1. Short- and medium-term macroeconomic goals In this external context, fiscal and monetary policies have been aimed at directing an orderly process of adjustment of domestic expenditure in order to moderate the current account deficit and maintain a controlled inflationary path. Specifically, these policies aim in the short term to keep the current account deficit for this year within prudent limits, around US 5,000 million and at the same time achieve a reduction of the deficit for next year. In the course of the second half of this year, domestic spending should start to grow below output, and the same should happen over the next year. As a result, the trade balance and the current account will show a progressive improvement. Over the medium term, a moderate current account deficit of around 4% to 5% of GDP is expected, consistent with the stability of external solvency ratios. For the Central Bank, it is an absolute priority to maintain the inflation rate on a path of gradual and persistent reduction. This objective is even more important at a time of relative price adjustment and increased volatility in financial markets. The commitment of policies to price stability plays a key role in anchoring the expectations of economic agents, especially in a highly indexed economy such as Chile's. In the short term, this commitment is expressed in maintaining the inflation target set for this year and, in particular, ensuring conditions for continuing the process of reducing inflation in 1999 and in the years to come. The ultimate goal is to achieve rates similar to those observed among the main industrialized economies in the relatively near future, i.e. around 3a1/o. This is the main contribution of monetary policy and the Central Bank to the development of the country. In the short term, the policies implemented will result in a calculated reduction in the rate of growth of the economy's spending, which, after exhibiting an expansion rate of more than 14% in the first quarter of this year, should fall below the growth of economic activity during the second half of this year. The latter, measured by GDP and affected by lower exports as a result of the Asian crisis and by the effort to contain spending, will show appreciable growth this year (above 5%). In 1999, meanwhile, it should not be substantively different. The trajectory of economic activity will show a further slowdown in the pace of growth in the second half of this year and perhaps early next year, before entering a recovery towards potential growth levels in the following years. As regards monetary policy, it has been pointed out that the Central Bank has been too strict and that there is a risk of over-adjustment. The fact is that this policy has been extremely prudent and in line with events. Indeed, in the face of the - Revenue reduction resulting from the Asian crisis, an adjustment in global spending has been combined with greater space external financing, through a temporarily high current account deficit. It is clear, on the one hand, that if it is not It had acted by tightening monetary policy last January-February, the extraordinary expansion of spending observed towards the end of 97 and the beginning of 98 at a time when the effects of the Asian crisis on external revenues were already felt, the situation today would be unmanageable. On the other hand, the current account deficit will still be temporarily higher, this year and next, than in previous years, reflecting that part of the lower external revenues will be absorbed by greater external financing. 3.2. Policies in implementation The policy measures implemented through the first half of the year are consistent with the fulfilment of the proposed macroeconomic objectives. In the monetary area, the Central Bank has pushed for an increase in the cost of credit in order to deliver relevant price signals for a restriction of private spending by firms and consumers. In the last year, monetary aggregates and global credit have shown a general slowdown in their pace of growth, pointing to the trends that spending should take in the coming months. Also, in exceptional periods of turbulence, monetary policy has been aimed at maintaining tighter control of liquidity in order not to exacerbate these volatilities and speculative cycles against the peso. The result has been marked by specific episodes of increases in short-term interest rates, such as that observed in the last weeks of June and the beginning of July, a situation that has been in the process of progressive normalization. These episodes of high volatility in daily interest rates generate some degree of distortion in the current calculation of the conventional maximum rate, which is based on the monthly weighted average by type of operation, a formula that leaves this rate misaligned when there are sudden short-term movements. For this reason, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions, together with the Central Bank, are working to solve these distortions, seeking to leave the calculation of this interest rate more tied to the liquidity conditions of the interbank market. In the exchange rate area, the actions of the Central Bank have sought to cushion the sudden movements of the nominal exchange rate, allowing an orderly depreciation of the peso to materialize in accordance with the evolution of fundamentals. This action has resulted in a greater presence of the Central Bank in the exchange market, making occasional interventions in order to avoid erratic movements and an overreaction in the exchange rate. In this period the Central Bank has made sales in the exchange markets, thus reversing the trend of accumulation that had occurred in previous years, when International Reserves were bought at or near the floor of the previous band. More recently, the Central Bank has chosen to make this exchange rate policy explicit, narrowing the exchange rate band to an amplitude of 5.5% in the vicinity of the dollar agreement. As is known, the extremes of this band are currently around 456 per dollar per floor and 482 per dollar per ceiling, with daily adjustments according to the dollar agreement rule. This decision was basically taken with the purpose of giving a clearer signal to the market of the range of exchange rate values that the Central Bank considers appropriate to the evolution of the fundamental variables of the Chilean economy, without renouncing a reasonable margin of volatility to accommodate short-term financial changes. It is reiterated that the Central Bank is firmly committed to maintaining the value of the peso within this band. In addition, two new instruments have been incorporated to facilitate the hedging of foreign exchange risks: the issuance of Readjustable Dollar Notes (PRD), which have been widely accepted in the market and have corroborated the hypothesis that a significant part of the demand for foreign currency is due to the interest of the private sector to hedge its exchange positions; and the Retropurchase Pacts (CPR), offered in order to "prune" the most pessimistic expectations of the market. Finally, the reserve requirement in foreign currency was lowered, from 30% to 10%, in order to counteract the increase in the spreads that Chilean companies currently face in their loans from abroad. In this regard, it is important to note that the reduction in the reserve requirement rate is having and will have a significant impact on the Central Bank's international reserves, in the order of US 300 million (out of a total reserves of about US 15,000 million). In the fiscal area, an important effort has been made to promote an adjustment of government and public enterprise expenditures in line with the reduction in government revenues. The successive cuts in current and capital expenditures made in January, April and June add up to US535 million, about 0.7% of GDP, in addition to the creation of the Infrastructure Fund for US125 million. In addition, the government announced its willingness to ensure that public absorption shows an increase this year of around 5.5%, similar to GDP growth, a fact that will allow maintaining a situation of surplus in the fiscal accounts. The impacts of these adjustments should already begin to be observed in the execution results of the second and third quarters of the year. Finally, just as important as the cuts made in 1998 is the announcement of a cautious fiscal policy for 1999. The commitment made to limit the growth of public spending half a percentage point below the growth of the economy is a signal that helps to dispel doubts, especially in a year with presidential elections. In summary, a balanced set of actions involving monetary, exchange rate and fiscal policies has been adopted. This package is consistent with macroeconomic objectives for the short and medium term. 3.3. Results to date The policy mix in place has begun to show its impact on domestic expenditure and, within it, on private consumption and lower inventory accumulation. In the first quarter, GDP showed a moderation in its growth, while domestic demand continued with a high dynamism. However, within demand, the bulk of the increase is explained by the strong accumulation of inventories that occurred in this period, a more volatile and transitory component of expenditure. Preliminary records for the second quarter indicate that domestic demand is likely to show a significant reduction in its growth rate but still above GDP. The ongoing correction should deepen over the next few quarters, and domestic spending growth should be lower than output growth. Within domestic demand, private consumption and inventories are beginning to show greater signs of adjustment, while fixed investment remains highly dynamic. Commitments to reduce the rate of growth of public expenditure should in turn contribute to this trend. On the other hand, net external demand, the result of the volume of exports minus imports, has decreased in the last twelve months, a situation that explains the lower rate of growth of output. Between January and June, the value of "rest" exports showed a significant increase (7%), explained by strong increases in volumes. On the other hand, copper exports decrease by about 23% annually, as a result of the fall in prices, close to 25%. Traditional exports other than copper also show a decrease in volumes influenced by products such as fishmeal (due to lower catches), chopped wood (as a result of lower demand in Korea), pulp logs and certain mining products. Fresh fruit, on the other hand, has shown a recovery with respect to the falls observed in the first quarter, reaching, in the period April - June, an increase in the value of shipments of 34%, compared to the same period of 1997. Within this scenario, it is important to highlight that the most affected exports, copper and other main products, are those whose behavior is less sensitive to the evolution of the exchange rate and possible competitiveness problems, while the performance of non-traditional exports continues to show great dynamism. Imports have shown a downward rate of growth. Within these, consumer imports show a great slowdown. Thus, while in the first quarter they grew slightly above 30% annually, in April they grew at 20%, in May at 15% and in June at 7.5%. In contrast, imports of machinery and equipment maintain a steady rate of expansion of around 13% per year. The progress observed in the moderation of imports should be deepened in the second part of the year. Inflation remains stable, slightly below 5.5 percent annually, and it is estimated that further progress in annual inflation will be seen in the second part of the year, in line with the target set for the end of the year. However, the risks on this front cannot be ignored. Core inflation measures have been on the rise in recent months and nominal cost pressures from imported goods are relevant. The ongoing adjustment and clear signs of commitment to the inflation target have moderated the pass-through of these price pressures. And demand pressures will continue to ease for the rest of the year. Finally, it is important to distinguish between transitory pressures on the price level, resulting from an adjustment in relative prices such as that observed in recent months, from permanent pressures on the inflationary trend. In other words, there are no structural causes in the Chilean economy that prevent continuing to promote a reduction in the inflationary trend during this and the coming years. 4. Conclusions In conclusion, the adjustment programme is proceeding well and results are already observed, such as the evolution of inflation (in an environment of greater inflationary risk) and the moderation of domestic spending. More importantly, the risks facing the Chilean economy at this juncture are limited. Indeed, despite the fact that in real terms the price of copper is at historical lows, the expected values of the main variables such as inflation, growth, unemployment and current account balance are limited within moderate ranges. Thus, the current account deficit will be around US5 billion this year and will be lower in 1999; Inflation is in line with a controlled and downward trajectory and economic growth rates, although they will be affected, will still be positive, remaining about two percentage points below their potential during this and next year. However, this is the least that can be expected in the face of the severity of the Asian crisis and is undoubtedly an absolutely necessary condition for resuming a higher rate of growth with stability from the next millennium. In any case, the growth rates of the Chilean economy this year and next compare favorably with those of most countries in the world. The latest exchange rate policy measures reflect and seek to reaffirm precisely this confidence in the fundamentals of the Chilean economy. In particular, an explicit commitment by the Central Bank to a limited range for the exchange rate has been reinforced. However, the implementation of this macroeconomic programme is not without risk. The external scenario could deteriorate, either by a deepening recession in Asia or by an increase in interest rates in the US economy. The rate of adjustment of domestic demand and imports may be lower than expected or the imported cost pressures observed in previous months could begin to be passed on to a greater extent to inflation. Consequently, fiscal and monetary policy instruments should be more flexible to accommodate changes in circumstances if required. New instruments in the fiscal area would be an enormous contribution to better gauge the impact and distribution of the adjustment policies carried out. On the other hand, an even and compensated reduction in import tariffs, however gradual, would help to make better use of our resources and increase productivity, wages and the real exchange rate. There is no doubt that we are facing a more complex and uncertain external scenario than in previous years, but fundamentals are solid and latent risks are limited. Investment rates are the highest in the last four decades and their return in terms of growth has been amply demonstrated. For more than a decade, exports have shown sustained real growth above GDP. The unemployment rate is at its lowest levels in twenty years and real wages have been growing in line with the high rate of productivity growth. The position of financial solvency is also on excellent footing. For more than a decade, a "strong" system of financial regulation and supervision has been in place. Banks have adequate levels of capitalization and the levels of non-performing loans, although they show some increase, are minimal. The external solvency position, measured as the ratio of net external liabilities to GDP or exports, has been steadily improving over the past decade, and there is no prospect of a deterioration in the coming years. The external liquidity position is also extremely strong. Short-term external debt is minimal and the country has accumulated a high level of International Reserves in relation to imports or liquid financial liabilities. In addition, about half of the current account deficit corresponds to accrued profits that do not constitute liquid obligations. Finally, macroeconomic policies are serious, prudent and alert. The fiscal sector has been showing a sustained surplus for more than a decade, and this year or next should be no exception. Total public, domestic and external sector debt, including debt to the Central Bank, is less than 20 per cent of GDP. The Central Bank's policies have been instrumental in ensuring that inflation has shown a clearly downward trajectory, while exchange rate policy has been flexible enough to facilitate exchange rate adjustments that correspond to major market trends. In any case, faced with a difficult external situation such as the current one, we can expect specific episodes of an erratic nature, such as sharp falls or recoveries in the most important stock markets in the world, or sudden changes in parities between relevant currencies in trade that do not affect the fundamentals of our economy. This requires more than ever a flexible policy approach, one that reacts without overreacting to such events but at the same time acts with force, clarity and determination if events so require. The Central Bank has done so, and will continue to do so.
text_original: Principales Aspectos de la Actual Coyuntura Macroeconmica Exposicin de Carlos Massad, Presidente del Banco Central de Chile, ante la Comisin de Hacienda del Senado, el 5 de agosto de 1998.  Introduccin El desempeo de la economa chilena en el ltimo ao ha sido satisfactorio, a pesar de las mayores dificultades que presenta el escenario externo. En este perodo se ha logrado combinar la reduccin de la inflacin con la mantencin de un ritmo de crecimiento econmico adecuado y una ampliacin acotada del dficit de la cuenta corriente.  El escenario internacional y sus consecuencias sobre la economa chilena 2.1 El escenario internacional Las turbulencias financieras que emergieron en Asia a mediados del ao pasado han tendido a atenuarse, pero los mercados financieros mantienen un estado de mayor sensibilidad, pues an existen dudas importantes respecto de la profundidad y duracin de la crisis en la regin y sobre la forma en que se resolvern los profundos problemas financieros que la afectan. Sin embargo, los efectos globales de la crisis parecen relativamente acotados. Se espera una reduccin del ritmo de expansin econmica mundial respecto de los ltimos dos aos, pero con un impacto menos pronunciado que situaciones anteriores de recesin internacional como 1974-75, 1980-83  1990-91. Las estimaciones de consenso sealan que la economa mundial crecer en torno al 2,5% en 1998 y con una probabilidad de crecimiento similar el prximo ao o incluso una recuperacin hacia tasas cercanas al 3% si hay un repunte en el Asia. Sin embargo, a estas alturas es claro que el reflotamiento de la economa japonesa tomar un tiempo bastante largo. Hay enormes dificultades polticas para llevar a cabo las reformas estructurales que son necesarias para enfrentar la actual crisis, situacin que retardar la recuperacin de este pas y tambin de la regin. Declaraciones recientes de altas autoridades japonesas apuntan claramente en esta direccin. La disminucin en el ritmo de crecimiento de Asia explica ms del 70% de la disminucin del crecimiento mundial esperado para este ao. A este menor dinamismo se agrega una trayectoria de aterrizaje suave de la economa norteamericana y una desaceleracin ms significativa de Latinoamrica. Las economas europeas, en tanto, mantienen un crecimiento similar al del ao pasado y se proyecta su continuacin en 1998. La crisis de Asia ayudar a mantener la trayectoria de reduccin en la inflacin mundial que se ha observado en los ltimos aos. En efecto, el debilitamiento global de la demanda y la actividad econmica, las reducciones de los precios internacionales de las materias primas y las devaluaciones de Asia ejercern un efecto negativo sobre el nivel global de la inflacin. A su vez, las favorables perspectivas inflacionarias y la mayor preferencia de los inversionistas internacionales por las monedas, mercados e instrumentos considerados ms seguros han llevado a una disminucin de las tasas de inters de los pases industriales, al menos respecto de los niveles que se esperaban con anterioridad a la crisis. Ello ha conducido hacia una cada de las tasas de inters de largo plazo en las principales monedas. Por el contrario, las tasas de inters de las economas emergentes han tendido a aumentar en forma generalizada. A su vez, los flujos de capital hacia los pases emergentes, especialmente los flujos de cartera, han sufrido una disminucin significativa durante el presente ao. Finalmente, la crisis de los pases del sudeste asitico ha conllevado un menor dinamismo de la demanda de los principales productos bsicos, en particular, de cobre y petrleo. Los ndices de precios de bienes primarios muestran descensos sobre el 20% en un ao, medido en dlares. El mercado internacional de cobre ha presentado un escenario deprimido durante los ltimos meses, lo que ha conducido el precio hasta niveles en torno a 75c/lb. Si bien los inventarios han mostrado una tendencia decreciente desde fines del primer trimestre, sta no ha sido suficiente como para impulsar el precio del cobre. Por otra parte, el panorama externo tampoco es favorable para esperar la recuperacin del precio en el corto plazo. Las perspectivas de crecimiento mundial no indican una recuperacin rpida y para el perodo 1998-2000 se espera un aumento de la capacidad de produccin de cobre. En conclusin, es prudente suponer que, al menos durante lo que resta del presente ao y parte del prximo, la situacin no variar significativamente respecto de los niveles actuales.  Consecuencias sobre la economa chilena Los efectos del deterioro en el escenario externo sobre la economa nacional son variados. En primer lugar, se estima una reduccin de los trminos de intercambio entre 5% y 10% para el presente ao. La principal disminucin se observa en el precio del cobre y otros minerales, cadas que se ven parcialmente compensadas por la disminucin observada en los precios de las importaciones hacia Chile. La disminucin de trminos de intercambio reduce el ingreso nacional y tiende a elevar el dficit de la cuenta corriente. En segundo lugar, se observa una cada en el nivel absoluto de precios de las importaciones para Chile, situacin que reduce las presiones de inflacin importada. Sin embargo, esta situacin no puede proyectarse a futuro, considerando que es menos probable que el dlar contine el ritmo de apreciacin internacional que se ha venido observando en el ltimo ao. As, las perspectivas futuras sealan un incremento de la inflacin externa hasta niveles levemente superiores al 2%. En tercer lugar, hay efectos sobre los volmenes de comercio exterior. En lo que va corrido de este ao se ha producido una severa contraccin de los mercados de destino de algunas de las exportaciones. Excluyendo las exportaciones de cobre, el valor de las exportaciones al Asia se ha reducido en cerca de 15% anual en los primeros cinco meses de 1998. Y, al mismo tiempo, existe una mayor presin de oferta de importaciones desde Asia, como consecuencia de la depreciacin de las monedas y la contraccin de los mercados de la regin. En cuarto lugar, tambin se detecta una reduccin en los flujos de entrada de capital por inversiones de cartera y un aumento en el costo de financiamiento externo de largo plazo. Sin embargo, hay que destacar que los aumentos observados han sido menores en relacin a lo registrado en otras economas de la regin y, en trminos absolutos, el costo del financiamiento externo de Chile sigue siendo muy inferior al de cualquier otro pas de la regin. Asimismo, se mantiene la favorable clasificacin de riesgo de inversin alcanzada por Chile.  La Economa Chilena en el Corto y Mediano Plazo  Las metas macroeconmicas de corto y mediano plazo En este contexto externo, las polticas fiscal y monetaria se han dirigido a encauzar un proceso ordenado de ajuste del gasto interno con el fin de moderar el dficit de la cuenta corriente y mantener una trayectoria inflacionaria controlada. En concreto, estas polticas apuntan en el corto plazo a mantener el dficit de cuenta corriente para el presente ao dentro de lmites prudentes, en torno a los US$5.000 millones y al mismo tiempo lograr una reduccin del dficit para el prximo ao. En el curso del segundo semestre del presente ao, el gasto interno debe comenzar a crecer por debajo del producto, y lo mismo debe ocurrir durante el prximo ao. Como consecuencia de lo anterior, la balanza comercial y la cuenta corriente presentarn una mejora progresiva. En el mediano plazo se prev un dficit de la cuenta corriente moderado, del orden del 4% al 5% del PIB, coherente con la estabilidad de las relaciones de solvencia externa. Para el Banco Central es absolutamente prioritario mantener la tasa de inflacin sobre una trayectoria de reduccin gradual y persistente. Este objetivo es an ms importante en una etapa de ajuste de precios relativos y mayor volatilidad en los mercados financieros. El compromiso de las polticas con la estabilidad de precios desempea un rol clave para anclar las expectativas de los agentes econmicos, especialmente en una economa altamente indizada como la chilena. En el corto plazo, este compromiso se expresa en mantener la meta de inflacin planteada para el presente ao y, especialmente, asegurar condiciones para continuar el proceso de reduccin de la inflacin en 1999 y en los aos venideros. El objetivo final es alcanzar en un horizonte relativamente cercano tasas similares a las que se observan entre las principales economas industrializadas, esto es, en torno al 3/o. Esta es la principal contribucin de la poltica monetaria y el Banco Central al desarrollo del pas. En el corto plazo, las polticas implementadas se traducirn en una reduccin calculada del ritmo de crecimiento del gasto de la economa, el que, luego de exhibir una tasa de expansin superior al 14% en el primer trimestre del presente ao, debiera caer por debajo del crecimiento de la actividad econmica durante el segundo semestre en curso. Esta ltima, medida por el PIB y afectada por las menores exportaciones a raz de la crisis asitica y por el propio esfuerzo de contencin del gasto, mostrar en el presente ao de todas formas un crecimiento apreciable (por sobre el 5%). En 1999, en tanto, no debiera ser sustantivamente diferente. La trayectoria de la actividad econmica mostrar una desaceleracin adicional del ritmo de crecimiento en el segundo semestre de este ao y tal vez a principios del prximo, para luego entrar en una recuperacin hacia los niveles de crecimiento potencial en los aos siguientes. En cuanto a la poltica monetaria, se ha sealado que el Banco Central ha sido demasiado estricto y que se arriesga un sobreajuste. Lo cierto es que esta poltica ha sido extremadamente prudente y ajustada a los acontecimientos. En efecto, frente a la reduccin de ingresos resultante de la crisis asitica, se ha combinado un ajuste en el gasto global con un espacio de mayor financiamiento externo, a travs de un dficit en la cuenta corriente transitoriamente alto. Es evidente, por una parte, que si no se hubiese actuado endureciendo la poltica monetaria en enero-febrero pasados, la extraordinaria expansin del gasto observada hacia fines del 97 y principios del 98 en un momento en que ya se sentan los efectos de la crisis asitica sobre los ingresos externos, la situacin hoy da sera inmanejable. Por otro lado, el dficit en la cuenta corriente de todas formas ser transitoriamente mayor, este ao y el prximo, al de aos anteriores, lo cual refleja que parte de los menores ingresos externos sern absorbidos por un mayor financiamiento externo.  Las polticas en implementacin Las medidas de poltica que se han implementado a travs del primer semestre del ao son coherentes con el cumplimiento de los objetivos macroeconmicos propuestos. En el rea monetaria, el Banco Central ha impulsado un incremento en el costo del crdito con el fin de entregar las seales de precios relevantes para una restriccin del gasto privado de empresas y consumidores. En el ltimo ao, los agregados monetarios y el crdito global han mostrado una desaceleracin generalizada en su ritmo de crecimiento, sealando las tendencias que debe tomar el gasto en los prximos meses. Asimismo, en perodos excepcionales de turbulencias, la poltica monetaria se ha dirigido a mantener un control ms estricto de la liquidez con el fin de no exacerbar estas volatilidades y ciclos especulativos contra el peso. El resultado ha sido marcado por episodios puntuales de incrementos en las tasas de inters de corto plazo, como el observado en las ltimas semanas de junio y primeras de julio, situacin que ha do en proceso de progresiva normalizacin. Estos episodios de alta volatilidad en las tasas de inters diarias, generan algn grado de distorsin en el clculo actual de la tasa mxima convencional, el cual se realiza en base al promedio ponderado mensual por tipo de operacin, frmula que deja a esta tasa desalineada cuando hay movimientos bruscos de corto plazo. Por tal motivo, la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras en conjunto con el Banco Central, se encuentran trabajando para solucionar estas distorsiones, buscando dejar el clculo de esta tasa de inters ms amarrado a las condiciones de liquidez del mercado interbancario. En el rea cambiara, las acciones del Banco Central han buscado amortiguar los movimientos bruscos del tipo de cambio nominal, permitiendo que se materialice una depreciacin ordenada del peso en concordancia con la evolucin de los fundamentos. Este accionar se ha traducido en una mayor presencia del Banco Central en el mercado cambiarlo, realizando intervenciones ocasionales con el fin de evitar que se produzcan movimientos errticos y una sobrerreaccin en el tipo de cambio. En este perodo el Banco Central ha realizado ventas en los mercados cambiarlos, revirtiendo as la tendencia de acumulacin que se haba producido en aos anteriores, cuando se compraron Reservas Internacionales al piso o cerca del piso de la anterior banda. Ms recientemente, el Banco Central ha optado por explicitar esta poltica cambiara, angostando la banda cambiara a una amplitud de 5,5% en la vecindad del dlar acuerdo. Como es conocido, los extremos de esta banda se encuentran en la actualidad en torno a $456 por dlar el piso y $482 por dlar el techo, con reajustes diarios segn la regla del dlar acuerdo. Esta decisin se tom bsicamente con el propsito de dar una seal ms clara al mercado del rango de valores del tipo de cambio que al Banco Central le parecen adecuados a la evolucin de las variables fundamentales de la economa chilena, sin renunciar a un margen de volatilidad razonable para acomodar cambios financieros de corto plazo. Se reitera que el Banco Central est firmemente comprometido a mantener el valor del peso dentro de esta banda. Asimismo, se han incorporado dos nuevos instrumentos para facilitar la cobertura de riesgos cambiarios: la emisin de Pagars Reajustables en Dlares (PRD), que han tenido gran aceptacin en el mercado y han corroborado la hiptesis de que una parte importante de la demanda por moneda extranjera obedece al inters del sector privado por cubrir sus posiciones cambiaras; y los Pactos de Retrocompra (CPR), ofrecidos con el fin de "podar" las expectativas ms pesimistas del mercado. Por ltimo, se rebaj el encaje en moneda extranjera, de 30% a 10%, con el fin de contrarrestar el aumento en los spreads que hoy da enfrentan las empresas chilenas en sus crditos del exterior. A este respecto, es importante notar que la reduccin de la tasa de encaje est teniendo y tendr en los prximos meses un impacto relevante sobre las reservas internacionales del Banco Central, del orden de los US$ 300 millones (de un total de reservas de cerca de US$ 15.000 millones). En el rea fiscal, se ha realizado un esfuerzo de importancia para impulsar un ajuste de los gastos del gobierno y de las empresas pblicas acorde con la reduccin de ingresos del gobierno. Los sucesivos recortes de gastos corrientes y de capital realizados en enero, abril y junio suman a la fecha US$535 millones, cerca de 0,7% del PIB, a lo que se suma la creacin del Fondo de Infraestructura por US$125 millones. Adems, el gobierno anunci su disposicin a cautelar que la absorcin pblica muestre un incremento este ao en torno al 5,5%, similar al crecimiento del PIB, hecho que permitir mantener una situacin de supervit en las cuentas fiscales. Los impactos de estos ajustes ya debieran comenzar a observarse en los resultados de ejecucin del segundo y tercer trimestre del ao. Finalmente, tan importante como los recortes realizados en 1998, es el anuncio de una poltica fiscal cautelosa para 1999. El compromiso adquirido para acotar el crecimiento del gasto pblico medio punto porcentual por debajo del crecimiento de la economa es una seal que contribuye a despejar dudas, especialmente en un ao con elecciones presidenciales. En resumen, se ha adoptado un conjunto equilibrado de acciones que involucra las polticas monetaria, cambiara y fiscal. Este conjunto es coherente con los objetivos macroeconmicos para el corto y mediano plazo.  Los resultados hasta la fecha La combinacin de polticas en aplicacin ha comenzado a mostrar su impacto sobre el gasto interno y, dentro de ste, sobre el consumo privado y la menor acumulacin de inventarios. En el primer trimestre, el PIB mostr una moderacin de su crecimiento, mientras que la demanda interna continu con un alto dinamismo. Sin embargo, dentro de la demanda el grueso del incremento se explica por la fuerte acumulacin de existencias que se produjo en este perodo, componente de carcter ms voltil y transitorio dentro del gasto. Los antecedentes preliminares para el segundo trimestre sealan que la demanda interna probablemente mostrar una reduccin importante en su tasa de crecimiento pero an por encima del PIB. La correccin en proceso debe profundizarse en el curso de los prximos trimestres, y el crecimiento del gasto interno debera ser menor al crecimiento del producto. Dentro de la demanda interna, el consumo privado y los inventarios comienzan a mostrar mayores seales de ajuste, mientras que la inversin fija mantiene un elevado dinamismo. Los compromisos de reduccin del ritmo de crecimiento del gasto pblico debieran a su vez colaborar en esta tendencia. Por su parte, la demanda externa neta, el resultado del volumen de exportaciones menos las importaciones, presenta una disminucin en los ltimos doce meses, situacin que explica el menor ritmo de crecimiento del producto. Entre enero y junio, el valor de las exportaciones "resto" mostr un incremento importante (7%), explicado por fuertes incrementos en volmenes. En cambio, las exportaciones de cobre disminuyen cerca de 23% anual, como consecuencia de la cada en precios, cercana al 25%. Las exportaciones tradicionales distintas del cobre, tambin muestran una disminucin de volmenes influida por productos como la harina de pescado (debido a menores capturas), la madera trozada (como consecuencia de menor demanda en Corea), los rollizos para pulpa y ciertos productos mineros. La fruta fresca, en cambio, ha mostrado una recuperacin respecto de las cadas observadas en el primer trimestre, llegndose, en el lapso abril - junio, a un aumento en el valor de los embarques de 34%, con respecto de igual perodo de 1997. Dentro de este panorama, es importante destacar que las exportaciones ms afectadas, cobre y otros productos principales, son aquellas cuyo comportamiento es menos sensible a la evolucin del tipo de cambio y eventuales problemas de competitividad, mientras que el desempeo de las exportaciones no tradicionales contina evidenciando un gran dinamismo. Las importaciones han mostrado un ritmo de crecimiento descendente. Dentro de stas, las importaciones de consumo muestran una gran desaceleracin. As, mientras en el primer trimestre crecieron levemente por sobre el 30% anual, en abril crecan al 20%, en mayo al 15 % y en junio al 7,5%. En contraste, las importaciones de maquinaria y equipos mantienen un ritmo constante de expansin en torno al 13% anual. Los progresos observados en la moderacin de las importaciones deben profundizarse en la segunda parte del ao. La inflacin se mantiene estable, levemente por debajo de 5,5% anual, y se estima que en la segunda parte del ao se observarn progresos adicionales en la inflacin anual, en lnea con la meta planteada para fines de ao. Sin embargo, no se pueden desconocer los riesgos en este frente. Las mediciones de inflacin subyacente han registrado un comportamiento al alza en meses recientes y las presiones de costos nominales provenientes de los bienes importados son relevantes. El ajuste en marcha y las claras seales de compromiso con la meta de inflacin han moderado el traspaso de estas presiones a precios. Y en lo que resta del ao continuarn disminuyendo las presiones de demanda. Por ltimo, es importante distinguir entre las presiones transitorias sobre el nivel de precios, derivadas de un ajuste de precios relativos como el que se ha observado en los ltimos meses, de las presiones permanentes sobre la tendencia inflacionaria. En otras palabras, no hay causas estructurales en la economa chilena que impidan continuar impulsando una reduccin en la tendencia inflacionaria durante ste y los prximos aos.  Conclusiones En conclusin, el programa de ajuste est marchando adecuadamente y ya se observan resultados, como la evolucin de la inflacin (en un ambiente de mayor riesgo inflacionario) y la moderacin del gasto interno. Ms importante es destacar que los riesgos que enfrenta la economa chilena en la presente coyuntura son acotados. En efecto, a pesar de que en trminos reales el precio del cobre se encuentra en niveles mnimos histricos, los valores esperados de las principales variables como inflacin, crecimiento, desempleo y saldo de la cuenta corriente, estn acotados dentro de rangos moderados. As, el dficit corriente se situar en torno a los US$5.000 millones en el presente ao y ser inferior en 1999; la inflacin est en lnea con una trayectoria controlada y descendente y las tasas de crecimiento econmico, aunque se vern afectadas, de todas formas sern positivas situndose unos dos puntos porcentuales por debajo de su potencial durante ste y el prximo ao. Sin embargo, esto es lo menos que se puede esperar frente a la severidad de la crisis asitica y es, sin duda, una condicin absolutamente necesaria para retomar un ritmo mayor de crecimiento con estabilidad a partir del prximo milenio. En cualquier caso, las tasas de crecimiento de la economa chilena este ao y el prximo se comparan favorablemente con las de la mayora de los pases del mundo. Las ltimas medidas de poltica cambiara reflejan y buscan reafirmar precisamente esta confianza en los fundamentos de la economa chilena. En particular, se ha reforzado un compromiso explcito del Banco Central con un rango acotado para el tipo de cambio. Sin embargo, la realizacin de este programa macroeconmico no est exenta de riesgos. El escenario externo podra verse desmejorado, ya sea por una profundizacin de la recesin en Asia o por un incremento de las tasas de inters de la economa norteamericana. La velocidad de ajuste de la demanda interna y las importaciones podra ser menor a lo esperado o las presiones de costos importados que se han observado en los meses anteriores podran comenzar a traspasarse en mayor medida a inflacin. En consecuencia, el instrumental de polticas fiscal y monetaria debe presentar un grado mayor de flexibilidad para acomodarse a cambios en las circunstancias si as es requerido. Nuevos instrumentos en el rea fiscal seran una enorme contribucin para calibrar de mejor forma el impacto y distribucin de las polticas de ajuste llevadas a cabo. Por su parte, una reduccin pareja y compensada de aranceles de importacin, por gradual que sea, ayudara a usar mejor nuestros recursos y a incrementar la productividad, las remuneraciones y el tipo de cambio real. Es indudable que se enfrenta un escenario externo ms complejo e incierto que en aos anteriores, pero los fundamentos son slidos y los riesgos latentes estn acotados. Las tasas de inversin son las ms altas de las ltimas cuatro dcadas y su retorno en trminos de crecimiento ha sido ampliamente demostrado. Las exportaciones han mostrado por ms de una dcada un crecimiento real sostenido y superior al PIB. La tasa de desempleo se encuentra en los niveles ms bajos de los ltimos veinte aos y los salarios reales han venido creciendo en forma acorde con la elevada tasa de crecimiento de la productividad. La posicin de solvencia financiera tambin est en excelente pie. Por ms de una dcada, se ha implementado un sistema de regulacin y supervisin financiera "fuerte". La banca cuenta con niveles adecuados de capitalizacin y los niveles de cartera vencida, aunque muestran algn incremento, son mnimos. La posicin de solvencia externa, medida como la relacin de pasivos externos netos a PIB o respecto de exportaciones, ha do en continua mejora a lo largo de la ltima dcada, y no hay perspectivas de un desmejoramiento en los prximos aos. Asimismo, la posicin de liquidez externa es extraordinariamente slida. La deuda externa de corto plazo es mnima y el pas ha acumulado un elevado nivel de Reservas Internacionales en relacin a las importaciones o a los pasivos financieros lquidos. Adems, cerca de la mitad del dficit de la cuenta corriente corresponde a utilidades devengadas que no constituyen obligaciones lquidas. Finalmente, las polticas macroeconmicas son serias, prudentes y alertas. El sector fiscal ha venido mostrando un supervit sostenido por ms de un decenio y este ao o el prximo no deben ser la excepcin. La deuda total del sector pblico, interna y externa, incluida la deuda con el Banco Central, es inferior al 20% del PIB. Las polticas del Banco Central han sido determinantes para que la inflacin haya mostrado una trayectoria claramente descendente, en tanto la poltica cambiara ha sido lo suficientemente flexible como para facilitar los ajustes del tipo de cambio que corresponden a las grandes tendencias del mercado. En todo caso, frente a una situacin externa difcil como la actual, cabe esperar episodios puntuales de carcter errtico, como fuertes cadas o recuperaciones en las bolsas ms importantes del mundo, o bruscos cambios de paridades entre monedas relevantes en el comercio que no afectan los fundamentos de nuestra economa. Ello requiere ms que nunca un enfoque de polticas flexibles, que reaccione sin sobrerreaccionar frente a tales eventos pero que, a la vez, acte con fuerza, claridad y decisin si los acontecimientos as lo exigen. El Banco Central as lo ha hecho, y lo seguir haciendo.

Title: Speech by the President of the Central Bank of Chile to the Senate
text: Valpara92so, 8 September 1998 SPEECH BY THE PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE TO THE SENATE ON THE OCCASION OF THE PRESENTATION OF THE 1998 ANNUAL REPORT I. Introduction What began as a crisis that seemed limited to an Asian country transformed into what is now recognized as a global crisis. The weakness of financial systems and the lack of complete information on external obligations amplified what could have been a simple process of adjusting a deficit current account into a problem that infected many countries. The violent devaluation of their currencies, instead of lessening the difficulties, aggravated them, and the loss of market confidence spread to emerging countries, even Latin America. The Chilean economy is facing difficult times. Although its fundamentals are solid, the external crisis, with its negative effects on foreign trade and the capital account, forces us to moderate the pace of economic growth until stability in international markets is restored. The fragility of the global economy requires discipline and prudence in the formulation of macroeconomic objectives and flexibility in policy implementation. The macroeconomic program presented in this Senate Report seeks to meet these requirements. The main objective of this programme is to strengthen domestic and external macroeconomic and financial stability, within a very restrictive international framework. To achieve this, it proposes to gradually reduce the current account deficit on a sustainable path in the medium and long term, consolidate the enormous progress made in reducing inflation and achieve, as a result, a rate of economic growth in the short term consistent with the adverse global scenario. This will open the doors to resume in the coming years the rapid process of economic and social development that has characterized our country in this decade. The outlook for the trajectory of the world economy over the next two years has deteriorated progressively as the real extent of the recession in Asia and the extent of its effects to the rest of the world's economies become known. Likewise, the volatility of international financial markets that are de facto closed for the vast majority of emerging countries persists. These external developments have important consequences for the Chilean economy. On the one hand, the slowdown in the global economy has reduced the dynamism of demand for major commodities. In particular, the price of copper has fluctuated near 75 cents a pound in recent months, almost 20 cents below initial expectations, and the external outlook is not favorable to expect a rebound in this price in the short term. Adding the increases and decreases in other prices, it is estimated that for this year the reduction in the terms of trade will reach about 10%, which subtracts from national income the equivalent of two percentage points, about US 1,600 million. Our country is 1.6 billion dollars poorer as a result of external factors. On the other hand, in this scenario of greater uncertainty, international investors have turned to currencies, markets and instruments considered safer, driving a strong generalized increase in the cost of external financing of emerging economies and a reduction in the volume of capital flows to these countries. In the particular case of the Chilean economy, there has also been a greater demand from companies, financial institutions and individuals resident in Chile to accumulate assets abroad, increasing the international diversification of their portfolio and covering risks associated with exchange rate fluctuations. However, there are also internal developments of importance to understand the current conjuncture. In recent years, domestic demand has been characterized by a high dynamism. This period has seen a marked and sustained increase in the total investment rate, reaching 27 per cent of GDP in 1997, without being accompanied by a similar increase in national savings, all measured at current prices. Indeed, the savings rate has remained practically stable in the last six years, with fluctuations around an average of 21% of GDP. Another way of looking at the same thing, the current account deficit has been gradually widening over the last few years. This development is a consequence of the prevailing optimism at the level of companies and consumers within a context of greater availability of domestic and external financing. Indeed, there has been increasing pressure for funds in the domestic credit market, driving up domestic interest rates and, at the same time, greater use of external savings (current account deficit). For its part, the strong appetite of international investors to increase their participation in the Chilean economy, even paying the cost of reserve requirements to external financing, has more than provided the necessary resources to finance this deficit. Thus, during 1997 the economy received net external resources of approximately 10% of GDP, almost double the financing requirements of the current account deficit. The difference increased the Central Bank's reserves. In this context of strong domestic demand pressures, the external crisis and its negative impact on the terms of trade and the supply of external financing, as well as the increase in demand for foreign assets, made it inevitable to apply an effort to contain domestic demand to bring the current account deficit towards levels in line with the new international scenario. For its part, the national financial system is in a solid position. The indicator of annualized profitability of banks reached levels close to 14% in July, a figure that is considered adequate. Likewise, the growth of placements in twelve months, although declining, currently remains above 12% and the non-performing loan portfolio as a percentage of total placements, remains at reasonable levels, around 1.2%. The information regarding the private risk classification of financial institutions indicates that the risk of bank and financial instruments has improved compared to last year. It should be noted that the capital requirement of the financial system, measured around the Basel Indicator, as of June shows a capitalization level of 11.5% on risky assets, almost 2% more than last year. Despite the soundness of the financial system, the greater uncertainty at the global level, the changes in relative prices underway and the process of adjusting the economy's growth in the face of the external crisis, make it necessary to strengthen the supervision of financial markets and modernize some regulations in order to reconcile the opening of new spaces for financial activity with the necessary improvement of prudential standards. II. Policies in application In the recent period, the economic policy mix has been geared towards achieving a prudent mix between increased external financing and correction of the level of domestic spending. The actions of the Central Bank have sought to promote an orderly adjustment of relative prices and avoid a deterioration in the trend of reducing inflation. Among the main measures adopted are the application of a monetary policy with a more restrictive stance from January of this year, together with a greater degree of flexibility in the management of liquidity and the realization of occasional interventions in the foreign exchange market. More recently, on June 25, the implementation of a narrower band as a guide for the exchange rate, the provision of new foreign exchange hedging instruments and the reduction of foreign currency reserve requirements were announced. In order to avoid a short-term overreaction in the value of the exchange rate and facilitate the process of portfolio recomposition, the Central Bank has sold foreign currency on different occasions in the exchange market, thus reversing the accumulation trend that had occurred in previous years, when international assets were purchased at or near the floor of the previous floating band of the exchange rate. In addition, over the past eight months, and as a result of heightened international uncertainty, monetary policy has been aimed at allowing a greater degree of flexibility in short-term interest rates. This has sought to avoid exacerbating volatilities in the exchange rate and curbing speculative processes against the peso, through stricter control of liquidity in national currency. This is an appropriate response to deal with periods of financial turbulence; this is demonstrated by international evidence and, in particular, by recent experience of Southeast Asian economies. This situation became more evident in the months of January and June, as well as in the last weeks of August as a result of the crisis in Russia. In fact, the sharp increases of more than 1,000 basis points experienced by the spreads of the external debt of almost all emerging countries, together with the expectations of currency depreciation, generate very high domestic interest rates in all of them. There is no doubt that in periods of turbulence and uncertainty such as the current one, the defense of macroeconomic stability can generate costs, both in terms of higher interest rates and the moderation of the growth rate, but such defense is essential to avoid the enormous losses that can bring the deterioration of confidence in macroeconomic management. International evidence, and especially the recent experience of the countries of South-East Asia, clearly shows that a hesitant policy, which does not decide to adopt the necessary adjustment measures, can end in a loss of financial confidence, a situation that entails devastating consequences in the banking system, and enormous and lasting losses in production and employment. as well as setbacks in political and social stability. For its part, fiscal policy has promoted an additional moderation of domestic spending, making cuts to the expenditure budget of the Treasury and public companies. The impact of these cuts should operate fully in the second half of 1998, so that the growth of public absorption for the rest of the year should be below the growth observed in its first part. Also as important as the cuts made in 1998 is the announcement of a cautious fiscal policy for 1999. The announced commitment to limit the growth of public spending to half a percentage point below the growth of the economy, that is, an increase not exceeding 3.3% real, is a signal that helps to dispel doubts, especially in a year with presidential elections. This commitment and its fulfillment is highly valued by the Central Bank, as is the willingness to make further adjustments if necessary. It should also be noted that the commitment already assumed significantly limits the possible adjustment to be granted in the negotiations of salaries in the public sector. The contribution of public expenditure to reducing the rate of growth of total expenditure in the economy is a contribution to the growth of the economy. As public spending targets become effective, the necessary level of interest rates will be reduced to achieve the desired adjustment, while strengthening the external sector of our economy. Without the adjustment of public spending, the burden that would fall on the productive sector of the economy and on employment would be even greater. I must point out here that, on returning from our recent trip to Washington, we discussed with the Minister of Finance the advisability of making an even greater effort, bringing the growth of public spending below 3.3%. The Minister has welcomed this comment. The most recent record indicates that the main economic variablesd1growth, current account, and inflationd1are moving in the right direction. In the first half of this year, the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) increased by 6.3% compared to the same period of the previous year, while domestic demand grew by 10% in the same period, but on a path of moderation. The outlook for the current account deficit remains within reasonable limits given external circumstances; and inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed a decrease from 6.0% observed at the end of last year to 5.2% last August. For its part, preliminary information shows that total imports, for the first time, have been reduced in absolute terms in August compared to August last year, and also compared to July this year. There is no doubt that the adjustment process is underway. The macroeconomic programme presented in this report for this and next year is based on the consolidation of these trends. III. The Goals of the Macroeconomic Program First, the inflation rate must continue on a path of gradual decline. In the short term, this commitment is expressed in achieving the inflation target set for this year, recognizing that the pressures coming from the weakening of the peso and the inertia in the pace of growth of nominal wages could delay that achievement by a few months. Macroeconomic policies will also be geared towards around /-4.3% in 1999, with continued progress towards price stability in the coming years. Perseverance in the objective of reducing inflation is a fundamental element in framing the prudence and discipline required of all economic policies. The forced cooling of the economy and the favorable trajectory of international inflation open spaces to make additional progress towards price stability, without generating costs on the economy. The downward inflation target complements the expected correction in other macroeconomic variables such as the level of domestic spending and the current account deficit, while helping to stabilize financial markets and strengthening the economic policy package. So far, inflation measured by the CPI has remained stable so far this year, fluctuating slightly above 5.0% annually. In this period, the moderation in the pace of inflation has been favoured by the normalisation shown by the prices of perishable goods and the decline in fuel prices. However, core inflation indicators, unlike CPI inflation, show a slightly upward trajectory through the year. This increase is partly explained by increases in the prices of non-tradable items and, in particular, services. This upward trend in core inflation measures is a consequence of higher domestic demand pressures that began to deepen in the second half of last year, the push in wage costs and higher import cost pressures. Despite this upward trend, the current scenario is conducive to consolidating progress in reducing inflation over the coming quarters. The more moderate performance of sales and the accumulation of surplus capacity will lead to a reduction in trade margins and, in the same way, the wage increases observed so far should tend to moderate in the coming months or, alternatively, the pace of employment growth will show even greater signs of adjustment. In addition, the decrease in raw material costs and the reduction in import prices in dollars for this year, as well as a positive but low level of external inflation for next year, will reduce external inflationary pressures. The consolidation of the expected results in the reduction of wage costs and domestic inflation pressures require that public and private wage negotiations be framed within the parameters of lower inflation and productivity growth expected for this and next year. Otherwise, imbalances will occur that will eventually be reflected in higher unemployment. I would like to reiterate on this occasion that, under the conditions of adjustment indispensable for the Chilean economy, it is extremely important to recognize the need to moderate wage pressures in order to avoid unnecessarily high increases in unemployment rates. In times of tightness, it is inevitable to choose between higher wages or maintaining employment. Demand constraints will, at the same time, prevent widespread increases in trade margins or profits. Second, the current account deficit in 1998 is estimated to reach around US 5.15 billion, but on a path of reduction towards next year, to around US 4.5 billion in 1999 (around 5.5% of GDP). The projected figure for this year is above the deficit that was expected a year ago, US 4,400 million, which represents a prudent increase in the use of financing in foreign trade, but at the same time it is at least US 1,000 million lower than what could have been generated without the adjustment process in implementation. Thus, a gradual adjustment of the external sector is sought to minimize negative effects on the product. In the medium term, a further reduction in the current account deficit is sought to reach more moderate levels, in the order of 4% to 5% of GDP, which necessarily poses the challenge of substantially increasing domestic savings if we want to maintain growth as we have become accustomed to in the last decade. For this year as a whole, the volume of sales abroad would grow above 7.0%, led by the growth of non-traditional exports. This result compares favorably with previous periods of slowdown in the world economy, in which Chilean exports have experienced more marked declines in their growth rate. Thus, exports continue to show a sustained rate of expansion and higher than GDP growth, as has happened almost continuously over the last decade. No significant changes in export commodity prices are expected for next year. For its part, the volume of shipments abroad would experience an increase of approximately 10%, a result that is strongly influenced by the increase of about 15% in copper shipments expected for 1999. For its part, the process of adjustment of imports is expected to be accentuated in the second half of this year, and its growth would be very moderate in 1999, consistent with the expected evolution of domestic demand. Third, the correction in the balance of the external accounts requires accentuating the effort to contain domestic demand in the remainder of this year and next. In the short term, this situation, together with the lower boost in external demand, will lead to a moderation in the rate of growth of economic activity in 1998, which will in any case be an appreciable figure (around 5%). At the same time, domestic demand growth in 1999 is required to be very moderate, which, together with the pick-up in net external demand -- that is, the gap between exports and imports -- would bring GDP growth to about 3.8 percent. This result, although close to half the trend growth of the last decade, is adequate considering the complex external scenario and represents almost double the projected global growth for 1999. To the extent that the expected corrections in the ratio of expenditure to national income continue to advance and that there is no further deterioration of the external scenario, the economy will be in the appropriate conditions to enter a phase of gradual acceleration that will lead to growth rates closer to its potential. In any case, it should not be lost sight of the fact that the average economic growth of the present decade, even with the moderate expansion expected for 1999, is the highest of this century. Despite the short-term contingencies, we must not lose sight of the fact that the medium-term fundamentals of the Chilean economy remain solid, and that it is possible to continue showing a performance as successful as that of the last decade going forward. Ultimately, the economy's growth potential depends on its ability to invest in physical and human capital, the flexibility of markets and entrepreneurship to incorporate new technologies and develop new products and services. At present, the fixed investment rate is the highest since historical records exist, progress has been observed in the level of education of the labor force and new sectors are emerging that take the lead in economic growth. Looking ahead, the main constraint to resuming the path of high and sustained growth is the effort of domestic savings. The national savings rate must increase to at least 23% of GDP, about two points more than the average of the last six years, in order to maintain the investment rate at a level similar to that observed in recent years, while the current account deficit does not exceed prudent limits. in the range of 4% to 5% of GDP. That is the task ahead. IV. Conclusions The Chilean economy is facing complex times. The Asian crisis, with its effects on foreign trade and the cost and availability of external financing, has tested and will continue to test the country's willingness to face the challenges associated with these times of turbulence and international uncertainty. While the financial position is healthy and the economy has its solid fundamentals, now is the time to reaffirm conviction in prudent and demanding macroeconomic policies. It is impossible for the country to maintain growth close to potential as long as the external turbulence does not subside and a process of recovery of stability in world markets is consolidated. Failure to recognize that a relatively harsher period must be faced would have an irremediably negative effect on the country's economic management, a situation that in itself would significantly deepen the effects of the Asian crisis. The globalization of markets and Chile's strong link with the rest of the world, which have allowed the country a decade of sustained growth, also contain a disciplining element on the management of macroeconomic policies that cannot be ignored and that requires a permanently cautious attitude and great zeal in defense of stability precisely in times of trial. Easy solutions do not exist. All come with costs. At the current juncture, it is necessary to reaffirm the commitment to the process of gradual but persistent reduction of inflation, to a figure close to 3% per year, as well as to pursue the aim of reducing the current account deficit from 1999 until it reaches reasonable levels between 4% and 5% of GDP in the medium term. Monetary policy instruments need to be applied in a manner consistent with these purposes, relying on the continuation of a responsible and time-adjusted fiscal policy. The success of this enterprise will mean that the national economy will return to its potential growth in the coming years, and that increases in the unemployment rate and the reduction in the rate of growth of wages will be limited and also temporary phenomena. But that success depends crucially on the credibility of policies. The equation is simple: the greater the credibility of macroeconomic policies, however demanding, the less sacrifice is made in slowing economic growth, employment and wages. Premature easing of adjustment policies or overreactions in the exchange rate will only ruin the stability achieved over a decade and lead the country to a longer period of lower growth and higher inflation. However, external circumstances are changing, and force us to adjust our policies. For example, in recent days there have been pressures against the peso motivated by the contagion effect of negative international evaluations of the policies of other countries. Five banks in the country recklessly managed their liquidity, forcing unusual hikes in interbank rates. In order to discourage a repetition of situations like these, the Board of the Central Bank agreed to divide the reserve period into two subperiods, to seek a more cautious behavior in the management of liquidity in the market. The corresponding agreement was published yesterday, and will apply in the next reserve period, which begins tomorrow, September 9. Mr. President, Senators, On Friday, September 4, at noon, an unprecedented meeting concluded in Washington: the Finance Ministers and the Presidents of the Central Banks of nine Latin American countries, the United States and Canada, at the invitation of the Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund, met at the headquarters of this organization. The presidents of the World Bank and the IDB also participated. The purpose of the meeting was to exchange ideas on economic policies aimed at addressing the difficult situations of some of them in the context of a worsening international crisis. During the meeting, it was announced that an international risk rating agency had downgraded the classification of Brazil and Venezuela, and that it said it was considering a reduction in the classification of Argentina and Mexico. Russia has suspended its payments; Japan has not yet begun a recovery process, and remains in recession with a loss of output of 3.5%. Korea has fallen more than 6%; Indonesia has done so 16%; Malaysia has fallen 7%; Thailand 6.5%. The projection of the growth of the world economy has already been reduced three times in the last 6 months. Moreover, not three weeks ago we received a draft of the IMF's 1999 projection of the world economy, and we have already been informed in Washington that this projection will be revised down again before the end of this month. In that context, we have maintained the need for the world to act together to address the crisis. We point out that the richest countries of the world have in their hands to adopt in concert the policies that could push up the world economy, so that the necessary adjustments are made in an environment of growth and not recession. While the difficult international agreements required, if at all, are achieved, we cannot avoid receiving negative pressures on our economy from the outside. President Frei brought this concern to the meeting of the Presidents of the Rio Group countries, which will make it possible to exercise the necessary political actions to achieve substantive progress at the next Board of Governors of the World Bank and the IMF next October. We are prepared to continue growing, despite them. Over the years, the country has built very solid foundations in its policies and institutions. But we cannot avoid slowing down our growth to avoid generating insurmountable imbalances that would threaten much more than our economy. We will continue to press for the necessary international solutions. But, with or without them, the responsibility for the Chilean economy lies with Chileans. Faced with today's difficulties, we believe that it is necessary to unite wills rather than accentuate disagreements; protect the weakest rather than give up the necessary adjustments; confronting difficulties and obstacles rather than hiding them; And to demonstrate, once again, that this country, with a difficult economy and geography, overcomes external shocks and is capable of building on them.
text_original: Valparaso, 8 de septiembre de 1998 DISCURSO DEL PRESIDENTE DEL BANCO CENTRAL DE CHILE AL SENADO CON OCASIN DE LA PRESENTACIN DEL INFORME ANUAL 1998  Introduccin Lo que comenz como una crisis que pareca acotada a un pas del Asia se transform en lo que hoy ya se reconoce como una crisis global. La debilidad de los sistemas financieros y la falta de informacin completa sobre las obligaciones externas amplificaron lo que pudo ser un simple proceso de ajuste de una cuenta corriente deficitaria hasta convertirlo en un problema que contagi a muchos pases. La violenta devaluacin de sus monedas, en vez de aminorar las dificultades las agrav, y la prdida de confianza de los mercados se extendi a los pases emergentes, incluso a la Amrica Latina. La economa chilena enfrenta tiempos difciles. Aunque sus fundamentos son slidos, la crisis externa, con sus negativos efectos sobre el comercio exterior y la cuenta de capitales, obliga a moderar el ritmo de crecimiento econmico mientras no se recupere la estabilidad en los mercados internacionales. La fragilidad de la economa mundial exige disciplina y prudencia en la formulacin de los objetivos macroeconmicos y flexibilidad en la aplicacin de las polticas. El programa macroeconmico que se presenta en este Informe al Senado busca cumplir con estos requisitos. Como objetivo principal de este programa se persigue afianzar la estabilidad macroeconmica y financiera interna y externa, en un marco internacional muy restrictivo. Para lograrlo, se plantea reducir gradualmente el dficit de la cuenta corriente sobre una trayectoria sostenible en el mediano y largo plazo, consolidar los enormes avances hechos en la disminucin de la inflacin y lograr, como resultado, una tasa de crecimiento econmico en el corto plazo coherente con el adverso escenario mundial. Ello abrir las puertas para retomar en los aos prximos el rpido proceso de desarrollo econmico y social que ha caracterizado a nuestro pas en esta dcada. Las perspectivas sobre la trayectoria de la economa mundial durante los prximos dos aos han experimentado un progresivo deterioro a medida que se conocen los alcances reales de la recesin en Asia y la extensin de sus efectos al resto de las economas del mundo. Asimismo, persiste la volatilidad de los mercados financieros internacionales de hecho cerrados para la gran mayora de los pases emergentes. Estos desarrollos externos tienen consecuencias de importancia sobre la economa chilena. Por una parte, la desaceleracin de la economa mundial ha restado dinamismo a la demanda de los principales productos bsicos. En particular, el precio del cobre ha fluctuado cerca de los 75 centavos de dlar la libra en los ltimos meses, casi 20 centavos por debajo de las expectativas iniciales, y el panorama externo no es favorable para esperar un repunte de este precio en el corto plazo. Sumando los aumentos y disminuciones en otros precios, se estima que para el presente ao la reduccin de los trminos de intercambio alcanzar cerca del 10%, lo que resta del ingreso nacional el equivalente a dos puntos porcentuales, unos US$ 1.600 millones. Nuestro pas es $ 1.600 millones de dlares ms pobre como consecuencia de factores externos. Por otra parte, en este escenario de mayor incertidumbre, los inversionistas internacionales se han volcado hacia las monedas, mercados e instrumentos considerados ms seguros, impulsando un fuerte incremento generalizado en el costo del financiamiento externo de las economas emergentes y una reduccin en el volumen de los flujos de capital hacia estos pases. En el caso particular de la economa chilena, adems, se ha observado una mayor demanda de las empresas, instituciones financieras y personas residentes en Chile por acumular activos en el exterior, incrementando la diversificacin internacional de su portafolio y cubriendo riesgos asociados a las fluctuaciones del tipo de cambio. Sin embargo, tambin hay desarrollos internos de importancia para entender la actual coyuntura. A travs de los ltimos aos la demanda interna se ha caracterizado por un elevado dinamismo. En este perodo se ha observado un marcado y sostenido incremento en la tasa de inversin total, que ha llegado hasta un 27% del PIB en 1997, sin que haya sido acompaado por un aumento similar del ahorro nacional, todo medido a precios corrientes. En efecto, la tasa de ahorro ha permanecido prcticamente estable en el ltimo sexenio, con fluctuaciones en torno a un promedio de 21% del PIB. Otra forma de ver lo mismo, el dficit de la cuenta corriente se ha do ampliando gradualmente a lo largo de los ltimos aos. Este desarrollo es consecuencia del optimismo prevaleciente a nivel de las empresas y consumidores dentro de un contexto de mayor disponibilidad de financiamiento interno y externo. En efecto, se ha generado una presin creciente por fondos en el mercado de crdito domstico, impulsando al alza las tasas de inters internas y, a la vez, un mayor uso del ahorro externo (dficit de la cuenta corriente). Por su parte, el fuerte apetito de los inversionistas internacionales por incrementar su participacin en la economa chilena, aun pagando el costo del encaje al financiamiento externo, ha provisto con creces los recursos necesarios para financiar este dficit. As, durante 1997 la economa recibi recursos externos netos de aproximadamente 10% del PIB, casi el doble de los requerimientos de financiamiento del dficit de la cuenta corriente. La diferencia increment las reservas del Banco Central. En este contexto de fuertes presiones de demanda interna, la crisis externa y su negativo impacto sobre la relacin de trminos de intercambio y la oferta de financiamiento externo, as como el aumento de la demanda por activos extranjeros, hicieron inevitable la aplicacin de un esfuerzo de contencin de la demanda interna para llevar el dficit de cuenta corriente hacia niveles acordes con el nuevo escenario internacional. Por su parte, el sistema financiero nacional muestra una posicin slida. El indicador de rentabilidad anualizado de la banca alcanz a julio niveles cercanos al 14%, cifra que se considera adecuada. Asimismo, el crecimiento de las colocaciones en doce meses, aunque declinante, se mantiene en la actualidad por sobre el 12% y la cartera vencida como porcentaje del total de colocaciones, se mantiene en niveles razonables, en torno a 1.2%. La informacin referente a la clasificacin privada de riesgo de las instituciones financieras, indica que el riesgo de los instrumentos de los bancos y financieras ha mejorado respecto del ao pasado. Cabe destacar que el requerimiento de capital del sistema financiero, medido en torno al Indicador de Basilea, a junio arroja un nivel de capitalizacin de 11.5% sobre los activos riesgosos, casi 2% ms que el ao pasado. No obstante la solidez del sistema financiero, la mayor incertidumbre a nivel global, los cambios en precios relativos en marcha y el propio proceso de ajuste del crecimiento de la economa frente a la crisis externa, hacen necesario reforzar la supervisin de los mercados financieros y modernizar algunas regulaciones de manera de conciliar la apertura de nuevos espacios para la actividad financiera con el necesario perfeccionamiento de normas prudenciales.  Las Polticas en Aplicacin En el perodo reciente, la combinacin de polticas econmicas se ha orientado a lograr una mezcla prudente entre mayor financiamiento externo y correccin del nivel de gasto interno. Las acciones del Banco Central han buscado promover un ajuste ordenado de precios relativos y evitar un deterioro en la tendencia de reduccin de la inflacin. Entre las principales medidas adoptadas, se cuentan la aplicacin de una poltica monetaria con una orientacin ms restrictiva a partir de enero del presente ao, junto con un mayor grado de flexibilidad en el manejo de la liquidez y la realizacin de intervenciones ocasionales en el mercado de divisas. Ms recientemente, el 25 de junio, se anunci la implementacin de una banda ms estrecha como gua para el tipo de cambio, la provisin de nuevos instrumentos de cobertura cambiara y la reduccin del encaje en moneda extranjera. Con el fin de evitar una sobrerreaccin de corto plazo en el valor del tipo de cambio y facilitar el proceso de recomposicin de cartera, el Banco Central ha vendido en diferentes ocasiones divisas en el mercado cambiarlo, revirtiendo as la tendencia de acumulacin que se haba producido en aos anteriores, cuando se compraron los activos internacionales al valor del piso o cerca del piso de la anterior banda de flotacin del tipo de cambio. Asimismo, a lo largo de los ltimos ocho meses, y como consecuencia de la mayor incertidumbre internacional, la poltica monetaria se ha dirigido a permitir un mayor grado de flexibilidad a las tasas de inters de corto plazo. Se ha buscado con ello evitar exacerbar las volatilidades en el tipo de cambio y frenar procesos especulativos contra el peso, mediante un control ms estricto de la liquidez en moneda nacional.
