Esta es una respuesta apropiada para enfrentar perodos de turbulencias financieras; as lo demuestra la evidencia internacional y, en particular, la que se desprende de la experiencia reciente de las economas del Sudeste Asitico. Esta situacin se hizo ms evidente en los meses de enero y junio, as como tambin en las ltimas semanas de agosto como consecuencia de la crisis en Rusia. De hecho, los fuertes incrementos de ms de 1.000 puntos base que han experimentado los spreads de la deuda externa de casi todos los pases emergentes, unidos a las expectativas de depreciacin de las monedas, generan tasas internas de inters muy altas en todos ellos. No cabe dudas que en perodos de turbulencias e incertidumbre como el actual, la defensa de la estabilidad macroeconmica puede generar costos, tanto en trminos de mayores tasas de inters como de la moderacin de la tasa de crecimiento, pero dicha defensa es indispensable para evitar las enormes prdidas que puede traer el deterioro de la confianza en el manejo macroeconmico. La evidencia internacional, y especialmente la experiencia reciente de los pases del Sudeste Asitico, demuestran claramente que una poltica vacilante, que no se decide a adoptar las medidas de ajuste necesarias, puede terminar en una prdida de confianza financiera, situacin que arrastra consigo consecuencias devastadoras en el sistema bancario, y prdidas enormes y duraderas en la produccin y en el empleo, as como tambin retrocesos en la estabilidad poltica y social. Por su parte, la poltica fiscal ha impulsado una moderacin adicional del gasto interno, realizando recortes al presupuesto de gastos del Fisco y de las empresas pblicas. El impacto de estos recortes debiera operar con plenitud en la segunda mitad de 1998, de tal forma que el crecimiento de la absorcin pblica para el resto del ao debe estar por debajo del crecimiento observado en su primera parte. Asimismo, tan importante como los recortes realizados en 1998, es el anuncio de una poltica fiscal cautelosa para 1999. El compromiso anunciado para acotar el crecimiento del gasto pblico a medio punto porcentual por debajo del crecimiento de la economa, esto es un aumento no superior al 3,3% real, es una seal que contribuye a despejar dudas, especialmente en un ao con elecciones presidenciales. Este compromiso y su cumplimiento es altamente valorado por el Banco Central, como tambin lo es la disposicin a realizar nuevos ajustes si fuese necesario. Es de notar, adems, que el compromiso ya asumido acota en forma importante el reajuste posible de conceder en las negociaciones de salarios del sector pblico. El aporte del gasto pblico a la reduccin del ritmo de crecimiento del gasto total de la economa es una contribucin al crecimiento de sta. A medida que las metas del gasto pblico se hagan efectivas, se ir reduciendo el nivel necesario de las tasas de inters para lograr el ajuste deseado, a la vez que permitir fortalecer al sector externo de nuestra economa. Sin el ajuste del gasto pblico el peso que recaera sobre el sector productivo de la economa y sobre el empleo sera aun mayor. Debo aqu sealar que, al volver de nuestro reciente viaje a Washington, hemos comentado con el Ministro de Hacienda la conveniencia de hacer un esfuerzo an mayor, llevando el crecimiento del gasto pblico por debajo del 3,3%. El Ministro ha recogido positivamente este comentario. Los antecedentes ms recientes indican que las principales variables econmicas crecimiento, cuenta corriente e inflacin se mueven en la direccin apropiada. En el primer semestre del presente ao, el Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) aument en 6,3% respecto de igual perodo del ao anterior, mientras que la demanda interna creci en 10% en el mismo perodo, pero sobre una trayectoria de moderacin. Las perspectivas para el dficit de la cuenta corriente se mantienen dentro de lmites razonables dadas las circunstancias externas; y la inflacin medida por el ndice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) mostr una disminucin desde 6,0% observado a fines del ao pasado hasta 5,2% en agosto ltimo. Por su parte, informaciones preliminares muestran que las importaciones totales, por primera vez, se han reducido en trminos absolutos en el mes de agosto comparado con agosto del ao pasado, y tambin comparado con el mes de julio de este ao. No hay dudas que el proceso de ajuste est en marcha. El programa macroeconmico que se presenta en este informe para este y el prximo ao se basa en la consolidacin de estas tendencias.  Las Metas del Programa Macroeconmico En primer lugar, la tasa de inflacin ha de continuar sobre una trayectoria de reduccin gradual. En el corto plazo, este compromiso se expresa en alcanzar la meta de inflacin planteada para el presente ao, reconociendo que las presiones provenientes del debilitamiento del peso y la inercia en el ritmo de crecimiento de los salarios nominales podran retrasar ese logro algunos meses. Asimismo, las polticas macroeconmicas se orientarn para conseguir que en 1999 la inflacin se site alrededor de +/-4,3%, para continuar en los aos venideros los avances hacia la estabilidad de precios. La perseverancia en el objetivo de reduccin de la inflacin constituye un elemento fundamental para enmarcar la prudencia y disciplina que se requiere del conjunto de polticas econmicas. El enfriamiento obligado de la economa y la favorable trayectoria de la inflacin internacional abren espacios para realizar avances adicionales hacia la estabilidad de precios, sin generar costos sobre la economa. La meta inflacionaria descendente complementa la correccin esperada en otras variables macroeconmicas como el nivel de gasto interno y el dficit de la cuenta corriente, al tiempo que contribuye a estabilizar los mercados financieros y fortalece el conjunto de polticas econmicas. Hasta ahora la inflacin medida por el IPC se ha mantenido estable en lo que va corrido del ao, fluctuando levemente por encima de 5,0% anual. En este perodo, la moderacin del ritmo inflacionario se ha visto favorecida por la normalizacin que mostraron los precios de los productos pereciles y la disminucin de los precios de los combustibles. Sin embargo, los indicadores de inflacin subyacente, a diferencia de la inflacin medida por el IPC, muestran una trayectoria levemente ascendente a travs del ao. Este aumento se explica en parte importante, por los incrementos de precios de los rubros no transables y, en particular, de los servicios. Esta evolucin ascendente de las mediciones de inflacin subyacente es consecuencia de las mayores presiones de demanda interna que comenzaron a acentuarse en la segunda mitad del ao pasado, el empuje de los costos salariales y las mayores presiones de costos de importaciones. A pesar de esta tendencia alcista, el escenario actual es propicio para consolidar dentro de los prximos trimestres los avances en la reduccin de la inflacin. El comportamiento ms moderado de las ventas y la acumulacin de excedentes de capacidad llevarn a reducir mrgenes comerciales y, del mismo modo, los aumentos salariales que se observan hasta ahora deben tender a moderarse en los meses venideros o, alternativamente, el ritmo de crecimiento del empleo mostrar an mayores seales de ajuste. Adems, la disminucin en los costos de materias primas y la reduccin de los precios de importaciones en dlares para el presente ao, as como un nivel de inflacin externa positivo, pero bajo, para el prximo ao, permitirn reducir presiones inflacionarias externas. La consolidacin de los resultados esperados en la reduccin de los costos salariales y las presiones de inflacin domstica, requieren que las negociaciones de salarios pblicos y privados se enmarquen dentro de los parmetros de menor inflacin y crecimiento de productividad que se esperan para este y el ao prximo. De lo contrario, se producirn desequilibrios que finalmente se reflejarn en mayor desempleo. Quisiera reiterar en esta oportunidad que, bajo las condiciones de ajuste indispensables para la economa chilena, es extraordinariamente importante que se reconozca la necesidad de moderar las presiones salariales para evitar aumentos innecesariamente elevados en las tasas de desempleo. En tiempos de estrechez, es inevitable elegir entre mayores salarios o mantencin del empleo. Las limitaciones de la demanda impedirn, a la vez, que se manifiesten ampliaciones generalizadas de mrgenes comerciales o de utilidades. En segundo lugar, se estima que el dficit de cuenta corriente de 1998 alcanzar alrededor de los US$ 5.150 millones, pero sobre una trayectoria de reduccin hacia el prximo ao, para situarse alrededor de US$ 4.500 millones en 1999 (en torno a 5,5% del PIB). La cifra proyectada para el presente ao est por encima del dficit que se prevea un ao atrs, US$ 4.400 millones, lo que representa un incremento prudente en el uso del financiamiento en el comercio externo, pero al mismo tiempo es inferior en al menos US$ 1.000 millones al que se podra haber generado de no mediar el proceso de ajuste en implementacin. As se busca un ajuste gradual del sector externo que minimice efectos negativos sobre el producto. En el mediano plazo, se busca una reduccin adicional en el dficit de la cuenta corriente para alcanzar niveles ms moderados, del orden del 4% al 5% del PIB, lo cual necesariamente plantea el desafo de aumentar substancialmente el ahorro interno si queremos mantener un crecimiento como el que acostumbramos en la ltima dcada. Para el presente ao en su conjunto, el volumen de las ventas al exterior crecera por encima de 7,0%, liderado por el crecimiento de las exportaciones no tradicionales. Este resultado se compara favorablemente con perodos anteriores de desaceleracin en la economa mundial, en que las exportaciones chilenas han experimentado disminuciones ms marcadas en su tasa de crecimiento. As, las exportaciones continan mostrando un ritmo de expansin sostenido y superior al crecimiento del PIB, como ha ocurrido en forma casi continua a lo largo de la ltima dcada. Para el prximo ao no se esperan cambios significativos en los precios de las materias primas de exportacin. Por su parte, el volumen de los envos al exterior experimentara un aumento de aproximadamente 10%, resultado que se encuentra muy influido por el incremento de alrededor de 15% en los envos de cobre que se espera para 1999. Por su parte, el proceso de ajuste de las importaciones se acentuara en la segunda mitad de este ao, y su crecimiento sera muy moderado en 1999, coherente con la evolucin esperada de la demanda interna. En tercer lugar, la correccin en el saldo de las cuentas externas requiere acentuar el esfuerzo de contencin de la demanda interna en lo que resta de este ao y el prximo. En el corto plazo, esta situacin, junto al menor empuje de la demanda externa, llevarn a una moderacin del ritmo de crecimiento de la actividad econmica en 1998, que de todos modos ser una cifra apreciable (alrededor de 5%). A su vez, se requiere que el crecimiento de la demanda interna en 1999 sea muy moderado, lo que, junto con el repunte en la demanda externa neta -- esto es, la diferencia entre exportaciones e importaciones-- llevara el crecimiento del PIB a un valor de alrededor de 3,8%. Este resultado, si bien, cerca de la mitad del crecimiento de tendencia de la ltima dcada, es adecuado considerando el complejo escenario externo y representa casi el doble del crecimiento mundial proyectado para 1999. En la medida que continen avanzando las correcciones esperadas en la relacin de gasto a ingreso nacional y que no se produzca un deterioro adicional del escenario externo, la economa estar en las condiciones apropiadas para entrar en una fase de gradual aceleracin que conducir hacia tasas de crecimiento ms cercanas a su potencial. En cualquier caso, no debe perderse de vista que el crecimiento econmico promedio de la presente dcada, an con la moderada expansin esperada para 1999, es el mayor de este siglo. A pesar de las contingencias de corto plazo, no se debe perder de vista que los fundamentos de mediano plazo de la economa chilena permanecen slidos, y que es posible hacia el futuro continuar mostrando un desempeo tan exitoso como el de la ltima dcada. En definitiva, el potencial de crecimiento de la economa depende de su capacidad de inversin en capital fsico y humano, la flexibilidad de los mercados y la iniciativa empresarial para incorporar nuevas tecnologas y desarrollar nuevos productos y servicios. En la actualidad, la tasa de inversin fija es la mayor desde que existen registros histricos, se observan progresos en el nivel de educacin de la fuerza de trabajo y aparecen nuevos sectores que toman el liderazgo en el crecimiento econmico. Hacia el futuro, la principal limitante para retomar la senda de crecimiento alto y sostenido es el esfuerzo de ahorro interno. La tasa de ahorro nacional debe aumentar por lo menos hasta 23% del PIB, cerca de dos puntos ms que el promedio del ltimo sexenio, con el fin de mantener la tasa de inversin en un nivel similar al observado en los ltimos aos, al mismo tiempo que el dficit de la cuenta corriente no supere lmites prudentes, en el rango de 4% a 5% del PIB. Esa es la tarea que tenemos por delante.  Conclusiones La economa chilena enfrenta tiempos complejos. La crisis asitica, con sus efectos sobre el comercio exterior y el costo y disponibilidad del financiamiento externo, ha puesto y seguir poniendo a prueba la voluntad del pas para enfrentar los retos asociados a estos tiempos de turbulencia e incertidumbre internacional. Aunque la posicin financiera es saludable y la economa tiene sus fundamentos slidos, esta es la hora de reafirmar la conviccin en polticas macroeconmicas prudentes y exigentes. Es imposible para el pas mantener un crecimiento cercano al potencial en tanto las turbulencias externas no amainen y se consolide un proceso de recuperacin de la estabilidad en los mercados mundiales. No reconocer que se debe afrontar un perodo relativamente ms duro provocara un efecto irremediablemente negativo en la administracin econmica del pas, situacin que por s misma profundizara significativamente los efectos de la crisis asitica. La globalizacin de los mercados y la fuerte vinculacin de Chile con el resto del mundo, que han permitido al pas una dcada de sostenido crecimiento, contienen tambin un elemento disciplinador sobre el manejo de las polticas macroeconmicas que no es posible soslayar y que obliga a una actitud permanentemente cautelosa y de gran celo en defensa de la estabilidad justamente en los momentos de prueba. Las soluciones fciles no existen. Todas acarrean costos. En la actual coyuntura, cabe reafirmar el compromiso con el proceso de reduccin gradual pero persistente de la inflacin, hasta llevarla a una cifra cercana a 3% anual, as como perseguir el propsito de que el dficit en cuenta corriente se reduzca a partir de 1999 hasta que alcance niveles razonables entre 4% y 5% del PIB en el mediano plazo. Los instrumentos de poltica monetaria han de aplicarse de manera coherente con estos propsitos, confiando en la continuacin de una poltica fiscal responsable y ajustada a los tiempos. El xito de esta empresa se traducir en que la economa nacional retornar en los prximos aos a su crecimiento potencial, y en que los incrementos en la tasa de desempleo y la reduccin en la tasa de crecimiento de los salarios sern fenmenos acotados y tambin temporales. Pero ese xito depende en forma crucial de la credibilidad de las polticas. La ecuacin es simple: a mayor credibilidad en las polticas macroeconmicas, por exigentes que sean, menor el sacrificio en cuanto a la desaceleracin del crecimiento econmico, del empleo y los salarios. El relajamiento prematuro de las polticas de ajuste o reacciones exageradas en el tipo de cambio, slo arruinarn la estabilidad conseguida a lo largo de una dcada y conducirn al pas a un perodo ms prolongado de menor crecimiento y mayor inflacin. Sin embargo, las circunstancias externas son cambiantes, y obligan a ajustar nuestras polticas. Por ejemplo, en das pasados se han producido presiones contra el peso motivadas por el efecto contagio de las negativas evaluaciones internacionales de las polticas de otros pases. Cinco bancos en el pas manejaron de manera poco prudente su liquidez, forzando alzas inusuales de las tasas interbancarias. Con el fin de desestimular una repeticin de situaciones como stas, el Consejo del Banco Central acord dividir el perodo de encaje en dos subperodos, para buscar un comportamiento ms cauteloso en el manejo de la liquidez en el mercado. El acuerdo correspondiente se public en el da de ayer, y se aplicar en el prximo perodo de encaje, que comienza maana 9 de septiembre. Seor Presidente, seores Senadores: El viernes 4 de septiembre recin pasado, al medioda, concluy en Washington una reunin sin precedentes: los Ministros de Hacienda y los Presidentes de los Bancos Centrales de nueve pases latinoamericanos, de los Estados Unidos y de Canad, a invitacin del Director Gerente del Fondo Monetario Internacional, se reunieron en la sede de este organismo. Participaron tambin los presidentes del Banco Mundial y del BID. El propsito de la reunin fue intercambiar ideas sobre polticas econmicas dirigidas a enfrentar las difciles situaciones de algunos de ellos en el contexto de una crisis internacional que se agrava. En el curso de la reunin, se anunci que una clasificadora internacional de riesgo haba degradado la clasificacin de Brasil y de Venezuela, y que sealaba estar estudiando una reduccin de la clasificacin de Argentina y de Mxico. Rusia ha suspendido sus pagos; Japn an no inicia un proceso de recuperacin, y se mantiene en recesin con una prdida de producto de 3,5%. Corea ha cado ms de 6%; Indonesia lo ha hecho 16%; Malasia ha cado 7%; Tailandia 6,5%. La proyeccin del crecimiento de la economa mundial ha sido ya reducida tres veces en los ltimos 6 meses. An ms, no hace tres semanas que recibimos un borrador de la proyeccin de la economa mundial para 1999 hecha por el FMI, y ya se nos ha informado en Washington que esa proyeccin ser nuevamente revisada hacia abajo antes de fines de este mes. En ese contexto, hemos sostenido la necesidad de que el mundo acte en conjunto para enfrentar la crisis. Sealamos que los pases ms ricos del orbe tienen en sus manos adoptar concertadamente las polticas que podran empujar hacia arriba la economa mundial, de modo que los ajustes necesarios se hagan en un ambiente de crecimiento y no de recesin. Mientras se logran los difciles acuerdos internacionales requeridos, si es que se logran, no podremos evitar recibir desde el exterior presiones negativas sobre nuestra economa. El Presidente Fre llev esta preocupacin a la reunin de los Presidentes de los pases del Grupo de Ro, lo que har posible ejercer las acciones polticas necesarias para lograr avances sustantivos en la prxima Asamblea de Gobernadores del Banco Mundial y del FMI en octubre prximo. Estamos preparados para continuar creciendo, pese a ellas. El pas ha construido a travs de los aos bases muy slidas en sus polticas y sus instituciones. Pero no podemos evitar reducir el ritmo de nuestro crecimiento para evitar la generacin de desequilibrios insalvables que amenazaran mucho ms que nuestra economa. Continuaremos presionando por las soluciones internacionales necesarias. Pero, con o sin ellas, la responsabilidad de la economa chilena recae sobre los chilenos. Frente a la dificultades de hoy, pensamos que es necesario aunar las voluntades ms que acentuar los desacuerdos; proteger a los ms dbiles antes que renunciar a los ajustes necesarios; enfrentar las dificultades y los obstculos antes que esconderlos; y demostrar, una vez ms, que este pas, de economa y geografa difciles, se sobrepone a los embates externos y es capaz de construir sobre ellos.

Title: Economic developments in 1998 and prospects for 1999
text: Economic Developments in 1998 and Outlook for 1999 Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, before the Senate Finance Committee, Wednesday, January 6, 1999. I. Introduction During 1998, the Chilean economy faced an external scenario of enormous complexity. The Asian crisis and its effects on foreign trade and the capital account necessitated a set of policies aimed at stabilizing financial markets and moderating the pace of growth in domestic spending. This document presents an account and evaluation of the Major economic and financial developments from the past year, and then explore the economic outlook for this year. The main message of this presentation is to point out a cautiously optimistic position regarding what the trajectory of the economy will be during 1999. Indeed, despite external difficulties, the Chilean economy has successfully maintained a trajectory of macroeconomic stability, reaching the inflation and current account targets scheduled for 1998, and is well on track to continue on this path this year. This situation has helped restore confidence in financial markets and monetary policy has pushed interest rates to levels similar to those prevailing at the beginning of the year. In the future, decisions in this area will continue to reflect progress in meeting macroeconomic targets, a situation that will allow a gradual recovery of economic growth to begin. However, it is necessary to emphasize that the policies of the Central Bank will seek to privilege that this recovery of economic growth is lasting. In the context of a semi-recessionary global scenario with greater relative scarcity of external financing, there is not the necessary space to attempt a rapid recovery of output through a boost to domestic demand without seriously jeopardizing the progress already made in reducing the current account deficit and stability of financial and exchange markets. II. The International Stage in 1998 A little more than a year after the Asian crisis began, its negative effects on the world economy have far exceeded the projections that could be made at the beginning of this episode. This deterioration is reflected in the IMF's continued revisions to its global growth projections for 1998 and 1999. Table 1 shows the evolution of these projections from October 1997 to date. At the beginning of the crisis, October 1997, when its effects were still mainly localized in Asia, the IMF projected an expansion of the world economy in 1998 and 1999 of around 4.5%, similar to the growth of the previous year. However, as the real and financial effects of the crisis began to branch out to other regions and new factors were added such as Japan's recession and financial difficulties and subsequently the collapse of Russian bonds and their contagion effect to other financial markets, global growth projections were progressively adjusted downwards. The most recent estimate for December 1998 estimates last year's global growth at around 2.2 per cent, half of what was initially anticipated. It is also now perceived that the speed of recovery of the world economy will be slower than initially anticipated, with the rate of expansion in 1999 estimated to be virtually identical to the 1998 estimate, higher growth in Asia, but lower in Europe, the United States and Latin America. Table 1: IMF Growth Projections On a positive note, the most recent revisions tend to reaffirm previous estimates, reflecting a greater degree of confidence and a narrowing of the main global risk factors behind these projections. Developments in the price of copper and other raw materials have also reflected the progressive deterioration in the growth outlook for global demand. Thus, the price of copper has shown that since the beginning of the crisis, October 1997, to date, a fall from about one dollar to levels around 65 cents per pound in the most recent observations. The accumulation of inventories and the poor prospects for world growth do not augur a rapid recovery in this price, at least during 1999. To illustrate the magnitude of the situation, it can be stated that in real terms the current price of copper is the lowest observed since the 30s, when the world economy was in the midst of the great depression. The history of recent decades shows that practically in every episode of sharp declines in the price of copper, the Chilean economy has shown sharp declines in its economic growth rate, in addition to imbalances in other areas such as balance of payments financing and inflation. From this historical perspective, the recent performance of the Chilean economy is very favorable, because even despite facing the lowest price levels in recent decades, inflation, the balance of payments and public finances remain within a stable trajectory and the country will not stop growing. Figure 2: Copper Price and Business Cycle 1960-1998 GRAPH 2 Real Copper Price and the Economic Cycle The rest of export prices also showed a decrease in 1998, with an overall fall in prices estimated at around 17 per cent, partially offset by the corresponding fall in the price of imports, resulting in a net fall in terms of trade of around 11.5 per cent in 1998. Indeed, it should be remembered that the fall in terms of trade meant subtracting about US 2,000 million of income from Chileans. At the margin, commodity prices deteriorated towards the end of 1998, with a slight recovery expected through 1999. However, it is estimated that in 1999 the terms of trade will be lower than those observed on average in 1998, although not lower than those currently in force. On the other hand, the Asian crisis has also had effects on the distribution of capital. International investorsd1both domestic and foreignd1have reviewed their investment strategies in emerging markets. In particular, the crisis has led to a reassessment of the risks of these investments, as well as lower global demand for risky assets. Even for countries with a sound macroeconomic and financial situation, such as Chile, the change in attitude and losses suffered by international investors has meant falls in the prices of their international liabilities (stocks and bonds), along with lower availability and higher external financing costs. Figure 3: EMBI and ADR s (97-98) All of the above has involved some changes in our capital account: reductions in the net volume of inflows and changes in the composition of inflows and outflows. Indeed, preliminary estimates indicate that medium- and long-term capital inflows would have remained virtually unchanged from 1997, with a reduction in foreign direct investment of close to US500 million, offset by a higher level of medium- and long-term indebtedness. In contrast, investment flows from residents abroad, direct and portfolio, would have experienced an increase of close to US1.6 billion compared to 1997, while the accumulation of short-term assets would increase by over US3 billion. Finally, portfolio investments to Chile, ADRs and bonds, also show a significant reduction, preliminarily estimated at around US2 billion below the values observed in 1997. Still, net capital inflows, including errors and omissions, would have reached just over 2.5 billion during 1998, well below the 7.4 billion recorded in 1997. The deterioration in the external scenario found the Chilean economy in a phase of strong acceleration of domestic demand, with the consequent pressures of widening in the current account deficit. The expansion of domestic demand became more evident towards the end of 1997 and was mainly channelled into external markets, driving strong import growth and additional pressures on the current account deficit. However, part of this pressure also shifted to domestic markets, generating very dynamic output growth in the second half of last year and a narrowing of the labor market with consequent pressures on domestic inflation trends and wages. Indeed, the rate of job creation began to increase in the second half of 1997, and this higher level of employment continued throughout the first part of this year, bringing the unemployment rate below its historical trend. Similarly, the trend of non-tradable inflation began to show a gradual pick-up towards the end of 1998, while nominal wage growth remained stagnant at around 8 per cent per annum, moderating only towards the end of the year. III. The 1998 Targets and the Macroeconomic Policy Orientation In this context, it was necessary to pursue an adjustment policy aimed at reducing, over a limited period of time, the current account deficit, while keeping inflation on a stable and gradually downward path. In concrete terms, the objectives sought were to achieve a current account deficit of around 6.5 percent of GDP in 1998, about 5 billion, and about 4 billion, 5 percent of GDP in 1999, as well as inflation of around 4.5 percent in 1998 and about 4.3 percent in 1999. Inflation targets and the current account balance are the guiding axis of macroeconomic policies. These objectives indicate the budgetary constraints that the evolution of domestic spending must recognize in order to be able to maintain over time a high and stable economic growth trajectory, as satisfactory as that observed during the last decade. On the contrary, a complacent attitude towards these goals sooner or later produces a deterioration in the confidence of the financial markets, causing sudden changes in relative prices and financing conditions that ultimately entail great costs for the economy. This situation was particularly risky in a period of high financial instability such as the one that has characterized international markets in recent times. Thus, in the course of 1998, macroeconomic policies adopted a restrictive approach aimed at moderating the growth of domestic demand and restoring confidence in financial markets. In terms of monetary policy, the Central Bank promoted an increase in its monetary instance rate in order to raise the general cost of credit and moderate the pace of private spending by companies and consumers. In addition, on exceptional occasions, a greater degree of additional flexibility to interest rates was allowed to absorb extraordinary speculation pressures in the foreign exchange markets. In the exchange rate area, the actions of the Central Bank were aimed at recognizing and respecting the most permanent trends of the exchange rate, but seeking to cushion their sudden movements. This is how, in December in twelve months, there was a nominal depreciation of the peso against the dollar of around 14% compared to pre-crisis levels and the most recent estimates of the real exchange rate show a depreciation of around 4%. During 1998 there was a break in the appreciation trend that the peso had been showing in recent years, as well as an increase in the perception of risk changed in the face of the deterioration of the external scenario and the widening of the current account deficit. Market participants responded to these changes by hedging foreign exchange futures markets and adjusting their portfolio of assets and liabilities aimed at reducing exposure to currency fluctuations, which contributed to currency pressures. Faced with these pressures, the Central Bank used its exchange rate and monetary policy to cushion the speed of movements in the exchange rate in order to restore confidence in the value of the peso and thus avoid a progressive erosion of monetary credibility and a speculative spiral process against the peso. Thus, during 1998 the Central Bank participated more actively in the foreign exchange market, playing a stabilizing role by selling to the market international reserves that had been acquired near the floor of the previous exchange rate band; the issuance of the 3-year and 4-year PRDs was also initiated in order to facilitate the process of hedging risk to change it; and finally, greater flexibility of interest rates was left as an adjustment mechanism in the face of extraordinary pressures in the exchange market. For its part, the policy of regulating the capital account responded during 1998 by reducing the barriers to capital inflows. Thus, the reserve exchange rate, or its equivalent cost, decreased from 30% to 0%, compensating for the increase in the cost of external financing and the lower relative availability of it. Since mid-October, as international financial markets have shown greater stability, and there has been an appropriate convergence of macroeconomic performance towards the programmed objectives, the Central Bank has reduced the policy interest rate four times, bringing it to a level slightly higher than that prevailing at the beginning of last year. And, along with the above, progress has been made towards a greater degree of exchange rate flexibility. This greater flexibility is expressed in the extension of the band of 22 December and the continuation of its widening in the course of this year. Figure 4: Exchange rate band (1997-98) GRAPH 4 Nominal Exchange Rate and Exchange Band (Ftesos per dollar) For its part, throughout 1998 the government announced the restrictive stance of fiscal policy through a series of cuts in public spending with respect to the budget approved for 1998, in order to achieve real growth of around 5.5%, an adjustment that would have been concentrated in the last quarter of 1998 on which no information is yet available. Likewise, for this year, the approved budget contemplates a real increase of around 2.8%, slightly below the expected rate of expansion of economic activity, although above the growth of domestic demand. The Central Bank has repeatedly expressed the importance of achieving these commitments in order to achieve the macroeconomic objectives outlined above with a balanced combination of fiscal and monetary policy. IV. Results of the Macroeconomic Programme in 1998 and Outlook for 1999 The evolution of macroeconomic figures for 1998 reflects the effects of the progressive deterioration of the world economy, together with the impact of domestic policies implemented to adjust the economy. In financial markets, after periods of intense internal and external turbulence, there has been a greater degree of stability in recent months, as well as a strengthening of expectations. Short-, medium- and long-term interest rates have shown a downward trend; the exchange rate has remained relatively stable and the premium on dollars sold in futures has declined; and in recent weeks there has been a gradual recovery in external financing flows; as well as a reduction in the spread cost of external financing; And only yesterday an important risk assessment agency reaffirmed the favorable investment rating achieved by the Chilean economy. All this background reflects a vote of confidence in the success of the adjustment programme that has been carried out and serves as a basis for sustaining a gradual recovery in the pace of growth of the economy. Graph 5: IPSA (1998) GRAPHICS With regard to the external accounts, on the basis of preliminary history, the target for the 1998 current account deficit is estimated to have been met. Indeed, the current account deficit is estimated to reach around 6.3 percent of GDP compared with 6.5 percent of the original projection. Table 2: Macroeconomic Estimates 1998 The outlook for 1999 indicates a further moderation in the external deficit as a result of an improvement in the trade balance. On the one hand, the entry into operation of new copper projects and a partial recovery of some major exports (forestry, fishmeal, gold and others) compensate for the lower prices observed at present, with the result that exports would show an increase in value, while imports would remain around the levels reached in 1998 as a whole, since a moderate evolution of domestic demand and the deepening of the effects of the real depreciation of the peso are expected. Graph 6: Trade balance (cumulative 12 million, 1995-98) Figure 7: imports (quarterly prom., 1997 vs. 1998) With regard to prices, the inflation result for 1998 was framed within the programmed target, which is an important achievement considering the adverse conditions of demand pressures that were faced during the first part of the year. 1998 and increased cost pressures as a result of exchange rate depreciation. Conditions are ripe for continuing the downward inflation trajectory in 1999 and reaching the target of around 4.3 percent stipulated last September. However, an important factor in consolidating this inflation projection is a moderation in the pace of nominal wage growth and non-tradable inflation consistent with the market conditions that will prevail this year. The most recent remuneration figures measured by the INE provide positive signals in this direction. In turn, domestic demand growth would be close to one point below the output growth projection. The reduction in the growth estimate reflects, in the main, that the contraction of domestic demand in the second part of the year was deeper than anticipated in the Report to the Senate last September, as well as lower growth in external demand, in its component of main exports, together with lower prices for these exports. The lower performance of economic growth in the second part of 1998 is closely linked to developments in the world economy and international financial markets in this period. The collapse of Russian bonds brought a strong wave of pessimism about international financial markets, a situation that led to a sharp increase in the cost of external financing of emerging economies, as well as the freezing or reduction of investment positions in these economies. Within this global context, a round of greater instability was also generated in local markets, promoting a process of speculation against the peso that led to an increase in market interest rates and finally the monetary instance above the values that had been previously anticipated. This set of internal and external factors determined that ultimately the growth of activity in the second half of last year was lower than anticipated. In summary, the economic growth of the Chilean economy would have been reduced to just over half of what was anticipated prior to the crisis, a correction that is lower in relative terms than the growth of the world economy according to the IMF. For this year, a path of gradual recovery of economic growth is expected, but approaching potential growth towards the fourth quarter. The gradual recovery path of the economy would be supported by the boost in net external demand, both due to the expected growth of main exports, and also by the maintenance of a level of imports similar to that observed this year. Domestic demand, meanwhile, would continue to contract in the first part of 1999, before picking up in the second part of the year. Figure 10: Demand and GDP (annual variation, 1995-98:3) GRAPH 10 It is worth comparing the results of the adjustment of the Chilean economy with those of other countries that have also been affected by the Asian crisis. The attached annex presents a series of indicators summarizing policy responses as well as key macroeconomic outcomes for a range of countries in Latin America, Asia and Oceania. Compared with the rest of the countries considered, Chile's growth in 1998 is the second highest, while that of 1999 would be in the upper end of this group. This is a significant achievement considering that the real shock that affected the Chilean economy in 1998 is considerably greater than that of other economies because of its greater exposure to commodity price fluctuations and the higher relative volume of trade with Asia. Finally, in terms of the gap between projected growth for 1998 and the potential of each country, Chile shows the third smallest reduction in the growth rate. VI. Conclusions In conclusion, despite the fact that during 1998, the Chilean economy faced an external scenario of enormous complexity, it has been successfully maintained a trajectory of macroeconomic stability. This situation has helped to restore confidence in financial markets and puts the economy well on a footing to begin a process of gradual recovery of growth throughout this year. Annex 1 Comparison of the policies and results of the Chilean economy with other countries It has been argued that the adjustment would have been inefficient because although the combination of high interest rates and moderate nominal exchange rate flexibility has achieved the desired adjustment in the current account, it has been at the cost of a sacrifice of economic growth greater than strictly necessary. This statement can be examined in the light of the experience of other emerging economies during this international juncture. Analysis of the experience of other countries provides a rich source of information, as it allows comparisons of different policy reactions to a similar external shock. Indeed, as far as exchange rate policy is concerned, at one extreme are the cases of Argentina, which has maintained its currency board, and Brazil, which has allowed a very limited degree of flexibility. At the other extreme are the cases of Mexico, Peru and New Zealand, which have maintained a flotation system. With intermediate degrees of flexibility are Colombia and Ecuador (with relatively wide bands) and Chile (with a narrower band). Other factors of heterogeneity correspond to fiscal policy reactions, the size of the shock that each country has had to endure, and the cyclical position that each country initially had. Title: Capital flows: evolution and policies in the 90s
text: Capital Flow: Evolution and Policies in the 90s Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the seminar "Globalization of financial markets and its impact on developing countries" organized by the JacquesMaritain International Institute and the Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean of the United Nations, ECLAC. 29 March 1999. I would like to thank ECLAC and the Jacques Maritain International Institute for the invitation to participate in this seminar. I wish share with you some ideas on the process ofinternational financial globalization and the policy of opening up the world to the outside world. Chilean capital account during the present decade. After the various episodes of financial crisis at the international level, from the one that affected Latin America in the 80s to the one that In mid-1997, the major concern has been the definition of a new architecture for the financial system. international, which makes it more resilient and more capable of facing them. However, time constraints prevent me from Take charge of that important discussion in this seminar, in which I want to concentrate my presentation on what I think can be. Today, our main contribution is to examine Chile's experience in financial integration. The financial phenomenon of the 90s has been globalization or globalization, driven by technological change and the development of communications that reduce distances and unify the world. In the case of Latin America, the net flow of private capital from near-zero levels on average for the second half of the 80s, to 46 billion in the period 1990-96 and almost 90 billion in 1997. In 1998, this figure fell as a result of the international crisis, even includingprivatizations. in Brazil. For all developing countries, the net flow of private capital in 1997 is approximately 130 billion of dollars, 7 times higher than that recorded on average during the second half of the eighties, and similar tothe average of the period 1990-96. In 1998, however, this value fell by 30%, affected by the crisis in Asia. The process of financial globalization favors development and opens up multiple opportunities for a country that, like Chile, seeks overcomingunderdevelopment and poverty, but it also means significant risks of serious macroeconomic imbalances and Financial. This makes it necessary to define a policy of external financial openness characterized by prudence and gradualness, But in no case does it justify not taking advantage of it. In the present decade, Chile has achieved many achievements, including the return to democratic institutions and unprecedented macroeconomic successes, such as reducing inflation to less than 5% per year, economic growth at average of 7% per year for more than a decade, and the preservation ofexternal balances. This has been a stimulus to income. of foreign exchange, which led between 1990 and 1997 to a continuous strengthening of the Chilean peso. The authority intervened to soften the rate real appreciation of the currency, with a view to maintaininga real exchange rate consistent with external equilibrium, that is, with a sustainable medium- and long-term position of the external balance in current account. In the capital flows to Chile in the nineties, two periods are distinguished. The first of these covers until the first semester of 1997, a period in which the country observed the inflow of a significant flow of resources, within the framework of an economic panorama Stable international. The second period, after July 1997, is framed within the international context generated by the financial crisis in Asian countries; It shows that the flow of capital to emerging countries is reduced by Significantly. In this way, the policies adopted to avoid astrong exchange rate overappreciation of the first period They were fully justified when the international scenario becomes more volatile and the worsening and extension of the crisis In Asian countries, it has a significant impact onthe Chilean economy: lower demand for our export products and a deterioration in our terms of trade of around 12% between 1997 and 1998; A further deterioration in 1999. The crisis also reduces the net inflow of capital, as a result of a reallocation of capitals. Portfolios of foreign investors and the effort of domestic investors to hedge against the exchange risk at which they were strongly exposed, product of the long period of real appreciation of the peso. Indeed, in 1998, the flow of capital Chile's external relations fell to almost half the 1997 figure. Financial Integration Policy: Advantages Throughout the decade, Chile has developed a policy of opening up its economy,in a gradual and sustained manner, with the In order to be able to cover the financing needs and to take advantage of the advantages derived in the long term of the financial development. Efforts should, however, be sought to minimize the secondary effects of financial integration, such as Disruptions to macroeconomic stability that could result from too violent changes in net income of external capital. The main advantages of external financial integration include: (1) stabilizing over time the consumption profile of people, with lower costs than in the case of a capital account withrestions, complementing the domestic savings effort through external savings, thereby accelerating investment and growth; (2) enables risk diversification by taking positions in assets and liabilities with non-national risks, reducing the volatility of national income and consumption; (3) makes it possible to complement residents' investment with foreign investment, incorporating new technologies for the exploitation and management of resources; (4) External investment access to new markets, where the comparative advantages of the Chilean productive sectors can be taken advantage of and; (5) enables the delivery of a more efficient and comprehensive provision of financial services for home users by opening up competitionto external agents. Financial Integration and Sharpening of Economic Cycles However, it should be noted that financial openness also represents a number of challenges and risks, especially for a small economy. First of all, mention should be made of the transition from a closed capital account or without access to international markets to an open one, which can lead to a massive inflow of capital; Such an entry responds so much to a possible differential betweeninternal and external rates, such as the adjustment of the stock of assets that become part of the portfolio of foreign investors to balance risks and returns until the desired level of them is reached. This process can generate excessive increases inthe prices of domestic assets which, in turn, can lead to unsustainable increases in Domestic aggregate demand with consequent upward pressures on the prices of non-tradable goods and services and on widening of the current account deficit. These are transitory phenomena since the correction in domestic demand Forced by the deterioration in the external accounts, it will end up bursting the bubble in the price of national assets, as we have experimented in Chile, especially in the eighties, thus forcing a correction in its value that can be painful and accompanied by recessive symptoms. This is precisely shown in the financial integration experiences of Mexico in 1994-95, Asia in 1997 and Russia in 1998. where changes in expectations of return on assets, hedging risks or contagion effects, led to increases in market volatility and major reversals in capital flows and the value of domestic assets. It should be borne in mind that in an open economy that receives a strong flow of external capital, monetary policy is not in a position to avoid the expansionary impact on the price of assets, since it loses part of its autonomy and effectiveness in regarding the control of domestic demand. At such a stage of the capital cycle, the reduction in the relevant external interest rate Generated by the interest of foreign investors to acquire assets in the country, it joins the exchange rate optimism topressure the value of the national currency towards appreciation. This limits the effective range in which monetary policy can influence the spending through increases in the real interest rate. Capital account regulations and policies allow, Some measure, isolating the domestic capital market d0 especially short-term d0 returning it to monetary policy Some room to operate with interest rate increases. This at least partially improves its effectivenessin controlling the on the expansion of domestic spending, as our own experience has shown. On the other hand, it has been amply demonstrated that the soundness of the financial system is key to moderating the impacts cyclicals of capital flows. A financial system under an inadequate regulatory framework amplifies the cyclical effects of economy. Poorly supervised banks with superficial risk management tend to finance the excessive growth of the consumption andspeculative investment in the expansionary phase; this leads to both an inefficient allocation of resources and Excessive risks that end with a financial crisis in the downturn phase when asset prices decline. Information asymmetries and limitations play an important role in amplifying the business cycles generated by financial intermediation. In particular, according to some observers, globalization makes the selection of investments, given the increasegenerated in the menu of available assets, making it more expensive and difficult to acquire the information on individual investment possibilities. Lack of self-information stimulates herd behavior or imitation of the actionsof other investors, which is a way of basing decisions on other people's information. In the sector Banking, on the other hand, we have that the limitation of information can lead to the adverse selection of debtors, which occurs when there is little informationabout the quality of them. This leads banks, under this situation, to tend to lend Resources with interest rates that reflect the risk of an average debtor, discouraging low-risk firms from Taking debt and, at the sametime, stimulates the over-indebtedness of high-risk companies. Finally, a problem occurs of moral hazard, with excessive risk-taking when the losses of a project are mostly assumed by the creditors of the company that develops it, while the profits are received by its managers. This problem is common in the case of of the existence of a lender of last resort to the financial system, such as the Central Bank, under a scheme of Inadequate supervision. This is reflected in excessive risk-taking by debtors and financial institutions that It is particularly accentuated when abundant external resources are available, which tends to amplify the cyclical effects of Capital inflows. Thus, a significant inflow of capital may imply an excessive expansion of aggregate demand, with negative effects on the financial system and exacerbation of business cycles. This problem is significantly aggravated when regulation, Financial market supervision and transparency are inadequate. Evolution of the Regulatory Framework in Chile Taking into account the advantages and disadvantages of external integration, the policy of openness employed by the Thepresent decade has been characterized by the maintenance of a system of financial supervision that has been very strict that limits risks in the financial system, and by implementing a set of regulations to the opening of the Capital account, within the framework of the monetary and fiscal policies experienced. These have been aimed at controlling the degree integration of domestic and external markets and prioritise faster progress in the integration of direct investment and medium- and long-term indebtedness. The policy instruments used to conduct the opening process have been exchange regulations and those affecting different capital flows. In terms of exchange regulations, it shouldbe noted that in the present decade the foreign exchange market has evolved permanently from a highly regulated dual market d0 formal and informal d0 to an increasingly unified one. The dual approach of the foreign exchange market was gradually modified during thenon-sale. Confidence in the Chilean economy and the stability of its External accounts have made it possible to gradually reduce exchange restrictions, particularly those affecting the foreign trade, allowing the unification of markets, whichis reflected in the fact that since 1996 there has been no price differential between both foreign exchange markets. In terms of capital flow regulations, these have been focused on (a) reducing capital inflows to amounts considered "worthy" by the economy; (b) maintain a degree of independence from monetary policy; (c) reduce the volatility of capital movements to and from Chile; (d) maintain a sound external financial position at the country level, both interms of liquidity and solvency. The main regulations apply to capital inflows and have been categorized by type of operation d1 credit, investment direct, portfolio investmentd1, a one-year Central Bank deposit. Outstanding among theseare the reserve requirements for debt and investments portfolio, in force from 1991 to 1998; the period of permanence of one year for investments in general, and the conditions minimums for bond issuers and ADRs. The reserve requirement in foreign currency, currently at 0% rate, aims to compensate for the differential between internal and external interest rates, reducing the possibilities of arbitrage by increasing entry costs; Thus, it discourages short-term capitalinflows, thus giving greater independence to monetary and exchange rate policy. The rules on permanence and minimum deadlines are intended to discourage the entry of speculative capital and restrict liquidity of external institutional investors, so as to avoid a transitory and over-diension of capitals for this concept. The minimum amounts and risk classifications have been intended to decrease the likelihood of that a Chilean company, issuer of debt or equity in international markets, may not comply with its external commitments, thus causing a negative image effect for the financing of other local companies. To the extent that domestic and external conditions, and in particular the development and deepening of trans Titles of Chilean companies, have allowed it, these requirements have been relaxed. Capital outflows, which have been categorized by agent d1 individuals and companies, institutional investors, banks and exporters d1 have been closely relatedto exchange restrictions. These have been removed according to the conditions have allowed and today, in general terms, the outflow of capital is completely free through the informal exchange market, although there are still some limitations on the access of individuals and companies to the formal exchange market. In the case of banks and Institutional investors, there are maximum amounts for the holding of foreign assets, related to a regulation prudential and not with a change regulation. Luxuries of Capitals The favourable positioning of the Chilean economy in international markets is evident in the evolution of experienced capital flows into the country. While in the period 1990 - 1995 the average capital inflowreached 6.8% of GDP in the period 1996-1997 increased to 8.8% and decreased to 3.3% in 1998, as a result of the crisis of Asia and its subsequent repercussions. Southeast Asian countries without controls on the flow of capitalis, prior to the crisis showed income from abroad around 10% of GDP. In post-crisis form, and as a result of the Volatility that the composition of the flow of capital represented for these countries, a net outflow of capital, making the internal situation of their economies even more difficult. Some even implemented controls at the exit of Capital. As a result of measures to discourage the entry of speculative capital into Chile, there has been a Important change in the composition of the capital account, giving solidity and stability to the opening process: while in 1990 23 per cent of capital account flows were medium-term and 42 per cent were short-term loans during the period 1997-1998, medium-term credit flows accounted for 67 per cent of flows, and short-term credit flows accountedfor a Stock reduction equivalent to 29% of net capital flows in 1998. For its part, foreign investment has shown a High dynamism, increasing its participation in relation to external indebtedness. While in 1990 35% of flows In responseto foreign investment, in the period 1997-1998 its share reached more than 64% of capital flows. It should be noted that these figures incorporate Chilean investment abroad, which has been increasing year after year, both for ininstitutional investors as well as for companies and individuals. Foreign direct investment, due to its long-term horizon, is strongly associated with perceptions of stability. economic and political investors. Chile, in this sense,has extraordinarily positive rates. Indeed, the Foreign direct investment in our country averaged for the period 1996-98 at a level of just over 6 per cent of GDP. This figure is approximately double that recorded in termsof the product, by the rest of the Latin American countries. and Southeast Asian countries, and about 50% higher than Eastern European countries such as Poland, Hungary and the Republic Czech. This solidity in the external accounts has been reflectedin indicators that reflect a low vulnerability of our economy. Chile's reserves are almost four times the short-term external debt plus amortizations for the current period. This the same indicator for the rest of Latin America andAsia is 0.8 and 1.1, respectively. Also, today the reserves are equivalent to almost half of the total external debt in our country, in circumstances that for the rest of Latin America are a fourth Part and just over a third for theAsian countries in which the crisis broke out. This position of solidity is allowing to circumvent the obstacles generated by the current crisis in such a way that the national economy is in a position to start its recovery after a temporary slowdownin its rate of growth. Conclusions The positive economic results achieved by the country during the present decade, reaffirm the quality of policies Economic. In particular, the gradual and sustained opening of the capital account has been a successful process. From the year After an international crisis, it has had strong effects on commodity prices; However, contrary to what is Ocurrido at other stages of our history, or to other countries in the current conjuncture, our external accounts are solid And the economy overcomes the trance only with a temporary slowdown in growth. In the midst of an international stage Inwhich external conditions show only a tendency to stabilize, it is advisable to maintain cautious policies with long-term prospects. In this context, the policies of the Central Bank will seek to privilege a gradual but lasting recovery of economic growth, preserving macroeconomic stability and reiterating its commitment to a process of sustained reduction of inflation, as well as to the reasonable balance of external accounts. In a seminaror sponsored by the Maritain Institute, the explicit consideration of the value elements implicit in our Posture is especially necessary. In Maritain's words, "The practical sciences seek to know, not to know, but to to seek by actions the good of man (a good other than the pure act of knowing the truth)." Financial integration well Managed, it allows to take advantage of the opportunities offered by a much wider globalized world, with more and better trade international, with sustained economic growth and gradual convergence towards world living standards developed. All this is very important for developing countries that, like Chile, seek to overcome poverty and offer equals. Opportunities for progress to all its inhabitants. Only through sustained growth, achievable by taking advantage of these opportunities, the challenge of overcoming poverty is possible; Only with stable and sustained growth can the Opportunities towardsRiba and not downwards, allowing access to education, health and better standards and quality of life to the population as a whole. In this decade there are clear signs of progress in this regard: Chile's poverty rates have been Reduced by half andnumerous indicators show significant progress in social areas of education and health. The Maintaining policies that contribute to sustained growth within a framework of stability is the best contribution that the monetarian authority can make to the country, thus generating conditions to sustain and accentuate these advances. The person Not the policies themselves, are at the center of our attention and our ethical obligation. Perhaps I should quote here another thought of Maritain, which is reiterated in several of his books "In the Degrees of Knowledge." and in "Philosophy of History": "Nature has laws that may be immutable but events are not. events are influenced by manycausalities in their space-time dimension and, therefore, events are a mix of nature and adventure." If we apply this to history, Maritain said, we also have the freedom of man, who is the freedom of man. basis of his philosophical thought.
