Adems, la aplicacin de una poltica fiscal ms restrictiva durante ste y el prximo ao, tal como lo ratificaran las nuevas autoridades del Ministerio de Hacienda, ayudar en forma decisiva a moderar las posibles presiones que se generen sobre la inflacin. Contribuye tambin a que el efecto de reajustes transitorios de precios no retroalimente la espiral de expectativas inflacionarias en los meses venideros.  Asimismo, la reduccin del dficit fiscal, facilitar una mayor competitividad de los productos chilenos en los mercados forneos, a travs de la permanencia de un tipo de cambio real ms alto. Por los elementos antes mencionados y por la posicin en el ciclo en que se encuentra nuestra economa, considero qel restablecimiento del equilibrio fiscal, tal como lo ha sealado el gobierno, es un tema prioritario que debe considerar la poltica econmica del gobierno durante el presente ao y el prximo. El gobierno y el Ministro de Hacienda necesitan, y merecen, el apoyo de todo el pas para mantener con decisin sus objetivos de poltica en este campo.  La poltica monetaria, en coordinacin con la poltica fiscal, deber favorecer y crear las condiciones tales para que se alcancen los objetivos de crecimiento econmico sobre su trayectoria de tendencia en un contexto de inflacin baja y estable, dentro de la meta objetivo de mediano plazo. Es til resaltar que para la consecucin de este ltimo objetivo, tambin contribuyen importantes modificaciones institucionales introducidas en el pasado reciente, cuyo resultado ha sido una mayor flexibilidad cambiara y una cada vez mayor apertura de la cuenta de capitales, que esperamos seguir perfeccionando, con la debida prudencia, de ahora en adelante.  Quisiera destacar, adems, que sobre la base de la experiencia, ha sido posible establecer una coordinacin fluida y constructiva entre el Ministerio de Hacienda y el Banco Central.  Nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria del Banco Central  Durante los noventa, en cumplimiento del mandato constitucional del Banco Central de velar por la estabilidad de precios, ao a ao se fueron fijando metas para la inflacin, cada vez ms bajas. Las metas puntuales fueron muy tiles para reducir la inflacin durante el decenio pasado y para construir un grado cada vez mayor de credibilidad. Hemos alcanzado ya una tasa de inflacin cercana al estado de rgimen. Esto implica que la poltica monetaria debe mirar ahora no los acontecimientos da a da, sino el mediano plazo. Ya no se requiere reducir ms la inflacin cada ao, sino que se necesita mantener tasas de inflacin dentro de parmetros definidos. En este contexto es que el nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria, enfatiza para la inflacin un horizonte de fijacin de mediano plazo de la meta (ms all de un ao) y un valor rango ms que una cifra puntual y precisa.  La extensin del horizonte de fijacin de la meta de un ao hacia el mediano plazo, obliga al Banco Central a enfatizar ms la realizacin de ejercicios de proyeccin y de seguimiento del comportamiento de las expectativas de los agentes privados sobre la inflacin futura. Diversos estudios confirman que normas de comportamiento de un Banco Central que se basan en expectativas y predicciones de la evolucin futura de la inflacin son ms eficientes porque disminuyen la variabilidad tanto de la inflacin como del producto. En forma simple, estas normas incorporan el hecho de que existen rezagos en la transmisin de la poltica monetaria y, por tanto, actan con la anticipacin adecuada.  La seleccin de un rango y no de un objetivo puntual para la inflacin permite acomodar diversos tipos de impactos de tal forma que la inflacin tenga un margen de fluctuacin en el corto plazo sin que el Banco Central se vea obligado a ser excesivamente activo con el fin de no desviarse transitoriamente de la meta. El uso de un rango es un reconocimiento de que existe un grado de incertidumbre sobre el comportamiento de la economa y sobre el rezago con el que la poltica monetaria acta sobre la inflacin; es un reconocimiento de que siempre existe la posibilidad de que se presenten fenmenos que afectan la economa y la inflacin, que son imposibles de anticipar.  Este nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria, entrega la flexibilidad necesaria para evaluar estos fenmenos y actuar tomando en consideracin las repercusiones que stos ocasionan en la economa. Sin embargo, el funcionamiento apropiado del nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria requiere evitar que el efecto de los shocks externos o internos se concentre en un solo mercado. En el pasado reciente, limitado por la operacin de las bandas cambiaras y su efecto sobre la evaluacin de los riesgos privados, el Banco Central no estuvo en condiciones de distribuir en varios mercados el efecto de eventos inesperados. Ahora, despus de un cuidadoso trabajo preparatorio que tom casi dos aos, ha sido posible introducir la flotacin cambiara que, en conjunto con una poltica fiscal responsable, alivia el peso que recaa slo sobre la tasa de inters. El nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria es coherente con un sistema de mayor flexibilidad cambiara, tal como el que existe hoy en la economa chilena.  Este esquema reconoce que la tasa de inters no es un instrumento eficiente para enfrentar los efectos de primera vuelta, o de impacto, de presiones inflacionarias originadas en aumentos de costos. Sin embargo, la tasa de inters debe usarse, con la debida prudencia, para transmitir seales claras de que el Banco Central no facilitar la generalizacin de tales presiones. Si la poltica monetaria acomodara todas las reacciones frente a presiones especficas de costos, caeramos inevitablemente en la vieja trampa de la espiral precios-salarios a impulsos de la indizacin y de las reacciones de cada sector que cree tener un grado de poder monoplico sobre el mercado. Algunas de estas reacciones se han hecho pblicas en semanas recientes, y es mi deber llamar la atencin sobre ellas y los peligros que implican.  Debo dejar en claro que una decisin de no intervenir cuando la inflacin efectiva se encuentra dentro del rango meta, no debe ser confundida con inactividad, o con la intencin de conseguir una supuesta reactivacin econmica ms rpida o menores tasas de desempleo aceptando una inflacin mayor. Es indispensable reiterar que la historia econmica moderna demuestra con claridad que los intentos de aumentar el empleo tolerando inflaciones ms altas han resultado en fracaso. As, mantener el crecimiento del PIB en tasas cercanas al crecimiento del producto potencial es coherente con una inflacin baja y estable. En ltima instancia, el nivel de inflacin depende de la poltica monetaria y de las expectativas de los agentes, es decir, de la credibilidad que tengan los objetivos fijados por el Banco Central.  La evolucin del IPC a travs del ao 2000 seguramente mostrar incrementos mes a mes cada vez menores a partir de mediados del ao, aunque los aumentos en 12 meses reflejarn dicha tendencia con claridad slo ms adelante. Para los efectos de la meta de inflacin, resulta ms apropiado considerar una medida de la inflacin que excluye las presiones de costos de primera vuelta, como lo hace el IPC subyacente. Cuando se miran plazos ms largos, como el horizonte actual de 12 a 24 meses del nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria, la diferencia entre ambos ndices, IPC total e IPC subyacente, tiende a desaparecer. Pero en el anlisis mes a mes, dichas diferencia pueden llevar a los agentes a confusiones innecesarias. Debo decirlo claramente: para la poltica monetaria nueva, lo que importa son las tendencias en el horizonte medio, y la poltica se decidir de acuerdo con ellas y con las seales que se desea entregar al mercado.  Por esta razn, el Consejo del Banco Central ha decidido publicar un Informe de Poltica Monetaria, cuatrimestral, que explicar su visin sobre las tendencias de mediano plazo en la tasa de inflacin, y las probabilidades de que la inflacin registrada se aparte de dichas tendencias. Por esta misma razn, hemos acordado acortar el perodo de retraso en la publicacin de minutas de nuestras discusiones. De hecho, la mayor transparencia, al igual que la flotacin cambiara, es un ingrediente indispensable del nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria. El primer Informe de Poltica Monetaria se entregar en el mes de mayo a la Comisin de Hacienda del Senado y al conocimiento pblico.  - Conclusiones  Antes de terminar, quiero reiterar que la reactivacin de la economa ya est en marcha, pues los indicadores de actividad est estn mostrando una clara evolucin positiva. Adicionalmente, por el lado del escenario internacional tambin se esperan buenas noticias respecto del crecimiento econmico mundial, lo cual favorece las perspectivas de crecimiento en nuestro pas en el futuro cercano.  En el plano interno, la tasa de inters de poltica monetaria contina con una orientacin levemente expansiva respecto de su impacto sobre la demanda, en forma coherente con las holguras en el grado de utilizacin de los recursos de la economa y en un contexto donde se espera una poltica fiscal contractiva durante el ao. Esta situacin facilita que la demanda interna transitoriamente pueda crecer ms rpidamente que el producto. No obstante, en el mediano plazo este crecimiento debe acercarse progresivamente al potencial de la economa, de tal forma de evitar que se incuben presiones inflacionarias no deseadas.  El nuevo esquema de poltica monetaria aplicada aplicado por el Banco Central, en coordinacin con las dems polticas econmicas, buscar en la actual coyuntura que el crecimiento econmico contine sobre una trayectoria saludable, con una inflacin baja y estable, para lo cual actuar con carcter anticipativo y preventivo, en coherencia con este propsito y con la debida anticipacin.

Title: Analysis of the Economic Outlook and Medium-Term Economic Projections
text: Analysis of the Economic Outlook and Medium-Term Economic Projections Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at Sociedad Nacional de Miner92a. 21 June 2000 Introduction I want to thank the National Mining Society for the opportunity to share with you the vision of the economic situation that the Central Bank currently has, taking as a starting point the recently published Monetary Policy Report for May. I will comment on projections of inflation and economic growth, but within a framework of analysis aimed at deepening some aspects, such as i) the assumption of constant monetary policy interest rate during the projection horizon; (ii) the assumed future trajectory for the exchange rate and (i) the different measures of inflation. I. Base Projection Scenario From late 1999 to date, the Chilean economy has continued on a trajectory of growth and low inflation. Indeed, the figures for May from the National Institute of Statistics indicate that core inflation measured by the CPI remains for the eighth consecutive month below 3% annually, while inflation measured by the total CPI stands at 3.6%. The fact that the latter is above the former is due to mainly to the increase experienced by the prices linked to oil, energy and transport during the current year. Despite this, there is no evidence of an acceleration in the rest of the prices at the consumer level. However, there is evidence that in the case of the Chilean economy the empirical link between the CPI and the MPI is quite weak. Nominal wages showed an upward trend during the first quarter of the year, which moderated slightly during April. In summary, excluding the oil effect, there are no signs of changes in the trend of inflation, which remains controlled and below 3.0% per year. Externally, growth prospects for the world economy remain favourable. The expectation of a soft landing of the US economy currently seems more likely than the possibility of a violent slowdown in US activity. The dynamism of economic activity in Europe has increased, and there is a healthy speed of recovery in the emerging economies of Asia and Latin America, although the latter region moderated its pace of recovery during the first quarter of this year. However, growth in the world economy is expected to be slightly above 4 per cent per annum during the years 2000 and 2001. The prices of the futures markets during this week show a downward trajectory for the price of crude oil in the remainder of this year, reflecting an expectation of a significant increase in production in the coming months. Over the past few weeks, the volatility of international financial markets has remained in step with the background to the US economy. As expected, the Federal Reserve raised its target interest rate by 50 basis points last May, to 6.5%. The latest record of the US economy shows signs of a gradual slowdown in activity. The market consensus expects an additional 50 base hikes in the remainder of the year. International inflation is expected to increase moderately from 1998 and 1999. In turn, external inflation measured in dollars will increase further as a result of the expected depreciation of the dollar in international markets, as global growth becomes more balanced between the United States and the rest of the developed economies. At the domestic level, during 2000, monetary conditions have become somewhat less expansionary. Indeed, the monetary policy interest rate was raised twice during the first quarter of the year in order to prevent temporary cost pressures, such as those linked to oil prices, from taking root in the inflationary trend and in the expectations of economic agents. The successful result of this placement of external debt is a clear representation of the confidence in the Chilean economy in the world financial markets. From Chile's point of view, the international issuance of bonds in UF, by Chilean companies, is a way to reduce the exchange risk. However, the prospects for recovery in investment are still weak, at least for the remainder of this year, taking into account the surplus of installed capacity and the expected contraction in public investment. In terms of prices and in a medium-term perspective, no significant changes in the price of fuels are anticipated, although there could be variations, given the recent evolution of the exchange rate and the price of gasoline and diesel oil in international markets. In any case, changes in these prices would mainly affect the short-term evolution of inflation, and not its trend represented by core inflation, although this will depend on the persistence shown by the price that currently prevails in international markets. Inflation expectations in the private sector, according to the results of the surveys carried out by the Central Bank, have moved marginally upwards since April, with inflation expected for December 2000 standing at 4.2% in June. Despite this higher inflation expectation for the current year, it should be noted that in 2001 it remained stable at 3.5%. II. Risk Balance Overall, the balance of risks to the central projection for economic growth is now more balanced than in the May Report, mainly due to the greater likelihood that the US economy will achieve a soft landing. However, the risks associated with the baseline scenario of total and core CPI inflation have changed. First, the recent behaviour of oil prices in international markets incorporates an additional element that moves upward inflation risks, especially in the short term and in particular inflation measured by the total CPI. Although these effects are transitory, from the perspective of monetary policy it is important to be careful not to trigger knock-on effects on other prices and inflationary expectations. So far the fuel price increases at the beginning of the year have had only a minor impact on the rest of the economy's prices, but the accumulation of increases could modify this scenario. For this reason, this is a factor of care that should continue under observation, because it could alter the medium-term projections of the total CPI. In addition, the continued volatility of international financial markets increases the risk of exchange rate depreciation. These greater risks, which mean a greater probability of rising inflation, are partially offset by a more favorable external scenario, in the sense that the US economy slows down more gradually. III. Projections Before commenting in particular on last May's projections and the way in which they would have been modified in the light of the additional background gathered recently, I think it is useful to clarify some important concepts when interpreting the results of the projections. First, it is essential to bear in mind that the projections are conditional on the following working assumption: that the monetary policy interest rate remains stable at its current level throughout the projection horizon that corresponds to two years. This working assumption is based on the fact that the main objective of the projection exercise is to assess whether the current level of the policy rate is consistent with an expected trajectory for inflation within the target range. Thus, if it is detected, for example, that the probability of inflation exceeding the target range in the 24-month assessment horizon is increasing, then the Central Bank Board could decide to raise the policy interest rate with the aim of bringing inflation back into line within the limits of the predefined range. Second, while not a projection element in itself, having a future trajectory for the nominal and real exchange rate is an indispensable input to the projection exercise. This is because the evolution of the nominal exchange rate, together with international inflation, influences the prices of importable goods and the conditions of external competitiveness. However, this indicator shows a relatively high degree of volatility, as a result of a high variability in perishable food prices, mainly explained by seasonal and climatic factors, and fuel prices, strongly linked to the evolution of the international price of oil. The main utility of these trend inflation indicators is their greater link with the demand conditions prevailing in the economy. For this reason, the Board of the Central Bank mainly attends to the projected evolution of these core inflation measurements, in order to make its monetary policy decisions. It is important to bear in mind that the more uncertainty there is about the evolution of the different variables that affect inflation, and that are beyond the control of monetary policy, the greater the width of the band. As this uncertainty is always greater the farther away the projection horizon, the wider the bands for the farther horizons. In addition, if from a certain moment within the projection horizon the risks are perceived more charged towards one direction or another, then the bands in the remaining period will be wider towards the respective side, that is, the one that concentrates the greatest probability. In other words, the amplitude of the intervals reflects the degree of uncertainty surrounding monetary policy decision-making, and the possible asymmetry of risks. This has important implications for how the band's breadth is analyzed and interpreted. The extension of the horizon for setting the one-year target towards the medium term forces the Central Bank to place greater emphasis on carrying out projection exercises and monitoring the behavior of private agents' expectations about future inflation. Keeping inflation within a target range rather than a target point gives greater flexibility and autonomy to the actions of monetary policy. For this reason, the Council I chair has decided to systematically increase the level of information it provides to the market, mainly in relation to its view on medium-term trends in the inflation rate, through its Monetary Policy Reports. At the same time, it has been decided to shorten the publication time of the minutes of the monthly monetary policy meetings, as a way to provide greater tools for the decisions of market agents. Finally, I would like to emphasize that the level of inflation depends to a large extent on the expectations of market agents, that is, on the credibility of the objectives set by the Central Bank. Monetary policy is most effective and credible when the general public and financial actors in particular are clearly aware of its fundamentals. La meta operacional de mediano plazo se define en trminos de la variacin del Indice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC). No obstante, este indicador muestra un grado relativamente alto de volatilidad, como resultado de una alta variabilidad de los precios de alimentos perecibles, explicada fundamentalmente por factores estacionales y climticos, y de los precios de los combustibles, vinculados fuertemente a la evolucin del precio internacional del petrleo. La extensin del horizonte de fijacin de la meta de un ao hacia el mediano plazo, obliga al Banco Central a enfatizar ms la realizacin de ejercicios de proyeccin y de seguimiento del comportamiento de las expectativas de los agentes privados sobre la inflacin futura. Para finalizar, quiero enfatizar que el nivel de inflacin depende en gran medida de las expectativas de los agentes del mercado, es decir, de la credibilidad que se tenga sobre los objetivos fijados por el Banco Central. La poltica monetaria es ms efectiva y creble cuando el pblico en general y los agentes financieros en particular, conocen claramente sus fundamentos. Title: External shocks and financial policy in the global economy
text: External Shocks and Financial Policy in the Global Economy Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile at the VI Financial Meeting "Business and Economic Outlook: How to Win the Second Half" organized by ICARE, July 25, 2000. I would like to thank ICARE for its invitation and take this opportunity to reflect on what it means for a small and open economy like Chile's to live in a world that is characterized by an increasing integration of its markets and at the same time is affected by strong volatilities. I would like to refer mainly to the progress we have made at the macroeconomic and financial level and to the future challenges in the micro-finance sphere. 1. In small countries highly dependent on global economic developments, external market volatilities manifest themselves mainly through fluctuations in commodity prices (terms of trade) and changing international financial conditions, which may imply varying degrees of constraints on external financing conditions. There are two options for dealing with external volatility: trying to suppress it, or learning to live with it. In Chile we have chosen to confront the volatilities that affect our economy by moving towards a regime that allows us to accommodate this phenomenon, that is, to solve or eliminate the weaknesses that magnify and propagate volatility within the economy. This means, in practice, moving towards an ever stronger link with financial markets. and the development and deepening of the national financial system. This will reduce liquidity constraints and, ultimately, the volatility itself that is affecting the economy. Thus, a wide range of possibilities for future growth opens up, through a modern, developed and integrated financial market. 6. At this point I would like to emphasize, however, that it is not easy to move from a regime of suppressive controls to a regime where the accommodation of policies and instruments to coexist with volatility predominates. On the contrary, it is a difficult road and even more, not without risks. However, this does not mean that after evaluating the costs and benefits, in the long term it is, without any doubt, the most beneficial approach for the country. 7. In Chile, we have been able to learn important lessons from the past, so we have been carrying out a gradual and orderly transition process in the direction of learning to live with volatilities, a process that began some years ago. 8. We believe that an important contribution that countries' central banks can make to ensuring greater financial stability is to help create the conditions for the effects of (especially external) shocks to be spread across different markets. In this way, what is sought, for example, is that exchange rate adjustments can help alleviate pressures on interest rates, thus reducing volatility in each of the markets individually, within a policy scheme that is internally coherent. 9. In this type of scheme, an important point to keep in mind is that fiscal policy plays a fundamental and complementary role with other macroeconomic policies when faced with a major external shock, such as those that our economy has had to save during its history. 10. This is how, in recent years we have taken great steps towards the implementation of mechanisms that help to coexist better with volatilities. 11. Previously, the limited integration of foreign exchange markets, as well as controls on the entry of foreign capital, through market-related instruments, supported by a mandatory non-discriminatory minimum period of permanence of foreign capital in the country, sought to eliminate or reduce the volatility of capital movements. Such controls were consistent with a relatively narrow band of exchange rates that limited the peso's volatility against the dollar, but inevitably amplified interest rate movements. This regime, which began operating in the early 90s, acted in parallel with increasingly strengthened banking supervision and regulation, which included the application of the Basel principles, which were incorporated into the banking legislation developed after the financial crisis of the 80s. 12. However, as regulation and supervision improved, the financial system developed more and more. For several years, the actions of the Central Bank were aimed at increasing the integration of exchange markets, until in 1997 access to the formal exchange market was released. More recently, the Central Bank began to introduce, in close cooperation with the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions, new, strict and prudential rules in the financial system, aimed at limiting the risks of banks, but at the same time providing greater flexibility in the type of operations and derivatives that banks can carry out both abroad and in Chile. This is how, together with the discipline achieved in the control of inflation during the decade of the '90s, very important measures were implemented that sought the expansion of markets and risk hedging instruments, whether of currencies, interest rates or maturities, in such a way as to achieve an efficient and substantial rearrangement of the portfolios of private non-bank agents. These measures include credit derivatives, forwards, futures and swaps of interest rates, currencies and readjustability units, interbank and repo operations in foreign currency and zero coupon bonds of the Central Bank. 13. In other words, the ground was gradually prepared at the national financial level through the provision of the necessary tools so that the private agents themselves were responsible for taking the appropriate hedging instruments to hedge against the main financial risks prevailing in our country. 14. In fact, even the accounting system used in the Central Bank had to be modified, since historically international reserves and external liabilities were converted to pesos for accounting purposes through the use of the central rate of the exchange rate (exchange rate agreement), a mechanism that in 1998 was replaced by the valuation of external assets and liabilities at the market exchange rate (observed exchange rate). 15. This was probably the first public step towards regime change of exchange policy. 16. Subsequently, important modifications were made in the regulations of the capital account, as well as in the exchange rate regime, which sought greater openness and flexibility of these markets. This is how the floating band of the exchange rate was consistently widened, with only one exception forced by circumstances; The unremunerated reserve requirement for capital inflows was gradually reduced until it was set at 0% and the mandatory minimum period of permanence of foreign capital was reduced until its elimination, among other measures. At the same time, banks were authorized to operate foreign currency forwards; to finance international trade in foreign currency even between third countries; to make cross-border financial placements and investments in a growing range of countries, companies and instruments; and to operate interest rate derivatives, all aspects that may seem very natural and commonly used in more developed economies. but that they were excluded in a policy regime where policymakers sought to eliminate volatility rather than live with it. 18. When all these ingredients were introduced and were working properly, a situation that took several years of work to achieve, in September 1999 the Central Bank of Chile opted to abandon the floating band of the exchange rate, letting the peso float freely according to the rules of the market. Contrary to what happened in other countries, this was done at a time chosen by us, and not because we were cornered and with no other option. With this important measure, the Central Bank also formalized its firm commitment not to intervene in the exchange market, unless it is in extreme situations and with the obligation to publicly inform the reasons and amounts of the intervention. This achieves full coherence of the floating exchange rate scheme with the inflation targeting scheme. Another important milestone that has recently occurred in our financial market, and which has meant another step towards a better coexistence with volatilities, is related to the placement in international financial markets of external debt denominated in national currency. Indeed, at the end of May the Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance made it possible to issue UF bonds abroad. The World Bank has already made the first international issuance of bonds in Chilean currency indexed (UF), with a maturity of five years and at an interest rate of UF plus 6.6%, somewhat below that of similar documents of the Central Bank at that time. Similar issues have recently been announced. 21. This issue, having been made through this prestigious organization, is characterized by having a low level of risk at the international level. For this reason, it is an attractive source for foreign investors to take risks in Chilean currency and thus achieve greater diversification of their portfolios, which represents an important step towards the financial integration of our country with the rest of the world. The successful result of this placement of external debt is a clear representation of the confidence in the world financial markets regarding the Chilean economy. From Chile's point of view, the international issuance of UF bonds by our companies constitutes an important mechanism to reduce exchange rate risk. 22. Thus, we can certainly say that fundamental steps have been taken for the opening and integration of our financial market. However, we believe that there is still work to be done in this regard, in order to further strengthen ties with international markets that facilitate a further deepening of our instruments and markets. 23. With the exchange rate policy regime in force in our country, we have managed to dilute in more than one market the effects that could have on a small and open economy such as Chile's, the volatilities of international financial markets, such as those we experienced in the recent past, and that we will surely continue to observe. 24. In theoretical terms, we could think of an ideal system where it would be possible to reach a level of total regulation and supervision of the financial system, so that it is strict enough to deal with any kind of shock. But the question that immediately arises is whether such a regulatory regime to avoid risks at any cost, is not leaving viable and profitable projects outside the financial markets, implying in the long run a high cost for society? A very heavy regulatory hand can discourage innovation. One that is too light can put property rights at risk. 25. Clearly what really exists is a comparison between costs and benefits, linked to a series of variables that are related to the choice of the policy regime used (monetary and exchange rate), the way in which volatilities are faced and the regulatory regime that best suits the conditions of the economy. 26. The risks involved in the approach of accommodation to volatilities are obviously related to the transmission of these to those markets of the economy that are not sufficiently hedged to face them. Financial instruments and mechanisms can therefore be created that can cover the risks of such shocks efficiently and at reasonable costs. This strategy ensures the coherence of monetary and exchange rate policies. Options for Small and Medium Businesses T7. As we have seen, much progress has been made in the macro-financial sphere, but there is still a need to improve our micro-financial institutions. In fact, in a global world exposed to high volatility, small and medium-sized enterprises and start-ups in general require access to more fluid and more balanced financing between debt and equity. Currently, they basically access bank and supplier debt and not risk capital for financing. This exacerbates insolvency risks considering that new projects and companies undoubtedly face greater uncertainty and volatility. With an inadequate financing structure, these risks are enhanced and increased. I do not intend here to go into detail on these issues, nor to seek early solutions that are discussed in other areas. I would just like to point out a few lines of future work that seem to me to be particularly important. 28. Stimulating financing through venture capital is key. The creation of private investment funds that can issue instruments other than public offerings should stimulate financing through venture capital. This proposal was recently incorporated by the Executive Branch as part of the draft Law on takeover bids and will allow current investment funds and their administrators to be freed from regulation and supervision in the case of funds whose fundraising instruments are not public offering instruments. These private funds may be set up to finance SMEs and also to set up new businesses. 29. The draft Law on Takeover Bids, currently in the legislative process, also modifies other legal precepts that regulate investment funds in order to make the administration of the resources involved more flexible. Basically, a series of matters that the Law currently regulates are left to the free decision of what may be established by the internal regulations of the funds that must be agreed by the contributors. In addition, the vigilance committees are strengthened to safeguard this greater freedom. 30. The removal of legal investment limits reflects a trend towards greater flexibility, which significantly benefits the investment policies of such funds. In the same sense, the extension of the investment limits of the AFPs in quotas of investment funds projects a greater development for them. Similarly, the expansion of investment possibilities generates a greater development of this industry. Likewise, the funds will have greater flexibility by means of being able to make capital increases and decreases approved at an extraordinary meeting, and merge funds with each other. 31. There are also some issues that could additionally be addressed in the near future, which are related to equal taxation of investment alternatives. 32. In this area, it is necessary to highlight the relevance of the development of the venture capital industry. Indeed, companies without history, those not open to the stock exchange and in general emerging companies make up the so-called target market of the venture capital industry. This industry is key to financing new technological development projects, such as Internet projects, and in general for emerging companies, which have a greater potential for growth and contribution to the improvement of national productivity. 33. Similarly, this industry is important to improve the financing of SMEs, allowing a more balanced financing between debt and equity. This is relevant considering that these companies concentrate a high percentage of labor hiring and make an important contribution to the production of goods and services. To the extent that the indebtedness of these companies falls, the financial conditions to operate and endure over time are better, ensuring greater employment and production. While it is true that the venture capital industry needs to be given a greater boost, in practice we encounter some structural problems. Among them the lack of interest on the part of institutional investors or other investors, to make capital contributions to this industry, given that there are undoubtedly high relative costs per unit of investment. 35. Another variable that plays against this industry is the low liquidity of the quotas of investment funds in the formal secondary market. Undoubtedly, for the venture capital industry to develop, some special and necessary conditions are required in the future. 36. On the one hand, a stock market segment of emerging companies for new projects would be beneficial to implement and its operation should consider regulations less demanding than the rules in force for companies currently open to the stock market. Indeed, small companies cannot incur the same costs of opening up to the market as large companies with a stock market presence. In return, the companies that come to this new exchange should guarantee permanent and total transparency of their operations. There are already experiences in this regard in the world. 37. Germany has had a successful experience since 1997 with the new stock market segment designed for start-ups. The two most important changes developed for the new stock market refer to greater requirements for transparency of information and the requirement to comply with international accounting standards. All German stock markets are governed by the same law, but the development of these new markets establishes new rules by way of a private contract for those companies that wish to participate, a mechanism that we could well consider, duly adapted, in our country. 38. The biggest effect of this new market has been to allow tech start-ups to go public in Germany for the first time. In fact, in the last three years, more than 200 companies have opened to the public, far exceeding the openings that occurred in the first 50 years after World War II. There is also evidence that the availability of venture capital has increased as a result of the development of this alternative market. In fact, for companies of similar size there are lower spreads and greater liquidity in this market than in the traditional market, which has stimulated the opening of high-tech companies on the stock market. 39. Another special condition to develop the venture capital industry in our country could come from the improvement of the tax structure that allows an adequate treatment of capital gains from investments in new projects derived from venture capital. 40. Emerging projects financed by investment funds and venture capital typically initially produce large capital gains and few profit streams. However, depending on the tax structure (taxes on capital gains and profits) this investment decision could be more or less stimulated. 41. Regarding the possibility of accessing bank credit, different elements explain the difficulties faced by small and micro enterprises. Here are some hypotheses. 42. A first element has to do with the logic of diversification that has prevailed until now in regulation. Normally, it is not advisable for a bank to seek to concentrate its placements in certain segments, privileging diversified banks. For example, it is not currently possible for a banking institution to be able to engage preferentially in leasing and factoring, privileged vehicles for financing small businesses. The full integration of factoring and leasing businesses to banks can be quite useful for the purposes of better access to bank financing for SMEs. Moreover, the securitisation of SME credit could be considered at some future stage. 43. Second, the conventional maximum rate remains a constraint on financing a segment of small and microenterprises. In the case of microenterprises, this is financed mainly with loans in fixed installments in pesos, usually greater than 90 days. In this sense, a loan to a microentrepreneur is difficult to separate from the person who owns the business, so it is common for both financings to appear mixed with consumer loans. Recent changes in the conventional top rate have helped to lessen its effect on credit. Another restriction is related to recent legal modifications on collection procedures, which establish maximum limits on the collection of unpaid credits and tend to segment the credit market and make smaller debtors less attractive as credit subjects. 44. Third, the liberalization of foreign currency credit operations with domestic residents is a future step in the right direction. In an economy open to the outside world such as the Chilean economy, where international trade in goods and services represents over 50% of GDP, the development of financial intermediation in foreign currency has several advantages. First, companies in the tradable sector that have revenues in foreign currency can finance themselves in that same currency, thus eliminating the risk that comes from variations in the exchange rate. This is especially relevant for small and medium-sized local companies whose access to foreign currency financing abroad is very limited. On the other hand, it is possible that the participation of local banks in the foreign currency credit market with local companies implies a decrease in the margins charged to them, due to the better information and more complete relationship they have with domestic companies. These operations in foreign currency must, however, always keep in mind the necessary coverage of exchange risk. Finally, the provisioning scheme can potentially constitute an important brake on the development of small business financing. Recently, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions took a big step by relaxing the rules on provisions, maintaining the solvency and solidity that have characterized our financial system for many years. 46. In the same vein, so-called asset-based financing is not a widespread practice in Chilean banking. The use of collateral associated with inventories appears extremely expensive, and usually requires the use of so-called warrants, which are scarcely used among banks. Regarding accounts receivable, they are not accepted as collateral for portfolio classification purposes, so they are not a very attractive instrument to reduce risk. 47. A characteristic of small and medium-sized enterprises is the absence of continuous financial statements that appropriately reflect the economic/financial reality of the company. This segment of companies rarely has audited financial statements, making it difficult to analyze payment capacity from a flow perspective. Based on these elements, it is already very difficult for a small company to be in the best risk category, being the second best category, the highest to which they can aspire, for which they must have the appropriate guarantees. This puts them in a situation of greater vulnerability, since in certain situations, the reclassification towards a third category of risk involves a discreet and significant jump in the constitution of provisions. 48. Therefore, the recent announcement by the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions to add intermediate categories of risk classification is considered positive. Perhaps in the future regulatory modifications could be studied that allow, in a good portfolio classification system, to expand the sources of information other than the financial statements of the company, such as that the bank can obtain the information associated with the owner of the company and its history. In this line, it would be about accepting as part of the information to be considered, a logical sequence of credits according to amount and size, which would allow recognizing as valid the information obtained based on historical credit relationships. 49. Secondly, the rules for portfolio classification and credit risk provisions should maintain the central payment criteria and the bank's general knowledge of the debtor. However, the possibility of increasing the relative importance of payment behaviour and collateral in relation to expected future flows is a promising direction of work that could better recognize the various existing techniques for mitigating credit risks. 50. Third, another promising direction of future work is to analyze the possibility of accepting invoices as valid guarantees for classification purposes, along with the bills and other guarantees that currently exist. Obviously, invoices from solid and well-known companies would be considered. Moreover, in the case of factoring subsidiaries, this instrument forms an integral part of the business. It should be recalled that the banking law allowed the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions to incorporate factoring subsidiaries within the bank as a general rule . In that sense, it is likely that in the future invoices will be accepted as a guarantee instrument within banks. This aims to expand the range of asset-based financing possibilities. 51. Finally, another alternative would be that personal guarantees can be considered with a greater weighting in the credit rating. This means recognizing the strong incentive to pay that guarantees based on the personal assets of the business owner can represent. 52. In general, these work suggestions in no way aim to weaken the risk assessment of this segment of companies, and are based on the specificities of their behavior. 53. On the other hand, it must be recognized that the financial system is itself an industry and that, as such, it must be strengthened, in particular considering its possibilities for exporting services and the high component of knowledge and technology it uses. The Chilean financial system is very competitive and solid, compared to its regional peers. To enhance the development and competitiveness of the financial industry, it is necessary to continue improving our regulatory institutions. Considering the small size of our market, the greatest attraction would be to promote the internationalization of the system. Indeed, the Chilean financial system must continue to advance in its internationalization in order to contribute to the diversification of risks and the export of services. In this sense, the key is to create the conditions so that, from Chile, growing financial services can be offered to the rest of the region. In this strategy, it would be a fatal mistake to try to reduce the importance of the risk assessment of any group of companies. Consideration may be given to gradually liberalizing opportunities for low-risk cross-border operations related to foreign trade, as well as new alternatives for outward financial investment for banks. 55. On the other hand, to the extent that Chile integrates economically and financially with neighboring countries, in particular Mercosur, and progress is made in the financial and macroeconomic convergence of these countries, it will be possible to think of a scheme that gradually converges to one like that of the European Economic Community, which is a fully integrated economic area. where a bank from any country can easily be installed elsewhere, with a branch or a subsidiary. Likewise, any bank in one country can make cross-border loans in another nation without major requirements for country risk provisions. 56. There is still much to be done in order to deepen banking internationalization. However, for years our country has been working with perseverance and maturity to introduce structural reforms to improve links with the international financial system and develop local financial markets. Thus, much progress has been made in the development of markets for institutional investors, which necessarily improves the quality of business management since these institutions invest where management is efficient. 57. The elimination of barriers to the entry of capital from abroad and the development of derivative and insurance financial products have also contributed to this greater development as a way to give greater liquidity and depth to national instruments and markets. Financial integration, by making it possible to diversify portfolios with investments abroad; as well as the issuance of external debt in national currency, contribute to making the guarantees of the national financial market less vulnerable to macroeconomic risk. 58. In this context, I am concerned about the line of thinking that emerges these days and that assigns the regulatory system a police role, aimed at prosecuting financial operations of illegal origin. The design of the regulatory system for this purpose would involve an enormous number of operations to pursue a few. Policing functions are not specific to financial regulation, which is intended to be prudential, not police. The regulatory system can establish rules that allow, eventually, to identify operations and agents linked to crime. But it is not reasonable to establish a system full of controls for all operations, in order to pursue a few. Banking institutions may report suspicious transactions, but the task of investigating and prosecuting them is not the responsibility of the financial system but of the justice and police organizations. I am certain that all financial institutions will continue to cooperate with justice, as they have always done. 59. Our country, gradually and in a very solid way, has been moving forward so that there is less and less probability that a fall in the terms of trade will cause the real guarantees of the financial system to disappear and with them the sources of internal and external financing, as happened in 1982. 60. I believe that accommodation to volatilities through appropriate mechanisms is the most efficient way to minimize the impacts of shocks in small economies integrated into a global world such as Chile's, since it has been demonstrated that it is impossible to eliminate such volatilities. We are today in a coherent monetary and exchange rate policy regime, specially designed to deal better than in the past with external volatilities. A floating exchange rate regime and an inflation-targeting scheme as an anchor of monetary policy, which uses the interest rate as an instrument, are coupled with flexible and high-quality financial regulation and supervision. This, together with responsible and prudent fiscal management of a countercyclical rather than a procyclical nature, constitute the basis for strengthening our confidence in the future. 61. The coming changes will be rapid and profound, and their scope we cannot even imagine today. The new information and communication technologies will surely render obsolete many of the institutions as we conceive them today, and many of the instruments we use today. That is why financial regulation must give priority to flexibility. The worst mistake we could make would be to try to regulate the unregulable, to try to regulate the unknown, to put progress in a straitjacket. Financial regulation must open the doors to innovation, seeking to basically guarantee property rights and transparency. The revisions to the financial and exchange regulations in which the Central Bank has advanced in the last three years, definitely point in that direction, and will continue to do so. The Central Bank's communications policy also follows this vision, and will continue to do so, deepening the transparency of its decisions and analyses. Our financial system, the healthiest and strongest of the emerging countries and superior to that of many industrialized countries, will have much more to offer at the regional level, in our "geographical neighborhood", to the progress of our country and our neighbors.

En Chile hemos elegido enfrentar las volatilidades que afectan a nuestra economa a travs de avanzar hacia un rgimen que permita acomodarse a este fenmeno, es decir, solucionar o eliminar las debilidades que magnifican y propagan la volatilidad al interior de la economa. En este punto quiero destacar, sin embargo, que no es fcil desplazarse desde un rgimen de controles supresivos hacia un rgimen donde predomina la acomodacin de las polticas e instrumentos para convivir con la volatilidad. Creemos que una contribucin importante que pueden hacer los bancos centrales de los pases con miras a garantizar una mayor estabilidad financiera, es ayudar a crear las condiciones necesarias para que los efectos de los shocks (especialmente externos) se distribuyan en diferentes mercados. En este tipo de esquema, un punto importante a tener en mente es que la poltica fiscal cumple un rol fundamental y complementario con las restantes polticas macroeconmicas cuando se enfrenta un shock externo de importancia, como los que ha tenido que salvar nuestra economa durante su historia. Ms recientemente, el Banco Central comenz a introducir, en estrecha cooperacin con la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras, normas nuevas, estrictas y prudenciales en el sistema financiero, destinadas a acotar los riesgos de los bancos, pero entregando a su vez mayor flexibilidad en el tipo de operaciones y derivados que la banca puede realizar tanto en el exterior como en Chile. En este mbito se hace necesario destacar la relevancia del desarrollo de la industria de capital de riesgo. En efecto, las empresas sin historia, las no abiertas a la bolsa y en general las empresas emergentes conforman el denominado mercado objetivo de la industria de capital de riesgo. Esta industria es clave para financiar nuevos proyectos de desarrollo tecnolgico, como por ejemplo, proyectos de Internet, y en general para las empresas emergentes, las que presentan un mayor potencial de crecimiento y de aporte a la mejora de la productividad nacional.  De igual forma, esta industria es importante para mejorar el financiamiento de las PYME, permitiendo un financiamiento ms equilibrado entre deuda y capital. Lo anterior es de relevancia al considerar que estas empresas concentran un alto porcentaje de contratacin de mano de obra y realizan una importante contribucin a la produccin de bienes y servicios. En la medida que el endeudamiento de estas empresas baje, las condiciones financieras para operar y perdurar en el tiempo son mejores, asegurndose un mayor empleo y produccin. Entre ellos la falta de inters por parte de los inversionistas institucionales u otros inversionistas, para realizar aportes de capital a esta industria, dado que sin duda existen altos costos relativos por unidad de inversin.  Otra variable que juega en contra de esta industria es la poca liquidez de las cuotas de los fondos de inversin en el mercado secundario formal. Sin duda que para que la industria de capital de riesgo se desarrolle, se requieren algunas condiciones especiales y necesarias a futuro.  Por una parte, un segmento de bolsa de empresas emergentes para proyectos nuevos sera beneficiosa de implementar y su funcionamiento debiera considerar regulaciones menos exigentes que las reglas vigentes para las empresas abiertas actualmente al mercado de valores. En efecto, las pequeas empresas no pueden incurrir en los mismos costos de apertura al mercado que las grandes empresas con presencia burstil. Como contrapartida las empresas que acudiesen a esta nueva bolsa debieran garantizar permanente y total transparencia de sus operaciones. Ya hay experiencias a este respecto en el mundo.  Alemania ha tenido una experiencia exitosa desde 1997 con el nuevo segmento del mercado accionario diseado para empresas emergentes. Los dos cambios ms importantes desarrollados para el nuevo mercado accionario, se refieren a mayores exigencias de transparencia de informacin y el requisito de cumplir con los estndares contables internacionales. Todos los mercados accionarios alemanes se rigen por una misma ley, pero el desarrollo de estos nuevos mercados establece nuevas reglas por la va de un contrato privado para aquellas empresas que deseen participar, un mecanismo que bien pudisemos considerar, debidamente adaptado, en nuestro pas.  El mayor efecto de este nuevo mercado ha sido permitir que empresas tecnolgicas emergentes se abran a la bolsa en Alemania por primera vez. De hecho, en los ltimos tres aos, ms de 200 empresas se han abierto al pblico, lo que excede ampliamente las aperturas ocurridas en los primeros 50 aos luego de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. Tambin existe evidencia que la disponibilidad de capital de riesgo ha aumentado como resultado del desarrollo de este mercado alternativo. De hecho, para empresas de tamao similar existen menores spreads y mayor liquidez en este mercado que en el mercado tradicional, lo que ha estimulado la apertura en bolsa de empresas de alta tecnologa.  Otra condicin especial para desarrollar la industria de capital de riesgo en nuestro pas, podra venir del perfeccionamiento de la estructura tributaria que permita un tratamiento adecuado a las ganancias de capital provenientes de inversiones en proyectos nuevos derivados del capital de riesgo.  Proyectos emergentes financiados por fondos de inversin y capital de riesgo, tpicamente producen inicialmente grandes ganancias de capital y pocos flujos de utilidad. Sin embargo, dependiendo de la estructura tributaria (impuestos a las ganancias de capital y a las utilidades) se podra estimular ms o menos esta decisin de inversin.  Respecto de la posibilidad de acceder al crdito bancario, distintos elementos explican las dificultades que enfrentan la pequea y micro empresa. A continuacin revisamos algunas hiptesis.  Un primer elemento tiene que ver con la lgica de diversificacin que ha imperado hasta ahora en la regulacin. Normalmente, resulta poco recomendable que un banco busque concentrar sus colocaciones en determinados segmentos, privilegindose bancos diversificados. Por ejemplo, no es posible en la actualidad que una institucin bancaria pueda dedicarse preferentemente al leasing y al factoring, vehculos privilegiados de financiamiento de la pequea empresa. La plena integracin de los negocios de factoring y leasing a los bancos puede ser de bastante utilidad para efectos de un acceso ms adecuado de las PYME al financiamiento bancario. Ms an, se podra considerar en alguna etapa futura la securitizacin de crditos de las PYME.  En segundo lugar, la tasa mxima convencional sigue siendo una restriccin para el financiamiento de un segmento de la pequea y microempresa. En el caso de la microempresa, sta se financia principalmente con crditos en cuotas fijas en pesos, normalmente superiores a 90 das. En este sentido, un crdito a un microempresario es difcilmente separable de la persona duea del negocio, por lo cual es comn que ambos financiamientos aparezcan mezclados con los crditos de consumo. Los cambios recientes en la tasa mxima convencional han contribuido a aminorar su efecto sobre los crditos. Otra restriccin dice relacin con recientes modificaciones legales sobre los procedimientos de cobranzas, que establecen topes mximos al cobro de crditos impagos y que tienden a segmentar el mercado crediticio y a hacer menos atractivos como sujetos de crdito a aquellos deudores de menor tamao.  En tercer lugar, la liberalizacin de operaciones crediticias en moneda extranjera con residentes domsticos constituye un paso futuro en la direccin correcta. En una economa abierta al exterior como es la economa chilena, donde el comercio internacional de bienes y servicios representa sobre el 50% del PIB, el desarrollo de la intermediacin financiera en moneda extranjera presenta varias ventajas. Primero, las empresas del sector transable que tienen ingresos en moneda extranjera pueden financiarse en esa misma moneda, eliminando as el riesgo que proviene de las variaciones en el tipo de cambio. Esto es especialmente relevante para las empresas locales de tamao mediano y pequeo cuyo acceso al financiamiento en moneda extranjera en el exterior es muy limitado. Por otra parte, es posible que la participacin de los bancos locales en el mercado de crditos en moneda extranjera con empresas locales implique una disminucin de los mrgenes que se les cobran a stas, por la mejor informacin y ms completa relacin que ellos tienen con las empresas domsticas. Estas operaciones en moneda extranjera deben, sin embargo, tener siempre presente la necesaria cobertura del riesgo cambiarlo. Recientemente la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras dio un gran paso al flexibilizar las normas sobre provisiones, mantenindose inclumes la solvencia y solidez que han caracterizado a nuestro sistema financiero desde hace muchos aos.  En la misma lnea, el llamado financiamiento basado en los activos no es una prctica generalizada en la banca chilena. El uso de garantas asociadas a los inventarios aparece extremadamente costoso, y normalmente requiere el uso de los llamados warrants, los que son escasamente utilizados entre los bancos. Respecto de las cuentas por cobrar, no son aceptadas como garantas para efectos de la clasificacin de cartera, con lo cual no son un instrumento muy atractivo para disminuir el riesgo.  Una caracterstica de las pequeas y medianas empresas es la ausencia de estados financieros continuos que reflejen apropiadamente la realidad econmico/financiera de la empresa. Este segmento de empresas rara vez tiene estados financieros auditados, lo que dificulta el anlisis de la capacidad de pago desde una perspectiva de flujos. Con base en estos elementos, de por s es muy difcil que una pequea empresa quede en la mejor categora de riesgo, siendo la segunda mejor categora, la ms alta a la que pueden aspirar, para lo cual deben contar con las garantas apropiadas. Esto las pone en una situacin de mayor vulnerabilidad, ya que ante determinadas situaciones, la reclasificacin hacia una tercera categora de riesgo involucra un salto discreto y significativo en la constitucin de provisiones.  Por ello, es considerado como positivo el reciente anuncio de la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras de agregar categoras intermedias de clasificacin de riesgo. Tal vez en el futuro se podran estudiar modificaciones regulatorias que permitan, en un buen sistema de clasificacin de cartera, ampliar las fuentes de informacin distintas de los estados financieros de la empresa, como por ejemplo, que el banco pueda obtener la informacin asociada al dueo de la empresa y su historia. En esta lnea, se tratara de aceptar como parte de la informacin a considerar, una secuencia lgica de crditos segn monto y tamao, lo que permitira reconocer como vlida la informacin obtenida con base en las relaciones histricas de crdito.  En segundo trmino, las normas de clasificacin de cartera y de provisiones por riesgo de crdito deben mantener los criterios centrales de pagos y el conocimiento general que el banco tenga del deudor. Sin embargo, la posibilidad de incrementar la importancia relativa del comportamiento de pagos y de las garantas en relacin con los flujos esperados en el futuro, es una direccin de trabajo promisoria que pudiese reconocer de mejor manera las diversas tcnicas existentes de mitigacin de los riesgos de crdito.  En tercer lugar, otra direccin promisoria de trabajo futuro es analizar la posibilidad de aceptar las facturas como garantas vlidas para efectos de la clasificacin, junto con las letras y otras garantas que existen en la actualidad. Evidentemente, se consideraran las facturas de empresas slidas y conocidas. Por lo dems, en el caso de las filiales de factoring, este instrumento forma parte integrante del negocio. Cabe recordar que la ley de bancos permiti a la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras incorporar como norma general las filiales de factoring dentro del banco. En ese sentido, es probable que en el futuro las facturas sean aceptadas como un instrumento de garanta dentro de los bancos. Esto apunta a ampliar la gama de posibilidades de financiamiento basado en los activos.  Por ltimo, otra alternativa sera que las garantas personales se puedan considerar con una mayor ponderacin en la clasificacin crediticia. Esto significa reconocer el fuerte incentivo al pago que pueden significar las garantas basadas en activos personales del dueo del negocio.  En general, estas sugerencias de trabajo, de ningn modo apuntan a debilitar la evaluacin del riesgo de este segmento de empresas, y parten de la base de las especificidades que tiene su comportamiento.  Por otra parte, se debe reconocer que el sistema financiero constituye en s mismo una industria y que, como tal, debe ser potenciada, en particular considerando sus posibilidades de exportacin de servicios y el alto componente de conocimiento y tecnologa que utiliza. El sistema financiero chileno es muy competitivo y slido, comparado con sus pares regionales. Para potenciar el desarrollo y la competitividad de la industria financiera, es necesario seguir perfeccionando nuestra institucionalidad regulatoria. Considerando lo pequeo de nuestro mercado, el mayor atractivo estara en potenciar la internacionalizacin del sistema. En efecto, el sistema financiero chileno debe seguir avanzando en su internacionalizacin para efectos de contribuir a la diversificacin de riesgos y a la exportacin de servicios. En este sentido, la clave es crear las condiciones para que, desde Chile, se puedan ofrecer crecientes servicios financieros al resto de la regin. En esta estrategia, sera un error fatal pretender reducir la importancia de la evaluacin de riesgos de cualquier grupo de empresas.
