Por otra parte, en la medida que Chile se vaya integrando econmica y financieramente con los pases vecinos, en particular con el Mercosur, y se logre avanzar en la convergencia financiera y macroeconmica de estos pases, ser posible pensar en un esquema que gradualmente converja a uno como el de la Comunidad Econmica Europea, que es un rea econmica plenamente integrada, donde un banco de cualquier pas puede instalarse fcilmente en otro lugar, con una sucursal o una subsidiaria. Asimismo, cualquier banco de un pas puede hacer crditos transfronterizos en otra nacin sin mayores exigencias de provisiones por riesgo pas.  Hay todava mucho por hacer con el objeto de profundizar en la internacionalizacin bancaria. Sin embargo durante aos en nuestro pas se ha venido trabajando con perseverancia y madurez para introducir las reformas estructurales que permitan mejorar los vnculos con el sistema financiero internacional y desarrollar los mercados financieros locales. As, se ha avanzado mucho en el desarrollo de mercados para los inversionistas institucionales, lo que necesariamente mejora la calidad de la administracin de las empresas pues estas instituciones invierten donde la administracin es eficiente.  A este mayor desarrollo, tambin han contribuido la eliminacin de las barreras a la entrada de capitales desde el exterior y el desarrollo de los productos financieros derivados y de seguros como una forma de dar mayor liquidez y profundidad a los instrumentos y mercados nacionales. La integracin financiera, al hacer posible la diversificacin de los portafolios con inversiones en el exterior; as como la emisin de deuda externa en moneda nacional, contribuyen para que las garantas del mercado financiero nacional sean menos vulnerables al riesgo macroeconmico.  En este contexto, me preocupa la lnea de pensamiento que surge en estos das y que asigna al sistema regulatorio un rol policial, dirigido a perseguir operaciones financieras de origen ilegal. El diseo del sistema regulatorio con este objeto entrabara un enorme nmero de operaciones para perseguir unas pocas. Las funciones policiales no son propias de la regulacin financiera, cuyo objetivo es prudencial, no policial. El sistema regulatorio puede dejar establecidas normas que permitan, eventualmente, identificar operaciones y agentes vinculados al crimen. Pero no es razonable establecer un sistema lleno de controles para todas las operaciones, con el fin de perseguir unas pocas. Las instituciones bancarias pueden sealar operaciones que les merezcan sospecha, pero la tarea de investigarlas y perseguirlas no corresponde al sistema financiero sino a las organizaciones de la justicia y la polica. Estoy cierto que todas las instituciones financieras continuarn prestando su colaboracin a la justicia, como lo han hecho siempre.  Nuestro pas, paulatinamente y en forma muy slida, ha do avanzando para que cada vez existan menores probabilidades de que una cada de los trminos de intercambio haga que desaparezcan las garantas reales del sistema financiero y con stas las fuentes de financiamiento interno y externo, como ocurri en 1982.  Creo que la acomodacin a las volatilidades mediante los mecanismos adecuados, es la forma ms eficiente de minimizar los impactos de los shocks en economas pequeas e integradas a un mundo global como la chilena, ya que ha quedado demostrado que es imposible eliminar tales volatilidades. Estamos hoy en un rgimen de poltica monetaria y cambiara coherente, especialmente diseado para enfrentar mejor que en el pasado las volatilidades externas. Un rgimen de flotacin cambiara y un esquema de metas de inflacin como ancla de la poltica monetaria, que utiliza la tasa de inters como instrumento, se unen a una regulacin y supervisin financieras flexible y de alta calidad. Esto, junto a un manejo fiscal responsable y prudente de carcter anticclico en vez de procclico, constituyen las bases para afianzar nuestra confianza en el futuro.  Los cambios que vienen sern rpidos y profundos, y su alcance ni siquiera podemos imaginarlo hoy. Las nuevas tecnologas de la informacin y la comunicacin seguramente dejarn obsoletas a muchas de las instituciones tal como hoy las concebimos, y a muchos de los instrumentos que hoy utilizamos. Por eso, la regulacin financiera debe privilegiar la flexibilidad. El peor error que pudisemos cometer sera el de intentar regular lo irregulable, pretender normar lo desconocido, ponerle al progreso una camisa de fuerza. La regulacin financiera debe abrir las puertas a la innovacin, buscando garantizar bsicamente los derechos de propiedad y la transparencia. Las revisiones a las regulaciones en materia financiera y cambiara en las que ha avanzado el Banco Central en los ltimos tres aos, apuntan definitivamente en esa direccin, y seguirn hacindolo. La poltica de comunicaciones del Banco Central se atiene tambin a esa visin, y continuar hacindolo, profundizando la transparencia de sus decisiones y de sus anlisis. Nuestro sistema financiero, el ms sano y fuerte de los pases emergentes y superior al de muchos pases industrializados, tendr mucho ms que ofrecer en el plano regional, en nuestro "barrio geogrfico", al progreso de nuestro pas y de nuestros vecinos.

Title: Economic Developments in 2000 and Outlook for 2001 and 2002
text: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENTS IN 2000 AND PROSPECTS FOR 2001 AND 2002 Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, in the Senate on the occasion of the presentation of the Report Annual.13 September 2000. I. Introduction 1. One year ago, on the occasion of the Annual Report to the Senate, we presented in this Chamber a comprehensive policy analysis. implemented by the Central Bank, its effects on the economy and macroeconomic projections for this year. 2. The national economy was just beginning a process of recovery, after overcoming a difficult international situation, aggravated for a period of excessive domestic expenditure, and it was expected that this process would be consolidated during the current year with a rate of anticipated growth of the order of 5%. This projection, considered by many optimistic, was based on the expectation of a a general improvementin global growth and a normalization of conditions in international financial markets, as well as in boosting domestic monetary conditions. 3. Although more dynamic domestic demand andimported cost forecasts were expected, no risks were perceived significant acceleration of inflation, considering the gaps in the degree of use of resources in the economy. An increase in the inflationary record was foreseeable, butwithin limited limits. The inflation projection for At the end of 2000, it was around 3.5 per cent. 4. At the same time, we announced a series of modifications on the way of implementing the Central Bank's policies with the In order to adapt them to the newrealities. In the field of monetary policy, the achievements made in the field of control and reduced inflation prompted an improvement in the inflation targeting scheme that the Bank had implemented in 1991. Wonthe batal of ten years to bring the centennial Chilean inflation to levels that do not hinder growth and that promote a better distribution of income, it was now appropriate to maintain it at those levels, which allowed a more symmetrical monetary policy . Thus, the inflation target went from being a single and annual figure, which sought to reduce gradually but persistently the pace of price growth, to a range target, symmetrical and permanent, established between 2% and 4%. In the area of exchange rate policy, the Central Bank announced its intention not to intervene in the foreign exchange market, except in exceptional circumstances; It eliminated its commitment to support the edges of the exchange rate band, and the peso went from a Aband to a free-floating system. These two changes constitute a new monetary policy regime, which allows better absorb external and internal impacts, and avoid concentrating on a single instrument, as happened in the past, adjustment efforts and policies. 5. A number of initiatives have also been taken over the past year to increase the degree of transparency. of the policies implemented, including the periodic publication, with a lag of three months, of minuteson the meetings of the Council, publication of the calendar of monetary policy meetings and the Monetary Policy Report, with an analysis complete projections, assumptions and risks relevant to this policy. 6. Finally, with regard tofiscal policy, in September last year there was a greater degree of uncertainty as to which It would be the future of fiscal accounts considering that the country was approaching a period of presidential elections. 7. From September of last year to date, many things have happened. Externally, economic projections international, led by the dynamism of the US, have improved beyond what was initially estimated. The international price of oil has reachedrecord levels, well above what anyone could have predicted a year ago, and these increases are They have been gradually transferred to domestic consumers. International financial markets have continued exhibiting episodes of volatility,and the supply of international capital has remained scarcer, accentuated by the high US current account deficit. 8. Internally, the new government authorities have signalled a clear commitmentto fiscal discipline and framed this intention within an explicit rule aimed at maintaining the structural surplus of the Central Government at 1% of GDP. This gives fiscal policy a countercyclical character, and is a key support for the new monetary policy regime. 9. The new monetary policy pattern has made it possible to efficiently accommodate short-term inflationary surprises associated with higher fuel prices. And the flexibility of exchange rate policy has made it possible to avoidthat the impact of unexpected events, including volatility in international financial markets, focus exclusively on some markets, particularly in the interest rate, thus giving monetary policy greater autonomythan existed in the past. Finally, measures have been taken to deepen the financial integration of the national economy with the external markets, including the elimination of the minimum permanence year for investment flows. 10. The three components of thenew economic policy regime: the target range, the floating of the peso and the fiscal budget with Structural surpluses are essential to address the inevitable volatilities in an increasingly interconnected world. The New economy requiresto live with volatility, rather than trying, in vain, to suppress it. It requires flexibility and the ability to adaptation in all markets, both products and factors, and needs them to adapt in that direction of ours. institutions, our standards and our instruments. 11. Last May, as part of its Monetary Policy Report, the Central Bank presented an update on the scenario macroeconomic, and its projections for the main economic variables in view of its impacton the outlook Inflationary. This report reviews this scenario, and its consequences on the behavior of inflation and the economy national. II. Recent economic developments and medium-term prospects 12. At the beginningof last May, when the first monetary policy report was published, the information available showed that economic activity and employment were on a growth trajectory; the expansion of trading partners boosted innovations; private expectations of economic growth, as well as consumer confidence, They were gradually improving and inflation was steadily developing. In fact, the level of GDP in the last quarter of 1999 It had exceeded the highest levels of the past, leaving behind the recession in the productive sphere. 13. Certainly, there were some symptoms of slowdown in the behavior of money, sales of trade and of the real estate market, but as a whole the prospects for the Chilean economy were satisfactory, supported by a favourable external scenario and the stimulus of monetary conditions. In turn, the expected evolution for inflation was consistent with the target set for the mediumnon-term, even though it was clear that it would show an increase in the months subsequent as a result of the drag of the rise in the price of oil. 14. In this general context, the monetary policy interest rate was assessed at 5.5% (on the variation of the UF) It was appropriate to preserve an environment of price stability, which in turn favours sustainable economic growth. Private expectations, on the other hand, anticipated a rapid increase in the policy interest ratetowards its historical average. d0 close to 6.5% (over UF) d0 based on a more expansive diagnosis of spending in the national economy. 15. However, from May to the end of August, evidence of lower dynamism in domestic demand accumulated. was negatively tilting the balance of inflationary risks and finally led the Central Bank to reduce its rate of Monetary policy interest at 50 basis points at its meeting on August 28. Information we receive for the purposes of August was strong enough not to delay a decision on the matter. 16. This decision was taken in order to maintain thetrend in domestic demand in line with the inflation target of between 2% and 4% considering that, under an alternative scenario in which the policy interest rate was not corrected, the outlook for the Total and core inflation would havebeen close to 2% per year by the end of 2001 and through 2002, with a significant risk of Break the lower limit of the established target range. 17. The effect of the reduction in the monetary policy interest rate on demand is expected to be ocurra through the usual transmission mechanisms, including a positive effect on agents' expectations. 18. In the international arena, and after a period of greater uncertainty and financial turbulence between the end of April and the endof April In May, expectations of continued dynamism in the world economy (over 4% per year over the next two years) took hold. years), the risk of a sharp rise in US interest rates was reduced, while financing conditions international improved slightly. 19. Even so, in terms of markets, there was still a situation of low availability of international liquidity for emerging economies, fuelled by the strong absorption of financial resources by the USeconomy. Oil prices experienced an additional and unexpected increase in foreign markets, standing above 30 dollars per year. barrel. This situation led to an increase in production costs and a lossof real income for the Chilean economy by on what was expected in May, a loss that has been gradually passed on to domestic consumers. Indeed, by Every dollar that raises the international price of oil the national incomes e reduces by about 0.1% in a year. Although it is assumes that the price of crude oil will show a gradual decline over the next 24 months, the current projection is higher than which had been anticipated last May. 20. At the national level, more substantial evidence of a decline in the dynamism of the product and employment. The background for the second quarter confirmed a decline in the rate of GDP expansion, a rate of the order of 2% per year measured between quarters and corrected for seasonality, while the rate of creation of Jobs stopped, which meant the rebound in the unemployment rate in recent months. 21. Similarly, although the rate of growth of domestic demandincreased by an increase, its components more permanent measures, such as consumption and investment, experienced a slowdown between April and July. In this context, the Economic growth expectations and confidence indices reversed their previous improvement. 22. On the other hand, the increase in domestic fuel prices, due to the sharp increase in the international price of fuels. oil, was higher thanexpected. However, measures of core inflation (which exclude fuels and perishables, but include those of collective mobilization), together with the variation of wages, showed a Stable behaviour and evenslightly downward. This trajectory reveals, so far, few second-round effects. associated with rising oil prices, and is a better reflection of long-lasting pressures on inflation than it does the measure of the total CPI. Likewise, during the last months the inflationary expectations of the private sector have been maintained. stable and even registered a slight decrease. 23. With this information, expectations of increases in the monetary policy interest rate thatprevailed in the Market in May were gradually decreasing in the following months, which brought with it a reduction significant of the entire structure of interest rates and the consequent increase in the nominal and real exchange rate. 24. As a result of these developments, at the monetary policy meetings held by the Central Bank Board in the In June, July and August, the balance of inflationary risks gradually corrected downwards with respect to whatwas It had assessed in May on the occasion of the previous monetary policy report. At the same time, monetary conditions in the Financial markets became increasingly expansionary. 25. Finally, at the monetary policy meeting on28 August, the accumulated evidence was considered sufficient to conclude that, if the monetary policy interest rate remains unchanged at 5.5% (over UF), the demand boost will domestic markets in the coming quarters would besmaller than anticipated last May, which would reduce the medium-term inflationary pressures. 26. On this last point, I would like to reiterate that the inflation target is symmetrical and therefore the Central Bank acts with equal resolution andfirmness both when inflation threatens to persistently exceed the upper limit of the range and when it is outlined below the lower limit, within the projection horizon. 27. There are relevant changes in macroeconomic conditions that have changed the scenario in which the Chilean economy and that must be taken into account when projecting its future evolution,both or in terms of inflation and Growth and jobs 38. These effects are undoubtedly accentuated by technological change in informationand communications initiated at the end of the twentieth century. 40. With regard to monetary policy, the corollary of this vision of the future scenario is that the risks of an acceleration of the Inflation in the coming quarters are low, and if theconditions implied in the projections are maintained, the rates of interest may remain at their current level. 41. Notwithstanding the foregoing, it is necessary to point out that a diagnosis that puts greater weight on the historical evidence of the decade Itwould point to a rapid consolidation of the recovery already underway, supported by the promising prospects it offers. the world economy, as well as expansionary levels of interest rates and the real exchange rate. This scenario would lead to a increased transmissionof inflationary pressures. 42. In addition, the capital account continued to be liberalized this year, facilitating a greater degree of liberalization. international financial integration. Among the most significant, he highlighted the elimination of the minimum period of permanence of a year for investments and capital contributions, a measure consistent with the new scheme of macroeconomic policies and with the free Floating of the exchange rate. This issue,having been made by this prestigious international organization, is It is characterized by having a low level of risk at the global level. For this reason, it is an attractive instrument for Foreign investors by the fact that they cantake risks in Chilean currency and thus achieve greater diversification of their portfolios, which represents an important step towards the financial integration of our country with the rest of the world. 49. The external scenario in which the Chilean economy operates is different from the one we experienced in the past decade. To take advantage of these opportunities, it is crucial to preserve and increase the flexibility and adaptability of our internal markets. Deterioration in this area would negatively affect investment and productivity in the Chilean economy, reduce our investment. potential for growth in the medium term and would directly restrict the use of new and better opportunities for our country. Conclusions 50. With all this background in view, and after the recent monetary policy decision, the balance of risks appears as balanced. The Threat of a lasting pick-up in inflation as a result of a rapid recovery in demandbetween a price of higher oil, offset by the negative risks of a prolongation of the lower dynamism of domestic demand and a faster-than-expected decline in global economic growth. 51. However, the elements of uncertainty are greater than in the past, and monetary policy will have to be managed with The flexibility necessary to preserve an environment of low and stable inflation, an indispensable pillar of economic progress for all Chileans. 52. La proyeccin de la inflacin medida por el IPCX es similar a la de mayo, mientras que la de inflacin IPC es menor debido a una cada esperada en el precio de los combustibles ms acentuada que la prevista anteriormente. 37. Hay cambios relevantes en las condiciones macroeconmicas que han modificado el escenario en el que se desenvuelve la economa chilena y que deben ser tomados en cuenta al proyectar su evolucin futura, tanto en trminos de inflacin como de crecimiento y empleo 38. Entre estos cambios, que se han ido desarrollando en el curso del ltimo ao y medio, cabe destacar: (1) la menor oferta de capitales internacionales; (2) la adopcin y mantencin de un esquema de flotacin cambiaria que transparenta los riesgos financieros del endeudamiento en moneda extranjera; (3) el mayor nivel de compromisos financieros acumulados por los consumidores y las empresas nacionales; y (4) el esfuerzo de consolidacin fiscal puesto en marcha recientemente. 39. En su conjunto, la consecuencia principal de estos desarrollos, es que el ritmo de crecimiento de la demanda interna durante los prximos aos debera ser inferior al observado durante la dcada pasada. Esta situacin a su vez produce otros efectos en la economa: (1) por una parte, cabe esperar un mayor peso relativo de los sectores productores de bienes transables internacionalmente en la composicin del producto y un menor dficit externo, a niveles ms altos de exportaciones e importaciones; (2) de otro lado, es probable que se verifiquen ajustes ms duraderos de precios relativos, como la compresin de los mrgenes de comercializacin, el menor crecimiento de salarios reales y la depreciacin del tipo de cambio real; y (3) los ajustes sectoriales inducidos por el cambio en los precios relativos requieren de gran flexibilidad en los mercados de productos y factores para materializarse con el mnimo costo social. Estos efectos se ven, sin duda, acentuados por el cambio tecnolgico en materia de informacin y comunicaciones iniciado a fines del siglo XX. 40. Con relacin a la poltica monetaria, el corolario de esta visin del escenario futuro es que los riesgos de una aceleracin de la inflacin en los prximos trimestres son reducidos, y que, de mantenerse las condiciones implcitas en las proyecciones, las tasas de inters pueden permanecer en su nivel actual. 41. No obstante lo anterior, es necesario sealar que un diagnstico que ponga mayor peso en la evidencia histrica de la dcada pasada apuntara a una rpida consolidacin de la recuperacin ya en marcha, apoyada en las promisorias perspectivas que ofrece la economa mundial, as como en niveles expansivos de tasas de inters y del tipo de cambio real. Este escenario propiciara una transmisin mayor de las presiones inflacionarias. 42. A la luz de la evidencia que se fue acumulando en los ltimos meses, el Consejo del Banco Central le asign una mayor probabilidad de ocurrencia al escenario de menor dinamismo de la demanda interna, y, como consecuencia, decidi reducir la tasa de inters de poltica en la reunin del 28 de agosto. Sin embargo, no se puede descartar del todo un escenario ms asimilable a la evidencia histrica, pese a los importantes cambios registrados en diversas variables fundamentales. La informacin futura ser sin duda crucial para validar una u otra visin. 43. Los riesgos evaluados no slo conciernen a los desarrollos de la demanda y oferta internas. An persiste en el entorno internacional, aunque tal vez con menos fuerza, el riesgo de un aterrizaje forzoso de la economa norteamericana. Ello podra disminuir las perspectivas de mediano plazo para el crecimiento de la economa chilena y su tasa de inflacin, no obstante que, en un horizonte menor a un ao, la depreciacin previsible del peso podra elevar el registro inflacionario. Asimismo, el precio del petrleo y el tipo de cambio son variables voltiles y notoriamente difciles de proyectar en el corto plazo. Una trayectoria de stas distinta a la considerada en el escenario base podra tener incidencia en las proyecciones de inflacin en el corto y mediano plazo. 44. Finalmente, no se puede dejar de mencionar la mayor preocupacin que existe en el sector privado sobre el grado de flexibilidad que exhibirn en el futuro los distintos mercados internos, y su capacidad de adaptacin a los cambios en el escenario externo y la tecnologa. Asimismo, el cumplimiento de la orientacin ms estricta que deber exhibir la poltica fiscal durante ste y los prximos aos condiciona las proyecciones de demanda y tipo de cambio y, por tanto influye sobre las expectativas, los precios relativos y la adaptacin de la economa a estos con mayor o menor rapidez. 45. En los temas de flexibilizacin y adaptacin, el Banco Central ha tenido un rol destacado. A los ya mencionados cambios en la implementacin de la poltica monetaria y flexibilizacin del mercado cambiario, se unen importantes medidas tomadas tendientes a una mayor modernizacin del sistema financiero chileno, as como tambin hacia una creciente integracin de este en los mercados financieros internacionales. 46. De igual forma, se han tomado importantes decisiones tendientes a reducir los riesgos y aumentar la eficiencia del sistema financiero nacional, en funcin de los requerimientos de los estndares mundiales, junto con buscar mayor perfeccionamiento y modernizacin del sistema de pagos. 47. Adicionalmente, durante el presente ao se continu liberalizando la cuenta de capitales, facilitando un mayor grado de integracin financiera internacional. Dentro de lo ms significativo, destac la eliminacin del plazo mnimo de permanencia de un ao para las inversiones y aportes de capital, medida coherente con el nuevo esquema de polticas macroeconmicas y con la libre flotacin del tipo de cambio. Una lista completa de todas estas medidas se encuentra en el Informe que hoy tenemos el honor de poner a disposicin del Honorable Senado. 48. Otro hito importante ocurrido durante el presente ao, dice relacin con la emisin internacional de bonos indizados en moneda chilena realizada por el Banco Mundial. Esta emisin, por haber sido hecha por ese prestigioso organismo internacional, se caracteriza por tener un bajo nivel de riesgo en el plano mundial. Por esta razn, se constituye en un instrumento atractivo para los inversionistas extranjeros por el hecho de poder tomar riesgos en moneda chilena y lograr as una mayor diversificacin de sus carteras, lo que representa un paso importante hacia la integracin financiera de nuestro pas con el resto del mundo. 49. El escenario externo en el que se desenvuelve la economa chilena es distinto del que vivimos en la dcada pasada. El financiamiento externo probablemente ser menos abundante en los aos venideros pero, a la vez, la revolucin tecnolgica en marcha en el mundo ofrece nuevas oportunidades sobre las cuales cimentar nuestro crecimiento futuro. Para aprovechar estas oportunidades, es crucial preservar e incrementar la flexibilidad y capacidad de adaptacin de nuestros mercados internos. Deterioros en este mbito afectaran negativamente la inversin y la productividad de la economa chilena, disminuiran nuestro potencial de crecimiento en el mediano plazo y coartaran de plano el aprovechamiento de nuevas y mejores oportunidades para nuestro pas. Conclusiones 50. Con todos estos antecedentes a la vista, y luego de la reciente decisin de poltica monetaria, el balance de riesgos aparece como equilibrado. La inflacin se proyecta alineada con el valor central del rango meta definido, dentro del horizonte de poltica, no obstante que en el corto plazo es posible que la inflacin medida por el IPC total supere en forma transitoria el 4% anual. La amenaza de un repunte duradero de la inflacin como consecuencia de una rpida recuperacin de la demanda interna o un precio del petrleo ms elevado, se compensa con los riesgos negativos de una prolongacin del menor dinamismo de la demanda interna y una disminucin ms rpida de lo previsto del crecimiento de la economa mundial. 51. Sin embargo, los elementos de incertidumbre son mayores que en el pasado, y la poltica monetaria deber administrarse con la flexibilidad necesaria para preservar un ambiente de inflacin baja y estable, pilar indispensable del progreso econmico de todos los chilenos. 52. En los meses que vienen, continuaremos la tarea de simplificar procedimientos, flexibilizar regulaciones, y facilitar la mayor internacionalizacin de nuestro sistema financiero. As mismo, pondremos nfasis en la modernizacin de nuestros sistemas de pagos. Tambin buscaremos introducir en el sistema financiero normas que impulsen y mejoren no slo los actuales mecanismos crediticios, sino tambin aquellos que den cabida creciente a formas de financiamiento, como la securitizacin y el capital de riesgo, ms vinculadas a las necesidades de la modernizacin de nuestra economa.

Title: The role of Foreign Investment as an engine of development
text: The role of foreign investment as an engine for development Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Forum "Chile-European Union: Economic and Political Development of a Future Relationship", held in Santiago, on November 9, 2000. With the independence of the Central Bank in 1989, despite repeated attempts to stabilize inflation, much work remained to be done in this regard. The strategy of economic openness made it essential to reduce inflation to low and stable levels, similar to those prevailing in industrialized countries. The trajectory towards these levels of inflation developed in the context of macroeconomic stability, together with a healthy financial system and increasingly solid external accounts. Thus, the Central Bank was left with greater freedom to focus its attention on reducing inflation, implementing from 1990 a new framework for monetary policy, known as the inflation targeting system. The benefits of this scheme gradually manifested themselves over the course of ten years. A gradual process was necessary, given the widespread indexation of our economy. Endemic inflation, which characterized the Chilean economy practically throughout the last century, was finally controlled towards the end of the nineties, reaching in 1999 a level (2.3%) comparable to that of the industrialized countries and consistent with the current medium-term target, set in a range between 2% and 4%, centered at 3%. While external events that began in South-East Asia in mid-1997 implied a slowdown in the pace of activity in the following years, this has certainly not meant fundamental macroeconomic imbalances. Indeed, in terms of trend, discounting the episodes of excess spending in the years 1996-1998 and the Asian crisis, we can point out that we are currently on the long-term path, or very close to it. The crisis that occurred in our country at the beginning of the eighties and its aftermath, product of a strong international financial retraction, meant the reintroduction of exchange restrictions and controls on capital movements abolished towards the end of the seventies, during the process of opening our economy at that time. With the reintroduction of these restrictions at the beginning of the following decade, it was sought to isolate, at that time, the domestic economy from the conditions of international financial markets, facilitating the operation of productive activities under conditions of interest rates and exchange rates less restrictive than those that would have prevailed if the exchange market had operated freely. Later, at the beginning of the nineties, and as a result of the profound economic and political transformations that the country went through, the external financial situation improved rapidly. This is how the retraction of the eighties began to be replaced by a level of external financing that, abundantly, threatened to become excessive, which meant that the authorities reacted in the first instance through imposing regulations that sought to limit the entry of capital, particularly those of a speculative nature of a shorter term. The idea behind these regulations can be summarized in the following points: (1) reducing capital inflows to levels that could be sustained by our economy; (2) maintain the independence of monetary policy; (3) reduce the volatility of capital movements to and from Chile; (4) maintain a healthy financial situation, both in terms of liquidity and solvency; (5) avoid the risk of contagion from imbalances in third countries and (6) avoid massive capital outflows in short periods. All regulations implemented were market-linked and non-discriminatory. The compulsory unpaid reserve requirement, currently non-existent, is the best known of them. Towards the end of the nineties, in the face of new external conditions, characterized by a marked decrease in capital flows, the necessary conditions were created to integrate our capital market more efficiently with the rest of the world. This was achieved through the introduction of prudential rules aimed at seeking the opening of new businesses and instruments, such as hedging operations through a wider range of derivative products; the formalization of the regulation of currency mismatches in the active and passive operations of financial institutions; and the authorization to operate in foreign currency by these institutions. among others. With this, a new advance in financial integration became possible: the free floating of the peso. Consistent with this greater financial openness and modernization, capital account restrictions were gradually removed as they became unnecessary, until they disappeared once the exchange rate float took hold. The global integration of our country has covered both commercial aspects, through the development of new markets and products, and financial aspects. In this last respect, a financial market has made an important contribution to the gradual and sustainable adaptation to new developments and needs of the markets, with modern regulations that have made it possible to take important steps towards further development and deepening. Although the depth of the domestic financial market is at an adequate level and in accordance with the degree of economic development that our country has, there are possible aspects to improve, from the point of view of the search for the potentialities of new markets and the deepening of the liquidity of fixed income instruments. To make progress on this issue, it is necessary to keep inflation low and stable, within the target range in the medium term, as well as to support initiatives to modernize national financial markets to achieve efficient financial internationalization. In this regard, and in parallel with the significant progress made in recent years in opening up financial and capital markets, in September 1999 the Chilean economy moved to a new stage in its exchange rate policy. Thus, after the achievement of a long-term equilibrium level of inflation, and the implementation of complementary prudential measures, it was considered that the conditions were in place to opt for a system of exchange rate flexibility consistent with exchange rate freedom, such as the one that exists today in the Chilean economy. The greater flexibility of the exchange market gives monetary policy greater degrees of autonomy, a fact that avoids concentrating in the money market the effects of shocks, which have been in most cases of external origin. Indeed, for a small and open economy like Chile's, with relatively inflexible domestic prices and exposed to significant external shocks, this seems to be a better alternative today than to abandon the national currency in favor of another country's currency or to join a monetary union. Chile's economic evolution over the past quarter century has meant that it is considered in the international business arena as an attractive country for investment. Thus, in recent years, gross capital receipts as a percentage of gross domestic product (GDP) have steadily upwards, with minimal inflows in the early eighties, which became between 5% and 6% in the mid-nineties, to end 1999 with the record figure of 13.7% of GDP. one of the highest in Latin America. (Figure 4) Investment Total Gross Foreign Investment (% of GDP) The prestige of the Chilean economy is based, on the one hand, on the achievements in terms of macroeconomic balances and political stability, and, on the other, on the permanent development and modernization of the main markets, all in a generalized environment of high quality and solidity of the country's institutions. Certainly, we have earned this prestige with real and concrete actions, and it represents an asset on which we must continue to persevere. The strategy of international integration of our economy has covered all areas, privileging both trade development, through free trade agreements, and the integration of financial and capital markets. Indeed, the importance that free trade agreements with Latin American countries and Canada have acquired for our country is due to the need to exercise the competitive advantages that our country holds, through the process of international economic insertion. Thus, in recent years, Chilean exports have been the most dynamic component of economic activity, showing a high capacity for diversification both at the product and market levels. In fact, in 1960 mining exports accounted for about 87% of total exports, while industrial exports did not reach 10%. During this year, the latter have come to represent about 45% of total sales abroad, a share similar to that currently held by mining exports. The availability of resources from abroad is of great importance for a small economy that seeks to consolidate an internationalization process. But as important for a country as the source of financing from abroad, is the possibility of accessing larger and better markets for national investors who go out into the world to conduct their business. The presence of foreign companies in the most dynamic sectors of our economy has allowed the introduction of new technologies and the development of advanced production processes, which has meant a valuable contribution to the country as a whole, which has finally resulted in generalized increases in productivity and efficiency. In addition, important strategic alliances have been facilitated between national and foreign companies, to share technologies, knowledge and penetration into new markets. Certainly, the development of these strategic alliances in recent years has facilitated the insertion of national capital in a privileged place at the regional and global levels. The possibility of participating in an increasingly globalized world facilitates a greater degree of diversification of investments. This is because there is a greater possibility of having a more balanced distribution of destinations and products, thus minimizing risks, both for those who invest in Chile, and for Chileans who go out to the international financial and commercial markets. Similarly, the increases in efficiency and productivity gains obtained in recent years, allow us to think about a promising future for national companies that go out into the world to do new business. The world of the future will be one in which the flow of capital will have a two-way road: domestic entrepreneurs will also invest abroad, while foreigners will do so in their countries and ours. This will reduce global risk, and everyone, entrepreneurs and workers, will be able to benefit from a national economy that is inserted into an expanding world economy. In this two-way process, there are advantages for both Chileans and foreigners. By diversifying our investment portfolio into global markets, it is possible to reduce risks and, in many cases, improve performance. The same goes for the foreign investor who decides to invest in our country, benefiting from responsible policies and serious institutions in all areas.

Al independizarse el Banco Central en el ao 1989, a pesar de los repetidos intentos de estabilizar la inflacin, quedaba an mucho trabajo por hacer en este sentido. La estrategia de apertura econmica haca indispensable reducir la inflacin a niveles bajos y estables, similares a los prevalecientes en los pases industrializados. La trayectoria hacia estos niveles de inflacin se fue desarrollando en el contexto de estabilidad macroeconmica, junto con un sistema financiero saludable y cuentas externas cada vez ms slidas. As, el Banco Central qued con mayor libertad para enfocar su atencin en la reduccin de la inflacin, implementando a partir de 1990 un nuevo marco para la poltica monetaria, conocido como el sistema de metas de inflacin. Los beneficios de este esquema se manifestaron gradualmente en el curso de diez aos. Fue necesario un proceso gradual, dada la indizacin generalizada de nuestra economa. La inflacin endmica, que caracteriz a la economa chilena prcticamente durante todo el siglo pasado, finalmente fue controlada hacia fines de los noventa, llegando en 1999 a un nivel (2,3%) comparable con el de los pases industrializados y consistente con la actual meta a mediano plazo, fijada en un rango entre 2% y 4%, centrada en 3%. La crisis ocurrida en nuestro pas a comienzos de los ochenta y sus secuelas, producto de una fuerte retraccin financiera internacional, signific la reintroduccin de restricciones cambiaras y controles a los movimientos de capital abolidos hacia fines de los aos setenta, durante el proceso de apertura de nuestra economa en esa poca. Con la reintroduccin de estas restricciones a comienzos de la dcada siguiente, se busc aislar, en ese entonces, a la economa interna de las condiciones de los mercados financieros internacionales, facilitando la operacin de las actividades productivas en condiciones de tasas de inters y de tipo de cambio menos restrictivas que las que habran prevalecido si el mercado cambiarlo hubiese operado libremente. Posteriormente, a comienzos de la dcada de los noventa, y producto de las profundas transformaciones econmicas y polticas por las que pas el pas, la situacin financiera externa mejor rpidamente. Es as como la retraccin de los ochenta pas a ser reemplazada por un nivel de financiamiento externo que, de abundante, amenaz con transformarse en excesivo, lo cual signific que las autoridades reaccionaran en una primera instancia a travs de imponer regulaciones que buscaron limitar la entrada de capitales, particularmente aquellos de carcter especulativo de ms corto plazo. La dea que estaba detrs de estas regulaciones se puede resumir en los siguientes puntos: (1) reducir las entradas de capitales a niveles que pudieran ser sustentados por nuestra economa; (2) mantener la independencia de la poltica monetaria; (3) reducir la volatilidad de los movimientos de capitales desde y hacia Chile; (4) mantener una situacin financiera sana, tanto en trminos de liquidez como de solvencia; (5) evitar el riesgo de contagio de desequilibrios de terceros pases y (6) evitar salidas masivas de capitales en perodos cortos. Todas las regulaciones implementadas fueron vinculadas al mercado y no discriminatorias. El encaje obligatorio no remunerado, hoy inexistente, es lo ms conocido de ellas. Hacia fines de los aos noventa, ante las nuevas condiciones externas, caracterizadas por una disminucin notoria de los flujos de capitales, se fueron creando las condiciones necesarias para integrar en forma ms eficiente nuestro mercado de capitales con el resto del mundo. Esto se logr a travs de la introduccin de normas prudenciales tendientes a buscar la apertura de nuevos negocios e instrumentos, tales como las operaciones de cobertura de riesgo mediante una mayor gama de productos derivados; la formalizacin de la regulacin de descalces de monedas en las operaciones activas y pasivas de instituciones financieras; y la autorizacin para operar en moneda extranjera por parte de dichas instituciones, entre otras.
