Monto de Operaciones Forward de Dlares en MCE llancn Central de Chile Otro paso es la ampliacin de la base de inversionistas extranjeros dispuestos a invertir y emitir deuda en moneda local. A partir de 1998, el Banco Central autoriz la emisin de endeudamiento en moneda local en el exterior y, ms recientemente, se ha eliminado el diferencial de impuesto que afectaba a los intereses de deuda externa en moneda nacional hasta igualarlo a las condiciones de la deuda en moneda extranjera. En meses recientes hemos visto pasos incipientes en el desarrollo de un mercado internacional de pesos o UF's. El ao recin pasado, el Banco Mundial emiti un bono en UF por 105 millones de dlares, y posteriormente, el Banco Central de Uruguay hizo una segunda emisin por un monto similar, al tiempo que otros emisores internacionales han anunciado su intencin de realizar operaciones en UF o en pesos. La presencia de estos instrumentos ayuda a generar un mercado internacional que facilita la diversificacin del riesgo cambiado en Chile. En efecto, estas emisiones permiten a los inversionistas institucionales en Chile, que tienen una demanda natural por instrumentos denominados en UF al igual que sus pasivos, acceder a inversiones en esta moneda, pero sin la necesidad de continuar concentrando su riesgo de crdito en empresas chilenas. Al mismo tiempo, los extranjeros pueden transferir el riesgo cambiado que absorben al emitir deuda en UF, transfirindolo a empresas chilenas que se encuentran endeudadas en moneda extranjera y que desean reducir su exposicin cambiara. De esta forma, logramos una mejor combinacin de riesgo y rentabilidad para todos los participantes. En la medida que las empresas locales logran condiciones adecuadas de financiamiento de largo plazo en moneda local, tambin se fortalece la salud financiera de la economa chilena. Finalmente, un tema que estuvo presente en el debate de poltica econmica en los ltimos aos se refiere a las restricciones al ingreso de capitales, como el encaje y el requisito de permanencia. Estas medidas se mantuvieron mientras exista una gran afluencia de capitales hacia la economa chilena, y al mismo tiempo, la falta de normas de calce adecuadas en el mercado financiero y un rgimen cambiarlo mixto, no ayudaban a que el sector privado controlara voluntariamente su exposicin al riesgo cambiarlo. Las regulaciones cumplieron un papel importante ayudando a limitar el volumen de las entradas de capital y extendiendo la madurez del endeudamiento externo. Sin embargo, en el contexto actual en el que se desenvuelven los mercados financieros internacionales sera contraproducente utilizar estas restricciones. Ms an, considerando los avances realizados internamente en trminos de estabilizacin de la inflacin en torno a su meta de largo plazo, la flotacin cambiara, el establecimiento de una regla fiscal, el desarrollo de los mercados de cobertura cambiara y normas de calce debemos continuar avanzando en la misma direccin de mayor integracin financiera internacional.

Title: Monetary Policy in Chile in the Last Decade
text: Monetary Policy in Chile in the Last Decade PRESENTATION BY MR. CARLOS MASSAD A., PRESIDENT OF THE CENTRAL BANK OF CHILE, MADE AT THE Vil FINANCIAL MEETING ORGANIZED BY ICARE , on August 28, 2001. The conduct of monetary policy in Chile aims to ensure the stability of the currency and the normal functioning of internal and external payments. In practice, the objective of price stability translates into maintaining the current inflationary pace, which is similar to that prevailing in developed countries. Achieving the goal of a normal functioning of internal and external payments is interpreted as the proper functioning of the financial system d0 that is, that it provides liquidity at times when the economy requires it d0 and the maintenance of a sustainable current account deficit over time. The interest in maintaining the inflation rate at international levels is primarily due to the consensus that exists around the efficiency and welfare gains that are achieved under stable macroeconomic conditions. International empirical evidence shows that countries with high inflation rates have a lower growth rate. In fact, high inflation, a problem in itself, is also a symptom of even more serious diseases. In historical terms, obtaining inflation rates comparable to the international level was achieved in Chile on the basis of two policy guidelines: the use of gradualist but persistent mechanisms to contain inflation and consistency in the management of the different instruments of monetary policy. The gradualness and persistence are due both to the recognition that the high degree of indexation of the national economy limits the speed at which inflation can be reduced, and to the credibility costs that would be incurred if inflationary gains were reversed. This gradualness, however, has not limited the Central Bank to take the necessary measures to face crisis situations in international markets. Controlling inflation has been a highly successful and unique experience in Chile's history since 1,940. In fact, this is the first time that inflation has been maintained at the level of developed countries in a sustained manner and without producing macroeconomic imbalances. Stabilization processes carried out in the early sixties and eighties also allowed annual inflation to be reduced to levels close to 5%, but these achievements were only transitory and, by their nature, accumulated imbalances that led to a collapse of the effort. The experience of the nineties, on the other hand, was that of gradual and sustained progress, in which the control of inflation did not lead to major imbalances and which, due to its solidity, augurs that its results are lasting (graph 1). The reduction in inflation in Chile in the past decade was based on five fundamental pillars. These are: (i) great discipline and conviction to advance steadily in the fight against inflation; (i) recognition of the constraints imposed by the existence of indexation mechanisms in the economy; (IIL) the implementation of a well-defined nominal anchor and update in the face of new developments in the macroeconomic environment; (iv) an exchange rate policy based on the objective of maintaining a narrow current account deficit and avoiding the use of the nominal exchange rate as an anti-inflationary tool; and (v) a flexible macroeconomic policy scheme capable of timely response to changes in macroeconomic conditions (Figure 2). The maintenance of an unrestricted discipline in the control of inflation was the basis for building an important degree of credibility in the policies of the Central Bank. This discipline has had different manifestations. First, through the use of tight monetary policies in the face of the threat of inflationary flare-ups. A clear example of this policy occurred at the beginning of 1 990 when short-term rates were increased by more than two percentage points in less than a month (modifying medium and long-term rates) and a clear signal was given that for the new authorities of the issuing institute, Inflationary control was its main objective. Secondly, through the establishment and fulfillment of the inflation targeting scheme that not only formalized the anti-inflationary vocation of the Central Bank, but also constituted a pioneering experience of successful management of monetary policy. Likewise, the fact that the inflation target that was announced was more demanding every year showed that it was possible to approach inflation rates in developed countries. Unlike other stabilization efforts in Chile and other developing countries, the reduction in the inflation rate took place in an open and competitive economy, without price controls, a healthy fiscal sector, and without ever resorting to nominal exchange rate setting (figure 3). A fundamental element on which this credibility rests is the independence and autonomy of the Central Bank enshrined in its Constitutional Organic Law. Empirical analyses for a substantial number of countries, and ultimately Chile's own history, show that central bank independence helps control the level of inflation. Moreover, in those countries where the central bank is autonomous, it is not observed that the growth rate of gross domestic product (GDP) is lower, nor that the variability of output is greater. This means that there would be no costs associated with the inflationary control provided by central bank independence in terms of a lower willingness (and/or capacity) to stabilize output. The independence and autonomy of the issuing institute are mainly operational. They do not mean that the Central Bank is an entity isolated from society over which political power has no control. The Central Bank is an institution of high political responsibility, which reports to both the President of the Republic and the Senate. In this sense, the role of the meetings of its Council with the Senate Finance Committee is key both to keeping society informed and penetrated by macroeconomic discussion and conduct, and for the Bank to receive feedback on its policies. On the other hand, to ensure a consistent management of monetary policy, its Council is composed of members who remain in office for ten years, which allows due importance to be given to medium and long-term considerations in the evaluation of different policy alternatives. Likewise, the plurality among the members of the Council on macroeconomic policy visions forms a picture where different sensitivities are represented, without undermining a technically rigorous analysis. Finally, the Central Bank has borrowing capacity inside and outside the country, which allows it to carry out sterilization operations and act as lender of last resort to the domestic financial system in the event of a systemic crisis of confidence. Unlike other experiences where a reduction in inflation was achieved in a very short time, in Chile a gradual progress scheme was chosen. In the background of this decision was (and is) the massive existence of indexation in the economy. This places an essential constraint on the speed with which inflation control policies can be carried out. Indexing originates as a defense of agents against inflationary surprises and is verified in various contracts and situations. This mechanism individually protects agents against inflationary shocks but ends up producing more persistent and volatile inflation at the aggregate level, as well as an environment with greater limitations when initiating a stabilization plan. Considering these elements, the Bank pursued a policy of gradual progress in controlling inflation, which created room for sustained reductions and made future inflation more predictable. This gradualness made it possible to reduce the costs associated with inflationary control. The massive indexation of our economy generates an additional problem to the persistence and volatility of inflation; Because monetary policy is conducted primarily through interest rates, the economy does not naturally have a nominal anchor. This means that there is no variable that automatically serves as a reference to determine the price level or for the inflation rate. In this context, in principle, any inflation rate could be consistent with the same set of fundamental variables. In part, anticipating this shortfall, the issuing institute began to announce inflation projections from 1 990, which then became explicit inflation targets. These targets allow for a nominal anchor at a low cost, which gives way to contracts that incorporate future inflation. Public sector wage negotiations have been an example of such contracts. Setting inflation targets The main merit of an inflation-targeting regime is to restrict the discretion of the monetary authority but, at the same time, allows it to carry out stabilization policies. Operating fully, an inflation-targeting regime establishes specific and verifiable objectives for which the Central Bank must respond, thus strengthening its transparency and credibility, but giving it freedom to use the instruments and policies in the way it deems appropriate to achieve the proposed targets. Communication with the public improves with the existence of a simple and easy-to-understand indicator, generating a strong effect on inflationary expectations. The setting of an inflation target does not imply that those who are governed by this scheme are anti-inflationary maniacs. The purpose of stabilizing the product in the short term, far from being ignored, is present in the degrees of limited discretion that the regime allows and in the way in which the horizon of the goal, the breadth of its range and the escape clauses are defined. However, it is key that the eventual concern about the stabilization of output is consistent with reaching the inflation target in the medium term and over time. How much weight is given to output stabilization within an inflation-targeting regime is likely to depend on how high inflation initially is. When analyzing Chile's experience with inflation targeting, two stages can be clearly distinguished. The first and most extensive corresponds to the transition from high inflation rates to the long-term levels that are the Central Bank's objective, i.e. the period from September 1 990 to September 1 999. At this stage, the Central Bank carried out a hard monetary policy, defining a short-term horizon for the inflation target (one year), applied a target point (at least since 1 994) and used the total variation of the consumer price index (CPI) as an indicator of inflation. However, the reduction in inflation was planned to materialize very gradually, reflecting concerns about economic growth in the short and medium term. In this period, the Central Bank simultaneously pursued targets for the current account deficit and the nominal exchange rate, allowing the latter to float within a predetermined band. The conduct of monetary policy, however, did not reach adequate levels of transparency, since no explicit projections for the inflation rate were disclosed beyond the target itself or detailed or regular written reports, with the sole exception of the Annual Report to the Senate. Thus, there was insufficient information on the reasons that led the Central Bank to make changes in monetary policy, thus limiting the effectiveness of the same policies by not fully affecting the expectations of economic agents (Graphs 4 and 5). History records several experiences in the world in which the monetary authority focuses on obtaining anti-inflationary results through the use of the exchange rate as the nominal anchor of the economy. Many times these gains evaporate quickly when, after a currency crisis, a new inflationary spiral is unleashed. Even countries that have adopted convertibility systems can find themselves in this kind of problem. The disinflation strategy followed by the Central Bank in the nineties was very careful to avoid using the exchange rate to control inflation. In fact, exchange rate policy sought rather to be consistent with the objective of keeping the current account deficit within sustainable ranges. The objective of keeping the exchange rate within the floating band was not always achieved during the first stage of inflation targeting. Despite foreign exchange purchase efforts as part of sterilizing the massive capital inflow, Chile's rapid productivity growth and success as an emerging economy induced an equilibrium appreciation in the real exchange rate. The fact that this assessment has been shown in the significant volumes of international reserves that we accumulated between 1 990 and 1 997, despite the existence of reserve requirements for capital inflows, which supported the lower limit of the band. Even so, the real exchange rate appreciated by about 30 percent during that period (Chart 6). In terms of results of this first inflation-targeting stage, the fall in inflation during the nineties was gradual, but solid and persistent. The experience began with inflation of 27% in 1990 to reach only 2.3% in 1 999, a fact not seen since the deflationary experiences of the thirties. Economic growth, despite the recession experienced in 1 999 after the Asian crisis, averaged 6.4% per year during the decade, making this a period of sustained growth without parallel. Obviously, this result was not only a consequence of monetary policy and the inflation targeting regime, although the almost strict achievement of the announced targets was certainly important. The return to democracy, the structural reforms implemented during the seventies and eighties, and the policies that followed allowed the country to reap the benefits of the massive flow of external capital during the nineties, which fostered growth and favored the control of inflation. Another key factor was the significant contribution of fiscal savings to total national savings (which was also high by Latin American standards), at least until 1 996, as this has declined significantly in the subsequent period (Graphs 7 and 8). Moreover, the fact that the equilibrium real exchange rate appreciated during the nineties was undoubtedly a factor that helped control inflation. This, however, should not be understood as using the nominal exchange rate as the catalyst for disinflation. On the contrary, the real exchange rate appreciated due to structural conditions of the economy, to which the reduction in inflation itself contributed, and the Central Bank only recognized this equilibrium adjustment. If, in addition, this adjustment benefited the fight against inflation, welcome, but it was never the determining or central factor of the inflation control scheme. While inflation reduction has been a common occurrence in the world during the nineties, recent studies indicate that inflation-targeting countries were able to reduce inflation by more than 7% on average between 1,985 and 1,997, compared with a reduction of about 3.5% for non-inflation-targeting countries. Floating monetary policy The second stage of inflation targeting began in September 1,999, when the exchange rate band was finally abandoned and inflation became the Central Bank's only formal and explicit target. At this stage, a full operational level (or regime) of the inflation targeting scheme has been reached, with a permanent improvement of statistical and analytical models within the Central Bank, the publication of the Monetary Policy Report with the analysis, assumptions and explicit projections, in addition to the inflation targets, and growth projections; the public announcement of the dates of monetary policy meetings six months in advance, and the publication of the minutes of these meetings with a delay of 90 days (Chart 9). The performance of the economy in this second stage has been marked by the ups and downs of the world economy, despite which the inflation targeting scheme has been particularly successful. Among the determinants of the current scenario, three changes in the external outlook since the end of 1 997 should be highlighted: the lower demand for domestic assets by the rest of the world since the Asian crisis, the unfavorable evolution of the terms of trade and the greater uncertainty that has characterized international markets in the recent period. None of these elements are new, but their simultaneous occurrence has affected not only the Chilean economy, but also most emerging economies. In a small and open economy, external variables have a strong impact on domestic economic developments, especially when financial markets do not reach a level of depth and sophistication that allows external cycles to be better absorbed and distributed (Graphs 10, 11, and 12). Although after the low inflation of 1 999 (2.3 per cent) it slightly exceeded the upper bound of the target in 2000 (reaching 4.5 per cent), the increase in total inflation is strictly a reflection of the sharp rises in the international price of oil (a phenomenon that occurred in most countries of the world). Core inflation indicators for 2000 and so far in 2001 are no different from those in 1 999 and thus reveal that the trend in inflation over the medium term is in line with the Central Bank's objective of maintaining price stability (Chart 13). This second stage is also characterized by significant progress in liberalizing the capital account of the balance of payments. This is consistent with avoiding movements in the real exchange rate beyond what is considered reasonable for a small economy open to international trade. Among the most important deregulations is the reduction to 0% of the unremunerated reserve requirement for capital inflows and the elimination of the requirements of permanence of at least one year for some forms of capital. These regulations, which allowed domestic interest rates to be maintained at a higher level than foreign ones, had been imposed to avoid affecting the exchange rate during a tightening policy cycle. However, the maturity of the Chilean financial system and the credibility of the Central Bank's policies made it possible to eliminate these regulations. Recently, the issuing institute has taken steps to advance the de-indexation of the economy by abandoning the use of real monetary policy rates for nominal instruments. This policy is consistent with the convergence of inflation to international levels and, in particular, with the floating exchange rate regime in operation since 1 999. Until last July, the mechanics of operation of monetary policy consisted of specifying as an objective the prize of interest rates over the variation of the development unit (UF). This meant that on the 9th of each month, the Central Bank modified the level of the nominal rate at which it intervened in the money market and placed its liquidity instruments in order to adapt it to the known rate of variation of the UF. The extraordinary increases in the UF in some months tended to be offset by smaller variations in other months. Nominalization of the policy rate The nominalization of monetary policy consists of specifying the target of the current rate in terms of a fixed nominal rate, rather than a premium on the UF. The rate at which the Central Bank offers its papers and at which the cost of its liquidity facilities is established is set by the Central Bank Council based on the medium-term inflation projection. The nominalization of monetary policy should not affect the average level of interest rates, real or nominal, and thus the policy stance. The only effect should be a reduction in the short-term (month-to-month) variability of nominal interest rates and an increase in the short-term volatility of UF rates (also month-to-month). In the discussion on the nominalization of the monetary policy rate target (MPR) that has been carried out in the Bank over time, a series of arguments have been raised for and against this decision. Among the arguments in favor of nominalization is that it reduces the volatility of liquid monetary aggregates, decreases exchange rate volatility, simplifies international financial integration, facilitates the matching of financing of non-readjustable placements, and provides greater transparency to the rates of non-readjustable placements. Opponents of the nominalization of the MPR point out that the variability of inflation expectations harms the monetary policy signal in a nominal scheme and that compensating for this requires a greater degree of monetary activism. For nine months we examined this argument. In this entire period, there was not a single instance in which, in order to achieve the Central Bank's goal, greater activism in a nominal rate policy than in a real rate policy would have been required. In the current circumstances, the disadvantages of having an indexed scheme that can add volatility to the exchange rate become more apparent. Faced with significant (and transitory) reductions in inflation, the Central Bank, if a real rate target is set, is forced to intervene to validate an extremely low level of nominal rates, which reduces the cost of dragging short positions in pesos and can have adverse consequences on the stability of the foreign exchange market. The review of recent experience reveals that, in an inflation-targeting scheme and when the Central Bank's policies enjoy high credibility, inflationary expectations move within relatively limited ranges. Stable expectations reduce the supposed disadvantages of a nominal-rate monetary policy regime compared to a readjustable one. The policy signal is transparent to actors and no major activism is required (figure 14). In addition, with low trend inflation rates, the probability of negative inflation rates increases in certain months of the year, which could lead, in the scheme of policies based on real rates, to negative nominal rates that, as such, would be unmanageable. Deepening the regulatory institutionality of the Chilean financial system Finally, the future conduct of monetary policy under the inflation targeting scheme requires that the regulatory institutionality of the Chilean financial system be deepened. A healthy economy requires a strong and secure banking sector that allocates funds to borrowers in an appropriate risk-return combination to ensure the efficient functioning of the payment system. The financial system is information-intensive and therefore subject to problems arising from market failures such as asymmetric information or moral hazard. This justifies regulation by the authority. A modern system of supervision includes several aspects: emphasis on prudential regulation; creation of incentives for the market to supervise financial institutions; adequate procedures to solve situations of financial instability; transparency for the capital market to function through control standards; and operation of private institutions that contribute to market efficiency, as risk classifiers and external auditors. Chile's experience in banking regulation and supervision over the past twenty years is rich and varied. In the late seventies, the country implemented free banking policies, minimizing state supervision in the banking system. Indeed, it was believed that the invisible hand of the market would lead to a solid and efficient situation of the banking system. However, the country fell, in the early eighties, into the deepest crisis of the twentieth century after the Great Depression. After that, there was a clear change of philosophy as the regulation and supervision of the banking system was profoundly reformed. In response to episodes of financial fragility, a more active supervisory role was designed and the strengthening of state institutions was encouraged, with the aim of ensuring that adequate management of the new incentive framework would promote economic development and financial stability. Thus, after the crisis, the emphasis of the economic authorities was placed on improving the systems of regulation, supervision and access to information of financial companies. Regulatory changes led to the establishment of maximum mismatches in foreign currency, stricter rules for the recognition of income, classification of assets and provisions requirements, establishment of better methods of delivery of relevant information by banks, the replacement of implicit deposit insurance by explicit partial coverage insurance, a regime of early corrections of possible solvency problems, an effective and clear scheme to solve the problem of insolvent institutions, the implementation of stricter limits for related loans and the obligation for such operations to be carried out under market conditions. In a second stage, once the stability and solvency of the system had been recovered, the regulatory institutionality faced new challenges associated with the process of globalization and the international insertion and integration of the economy, the consolidation of financial agents and the sophistication of new financial products. The main financial reforms dictated by the regulatory authorities in recent years can be summarized in those that tend to better limit financial risks, allowing, in turn, the authorization of new banking operations; those that complement the rules related to internationalization and others that allow the creation of new products. An additional element in the deepening of the financial market is obtained, indirectly, with the decision of the Central Bank to use a nominal interest rate as the policy rate. This will allow an improvement in the structure of assets and liabilities not only of the Bank itself, but also of the private financial sector to the extent that the currency matches that each sector has in its portfolios are improved. This will benefit all actors in the financial sector and the economy as a whole. On the subject of banking internationalization, it is worth highlighting the undoubted benefits that appear with the opening to the outside. The internationalization of banking may imply a sharp increase in the efficiency of the financial sector. According to international experience, new services appear, greater financial innovation, better use of a bank's capital and greater diversification of risk. As a result, new sources of growth are emerging and the development of services exports is promoted. However, with internationalization some risks arise, and it is necessary to adopt measures that allow them to be kept limited. To face the risks and difficulties of the process of internationalization of banking, a set of regulatory mechanisms has been proposed. In particular, the Central Bank participates in the regulation of investment abroad of banks, both in the field of foreign exchange and in the area of financial regulation, safeguarding the interests of people in topics such as the acquisition of shares and installation of subsidiaries and joint ventures or the regulation of financial investments and cross-border credits. In this last area, it has its own foreign exchange powers and shares responsibilities with the Superintendency of Banks in the establishment of patrimonial requirements and provisions to carry out such operations. In recent years, a number of product innovations have been developed in the Chilean financial system. The country now has a developed market for consumer, commercial, foreign trade and mortgage placements. There is a large market for fixed and variable income instruments, including buyback agreements widely used by the Central Bank in managing liquidity in the interbank market (Figure 15). The Central Bank has recently proceeded to expand the range of products linked to payments, savings and financial risk management, authorizing the issuance of electronic money, and the operation of new derivative products that facilitate the management of financial risks. The latter include futures in currencies, local and international interest rates, and certain forms of instruments and swaps. Likewise, the requirement of prior authorization to make derivatives of interest rates abroad was lifted. The possibility of having derivatives on interest rates will allow banks to readjust their positions exposed to interest rate risk more cheaply and quickly. In turn, the Central Bank has helped to deepen and complete markets through the issuance of instruments readjustable according to changes in the exchange rate, which allow to cover exchange risks and exchange promissory notes payable in coupons for zero coupon promissory notes, which allows to satisfy the demand for instruments of longer duration and the construction of a curve of zero coupon yield as an axis for the operation of the market of derivatives of interest. For a more efficient development of the exchange market, interbank loans and pacts between financial institutions in foreign currency have also been authorized. However, the rapid growth of financial instruments, in particular derivatives, may enhance the risks facing the financial system. Therefore, it has been necessary to limit the excessive risk-taking that banking institutions face through the taking of net positions in foreign currency, the existence of mismatches in the terms of assets and liabilities, and the mismatches between the interest rates agreed for assets and liabilities as well as the dependence on interbank financing, which can lead to risks of contagion. At present, most of the risks faced by banks are adequately limited, whether they are currency, interest rate, inflation, or liquidity risks. The Central Bank has gradually introduced significant improvements to the regulations on matching assets and liabilities in foreign currency, maturities and interest rates. Given that during the last decade the decreasing inflation targets proposed by the Central Bank have been systematically met and that, in addition, the level and volatility of inflation have decreased in recent years, an increase in the mismatch between assets and liabilities does not represent a significant increase in the risk exposure of the financial system due to inflation. This is also consistent with the steps the Central Bank has taken to stimulate deeper financial markets in local currency and, as noted, with the decision to move towards nominal monetary policy rates. We have already reported publicly on the reform and modernization of the payment system being prepared by the Central Bank. The main objective of this project is to establish more efficient and secure settlement mechanisms. In its central aspects, the reform seeks to ensure that the risks of settlement of payments between financial institutions are duly assumed and safeguarded by the same institutions, preventing them from being transferred to the rest of the financial system, to the public or to the Central Bank. The possibility of making electronic transfers in real time and against available balances will eliminate a substantial part of the risks present in the settlement of payments (table 1). But progress in modernizing our financial system requires additional steps, which are facilitated by two interlinked recent developments: the consolidation of inflation at low and stable rates, and the nominalization of the monetary policy interest rate. One of these additional steps concerns the payment of interest on demand obligations and checking accounts. This is an issue that must be carefully addressed to ensure its consistency with the rest of financial regulation. Other aspects relate to the regulation of passbooks and the ongoing reforms to the payment system. We also believe it is necessary to initiate a global review of the deposit guarantee scheme that has been in operation since 1 986 in Chile, and that it is appropriate to rethink in the light of these modernizations. The General Banking Law (LGB) and the complementary regulations of the Central Bank and the Superintendency of Banks clearly distinguish between demand deposits and term bonds. The obligations at sight are payable and payable at all events and, in the event of solvency problems or forced liquidation of a financial institution, they have the guarantee of the Central Bank in case of insufficient resources in the affected institution. As a safeguard measure, the LGB requires the establishment of a technical reserve on demand obligations that exceed the bank's core capital by 2.5 times, in addition to a priority of depositors with demand resources over other creditors. Term obligations, on the other hand, have a limited guarantee, valid only for natural persons and with a maximum limit per depositor. Consistent with the above, the current financial regulations of the Central Bank allow the payment of interest and adjustments on term obligations, but prohibits such payment on deposits of the public to less than 30 days, which are considered in sight in the LGB. The authorization to pay interest on certain demand obligations is an initiative that has a number of advantages from the point of view of efficiency and competition in the financial system. But at the same time, it is necessary to reconcile this situation with the existing guarantee scheme. In this regard, it should be considered that the payment of interest on exposed obligations is likely to increase the basis on which the Central Bank guarantee is applied. In addition, a regime in which they benefit from the payment of interest and are also guaranteed at all events, could generate serious distortions in the system: by eliminating the necessary balance between profitability and risk that any financial instrument must exhibit, a moral hazard is created that will be particularly visible in the case of institutions that could exhibit solvency problems, present an inadequate level of capital or face higher levels of risk. The elaboration of the regulations must take into account these aspects, taking into account the international experience in the matter and the particularities of the Chilean case. On the other hand, it is also necessary to modify the regulations that currently govern savings books, especially those with an unconditional turnaround, in order to adapt them to the new realities of the financial markets, including aspects related to nominalization, in an environment of low inflation and technological advances. In any case, it is essential that the orientation of this type of instrument to its primary objective of promoting people's savings is preserved. Finally, in line with the above aspects, it is considered necessary to advance in a critical examination of the current deposit guarantee and insurance scheme, taking into account relevant international experience and progress in the reform of the high-value payment system. This should lead to the design of more effective depositor protection mechanisms, which will result in a healthier and more effective system, and in which the moral hazard problems faced by many of these mechanisms are adequately addressed. This initiative should be addressed in a joint effort between the Central Bank, the Superintendency of Banks and Financial Institutions and the Ministry of Finance. This set of initiatives represents an orderly and coherent process of modernization of financial regulations that, with due respect for their stability, should contribute to the development of a more efficient and more competitive financial system in our country. As in the past, we expect the collaboration of the Association of Banks and Financial Institutions at certain stages of its preparation. The current regulatory and supervisory system has a solid foundation. However, financial systems and their regulations are faced with continuous evolutionary processes. The increasing complexity of the financial system in conjunction with the greater internalization of banking requires that prudential regulation increasingly rely on self-regulation by the financial entities themselves. The market itself, and the organized financial institutions themselves, must be able to provide elements of discipline for the proper functioning of the financial sector. This, however, requires permanent and effective vigilance on the part of the monetary and banking authorities. Effective market discipline requires meaningful, reliable, and timely disclosures of information to the public. Although progress has continued in recent years in the transparency of banking information, it is necessary to persevere in this path with the periodic delivery of information on financial risks associated with interest rates, foreign currencies, liquidity, inflation and systemic risks associated with the interbank loan market and the payment system. More information should also be provided on the quantity, quality and prices of the guarantees received by banks, which will allow us to know more precisely the credit risks they incur. Finally, greater self-regulation of financial institutions, and placing high demands on the managerial and technical levels that work in them, must be accompanied by increasing levels of responsibility on the part of their directors. In this sense, concrete steps must be taken to increase the levels of transparency and professionalization of decision-making, taking into account both the interests of investors and those of the companies and people at whose service the financial system should be. I call on the Association of Banks and Financial Institutions to establish mechanisms that support the transparency of the system and its self-regulation.

La conduccin de la poltica monetaria en Chile tiene por finalidad velar por la estabilidad de la moneda y el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos. A diferencia de otras experiencias donde se consigui una disminucin de la inflacin en un plazo muy breve, en Chile se opt por un esquema de avances graduales. La masiva indizacin de nuestra economa genera un problema adicional al de persistencia y volatilidad de la inflacin; debido a que la poltica monetaria se realiza principalmente a travs de las tasas de inters, la economa no tiene un ancla nominal en forma natural. La comunicacin con el pblico mejora con la existencia de un indicador simple y de fcil comprensin, generando un fuerte efecto en las expectativas inflacionarias. La fijacin de una meta de inflacin no implica que quienes se rigen por este esquema sean maniticos antiinflacionarios. Cuanto peso se le d a la estabilizacin del producto dentro de un rgimen de metas de inflacin, depende probablemente cun alta sea inicialmente la inflacin. Al analizar la experiencia chilena con las metas de inflacin se pueden distinguir claramente dos etapas. La conduccin de la poltica monetaria, sin embargo, no alcanzaba niveles de transparencia adecuados, puesto que no se divulgaban proyecciones explcitas para la tasa de inflacin ms all de la meta misma ni informes escritos detallados o regulares, con la sola excepcin del Informe Anual al Senado. La historia consigna varias experiencias en el mundo en que la autoridad monetaria se concentra en obtener resultados antiinflacionarios a travs de la utilizacin del tipo de cambio como ancla nominal de la economa. Muchas veces estas ganancias se evaporan rpidamente cuando, luego de una crisis cambiara, se desata una nueva espiral inflacionaria. Incluso pases que han adoptado sistemas de convertibilidad pueden encontrarse en este tipo de problema. La estrategia de desinflacin seguida por el Banco Central en los aos noventa fue muy cuidadosa en evitar utilizar el tipo de cambio para controlar la inflacin. De hecho, la poltica cambiara busc ms bien ser coherente con el objetivo de mantener el dficit de cuenta corriente dentro de rangos sostenibles. El objetivo de mantener el tipo de cambio dentro de la banda de flotacin no siempre fue logrado durante la primera etapa de las metas de inflacin. A pesar de los esfuerzos de compras de divisas como parte de la esterilizacin del masivo influjo de capitales, el rpido crecimiento de la productividad en Chile y su xito como economa emergente indujeron una apreciacin de equilibrio en el tipo de cambio real. La constatacin del esfuerzo por dilatar dicha apreciacin est en los importantes volmenes de reservas internacionales que acumulamos entre 1 990 y 1 997, a pesar de la existencia del encaje a los influjos de capitales, que apoyaba el lmite inferior de la banda. Aun con todo eso el tipo de cambio real se apreci cerca de 30% durante ese lapso (grfico 6). En trminos de resultados de esta primera etapa con metas de inflacin, la cada de la inflacin durante los noventa fue gradual, pero slida y persistente. La experiencia comenz con la inflacin de 27% en 1990 para llegar a slo 2,3% en 1 999, un hecho no visto desde las experiencias deflacionarias de los aos treinta. El retorno a la democracia, las reformas estructurales implementadas durante los setenta y ochenta, y las polticas que siguieron permitieron al pas cosechar los beneficios del masivo flujo de capitales externos durante los noventa, que fomentaron el crecimiento y favorecieron el control de la inflacin. Ms an, el hecho de que el tipo de cambio real de equilibrio se haya apreciado durante los noventa fue, sin duda, un factor que ayud al control de la inflacin. El desempeo de la economa en esta segunda etapa ha estado marcado por los vaivenes de la economa mundial, pese a lo cual el esquema de metas de inflacin ha sido particularmente exitoso. Entre los determinantes del escenario actual se deben destacar tres cambios en el panorama externo desde fines de 1 997: la menor demanda de activos nacionales por parte del resto del mundo desde la crisis asitica, la evolucin desfavorable de los trminos de intercambio y la mayor incertidumbre que ha caracterizado a los mercados internacionales en el perodo reciente. Ninguno de estos elementos es nuevo, pero su ocurrencia simultnea ha afectado no slo a la economa chilena, sino tambin a la mayora de las economas emergentes. En una economa pequea y abierta las variables externas tienen una fuerte incidencia en los desarrollos econmicos internos, especialmente cuando los mercados financieros no alcanzan un nivel de profundidad y sofisticacin que permitan absorber y distribuir mejor los ciclos externos (grficos 10, 11 y 12). Si bien tras la reducida inflacin de 1 999 (2,3%) sta sobrepas levemente la cota superior de la meta en el ao 2000 (al llegar a 4,5%), el aumento en la inflacin total es estrictamente el reflejo de las fuertes alzas en el precio internacional del petrleo (fenmeno que se dio, por lo dems, en la mayora de los pases del mundo). Los indicadores de inflacin subyacente para el 2000 y lo que va del ao 2001 no son diferentes a los de 1 999, y, por tanto, revelan que la tendencia de la inflacin en el mediano plazo est en lnea con el objetivo del Banco Central de mantener estabilidad de precios (grfico 13). Esta segunda etapa se caracteriza tambin por avances significativos en la liberalizacin de la cuenta de capitales de la balanza de pagos. Ello es consistente con evitar movimientos del tipo de cambio real ms all de lo que se considera razonable para una economa pequea y abierta al comercio internacional. Entre las desregulaciones ms importantes se encuentra la reduccin a 0% del encaje no remunerado a las entradas de capital y la eliminacin de los requerimientos de permanencia de al menos un ao para algunas formas de capital. Estas regulaciones, que permitan mantener tasas de inters domsticas a un nivel superior al de las extranjeras, se haban impuesto para evitar afectar al tipo de cambio durante un ciclo de poltica restrictiva. Sin embargo, la madurez del sistema financiero chileno y la credibilidad en las polticas del Banco Central permitieron eliminar estas regulaciones. Recientemente, el instituto emisor ha dado pasos para avanzar en la desindizacin de la economa al abandonar el uso de tasas reales de poltica monetaria por instrumentos nominales. Esta poltica es consistente con la convergencia de la inflacin a niveles internacionales y, en particular, con el rgimen de flotacin cambiara en operacin desde 1 999. Hasta el mes de julio pasado, la mecnica de operacin de la poltica monetaria consista en especificar como objetivo el premio de las tasas de inters sobre la variacin de la unidad de fomento (UF). Esto significaba que el da 9 de cada mes, el Banco Central modificaba el nivel de la tasa nominal al cual intervena en el mercado monetario y colocaba sus instrumentos de liquidez con el fin de adecuarla a la tasa de variacin de la UF conocida. Los aumentos extraordinarios de la UF en algunos meses se tendan a compensar con variaciones menores en otros meses. Nominalizacin de la tasa de poltica monetaria La nominalizacin de la poltica monetaria consiste en especificar el objetivo de tasa reerencial en trminos de una tasa nominal fija, en lugar de un premio sobre la UF. La tasa a la cual el Banco Central ofrece sus papeles y a la cual se establece el costo de sus facilidades de liquidez es fijada por el Consejo del Banco Central en funcin de la proyeccin de inflacin de mediano plazo. La nominalizacin de la poltica monetaria no debiera afectar el nivel promedio de las tasas de inters, reales o nominales, y por lo tanto la orientacin de dicha poltica. El nico efecto debiera ser una reduccin de la variabilidad de corto plazo (mes a mes) de las tasas de inters nominales y un aumento de la volatilidad de corto plazo de las tasas en UF (tambin mes a mes). En la discusin sobre la nominalizacin del objetivo de tasa de poltica monetaria (TPM) que se ha realizado en el Banco a travs del tiempo se han planteado una serie de argumentos a favor y en contra de esta decisin. Entre los argumentos a favor de la nominalizacin se encuentra que sta reduce la volatilidad de los agregados monetarios lquidos, disminuye la volatilidad del tipo de cambio, simplifica la integracin financiera internacional, facilita el calce de financiamiento de colocaciones no reajustables, y otorga mayor transparencia a las tasas de las colocaciones no reajustables. Los detractores de la nominalizacin de la TPM sealan que la variabilidad de las expectativas inflacionarias perjudica la seal de poltica monetaria en un esquema nominal y que para compensar lo anterior se requiere un grado mayor de activismo monetario. Durante nueve meses examinamos este argumento. En todo ese perodo, no se registr un solo caso en que, para lograr la meta del Banco Central, se hubiese requerido un mayor activismo en una poltica de tasa nominal que en una de tasa real. En las circunstancias actuales, se hacen ms evidentes las desventajas de tener un esquema indizado que puede agregar volatilidad al tipo de cambio. Ante reducciones significativas (y transitorias) de la inflacin, el Banco Central, si se fija un objetivo de tasa real, se ve obligado a intervenir para validar un nivel de tasas nominales extremadamente reducido, lo que disminuye el costo de arrastrar posiciones cortas en pesos y puede tener consecuencias adversas sobre la estabilidad del mercado de divisas. La revisin de la experiencia reciente revela que, en un esquema de metas de inflacin y cuando las polticas del Banco Central gozan de alta credibilidad, las expectativas inflacionarias se mueven dentro de rangos relativamente acotados. La estabilidad de las expectativas disminuye las supuestas desventajas de un rgimen de poltica monetaria con tasa nominal respecto de uno reajustable. La seal de poltica es transparente para los agentes y no se requiere de un activismo mayor en esta materia (grfico 14). Adems, con tasas bajas de inflacin de tendencia, aumenta la probabilidad de tasas de inflacin negativas en ciertos meses del ao, lo que podra llevar, en el esquema de polticas basadas en tasas reales, a tasas nominales negativas que, como tales, seran inmanejables. Profundizacin de la institucionalidad regulatoria del sistema financiero chileno Finalmente, la conduccin futura de la poltica monetaria bajo el esquema de metas de inflacin requiere que se profundice la institucionalidad regulatoria del sistema financiero chileno. Una economa sana requiere un sector bancario slido y seguro que asigne fondos a los prestatarios en una adecuada combinacin de riesgo-retorno para asegurar el funcionamiento eficiente del sistema de pagos. El sistema financiero es intensivo en el uso de informacin y, por lo tanto, est sujeto a problemas derivados de fallas de mercado como son la informacin asimtrica o el riesgo moral. Ello justifica la regulacin por parte de la autoridad. Un sistema moderno de supervisin contempla diversos aspectos: nfasis en la regulacin prudencial; creacin de incentivos para que el mercado supervise las instituciones financieras; procedimientos adecuados para solucionar situaciones de inestabilidad financiera; transparencia para que el mercado de capitales funcione a travs de estndares de control; y funcionamiento de las instituciones privadas que contribuyan a la eficacia del mercado, como clasificadores de riesgo y auditores externos. La experiencia de Chile en el tema de regulacin y supervisin bancaria en los ltimos veinte aos es rica y variada. A fines de los setenta, el pas implemento polticas de banca libre, minimizando la supervisin estatal en el sistema bancario. En efecto, se crey que la mano invisible del mercado llevara a una situacin slida y eficiente del sistema bancario. No obstante, el pas cay, a principios de la dcada de los ochenta, en la crisis ms profunda del siglo XX despus de la gran Depresin. Con posterioridad a ella, hubo un claro cambio de filosofa al reformarse la regulacin y supervisin del sistema bancario de manera profunda. Como respuesta a los episodios de fragilidad financiera, se dise un rol ms activo de supervisin y se incentiv el fortalecimiento de la institucionalidad estatal, con el objetivo de que una adecuada gestin del nuevo marco de incentivos promoviera el desarrollo econmico y la estabilidad financiera. As, despus de la crisis, el nfasis de las autoridades econmicas fue puesto en mejorar los sistemas de regulacin, supervisin y acceso a la informacin de las empresas financieras. Los cambios regulatorios llevaron al establecimiento de descalces mximos en moneda extranjera, reglas ms estrictas para el reconocimiento de ingresos, clasificacin de activos y exigencias de provisiones, establecimiento de mejores mtodos de entrega de informacin relevante por parte de los bancos, el reemplazo del seguro implcito a los depsitos por un seguro explcito de cobertura parcial, un rgimen de correcciones anticipadas de eventuales problemas de solvencia, un esquema efectivo y claro para solucionar el problema de instituciones insolventes, la implementacin de lmites ms estrictos para los prstamos relacionados y la obligacin de que dichas operaciones se efecten en condiciones de mercado. En una segunda etapa, ya recuperada la estabilidad y solvencia del sistema, la institucionalidad regulatoria enfrent nuevos desafos asociados al proceso de globalizacin y de insercin e integracin internacional de la economa, a la consolidacin de los agentes financieros y a la sofisticacin de nuevos productos financieros. Las principales reformas financieras dictadas por las autoridades reguladoras en los ltimos aos, pueden resumirse en aquellas que propenden a acotar de mejor forma los riesgos financieros, permitiendo, a su vez, la autorizacin de nuevas operaciones bancarias; aquellas que complementan las normas relativas a la internacionalizacin y otras que permiten la creacin de nuevos productos. Un elemento adicional en la profundizaron del mercado financiero se obtiene, indirectamente, con la decisin del Banco Central de utilizar una tasa nominal de inters como tasa de poltica monetaria. Ello permitir un mejoramiento de la estructura de activos y pasivos no slo del mismo Banco, sino adems del sector financiero privado en la medida que se mejoran los calces de monedas que cada sector posee en sus portafolios. Ello redundar en un beneficio para todos los agentes del sector financiero y para toda la economa. En el tema de la internacionalizacin bancaria, cabe destacar los indudables beneficios que aparecen con la apertura hacia el exterior. La internacionalizacin de la banca puede implicar un fuerte aumento de la eficacia del sector financiero. De acuerdo con la experiencia internacional, aparecen nuevos servicios, mayor innovacin financiera, mejor aprovechamiento del capital de un banco y una mayor diversificacin del riesgo. En consecuencia, aparecen nuevas fuentes de crecimiento y se promueve el desarrollo de la exportacin de servicios. Sin embargo, con la internacionalizacin surgen algunos riesgos, y se requiere adoptar medidas que permitan mantenerlos acotados. Para enfrentar los riesgos y dificultades del proceso de internacionalizacin de la banca, se ha planteado un conjunto de mecanismos de regulacin. En particular, el Banco Central participa en la regulacin de la inversin en el exterior de los bancos, tanto en el mbito cambiarlo como en el rea de la regulacin financiera, cautelando los intereses de las personas en tpicos tales como la adquisicin de acciones e instalacin de filiales y joint ventures o la regulacin de las inversiones financieras y los crditos transfronterizos. En este ltimo mbito, dispone de sus propias facultades cambiaras y comparte responsabilidades con la Superintendencia de Bancos en el establecimiento de requisitos patrimoniales y de provisiones para efectuar dichas operaciones. En los ltimos aos, en el sistema financiero chileno se han desarrollado una serie de innovaciones en productos. El pas cuenta ahora con un mercado desarrollado de colocaciones de consumo, comerciales, de comercio exterior e hipotecarias. Existe un amplio mercado de instrumentos de renta fija y variable, incluyendo pactos de retrocompra ampliamente utilizados por el Banco Central en el manejo de liquidez del mercado interbancario (grfico 15). El Banco Central ha procedido recientemente a ampliar la gama de productos vinculados a pagos, ahorro y manejo de riesgos financieros, autorizando la emisin de dinero electrnico, y la operacin de nuevos productos derivados que facilitan el manejo de los riesgos financieros. Dentro de estos ltimos destacan los futuros en monedas, tasas de inters locales e internacionales, y determinadas formas de instrumentos orwards y swaps. Asimismo, se levant el requisito de autorizacin previa para realizar derivados de tasas de inters con el exterior. La posibilidad de contar con derivados sobre tasas de inters permitir a los bancos una readecuacin ms barata y rpida de sus posiciones expuestas a riesgo de tasas de inters. A su vez, el Banco Central ha ayudado a profundizar y completar mercados mediante la emisin de instrumentos reajustables segn las variaciones del tipo de cambio, los que permiten cubrir riesgos cambiarlos y canjear pagars pagaderos en cupones por pagars cero cupn, lo que permite satisfacer la demanda por instrumentos de mayor duracin y la construccin de una curva de rendimiento cero cupn como eje para la operatoria del mercado de derivados de tasas de inters. Para un desarrollo ms eficiente del mercado cambiarlo, tambin se han autorizado prstamos interbancarios y pactos entre instituciones financieras en moneda extranjera. No obstante, el vertiginoso crecimiento de los instrumentos financieros, en particular los derivados, puede potenciar los riesgos a que se enfrenta el sistema financiero. Por ello, ha sido necesario acotar la toma de riesgos excesivos que las instituciones bancarias enfrentan mediante la toma de posicin neta en moneda extranjera, la existencia de descalces en los plazos de activos y pasivos, y los descalces entre las tasas de inters pactadas para activos y pasivos as como por la dependencia del financiamiento interbancario, que puede llevar a riesgos de contagio. En la actualidad, la mayora de los riesgos que enfrentan los bancos se encuentran adecuadamente acotados, sean stos riesgos de monedas, de tasas de inters, de inflacin, o de liquidez. El Banco Central ha introducido, paulatinamente, importantes mejoras a la normativa sobre calce de activos y pasivos en moneda extranjera, plazos y tasas de inters. Dado que durante la ltima dcada se han cumplido sistemticamente las metas de inflacin decreciente que se ha propuesto el Banco Central y que, adems, el nivel y volatilidad de la inflacin han disminuido en los ltimos aos, un incremento del descalce entre activos y pasivos no representa un incremento relevante de la exposicin al riesgo del sistema financiero a causa de la inflacin. Lo anterior, es tambin coherente con los pasos que el Banco Central ha dado para estimular una mayor profundidad del mercado financiero en moneda local y, como sealara, con la decisin de moverse hacia tasas de poltica monetaria nominales. Ya hemos informado pblicamente acerca de la reforma y modernizacin del sistema de pagos que prepara el Banco Central. Este proyecto tiene como objetivo fundamental establecer mecanismos de liquidacin ms eficaces y seguros. En sus aspectos centrales la reforma busca asegurar que los riesgos de liquidacin de pagos entre las instituciones financieras sean debidamente asumidos y cautelados por las mismas instituciones, evitando que estos se transfieran al resto del sistema financiero, al pblico o al Banco Central. La posibilidad de realizar transferencias electrnicas en tiempo real y contra saldos disponibles permitir eliminar una parte sustancial de los riesgos presentes en la liquidacin de pagos (tabla 1). Pero el avance en la modernizacin de nuestro sistema financiero requiere de pasos adicionales, que se ven facilitados por dos hechos recientes vinculados entre s: la consolidacin de la inflacin en tasas bajas y estables, y la nominalizacin de la tasa de inters de poltica monetaria. Uno de estos pasos adicionales se refiere al pago de intereses sobre obligaciones a la vista y cuentas corrientes. Este es un tema que debe ser abordado cuidadosamente para cautelar su coherencia con el resto de la regulacin financiera. Otros aspectos se refieren a la normativa de las libretas de ahorro y las reformas en marcha al sistema de pagos. Asimismo, creemos necesario que se inicie una revisin global del esquema de garantas a los depsitos que funciona desde 1 986 en Chile, y que resulta conveniente replantear a la luz de estas modernizaciones. La Ley General de Bancos (LGB) y las normas complementarias del Banco Central y de la Superintendencia de Bancos distinguen claramente entre las captaciones a la vista y las obligaciones a plazo. Las obligaciones a la vista son exigibles y pagaderas a todo evento y, ante problemas de solvencia o liquidacin forzosa de una institucin financiera, cuentan con la garanta del Banco Central en caso de insuficiencia de recursos en la institucin afectada. Como medida de resguardo, la LGB exige constituir reserva tcnica sobre las obligaciones a la vista que exceden en 2,5 veces el capital bsico del banco, adems de una prelacin de los depositantes con recursos a la vista respecto de otros acreedores. Las obligaciones a plazo, en cambio, tienen una garanta limitada, valedera slo para las personas naturales y con un tope mximo por depositante. En coherencia con lo anterior, la actual normativa financiera del Banco Central permite el pago de intereses y reajustes sobre obligaciones a plazo, pero prohbe dicho pago sobre captaciones del pblico a menos de 30 das, que se consideran a la vista en la LGB. La autorizacin de pago de intereses sobre ciertas obligaciones a la vista es una iniciativa que tiene una serie de ventajas desde el punto de vista de la eficacia y competencia en el sistema financiero. Pero al mismo tiempo, es necesario conciliar esta situacin con el esquema de garantas vigente. Al respecto, se debe considerar que el pago de intereses sobre obligaciones vista probablemente aumenta la base sobre la cual se aplica la garanta del Banco Central. Adems, un rgimen en que stas se benefician del pago de intereses y adems se garantizan a todo evento, podra generar graves distorsiones en el sistema: al eliminar el necesario balance entre rentabilidad y riesgo que debe exhibir todo instrumento financiero, se crea un riesgo moral que ser particularmente visible en el caso de instituciones que pudieran exhibir problemas de solvencia, presentar un nivel de capital inadecuado o enfrentar mayores niveles de riesgo. La elaboracin de la normativa debe tomar en cuenta estos aspectos, recogiendo la experiencia internacional en la materia y las particularidades del caso chileno. Por otra parte, se hace necesario tambin modificar la normativa que rige en la actualidad las libretas de ahorro, especialmente aquellas con giro incondicional, con el fin de adecuarlas a las nuevas realidades de los mercados financieros, incluyendo aspectos relacionados con la nominalizacin, en un ambiente de baja inflacin y avances tecnolgicos. En todo caso, es esencial que se preserve la orientacin de este tipo de instrumentos a su objetivo primordial de fomento al ahorro de las personas. Finalmente, en lnea con los aspectos anteriores, se estima necesario avanzar en un examen crtico del esquema vigente de garanta y seguro de depsitos, tomando en cuenta para ello la experiencia internacional relevante y los avances en la reforma al sistema de pagos de alto valor. Ello debera llevar al diseo de mecanismos ms eficaces de proteccin a los depositantes, lo que se traducir en un sistema ms sano y eficaz, y en el que se cautelen debidamente los problemas de riesgo moral a que estn afectos muchos de estos mecanismos. Esta iniciativa debe abordarse en un trabajo conjunto entre el Banco Central, la Superintendencia de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras y el Ministerio de Hacienda. Este conjunto de iniciativas representa un proceso ordenado y coherente de modernizacin de la normativa financiera que, cautelando debidamente su estabilidad, debe contribuir al desarrollo de un sistema financiero ms eficaz y ms competitivo en nuestro pas. Tal como en el pasado, esperamos la colaboracin de la Asociacin de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras en determinadas etapas de su elaboracin. El sistema de regulacin y supervisin actual tiene slidas bases. Sin embargo, los sistemas financieros y sus regulaciones se ven enfrentados a procesos evolutivos continuos. La creciente complejidad del sistema financiero en conjunto con la mayor internalizacin de la banca requiere que la regulacin prudencial descanse cada vez ms en la autorregulacin por parte de los mismos entes financieros. El mismo mercado, y las propias instituciones financieras organizadas, deben ser capaces de proveer elementos de disciplina para el correcto funcionamiento del sector financiero. Ello, no obstante, requiere la vigilancia permanente y efectiva por parte de las autoridades monetaria y bancaria. Una disciplina de mercado eficaz requiere divulgaciones significativas, confiables y oportunas de informacin al pblico. Si bien en los ltimos aos se ha continuado avanzando en la transparencia de la informacin bancaria, es necesario perseverar en este camino con la entrega peridica de informacin sobre riesgos financieros asociados a tasas de inters, monedas extranjeras, liquidez, inflacin y riesgos sistmicos asociados al mercado de prstamos interbancarios y al sistema de pagos. Tambin se debe entregar mayor informacin sobre cantidad, calidad y precios de las garantas recibidas por los bancos, lo que permitir conocer ms precisamente los riesgos de crdito en que estos incurren. Finalmente, una mayor autorregulacin de las entidades financieras, y poner grandes exigencias en los niveles gerenciales y tcnicos que trabajan en ellas debe ir acompaada de crecientes niveles de responsabilidad por parte de sus directores. En este sentido, se deben dar pasos concretos para aumentar los niveles de transparencia y profesionalizacin de la toma de decisiones, tomando en cuenta tanto los intereses de los inversionistas como aquellos de las empresas y personas a cuyo servicio debe estar el sistema financiero. Hago un llamado a la Asociacin de Bancos e Instituciones Financieras a establecer mecanismos que apoyen la transparencia del sistema y su autorregulacin.

Title: Economic developments in 2001 and prospects for 2002 and 2003
text: ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENTS IN 2001 AND PROSPECTS FOR 2002 AND 2003 Presentation by Carlos Massad, President of the Central Bank of Chile, at the Senate on the occasion of the presentation of the Annual Report.September 12, 2001 I. Introduction 1. We have followed with dismay the news about yesterday's tragic events in the United States. Before presenting to you the September Monetary Policy Report, I would like to express our conviction that peace, integration and cooperation among peoples are the only foundations on which humanity can build its sustained progress. We reject and condemn this terrorist act. 2. Our Monetary Policy Report was prepared prior to yesterday's events. It is too early for a thorough assessment of the consequences of such events. We believe that the thrust of our report remains, but that the risks are accentuated. I will comment a little more on this at the end of this presentation. 3. The developments of the Chilean economy in the last year have been determined both by the instability of international markets and by the slow recovery of domestic demand. A small and open economy such as Chile's cannot be oblivious to the events that are happening in the main countries of the globe and the region. 4. Towards the end of August last year, the surprise slowdown in output and domestic demand induced the Central Bank to initiate successive reductions in the monetary policy interest rate. Since then to date, the Central Bank has lowered the governing interest rate six times, which has meant a fall of 200 basis points. Likewise, an international scenario in which the expectation of a continued dynamism of the world economy (of the order of 4% per year in 2001 and 2002) and the relative improvement of international financing conditions augured a more optimistic vision about the future development of the Chilean economy. At that time, the increase in specific prices associated with the oil price hikes of early 2000 was expected to have a transitory impact on inflation. Based on this, a gradual reduction in oil prices and the persistence of domestic market capacity slack were projected for a medium-term horizon, both elements conducive to inflationary prospects tending to the center of the target range in the projection horizon. 7. The sharp increase in the nominal exchange rate in 2001, as a result of the unfavourable external scenario and the difficulties experienced by neighbouring countries, has meant that current inflation projections for the coming quarters will be higher than those forecast in September 2000. Likewise, the current inflation projections are consistent with an economy that does not yet show clear signs of dynamism in its domestic demand, with slack in its markets still important. 8. In addition to the above, the deterioration of the international scenario in recent months, particularly in the terms of trade, will have repercussions on income and therefore on consumption, which tends to reduce medium-term inflationary pressures. 9. With regard to the evolution of GDP, in September 2000 it was considered that it was possible to expect average growth over the next 24 months of around 5.8 per cent per annum. This is under the scenario of a more expansionary monetary policy, together with a framework of consolidation of the structural fiscal surplus at 1% of GDP and a favorable international scenario for the Chilean economy. However, the marked deterioration of the international environment, due to the non-consolidation of the reactivation of the US economy and the impact that this situation has had on the main nations of the world, has meant lower expected growth for Chile's trading partners and a sharp decrease in the prices of Chile's main exports. 10. This worsening of the international scenario has created an unfavorable environment for local economic growth, which has meant that recent projections are below the forecasts made last year. II. Recent economic developments and medium-term prospects 11. In recent months, inflation has remained within the target range, although with pronounced swings. Beyond product-specific effects, price growth so far has been consistent with the evolution of activity and spending, the trajectory of external prices in dollars, the pace of expansion of labor costs and fuel prices. All this makes it foreseeable, for this second semester, a growth of the economy greater than the 3.5% registered in the first half of the year, together with a stable annual inflation trajectory in the medium term, but somewhat volatile in the short term. The downward correction is mainly due to the fact that the external macroeconomic scenario facing the Chilean economy, since the middle of last year, has certainly been much less promising than anticipated a year ago. 37. The oil shock was and continues to be more intense and lasting than expected, negatively affecting household disposable income and firms' production costs. This, together with the rapid slowdown in the world economy, the continuation of the terms of trade at low levels and the frequent turbulence in international financial markets, have created an unfavorable environment for national economic growth. However, it is also clear that there are factors in the country that have influenced the slowdown in domestic demand observed since the second quarter of last year and that have their own dynamics beyond the external environment. 38. The same most adverse international scenario has exposed several shortcomings in the functioning of domestic markets, some already traditional (such as the lack of flexibility in real wages) and others that are more attributable to problems of regulation (or excess of it) accumulated in the past or feared, by some sectors, for the future. 39.
