This trajectory of inflation is consistent with several factors. First, although the pass-through from depreciation to inflation appears to have been low so far, it is not zero, which is likely to manifest itself in an acceleration of annual inflation towards the middle of next year. In addition, the central scenario assumes a real exchange rate that tends slightly towards appreciation with respect to the average reached in August. 42. Second, the deterioration of the international scenario, particularly in external prices in dollars, tends to reduce medium-term inflationary pressures, which will remain contained despite the foreseeable acceleration in activity during the second half of the year and beyond. 43. Third, the expected reduction in oil prices will not generate additional reductions in inflation beyond those already observed. Finally, medium-term inflation expectations are clearly within the target range and close to 3%. 44. As always, all projections delivered in this Report are in line with the events that the Board estimates are most likely over the next eight quarters, and which constitute the baseline projection scenario. However, it is possible that the economy over the next two years will follow different paths than expected, which configures a series of alternative scenarios and the balance of risks. These alternative events are associated with the international environment and the evolution of the domestic economy. 45. Among the former, the uncertainty associated with the situation in emerging economies stands out. Although much of the negative scenario considered in previous reports has materialized during the second and third quarters, it is clear that the situation could deteriorate further. This would likely be accompanied by a further transitory depreciation of the peso. On the other hand, the magnitude of the impact on inflation of the recent depreciation of the peso and the timing of its manifestation can be estimated only in rough terms, adding additional degrees of uncertainty to those already existing about the path of the exchange rate. 46. Although the US has maintained positive, albeit low, growth so far and is expected to grow at reasonable rates in the following six months, there are significant risks of a further slowdown in the US economy, not ruling out a recessionary picture. The alternative scenario is conformed, then, by a more prolonged slowdown in world growth, in the near future, which would keep the prices of the main export products at depressed levels, limiting the growth of domestic spending. 47. Domestically, despite incipient signs that activity will enter a path of acceleration during the second half of the year, it is still too early to ensure sustained growth in spending. In fact, the growth of industrial production and imports suffered in July, altering the upward trend it brought from previous months. 48. The occurrence of these alternative scenarios, both externally and internally, can certainly modify inflation and growth projections. The Council considers that, in the light of the information available so far, the balance of risks to activity is skewed to the downside. There is still some uncertainty about the persistence of the acceleration of domestic economic activity, as the speed of growth of the world economy in the coming years and the terms-of-trade scenario are very uncertain. 49. On the other hand, there is a risk that regional turbulence will be exacerbated, pushing for a greater depreciation of the peso compared to what was estimated in the central scenario. Moreover, as mentioned above, the relative lack of certainty regarding the precise timing and magnitude of the pass-through of such a phenomenon to domestic prices may, under certain circumstances, lead to an increase in medium-term inflation expectations. Against this background, the Council considers that the balance of risks to inflation is somewhat skewed to the upside. 50. It is important to note that these balances of risks to inflation and growth do not imply that the most likely alternative scenario is one that combines higher inflationary pressures with lower economic growth. Rather, alternative scenarios are shaped by relatively independent sets of events, such as the evolution of the world economy as a whole and the financial outlook in the economies of the region, and are constructed assuming that the MPR remains constant at its current level. 51. In any case, the Central Bank will continue to pay attention to the effective occurrence of any of these alternative scenarios, so as to use its monetary policy with all the necessary flexibility so as not to compromise the achievement of the inflation target. The Council will pay particular attention in the coming months to the speed of growth of consumption and employment, as well as to developments in the world economy, in particular the pace of growth in the US and the financial situation in the rest of the emerging economies. III. Context in which policies are developed 52. A point that I would like to highlight once again concerns the context in which Chilean economic policy is developed. Certainly, the policy framework in force in our country is one in which the best cushioning of the negative effects received from abroad can be achieved. Small countries highly dependent on global economic developments are exposed to fluctuations and volatilities with a significant degree of amplification and spread to local markets, mainly because the links with the international financial system are weak and because national financial systems lack a significant degree of deepening and further development. 53. An important contribution that countries' central banks can make to ensuring greater financial stability is to help create the conditions for the effects of external shocks to be spread across different markets. 54. The inflation targeting scheme, in force in Chile since the beginning of the last decade, has been a fundamental pillar for achieving macroeconomic stability and for strengthening the credibility of the monetary authority, characteristics highly desired by any Central Bank, particularly in episodes of generalized financial instabilities. This scheme, together with the free floating exchange rate, has allowed in recent years that the effects of external shocks are not concentrated in specific markets, as happened in the past in the Chilean economy. 55. The free floating of the exchange rate, which has been operating in our country since September 1999, has facilitated the implementation of an expansionary monetary policy by the Central Bank, with interest rate levels considered historically low, such as those that have prevailed in recent months. At the same time, it has allowed a continuous development of the export sector, in particular of those non-traditional products, a fact that is highly relevant if we take into account the downward revisions of the growth of the main countries of the world. In terms of capital accounting, during the nineties the Chilean monetary authority conducted a prudent and gradual process of liberalization, designed to achieve full integration with international financial markets, but trying to minimize the risks that could jeopardize the process of financial stability and macroeconomic of our country. 57. Thus, last April, and to the extent that the foundations were laid for full financial integration with a minimum of associated risks, the Central Bank culminated with the process of liberalization of the capital account. In practice, the new regulations eliminated the exchange restrictions that until then had affected investment and financing decisions. Among other measures, they highlighted the elimination of the reserve requirement for capital from abroad and the requirement for prior authorization that took place for certain capital movements to and from abroad. 58. More recently, the nominalization of the policy rate has been a logical consequence of the modernization of the Central Bank's monetary policy. Since the mid-eighties, monetary policy was implemented through readjustable interest rates. This was the instrument considered appropriate for that time, due to the history of high and variable inflation that existed in Chile and the relative depth of fixed income financial markets indexed to the UF. 59. In 1999, after the floating exchange rate, substantial progress was made in opening the capital account and increasing transparency in the conduct of monetary policy. The natural step of this process was the nominalization of monetary policy, considered fundamental for the integration of our economy with international financial markets and for the development and deepening of markets for products denominated in pesos. 60. Within this set of policies, an important complement has been the behavior of fiscal policy in recent years, particularly after the announcement of a policy based on a structural surplus, a fact that has undoubtedly become an additional pillar on which the country's other macroeconomic policies have been based. 61. In terms of results, it can be argued that this set of policies has been fully successful and coherent, since the growth rate of our country, although below its potential, is one of the highest within the Latin American context and emerging countries, without considering the large countries with more closed economies. Major investment projects in infrastructure and real estate, announced by the President of the Republic for the coming years, will mean an additional stimulus for domestic demand and employment. This will make it possible to change the face in most regions, resume greater economic dynamism and make our country grow, possibly above what is projected in this Report, if the world economy returns to the path of a clear recovery. IV. Deepening and modernization of the national financial system 63. The future conduct of monetary policy under the inflation targeting scheme requires that the Regulatory institutionality of the Chilean financial system. A healthy economy requires maintaining a strong and secure banking sector that allocates funds to borrowers in an appropriate risk-return combination to ensure Efficient operation of the payment system. 64. The justification for a system based on regulation is based on possible market failures, such as the existence of asymmetric information or moral hazard. A modern supervisory system includes several aspects: emphasis on prudential regulation; creating incentives for the market to supervise financial institutions; appropriate procedures for resolving situations of financial instability; transparency for the capital market to function through control standards; and operation of private institutions that contribute to market efficiency, such as risk classifiers and external auditors. Modern Monitoring System Prudential regulation. Market incentives for supervision. Proper procedures. Greater transparency. Private institutions contribute to efficiency (classifiers risk, external auditors). Monetary Policy Report, September 2001 30 65. After the crisis of the 80s, once the stability and solvency of the system was recovered, the regulatory institutionality faced new challenges associated with the process of globalization and the insertion and international integration of the economy, the consolidation of financial agents and the sophistication of new products. 66. The main financial reforms dictated by the regulatory authorities in recent years can be summarized in those that tend to better limit financial risks, complemented by the authorization of new banking operations. 67. An additional element in the deepening of the financial market is obtained, indirectly, with the decision of the Central Bank to use a nominal interest rate as the policy rate. This will allow an improvement in the structure of assets and liabilities not only of the Central Bank itself, but also of the private financial sector to the extent that the currency adjustments that each sector has in its portfolios are improved. This will benefit all actors in the financial sector and the economy as a whole. 68. The internationalization of banking may imply a strong increase in the efficiency of the financial sector. New services, greater financial innovation, better use of a bank's capital and greater risk diversification appear. As a result, new sources of growth are emerging and the development of services exports is promoted. 69. However, with internationalization some risks arise, and it is necessary to adopt measures that allow them to be kept limited. To this end, a set of mechanisms have been proposed, such as the regulation of banks' investment abroad. 70. In recent years, a series of product innovations have been developed in the Chilean financial system. The country now has a developed market for consumer, commercial, foreign trade and mortgage placements. There is a broad market for fixed and variable income instruments, including buyback agreements widely used by the Central Bank in managing liquidity in the interbank market. 71. However, recently the Central Bank has proceeded to expand the range of products linked to payments, savings and financial risk management, authorizing the issuance of electronic money, and the operation of new derivative products that facilitate the management of financial risks. Among the latter, futures in currencies, local and international interest rates, and certain forms of forward instruments and swaps stand out. Likewise, the requirement of prior authorization to operate with interest rate derivatives abroad was lifted. 72. In turn, the Central Bank has helped to deepen and complete markets through the issuance of instruments readjustable according to variations in the exchange rate, which allow to cover exchange risks and exchange promissory notes payable in coupons for zero coupon promissory notes, satisfying the demand for long-term instruments. For a more efficient development of the exchange market, interbank loans and pacts between financial institutions in foreign currency have also been authorized. 73. However, the rapid growth of financial instruments, in particular derivatives, may enhance the risks facing the financial system. Therefore, it has been necessary to limit the excessive risk-taking that banking institutions face for taking a net position in foreign currency. 74. At present, most of the risks faced by banks are adequately controlled, whether they are currency, interest rate, inflation, liquidity or contagion risks. The Central Bank has gradually introduced significant improvements to the regulations on matching assets and liabilities in various currencies, maturities and interest rates. 75. Public information has been provided on the reform and modernization of the payment system being prepared by the Central Bank. The main objective of this project is to establish more efficient and secure settlement mechanisms. In its central aspects, the reform seeks to ensure that the risks of settlement of payments between financial institutions are duly assumed and safeguarded by the same institutions, preventing them from being transferred to the rest of the financial system, to the public or to the Central Bank. The possibility of making electronic transfers in real time and against available balances will eliminate a substantial part of the risks present in the settlement of payments. 76. Progress in modernizing our financial system requires additional steps, which are facilitated by two recent interlinked events: the consolidation of low and stable annual inflation, and the nominalization of the monetary policy interest rate. 77. One of the additional steps, on which a rigorous study is being made, refers to the payment of interest on demand obligations and current accounts. This is an issue that must be approached with sufficient care in order to safeguard consistency with the rest of financial regulation. Other aspects relate to the regulation of passbooks and the ongoing reforms to the payment system. We also believe that it is necessary to initiate a comprehensive review of the deposit guarantee scheme, which has been in place in the country since 1986, and that it is appropriate to rethink in the light of these modernizations. 78. The current financial regulations of the Central Bank allow the payment of interest and adjustments on term obligations, but prohibit such payment on deposits of the public to less than 30 days, which are considered in sight in the General Law of Banks. 79. The authorization to pay interest on certain demand obligations is an initiative that has a number of advantages from the point of view of the efficiency and competition of the financial system. However, it is necessary to reconcile this need for greater competition and efficiency with the existing guarantee scheme. 80. It should be considered that the payment of interest on exposed obligations is likely to increase the basis on which the Central Bank guarantee is applied. In addition, a regime in which they benefit from interest payments and are also guaranteed at all events could encourage serious distortions in the system. Indeed, by eliminating the necessary balance between profitability and risk, a moral hazard is created that will be particularly evident in the case of institutions that could exhibit solvency problems and therefore greater risk. 81. In line with the above, it is considered necessary to advance in a critical examination of the current deposit guarantee and insurance scheme. This should lead to the design of more efficient depositor protection mechanisms, resulting in a healthier and more efficient system, and in which the moral hazard problems affected by many of these mechanisms are duly addressed. This initiative should be addressed in a joint effort between the Central Bank, the SBIF and the Ministry of Finance. 82. The current regulatory and supervisory system has a solid foundation. However, financial systems and their regulations are faced with continuous evolutionary processes. The increasing complexity of systems, together with the greater internationalization of banking, requires that prudential regulation increasingly rely on self-regulation by the financial entities themselves. 83. The market itself, and the organized financial institutions themselves, must be able to provide elements of discipline for the proper functioning of the financial sector, for which it is essential to persevere in the delivery of relevant, timely and reliable information to the public. 84. This has meant an increasing level of managerial skills appropriate to the new times and a Primary commitment on the part of the directors of financial institutions. Concrete steps have thus been taken to increase the levels of transparency and professionalization of decisions. 85. This, however, requires permanent and effective vigilance on the part of the monetary and banking authorities. 86. In this general context, I am pleased to inform the Senate that we have concluded a preliminary agreement with the Ministry of Finance to transform part of the debt in dollars of the Treasury with the Central Bank into debt in pesos. This will help resolve the Central Bank's equity deficit, and will be an important contribution to the Bank's institutional strengthening. This agreement must soon be submitted to Congress for legal sanction. 87. Finally, I cannot fail to make an additional comment on yesterday's terrible events in the United States. We deeply regret the casualties caused and the damage inflicted. But beyond the pain of yesterday and today, there will surely be other consequences that today are difficult to foresee. We have made an internal analysis in the Central Bank of the possible consequences, and we maintain a minute-by-minute assessment of the situation of the markets and their prospects. The current macroeconomic policy scheme is the best to face this situation, and we are prepared to adopt the measures that may be necessary to minimize the effects of this tragedy on the Chilean economy. Yesterday, we have already arranged the necessary measures to ensure an orderly functioning of the financial markets and to provide an adequate provision of liquidity in accordance with the needs in these special circumstances. Likewise, the Central Bank will keep an attentive eye on the changed market, in order to adapt its operations to the requirements for risk coverage and liquidity in foreign currency, taking care to avoid disruptive financial effects in that market.

Los pases pequeos y altamente dependientes de los desarrollos econmicos mundiales, estn expuestos a fluctuaciones y volatilidades con un grado importante de amplificacin y propagacin hacia los mercados locales, debido principalmente a que los vnculos existentes con el sistema financiero internacional son dbiles y a que a los sistemas financieros nacionales les falta un grado importante de profundizacin y mayor desarrollo. El esquema de metas de inflacin, vigente en Chile desde comienzos de la dcada pasada, ha sido un pilar fundamental para la consecucin de la estabilidad macroeconmica y para afianzar la credibilidad en la autoridad monetaria, caractersticas altamente deseadas por todo Banco Central, en particular en episodios de inestabilidades financieras generalizadas. Este esquema, unido a la libre flotacin cambiara, ha permitido en los ltimos aos que los efectos de los shocks externos no se concentren en mercados especficos, tal como sucedi en el pasado en la economa chilena.  La libre flotacin del tipo de cambio, que opera en nuestro pas desde septiembre de 1999, ha facilitado la implementacin de una poltica monetaria expansiva por parte del Banco Central, con niveles de tasas de inters consideradas como histricamente bajas, tal como las que han prevalecido en los ltimos meses. Al mismo tiempo, ha permitido un desarrollo continuo del sector exportador, en particular de aquellos productos no tradicionales, hecho altamente relevante si se tienen en cuenta las revisiones a la baja del crecimiento de los principales pases del mundo. As, en el pasado mes de abril, y en la medida que se fueron sentando las bases para una plena integracin financiera con un mnimo de riegos asociados, el Banco Central culmin con el proceso de liberalizacin de la cuenta de capitales. En la prctica, la nueva normativa elimin las restricciones cambiaras que hasta ese momento afectaban a las decisiones de inversin y financiamiento. Entre otras medidas, destacaron la eliminacin del requisito de encaje a los capitales provenientes del exterior y del requerimiento de autorizacin previa que tena lugar para ciertos movimientos de capitales desde y hacia el exterior.  Ms recientemente, la nominalizacin de la tasa de poltica monetaria ha sido una consecuencia lgica de la modernizacin de la poltica monetaria del Banco Central. Desde mediados de los aos ochenta, la poltica monetaria se implemento a travs de las tasas de inters reajustables. Este fue el instrumento considerado como adecuado para ese momento, debido a la historia de elevada y variable inflacin que exista en Chile y la relativa profundidad de los mercados financieros de renta fija indizada a la UF.  Durante los aos noventa el Banco Central avanz en diversas direcciones que apuntaban a modernizar el instrumental de poltica, definiendo primero la tasa interbancaria diaria como el instrumento relevante, en 1995, para luego crear mercados incipientes en pesos, al introducir documentos nominales a 90 das y un ao. En 1999, luego de la flotacin cambiara, se avanz substantivamente en abrir la cuenta de capitales y aumentar la transparencia en la conduccin de la poltica monetaria. El paso natural de este proceso fue la nominalizacin de la poltica monetaria, considerado como fundamental para la integracin de nuestra economa con los mercados financieros internacionales y para el desarrollo y profundizacin de los mercados de productos denominados en pesos.  Dentro de este conjunto de polticas, un complemento importante ha sido el comportamiento de la poltica fiscal durante los ltimos aos, en particular luego del anuncio de una poltica basada en un supervit estructural, hecho que sin duda alguna se ha constituido en un pilar adicional sobre el cual se han asentado las dems polticas macroeconmicas del pas.  En materia de resultados, se puede argumentar que este conjunto de polticas ha sido plenamente exitoso y coherente, pues la tasa de crecimiento de nuestro pas, si bien est por debajo de lo que es su potencial, es de las ms elevadas dentro del contexto latinoamericano y de los pases emergentes, sin considerar los grandes pases de economas ms cerradas, China e India. Ya es sabido que pases de Asia como Singapur y Taiwn se encuentran en recesin, en tanto que un nmero importante de pases de Amrica Latina han revisado drsticamente a la baja sus proyecciones de crecimiento para ste y el prximo ao.
