Microdata-based stress exercises compute agents' debt at risk as the product of an estimated probability of default for the volume of credit held by each debtor. These consider scenarios with sharp interest rate hikes and significant falls in economic activity and employment. In general, the estimates show that the aggregate risks remain stable, but draw attention to some specific points. In the case of firms, in the base scenario as of November 2021, debt at risk also remains at levels similar to those reached in the previous IEF, with data as of September. Based on this initial situation, three risk scenarios are proposed that incorporate a year of falling sales and increases in interest rates and inflation. The adverse and severe scenarios consider falls in activity consistent with the exercise of banking stress, and a Covid scenario is added that includes a greater drop in sales, in line with what was observed at the peak of the pandemic. On top of them, a medium-term rate shock of 500 basis points and an increase in inflation 4 percentage points above that observed, which would take it above 11% over one year. The results show that a fall in sales and an increase in the cost of financing would be the most relevant factors for the increase in firms' debt at risk, followed far behind by the effect of the indexation of debts to the UF, given that there is a smaller proportion of loans in this denomination. Falls in sales affect the generation of income for firms, while an increase in interest rates stresses their financial burden. All this increases the probability of default and the debt at risk. It should be noted that this stress test has a similar impact to that of previous years, where the debt at risk would be covered by the sum of the effective and additional provisions and those estimated from the bank stress test. Given that the scenarios applied are similar, the exercise carried out shows that the provisions are sufficient to cover the expected losses of the portfolio. It should be noted that this estimate does not consider the additional mitigation of losses provided by the guarantees associated with the loans, so it can be understood as a higher level of risk estimation. Notwithstanding the fact that at the aggregate level the results indicate stable risk levels, the analysis carried out exhibits a heterogeneous impact by sectors, with a greater incidence in those with greater debt refinancing needs, which suggests an issue to monitor. On the household side, by applying extreme conditions contained in the scenarios, to which is added an increase of 7% in the unemployment rate, the debt at risk it reacts with particular sensitivity to the shock of unemployment and interest rates, affecting the lowest income quintiles the most. It should be noted that the effect of the inflation shock on household debt at risk is more limited. This is due to the fact that the effect of debts in UF  associated with mortgage loans that concentrate households in higher-income quintiles  is mitigated by a greater frequency of readjustment of the salaries of this group. A robust market, with high local savings, allows the financing of credit with less exposure to the dollar with the consequent advantages in terms of exposure to external shocks and interest rates. It is particularly beneficial to promote the availability of stable long-term savings funds, which strengthens the domestic capital market by favoring the financing of long-term loans with less incidence of external financing, and allows mitigating scenarios of external financial turbulence. Faced with capital outflows from non-residents due to global risk scenarios, agents that manage long-term savings tend to cushion the impact on the local market by bringing in capital and taking advantage of the price conditions in local assets, which translates into a stabilization of the prices of local assets, including the value of our currency. Meanwhile, a deep capital market allows for investment horizons that favor the provision of risk coverage to companies, through derivative contracts, or the development of an insurance industry that provides benefits to households and productive activities. In short, a deep market favors financing at lower rates of mortgage credit, which is very sensitive for households, of long-term investment projects, for example, in public infrastructure, as well as fiscal financing in better rate and term conditions, all of which results in greater opportunities for economic growth, jobs and benefits for society as a whole. Its robustness requires scrutiny and continuous improvement in a challenging environment. In this regard, the Bank and the other regulatory authorities of the national financial system are working on the suggestions emanating from a recent evaluation by the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank. The main recommendations relate to the need to strengthen the integrated supervision of financial conglomerates, the creation of a bank resolution framework and a consolidated credit reporting system. Both this assessment, and several previous reports, have highlighted the benefits of advancing in this dimension. Other recommendations relate to the implementation of an institutional bank resolution system, updating the deposit insurance scheme. With regard to the Central Bank's field of action, progress continues with the financial policy agenda to strengthen the local market, with initiatives related to payment systems, convergence with international standards in the regulation of bank liquidity and the beginning of the implementation of the Countercyclical Capital Requirement mechanism. The latter is a macro-prudential tool available to the Central Bank and whose implementation fits within the framework of the new regulatory provisions of Basel III, which consists of the option of setting a countercyclical capital buffer that may fluctuate between 0 and 2.5% of risk-weighted bank assets, and which will be examined biannually at the Financial Policy Meetings. Although this decision rests with the Council, the process involves a high level of coordination with the CMF, which must issue a favorable prior report if necessary. In fact, prior to the publication of this Report, the Board held the first Financial Policy Meeting, where it determined to keep the countercyclical capital buffer inactive. This, in a context where credit growth remains limited and whose reason for GDP remains below its long-term trend. Climate Change, the Financial System and Central Banking Along with the short-term risks to financial stability analyzed in this IEF, a thematic chapter associated with climate change is included, which accounts for the challenges it implies and the need to make progress in quantifying the risks to the stability of the financial system. Agents will be affected in multiple dimensions, and we must be prepared to anticipate potential systemic effects. This will require adequate tools to quantify their impact. This has motivated the Bank to design a work agenda in line with its objectives, which includes the development of stress tests with climate considerations for the banking system, incorporating this issue into its financial stability monitoring tools, and generating knowledge and statistics for the better fulfillment of its functions. It is important to note that this involves multiple challenges, as it requires the development of very long-term models unlike the models normally used by central banks and stress tests, and of high complexity. Efforts involve a set of dimensions that we must learn to measure and relate appropriately, which entails a complex learning process. This thematic chapter is a first step towards the realization of these objectives, always in line with its mandate. IEF 2022S1 Thematic Chapter Climate Change, the Financial System and Central Banking The consequences of climate change are already visible and will deepen in the coming decades under practically all scenarios, with negative impacts on the economy and financial stability. Agents will be affected in multiple dimensions with potentially systemic effects, which need to be evaluated and mitigated. This process entails risks that will fall on the financial system, which must be anticipated and have adequate tools to quantify their impact. This has motivated the BCCh to design a work agenda in line with its objectives, which includes the development of stress tests with climate considerations for the banking system, incorporating this topic into its financial stability monitoring tools and generating knowledge and statistics for the better fulfillment of its functions. This thematic chapter is a first step towards the realization of these objectives in line with its mandate. Final Comments Since the previous IEF, international financial conditions have deteriorated in a context of high uncertainty. The prolongation of Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and the massive quarantines in China, have accentuated inflationary pressures, which has led the authorities to accelerate their monetary normalization process. All of this has reduced global growth prospects. At the local level, the macroeconomic imbalances accumulated during 2021, political uncertainty, and the shallower depth of the capital market, especially in the long term, have not only limited the financing capacity of longer-term projectsincluding the purchase of homesbut have also reduced the economy's possibilities to absorb external shocks. Households and firms have been able to continue paying their debts, although some sectors are more vulnerable to the deterioration in financing conditions. Banks are resilient and have an adequate solvency and liquidity position. Among the main risks are i) Deterioration of global liquidity and ii) Deepening of the macroeconomic imbalances accumulated in 2021 and measures that go along these lines. In addition, and as a challenge ahead, it is necessary to rebuild slack in our economy, and among them, to strengthen a capital market that allows greater financing in local currency at more convenient rates for long-term projects, including mortgage loans, infrastructure projects, etc., and whose robustness and good functioning result in greater stability for the economy and less exposure to external financial turbulence. En este contexto, resalta la importancia de recomponer un fondo estable de ahorros de largo plazo, lo que favorece el financiamiento de proyectos de inversin y facilita la mitigacin de turbulencias financieras externas. Finalmente, quiero aprovechar esta ocasin para poner en conocimiento de esta Comisin el inicio de un nuevo proceso de planificacin estratgica al interior del Banco Central, trabajo que dar origen a la carta de navegacin institucional para el perodo 2023 - 2027. En su desarrollo, contempla la realizacin de diversas instancias de encuentro y participacin con las distintas reas de la organizacin, as como diversas instancias de escucha activa con nuestros distintos grupos de referencia. Llevaremos a cabo este trabajo inspirado en la visin de seguir siendo una institucin confiable, de carcter tcnico y probada excelencia en el logro de sus objetivos, siempre velando por el principal atributo del Banco Central: la confianza que la ciudadana ha depositado en nosotros. Muchas gracias 22

Title: Riesgos y Oportunidades para la Economa Chilena . Rosanna Costa, Presidenta
text: Risks and opportunities for the Chilean economy i1) Rosanna Costa President, Central Bank of Chile November 25, 2022 Introduction Good morning. I would like to begin by thanking you for the invitation to present at this activity of the Chile Investment Forum, as well as greeting the other speakers, Jose de Gregorio, remembered former President of the Central Bank, and Jorge Selaive, who was also part of the Bank. I will dedicate this presentation to reviewing the advances, risks and opportunities facing our economy. Let me start with a brief analysis of what has happened in the most recent moment. The current state of the Chilean macro The Chilean economy has entered a phase of adjustment after the significant imbalances it accumulated in previous quarters. The data of the last few months account for two relevant phenomena. On the one hand, annual inflation has stopped increasing and, as expected, shows a slight decline. It is important to note that although the latest data  the CPI for October  surprised to the downside after several months of significant upward differences, it is only an observation and, without a doubt, by itself, does not constitute a sufficient piece of information to draw further conclusions. On the other hand, spending, and especially private consumption, has begun to undo the strong increases it showed in 2021. The Central Bank has made a significant adjustment of monetary policy, taking it to a clearly restrictive level. At our last Monetary Policy Meeting, which we held in October, we raised the Monetary Policy Rate to 11.25%, totaling a very significant increase compared to the technical minimum of 0.5% in July 2021. As we mentioned in the communique of that Meeting, we estimate that the MPR has reached the maximum level of the current cycle. We also noted that the rate would remain at 11.25% for the time needed to ensure inflation convergence to the target over the two-year policy horizon. Similarly, we emphasize that the risks of the macroeconomic scenario are very high and their short- and medium-term implications must be carefully evaluated. The inevitable questions are: how has our central scenario and risks evolved from the IPoM until now? And, of course, what are its implications for politics? f1) Presentation made at the Chile Investment Forum Seminar "A look at the main economic and financial challenges for 2023". Santiago, Chile. monetary? In what follows I will review the recent evolution of the main variables, however, the in-depth analysis of them and the degree of incidence of each one will be developed in the December IPoM. To begin with, it is important to remember how we got to the inflationary situation we face today. To this end, it is useful to review the evolution of inflation projections in some of our IPoM and what we expected to happen with the activity gap (Chart 1). In March 2021, when inflation was at 3% and we projected that it would remain around that level for the next two years, we saw a gap that would later widen due to the reimposition of health restrictions during that time. This deterioration, in any case, was considered transitory. In fact, what the data showed us later was an economy that adapted much better to the quarantines, with effects on activity that were less than expected. In the second quarter of 2021, a very significant boost was added to the economy, through a third withdrawal of pension funds and universal fiscal transfers that were extended during the second half of that year. It is important to note that we are talking about a third withdrawal and, therefore, its effect and that of the transfers on the spending capacity of households was cumulative on the liquidity they had already received from the two previous withdrawals. This sum of resources had a very significant impact on spending, with a gap that, far from going towards balance, became significantly positive towards the third quarter of last year. Added to this was the effect on the exchange rate, which incorporated factors of local uncertainty, which to this day keep it in real terms well above its historical levels, adding that its pass-through coefficient to domestic prices was higher given the origin of its depreciation. As the months progressed, the evolution of demand showed that the effect of household liquidity on consumption was even greater than initially expected. Added was the assessment that inflationary persistence was increasing, amid constant and significant upward surprises in inflation and expectations that increased over different maturities In several IPoMs of the last year we have identified the relevance of the sum of the local factors that I have just mentioned on the rise in inflation, indicating that in the order of two thirds of the increase that we have accumulated has been related to them. The remaining third is associated with various external shocks . Among these, the problems in global distribution chains, which have been dragging on far beyond what was initially thought, the lack of inventories and the impacts of the war in Ukraine on commodity prices. In addition, the appreciation of the dollar at the global level, a more recent phenomenon, motivated by greater risk aversion in a context of high global inflation, financial conditions that have tightened in the world and high volatility in the financial markets. However, the medium-term inflationary effects of the latter factor mitigate the short-term impacts. Thus, we arrive at our last IPoM, in September, where we estimate that annual inflation would peak in the third quarter of this year. While the data for September and October are aligned with that projection, annual inflation remains very high and it is too early to speak clearly of a change in trend. These data would show that the problem did not continue to worsen, but they are still far from the levels of inflation that the economy requires. In fact, when we compare the inflation projected for the end of the year in the IPoM, which was 12%, it is still below what market prices and expert surveys consider today, despite the downward surprise in October. Going to the most recent data, annual inflation has fallen, reaching 12.8% in October. At the cluster level, it is interesting to note that core CPI  as measured by the non-volatile CPI  also declined, which is somewhat more evident in goods prices. By contrast, food prices continue to rise in annual terms (Chart 2). Behind the recent behavior of inflation there is a set of factors. On the one hand, it is important to mention that some elements that were putting pressure on costs have begun to ease, highlighting the drop in transportation costs and gasoline. The price of food in global markets has also begun to fall, although, as I mentioned earlier, its pass-through to local prices is not yet visible (Chart 3). Either way, while all of these cost factors haven't returned to levels that could be considered normal, at least they're stopping pushing as hard. On the other hand, although incipiently, there is a slight downward trend in core inflation, particularly in goods, despite the depreciation that the peso has accumulated in the year. Beyond the recent behavior of these elements, the evolution of inflation is based on a monetary policy that has made a significant adjustment and is promoting the resolution of the imbalances present in the economy. A fiscal policy is added that has also made a relevant adjustment in spending. As for inflation expectations, these remain high. In particular, two-year measures persist above 3%, with expectations of companies well above that value. Over the year, experts' expectations have fallen somewhat more sharply (Chart 4). Regarding the resolution of the imbalances accumulated in 2021, the data for the third quarter confirm, in general, that the economy is already in an adjustment phase. As usual, there are always some differences with respect to what was projected, although the preliminary evaluation shows an adjustment underway, despite recognizing a better performance of the investment. In the case of private consumption, two facts stand out. First, the continuation of the correction in the consumption of durable goods. At the time of greater availability of liquidity by households  around the third quarter of 2021  this part of consumption increased by more than 50% compared to the level it showed in the third quarter of 2019 (Chart 5). As it is largely concentrated in imported goods, the sharp rise in this consumption had an impact on the current account. By the third quarter of this year, a relevant part of that increase has been undone. A second fact to highlight is the trajectory of the consumption of services, which after the lifting of limitations on supply  due to health restrictions  shows a gradual recovery towards levels above those reached prior to the pandemic, and around what seem to be more consistent with an extrapolation of its trend. The evolution of consumption has taken place in a context in which the liquidity received during 2021 has been exhausted, employment has stagnated and real wages have been falling for several months (Graph 6). In the latter case, it highlights that the annual variation in real wages has been negative for almost a year. On the investment side, the data for the third quarter show a clearly better performance than expected. Both gross fixed capital formation in machinery and equipment and in construction and works reported a positive result in the quarter, especially the former (Chart 7). In this part of the expenditure, investment in machinery and equipment for electricity generation projects stood out. Investment in trucks and buses also contributed to the result. In the GFCF under construction and other works, the increase in investment associated with services and housing construction was striking. However, the outlook for investment remains weak. The latest cadastre of the Capital Goods Corporation shows declining investment amounts for the period 2022 - 2025 and the expectations of companies remain at pessimistic values. In any case, the levels of uncertainty have been reduced in recent months, which could help somewhat in the behavior of investment going forward (Chart 8). Continuing with this process of adjustment of the economy is vital, among other elements, to reduce the high current account deficit. In the last rolling year, it accumulated a deficit of 9.9% of GDP, the highest figure in many years. By component, it shows a low level of the balance of trade in goods, together with negative balances in services and income (Chart 9). It is important to remember that the deficit observed since 2021 is largely due to lower national savings. As I explained a few minutes ago, the fiscal measures in the midst of the pandemic plus the withdrawals of pension funds caused an unprecedented expansion of domestic demand. Both government and household savings fell significantly in 2021, an effect that still persists in the annual accumulated deficit as of the third quarter of 2022. In addition, the recovery in investment since 2021  including its better performance in the third quarter  and lower sales, all of which have contributed to companies' savings returning to negative values. In any case, the factors behind the loss of national savings have been in retreat. Tax aid is not as large as last year's and private consumption has moderated. Other factors behind the current account deficit are the fall in the terms of trade and high transportation costs. The latter explain much of the deterioration in the balance of services and, as I mentioned a few minutes ago, they are correcting. The high level of the current account deficit is certainly a fact of concern. We are following it closely and we estimate that in the coming it will begin to reduce. Under the inflation targeting regime, the increases in the MPR and the depreciation of the peso will contribute to the increase in private savings and the reduction of demand and supply imbalances. Greater public savings and the return of other factors, such as high transport costs, will also collaborate. Thus, we expect 2023 and 2024 to return to sustainable levels. Risks and opportunities for the Chilean economy Let me conclude with some thoughts on the risks and opportunities facing our economy. Without a doubt, we are in a complex moment and solving it is a priority task. Reducing inflation cannot wait, families need to recover their purchasing power and leave behind the concern about changes in prices. At the Central Bank we are committed to reducing inflation to 3%. The action of monetary policy is cooperating with the adjustment of the economy, which is directing prices in that direction. As we have mentioned, we are doing what is necessary to make this process orderly, brief and as inexpensive as possible. But there are significant risks. The evolution of the global economic scenario has become a significant source of concern. Both the emerging and developed worlds have become more sensitive to abrupt changes in global financial conditions. The increase in government and corporate indebtedness is a relevant factor at this point, especially in an environment in which the rise in inflation and the reaction of central banks have been raising debt costs and risk aversion (Chart 10). The external boost that our economy will receive has been reduced in recent quarters. In fact, the outlook for global growth has deteriorated progressively over the course of this year, and the probability of a recession in developed economies rises to 60%. The most recent market projections  Consensus Forecasts for November 2022  consider that the Eurozone's GDP will contract by 0.2% in 2023, while that of the US will have a slightly positive variation (0.2%) (Chart 11). This scenario confronts us with high volatility, whose impacts on the economy can be significant. Markets have been reacting with unusual force to both unexpected data and statements. For example, it could not be ruled out that, in the event of surprises in inflation, especially in the US, we will observe sudden movements in the exchange rate, rates or risk premiums. Although these movements may be temporary, their magnitude could cause significant impacts or introduce greater degrees of uncertainty in local markets. In this complex scenario, it is important that we make every effort to improve our ability to mitigate shocks . On the one hand, we must continue to make progress in the process of inflation convergence. As I said, our economy is already in a phase of adjustment of the imbalances accumulated in 2021, a process that is not without costs, but it is necessary and inevitable. On the other hand, it is important for the economy to be able to rebuild the buffers that have allowed it to cushion external shocks in the past. Our capital market has been strongly affected in recent years, and has not managed to recover its depth and stabilizing role in the face of external financial pressures. It is particularly important to prioritize measures and policies aimed at promoting stable long-term savings. Beyond the challenges imposed by this situation, a solid and deep capital market is a significant contribution to economic development, because, among many things, it also allows financing for public and private projects. On the economic policy side, restoring balances and increasing our resilience depends on all our efforts pointing in the same direction. Otherwise, we will only make the process more difficult, lengthen it and end up generating higher costs. The economy will adjust in one way or another, but it is up to us to make the process as smooth as possible. In conclusion, I would just like to reiterate the Central Bank's commitment to the process of reducing inflation. We understand that this is a priority task for all families and we are doing our best to make this happen soon and mean the lowest possible cost for everyone. Thanks a lot. text_original: Riesgos y oportunidades para la economa chilena 1) Rosanna Costa Presidenta, Banco Central de Chile 25 de noviembre de 2022 Introduccin Muy buenos das. Quiero partir por agradecer la invitacin a presentar en esta actividad del Chile Investment Forum, tambin saludar a los otros expositores, Jos de Gregorio, recordado ex Presidente del Banco Central, y Jorge Selaive quien tambin fue parte del Banco. Dedicar esta exposicin a repasar los avances, riesgos y oportunidades que enfrenta nuestra economa. Djenme partir con un breve anlisis de lo que ha ocurrido en lo ms reciente. El estado actual de la macro chilena La economa chilena ha ingresado en una fase de ajuste tras los importantes desequilibrios que acumul en trimestres previos. Los datos de los ltimos meses dan cuenta de dos fenmenos relevantes. Por un lado, la inflacin anual ha dejado de aumentar y, acorde con lo esperado, muestra un leve retroceso. Es importante notar que si bien el ltimo dato el IPC de octubre- sorprendi a la baja tras varios meses de significativas diferencias al alza, es solo una observacin y, sin duda, por s sola, no constituye una pieza de informacin suficiente para sacar mayores conclusiones. Por otro lado, el gasto, y especialmente el consumo privado, ha empezado a deshacer los fuertes incrementos que mostr en 2021. El Banco Central ha efectuado un ajuste significativo de la poltica monetaria, llevndola a una instancia claramente restrictiva. En nuestra ltima Reunin de Poltica Monetaria, que realizamos en octubre, elevamos la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria hasta 11,25%, totalizando un aumento muy relevante respecto del mnimo tcnico de 0,5% en que se encontraba en julio de 2021. Como mencionamos en el comunicado de esa Reunin, estimamos que la TPM ha llegado al nivel mximo del actual ciclo. Asimismo, sealamos que la tasa se mantendra en 11,25% por el tiempo necesario para asegurar la convergencia de la inflacin a la meta en el horizonte de poltica de dos aos. Del mismo modo, enfatizamos que los riesgos del escenario macroeconmico son muy elevados y sus implicancias de corto y mediano plazo deben ser evaluadas cuidadosamente. Las preguntas inevitables son cmo ha evolucionado nuestro escenario central y los riesgos desde el IPoM hasta ahora? Y, por supuesto, cules son sus implicancias para la poltica f1) Presentacin realizada en el Seminario del Chile Investment Forum "Una mirada a los principales desafos econmicos y financieros para el 2023". Santiago, Chile. 1 monetaria? En lo que sigue voy a revisar la evolucin reciente de las principales variables, no obstante, el anlisis profundo de las mismas y el grado de incidencia de cada una corresponder desarrollarlo en el IPoM de diciembre. Para comenzar es importante recordar cmo llegamos hasta la situacin inflacionaria que enfrentamos hoy. Para esto, es til revisar la evolucin de las proyecciones de inflacin en algunos de nuestros IPoM y qu esperbamos ocurriera con la brecha de actividad (grfico 1). En marzo de 2021, cuando la inflacin estaba en 3% y proyectbamos que se mantendra en torno a ese nivel por los prximos dos aos, veamos una brecha que ms adelante tendra una ampliacin debido a la reimposicin de restricciones sanitarias durante esa poca. Ese deterioro, en todo caso, se estimaba transitorio. De hecho, lo que nos mostraron los datos con posterioridad fue una economa que se adapt de mucho mejor forma a las cuarentenas, con efectos en la actividad que fueron menores a lo esperado. En el segundo trimestre de 2021 se aadi un impulso muy significativo a la economa, a travs de un tercer retiro de fondos previsionales y transferencias fiscales universales que se extendieron durante la segunda mitad de ese ao. Es importante notar que estamos hablando de un tercer retiro y, por tanto, su efecto y el de las transferencias en la capacidad de gasto de los hogares era acumulativo sobre la liquidez que ya haban recibido a partir de los dos retiros anteriores. Esta suma de recursos provoc un impacto muy significativo en el gasto, con una brecha que, lejos de ir hacia el equilibrio, se torn significativamente positiva hacia el tercer trimestre del ao pasado. A ello se sum el efecto en el tipo de cambio, que incorporaba factores de incertidumbre local, que hasta hoy lo mantienen en trminos reales bastante sobre sus niveles histricos, sumando que su coeficiente de traspaso a precios internos fue mayor dado el origen de su depreciacin. En la medida que avanzaron los meses, la evolucin de la demanda dio cuenta que el efecto de la liquidez de los hogares en el consumo fue incluso mayor al inicialmente esperado. Se aadi la evaluacin de que la persistencia inflacionaria iba en aumento, en medio de constantes y significativas sorpresas al alza de la inflacin y expectativas que se incrementaban a distintos plazos En varios IPoM del ltimo ao hemos identificado la relevancia de la suma de los factores locales que acabo de mencionar sobre el alza de la inflacin, indicando que del orden de dos tercios del incremento que hemos acumulado se ha relacionado con ellos. El tercio restante se asocia a diversos shocks de ndole externa. Entre estos, los problemas en las cadenas de distribucin global, que se han ido prolongando mucho ms all de lo inicialmente pensado, la falta de inventarios y los impactos de la guerra en Ucrania sobre los precios de los commodities. Se agrega la apreciacin del dlar a nivel global, fenmeno ms reciente, motivado por la mayor aversin al riesgo en un contexto de elevada inflacin global, condiciones financieras 2 que se han do estrechando en el mundo y una alta volatilidad en los mercados financieros. Con todo, los efectos inflacionarios de mediano plazo de este ltimo factor mitigan los impactos de corto plazo. De este modo, llegamos a nuestro ltimo IPoM, el de septiembre, donde estimamos que la inflacin anual alcanzara su peak en el tercer trimestre de este ao. Si bien los datos de septiembre y octubre estn alineados con esa proyeccin, la inflacin anual sigue siendo muy elevada y es demasiado pronto para hablar con claridad de un cambio de tendencia. Estos datos estaran dando cuenta de que el problema no sigui agravndose, pero estn an muy lejos de los niveles de inflacin que la economa requiere. De hecho, cuando comparamos la inflacin proyectada para fines de ao en el IPoM, que era de 12%, ella sigue estando por debajo de lo que consideran hoy los precios de mercado y las encuestas a expertos, pese a la sorpresa a la baja de octubre. Yendo a los datos ms recientes, la inflacin anual ha descendido, llegando a 12,8% en octubre. A nivel de agrupaciones, es interesante notar que el IPC subyacente medido por el IPC sin voltiles tambin descendi, el que es algo ms evidente en los precios de los bienes. Por el contrario, el precio de los alimentos sigue aumentando en trminos anuales (grfico 2). Detrs del comportamiento reciente de la inflacin hay un conjunto de factores. Por un lado, es importante mencionar que algunos elementos que estaban presionando los costos han comenzado a aliviarse, destacando la baja de los costos de transporte y la gasolina. El precio de los alimentos en los mercados globales tambin ha comenzado a ceder, aunque, como coment recin, an no se observa su traspaso a los precios locales, que siguen aumentando (grfico 3). De cualquier forma, si bien todos estos factores de costos no han vuelto a niveles que podran considerarse normales, al menos estn dejando de presionar con tanta fuerza. Por otro lado, aunque de forma incipiente, asoma una leve tendencia a la baja en la inflacin subyacente, particularmente en bienes, pese a la depreciacin que ha acumulado el peso en el ao. Ms all del comportamiento reciente de estos elementos, la evolucin de la inflacin se fundamenta en una poltica monetaria que ha hecho un ajuste significativo y est propiciando la resolucin de los desequilibrios presentes en la economa. Se aade una poltica fiscal que tambin ha realizado un ajuste relevante del gasto. En cuanto a las expectativas de inflacin, estas siguen siendo elevadas. En particular, las medidas a dos aos plazo persisten por sobre 3%, con expectativas de empresas bastante por sobre ese valor. A un ao plazo, las expectativas de expertos han tenido un descenso algo ms marcado (grfico 4). Respecto de la resolucin de los desequilibrios acumulados en 2021, los datos del tercer trimestre confirman, en general, que la economa ya est en una fase de ajuste. Como es habitual, siempre 3 existen algunas diferencias respecto de lo proyectado, aunque la evaluacin preliminar da cuenta de un ajuste en marcha, no obstante reconocer un mejor desempeo de la inversin. En el caso del consumo privado, resaltan dos hechos. Primero, la continuacin de la correccin del consumo de bienes durables. En el momento de mayor disponibilidad de liquidez por parte de los hogares alrededor del tercer trimestre de 2021, esta parte del consumo lleg a aumentar por sobre un 50% respecto del nivel que mostraba en el tercer trimestre de 2019 (grfico 5). Al ser en gran medida concentrado en bienes importados, la fuerte alza de este consumo tuvo un impacto en la cuenta corriente. Al tercer trimestre de este ao, se ha deshecho una parte relevante de esa alza. Un segundo hecho a resaltar es la trayectoria del consumo de servicios, que tras el levantamiento de las limitaciones a la oferta por las restricciones sanitarias muestra una recuperacin gradual hacia niveles sobre los alcanzados previos a la pandemia, y en torno a lo que parecen ser ms coherentes con una extrapolacin de su tendencia. La evolucin del consumo se ha dado en un contexto en que se ha do agotando la liquidez recibida durante 2021, el empleo se ha estancado y los salarios reales muestran cadas desde hace varios meses (grfico 6). En este ltimo caso, destaca que la variacin anual de los salarios reales ha sido negativa durante casi un ao. Por el lado de la inversin, los datos del tercer trimestre muestran un desempeo claramente mejor al esperado. Tanto la formacin bruta de capital fijo en maquinaria y equipos como en construccin y obras dieron cuenta de un resultado positivo en el trimestre, especialmente la primera de ellas (grfico 7). En esta parte del gasto destac la inversin en maquinaria y equipos para proyectos de generacin elctrica. Contribuy tambin al resultado la inversin en camiones y buses. En la FBCF en construccin y otras obras llam la atencin el incremento en la inversin asociada a servicios y edificacin habitacional. Con todo, las perspectivas para la inversin siguen siendo dbiles. El ltimo catastro de la Corporacin de Bienes de Capital muestra montos de inversin a la baja para el perodo 2022 - 2025 y las expectativas de las empresas siguen en valores pesimistas. En todo caso, los niveles de incertidumbre se han reducido en los ltimos meses, lo que podra ayudar algo en el comportamiento de la inversin en adelante (grfico 8). Continuar con este proceso de ajuste de la economa es vital, entre otros elementos, para reducir el elevado dficit de la cuenta corriente. En el ltimo ao mvil, sta acumul un dficit de 9,9% del PIB, la mayor cifra en muchos aos. Por componentes, muestra un bajo nivel del saldo de la balanza comercial de bienes, junto con saldos negativos en servicios y rentas (grfico 9). Es importante recordar que el dficit observado desde 2021 responde en buena parte al menor ahorro nacional. Como expliqu hace unos minutos, las medidas fiscales en medio de la pandemia ms los retiros de fondos previsionales provocaron una indita expansin de la demanda interna. Tanto el ahorro del gobierno como de los hogares cay significativamente en 2021, efecto que an 4 persiste en el dficit acumulado anual al tercer trimestre de 2022. Se suma la recuperacin de la inversin desde 2021 incluido su mejor desempeo en el tercer trimestre y menores ventas, todo lo que ha contribuido a que el ahorro de las empresas vuelva a valores negativos. En todo caso, los factores tras la prdida del ahorro nacional han ido en retirada. Las ayudas fiscales no tienen la envergadura de las del ao pasado y se ha moderado el consumo privado. Otros factores tras el dficit de la cuenta corriente son la cada en los trminos de intercambio y los altos costos de transporte. Estos ltimos explican gran parte del deterioro de la balanza de servicios y como mencion hace unos minutos, estn corrigindose. Sin duda que el elevado nivel del dficit de la cuenta corriente es un hecho que nos preocupa. Lo seguimos atentamente y estimamos que en lo venidero comenzar a reducirse. En el marco del rgimen de metas de inflacin, las alzas de la TPM y la depreciacin del peso contribuirn al aumento del ahorro privado y la reduccin de los desequilibrios de demanda y oferta. Tambin colaborar el mayor ahorro pblico y la devolucin de otros factores, como los altos costos de transporte. As, esperamos que 2023 y 2024 vuelva a niveles sostenibles. Riesgos y oportunidades para la economa chilena Permtanme finalizar con algunas reflexiones sobre los riesgos y oportunidades que enfrenta nuestra economa. Sin duda que estamos en un momento complejo y resolverlo es tarea prioritaria. Reducir la inflacin no puede esperar, las familias necesitan recuperar su capacidad de compra y dejar atrs la preocupacin por los cambios en los precios. En el Banco Central estamos comprometidos con la reduccin de la inflacin a 3%. La accin de la poltica monetaria est cooperando al ajuste de la economa, lo que encamina los precios en esa direccin. Como hemos mencionado, estamos haciendo lo necesario para que este proceso sea ordenado, breve y lo menos costoso posible. Pero hay riesgos importantes. La evolucin del escenario econmico mundial se ha transformado en una fuente significativa de preocupacin. Tanto el mundo emergente como el desarrollado se ha vuelto ms sensible a cambios abruptos en las condiciones financieras globales. El aumento del endeudamiento de gobiernos y empresas es un factor relevante en este punto, especialmente en un ambiente en que el alza de la inflacin y la reaccin de los bancos centrales ha ido elevando los costos de la deuda y la aversin al riesgo (grfico 10). El impulso externo que recibir nuestra economa se ha do reduciendo en los ltimos trimestres. De hecho, las perspectivas de crecimiento mundial se han deteriorado de forma progresiva a lo largo de este ao y la probabilidad de una recesin en las economas desarrolladas se empina a 60%. Las proyecciones ms recientes de mercado  Consensus Forecasts de noviembre 2022 5 consideran que el PIB de la Eurozona se contraer 0,2% en 2023, mientras el de EE.UU. tendr una variacin levemente positiva (+0,2%) (grfico 11). Este panorama nos enfrenta a una elevada volatilidad, cuyos impactos en la economa pueden llegar a ser significativos. Los mercados han estado reaccionando con inusual fuerza tanto a datos inesperados como a declaraciones. Por ejemplo, no podra descartarse que, ante sorpresas en la inflacin, especialmente en EE.UU., observemos movimientos bruscos en el tipo de cambio, tasas o premios por riesgo. Si bien estos movimientos pueden ser pasajeros, su magnitud podra provocar impactos de magnitud importante o introducir mayores grados de incertidumbre en los mercados locales. En este escenario tan complejo, es importante que hagamos todos los esfuerzos posibles por mejorar nuestra capacidad de mitigar los shocks. Por un lado, debemos seguir avanzando en el proceso de convergencia de la inflacin. Como lo dije, nuestra economa ya est en una fase de ajuste de los desbalances acumulados en 2021, proceso que no est exento de costos, pero es necesario e inevitable. Por otro lado, es importante que la economa logre recomponer los buffers que le han permitido amortiguar los shocks externos en el pasado. Nuestro mercado de capitales se vio fuertemente afectado en los ltimos aos, y no ha logrado recuperar su profundidad y rol estabilizador frente a las presiones financieras externas. Particularmente relevante es que se prioricen medidas y polticas orientadas a favorecer un ahorro estable de largo plazo. Ms all de los desafos que impone esta coyuntura, un mercado de capitales slido y profundo es un aporte significativo al desarrollo econmico, porque, entre muchas cosas, permite adems disponer de financiamiento para proyectos pblicos y privados. Del lado de las polticas econmicas, recuperar los equilibrios y aumentar nuestra capacidad de resiliencia depende de que todos nuestros esfuerzos apunten en la misma direccin. De otra forma, solo lograremos dificultar el proceso, alargarlo y terminar generando mayores costos. La economa se ajustar de un modo u otro, pero de nosotros depende que el proceso sea lo ms fluido posible. Para finalizar, solo quisiera reiterar el compromiso del Banco Central con el proceso de reduccin de la inflacin. Entendemos que esta es una tarea prioritaria para todas las familias y estamos realizando nuestros mejores esfuerzos para que esto ocurra pronto y signifique el menor costo posible para todos. Title: Avances y Desafos de la Economa Chilena - Rosanna Costa
text: bench central Chile Progress and challenges of the Chilean economy () Rosanna Costa President, Central Bank of Chile December 6, 2023 Good morning and thank you for the invitation. This is the third time that I participate in this traditional seminar organized by SOFOFA and the Universidad del Desarrollo. In the run-up to a new Monetary Policy Report (MPR), which we will publish in a couple of weeks, I would like to take this opportunity to review the recent economic situation and make some reflections for the end of 2023. A year ago, when we met in this very instance, our economy was going through a difficult situation. After the succession of several internal and external shocks  which have already been discussed at length  the economy accumulated significant imbalances and annual inflation was around 13%, slightly lower than the 14.1% recorded in August 2022. Monetary policy had reacted strongly, significantly increasing the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), to 11.25%, a level it had reached in October 2022. In addition, our projections of the MPR of December a year ago indicated that inflation would continue to fall, that it would take at least until 2024 to return to the 3% target and that the MPR would remain at 11.25% until we had greater certainty that the process of inflationary convergence was on the right track. Today, our estimates have materialized. We have solved a good part of the problems that afflicted us and the economy has undone the negative impacts of the excessive increase in spending that, in our case, was a central factor in the explanation of the inflationary dynamics. In this context, economic activity and private consumption have moved into a stabilization phase, savings show some recovery and the account deficit The current has decreased markedly (Graph 1). Externally, the rise in commodity prices and prices have eased. food caused by Russia's invasion of Ukraine. At the same time, global supply chains have been replenished following disruptions caused by the pandemic. Thus, the cost shock has been dissipating, which has had a special impact on the evolution of the prices of volatile items, which are leading the decline in inflation in most countries, including Chile. The sum of these developments has allowed the closing of the activity gap and the mitigation of inflationary pressures from an economy that for a long time was central Chile growing far beyond their means. Consistent with this, inflation has had a significant drop, despite the fact that it still remains at levels above 3% annually (Chart 2). In this context, both the projections of the IPoM for September of this year and the market expectations  which contain more up-to-date information  suggest that inflation will return to the 3% target during 2024 and that in the two-year term it will be around that figure (Chart 3). This is a significant change from what we saw last year, when medium-term inflation expectations exceeded 5% in some measurements. Undoubtedly, the fact that two-year expectations have once again been aligned with the target is good news, as it reflects a correct evolution of the macro and the validity of the measures adopted to contain inflation. In addition, it cooperates in the correct transmission of monetary policy to the economy. The pricing dynamics of companies have also been normalizing. The frequency of upward adjustments by these companies has decreased significantly compared to last year and is closer to its usual periodicity. This is consistent with demand and cost pressures that have been subsiding, beyond the fluctuations of exchange rates and other supply factors in recent times (Chart 4). As we have pointed out, there is no doubt that the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) will continue to decline. This was determined in our last three Monetary Policy Meetings (MPRs)  July, September and October  when we lowered the MPR by a total of 225 basis points. This lower monetary restriction has been visible especially in the commercial portfolio and in some lower-risk segments in the consumer portfolio, thus improving the cost of financing for both companies and individuals. The accommodation of imbalances has also led to a decrease in aggregate corporate indebtedness, although with heterogeneity between sectors, while household financial indicators have tended to stabilize. In this context, banks have remained resilient and have sufficient liquidity, provisions and capital to face severe stress episodes. Like the rest of the economic actors, it is important that it continues to strengthen its capacities to face new adverse events and the challenges ahead, such as the expiration of the support policies established during the pandemic, the increase in credit risk and the convergence to Basel III. On the fiscal front, it is pertinent to highlight the consolidation process, which has helped to resolve imbalances, but which is also essential to continue improving financing conditions for the rest of the economic agents. central Chile Thus, we must recognize that the Chilean economy has been making progress in resolving its imbalances. However, there are a number of challenges ahead and the risks are not minor. A first factor to consider is the fact that the action of central banks and the reaction of inflation have not been the same in all economies. Whether due to the promptness with which action was taken and/or the magnitude of monetary tightening, inflation and, mainly, its outlook are responding differently between countries. This has implications for both the current and expected levels of interest rates in different economies, putting pressure on currencies via movements in the rate differential. For example, in Latin America, with a few exceptions, inflation has fallen faster. However, inflation expectations have not responded in the same way. In fact, Chile is one of the countries that has managed to reduce inflation and align expectations with the 3% target, which has also meant that it is one of the economies where the expected path for the monetary policy rate leads the reduction of monetary tightening (Chart 5). In developed economies, on the other hand, central banks were slow to react and their inflation outlook has also been slower to adjust. The United States stands out, where the resilience of consumption and the labor market have supported persistent inflation, despite advances in the latter. In this case, the outlook for monetary policy has become clearly more restrictive than a few months ago, with the fedfunds rate already reaching higher levels than previously expected and will remain elevated for longer (Chart 6). All this has led to tighter-than-expected financial conditions. While monetary policy developments in the developed world have altered the outlook for shorter rates, a second factor has emerged that has also tightened longer-term financial conditions, with greater uncertainty about the level at which these rates will converge. Without wishing to ponder the relative relevance of each element, one can highlight the incipient doubts about fiscal policy in the United States, the noise associated with a more complex geopolitical environment after the recent events in the Middle East, and the apprehensions regarding the savings-investment balance in the medium term, in a context of higher war expenditures and to finance adaptation to climate change. As I pointed out, the relative relevance of each of the aforementioned elements is complex to estimate, especially in a context where we had an abrupt and significant increase in these rates during part of October and November. That was one of the most significant events of the last few years. weeks, as it caused a significant tightening of global financial conditions. In that period, the U.S. 10-year interest rate exceeded 5%, climbing to levels that were not at all levels. central Chile they had been observed for many years. This rise, in addition, permeated the rest of the economies. In Chile, in fact, the 10-year term rate reached values in the order of 7%, 150bp more than its average for the first half of the year. Equally noteworthy is the reversal of this increase observed in recent weeks. However, and beyond this relevant event, a trend remains in which, in most cases, long-term rates are above the levels of the beginning of the year (Chart 7). The dollar has also had ups and downs, which has affected the performance of the rest of the currencies, especially emerging currencies. Several of them have also felt the impact of a lower interest rate differential, due to the divergence in the path of monetary policies that I have already discussed. Without going any further, the Chilean peso has depreciated in the order of 9% since June to date, having reached values close to 950 during the second half of October. These exchange rate levels occurred on dates close to our last RPM. In it, as reported in the respective minutes, we observed that there was no single hypothesis that explained this greater depreciation. Our analysis pointed rather to risk factors, associated with the expected trajectories for monetary policy in Chile and the US that I have just mentioned, in a global context of uncertainty, which added volatility to the markets and with falling commodity prices. In any case, the levels of volatility that we have observed in local markets in recent times  following the trends of foreign markets  are not too far from their historical patterns (Chart 8). In the case of the Chilean exchange rate, its volatility continues to be at the top of the group of emerging economies, while for interest rates it is more limited. However, a few weeks ago the peso appreciated. Some of that strengthening came in the immediate aftermath of the October RPM. Another part has followed the dollar's movements globally (Chart 9). In short, externally, the emerging world faces a significant challenge. Particularly, how to deal with a significant increase in volatility in global financial markets, from which the Chilean market has not been exempt. In fact, this was one of the points we highlighted in the October RPM and in the Financial Stability Report (FSR) for the current semester. Although the tension has decreased significantly compared to the end of October, this is an element in development that we will have to continue to observe from now on and weigh appropriately, given its possible impacts on macro and inflationary convergence. central Chile A third factor is the evolution of the local economy and what trends we can extract from the economic information we are observing. A few weeks ago we learned the National Accounts figures for the third quarter, which showed GDP growth of 0.6% annually in that period, slightly higher than what we had forecast in September. Both this data and the Imacec for October, which registered an annual increase of 0.3%, show an economy that, in aggregate terms, once again ratifies that it is in a stabilization phase. In any case, underlying this result is the usual heterogeneity that occurs between economic sectors and that is important to address. The start-up of Quebrada Blanca Phase II, among other elements, has given some greater impetus to copper production. This was especially visible in mining activity during the third quarter. Non-mining activity, meanwhile, looks stable. The positive impact of the greater availability of water resources on electricity generation and the resilience of different branches linked to services stands out, to which industry is added at the margin, although without sufficient strength to consider the latter a clear trend. Likewise, several lines of commerce show an incipient rebound, although this sector still exhibits limited dynamism. For its part, the construction sector has continued to weaken. The situation in this area and in real estate has been affected by last year's cost increases, the deterioration of demand and financing restrictions. Both sectors would be among the most affected in the face of possible stress scenarios analysed in the last IEF (Graph 10). In terms of expenditure, at the aggregate level, there are no major differences between the actual data and the projections. Private consumption confirms its tendency to stabilize, after a strong adjustment during 2022 and until the first months of the current year. This is especially true in the demand for goods, while demand for services has completed several quarters without major changes (Graph 11). This performance of consumption occurs at the same time as a labor market that has been evolving according to the state of the economic cycle, with weak job creation and expectations that this outlook would continue in the coming months. However, real household incomes have gradually recovered, due to the positive impact of lower inflation. In gross fixed capital formation, the figures have been particularly volatile in its machinery and equipment component, something we have been observing for several quarters (Chart 12). Construction and works maintains a complex situation, which was endorsed by the qualitative information provided by the companies in the Business Perceptions Report (IPN) of November. In the latest survey applied within the framework of this report, a third of companies plan to invest next year. These allude to economic uncertainty as the main reason for not investing, to which has been added a growing concern about the performance of demand. central Chile Continuing on the qualitative level, the perceptions of companies and individuals persist at pessimistic levels. In fact, in our latest IPN  from November 2023  several elements are pointed out that should be followed carefully. On the one hand, companies highlighted the negative impact of the rise in costs they observed in recent months. This increase was largely associated with the depreciation of the exchange rate that occurred during the period of collection of the information, something that was replicated in the latest available version of the Survey of Determinants and Price Expectations (EDEP). In response, companies pointed out that this was damaging their margins, since it had also become more difficult to readjust prices given the weakness they perceived in demand. On the other hand, its prospects for business performance in 2024 were deteriorating. In any case, there is heterogeneity among economic sectors, as in the figures for the third quarter that I just commented on. Final comments In light of this background, and without anticipating projections, which are the subject of the IPoM that we will announce on December 20, allow me to conclude with some reflections. As I told you at the beginning of my presentation, we are culminating a year that began with very significant imbalances in the economy, with inflation that exceeded double digits and a monetary policy that acted accordingly with this complex scenario. With everyone's efforts, we have managed to significantly reduce these imbalances, highlighting that inflation has decreased by more than 7 percentage points in the last year, which has allowed Chile to be one of the first countries to begin to cut its interest rate However, there are two issues that I would not like to miss regarding this 2023. The first is not to forget the challenging and adverse experience of living with inflation considerably high. Just a few months ago, inflation was among the main concerns of households and businesses. Undoubtedly, in one way or another, the vast majority of the country's inhabitants felt the negative impact of the high, rapid and widespread increase in prices in the economy. The impact was even greater for low-income families, who saw their purchasing power greatly affected. It is important to remember the difficult times, to avoid repeating them and to draw lessons. The second point is to remember that, although the advances in controlling inflation have indeed been important and we can outline their convergence, if there are no unexpected events, this process is not yet over. Inflation stands at 5% annually and we must be thorough to achieve its convergence to the 3% target, as it is a condition that allows the economy to develop to its full potential. central Chile In this way, we are moving towards a challenging 2024, in an uncertain global environment, which has recently shown us its sensitive reaction to different economic and financial events, all of which has an impact on local markets. It is necessary that we carefully evaluate the evolution of the macro, extracting the trends indicated by the information we are receiving and what their implications are for inflation and its convergence to the target, which has been more complex in recent times, given that we have had to lead the economy through intense shocks. successive and infrequent. However, and without losing sight of these risks, it is also true that starting a new year with an economy that has been solving its inflationary problems represents a better relative position to strengthen our economic activity. In addition, the reduction of the MPR will have a positive impact on access to financing for both companies and individuals. We are in an environment of high volatility, where it becomes more complex to correctly read the information that each figure or movement of the markets gives us. Therefore, as I have just mentioned, it is necessary that, beyond a specific figure or the difference it has with respect to what was expected, we carefully evaluate the evolution of the macro and extract the trends. An economy that recovers its equilibrium allows activity to resume higher rates of expansion and develop in accordance with its potential. For this reason, it is essential that we pay attention to medium-term growth and the ways in which we can increase it. In this context, I can tell you that in our next IPoM, in addition to shedding light on the form that the process of reducing the monetary policy rate will take, we will announce a review of the structural parameters of the economy, including medium-term or trend growth and the neutral level of the interest rate. This will allow us to better calibrate our next decisions, so that we can more precisely refine the doses of adjustment that the economy needs. As always, there are risks present and they are taking on new dimensions. In particular, recent months have seen tighter global financial conditions and high financial volatility. An economy in order, as I said before, would allow us to better face scenarios that become more adverse, so it is important that we continue on that path and on the path of recovering our capacities.
