Si bien no reviste un riesgo para el sistema financiero, s requiere atencin y seguimiento, en particular en circunstancias en las cuales los hogares estn experimentando el impacto negativo de la elevada inflacin sobre el poder de compra de sus ingresos, en una economa que sigue combatiendo los efectos de los desbalances ampliamente referidos. Los espacios para abordarlo en un contexto inflacionario son ms acotados. El Banco Central ha manifestado claramente su compromiso con la convergencia de la inflacin a la meta. Este proceso no tiene atajos fciles. Inflaciones altas que se mantienen en el tiempo se vuelven cada vez ms persistentes y difciles de controlar, agravando los ciclos de combatirla. Una inflacin elevada es muy costosa para todos, pero especialmente para las personas ms vulnerables. Muchas gracias. 12

Title: Evolucin y Tendencias de los Pagos. Rosanna Costa, Presidenta
text: bench central Chile EVOLUTION AND TRENDS IN PAYMENTS ()Rosan na Costa President of the Central Bank of Chile August 8, 2023 Introduction Good morning. First of all, I want to thank the attendees of this event, in which the Second Report on Payment Systems of the Central Bank of Chile (ISiP) is presented. Following the practice of other emerging and advanced economies, the Central Bank published its First Payment Systems Report just over a year ago. This allows us to complement the information usually provided to the market through the Monetary Policy Report and the Financial Stability Report, and is in line with our mandate to ensure the normal functioning of internal and external payments, one of the Bank's two central objectives. To discuss the main trends and developments presented in this version of the 2023 Payment System Report, today we are joined by representatives of different financial institutions and infrastructures, some with many years of experience in the payments ecosystem and others who have been joining this market more recently. We also have the attendance of representatives of local and international regulatory and supervisory institutions. I would also like to thank in a very special way the outstanding panelists and exhibitors who will share their vision on future trends and challenges, which will undoubtedly be relevant for the evolution and development of payment systems for Chile. I would like to take this opportunity to thank the Central Bank teams that collaborated in the preparation of the ISiP and those who contributed to the development of this event. Payments make it easier for economic activity to take place and are at the heart of central banks' functions Every day, people make payments for goods and services. In the same way, companies carry out transactions, which, in addition to goods and services, in many cases include various financial instruments, such as stocks, bonds, derivatives, among others. bench central Chile As we are used to these transactions being carried out relatively easily and through multiple means today, we generally do not consider the possibility that the means of payment we use every day are not available, and new generations are often surprised at how payments were settled in the past. When we use electricity, water or internet supply services, we expect them to be always available, regardless of the complex network of processes and infrastructures (pipes, pylons and telecommunications) that make this possible. In the same way, for each payment to reach its recipient, there is also a complex network of institutions, operational processes and risk management that must function properly. In this sense, in a modern economy, a payment system works properly when aspects such as: (i) availability of banknotes and coins are sufficiently secured and protected; (ii) access to and availability of electronic means of payment; (iii) extensive merchant acquiring networks (which allow payment online and in person with electronic means of payment); (iv) efficient and secure clearing and settlement processes for payments; (v) adequate security measures to prevent fraud and money laundering; (vi) safeguarding the use of our personal data; (vii) competition in order to have efficient means and; (viii) adequate technology that facilitates access to and generation of payments. All this requires the participation of a very broad set of financial institutions, payment providers, Financial Market Infrastructures (MFIs), and technology service providers, among others. And, of course, the role of financial authorities in the regulation, supervision and monitoring of the operation of payment systems. Given the relevance of payment systems to the functioning of the financial system and the economy as a whole, in addition to the issuance of legal tender, central banks in most parts of the world have mandates related to the continuity of payment systems and their efficient and secure operation. In Chile, the Central Bank's contribution to this objective is permanent: (i) through the distribution of cash to the population in the amount and opportunity that requires it; (ii) directly operating and managing the interbank payment system (known as the Real-Time Gross Settlement System or RTGS); and (iii) establishing prudential regulation standards for adequate risk management of the main players in both high- and low-value payment systems. In this last dimension, the role of the Financial Market Commission is fundamental, which allows the supervision of the regulations established by the BCCh or directly establishing standards and central Chile requiring compliance in the case of securities clearing and settlement systems. Technological innovation in payments is permanent and accelerated Technological advances in this area are dizzying and are a particularly relevant catalyst for the transformation of the payments industry. This is addressed in the Payment System Report and will be discussed in greater depth this morning in the two panels of this Seminar. Among the main trends that are observed, both in the world and in Chile, is the rapid irruption of digital payments, leading traditional means such as checks or cash payments to persistently lose share. Initially, this process occurred mainly through the growth of card payments, which allowed face-to-face payments in stores. However, in recent years, along with the growth of e-commerce, what we understand as a "card" has been evolving with the development of multiple applications and systems that allow payments to be made online, through cell phones or with QR codes. This dematerializes the cards, and at the same time allows for increased competition. Thus, in today's digital payments, P2P payments (e.g., person-to-person or person-to-merchant) that allow instant transfers of funds between accounts are increasingly relevant. Faced with the potential of these payment methods, a growing number of central banks around the world, including the Central Bank of Chile, are developing technological projects or policy developments to promote the development of so-called instant payments. We hope to be able to deepen the analysis and perspectives in this dimension, which is described in the Report, in the first panel of this seminar. In Chile, as can be seen in the Payment System Report published today and as we will see during this day, we have a very relevant use of Electronic Funds Transfers (EFTs), with accumulated annual transactions that exceed 80% of GDP. However, we still identify a relevant space for the emergence and expansion of new payment applications, based on the available TEF system. In this sense, some entrepreneurs are already advancing in such applications through a process called "payment initiation". This activity is now regulated by the recently enacted Fintee Law, which allows the development of open finance systems or open banking and encourages the multiplication of payment applications in the local market, as well as the possibility of integrating them with other financial services. To collect experiences and real cases of these new modalities of approach to the offer of financial services, we have scheduled the second panel of this seminar. central Chile How does the BCCh face this scenario? Given the relevance of payments in the mandate of the Central Bank, and the accelerated process of innovation that this industry is going through, its incorporation into the new Strategic Plan of the BCCh for the period 2023-2027 arose naturally. One of the five strategic objectives of this Plan is to "contribute to the development of efficient and inclusive means of payment", for which we want to promote payment systems that are in line with technological changes and user preferences, adapting the regulatory framework and infrastructures, as necessary. What are the elements that are marking the payments industry today and that are relevant for our country? First, the Fintech industry ceased to be a promise and became a reality. The new business models and proposals that we observe in the retail payments ecosystem, as well as the Fintech Law, are certainly a recognition of that. Therefore, its potential benefits and its interaction with other financial institutions and infrastructures in terms of efficiency, financial inclusion and competition are beginning to materialize. At the same time, potential risks to financial stability are also becoming increasingly present, as they grow in the number of users, amounts transacted and in their degree of interconnection within the system. Secondly, new activities or business models such as open banking or cross-border acquiring not initially contemplated in the regulatory framework represent a challenge. To the extent that they are activities that generate value for users and the economy and achieve relevant degrees of penetration, it is necessary to channel these activities within the regulatory perimeter, in order to mitigate the risks for both their users and the financial system and that all payments are correctly settled to their beneficiaries. Third, as I mentioned earlier, in several jurisdictions the use of cash  nothing less than the traditional means of payment provided by central banks  is ceding territory, with a progressive migration to electronic means of payment. The Covid pandemic was a trigger that mobilized and brought electronic media closer to the usual routine of homes. Fourthly, also at the international level, it is observed that technology makes it possible to make all processes related to payments more efficient and secure. An adequate balance that allows progress in innovation without risking the integrity of a secure and efficient payment system is essential. Part of these developments are at the local level in the strengthening of our instant payment system; the modernization of the System central Chile RTGS to operate longer hours and with more participants; and the incorporation of the Chilean peso into CLS, among other potentialities. Finally, there are frictions  some of them long-standing  that cannot necessarily be resolved through the powers of the Central Bank, but we certainly observe and monitor with special interest, as they affect the satisfaction of users with respect to their means of payment, as they are related to the efficiency of the payment system as a whole. The foregoing includes, among others, aspects related to the distribution of cash, the universal acceptance of prepaid cards, and tariff aspects related to payment cards. What are we up to? The BCCh's concern about the functioning of payment systems is certainly not recent. In fact, in recent years we have made a series of regulatory adjustments, for example, to enable the operation of the 4-Party Model for the issuance and operation of payment cards; in addition to promoting the adoption of international best practices for Financial Market Infrastructures. We have a Payment Schedule, which is described in detail in Chapter 3 of this Payment Report. Its main components are: i) the regulation of Low Value Payment Chambers, which will strengthen the existing instant payment system; ii) the adjustments to the rules of Operation and Issuance of Payment Cards that were put up for consultation a few weeks ago and that, among other things, will strengthen the regulatory framework of Payment Service Providers and regulate the so-called cross-border acquiring; (iii) the settlement of the clearing house's operations of payment transactions in dollars in the RTGS System, which will allow spot exchange operations to be carried out with greater safeguards for banking companies; iv) persevere with efforts to incorporate the Chilean peso into the CLS System, which would be facilitated with the eventual approval of the Resilience Bill; and v) to continue with the process of exploring the eventual issuance of the Chilean peso in digital format, the next milestone of which is the publication of a Second Report in the coming weeks in which the progress made from last year to now will be communicated. The Strategic Plan sets a direction and an objective, always linked to our legal mandate to ensure the normal functioning of payments. By declaring as a strategic objective "to contribute to the development of efficient and inclusive means of payment", we ratify that at the center of our work is to support the rapid evolution of payments, considering degrees of flexibility to adapt it based on circumstances, which can be especially dynamic in terms of payments. Therefore, the Payment Agenda just described can be adapted to changes in the environment. It should be noted that, in any case, there is a permanent challenge of reconciling different objectives: how to ensure the efficiency and security of the payment system, without inhibiting innovation; or secure central Chile the provision of cash and at the same time explore the eventual issuance of the peso in another format. Thus, during the period of validity of this Strategic Plan, our efforts will focus on deepening the understanding of the determining factors in the development and use of the different means of payment  cash and electronic payments  and identifying areas for improvement for the local payment system. To this end, it is important to timely recognize the technological changes and people's preferences that affect the access, security, and efficiency of payment methods, including existing business models and payment methods and those emerging or developing. To this end, in addition to internal analysis, information collection, and surveys, it is important to deepen the monitoring of relevant metrics and indicators, and market intelligence, as well as new instances of interaction with the payment industry and users of the system. We will continue to monitor developments in this area in order to be able to provide a regulatory framework for payment methods and infrastructure that generates an environment conducive to their proper functioning. In addition, it is envisaged to further modernise the payment infrastructure managed by the Central Bank (RTGS system and related systems) to adapt it to future challenges. Finally, like most central banks, we need to keep an eye on developments globally on central bank digital currencies. We must be up to date in knowledge, analysis and have the capabilities to address its risks and potential benefits. All of the above in order to have a payment system that contributes to the well-being of society. This seminar is part of these efforts. The market developments and initiatives of the Central Bank of Chile that I have described above are part of the contents of this edition of the Payments Report, which contains information and statistics that we hope will contribute to the consolidation of the objectives set. A more detailed description of the main contents of this Report will be presented below by Rosario Celedon, Manager of the Financial Policy Division of the Central Bank of Chile. Thanks a lot.
text_original: banco central Chile EVOLUCIN Y TENDENCIAS DE LOS PAGOS (*) Rosan na Costa Presidenta del Banco Central de Chile 8 de agosto 2023 Introduccin Buenos das. En primer lugar, quiero agradecer a los asistentes a este evento, en el que se presenta el Segundo Informe de Sistemas de Pago del Banco Central de Chile (ISiP). Siguiendo la prctica de otras economas emergentes y avanzadas, el Banco Central public su Primer Informe de Sistemas de Pago hace algo ms de un ao. Esto permite complementar la informacin entregada habitualmente al mercado a travs del Informe de Poltica Monetaria y el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera, y se encuentra en lnea con nuestro mandato de velar por el normal funcionamiento de los pagos internos y externos, uno de los dos objetivos centrales del Banco. Para discutir las principales tendencias y desarrollo que se presentan en esta versin del Informe de Sistema de Pagos 2023 hoy nos acompaan representantes de distintas entidades financieras e infraestructuras, algunos con muchos aos de experiencia en el ecosistema de pagos y otros que se han ido incorporando a este mercado ms recientemente. Tambin tenemos la concurrencia de representantes de instituciones de regulacin y supervisin, locales e internacionales. Quiero agradecer tambin de manera muy especial a los destacados panelistas y expositores que compartirn su visin sobre tendencias y desafos futuros, que sin duda sern relevantes para la evolucin y desarrollo de los sistemas de pago para Chile. Aprovecho de agradecer a los equipos del Banco Central que colaboraron en la preparacin del ISiP y a quienes contribuyeron al desarrollo de este evento. Los pagos facilitan que la actividad econmica se lleve a cabo y estn en el centro de las funciones de los bancos centrales Todos los das, las personas realizamos pagos por bienes y servicios. De la misma forma, las empresas realizan transacciones, las que, adems de bienes y servicios, en muchos casos incluyen diversos instrumentos financieros, como acciones, bonos, derivados, entre otros. (*) Presentacin realizada en el Seminario Presentacin Informe de Sistemas de Pago 2023. 1 banco central Chile Como estamos acostumbrados a que, en la actualidad, estas transacciones se realicen con relativa facilidad y a travs de mltiples medios, generalmente no consideramos la posibilidad de que los medios de pagos que usamos todos los das no estn disponibles, y las nuevas generaciones muchas veces se sorprenden de cmo se liquidaban los pagos en el pasado. Cuando utilizamos servicios de suministro de electricidad, agua o internet, esperamos que estn siempre disponibles, sin considerar la compleja red de procesos e infraestructuras (tuberas, torres de alta tensin y telecomunicaciones) que lo hacen posible. De la misma manera, para que cada pago llegue a su destinatario existe tambin una compleja red de instituciones, procesos operacionales y gestin de riesgos que deben funcionar adecuadamente. En este sentido, en una economa moderna, un sistema de pago funciona apropiadamente cuando se encuentran suficientemente asegurados y resguardados aspectos tales como: (i) disponibilidad de billetes y monedas; (ii) acceso y disponibilidad de medios de pagos electrnicos; (iii) redes de adquirencia de comercios extensas (que permiten pagar en lnea y en forma presencial con medios de pago electrnicos); (iv) procesos de compensacin y liquidacin de pagos eficientes y seguros; (v) medidas de seguridad adecuadas para prevenir el fraude y el lavado de activos; (vi) resguardo del uso de nuestros datos personales; (vii) competencia de modo de contar con medios eficientes y; (viii) tecnologa adecuada que facilite el acceso y generacin de los pagos. Todo esto requiere la participacin de un conjunto muy amplio de entidades financieras, proveedores de medios de pago, Infraestructuras de los Mercados Financieros (IMF), y proveedores de servicios tecnolgicos, entre otros. Y, por cierto, el rol de las autoridades financieras en la regulacin, supervisin y monitoreo/oversight del funcionamiento de los sistemas de pagos. Dada la relevancia de los sistemas de pago para el funcionamiento del sistema financiero y de la economa en su conjunto, adems de la emisin del dinero de curso legal, los bancos centrales en la mayor parte del mundo tienen mandatos relacionados con la continuidad de los sistemas de pagos y su funcionamiento eficiente y seguro. En Chile, la contribucin del Banco Central a ese objetivo es permanente: (i) a travs de la distribucin de efectivo a la poblacin en la cantidad y oportunidad que lo requiera; (ii) operando y gestionando directamente el sistema de pagos interbancario (conocido como Sistema de Liquidacin Bruta en Tiempo Real o LBTR); y (iii) estableciendo estndares de regulacin prudencial para una adecuada gestin de riesgo de los principales actores de los sistemas de pago tanto de alto como bajo valor. En esta ltima dimensin, resulta fundamental el rol de la Comisin para el Mercado Financiero, que permite la fiscalizacin de las regulaciones establecidas por el BCCh o estableciendo directamente estndares y 2 banco central Chile exigiendo su cumplimiento en el caso de los sistemas de compensacin y liquidacin de valores. La innovacin tecnolgica en los pagos es permanente y acelerada Los avances tecnolgicos en esta rea son vertiginosos y son un catalizador especialmente relevante para la transformacin de la industria de pagos. Esto se aborda en el Informe de Sistema de Pagos y se discutir con mayor profundidad durante esta maana en los dos paneles de este Seminario. Entre las principales tendencias que se observan, tanto en el mundo como en Chile, est la rpida irrupcin de los pagos digitales, llevando a que los medios tradicionales como cheques o pagos en efectivo pierdan participacin de manera persistente. Inicialmente, este proceso se produca fundamentalmente a travs del crecimiento de pagos con tarjetas, que permitan pagos presenciales en los comercios. Sin embargo, en los ltimos aos, junto con el crecimiento del comercio electrnico, lo que entendemos por "tarjeta" ha ido evolucionando con el desarrollo de mltiples aplicaciones y sistemas que permiten instruir pagos en lnea, a travs de telfonos celulares o con cdigos QR. Ello desmaterializa a las tarjetas, y a la vez permite aumentar la competencia. As, en los pagos digitales de la actualidad son cada vez ms relevantes los pagos P2P (por ejemplo, persona a persona o persona a comercio) que permiten transferencias instantneas de fondos entre cuentas. Frente al potencial de estas modalidades de pago, un nmero creciente de bancos centrales en el mundo, incluyendo el Banco Central de Chile, estn elaborando proyectos tecnolgicos o desarrollos de poltica para promover el desarrollo de los denominados pagos instantneos. Esperamos poder profundizar el anlisis y perspectivas en esta dimensin, que est descrita en el Informe, en el primer panel de este seminario. En Chile, como se da cuenta en el Informe de Sistema de Pagos que se publica hoy y como veremos durante esta jornada, contamos con un muy relevante uso de Transferencias Electrnicas de Fondos (TEF), con transacciones anuales acumuladas que superan el 80% del PIB. Sin embargo, todava identificamos un espacio relevante para el surgimiento y expansin de nuevas aplicaciones de pago, basadas en el sistema de TEF disponible. En este sentido, algunos emprendedores ya estn avanzando en tales aplicaciones a travs de un proceso denominado "iniciacin de pagos". Esta actividad pasa a estar regulada en la Ley Fintee, recientemente promulgada, lo que permite el desarrollo de los sistemas de finanzas abiertas u open banking y propicia la multiplicacin de las aplicaciones de pago en el mercado local, as como la posibilidad de integrarlas con otros servicios financieros. Para recoger experiencias y casos reales de estas nuevas modalidades de aproximacin a la oferta de servicios financieros tenemos programado el segundo panel de este seminario. 3 banco central Chile Cmo enfrenta el BCCh este escenario? Dada la relevancia que tienen los pagos en el mandato del Banco Central, y el proceso acelerado de innovacin por el que atraviesa esta industria, su incorporacin en el nuevo Plan Estratgico del BCCh para el perodo 2023-2027 surgi de manera natural. Uno de los cinco objetivos estratgicos de este Plan es "contribuir al desarrollo de medios de pago eficientes e inclusivos, para lo cual queremos promover sistemas de pagos que estn en lnea con los cambios tecnolgicos y de preferencias de los usuarios, adaptando el marco regulatorio e infraestructuras, segn sea necesario. Cules son los elementos que hoy estn marcando la industria de pagos y que son relevantes para nuestro pas? En primer lugar, la industria Fintech dej de ser una promesa y pas a ser una realidad. Los nuevos modelos de negocios y propuestas que observamos en el ecosistema de pagos minoristas, as como la Ley Fintech, ciertamente son un reconocimiento de aquello. Por ende, sus potenciales beneficios y su interaccin con otras instituciones e infraestructuras financieras en trminos de eficiencia, inclusin financiera y competencia se empiezan a materializar. Al mismo tiempo, los potenciales riesgos para la estabilidad financiera tambin pasan a estar cada vez ms presentes, en la medida que crecen en el nmero de usuarios, montos transados y en su grado de interconexin dentro del sistema. En segundo lugar, nuevas actividades o modelos de negocio como el open banking o la adquirencia transfronteriza no contemplados inicialmente en el marco regulatorio, representan un desafo. En la medida en que sean actividades que generen valor para los usuarios y la economa y logren grados de penetracin relevantes, es necesario canalizar estas actividades en el permetro regulatorio, de manera de mitigar los riesgos tanto para sus usuarios como para el sistema financiero y que todos los pagos sean liquidados correctamente a sus beneficiarios. En tercer lugar, como mencion anteriormente, en diversas jurisdicciones el uso del efectivo nada menos que el medio de pago tradicional provisto por los bancos centrales- cede territorio, con una progresiva migracin a medios de pago electrnicos. La pandemia del Covid fue un gatillo que moviliz y acerc los medios electrnicos a la habitualidad de los hogares. En cuarto lugar, tambin a nivel internacional, se observa que la tecnologa permite hacer ms eficientes y seguros todos los procesos relacionados con los pagos. Un adecuado balance que permita avanzar en innovacin sin arriesgar la integralidad de un sistema de pagos seguro y eficiente es fundamental. Parte de estos desarrollos estn a nivel local en el fortalecimiento de nuestro sistema de pagos instantneos; la modernizacin del Sistema 4 banco central Chile LBTR para que funcione por ms horas y con ms participantes; y la incorporacin del peso chileno a CLS, entre otras potencialidades. Por ltimo, existen fricciones algunas de larga data que no necesariamente pueden ser resueltas a travs de las atribuciones con que cuenta el Banco Central, pero ciertamente observamos y monitoreamos con especial inters, pues inciden en la satisfaccin de los usuarios respecto de sus medios de pago, pues se relacionan con la eficiencia del sistema de pago en su conjunto. Lo anterior incluye, entre otros, aspectos vinculados a la distribucin del efectivo, la aceptacin universal de tarjetas de prepago, y aspectos tarifarios relacionados con las tarjetas de pago. En qu estamos? La preocupacin del BCCh por el funcionamiento de los sistemas de pago ciertamente no es reciente. De hecho, en los ltimos aos hemos realizado una serie de ajustes normativos, por ejemplo, para habilitar el funcionamiento del Modelo de 4 Partes para la emisin y operacin de tarjetas de pago; adems de promover la adopcin de las mejores prcticas internacionales para las Infraestructuras del Mercado Financiero. Tenemos una Agenda de Pagos, que se describe en detalle en el Captulo 3 de este Informe de Pagos. Sus principales componentes son: i) la regulacin de Cmaras de Pago de Bajo Valor, que fortalecer el sistema de pagos instantneos existentes; ii) los ajustes a las normas de Operacin y Emisin de Tarjetas de Pago que fueron puestos en consulta hace pocas semanas y que, entre otras cosas, fortalecer el marco regulatorio de los Proveedores de Servicios de Pago y regular la denominada adquirencia transfronteriza; iii) la liquidacin de las operaciones de la cmara de compensacin de operaciones de pago en dlares en el Sistema LBTR, que permitir que las operaciones de cambio spot se realicen con mayores resguardos para las empresas bancarias; iv) perseverar con los esfuerzos para incorporar al peso chileno al Sistema CLS, lo que se facilitara con la eventual aprobacin del Proyecto de Ley de Resiliencia; y v) continuar con el proceso de exploracin de la eventual emisin del peso chileno en formato digital, cuyo siguiente hito es la publicacin de un Segundo Informe en las prximas semanas en el que se comunicarn los avances realizados desde el ao pasado hasta ahora. El Plan Estratgico marca una direccin y un objetivo, siempre vinculado a nuestro mandato legal de velar por el normal funcionamiento de los pagos. Al declarar como objetivo estratgico "contribuir al desarrollo de medios de pago eficientes e inclusivos", ratificamos que en el centro de nuestro quehacer est dar soporte a la rpida evolucin de los pagos, considerando grados de flexibilidad para adaptarlo en base a las circunstancias, las que pueden ser especialmente dinmicas en lo que a pagos se refiere. Por lo tanto, la Agenda de Pagos recin descrita se podr ir adaptando a los cambios en el entorno. Cabe notar que, en todo caso, existe un desafo permanente de conciliar diferentes objetivos: cmo asegurar la eficiencia y seguridad del sistema de pagos, sin inhibir la innovacin; o asegurar 5 banco central Chile la provisin de efectivo y explorar al mismo tiempo la eventual emisin del peso en otro formato. As, durante el periodo de vigencia de este Plan Estratgico, nuestro esfuerzo se centrar en profundizar la comprensin de factores determinantes del desarrollo y uso de los distintos medios de pago efectivo y pagos electrnicos, e identificar los espacios de mejora para el sistema de pagos local. Para estos efectos, es importante reconocer oportunamente los cambios tecnolgicos y de las preferencias de las personas que incidan sobre el acceso, seguridad y eficiencia de los medios de pago, incluyendo los modelos de negocio y medios de pago existentes y aquellos emergentes o en desarrollo. Para ello, adems del anlisis interno, recopilacin de informacin, y encuestas, es importante profundizar el seguimiento de mtricas e indicadores relevantes, e inteligencia de mercado, as como nuevas instancias de interaccin con la industria de pagos y los usuarios del sistema. Continuaremos monitoreando los desarrollos en este mbito a fin de ser capaces de proveer un marco regulatorio para los medios de pago y de infraestructura que genere un entorno propicio para su adecuado funcionamiento. Adems, se contempla seguir modernizando la infraestructura de pagos gestionada por el Banco Central (Sistema LBTR y sistemas conexos) para adaptarla a desafos futuros. Por ltimo, al igual que la mayora de los bancos centrales, debemos estar atentos a los desarrollos a nivel global sobre monedas digitales de bancos centrales. Debemos estar al da en el conocimiento, anlisis y contar con las capacidades para atender sus riesgos y sus potenciales beneficios. Todo lo anterior con el fin de disponer de un sistema de pagos que contribuya al bienestar de la sociedad. Este seminario forma parte de estos esfuerzos. Los desarrollos de mercado e iniciativas del Banco Central de Chile que les he descrito anteriormente son parte de los contenidos de esta edicin del Informe de Pagos, el cual contiene informacin y estadsticas que esperamos contribuyan en la consolidacin de los objetivos planteados. Una descripcin ms detallada de los principales contenidos de este Informe ser presentada a continuacin por Rosario Celedn, Gerenta de la Divisin de Poltica Financiera del Banco Central de Chile. Muchas gracias. 6

Title: Informe de Estabilidad Financiera Segundo Semestre 2023 - Rosanna Costa, Presidenta
text: bench central Chile Presentation of the Stability Report Financial before the Finance Committee of the Honorable Senate of the Republic Rosanna Costa President Central Bank of Chile November 8, 2023 Introduction Mr. Chairman of the Finance Committee, Senator Ricardo Lagos Weber, Senators who are members of this Commission. I am grateful for the invitation to present the vision of the Board of the Central Bank of Chile on the recent developments in the financial sector and implications for financial stability that are detailed in the Financial Stability Report (FSR) that we published this morning. This presentation is preceded by the Financial Policy Meeting that we held this Monday and Tuesday, an instance in which the Board of the Central Bank decided to maintain the Countercyclical Capital Requirement (CCR) for the banking system at a level of 0.5% of risk-weighted assets, which will be payable as of May 2024. This means that we are not making any changes from the decision we took last May. This Meeting is accompanied by a Financial Stability Report, which is part of the fulfillment of the objective of ensuring the stability of internal and external payments. From this perspective, the purpose of this Report is to focus on the vulnerabilities, risks, and mitigators of our financial system to absorb severe shocks. It is, therefore, a Report that, unlike the Monetary Policy Report, does not present projection scenarios, but, on the contrary, focuses on risk scenarios that, although less likely, are possible. The background information we have shows that the Chilean economy has continued to make progress in resolving its macroeconomic imbalances of previous years, which would allow us to better face unexpected shocks. Thus, in addition to the reduction in inflation and short-term interest rates  particularly those that are more related to monetary policy  there is a fall in corporate indebtedness and a normalization of the financial indicators of credit users. In any case, as usual, heterogeneity is observed among the different actors in the economy. For its part, local banks have sufficient liquidity, provisions, and capital to face severe stress scenarios. The external scenario has also offered some favorable news. Among them, that the events that affected regional banking in the United States during March have not generated tensions in global financial markets again. In fact, these have been the subject of a broad debate, from which lessons are already being drawn for bank supervision, regulation and resolution, which could lead to a redefinition of global regulation standards in the medium and long term. However, vulnerabilities are still present. However, on the international stage, events dominate that have increased risks. On the one hand, the evolution of the United States economy continues to be a source of uncertainty for global markets. In recent months we have seen a greater dynamism of its activity. which has increased doubts about how its inflation will evolve and has made both the Federal Reserve and the market expect that the monetary policy of that country to remain restrictive for longer. Doubts have been added regarding its fiscal situation, in the midst of a challenging economic and political environment in that country. More recently, the impact of greater geopolitical tensions has been added to the already complex international panorama, particularly after the events in the Middle East. In this context, we have observed a significant increase in volatility in global financial markets. They are being especially sensitive to any news that turns out to be somewhat different from what was expected, registering relevant changes in different variables in short periods of time. Internally, similar behavior has been observed, particularly in the foreign exchange market. The presence of increased volatility, by itself, is an element that should be observed with caution. On the one hand, it is important to understand its causes. On the other hand, it makes it difficult to extract clear signals regarding market trends and, of course, to correctly assess their short- and medium-term implications. For the time being, beyond the most recent movements, global financial conditions, particularly for emerging economies, have narrowed compared to what was observed a few months ago. The main risk faced is a worsening of this tightness, which will give way to abrupt changes in the markets. In this context, it is important that all actors in the economy continue to strengthen their capacities. In relation to banking, the expiration of the support policies established during the pandemic is approaching, in addition to the increase in credit risk and the convergence to Basel III. In the case of credit users and providers, the main risk is an abrupt deterioration in external financial conditions. In this context, the need to continue adopting measures aimed at strengthening the resilience and capacity of the financial system to cushion adverse events is reaffirmed. Next, I will review the background information that is part of the Financial Stability Report. Situation of the financial system International scenario As I indicated a few moments ago, the risks of the international scenario have increased and continue to be the main source of concern for the global macro-financial scenario. In this context, the main change has been the tightening and volatility of global financial conditions. In this scenario, US long-term interest rates have increased significantly, which has been transmitted to the rest of the economies, including Chile's. The ten-year rate in the United States has reached levels not seen since 2007, while rates in emerging and developed economies have also risen sharply (Chart 1). In recent days, after the meeting where the Federal Reserve decided to maintain its rate and the publication of data from the US labor market, these rates have had some setback. In any case, they remain high if they are reviewed in a historical perspective. On the other hand, the Federal Reserve (Fed) has reinforced the message of prolonged monetary tightening, without ruling out further hikes in the federal funds rate, which has increased the difference in the inflationary and monetary policy trajectory between economies. Thus, while in the developed world the process of inflationary convergence is more delayed, in the emerging world it has advanced faster and its monetary policies show prospects of less restriction (Chart 2). Thus, after a period of greater optimism, in recent months global financial markets have reported a lower appetite for risk, strengthening the dollar and negatively affecting the price of riskier assets. Compared to the beginning of September, the dollar -DXY- rose about 3% and the global risk indicator -VIX- increased. In any case, a reversal of these trends has been observed in recent days. As for the stock markets, they presented losses across the board, highlighting the fall of the emerging markets (Chart 3). The Chilean financial market has incorporated this greater perception of global risk, with an increase in the cost of long-term financing for all types of agents. Sovereign bond rates have had relevant increases since September to date  above emerging and developed economies. These increases were around lOOpb, both in nominal terms and in UF. In the case of the corporate sector, the 10-year UF rate is close to its highs in the last fifteen years. Mortgage loan rates have also risen, reaching 4.35%, one of the highest values since 2013 (Graph 4). It is important to remember that mortgage rates, because they correspond to long-term financing, are less related to monetary policy and do respond more to these changes in long-term financing. The response of the local financial market occurs in a context where the indicators that account for the depth of the local capital market remain low from a historical perspective. During this year, the fixed income market has presented higher amounts traded in nominal terms, considering both stock market and off-wheel operations, also known as OTC. However, measured in real terms, these amounts are equivalent to about half of what was recorded before the pandemic. In turn, local bond issuances are below their historical averages and the 2022 record, especially in the corporate sector. On the other hand, the assets of pension funds and mutual funds have not shown relevant changes in recent times. Thus, by the second quarter of 2023 they had stabilized at around 57% and 15% of GDP, respectively (Chart 5). The cost of short-term financing has decreased at the margin, in line with the traditional transmission pattern of local monetary policy. At the level of commercial credit, the reduction has been transversal by company size, an analysis that we had already released in a box of the Monetary Policy Report last September. On this occasion, as presented in one of the IEF boxes, we add the analysis for consumer loans, also based on microdata. A review of the data based on the credit history of the debtors shows reductions in the rates charged to the vast majority of customers. The difference occurs in those with no credit history, for whom the cost of credit has increased. This difference reflects, in part, the need to make progress in the provision of information on consolidated debt and payment behavior of individuals, as it is a direct benefit for those whose credit behavior is good (Chart 6). The peso has depreciated, following the global evolution of the dollar, the lower interest rate differential and the deterioration of the terms of trade. Thus, compared to the beginning of September, the exchange rate is about 8% higher, this without considering that during October it reached levels higher than the current ones. Multilateral measures have also had relevant increases, with increases of between 6 and 7% since the beginning of September. In recent days, after the communication and decisions of the Central Bank and the evolution of global markets, this trend has been partially reversed. Meanwhile, the local stock market has fallen, in line with the global trend (Chart 7). Stock market and exchange rate volatility has increased recently, also following trends in foreign markets. In the case of the Chilean exchange rate, its volatility remains at the top of the group of emerging economies. Interest rate volatility remains at levels similar to the previous Report, despite the above-mentioned increase in the level of interest rates (Chart 8). Importantly, the tightening of global financial conditions finds the world economy in a stage of limited growth, with high risks of further deterioration and lower expansion prospects for the coming years. According to the September IPoM projections, in 2023 the growth of global economic activity will be below its average of the last twenty years, and the outlook for 2024 reflects a further slowdown, both for developed and emerging economies. Thus, while in developed economies GDP growth would go from 1.3 to 0.1% between 2023 and 2024, in emerging economies it would rise from 3.8 to 3.5% in the same period. Added to this are several of the risk factors I have already discussed (Graph 9). Local scenario As I mentioned at the beginning of this presentation, this environment of greater external risks finds the Chilean economy on a better footing than a few quarters ago. The evolution of activity and expenditure - particularly consumption - shows that the macroeconomic imbalances accumulated in previous years have been resolved. Inflation has fallen from the high levels it reached in 2022, consolidating the process of convergence to the target. National savings have partly recovered, resulting in a significant reduction in the current account deficit. In this context, we have begun the process of reducing the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR), accumulating declines of 225bp from July to date. This process will continue in line with the evolution of the economy and the inflationary outlook, so that we ensure the convergence of inflation to the 3% target. Situation of companies On the business side, the smaller imbalances have resulted in a decrease in their aggregate indebtedness, as a result of a fall in most of their components. As of June 2023, corporate debt reached 109% of GDP. At that date, the financial indicators of the largest companies did not show major changes, with no relevant currency mismatches observed (Chart 10). More recent data show that companies have reduced the use of short-term debts, which are the most risky due to their exposure to high interest rates in historical comparison. Data released after the IEF in May show that commercial defaults have stabilized, with greater increases in the trade, construction and real estate sectors, and in companies that accessed Fogape-Covid loans. In any case, there are greater delays in the payment of debts, which could anticipate greater delinquency, such as that observed in September (Graph 11). Certain regulated sectors, such as ISAPRES, continue to be vulnerable. As in the previous IEF, stress exercises for companies show that one of their main vulnerabilities is exposure to interest rate risk. This is a risk that should decrease in the coming years, as the banking sector passes through the reduction of reference rates in the cost of commercial credits. The impact of the sales shock simulated in the stress test increases, highlighting its relevance among medium and large companies and in the trade, manufacturing and real estate sectors. This is explained by the fact that these groups register a lower level of effective sales than in the previous year and the size of their debt is larger. With a lower impact, the risk of indexation is mitigated by the lower holding of debt in UF. All in all, the debt at effective risk increased from 0.8 to 0.9% of GDP between the two years. This is almost entirely explained by the higher non-payment of companies that took advantage of support policies during the pandemic (Graph 12). As a reference, the estimated debt-at-risk is of a level similar to the sum of the actual commercial provisions and the additional expense of the banking stress exercise to which I will refer later, which suggests that banks have covered credit risk in a manner consistent with what emerges from this type of exercise based on microdata. It is important to remember that stress exercises correspond to hypothetical situations that subject the economy to extreme shocks, with very significant impacts on activity, employment and financial conditions. Its objective is to evaluate whether the current slack is sufficient to face these extremely adverse scenarios. It should be noted that, in view of the already tight external financial conditions, this Report conducted stress tests subject to more demanding shocks than usual for firms, households, and banks. Household situation As for households, their debt indicators have tended to stabilize in recent months, reducing their exposure to changes in interest rates. Thus, it can be seen that the lower dynamism of revolving loans, together with the reduction in the MPR, will contribute to reducing the vulnerability of the lowest income quintiles to high interest rates. Higher-income groups have shown a certain increase in their financial burden, due to the effect of inflation on mortgage payments. Total default shows some stabilization in the margin (Chart 13). In the future, a severe deterioration in the labor market is the main risk to households' ability to pay. As for the stress exercises for households, these show that the debt at effective risk increased from 1.2% in December last year to 1.4% of GDP in the second quarter of this year, in line with the higher effective default on consumer loans and the weakness of the labor market. Under the stress scenario, debt at total risk would amount to 4.1% of GDP (3.4% in the previous Report). Due to shocks, the risk of severe job destruction is what explains most of the increase, reaching 1.07% of GDP (0.3pp more than in December) and would be concentrated in the lowest income quintiles. Compared to the previous year, the rate shock has similar effects on the increase in debt at risk, while the indexation shock has a somewhat greater impact due to the greater holding of mortgage debt among higher-income households (Chart 14). Information subsequent to that used in this exercise indicates a stabilization in effective debt at risk, mainly as a result of a reduction in the use of short-term debt. Real estate The risk picture for the real estate sector is similar to that of the previous report. In the last two years, the industry has faced rising costs, weakened demand  with structural changes  and restrictive financing conditions. All this led to a fall in prices and an increase in inventories. Bank defaults by real estate companies have increased since mid-2022 and in the prospective risk exercise they appear within the main affected sectors, along with construction companies. In particular, the recent rise in long-term rates and their impact on mortgage rates could weaken the recent recovery in demand for housing. Tax situation On the fiscal front, consolidation has contributed to the resolution of macroeconomic imbalances. Maintaining it, with expenditures that are consistent with long-term structural revenues, is essential for the economy to have the capacity to mitigate the impact of future shocks, as indicated by the Autonomous Fiscal Council. It is important to note that there will be an increase in fiscal debt maturities in the coming years, in a context of tighter financial conditions. However, after a decade of increases in public debt, the background information set out in the latest Finance Report Public reports indicate that debt would continue to grow, to stabilize at 41% of GDP in the coming years. Banking situation Bank credit activity remains weak, affected by the low dynamism of the commercial segment. This portfolio has continued to decrease since the last Report, which is explained by the lower demand momentum in the last year and by credit supply conditions that continue to be perceived as restrictive according to various sources. Loans to households also remain weak, especially due to what is happening in the consumer portfolio and the moderation in the margin of mortgage credit flows (Graph 15). Banks have accumulated provisions for a possible increase in credit risk and have adequate levels of liquidity. In recent months, non-performing loans in the consumer and commercial portfolios have stabilised at levels of around 2.7% and 2.2% of the portfolio, respectively. However, banks maintain a high level of total provisions in historical perspective. Meanwhile, profitability shows a downward trend, with a recovery in net interest income and a lower margin for readjustability (Chart 16). Financial regulation developments at the local level Among the developments in local financial policy, the approval of the Law that Strengthens the Resilience of the Financial System and its Infrastructures and the beginning of the implementation of the Fintee Law stand out. Among other advances in the former, is the expansion of access to unbanked entities to the payment system operated by the Central Bank  the RTGS System. Likewise, the Central Bank will have new tools for liquidity management, both in normal times and in stressful situations. With respect to the Bank's Regulation Agenda, public consultation processes were opened in advance of the development of the initiatives announced in the previous Report: new tools for the management of banks' liquidity by enabling retained securitization schemes that would expand the availability of eligible collateral in operations with the Central Bank; incorporate appropriate safeguards to allow the operation of new business models in the payment card market; and improving information management in the final stage of the exchange rate modernization process. Main risks It is important to remember that financial policy has a risk-focused forward-looking view. This means that we constantly assess the occurrence of shocks that could have significant effects on the financial system and the economy. Sometimes, these shocks are of a low probability, but they have the characteristic that their realization could be very harmful. In this Report, we estimate that the evolution of external financial conditions is the main risk to monitor for global financial stability. On the one hand, tightening global financial conditions cannot be ruled out. On the other hand, after years of low interest rates, the search for yield and the evolution of financial markets could have incubated vulnerabilities in some sectors. The risks of reversal, financial fragmentation and tensions in non-bank financial intermediaries stand out. Geopolitical tensions are also a source of concern. The results of the exercises applied to banks indicate that sufficient levels of solvency and liquidity would be maintained to face the materialization of credit and market risks in stressed scenarios1/. The initial situation shows that banks maintain a Capital Adequacy Index (IAC) similar to that of the previous report (15.6 versus 15.5%), with profits that have moderated somewhat as the margin for readjustments decreases. This has been partially offset by net interest income. In the stress exercises, the impact of the severe scenario increased from 2.7 to 3 percentage points of the IAC. Therefore, capital slacks allow banks to face greater shocks, without the impact on the IAC differing substantially from the previous year (Chart 17). The results show that credit risk remains stable compared to the previous semester, contributing to the low dynamism of the consumer and commercial credit portfolio, and the provisioning policy. Market risk also remains contained, despite the volatility of international markets. This is helped by the fact that banks maintain a low term mismatch compared to the pre-pandemic period, even offsetting the greater rate shock applied. Valuation risk remains stable, although with a slight increase in currency risk, in line with the assumption of greater exchange rate depreciation. The results indicate that banks would maintain adequate levels of liquidity, above the regulatory requirements, which allows them to face disruptive events (Graph 17). However, like the rest of the agents in the economy, it is important that banks continue to strengthen their capacities to face new adverse events and address the expiration of the support policies delivered during the pandemic. Countercyclical Capital Requirement As I indicated at the beginning of this presentation, at our Financial Policy Meeting in the second half of 2023, the Board decided to maintain the Countercyclical Capital Requirement (CCR) for the banking system at a level of 0.5% of risk-weighted assets, which will be payable from May 2024. V This tool uses accounting data from the banking system to June and from the market until August of this year, considering an adverse stress scenario and a severe one. The adverse implies a slow and persistent slowdown in the economy. The severe one is an abrupt contraction in activity, accompanied by an increase in funding costs and a decrease in investment. In both, the falls in external demand and the deterioration of financial conditions have an effect on the cost of funding and the exchange rate. These shocks are greater than those of past years. As last May, when we activated the requirement, its maintenance is justified as a precautionary measure in the face of high external uncertainty, while, at the local level, the process of resolving macroeconomic imbalances continues. In fact, the increase in external risks keeps the possibility of an extreme negative event in place, which implies a significant decrease in credit. Thus, having a previously constituted capital buffer, which can be released when an event of this nature occurs, would help mitigate the impacts on the provision of credit to households and companies. The use of RCC and its relationship with other tools is still a matter of international debate. Throughout 2024, the Bank will review the CCR's implementation framework, including the definition of its neutral level. Final Thoughts Dear Senators. The Constitutional Organic Law gives the Bank the responsibility of ensuring the normal functioning of internal and external payments. In practice, this translates into a conduct of financial policy that, within the scope of its own competence, contributes to the stability of the financial system. Such stability occurs when the financial system performs its functions normally, without relevant disruptions, even in the face of adverse temporary situations. This is key to the correct transmission of monetary policy and, therefore, to generate an environment conducive to the economy developing its full potential. As economic theory points out, a stable financial system will be able to fulfill its key functions well, including efficient financing of investment. In this context, this Report is prepared to assess the health of the financial system and its capacity to face severe shocks. It should not be understood as a projection, but as one that focuses on the risks, vulnerabilities and mitigators of the system, always thinking about systemic risks. From this perspective, I would like to point out that in recent years we have faced a series of episodes that have tested our abilities and made us use part of the slack we have accumulated over the years. After several quarters since these events reached their peak, the Chilean economy has made progress in resolving macroeconomic imbalances. This puts us on a better footing to face the challenges of the future, but it does not exempt us from the fact that we must continue to make progress in consolidating this process. For example, while the gradual rebound in national savings has helped to tighten the current account deficit, the challenge is to bring it to higher levels. Although there are no obvious recipes for achieving this, macro and financial stability contribute to this end. Inflation has been reduced, but the process of convergence to the target has not been completed. Thus, a non-exhaustive overview indicates that after a complex period we have made progress, but we still have work to do and there are also some issues that may have more structural components and that represent short, medium and long-term challenges. One of these priority issues is the depth of our capital market. There are various metrics to quantify the liquidity and depth of financial markets, several of which we have previously documented. An update of what was shown in the previous IEF shows that, from the end of 2017 to October 2023, liquidity indicators in the fixed income and equity markets of some Latin America countries continue to show deterioration, which are somewhat more intense in Chile (Table 1). As I showed a few minutes ago, transactions in the local fixed income market have not recovered the levels of previous years. It is important to remember that a capital market with greater liquidity allows for adequate long-term financing, at a lower cost, while mitigating the impact of external shocks. As we have pointed out on other occasions, a deep market facilitates access to liquidity, both for companies and individuals, supporting economic growth and job creation, through an increase in investment and greater access to durable goods. It also reduces dependence on external financing and enables the development of the derivatives market, with the consequent lower exposure to foreign exchange risk. A deep capital market also facilitates the economy's accumulation of savings, improving access to long-term financing. Finally, it acts as a mechanism for absorbing external shocks, mitigating their effects on local agents. This role has been diminished in recent years and is becoming relevant in a context of greater global uncertainty. Dear Senators, the increase in external risks reaffirms the need to continue to rebuild slack and adopt measures aimed at strengthening the resilience of all economic actors and the financial system. The global economy is in a complex situation, which implies significant risks for emerging countries. Greater instability is added as a result of geopolitical conflicts. At the Central Bank, we will continue to work to meet our objectives and ensure that people and companies find the best possible conditions to develop their potential and achieve better well-being for all. text_original: banco central Chile Presentacin del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera ante la Comisin de Hacienda del Honorable Senado de la Repblica* Rosanna Costa Presidenta Banco Central de Chile 8 de noviembre de 2023 *EI Informe de Estabilidad Financiera del segundo semestre de 2023 se puede encontrar en http://www.bcentral.cl. Introduccin Seor Presidente de la Comisin de Hacienda, Senador Ricardo Lagos Weber, Senadores miembros de esta Comisin. Agradezco la invitacin para presentar la visin del Consejo del Banco Central de Chile sobre los desarrollos recientes del sector financiero e implicancias para la estabilidad financiera que se detallan en el Informe de Estabilidad Financiera (IEF) que publicamos esta maana. Esta presentacin viene precedida de la Reunin de Poltica Financiera que sostuvimos este lunes y martes, instancia en la que el Consejo del Banco Central decidi mantener el Requerimiento de Capital Contracclico (RCC) para el sistema bancario en un nivel de 0,5% de los activos ponderados por riesgo, el que ser exigible a partir de mayo de 2024. Esto significa que no realizamos cambios respecto de la decisin que adoptamos en mayo pasado. Esta Reunin se acompaa de un Informe de Estabilidad Financiera, que se inserta en el cumplimiento del objetivo de velar por la estabilidad de los pagos internos y externos. Desde esta perspectiva, el propsito de este Informe es centrarse en las vulnerabilidades, riesgos y mitigadores de nuestro sistema financiero para absorber shocks severos. Se trata, por tanto, de un Informe que, a diferencia del Informe de Poltica Monetaria, no presenta escenarios de proyeccin, sino que, por el contrario, se centra en escenarios de riesgos que, aunque menos probables, son posibles. Los antecedentes que disponemos muestran que la economa chilena ha seguido avanzando en la resolucin de sus desequilibrios macroeconmicos de aos previos, lo que nos permitira enfrentar de mejor forma shocks inesperados. As, a la reduccin de la inflacin y de las tasas de inters de corto plazo -particularmente aquellas que tienen mayor relacin con la poltica monetaria-, se suma una cada en el endeudamiento de las empresas y una normalizacin de los indicadores financieros de los usuarios de crdito. En todo caso, como es habitual, se observa heterogeneidad entre los distintos actores de la economa. Por su parte, la banca local cuenta con liquidez, provisiones y capital suficiente para enfrentar escenarios de tensin severos. El escenario externo tambin ha ofrecido algunas noticias favorables. Entre ellas, que los eventos que afectaron la banca regional de Estados Unidos durante marzo no han vuelto a generar tensiones en los mercados financieros globales. De hecho, estos han sido objeto de un amplio debate, del cual ya se estn extrayendo lecciones para la supervisin, regulacin y resolucin bancaria, las que podra decantar en una redefinicin de estndares de regulacin global en el mediano y largo plazo. Con todo, las vulnerabilidades siguen presentes. Sin embargo, en el escenario internacional dominan eventos que han incrementado los riesgos. Por un lado, la evolucin de la economa de Estados Unidos sigue siendo una fuente de incertidumbre para los mercados globales. En los ltimos meses hemos visto un mayor dinamismo de su actividad. 1 lo que ha aumentado las dudas sobre cmo evolucionar su inflacin y ha hecho que tanto la Reserva Federal como el mercado esperen que la poltica monetaria de ese pas se mantenga restrictiva por ms tiempo. Se han sumado dudas respecto de su situacin fiscal, en medio de un ambiento econmico y poltico desafiante en ese pas. En lo ms reciente, al ya complejo panorama internacional, se ha agregado el impacto de las mayores tensiones geopolticas, particularmente tras los eventos que se viven en Medio Oriente. En este contexto, hemos observado un alza significativa de la volatilidad en los mercados financieros globales. Estos, estn siendo especialmente sensibles a cualquier noticia que resulte algo distinta de lo esperado, registrndose cambios relevantes en distintas variables en perodos cortos de tiempo. Internamente, se ha observado un comportamiento similar, particularmente en el mercado cambiarlo. La presencia de una mayor volatilidad, por si sola, es un elemento que debe ser observado con cautela. Por un lado, es importante entender sus causas. Por otro, dificulta extraer seales claras respecto de las tendencias de los mercados y, por supuesto, aquilatar correctamente sus implicancias de corto y mediano plazo. Por lo pronto, ms all de los movimientos ms recientes, las condiciones financieras globales, particularmente para las economas emergentes, se han estrechado respecto de lo que se observaba hace unos meses. El principal riesgo que se enfrenta es una agudizacin de esta estrechez, que d paso a cambios abruptos en los mercados. En este contexto, es importante que todos los actores de la economa sigan fortaleciendo sus capacidades. En lo que dice relacin con la banca, se aproxima el vencimiento de las polticas de apoyo establecidas durante la pandemia, a lo que se suma el aumento del riesgo de crdito y la convergencia a Basilea III. En el caso de los usuarios y oferentes de crdito, el principal riesgo es un deterioro abrupto de las condiciones financieras externas. En este contexto, se reafirma la necesidad de continuar adoptando medidas orientadas a fortalecer la resiliencia y capacidad del sistema financiero para amortiguar eventos adversos. A continuacin, revisar los antecedentes que forman parte del Informe de Estabilidad Financiera. Situacin del sistema financiero Escenario internacional Como indiqu hace unos momentos, los riesgos del escenario internacional se han incrementado y siguen siendo la principal fuente de preocupacin para el escenario macro-financiero global. En ese contexto, el principal cambio ha sido el estrechamiento y volatilidad de las condiciones financieras mundiales. En este escenario, las tasas de inters de largo plazo estadounidenses han aumentado de forma relevante, lo que se ha transmitido al resto de las economas, incluida la chilena. La tasa a diez aos plazo de Estados Unidos se ha situado en niveles que no se observaban desde 2007, mientras las 2 tasas de economas emergentes y desarrolladas tambin han tenido aumentos importantes (grfico 1). En los ltimos das, tras la reunin donde la Reserva Federal decidi mantener su tasa y la publicacin de datos del mercado laboral estadounidense, estas tasas han tenido algn retroceso. En todo caso, siguen siendo elevadas si se revisan en una perspectiva histrica. Escenario local Como mencion al inicio de esta presentacin, este entorno de mayores riesgos externos encuentra a la economa chilena en un mejor pie que hace algunos trimestres. La evolucin de la actividad y el gasto -particularmente el consumo- da cuenta de que se han do resolviendo los desequilibrios macroeconmicos acumulados en aos anteriores. La inflacin ha descendido desde los elevados niveles que alcanz en 2022, afianzndose el proceso de convergencia a la meta. El ahorro nacional se ha recuperado en parte, con lo que el dficit de la cuenta corriente ha disminuido significativamente. En este contexto, hemos iniciado el proceso de reduccin de la Tasa de Poltica Monetaria (TPM), acumulando bajas por 225pb desde julio a la fecha. Situacin de las empresas Por el lado de las empresas, los menores desequilibrios se han traducido en una disminucin de su endeudamiento agregado, producto de una cada en la mayora de sus componentes. Este es un riesgo que debiera disminuir en los prximos ejercicios, a medida que el sector bancario traspase la baja de tasas de referencia en el costo de los crditos comerciales. El impacto del shock de ventas que se simula en la prueba de estrs aumenta, destacando su relevancia entre las empresas medianas y grandes y en los sectores comercio, manufactura e inmobiliario. Su objetivo es evaluar si las holguras actuales son suficientes para enfrentar estos escenarios extremadamente adversos. Principales riesgos Es importante recordar que la poltica financiera tiene una mirada prospectiva centrada en riesgos. Esto significa que evaluamos constantemente la ocurrencia de shocks que podran provocar efectos significativos en el sistema financiero y la economa. En ocasiones, estos shocks son de una baja probabilidad, pero tienen la caracterstica que su concrecin podra ser muy daina. En este Informe, estimamos que la evolucin de las condiciones financieras externas es el principal riesgo que monitorear para la estabilidad financiera global. 7 Por un lado, no puede descartarse que la estrechez de las condiciones financieras globales se intensifique. Por otro, luego de aos de tasas de inters en niveles bajos, la bsqueda de rentabilidad y la evolucin de los mercados financieros podra haber incubado vulnerabilidades en algunos sectores. Destacan los riesgos de reversin, de fragmentacin financiera y las tensiones en los intermediarios financieros no bancarios. Asimismo, las tensiones geopolticas tambin son una fuente de preocupacin. Los resultados de los ejercicios aplicados a la banca indican que se mantendran niveles de solvencia y liquidez suficientes para enfrentar la materializacin de riesgos de crdito y de mercado en escenarios tensionados1/. Los resultados muestran que el riesgo de crdito se mantiene estable respecto del semestre previo, en lo que contribuye el bajo dinamismo de la cartera de crdito de consumo y comercial, y la poltica de provisiones. El riesgo de mercado tambin se mantiene contenido, pese a la volatilidad de los mercados internacionales. Contribuye en ello que la banca mantiene un bajo descalce de plazo comparado con el perodo prepandemia, compensando incluso el mayor shock de tasas aplicado. El riesgo de valoracin sigue estable, aunque con una leve alza en el riesgo de moneda, en lnea con el supuesto de mayor depreciacin cambiara. Los resultados indican que la banca mantendra niveles adecuados de liquidez, por sobre los requerimientos reglatenos, que les permite enfrentar eventos disruptivos (grfico 17). Con todo, al igual que el resto de los agentes de la economa, es importante que la banca continu fortaleciendo sus capacidades para enfrentar nuevos eventos adversos y abordar el vencimiento de las polticas de apoyo entregadas durante la pandemia. En la prctica, esto se traduce en una conduccin de la poltica financiera que, desde el mbito propio de su competencia, contribuya a la estabilidad del sistema financiero. Dicha estabilidad se da cuando el sistema financiero realiza sus funciones con normalidad, sin disrupciones relevantes, an frente a situaciones temporales adversas. Esto resulta clave para la correcta transmisin de la poltica monetaria y, por ende, para generar un medio ambiente propicio para que la economa desarrolle todo su potencial. Como lo seala la teora econmica, un sistema financiero estable podr cumplir bien sus funciones clave, entre ellas un financiamiento eficiente a la inversin. En ese contexto, este Informe se prepara con el objeto de evaluar la salud del sistema financiero y su capacidad para enfrentar shocks severos. No debe entonces entenderse como una proyeccin, sino como uno que se enfoca en los riesgos, las vulnerabilidades y los mitigadores del sistema, siempre pensando en riesgos sistmicos. Desde esa perspectiva, destaco que en los ltimos aos nos hemos enfrentado a un conjunto de episodios que han puesto a prueba nuestras capacidades y nos han hecho utilizar parte de las holguras que acumulamos durante aos. Luego de varios trimestres desde que estos eventos alcanzaran su punto ms lgido, la economa chilena ha avanzado en la resolucin de los desequilibrios macroeconmicos. Esto nos coloca en un mejor pie para enfrentar los desafos del futuro, pero no nos exime del hecho que debemos seguir avanzando en la consolidacin de este proceso. Por ejemplo, si bien el gradual repunte del ahorro nacional ha contribuido a estrechar el dficit de la cuenta corriente, el desafo es lograr que este alcance mayores niveles. Aunque no hay recetas obvias para lograr esto, la estabilidad macro y financiera contribuyen a este fin. La inflacin se ha reducido, pero el proceso de convergencia a la meta no se ha completado. 9 De este modo, un recorrido no exhaustivo nos indica que tras un perodo complejo hemos do logrando avances, pero nos queda tarea pendiente y tambin se vislumbran algunos temas que pueden tener componentes ms estructurales y que representan desafos de corto, mediano y largo plazo. Uno de estos temas prioritarios es el de la profundidad de nuestro mercado de capitales. Existen diversas mtricas para cuantificar la liquidez y profundidad de los mercados financieros, varias de ellas las hemos documentado previamente. Una actualizacin de lo mostrado en el IEF previo, da cuanta que, desde fines de 2017 y hasta octubre de 2023, los indicadores de liquidez en los mercados de renta fija y variable de algunos pases de Latinoamrica siguen mostrando deterioros, los que son algo ms intensos en Chile (tabla 1). Como mostr haces unos minutos, las transacciones en el mercado de renta fija local no han recuperado los niveles de aos previos. Es importante recordar que un mercado de capitales con mayor liquidez permite sostener apropiadamente el financiamiento de largo plazo, a un costo ms bajo, a la vez que mitiga el impacto de los shocks externos. Como hemos sealado en otras ocasiones, un mercado profundo facilita el acceso a liquidez, tanto para empresas como personas, apoyando el crecimiento econmico y la generacin de empleo, mediante un incremento en la inversin y un mayor acceso a bienes durables. Asimismo, reduce la dependencia del financiamiento externo y posibilita el desarrollo del mercado de derivados, con la consecuente menor exposicin al riesgo cambiario. Un mercado de capitales profundo tambin facilita la acumulacin de ahorro de la economa, mejorando el acceso a financiamiento de largo plazo. Finalmente, acta como un mecanismo de absorcin de shocks externos, mitigando sus efectos sobre los agentes locales. Este rol se ha visto disminuido en los ltimos aos y cobra relevancia en un contexto de mayor incertidumbre global.
